${
  $d A B X i n p $.

  putnambench-putnam-1964-a3 $a |- A. X e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
    A. A e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
      A. B e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
        (
          (
            (
              (
                (
                  ran X C_
                    { p e. RR | ( 0 < p /\ p < 1 ) }
                  /\
                  { p e. RR | ( 0 < p /\ p < 1 ) } C_
                    (
                      ( cls ` ( TopOpen ` RRfld ) )
                      `
                      ran X
                    )
                )
                /\
                X : NN0 -1-1-> RR
              )
              /\
              A =
                (
                  n e. NN0 |->
                    (
                      ( X ` n )
                      -
                      sup
                      (
                        (
                          { 0 }
                          u.
                          { p e. RR |
                            (
                              p < ( X ` n )
                              /\
                              E. i e. NN0
                                (
                                  i < n
                                  /\
                                  p = ( X ` i )
                                )
                            )
                          }
                        )
                        ,
                        RR
                        ,
                        <
                      )
                    )
                )
            )
            /\
            B =
              (
                n e. NN0 |->
                  (
                    inf
                    (
                      (
                        { 1 }
                        u.
                        { p e. RR |
                          (
                            ( X ` n ) < p
                            /\
                            E. i e. NN0
                              (

                      ,

                      ,

                    -

          )
          ->
          sum_ n e. NN0
            (
              ( ( A ` n ) x. ( B ` n ) )
              x.
              ( ( A ` n ) + ( B ` n ) )

title: putnam_1964_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a3:
% distinct points dense in (0, 1) determine successive left and right gaps,
% whose products a_n*b_n*(a_n+b_n) sum to 1/3. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1964_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_set: TYPE = [real -> bool]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  range_set(x: real_sequence): real_set =
    LAMBDA (value: real):
      EXISTS (index: nat): value = x(index)

  open_unit_interval(value: real): bool =
    0 < value AND value < 1

  range_in_open_unit_interval(x: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat): open_unit_interval(x(index))

  dense_in_open_unit_interval(x: real_sequence): bool =
    range_in_open_unit_interval(x)
      AND FORALL (value: real):
        open_unit_interval(value) IMPLIES
          FORALL (radius: posreal):
            EXISTS (index: nat):
              abs(x(index) - value) < radius

  injective_sequence(x: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (first, second: nat):
      x(first) = x(second) IMPLIES first = second

  left_candidates(x: real_sequence, index: nat): real_set =
    LAMBDA (value: real):
      value = 0
        OR (value < x(index)
          AND EXISTS (earlier: nat):
            earlier < index AND value = x(earlier))

  right_candidates(x: real_sequence, index: nat): real_set =
    LAMBDA (value: real):
      value = 1
        OR (x(index) < value
          AND EXISTS (earlier: nat):
            earlier < index AND value = x(earlier))

  is_upper_bound(A: real_set, bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (value: real): A(value) IMPLIES value <= bound

  is_lower_bound(A: real_set, bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (value: real): A(value) IMPLIES bound <= value

  is_supremum(A: real_set, supremum_value: real): bool =
    is_upper_bound(A, supremum_value)
      AND FORALL (bound: real):
        is_upper_bound(A, bound) IMPLIES supremum_value <= bound

  is_infimum(A: real_set, infimum_value: real): bool =
    is_lower_bound(A, infimum_value)
      AND FORALL (bound: real):
        is_lower_bound(A, bound) IMPLIES bound <= infimum_value

  gap_definitions(
      x, a, b: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      is_supremum(
        left_candidates(x, index),
        x(index) - a(index))
        AND is_infimum(
          right_candidates(x, index),
          x(index) + b(index))

  gap_products(a, b: real_sequence): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (index: nat):
      a(index) * b(index) * (a(index) + b(index))

  partial_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  series_sums_to(values: real_sequence, total: real): bool =
    FORALL (radius: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(partial_sum(values, count) - total) < radius

  putnam_1964_a3: bool =
    FORALL (x, a, b: real_sequence):
      (dense_in_open_unit_interval(x)
        AND injective_sequence(x)
        AND gap_definitions(x, a, b))
      IMPLIES
        series_sums_to(gap_products(a, b), 1 / 3)
END putnam_1964_a3

import Mathlib

open Set Function

/--
The sequence of integers $u_n$ is bounded and satisfies
\[
u_n = \frac{u_{n-1} + u_{n-2} + u_{n-3}u_{n-4}}{u_{n-1}u_{n-2} + u_{n-3} + u_{n-4}}.
\]
Show that it is periodic for sufficiently large $n$.
-/
theorem putnam_1964_a4
(u : ℕ → ℤ)
(boundedu : ∃ B T : ℤ, ∀ n : ℕ, B ≤ u n ∧ u n ≤ T)
(hu : ∀ n ≥ 4, u n = ((u (n - 1) + u (n - 2) + u (n - 3) * u (n - 4)) : ℝ) / (u (n - 1) * u (n - 2) + u (n - 3) + u (n - 4)) ∧ (u (n - 1) * u (n - 2) + u (n - 3) + u (n - 4)) ≠ 0)
: (∃ N c : ℕ, c > 0 ∧ ∀ n ≥ N, u (n + c) = u n) :=
sorry

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1964_a4:
;; every bounded integer sequence satisfying the given exact fractional
;; four-term recurrence with nonzero denominators is eventually periodic.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A state (u_n u_(n+1) u_(n+2) u_(n+3)) has a unique successor under the
;; recurrence. Thus every source sequence is uniquely represented by its four
;; initial integers and the recursive orbit below, while every orbit satisfying
;; the integrality and nonzero-denominator conditions is a source sequence.

(defun putnam-1964-a4-denominator (quad)
  (+
   (* (cadddr quad) (caddr quad))
   (cadr quad)
   (car quad)))

(defun putnam-1964-a4-numerator (quad)
  (+
   (cadddr quad)
   (caddr quad)
   (* (cadr quad) (car quad))))

(defun putnam-1964-a4-next-state (quad)
  (list
   (cadr quad)
   (caddr quad)
   (cadddr quad)
   (/
    (putnam-1964-a4-numerator quad)
    (putnam-1964-a4-denominator quad))))

(defun putnam-1964-a4-orbit-state (initial-state steps)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix steps)))
  (if (zp steps)
      initial-state
    (putnam-1964-a4-next-state
     (putnam-1964-a4-orbit-state
      initial-state (- steps 1)))))

(defun putnam-1964-a4-orbit-value (initial-state n)
  (car
   (putnam-1964-a4-orbit-state initial-state n)))

(defun-sk putnam-1964-a4-orbit-bounded-by-p
    (initial-state lower upper)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (natp n)
     (let ((value
            (putnam-1964-a4-orbit-value initial-state n)))
       (and
        (integerp value)
        (<= lower value)
        (<= value upper))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1964-a4-bounded-integer-orbit-p
    (initial-state)
  (exists (lower upper)
    (and
     (integerp lower)
     (integerp upper)
     (putnam-1964-a4-orbit-bounded-by-p
      initial-state lower upper))))

(defun-sk putnam-1964-a4-nonzero-denominators-p
    (initial-state)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (natp n)
     (not
      (equal
       (putnam-1964-a4-denominator
        (putnam-1964-a4-orbit-state initial-state n))
       0)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1964-a4-periodic-tail-p
    (initial-state cutoff period)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (<= cutoff n))
     (equal
      (putnam-1964-a4-orbit-value
       initial-state (+ n period))
      (putnam-1964-a4-orbit-value initial-state n)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1964-a4-eventually-periodic-p
    (initial-state)
  (exists (cutoff period)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (posp period)
     (putnam-1964-a4-periodic-tail-p
      initial-state cutoff period))))

(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-1964-a4-statement ()
  (forall (u0 u1 u2 u3)
    (implies
     (and
      (integerp u0)
      (integerp u1)
      (integerp u2)
      (integerp u3))
     (let ((initial-state (list u0 u1 u2 u3)))
       (implies
        (and
         (putnam-1964-a4-bounded-integer-orbit-p
          initial-state)
         (putnam-1964-a4-nonzero-denominators-p
          initial-state))
        (putnam-1964-a4-eventually-periodic-p
         initial-state))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1964_a4:
-- every bounded integer-valued sequence satisfying the given fourth-order
-- rational recurrence is eventually periodic. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1964A4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

NatStrictLess : Nat -> Nat -> Set
NatStrictLess m n =
  suc m <=N n

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

four : Nat
four =
  suc (suc (suc (suc zero)))

module Putnam1964A4Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) where

  IntegerValued : (Nat -> R) -> Set
  IntegerValued u =
    (n : Nat) ->
    Exists Int (\ z -> u n == fromInt reals z)

  Bounded : (Nat -> R) -> Set
  Bounded u =
    Exists R
      (\ lower ->
        Exists R
          (\ upper ->
            (n : Nat) ->
            lessOrEqual reals lower (u n)
            and
            lessOrEqual reals (u n) upper))

  numerator : (Nat -> R) -> Nat -> R
  numerator u n =
    add reals
      (add reals
        (u (n - suc zero))
        (u (n - suc (suc zero))))
      (multiply reals
        (u (n - suc (suc (suc zero))))
        (u (n - four)))

  denominator : (Nat -> R) -> Nat -> R
  denominator u n =
    add reals
      (add reals
        (multiply reals
          (u (n - suc zero))
          (u (n - suc (suc zero))))
        (u (n - suc (suc (suc zero)))))
      (u (n - four))

  SatisfiesRecurrence : (Nat -> R) -> Set
  SatisfiesRecurrence u =
    (n : Nat) ->
    four <=N n ->
    (u n == divide reals (numerator u n) (denominator u n))
    and
    denominator u n != zeroR reals

  EventuallyPeriodic : (Nat -> R) -> Set
  EventuallyPeriodic u =
    Exists Nat
      (\ cutoff ->
        Exists Nat
          (\ period ->
            NatStrictLess zero period
            and
            ((n : Nat) ->
              cutoff <=N n ->
              u (n + period) == u n)))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (u : Nat -> R) ->
    Bounded u ->
    SatisfiesRecurrence u ->
    IntegerValued u ->
    EventuallyPeriodic u

putnam-1964-a4 : Set1
putnam-1964-a4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  Putnam1964A4Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a4:
  every bounded integer sequence satisfying the given fourth-order rational
  recurrence with nonzero denominators is eventually periodic. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory realTheory intrealTheory;

val putnam_1964_a4 =
  ``!u : num -> int.
      (?B T : int.
         !n : num. B <= u n /\ u n <= T) /\
      (!n : num.
         4 <= n
         ==>
         real_of_int (u n) =
           (real_of_int (u (n - 1)) +
            real_of_int (u (n - 2)) +
            real_of_int (u (n - 3)) * real_of_int (u (n - 4))) /
           (real_of_int (u (n - 1)) * real_of_int (u (n - 2)) +
            real_of_int (u (n - 3)) +
            real_of_int (u (n - 4))) /\
         (real_of_int (u (n - 1)) * real_of_int (u (n - 2)) +
          real_of_int (u (n - 3)) +
          real_of_int (u (n - 4))) <> 0)
      ==>
      ?N c : num.
        0 < c /\
        !n : num. N <= n ==> u (n + c) = u n``;

title: putnam_1964_a4
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a4:
  eventual periodicity of a bounded integer sequence satisfying a fourth-order
  rational recurrence with nonzero denominator. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  ZZ ^m NN0 is the class of total integer-valued sequences indexed by the
  nonnegative integers. Since every sequence value is an integer, the field
  quotient in the recurrence is required to equal that integer exactly.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d A B T N c n $.

  putnambench-putnam-1964-a4 $a |- A. A e. ( ZZ ^m NN0 )
    (
      (
        E. B e. ZZ E. T e. ZZ
          A. n e. NN0
            (
              B <_ ( A ` n )
              /\
              ( A ` n ) <_ T
            )
        /\
        A. n e. NN0
          (
            4 <_ n
            ->
            (
              ( A ` n ) =
                (
                  (
                    ( A ` ( n - 1 ) )
                    +
                    (
                      ( A ` ( n - 2 ) )
                      +
                      (
                        ( A ` ( n - 3 ) )
                        x.
                        ( A ` ( n - 4 ) )
                      )
                    )
                  )
                  /
                  (
                    (
                      ( A ` ( n - 1 ) )
                      x.
                      ( A ` ( n - 2 ) )
                    )
                    +
                    (
                      ( A ` ( n - 3 ) )
                      +
                      ( A ` ( n - 4 ) )
                    )
                  )
                )
              /\
              (
                (
                  ( A ` ( n - 1 ) )
                  x.
                  ( A ` ( n - 2 ) )
                )
                +
                (
                  ( A ` ( n - 3 ) )
                  +
                  ( A ` ( n - 4 ) )
                )
              ) =/= 0
            )
          )
      )
      ->
      E. N e. NN0 E. c e. NN0
        (
          0 < c
          /\
          A. n e. NN0
            (
              N <_ n
              ->
              ( A ` ( n + c ) ) = ( A ` n )
            )
        )
    )
  $.
$}

:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a4:
:: a bounded integer sequence satisfying the stated rational recurrence with
:: nonzero denominator is eventually periodic. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    NUMBERS, XREAL_0, XCMPLX_0, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3,
    REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1, ORDINAL1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, RAT_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, REAL_1,
    NAT_1, INT_1, RAT_1, NAT_D;
  constructors RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, REAL_1, NAT_1, INT_1, RAT_1, NAT_D;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, NAT_1,
    INT_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, RAT_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for u being Function of NAT,INT st
    (ex B,T being Integer st
      for n being Nat holds B <= u.n & u.n <= T) &
    (for n being Nat st 4 <= n holds
      u.n =
        (u.(n -' 1) + u.(n -' 2) + u.(n -' 3) * u.(n -' 4)) /
        (u.(n -' 1) * u.(n -' 2) + u.(n -' 3) + u.(n -' 4)) &
      u.(n -' 1) * u.(n -' 2) + u.(n -' 3) + u.(n -' 4) <> 0)
  holds
    ex N,c being Nat st
      0 < c &
      for n being Nat st N <= n holds u.(n + c) = u.n
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1964_a4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a4:
% a bounded integer sequence satisfying the stated four-term rational
% recurrence with nonzero denominators is eventually periodic. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1964_a4: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> int]

  nat_subtract(n, k: nat): nat =
    IF n >= k THEN n - k ELSE 0 ENDIF

  recurrence_numerator(u: integer_sequence, n: nat): int =
    u(nat_subtract(n, 1))
      + u(nat_subtract(n, 2))
      + u(nat_subtract(n, 3)) * u(nat_subtract(n, 4))

  recurrence_denominator(u: integer_sequence, n: nat): int =
    u(nat_subtract(n, 1)) * u(nat_subtract(n, 2))
      + u(nat_subtract(n, 3))
      + u(nat_subtract(n, 4))

  bounded_sequence(u: integer_sequence): bool =
    EXISTS (lower, upper: int):
      FORALL (n: nat):
        lower <= u(n) AND u(n) <= upper

  satisfies_recurrence(u: integer_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n >= 4 IMPLIES
        recurrence_denominator(u, n) /= 0
          AND u(n) * recurrence_denominator(u, n)
            = recurrence_numerator(u, n)

  eventually_periodic(u: integer_sequence): bool =
    EXISTS (start, period: nat):
      period > 0
        AND FORALL (n: nat):
          n >= start IMPLIES u(n + period) = u(n)

  putnam_1964_a4: bool =
    FORALL (u: integer_sequence):
      (bounded_sequence(u) AND satisfies_recurrence(u))
        IMPLIES eventually_periodic(u)
END putnam_1964_a4

title: putnam_1964_a5
content:
import Mathlib

open Set Function Filter Topology

/--
Prove that there exists a constant $k$ such that for any sequence $a_i$ of positive numbers,
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n}{a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n} \leq k \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{a_n}.
\]
-/
theorem putnam_1964_a5
    (pa : (ℕ → ℝ) → Prop)
    (hpa : ∀ a, pa a ↔ (∀ n : ℕ, a n > 0) ∧ ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun N ↦ ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, 1 / a n) atTop (𝓝 L)) :
    ∃ k : ℝ, ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, pa a →
      ∑' n : ℕ, (n + 1) / (∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), a i) ≤ k * ∑' n : ℕ, 1 / a n :=
  sorry

title: putnam_1964_a5
content:
From mathcomp Require Import all_algebra all_ssreflect.
From mathcomp Require Import reals sequences normedtype topology.
From mathcomp Require Import classical_sets cardinality.
Import numFieldNormedType.Exports.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.
Local Open Scope classical_set_scope.
Local Open Scope card_scope.

Variable R : realType.
Theorem putnam_1964_a5
    (pa : (nat -> R) -> Prop := fun a =>
        (forall n : nat, a n > 0) /\
        (exists L : R, (fun N => \sum_(0 <= n < N) 1/(a n)) @ \oo --> L))
    : exists k : R, forall a : nat -> R, pa a ->
        (exists L1 L2 : R, 
            (fun N : nat => \sum_(0 <= n < N) ((n%:R + 1)/(\sum_(i < n.+1) a i))) @ \oo --> L1 /\
            (fun N : nat => \sum_(0 <= n < N) (1/(a n))) @ \oo --> L2 /\
            L1 <= k * L2).
Proof. Admitted.

theory putnam_1964_a5 imports Complex_Main

theorem putnam_1964_a5:
  fixes pa :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  defines "pa \<equiv> (\<lambda>a::nat\<Rightarrow>real. (\<forall>n::nat. a n > 0) \<and> summable (\<lambda>n::nat. 1 / a n))"
  shows "\<exists>k::real. \<forall>a::nat\<Rightarrow>real. (pa a \<longrightarrow> (\<Sum>n::nat. (n+1) / (\<Sum>i::nat=0..n. a i)) \<le> k * (\<Sum>n::nat. 1 / a n))"
  sorry

end

putnam_1964_a5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1964_a5:
;; one real constant uniformly bounds the series of prefix-sum ratios for
;; every positive real sequence with convergent reciprocal series. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The scalar arguments present the Dedekind-complete ordered field of real
;; numbers. A tame APPLY$ object presents an arbitrary natural-indexed real
;; sequence. Both infinite sums are defined by epsilon convergence of their
;; finite partial sums, and all limit and bound witnesses remain internal.

(defun p1964a5-member-p (carrier x)
  (if (apply$ carrier (list x)) t nil))

(defun p1964a5-unary (operation x)
  (apply$ operation (list x)))

(defun p1964a5-binary (operation x y)
  (apply$ operation (list x y)))

(defun p1964a5-subtract (add negate x y)
  (p1964a5-binary add x (p1964a5-unary negate y)))

(defun p1964a5-less-equal-p (less x y)
  (not (apply$ less (list y x))))

(defun p1964a5-absolute (less negate zero x)
  (if (apply$ less (list x zero))
      (p1964a5-unary negate x)
    x))

(defun-sk p1964a5-field-laws-p
    (carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p1964a5-member-p carrier x)
      (p1964a5-member-p carrier y)
      (p1964a5-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (p1964a5-member-p
       carrier (p1964a5-binary add x y))
      (p1964a5-member-p
       carrier (p1964a5-binary multiply x y))
      (p1964a5-member-p carrier (p1964a5-unary negate x))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (p1964a5-member-p carrier (p1964a5-unary inverse x)))
      (equal
       (p1964a5-binary add (p1964a5-binary add x y) z)
       (p1964a5-binary add x (p1964a5-binary add y z)))
      (equal
       (p1964a5-binary add x y)
       (p1964a5-binary add y x))
      (equal (p1964a5-binary add x zero) x)
      (equal
       (p1964a5-binary add x (p1964a5-unary negate x))
       zero)
      (equal
       (p1964a5-binary
        multiply (p1964a5-binary multiply x y) z)
       (p1964a5-binary
        multiply x (p1964a5-binary multiply y z)))
      (equal
       (p1964a5-binary multiply x y)
       (p1964a5-binary multiply y x))
      (equal (p1964a5-binary multiply x one) x)
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal
        (p1964a5-binary
         multiply x (p1964a5-unary inverse x))
        one))
      (equal
       (p1964a5-binary
        multiply x (p1964a5-binary add y z))
       (p1964a5-binary
        add
        (p1964a5-binary multiply x y)
        (p1964a5-binary multiply x z)))))))

(defun-sk p1964a5-order-laws-p
    (carrier zero add multiply less)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p1964a5-member-p carrier x)
      (p1964a5-member-p carrier y)
      (p1964a5-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (not (apply$ less (list x x)))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (apply$ less (list x y))
       (apply$ less (list y x)))
      (implies
       (and
        (apply$ less (list x y))
        (apply$ less (list y z)))
       (apply$ less (list x z)))
      (implies
       (apply$ less (list x y))
       (apply$
        less
        (list
         (p1964a5-binary add x z)
         (p1964a5-binary add y z))))
      (implies
       (and
        (apply$ less (list zero x))
        (apply$ less (list zero y)))
       (apply$
        less
        (list
         zero
         (p1964a5-binary multiply x y))))))))

(defun-sk p1964a5-set-nonempty-p (carrier set)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (p1964a5-member-p carrier x)
     (apply$ set (list x)))))

(defun-sk p1964a5-upper-bound-p (carrier less set bound)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (p1964a5-member-p carrier x)
      (apply$ set (list x)))
     (p1964a5-less-equal-p less x bound))))

(defun-sk p1964a5-bounded-above-p (carrier less set)
  (exists (bound)
    (and
     (p1964a5-member-p carrier bound)
     (p1964a5-upper-bound-p carrier less set bound))))

(defun-sk p1964a5-supremum-p (carrier less set supremum)
  (forall (bound)
    (and
     (p1964a5-member-p carrier supremum)
     (p1964a5-upper-bound-p carrier less set supremum)
     (implies
      (and
       (p1964a5-member-p carrier bound)
       (p1964a5-upper-bound-p carrier less set bound))
      (p1964a5-less-equal-p less supremum bound)))))

(defun-sk p1964a5-has-supremum-p (carrier less set)
  (exists (supremum)
    (p1964a5-supremum-p carrier less set supremum)))

(defun-sk p1964a5-dedekind-complete-p (carrier less)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (tamep-functionp set)
      (p1964a5-set-nonempty-p carrier set)
      (p1964a5-bounded-above-p carrier less set))
     (p1964a5-has-supremum-p carrier less set))))

(defun p1964a5-real-field-p
    (carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse less)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp add)
   (tamep-functionp multiply)
   (tamep-functionp negate)
   (tamep-functionp inverse)
   (tamep-functionp less)
   (p1964a5-member-p carrier zero)
   (p1964a5-member-p carrier one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (p1964a5-field-laws-p
    carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse)
   (p1964a5-order-laws-p carrier zero add multiply less)
   (apply$ less (list zero one))
   (p1964a5-dedekind-complete-p carrier less)))

(defun-sk p1964a5-natural-real-sequence-p (carrier sequence)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (natp n)
     (p1964a5-member-p
      carrier (apply$ sequence (list n))))))

(defun-sk p1964a5-positive-sequence-p (zero less sequence)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (natp n)
     (apply$
      less
      (list zero (apply$ sequence (list n)))))))

(defun p1964a5-natural-value (n zero one add)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      zero
    (p1964a5-binary
     add
     one
     (p1964a5-natural-value (- n 1) zero one add))))

(defun p1964a5-prefix-sum (count sequence zero add)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      zero
    (p1964a5-binary
     add
     (p1964a5-prefix-sum (- count 1) sequence zero add)
     (apply$ sequence (list (- count 1))))))

(defun p1964a5-reciprocal-term
    (sequence n one multiply inverse)
  (p1964a5-binary
   multiply
   one
   (p1964a5-unary
    inverse (apply$ sequence (list n)))))

(defun p1964a5-left-term
    (sequence n zero one add multiply inverse)
  (p1964a5-binary
   multiply
   (p1964a5-natural-value (+ n 1) zero one add)
   (p1964a5-unary
    inverse
    (p1964a5-prefix-sum (+ n 1) sequence zero add))))

(defun p1964a5-reciprocal-partial-sum
    (count sequence zero one add multiply inverse)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      zero
    (p1964a5-binary
     add
     (p1964a5-reciprocal-partial-sum
      (- count 1) sequence zero one add multiply inverse)
     (p1964a5-reciprocal-term
      sequence (- count 1) one multiply inverse))))

(defun p1964a5-left-partial-sum
    (count sequence zero one add multiply inverse)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)

    (p1964a5-binary
     add

      (- count 1) sequence zero one add multiply inverse)
     (p1964a5-left-term
      sequence (- count 1) zero one add multiply inverse))))

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1964_a5:
-- a universal constant bounds the series of normalized reciprocal prefix sums
-- for every positive real sequence with convergent reciprocal series. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals (subtract reals center radius) x
  and
  StrictLess reals x (add reals center radius)

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : _) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals term limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n term)
    limit

PositiveSequence :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Set
PositiveSequence reals a =
  (n : Nat) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (a n)

reciprocalTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
reciprocalTerm reals a n =
  divide reals (oneR reals) (a n)

weightedPrefixTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
weightedPrefixTerm reals a n =
  divide reals
    (fromNat reals (suc n))
    (sumFirst reals (suc n) a)

module Putnam1964A5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) where

  Admissible :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  Admissible a =
    PositiveSequence reals a
    and
    Exists R
      (\ reciprocalSum ->
        SeriesHasSum reals
          (reciprocalTerm reals a)
          reciprocalSum)

  BoundHolds :
    R ->
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  BoundHolds k a =
    Exists R
      (\ reciprocalSum ->
        SeriesHasSum reals
          (reciprocalTerm reals a)
          reciprocalSum
        and
        Exists R
          (\ weightedSum ->
            SeriesHasSum reals
              (weightedPrefixTerm reals a)
              weightedSum
            and
            lessOrEqual reals
              weightedSum
              (multiply reals k reciprocalSum)))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    Exists R
      (\ k ->
        (a : Nat -> R) ->
        Admissible a ->
        BoundHolds k a)

putnam-1964-a5 : Set1
putnam-1964-a5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  Putnam1964A5Statement.proposition reals

(*

  a universal constant bounds the series of normalized reciprocal partial
  sums for every positive real sequence with convergent reciprocal series.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;
open real_topologyTheory;

val putnam_1964_a5 =
  ``?k : real.
      !a : num -> real.
        (!n : num. 0 < a n) /\
        (?L2 : real.
           (((\N : num.
                SIGMA
                  (\n : num. (1 : real) / a n)
                  (count N)) --> L2) sequentially))
        ==>
        ?L1 L2 : real.
          (((\N : num.
               SIGMA
                 (\n : num.
                    &(n + 1) /
                    SIGMA
                      (\i : num. a i)
                      (count (n + 1)))
                 (count N)) --> L1) sequentially) /\
          (((\N : num.
               SIGMA
                 (\n : num. (1 : real) / a n)
                 (count N)) --> L2) sequentially) /\
          L1 <= k * L2``;

content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a5:
% a universal constant bounds the series of indices divided by positive
% sequence prefix sums by the convergent reciprocal series. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1964_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN 0 ELSE numerator / denominator ENDIF

  partial_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  series_sums_to(values: real_sequence, total: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(partial_sum(values, count) - total) < epsilon_value

  reciprocal_terms(a: real_sequence): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (index: nat): safe_div(1, a(index))

  weighted_prefix_terms(a: real_sequence): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (index: nat):
      safe_div(
        (index + 1) :: real,
        partial_sum(a, index + 1))

  admissible(a: real_sequence): bool =
    (FORALL (index: nat): 0 < a(index))
      AND EXISTS (reciprocal_total: real):
        series_sums_to(reciprocal_terms(a), reciprocal_total)

  putnam_1964_a5: bool =
    EXISTS (k: real):
      FORALL (a: real_sequence):
        admissible(a) IMPLIES
          EXISTS (weighted_total, reciprocal_total: real):
            series_sums_to(
              weighted_prefix_terms(a), weighted_total)
              AND series_sums_to(
                reciprocal_terms(a), reciprocal_total)
              AND weighted_total <= k * reciprocal_total
END putnam_1964_a5

title: putnam_1964_a6

import Mathlib

open Set Function Filter Topology

/--
Let $S$ be a finite set of collinear points. Let $k$ be the maximum distance between any two points of $S$. Given a pair of points of $S$ a distance $d < k$ apart, we can find another pair of points of $S$ also a distance $d$ apart. Prove that if two pairs of points of $S$ are distances $a$ and $b$ apart, then $\frac{a}{b}$ is rational.
-/
theorem putnam_1964_a6
(S : Finset ℝ)
(pairs : Set (ℝ × ℝ))
(hpairs : pairs = {(a, b) | (a ∈ S) ∧ (b ∈ S) ∧ (a < b)})
(distance : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ)
(hdistance : distance = fun (a, b) ↦ b - a)
(hrepdist : ∀ p ∈ pairs, (∃ m ∈ pairs, distance m > distance p) → ∃ q ∈ pairs, q ≠ p ∧ distance p = distance q)
: (∀ p q : pairs, q ≠ p → ∃ r : ℚ, distance p / distance q = r) :=
sorry

From mathcomp Require Import all_algebra all_ssreflect.
From mathcomp Require Import reals topology normedtype.
From mathcomp Require Import classical_sets cardinality.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.
Local Open Scope classical_set_scope.

Variable R : realType.
Theorem putnam_1964_a6 
    (T : set R)
    (hTfin : finite_set T)
    (pairs : set (R * R) := [set p : R * R | p.1 \in T /\ p.2 \in T /\ p.1 < p.2])
    (distance : (R * R) -> R := fun p => p.2 - p.1)
    (hrepdist : forall p : R * R, p \in pairs ->
        (exists m : R * R, m \in pairs /\ distance m > distance p) ->
        (exists q : R * R, q \in pairs /\ q <> p /\ distance p = distance q))
    : forall p q : R * R, (p \in pairs /\ q \in pairs /\ q <> p) ->
        exists n d : int, d <> 0 /\ distance p / distance q = (n%:~R)/(d%:~R).
Proof. Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a6:
  rationality of ratios of distances between ordered pairs from a finite
  set of collinear real points under the repeated-distance condition. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `!S:real->bool.
     let pairs =
       {p:real#real |
          FST p IN S /\ SND p IN S /\ FST p < SND p} in
     let distance = \p:real#real. SND p - FST p in
     FINITE S /\
     (!p:real#real.
        p IN pairs
        ==> ((?m:real#real.
                m IN pairs /\ distance m > distance p)
             ==> ?q:real#real.
                   q IN pairs /\ ~(q = p) /\
                   distance p = distance q))
     ==> !p q:real#real.
           p IN pairs /\ q IN pairs /\ ~(q = p)
           ==> ?n d:int.
                 ~(d = (&0:int)) /\
                 distance p / distance q =
                 real_of_int n / real_of_int d`;;

title: putnam_1964_a6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a6:
;; repeated nonmaximal distances in a finite set of real collinear points
;; force every ratio of two pair distances to be rational. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A finite set of reals is represented exactly by rational coordinate
;; vectors in a basis of its finite-dimensional Q-span.  PROBE is a rational
;; linear functional that preserves the order of the represented points and
;; separates distinct pair-distance vectors.  Such a probe exists because
;; only finitely many strict comparisons and hyperplanes must be avoided.
;;
;; Conversely, for any valid finite vector representation, the rational probe
;; can be perturbed arbitrarily slightly to a Q-linearly independent real
;; tuple without changing those finitely many comparisons.  Dot product with
;; that tuple embeds the vectors into the reals.  It preserves point order,
;; distance equality and distance order, while two positive distances have a
;; rational ratio exactly when their rational coordinate vectors are
;; proportional.  Thus the representation is bidirectionally equivalent to
;; the finite-real-set statement, rather than a restriction to rational
;; points.

(defun putnam-1964-a6-rational-vector-p (vector width)
  (if (consp vector)
      (and (rationalp (car vector))
           (putnam-1964-a6-rational-vector-p
            (cdr vector) (- width 1)))
    (and (equal vector nil)
         (equal width 0))))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-point-list-p (points width)
  (if (consp points)
      (and (putnam-1964-a6-rational-vector-p
            (car points) width)
           (putnam-1964-a6-point-list-p
            (cdr points) width))
    (equal points nil)))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-dot-product (left right)
  (if (and (consp left) (consp right))
      (+ (* (car left) (car right))
         (putnam-1964-a6-dot-product
          (cdr left) (cdr right)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-vector-subtract (left right)
  (if (and (consp left) (consp right))
      (cons (- (car left) (car right))
            (putnam-1964-a6-vector-subtract
             (cdr left) (cdr right)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-projections-differ-from-p
    (point remaining probe)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (not
        (equal
         (putnam-1964-a6-dot-product point probe)
         (putnam-1964-a6-dot-product
          (car remaining) probe)))
       (putnam-1964-a6-projections-differ-from-p
        point (cdr remaining) probe))
    t))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-point-projections-distinct-p
    (points probe)
  (if (consp points)
      (and
       (putnam-1964-a6-projections-differ-from-p
        (car points) (cdr points) probe)
       (putnam-1964-a6-point-projections-distinct-p
        (cdr points) probe))
    t))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-pairs-with-first
    (point remaining probe)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let ((other (car remaining)))
        (cons
         (if (< (putnam-1964-a6-dot-product point probe)
                (putnam-1964-a6-dot-product other probe))
             (list point other)
           (list other point))
         (putnam-1964-a6-pairs-with-first
          point (cdr remaining) probe)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-pairs (points probe)
  (if (consp points)
      (append
       (putnam-1964-a6-pairs-with-first
        (car points) (cdr points) probe)
       (putnam-1964-a6-pairs (cdr points) probe))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-pair-distance (pair)
  (putnam-1964-a6-vector-subtract
   (cadr pair) (car pair)))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-distance-value (pair probe)
  (putnam-1964-a6-dot-product
   (putnam-1964-a6-pair-distance pair)
   probe))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-distance-separated-from-p
    (pair remaining probe)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (let ((left-distance
             (putnam-1964-a6-pair-distance pair))
            (right-distance
             (putnam-1964-a6-pair-distance
              (car remaining))))
        (and
         (implies
          (not (equal left-distance right-distance))
          (not
           (equal
            (putnam-1964-a6-dot-product
             left-distance probe)
            (putnam-1964-a6-dot-product
             right-distance probe))))
         (putnam-1964-a6-distance-separated-from-p
          pair (cdr remaining) probe)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-distance-projections-separated-p
    (pairs probe)
  (if (consp pairs)
      (and
       (putnam-1964-a6-distance-separated-from-p
        (car pairs) (cdr pairs) probe)
       (putnam-1964-a6-distance-projections-separated-p
        (cdr pairs) probe))
    t))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-has-longer-distance-p
    (pair pairs probe)
  (if (consp pairs)
      (or
       (< (putnam-1964-a6-distance-value pair probe)
          (putnam-1964-a6-distance-value
           (car pairs) probe))
       (putnam-1964-a6-has-longer-distance-p
        pair (cdr pairs) probe))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-has-other-equal-distance-p
    (pair pairs)
  (if (consp pairs)
      (or
       (and
        (not (equal pair (car pairs)))
        (equal
         (putnam-1964-a6-pair-distance pair)
         (putnam-1964-a6-pair-distance
          (car pairs))))
       (putnam-1964-a6-has-other-equal-distance-p
        pair (cdr pairs)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-repeated-distance-hypothesis-p
    (remaining all-pairs probe)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (implies
        (putnam-1964-a6-has-longer-distance-p
         (car remaining) all-pairs probe)
        (putnam-1964-a6-has-other-equal-distance-p
         (car remaining) all-pairs))

        (cdr remaining) all-pairs probe))
    t))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-first-nonzero-ratio
    (numerator denominator)
  (if (and (consp numerator) (consp denominator))
      (if (equal (car denominator) 0)
          (putnam-1964-a6-first-nonzero-ratio
           (cdr numerator) (cdr denominator))
        (cons (car numerator) (car denominator)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-proportional-with-pivot-p
    (numerator denominator pivot-numerator pivot-denominator)
  (if (and (consp numerator) (consp denominator))
      (and
       (equal
        (* (car numerator) pivot-denominator)
        (* (car denominator) pivot-numerator))
       (putnam-1964-a6-proportional-with-pivot-p
        (cdr numerator)
        (cdr denominator)
        pivot-numerator
        pivot-denominator))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-rationally-proportional-p
    (numerator denominator)
  (let ((pivot
         (putnam-1964-a6-first-nonzero-ratio
          numerator denominator)))
    (and
     pivot
     (putnam-1964-a6-proportional-with-pivot-p
      numerator denominator (car pivot) (cdr pivot)))))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-ratios-from-pair-rational-p
    (pair pairs)
  (if (consp pairs)
      (and
       (implies
        (not (equal pair (car pairs)))
        (putnam-1964-a6-rationally-proportional-p
         (putnam-1964-a6-pair-distance pair)
         (putnam-1964-a6-pair-distance
          (car pairs))))
       (putnam-1964-a6-ratios-from-pair-rational-p
        pair (cdr pairs)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1964-a6-all-ratios-rational-p
    (remaining all-pairs)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (putnam-1964-a6-ratios-from-pair-rational-p
        (car remaining) all-pairs)
       (putnam-1964-a6-all-ratios-rational-p
        (cdr remaining) all-pairs))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1964-a6-statement
    (points probe)
  (implies
   (and
    (true-listp points)
    (true-listp probe)
    (putnam-1964-a6-rational-vector-p
     probe (len probe))
    (putnam-1964-a6-point-list-p
     points (len probe))
    (no-duplicatesp-equal points)
    (putnam-1964-a6-point-projections-distinct-p
     points probe))
   (let ((pairs
          (putnam-1964-a6-pairs points probe)))
     (implies
      (and
       (putnam-1964-a6-distance-projections-separated-p
        pairs probe)
       (putnam-1964-a6-repeated-distance-hypothesis-p
        pairs pairs probe))

title: putnam_1964_a6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1964_a6:
-- repeated nonmaximal distances among a finite set of real points force the
-- distance ratio of any two distinct ordered pairs to be rational. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1964A6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

Predicate : Set -> Set1
Predicate A =
  A -> Set

record Pair (A : Set) : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    first-coordinate  : A
    second-coordinate : A

open Pair

record FiniteSubset
  {A : Set}
  (S : Predicate A) : Set where
  field
    size :
      Nat
    enumerate :
      Fin size -> A
    enumerated-member :
      (i : Fin size) -> S (enumerate i)
    enumeration-complete :
      (x : A) ->
      S x ->
      Exists (Fin size) (\ i -> x == enumerate i)

module Putnam1964A6Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) where

  OrderedPair :
    Predicate R ->
    Pair R ->
    Set
  OrderedPair S p =
    S (first-coordinate p)
    and
    S (second-coordinate p)
    and
    StrictLess reals
      (first-coordinate p)
      (second-coordinate p)

  distance :
    Pair R ->
    R
  distance p =
    subtract reals
      (second-coordinate p)
      (first-coordinate p)

  IsRational :
    R ->
    Set
  IsRational x =
    Exists Int
      (\ numerator ->
        Exists Int
          (\ denominator ->
            denominator != pos zero
            and
            x ==
            divide reals
              (fromInt reals numerator)
              (fromInt reals denominator)))

  RepeatsEveryNonmaximalDistance :
    Predicate R ->
    Set
  RepeatsEveryNonmaximalDistance S =
    (p : Pair R) ->
    OrderedPair S p ->
    Exists (Pair R)
      (\ m ->
        OrderedPair S m
        and
        StrictLess reals (distance p) (distance m)) ->
    Exists (Pair R)
      (\ q ->
        OrderedPair S q
        and
        q != p
        and
        distance p == distance q)

  proposition : Set1
  proposition =
    (S : Predicate R) ->
    FiniteSubset S ->
    RepeatsEveryNonmaximalDistance S ->
    (p q : Pair R) ->
    OrderedPair S p ->
    OrderedPair S q ->
    q != p ->
    IsRational
      (divide reals (distance p) (distance q))

putnam-1964-a6 : Set1
putnam-1964-a6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  Putnam1964A6Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a6:
  for a finite set of real point coordinates with every nonmaximal pairwise
  distance repeated, all ratios of distinct pair distances are rational.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open integerTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory intrealTheory;

val putnam_1964_a6 =
  ``let pairs =
      \S : real set.
        {p : real # real |
           FST p IN S /\ SND p IN S /\ FST p < SND p}
    in
      let distance =
        \p : real # real. SND p - FST p
      in
        !S : real set.
          FINITE S /\
          (!p : real # real.
             p IN pairs S
             ==>
             ((?m : real # real.
                 m IN pairs S /\ distance m > distance p)
              ==>
              ?q : real # real.
                q IN pairs S /\
                q <> p /\
                distance p = distance q))
          ==>
          !p q : real # real.
            p IN pairs S /\
            q IN pairs S /\
            q <> p
            ==>
            ?n d : int.
              d <> 0 /\
              distance p / distance q =
                real_of_int n / real_of_int d``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a6:
  a finite set of real points whose every nonmaximal pairwise distance is
  repeated has rational ratios between distances of distinct ordered pairs.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The source set of collinear points is represented by a finite subset S of
  RR. Its auxiliary set pairs and function distance are inlined: a pair is
  <. a , b >. with a and b in S and a < b, and its distance is b - a.
  Thus ordered-pair inequality preserves the source condition q != p.

  The hypothesis says that whenever such a pair has a strictly longer pair,
  a distinct pair has the same distance. The conclusion says that the
  quotient of the distances of any two distinct pairs belongs to QQ.
  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a b c d e f S $.

  putnambench-putnam-1964-a6 $a |- A. S
    (
      (
        (
          S C_ RR
          /\
          S e. Fin
        )
        /\
        A. a e. S A. b e. S
          (
            a < b
            ->
            (
              (
                E. c e. S E. d e. S
                  (
                    c < d
                    /\
                    ( b - a ) < ( d - c )
                  )
              )
              ->
              E. e e. S E. f e. S
                (
                  e < f
                  /\
                  (
                    <. e , f >. =/= <. a , b >.
                    /\
                    ( b - a ) = ( f - e )
                  )
                )
            )
          )
      )
      ->
      A. a e. S A. b e. S A. c e. S A. d e. S
        (
          (
            (
              a < b
              /\
              c < d
            )
            /\
            <. c , d >. =/= <. a , b >.
          )
          ->
          ( ( b - a ) / ( d - c ) ) e. QQ
        )
    )
  $.
$}

:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a6:
:: finite collinear point sets with every nonmaximal distance repeated have
:: rational ratios between all pairwise distances. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    BINOP_1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3,
    REAL_1, RAT_1, FINSET_1, ZFMISC_1, MCART_1, ORDINAL1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ZFMISC_1, XTUPLE_0, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    REAL_1, XXREAL_0, RAT_1, MCART_1, FINSET_1, BINOP_1;
  constructors ZFMISC_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, REAL_1, XXREAL_0,
    RAT_1, FINSET_1, XTUPLE_0, BINOP_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, RAT_1,
    FINSET_1, MEMBERED, XTUPLE_0, MCART_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for S being finite Subset of REAL,
      pairs being Subset of [:REAL,REAL:],
      distance being Function of [:REAL,REAL:],REAL st
    pairs = {[a,b] where a,b is Real :
      a in S & b in S & a < b} &
    (for a,b being Real holds
      distance.(a,b) = b - a) &
    (for p being Element of [:REAL,REAL:] st p in pairs holds
      (ex m being Element of [:REAL,REAL:] st
        m in pairs & distance.m > distance.p)
      implies
      ex q being Element of [:REAL,REAL:] st
        q in pairs & q <> p & distance.p = distance.q)
  holds
    for p,q being Element of [:REAL,REAL:] st
      p in pairs & q in pairs & q <> p
    holds distance.p / distance.q in RAT
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1964_a6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_a6:
% a finite set of collinear real points with every nonmaximal pairwise distance
% repeated has rational ratios between all pairwise distances. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1964_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[real]

  point_pair: TYPE = [# left_point: real, right_point: real #]

  admissible_pair(S: finite_set[real], p: point_pair): bool =
    S(left_point(p))
      AND S(right_point(p))
      AND left_point(p) < right_point(p)

  distance(p: point_pair): real =
    right_point(p) - left_point(p)

  repeated_nonmaximal_distances(S: finite_set[real]): bool =
    FORALL (p: point_pair):
      admissible_pair(S, p)
        IMPLIES
          ((EXISTS (m: point_pair):
              admissible_pair(S, m)
                AND distance(m) > distance(p))
            IMPLIES
              EXISTS (q: point_pair):
                admissible_pair(S, q)
                  AND q /= p
                  AND distance(p) = distance(q))

  putnam_1964_a6: bool =
    FORALL (S: finite_set[real]):
      repeated_nonmaximal_distances(S)
        IMPLIES
          FORALL (p, q: point_pair):
            (admissible_pair(S, p)
              AND admissible_pair(S, q)
              AND q /= p)
            IMPLIES rational?(distance(p) / distance(q))
END putnam_1964_a6

import Mathlib

open Set Function Filter Topology

/--
Let $a_n$ be a sequence of positive integers such that $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} 1/a_n$ converges. For all $n$, let $b_n$ be the number of $a_n$ which are at most $n$. Prove that $\lim_{n \to \infty} b_n/n = 0$.
-/
theorem putnam_1964_b1
    (a b : ℕ → ℕ)
    (h : ∀ n, 0 < a n)
    (h' : Summable fun n ↦ (1 : ℝ) / a n)
    (h'' : ∀ n, b n = {k | a k ≤ n}.ncard) :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ (b n : ℝ) / n) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
  sorry

From mathcomp Require Import classical_sets cardinality.

Unset Strict Implicit.

Variable R : realType.
Theorem putnam_1964_b1
    (a b : nat -> nat)
    (h : forall n : nat, lt 0 (a n))
    (h' : exists L : R, (fun N => \sum_(0 <= n < N) 1/(a n)%:R) @ \oo --> L)
    (h'' : forall n : nat, [set : 'I_(b n)] #= [set k : nat | le (a k) n])
    (f : nat -> R := fun n => (b n)%:R / n%:R)
    : f @ \oo --> 0.
Proof. Admitted.

;; for a positive integer sequence with convergent reciprocal series, the

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1964_b1:
-- a positive integer sequence with convergent reciprocal series has a counting
-- function whose ratio to the threshold tends to zero. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1964B1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

NatStrictLess : Nat -> Nat -> Set
NatStrictLess m n =
  suc m <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

Predicate : Set -> Set1
Predicate A =
  A -> Set

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (S : Predicate A)
  (count : Nat) : Set where
  field
    enumerate :
      Fin count -> A
    enumerated-member :
      (i : Fin count) ->
      S (enumerate i)
    enumeration-complete :
      (x : A) ->
      S x ->
      Exists (Fin count) (\ i -> x == enumerate i)
    enumeration-injective :
      (i j : Fin count) ->
      enumerate i == enumerate j ->
      i == j

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

SeriesConverges :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Set
SeriesConverges {R} reals term =
  Exists R
    (\ limit ->
      ConvergesTo reals
        (\ n -> sumFirst reals n term)
        limit)

module Putnam1964B1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) where

  reciprocalTerm :
    (Nat -> Nat) ->
    Nat ->
    R
  reciprocalTerm a n =
    divide reals
      (oneR reals)
      (fromNat reals (a n))

  indicesAtMost :
    (Nat -> Nat) ->
    Nat ->
    Predicate Nat
  indicesAtMost a threshold k =
    a k <=N threshold

  countingRatio :
    (Nat -> Nat) ->
    Nat ->
    R
  countingRatio b n =
    divide reals
      (fromNat reals (b n))
      (fromNat reals n)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (a b : Nat -> Nat) ->
    ((n : Nat) ->
      NatStrictLess zero (a n)) ->
    SeriesConverges reals (reciprocalTerm a) ->
    ((n : Nat) ->
      HasCardinality (indicesAtMost a n) (b n)) ->
    ConvergesTo reals
      (countingRatio b)
      (zeroR reals)

putnam-1964-b1 : Set1
putnam-1964-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  Putnam1964B1Statement.proposition reals

  a positive integer sequence with convergent reciprocal series has a
  counting function for terms at most n whose ratio to n tends to zero.
  This file contains no proof.

content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_b1:
% for a positive-integer sequence whose reciprocal series converges, the
% number of terms at most n divided by n tends to zero. This file contains
% no proof.

putnam_1964_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  natural_set: TYPE = [nat -> bool]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  partial_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  series_converges(values: real_sequence): bool =
    EXISTS (total: real):
      FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
          FORALL (count: nat):
            cutoff <= count IMPLIES
              abs(partial_sum(values, count) - total) < epsilon_value

  reciprocal_terms(a: natural_sequence): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (index: nat):
      safe_div(1, a(index) :: real)

  injective_below(
      enumeration: natural_sequence,
      bound: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      i < bound AND j < bound
        AND enumeration(i) = enumeration(j)
      IMPLIES i = j

  enumerates_exactly(
      enumeration: natural_sequence,
      set_value: natural_set,
      bound: nat): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      set_value(index)
        IFF
          EXISTS (position: nat):
            position < bound AND enumeration(position) = index

  has_cardinality(set_value: natural_set, cardinality: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (enumeration: natural_sequence):
      injective_below(enumeration, cardinality)
        AND enumerates_exactly(enumeration, set_value, cardinality)

  terms_at_most(a: natural_sequence, bound: nat): natural_set =
    LAMBDA (index: nat):
      a(index) <= bound

  counts_terms_at_most(
      a, b: natural_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (bound: nat):
      has_cardinality(terms_at_most(a, bound), b(bound))

  tends_to_zero(values: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(values(index)) < epsilon_value

  count_ratios(b: natural_sequence): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (index: nat):
      safe_div(b(index) :: real, index :: real)

  putnam_1964_b1: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: natural_sequence):
      ((FORALL (index: nat): 0 < a(index))
        AND series_converges(reciprocal_terms(a))
        AND counts_terms_at_most(a, b))
      IMPLIES tends_to_zero(count_ratios(b))
END putnam_1964_b1

/--
Let $S$ be a finite set. A set $P$ of subsets of $S$ has the property that any two members of $P$ have at least one element in common and that $P$ cannot be extended (whilst keeping this property). Prove that $P$ contains exactly half of the subsets of $S$.
-/
theorem putnam_1964_b2
(S : Type*) [Fintype S] [Nonempty S]
(P : Finset (Set S))
(hPP : ∀ T ∈ P, ∀ U ∈ P, T ∩ U ≠ ∅)
(hPS : ¬∃ T : Set S, T ∉ P ∧ (∀ U ∈ P, T ∩ U ≠ ∅))
: (P.card = 2 ^ (Fintype.card S - 1)) :=
sorry

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1964_b2:
  a maximal pairwise-intersecting family of subsets of a nonempty finite set
  contains exactly half of all subsets. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `!n:num. !P:(A->bool)->bool.
     0 < n /\
     (:A) HAS_SIZE n /\
     FINITE P /\
     (!s t:A->bool.
        s IN P /\ t IN P
        ==> ~(s INTER t = {})) /\
     ~(?s:A->bool.
         ~(s IN P) /\
         (!t:A->bool.
            t IN P
            ==> ~(s INTER t = {})))
     ==> CARD P = 2 EXP (n - 1)`;;
