theory putnam_1967_b1 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Elementary_Metric_Spaces"
"HOL-Analysis.Elementary_Topology"
"HOL-Analysis.Linear_Algebra"
"HOL-Analysis.Finite_Cartesian_Product"
"HOL-Analysis.Line_Segment"
"HOL-Number_Theory.Cong"
begin

(* Note: Boosts domains from ZMod 6 to nat *)
theorem putnam_1967_b1:
  fixes r :: "real"
    and L :: "nat \<Rightarrow> real^2"
    and P Q R :: "real^2"
  defines "P \<equiv> midpoint (L 1) (L 2)"
    and "Q \<equiv> midpoint (L 3) (L 4)"
    and "R \<equiv> midpoint (L 5) (L 0)"
  assumes hr : "r > 0"
    and hcyclic : "\<exists> center :: real^2. (\<forall> i \<in> {0::nat..5}. dist center (L i) = r)"
    and horder : "\<forall> i \<in> {0::nat..5}. \<forall> j \<in> {0::nat..5}. i \<noteq> j \<longrightarrow>  [i + 1 = j] (mod 6) \<or> [i = j + 1] (mod 6) \<or> closed_segment (L i) (L j) \<inter> interior (convex hull {L 0, L 1, L 2, L 3, L 4, L 5}) \<noteq> {}"
    and hlens : "dist (L 0) (L 1) = r \<and> dist (L 2) (L 3) = r \<and> dist (L 4) (L 5) = r"
    and hdist : "L 1 \<noteq> L 2 \<and> L 3 \<noteq> L 4 \<and> L 5 \<noteq> L 0"
  shows "dist P Q = dist R P \<and> dist Q R = dist P Q"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_1967_b1
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1967_b1:
  the midpoints of three alternating sides of a cyclic hexagon form an
  equilateral triangle under the stated side-length and ordering conditions.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let edist =
     \(x:real#real) (y:real#real).
       sqrt ((FST x - FST y) pow 2 + (SND x - SND y) pow 2) in
   let midpoint =
     \(x:real#real) (y:real#real).
       ((FST x + FST y) / &2, (SND x + SND y) / &2) in
   let segment =
     \(a:real#real) (b:real#real) (x:real#real).
       ?t:real.
         &0 <= t /\ t <= &1 /\
         FST x = (&1 - t) * FST a + t * FST b /\
         SND x = (&1 - t) * SND a + t * SND b in
   let convex_hull6 =
     \(L:num->real#real) (x:real#real).
       ?a0 a1 a2 a3 a4 a5:real.
         &0 <= a0 /\ &0 <= a1 /\ &0 <= a2 /\
         &0 <= a3 /\ &0 <= a4 /\ &0 <= a5 /\
         a0 + a1 + a2 + a3 + a4 + a5 = &1 /\
         FST x =
           a0 * FST (L 0) + a1 * FST (L 1) + a2 * FST (L 2) +
           a3 * FST (L 3) + a4 * FST (L 4) + a5 * FST (L 5) /\
         SND x =
           a0 * SND (L 0) + a1 * SND (L 1) + a2 * SND (L 2) +
           a3 * SND (L 3) + a4 * SND (L 4) + a5 * SND (L 5) in
   let interior =
     \(S:(real#real)->bool) (x:real#real).
       ?e:real.
         &0 < e /\
         !y:real#real. edist x y < e ==> S y in
   !r:real. !L:num->real#real. !P Q R:real#real.
     P = midpoint (L 1) (L 2) /\
     Q = midpoint (L 3) (L 4) /\
     R = midpoint (L 5) (L 0) /\
     r > &0 /\
     (?O:real#real.
        !i:num. i < 6 ==> edist O (L i) = r) /\
     (!i j:num.
        i < 6 /\ j < 6 /\ ~(i = j)
        ==> (i + 1) MOD 6 = j \/
            i = (j + 1) MOD 6 \/
            ?x:real#real.
              segment (L i) (L j) x /\ interior (convex_hull6 L) x) /\
     edist (L 0) (L 1) = r /\
     edist (L 2) (L 3) = r /\
     edist (L 4) (L 5) = r /\
     ~(L 1 = L 2) /\
     ~(L 3 = L 4) /\
     ~(L 5 = L 0)
     ==> edist P Q = edist R P /\ edist Q R = edist P Q`;;

title: putnam_1967_b1
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
;; putnam_1967_b1: alternating radius-length sides of a cyclically ordered
;; hexagon have the other three side midpoints forming an equilateral triangle.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; After replacing distances by squared distances and convex-hull interior by
;; positive barycentric coordinates, the source is a first-order formula over
;; real closed fields. A real counterexample therefore exists iff one exists
;; over the real algebraic numbers. One isolated algebraic number alpha and
;; rational functions of alpha encode every finite algebraic tuple.
;;
;; The six-point list is definitionally equivalent to the source function on
;; ZMod 6. The midpoint variables are eliminated by substitution. The circle
;; center and the nine segment-intersection witnesses occur existentially only
;; in the source antecedent, so
;;
;;   ((exists w, A(w)) implies C) iff (forall w, A(w) implies C).
;;
;; Free ACL2 arguments supply exactly this universal closure, without changing
;; the source quantifier scope. Positive barycentric coefficients characterize
;; ordinary convex-hull interior once a noncollinear triple makes the hull
;; full-dimensional.

;; Rational polynomials in alpha use descending coefficient order.

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-p (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (and (rationalp (car p))
           (putnam-1967-b1-rp-p (cdr p)))
    (equal p nil)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (if (equal (car p) 0)
          (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize (cdr p))
        p)
    nil))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-neg (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (cons (- (car p))
            (putnam-1967-b1-rp-neg (cdr p)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-add-raw (p q)
  (declare (xargs :measure (+ (acl2-count p) (acl2-count q))))
  (cond
   ((endp p) q)
   ((endp q) p)
   ((< (len p) (len q))
    (cons (car q)
          (putnam-1967-b1-rp-add-raw p (cdr q))))
   ((< (len q) (len p))
    (cons (car p)
          (putnam-1967-b1-rp-add-raw (cdr p) q)))
   (t
    (cons (+ (car p) (car q))
          (putnam-1967-b1-rp-add-raw (cdr p) (cdr q))))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-add (p q)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-add-raw p q)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-sub (p q)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rp-add
   p (putnam-1967-b1-rp-neg q)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-scale (c p)
  (if (consp p)
      (cons (* c (car p))
            (putnam-1967-b1-rp-scale c (cdr p)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-zeroes (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (cons 0 (putnam-1967-b1-zeroes (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-scale-shift (c p shift)
  (append (putnam-1967-b1-rp-scale c p)
          (putnam-1967-b1-zeroes shift)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul-raw (p q)
  (if (consp p)
      (putnam-1967-b1-rp-add
       (putnam-1967-b1-rp-scale-shift
        (car p) q (len (cdr p)))
       (putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul-raw (cdr p) q))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul (p q)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul-raw p q)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-eval-aux (p x accumulator)
  (if (consp p)
      (putnam-1967-b1-rp-eval-aux
       (cdr p) x (+ (* accumulator x) (car p)))
    accumulator))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-eval (p x)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rp-eval-aux p x 0))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-derivative-aux (p degree)
  (if (consp p)
      (if (zp degree)
          nil
        (cons (* degree (car p))
              (putnam-1967-b1-rp-derivative-aux
               (cdr p) (- degree 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-derivative (p)
  (let ((p (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize p)))
    (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize
     (putnam-1967-b1-rp-derivative-aux
      p (nfix (- (len p) 1))))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-rem-fuel (p q fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((p (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize p))
        (q (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize q)))
    (if (or (zp fuel)
            (endp q)
            (< (len p) (len q)))
        p
      (putnam-1967-b1-rp-rem-fuel
       (putnam-1967-b1-rp-sub
        p
        (putnam-1967-b1-rp-scale-shift
         (/ (car p) (car q))
         q
         (- (len p) (len q))))
       q
       (- fuel 1)))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-rem (p q)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rp-rem-fuel
   p q (+ 1 (len (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize p)))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-sturm-tail (previous current fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((current (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize current)))
    (if (or (zp fuel) (endp current))
        nil
      (cons
       current
       (putnam-1967-b1-rp-sturm-tail
        current
        (putnam-1967-b1-rp-neg
         (putnam-1967-b1-rp-rem previous current))
        (- fuel 1))))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-sturm-sequence (p q)
  (let ((p (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize p))
        (q (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize q)))
    (if (endp p)
        nil
      (cons
       p
       (if (endp q)
           nil
         (cons
          q
          (putnam-1967-b1-rp-sturm-tail
           p q (+ 1 (len p) (len q)))))))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rational-sign (x)
  (cond ((< x 0) -1)
        ((< 0 x) 1)
        (t 0)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-variations-aux
    (polynomials x previous-sign)
  (if (consp polynomials)
      (let ((sign
             (putnam-1967-b1-rational-sign
              (putnam-1967-b1-rp-eval (car polynomials) x))))
        (if (equal sign 0)
            (putnam-1967-b1-rp-variations-aux
             (cdr polynomials) x previous-sign)
          (+ (if (and (not (equal previous-sign 0))
                      (not (equal sign previous-sign)))
                 1
               0)
             (putnam-1967-b1-rp-variations-aux
              (cdr polynomials) x sign))))
    0))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-variations (polynomials x)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rp-variations-aux polynomials x 0))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-cauchy-index (p q lower upper)
  (let ((sequence
         (putnam-1967-b1-rp-sturm-sequence p q)))
    (- (putnam-1967-b1-rp-variations sequence lower)
       (putnam-1967-b1-rp-variations sequence upper))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rp-root-count (p lower upper)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rp-cauchy-index
   p (putnam-1967-b1-rp-derivative p) lower upper))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-primitive-p (primitive lower upper)
  (and
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-p primitive)
   (consp (putnam-1967-b1-rp-normalize primitive))
   (rationalp lower)
   (rationalp upper)
   (< lower upper)
   (not (equal (putnam-1967-b1-rp-eval primitive lower) 0))
   (not (equal (putnam-1967-b1-rp-eval primitive upper) 0))
   (equal
    (putnam-1967-b1-rp-root-count primitive lower upper)
    1)
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-1967-b1-rp-cauchy-index
      primitive
      (putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul
       (putnam-1967-b1-rp-derivative primitive)
       (putnam-1967-b1-rp-derivative primitive))
      lower
      upper)
     0))))

;; The Sturm-Tarski query over the isolated root alpha is sign(g(alpha)).
(defun putnam-1967-b1-alg-sign
    (primitive lower upper g)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rp-cauchy-index
   primitive
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul
    (putnam-1967-b1-rp-derivative primitive)
    g)
   lower
   upper))

;; A field element is (numerator denominator), evaluated at alpha.

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-numerator (value)
  (car value))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-denominator (value)
  (cadr value))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-code-p
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (and
   (true-listp value)
   (equal (len value) 2)
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-p
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-numerator value))
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-p
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-denominator value))
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-1967-b1-alg-sign
      primitive lower upper
      (putnam-1967-b1-rf-denominator value))
     0))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-list-p
    (primitive lower upper values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (putnam-1967-b1-rf-code-p
        primitive lower upper (car values))
       (putnam-1967-b1-rf-list-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-zero ()
  (list nil (list 1)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-one ()
  (list (list 1) (list 1)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-neg (value)
  (list
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-neg
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-numerator value))
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-denominator value)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-add (left right)
  (list
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-add
    (putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-numerator left)
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-denominator right))
    (putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-numerator right)
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-denominator left)))
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-denominator left)
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-denominator right))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub (left right)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rf-add
   left (putnam-1967-b1-rf-neg right)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-mul (left right)
  (list
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-numerator left)
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-numerator right))
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-denominator left)
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-denominator right))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-sign
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (putnam-1967-b1-alg-sign
   primitive lower upper
   (putnam-1967-b1-rp-mul
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-numerator value)
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-denominator value))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-equal-p
    (primitive lower upper left right)
  (equal
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sign
    primitive lower upper
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub left right))
   0))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-positive-p
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (equal
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sign
    primitive lower upper value)
   1))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-nonnegative-p
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (not
   (equal
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sign
     primitive lower upper value)
    -1)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-point-code-p
    (primitive lower upper point)
  (and
   (true-listp point)
   (equal (len point) 2)
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-list-p
    primitive lower upper point)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-point-list-p
    (primitive lower upper points)
  (if (consp points)
      (and
       (putnam-1967-b1-point-code-p
        primitive lower upper (car points))
       (putnam-1967-b1-point-list-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr points)))
    (equal points nil)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-witness-code-p
    (primitive lower upper witness)
  (and
   (true-listp witness)
   (equal (len witness) 7)
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-list-p
    primitive lower upper witness)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-witness-list-p
    (primitive lower upper witnesses)
  (if (consp witnesses)
      (and
       (putnam-1967-b1-witness-code-p
        primitive lower upper (car witnesses))
       (putnam-1967-b1-witness-list-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr witnesses)))
    (equal witnesses nil)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-square (value)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rf-mul value value))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-distance-squared (left right)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rf-add
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-square
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub (nth 0 left) (nth 0 right)))
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-square
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub (nth 1 left) (nth 1 right)))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-orientation (a b c)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-mul
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub (nth 0 b) (nth 0 a))
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub (nth 1 c) (nth 1 a)))
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-mul
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub (nth 1 b) (nth 1 a))
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub (nth 0 c) (nth 0 a)))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-noncollinear-with-pair-p
    (primitive lower upper a b remaining)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (or
       (not
        (equal
         (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sign
          primitive lower upper
          (putnam-1967-b1-orientation a b (car remaining)))
         0))
       (putnam-1967-b1-noncollinear-with-pair-p
        primitive lower upper a b (cdr remaining)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-noncollinear-with-first-p
    (primitive lower upper a remaining)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (or
       (putnam-1967-b1-noncollinear-with-pair-p
        primitive lower upper a (car remaining) (cdr remaining))
       (putnam-1967-b1-noncollinear-with-first-p
        primitive lower upper a (cdr remaining)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-full-dimensional-p
    (primitive lower upper points)
  (if (consp points)
      (or
       (putnam-1967-b1-noncollinear-with-first-p
        primitive lower upper (car points) (cdr points))
       (putnam-1967-b1-full-dimensional-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr points)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-all-on-circle-p
    (primitive lower upper center radius-squared points)
  (if (consp points)
      (and
       (putnam-1967-b1-rf-equal-p
        primitive lower upper
        (putnam-1967-b1-distance-squared center (car points))
        radius-squared)
       (putnam-1967-b1-all-on-circle-p
        primitive lower upper center radius-squared (cdr points)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-positive-list-p
    (primitive lower upper values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (putnam-1967-b1-rf-positive-p
        primitive lower upper (car values))
       (putnam-1967-b1-positive-list-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr values)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-rf-sum (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (putnam-1967-b1-rf-add
       (car values)
       (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sum (cdr values)))
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-zero)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-weighted-coordinate-sum
    (weights points coordinate)
  (if (and (consp weights) (consp points))
      (putnam-1967-b1-rf-add
       (putnam-1967-b1-rf-mul
        (car weights)
        (nth coordinate (car points)))
       (putnam-1967-b1-weighted-coordinate-sum
        (cdr weights) (cdr points) coordinate))
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-zero)))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-segment-coordinate
    (left right parameter coordinate)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rf-add
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-mul
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-one)
     parameter)
    (nth coordinate left))
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-mul
    parameter
    (nth coordinate right))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-interior-segment-witness-p
    (primitive lower upper points left-index right-index witness)
  (let* ((parameter (nth 0 witness))
         (weights (cdr witness))
         (left (nth left-index points))
         (right (nth right-index points))
         (one-minus-parameter
          (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub
           (putnam-1967-b1-rf-one)
           parameter)))
    (and
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-nonnegative-p
      primitive lower upper parameter)
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-nonnegative-p
      primitive lower upper one-minus-parameter)
     (putnam-1967-b1-positive-list-p
      primitive lower upper weights)
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-equal-p
      primitive lower upper
      (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sum weights)
      (putnam-1967-b1-rf-one))
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-equal-p
      primitive lower upper
      (putnam-1967-b1-segment-coordinate
       left right parameter 0)
      (putnam-1967-b1-weighted-coordinate-sum
       weights points 0))
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-equal-p
      primitive lower upper
      (putnam-1967-b1-segment-coordinate
       left right parameter 1)
      (putnam-1967-b1-weighted-coordinate-sum
       weights points 1)))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-cyclic-order-witnesses-p
    (primitive lower upper points witnesses)
  (and
   (putnam-1967-b1-interior-segment-witness-p
    primitive lower upper points 0 2 (nth 0 witnesses))
   (putnam-1967-b1-interior-segment-witness-p
    primitive lower upper points 0 3 (nth 1 witnesses))
   (putnam-1967-b1-interior-segment-witness-p
    primitive lower upper points 0 4 (nth 2 witnesses))
   (putnam-1967-b1-interior-segment-witness-p
    primitive lower upper points 1 3 (nth 3 witnesses))
   (putnam-1967-b1-interior-segment-witness-p
    primitive lower upper points 1 4 (nth 4 witnesses))
   (putnam-1967-b1-interior-segment-witness-p
    primitive lower upper points 1 5 (nth 5 witnesses))
   (putnam-1967-b1-interior-segment-witness-p
    primitive lower upper points 2 4 (nth 6 witnesses))
   (putnam-1967-b1-interior-segment-witness-p
    primitive lower upper points 2 5 (nth 7 witnesses))
   (putnam-1967-b1-interior-segment-witness-p
    primitive lower upper points 3 5 (nth 8 witnesses))))

(defun putnam-1967-b1-points-distinct-p
    (primitive lower upper left right)
  (or
   (not
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-equal-p
     primitive lower upper (nth 0 left) (nth 0 right)))
   (not
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-equal-p
     primitive lower upper (nth 1 left) (nth 1 right)))))

;; This is four times the squared distance between the two midpoints.
(defun putnam-1967-b1-midpoint-distance-numerator
    (first-a first-b second-a second-b)
  (putnam-1967-b1-rf-add
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-square
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-add (nth 0 first-a) (nth 0 first-b))
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-add (nth 0 second-a) (nth 0 second-b))))
   (putnam-1967-b1-rf-square
    (putnam-1967-b1-rf-sub
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-add (nth 1 first-a) (nth 1 first-b))
     (putnam-1967-b1-rf-add (nth 1 second-a) (nth 1 second-b))))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1967-b1-statement
    (primitive lower upper radius center points witnesses)
  (let* ((radius-squared
          (putnam-1967-b1-rf-square radius))
         (l0 (nth 0 points))
         (l1 (nth 1 points))
         (l2 (nth 2 points))
         (l3 (nth 3 points))
         (l4 (nth 4 points))
         (l5 (nth 5 points))
         (pq
          (putnam-1967-b1-midpoint-distance-numerator
           l1 l2 l3 l4))
         (rp
          (putnam-1967-b1-midpoint-distance-numerator
           l5 l0 l1 l2))
         (qr
          (putnam-1967-b1-midpoint-distance-numerator
           l3 l4 l5 l0)))
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1967-b1-primitive-p primitive lower upper)
      (putnam-1967-b1-rf-code-p
       primitive lower upper radius)
      (putnam-1967-b1-point-code-p
       primitive lower upper center)
      (true-listp points)
      (equal (len points) 6)
      (putnam-1967-b1-point-list-p
       primitive lower upper points)
      (true-listp witnesses)
      (equal (len witnesses) 9)
      (putnam-1967-b1-witness-list-p
       primitive lower upper witnesses)
      (putnam-1967-b1-rf-positive-p
       primitive lower upper radius)
      (putnam-1967-b1-full-dimensional-p
       primitive lower upper points)
      (putnam-1967-b1-all-on-circle-p
       primitive lower upper center radius-squared points)
      (putnam-1967-b1-cyclic-order-witnesses-p
       primitive lower upper points witnesses)
      (putnam-1967-b1-rf-equal-p
       primitive lower upper
       (putnam-1967-b1-distance-squared l0 l1)
       radius-squared)
      (putnam-1967-b1-rf-equal-p
       primitive lower upper
       (putnam-1967-b1-distance-squared l2 l3)
       radius-squared)
      (putnam-1967-b1-rf-equal-p
       primitive lower upper
       (putnam-1967-b1-distance-squared l4 l5)
       radius-squared)
      (putnam-1967-b1-points-distinct-p
       primitive lower upper l1 l2)
      (putnam-1967-b1-points-distinct-p
       primitive lower upper l3 l4)
      (putnam-1967-b1-points-distinct-p
       primitive lower upper l5 l0))
     (and
      (putnam-1967-b1-rf-equal-p

title: putnam_1967_b1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1967_b1:
-- a cyclic hexagon with three alternating sides equal to the circle radius has
-- an equilateral triangle formed by the other three side midpoints. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

two :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
two reals =
  add reals (oneR reals) (oneR reals)

half :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
half reals =
  inverse reals (two reals)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

Nonnegative :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
Nonnegative reals x =
  lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

squaredDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
squaredDistance reals p q =
  add reals
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q)))
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)))

distance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
distance reals p q =
  squareRoot reals (squaredDistance reals p q)

affinePoint :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R
affinePoint reals t p q =
  point
    (add reals
      (multiply reals
        (subtract reals (oneR reals) t)
        (x-coordinate p))
      (multiply reals t (x-coordinate q)))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals
        (subtract reals (oneR reals) t)
        (y-coordinate p))
      (multiply reals t (y-coordinate q)))

midpoint :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R
midpoint reals p q =
  affinePoint reals (half reals) p q

data Fin6 : Set where
  i0 i1 i2 i3 i4 i5 : Fin6

next6 : Fin6 -> Fin6
next6 i0 = i1
next6 i1 = i2
next6 i2 = i3
next6 i3 = i4
next6 i4 = i5
next6 i5 = i0

sum6 :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Fin6 -> R) ->
  R
sum6 reals values =
  add reals (values i0)
    (add reals (values i1)
      (add reals (values i2)
        (add reals (values i3)
          (add reals (values i4) (values i5)))))

weightedPoint6 :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Fin6 -> R) ->
  (Fin6 -> Point R) ->
  Point R
weightedPoint6 reals weights vertices =
  point
    (sum6 reals
      (\ i ->
        multiply reals
          (weights i)
          (x-coordinate (vertices i))))
    (sum6 reals
      (\ i ->
        multiply reals
          (weights i)
          (y-coordinate (vertices i))))

ConvexHull6 :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Fin6 -> Point R) ->
  Point R ->
  Set
ConvexHull6 {R} reals vertices p =
  Exists (Fin6 -> R)
    (\ weights ->
      ((i : Fin6) -> Nonnegative reals (weights i))
      and
      sum6 reals weights == oneR reals
      and
      p == weightedPoint6 reals weights vertices)

ClosedSegment :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
ClosedSegment {R} reals p q x =
  Exists R
    (\ t ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) t
      and
      lessOrEqual reals t (oneR reals)
      and
      x == affinePoint reals t p q)

InteriorOfConvexHull6 :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Fin6 -> Point R) ->
  Point R ->
  Set
InteriorOfConvexHull6 {R} reals vertices p =
  Exists R
    (\ epsilon ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon
      and
      ((q : Point R) ->
        StrictLess reals (distance reals p q) epsilon ->
        ConvexHull6 reals vertices q))

SegmentMeetsInterior :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Fin6 -> Point R) ->
  Fin6 ->
  Fin6 ->
  Set
SegmentMeetsInterior {R} reals vertices i j =
  Exists (Point R)
    (\ x ->
      ClosedSegment reals (vertices i) (vertices j) x
      and
      InteriorOfConvexHull6 reals vertices x)

CyclicOrder :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Fin6 -> Point R) ->
  Set
CyclicOrder reals vertices =
  (i j : Fin6) ->
  i != j ->
  next6 i == j
  or
  i == next6 j
  or
  SegmentMeetsInterior reals vertices i j

module Putnam1967B1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (r : R) ->
    (L : Fin6 -> Point R) ->
    (P Q T : Point R) ->
    P == midpoint reals (L i1) (L i2) ->
    Q == midpoint reals (L i3) (L i4) ->
    T == midpoint reals (L i5) (L i0) ->
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) r ->
    Exists (Point R)
      (\ center ->
        (i : Fin6) ->
        distance reals center (L i) == r) ->
    CyclicOrder reals L ->
    (distance reals (L i0) (L i1) == r
      and
      distance reals (L i2) (L i3) == r
      and
      distance reals (L i4) (L i5) == r) ->
    (L i1 != L i2
      and
      L i3 != L i4
      and
      L i5 != L i0) ->
    distance reals P Q == distance reals T P
    and
    distance reals Q T == distance reals P Q

putnam-1967-b1 : Set1
putnam-1967-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1967B1Statement.proposition reals

title: putnam_1967_b1
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1967_b1:
  the midpoints of the three unconstrained sides of a cyclic hexagon whose
  alternating side lengths equal the radius form an equilateral triangle.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory
     transcTheory;

val putnam_1967_b1 =
  ``let sqdist =
      \P Q : real # real.
        (FST P - FST Q) pow 2 + (SND P - SND Q) pow 2
    in
    let dist =
      \P Q : real # real. sqrt (sqdist P Q)
    in
    let midpoint =
      \P Q : real # real.
        ((FST P + FST Q) / 2, (SND P + SND Q) / 2)
    in
    let closed_segment =
      \A B : real # real.
      \X : real # real.
        ?t : real.
          0 <= t /\ t <= 1 /\
          X = ((1 - t) * FST A + t * FST B,
               (1 - t) * SND A + t * SND B)
    in
    let in_convex_hull =
      \L : num -> real # real.
      \X : real # real.
        ?w : num -> real.
          (!i : num. i < 6 ==> 0 <= w i) /\
          SIGMA w (count 6) = 1 /\
          X = (SIGMA (\i : num. w i * FST (L i)) (count 6),
               SIGMA (\i : num. w i * SND (L i)) (count 6))
    in
    let in_interior =
      \L : num -> real # real.
      \X : real # real.
        ?e : real.
          0 < e /\
          !Y : real # real.
            sqdist X Y < e pow 2 ==> in_convex_hull L Y
    in
      !r : real. !L : num -> real # real. !P Q R : real # real.
        P = midpoint (L 1) (L 2) /\
        Q = midpoint (L 3) (L 4) /\
        R = midpoint (L 5) (L 0) /\
        0 < r /\
        (?O : real # real.
           !i : num.
             i < 6 ==> dist O (L i) = r) /\
        (!i j : num.
           i < 6 /\ j < 6 /\ i <> j
           ==>
           (i + 1) MOD 6 = j \/
           i = (j + 1) MOD 6 \/
           ?X : real # real.
             closed_segment (L i) (L j) X /\
             in_interior L X) /\
        dist (L 0) (L 1) = r /\
        dist (L 2) (L 3) = r /\
        dist (L 4) (L 5) = r /\
        L 1 <> L 2 /\ L 3 <> L 4 /\ L 5 <> L 0
        ==>
        dist P Q = dist R P /\ dist Q R = dist P Q``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1967_b1: a cyclically ordered hexagon inscribed in a circle, with
  three alternating side lengths equal to the radius, has an equilateral
  triangle formed by the midpoints of the other three sides. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P67B1I is the two-coordinate index set, P67B1V is the six-element cyclic
  vertex index set, and P67B1R2 is the real coordinate plane with its
  standard finite product topology P67B1Top. P67B1Succ is cyclic successor
  on 0 ... 5. P67B1Dist is Euclidean distance, P67B1Mid is coordinatewise
  midpoint, P67B1Segment is the closed affine segment, and P67B1Hull is the
  convex hull of the finite vertex range via nonnegative barycentric weights.

  Reindexing ZMod 6 by 0 ... 5 preserves its cyclic successor and all
  quantifiers exactly. The final declaration is the single unproved $a
  corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P67B1I P67B1V P67B1R2 P67B1Top P67B1Succ $.
$c P67B1Dist P67B1Mid P67B1Segment P67B1Hull $.

p67b1-coordinate-index-syntax $a class P67B1I $.
p67b1-vertex-index-syntax $a class P67B1V $.
p67b1-plane-syntax $a class P67B1R2 $.
p67b1-topology-syntax $a class P67B1Top $.
p67b1-successor-syntax $a class P67B1Succ $.
p67b1-distance-syntax $a class ( P67B1Dist A B ) $.
p67b1-midpoint-syntax $a class ( P67B1Mid A B ) $.
p67b1-segment-syntax $a class ( P67B1Segment A B ) $.
p67b1-hull-syntax $a class ( P67B1Hull A ) $.

p67b1-coordinate-index-definition $a |- P67B1I = ( 1 ... 2 ) $.

p67b1-vertex-index-definition $a |- P67B1V = ( 0 ... 5 ) $.

p67b1-plane-definition $a |- P67B1R2 = ( RR ^m P67B1I ) $.

p67b1-topology-definition $a |- P67B1Top =
  (
    Xt_ `
      ( P67B1I X. { ( topGen ` ran (,) ) } )
  )
$.

p67b1-successor-definition $a |- P67B1Succ = (
  i e. P67B1V |->
    if (
      i = 5 ,
      0 ,
      ( i + 1 )
    )
) $.

${
  $d A B j $.

  p67b1-distance-definition $a |- (
    P67B1Dist A B
  ) = (
    sqrt
    `
    (
      sum_ j e. P67B1I
        ( ( ( A ` j ) - ( B ` j ) ) ^ 2 )
    )
  ) $.

  p67b1-midpoint-definition $a |- (
    P67B1Mid A B
  ) = (
    j e. P67B1I |->
      (
        ( ( A ` j ) + ( B ` j ) )
        /
        2
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d A B j t z $.

  p67b1-segment-definition $a |- (
    P67B1Segment A B
  ) = {
    z e. P67B1R2 |
    E. t e. ( 0 [,] 1 )
      z =
        (
          j e. P67B1I |->
            (
              ( ( 1 - t ) x. ( A ` j ) )
              +
              ( t x. ( B ` j ) )
            )
        )
  } $.
$}

${
  $d A j w x z $.

  p67b1-hull-definition $a |- (
    P67B1Hull A
  ) = {
    z e. P67B1R2 |
    E. w
      (
        (
          w : A --> RR
          /\
          A. x e. A 0 <_ ( w ` x )
        )
        /\
        (
          ( sum_ x e. A ( w ` x ) ) = 1
          /\
          z =
            (
              j e. P67B1I |->
                sum_ x e. A
                  (
                    ( w ` x )
                    x.
                    ( x ` j )
                  )
            )
        )
      )
  } $.
$}

${
  $d L O P Q R i j r $.

  putnambench-putnam-1967-b1 $a |- (
    A. r e. RR
    A. L e. ( P67B1R2 ^m P67B1V )
    A. P e. P67B1R2
    A. Q e. P67B1R2
    A. R e. P67B1R2
      (
        (
          P = ( P67B1Mid ( L ` 1 ) ( L ` 2 ) )
          /\
          (
            Q = ( P67B1Mid ( L ` 3 ) ( L ` 4 ) )
            /\
            (
              R = ( P67B1Mid ( L ` 5 ) ( L ` 0 ) )
              /\
              (
                0 < r
                /\
                (
                  E. O e. P67B1R2
                    A. i e. P67B1V
                      ( P67B1Dist O ( L ` i ) ) = r
                  /\
                  (
                    A. i e. P67B1V
                    A. j e. P67B1V
                      (
                        i =/= j
                        ->
                        (
                          ( P67B1Succ ` i ) = j
                          \/
                          (
                            i = ( P67B1Succ ` j )
                            \/
                            (
                              (
                                P67B1Segment
                                  ( L ` i )
                                  ( L ` j )
                              )
                              i^i
                              (
                                ( int ` P67B1Top )
                                `
                                ( P67B1Hull ( ran L ) )
                              )
                            )
                            =/=
                            (/)
                          )
                        )
                      )
                    /\
                    (
                      (
                        ( P67B1Dist ( L ` 0 ) ( L ` 1 ) ) = r
                        /\
                        (
                          ( P67B1Dist ( L ` 2 ) ( L ` 3 ) ) = r
                          /\
                          ( P67B1Dist ( L ` 4 ) ( L ` 5 ) ) = r
                        )
                      )
                      /\
                      (
                        ( L ` 1 ) =/= ( L ` 2 )
                        /\
                        (
                          ( L ` 3 ) =/= ( L ` 4 )
                          /\
                          ( L ` 5 ) =/= ( L ` 0 )
                        )
                      )
                    )
                  )
                )
              )
            )
          )
        )
        ->
        (
          ( P67B1Dist P Q ) = ( P67B1Dist R P )
          /\
          ( P67B1Dist Q R ) = ( P67B1Dist P Q )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

title: putnam_1967_b1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1967_b1:
% three alternating-side midpoints of a cyclic hexagon satisfying the stated
% chord and ordering hypotheses form an equilateral triangle. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1967_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]
  point_set: TYPE = [point -> bool]
  vertex_index: TYPE = below(6)
  vertices: TYPE = [vertex_index -> point]

  squared_distance(P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(Q) - x_coord(P)) ^ 2
      + (y_coord(Q) - y_coord(P)) ^ 2

  distance(P, Q: point): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (length: real):
        0 <= length
          AND length * length = squared_distance(P, Q))

  midpoint(P, Q: point): point =
    (# x_coord := (x_coord(P) + x_coord(Q)) / 2,
       y_coord := (y_coord(P) + y_coord(Q)) / 2 #)

  affine_combination(t: real, P, Q: point): point =
    (# x_coord := (1 - t) * x_coord(P) + t * x_coord(Q),
       y_coord := (1 - t) * y_coord(P) + t * y_coord(Q) #)

  closed_segment(P, Q: point): point_set =
    LAMBDA (X: point):
      EXISTS (t: real):
        0 <= t AND t <= 1
          AND X = affine_combination(t, P, Q)

  point_subset(A, B: point_set): bool =
    FORALL (P: point):
      A(P) IMPLIES B(P)

  convex(A: point_set): bool =
    FORALL (P, Q: point), (t: real):
      A(P) AND A(Q) AND 0 <= t AND t <= 1
        IMPLIES A(affine_combination(t, P, Q))

  convex_hull(A: point_set): point_set =
    LAMBDA (P: point):
      FORALL (C: point_set):
        convex(C) AND point_subset(A, C) IMPLIES C(P)

  euclidean_interior(A: point_set): point_set =
    LAMBDA (P: point):
      EXISTS (radius: real):
        0 < radius
          AND FORALL (Q: point):
            squared_distance(P, Q) < radius ^ 2
              IMPLIES A(Q)

  vertex_set(L: vertices): point_set =
    LAMBDA (P: point):
      EXISTS (i: vertex_index):
        P = L(i)

  sets_intersect(A, B: point_set): bool =
    EXISTS (P: point):
      A(P) AND B(P)

  cyclic_successor(i, j: vertex_index): bool =
    (i = 0 AND j = 1)
      OR (i = 1 AND j = 2)
      OR (i = 2 AND j = 3)
      OR (i = 3 AND j = 4)
      OR (i = 4 AND j = 5)
      OR (i = 5 AND j = 0)

  putnam_1967_b1: bool =
    FORALL (r: real), (L: vertices), (P, Q, R: point):
      (P = midpoint(L(1), L(2))
        AND Q = midpoint(L(3), L(4))
        AND R = midpoint(L(5), L(0))
        AND r > 0
        AND (EXISTS (O: point):
          FORALL (i: vertex_index):
            distance(O, L(i)) = r)
        AND (FORALL (i, j: vertex_index):
          i /= j
            IMPLIES
              cyclic_successor(i, j)
                OR cyclic_successor(j, i)
                OR sets_intersect(
                  closed_segment(L(i), L(j)),
                  euclidean_interior(convex_hull(vertex_set(L)))))
        AND distance(L(0), L(1)) = r
        AND distance(L(2), L(3)) = r
        AND distance(L(4), L(5)) = r
        AND L(1) /= L(2)
        AND L(3) /= L(4)
        AND L(5) /= L(0))
      IMPLIES
        distance(P, Q) = distance(R, P)
          AND distance(Q, R) = distance(P, Q)
END putnam_1967_b1

import Mathlib

open Nat Topology Filter

/--
Let $0 \leq p \leq 1$ and $0 \leq r \leq 1$ and consider the identities
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $(px+(1-p)y)^2=Ax^2+Bxy+Cy^2$,
\item[(b)] $(px+(1-p)y)(rx+(1-r)y)=\alpha x^2+\beta xy+\gamma y^2$.
\end{enumerate}
Show that (with respect to $p$ and $r$)
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\max\{A,B,C\} \geq 4/9$,
\item[(b)] $\max\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\} \geq 4/9$.
\end{enumerate}
-/
theorem putnam_1967_b2
(p r A B C α β γ : ℝ)
(prbound : 0 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ r ∧ r ≤ 1)
(id1 : ∀ x y : ℝ, (p * x + (1 - p) * y) ^ 2 = A * x ^ 2 + B * x * y + C * y ^ 2)
(id2 : ∀ x y : ℝ, (p * x + (1 - p) * y) * (r * x + (1 - r) * y) = α * x ^ 2 + β * x * y + γ * y ^ 2)
: max (max A B) C ≥ 4 / 9 ∧ max (max α β) γ ≥ 4 / 9 :=
sorry

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1967_b2:
;; lower bounds for the largest coefficients in two quadratic identities
;; determined by parameters in the real unit interval. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Comparing coefficients makes the two universally quantified real
;; polynomial identities equivalent to the six equations below:
;;
;;   A = p^2,  B = 2*p*(1-p),  C = (1-p)^2,
;;   alpha = p*r,
;;   beta = p*(1-r) + (1-p)*r,
;;   gamma = (1-p)*(1-r).
;;
;; Standard ACL2 has exact rationals rather than a primitive real sort. The
;; rational predicate is nevertheless bidirectionally equivalent to the
;; source universal real statement. Every rational instance is a real
;; instance. Conversely, a real counterexample makes at least one of the two
;; maxima strictly less than 4/9. After the coefficient equations eliminate
;; A, B, C, alpha, beta, and gamma, that strict violation is an open condition
;; on p and r relative to the closed square [0,1]^2. Rational points are dense
;; in that square, so a nearby rational p,r preserves the interval bounds and
;; the same strict violation; defining the six coefficients by the displayed
;; equations gives an exact rational counterexample.
(defun putnambench-putnam-1967-b2-statement
    (p r a b c alpha beta gamma)
  (implies
   (and
    (rationalp p)
    (rationalp r)
    (rationalp a)
    (rationalp b)
    (rationalp c)
    (rationalp alpha)
    (rationalp beta)
    (rationalp gamma)
    (<= 0 p)
    (<= p 1)
    (<= 0 r)
    (<= r 1)
    (equal a (* p p))
    (equal b (* 2 p (- 1 p)))
    (equal c (* (- 1 p) (- 1 p)))
    (equal alpha (* p r))
    (equal beta
           (+ (* p (- 1 r))
              (* (- 1 p) r)))
    (equal gamma (* (- 1 p) (- 1 r))))
   (and
    (or (<= (/ 4 9) a)
        (<= (/ 4 9) b)
        (<= (/ 4 9) c))
    (or (<= (/ 4 9) alpha)
        (<= (/ 4 9) beta)
        (<= (/ 4 9) gamma)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- coefficient maxima in two real quadratic identities formed from convex
-- linear combinations are at least four ninths. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

maximum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
maximum reals x y with order-total reals x y
... | left _ = y
... | right _ = x

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc (suc (suc (suc zero)))

nineN : Nat
nineN =
  suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc zero))))))))

module Putnam1967B2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) where

  oneMinus : R -> R
  oneMinus x =
    subtract reals (oneR reals) x

  fourNinths : R
  fourNinths =
    divide reals (fromNat reals fourN) (fromNat reals nineN)

  firstIdentity :
    R -> R -> R -> R -> R -> Set
  firstIdentity p A B C x =
    (y : R) ->
    square reals
      (add reals
        (multiply reals p x)
        (multiply reals (oneMinus p) y))
    ==
    add reals
      (add reals
        (multiply reals A (square reals x))
        (multiply reals (multiply reals B x) y))
      (multiply reals C (square reals y))

  secondIdentity :
    R -> R -> R -> R -> R -> R -> Set
  secondIdentity p r alpha beta gamma x =
    (y : R) ->
    multiply reals
      (add reals
        (multiply reals p x)
        (multiply reals (oneMinus p) y))
      (add reals
        (multiply reals r x)
        (multiply reals (oneMinus r) y))
    ==
    add reals
      (add reals
        (multiply reals alpha (square reals x))
        (multiply reals (multiply reals beta x) y))
      (multiply reals gamma (square reals y))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (p r A B C alpha beta gamma : R) ->
    (lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) p
      and lessOrEqual reals p (oneR reals)
      and lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) r
      and lessOrEqual reals r (oneR reals)) ->
    ((x : R) -> firstIdentity p A B C x) ->
    ((x : R) -> secondIdentity p r alpha beta gamma x) ->
    (lessOrEqual reals
      fourNinths
      (maximum reals (maximum reals A B) C))
    and
    (lessOrEqual reals
      fourNinths
      (maximum reals (maximum reals alpha beta) gamma))

putnam-1967-b2 : Set1
putnam-1967-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  Putnam1967B2Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1967_b2:
  coefficient lower bounds for two quadratic identities formed from convex
  combinations of two real variables. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open realTheory;

val putnam_1967_b2 =
  ``!p r A B C alpha beta gamma : real.
      0 <= p /\ p <= 1 /\ 0 <= r /\ r <= 1 /\
      (!x y : real.
         (p * x + (1 - p) * y) pow 2 =
         A * x pow 2 + B * x * y + C * y pow 2) /\
      (!x y : real.
         (p * x + (1 - p) * y) * (r * x + (1 - r) * y) =
         alpha * x pow 2 + beta * x * y + gamma * y pow 2)
      ==>
      max (max A B) C >= 4 / 9 /\
      max (max alpha beta) gamma >= 4 / 9``;

title: putnam_1967_b2
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1967_b2: coefficients in two real quadratic identities determined
  by parameters in the closed unit interval have the stated four-ninths
  lower bounds on their maxima. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The set.mm conditional if ( u <_ v , v , u ) is the maximum of the two
  real numbers u and v, so the two nested conditionals below are exactly the
  source maxima max(max(A,B),C) and max(max(alpha,beta),gamma). The source
  coefficients alpha, beta, and gamma are named a, b, and c here. The final
  declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d A B C a b c p r x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-1967-b2 $a |- A. p e. RR A. r e. RR
    A. A e. RR A. B e. RR A. C e. RR
    A. a e. RR A. b e. RR A. c e. RR
      (
        (
          (
            ( 0 <_ p /\ p <_ 1 )
            /\
            ( 0 <_ r /\ r <_ 1 )
          )
          /\
          (
            A. x e. RR A. y e. RR
              (
                ( ( p x. x ) + ( ( 1 - p ) x. y ) ) ^ 2
              )
              =
              (
                (
                  ( A x. ( x ^ 2 ) )
                  +
                  ( ( B x. x ) x. y )
                )
                +
                ( C x. ( y ^ 2 ) )
              )
          )
          /\
          A. x e. RR A. y e. RR
            (
              (
                ( p x. x )
                +
                ( ( 1 - p ) x. y )
              )
              x.
              (
                ( r x. x )
                +
                ( ( 1 - r ) x. y )
              )
            )
            =
            (
              (
                ( a x. ( x ^ 2 ) )
                +
                ( ( b x. x ) x. y )
              )
              +
              ( c x. ( y ^ 2 ) )
            )
        )
        ->
        (
          ( 4 / 9 )
          <_
          if (
            if ( A <_ B , B , A ) <_ C ,
            C ,
            if ( A <_ B , B , A )
          )
          /\
          ( 4 / 9 )
          <_
          if (
            if ( a <_ b , b , a ) <_ c ,
            c ,
            if ( a <_ b , b , a )
          )
        )
      )
  $.
$}

:: lower bounds for the largest coefficients in two quadratic polynomial
:: identities determined by parameters in the unit interval. This file

environ

title: putnam_1967_b2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1967_b2:
% coefficient lower bounds for two quadratic identities formed from convex
% combinations of two real variables. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1967_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_max(left, right: real): real =
    IF left >= right THEN left ELSE right ENDIF

  putnam_1967_b2: bool =
    FORALL (p, r, A, B, C, alpha, beta, gamma: real):
      (0 <= p AND p <= 1
        AND 0 <= r AND r <= 1
        AND (FORALL (x, y: real):
          (p * x + (1 - p) * y) ^ 2
            = A * x ^ 2 + B * x * y + C * y ^ 2)
        AND (FORALL (x, y: real):
          (p * x + (1 - p) * y)
              * (r * x + (1 - r) * y)
            = alpha * x ^ 2 + beta * x * y + gamma * y ^ 2))
      IMPLIES
        real_max(real_max(A, B), C) >= 4 / 9
          AND real_max(real_max(alpha, beta), gamma) >= 4 / 9
END putnam_1967_b2

import Mathlib

open Nat Topology Filter

/--
If $f$ and $g$ are continuous and periodic functions with period $1$ on the real line, then $\lim_{n \to \infty} \int_0^1 f(x)g(nx)\,dx=(\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx)(\int_0^1 g(x)\,dx)$.
-/
theorem putnam_1967_b3
(f g : ℝ → ℝ)
(fgcont : Continuous f ∧ Continuous g)
(fgperiod : Function.Periodic f 1 ∧ Function.Periodic g 1)
: Tendsto (fun n : ℤ => ∫ x in Set.Ioo 0 1, f x * g (n * x)) atTop (𝓝 ((∫ x in Set.Ioo 0 1, f x) * (∫ x in Set.Ioo 0 1, g x))) :=
sorry

From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect all_algebra.
From mathcomp Require Import reals normedtype trigo measure lebesgue_measure lebesgue_integral topology.
From mathcomp Require Import classical_sets.
Import numFieldNormedType.Exports.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.
Local Open Scope classical_set_scope.

Variable R : realType.
Definition mu := [the measure _ _ of @lebesgue_measure R].
Theorem putnam_1967_b3
    (f g : R -> R)
    (fgcont : continuous f /\ continuous g)
    (fgperiod : periodic f 1 /\ periodic g 1)
    : (fun n : nat => \int[mu]_(x in [set y | 0 < y < 1]) (f x * g (n%:~R * x))) --> 
        (\int[mu]_(x in [set y | 0 < y < 1]) f x) * (\int[mu]_(x in [set y | 0 < y < 1]) g x).
Proof. Admitted.

putnam_1967_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1967_b3:
;; continuous real-valued functions of period one have asymptotically
;; decorrelated unit-interval integrals under integer dilation. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The two conservative generic symbols are arbitrary regular rational Cauchy
;; names for values on rational points of [0,1]. The predicates below require
;; uniform continuity and equality of the endpoint values. Hence each
;; admissible name has a unique continuous extension to [0,1], and its
;; endpoint identification has a unique continuous 1-periodic extension to
;; the real line. Conversely, every continuous real-valued 1-periodic
;; function supplies such a name. Thus rational arguments and approximants
;; encode, rather than restrict, the source's arbitrary real functions.
;;
;; Uniform right-endpoint Riemann sums with value precision tending to zero
;; converge to the Lebesgue integrals in the source because all relevant
;; integrands are continuous on [0,1]. The inner mesh cutoff keeps those
;; integral limits internal. The outer epsilon/dilation cutoff is exactly the
;; asserted limit as the natural (equivalently, integer at-top) dilation tends
;; to infinity.

(defstub p67b3-f-approx (x precision) t)
(defstub p67b3-g-approx (x precision) t)

(defun p67b3-abs (x)
  (if (< x 0) (- x) x))

(defun p67b3-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and (rationalp x)
       (< 0 x)))

(defun p67b3-unit-rational-p (x)
  (and (rationalp x)
       (<= 0 x)
       (<= x 1)))

(defun p67b3-value (kind x precision)
  (if (equal kind :f)
      (p67b3-f-approx x precision)
    (p67b3-g-approx x precision)))

(defun-sk p67b3-regular-name-p (kind)
  (forall (x epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (p67b3-unit-rational-p x)
      (p67b3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (p67b3-positive-rational-p eta))
     (and
      (rationalp (p67b3-value kind x epsilon))
      (rationalp (p67b3-value kind x eta))
      (<=
       (p67b3-abs
        (- (p67b3-value kind x epsilon)
           (p67b3-value kind x eta)))
       (+ epsilon eta))))))

;; At precision epsilon/8, the displayed 3*epsilon/4 bound is equivalent to
;; exact value distance below epsilon after passing to the represented reals.

(defun-sk p67b3-uniform-continuity-neighborhood-p
    (kind epsilon delta)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (p67b3-unit-rational-p x)
      (p67b3-unit-rational-p y)
      (< (p67b3-abs (- x y)) delta))
     (<
      (p67b3-abs
       (- (p67b3-value kind x (/ epsilon 8))
          (p67b3-value kind y (/ epsilon 8))))
      (* 3/4 epsilon)))))

(defun-sk p67b3-uniform-continuity-radius-exists-p
    (kind epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (p67b3-positive-rational-p delta)
     (p67b3-uniform-continuity-neighborhood-p
      kind epsilon delta))))

(defun-sk p67b3-uniformly-continuous-p (kind)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p67b3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (p67b3-uniform-continuity-radius-exists-p
      kind epsilon))))

(defun-sk p67b3-endpoints-equal-p (kind)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p67b3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (<=
      (p67b3-abs
       (- (p67b3-value kind 0 epsilon)
          (p67b3-value kind 1 epsilon)))
      (* 2 epsilon)))))

(defun p67b3-admissible-periodic-function-p (kind)
  (and
   (p67b3-regular-name-p kind)
   (p67b3-uniformly-continuous-p kind)
   (p67b3-endpoints-equal-p kind)))

(defun p67b3-mesh-precision (pieces)
  (if (posp pieces)
      (/ 1 pieces)
    1))

(defun p67b3-periodic-argument (x)
  (- x (floor x 1)))

(defun p67b3-integral-numerator
    (kind index pieces)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (zp index)
      0
    (let* ((x (/ index pieces))
           (precision (p67b3-mesh-precision pieces)))
      (+
       (p67b3-value kind x precision)
       (p67b3-integral-numerator
        kind (- index 1) pieces)))))

(defun p67b3-integral-approx (kind pieces)
  (if (posp pieces)
      (/
       (p67b3-integral-numerator
        kind pieces pieces)
       pieces)
    0))

(defun p67b3-correlation-numerator
    (index pieces dilation)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (zp index)
      0
    (let* ((x (/ index pieces))
           (precision (p67b3-mesh-precision pieces))
           (periodic-x
            (p67b3-periodic-argument
             (* dilation x))))
      (+
       (*
        (p67b3-value :f x precision)
        (p67b3-value :g periodic-x precision))
       (p67b3-correlation-numerator
        (- index 1) pieces dilation)))))

(defun p67b3-correlation-integral-approx
    (dilation pieces)
  (if (and (natp dilation)
           (posp pieces))
      (/
       (p67b3-correlation-numerator
        pieces pieces dilation)
       pieces)
    0))

(defun p67b3-limit-difference-approx
    (dilation pieces)
  (-
   (p67b3-correlation-integral-approx
    dilation pieces)
   (*
    (p67b3-integral-approx :f pieces)
    (p67b3-integral-approx :g pieces))))

;; For fixed dilation, letting PIECES tend to infinity recovers the exact
;; difference between the correlation integral and the product of the two
;; means. Requiring an eventual bound for every positive rational epsilon is
;; equivalent to convergence of that exact difference to zero.

(defun-sk p67b3-integration-tail-p
    (dilation epsilon mesh-cutoff)
  (forall (pieces)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp pieces)
      (posp mesh-cutoff)
      (<= mesh-cutoff pieces))
     (<
      (p67b3-abs
       (p67b3-limit-difference-approx
        dilation pieces))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p67b3-integration-cutoff-exists-p
    (dilation epsilon)
  (exists (mesh-cutoff)
    (and
     (posp mesh-cutoff)
     (p67b3-integration-tail-p
      dilation epsilon mesh-cutoff))))

(defun-sk p67b3-dilation-tail-p
    (epsilon dilation-cutoff)
  (forall (dilation)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp dilation)
      (natp dilation-cutoff)
      (<= dilation-cutoff dilation))
     (p67b3-integration-cutoff-exists-p
      dilation epsilon))))

(defun-sk p67b3-dilation-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (dilation-cutoff)
    (and
     (natp dilation-cutoff)
     (p67b3-dilation-tail-p
      epsilon dilation-cutoff))))

(defun-sk p67b3-correlation-limit-p ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p67b3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (p67b3-dilation-cutoff-exists-p epsilon))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1967-b3-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (p67b3-admissible-periodic-function-p :f)
    (p67b3-admissible-periodic-function-p :g))
   (p67b3-correlation-limit-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1967_b3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1967_b3:
-- for continuous real functions of period one, the unit-interval integrals of
-- f(x) * g(n*x) tend to the product of their unit-interval integrals. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ContinuousAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ContinuousAt {R} reals function point =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals (function point) epsilon (function x)))

Continuous :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
Continuous {R} reals function =
  (point : R) ->
  ContinuousAt reals function point

PeriodicOne :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
PeriodicOne {R} reals function =
  (x : R) ->
  function (add reals x (oneR reals)) == function x

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

uniformUnitSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
uniformUnitSum reals function pieces =
  divide reals
    (sumFirst reals pieces
      (\ k ->
        function
          (divide reals
            (fromNat reals k)
            (fromNat reals pieces))))
    (fromNat reals pieces)

RiemannIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
RiemannIntegralValue reals function integralValue =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> uniformUnitSum reals function (suc n))
    integralValue

record UnitIntervalIntegration
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    integral : (R -> R) -> R
    integral-of-continuous :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      Continuous reals function ->
      RiemannIntegralValue reals function (integral function)

open UnitIntervalIntegration

putnamIntegrand :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  R
putnamIntegrand reals f g n x =
  multiply reals
    (f x)
    (g (multiply reals (fromNat reals n) x))

putnam-1967-b3 : Set1
putnam-1967-b3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (integration : UnitIntervalIntegration reals) ->
  (f g : R -> R) ->
  Continuous reals f ->
  Continuous reals g ->
  PeriodicOne reals f ->
  PeriodicOne reals g ->
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      integral integration
        (putnamIntegrand reals f g n))
    (multiply reals
      (integral integration f)
      (integral integration g))

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1967_b3:
  the limiting integral identity for two continuous real functions of period
  one, with one function evaluated at increasingly rapid integer dilations.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory realTheory real_topologyTheory integrationTheory;

val putnam_1967_b3 =
  ``!f g : real -> real.
      f continuous_on UNIV /\
      g continuous_on UNIV /\
      (!x : real. f (x + 1) = f x) /\
      (!x : real. g (x + 1) = g x)
      ==>
      ((\n : num.
          integration$integral (interval [0, 1])
            (\x : real. f x * g (&n * x))) -->

        integration$integral (interval [0, 1]) g))
        sequentially``;

  putnam_1967_b3: for continuous real-valued functions of period one, the
  oscillatory unit-interval integral converges to the product of their
  unit-interval means. This file contains no proof.

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  F and G range over arbitrary total real-valued functions on the reals.
  Membership in RR -cn-> RR expresses continuity, and the two translation
  equations express period one. The limit is taken at positive infinity over
  the integers, as in the Isabelle and Lean sources; restricting the same
  eventual limit to natural indices gives the Rocq formulation.

  The Lebesgue integrals use the open interval (0,1), matching the Lean and
  Rocq sources. Adding or removing the endpoints does not change these
  integrals and therefore also matches the Isabelle interval integral. The
  final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d F G n x $.

  putnambench-putnam-1967-b3 $a |-
    A. F e. ( RR ^m RR )
    A. G e. ( RR ^m RR )
      (
        (
          (
            F e. ( RR -cn-> RR )
            /\
            G e. ( RR -cn-> RR )
          )
          /\
          (
            A. x e. RR
              ( F ` ( x + 1 ) ) = ( F ` x )
            /\
            A. x e. RR
              ( G ` ( x + 1 ) ) = ( G ` x )
          )
        )
        ->
        (
          n e. ZZ |->
            S. ( 0 (,) 1 )
              (
                ( F ` x )
                x.
                ( G ` ( n x. x ) )
              )
              _d x
        )
        ~~>
        (
          (
            S. ( 0 (,) 1 )
              ( F ` x )
              _d x
          )
          x.
          (
            S. ( 0 (,) 1 )
              ( G ` x )
              _d x
          )
        )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1967_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1967_b3:
% asymptotic factorization of unit-interval integrals for two continuous
% real-valued functions of period one. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1967_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  integer_real_sequence: TYPE = [int -> real]

  continuous(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real), (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (y: real):
          abs(y - x) < delta IMPLIES
            abs(f(y) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  periodic_with_period_one(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      f(x + 1) = f(x)

  valid_partition(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = 0
      AND points(count) = 1
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          points(index) < points(index + 1)

  valid_tags(
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index) <= tags(index)
          AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1)

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      f: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count - 1)
        + f(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_unit_interval_integral(
      f: real_function,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
        FORALL
            (points, tags: real_sequence),
            (count: nat):
          (valid_partition(points, count)
            AND valid_tags(points, tags, count)
            AND mesh_less_than(
              points, count, mesh_bound))
          IMPLIES
            abs(
              riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count)
                - integral_value)
              < epsilon_value

  unit_interval_integral(f: real_function): real =
    IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
        has_unit_interval_integral(f, integral_value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
          has_unit_interval_integral(
            f, integral_value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  converges_at_integer_top(
      sequence: integer_real_sequence,
      value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: int):
        FORALL (index: int):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  oscillatory_integral(
      f, g: real_function,
      index: int): real =
    unit_interval_integral(
      LAMBDA (x: real):
        f(x) * g((index :: real) * x))

  putnam_1967_b3: bool =
    FORALL (f, g: real_function):
      (continuous(f)
        AND continuous(g)
        AND periodic_with_period_one(f)
        AND periodic_with_period_one(g))
      IMPLIES
        converges_at_integer_top(
          LAMBDA (index: int):
            oscillatory_integral(f, g, index),
          unit_interval_integral(f)
            * unit_interval_integral(g))
END putnam_1967_b3

import Mathlib

open Nat Topology Filter

-- Note: uses (ℕ → Set.Icc 1 n → Bool) instead of (Set.Icc 0 n → Set.Icc 1 n → Bool)
/--
A certain locker room contains $n$ lockers numbered $1,2,3,\cdots,n$ and all are originally locked. An attendant performs a sequence of operations $T_1,T_2,\cdots,T_n$ whereby with the operation $T_k$, $1 \leq k \leq n$, the condition of being locked or unlocked is changed for all those lockers and only those lockers whose numbers are multiples of $k$. After all the $n$ operations have been performed it is observed that all lockers whose numbers are perfect squares (and only those lockers) are now open or unlocked. Prove this mathematically.
-/
theorem putnam_1967_b4
(n : ℕ)
(lockers : ℕ → Set.Icc 1 n → Bool)
(npos : n ≥ 1)
(hlockers0 : ∀ i : Set.Icc 1 n, lockers 0 i = false)
(hlockersk : ∀ k ∈ Set.Icc 1 n, ∀ i : Set.Icc 1 n, lockers k i = if k ∣ i then !(lockers (k - 1) i) else (lockers (k - 1) i))
: ∀ i : Set.Icc 1 n, lockers n i ↔ (∃ j : ℤ, j ^ 2 = i) :=
sorry

(* Note : Leaving this one as is because I do not see a compelling reason to modify to depend on mathcomp here. *)
Theorem putnam_1967_b4
    (n : nat)
    (lockers : nat -> nat -> bool)
    (npos : n >= 1)
    (hlockers0 : forall i : nat, 1 <= i <= n -> lockers 0 i = false)
    (hlockersk : forall k i : nat, 1 <= k <= n -> 1 <= i <= n -> ((Nat.divide k i -> lockers k i = negb (lockers (k - 1) i)) /\ (~Nat.divide k i -> lockers k i = lockers (k - 1) i)))
    : (forall i : nat, 1 <= i <= n -> (lockers n i = true <-> exists j : nat, j ^ 2 = i)).
Proof. Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1967_b4:
  toggling each numbered locker at every operation whose number divides its
  index leaves exactly the perfect-square lockers open. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

let statement =
  `!n:num. !lockers:num->num->bool.
     1 <= n /\
     (!i:num.
        1 <= i /\ i <= n
        ==> lockers 0 i = F) /\
