$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1969_b5:
  a positive strictly increasing integer sequence with convergent reciprocal
  series has a counting function whose ratio to its real threshold tends to
  zero at positive infinity. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  A is a positive-integer sequence indexed by NN0, and K is its counting
  function on real thresholds. The first quantified premise states strict
  increase; positivity follows from the codomain. The second expands
  convergence of the reciprocal partial sums,
  using the half-open interval 0 ..^ n for the first n terms. The cardinality
  equation defines K(x) as the number of indices whose sequence values do not
  exceed x; equality to the natural number K(x) also records finiteness.

  The conclusion is the epsilon-threshold expansion of K(t) / t tending to
  zero as the real variable t tends to positive infinity. The final
  declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d A C K M N e i m n t x $.

  putnambench-putnam-1969-b5 $a |- A. A A. K
    (
      (
        (
          (
            A : NN0 --> NN
            /\
            K : RR --> NN0
          )
          /\
          (
            A. n e. NN0 0 < ( A ` n )
            /\
            A. m e. NN0
              A. n e. NN0
                (
                  m < n
                  ->
                  ( A ` m ) < ( A ` n )
                )
          )
        )
        /\
        (
          E. C e. RR
            A. e e. RR
              (
                0 < e
                ->
                E. N e. NN0
                  A. n e. NN0
                    (
                      N <_ n
                      ->
                      (
                        abs
                        `
                        (
                          (
                            sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                              ( 1 / ( A ` i ) )
                          )
                          -
                          C
                        )
                      )
                      < e
                    )
              )
          /\
          A. x e. RR
            (
              ( K ` x )
              =
              (
                #
                `
                { n e. NN0 | ( A ` n ) <_ x }
              )
            )
        )
      )
      ->
      A. e e. RR
        (
          0 < e
          ->
          E. M e. RR
            A. t e. RR
              (
                M <_ t
                ->
                (
                  abs
                  `
                  (
                    (
                      ( K ` t )
                      /
                      t
                    )
                    -
                    0
                  )
                )
                < e
              )
        )
    )
  $.
$}

:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1969_b5:
:: a strictly increasing positive integer sequence with convergent reciprocal
:: series has a counting function whose ratio to x tends to zero at positive
:: infinity. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    NUMBERS, XREAL_0, COMPLEX1, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3,
    REAL_1, NAT_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, SEQ_1, SEQ_2, ORDINAL1,
    ORDINAL2, SEQ_4, SERIES_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, REAL_1,
    COMPLEX1, XXREAL_0, NAT_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, SEQ_1, SEQ_2,
    COMSEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4, SERIES_1;
  constructors FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1, REAL_1, COMPLEX1,
    XXREAL_0, NAT_1, SEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4, BINOP_2, COMSEQ_2,
    SERIES_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0, VALUED_1,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, NAT_1, SEQ_4;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for a being Function of NAT,NAT,
      k being Function of REAL,NAT st
    (for m,n being Nat st m < n holds a.m < a.n) &
    (for n being Nat holds 0 < a.n) &
    (ex s being Real_Sequence st
      (for n being Nat holds s.n = 1 / (a.n qua Real)) &
      Partial_Sums(s) is convergent) &
    (for x being Real holds
      k.x = card
        {n where n is Element of NAT : (a.n qua Real) <= x})
  holds
    for epsilon being Real st 0 < epsilon holds
      ex B being Real st
        for x being Real st B <= x holds
          |.(k.x qua Real) / x.| < epsilon
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1969_b5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1969_b5:
% a strictly increasing positive integer sequence with convergent reciprocal
% series has counting function k(x) satisfying k(x) / x -> 0 at positive
% infinity. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1969_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[nat]

  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  counting_function: TYPE = [real -> nat]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  partial_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  series_converges(values: real_sequence): bool =
    EXISTS (total: real):
      FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
          FORALL (count: nat):
            cutoff <= count IMPLIES
              abs(partial_sum(values, count) - total) < epsilon_value

  reciprocal_terms(a: natural_sequence): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (index: nat):
      safe_div(1, a(index) :: real)

  strictly_increasing(a: natural_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (lower, upper: nat):
      lower < upper IMPLIES a(lower) < a(upper)

  positive(a: natural_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      0 < a(index)

  counts_terms_at_most(
      a: natural_sequence,
      k: counting_function): bool =
    FORALL (bound: real):
      EXISTS (terms: finite_set[nat]):
        (FORALL (index: nat):
          terms(index) IFF (a(index) :: real) <= bound)
          AND card(terms) = k(bound)

  tends_to_zero_at_real_top(
      values: [real -> real]): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (threshold: real):
        FORALL (x: real):
          threshold <= x IMPLIES
            abs(values(x)) < epsilon_value

  count_ratio(k: counting_function): [real -> real] =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      safe_div(k(x) :: real, x)

  putnam_1969_b5: bool =
    FORALL (a: natural_sequence), (k: counting_function):
      (strictly_increasing(a)
        AND positive(a)
        AND series_converges(reciprocal_terms(a))
        AND counts_terms_at_most(a, k))
      IMPLIES tends_to_zero_at_real_top(count_ratio(k))
END putnam_1969_b5

import Mathlib

open Matrix Filter Topology Set Nat

/--
Let $A$ be a $3 \times 2$ matrix and $B$ be a $2 \times 3$ matrix such that $$AB =
\begin{pmatrix}
8 & 2 & -2 \\
2 & 5 & 4 \\
-2 & 4 & 5
\end{pmatrix}.
$$ Prove that $$BA =
\begin{pmatrix}
9 & 0 \\
0 & 9
\end{pmatrix}.$$
-/
theorem putnam_1969_b6
(A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 2) ℝ)
(B : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 3) ℝ)
(p : Fin 3 → Fin 3 → ℝ)
(hp : p 0 0 = 8 ∧ p 0 1 = 2 ∧ p 0 2 = -2 ∧
p 1 0 = 2 ∧ p 1 1 = 5 ∧ p 1 2 = 4 ∧
p 2 0 = -2 ∧ p 2 1 = 4 ∧ p 2 2 = 5)
(hAB : A * B = Matrix.of p)
: B * A = 9 * (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ) :=
sorry

theory putnam_1969_b6 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Finite_Cartesian_Product"
begin

theorem putnam_1969_b6:
  fixes A :: "real^2^3"
  and B :: "real^3^2"
  and p :: "real^3^3"
  assumes hp: "p$1$1 = 8 \<and> p$1$2 = 2 \<and> p$1$3 = -2 \<and>
  p$2$1 = 2 \<and> p$2$2 = 5 \<and> p$2$3 = 4 \<and>
  p$3$1 = -2 \<and> p$3$2 = 4 \<and> p$3$3 = 5"
  and hAB: "A ** B = p"
  shows "B ** A = mat 9"
  sorry

end

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1969_b6:
;; real 3-by-2 and 2-by-3 matrices whose product is the specified 3-by-3
;; matrix have reverse product equal to 9 times the 2-by-2 identity.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The scalar domain is presented as an arbitrary real-closed ordered field.
;; This preserves the source domain because real-closed ordered fields have
;; the same first-order theory as the real numbers, and the matrix assertion
;; below is a first-order sentence in the ordered-field language. The source's
;; auxiliary matrix p is eliminated definitionally by substituting its nine
;; specified entries into A*B.

(defstub p69b6-real-p (real-type value) t)
(defstub p69b6-zero (real-type) t)
(defstub p69b6-one (real-type) t)
(defstub p69b6-add (real-type left right) t)
(defstub p69b6-mul (real-type left right) t)
(defstub p69b6-neg (real-type value) t)
(defstub p69b6-inv (real-type value) t)
(defstub p69b6-less (real-type left right) t)

(defun-sk p69b6-field-laws-p (real-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p69b6-real-p real-type x)
      (p69b6-real-p real-type y)
      (p69b6-real-p real-type z))
     (let* ((zero (p69b6-zero real-type))
            (one (p69b6-one real-type))
            (xy-add (p69b6-add real-type x y))
            (yz-add (p69b6-add real-type y z))
            (xy-mul (p69b6-mul real-type x y))
            (yz-mul (p69b6-mul real-type y z))
            (neg-x (p69b6-neg real-type x))
            (inv-x (p69b6-inv real-type x)))
       (and
        (p69b6-real-p real-type xy-add)
        (p69b6-real-p real-type xy-mul)
        (p69b6-real-p real-type neg-x)
        (p69b6-real-p real-type inv-x)
        (equal (p69b6-add real-type xy-add z)
               (p69b6-add real-type x yz-add))
        (equal xy-add (p69b6-add real-type y x))
        (equal (p69b6-add real-type x zero) x)
        (equal (p69b6-add real-type x neg-x) zero)
        (equal (p69b6-mul real-type xy-mul z)
               (p69b6-mul real-type x yz-mul))
        (equal xy-mul (p69b6-mul real-type y x))
        (equal (p69b6-mul real-type x one) x)
        (implies
         (equal x zero)
         (equal inv-x zero))
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (equal (p69b6-mul real-type x inv-x) one))
        (equal
         (p69b6-mul real-type x yz-add)
         (p69b6-add
          real-type
          (p69b6-mul real-type x y)
          (p69b6-mul real-type x z))))))))

(defun-sk p69b6-order-laws-p (real-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p69b6-real-p real-type x)
      (p69b6-real-p real-type y)
      (p69b6-real-p real-type z))
     (let ((zero (p69b6-zero real-type)))
       (and
        (not (p69b6-less real-type x x))
        (or
         (equal x y)
         (p69b6-less real-type x y)
         (p69b6-less real-type y x))
        (implies
         (and
          (p69b6-less real-type x y)
          (p69b6-less real-type y z))
         (p69b6-less real-type x z))
        (implies
         (p69b6-less real-type x y)
         (p69b6-less
          real-type
          (p69b6-add real-type x z)
          (p69b6-add real-type y z)))
        (implies
         (and
          (p69b6-less real-type zero x)
          (p69b6-less real-type zero y))
         (p69b6-less
          real-type
          zero
          (p69b6-mul real-type x y))))))))

(defun p69b6-real-list-p (real-type values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (p69b6-real-p real-type (car values))
       (p69b6-real-list-p real-type (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

;; Coefficients are in ascending order. This is Horner evaluation.
(defun p69b6-polynomial-value (real-type coefficients x)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (p69b6-add
       real-type
       (car coefficients)
       (p69b6-mul
        real-type
        x
        (p69b6-polynomial-value
         real-type (cdr coefficients) x)))
    (p69b6-zero real-type)))

(defun-sk p69b6-square-root-exists-p (real-type x)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (p69b6-real-p real-type root)
     (not
      (p69b6-less
       real-type root (p69b6-zero real-type)))
     (equal
      (p69b6-mul real-type root root)
      x))))

(defun-sk p69b6-nonnegative-square-root-property-p (real-type)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (p69b6-real-p real-type x)
      (not
       (p69b6-less
        real-type x (p69b6-zero real-type))))
     (p69b6-square-root-exists-p real-type x))))

(defun p69b6-odd-degree-polynomial-p
    (real-type coefficients)
  (and
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (<= 2 (len coefficients))
   (evenp (len coefficients))
   (p69b6-real-list-p real-type coefficients)
   (not
    (equal
     (car (last coefficients))
     (p69b6-zero real-type)))))

(defun-sk p69b6-polynomial-root-exists-p
    (real-type coefficients)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (p69b6-real-p real-type root)
     (equal
      (p69b6-polynomial-value
       real-type coefficients root)
      (p69b6-zero real-type)))))

(defun-sk p69b6-odd-degree-root-property-p (real-type)
  (forall (coefficients)
    (implies
     (p69b6-odd-degree-polynomial-p
      real-type coefficients)
     (p69b6-polynomial-root-exists-p
      real-type coefficients))))

(defun p69b6-real-closed-field-p (real-type)
  (let ((zero (p69b6-zero real-type))
        (one (p69b6-one real-type)))
    (and
     (p69b6-real-p real-type zero)
     (p69b6-real-p real-type one)
     (not (equal zero one))
     (p69b6-field-laws-p real-type)
     (p69b6-order-laws-p real-type)
     (p69b6-less real-type zero one)
     (p69b6-nonnegative-square-root-property-p real-type)
     (p69b6-odd-degree-root-property-p real-type))))

(defun p69b6-natural (real-type n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (p69b6-zero real-type)
    (p69b6-add
     real-type
     (p69b6-one real-type)
     (p69b6-natural real-type (1- n)))))

(defun p69b6-sum2 (real-type x1 y1 x2 y2)
  (p69b6-add
   real-type
   (p69b6-mul real-type x1 y1)
   (p69b6-mul real-type x2 y2)))

(defun p69b6-sum3
    (real-type x1 y1 x2 y2 x3 y3)
  (p69b6-add
   real-type
   (p69b6-add
    real-type
    (p69b6-mul real-type x1 y1)
    (p69b6-mul real-type x2 y2))
   (p69b6-mul real-type x3 y3)))

(defun p69b6-matrix-entries-p
    (real-type
     a00 a01 a10 a11 a20 a21
     b00 b01 b02 b10 b11 b12)
  (and
   (p69b6-real-p real-type a00)
   (p69b6-real-p real-type a01)
   (p69b6-real-p real-type a10)
   (p69b6-real-p real-type a11)
   (p69b6-real-p real-type a20)
   (p69b6-real-p real-type a21)
   (p69b6-real-p real-type b00)
   (p69b6-real-p real-type b01)
   (p69b6-real-p real-type b02)
   (p69b6-real-p real-type b10)
   (p69b6-real-p real-type b11)
   (p69b6-real-p real-type b12)))

(defun p69b6-forward-product-p
    (real-type
     a00 a01 a10 a11 a20 a21
     b00 b01 b02 b10 b11 b12)
  (let ((two (p69b6-natural real-type 2))
        (four (p69b6-natural real-type 4))
        (five (p69b6-natural real-type 5))
        (eight (p69b6-natural real-type 8)))
    (and
     (equal (p69b6-sum2 real-type a00 b00 a01 b10)
            eight)
     (equal (p69b6-sum2 real-type a00 b01 a01 b11)
            two)
     (equal (p69b6-sum2 real-type a00 b02 a01 b12)
            (p69b6-neg real-type two))
     (equal (p69b6-sum2 real-type a10 b00 a11 b10)
            two)
     (equal (p69b6-sum2 real-type a10 b01 a11 b11)
            five)
     (equal (p69b6-sum2 real-type a10 b02 a11 b12)
            four)
     (equal (p69b6-sum2 real-type a20 b00 a21 b10)
            (p69b6-neg real-type two))
     (equal (p69b6-sum2 real-type a20 b01 a21 b11)
            four)
     (equal (p69b6-sum2 real-type a20 b02 a21 b12)
            five))))

(defun p69b6-reverse-product-p
    (real-type
     a00 a01 a10 a11 a20 a21
     b00 b01 b02 b10 b11 b12)
  (let ((zero (p69b6-zero real-type))
        (nine (p69b6-natural real-type 9)))
    (and
     (equal
      (p69b6-sum3
       real-type b00 a00 b01 a10 b02 a20)
      nine)
     (equal
      (p69b6-sum3
       real-type b00 a01 b01 a11 b02 a21)
      zero)
     (equal
      (p69b6-sum3
       real-type b10 a00 b11 a10 b12 a20)
      zero)
     (equal
      (p69b6-sum3
       real-type b10 a01 b11 a11 b12 a21)
      nine))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1969-b6-statement
    (real-type
     a00 a01 a10 a11 a20 a21
     b00 b01 b02 b10 b11 b12)
  (implies
   (and
    (p69b6-real-closed-field-p real-type)
    (p69b6-matrix-entries-p
     real-type
     a00 a01 a10 a11 a20 a21
     b00 b01 b02 b10 b11 b12)
    (p69b6-forward-product-p
     real-type
     a00 a01 a10 a11 a20 a21
     b00 b01 b02 b10 b11 b12))
   (p69b6-reverse-product-p
    real-type
    a00 a01 a10 a11 a20 a21
    b00 b01 b02 b10 b11 b12)))

title: putnam_1969_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1969_b6:
-- real rectangular matrices A and B whose product is the specified 3 by 3
-- matrix have reverse product equal to 9 times the 2 by 2 identity matrix.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc threeN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc fourN

sixN : Nat
sixN =
  suc fiveN

sevenN : Nat
sevenN =
  suc sixN

eightN : Nat
eightN =
  suc sevenN

nineN : Nat
nineN =
  suc eightN

index0of2 : Fin twoN
index0of2 =
  fzero

index1of2 : Fin twoN
index1of2 =
  fsuc fzero

index0of3 : Fin threeN
index0of3 =
  fzero

index1of3 : Fin threeN
index1of3 =
  fsuc fzero

index2of3 : Fin threeN
index2of3 =
  fsuc (fsuc fzero)

Matrix :
  Set ->
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Set
Matrix R rows columns =
  Fin rows -> Fin columns -> R

MatrixEqual :
  {R : Set} {rows columns : Nat} ->
  Matrix R rows columns ->
  Matrix R rows columns ->
  Set
MatrixEqual {rows = rows} {columns = columns} A B =
  (i : Fin rows) ->
  (j : Fin columns) ->
  A i j == B i j

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

matrixMultiply :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {rows middle columns : Nat} ->
  Matrix R rows middle ->
  Matrix R middle columns ->
  Matrix R rows columns
matrixMultiply reals A B i j =
  sumFin reals
    (\ k -> multiply reals (A i k) (B k j))

nineIdentity :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Matrix R twoN twoN
nineIdentity reals fzero fzero =
  fromNat reals nineN
nineIdentity reals fzero (fsuc fzero) =
  zeroR reals
nineIdentity reals (fsuc fzero) fzero =
  zeroR reals
nineIdentity reals (fsuc fzero) (fsuc fzero) =
  fromNat reals nineN

SpecifiedProduct :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Matrix R threeN threeN ->
  Set
SpecifiedProduct reals p =
  p index0of3 index0of3 == fromNat reals eightN
  and
  p index0of3 index1of3 == fromNat reals twoN
  and
  p index0of3 index2of3 == negate reals (fromNat reals twoN)
  and
  p index1of3 index0of3 == fromNat reals twoN
  and
  p index1of3 index1of3 == fromNat reals fiveN
  and
  p index1of3 index2of3 == fromNat reals fourN
  and
  p index2of3 index0of3 == negate reals (fromNat reals twoN)
  and
  p index2of3 index1of3 == fromNat reals fourN
  and
  p index2of3 index2of3 == fromNat reals fiveN

putnam-1969-b6 : Set1
putnam-1969-b6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (A : Matrix R threeN twoN) ->
  (B : Matrix R twoN threeN) ->
  (p : Matrix R threeN threeN) ->
  SpecifiedProduct reals p ->
  MatrixEqual (matrixMultiply reals A B) p ->
  MatrixEqual
    (matrixMultiply reals B A)
    (nineIdentity reals)

title: putnam_1969_b6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1969_b6:
  rectangular real matrices whose product is the specified 3 by 3 matrix
  have reverse product equal to nine times the 2 by 2 identity matrix. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;

val putnam_1969_b6 =
  ``!A : num -> num -> real.
    !B : num -> num -> real.
    !p : num -> num -> real.
      p 0 0 = 8 /\ p 0 1 = 2 /\ p 0 2 = ~2 /\
      p 1 0 = 2 /\ p 1 1 = 5 /\ p 1 2 = 4 /\
      p 2 0 = ~2 /\ p 2 1 = 4 /\ p 2 2 = 5 /\
      (!i j : num.
         i < 3 /\ j < 3
         ==>
         SIGMA (\k : num. A i k * B k j) (count 2) = p i j)
      ==>
      (!i j : num.
         i < 2 /\ j < 2
         ==>
         SIGMA (\k : num. B i k * A k j) (count 3) =
           if i = j then 9 else 0)``;

title: putnam_1969_b6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1969_b6: reversing the product of real three-by-two and two-by-three
  matrices whose forward product has the specified entries gives nine times
  the two-by-two identity matrix. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The sets 0 ..^ 3 and 0 ..^ 2 are the index carriers for Fin 3 and Fin 2.
  Thus a, b, and p range over exactly the real 3-by-2, 2-by-3, and 3-by-3
  matrices in the sources. RRfld maMul is SetMM's rectangular matrix
  multiplication. The maps-to expression in the conclusion is the 2-by-2
  diagonal matrix with both diagonal entries equal to 9, hence exactly 9 I.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a b i j p $.

  putnambench-putnam-1969-b6 $a |-
    A. a e.
      (
        RR
        ^m
        ( ( 0 ..^ 3 ) X. ( 0 ..^ 2 ) )
      )
      A. b e.
        (
          RR
          ^m
          ( ( 0 ..^ 2 ) X. ( 0 ..^ 3 ) )
        )
        A. p e.
          (
            RR
            ^m
            ( ( 0 ..^ 3 ) X. ( 0 ..^ 3 ) )
          )
          (
            (
              (
                ( 0 p 0 ) = 8
                /\
                (
                  ( 0 p 1 ) = 2
                  /\
                  (
                    ( 0 p 2 ) = ( -u 2 )
                    /\
                    (
                      ( 1 p 0 ) = 2
                      /\
                      (
                        ( 1 p 1 ) = 5
                        /\
                        (
                          ( 1 p 2 ) = 4
                          /\
                          (
                            ( 2 p 0 ) = ( -u 2 )
                            /\
                            (
                              ( 2 p 1 ) = 4
                              /\
                              ( 2 p 2 ) = 5
                            )
                          )
                        )
                      )
                    )
                  )
                )
              )
              /\
              (
                a
                (
                  RRfld
                  maMul
                  <.
                    ( 0 ..^ 3 ) ,
                    ( 0 ..^ 2 ) ,
                    ( 0 ..^ 3 )
                  >.
                )
                b
              )
              =
              p
            )
            ->
            (
              (
                b
                (
                  RRfld
                  maMul
                  <.
                    ( 0 ..^ 2 ) ,
                    ( 0 ..^ 3 ) ,
                    ( 0 ..^ 2 )
                  >.
                )
                a
              )
              =
              (
                i e. ( 0 ..^ 2 ) , j e. ( 0 ..^ 2 ) |->
                  if ( i = j , 9 , 0 )
              )
            )
          )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1969_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1969_b6:
% real matrices A of size 3-by-2 and B of size 2-by-3 whose product is the
% specified 3-by-3 matrix have reverse product equal to 9 times the
% 2-by-2 identity matrix. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1969_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  index_2: TYPE = below(2)
  index_3: TYPE = below(3)

  matrix_3_by_2: TYPE = [index_3, index_2 -> real]
  matrix_2_by_3: TYPE = [index_2, index_3 -> real]
  matrix_3_by_3: TYPE = [index_3, index_3 -> real]

  product_3_by_3(
      A: matrix_3_by_2,
      B: matrix_2_by_3,
      row, column: index_3): real =
    A(row, 0) * B(0, column)
      + A(row, 1) * B(1, column)

  product_2_by_2(
      B: matrix_2_by_3,
      A: matrix_3_by_2,
      row, column: index_2): real =
    B(row, 0) * A(0, column)
      + B(row, 1) * A(1, column)
      + B(row, 2) * A(2, column)

  specified_matrix(p: matrix_3_by_3): bool =
    p(0, 0) = 8
      AND p(0, 1) = 2
      AND p(0, 2) = -2
      AND p(1, 0) = 2
      AND p(1, 1) = 5
      AND p(1, 2) = 4
      AND p(2, 0) = -2
      AND p(2, 1) = 4
      AND p(2, 2) = 5

  putnam_1969_b6: bool =
    FORALL
        (A: matrix_3_by_2),
        (B: matrix_2_by_3),
        (p: matrix_3_by_3):
      (specified_matrix(p)
        AND
          (FORALL (row, column: index_3):
            product_3_by_3(A, B, row, column)
              = p(row, column)))
      IMPLIES
        (FORALL (row, column: index_2):
          product_2_by_2(B, A, row, column)
            = IF row = column THEN 9 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
END putnam_1969_b6

import Mathlib

open Metric Set EuclideanGeometry

/--
Prove that, for all $a > 0$ and $b > 0$, the power series of $e^{ax} \cos (bx)$ with respect to $x$ has either zero or infinitely many zero coefficients.
-/
theorem putnam_1970_a1
(a b : ℝ)
(ha : a > 0)
(hb : b > 0)
(f : ℝ → ℝ)
(f_def : f = fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (a*x) * Real.cos (b*x))
(p : ℕ → ℝ)
(hp : ∃ c : ℝ, c > 0 ∧ ∀ x ∈ ball 0 c, ∑' n : ℕ, (p n)*x^n = f x)
(S : Set ℕ)
(S_def : S = {n : ℕ | p n = 0})
: S = ∅ ∨ ¬Finite S :=
sorry

From mathcomp Require Import all_algebra all_ssreflect.
From mathcomp Require Import reals exp sequences topology normedtype trigo.
From mathcomp Require Import classical_sets cardinality.
Import numFieldNormedType.Exports.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.
Local Open Scope classical_set_scope.
Local Open Scope card_scope.

Variable R : realType.
Theorem putnam_1970_a1
    (a b : R)
    (ha : a > 0)
    (hb : b > 0)
    (f : R -> R := fun x : R => expR (a * x) * cos (b * x))
    (p : nat -> R)
    (hp : exists c : R, c > 0 /\ forall x : R, ball 0 c x -> (fun n : nat => \sum_(0 <= i < n) (p i) * x ^+ i) @ \oo --> f x)
    (S := [set n : nat | p n = 0])
    : S = set0 \/ infinite_set S.
Proof. Admitted.

title: putnam_1970_a1
putnam_1970_a1
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1970_a1:
;; for positive real a and b, the power series of exp(a*x)*cos(b*x) has
;; either no zero coefficients or infinitely many zero coefficients. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The arguments of the final predicate present the complete ordered field of
;; reals and its exponential and cosine functions. Completeness characterizes
;; the ordered field up to its unique order-preserving isomorphism with R, and
;; the globally convergent power series below uniquely characterize exp and
;; cos. APPLY$ function objects retain the arbitrary coefficient function
;; p : N -> R; it is not replaced by a finite table or a rational subdomain.

(defun putnam-1970-a1-member-p (carrier x)
  (if (apply$ carrier (list x)) t nil))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-unary (operation x)
  (apply$ operation (list x)))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-binary (operation x y)
  (apply$ operation (list x y)))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-positive-p (carrier less zero x)
  (and
   (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier x)
   (apply$ less (list zero x))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-field-laws-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier x)
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier y)
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p
       carrier (putnam-1970-a1-binary add x y))
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p
       carrier (putnam-1970-a1-binary multiply x y))
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p
       carrier (putnam-1970-a1-unary negate x))
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p
       carrier (putnam-1970-a1-unary inverse x))
      (equal
       (putnam-1970-a1-binary
        add (putnam-1970-a1-binary add x y) z)
       (putnam-1970-a1-binary
        add x (putnam-1970-a1-binary add y z)))
      (equal
       (putnam-1970-a1-binary add x y)
       (putnam-1970-a1-binary add y x))
      (equal (putnam-1970-a1-binary add x zero) x)
      (equal
       (putnam-1970-a1-binary
        add x (putnam-1970-a1-unary negate x))
       zero)
      (equal
       (putnam-1970-a1-binary
        multiply (putnam-1970-a1-binary multiply x y) z)
       (putnam-1970-a1-binary
        multiply x (putnam-1970-a1-binary multiply y z)))
      (equal
       (putnam-1970-a1-binary multiply x y)
       (putnam-1970-a1-binary multiply y x))
      (equal (putnam-1970-a1-binary multiply x one) x)
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal
        (putnam-1970-a1-binary
         multiply x (putnam-1970-a1-unary inverse x))
        one))
      (equal
       (putnam-1970-a1-binary
        multiply x (putnam-1970-a1-binary add y z))
       (putnam-1970-a1-binary
        add
        (putnam-1970-a1-binary multiply x y)
        (putnam-1970-a1-binary multiply x z)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-order-laws-p
    (carrier add multiply zero less)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier x)
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier y)
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (not (apply$ less (list x x)))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (apply$ less (list x y))
       (apply$ less (list y x)))
      (implies
       (and
        (apply$ less (list x y))
        (apply$ less (list y z)))
       (apply$ less (list x z)))
      (implies
       (apply$ less (list x y))
       (apply$
        less
        (list
         (putnam-1970-a1-binary add x z)
         (putnam-1970-a1-binary add y z))))
      (implies
       (and
        (apply$ less (list zero x))
        (apply$ less (list zero y)))
       (apply$
        less
        (list
         zero
         (putnam-1970-a1-binary multiply x y))))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-set-nonempty-p (carrier set)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier x)
     (apply$ set (list x)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-upper-bound-p
    (carrier less set bound)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier x)
      (apply$ set (list x)))
     (not (apply$ less (list bound x))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-bounded-above-p
    (carrier less set)
  (exists (bound)
    (and
     (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier bound)
     (putnam-1970-a1-upper-bound-p
      carrier less set bound))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-supremum-p
    (carrier less set supremum)
  (forall (bound)
    (and
     (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier supremum)
     (putnam-1970-a1-upper-bound-p
      carrier less set supremum)
     (implies
      (and
       (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier bound)
       (putnam-1970-a1-upper-bound-p
        carrier less set bound))
      (not (apply$ less (list bound supremum)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-has-supremum-p
    (carrier less set)
  (exists (supremum)
    (putnam-1970-a1-supremum-p
     carrier less set supremum)))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-dedekind-complete-p
    (carrier less)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (tamep-functionp set)
      (putnam-1970-a1-set-nonempty-p carrier set)
      (putnam-1970-a1-bounded-above-p carrier less set))
     (putnam-1970-a1-has-supremum-p
      carrier less set))))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-real-field-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp add)
   (tamep-functionp multiply)
   (tamep-functionp negate)
   (tamep-functionp inverse)
   (tamep-functionp less)
   (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier zero)
   (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (putnam-1970-a1-field-laws-p
    carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one)
   (putnam-1970-a1-order-laws-p
    carrier add multiply zero less)
   (apply$ less (list zero one))
   (putnam-1970-a1-dedekind-complete-p
    carrier less)))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-power (multiply one x exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      one
    (putnam-1970-a1-binary
     multiply
     x
     (putnam-1970-a1-power
      multiply one x (- exponent 1)))))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-natural-value (add zero one n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      zero
    (putnam-1970-a1-binary
     add
     one
     (putnam-1970-a1-natural-value
      add zero one (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-factorial-value
    (add multiply zero one n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      one
    (putnam-1970-a1-binary
     multiply
     (putnam-1970-a1-natural-value
      add zero one n)
     (putnam-1970-a1-factorial-value
      add multiply zero one (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-exp-term
    (add multiply inverse zero one x n)
  (putnam-1970-a1-binary
   multiply
   (putnam-1970-a1-power multiply one x n)
   (putnam-1970-a1-unary
    inverse
    (putnam-1970-a1-factorial-value
     add multiply zero one n))))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-exp-prefix
    (add multiply inverse zero one x count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      zero
    (let ((index (- count 1)))
      (putnam-1970-a1-binary
       add
       (putnam-1970-a1-exp-prefix
        add multiply inverse zero one x index)
       (putnam-1970-a1-exp-term
        add multiply inverse zero one x index)))))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-cos-term
    (add multiply negate inverse zero one x n)
  (let* ((degree (* 2 n))
         (unsigned
          (putnam-1970-a1-binary
           multiply
           (putnam-1970-a1-power
            multiply one x degree)
           (putnam-1970-a1-unary
            inverse
            (putnam-1970-a1-factorial-value
             add multiply zero one degree)))))
    (if (evenp n)
        unsigned
      (putnam-1970-a1-unary negate unsigned))))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-cos-prefix
    (add multiply negate inverse zero one x count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      zero
    (let ((index (- count 1)))
      (putnam-1970-a1-binary
       add
       (putnam-1970-a1-cos-prefix
        add multiply negate inverse zero one x index)
       (putnam-1970-a1-cos-term
        add multiply negate inverse zero one x index)))))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-close-p
    (add multiply negate less left right epsilon)
  (let ((difference
         (putnam-1970-a1-binary
          add left (putnam-1970-a1-unary negate right))))
    (apply$
     less
     (list
      (putnam-1970-a1-binary
       multiply difference difference)
      (putnam-1970-a1-binary
       multiply epsilon epsilon)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-exp-tail-p
    (add multiply negate inverse zero one less
     exponential x epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (count)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp count)
      (<= cutoff count))
     (putnam-1970-a1-close-p
      add multiply negate less
      (putnam-1970-a1-exp-prefix
       add multiply inverse zero one x count)
      (putnam-1970-a1-unary exponential x)
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-exp-cutoff-exists-p
    (add multiply negate inverse zero one less
     exponential x epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (putnam-1970-a1-exp-tail-p
      add multiply negate inverse zero one less
      exponential x epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-exp-series-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less exponential)
  (forall (x epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier x)
      (putnam-1970-a1-positive-p
       carrier less zero epsilon))
     (and
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p
       carrier (putnam-1970-a1-unary exponential x))
      (putnam-1970-a1-exp-cutoff-exists-p
       add multiply negate inverse zero one less
       exponential x epsilon)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-cos-tail-p
    (add multiply negate inverse zero one less
     cosine x epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (count)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp count)
      (<= cutoff count))
     (putnam-1970-a1-close-p
      add multiply negate less
      (putnam-1970-a1-cos-prefix
       add multiply negate inverse zero one x count)
      (putnam-1970-a1-unary cosine x)
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-cos-cutoff-exists-p
    (add multiply negate inverse zero one less
     cosine x epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (putnam-1970-a1-cos-tail-p
      add multiply negate inverse zero one less
      cosine x epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-cos-series-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less cosine)
  (forall (x epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier x)
      (putnam-1970-a1-positive-p
       carrier less zero epsilon))
     (and
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p
       carrier (putnam-1970-a1-unary cosine x))
      (putnam-1970-a1-cos-cutoff-exists-p

(defun putnam-1970-a1-exp-cos-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less

  (and
   (tamep-functionp exponential)
   (tamep-functionp cosine)
   (putnam-1970-a1-exp-series-p
    carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less
    exponential)
   (putnam-1970-a1-cos-series-p
    carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-coefficient-values-p

  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (natp n)

      carrier (apply$ coefficients (list n))))))

(defun putnam-1970-a1-power-series-prefix
    (coefficients add multiply zero one x count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      zero
    (let ((index (- count 1)))
      (putnam-1970-a1-binary
       add
       (putnam-1970-a1-power-series-prefix

        multiply

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-power-series-tail-p
    (coefficients add multiply negate zero one less
     x target epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (count)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp count)
      (<= cutoff count))

      (putnam-1970-a1-power-series-prefix

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-power-series-cutoff-exists-p
    (coefficients add multiply negate zero one less
     x target epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-power-series-converges-p

(defun putnam-1970-a1-target-value

  (putnam-1970-a1-binary
   multiply
   (putnam-1970-a1-unary
    exponential
    (putnam-1970-a1-binary multiply a x))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-local-expansion-all-x-p
    (carrier coefficients add multiply negate zero one less
     exponential cosine a b radius)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1970-a1-member-p carrier x)
      (apply$
       less
       (list
        (putnam-1970-a1-unary negate radius)
        x))
      (apply$ less (list x radius)))
     (putnam-1970-a1-power-series-converges-p
      carrier coefficients add multiply negate zero one less

      (putnam-1970-a1-target-value

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-local-expansion-p
    (carrier coefficients add multiply negate zero one less

  (exists (radius)

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-zero-set-empty-p
    (coefficients zero)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (natp n)

           (apply$ coefficients (list n))

    (coefficients zero threshold)
  (exists (n)
    (and
     (natp n)
     (< threshold n)
     (equal
      (apply$ coefficients (list n))

(defun-sk putnam-1970-a1-zero-set-infinite-p
    (coefficients zero)
  (forall (threshold)
    (implies
     (natp threshold)
     (putnam-1970-a1-zero-above-exists-p
      coefficients zero threshold))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1970-a1-statement
    (a b coefficients
     carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less
     exponential cosine)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-1970-a1-real-field-p
     carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
    (putnam-1970-a1-exp-cos-p
     carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less
     exponential cosine)
    (putnam-1970-a1-positive-p carrier less zero a)
    (putnam-1970-a1-positive-p carrier less zero b)
    (tamep-functionp coefficients)
    (putnam-1970-a1-coefficient-values-p

    (putnam-1970-a1-local-expansion-p

    (putnam-1970-a1-zero-set-empty-p
     coefficients zero)
    (putnam-1970-a1-zero-set-infinite-p
     coefficients zero))))

:q

title: putnam_1970_a1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1970_a1:
-- for positive real a and b, the local power-series coefficients of
-- exp(a*x) * cos(b*x) have either no zero terms or infinitely many zero terms.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

alternatingPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingPower reals n =
  naturalPower reals
    (negate reals (oneR reals))
    n

exponentialTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

cosineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
cosineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (twoN * n)))
    (fromNat reals (factorial (twoN * n)))

record StandardExponentialCosine
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) : Set1 where
  field
    exponential cosine : R -> R
    exponential-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (exponentialTerm reals x)
        (exponential x)
    cosine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (cosineTerm reals x)
        (cosine x)

open StandardExponentialCosine

powerSeriesTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
powerSeriesTerm reals coefficients x n =
  multiply reals
    (coefficients n)
    (naturalPower reals x n)

HasLocalExpansion :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  StandardExponentialCosine reals ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Set
HasLocalExpansion reals functions a b coefficients =
  Exists _
    (\ radius ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) radius
      and
      ((x : _) ->
        CloseTo reals (zeroR reals) radius x ->
        SeriesHasSum reals
          (powerSeriesTerm reals coefficients x)
          (multiply reals
            (exponential functions (multiply reals a x))
            (cosine functions (multiply reals b x)))))

ZeroSetEmpty :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Set
ZeroSetEmpty reals coefficients =
  (n : Nat) ->
  coefficients n != zeroR reals

FiniteZeroSet :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Set
FiniteZeroSet reals coefficients =
  Exists Nat
    (\ cardinality ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality -> Nat)
        (\ enumeration ->
          (n : Nat) ->
          coefficients n == zeroR reals ->
          Exists (Fin cardinality)
            (\ i -> enumeration i == n)))

putnam-1970-a1 : Set1
putnam-1970-a1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (functions : StandardExponentialCosine reals) ->
  (a b : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) a ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) b ->
  (coefficients : Nat -> R) ->
  HasLocalExpansion reals functions a b coefficients ->
  ZeroSetEmpty reals coefficients
  or
  Not (FiniteZeroSet reals coefficients)

title: putnam_1970_a1
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1970_a1:
  the power series of exp (a*x) * cos (b*x), for positive real a and b, has
  either no zero coefficients or infinitely many. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory seqTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_1970_a1 =
  ``!a b : real. !p : num -> real.
      0 < a /\ 0 < b /\
      (?c : real.
         0 < c /\
         !x : real.
           abs x < c
           ==>
           (\n : num. p n * x pow n) sums
             (exp (a * x) * cos (b * x)))
      ==>
      {n : num | p n = 0} = EMPTY \/
      INFINITE {n : num | p n = 0}``;

title: putnam_1970_a1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1970_a1: the power series of exp(a x) cos(b x), for positive real
  a and b, has either no zero coefficients or infinitely many zero
  coefficients. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P ranges over all real-valued sequences indexed by NN0. The source
  definitions of f(x) = exp(a x) cos(b x) and of the zero-coefficient set
  are inlined. The epsilon-N premise states convergence, at every real x in
  an open ball about zero, of the partial sums indexed by 0 ..^ m to f(x).
  This is bidirectionally equivalent to the source power-series identity:
  convergence gives the infinite-sum equality, while any source neighborhood
  may be shrunk around zero so that exp(a x) cos(b x) is nonzero and its
  infinite-sum equality forces convergence. The conclusion says that the
  zero-coefficient set is empty or is not a member of Fin.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d P N a b c e m n x $.

  putnambench-putnam-1970-a1 $a |-
    A. a e. RR
      A. b e. RR
        A. P e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
          (
            (
              (
                0 < a
                /\
                0 < b
              )
              /\
              E. c e. RR
                (
                  0 < c
                  /\
                  A. x e. RR
                    (
                      ( abs ` x ) < c
                      ->
                      A. e e. RR
                        (
                          0 < e
                          ->
                          E. N e. NN0
                            A. m e. NN0
                              (
                                N <_ m
                                ->
                                (
                                  abs
                                  `
                                  (
                                    (
                                      sum_ n e. ( 0 ..^ m )
                                        (
                                          ( P ` n )
                                          x.
                                          ( x ^ n )
                                        )
                                    )
                                    -
                                    (
                                      ( exp ` ( a x. x ) )
                                      x.
                                      ( cos ` ( b x. x ) )
                                    )
                                  )
                                )
                                < e
                              )
                        )
                    )
                )
            )
            ->
            (
              { n e. NN0 | ( P ` n ) = 0 } = (/)
              \/
              { n e. NN0 | ( P ` n ) = 0 } e/ Fin
            )
          )
  $.
$}

content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1970_a1:
:: the power series of exp(a*x) times cos(b*x), for positive a and b, has

environ

    FUNCT_2, PARTFUN1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, NUMBERS, NAT_1, CARD_1,

    RVSUM_1, BINOP_1, BINOP_2, SETWISEO, SETWOP_2, POWER;

    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_2, REAL_1, COMPLEX1, NAT_1,
    NAT_D, INT_1, RELAT_1, BINOP_1, BINOP_2, SETWISEO, SETWOP_2,
    FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    FINSEQOP, FINSET_1, CARD_1, NEWTON, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, SEQ_1,
    SEQ_2, COMSEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4, PREPOWER, ABIAN, SERIES_1,
    SIN_COS, RVSUM_1, POWER;
  constructors REAL_1, NUMBERS, RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, BINOP_1,
    BINOP_2, SETWISEO, SETWOP_2, FINSOP_1, FINSEQOP, FINSEQ_4, NAT_1,
    NAT_D, NEWTON, INT_1, XXREAL_0, COMPLEX1, SEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4,
    PREPOWER, ABIAN, COMSEQ_2, SERIES_1, SIN_COS, RVSUM_1, POWER;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, PARTFUN1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSET_1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, NAT_1, INT_1, NEWTON,
    VALUED_0, VALUED_1, MEMBERED, FRAENKEL, BINOP_2, RVSUM_1,
    PREPOWER, SEQ_4, ABIAN, SEQ_1, SIN_COS;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for a,b being Real holds
  for p being Real_Sequence st
    0 < a & 0 < b &
    (ex c being Real st
      0 < c &
      for x being Real st |.x.| < c holds
        ex s being Real_Sequence st
          (for n being Nat holds s.n = p.n * (x |^ n)) &
          Partial_Sums(s) is convergent &
          lim Partial_Sums(s) = exp_R.(a*x) * cos(b*x))
  holds
    (for n being Nat holds p.n <> 0) or
    {n where n is Element of NAT : p.n = 0} is infinite
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1970_a1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1970_a1:
% for positive real a and b, the power series of exp(a*x) * cos(b*x) has
% either no zero coefficients or infinitely many. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1970_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  partial_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(values: real_sequence, limit: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(partial_sum(values, count) - limit) < epsilon_value

  exponential_terms(x: real): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (index: nat):
      safe_div(x ^ index, factorial(index) :: real)

  cosine_terms(x: real): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (index: nat):
      safe_div(
        ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index),
        factorial(2 * index) :: real)

  power_series_terms(p: real_sequence, x: real): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (index: nat): p(index) * x ^ index

  locally_represents_exp_cos(
      a, b: real,
      p: real_sequence): bool =
    EXISTS (radius: real):
      radius > 0
        AND FORALL (x: real):
          abs(x) < radius IMPLIES
            EXISTS (exp_value, cos_value: real):
              converges_to(exponential_terms(a * x), exp_value)
                AND converges_to(cosine_terms(b * x), cos_value)
                AND converges_to(
                  power_series_terms(p, x),
                  exp_value * cos_value)

  has_no_zero_coefficients(p: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat): p(index) /= 0

  has_infinitely_many_zero_coefficients(p: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (bound: nat):
      EXISTS (index: nat):
        bound <= index AND p(index) = 0

  putnam_1970_a1: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: real), (p: real_sequence):
      (a > 0
        AND b > 0
        AND locally_represents_exp_cos(a, b, p))
      IMPLIES
        (has_no_zero_coefficients(p)
          OR has_infinitely_many_zero_coefficients(p))
END putnam_1970_a1

title: putnam_1970_a2
content:
import Mathlib

open Metric Set EuclideanGeometry

/--
Let $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$, $E$, $F$, and $G$ be real numbers satisfying $B^2 - 4AC < 0$. Prove that there exists some $\delta > 0$ such that no points $(x, y)$ in the punctured disk $0 < x^2 + y^2 < \delta$ satisfy $$Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + Dx^3 + Ex^2y + Fxy^2 + Gy^3 = 0.$$
-/
theorem putnam_1970_a2
(A B C D E F G : ℝ)
(hle : B^2 - 4*A*C < 0)
: ∃ δ > 0, ¬∃ x y : ℝ, x^2 + y^2 ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (δ^2) ∧
A*x^2 + B*x*y + C*y^2 + D*x^3 + E*x^2*y + F*x*y^2 + G*y^3 = 0 :=
sorry

title: putnam_1970_a2
content:
From mathcomp Require Import all_algebra all_ssreflect.
From mathcomp Require Import reals.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.

Variable R : realType.
Theorem putnam_1970_a2
    (A B C D E F G : R)
    (hle : B ^+ 2 - 4 * A * C < 0)
    : exists delta : R, delta > 0 /\ (~ exists x y : R, 0 < x ^+ 2 + y ^+ 2 < delta ^+ 2 /\ 
    A * x ^+ 2 + B * x * y + C * y ^+ 2 + D * x ^+ 3 + E * x ^+ 2 * y + F * x * y ^+ 2 + G * y ^+ 3 = 0).
Proof. Admitted.

theorem putnam_1970_a2:

  assumes hle : "B^2 - 4*A*C < 0"
  shows "\<exists> \<delta> > 0. \<not> (\<exists> x y :: real. x^2 + y^2 \<noteq> 0 \<and> x^2 + y^2 < \<delta>^2 \<and>
    A*x^2 + B*x*y + C*y^2 + D*x^3 + E*x^2*y+ F*x*y^2 + G*y^3 = 0)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1970_a2:
  under a negative quadratic discriminant, a real bivariate polynomial with
  quadratic and cubic terms has no nonzero zeros sufficiently near the origin.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `!A B C D E F G:real.
     B pow 2 - &4 * A * C < &0
     ==> ?delta:real.
           &0 < delta /\
           ~(?x y:real.
               ~(x pow 2 + y pow 2 = &0) /\
               x pow 2 + y pow 2 < delta pow 2 /\
               A * x pow 2 + B * x * y + C * y pow 2 +
               D * x pow 3 + E * x pow 2 * y +
               F * x * y pow 2 + G * y pow 3 = &0)`;;

title: putnam_1970_a2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1970_a2:
;; a real quadratic form with negative discriminant remains nonzero near the
;; origin after adding arbitrary homogeneous cubic terms. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Ordinary ACL2 has only rational native scalars, so the source real numbers
;; are presented as an arbitrary linearly ordered field. The theorem is
;; algebraic and holds over every such field; no completeness or Archimedean
;; axiom is needed. In particular, the existential radius and the universal
;; points below range over the same full scalar carrier, preserving the source
;; quantifier order without a coded-number-field restriction.

(defstub p1970a2-scalar-p (x) t)
(defstub p1970a2-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub p1970a2-multiply-op (x y) t)
(defstub p1970a2-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub p1970a2-inverse-op (x) t)
(defstub p1970a2-less-op (x y) t)

(defun p1970a2-add (x y)
  (p1970a2-add-op x y))

(defun p1970a2-multiply (x y)
  (p1970a2-multiply-op x y))

(defun p1970a2-negate (x)
  (p1970a2-negate-op x))

(defun p1970a2-inverse (x)
  (p1970a2-inverse-op x))

(defun p1970a2-subtract (x y)
  (p1970a2-add x (p1970a2-negate y)))

(defun p1970a2-less-p (x y)
  (if (p1970a2-less-op x y) t nil))

(defun p1970a2-square (x)
  (p1970a2-multiply x x))

(defun p1970a2-cube (x)
  (p1970a2-multiply (p1970a2-square x) x))

(defun p1970a2-four (one)
  (p1970a2-add
   (p1970a2-add one one)
   (p1970a2-add one one)))

(defun-sk p1970a2-field-laws-p (zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p1970a2-scalar-p x)
      (p1970a2-scalar-p y)
      (p1970a2-scalar-p z))
     (and
      (p1970a2-scalar-p (p1970a2-add x y))
      (p1970a2-scalar-p (p1970a2-multiply x y))
      (p1970a2-scalar-p (p1970a2-negate x))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (p1970a2-scalar-p (p1970a2-inverse x)))
      (equal
       (p1970a2-add (p1970a2-add x y) z)
       (p1970a2-add x (p1970a2-add y z)))
      (equal (p1970a2-add x y)
             (p1970a2-add y x))
      (equal (p1970a2-add x zero) x)
      (equal
       (p1970a2-add x (p1970a2-negate x))
       zero)
      (equal

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1970_a2:
-- a real quadratic form with negative discriminant, perturbed by arbitrary
-- cubic terms, has no nonzero zero sufficiently near the origin.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    addR multiplyR : R -> R -> R
    negateR inverseR : R -> R
    lessOrEqualR : R -> R -> Set
    fromNatR : Nat -> R

    oneR-not-zeroR :
      oneR != zeroR

    addR-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> addR x y == addR y x
    addR-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> addR (addR x y) z == addR x (addR y z)
    addR-zero :
      (x : R) -> addR x zeroR == x
    addR-inverse :
      (x : R) -> addR x (negateR x) == zeroR

    multiplyR-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiplyR x y == multiplyR y x
    multiplyR-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiplyR (multiplyR x y) z ==
      multiplyR x (multiplyR y z)
    multiplyR-one :
      (x : R) -> multiplyR x oneR == x
    multiplyR-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiplyR x zeroR == zeroR
    distributeR :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiplyR x (addR y z) ==
      addR (multiplyR x y) (multiplyR x z)
    inverseR-zero :
      inverseR zeroR == zeroR
    multiplyR-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiplyR x (inverseR x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqualR x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR y z ->
      lessOrEqualR x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y or lessOrEqualR y x
    addR-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR (addR z x) (addR z y)
    multiplyR-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR (multiplyR x y)
    zeroR-less-than-oneR :
      lessOrEqualR zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNatR-zero :
      fromNatR zero == zeroR
    fromNatR-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNatR (suc n) == addR (fromNatR n) oneR
    fromNatR-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNatR (m + n) == addR (fromNatR m) (fromNatR n)
    fromNatR-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNatR (m * n) == multiplyR (fromNatR m) (fromNatR n)
    fromNatR-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNatR m == fromNatR n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqualR x (fromNatR n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqualR x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqualR x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqualR x upper) ->
            lessOrEqualR supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  addR reals x (negateR reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiplyR reals x x

cube :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
cube reals x =
  multiplyR reals (square reals x) x

two :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
two reals =
  addR reals (oneR reals) (oneR reals)

four :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
four reals =
  addR reals (two reals) (two reals)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqualR reals x y and x != y

discriminant :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
discriminant reals A B C =
  subtract reals
    (square reals B)
    (multiplyR reals
      (four reals)
      (multiplyR reals A C))

squaredRadius :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
squaredRadius reals x y =
  addR reals (square reals x) (square reals y)

polynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
polynomial reals A B C D E F G x y =
  addR reals
    (addR reals
      (addR reals
        (addR reals
          (multiplyR reals A (square reals x))
          (multiplyR reals
            (multiplyR reals B x)
            y))
        (multiplyR reals C (square reals y)))
      (multiplyR reals D (cube reals x)))
    (addR reals
      (addR reals
        (multiplyR reals
          (multiplyR reals E (square reals x))
          y)
        (multiplyR reals
          (multiplyR reals F x)
          (square reals y)))
      (multiplyR reals G (cube reals y)))

module Putnam1970A2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (A B C D E F G : R) ->
    StrictLess reals
      (discriminant reals A B C)
      (zeroR reals) ->
    Exists R
      (\ delta ->
        StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
        and
        Not
          (Exists R
            (\ x ->
              Exists R
                (\ y ->
                  StrictLess reals
                    (zeroR reals)
                    (squaredRadius reals x y)
                  and
                  StrictLess reals
                    (squaredRadius reals x y)
                    (square reals delta)
                  and
                  polynomial reals A B C D E F G x y
                    ==
                  zeroR reals))))

putnam-1970-a2 : Set1
putnam-1970-a2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1970A2Statement.proposition reals

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1970_a3:
   the longest run of equal nonzero terminal decimal digits of a perfect
   square, and the least square attaining it. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List.

Fixpoint decimal_digits_fuel (fuel n : nat) : list nat :=
  match fuel with
  | O => nil
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb n 10
      then n :: nil
      else Nat.modulo n 10 :: decimal_digits_fuel fuel' (Nat.div n 10)
  end.

Definition decimal_digits (n : nat) : list nat :=
  decimal_digits_fuel (S n) n.

Definition decimal_digit (n k : nat) : nat :=
  nth k (decimal_digits n) 0.

Definition terminal_run_length (L : nat -> nat) : Prop :=
  forall n : nat,
    (0 < n)%nat ->
    (L n <= length (decimal_digits n))%nat /\
    (forall k : nat,
      (k < L n)%nat ->
      decimal_digit n k = decimal_digit n 0) /\
    (L n <> length (decimal_digits n) ->
      decimal_digit n (L n) <> decimal_digit n 0).

Definition putnam_1970_a3_solution : nat * nat := (3, 1444).

Theorem putnam_1970_a3
    (L : nat -> nat)
    (hL : terminal_run_length L) :
  (exists n : nat,
    decimal_digit (n * n) 0 <> 0 /\
    L (n * n) = fst putnam_1970_a3_solution) /\
  (forall n : nat,
    decimal_digit (n * n) 0 <> 0 ->
    (L (n * n) <= fst putnam_1970_a3_solution)%nat) /\
  (exists m : nat, m * m = snd putnam_1970_a3_solution) /\
  L (snd putnam_1970_a3_solution) = fst putnam_1970_a3_solution /\
  decimal_digit (snd putnam_1970_a3_solution) 0 <> 0 /\
  forall n : nat,
    decimal_digit (n * n) 0 <> 0 /\
    L (n * n) = fst putnam_1970_a3_solution ->
    (snd putnam_1970_a3_solution <= n * n)%nat.
Admitted.

;; Defining that function directly eliminates the arbitrary L without changing
;; the proposition.  Lean's digit list for zero is empty while Isabelle's is
;; [0], but every conclusion involving a square is guarded by a nonzero units
;; digit, so the two definitions agree on every relevant input.
(defun putnam-1970-a3-trailing-run-aux (n digit place fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (or (not (natp n))
          (not (natp place))
          (zp place)
          (zp fuel)
          (< n place))
      0
    (if (equal (mod (floor n place) 10) digit)
        (+ 1
           (putnam-1970-a3-trailing-run-aux
            n digit (* 10 place) (- fuel 1)))
      0)))

(defun putnam-1970-a3-trailing-run-length (n)
  (if (natp n)
      (putnam-1970-a3-trailing-run-aux n (mod n 10) 1 n)
    0))

(defun putnam-1970-a3-square (n)
  (* n n))

(defun putnam-1970-a3-square-has-nonzero-units-p (n)
  (and (natp n)
       (not (equal (mod (putnam-1970-a3-square n) 10) 0))))

;; The fixed clauses give the source existential witnesses: 38^2 = 1444 has
;; a nonzero units digit and trailing-run length 3.  The parameter N expresses
;; both unbounded universal clauses: no eligible square has a longer run, and
;; every eligible square with run length 3 is at least 1444.
(defun putnambench-putnam-1970-a3-statement (n)
  (and
   (equal (putnam-1970-a3-square 38) 1444)
   (putnam-1970-a3-square-has-nonzero-units-p 38)
   (equal
    (putnam-1970-a3-trailing-run-length
     (putnam-1970-a3-square 38))
    3)
   (implies
    (natp n)
    (and
     (implies
      (putnam-1970-a3-square-has-nonzero-units-p n)
      (<=
       (putnam-1970-a3-trailing-run-length
        (putnam-1970-a3-square n))
       3))
     (implies
      (and
       (putnam-1970-a3-square-has-nonzero-units-p n)
       (equal
        (putnam-1970-a3-trailing-run-length
         (putnam-1970-a3-square n))
        3))
      (<= 1444 (putnam-1970-a3-square n)))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1970_a3:
-- the longest nonzero repeated terminal decimal digit run among perfect
-- squares has length 3, first attained by the square 1444.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=_ _<_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record _×_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    first-component  : A
    second-component : B

open _×_

data _<=_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <= n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> suc m <= suc n

_<_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m < n =
  suc m <= n

natLess : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
natLess zero zero =
  false
natLess zero (suc n) =
  true
natLess (suc m) zero =
  false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) =
  natLess m n

naturalDiv : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero =
  zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero =
  zero
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

ten : Nat
ten =
  10

digitsWithFuel : Nat -> Nat -> List Nat
digitsWithFuel zero n =
  n ∷ []
digitsWithFuel (suc fuel) n with natLess n ten
... | true =
  n ∷ []
... | false =
  naturalMod n ten ∷
  digitsWithFuel fuel (naturalDiv n ten)

digits : Nat -> List Nat
digits n =
  digitsWithFuel n n

length : {A : Set} -> List A -> Nat
length [] =
  zero
length (x ∷ xs) =
  suc (length xs)

lookupDefault : {A : Set} -> A -> Nat -> List A -> A
lookupDefault default zero [] =
  default
lookupDefault default zero (x ∷ xs) =
  x
lookupDefault default (suc n) [] =
  default
lookupDefault default (suc n) (x ∷ xs) =
  lookupDefault default n xs

digitAt : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
digitAt n k =
  lookupDefault zero k (digits n)

square : Nat -> Nat
square n =
  n * n

three : Nat
three =
  3

putnam-1970-a3-solution : Nat × Nat
putnam-1970-a3-solution =
  pair three 1444

DefinesTerminalRunLength : (Nat -> Nat) -> Set
DefinesTerminalRunLength L =
  (n : Nat) ->
  L n <= length (digits n)
  and
  ((k : Nat) ->
    k < L n ->
    digitAt n k == digitAt n zero)
  and
  (L n != length (digits n) ->
    digitAt n (L n) != digitAt n zero)

putnam-1970-a3 : Set
putnam-1970-a3 =
  (L : Nat -> Nat) ->
  DefinesTerminalRunLength L ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ n ->
      digitAt (square n) zero != zero
      and
      L (square n) == first-component putnam-1970-a3-solution)
  and
  ((n : Nat) ->
    digitAt (square n) zero != zero ->
    L (square n) <= first-component putnam-1970-a3-solution)
  and
  Exists Nat
    (\ m ->
      square m == second-component putnam-1970-a3-solution)
  and
  L (second-component putnam-1970-a3-solution)
    ==
  first-component putnam-1970-a3-solution
  and
  digitAt (second-component putnam-1970-a3-solution) zero != zero
  and
  ((n : Nat) ->
    (digitAt (square n) zero != zero
    and
    L (square n) == first-component putnam-1970-a3-solution) ->
    second-component putnam-1970-a3-solution <= square n)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1970_a3:
  the longest nonzero repeated decimal digit ending a perfect square has
  length 3, first attained by the square 1444. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory numposrepTheory;

val putnam_1970_a3 =
  ``!L : num -> num.
      (!n : num.
         L n <= LENGTH (n2l 10 n) /\
         (!k : num.
            k < L n
            ==>
            EL k (n2l 10 n) = EL 0 (n2l 10 n)) /\
         (L n <> LENGTH (n2l 10 n)
          ==>
          EL (L n) (n2l 10 n) <> EL 0 (n2l 10 n)))
      ==>
      (?n : num.
         EL 0 (n2l 10 (n ** 2)) <> 0 /\
         L (n ** 2) = 3) /\
      (!n : num.
         EL 0 (n2l 10 (n ** 2)) <> 0
         ==>
         L (n ** 2) <= 3) /\
      (?m : num. m ** 2 = 1444) /\
      L 1444 = 3 /\
      EL 0 (n2l 10 1444) <> 0 /\
      !n : num.
        EL 0 (n2l 10 (n ** 2)) <> 0 /\
        L (n ** 2) = 3
        ==>
        1444 <= n ** 2``;
