title: putnam_1971_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1971_b3:
% the Lebesgue measure of times after a positive delay when one floor count is
% twice the delayed floor count is exactly one. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1971_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_set: TYPE = [real -> bool]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  partial_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(values: real_sequence, limit: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(values(count) - limit) < epsilon_value

  interval_length(left_endpoint, right_endpoint: real): real =
    IF left_endpoint < right_endpoint THEN
      right_endpoint - left_endpoint
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  open_interval_cover(
      covered: real_set,
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      covered(x) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (index: nat):
          left_endpoints(index) < x
            AND x < right_endpoints(index)

  cover_partial_length(
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence,
      count: nat): real =
    partial_sum(
      LAMBDA (index: nat):
        interval_length(
          left_endpoints(index),
          right_endpoints(index)),
      count)

  cover_has_total_length(
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence,
      total: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat):
        cover_partial_length(
          left_endpoints, right_endpoints, count),
      total)

  has_lebesgue_outer_measure(
      covered: real_set,
      measure_value: real): bool =
    measure_value >= 0
      AND (FORALL
          (left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence),
          (total: real):
        (open_interval_cover(
            covered, left_endpoints, right_endpoints)
          AND cover_has_total_length(
            left_endpoints, right_endpoints, total))
        IMPLIES measure_value <= total)
      AND (FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS
            (left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence),
            (total: real):
          open_interval_cover(
            covered, left_endpoints, right_endpoints)
            AND cover_has_total_length(
              left_endpoints, right_endpoints, total)
            AND total < measure_value + epsilon_value)

  matching_times(delay: real): real_set =
    LAMBDA (time: real):
      time >= delay
        AND floor(time) = 2 * floor(time - delay)

  putnam_1971_b3: bool =
    FORALL (delay: real):
      delay > 0 IMPLIES
        has_lebesgue_outer_measure(
          matching_times(delay),
          1)
END putnam_1971_b3

title: putnam_1971_b6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1971_b6:
;; for every positive integer x, the sum from 1 through x of the greatest odd
;; divisor of n divided by n differs from 2*x/3 by less than 1 in absolute
;; value. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For positive n, every positive divisor is at most n. Descending from n
;; therefore returns exactly the greatest odd divisor, with 1 as the final
;; possible candidate.
(defun putnam-1971-b6-greatest-odd-divisor-through (n candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (and (natp n)
           (natp candidate))
      (if (zp candidate)
          1
        (if (and (equal (mod n candidate) 0)
                 (equal (mod candidate 2) 1))
            candidate
          (putnam-1971-b6-greatest-odd-divisor-through
           n (- candidate 1))))
    0))

(defun putnam-1971-b6-greatest-odd-divisor (n)
  (if (and (natp n)
           (< 0 n))
      (putnam-1971-b6-greatest-odd-divisor-through n n)
    0))

;; This is the exact rational sum of delta(n)/n for n = 1 through x.
(defun putnam-1971-b6-sum-through (x)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix x)))
  (if (natp x)
      (if (zp x)
          0
        (+ (putnam-1971-b6-sum-through (- x 1))
           (/ (putnam-1971-b6-greatest-odd-divisor x)
              x)))
    0))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1971-b6-statement (x)
  (implies
   (and (natp x)
        (< 0 x))
   (< (abs
       (- (putnam-1971-b6-sum-through x)
          (/ (* 2 x) 3)))
      1)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1971_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1971_b6:
-- the partial sum of the greatest odd divisor of n divided by n stays within
-- one of 2x/3 for every positive natural number x. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : (n : Nat) -> Positive (suc n)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

Divides :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Set
Divides divisor number =
  Exists Nat
    (\ quotient -> divisor * quotient == number)

Odd :
  Nat ->
  Set
Odd number =
  Exists Nat
    (\ k -> number == suc (twoN * k))

GreatestOddDivisor :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Set
GreatestOddDivisor divisor number =
  Divides divisor number
  and
  Odd divisor
  and
  ((candidate : Nat) ->
    Divides candidate number ->
    Odd candidate ->
    candidate <=N divisor)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

AbsoluteValueLessThan :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
AbsoluteValueLessThan reals value bound =
  StrictLess reals (negate reals bound) value
  and
  StrictLess reals value bound

sumFromOne :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFromOne reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFromOne reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFromOne reals n term)
    (term (suc n))

greatestOddDivisorSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Nat ->
  R
greatestOddDivisorSum reals delta x =
  sumFromOne reals x
    (\ n ->
      divide reals
        (fromNat reals (delta n))
        (fromNat reals n))

twoThirdsTimes :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
twoThirdsTimes reals x =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (fromNat reals twoN)
      (fromNat reals x))
    (fromNat reals threeN)

putnam-1971-b6 : Set1
putnam-1971-b6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (delta : Nat -> Nat) ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    Positive n ->
    GreatestOddDivisor (delta n) n) ->
  (x : Nat) ->
  Positive x ->
  AbsoluteValueLessThan reals
    (subtract reals
      (greatestOddDivisorSum reals delta x)
      (twoThirdsTimes reals x))
    (oneR reals)

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1971_b6:
% the sum of the greatest odd divisor of each positive integer n, divided by
% n, differs from 2x/3 by less than one through every positive x. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1971_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  is_odd(value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (half: nat):
      value = 2 * half + 1

  is_greatest_odd_divisor(
      divisor, value: nat): bool =
    is_odd(divisor)
      AND nat_divides(divisor, value)
      AND (FORALL (candidate: nat):
        is_odd(candidate)
          AND nat_divides(candidate, value)
        IMPLIES candidate <= divisor)

  is_greatest_odd_divisor_function(
      delta: natural_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (value: nat):
      value > 0 IMPLIES
        is_greatest_odd_divisor(delta(value), value)

  odd_divisor_sum(
      delta: natural_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      odd_divisor_sum(delta, count - 1)
        + (delta(count) :: real) / (count :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  putnam_1971_b6: bool =
    FORALL (delta: natural_sequence):
      is_greatest_odd_divisor_function(delta)
        IMPLIES
          FORALL (x: nat):
            x > 0 IMPLIES
              abs(
                odd_divisor_sum(delta, x)
                  - 2 * (x :: real) / 3)
                < 1
END putnam_1971_b6

-- no four consecutive binomial coefficients with positive lower index and
-- valid upper index form an arithmetic progression. This file contains no proof.

module Putnam1972A1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

three : Nat
three =
  suc two

choose : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
choose n zero =
  one
choose zero (suc k) =
  zero
choose (suc n) (suc k) =
  choose n (suc k) + choose n k

ArithmeticProgression : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Set
ArithmeticProgression a b c d =
  (d + b == c + c)
  and
  (c + a == b + b)

putnam-1972-a1 : Set
putnam-1972-a1 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  Not
    (Exists Nat
      (\ r ->
        Positive r
        and
        ((r + three) <=N n
        and
        ArithmeticProgression
          (choose n r)
          (choose n (r + one))
          (choose n (r + two))
          (choose n (r + three)))))

  binomial_coefficient(n, k: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF k = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSIF n = 0 THEN
      0

        + binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k)

            AND r + 3 <= n
            AND four_in_arithmetic_progression(
              (binomial_coefficient(n, r) :: int),
              (binomial_coefficient(n, r + 1) :: int),
              (binomial_coefficient(n, r + 2) :: int),
              (binomial_coefficient(n, r + 3) :: int)))

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1972_a2:
;; binary operations satisfying both involution laws are commutative, but
;; need not be associative. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; CARRIER and OP are ACL2 function objects. The generated predicate lambdas
;; return T outside CARRIER, so FN-EQUAL with the matching constant-T lambda
;; expresses universal quantification over exactly the represented type.

(defun putnam-1972-a2-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-1972-a2-quoted function)
        (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-1972-a2-quoted function)
        (list 'cons left
              (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-1972-a2-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-operation-term (op left right)
  (putnam-1972-a2-apply2-term op left right))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-all-in-carrier-term
    (carrier variables)
  (if (endp variables)
      t
    (list 'if
          (putnam-1972-a2-carrier-term
           carrier (car variables))
          (putnam-1972-a2-all-in-carrier-term
           carrier (cdr variables))
          nil)))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-restricted-predicate-term
    (carrier variables proposition)
  (list 'if
        (putnam-1972-a2-all-in-carrier-term
         carrier variables)
        proposition
        t))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda formals t))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-closure-function (carrier op)
  (let ((op-xy
         (putnam-1972-a2-operation-term op 'x 'y)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y)
     (putnam-1972-a2-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x y)
      (putnam-1972-a2-carrier-term carrier op-xy)))))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-left-involution-function (carrier op)
  (let ((op-xy
         (putnam-1972-a2-operation-term op 'x 'y)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y)
     (putnam-1972-a2-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x y)
      (list
       'equal
       (putnam-1972-a2-operation-term op 'x op-xy)
       'y)))))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-right-involution-function (carrier op)
  (let ((op-yx
         (putnam-1972-a2-operation-term op 'y 'x)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y)
     (putnam-1972-a2-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x y)
      (list
       'equal
       (putnam-1972-a2-operation-term op op-yx 'x)
       'y)))))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-commutative-function (carrier op)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(x y)
   (putnam-1972-a2-restricted-predicate-term
    carrier
    '(x y)
    (list
     'equal
     (putnam-1972-a2-operation-term op 'x 'y)
     (putnam-1972-a2-operation-term op 'y 'x)))))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-involution-structure-p (carrier op)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp op)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1972-a2-closure-function carrier op)
    (putnam-1972-a2-true-function '(x y)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1972-a2-left-involution-function carrier op)
    (putnam-1972-a2-true-function '(x y)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1972-a2-right-involution-function carrier op)
    (putnam-1972-a2-true-function '(x y)))))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-universal-part-p (carrier op)
  (implies
   (putnam-1972-a2-involution-structure-p carrier op)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1972-a2-commutative-function carrier op)
    (putnam-1972-a2-true-function '(x y)))))

;; The source asks only for existence of a nonassociative example. Keep the
;; carrier, operation, and nonassociativity witness under internal quantifiers.
(defun-sk putnam-1972-a2-nonassociative-p (carrier op)
  (exists (x y z)
    (and
     (apply$ carrier (list x))
     (apply$ carrier (list y))
     (apply$ carrier (list z))
     (not
      (equal
       (apply$ op
               (list x (apply$ op (list y z))))
       (apply$ op
               (list (apply$ op (list x y)) z)))))))

(defun putnam-1972-a2-nonassociative-structure-p (carrier op)
  (and
   (putnam-1972-a2-involution-structure-p carrier op)
   (putnam-1972-a2-nonassociative-p carrier op)))

(defun-sk putnam-1972-a2-nonassociative-example-exists-p ()
  (exists (carrier op)
    (putnam-1972-a2-nonassociative-structure-p carrier op)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1972-a2-statement (carrier op)
  (and
   (putnam-1972-a2-universal-part-p carrier op)
   (putnam-1972-a2-nonassociative-example-exists-p)))

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1972_a2: binary
% operations satisfying two involutive laws are commutative, while such an
% operation need not be associative. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1972_a2[S: TYPE]: THEORY
BEGIN
  operation: TYPE = [S, S -> S]

  satisfies_involutive_laws(op: operation): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: S):
      op(x, op(x, y)) = y
        AND op(op(y, x), x) = y

  commutative(op: operation): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: S):
      op(x, y) = op(y, x)

  all_such_operations_are_commutative: bool =
    FORALL (op: operation):
      satisfies_involutive_laws(op) IMPLIES commutative(op)

  real_set: TYPE = [real -> bool]
  real_operation: TYPE = [real, real -> real]

  closed_involutive_magma(
      carrier: real_set,
      op: real_operation): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: real):
      carrier(x) AND carrier(y) IMPLIES
        carrier(op(x, y))
          AND op(x, op(x, y)) = y
          AND op(op(y, x), x) = y

  associative_on(
      carrier: real_set,
      op: real_operation): bool =
    FORALL (x, y, z: real):
      carrier(x) AND carrier(y) AND carrier(z) IMPLIES
        op(x, op(y, z)) = op(op(x, y), z)

  a_nonassociative_example_exists: bool =
    EXISTS (carrier: real_set), (op: real_operation):
      closed_involutive_magma(carrier, op)
        AND NOT associative_on(carrier, op)

  putnam_1972_a2: bool =
    all_such_operations_are_commutative
      AND a_nonassociative_example_exists
END putnam_1972_a2

-- every natural number greater than one fails to divide 2 to its own power
-- minus one in the integers. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixl 6 _+z_ _-z_
infixl 7 _*z_
infixr 8 _^z_
infix 4 _∣_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set → Set
Not A =
  A → Bottom

data GreaterThanOne : Nat → Set where
  greater-than-one :
    {k : Nat} →
    GreaterThanOne (suc (suc k))

difference : Nat → Nat → Int
difference zero zero = pos zero
difference (suc m) zero = pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) = negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) = difference m n

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero = pos zero
negative (suc n) = negsuc n

negateInt : Int → Int
negateInt (pos n) = negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) = pos (suc n)

_+z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m +z pos n = pos (m + n)
pos m +z negsuc n = difference m (suc n)
negsuc m +z pos n = difference n (suc m)
negsuc m +z negsuc n = negsuc (suc (m + n))

_-z_ : Int → Int → Int
x -z y = x +z negateInt y

_*z_ : Int → Int → Int
pos m *z pos n = pos (m * n)
pos m *z negsuc n = negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *z pos n = negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *z negsuc n = pos (suc m * suc n)

_^z_ : Int → Nat → Int
base ^z zero = pos 1
base ^z (suc exponent) = base *z (base ^z exponent)

record _∣_ (divisor dividend : Int) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Int
    equation : divisor *z quotient ≡ dividend

putnam-1972-a5 : Set
putnam-1972-a5 =
  (n : Nat) →
  GreaterThanOne n →
  Not (pos n ∣ ((pos 2 ^z n) -z pos 1))

title: putnam_1972_a6
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1972_a6:
   vanishing lower moments and a normalized nth moment force an integrable
   real function on [0,1] to be large on a set of positive Lebesgue measure.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals ClassicalDescription.

Set Implicit Arguments.
#[local] Open Scope R_scope.

Definition set (A : Type) := A -> Prop.

Definition empty_set {A : Type} : set A :=
  fun _ => False.

Definition set_complement {A : Type} (E : set A) : set A :=
  fun x => ~ E x.

Definition countable_union {A : Type} (E : nat -> set A) : set A :=
  fun x => exists n : nat, E n x.

Definition same_set {A : Type} (E F : set A) : Prop :=
  forall x : A, E x <-> F x.

Definition subset {A : Type} (E F : set A) : Prop :=
  forall x : A, E x -> F x.

Definition disjoint_sets {A : Type} (E F : set A) : Prop :=
  forall x : A, ~ (E x /\ F x).

Definition pairwise_disjoint {A : Type} (E : nat -> set A) : Prop :=
  forall i j : nat, i <> j -> disjoint_sets (E i) (E j).

Definition sigma_class {A : Type} (C : set (set A)) : Prop :=
  C empty_set /\
  (forall E : set A, C E -> C (set_complement E)) /\
  (forall E : nat -> set A,
      (forall n : nat, C (E n)) ->
      C (countable_union E)).

Definition open_real_set (U : set R) : Prop :=
  forall x : R,
    U x ->
    exists epsilon : R,
      0 < epsilon /\
      forall y : R, Rabs (y - x) < epsilon -> U y.

Definition borel_set (E : set R) : Prop :=
  forall C : set (set R),
    sigma_class C ->
    (forall U : set R, open_real_set U -> C U) ->
    C E.

Inductive extended_nonnegative : Type :=
| ennreal_finite :
    forall value : R, 0 <= value -> extended_nonnegative
| ennreal_infinity : extended_nonnegative.

Arguments ennreal_finite value nonnegative : clear implicits.

Definition ennreal_zero : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_finite 0 (Rle_refl 0).

Definition ennreal_le
    (x y : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  match x, y with
  | ennreal_finite a _, ennreal_finite b _ => a <= b
  | ennreal_finite _ _, ennreal_infinity => True
  | ennreal_infinity, ennreal_finite _ _ => False
  | ennreal_infinity, ennreal_infinity => True
  end.

Definition ennreal_positive (x : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  match x with
  | ennreal_finite value _ => 0 < value
  | ennreal_infinity => True
  end.

Definition ennreal_add
    (x y : extended_nonnegative) : extended_nonnegative :=
  match x, y with
  | ennreal_finite a a_nonnegative,
    ennreal_finite b b_nonnegative =>
      ennreal_finite (a + b)
        (Rplus_le_le_0_compat a b a_nonnegative b_nonnegative)
  | _, _ => ennreal_infinity
  end.

Definition ennreal_mul
    (x y : extended_nonnegative) : extended_nonnegative :=
  match x, y with
  | ennreal_finite a a_nonnegative,
    ennreal_finite b b_nonnegative =>
      ennreal_finite (a * b)
        (Rmult_le_pos a b a_nonnegative b_nonnegative)
  | ennreal_finite a _, ennreal_infinity
  | ennreal_infinity, ennreal_finite a _ =>
      if Req_EM_T a 0 then ennreal_zero else ennreal_infinity
  | ennreal_infinity, ennreal_infinity => ennreal_infinity
  end.

Fixpoint ennreal_partial_sum
    (u : nat -> extended_nonnegative) (n : nat) : extended_nonnegative :=
  match n with
  | O => ennreal_zero
  | S k => ennreal_add (ennreal_partial_sum u k) (u k)
  end.

Definition ennreal_supremum
    (values : extended_nonnegative -> Prop)
    (bound : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  (forall value : extended_nonnegative,
      values value -> ennreal_le value bound) /\
  (forall upper : extended_nonnegative,
      (forall value : extended_nonnegative,
          values value -> ennreal_le value upper) ->
      ennreal_le bound upper).

Definition ennreal_series_sum
    (u : nat -> extended_nonnegative)
    (sum : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  ennreal_supremum
    (fun value =>
      exists n : nat, value = ennreal_partial_sum u n)
    sum.

Record nonnegative_real : Type := {
  nnreal_value : R;
  nnreal_nonnegative : 0 <= nnreal_value
}.

Definition ennreal_of_nonnegative
    (x : nonnegative_real) : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_finite (nnreal_value x) (nnreal_nonnegative x).

Definition ennreal_represents
    (x : extended_nonnegative) (value : R) : Prop :=
  exists nonnegative : 0 <= value,
    x = ennreal_finite value nonnegative.

Definition ennreal_finite_value (x : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  exists value : R, ennreal_represents x value.

Record measure_space (A : Type) := {
  measurable : set A -> Prop;
  measurable_empty : measurable empty_set;
  measurable_complement :
    forall E : set A,
      measurable E ->
      measurable (set_complement E);
  measurable_countable_union :
    forall E : nat -> set A,
      (forall n : nat, measurable (E n)) ->
      measurable (countable_union E);
  measure : set A -> extended_nonnegative;
  measure_extensional :
    forall E F : set A,
      same_set E F ->
      measure E = measure F;
  measure_empty : measure empty_set = ennreal_zero;
  measure_countable_additive :
    forall E : nat -> set A,
      (forall n : nat, measurable (E n)) ->
      pairwise_disjoint E ->
      ennreal_series_sum
        (fun n => measure (E n))
        (measure (countable_union E))
}.

Definition is_borel_measure (mu : measure_space R) : Prop :=
  forall E : set R, measurable mu E <-> borel_set E.

Definition half_open_interval (a b : R) : set R :=
  fun x => a <= x < b.

Definition is_lebesgue_measure (mu : measure_space R) : Prop :=
  is_borel_measure mu /\
  forall a b : R,
    a <= b ->
    ennreal_represents
      (measure mu (half_open_interval a b)) (b - a).

Definition measurable_real_function {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (f : A -> R) : Prop :=
  forall bound : R,
    measurable mu (fun x => f x < bound).

Definition finite_partition {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A)
    (n : nat) (cells : nat -> set A) : Prop :=
  (0 < n)%nat /\
  (forall i : nat, (i < n)%nat -> measurable mu (cells i)) /\
  (forall i j : nat,
      (i < n)%nat ->
      (j < n)%nat ->
      i <> j ->
      disjoint_sets (cells i) (cells j)) /\
  (forall x : A,
      exists i : nat, (i < n)%nat /\ cells i x).

Definition simple_integral_below {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A)
    (f : A -> extended_nonnegative)
    (value : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  exists (n : nat)
         (coefficients : nat -> nonnegative_real)
         (cells : nat -> set A),
    finite_partition mu n cells /\
    (forall (x : A) (i : nat),
      (i < n)%nat ->
      cells i x ->
      ennreal_le (ennreal_of_nonnegative (coefficients i)) (f x)) /\
    value =
      ennreal_partial_sum
        (fun i =>
          ennreal_mul
            (ennreal_of_nonnegative (coefficients i))
            (measure mu (cells i)))
        n.

Definition lintegral_has_value {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A)
    (f : A -> extended_nonnegative)
    (value : extended_nonnegative) : Prop :=
  ennreal_supremum (simple_integral_below mu f) value.

Definition real_indicator {A : Type}
    (E : set A) (f : A -> R) (x : A) : R :=
  if excluded_middle_informative (E x) then f x else 0.

Definition absolute_ennreal (x : R) : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_finite (Rabs x) (Rabs_pos x).

Definition positive_part (x : R) : R :=
  Rmax x 0.

Definition negative_part (x : R) : R :=
  Rmax (- x) 0.

Definition positive_ennreal (x : R) : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_finite (positive_part x) (Rmax_r x 0).

Definition negative_ennreal (x : R) : extended_nonnegative :=
  ennreal_finite (negative_part x) (Rmax_r (- x) 0).

Definition integrable {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (f : A -> R) : Prop :=
  measurable_real_function mu f /\
  exists value : extended_nonnegative,
    lintegral_has_value mu (fun x => absolute_ennreal (f x)) value /\
    ennreal_finite_value value.

Definition integrable_on {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (E : set A) (f : A -> R) : Prop :=
  integrable mu (real_indicator E f).

Definition lebesgue_integral_has_value {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (f : A -> R) (value : R) : Prop :=
  measurable_real_function mu f /\
  exists (positive_integral negative_integral : extended_nonnegative)
         (positive_value negative_value : R),
    lintegral_has_value mu
      (fun x => positive_ennreal (f x)) positive_integral /\
    lintegral_has_value mu
      (fun x => negative_ennreal (f x)) negative_integral /\
    ennreal_represents positive_integral positive_value /\
    ennreal_represents negative_integral negative_value /\
    value = positive_value - negative_value.

Definition set_integral_has_value {A : Type}
    (mu : measure_space A) (E : set A)
    (f : A -> R) (value : R) : Prop :=
  lebesgue_integral_has_value mu (real_indicator E f) value.

Definition closed_unit_interval : set R :=
  fun x => 0 <= x <= 1.

Theorem putnam_1972_a6
    (mu : measure_space R)
    (hmu : is_lebesgue_measure mu)
    (f : R -> R)
    (n : nat)
    (hfintegrable : integrable_on mu closed_unit_interval f)
    (hfint :
      forall i : nat,
        (i < n)%nat ->
        set_integral_has_value mu closed_unit_interval
          (fun x : R => x ^ i * f x) 0)
    (hfintlast :
      set_integral_has_value mu closed_unit_interval
        (fun x : R => x ^ n * f x) 1) :
  exists S : set R,
    subset S closed_unit_interval /\
    measurable mu S /\
    ennreal_positive (measure mu S) /\
    forall x : R,
      S x ->
      Rabs (f x) >= 2 ^ n * (INR n + 1).
Admitted.

title: putnam_1972_a6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1972_a6:
  a normalized highest moment and vanishing lower moments force an integrable
  real function on [0,1] to exceed a specified level on a set of positive
  Lebesgue measure. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let interval01 = {x:real | &0 <= x /\ x <= &1} in
   let cover_bound =
     \(s:real->bool) (B:real).
       &0 <= B /\
       ?a b:num->real.
         (!k. a k <= b k) /\
         (!x. x IN s ==> ?k. a k < x /\ x < b k) /\
         (!N. sum (0..N) (\k. b k - a k) <= B) in
   let outer_measure =
     \(s:real->bool). inf {B:real | cover_bound s B} in
   let measurable01 =
     \(s:real->bool).
       s SUBSET interval01 /\
       outer_measure s + outer_measure (interval01 DIFF s) = &1 in
   let nonnegative_simple =
     \(h:real->real).
       FINITE (IMAGE h interval01) /\
       (!x. x IN interval01 ==> &0 <= h x) /\
       (!c. c IN IMAGE h interval01
            ==> measurable01 {x | x IN interval01 /\ h x = c}) in
   let simple_integral =
     \(h:real->real).
       sum (IMAGE h interval01)
         (\c. c * outer_measure {x | x IN interval01 /\ h x = c}) in
   let lower_integrals =
     \(g:real->real).
       {z:real |
          ?h:real->real.
            nonnegative_simple h /\
            (!x. x IN interval01 ==> h x <= g x) /\
            z = simple_integral h} in
   let finite_nonnegative_integral =
     \(g:real->real).
       ?B:real. !z. z IN lower_integrals g ==> z <= B in
   let nonnegative_integral =
     \(g:real->real). sup (lower_integrals g) in
   let positive_part =
     \(g:real->real) x. if &0 <= g x then g x else &0 in
   let negative_part =
     \(g:real->real) x. if g x <= &0 then --(g x) else &0 in
   let measurable_function =
     \(g:real->real).
       !a:real. measurable01 {x | x IN interval01 /\ g x < a} in
   let lebesgue_integrable =
     \(g:real->real).
       measurable_function g /\
       finite_nonnegative_integral (positive_part g) /\
       finite_nonnegative_integral (negative_part g) in
   let lebesgue_integral =
     \(g:real->real).
       nonnegative_integral (positive_part g) -
       nonnegative_integral (negative_part g) in
   !f:real->real n:num.
     lebesgue_integrable f /\
     (!i:num.
        i < n
        ==> lebesgue_integral (\x. x pow i * f x) = &0) /\
     lebesgue_integral (\x. x pow n * f x) = &1
     ==> ?s:real->bool.
           s SUBSET interval01 /\
           measurable01 s /\
           &0 < outer_measure s /\
           (!x. x IN s
                ==> (&2:real) pow n * &(n + 1) <= abs(f x))`;;

title: putnam_1972_a6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1972_a6:
;; vanishing lower moments and a normalized nth moment force an integrable
;; real function on [0,1] to be at least 2^n(n+1) in absolute value on a set of
;; positive Lebesgue measure. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The universal source statement is encoded by the absence of its
;; counterexamples. A code (POINTS, VALUES) denotes the rational step function
;; with value VALUES[j] on the interval from POINTS[j] to POINTS[j+1].
;; The list can have arbitrary finite length, and the moment formula below is
;; the exact integral of that step function, not a finite sampling.
;;
;; This restriction to rational step-function counterexamples is
;; bidirectionally exact. Any encoded counterexample is directly an integrable
;; real source counterexample. Conversely, suppose a source counterexample f
;; exists and put M = 2^n(n+1). Then |f| < M almost everywhere. On the
;; finite-dimensional space of real polynomials of degree at most n, the
;; moment functional p |-> integral(p*f) is therefore strictly bounded by
;; M times the L1 norm. Compactness of the polynomial unit sphere gives a
;; uniform bound c < M. L1-L-infinity duality supplies a representative with
;; essential bound c. Rational step functions are dense in L1, and corrections
;; on n+1 small rational intervals have an invertible rational moment matrix.
;; Thus one can approximate the representative and correct all n+1 moments
;; exactly while retaining a strict bound below M. This produces an encoded
;; counterexample. Hence the predicate below has exactly the source theorem's
;; counterexamples and does not replace an arbitrary function by samples.

(defun putnam-1972-a6-rational-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and (rationalp (car values))
           (putnam-1972-a6-rational-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-1972-a6-strictly-increasing-p (points)
  (if (consp (cdr points))
      (and (< (car points) (cadr points))
           (putnam-1972-a6-strictly-increasing-p (cdr points)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1972-a6-last (values)
  (if (consp (cdr values))
      (putnam-1972-a6-last (cdr values))
    (car values)))

(defun putnam-1972-a6-step-code-p (points values)
  (and
   (true-listp points)
   (true-listp values)
   (consp values)
   (equal (len points) (+ 1 (len values)))
   (putnam-1972-a6-rational-list-p points)
   (putnam-1972-a6-rational-list-p values)
   (equal (car points) 0)
   (equal (putnam-1972-a6-last points) 1)
   (putnam-1972-a6-strictly-increasing-p points)))

;; Integral of x^POWER times the coded step function over [0,1].
(defun putnam-1972-a6-moment (power points values)
  (if (consp values)
      (+
       (*
        (car values)
        (/
         (- (expt (cadr points) (+ power 1))
            (expt (car points) (+ power 1)))
         (+ power 1)))
       (putnam-1972-a6-moment
        power (cdr points) (cdr values)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1972-a6-lower-moments-zero-p
    (remaining points values)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (and
     (equal
      (putnam-1972-a6-moment
       (- remaining 1) points values)
      0)
     (putnam-1972-a6-lower-moments-zero-p
      (- remaining 1) points values))))

(defun putnam-1972-a6-values-below-p (values bound)
  (if (consp values)
      (and (< (abs (car values)) bound)
           (putnam-1972-a6-values-below-p (cdr values) bound))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-1972-a6-threshold (n)
  (* (expt 2 n) (+ n 1)))

(defun putnam-1972-a6-step-counterexample-p
    (n points values)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (putnam-1972-a6-step-code-p points values)
   (putnam-1972-a6-lower-moments-zero-p n points values)
   (equal (putnam-1972-a6-moment n points values) 1)
   (putnam-1972-a6-values-below-p
    values
    (putnam-1972-a6-threshold n))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1972-a6-statement
    (n points values)
  (not
   (putnam-1972-a6-step-counterexample-p
    n points values)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1972_a6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1972_a6:
-- an integrable real function with vanishing lower moments and normalized
-- nth moment is large on a measurable set of positive measure. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1972A6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A = A -> Bottom

Not1 : Set1 -> Set1
Not1 A = A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y = Not (x == y)

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record Exists1 (A : Set) (P : A -> Set1) : Set1 where
  constructor witness1
  field
    value1    : A
    property1 : P value1

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data _<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<   : {n : Nat} -> zero <N suc n
  suc<suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <N n -> suc m <N suc n

Predicate : Set -> Set1
Predicate A = A -> Set

emptySet :
  {A : Set} ->
  Predicate A
emptySet _ =
  Bottom

wholeSet :
  {A : Set} ->
  Predicate A
wholeSet _ =
  Top

complement :
  {A : Set} ->
  Predicate A ->
  Predicate A
complement S x =
  Not (S x)

countableUnion :
  {A : Set} ->
  (Nat -> Predicate A) ->
  Predicate A
countableUnion sets x =
  Exists Nat (\ n -> sets n x)

Subset :
  {A : Set} ->
  Predicate A ->
  Predicate A ->
  Set
Subset {A} S T =
  (x : A) -> S x -> T x

PairwiseDisjoint :
  {A : Set} ->
  (Nat -> Predicate A) ->
  Set
PairwiseDisjoint {A} sets =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  i != j ->
  (x : A) ->
  sets i x ->
  sets j x ->
  Bottom

record CompleteOrderedField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : Predicate R) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SequentialLimit {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
sumFirst reals terms zero =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals terms (suc n) =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals terms n)
    (terms n)

record StandardRealAnalysis (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    algebra : CompleteOrderedField R
    squareRoot : R -> R
    positivePart : R -> R

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) x ->
      square algebra (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra x (zeroR algebra) ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR algebra
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) y ->
      square algebra y == x ->
      squareRoot x == y

    positive-part-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) (positivePart x)
    positive-part-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) x ->
      positivePart x == x
    positive-part-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra x (zeroR algebra) ->
      positivePart x == zeroR algebra

open StandardRealAnalysis

HalfOpen :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Predicate R
HalfOpen reals lower upper x =
  lessOrEqual reals lower x
  and
  StrictLess reals x upper

ClosedInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Predicate R
ClosedInterval reals lower upper x =
  lessOrEqual reals lower x
  and
  lessOrEqual reals x upper

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

absoluteValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  R ->
  R
absoluteValue analysis x =
  add (algebra analysis)
    (positivePart analysis x)
    (positivePart analysis (negate (algebra analysis) x))

data BorelCode
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) : Set where
  emptyB          : BorelCode reals
  openRayB        : R -> BorelCode reals
  complementB     : BorelCode reals -> BorelCode reals
  countableUnionB : (Nat -> BorelCode reals) -> BorelCode reals

decodeBorel :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  BorelCode reals ->
  Predicate R
decodeBorel reals emptyB =
  emptySet
decodeBorel reals (openRayB endpoint) x =
  StrictLess reals endpoint x
decodeBorel reals (complementB code) =
  complement (decodeBorel reals code)
decodeBorel reals (countableUnionB codes) =
  countableUnion (\ n -> decodeBorel reals (codes n))

LocallyNull :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  (R -> R -> Predicate R -> R) ->
  Predicate R ->
  Set
LocallyNull reals intervalMeasure N =
  (lower upper : _) ->
  lessOrEqual reals lower upper ->
  intervalMeasure lower upper N == zeroR reals

record CompletedBorelWitness
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (intervalMeasure : R -> R -> Predicate R -> R)
  (S : Predicate R) : Set where
  field
    representative : BorelCode reals
    nullEnvelope : BorelCode reals
    null-envelope-locally-null :
      LocallyNull reals intervalMeasure
        (decodeBorel reals nullEnvelope)
    agrees-off-null :
      (x : R) ->
      Not (decodeBorel reals nullEnvelope x) ->
      Iff (S x) (decodeBorel reals representative x)

open CompletedBorelWitness

record BorelIntervalMeasureLaws
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R)
  (intervalMeasure : R -> R -> Predicate R -> R) : Set1 where
  field
    borel-measure-congruent :
      (lower upper : R) ->
      (S T : Predicate R) ->
      ((x : R) -> Iff (S x) (T x)) ->
      intervalMeasure lower upper S ==
      intervalMeasure lower upper T
    borel-measure-empty :
      (lower upper : R) ->
      intervalMeasure lower upper emptySet == zeroR reals
    borel-measure-nonnegative :
      (lower upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals lower upper ->
      (code : BorelCode reals) ->
      lessOrEqual reals
        (zeroR reals)
        (intervalMeasure lower upper (decodeBorel reals code))
    borel-measure-restricted :
      (lower upper : R) ->
      (S : Predicate R) ->
      intervalMeasure lower upper S ==
      intervalMeasure lower upper
        (\ x -> S x and HalfOpen reals lower upper x)
    borel-measure-half-open :
      (lower upper start endpoint : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals lower start ->
      lessOrEqual reals start endpoint ->
      lessOrEqual reals endpoint upper ->
      intervalMeasure lower upper
        (HalfOpen reals start endpoint) ==
      subtract reals endpoint start
    borel-measure-countable-additivity :
      (lower upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals lower upper ->
      (codes : Nat -> BorelCode reals) ->
      PairwiseDisjoint
        (\ n -> decodeBorel reals (codes n)) ->
      SequentialLimit reals
        (\ count ->
          sumFirst reals
            (\ n ->
              intervalMeasure lower upper
                (decodeBorel reals (codes n)))
            count)
        (intervalMeasure lower upper
          (decodeBorel reals (countableUnionB codes)))

record RestrictedLebesgueMeasure
  {R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R) : Set1 where
  private
    reals = algebra analysis

  field
    intervalMeasure : R -> R -> Predicate R -> R
    measurable : Predicate R -> Set
    measureFromZero : R -> Predicate R -> R

    measure-from-zero :
      (upper : R) ->
      (S : Predicate R) ->
      measureFromZero upper S ==
      intervalMeasure (zeroR reals) upper S
    measurable-exact :
      (S : Predicate R) ->
      Iff
        (measurable S)
        (CompletedBorelWitness reals intervalMeasure S)
    borel-measure-laws :
      BorelIntervalMeasureLaws reals intervalMeasure
    borel-measure-unique :
      (candidate : R -> R -> Predicate R -> R) ->
      BorelIntervalMeasureLaws reals candidate ->
      (lower upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals lower upper ->
      (code : BorelCode reals) ->
      candidate lower upper (decodeBorel reals code) ==
      intervalMeasure lower upper (decodeBorel reals code)
    interval-measure-completion :
      (lower upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals lower upper ->
      (S : Predicate R) ->
      (completion :
        CompletedBorelWitness reals intervalMeasure S) ->
      intervalMeasure lower upper S ==
      intervalMeasure lower upper
        (decodeBorel reals (representative completion))

    measurable-empty :
      measurable emptySet
    measurable-complement :
      (S : Predicate R) ->
      measurable S ->
      measurable (complement S)
    measurable-countable-union :
      (sets : Nat -> Predicate R) ->
      ((n : Nat) -> measurable (sets n)) ->
      measurable (countableUnion sets)
    measurable-congruent :
      (S T : Predicate R) ->
      ((x : R) -> Iff (S x) (T x)) ->
      measurable S ->
      measurable T
    measurable-half-open :
      (lower upper : R) ->
      measurable (HalfOpen reals lower upper)
    measurable-open-ray :
      (endpoint : R) ->
      measurable (\ x -> StrictLess reals endpoint x)
    complete-on-null-sets :
      (upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) upper ->
      (N S : Predicate R) ->
      measurable N ->
      measureFromZero upper N == zeroR reals ->
      Subset S N ->
      measurable
        (\ x ->
          S x
          and
          HalfOpen reals (zeroR reals) upper x)

    measure-congruent :
      (upper : R) ->
      (S T : Predicate R) ->
      ((x : R) -> Iff (S x) (T x)) ->
      measureFromZero upper S == measureFromZero upper T
    measure-empty :
      (upper : R) ->
      measureFromZero upper emptySet == zeroR reals
    measure-nonnegative :
      (upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) upper ->
      (S : Predicate R) ->
      measurable S ->
      lessOrEqual reals
        (zeroR reals)
        (measureFromZero upper S)
    measure-restricted :
      (upper : R) ->
      (S : Predicate R) ->
      measureFromZero upper S ==
      measureFromZero upper
        (\ x -> S x and HalfOpen reals (zeroR reals) upper x)
    measure-half-open :
      (upper lower endpoint : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) lower ->
      lessOrEqual reals lower endpoint ->
      lessOrEqual reals endpoint upper ->
      measureFromZero upper (HalfOpen reals lower endpoint) ==
      subtract reals endpoint lower
    measure-countable-additivity :
      (upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) upper ->
      (sets : Nat -> Predicate R) ->
      ((n : Nat) -> measurable (sets n)) ->
      PairwiseDisjoint sets ->
      SequentialLimit reals
        (\ count ->
          sumFirst reals
            (\ n -> measureFromZero upper (sets n))
            count)
        (measureFromZero upper (countableUnion sets))

open RestrictedLebesgueMeasure

record NonnegativeSimpleBelow
  {R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (lebesgue : RestrictedLebesgueMeasure analysis)
  (upper : R)
  (function : R -> R) : Set1 where
  private
    reals = algebra analysis

  field
    cutoff : Nat
    values : Nat -> R
    pieces : Nat -> Predicate R

    values-nonnegative :
      (i : Nat) ->
      i <=N cutoff ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (values i)
    pieces-measurable :
      (i : Nat) ->
      i <=N cutoff ->
      measurable lebesgue (pieces i)
    pieces-disjoint :
      (i j : Nat) ->
      i <=N cutoff ->
      j <=N cutoff ->
      i != j ->
      (x : R) ->
      pieces i x ->
      pieces j x ->
      Bottom
    pieces-inside-interval :
      (i : Nat) ->
      i <=N cutoff ->
      Subset
        (pieces i)
        (HalfOpen reals (zeroR reals) upper)
    below-function :
      (i : Nat) ->
      i <=N cutoff ->
      (x : R) ->
      pieces i x ->
      lessOrEqual reals (values i) (function x)

open NonnegativeSimpleBelow

simpleIntegral :
  {R : Set} ->
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R) ->
  (lebesgue : RestrictedLebesgueMeasure analysis) ->
  {upper : R} ->
  {function : R -> R} ->
  NonnegativeSimpleBelow analysis lebesgue upper function ->
  R
simpleIntegral analysis lebesgue {upper = upper} simple =
  sumFirst (algebra analysis)
    (\ i ->
      multiply (algebra analysis)
        (values simple i)
        (measureFromZero lebesgue
          upper
          (pieces simple i)))
    (suc (cutoff simple))

data ExtendedNonnegative
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) : Set where
  finiteE   : R -> ExtendedNonnegative reals
  infinityE : ExtendedNonnegative reals

NonnegativeExtended :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  ExtendedNonnegative reals ->
  Set
NonnegativeExtended reals (finiteE value) =
  lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) value
NonnegativeExtended reals infinityE =
  Top

LessOrEqualE :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  ExtendedNonnegative reals ->
  ExtendedNonnegative reals ->
  Set
LessOrEqualE reals (finiteE x) (finiteE y) =
  lessOrEqual reals x y
LessOrEqualE reals (finiteE x) infinityE =
  Top
LessOrEqualE reals infinityE (finiteE y) =
  Bottom
LessOrEqualE reals infinityE infinityE =
  Top

RealBelowE :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedField R) ->
  R ->
  ExtendedNonnegative reals ->
  Set
RealBelowE reals x (finiteE y) =
  lessOrEqual reals x y
RealBelowE reals x infinityE =
  Top

record LowerLebesgueIntegralValue
  {R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (lebesgue : RestrictedLebesgueMeasure analysis)
  (upper : R)
  (function : R -> R)
  (value : ExtendedNonnegative (algebra analysis)) : Set1 where
  private
    reals = algebra analysis

  field
    value-nonnegative :
      NonnegativeExtended reals value
    simple-integrals-below :
      (simple :
        NonnegativeSimpleBelow
          analysis lebesgue upper function) ->
      RealBelowE reals
        (simpleIntegral analysis lebesgue simple)
        value
    least-upper-bound :
      (bound : ExtendedNonnegative reals) ->
      ((simple :
          NonnegativeSimpleBelow
            analysis lebesgue upper function) ->
        RealBelowE reals
          (simpleIntegral analysis lebesgue simple)
          bound) ->
      LessOrEqualE reals value bound

positivePartFunction :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
positivePartFunction analysis function x =
  positivePart analysis (function x)

negativePartFunction :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
negativePartFunction analysis function x =
  positivePart analysis
    (negate (algebra analysis) (function x))

MeasurableOnFromZero :
  {R : Set} ->
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R) ->
  RestrictedLebesgueMeasure analysis ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
MeasurableOnFromZero analysis lebesgue upper function =
  (threshold : _) ->
  measurable lebesgue
    (\ x ->
      HalfOpen
        (algebra analysis)
        (zeroR (algebra analysis))
        upper
        x
      and
      StrictLess
        (algebra analysis)
        threshold
        (function x))

record FiniteLowerIntegralValue
  {R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (lowerIntegral :
    (R -> R) ->
    R ->
    ExtendedNonnegative (algebra analysis))
  (upper : R)
  (function : R -> R)
  (value : R) : Set where
  private
    reals = algebra analysis

  field
    finite-value-nonnegative :
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) value
    finite-value-equation :
      lowerIntegral function upper == finiteE value

record IntegrableIntervalValue
  {R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (lebesgue : RestrictedLebesgueMeasure analysis)
  (lowerIntegral :
    (R -> R) ->
    R ->
    ExtendedNonnegative (algebra analysis))
  (upper : R)
  (function : R -> R)
  (value : R) : Set1 where
  private
    reals = algebra analysis

  field
    measurable-on-interval :
      MeasurableOnFromZero analysis lebesgue upper function
    positive-integral negative-integral : R
    positive-part-finite :
      FiniteLowerIntegralValue
        analysis lowerIntegral upper
        (positivePartFunction analysis function)
        positive-integral
    negative-part-finite :
      FiniteLowerIntegralValue
        analysis lowerIntegral upper
        (negativePartFunction analysis function)
        negative-integral
    signed-value :
      value ==
      subtract reals positive-integral negative-integral

data TotalizedLebesgueIntegralValue
  {R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (lebesgue : RestrictedLebesgueMeasure analysis)
  (lowerIntegral :
    (R -> R) ->
    R ->
    ExtendedNonnegative (algebra analysis))
  (upper : R)
  (function : R -> R)
  (value : R) : Set1 where
  integrable-value :
    IntegrableIntervalValue
      analysis lebesgue lowerIntegral upper function value ->
    TotalizedLebesgueIntegralValue
      analysis lebesgue lowerIntegral upper function value
  nonintegrable-value :
    Not1
      (Exists1 R
        (\ candidate ->
          IntegrableIntervalValue
            analysis lebesgue lowerIntegral
            upper function candidate)) ->
    value == zeroR (algebra analysis) ->
    TotalizedLebesgueIntegralValue
      analysis lebesgue lowerIntegral upper function value

-- In the standard real model, these fields are the completed-Borel Lebesgue
-- lower integral and its usual real-valued totalization, which is zero when
-- the function is not integrable.
record LebesgueIntervalIntegration
  {R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (lebesgue : RestrictedLebesgueMeasure analysis) : Set1 where
  private
    reals = algebra analysis

  field
    lowerIntegral :
      (R -> R) ->
      R ->
      ExtendedNonnegative reals
    integralFromZero : (R -> R) -> R -> R
    lower-integral-definition :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      ((x : R) ->
        lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (function x)) ->
      (upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) upper ->
      LowerLebesgueIntegralValue
        analysis lebesgue upper function
        (lowerIntegral function upper)
    lower-integral-unique :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      ((x : R) ->
        lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (function x)) ->
      (upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) upper ->
      (value : ExtendedNonnegative reals) ->
      LowerLebesgueIntegralValue
        analysis lebesgue upper function value ->
      lowerIntegral function upper == value
    totalized-integral-definition :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      (upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) upper ->
      TotalizedLebesgueIntegralValue
        analysis lebesgue lowerIntegral upper function
        (integralFromZero function upper)
    totalized-integral-unique :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      (upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) upper ->
      (value : R) ->
      TotalizedLebesgueIntegralValue
        analysis lebesgue lowerIntegral upper function value ->
      integralFromZero function upper == value

open LebesgueIntervalIntegration

module Putnam1972A6Statement
  {R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (lebesgue : RestrictedLebesgueMeasure analysis)
  (integration : LebesgueIntervalIntegration analysis lebesgue) where

  reals : CompleteOrderedField R
  reals =
    algebra analysis

  unitInterval : Predicate R
  unitInterval =
    ClosedInterval reals (zeroR reals) (oneR reals)

  IntegrableOnUnitInterval : (R -> R) -> Set1
  IntegrableOnUnitInterval function =
    Exists1 R
      (\ value ->
        IntegrableIntervalValue
          analysis
          lebesgue
          (lowerIntegral integration)
          (oneR reals)
          function
          value)

  momentIntegrand :
    (R -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    R ->
    R
  momentIntegrand f i x =
    multiply reals
      (naturalPower reals x i)
      (f x)

  lowerMomentsVanish :
    (R -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    Set
  lowerMomentsVanish f n =
    (i : Nat) ->
    i <N n ->
    integralFromZero integration
      (momentIntegrand f i)
      (oneR reals)
    ==
    zeroR reals

  threshold : Nat -> R
  threshold n =
    multiply reals
      (naturalPower reals
        (fromNat reals (suc (suc zero)))
        n)
      (fromNat reals (suc n))

  record LargeValueSet
    (f : R -> R)
    (n : Nat) : Set1 where
    field
      carrier : Predicate R
      inside-unit-interval :
        Subset carrier unitInterval
      carrier-measurable :
        measurable lebesgue carrier
      carrier-positive-measure :
        StrictLess reals
          (zeroR reals)
          (measureFromZero lebesgue (oneR reals) carrier)
      lower-bound-on-carrier :
        (x : R) ->
        carrier x ->
        lessOrEqual reals
          (threshold n)
          (absoluteValue analysis (f x))

  proposition : Set1
  proposition =
    (f : R -> R) ->
    (n : Nat) ->
    IntegrableOnUnitInterval f ->
    lowerMomentsVanish f n ->
    integralFromZero integration
      (momentIntegrand f n)
      (oneR reals)
    ==
    oneR reals ->
    LargeValueSet f n

putnam-1972-a6 : Set1
putnam-1972-a6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R) ->
  (lebesgue : RestrictedLebesgueMeasure analysis) ->
  (integration : LebesgueIntervalIntegration analysis lebesgue) ->
  Putnam1972A6Statement.proposition
    analysis lebesgue integration

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1972_a6:
  a lower bound on an integrable function over the unit interval from its
  vanishing lower moments and normalized nth moment. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory extrealTheory;
open sigma_algebraTheory measureTheory borelTheory;
open lebesgueTheory lebesgue_measureTheory;

val putnam_1972_a6 =
  ``!(f : real -> real) (n : num).
      let unit_interval =
        restrict_space lebesgue (interval [0, 1])
      in
        integrable unit_interval (Normal o f) /\
        (!i. i < n ==>
             integral unit_interval
               (\x. Normal (x pow i * f x)) = 0) /\
        integral unit_interval
          (\x. Normal (x pow n * f x)) = 1
        ==>
        ?S : real set.
          S SUBSET interval [0, 1] /\
          S IN measurable_sets lebesgue /\
          0 < measure lebesgue S /\
          !x. x IN S ==>
              (&2 : real) pow n * &(n + 1) <= abs (f x)``;

title: putnam_1972_a6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1972_a6:
% a lower bound attained on a positive-measure set by an integrable function
% with prescribed vanishing moments on the unit interval. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1972_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_set: TYPE = [real -> bool]
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  real_set_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real_set]

  finite_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      finite_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(values: real_sequence, limit: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(values(count) - limit) < epsilon_value

  interval_length(left_endpoint, right_endpoint: real): real =
    IF left_endpoint < right_endpoint THEN
      right_endpoint - left_endpoint
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  closed_interval(left_endpoint, right_endpoint: real): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      left_endpoint <= x AND x <= right_endpoint

  open_interval_cover(
      covered: real_set,
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      covered(x) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (index: nat):
          left_endpoints(index) < x
            AND x < right_endpoints(index)

  cover_partial_length(
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence,
      count: nat): real =
    finite_sum(
      LAMBDA (index: nat):
        interval_length(
          left_endpoints(index),
          right_endpoints(index)),
      count)

  cover_has_total_length(
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence,
      total: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat):
        cover_partial_length(
          left_endpoints, right_endpoints, count),
      total)

  has_outer_measure(covered: real_set, measure_value: real): bool =
    measure_value >= 0
      AND (FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS
            (left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence),
            (total: real):
          open_interval_cover(
            covered, left_endpoints, right_endpoints)
            AND cover_has_total_length(
              left_endpoints, right_endpoints, total)
            AND total < measure_value + epsilon_value)
      AND (FORALL
          (left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence),
          (total: real):
        (open_interval_cover(
            covered, left_endpoints, right_endpoints)
          AND cover_has_total_length(
            left_endpoints, right_endpoints, total))
        IMPLIES measure_value <= total)

  set_intersection(left_set, right_set: real_set): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      left_set(x) AND right_set(x)

  set_difference(left_set, right_set: real_set): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      left_set(x) AND NOT right_set(x)

  set_subset(left_set, right_set: real_set): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      left_set(x) IMPLIES right_set(x)

  lebesgue_measurable(measured_set: real_set): bool =
    FORALL
        (test_set: real_set),
        (test_measure, inside_measure, outside_measure: real):
      (has_outer_measure(test_set, test_measure)
        AND has_outer_measure(
          set_intersection(test_set, measured_set),
          inside_measure)
        AND has_outer_measure(
          set_difference(test_set, measured_set),
          outside_measure))
      IMPLIES
        test_measure = inside_measure + outside_measure

  lebesgue_measure(measured_set: real_set): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (measure_value: real):
        has_outer_measure(measured_set, measure_value))

  sublevel_set_on(
      domain: real_set,
      function_value: real_function,
      bound: real): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      domain(x) AND function_value(x) <= bound

  measurable_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set): bool =
    FORALL (bound: real):
      lebesgue_measurable(
        sublevel_set_on(domain, function_value, bound))

  pairwise_disjoint_below(
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (left_index, right_index: nat):
      left_index < count
        AND right_index < count
        AND left_index /= right_index
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (x: real):
          NOT (pieces(left_index)(x)
            AND pieces(right_index)(x))

  simple_value(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat,
      x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      simple_value(coefficients, pieces, count - 1, x)
        + IF pieces(count - 1)(x)
            THEN coefficients(count - 1)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  simple_integral(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      simple_integral(coefficients, pieces, count - 1)
        + coefficients(count - 1)
            * lebesgue_measure(pieces(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  nonnegative_simple_minorant_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set,
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    pairwise_disjoint_below(pieces, count)
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          coefficients(index) >= 0
            AND lebesgue_measurable(pieces(index))
            AND set_subset(pieces(index), domain))
      AND (FORALL (x: real):
        domain(x) IMPLIES
          0 <= simple_value(
            coefficients, pieces, count, x)
          AND simple_value(
            coefficients, pieces, count, x)
              <= function_value(x))

  nonnegative_integral_upper_bound_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set,
      upper_bound: real): bool =
    FORALL
        (coefficients: real_sequence),
        (pieces: real_set_sequence),
        (count: nat):
      nonnegative_simple_minorant_on(
        function_value, domain,
        coefficients, pieces, count)
      IMPLIES
        simple_integral(coefficients, pieces, count)
          <= upper_bound

  has_nonnegative_integral_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    measurable_on(function_value, domain)
      AND (FORALL (x: real):
        domain(x) IMPLIES function_value(x) >= 0)
      AND integral_value >= 0
      AND nonnegative_integral_upper_bound_on(
        function_value, domain, integral_value)
      AND (FORALL (upper_bound: real):
        nonnegative_integral_upper_bound_on(
          function_value, domain, upper_bound)
        IMPLIES integral_value <= upper_bound)

  positive_part(function_value: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      IF function_value(x) >= 0
      THEN function_value(x)
      ELSE 0
      ENDIF

  negative_part(function_value: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      IF function_value(x) <= 0
      THEN -function_value(x)
      ELSE 0
      ENDIF

  has_integral_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    measurable_on(function_value, domain)
      AND EXISTS (positive_integral, negative_integral: real):
        has_nonnegative_integral_on(
          positive_part(function_value),
          domain,
          positive_integral)
          AND has_nonnegative_integral_on(
            negative_part(function_value),
            domain,
            negative_integral)
          AND integral_value =
            positive_integral - negative_integral

  integrable_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set): bool =
    EXISTS (integral_value: real):
      has_integral_on(
        function_value, domain, integral_value)

  moment_integrand(
      function_value: real_function,
      degree: nat): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      x ^ degree * function_value(x)

  lower_moments_vanish(
      function_value: real_function,
      degree: nat): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < degree IMPLIES
        has_integral_on(
          moment_integrand(function_value, index),
          closed_interval(0, 1),
          0)

  threshold(degree: nat): real =
    (2 :: real) ^ degree * ((degree + 1) :: real)

  putnam_1972_a6: bool =
    FORALL (function_value: real_function), (degree: nat):
      (integrable_on(
          function_value, closed_interval(0, 1))
        AND lower_moments_vanish(function_value, degree)
        AND has_integral_on(
          moment_integrand(function_value, degree),
          closed_interval(0, 1),
          1))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (large_set: real_set):
          set_subset(
            large_set, closed_interval(0, 1))
            AND lebesgue_measurable(large_set)
            AND lebesgue_measure(large_set) > 0
            AND (FORALL (x: real):
              large_set(x) IMPLIES
                abs(function_value(x)) >= threshold(degree))
END putnam_1972_a6

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1972_b1:
;; no three consecutive coefficients of the real power series
;; sum_n x^n (x - 1)^(2n) / n! are all zero. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-1972-b1-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n
       (putnam-1972-b1-factorial (- n 1)))))

;; The source series is
;;
;;   exp(x (x - 1)^2) = exp(x) exp(-2 x^2) exp(x^3).
;;
;; Its coefficient of x^n is therefore the finite rational sum
;;
;;   sum_{i + 2j + 3k = n} (-2)^j / (i! j! k!).
;;
;; The inner sum fixes k and ranges over every possible j; i is then the
;; nonnegative remainder n - 2j - 3k.
(defun putnam-1972-b1-coefficient-inner-sum
    (n k term-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix term-count)))
  (if (zp term-count)
      0
    (let* ((j (- term-count 1))
           (i (- n (+ (* 2 j) (* 3 k)))))
      (+
       (/ (expt -2 j)
          (* (putnam-1972-b1-factorial i)
             (putnam-1972-b1-factorial j)
             (putnam-1972-b1-factorial k)))
       (putnam-1972-b1-coefficient-inner-sum
        n k j)))))

(defun putnam-1972-b1-coefficient-outer-sum
    (n term-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix term-count)))
  (if (zp term-count)
      0
    (let* ((k (- term-count 1))
           (remaining (- n (* 3 k)))
           (j-count (+ 1 (floor remaining 2))))
      (+
       (putnam-1972-b1-coefficient-inner-sum
        n k j-count)
       (putnam-1972-b1-coefficient-outer-sum
        n k)))))

(defun putnam-1972-b1-coefficient (n)
  (if (natp n)
      (putnam-1972-b1-coefficient-outer-sum
       n
       (+ 1 (floor n 3)))
    0))

;; Equality of real power series on a neighborhood of zero uniquely
;; determines every coefficient p(n). Thus the source hypotheses force p(n)
;; to equal the exact coefficient above. Conversely, these coefficients give
;; the source series, so eliminating S, p, and the local equality hypothesis
;; is bidirectionally equivalent to the original implication. The free
;; natural argument n is the universal form of the source's negated
;; existential conclusion.
(defun putnambench-putnam-1972-b1-statement (n)
  (implies
   (natp n)
   (not
    (and
     (equal (putnam-1972-b1-coefficient n) 0)
     (equal (putnam-1972-b1-coefficient (+ n 1)) 0)
     (equal (putnam-1972-b1-coefficient (+ n 2)) 0)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- no three consecutive coefficients vanish in a power series that agrees near
-- zero with the specified factorial-denominator series.
-- This file contains no proof.
