Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.

Variable R : realType.
Definition putnam_1974_a4_solution : nat -> R := fun n => (n%:R / 2 ^+ (n.-1)) * 'C(n.-1, n./2)%:R.
Theorem putnam_1974_a4
    (n : nat)
    (hn : gt n 0)
    : 1/(2 ^ (n.-1)) * (\sum_(0 <= k < (n./2).+1) ((n%:R - 2 * k%:R) * 'C(n, k)%:R)) = putnam_1974_a4_solution n.
Proof. Admitted.

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1974_a4:
-- for every positive natural n, a normalized half-range binomial sum equals
-- n times a central binomial coefficient divided by 2^(n - 1). This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

pred : Nat -> Nat
pred zero =
  zero
pred (suc n) =
  n

half : Nat -> Nat
half zero =
  zero
half (suc zero) =
  zero
half (suc (suc n)) =
  suc (half n)

power : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
power base zero =
  one
power base (suc exponent) =
  power base exponent * base

choose : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
choose n zero =
  one
choose zero (suc k) =
  zero
choose (suc n) (suc k) =
  choose n (suc k) + choose n k

sumThrough : Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat
sumThrough zero term =
  term zero
sumThrough (suc bound) term =
  sumThrough bound term + term (suc bound)

record NonnegativeFraction : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator   : Nat
    denominator : Nat

open NonnegativeFraction

infix 4 _~Q_

_~Q_ : NonnegativeFraction -> NonnegativeFraction -> Set
x ~Q y =
  numerator x * denominator y ==
  numerator y * denominator x

putnamSummand : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
putnamSummand n k =
  (n - two * k) * choose n k

putnamSum : Nat -> NonnegativeFraction
putnamSum n =
  fraction
    (sumThrough (half n) (putnamSummand n))
    (power two (pred n))

putnam-1974-a4-solution : Nat -> NonnegativeFraction
putnam-1974-a4-solution n =
  fraction
    (n * choose (pred n) (half n))
    (power two (pred n))

putnam-1974-a4 : Set
putnam-1974-a4 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  putnamSum n ~Q putnam-1974-a4-solution n

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat st 0 < n holds
    ex terms being FinSequence of REAL st
      len terms = (n div 2) + 1 &
      (for k being Nat st k <= n div 2 holds
        terms.(k + 1) =
          ((n qua Real) - 2 * (k qua Real)) * (n choose k)) &
      ((1 qua Real) / ((2 qua Real) |^ (n -' 1))) * Sum terms =
        ((n qua Real) / ((2 qua Real) |^ (n -' 1))) *
          ((n -' 1) choose (n div 2))
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1974_a4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1974_a4:
% for every positive natural number, a normalized finite binomial sum equals
% its stated closed form. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1974_a4: THEORY
BEGIN
  binomial_coefficient(n, k: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF k = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSIF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k - 1)
        + binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  binomial_sum(n, term_count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF term_count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET k: nat = term_count - 1 IN
        binomial_sum(n, term_count - 1)
          + ((n :: real) - 2 * (k :: real))
              * (binomial_coefficient(n, k) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE term_count

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_predecessor(n: nat): nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN 0 ELSE n - 1 ENDIF

  putnam_1974_a4_solution(n: nat): real =
    safe_div((n :: real), (2 :: real) ^ nat_predecessor(n))
      * (binomial_coefficient(
          nat_predecessor(n), ndiv(n, 2)) :: real)

  putnam_1974_a4: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n > 0 IMPLIES
        safe_div(1, (2 :: real) ^ nat_predecessor(n))
            * binomial_sum(n, ndiv(n, 2) + 1)
          = putnam_1974_a4_solution(n)
END putnam_1974_a4

open Set Nat Polynomial

abbrev putnam_1974_a6_solution : ℕ := sorry
-- 25
/--
Given $n$, let $k(n)$ be the minimal degree of any monic integral polynomial $f$ such that the value of $f(x)$ is divisible by $n$ for every integer $x$. Find the value of $k(1000000)$.
-/
theorem putnam_1974_a6
(hdivnallx : Polynomial ℤ → Prop)
(hdivnallx_def : hdivnallx = fun f => Monic f ∧ (∀ x : ℤ, (10^6 : ℤ) ∣ f.eval x))
: sInf {d : ℕ | ∃ f : Polynomial ℤ, hdivnallx f ∧ d = f.natDegree} = putnam_1974_a6_solution :=
sorry

Definition putnam_1974_a6_solution : nat := 25%nat.
Theorem putnam_1974_a6
    (hdivnallx : {poly int} -> Prop := fun f => (f \is monic) /\ (forall x : int, ((10^6) %| f.[x])%Z))
    : (exists f : {poly int}, hdivnallx f /\ size f = putnam_1974_a6_solution.+1) /\
      (forall d : nat, lt d putnam_1974_a6_solution -> ~ (exists f : {poly int}, hdivnallx f /\ size f = d.+1)).

  the minimum degree, namely 25, of a monic integer polynomial whose value
  at every integer is divisible by 1000000. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =

     \p:int list. \x:int.
       ITLIST (\c acc. c + x * acc) p (&0) in
   let admissible =
     \p:int list.
       ~(p = []) /\
       LAST p = &1 /\
       (!x:int. (&1000000:int) divides eval p x) in

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1974_a6:
;; the minimum degree of a monic integer polynomial whose value at every
;; integer is divisible by 1000000 is 25. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Coefficients are stored in ascending degree order. Requiring a list of
;; length D+1 with final coefficient one represents a monic integer
;; polynomial of degree exactly D.
(defun putnam-1974-a6-integer-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (integerp (car values))
       (putnam-1974-a6-integer-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-1974-a6-polynomial-evaluate
    (coefficients value)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (+ (car coefficients)
         (* value
            (putnam-1974-a6-polynomial-evaluate
             (cdr coefficients) value)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1974-a6-monic-degree-p
    (coefficients degree)
  (and
   (natp degree)
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (equal (len coefficients) (+ 1 degree))
   (putnam-1974-a6-integer-list-p coefficients)
   (equal (car (last coefficients)) 1)))

;; This is the source's universal condition over every integer input, stated
;; directly rather than replaced by a finite sample or residue enumeration.
(defun-sk putnam-1974-a6-all-values-divisible-p
    (coefficients)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (integerp value)
     (equal
      (mod
       (putnam-1974-a6-polynomial-evaluate
        coefficients value)
       1000000)
      0))))

(defun putnam-1974-a6-qualifying-polynomial-p
    (coefficients degree)
  (and
   (putnam-1974-a6-monic-degree-p coefficients degree)
   (putnam-1974-a6-all-values-divisible-p coefficients)))

(defun-sk putnam-1974-a6-qualifying-degree-exists-p
    (degree)
  (exists (coefficients)
    (putnam-1974-a6-qualifying-polynomial-p
     coefficients degree)))

(defun putnam-1974-a6-no-smaller-degree-p (degree-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix degree-count)))
  (if (zp degree-count)
      t
    (let ((degree (- degree-count 1)))
      (and
       (not
        (putnam-1974-a6-qualifying-degree-exists-p
         degree))
       (putnam-1974-a6-no-smaller-degree-p degree)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1974-a6-statement ()
  (and
   (putnam-1974-a6-qualifying-degree-exists-p 25)
   (putnam-1974-a6-no-smaller-degree-p 25)))

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1974_a6:
-- the least degree of a monic integer polynomial whose value at every integer
-- is divisible by 10^6 is 25. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=_ _<_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <= n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> suc m <= suc n

_<_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m < n =
  suc m <= n

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

three : Nat
three =
  suc two

four : Nat
four =
  suc three

five : Nat
five =
  suc four

six : Nat
six =
  suc five

ten : Nat
ten =
  five + five

powerNat : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
powerNat base zero =
  one
powerNat base (suc exponent) =
  powerNat base exponent * base

millionNat : Nat
millionNat =
  powerNat ten six

putnamDegree : Nat
putnamDegree =
  five * five

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

powerInt : Int -> Nat -> Int
powerInt x zero =
  pos one
powerInt x (suc exponent) =
  multiplyInt (powerInt x exponent) x

Polynomial : Set
Polynomial =
  Nat -> Int

evaluateThrough : Nat -> Polynomial -> Int -> Int
evaluateThrough zero coefficients x =
  coefficients zero
evaluateThrough (suc degree) coefficients x =
  addInt
    (evaluateThrough degree coefficients x)
    (multiplyInt
      (coefficients (suc degree))
      (powerInt x (suc degree)))

MonicOfDegree : Nat -> Polynomial -> Set
MonicOfDegree degree coefficients =
  coefficients degree == pos one
  and
  ((index : Nat) ->
    degree < index ->
    coefficients index == pos zero)

DivisibleByMillion : Int -> Set
DivisibleByMillion value =
  Exists Int
    (\ quotient ->
      value == multiplyInt (pos millionNat) quotient)

IntegerValuedMonicOfDegree : Nat -> Polynomial -> Set
IntegerValuedMonicOfDegree degree coefficients =
  MonicOfDegree degree coefficients
  and
  ((x : Int) ->
    DivisibleByMillion
      (evaluateThrough degree coefficients x))

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  A polynomial of degree d is represented by its complete integer
  coefficient function A on NN0: its coefficient at d is one, and every
  coefficient above d is zero. Its value at x is the finite coefficient
  sum through d. Thus this representation ranges over exactly the monic
  integer polynomials of degree d.

  excludes an internal witness at every smaller nonnegative degree, which

content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1974_a6:
% the minimum degree of a monic integer polynomial whose value at every
% integer is divisible by 1000000 is 25. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1974_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  coefficient_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> int]

  integer_polynomial_value(
      coefficients: coefficient_sequence,
      x: int,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET degree: nat = count - 1 IN
        integer_polynomial_value(
          coefficients, x, count - 1)
          + coefficients(degree) * x ^ degree
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  int_divides(divisor, value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: int):
      value = divisor * quotient

  monic_of_degree(
      coefficients: coefficient_sequence,
      degree: nat): bool =
    coefficients(degree) = 1
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        degree < index IMPLIES coefficients(index) = 0

  admissible_polynomial(
      coefficients: coefficient_sequence,
      degree: nat): bool =
    monic_of_degree(coefficients, degree)
      AND FORALL (x: int):
        int_divides(
          1000000,
          integer_polynomial_value(
            coefficients, x, degree + 1))

  putnam_1974_a6_solution: nat = 25

  putnam_1974_a6: bool =
    (EXISTS (coefficients: coefficient_sequence):
      admissible_polynomial(
        coefficients, putnam_1974_a6_solution))
      AND
    (FORALL (degree: nat):
      degree < putnam_1974_a6_solution IMPLIES
        NOT (EXISTS (coefficients: coefficient_sequence):
          admissible_polynomial(coefficients, degree)))
END putnam_1974_a6

title: putnam_1974_b1
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1974_b1:
   maximizing the sum of the ten pairwise Euclidean distances among five
   points on the unit circle is equivalent to the cyclic equal-edge
   configuration. This file contains no proof. *)

From Coq Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition point := (R * R)%type.

Definition point_distance (a b : point) : R :=
  sqrt ((fst a - fst b) ^ 2 + (snd a - snd b) ^ 2).

Record five_points := {
  point_0 : point;
  point_1 : point;
  point_2 : point;
  point_3 : point;
  point_4 : point
}.

Definition point_at (p : five_points) (i : nat) : point :=
  match i with
  | O => point_0 p
  | S O => point_1 p
  | S (S O) => point_2 p
  | S (S (S O)) => point_3 p
  | S (S (S (S O))) => point_4 p
  | _ => (0, 0)
  end.

Definition on_unit_circle (p : five_points) : Prop :=
  forall i : nat,
    (i < 5)%nat ->
    point_distance (point_at p i) (0, 0) = 1.

Definition total_distance (p : five_points) : R :=
    point_distance (point_0 p) (point_1 p)
  + point_distance (point_0 p) (point_2 p)
  + point_distance (point_0 p) (point_3 p)
  + point_distance (point_0 p) (point_4 p)
  + point_distance (point_1 p) (point_2 p)
  + point_distance (point_1 p) (point_3 p)
  + point_distance (point_1 p) (point_4 p)
  + point_distance (point_2 p) (point_3 p)
  + point_distance (point_2 p) (point_4 p)
  + point_distance (point_3 p) (point_4 p).

Definition permutation_of_five (ordering : nat -> nat) : Prop :=
  (forall i : nat,
      (i < 5)%nat ->
      (ordering i < 5)%nat) /\
  (forall i j : nat,
      (i < 5)%nat ->
      (j < 5)%nat ->
      ordering i = ordering j ->
      i = j) /\
  (forall j : nat,
      (j < 5)%nat ->
      exists i : nat,
        (i < 5)%nat /\ ordering i = j).

Definition points_distinct (p : five_points) : Prop :=
  forall i j : nat,
    (i < 5)%nat ->
    (j < 5)%nat ->
    point_at p i = point_at p j ->
    i = j.

Definition putnam_1974_b1_solution (p : five_points) : Prop :=
  points_distinct p /\
  exists (B : R) (ordering : nat -> nat),
    0 < B /\
    permutation_of_five ordering /\
    point_distance (point_at p (ordering 0%nat))
      (point_at p (ordering 1%nat)) = B /\
    point_distance (point_at p (ordering 1%nat))
      (point_at p (ordering 2%nat)) = B /\
    point_distance (point_at p (ordering 2%nat))
      (point_at p (ordering 3%nat)) = B /\
    point_distance (point_at p (ordering 3%nat))
      (point_at p (ordering 4%nat)) = B /\
    point_distance (point_at p (ordering 4%nat))
      (point_at p (ordering 0%nat)) = B.

Definition maximizes_total_distance (p : five_points) : Prop :=
  forall q : five_points,
    on_unit_circle q ->
    total_distance q <= total_distance p.

Theorem putnam_1974_b1
    (p : five_points)
    (hp : on_unit_circle p) :
  maximizes_total_distance p <-> putnam_1974_b1_solution p.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1974_b1:
  five points on the unit circle maximize the sum of their ten pairwise
  distances exactly when they admit a cyclic ordering with one common positive
  consecutive distance. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let edist =
     \(x:real#real) (y:real#real).
       sqrt ((FST x - FST y) pow 2 + (SND x - SND y) pow 2) in
   let on_unit_circle =
     \(p:num->real#real).
       !i. i < 5 ==> edist (p i) (&0,&0) = &1 in
   let distance_sum =
     \(p:num->real#real).
       sum (0..4)
         (\i. sum ((i + 1)..4) (\j. edist (p i) (p j))) in
   let putnam_1974_b1_solution =
     \(p:num->real#real).
       (!i j:num.
          i < 5 /\ j < 5 /\ p i = p j ==> i = j) /\
       ?B:real. ?ordering:num->num.
         &0 < B /\
         (!i. i < 5 ==> ordering i < 5) /\
         (!i j.
            i < 5 /\ j < 5 /\ ordering i = ordering j ==> i = j) /\
         (!i. i < 5
              ==> edist (p (ordering i))
                        (p (ordering ((i + 1) MOD 5))) = B) in
   !p:num->real#real.
     on_unit_circle p
     ==> (distance_sum p =
          sup (IMAGE distance_sum
                     {q:num->real#real | on_unit_circle q}) <=>
          putnam_1974_b1_solution p)`;;

title: putnam_1974_b1
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1974_b1:
;; five points on the Euclidean unit circle maximize the sum of their ten
;; pairwise distances exactly when they are the five distinct vertices of a
;; regular pentagon, equivalently when some cyclic ordering of the distinct
;; points has equal positive consecutive distances. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; After introducing a nonnegative variable for each Euclidean distance, the
;; source statement is first-order over real closed fields. Its validity over
;; the reals is therefore equivalent to validity over the real algebraic
;; numbers. One isolated algebraic number alpha and rational functions of
;; alpha encode every finite tuple of real algebraic coordinates and distances.
;;
;; Write M(p) for maximality and R(p) for the distinct equal-edge cyclic-order
;; condition characterizing the vertices of a regular pentagon. The source
;; equivalence M(p) <-> R(p) is represented by the equivalent pair
;;
;;   R(p) -> every unit-circle q has S(q) <= S(p),
;;   not R(p) -> S(p) < S(r) for every unit-circle r satisfying R(r).
;;
;; A regular unit-circle r exists. Hence the second clause says exactly that a
;; nonregular p is not maximal; conversely, the source equivalence makes every
;; such r maximal and therefore strictly better than any nonmaximal p. Free
;; ACL2 arguments provide the universal p, q, and r quantifiers. The finite
;; existential cyclic ordering is searched internally over all permutations.

;; Rational polynomials in alpha use descending coefficient order.

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-p (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (and (rationalp (car p))
           (putnam-1974-b1-rp-p (cdr p)))
    (equal p nil)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (if (equal (car p) 0)
          (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize (cdr p))
        p)
    nil))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-neg (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (cons (- (car p))
            (putnam-1974-b1-rp-neg (cdr p)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-add-raw (p q)
  (declare (xargs :measure (+ (acl2-count p) (acl2-count q))))
  (cond
   ((endp p) q)
   ((endp q) p)
   ((< (len p) (len q))
    (cons (car q)
          (putnam-1974-b1-rp-add-raw p (cdr q))))
   ((< (len q) (len p))
    (cons (car p)
          (putnam-1974-b1-rp-add-raw (cdr p) q)))
   (t
    (cons (+ (car p) (car q))
          (putnam-1974-b1-rp-add-raw (cdr p) (cdr q))))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-add (p q)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-add-raw p q)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-sub (p q)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rp-add
   p (putnam-1974-b1-rp-neg q)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-scale (c p)
  (if (consp p)
      (cons (* c (car p))
            (putnam-1974-b1-rp-scale c (cdr p)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-zeroes (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (cons 0 (putnam-1974-b1-zeroes (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-scale-shift (c p shift)
  (append (putnam-1974-b1-rp-scale c p)
          (putnam-1974-b1-zeroes shift)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul-raw (p q)
  (if (consp p)
      (putnam-1974-b1-rp-add
       (putnam-1974-b1-rp-scale-shift
        (car p) q (len (cdr p)))
       (putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul-raw (cdr p) q))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul (p q)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul-raw p q)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-eval-aux (p x accumulator)
  (if (consp p)
      (putnam-1974-b1-rp-eval-aux
       (cdr p) x (+ (* accumulator x) (car p)))
    accumulator))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-eval (p x)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rp-eval-aux p x 0))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-derivative-aux (p degree)
  (if (consp p)
      (if (zp degree)
          nil
        (cons (* degree (car p))
              (putnam-1974-b1-rp-derivative-aux
               (cdr p) (- degree 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-derivative (p)
  (let ((p (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize p)))
    (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize
     (putnam-1974-b1-rp-derivative-aux
      p (nfix (- (len p) 1))))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-rem-fuel (p q fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((p (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize p))
        (q (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize q)))
    (if (or (zp fuel)
            (endp q)
            (< (len p) (len q)))
        p
      (putnam-1974-b1-rp-rem-fuel
       (putnam-1974-b1-rp-sub
        p
        (putnam-1974-b1-rp-scale-shift
         (/ (car p) (car q))
         q
         (- (len p) (len q))))
       q
       (- fuel 1)))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-rem (p q)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rp-rem-fuel
   p q (+ 1 (len (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize p)))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-sturm-tail (previous current fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((current (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize current)))
    (if (or (zp fuel) (endp current))
        nil
      (cons
       current
       (putnam-1974-b1-rp-sturm-tail
        current
        (putnam-1974-b1-rp-neg
         (putnam-1974-b1-rp-rem previous current))
        (- fuel 1))))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-sturm-sequence (p q)
  (let ((p (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize p))
        (q (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize q)))
    (if (endp p)
        nil
      (cons
       p
       (if (endp q)
           nil
         (cons
          q
          (putnam-1974-b1-rp-sturm-tail
           p q (+ 1 (len p) (len q)))))))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rational-sign (x)
  (cond ((< x 0) -1)
        ((< 0 x) 1)
        (t 0)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-variations-aux
    (polynomials x previous-sign)
  (if (consp polynomials)
      (let ((sign
             (putnam-1974-b1-rational-sign
              (putnam-1974-b1-rp-eval (car polynomials) x))))
        (if (equal sign 0)
            (putnam-1974-b1-rp-variations-aux
             (cdr polynomials) x previous-sign)
          (+ (if (and (not (equal previous-sign 0))
                      (not (equal sign previous-sign)))
                 1
               0)
             (putnam-1974-b1-rp-variations-aux
              (cdr polynomials) x sign))))
    0))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-variations (polynomials x)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rp-variations-aux polynomials x 0))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-cauchy-index (p q lower upper)
  (let ((sequence
         (putnam-1974-b1-rp-sturm-sequence p q)))
    (- (putnam-1974-b1-rp-variations sequence lower)
       (putnam-1974-b1-rp-variations sequence upper))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rp-root-count (p lower upper)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rp-cauchy-index
   p (putnam-1974-b1-rp-derivative p) lower upper))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-primitive-p (primitive lower upper)
  (and
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-p primitive)
   (consp (putnam-1974-b1-rp-normalize primitive))
   (rationalp lower)
   (rationalp upper)
   (< lower upper)
   (not (equal (putnam-1974-b1-rp-eval primitive lower) 0))
   (not (equal (putnam-1974-b1-rp-eval primitive upper) 0))
   (equal
    (putnam-1974-b1-rp-root-count primitive lower upper)
    1)
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-1974-b1-rp-cauchy-index
      primitive
      (putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul
       (putnam-1974-b1-rp-derivative primitive)
       (putnam-1974-b1-rp-derivative primitive))
      lower
      upper)
     0))))

;; The Sturm-Tarski query over the isolated root alpha is sign(g(alpha)).
(defun putnam-1974-b1-alg-sign
    (primitive lower upper g)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rp-cauchy-index
   primitive
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul
    (putnam-1974-b1-rp-derivative primitive)
    g)
   lower
   upper))

;; A field element is (numerator denominator), evaluated at alpha.

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-numerator (value)
  (car value))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-denominator (value)
  (cadr value))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-code-p
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (and
   (true-listp value)
   (equal (len value) 2)
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-p
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-numerator value))
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-p
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-denominator value))
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-1974-b1-alg-sign
      primitive lower upper
      (putnam-1974-b1-rf-denominator value))
     0))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-list-p
    (primitive lower upper values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (putnam-1974-b1-rf-code-p
        primitive lower upper (car values))
       (putnam-1974-b1-rf-list-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-zero ()
  (list nil (list 1)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-one ()
  (list (list 1) (list 1)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-neg (value)
  (list
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-neg
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-numerator value))
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-denominator value)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-add (left right)
  (list
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-add
    (putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul
     (putnam-1974-b1-rf-numerator left)
     (putnam-1974-b1-rf-denominator right))
    (putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul
     (putnam-1974-b1-rf-numerator right)
     (putnam-1974-b1-rf-denominator left)))
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-denominator left)
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-denominator right))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-sub (left right)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rf-add
   left (putnam-1974-b1-rf-neg right)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-mul (left right)
  (list
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-numerator left)
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-numerator right))
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-denominator left)
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-denominator right))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-sign
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (putnam-1974-b1-alg-sign
   primitive lower upper
   (putnam-1974-b1-rp-mul
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-numerator value)
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-denominator value))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-equal-p
    (primitive lower upper left right)
  (equal
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sign
    primitive lower upper
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sub left right))
   0))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-positive-p
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (equal
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sign
    primitive lower upper value)
   1))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-nonnegative-p
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (not
   (equal
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sign
     primitive lower upper value)
    -1)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-point-code-p
    (primitive lower upper point)
  (and
   (true-listp point)
   (equal (len point) 2)
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-list-p
    primitive lower upper point)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-point-list-p
    (primitive lower upper points)
  (if (consp points)
      (and
       (putnam-1974-b1-point-code-p
        primitive lower upper (car points))
       (putnam-1974-b1-point-list-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr points)))
    (equal points nil)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-square (value)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rf-mul value value))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-distance-squared (left right)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rf-add
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-square
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sub (nth 0 left) (nth 0 right)))
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-square
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sub (nth 1 left) (nth 1 right)))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-point-equal-p
    (primitive lower upper left right)
  (and
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-equal-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 0 left) (nth 0 right))
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-equal-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 1 left) (nth 1 right))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-point-distinct-from-list-p
    (primitive lower upper point points)
  (if (consp points)
      (and
       (not
        (putnam-1974-b1-point-equal-p
         primitive lower upper point (car points)))
       (putnam-1974-b1-point-distinct-from-list-p
        primitive lower upper point (cdr points)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-distinct-point-list-p
    (primitive lower upper points)
  (if (consp points)
      (and
       (putnam-1974-b1-point-distinct-from-list-p
        primitive lower upper (car points) (cdr points))
       (putnam-1974-b1-distinct-point-list-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr points)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-unit-point-p
    (primitive lower upper point)
  (putnam-1974-b1-rf-equal-p
   primitive lower upper
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-add
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-square (nth 0 point))
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-square (nth 1 point)))
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-one)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-unit-points-p
    (primitive lower upper points)
  (if (consp points)
      (and
       (putnam-1974-b1-unit-point-p
        primitive lower upper (car points))
       (putnam-1974-b1-unit-points-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr points)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-distance-value-p
    (primitive lower upper left right value)
  (and
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-nonnegative-p
    primitive lower upper value)
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-equal-p
    primitive lower upper
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-square value)
    (putnam-1974-b1-distance-squared left right))))

;; DISTANCES is ordered as 01, 02, 03, 04, 12, 13, 14, 23, 24, 34.
(defun putnam-1974-b1-distance-list-p
    (primitive lower upper points distances)
  (and
   (true-listp distances)
   (equal (len distances) 10)
   (putnam-1974-b1-rf-list-p
    primitive lower upper distances)
   (putnam-1974-b1-distance-value-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 0 points) (nth 1 points) (nth 0 distances))
   (putnam-1974-b1-distance-value-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 0 points) (nth 2 points) (nth 1 distances))
   (putnam-1974-b1-distance-value-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 0 points) (nth 3 points) (nth 2 distances))
   (putnam-1974-b1-distance-value-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 0 points) (nth 4 points) (nth 3 distances))
   (putnam-1974-b1-distance-value-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 1 points) (nth 2 points) (nth 4 distances))
   (putnam-1974-b1-distance-value-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 1 points) (nth 3 points) (nth 5 distances))
   (putnam-1974-b1-distance-value-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 1 points) (nth 4 points) (nth 6 distances))
   (putnam-1974-b1-distance-value-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 2 points) (nth 3 points) (nth 7 distances))
   (putnam-1974-b1-distance-value-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 2 points) (nth 4 points) (nth 8 distances))
   (putnam-1974-b1-distance-value-p
    primitive lower upper (nth 3 points) (nth 4 points) (nth 9 distances))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-rf-sum (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (putnam-1974-b1-rf-add
       (car values)
       (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sum (cdr values)))
    (putnam-1974-b1-rf-zero)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-cons-to-each (value lists)
  (if (consp lists)
      (cons (cons value (car lists))
            (putnam-1974-b1-cons-to-each value (cdr lists)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-insert-everywhere (value values)
  (if (consp values)
      (cons
       (cons value values)
       (putnam-1974-b1-cons-to-each
        (car values)
        (putnam-1974-b1-insert-everywhere value (cdr values))))
    (list (list value))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-insert-into-all (value lists)
  (if (consp lists)
      (append
       (putnam-1974-b1-insert-everywhere value (car lists))
       (putnam-1974-b1-insert-into-all value (cdr lists)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-permutations (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (putnam-1974-b1-insert-into-all
       (car values)
       (putnam-1974-b1-permutations (cdr values)))
    (list nil)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-regular-order-p
    (primitive lower upper ordered-points)
  (let ((edge
         (putnam-1974-b1-distance-squared
          (nth 0 ordered-points) (nth 1 ordered-points))))
    (and
     (putnam-1974-b1-distinct-point-list-p
      primitive lower upper ordered-points)
     (putnam-1974-b1-rf-positive-p
      primitive lower upper edge)
     (putnam-1974-b1-rf-equal-p
      primitive lower upper edge
      (putnam-1974-b1-distance-squared
       (nth 1 ordered-points) (nth 2 ordered-points)))
     (putnam-1974-b1-rf-equal-p
      primitive lower upper edge
      (putnam-1974-b1-distance-squared
       (nth 2 ordered-points) (nth 3 ordered-points)))
     (putnam-1974-b1-rf-equal-p
      primitive lower upper edge
      (putnam-1974-b1-distance-squared
       (nth 3 ordered-points) (nth 4 ordered-points)))
     (putnam-1974-b1-rf-equal-p
      primitive lower upper edge
      (putnam-1974-b1-distance-squared
       (nth 4 ordered-points) (nth 0 ordered-points))))))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-regular-permutation-exists-p
    (primitive lower upper permutations)
  (if (consp permutations)
      (or
       (putnam-1974-b1-regular-order-p
        primitive lower upper (car permutations))
       (putnam-1974-b1-regular-permutation-exists-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr permutations)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-regular-p
    (primitive lower upper points)
  (putnam-1974-b1-regular-permutation-exists-p
   primitive lower upper
   (putnam-1974-b1-permutations points)))

(defun putnam-1974-b1-configuration-code-p
    (primitive lower upper points distances)
  (and
   (true-listp points)
   (equal (len points) 5)
   (putnam-1974-b1-point-list-p
    primitive lower upper points)
   (putnam-1974-b1-distance-list-p
    primitive lower upper points distances)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1974-b1-statement
    (primitive lower upper
     points point-distances
     competitor competitor-distances
     regular-reference regular-reference-distances)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-1974-b1-primitive-p primitive lower upper)
    (putnam-1974-b1-configuration-code-p
     primitive lower upper points point-distances)
    (putnam-1974-b1-configuration-code-p
     primitive lower upper competitor competitor-distances)
    (putnam-1974-b1-configuration-code-p
     primitive lower upper
     regular-reference regular-reference-distances))
   (and
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1974-b1-unit-points-p
       primitive lower upper points)
      (putnam-1974-b1-regular-p
       primitive lower upper points)
      (putnam-1974-b1-unit-points-p
       primitive lower upper competitor))
     (putnam-1974-b1-rf-nonnegative-p
      primitive lower upper
      (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sub
       (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sum point-distances)
       (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sum competitor-distances))))
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1974-b1-unit-points-p
       primitive lower upper points)
      (not
       (putnam-1974-b1-regular-p
        primitive lower upper points))
      (putnam-1974-b1-unit-points-p
       primitive lower upper regular-reference)
      (putnam-1974-b1-regular-p
       primitive lower upper regular-reference))
     (putnam-1974-b1-rf-positive-p
      primitive lower upper
      (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sub
       (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sum regular-reference-distances)
       (putnam-1974-b1-rf-sum point-distances)))))))

title: putnam_1974_b1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1974_b1:
-- five unit-circle points maximize their total pairwise Euclidean distance
-- exactly when a cyclic reordering has equal positive edge lengths. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infix 1 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

origin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R
origin reals =
  point (zeroR reals) (zeroR reals)

squaredDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
squaredDistance reals p q =
  add reals
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q)))
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)))

distance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
distance reals p q =
  squareRoot reals (squaredDistance reals p q)

data Fin5 : Set where
  i0 i1 i2 i3 i4 : Fin5

next5 : Fin5 -> Fin5
next5 i0 = i1
next5 i1 = i2
next5 i2 = i3
next5 i3 = i4
next5 i4 = i0

record Permutation5 : Set where
  constructor permutation
  field
    apply        : Fin5 -> Fin5
    applyInverse : Fin5 -> Fin5
    inverse-left :
      (i : Fin5) ->
      applyInverse (apply i) == i
    inverse-right :
      (i : Fin5) ->
      apply (applyInverse i) == i

open Permutation5

OnUnitCircle :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Fin5 -> Point R) ->
  Set
OnUnitCircle reals points =
  (i : Fin5) ->
  distance reals (points i) (origin reals) == oneR reals

totalPairwiseDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Fin5 -> Point R) ->
  R
totalPairwiseDistance reals points =
  add reals
    (distance reals (points i0) (points i1))
    (add reals
      (distance reals (points i0) (points i2))
      (add reals
        (distance reals (points i0) (points i3))
        (add reals
          (distance reals (points i0) (points i4))
          (add reals
            (distance reals (points i1) (points i2))
            (add reals
              (distance reals (points i1) (points i3))
              (add reals
                (distance reals (points i1) (points i4))
                (add reals
                  (distance reals (points i2) (points i3))
                  (add reals
                    (distance reals (points i2) (points i4))
                    (distance reals (points i3) (points i4))))))))))

DistanceSumOfUnitConfiguration :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
DistanceSumOfUnitConfiguration {R} reals value =
  Exists (Fin5 -> Point R)
    (\ points ->
      OnUnitCircle reals points
      and
      value == totalPairwiseDistance reals points)

UpperBound :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> Set) ->
  R ->
  Set
UpperBound {R} reals values upper =
  (value : R) ->
  values value ->
  lessOrEqual reals value upper

IsLeastUpperBound :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> Set) ->
  R ->
  Set
IsLeastUpperBound {R} reals values supremum =
  UpperBound reals values supremum
  and
  ((upper : R) ->
    UpperBound reals values upper ->
    lessOrEqual reals supremum upper)

MaximizesPairwiseDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Fin5 -> Point R) ->
  Set
MaximizesPairwiseDistance reals points =
  IsLeastUpperBound reals
    (DistanceSumOfUnitConfiguration reals)
    (totalPairwiseDistance reals points)

EqualPositiveCyclicEdges :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Fin5 -> Point R) ->
  Set
EqualPositiveCyclicEdges {R} reals points =
  Exists R
    (\ edgeLength ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) edgeLength
      and
      Exists Permutation5
        (\ ordering ->
          (i : Fin5) ->
          distance reals
            (points (apply ordering i))
            (points (apply ordering (next5 i)))
          ==
          edgeLength))

PairwiseDistinct :
  {R : Set} ->
  (Fin5 -> Point R) ->
  Set
PairwiseDistinct points =
  (i j : Fin5) ->
  i != j ->
  points i != points j

module Putnam1974B1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (points : Fin5 -> Point R) ->
    OnUnitCircle reals points ->
    (MaximizesPairwiseDistance reals points
      iff
      (PairwiseDistinct points
      and
      EqualPositiveCyclicEdges reals points))

putnam-1974-b1 : Set1
putnam-1974-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1974B1Statement.proposition reals

title: putnam_1974_b1
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1974_b1:
  five points on the real unit circle maximize the sum of their ten pairwise
  distances exactly when they can be cyclically ordered with one common
  positive side length. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;
open transcTheory;

val putnam_1974_b1 =
  ``let sqdist =
      \P Q : real # real.
        (FST P - FST Q) pow 2 + (SND P - SND Q) pow 2
    in
    let dist =
      \P Q : real # real. sqrt (sqdist P Q)
    in
    let norm =
      \P : real # real. sqrt (FST P pow 2 + SND P pow 2)
    in
    let on_unit_circle =
      \p : num -> real # real.
        !i : num. i < 5 ==> norm (p i) = 1
    in
    let distance_sum =
      \p : num -> real # real.
        SIGMA
          (\j : num.
             SIGMA
               (\i : num.
                  if i < j then dist (p i) (p j) else 0)
               (count 5))
          (count 5)
    in
    let permutes_five =
      \ord : num -> num.
        (!i : num. i < 5 ==> ord i < 5) /\
        (!i j : num.
           i < 5 /\ j < 5 /\ ord i = ord j ==> i = j) /\
        (!j : num. j < 5 ==> ?i : num. i < 5 /\ ord i = j)
    in
    let regular_configuration =
      \p : num -> real # real.
        (!i j : num.
           i < 5 /\ j < 5 /\ i <> j ==> p i <> p j) /\
        ?B : real. ?ord : num -> num.
          0 < B /\
          permutes_five ord /\
          !i : num.
            i < 5
            ==>
            dist (p (ord i)) (p (ord ((i + 1) MOD 5))) = B
    in
      !p : num -> real # real.
        on_unit_circle p
        ==>
        ((!q : num -> real # real.
            on_unit_circle q ==> distance_sum q <= distance_sum p) <=>
         regular_configuration p)``;

title: putnam_1974_b1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1974_b1: maximizing the sum of all ten pairwise distances among
  five points on the unit circle is equivalent to a cyclic ordering with
  one positive common consecutive distance. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P74B1I is the two-coordinate index set, P74B1V is the five-element
  ordinal, and P74B1R2 is the real Euclidean plane. P74B1Succ is cyclic
  successor on the indices 0 through 4, and P74B1Dist is Euclidean distance.
  P74B1Unit says that every indexed point has distance one from the origin.
  P74B1Score is the sum over the ten pairs i < j, and P74B1Values is the set
  of all such scores for unit-circle configurations.

  P74B1Solution requires the five points to be distinct and retains the
  internally existential positive common distance and permutation from the
  source solution specification. Distinctness excludes repeated-vertex
  cycles with equal chord lengths, so the predicate describes a regular
  pentagon. Replacing Fin 5 by its five-element ordinal and expanding the
  definitionally specified objective function are bijective, definitional
  reindexings. The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus
  statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P74B1I P74B1V P74B1R2 P74B1Zero P74B1Succ $.
$c P74B1Dist P74B1Unit P74B1Score P74B1Values P74B1Solution $.

p74b1-coordinate-index-syntax $a class P74B1I $.
p74b1-vertex-index-syntax $a class P74B1V $.
p74b1-plane-syntax $a class P74B1R2 $.
p74b1-zero-syntax $a class P74B1Zero $.
p74b1-successor-syntax $a class P74B1Succ $.
p74b1-distance-syntax $a class ( P74B1Dist A B ) $.
p74b1-unit-syntax $a wff ( P74B1Unit p ) $.
p74b1-score-syntax $a class ( P74B1Score p ) $.
p74b1-values-syntax $a class P74B1Values $.
p74b1-solution-syntax $a wff ( P74B1Solution p ) $.

p74b1-coordinate-index-definition $a |- P74B1I = ( 1 ... 2 ) $.

p74b1-vertex-index-definition $a |- P74B1V = 5 $.

p74b1-plane-definition $a |- P74B1R2 = ( RR ^m P74B1I ) $.

p74b1-zero-definition $a |- P74B1Zero =
  ( j e. P74B1I |-> 0 )
$.

p74b1-successor-definition $a |- P74B1Succ =
  (
    i e. P74B1V |->
      if (
        i = 4 ,
        0 ,
        ( i + 1 )
      )
  )
$.

${
  $d A B j $.

  p74b1-distance-definition $a |- (
    P74B1Dist A B
  ) = (
    sqrt
    `
    (
      sum_ j e. P74B1I
        ( ( ( A ` j ) - ( B ` j ) ) ^ 2 )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i p $.

  p74b1-unit-definition $a |- (
    ( P74B1Unit p )
    <->
    A. i e. P74B1V
      ( P74B1Dist ( p ` i ) P74B1Zero ) = 1
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i j p $.

  p74b1-score-definition $a |- (
    P74B1Score p
  ) = (
    sum_ j e. P74B1V
      sum_ i e. { i e. P74B1V | i < j }
        ( P74B1Dist ( p ` i ) ( p ` j ) )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d q r $.

  p74b1-values-definition $a |- P74B1Values = {
    r e. RR |
    E. q e. ( P74B1R2 ^m P74B1V )
      (
        ( P74B1Unit q )
        /\
        r = ( P74B1Score q )
      )
  } $.
$}

${
  $d B i o p $.

  p74b1-solution-definition $a |- (
    ( P74B1Solution p )
    <->
    (
      p : P74B1V -1-1-> P74B1R2
      /\
      E. B e. RR+
        E. o
          (
            o : P74B1V -1-1-onto-> P74B1V
            /\
            A. i e. P74B1V
              (
                P74B1Dist
                  ( p ` ( o ` i ) )
                  ( p ` ( o ` ( P74B1Succ ` i ) ) )
              )
              =
              B
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

putnambench-putnam-1974-b1 $a |-
    A. p e. ( P74B1R2 ^m P74B1V )
      (
        ( P74B1Unit p )
        ->
        (
          (
            ( P74B1Score p )
            =
            sup ( P74B1Values , RR , < )
          )
          <->
          ( P74B1Solution p )
        )
      )
  $.

title: putnam_1974_b1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1974_b1:
% five points on the real unit circle attain the supremum of the sum of their
% ten pairwise Euclidean distances exactly when a cyclic ordering has five
% equal positive successive distances. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1974_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  vertex: TYPE = below(5)
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]
  configuration: TYPE = [vertex -> point]
  vertex_permutation: TYPE = [vertex -> vertex]

  squared_norm(P: point): real =
    x_coord(P) ^ 2 + y_coord(P) ^ 2

  squared_distance(P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q)) ^ 2
      + (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q)) ^ 2

  sqrt_value(root, radicand: real): bool =
    0 <= root AND root * root = radicand

  on_unit_circle(p: configuration): bool =
    FORALL (i: vertex):
      squared_norm(p(i)) = 1

  distance_sum(p: configuration, total: real): bool =
    EXISTS (d01, d02, d03, d04, d12,
            d13, d14, d23, d24, d34: real):
      sqrt_value(d01, squared_distance(p(0), p(1)))
        AND sqrt_value(d02, squared_distance(p(0), p(2)))
        AND sqrt_value(d03, squared_distance(p(0), p(3)))
        AND sqrt_value(d04, squared_distance(p(0), p(4)))
        AND sqrt_value(d12, squared_distance(p(1), p(2)))
        AND sqrt_value(d13, squared_distance(p(1), p(3)))
        AND sqrt_value(d14, squared_distance(p(1), p(4)))
        AND sqrt_value(d23, squared_distance(p(2), p(3)))
        AND sqrt_value(d24, squared_distance(p(2), p(4)))
        AND sqrt_value(d34, squared_distance(p(3), p(4)))
        AND total =
          d01 + d02 + d03 + d04 + d12
            + d13 + d14 + d23 + d24 + d34

  unit_distance_upper_bound(bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (q: configuration), (total: real):
      (on_unit_circle(q) AND distance_sum(q, total))
        IMPLIES total <= bound

  unit_distance_supremum(value: real): bool =
    unit_distance_upper_bound(value)
      AND FORALL (bound: real):
        unit_distance_upper_bound(bound) IMPLIES value <= bound

  attains_unit_distance_supremum(p: configuration): bool =
    EXISTS (total: real):
      distance_sum(p, total)
        AND unit_distance_supremum(total)

  permutation(ordering: vertex_permutation): bool =
    (FORALL (i, j: vertex):
      ordering(i) = ordering(j) IMPLIES i = j)
      AND
        (FORALL (j: vertex):
          EXISTS (i: vertex):
            ordering(i) = j)

  pairwise_distinct(p: configuration): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: vertex):
      i /= j IMPLIES p(i) /= p(j)

  equal_positive_cyclic_edges(p: configuration): bool =
    EXISTS (edge_length: real), (ordering: vertex_permutation):
      edge_length > 0
        AND permutation(ordering)
        AND sqrt_value(
          edge_length,
          squared_distance(p(ordering(0)), p(ordering(1))))
        AND sqrt_value(
          edge_length,
          squared_distance(p(ordering(1)), p(ordering(2))))
        AND sqrt_value(
          edge_length,
          squared_distance(p(ordering(2)), p(ordering(3))))
        AND sqrt_value(
          edge_length,
          squared_distance(p(ordering(3)), p(ordering(4))))
        AND sqrt_value(
          edge_length,
          squared_distance(p(ordering(4)), p(ordering(0))))

  putnam_1974_b1: bool =
    FORALL (p: configuration):
      on_unit_circle(p)
        IMPLIES
          (attains_unit_distance_supremum(p)
            IFF
              (pairwise_distinct(p)
                AND equal_positive_cyclic_edges(p)))
END putnam_1974_b1

import Mathlib

/--
Let $y(x)$ be a continuously differentiable real-valued function of a real vairable $x$. Show that if $(y')^2 + y^3 \to 0$ as $x \to +\infty$, then $y(x)$ and $y'(x) \to 0$ as $x \to +\infty$.
-/
theorem putnam_1974_b2
(y : ℝ → ℝ)
(ycontdiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 y)
(limy : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => (deriv y x)^2 + (y x)^3) atTop (𝓝 0))
: Tendsto y atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ Tendsto (deriv y) atTop (𝓝 0) :=

title: putnam_1974_b2
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1974_b2: asymptotic vanishing of a continuously differentiable real function and its derivative; this file contains no proof. *)
From Stdlib Require Import Reals ClassicalEpsilon.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition real_derivative (f : R -> R) (x : R) : R :=
  epsilon (inhabits (0 : R)) (fun d : R => derivable_pt_lim f x d).

Definition tends_to_at_pos_infty (f : R -> R) (l : R) : Prop :=
  forall eps : R,
    eps > 0 ->
    exists M : R, forall x : R, x >= M -> Rabs (f x - l) < eps.

Theorem putnam_1974_b2
    (y : R -> R)
    (ycontdiff :
      (forall x : R, derivable_pt_lim y x (real_derivative y x)) /\
      continuity (real_derivative y))
    (limy :
      tends_to_at_pos_infty
        (fun x : R => (real_derivative y x) ^ 2 + (y x) ^ 3)
        0)
    : tends_to_at_pos_infty y 0 /\
      tends_to_at_pos_infty (real_derivative y) 0.
Admitted.

title: putnam_1974_b2
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1974_b2:
  a continuously differentiable real function whose squared derivative plus
  cubed value tends to zero at positive infinity has both the function and
  its derivative tend to zero there. This file contains no proof.
*)

let analysis_output = open_out "/dev/null";;
let analysis_formatter = Format.formatter_of_out_channel analysis_output;;
let analysis_loaded =
  Toploop.use_file analysis_formatter "Library/analysis.ml";;
Format.pp_print_flush analysis_formatter ();;
close_out analysis_output;;
if not analysis_loaded then failwith "failed to load Library/analysis.ml";;

let statement =
  `let deriv =
     \(f:real->real) (x:real). @d. (f diffl d) x in
   let continuous =
     \(f:real->real).
       !x e:real.
         &0 < e
         ==> ?d:real.
               &0 < d /\
               !z:real. abs (z - x) < d ==> abs (f z - f x) < e in
   let continuously_differentiable =
     \(f:real->real).
       (!x:real. (f diffl (deriv f x)) x) /\
       continuous (deriv f) in
   let tends_at_posinfinity =
     \(f:real->real) (l:real).
       !e:real.
         &0 < e
         ==> ?B:real.
               !x:real. B <= x ==> abs (f x - l) < e in
   !y:real->real.
     continuously_differentiable y /\
     tends_at_posinfinity
       (\x:real. (deriv y x) pow 2 + (y x) pow 3)
       (&0)
     ==>
     tends_at_posinfinity y (&0) /\
     tends_at_posinfinity (deriv y) (&0)`;;

title: putnam_1974_b2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1974_b2:
;; a continuously differentiable real function for which (y')^2 + y^3 tends
;; to zero at positive infinity has both y and y' tending to zero there. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A continuous real function is represented by regular rational Cauchy data
;; on rational inputs. Continuity on every bounded interval gives a unique
;; extension to all real inputs. All bounds, precisions, and cutoffs below are
;; unbounded internal quantifiers.

(defun p74b2-value (function x precision)
  (apply$ function (list x precision)))

(defun p74b2-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and (rationalp x)
       (< 0 x)))

(defun p74b2-positive-natural-p (x)
  (and (natp x)
       (< 0 x)))

(defun p74b2-abs (x)
  (if (< x 0) (- x) x))

(defun p74b2-in-bounded-interval-p (x bound)
  (and (<= (- bound) x)
       (<= x bound)))

(defun-sk p74b2-cauchy-values-p (function)
  (forall (x epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (p74b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (p74b2-positive-rational-p eta))
     (and
      (rationalp (p74b2-value function x epsilon))
      (rationalp (p74b2-value function x eta))
      (<=
       (p74b2-abs
        (-
         (p74b2-value function x epsilon)
         (p74b2-value function x eta)))
       (+ epsilon eta))))))

(defun-sk p74b2-continuity-neighborhood-p
    (function bound epsilon delta)
  (forall (x z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p74b2-positive-natural-p bound)
      (rationalp x)
      (rationalp z)
      (p74b2-in-bounded-interval-p x bound)
      (p74b2-in-bounded-interval-p z bound)
      (p74b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (p74b2-positive-rational-p delta)
      (< (p74b2-abs (- x z)) delta))
     (<=
      (p74b2-abs
       (-
        (p74b2-value function x (* 1/8 epsilon))
        (p74b2-value function z (* 1/8 epsilon))))
      (* 1/2 epsilon)))))

(defun-sk p74b2-continuity-delta-exists-p
    (function bound epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (p74b2-positive-rational-p delta)
     (p74b2-continuity-neighborhood-p
      function bound epsilon delta))))

(defun-sk p74b2-continuous-values-p (function)
  (forall (bound epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (p74b2-positive-natural-p bound)
      (p74b2-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (p74b2-continuity-delta-exists-p
      function bound epsilon))))

(defun p74b2-continuous-real-function-p (function)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp function)
   (p74b2-cauchy-values-p function)
   (p74b2-continuous-values-p function)))

;; Uniform convergence of difference quotients on each bounded interval is
;; equivalent here to having a continuous derivative. The function samples
;; use precision proportional to |h|, so division by h preserves the stated
;; error tolerance.

(defun-sk p74b2-derivative-neighborhood-p
    (function derivative bound epsilon delta)
  (forall (x h)
    (implies
     (and
      (p74b2-positive-natural-p bound)
      (rationalp x)
      (p74b2-in-bounded-interval-p x bound)
      (rationalp h)
      (not (equal h 0))
      (p74b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (p74b2-positive-rational-p delta)
      (< (p74b2-abs h) delta))
     (let* ((function-precision
             (* (p74b2-abs h) (* 1/16 epsilon)))
            (shifted-value
             (p74b2-value
              function (+ x h) function-precision))
            (value
             (p74b2-value function x function-precision))
            (difference-quotient
             (* (- shifted-value value) (/ h)))
            (derivative-value
             (p74b2-value derivative x (* 1/8 epsilon))))
       (<=
        (p74b2-abs
         (- difference-quotient derivative-value))
        (* 1/2 epsilon))))))

(defun-sk p74b2-derivative-delta-exists-p
    (function derivative bound epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (p74b2-positive-rational-p delta)
     (p74b2-derivative-neighborhood-p
      function derivative bound epsilon delta))))

(defun-sk p74b2-derivative-convergence-p
    (function derivative)
  (forall (bound epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (p74b2-positive-natural-p bound)
      (p74b2-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (p74b2-derivative-delta-exists-p
      function derivative bound epsilon))))

(defun p74b2-derivative-candidate-p (function derivative)
  (and
   (p74b2-continuous-real-function-p function)
   (p74b2-continuous-real-function-p derivative)
   (p74b2-derivative-convergence-p function derivative)))

;; The derivative is unique. DEFCHOOSE conservatively selects that internally
;; characterized function and does not add a derivative parameter to the
;; source statement.

(defchoose p74b2-derivative-function
    (derivative)
    (function)
  (p74b2-derivative-candidate-p function derivative))

(defun p74b2-c1-p (function)
  (p74b2-derivative-candidate-p
   function
   (p74b2-derivative-function function)))

;; A Cauchy-named value is at most EPSILON in absolute value exactly when all
;; sufficiently precise rational samples satisfy that closed bound. Requiring
;; this for every positive EPSILON is the usual zero-limit condition.

(defun-sk p74b2-value-small-tail-p
    (function x epsilon precision-bound)
  (forall (precision)
    (implies
     (and
      (p74b2-positive-rational-p precision)
      (< precision precision-bound))
     (<=
      (p74b2-abs
       (p74b2-value function x precision))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p74b2-value-small-p (function x epsilon)
  (exists (precision-bound)
    (and
     (p74b2-positive-rational-p precision-bound)
     (p74b2-value-small-tail-p
      function x epsilon precision-bound))))

(defun-sk p74b2-zero-limit-tail-p
    (function epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (< cutoff x))
     (p74b2-value-small-p function x epsilon))))

(defun-sk p74b2-zero-limit-cutoff-exists-p
    (function epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (rationalp cutoff)
     (p74b2-zero-limit-tail-p
      function epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk p74b2-tends-to-zero-at-infinity-p (function)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p74b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (p74b2-zero-limit-cutoff-exists-p
      function epsilon))))

;; The hypothesis uses the same Cauchy semantics for
;; (derivative(x))^2 + (function(x))^3.

(defun p74b2-expression-sample
    (function derivative x precision)
  (let ((y (p74b2-value function x precision))
        (dy (p74b2-value derivative x precision)))
    (+ (* dy dy)
       (* y (* y y)))))

(defun-sk p74b2-expression-small-tail-p
    (function derivative x epsilon precision-bound)
  (forall (precision)
    (implies
     (and
      (p74b2-positive-rational-p precision)
      (< precision precision-bound))
     (<=
      (p74b2-abs
       (p74b2-expression-sample
        function derivative x precision))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p74b2-expression-small-p
    (function derivative x epsilon)
  (exists (precision-bound)
    (and
     (p74b2-positive-rational-p precision-bound)
     (p74b2-expression-small-tail-p
      function derivative x epsilon precision-bound))))

(defun-sk p74b2-expression-limit-tail-p
    (function derivative epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (< cutoff x))
     (p74b2-expression-small-p
      function derivative x epsilon))))

(defun-sk p74b2-expression-limit-cutoff-exists-p
    (function derivative epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (rationalp cutoff)
     (p74b2-expression-limit-tail-p
      function derivative epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk p74b2-expression-tends-to-zero-at-infinity-p
    (function derivative)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p74b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (p74b2-expression-limit-cutoff-exists-p
      function derivative epsilon))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1974-b2-statement (y)
  (let ((dy (p74b2-derivative-function y)))
    (implies
     (and
      (p74b2-c1-p y)
      (p74b2-expression-tends-to-zero-at-infinity-p
       y dy))
     (and
      (p74b2-tends-to-zero-at-infinity-p y)
      (p74b2-tends-to-zero-at-infinity-p dy)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1974_b2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1974_b2:
-- a continuously differentiable real function for which (y')^2 + y^3 tends
-- to zero at positive infinity has both y and y' tending to zero there.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ContinuousAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ContinuousAt {R} reals function point =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals (function point) epsilon (function x)))

Continuous :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
Continuous {R} reals function =
  (point : R) ->
  ContinuousAt reals function point

whole :
  {A : Set} ->
  A ->
  Set
whole _ =
  Top

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
differenceQuotient reals function point x =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals (function x) (function point))
    (subtract reals x point)

DerivativeWithinAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  (R -> Set) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeWithinAt {R} reals function domain point derivativeValue =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        domain x ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        x != point ->
        CloseTo reals derivativeValue epsilon
          (differenceQuotient reals function point x)))

DerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeAt reals function point derivativeValue =
  DerivativeWithinAt
    reals
    function
    whole
    point
    derivativeValue

record StandardRealCalculus
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) : Set1 where

  field
    derivative : (R -> R) -> R -> R
    derivative-correct :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      (point derivativeValue : R) ->
      DerivativeAt reals function point derivativeValue ->
      derivative function point == derivativeValue
    derivative-totalized-at-zero :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      (point : R) ->
      Not (Exists R (DerivativeAt reals function point)) ->
      derivative function point == zeroR reals

open StandardRealCalculus

C1Differentiable :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardRealCalculus reals ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
C1Differentiable {R} reals calculus function =
  ((point : R) ->
    DerivativeAt reals function point
      (derivative calculus function point))
  and
  Continuous reals (derivative calculus function)

TendsAtPositiveInfinity :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
TendsAtPositiveInfinity {R} reals function limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ cutoff ->
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals cutoff x ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (function x))

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

cube :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
cube reals x =
  multiply reals (square reals x) x

energyExpression :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardRealCalculus reals ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
energyExpression reals calculus y x =
  add reals
    (square reals (derivative calculus y x))
    (cube reals (y x))

putnam-1974-b2 : Set1
putnam-1974-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (calculus : StandardRealCalculus reals) ->
  (y : R -> R) ->
  C1Differentiable reals calculus y ->
  TendsAtPositiveInfinity reals
    (energyExpression reals calculus y)
    (zeroR reals) ->
  TendsAtPositiveInfinity reals y (zeroR reals)
  and
  TendsAtPositiveInfinity reals
    (derivative calculus y)
    (zeroR reals)

  cubed value tends to zero at positive infinity has both its value and

open pred_setTheory realTheory real_topologyTheory limTheory;

val putnam_1974_b2 =

      (!x : real. higher_differentiable 1 y x) /\

  putnam_1974_b2: a continuously differentiable real function whose
  squared derivative plus cubed value tends to zero at positive infinity
  has both its value and derivative tend to zero. This file contains no proof.

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The variable y ranges over total real-valued functions on the reals.
  Membership in ( ( C^n ` RR ) ` 1 ) is set.mm's native assertion of global
  continuous differentiability through order one, and
  ( ( RR Dn y ) ` 1 ) is its real derivative. The relation ~~>r expresses
  convergence at positive infinity for real-indexed functions.

  Thus the antecedent and both conjuncts of the conclusion are direct
  target-native renderings of the three source limits. The final declaration
  is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p
  proof statement.
$)

${
  $d x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-1974-b2 $a |- A. y e. ( RR ^m RR )
    (
      (
        y e. ( ( C^n ` RR ) ` 1 )
        /\
        (
          x e. RR |->
            (
              ( ( ( ( RR Dn y ) ` 1 ) ` x ) ^ 2 )
              +
              ( ( y ` x ) ^ 3 )
            )
        )
        ~~>r
        0
      )
      ->
      (
        (
          x e. RR |->
            ( y ` x )
        )
        ~~>r
        0
        /\
        (
          x e. RR |->
            ( ( ( RR Dn y ) ` 1 ) ` x )
        )
        ~~>r
        0
      )
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1974_b2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1974_b2:
% a globally continuously differentiable real function whose squared
% derivative plus cubed value tends to zero has both value and derivative
% tend to zero at positive infinity. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1974_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  continuous(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real), (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (z: real):
          abs(z - x) < delta IMPLIES
            abs(f(z) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  has_derivative_at(
      f: real_function,
      derivative, x: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (h: real):
          (NOT (h = 0) AND abs(h) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                f(x + h) - f(x)
                  - derivative * h)
                < epsilon_value * abs(h)

  differentiable_at(f: real_function, x: real): bool =
    EXISTS (derivative: real):
      has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x)

  derivative_value(f: real_function, x: real): real =
    IF differentiable_at(f, x) THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (derivative: real):
          has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  derivative_function(f: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real): derivative_value(f, x)

  continuously_differentiable(f: real_function): bool =
    (FORALL (x: real): differentiable_at(f, x))
      AND continuous(derivative_function(f))

  tends_to_at_positive_infinity(
      f: real_function,
      limit_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (threshold: real):
        FORALL (x: real):
          threshold <= x IMPLIES
            abs(f(x) - limit_value) < epsilon_value

  differential_expression(y: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      derivative_function(y)(x) ^ 2 + y(x) ^ 3

  putnam_1974_b2: bool =
    FORALL (y: real_function):
      (continuously_differentiable(y)
        AND tends_to_at_positive_infinity(
          differential_expression(y), 0))
      IMPLIES
        tends_to_at_positive_infinity(y, 0)
          AND tends_to_at_positive_infinity(
            derivative_function(y), 0)
END putnam_1974_b2

title: putnam_1974_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1974_b3:
;; a real number alpha satisfying cos(pi*alpha) = 1/3 is irrational.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source statement is equivalent to the nonexistence of a rational
;; alpha with cos(pi*alpha)=1/3.  If alpha=p/q with q>0, the Chebyshev identity
;; gives T_q(1/3)=cos(p*pi), hence T_q(1/3) is 1 or -1.  Conversely, if
;; T_q(1/3) is 1 or -1, then q*arccos(1/3) is an integral multiple of pi,
;; producing a rational alpha with the source cosine value.  Thus it is
;; equivalent to require T_q(1/3) != +/-1 for every positive integer q.
;;
;; The integer S_q=3^q*T_q(1/3) satisfies
;; S_0=S_1=1 and S_q=2*S_(q-1)-9*S_(q-2), so comparison with +/-3^q
;; represents that condition exactly without adding a real cosine primitive.

(defun putnam-1974-b3-scaled-chebyshev (q)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix q)))
  (cond
   ((zp q) 1)
   ((equal q 1) 1)
   (t
    (-
     (* 2
        (putnam-1974-b3-scaled-chebyshev (- q 1)))
     (* 9
        (putnam-1974-b3-scaled-chebyshev (- q 2)))))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1974-b3-statement (q)
  (implies
