(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1977_b3:
  eventual balancing of positive irrational real triples under the specified
  coordinatewise doubling map, with the answer false. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

let analysis_output = open_out "/dev/null";;
let analysis_formatter = Format.formatter_of_out_channel analysis_output;;
let iter_loaded =
  Toploop.use_file analysis_formatter "Library/iter.ml";;
Format.pp_print_flush analysis_formatter ();;
close_out analysis_output;;
if not iter_loaded then failwith "failed to load Library/iter.ml";;

let statement =
  `let is_rational =
     \x:real.
       ?p q:int.
         ~(q = (&0:int)) /\
         x = real_of_int p / real_of_int q in
   let P =
     \(a,b,c):real#real#real.
       ~is_rational a /\
       ~is_rational b /\
       ~is_rational c /\
       &0 < a /\
       &0 < b /\
       &0 < c /\
       a + b + c = &1 in
   let balanced =
     \(a,b,c):real#real#real.
       a < &1 / &2 /\
       b < &1 / &2 /\
       c < &1 / &2 in
   let B =
     \(a,b,c):real#real#real.
       ((if a > &1 / &2 then &2 * a - &1 else &2 * a),
        (if b > &1 / &2 then &2 * b - &1 else &2 * b),
        (if c > &1 / &2 then &2 * c - &1 else &2 * c)) in
   let putnam_1977_b3_solution = F in
   ((!t:real#real#real.
       P t ==> ?n:num. balanced (ITER n B t)) <=>
    putnam_1977_b3_solution)`;;

title: putnam_1977_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1977_b3:
;; whether every positive irrational real triple summing to one has a finite
;; balanced iterate under the specified coordinatewise doubling map; the
;; proposed universal assertion is equivalent to False. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The scalar domain is an arbitrary Dedekind-complete ordered field, hence a
;; presentation of the real numbers up to order-preserving field isomorphism.
;; Tame APPLY$ function objects present its carrier, operations, order, and
;; subsets. Every field, order, and completeness law used by the encoding is
;; an explicit hypothesis of the root statement.

(defun p77b3-member-p (carrier value)
  (if (apply$ carrier (list value)) t nil))

(defun p77b3-unary-value (operation value)
  (apply$ operation (list value)))

(defun p77b3-binary-value (operation left right)
  (apply$ operation (list left right)))

(defun-sk p77b3-field-laws-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p77b3-member-p carrier x)
      (p77b3-member-p carrier y)
      (p77b3-member-p carrier z))
     (let* ((x-plus-y (p77b3-binary-value add x y))
            (y-plus-z (p77b3-binary-value add y z))
            (x-times-y (p77b3-binary-value multiply x y))
            (y-times-z (p77b3-binary-value multiply y z))
            (minus-x (p77b3-unary-value negate x))
            (inverse-x (p77b3-unary-value inverse x)))
       (and
        (p77b3-member-p carrier x-plus-y)
        (p77b3-member-p carrier x-times-y)
        (p77b3-member-p carrier minus-x)
        (p77b3-member-p carrier inverse-x)
        (equal
         (p77b3-binary-value add x-plus-y z)
         (p77b3-binary-value add x y-plus-z))
        (equal x-plus-y (p77b3-binary-value add y x))
        (equal (p77b3-binary-value add x zero) x)
        (equal (p77b3-binary-value add x minus-x) zero)
        (equal
         (p77b3-binary-value multiply x-times-y z)
         (p77b3-binary-value multiply x y-times-z))
        (equal x-times-y (p77b3-binary-value multiply y x))
        (equal (p77b3-binary-value multiply x one) x)
        (implies
         (equal x zero)
         (equal inverse-x zero))
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (equal
          (p77b3-binary-value multiply x inverse-x)
          one))
        (equal
         (p77b3-binary-value multiply x y-plus-z)
         (p77b3-binary-value
          add
          (p77b3-binary-value multiply x y)
          (p77b3-binary-value multiply x z))))))))

(defun-sk p77b3-order-laws-p
    (carrier add multiply zero less)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p77b3-member-p carrier x)
      (p77b3-member-p carrier y)
      (p77b3-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (not (p77b3-binary-value less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (p77b3-binary-value less x y)
       (p77b3-binary-value less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (p77b3-binary-value less x y)
        (p77b3-binary-value less y z))
       (p77b3-binary-value less x z))
      (implies
       (p77b3-binary-value less x y)
       (p77b3-binary-value
        less
        (p77b3-binary-value add x z)
        (p77b3-binary-value add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (p77b3-binary-value less zero x)
        (p77b3-binary-value less zero y))
       (p77b3-binary-value
        less
        zero
        (p77b3-binary-value multiply x y)))))))

(defun-sk p77b3-valid-set-p (carrier set)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (apply$ set (list x))
     (p77b3-member-p carrier x))))

(defun-sk p77b3-set-nonempty-p (carrier set)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (p77b3-member-p carrier x)
     (apply$ set (list x)))))

(defun-sk p77b3-upper-bound-p
    (carrier less set bound)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (p77b3-member-p carrier x)
      (apply$ set (list x)))
     (not (p77b3-binary-value less bound x)))))

(defun-sk p77b3-bounded-above-p (carrier less set)
  (exists (bound)
    (and
     (p77b3-member-p carrier bound)
     (p77b3-upper-bound-p carrier less set bound))))

(defun-sk p77b3-least-upper-bound-p
    (carrier less set supremum)
  (forall (bound)
    (implies
     (and
      (p77b3-member-p carrier bound)
      (p77b3-upper-bound-p carrier less set bound))
     (not (p77b3-binary-value less bound supremum)))))

(defun p77b3-supremum-p
    (carrier less set supremum)
  (and
   (p77b3-member-p carrier supremum)
   (p77b3-upper-bound-p carrier less set supremum)
   (p77b3-least-upper-bound-p
    carrier less set supremum)))

(defun-sk p77b3-has-supremum-p (carrier less set)
  (exists (supremum)
    (p77b3-supremum-p
     carrier less set supremum)))

(defun-sk p77b3-dedekind-complete-p (carrier less)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (tamep-functionp set)
      (p77b3-valid-set-p carrier set)
      (p77b3-set-nonempty-p carrier set)
      (p77b3-bounded-above-p carrier less set))
     (p77b3-has-supremum-p carrier less set))))

(defun p77b3-real-field-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp add)
   (tamep-functionp multiply)
   (tamep-functionp negate)
   (tamep-functionp inverse)
   (tamep-functionp less)
   (p77b3-member-p carrier zero)
   (p77b3-member-p carrier one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (p77b3-field-laws-p
    carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one)
   (p77b3-order-laws-p
    carrier add multiply zero less)
   (p77b3-binary-value less zero one)
   (p77b3-dedekind-complete-p carrier less)))

;; Arithmetic in the represented real field.

(defun p77b3-natural-value (n zero one add)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      zero
    (p77b3-binary-value
     add
     one
     (p77b3-natural-value (- n 1) zero one add))))

(defun p77b3-integer-value (n zero one add negate)
  (if (< n 0)
      (p77b3-unary-value
       negate
       (p77b3-natural-value (- n) zero one add))
    (p77b3-natural-value n zero one add)))

(defun p77b3-subtract-value (add negate left right)
  (p77b3-binary-value
   add left (p77b3-unary-value negate right)))

(defun p77b3-two-value (one add)
  (p77b3-binary-value add one one))

(defun p77b3-half-value (one add inverse)
  (p77b3-unary-value
   inverse (p77b3-two-value one add)))

;; An element is rational exactly when it belongs to the prime subfield:
;; denominator*x = numerator for some integer numerator and positive natural
;; denominator. Its negation is therefore the source's Irrational predicate.

(defun-sk p77b3-rational-real-p
    (value add multiply negate zero one)
  (exists (numerator denominator)
    (and
     (integerp numerator)
     (posp denominator)
     (equal
      (p77b3-binary-value
       multiply
       (p77b3-natural-value denominator zero one add)
       value)
      (p77b3-integer-value
       numerator zero one add negate)))))

(defun p77b3-irrational-real-p
    (carrier value add multiply negate zero one)
  (and
   (p77b3-member-p carrier value)
   (not
    (p77b3-rational-real-p
     value add multiply negate zero one))))

(defun p77b3-positive-real-p
    (carrier less zero value)
  (and
   (p77b3-member-p carrier value)
   (p77b3-binary-value less zero value)))

(defun p77b3-source-triple-p
    (carrier add multiply negate zero one less a b c)
  (and
   (p77b3-irrational-real-p
    carrier a add multiply negate zero one)
   (p77b3-irrational-real-p
    carrier b add multiply negate zero one)
   (p77b3-irrational-real-p
    carrier c add multiply negate zero one)
   (p77b3-positive-real-p carrier less zero a)
   (p77b3-positive-real-p carrier less zero b)
   (p77b3-positive-real-p carrier less zero c)
   (equal
    (p77b3-binary-value
     add
     (p77b3-binary-value add a b)
     c)
    one)))

(defun p77b3-balanced-p
    (less half a b c)
  (and
   (p77b3-binary-value less a half)
   (p77b3-binary-value less b half)
   (p77b3-binary-value less c half)))

(defun p77b3-balance-coordinate
    (value add multiply negate one less half)
  (let ((twice
         (p77b3-binary-value
          multiply
          (p77b3-two-value one add)
          value)))
    (if (p77b3-binary-value less half value)
        (p77b3-subtract-value add negate twice one)
      twice)))

(defun p77b3-iterate-coordinate
    (value n add multiply negate one less half)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      value
    (p77b3-iterate-coordinate
     (p77b3-balance-coordinate
      value add multiply negate one less half)
     (- n 1)
     add multiply negate one less half)))

(defun p77b3-balanced-iterate-p
    (a b c n add multiply negate one less half)
  (p77b3-balanced-p
   less
   half
   (p77b3-iterate-coordinate
    a n add multiply negate one less half)
   (p77b3-iterate-coordinate
    b n add multiply negate one less half)
   (p77b3-iterate-coordinate
    c n add multiply negate one less half)))

(defun-sk p77b3-balanced-iterate-exists-p
    (a b c add multiply negate one less half)
  (exists (n)
    (and
     (natp n)
     (p77b3-balanced-iterate-p
      a b c n add multiply negate one less half))))

;; This is the source's complete quantified claim:
;;   forall t, P(t) implies that some natural iterate B^n(t) is balanced.

(defun-sk p77b3-all-triples-eventually-balanced-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (forall (a b c)
    (implies
     (p77b3-source-triple-p
      carrier add multiply negate zero one less a b c)
     (p77b3-balanced-iterate-exists-p
      a b c add multiply negate one less
      (p77b3-half-value one add inverse)))))

(defun putnam-1977-b3-solution ()
  nil)

(defun putnambench-putnam-1977-b3-statement
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (implies
   (p77b3-real-field-p
    carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
   (iff
    (p77b3-all-triples-eventually-balanced-p
     carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
    (putnam-1977-b3-solution))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1977_b3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1977_b3:
-- the universal claim that iterating the specified componentwise balancing
-- map eventually balances every positive irrational unit-sum triple is false.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

    strict-order-decidable :
      (x y : R) ->
      (lessOrEqual x y and x != y)
      or
      Not (lessOrEqual x y and x != y)

open CompleteOrderedRealField

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

IsRational :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
IsRational reals x =
  Exists Int
    (\ numerator ->
      Exists Int
        (\ denominator ->
          denominator != pos zero
          and
          x ==
          divide reals
            (fromInt reals numerator)
            (fromInt reals denominator)))

Irrational :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
Irrational reals x =
  Not (IsRational reals x)

record Triple (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor triple
  field
    first-coordinate  : R
    second-coordinate : R
    third-coordinate  : R

open Triple

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

oneHalf :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
oneHalf reals =
  divide reals
    (oneR reals)
    (fromNat reals twoN)

PositiveIrrationalUnitTriple :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Triple R ->
  Set
PositiveIrrationalUnitTriple reals t =
  Irrational reals (first-coordinate t)
  and
  Irrational reals (second-coordinate t)
  and
  Irrational reals (third-coordinate t)
  and
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (first-coordinate t)
  and
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (second-coordinate t)
  and
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (third-coordinate t)
  and
  add reals
    (add reals (first-coordinate t) (second-coordinate t))
    (third-coordinate t)
    ==
    oneR reals

Balanced :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Triple R ->
  Set
Balanced reals t =
  StrictLess reals (first-coordinate t) (oneHalf reals)
  and
  StrictLess reals (second-coordinate t) (oneHalf reals)
  and
  StrictLess reals (third-coordinate t) (oneHalf reals)

balanceCoordinate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
balanceCoordinate reals x
  with strict-order-decidable reals (oneHalf reals) x
... | left _ =
  add reals
    (multiply reals (fromNat reals twoN) x)
    (negate reals (oneR reals))
... | right _ =
  multiply reals (fromNat reals twoN) x

balancingAct :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Triple R ->
  Triple R
balancingAct reals t =
  triple
    (balanceCoordinate reals (first-coordinate t))
    (balanceCoordinate reals (second-coordinate t))
    (balanceCoordinate reals (third-coordinate t))

iterate :
  {A : Set} ->
  (A -> A) ->
  Nat ->
  A ->
  A
iterate f zero x =
  x
iterate f (suc n) x =
  iterate f n (f x)

EventuallyBalanced :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Set
EventuallyBalanced {R} reals =
  (t : Triple R) ->
  PositiveIrrationalUnitTriple reals t ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ n ->
      Balanced reals
        (iterate (balancingAct reals) n t))

Equivalent : Set -> Set -> Set
Equivalent A B =
  (A -> B) and (B -> A)

putnam-1977-b3-solution : Set
putnam-1977-b3-solution =
  Bottom

putnam-1977-b3 : Set1
putnam-1977-b3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Equivalent
    (EventuallyBalanced reals)
    putnam-1977-b3-solution

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1977_b3:
  whether iterating the coordinatewise doubling balancing act on every
  positive irrational real triple summing to one eventually makes all three
  coordinates less than one half. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_of_ratTheory;

val putnam_1977_b3 =
  ``let P =
      \w : real # (real # real).
        FST w NOTIN q_set /\
        FST (SND w) NOTIN q_set /\
        SND (SND w) NOTIN q_set /\
        0 < FST w /\
        0 < FST (SND w) /\
        0 < SND (SND w) /\
        FST w + FST (SND w) + SND (SND w) = 1
    in
    let balanced =
      \w : real # (real # real).
        FST w < 1 / 2 /\
        FST (SND w) < 1 / 2 /\
        SND (SND w) < 1 / 2
    in
    let B =
      \w : real # (real # real).
        (if FST w > 1 / 2 then 2 * FST w - 1 else 2 * FST w,
         (if FST (SND w) > 1 / 2
          then 2 * FST (SND w) - 1
          else 2 * FST (SND w),
          if SND (SND w) > 1 / 2
          then 2 * SND (SND w) - 1
          else 2 * SND (SND w)))
    in
    let putnam_1977_b3_solution = F
    in
      ((!t : real # (real # real).
          P t ==> ?n : num. balanced (FUNPOW B n t))
       <=>
       putnam_1977_b3_solution)``;

$(

  putnam_1977_b3: not every positive irrational real triple with coordinate
  sum one becomes balanced after finitely many iterations of the specified
  coordinatewise doubling map. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P77B3R3 is the set of real ordered triples, represented by set.mm's nested
  pairs <. <. a , b >. , c >.  P77B3Admissible is the source predicate P:
  all three coordinates are positive and irrational and have sum one.
  P77B3Balanced requires all three coordinates to be strictly below one half.

  P77B3Step is exactly the source map B. IterComp is set.mm's native
  finite-iteration operator, so ((IterComp ` P77B3Step) ` n) ` t is B
  iterated n times at t, including the identity iterate at n = 0.

  The ground-truth solution is False. Therefore the final unproved $a
  assertion is the negation of the universal eventual-balancing proposition,
  which is logically equivalent to that proposition being equivalent to
  False. This database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P77B3R3 P77B3Admissible P77B3Balanced P77B3Step $.

p77b3-space-syntax $a class P77B3R3 $.
p77b3-admissible-syntax $a wff ( P77B3Admissible t ) $.
p77b3-balanced-syntax $a wff ( P77B3Balanced A ) $.
p77b3-step-syntax $a class P77B3Step $.

p77b3-space-definition $a |- P77B3R3 = ( ( RR X. RR ) X. RR ) $.

p77b3-admissible-definition $a |- (
  ( P77B3Admissible t )
  <->
  (
    ( 1st ` ( 1st ` t ) ) e/ QQ
    /\
    (
      ( 2nd ` ( 1st ` t ) ) e/ QQ
      /\
      (
        ( 2nd ` t ) e/ QQ
        /\
        (
          0 < ( 1st ` ( 1st ` t ) )
          /\
          (
            0 < ( 2nd ` ( 1st ` t ) )
            /\
            (
              0 < ( 2nd ` t )
              /\
              (
                (
                  ( 1st ` ( 1st ` t ) )
                  +
                  ( 2nd ` ( 1st ` t ) )
                )
                +
                ( 2nd ` t )
              )
              =
              1
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

p77b3-balanced-definition $a |- (
  ( P77B3Balanced A )
  <->
  (
    ( 1st ` ( 1st ` A ) ) < ( 1 / 2 )
    /\
    (
      ( 2nd ` ( 1st ` A ) ) < ( 1 / 2 )
      /\
      ( 2nd ` A ) < ( 1 / 2 )
    )
  )
) $.

p77b3-step-definition $a |- P77B3Step = (
  t e. P77B3R3 |->
    <.
      <.
        if (
          ( 1 / 2 ) < ( 1st ` ( 1st ` t ) ) ,
          ( ( 2 x. ( 1st ` ( 1st ` t ) ) ) - 1 ) ,
          ( 2 x. ( 1st ` ( 1st ` t ) ) )

        ,
        if (
          ( 1 / 2 ) < ( 2nd ` ( 1st ` t ) ) ,
          ( ( 2 x. ( 2nd ` ( 1st ` t ) ) ) - 1 ) ,
          ( 2 x. ( 2nd ` ( 1st ` t ) ) )
        )
      >.
      ,
      if (
        ( 1 / 2 ) < ( 2nd ` t ) ,
        ( ( 2 x. ( 2nd ` t ) ) - 1 ) ,
        ( 2 x. ( 2nd ` t ) )
      )
    >.
) $.

${

    A. t e. P77B3R3

          (
            P77B3Balanced

                `
                t

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1977_b3:
% positive irrational real triples summing to one do not always become
% balanced after finitely many iterations of the balancing map. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1977_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  triple: TYPE =
    [# first: real, second: real, third: real #]

  positive_irrational_unit_triple(t: triple): bool =
    NOT rational?(first(t))
      AND NOT rational?(second(t))
      AND NOT rational?(third(t))
      AND first(t) > 0
      AND second(t) > 0
      AND third(t) > 0
      AND first(t) + second(t) + third(t) = 1

  balanced(t: triple): bool =
    first(t) < (1 :: real) / 2
      AND second(t) < (1 :: real) / 2
      AND third(t) < (1 :: real) / 2

  balance_coordinate(x: real): real =
    IF x > (1 :: real) / 2 THEN
      2 * x - 1
    ELSE
      2 * x
    ENDIF

  balance_step(t: triple): triple =
    (# first := balance_coordinate(first(t)),
       second := balance_coordinate(second(t)),
       third := balance_coordinate(third(t)) #)

  balance_iterate(t: triple, count: nat): RECURSIVE triple =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      t
    ELSE
      balance_step(balance_iterate(t, count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  putnam_1977_b3_solution: bool = FALSE

  putnam_1977_b3: bool =
    (FORALL (t: triple):
      positive_irrational_unit_triple(t)
        IMPLIES
          EXISTS (count: nat):
            balanced(balance_iterate(t, count)))
      IFF putnam_1977_b3_solution
END putnam_1977_b3

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1977_b5:
;; a strict quadratic-sum bound for n real numbers implies that A is less
;; than twice every pairwise product. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A length-n list is definitionally equivalent to a function on Fin n, with
;; list order corresponding to the index order. Standard ACL2 represents the
;; entries by exact rationals. This is bidirectionally equivalent to validity
;; over the reals. One direction is immediate. Conversely, a real
;; counterexample has positive slack in the strict sum hypothesis. If its
;; failed pairwise conclusion is an equality, increasing A by less than that
;; slack makes the failure strict while preserving the hypothesis. Continuity
;; then gives a neighborhood of counterexamples, and density supplies rational
;; values in that neighborhood.
;;
;; The strict sum hypothesis is essential and agrees with the Lean, Isabelle,
;; and stated Putnam formulation. Replacing it by a non-strict inequality, as
;; in the Rocq spelling, admits n=2, values=(1 1), A=2 as a counterexample.

(defun putnam-1977-b5-rational-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and (rationalp (car values))
           (putnam-1977-b5-rational-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-1977-b5-sum (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (+ (car values)
         (putnam-1977-b5-sum (cdr values)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1977-b5-sum-squares (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (+ (* (car values) (car values))
         (putnam-1977-b5-sum-squares (cdr values)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1977-b5-bound-against-rest-p
    (first rest a)
  (if (consp rest)
      (and (< a (* 2 first (car rest)))
           (putnam-1977-b5-bound-against-rest-p
            first (cdr rest) a))
    t))

(defun putnam-1977-b5-all-pairs-p (values a)
  (if (consp values)
      (and (putnam-1977-b5-bound-against-rest-p
            (car values) (cdr values) a)
           (putnam-1977-b5-all-pairs-p (cdr values) a))
    t))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1977-b5-statement
    (n values a)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (< 1 n)
        (true-listp values)
        (equal (len values) n)
        (putnam-1977-b5-rational-list-p values)
        (rationalp a)
        (< (+ a
              (putnam-1977-b5-sum-squares values))
           (* (/ 1 (- n 1))
              (expt (putnam-1977-b5-sum values) 2))))
   (putnam-1977-b5-all-pairs-p values a)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1977_b5:
-- a strict quadratic bound on a finite real sequence forces every ordered
-- pair of distinct entries to have product greater than A / 2.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1977B5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finToNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (finToNat i)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

module Putnam1977B5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  hypothesisRightSide :
    {n : Nat} ->
    (Fin n -> R) ->
    R
  hypothesisRightSide {n} a =
    multiply reals
      (divide reals
        (oneR reals)
        (subtract reals
          (fromNat reals n)
          (oneR reals)))
      (square reals (sumFin reals a))

  pairBound :
    {n : Nat} ->
    (Fin n -> R) ->
    R ->
    Set
  pairBound {n} a A =
    (i j : Fin n) ->
    finToNat i <N finToNat j ->
    StrictLess reals
      A
      (multiply reals
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals twoN)
          (a i))
        (a j))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (n : Nat) ->
    twoN <=N n ->
    (a : Fin n -> R) ->
    (A : R) ->
    StrictLess reals
      (add reals
        A
        (sumFin reals (\ i -> square reals (a i))))
      (hypothesisRightSide a) ->
    pairBound a A

putnam-1977-b5 : Set1
putnam-1977-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1977B5Statement.proposition reals

  putnam_1977_b5: a strict quadratic-sum bound forces A below twice every
  pairwise product among n real numbers. This file contains no proof.

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  NN is SetMM's class of positive integers, and the explicit 1 < n hypothesis
  matches the published n > 1 assumption. The finite function a has domain
  1 ... n. Both inequalities are strict, unlike the non-strict hypothesis in

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a i j n r $.

  putnambench-putnam-1977-b5 $a |-
    A. n e. NN
    A. a e. ( RR ^m ( 1 ... n ) )
    A. r e. RR
      (
        (
          1 < n
          /\
          (
            r
            +
            sum_ i e. ( 1 ... n )
              ( ( a ` i ) ^ 2 )
          )
          <
          (
            (
              sum_ i e. ( 1 ... n )
                ( a ` i )
            )
            ^
            2
          )
          /
          ( n - 1 )
        )
        ->
        A. i e. ( 1 ... n )
        A. j e. ( 1 ... n )
          (
            i < j

title: putnam_1977_b5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1977_b5:
% a strict quadratic bound on a finite real sequence forces every pair of
% distinct ordered terms to have product greater than A/2. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1977_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  prefix_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      prefix_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  square_prefix_sum(
      values: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      square_prefix_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1) ^ 2
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  putnam_1977_b5: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (a: real_sequence), (A: real):
      (n > 1
        AND A + square_prefix_sum(a, n)
          < 1 / ((n :: real) - 1) * prefix_sum(a, n) ^ 2)
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (i, j: nat):
          (i < n AND j < n AND i < j)
            IMPLIES A < 2 * a(i) * a(j)
END putnam_1977_b5

title: putnam_1977_b6
content:
import Mathlib

open RingHom Set Nat Filter Topology

/--
Let $G$ be a group and $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ with $h$ elements. Suppose that $G$ contains some element $a$ such that $(xa)^3 = 1$ for all $x \in H$ (here $1$ represents the identity element of $G$). Let $P$ be the subset of $G$ containing all products of the form $x_1 a x_2 a \cdots x_n a$ with $n \ge 1$ and $x_i \in H$ for all $i \in \{1, 2, \dots, n\}$. Prove that $P$ is a finite set and contains no more than $3h^2$ elements.
-/
theorem putnam_1977_b6
{G : Type*}
[Group G]
(H : Subgroup G)
[Finite H]
(h : ℕ)
(h_def : h = Nat.card H)
(a : G)
(ha : ∀ x : H, (x*a)^3 = 1)
(P : Set G)
(hP : P = {g : G | ∃ xs : List H, (xs.length ≥ 1) ∧ g = (List.map (fun h : H => h*a) xs).prod})
: (Finite P) ∧ (P.ncard ≤ 3*h^2) :=
sorry

title: putnam_1977_b6
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1977_b6:
   a finite subgroup H and an element a satisfying (x a)^3 = 1 yield at most
   3 h^2 nonempty products x1 a x2 a ... xn a. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Arith.PeanoNat Ensembles Finite_sets.

Record putnam_1977_b6_group (G : Type) : Type := {
  putnam_1977_b6_mul : G -> G -> G;
  putnam_1977_b6_one : G;
  putnam_1977_b6_inv : G -> G;
  putnam_1977_b6_assoc :
    forall x y z : G,
      putnam_1977_b6_mul x (putnam_1977_b6_mul y z) =
      putnam_1977_b6_mul (putnam_1977_b6_mul x y) z;
  putnam_1977_b6_left_identity :
    forall x : G, putnam_1977_b6_mul putnam_1977_b6_one x = x;
  putnam_1977_b6_right_identity :
    forall x : G, putnam_1977_b6_mul x putnam_1977_b6_one = x;
  putnam_1977_b6_left_inverse :
    forall x : G,
      putnam_1977_b6_mul (putnam_1977_b6_inv x) x =
      putnam_1977_b6_one;
  putnam_1977_b6_right_inverse :
    forall x : G,
      putnam_1977_b6_mul x (putnam_1977_b6_inv x) =
      putnam_1977_b6_one
}.

Arguments putnam_1977_b6_mul {G} _ _ _.
Arguments putnam_1977_b6_one {G} _.
Arguments putnam_1977_b6_inv {G} _ _.

Definition putnam_1977_b6_is_subgroup
    {G : Type}
    (grp : putnam_1977_b6_group G)
    (H : Ensemble G) : Prop :=
  H (putnam_1977_b6_one grp) /\
  (forall x y : G,
    H x ->
    H y ->
    H (putnam_1977_b6_mul grp x y)) /\
  (forall x : G,
    H x ->
    H (putnam_1977_b6_inv grp x)).

Fixpoint putnam_1977_b6_power
    {G : Type}
    (grp : putnam_1977_b6_group G)
    (x : G)
    (n : nat) : G :=
  match n with
  | O => putnam_1977_b6_one grp
  | S k =>
      putnam_1977_b6_mul grp x (putnam_1977_b6_power grp x k)
  end.

Definition putnam_1977_b6_product
    {G : Type}
    (grp : putnam_1977_b6_group G)
    (a : G)
    (xs : list G) : G :=
  fold_right
    (fun x product : G =>
      putnam_1977_b6_mul grp
        (putnam_1977_b6_mul grp x a)
        product)
    (putnam_1977_b6_one grp)
    xs.

Theorem putnam_1977_b6
    (G : Type)
    (grp : putnam_1977_b6_group G)
    (H P : Ensemble G)
    (h : nat)
    (a : G)
    (hHsubgroup : putnam_1977_b6_is_subgroup grp H)
    (hHcard : cardinal G H h)
    (ha :
      forall x : G,
        H x ->
        putnam_1977_b6_power
          grp
          (putnam_1977_b6_mul grp x a)
          3 =
        putnam_1977_b6_one grp)
    (hP :
      forall g : G,
        P g <->
        exists xs : list G,
          xs <> nil /\
          Forall H xs /\
          g = putnam_1977_b6_product grp a xs) :
  Finite G P /\
  exists p : nat,
    cardinal G P p /\
    (p <= 3 * h ^ 2)%nat.
Admitted.

title: putnam_1977_b6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1977_b6:
  a finite subgroup whose translates by a fixed group element all have cube
  equal to the identity generates at most three times the square of its order
  distinct nonempty alternating products. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let is_group =
     \(mul:G->G->G) (identity:G) (ginv:G->G).
       (!x y z:G. mul (mul x y) z = mul x (mul y z)) /\
       (!x:G. mul identity x = x /\ mul x identity = x) /\
       (!x:G.
          mul (ginv x) x = identity /\ mul x (ginv x) = identity) in
   let is_subgroup =
     \(mul:G->G->G) (identity:G) (ginv:G->G) (H:G->bool).
       identity IN H /\
       (!x:G. x IN H ==> ginv x IN H) /\
       (!x y:G. x IN H /\ y IN H ==> mul x y IN H) in
   let alternating_product =
     \(mul:G->G->G) (identity:G) (a:G) (xs:G list).
       ITLIST (\x acc. mul (mul x a) acc) xs identity in
   !mul:G->G->G identity:G ginv:G->G H P:G->bool h:num a:G.
     is_group mul identity ginv /\
     is_subgroup mul identity ginv H /\
     FINITE H /\
     h = CARD H /\
     (!x:G.
        x IN H
        ==> mul (mul (mul x a) (mul x a)) (mul x a) = identity) /\
     P =
       {g:G |
          ?xs:G list.
            ~(xs = []) /\
            (!x:G. MEM x xs ==> x IN H) /\
            g = alternating_product mul identity a xs}
     ==> FINITE P /\ CARD P <= 3 * h EXP 2`;;

title: putnam_1977_b6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1977_b6:
;; a finite subgroup satisfying (x*a)^3 = 1 has at most 3*h^2 distinct
;; nonempty alternating products x_1*a*...*x_n*a. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; CARRIER, OP, and INV are ACL2 function objects. Generated predicate
;; lambdas return T outside CARRIER, so FN-EQUAL against a constant-T lambda
;; expresses each universally quantified group law on the represented type.

(defun putnam-1977-b6-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-1977-b6-quoted function)
        (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-1977-b6-quoted function)
        (list 'cons left
              (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-1977-b6-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-operation-term (op left right)
  (putnam-1977-b6-apply2-term op left right))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-inverse-term (inv element)
  (putnam-1977-b6-apply1-term inv element))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-all-in-carrier-term
    (carrier variables)
  (if (endp variables)
      (putnam-1977-b6-quoted t)
    (list 'if
          (putnam-1977-b6-carrier-term
           carrier (car variables))
          (putnam-1977-b6-all-in-carrier-term
           carrier (cdr variables))
          (putnam-1977-b6-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-restricted-predicate-term
    (carrier variables proposition)
  (list 'if
        (putnam-1977-b6-all-in-carrier-term
         carrier variables)
        proposition
        (putnam-1977-b6-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-and-term (left right)
  (list 'if left right (putnam-1977-b6-quoted nil)))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda formals (putnam-1977-b6-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-operation-closure-function (carrier op)
  (let ((op-xy
         (putnam-1977-b6-operation-term op 'x 'y)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y)
     (putnam-1977-b6-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x y)
      (putnam-1977-b6-carrier-term carrier op-xy)))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-inverse-closure-function (carrier inv)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(x)
   (putnam-1977-b6-restricted-predicate-term
    carrier
    '(x)
    (putnam-1977-b6-carrier-term
     carrier
     (putnam-1977-b6-inverse-term inv 'x)))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-associative-function (carrier op)
  (let* ((op-xy
          (putnam-1977-b6-operation-term op 'x 'y))
         (op-yz
          (putnam-1977-b6-operation-term op 'y 'z)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y z)
     (putnam-1977-b6-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x y z)
      (list
       'equal
       (putnam-1977-b6-operation-term op op-xy 'z)
       (putnam-1977-b6-operation-term op 'x op-yz))))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-identity-function (carrier op one)
  (let ((left
         (list
          'equal
          (putnam-1977-b6-operation-term
           op (putnam-1977-b6-quoted one) 'x)
          'x))
        (right
         (list
          'equal
          (putnam-1977-b6-operation-term
           op 'x (putnam-1977-b6-quoted one))
          'x)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-1977-b6-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x)
      (putnam-1977-b6-and-term left right)))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-inverse-law-function
    (carrier op inv one)
  (let* ((inv-x
          (putnam-1977-b6-inverse-term inv 'x))
         (left
          (list
           'equal
           (putnam-1977-b6-operation-term op inv-x 'x)
           (putnam-1977-b6-quoted one)))
         (right
          (list
           'equal
           (putnam-1977-b6-operation-term op 'x inv-x)
           (putnam-1977-b6-quoted one))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-1977-b6-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x)
      (putnam-1977-b6-and-term left right)))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-member-p (carrier element)
  (apply$ carrier (list element)))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-multiply (op left right)
  (apply$ op (list left right)))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-inverse (inv element)
  (apply$ inv (list element)))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-power (op base exponent one)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      one
    (putnam-1977-b6-multiply
     op
     base
     (putnam-1977-b6-power
      op base (- exponent 1) one))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-group-p (carrier op inv one)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp op)
   (tamep-functionp inv)
   (putnam-1977-b6-member-p carrier one)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1977-b6-operation-closure-function carrier op)
    (putnam-1977-b6-true-function '(x y)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1977-b6-inverse-closure-function carrier inv)
    (putnam-1977-b6-true-function '(x)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1977-b6-associative-function carrier op)
    (putnam-1977-b6-true-function '(x y z)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1977-b6-identity-function carrier op one)
    (putnam-1977-b6-true-function '(x)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1977-b6-inverse-law-function carrier op inv one)
    (putnam-1977-b6-true-function '(x)))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-subset-of-carrier-p
    (elements carrier)
  (if (endp elements)
      t
    (and
     (putnam-1977-b6-member-p carrier (car elements))
     (putnam-1977-b6-subset-of-carrier-p
      (cdr elements) carrier))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-subgroup-product-row-p
    (x elements subgroup op)
  (if (endp elements)
      t
    (and
     (member-equal
      (putnam-1977-b6-multiply op x (car elements))
      subgroup)
     (putnam-1977-b6-subgroup-product-row-p
      x (cdr elements) subgroup op))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-subgroup-product-closed-p
    (elements subgroup op)
  (if (endp elements)
      t
    (and
     (putnam-1977-b6-subgroup-product-row-p
      (car elements) subgroup subgroup op)
     (putnam-1977-b6-subgroup-product-closed-p
      (cdr elements) subgroup op))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-subgroup-inverse-closed-p
    (elements subgroup inv)
  (if (endp elements)
      t
    (and
     (member-equal
      (putnam-1977-b6-inverse inv (car elements))
      subgroup)
     (putnam-1977-b6-subgroup-inverse-closed-p
      (cdr elements) subgroup inv))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-subgroup-p
    (subgroup carrier op inv one)
  (and
   (true-listp subgroup)
   (no-duplicatesp-equal subgroup)
   (putnam-1977-b6-subset-of-carrier-p subgroup carrier)
   (member-equal one subgroup)
   (putnam-1977-b6-subgroup-product-closed-p
    subgroup subgroup op)
   (putnam-1977-b6-subgroup-inverse-closed-p
    subgroup subgroup inv)))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-cube-hypothesis-p
    (elements op a one)
  (if (endp elements)
      t
    (and
     (equal
      (putnam-1977-b6-power
       op
       (putnam-1977-b6-multiply op (car elements) a)
       3
       one)
      one)
     (putnam-1977-b6-cube-hypothesis-p
      (cdr elements) op a one))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-word-elements-p (word subgroup)
  (if (endp word)
      t
    (and
     (member-equal (car word) subgroup)
     (putnam-1977-b6-word-elements-p
      (cdr word) subgroup))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-product-word-p (word subgroup)
  (and
   (true-listp word)
   (consp word)
   (putnam-1977-b6-word-elements-p word subgroup)))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-product-words-p
    (words subgroup)
  (if (endp words)
      t
    (and
     (putnam-1977-b6-product-word-p
      (car words) subgroup)
     (putnam-1977-b6-product-words-p
      (cdr words) subgroup))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-product-value
    (word op a one)
  (if (endp word)
      one
    (putnam-1977-b6-multiply
     op
     (putnam-1977-b6-multiply op (car word) a)
     (putnam-1977-b6-product-value
      (cdr word) op a one))))

(defun putnam-1977-b6-product-values
    (words op a one)
  (if (endp words)
      nil
    (cons
     (putnam-1977-b6-product-value
      (car words) op a one)
     (putnam-1977-b6-product-values
      (cdr words) op a one))))

;; P is the image of nonempty H-words under PRODUCT-VALUE. For N = 3*h^2,
;; "P is finite and |P| <= N" is equivalent to saying that every list of
;; N+1 such words has two equal image values.

(defun-sk putnam-1977-b6-cardinality-bound-p
    (subgroup op a one h)
  (forall (words)
    (implies
     (and
      (true-listp words)
      (putnam-1977-b6-product-words-p words subgroup)
      (equal
       (len words)
       (+ 1 (* 3 (expt h 2)))))
     (not
      (no-duplicatesp-equal
       (putnam-1977-b6-product-values
        words op a one))))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1977-b6-statement
    (carrier op inv one subgroup h a)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-1977-b6-group-p carrier op inv one)
    (putnam-1977-b6-subgroup-p
     subgroup carrier op inv one)
    (natp h)
    (equal h (len subgroup))
    (putnam-1977-b6-member-p carrier a)
    (putnam-1977-b6-cube-hypothesis-p
     subgroup op a one))
   (putnam-1977-b6-cardinality-bound-p
    subgroup op a one h)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1977_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1977_b6:
-- a finite subgroup H of order h satisfying (x a)^3 = 1 has at most 3 h^2
-- distinct nonempty alternating products x1 a ... xn a. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1977B6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)
open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc; _⊔_)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Iff
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists
  {a p : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (property : A -> Set p) :
  Set (a ⊔ p) where

  constructor witness
  field
    value     : A
    satisfies : property value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record HasCardinality
  {a p : Level}
  {A : Set a}
  (P : A -> Set p)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set (a ⊔ p) where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      P (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (x : A) ->
      P x ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> x == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

record Group
  {ell : Level}
  (G : Set ell) :
  Set ell where

  field
    identity       : G
    inverse        : G -> G
    multiply       : G -> G -> G
    associative    : (x y z : G) ->
                     multiply (multiply x y) z ==
                     multiply x (multiply y z)
    identity-left  : (x : G) -> multiply identity x == x
    identity-right : (x : G) -> multiply x identity == x
    inverse-left   : (x : G) -> multiply (inverse x) x == identity
    inverse-right  : (x : G) -> multiply x (inverse x) == identity

record Subgroup
  {ell p : Level}
  {G : Set ell}
  (structure : Group G)
  (member : G -> Set p) :
  Set (ell ⊔ p) where

  open Group structure

  field
    membership-propositional :
      (x : G) ->
      (u v : member x) ->
      u == v
    contains-identity :
      member identity
    closed-under-inverse :
      (x : G) ->
      member x ->
      member (inverse x)
    closed-under-multiply :
      (x y : G) ->
      member x ->
      member y ->
      member (multiply x y)

data All
  {a p : Level}
  {A : Set a}
  (P : A -> Set p) :
  List A ->
  Set (a ⊔ p) where

  all[]  : All P []
  _all∷_ : {x : A} {xs : List A} ->
           P x ->
           All P xs ->
           All P (x ∷ xs)

open Group

power :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  Group G ->
  G ->
  Nat ->
  G
power structure x zero =
  identity structure
power structure x (suc exponent) =
  multiply structure x (power structure x exponent)

alternatingProduct :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  Group G ->
  G ->
  List G ->
  G
alternatingProduct structure a [] =
  identity structure
alternatingProduct structure a (x ∷ xs) =
  multiply structure
    (multiply structure x a)
    (alternatingProduct structure a xs)

ProductWord :
  {ell p : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  (structure : Group G) ->
  (member : G -> Set p) ->
  G ->
  G ->
  Set (ell ⊔ p)
ProductWord {G = G} structure member a g =
  Exists G
    (\ x ->
      member x
      and
      Exists (List G)
        (\ xs ->
          All member xs
          and
          g ==
          multiply structure
            (multiply structure x a)
            (alternatingProduct structure a xs)))

three : Nat
three =
  suc (suc (suc zero))

putnam-1977-b6 :
  (ell p q : Level) ->
  Set (lsuc (ell ⊔ (p ⊔ q)))
putnam-1977-b6 ell p q =
  (G : Set ell) ->
  (structure : Group G) ->
  (H : G -> Set p) ->
  Subgroup structure H ->
  (h : Nat) ->
  HasCardinality H h ->
  (a : G) ->
  ((x : G) ->
    H x ->
    power structure (multiply structure x a) three ==
    identity structure) ->
  (P : G -> Set q) ->
  ((g : G) ->
    Iff (P g) (ProductWord structure H a g)) ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cardinality ->
      HasCardinality P cardinality
      and
      cardinality <=N three * (h * h))

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1977_b6:
  a finite subgroup whose elements x satisfy (x*a)^3 = 1 generates, through
  nonempty products of factors x*a, a set of cardinality at most 3h^2.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory pred_setTheory groupTheory;

val putnam_1977_b6 =
  ``!(g : 'a group) (H : 'a group) (a : 'a) (h : num) (P : 'a set).
      Group g /\
      Subgroup H g /\
      FINITE H.carrier /\
      a IN g.carrier /\
      h = CARD H.carrier /\
      (!x : 'a.
         x IN H.carrier
         ==>
         g.exp (g.op x a) 3 = g.id) /\
      P =
        {y : 'a |
           ?xs : 'a list.
             xs <> [] /\
             (!x : 'a. MEM x xs ==> x IN H.carrier) /\
             y =
               FOLDR
                 (\x acc. g.op (g.op x a) acc)
                 g.id
                 xs}
      ==>
      FINITE P /\ CARD P <= 3 * h ** 2``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1977_b6: finite products x_1 a ... x_n a from a finite subgroup
  have cardinality at most three times the square of the subgroup order
  when every (x a)^3 is the group identity. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  In SetMM, G e. Grp is an arbitrary group, H e. ( SubGrp ` G ) is a
  subgroup, Fin and # express finiteness and finite cardinality, and .g is
  integer group exponentiation. Word H is the class of all finite sequences
  over H; deleting the empty word imposes the source condition n >= 1.

  For each remaining word w, composition with the map x |-> x (+g) a
  produces the ordered sequence x_1 a, ..., x_n a. Since every word has a
  consecutive integer domain, G gsum is its left-to-right group product.
  Thus the displayed range is definitionally the source set P, without
  externalizing the finite-sequence witness. The final declaration is the
  single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

${
  $d G H P a h w x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-1977-b6 $a |-
    A. h e. NN0 A. a e. ( Base ` G )
      (
        (
          (
            (
              G e. Grp
              /\
              H e. ( SubGrp ` G )
            )
            /\
            (
              H e. Fin
              /\
              ( # ` H ) = h
            )
          )
          /\
          (
            A. y e. H
              (
                3 ( .g ` G ) ( y ( +g ` G ) a )
              )
              =
              ( 0g ` G )
            /\
            P =
              ran
                (
                  w e. ( Word H \ { (/) } ) |->
                    (
                      G gsum
                        (
                          ( x e. H |-> ( x ( +g ` G ) a ) )
                          o.
                          w
                        )
                    )
                )
          )
        )
        ->
        (
          P e. Fin
          /\
          ( # ` P ) <_ ( 3 x. ( h ^ 2 ) )
        )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1977_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1977_b6:
% a finite subgroup satisfying (x*a)^3 = 1 yields at most 3*h^2 distinct
% nonempty products x_1*a*...*x_n*a. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1977_b6[
  Element: TYPE+,
  multiply: [Element, Element -> Element],
  inverse: [Element -> Element],
  one: Element
]: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[Element]

  element_set: TYPE = [Element -> bool]
  element_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> Element]

  group_laws: bool =
    (FORALL (x, y, z: Element):
      multiply(multiply(x, y), z)
        = multiply(x, multiply(y, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x: Element):
        multiply(one, x) = x
          AND multiply(x, one) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x: Element):
        multiply(inverse(x), x) = one
          AND multiply(x, inverse(x)) = one)

  is_subgroup(H: finite_set[Element]): bool =
    H(one)
      AND (FORALL (x, y: Element):
        H(x) AND H(y) IMPLIES H(multiply(x, y)))
      AND (FORALL (x: Element):
        H(x) IMPLIES H(inverse(x)))

  group_power(base: Element, exponent: nat): RECURSIVE Element =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      one
    ELSE
      multiply(
        group_power(base, exponent - 1),
        base)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  factor_product(
      xs: element_sequence,
      a: Element,
      length: nat): RECURSIVE Element =
    IF length = 0 THEN
      one
    ELSE
      multiply(
        factor_product(xs, a, length - 1),
        multiply(xs(length - 1), a))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE length

  product_set(
      H: finite_set[Element],
      a: Element): element_set =
    LAMBDA (g: Element):
      EXISTS (length: posnat), (xs: element_sequence):
        (FORALL (index: nat):
          index < length IMPLIES H(xs(index)))
          AND g = factor_product(xs, a, length)

  injective_below(
      enumeration: element_sequence,
      bound: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      i < bound
        AND j < bound
        AND enumeration(i) = enumeration(j)
      IMPLIES i = j

  enumerates_exactly(
      enumeration: element_sequence,
      set_value: element_set,
      bound: nat): bool =
    FORALL (g: Element):
      set_value(g)
        IFF
          EXISTS (index: nat):
            index < bound
              AND enumeration(index) = g

  has_cardinality_at_most(
      set_value: element_set,
      bound: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (cardinality: nat), (enumeration: element_sequence):
      cardinality <= bound
        AND injective_below(enumeration, cardinality)
        AND enumerates_exactly(
          enumeration, set_value, cardinality)

  putnam_1977_b6: bool =
    group_laws IMPLIES
      FORALL (H: finite_set[Element]),
             (h: nat),
             (a: Element),
             (P: element_set):
        (is_subgroup(H)
          AND h = card(H)
          AND (FORALL (x: Element):
            H(x) IMPLIES
              group_power(multiply(x, a), 3) = one)
          AND (FORALL (g: Element):
            P(g) IFF product_set(H, a)(g)))
        IMPLIES
          has_cardinality_at_most(P, 3 * h ^ 2)
END putnam_1977_b6

;; every 20-element subset of {1, 4, 7, ..., 100} contains two distinct
;; elements whose sum is 104. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source set S is fixed by its defining equality. Its elements are
;; exactly the integers from 1 through 100 congruent to 1 modulo 3. The source
;; set T has cardinality 20, so a duplicate-free true list of length 20 is a
;; bijective representation after forgetting enumeration order. Every source
;; T has such an enumeration, and every accepted list determines exactly one
;; source T. The recursive search keeps the two existential witnesses internal.

(defun putnam-1978-a1-in-s-p (k)
  (and
   (integerp k)
   (<= 1 k)
   (<= k 100)
   (equal (mod (- k 1) 3) 0)))

(defun putnam-1978-a1-subset-of-s-p (elements)
  (if (consp elements)
      (and
       (putnam-1978-a1-in-s-p (car elements))
       (putnam-1978-a1-subset-of-s-p (cdr elements)))
    (equal elements nil)))

(defun putnam-1978-a1-partner-exists-p (element remaining)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (or
       (and
        (not (equal element (car remaining)))
        (equal (+ element (car remaining)) 104))
       (putnam-1978-a1-partner-exists-p
        element (cdr remaining)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1978-a1-pair-exists-p (elements)
  (if (consp elements)
      (or
       (putnam-1978-a1-partner-exists-p
        (car elements) (cdr elements))
       (putnam-1978-a1-pair-exists-p (cdr elements)))
    nil))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1978-a1-statement (elements)
  (implies
   (and
    (true-listp elements)
    (no-duplicatesp-equal elements)
    (equal (len elements) 20)
    (putnam-1978-a1-subset-of-s-p elements))
   (putnam-1978-a1-pair-exists-p elements)))

open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=_ _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<= : {n : Nat} -> zero <= n
  suc<=  : {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> suc m <= suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

NatSubset : Set1
NatSubset =
  Nat -> Set

SubsetOf : NatSubset -> NatSubset -> Set
SubsetOf A B =
  (x : Nat) -> A x -> B x

record SameSubset (A B : NatSubset) : Set where

    backward : SubsetOf B A

  (S : NatSubset)
  (cardinality : Nat) :

    enumerated-member :

    enumeration-complete :

      S number ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> number == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

PutnamProgression : NatSubset
PutnamProgression k =
  Exists Nat
    (\ j ->
      j <= 33
      and
      k == 3 * j + 1)

putnam-1978-a1 : Set1
putnam-1978-a1 =
  (S T : NatSubset) ->
  SameSubset S PutnamProgression ->
  (SubsetOf T S and HasCardinality T 20) ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ m ->
      T m
      and
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          T n
          and
          m != n
          and
          m + n == 104))

% elements whose sum is 104. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1978_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[int]

  is_progression_set(S: finite_set[int]): bool =
    FORALL (value: int):
      S(value) IFF
        EXISTS (index: int):
          0 <= index
            AND index <= 33
            AND value = 3 * index + 1

  finite_subset(T, S: finite_set[int]): bool =
    FORALL (value: int):
      T(value) IMPLIES S(value)

  putnam_1978_a1: bool =
    FORALL (S, T: finite_set[int]):
      (is_progression_set(S)
        AND finite_subset(T, S)
        AND card(T) = 20)
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (m, n: int):
          T(m)
            AND T(n)
            AND m /= n
            AND m + n = 104
END putnam_1978_a1

import Mathlib

/--
Let $A$ be the real $n \times n$ matrix $(a_{ij})$ where $a_{ij} = a$ for $i < j$, $b \; (\neq a)$ for $i > j$, and $c_i$ for $i = j$. Show that $\det A = \frac{b p(a) - a p(b)}{b - a}$, where $p(x) = \prod_{i=1}^n (c_i - x)$.
-/
theorem putnam_1978_a2
(n : ℕ)
(npos : n > 0)
(a b : ℝ)
(hab : a ≠ b)
(c : Fin n → ℝ)
(A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
(hA : A = fun i j ↦ ite (i < j) a (ite (i > j) b (c i)))
(p : ℝ → ℝ)
(hp : p = fun x ↦ ∏ i : Fin n, (c i - x))
: (A.det = ((b * p a - a * p b) / (b - a))) :=
sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1978_a2:
   the determinant formula for a real matrix with constant entries above and
   below the diagonal. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals List Arith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope R_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_1978_a2_sum (xs : list R) : R :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0
  | x :: rest => x + putnam_1978_a2_sum rest
  end.

Definition putnam_1978_a2_delete_nth
    {T : Type} (j : nat) (xs : list T) : list T :=
  firstn j xs ++ skipn (S j) xs.

Definition putnam_1978_a2_cofactor_sign (j : nat) : R :=
  if Nat.even j then 1 else -1.

Fixpoint putnam_1978_a2_det
    (n : nat) (M : list (list R)) {struct n} : R :=
  match n with
  | O => 1
  | S k =>
      match M with
      | [] => 0
      | row :: rows =>
          putnam_1978_a2_sum
            (map
              (fun j : nat =>
                putnam_1978_a2_cofactor_sign j *
                nth j row 0 *
                putnam_1978_a2_det k
                  (map (putnam_1978_a2_delete_nth j) rows))
              (seq 0 (S k)))
      end
  end.

Definition putnam_1978_a2_matrix
    (n : nat) (a b : R) (c : list R) : list (list R) :=
  map
    (fun i : nat =>
      map
        (fun j : nat =>
          if Nat.ltb i j then a
          else if Nat.ltb j i then b
          else nth i c 0)
        (seq 0 n))
    (seq 0 n).

Definition putnam_1978_a2_polynomial (c : list R) (x : R) : R :=
  fold_right Rmult 1 (map (fun ci : R => ci - x) c).

Theorem putnam_1978_a2
    (n : nat)
    (npos : (0 < n)%nat)
    (a b : R)
    (hab : a <> b)
    (c : list R)
    (hc : length c = n)
    (A : list (list R))
    (hA : A = putnam_1978_a2_matrix n a b c)
    (p : R -> R)
    (hp : p = putnam_1978_a2_polynomial c) :
  putnam_1978_a2_det n A =
    (b * p a - a * p b) / (b - a).
Admitted.

theory putnam_1978_a2 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Finite_Cartesian_Product"
"HOL-Analysis.Determinants"
begin

theorem putnam_1978_a2:
  fixes n :: "nat"
    and a b :: "real"
    and A :: "real^'n^'n"
    and c :: "'n \<Rightarrow> real"
    and p :: "real \<Rightarrow> real"
    and prm :: "'n \<Rightarrow> nat"
  defines "A \<equiv> \<chi> i j :: 'n. if prm i < prm j then a else (if prm i > prm j then b else c i)"
    and "p \<equiv> \<lambda> x :: real. (\<Prod> i :: 'n \<in> UNIV. (c i - x))"
  assumes htype : "CARD('n) = n"
    and hprmresbij : "prm ` UNIV = {0..n-1}"
    and hab : "a \<noteq> b"
    and npos : "n > 0"
  shows "det A = ((b * p a - a * p b) / (b - a))"
  sorry

end
