content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a2:
;; the determinant of the real matrix with constant entries a above the
;; diagonal, b below it, and entries c_i on the diagonal equals
;; (b*p(a)-a*p(b))/(b-a), where p(x) is the product of c_i-x. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The variables a, b, and c_i are represented by algebraically independent
;; indeterminates in a canonical multivariate integer-polynomial ring.
;; Polynomial equality is therefore equality under every real assignment and
;; does not restrict the source variables to ACL2's rational number domain.
;;
;; Since a differs from b, the source conclusion is equivalent to
;;
;;   (b-a) * det(A) = b*p(a) - a*p(b).
;;
;; At a=b this cleared equation is 0=0. Thus its generic polynomial identity
;; is bidirectionally equivalent to the source's universally quantified
;; implication, including the source assumption a != b.

;; A polynomial is a sorted list of (monomial . coefficient) pairs. A
;; monomial is a sorted list of variable indices, repeated to record powers.

(defun putnam-1978-a2-monomial-multiply (left right)
  (declare (xargs :measure
                  (+ (acl2-count left) (acl2-count right))))
  (cond ((endp left) right)
        ((endp right) left)
        ((<= (car left) (car right))
         (cons (car left)
               (putnam-1978-a2-monomial-multiply
                (cdr left) right)))
        (t
         (cons (car right)
               (putnam-1978-a2-monomial-multiply
                left (cdr right))))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-insert
    (monomial coefficient polynomial)
  (cond ((equal coefficient 0) polynomial)
        ((endp polynomial)
         (list (cons monomial coefficient)))
        ((equal monomial (caar polynomial))
         (let ((sum (+ coefficient (cdar polynomial))))
           (if (equal sum 0)
               (cdr polynomial)
             (cons (cons monomial sum) (cdr polynomial)))))
        ((lexorder monomial (caar polynomial))
         (cons (cons monomial coefficient) polynomial))
        (t
         (cons (car polynomial)
               (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-insert
                monomial coefficient (cdr polynomial))))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-add (left right)
  (if (endp left)
      right
    (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-add
     (cdr left)
     (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-insert
      (caar left) (cdar left) right))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-negate (polynomial)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      nil
    (cons (cons (caar polynomial) (- (cdar polynomial)))
          (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-negate
           (cdr polynomial)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-subtract (left right)
  (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-add
   left
   (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-negate right)))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-multiply-term
    (monomial coefficient polynomial)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      nil
    (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-insert
     (putnam-1978-a2-monomial-multiply
      monomial (caar polynomial))
     (* coefficient (cdar polynomial))
     (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-multiply-term
      monomial coefficient (cdr polynomial)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-multiply (left right)
  (if (endp left)
      nil
    (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-add
     (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-multiply-term
      (caar left) (cdar left) right)
     (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-multiply
      (cdr left) right))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-one ()
  (list (cons nil 1)))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-variable (index)
  (list (cons (list index) 1)))

;; Variable 0 is a, variable 1 is b, and variable 2+i is c_i.

(defun putnam-1978-a2-a ()
  (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-variable 0))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-b ()
  (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-variable 1))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-c (index)
  (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-variable (+ 2 index)))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-range-from (start count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons start
          (putnam-1978-a2-range-from
           (+ 1 start) (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-matrix-row (row columns)
  (if (endp columns)
      nil
    (cons
     (cond ((< row (car columns))
            (putnam-1978-a2-a))
           ((> row (car columns))
            (putnam-1978-a2-b))
           (t
            (putnam-1978-a2-c row)))
     (putnam-1978-a2-matrix-row row (cdr columns)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-matrix-rows (rows columns)
  (if (endp rows)
      nil
    (cons (putnam-1978-a2-matrix-row
           (car rows) columns)
          (putnam-1978-a2-matrix-rows
           (cdr rows) columns))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-matrix (n)
  (let ((indices (putnam-1978-a2-range-from 0 n)))
    (putnam-1978-a2-matrix-rows indices indices)))

;; The determinant is the signed sum over all permutations of the columns.

(defun putnam-1978-a2-prefix-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (cons (cons item (car lists))
          (putnam-1978-a2-prefix-each item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-insert-everywhere (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list (list item))
    (cons (cons item list)
          (putnam-1978-a2-prefix-each
           (car list)
           (putnam-1978-a2-insert-everywhere
            item (cdr list))))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-insert-into-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-1978-a2-insert-everywhere item (car lists))
     (putnam-1978-a2-insert-into-each
      item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-permutations (list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list nil)
    (putnam-1978-a2-insert-into-each
     (car list)
     (putnam-1978-a2-permutations (cdr list)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-count-greater (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      0
    (+ (if (> item (car list)) 1 0)
       (putnam-1978-a2-count-greater item (cdr list)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-inversion-count (permutation)
  (if (endp permutation)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1978-a2-count-greater
        (car permutation) (cdr permutation))
       (putnam-1978-a2-inversion-count
        (cdr permutation)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-diagonal-product
    (matrix permutation row)
  (if (endp permutation)
      (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-one)
    (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-multiply
     (nth (car permutation) (nth row matrix))
     (putnam-1978-a2-diagonal-product
      matrix (cdr permutation) (+ 1 row)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-determinant-sum
    (matrix permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      nil
    (let* ((permutation (car permutations))
           (product
            (putnam-1978-a2-diagonal-product
             matrix permutation 0))
           (signed-product
            (if (equal
                 (mod
                  (putnam-1978-a2-inversion-count permutation)
                  2)
                 0)
                product
              (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-negate product))))
      (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-add
       signed-product
       (putnam-1978-a2-determinant-sum
        matrix (cdr permutations))))))

(defun putnam-1978-a2-determinant (matrix n)
  (putnam-1978-a2-determinant-sum
   matrix
   (putnam-1978-a2-permutations
    (putnam-1978-a2-range-from 0 n))))

;; Compute p(x) = product_i (c_i-x) in the same polynomial ring.

(defun putnam-1978-a2-p-value (x index count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-one)
    (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-multiply
     (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-subtract
      (putnam-1978-a2-c index) x)
     (putnam-1978-a2-p-value
      x (+ 1 index) (- count 1)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1978-a2-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (< 0 n))
   (let* ((a (putnam-1978-a2-a))
          (b (putnam-1978-a2-b))
          (matrix (putnam-1978-a2-matrix n))
          (determinant
           (putnam-1978-a2-determinant matrix n))
          (p-at-a (putnam-1978-a2-p-value a 0 n))
          (p-at-b (putnam-1978-a2-p-value b 0 n)))
     (equal
      (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-multiply
       (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-subtract b a)
       determinant)
      (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-subtract
       (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-multiply b p-at-a)
       (putnam-1978-a2-polynomial-multiply a p-at-b))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1978_a2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a2:
-- the determinant of a real matrix with constant entries above and below the
-- diagonal is expressed using the product of its shifted diagonal entries.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

data Comparison : Set where
  less    : Comparison
  equal   : Comparison
  greater : Comparison

compareFin :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n ->
  Comparison
compareFin fzero fzero =
  equal
compareFin fzero (fsuc j) =
  less
compareFin (fsuc i) fzero =
  greater
compareFin (fsuc i) (fsuc j) =
  compareFin i j

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

productFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
productFin reals {zero} term =
  oneR reals
productFin reals {suc n} term =
  multiply reals
    (term fzero)
    (productFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

Matrix : Set -> Nat -> Set
Matrix R n =
  Fin n -> Fin n -> R

skip :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin (suc n)
skip {zero} column ()
skip {suc n} fzero k =
  fsuc k
skip {suc n} (fsuc column) fzero =
  fzero
skip {suc n} (fsuc column) (fsuc k) =
  fsuc (skip column k)

firstRowMinor :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R (suc n) ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Matrix R n
firstRowMinor A column i j =
  A (fsuc i) (skip column j)

alternatingSign :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  R
alternatingSign reals fzero =
  oneR reals
alternatingSign reals (fsuc i) =
  negate reals (alternatingSign reals i)

determinant :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  R
determinant reals {zero} A =
  oneR reals
determinant reals {suc n} A =
  sumFin reals
    (\ column ->
      multiply reals
        (alternatingSign reals column)
        (multiply reals
          (A fzero column)
          (determinant reals (firstRowMinor A column))))

putnamMatrix :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  Matrix R n
putnamMatrix a b c i j with compareFin i j
... | less =
  a
... | equal =
  c i
... | greater =
  b

shiftedDiagonalProduct :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
shiftedDiagonalProduct reals c x =
  productFin reals (\ i -> subtract reals (c i) x)

closedForm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
closedForm reals a b c =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals
      (multiply reals b (shiftedDiagonalProduct reals c a))
      (multiply reals a (shiftedDiagonalProduct reals c b)))
    (subtract reals b a)

module Putnam1978A2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (n : Nat) ->
    Positive n ->
    (a b : R) ->
    a != b ->
    (c : Fin n -> R) ->
    determinant reals (putnamMatrix a b c)
    ==
    closedForm reals a b c

putnam-1978-a2 : Set1
putnam-1978-a2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1978A2Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1978_a2:
  the determinant formula for a real square matrix with constant entries
  above and below the diagonal and arbitrary diagonal entries. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory fcpTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;
open determinantTheory;

val putnam_1978_a2 =
  ``!n : num. !a b : real. !c : num -> real.
    !A : real['N]['N]. !p : real -> real.
      n = dimindex (:'N) /\
      0 < n /\
      a <> b /\
      A =
        (FCP i j.
           if i < j then a
           else if i > j then b
           else c i) /\
      (!x : real.
         p x = real_sigma$product (count n) (\i. c i - x))
      ==>
      determinant$det A = (b * p a - a * p b) / (b - a)``;

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The positive natural n has canonical index carrier 0 ..^ n. The diagonal

  p(x) as the product of c(i)-x over every index.

content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a2:
% the determinant formula for an n-by-n real matrix with constant entries
% above and below its arbitrary diagonal. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1978_a2: THEORY
BEGIN
  matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  quotient_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      0
    ELSE
      1
        + quotient_aux(
            numerator - denominator,
            denominator,
            fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  remainder_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      numerator
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator - denominator,
        denominator,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  safe_ndiv(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    quotient_aux(
      numerator,
      denominator,
      numerator + 1)

  safe_mod(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator,
        denominator,
        numerator + 1)
    ENDIF

  function_code_count(n: nat): nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN 1 ELSE n ^ n ENDIF

  permutation_entry(code, row, n: nat): nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      safe_mod(safe_ndiv(code, n ^ row), n)
    ENDIF

  permutation_code(code, n: nat): bool =
    code < function_code_count(n)
      AND (FORALL (row_1, row_2: nat):
        (row_1 < n
          AND row_2 < n
          AND permutation_entry(code, row_1, n)
            = permutation_entry(code, row_2, n))
        IMPLIES row_1 = row_2)

  pair_row(pair, n: nat): nat =
    safe_ndiv(pair, n)

  pair_column(pair, n: nat): nat =
    safe_mod(pair, n)

  inversion_at(code, pair, n: nat): bool =
    pair_row(pair, n) < n
      AND pair_column(pair, n) < n
      AND pair_row(pair, n) < pair_column(pair, n)
      AND permutation_entry(code, pair_row(pair, n), n)
        > permutation_entry(code, pair_column(pair, n), n)

  count_true(
      property: [nat -> bool],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_true(property, count - 1)
        + IF property(count - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  inversion_count(code, n: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      (LAMBDA (pair: nat): inversion_at(code, pair, n)),
      n * n)

  permutation_sign(code, n: nat): real =
    IF mod(inversion_count(code, n), 2) = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -1
    ENDIF

  permutation_product(
      A: matrix,
      code, n, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      permutation_product(A, code, n, count - 1)
        * A(
            count - 1,
            permutation_entry(code, count - 1, n))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  determinant_sum(
      A: matrix,
      n, limit: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET code: nat = limit - 1 IN
        determinant_sum(A, n, limit - 1)
          + IF permutation_code(code, n) THEN
              permutation_sign(code, n)
                * permutation_product(A, code, n, n)
            ELSE
              0
            ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  determinant(A: matrix, n: nat): real =
    determinant_sum(A, n, function_code_count(n))

  finite_product(
      c: real_sequence,
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      finite_product(c, x, count - 1)
        * (c(count - 1) - x)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_matrix_entries(
      A: matrix,
      c: real_sequence,
      a, b: real,
      n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      i < n AND j < n IMPLIES
        A(i, j) =
          IF i < j THEN
            a
          ELSIF i > j THEN
            b
          ELSE
            c(i)
          ENDIF

  is_diagonal_product(
      p: real_function,
      c: real_sequence,
      n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      p(x) = finite_product(c, x, n)

  putnam_1978_a2: bool =
    FORALL
        (n: nat),
        (a, b: real),
        (c: real_sequence),
        (A: matrix),
        (p: real_function):
      (n > 0
        AND a /= b
        AND has_matrix_entries(A, c, a, b, n)
        AND is_diagonal_product(p, c, n))
      IMPLIES
        determinant(A, n)
          = (b * p(a) - a * p(b)) / (b - a)
END putnam_1978_a2

import Mathlib

open Set Polynomial

abbrev putnam_1978_a3_solution : ℕ := sorry
-- 2
/--
Let $p(x) = 2(x^6 + 1) + 4(x^5 + x) + 3(x^4 + x^2) + 5x^3$. For $k$ with $0 < k < 5$, let
\[
I_k = \int_0^{\infty} \frac{x^k}{p(x)} \, dx.
\]
For which $k$ is $I_k$ smallest?
-/
theorem putnam_1978_a3
    (p : Polynomial ℝ)
    (hp : p = 2 * (X ^ 6 + 1) + 4 * (X ^ 5 + X) + 3 * (X ^ 4 + X ^ 2) + 5 * X ^ 3)
    (I : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hI : I = fun k ↦ ∫ x in Ioi 0, x ^ k / p.eval x) :
    IsLeast {y | ∃ k ∈ Ioo 0 5, I k = y} (I putnam_1978_a3_solution) :=
  sorry

From mathcomp Require Import all_algebra all_ssreflect.

Local Open Scope classical_set_scope.

Definition mu := [the measure _ _ of @lebesgue_measure R].
Definition putnam_1978_a3_solution : nat := 2.
Theorem putnam_1978_a3
    (p : {poly R} := 2 *: ('X^6 + 1%:P) + 4 *: ('X^5 + 'X) + 3 *: ('X^4 + 'X^2) + 5 *: 'X^3)
    (I : nat -> R := fun k => \int[mu]_(x in [set t : R | 0 <= t]) (fun x => x ^ k / p.[x]) x)
    : putnam_1978_a3_solution \in index_iota 1 5 /\ (forall k : nat, k \in index_iota 1 5 -> I putnam_1978_a3_solution <= I k).
Proof. Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a3:
;; the least of four improper real integrals of x^k divided by a fixed
;; reciprocal polynomial occurs at k = 2. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Under x = t/(1-t), the source integral on [0,infinity) becomes the
;; integral on [0,1] of
;;
;;   t^k (1-t)^(4-k) / Q(t),
;;
;; where Q is the degree-six homogenization of the source polynomial.
;; This transformed integrand extends continuously to both endpoints.
(defun putnam-1978-a3-denominator (point)
  (let ((u (- 1 point)))
    (+ (* 2
          (+ (expt point 6)
             (expt u 6)))
       (* 4
          (+ (* (expt point 5) u)
             (* point (expt u 5))))
       (* 3
          (+ (* (expt point 4) (expt u 2))
             (* (expt point 2) (expt u 4))))
       (* 5
          (expt point 3)
          (expt u 3)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a3-valid-k-p (k)
  (and (natp k)
       (<= 1 k)
       (<= k 4)))

(defun putnam-1978-a3-transformed-integrand (k point)
  (if (and (putnam-1978-a3-valid-k-p k)
           (rationalp point)
           (<= 0 point)
           (<= point 1))
      (/ (* (expt point k)
            (expt (- 1 point) (- 4 k)))
         (putnam-1978-a3-denominator point))
    0))

(defun putnam-1978-a3-riemann-sum-aux
    (k index subdivisions)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (zp index)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1978-a3-transformed-integrand
        k (/ index subdivisions))
       (putnam-1978-a3-riemann-sum-aux
        k (- index 1) subdivisions))))

(defun putnam-1978-a3-riemann-sum (k subdivisions)
  (if (and (putnam-1978-a3-valid-k-p k)
           (natp subdivisions)
           (< 0 subdivisions))
      (/ (putnam-1978-a3-riemann-sum-aux
          k subdivisions subdivisions)
         subdivisions)
    0))

;; Positive rationals are cofinal among positive real tolerances. The
;; eventual comparison of every pair of sufficiently fine Riemann sums is
;; equivalent to the comparison of their exact real limits.
(defun-sk putnam-1978-a3-comparison-tail-p
    (k epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (subdivisions-2 subdivisions-k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp subdivisions-2)
      (< 0 subdivisions-2)
      (<= cutoff subdivisions-2)
      (natp subdivisions-k)
      (< 0 subdivisions-k)
      (<= cutoff subdivisions-k))
     (<= (putnam-1978-a3-riemann-sum
          2 subdivisions-2)
         (+ (putnam-1978-a3-riemann-sum
             k subdivisions-k)
            epsilon)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1978-a3-comparison-cutoff-exists-p
    (k epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (< 0 cutoff)
     (putnam-1978-a3-comparison-tail-p
      k epsilon cutoff))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1978-a3-statement (k epsilon)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-1978-a3-valid-k-p k)
    (rationalp epsilon)
    (< 0 epsilon))
   (and
    (putnam-1978-a3-valid-k-p 2)
    (putnam-1978-a3-comparison-cutoff-exists-p
     k epsilon))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a3:
-- among the four nonnegative-half-line improper integrals of x^k divided by
-- the specified reciprocal-symmetric degree-six polynomial, the k = 2 value
-- is least. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SequentialLimit {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

rightRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
rightRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals (suc i))
              step)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function value =
  SequentialLimit reals
    (\ n ->
      rightRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    value

NonnegativeImproperIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
NonnegativeImproperIntegralValue {R} reals function value =
  Exists (Nat -> R)
    (\ partialIntegrals ->
      ((n : Nat) ->
        IntervalIntegralValue reals
          (zeroR reals)
          (fromNat reals n)
          function
          (partialIntegrals n))
      and
      SequentialLimit reals partialIntegrals value)

record StandardNonnegativeImproperIntegration
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    improperIntegral :
      (R -> R) ->
      R

    integral-correct :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      (value : R) ->
      NonnegativeImproperIntegralValue reals function value ->
      improperIntegral function == value

    integral-totalized-at-zero :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      Not
        (Exists R
          (NonnegativeImproperIntegralValue reals function)) ->
      improperIntegral function == zeroR reals

open StandardNonnegativeImproperIntegration

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc threeN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc fourN

sixN : Nat
sixN =
  suc fiveN

BetweenOneAndFour : Nat -> Set
BetweenOneAndFour k =
  oneN <=N k and k <=N fourN

putnamPolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
putnamPolynomial reals x =
  add reals
    (multiply reals
      (fromNat reals twoN)
      (add reals
        (naturalPower reals x sixN)
        (oneR reals)))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals
        (fromNat reals fourN)
        (add reals
          (naturalPower reals x fiveN)
          x))
      (add reals
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals threeN)
          (add reals
            (naturalPower reals x fourN)
            (naturalPower reals x twoN)))
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals fiveN)
          (naturalPower reals x threeN))))

putnamIntegrand :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  R
putnamIntegrand reals k x =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x k)
    (putnamPolynomial reals x)

module Putnam1978A3Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (integration : StandardNonnegativeImproperIntegration reals) where

  I : Nat -> R
  I k =
    improperIntegral integration
      (putnamIntegrand reals k)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    BetweenOneAndFour twoN
    and
    ((k : Nat) ->
      BetweenOneAndFour k ->
      lessOrEqual reals (I twoN) (I k))

putnam-1978-a3 : Set1
putnam-1978-a3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (integration : StandardNonnegativeImproperIntegration reals) ->
  Putnam1978A3Statement.proposition reals integration

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1978_a3:
  among the four improper integrals of x^k divided by the specified
  reciprocal-symmetric degree-six polynomial, the minimum occurs at k = 2.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory extrealTheory measureTheory;
open lebesgueTheory lebesgue_measureTheory;

val putnam_1978_a3 =
  ``let polynomial_value =
      \x : real.
        2 * (x pow 6 + 1) +
        4 * (x pow 5 + x) +
        3 * (x pow 4 + x pow 2) +
        5 * x pow 3
    in
    let nonnegative_reals = {x : real | 0 <= x}
    in
    let I =
      \k : num.
        let halfline = restrict_space lebesgue nonnegative_reals
        in
        let integrand =
          \x : real. Normal (x pow k / polynomial_value x)
        in
          if lebesgue$integrable halfline integrand then
            real (lebesgue$integral halfline integrand)
          else
            0
    in
      1 <= (2 : num) /\ 2 <= 4 /\
      !k : num. 1 <= k /\ k <= 4 ==> I 2 <= I k``;

title: putnam_1978_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a3:
% among the four improper integrals of x^k divided by the specified degree-six
% polynomial on the nonnegative real axis, the integral for k = 2 is smallest.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_1978_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  positive_real_function: TYPE = [posreal -> real]

  polynomial(x: real): real =
    2 * (x ^ 6 + 1)
      + 4 * (x ^ 5 + x)
      + 3 * (x ^ 4 + x ^ 2)
      + 5 * x ^ 3

  quotient_or_zero(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  integrand(degree: nat): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      quotient_or_zero(x ^ degree, polynomial(x))

  valid_tagged_partition(
      left, right: real,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = left
      AND points(count) = right
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          (points(index) < points(index + 1)
            AND points(index) <= tags(index)
            AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1))

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      f: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count - 1)
        + f(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_interval_integral(
      f: real_function,
      left, right, integral_value: real): bool =
    left < right
      AND FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
          FORALL
              (points, tags: real_sequence),
              (count: nat):
            (valid_tagged_partition(
                left, right, points, tags, count)
              AND mesh_less_than(points, count, mesh_bound))
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count)
                  - integral_value)
                < epsilon_value

  interval_integral(
      f: real_function,
      left, right: real): real =
    IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
        has_interval_integral(f, left, right, integral_value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
          has_interval_integral(
            f, left, right, integral_value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  converges_at_real_top(
      values: positive_real_function,
      limit_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: posreal):
        FORALL (radius: posreal):
          cutoff <= radius IMPLIES
            abs(values(radius) - limit_value) < epsilon_value

  has_improper_integral(
      degree: nat,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    converges_at_real_top(
      LAMBDA (radius: posreal):
        interval_integral(integrand(degree), 0, radius),
      integral_value)

  improper_integral(degree: nat): real =
    IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
        has_improper_integral(degree, integral_value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
          has_improper_integral(degree, integral_value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  putnam_1978_a3_solution: nat = 2

  putnam_1978_a3: bool =
    1 <= putnam_1978_a3_solution
      AND putnam_1978_a3_solution <= 4
      AND FORALL (degree: nat):
        (1 <= degree AND degree <= 4)
          IMPLIES
            improper_integral(putnam_1978_a3_solution)
              <= improper_integral(degree)
END putnam_1978_a3

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1978_a4:
   consequences of the binary-operation identity (ab)(cd) = ad and the
   existence of a finite operation satisfying three additional conditions.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List.

Definition putnam_1978_a4_finite_type (S : Type) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list S,
    forall x : S, List.In x enumeration.

Definition putnam_1978_a4_bypass
    {S : Type}
    (op : S -> S -> S) : Prop :=
  forall a b c d : S,
    op (op a b) (op c d) = op a d.

Theorem putnam_1978_a4 :
  (forall (S : Type) (op : S -> S -> S),
      putnam_1978_a4_bypass op ->
      forall a b c : S,
        op a b = c ->
        op c c = c /\
        forall d : S, op a d = op c d) /\
  (exists (S : Type) (op : S -> S -> S),
      putnam_1978_a4_finite_type S /\
      putnam_1978_a4_bypass op /\
      (forall a : S, op a a = a) /\
      (exists a b : S, op a b = a /\ a <> b) /\
      (exists a b : S, op a b <> a)).
Admitted.

theory putnam_1978_a4 imports Complex_Main
begin

definition putnam_1978_a4_bypass ::
  "'a set \<Rightarrow> ('a \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> 'a) \<Rightarrow> bool" where
"putnam_1978_a4_bypass \<equiv> \<lambda> S Smul.
  \<forall> a \<in> S. \<forall> b \<in> S. \<forall> c \<in> S. \<forall> d \<in> S.
    Smul (Smul a b) (Smul c d) = Smul a d"

theorem putnam_1978_a4:
  shows "(\<forall> (S :: 'a set) (Smul :: 'a \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> 'a).
        (((\<forall> a \<in> S. \<forall> b \<in> S. Smul a b \<in> S) \<and> putnam_1978_a4_bypass S Smul)
        \<longrightarrow> (\<forall> a \<in> S. \<forall> b \<in> S. \<forall> c \<in> S. Smul a b = c \<longrightarrow> (Smul c c = c \<and> (\<forall> d \<in> S. Smul a d = Smul c d))))) \<and>
        (\<exists> (S :: nat set) (Smul :: nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat).
        (\<forall> a \<in> S. \<forall> b \<in> S. Smul a b \<in> S) \<and>
        putnam_1978_a4_bypass S Smul \<and> finite S \<and>
        (\<forall> a \<in> S. Smul a a = a) \<and>
        (\<exists> a \<in> S. \<exists> b \<in> S. Smul a b = a \<and> a \<noteq> b) \<and>
        (\<exists> a \<in> S. \<exists> b \<in> S. Smul a b \<noteq> a))"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_1978_a4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a4:
;; consequences of the bypass identity (a*b)*(c*d) = a*d and the existence
;; of a finite idempotent bypass algebra with two specified nontrivial
;; multiplication behaviors. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For the universal part, DEFSTUB supplies an arbitrary carrier predicate and
;; binary operation conservatively. The existential finite algebra below is
;; represented separately by concrete finite data.

(defstub putnam-1978-a4-carrier (x) t)
(defstub putnam-1978-a4-operation (x y) t)

(defun putnam-1978-a4-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-1978-a4-quoted function)
        (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-1978-a4-quoted function)
        (list 'cons left
              (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-1978-a4-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-operation-term (op left right)
  (putnam-1978-a4-apply2-term op left right))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-all-in-carrier-term
    (carrier variables)
  (if (endp variables)
      (putnam-1978-a4-quoted t)
    (list 'if
          (putnam-1978-a4-carrier-term
           carrier (car variables))
          (putnam-1978-a4-all-in-carrier-term
           carrier (cdr variables))
          (putnam-1978-a4-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-restricted-predicate-term
    (carrier variables proposition)
  (list 'if
        (putnam-1978-a4-all-in-carrier-term
         carrier variables)
        proposition
        (putnam-1978-a4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda formals (putnam-1978-a4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-operation-closure-function
    (carrier op)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(a b)
   (putnam-1978-a4-restricted-predicate-term
    carrier
    '(a b)
    (putnam-1978-a4-carrier-term
     carrier
     (putnam-1978-a4-operation-term op 'a 'b)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-bypass-function (carrier op)
  (let* ((op-ab
          (putnam-1978-a4-operation-term op 'a 'b))
         (op-cd
          (putnam-1978-a4-operation-term op 'c 'd)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(a b c d)
     (putnam-1978-a4-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(a b c d)
      (list
       'equal
       (putnam-1978-a4-operation-term op op-ab op-cd)
       (putnam-1978-a4-operation-term op 'a 'd))))))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-member-p (element)
  (if (putnam-1978-a4-carrier element) t nil))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-multiply (left right)
  (putnam-1978-a4-operation left right))

(defun-sk putnam-1978-a4-operation-closed-p ()
  (forall (a b)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1978-a4-member-p a)
      (putnam-1978-a4-member-p b))
     (putnam-1978-a4-member-p
      (putnam-1978-a4-multiply a b)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1978-a4-bypass-p ()
  (forall (a b c d)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1978-a4-member-p a)
      (putnam-1978-a4-member-p b)
      (putnam-1978-a4-member-p c)
      (putnam-1978-a4-member-p d))
     (equal
      (putnam-1978-a4-multiply
       (putnam-1978-a4-multiply a b)
       (putnam-1978-a4-multiply c d))
      (putnam-1978-a4-multiply a d)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-algebra-p ()
  (and
   (putnam-1978-a4-operation-closed-p)
   (putnam-1978-a4-bypass-p)))

;; The existential finite algebra is represented by
;;
;;   (carrier pairs quadruples operation-table).
;;
;; CARRIER is a duplicate-free nonempty list. PAIRS and QUADRUPLES are
;; duplicate-free complete enumerations, certified by membership and the
;; cardinalities |S|^2 and |S|^4. OPERATION-TABLE has one closed value for
;; every ordered pair. Thus this data is definitionally equivalent, up to
;; enumeration order, to a finite type with a binary operation.
;;
;; ALWAYS$ and THEREIS$ retain the finite inner universal and existential
;; conditions. The final DEFUN-SK below explicitly quantifies the complete
;; finite-algebra witness; function extensionality is not used as a surrogate
;; for that existential quantifier.

;; The following helpers construct tame lambda terms. They run while building
;; the existential predicate and are not themselves called through APPLY$.

(defun putnam-1978-a4-expression-list (expressions)
  (if (endp expressions)
      (putnam-1978-a4-quoted nil)
    (list 'cons
          (car expressions)
          (putnam-1978-a4-expression-list
           (cdr expressions)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-data-call-expression
    (function argument-expressions)
  (putnam-1978-a4-expression-list
   (cons (putnam-1978-a4-quoted function)
         argument-expressions)))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-runtime-quote-expression (value-term)
  (putnam-1978-a4-expression-list
   (list (putnam-1978-a4-quoted 'quote)
         value-term)))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-dynamic-lambda-expression
    (formals body-term-expression)
  (putnam-1978-a4-expression-list
   (list (putnam-1978-a4-quoted 'lambda)
         (putnam-1978-a4-quoted formals)
         body-term-expression)))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-data-if-expression
    (test-expression then-expression else-expression)
  (putnam-1978-a4-data-call-expression
   'if
   (list test-expression then-expression else-expression)))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-data-and-expression (expressions)
  (if (endp expressions)
      (putnam-1978-a4-quoted '(quote t))
    (putnam-1978-a4-data-if-expression
     (car expressions)
     (putnam-1978-a4-data-and-expression
      (cdr expressions))
     (putnam-1978-a4-quoted '(quote nil)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-and-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-1978-a4-quoted t)
    (list 'if
          (car terms)
          (putnam-1978-a4-and-term (cdr terms))
          (putnam-1978-a4-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-not-term (term)
  (list 'if
        term
        (putnam-1978-a4-quoted nil)
        (putnam-1978-a4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-1978-a4-table-operation-expression
    (table-value-term left-term-expression right-term-expression)
  (let* ((nil-term-expression

title: putnam_1978_a4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a4:
-- a bypass binary operation satisfying (ab)(cd) = ad has the stated
-- idempotence and translation consequences, and admits a finite example
-- satisfying conditions (A), (B), and (C). This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1978A4 where

open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; _⊔_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not :
  {level : Level} ->
  Set level ->
  Set level
Not proposition =
  proposition -> Bottom

_!=_ :
  {level : Level} ->
  {A : Set level} ->
  A ->
  A ->
  Set level
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_
  {left-level right-level : Level}
  (A : Set left-level)
  (B : Set right-level) :
  Set (left-level ⊔ right-level) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record ExistsPair
  {level property-level : Level}
  (A : Set level)
  (P : A -> A -> Set property-level) :
  Set (level ⊔ property-level) where

  constructor pair-witness
  field
    left     : A
    right    : A
    property : P left right

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record Finite
  {level : Level}
  (A : Set level) :
  Set level where

  field
    cardinality : Nat
    toFin        : A -> Fin cardinality
    fromFin      : Fin cardinality -> A
    from-to      : (x : A) -> fromFin (toFin x) == x
    to-from      : (i : Fin cardinality) -> toFin (fromFin i) == i

Bypass :
  {level : Level} ->
  {S : Set level} ->
  (S -> S -> S) ->
  Set level
Bypass multiply =
  (a b c d : _) ->
  multiply (multiply a b) (multiply c d) == multiply a d

record ProductConsequences
  {level : Level}
  {S : Set level}
  (multiply : S -> S -> S)
  (a c : S) :
  Set level where

  field
    product-idempotent :
      multiply c c == c
    same-right-translations :
      (d : S) ->
      multiply a d == multiply c d

UniversalConclusion : Set1
UniversalConclusion =
  (S : Set) ->
  (multiply : S -> S -> S) ->
  Bypass multiply ->
  (a b c : S) ->
  multiply a b == c ->
  ProductConsequences multiply a c

record FiniteBypassExample : Set1 where
  field
    Carrier : Set
    multiply : Carrier -> Carrier -> Carrier
    finite-carrier : Finite Carrier
    bypass :
      Bypass multiply
    condition-A :
      (a : Carrier) ->
      multiply a a == a
    condition-B :
      ExistsPair Carrier
        (\ a b ->
          multiply a b == a
          and
          a != b)
    condition-C :
      ExistsPair Carrier
        (\ a b ->
          multiply a b != a)

putnam-1978-a4 : Set1
putnam-1978-a4 =
  UniversalConclusion
  and
  FiniteBypassExample

title: putnam_1978_a4

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1978_a4:
  consequences of the bypass law (ab)(cd) = ad for a binary operation, and
  existence of a finite example with specified idempotence and nontriviality.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory;

val putnam_1978_a4 =
  ``(!(mul : 'a -> 'a -> 'a).
       (!a b c d : 'a. mul (mul a b) (mul c d) = mul a d)
       ==>
       (!a b c : 'a.
          mul a b = c
          ==>
          mul c c = c /\ (!d : 'a. mul a d = mul c d))) /\
    (?S : num set.
       ?(mul : num -> num -> num).
         FINITE S /\
         (!a b : num. a IN S /\ b IN S ==> mul a b IN S) /\
         (!a b c d : num.
            a IN S /\ b IN S /\ c IN S /\ d IN S
            ==>
            mul (mul a b) (mul c d) = mul a d) /\
         (!a : num. a IN S ==> mul a a = a) /\
         (?a b : num.
            a IN S /\ b IN S /\ mul a b = a /\ a <> b) /\
         (?a b : num.
            a IN S /\ b IN S /\ mul a b <> a))``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1978_a4: consequences and a finite example for binary operations
  satisfying (a * b) * (c * d) = a * d. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  An arbitrary source carrier is represented by the set s, and f is a total
  binary operation represented as a function from s X. s to s. Application
  to an ordered pair represents the source multiplication.

  The first conjunct quantifies over every carrier and operation satisfying
  the bypass identity and states both requested consequences of a * b = c.
  The second conjunct keeps the finite carrier and its operation internally
  existential and states the bypass identity together with conditions
  (A), (B), and (C).

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a b c d f s $.

  putnambench-putnam-1978-a4 $a |- (
    (
      A. s
        A. f e. ( s ^m ( s X. s ) )
          (
            A. a e. s A. b e. s A. c e. s A. d e. s
              ( f ` <. ( f ` <. a , b >. ) , ( f ` <. c , d >. ) >. )
              =
              ( f ` <. a , d >. )
            ->
            A. a e. s A. b e. s A. c e. s
              (
                ( f ` <. a , b >. ) = c
                ->
                (
                  ( f ` <. c , c >. ) = c
                  /\
                  A. d e. s
                    ( f ` <. a , d >. ) = ( f ` <. c , d >. )
                )
              )
          )
    )
    /\
    E. s e. Fin
      E. f e. ( s ^m ( s X. s ) )
        (
          A. a e. s A. b e. s A. c e. s A. d e. s
            ( f ` <. ( f ` <. a , b >. ) , ( f ` <. c , d >. ) >. )
            =
            ( f ` <. a , d >. )
          /\
          (
            A. a e. s
              ( f ` <. a , a >. ) = a
            /\
            (
              E. a e. s E. b e. s
                (
                  ( f ` <. a , b >. ) = a
                  /\
                  a =/= b
                )
              /\
              E. a e. s E. b e. s
                ( f ` <. a , b >. ) =/= a
            )
          )
        )
  ) $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a4:
% consequences of the bypass identity for a binary operation, together with
% the existence of a finite example satisfying three extra laws. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1978_a4[Carrier: TYPE+]: THEORY
BEGIN
  operation: TYPE = [Carrier, Carrier -> Carrier]

  bypass(op: operation): bool =
    FORALL (a, b, c, d: Carrier):
      op(op(a, b), op(c, d)) = op(a, d)

  putnam_1978_a4: bool =
    (FORALL (op: operation):
      bypass(op) IMPLIES
        FORALL (a, b, c: Carrier):
          op(a, b) = c IMPLIES
            op(c, c) = c
              AND (FORALL (d: Carrier):
                op(a, d) = op(c, d)))
      AND
        (EXISTS (n: posnat):
          EXISTS (op: [below(n), below(n) -> below(n)]):
            (FORALL (a, b, c, d: below(n)):
              op(op(a, b), op(c, d)) = op(a, d))
              AND (FORALL (a: below(n)):
                op(a, a) = a)
              AND (EXISTS (a, b: below(n)):
                op(a, b) = a AND a /= b)
              AND (EXISTS (a, b: below(n)):
                op(a, b) /= a))
END putnam_1978_a4

title: putnam_1978_a5
putnam_1978_a5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a5:
;; for a nonempty finite family of real numbers in (0, pi), the product of
;; sin(x)/x is at most the corresponding power at their arithmetic mean.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; ACL2's exact rationals give a dense presentation of this universal real
;; inequality. For each fixed positive family size, the defect between the two
;; sides is continuous on (0,pi)^n. Hence a positive real defect would persist
;; at a nearby rational tuple, while every rational tuple is already a real
;; tuple. The rational presentation below is therefore bidirectionally
;; equivalent to the source's arbitrary real family, not a domain restriction.
;;
;; The even Leibniz partial sums increase to pi. Thus the union, over
;; domain-precision, of the rational intervals
;;
;;   (0, putnam-1978-a5-pi-lower(domain-precision))
;;
;; is exactly the rational part of (0,pi). Since domain-precision is
;; universally quantified with the other defun arguments, every rational
;; tuple in the source domain is captured once a sufficiently large lower
;; approximant is used.

(defun putnam-1978-a5-factorial (n)
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n
       (putnam-1978-a5-factorial (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-1978-a5-leibniz-prefix (terms)
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (sign (if (equal (mod index 2) 0) 1 -1)))
      (+ (putnam-1978-a5-leibniz-prefix index)
         (/ sign (+ (* 2 index) 1))))))

(defun putnam-1978-a5-pi-lower (domain-precision)
  (* 4
     (putnam-1978-a5-leibniz-prefix
      (* 2 (+ 1 (nfix domain-precision))))))

(defun putnam-1978-a5-positive-rational-list-below-p
    (values bound)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (rationalp (car values))
       (< 0 (car values))
       (< (car values) bound)
       (putnam-1978-a5-positive-rational-list-below-p
        (cdr values) bound))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-1978-a5-sum (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (+ (car values)
         (putnam-1978-a5-sum (cdr values)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1978-a5-product (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (* (car values)
         (putnam-1978-a5-product (cdr values)))
    1))

;; This is the Maclaurin prefix
;;
;;   sum_(j < terms) (-1)^j x^(2j+1)/(2j+1)!.
(defun putnam-1978-a5-sine-prefix (x terms)
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (degree (+ (* 2 index) 1))
           (sign (if (equal (mod index 2) 0) 1 -1)))
      (+ (putnam-1978-a5-sine-prefix x index)
         (/ (* sign (expt x degree))
            (putnam-1978-a5-factorial degree))))))

(defun putnam-1978-a5-sinc-prefix-product (values terms)
  (if (consp values)
      (* (/ (putnam-1978-a5-sine-prefix
             (car values) terms)
            (car values))
         (putnam-1978-a5-sinc-prefix-product
          (cdr values) terms))
    1))

(defun putnam-1978-a5-prefix-defect (values n terms)
  (let* ((mean
          (/ (putnam-1978-a5-sum values) n))
         (left-prefix
          (putnam-1978-a5-sinc-prefix-product
           values terms))
         (mean-prefix
          (/ (putnam-1978-a5-sine-prefix mean terms)
             mean)))
    (- left-prefix
       (expt mean-prefix n))))

;; For each fixed rational tuple, the prefix defect converges to the exact
;; source defect. The exact inequality defect <= 0 is therefore equivalent
;; to saying that every positive rational tolerance eventually bounds every
;; sufficiently long prefix defect. The cutoff is existential: no convergence
;; rate beyond the source proposition is asserted.
(defun-sk putnam-1978-a5-tail-p
    (values n epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (terms)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp terms)
      (<= cutoff terms))
     (< (putnam-1978-a5-prefix-defect
         values n terms)
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1978-a5-cutoff-exists-p
    (values n epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (< 0 cutoff)
     (putnam-1978-a5-tail-p
      values n epsilon cutoff))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1978-a5-statement
    (values n domain-precision epsilon)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp n)
    (< 0 n)
    (natp domain-precision)
    (rationalp epsilon)
    (< 0 epsilon)
    (equal (len values) n)
    (putnam-1978-a5-positive-rational-list-below-p
     values
     (putnam-1978-a5-pi-lower domain-precision)))
   (putnam-1978-a5-cutoff-exists-p
    values n epsilon)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1978_a5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a5:
-- the product of sin(a_i)/a_i for positive real numbers below pi is bounded
-- by the corresponding power evaluated at their arithmetic mean. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  suc zero
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

alternatingPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingPower reals n =
  naturalPower reals (negate reals (oneR reals)) n

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc (suc (suc (suc zero)))

sineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
sineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (suc (twoN * n))))
    (fromNat reals (factorial (suc (twoN * n))))

leibnizTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
leibnizTerm reals n =
  divide reals
    (alternatingPower reals n)
    (fromNat reals (suc (twoN * n)))

record StandardSineAndPi
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) : Set1 where
  field
    sine : R -> R
    pi : R

    sine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (sineTerm reals x)
        (sine x)
    pi-positive :
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) pi
    pi-leibniz-series :
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (leibnizTerm reals)
        (divide reals pi (fromNat reals fourN))

open StandardSineAndPi

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

productFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
productFin reals {zero} term =
  oneR reals
productFin reals {suc n} term =
  multiply reals
    (term fzero)
    (productFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

arithmeticMean :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
arithmeticMean reals {n} a =
  divide reals
    (sumFin reals a)
    (fromNat reals n)

module Putnam1978A5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (trigonometry : StandardSineAndPi reals) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (n : Nat) ->
    Positive n ->
    (a : Fin n -> R) ->
    ((i : Fin n) ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (a i)
      and
      StrictLess reals (a i) (pi trigonometry)) ->
    lessOrEqual reals
      (productFin reals
        (\ i ->
          divide reals
            (sine trigonometry (a i))
            (a i)))
      (naturalPower reals
        (divide reals
          (sine trigonometry (arithmeticMean reals a))
          (arithmeticMean reals a))
        n)

putnam-1978-a5 : Set1
putnam-1978-a5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (trigonometry : StandardSineAndPi reals) ->
  Putnam1978A5Statement.proposition reals trigonometry

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1978_a5:
  the product inequality comparing sinc values of finitely many reals in
  the open interval from zero to pi with the sinc of their arithmetic mean.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_1978_a5 =
  ``!n : num. !a : num -> real. !mu : real.
      0 < n /\
      (!i : num. i < n ==> 0 < a i /\ a i < pi) /\
      mu = SIGMA (\i : num. a i / &n) (count n)
      ==>
      real_sigma$product
        (count n)
        (\i : num. sin (a i) / a i) <=
      (sin mu / mu) pow n``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1978_a5: the product of sin(a_i)/a_i for finitely many real
  numbers in (0, pi) is bounded by the corresponding power at their
  arithmetic mean. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  NN is SetMM's class of positive natural numbers, so 1 ... n is a
  nonempty n-element index set. The class RR ^m ( 1 ... n ) contains
  every real-valued family on that set. This presentation is carried to
  Lean's Fin n family and Rocq's length-n sequence by their canonical
  index bijections, which preserve the finite sum and product.

  The equality defining m states that it is the arithmetic mean. Since
  n is positive, summing a_i / n as in the Lean and Rocq sources equals
  dividing the finite sum by n as in the Isabelle source and below.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a i m n $.

  putnambench-putnam-1978-a5 $a |-
    A. n e. NN
    A. a e. ( RR ^m ( 1 ... n ) )
    A. m e. RR
      (
        (
          A. i e. ( 1 ... n )
            (
              0 < ( a ` i )
              /\
              ( a ` i ) < _pi
            )
          /\
          m =
            (
              (
                sum_ i e. ( 1 ... n )
                  ( a ` i )
              )
              /
              n
            )
        )
        ->
        (
          prod_ i e. ( 1 ... n )
            (
              ( sin ` ( a ` i ) )
              /
              ( a ` i )
            )
        )
        <_
        (
          (
            ( sin ` m )
            /
            m
          )
          ^
          n
        )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1978_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1978_a5:
% the product of sinc values of finitely many reals in (0, pi) is at most
% the corresponding power of the sinc value of their arithmetic mean. This
% file contains no proof.

putnam_1978_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  sine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        sine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index + 1),
              factorial(2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  cosine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index),
              factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  sine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): sine_partial(x, count),
          value))

  cosine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): cosine_partial(x, count),
          value))

  pi: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        3 < value
          AND value < 4
          AND cosine(value / 2) = 0)

  prefix_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      prefix_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  sinc_product(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      sinc_product(values, count - 1)
        * safe_div(sine(values(count - 1)), values(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  arithmetic_mean(values: real_sequence, count: nat): real =
    safe_div(prefix_sum(values, count), count :: real)

  putnam_1978_a5: bool =
    FORALL (n: posnat), (a: real_sequence):
      (FORALL (index: nat):
        index < n IMPLIES
          0 < a(index) AND a(index) < pi)
      IMPLIES
        sinc_product(a, n)
          <= safe_div(
              sine(arithmetic_mean(a, n)),
              arithmetic_mean(a, n)) ^ n
END putnam_1978_a5

Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.
Local Open Scope seq_scope.

Variable R : realType.
Definition sq_dist (p q : (R * R)%type) := (p.1 - q.1) ^ 2 + (p.2 - q.2) ^ 2.
Definition ind_is_unit_dist_apart (p q : (R * R)%type) : R := if sq_dist p q == 1 then 1%R else 0%R.
Theorem putnam_1978_a6
    (n : nat)
    (npos : gt n 0)
    (A : seq (R*R))
    (hA : size A = n /\ uniq A)
    : ((1 / 2 : R) * (\sum_(p <- A) (\sum_(q <- A) ind_is_unit_dist_apart p q))
        < 2 * expR ((3 / 2 : R) * ln n%:R))%R.
Proof. Admitted.
