content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1980_b1:
-- the real parameters for which (exp x + exp (-x)) / 2 is at most exp (c * x^2)
-- for every real x are exactly those with c at least 1 / 2. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  suc zero
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

exponentialTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

record StandardExponential
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    exponential : R -> R
    exponential-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (exponentialTerm reals x)
        (exponential x)

open StandardExponential

two : Nat
two =
  suc (suc zero)

module Putnam1980B1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (standardExponential : StandardExponential reals) where

  half : R
  half =
    divide reals
      (oneR reals)
      (fromNat reals two)

  inequalityAt : R -> R -> Set
  inequalityAt c x =
    lessOrEqual reals
      (divide reals
        (add reals
          (exponential standardExponential x)
          (exponential standardExponential (negate reals x)))
        (fromNat reals two))
      (exponential standardExponential
        (multiply reals
          c
          (naturalPower reals x two)))

  qualifies : R -> Set
  qualifies c =
    (x : R) ->
    inequalityAt c x

  solution : R -> Set
  solution c =
    lessOrEqual reals half c

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (c : R) ->
    Iff (qualifies c) (solution c)

putnam-1980-b1 : Set1
putnam-1980-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (standardExponential : StandardExponential reals) ->
  Putnam1980B1Statement.proposition reals standardExponential

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1980_b1:
% the real constants c for which (exp(x) + exp(-x)) / 2 is at most
% exp(c * x^2) for every real x. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1980_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  putnam_1980_b1_solution(c: real): bool =
    c >= 1 / 2

  putnam_1980_b1: bool =
    FORALL (c: real):
      (FORALL (x: real):
        (real_exponential(x) + real_exponential(-x)) / 2
          <= real_exponential(c * x ^ 2))
      IFF putnam_1980_b1_solution(c)
END putnam_1980_b1

title: putnam_1980_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1980_b3:
;; characterize the initial real value a for which every term of the real
;; sequence u, defined by u(0) = a and u(n+1) = 2*u(n) - n^2, is positive.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; An arbitrary real number is represented exactly by a regular rational
;; Cauchy name.  At positive rational precision epsilon, the name supplies a
;; rational approximation whose distance from the represented real is at
;; most epsilon.  The regularity condition below is an exact, bidirectional
;; presentation of the completion of the rationals: every such name
;; determines one real number, and every real number admits such a name.
(defstub p80b3-a-approx (a precision) t)

;; Likewise, SEQUENCE is an exact name for an arbitrary function N -> R:
;; p80b3-u-approx supplies a regular rational Cauchy name independently at
;; every natural-number index.  Every real-valued sequence admits such a
;; pointwise name, so this representation does not restrict the source domain.
(defstub p80b3-u-approx (sequence index precision) t)

(defun p80b3-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and (rationalp x)
       (< 0 x)))

(defun-sk p80b3-real-name-p (a)
  (forall
   (epsilon eta)
   (implies
    (and (p80b3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
         (p80b3-positive-rational-p eta))
    (let ((left (p80b3-a-approx a epsilon))
          (right (p80b3-a-approx a eta)))
      (and (rationalp left)
           (rationalp right)
           (<= (abs (- left right))
               (+ epsilon eta)))))))

(defun-sk p80b3-sequence-name-p (sequence)
  (forall
   (index epsilon eta)
   (implies
    (and (natp index)
         (p80b3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
         (p80b3-positive-rational-p eta))
    (let ((left (p80b3-u-approx sequence index epsilon))
          (right (p80b3-u-approx sequence index eta)))
      (and (rationalp left)
           (rationalp right)
           (<= (abs (- left right))
               (+ epsilon eta)))))))

;; For regular names, two represented reals are equal exactly when their
;; same-precision approximations differ by at most 2*epsilon at every
;; positive rational epsilon.  Thus this predicate states u(0) = a.
(defun-sk p80b3-initial-value-p (a sequence)
  (forall
   (epsilon)
   (implies
    (p80b3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
    (let ((a-epsilon (p80b3-a-approx a epsilon))
          (u0-epsilon (p80b3-u-approx sequence 0 epsilon)))
      (and (rationalp a-epsilon)
           (rationalp u0-epsilon)
           (<= (abs (- u0-epsilon a-epsilon))
               (* 2 epsilon)))))))

;; The right-hand approximation uses precision epsilon/2 before multiplication
;; by 2, so it approximates 2*u(n)-n^2 within epsilon.  Comparing it with an
;; epsilon-approximation of u(n+1) using the bound 2*epsilon is therefore
;; exactly equivalent, for regular names, to
;;     u(n+1) = 2*u(n) - n^2
;; at every natural-number index.
(defun-sk p80b3-recurrence-p (sequence)
  (forall
   (index epsilon)
   (implies
    (and (natp index)
         (p80b3-positive-rational-p epsilon))
    (let* ((next-value
            (p80b3-u-approx sequence (+ 1 index) epsilon))
           (current-value
            (p80b3-u-approx sequence index (/ epsilon 2)))
           (right-hand-side
            (- (* 2 current-value)
               (* index index))))
      (and (rationalp next-value)
           (rationalp current-value)
           (<= (abs (- next-value right-hand-side))
               (* 2 epsilon)))))))

;; A represented real x is strictly positive exactly when there is a positive
;; rational lower bound L such that L <= x_epsilon + epsilon at every positive
;; rational precision.  The existential margin remains internal to positivity.
(defun-sk p80b3-positive-margin-p (sequence index lower)
  (forall
   (epsilon)
   (implies
    (p80b3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
    (let ((value (p80b3-u-approx sequence index epsilon)))
      (and (rationalp value)
           (<= lower (+ value epsilon)))))))

(defun-sk p80b3-positive-at-index-p (sequence index)
  (exists
   (lower)
   (and (p80b3-positive-rational-p lower)
        (p80b3-positive-margin-p sequence index lower))))

(defun-sk p80b3-positive-at-every-index-p (sequence)
  (forall
   (index)
   (implies
    (natp index)
    (p80b3-positive-at-index-p sequence index))))

;; For a regular name, the represented real is at least 3 exactly when every
;; epsilon-approximation plus its error allowance is at least 3.
(defun-sk p80b3-at-least-three-p (a)
  (forall
   (epsilon)
   (implies
    (p80b3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
    (let ((value (p80b3-a-approx a epsilon)))
      (and (rationalp value)
           (<= 3 (+ value epsilon)))))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1980-b3-statement (a sequence)
  (implies
   (and (p80b3-real-name-p a)
        (p80b3-sequence-name-p sequence)
        (p80b3-initial-value-p a sequence)
        (p80b3-recurrence-p sequence))
   (iff (p80b3-positive-at-every-index-p sequence)
        (p80b3-at-least-three-p a))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where

    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where

  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where

  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

module Putnam1980B3Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  indexSquare : Nat -> R
  indexSquare n =
    multiply reals
      (fromNat reals n)
      (fromNat reals n)

  RecurrenceHypothesis :
    R ->
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  RecurrenceHypothesis a u =
    u zero == a
    and
    ((n : Nat) ->
      u (suc n) ==
      subtract reals
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals twoN)
          (u n))
        (indexSquare n))

  AlwaysPositive :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  AlwaysPositive u =
    (n : Nat) ->
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (u n)

  Solution : R -> Set
  Solution a =
    lessOrEqual reals
      (fromNat reals threeN)
      a

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (a : R) ->
    (u : Nat -> R) ->
    RecurrenceHypothesis a u ->
    Iff
      (AlwaysPositive u)
      (Solution a)

putnam-1980-b3 : Set1
putnam-1980-b3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1980B3Statement.proposition reals

title: putnam_1980_b4

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1980_b4:
;; 1,066 subsets of a finite set, each containing more than half its elements,
;; have a 10-element subset meeting every one. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A finite set is represented by a duplicate-free true list. The order of
;; FAMILY represents the finite index set, and each entry is a duplicate-free
;; enumeration of the corresponding subset. Choosing enumerations gives this
;; representation for every source X and A, while forgetting list order and
;; reading positions as indices recovers them. Thus the representation is
;; bidirectional and does not restrict the element type or the finite sets.

(defun putnam-1980-b4-subsetp-equal (subset carrier)
  (if (consp subset)
      (and
       (member-equal (car subset) carrier)
       (putnam-1980-b4-subsetp-equal
        (cdr subset) carrier))
    (equal subset nil)))

(defun putnam-1980-b4-family-hypotheses-p
    (family carrier)
  (if (consp family)
      (and
       (true-listp (car family))
       (no-duplicatesp-equal (car family))
       (putnam-1980-b4-subsetp-equal
        (car family) carrier)
       (< (len carrier) (* 2 (len (car family))))
       (putnam-1980-b4-family-hypotheses-p
        (cdr family) carrier))
    (equal family nil)))

(defun putnam-1980-b4-intersects-p (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (or
       (member-equal (car left) right)
       (putnam-1980-b4-intersects-p
        (cdr left) right))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1980-b4-meets-every-p
    (candidate family)
  (if (consp family)
      (and
       (putnam-1980-b4-intersects-p
        candidate (car family))
       (putnam-1980-b4-meets-every-p
        candidate (cdr family)))
    (equal family nil)))

;; This exhaustive recursion ranges over every subset of CARRIER. CHOSEN is
;; constructed only from carrier elements, so a successful leaf is exactly an
;; internal 10-element subset witness meeting every member of FAMILY.
(defun putnam-1980-b4-transversal-exists-p
    (remaining chosen family)
  (declare (xargs :measure (len remaining)))
  (if (consp remaining)
      (or
       (putnam-1980-b4-transversal-exists-p
        (cdr remaining)
        (cons (car remaining) chosen)
        family)
       (putnam-1980-b4-transversal-exists-p
        (cdr remaining)
        chosen
        family))
    (and
     (equal remaining nil)
     (equal (len chosen) 10)
     (putnam-1980-b4-meets-every-p
      chosen family))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1980-b4-statement
    (carrier family)
  (implies
   (and
    (true-listp carrier)
    (no-duplicatesp-equal carrier)
    (<= 10 (len carrier))
    (true-listp family)
    (equal (len family) 1066)
    (putnam-1980-b4-family-hypotheses-p
     family carrier))
   (putnam-1980-b4-transversal-exists-p
    carrier nil family)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1980_b4:
-- among 1066 subsets of a finite set, each containing more than half of its
-- elements, there is a ten-element subset meeting every one. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1980B4 where

open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc; _⊔_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists
  {a p : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (P : A -> Set p) :
  Set (a ⊔ p) where

  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record FiniteSubset
  {a : Level}
  (T : Set a) :
  Set a where

  field
    cardinality : Nat
    element : Fin cardinality -> T
    injective :
      (i j : Fin cardinality) ->
      element i == element j ->
      i == j

open FiniteSubset

Member :
  {a : Level} ->
  {T : Set a} ->
  T ->
  FiniteSubset T ->
  Set a
Member x S =
  Exists (Fin (cardinality S))
    (\ i -> x == element S i)

SubsetOf :
  {a : Level} ->
  {T : Set a} ->
  FiniteSubset T ->
  FiniteSubset T ->
  Set a
SubsetOf {T = T} S U =
  (x : T) ->
  Member x S ->
  Member x U

Meets :
  {a : Level} ->
  {T : Set a} ->
  FiniteSubset T ->
  FiniteSubset T ->
  Set a
Meets {T = T} S U =
  Exists T
    (\ x -> Member x S and Member x U)

putnam-1980-b4 :
  {a : Level} ->
  Set (lsuc a)
putnam-1980-b4 {a} =
  (T : Set a) ->
  (X : FiniteSubset T) ->
  (A : Fin 1066 -> FiniteSubset T) ->
  10 <=N cardinality X ->
  ((i : Fin 1066) ->
    SubsetOf (A i) X
    and
    cardinality X <N 2 * cardinality (A i)) ->
  Exists (FiniteSubset T)
    (\ Y ->
      SubsetOf Y X
      and
      cardinality Y == 10
      and
      ((i : Fin 1066) -> Meets Y (A i)))

import Mathlib

open Set

abbrev putnam_1980_b5_solution : ℝ → Prop := sorry
-- fun t : ℝ => 1 ≥ t
/--
A function $f$ is convex on $[0, 1]$ if and only if $$f(su + (1-s)v) \le sf(u) + (1 - s)f(v)$$ for all $s \in [0, 1]$.
Let $S_t$ denote the set of all nonnegative increasing convex continuous functions $f : [0, 1] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ such that $$f(1) - 2f\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) + f\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \ge t\left(f\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) - 2f\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) + f(0)\right).$$
For which real numbers $t \ge 0$ is $S_t$ closed under multiplication?
-/
theorem putnam_1980_b5
    (T : Set ℝ)
    (hT : T = Icc 0 1)
    (P : ℝ → (ℝ → ℝ) → Prop)
    (IsConvex : (ℝ → ℝ) → Prop)

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1980_b5:
   multiplicative closure of nonnegative strictly increasing convex continuous
   real functions on [0,1] satisfying a parameterized finite-difference
   inequality; this file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_1980_b5_unit_interval (x : R) : Prop :=
  0 <= x <= 1.

Definition putnam_1980_b5_strictly_increasing_on_unit
    (f : R -> R) : Prop :=
  forall x y : R,
    putnam_1980_b5_unit_interval x ->
    putnam_1980_b5_unit_interval y ->
    x < y ->
    f x < f y.

Definition putnam_1980_b5_convex_on_unit
    (f : R -> R) : Prop :=
  forall u v s : R,
    putnam_1980_b5_unit_interval u ->
    putnam_1980_b5_unit_interval v ->
    putnam_1980_b5_unit_interval s ->
    f (s * u + (1 - s) * v) <=
      s * f u + (1 - s) * f v.

Definition putnam_1980_b5_continuous_on_unit
    (f : R -> R) : Prop :=
  forall x : R,
    putnam_1980_b5_unit_interval x ->
    forall epsilon : R,
      epsilon > 0 ->
      exists delta : R,
        delta > 0 /\
        forall y : R,
          putnam_1980_b5_unit_interval y ->
          Rabs (y - x) < delta ->
          Rabs (f y - f x) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_1980_b5_difference_condition
    (t : R) (f : R -> R) : Prop :=
  f 1 - 2 * f (2 / 3) + f (1 / 3) >=
    t * (f (2 / 3) - 2 * f (1 / 3) + f 0).

Definition putnam_1980_b5_class
    (t : R) (f : R -> R) : Prop :=
  (forall x : R,
      putnam_1980_b5_unit_interval x ->
      f x >= 0) /\
  putnam_1980_b5_strictly_increasing_on_unit f /\
  putnam_1980_b5_convex_on_unit f /\
  putnam_1980_b5_continuous_on_unit f /\
  putnam_1980_b5_difference_condition t f.

Definition putnam_1980_b5_solution (t : R) : Prop :=
  t <= 1.

Theorem putnam_1980_b5 :
  forall t : R,
    t >= 0 ->
    ((forall f g : R -> R,
        putnam_1980_b5_class t f ->
        putnam_1980_b5_class t g ->
        putnam_1980_b5_class t (fun x : R => f x * g x)) <->
      putnam_1980_b5_solution t).
Admitted.

theorem putnam_1980_b5:

  and "P \<equiv> \<lambda> (t :: real) (f :: real \<Rightarrow> real). f 1 - 2 * f (2 / 3) + f (1 / 3) \<ge> t * (f (2 / 3) - 2 * f (1 / 3) + f 0)"
  and "Convex \<equiv> \<lambda> f :: real \<Rightarrow> real. \<forall> u \<in> T. \<forall> v \<in> T. \<forall> s \<in> T. f (s * u + (1 - s) * v) \<le> s * (f u) + (1 - s) * (f v)"

title: putnam_1980_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1980_b5:
;; the parameters for which nonnegative strictly increasing convex continuous
;; functions satisfying a finite-difference inequality are closed under
;; pointwise multiplication. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Write a=f(0), b=f(1/3), c=f(2/3), and d=f(1).  Such values come from a
;; nonnegative strictly increasing convex continuous function on [0,1]
;; exactly when a>=0 and the three successive increments are positive and
;; nondecreasing: piecewise-linear interpolation gives the reverse direction.
;; The final inequality is precisely the defining P(t,f) condition.
(defun putnam-1980-b5-member-data-p (t-param a b c d)
  (and
   (rationalp t-param)
   (rationalp a)
   (rationalp b)
   (rationalp c)
   (rationalp d)
   (<= 0 a)
   (< a b)
   (< b c)
   (< c d)
   (<= (- b a) (- c b))
   (<= (- c b) (- d c))
   (<=
    (* t-param (+ c a (- (* 2 b))))
    (+ d b (- (* 2 c))))))

;; Nonnegativity, strict increase, convexity, and continuity are preserved by
;; the pointwise product of two source members.  Consequently closure under
;; multiplication is equivalent to this remaining P(t,f*g) inequality on
;; their four values.
(defun putnam-1980-b5-product-condition-p
    (t-param f0 f1 f2 f3 g0 g1 g2 g3)
  (<=
   (* t-param
      (+ (* f2 g2)
         (* f0 g0)
         (- (* 2 f1 g1))))
   (+ (* f3 g3)
      (* f1 g1)
      (- (* 2 f2 g2)))))

;; For t>1, let the successive increments of f=g be
;;
;;   1, 1+delta, 1+(t+1)*delta.
;;
;; Then P(t,f) and P(t,g) hold with equality.  The positive delta below is
;; small enough that P(t,f*g) fails, giving an internal counterexample rather
;; than exposing an existential function as a statement parameter.
(defun putnam-1980-b5-counterexample-delta (t-param)
  (if (and (rationalp t-param)
           (< 1 t-param))
      (/ (- t-param 1)
         (* 4
            (+ t-param 1)
            (+ t-param 2)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1980-b5-explicit-counterexample-p (t-param)
  (let* ((delta
          (putnam-1980-b5-counterexample-delta t-param))
         (a 0)
         (b 1)
         (c (+ 2 delta))
         (d (+ 3 (* (+ t-param 2) delta))))
    (and
     (putnam-1980-b5-member-data-p t-param a b c d)
     (not
      (putnam-1980-b5-product-condition-p
       t-param a b c d a b c d)))))

;; This is an exact rational encoding of the closed real statement, not a
;; restriction of its domain.  For rational t, any real counterexample to the
;; finite inequalities can be perturbed within their strict conditions to a
;; rational counterexample, and rational instances are real instances.
;; For a real t<=1, a product violation has a strictly smaller ratio, so a
;; rational parameter between that ratio and t would also be a counterexample.
;; For every real t>1, the explicit formula above is itself a real
;; counterexample.  Thus the universal rational statement below holds iff the
;; source universal real statement holds.
(defun putnambench-putnam-1980-b5-statement
    (t-param f0 f1 f2 f3 g0 g1 g2 g3)
  (implies
   (and
    (rationalp t-param)
    (<= 0 t-param))
   (if (<= t-param 1)
       (implies
        (and
         (putnam-1980-b5-member-data-p
          t-param f0 f1 f2 f3)
         (putnam-1980-b5-member-data-p
          t-param g0 g1 g2 g3))
        (putnam-1980-b5-product-condition-p
         t-param f0 f1 f2 f3 g0 g1 g2 g3))
     (putnam-1980-b5-explicit-counterexample-p
      t-param))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1980_b5:
-- the nonnegative parameters for which a class of increasing, convex,
-- continuous functions on [0,1] is closed under multiplication. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

Predicate : Set -> Set1
Predicate A =
  A -> Set

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : Predicate R) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ClosedUnitInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Predicate R
ClosedUnitInterval reals x =
  lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x
  and
  lessOrEqual reals x (oneR reals)

ContinuousWithinAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Predicate R ->
  R ->
  Set
ContinuousWithinAt {R} reals function domain point =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        domain x ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals (function point) epsilon (function x)))

ContinuousOn :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Predicate R ->
  Set
ContinuousOn {R} reals function domain =
  (x : R) ->
  domain x ->
  ContinuousWithinAt reals function domain x

StrictlyIncreasingOn :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Predicate R ->
  Set
StrictlyIncreasingOn {R} reals function domain =
  (x y : R) ->
  domain x ->
  domain y ->
  StrictLess reals x y ->
  StrictLess reals (function x) (function y)

ConvexOn :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Predicate R ->
  Set
ConvexOn {R} reals function domain =
  (u v s : R) ->
  domain u ->
  domain v ->
  domain s ->
  lessOrEqual reals
    (function
      (add reals
        (multiply reals s u)
        (multiply reals
          (subtract reals (oneR reals) s)
          v)))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals s (function u))
      (multiply reals
        (subtract reals (oneR reals) s)
        (function v)))

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

module Putnam1980B5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  oneThird : R
  oneThird =
    divide reals
      (oneR reals)
      (fromNat reals threeN)

  twoThirds : R
  twoThirds =
    divide reals
      (fromNat reals twoN)
      (fromNat reals threeN)

  DifferenceCondition :
    R ->
    (R -> R) ->
    Set
  DifferenceCondition t f =
    lessOrEqual reals
      (multiply reals
        t
        (add reals
          (subtract reals
            (f twoThirds)
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals twoN)
              (f oneThird)))
          (f (zeroR reals))))
      (add reals
        (subtract reals
          (f (oneR reals))
          (multiply reals
            (fromNat reals twoN)
            (f twoThirds)))
        (f oneThird))

  Qualifies :
    R ->
    (R -> R) ->
    Set
  Qualifies t f =
    ((x : R) ->
      ClosedUnitInterval reals x ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (f x))
    and
    StrictlyIncreasingOn reals f (ClosedUnitInterval reals)
    and
    ConvexOn reals f (ClosedUnitInterval reals)
    and
    ContinuousOn reals f (ClosedUnitInterval reals)
    and
    DifferenceCondition t f

  ClosedUnderMultiplication :
    R ->
    Set
  ClosedUnderMultiplication t =
    (f g : R -> R) ->
    Qualifies t f ->
    Qualifies t g ->
    Qualifies t
      (\ x -> multiply reals (f x) (g x))

  solution :
    R ->
    Set
  solution t =
    lessOrEqual reals t (oneR reals)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (t : R) ->
    lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) t ->
    Iff
      (ClosedUnderMultiplication t)
      (solution t)

putnam-1980-b5 : Set1
putnam-1980-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1980B5Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1980_b5:
  classification of the nonnegative parameters for which the nonnegative,
  strictly increasing, convex continuous functions on the unit interval
  satisfying the specified three-point inequality are closed under pointwise
  multiplication. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory realTheory real_topologyTheory;

val putnam_1980_b5 =
  ``let unit_interval = interval [0, 1]
    in
    let is_convex =
      \f : real -> real.
        !u v s : real.
          u IN unit_interval /\
          v IN unit_interval /\
          s IN unit_interval
          ==>
          f (s * u + (1 - s) * v) <=
          s * f u + (1 - s) * f v
    in
    let in_S =
      \t : real.
      \f : real -> real.
        (!x : real. x IN unit_interval ==> 0 <= f x) /\
        (!x y : real.
           x IN unit_interval /\
           y IN unit_interval /\
           x < y
           ==>
           f x < f y) /\
        is_convex f /\
        f continuous_on unit_interval /\
        f 1 - 2 * f (2 / 3) + f (1 / 3) >=
          t * (f (2 / 3) - 2 * f (1 / 3) + f 0)
    in
      !t : real.
        0 <= t
        ==>
        ((!f g : real -> real.
            in_S t f /\ in_S t g
            ==>
            in_S t (\x : real. f x * g x))
         <=>
         t <= 1)``;

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1980_b5:
% the nonnegative parameters for which a class of nonnegative, strictly
% increasing, convex, continuous functions on the unit interval satisfying a
% finite-difference inequality is closed under multiplication. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1980_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  in_unit_interval(x: real): bool =
    0 <= x AND x <= 1

  nonnegative_on_unit_interval(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      in_unit_interval(x) IMPLIES 0 <= f(x)

  strictly_increasing_on_unit_interval(
      f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: real):
      (in_unit_interval(x)
        AND in_unit_interval(y)
        AND x < y)
      IMPLIES f(x) < f(y)

  convex_on_unit_interval(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (u, v, s: real):
      (in_unit_interval(u)
        AND in_unit_interval(v)
        AND in_unit_interval(s))
      IMPLIES
        f(s * u + (1 - s) * v)
          <= s * f(u) + (1 - s) * f(v)

  continuous_on_unit_interval(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      in_unit_interval(x) IMPLIES
        FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
          EXISTS (delta: posreal):
            FORALL (y: real):
              (in_unit_interval(y)
                AND abs(y - x) < delta)
              IMPLIES abs(f(y) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  finite_difference_condition(
      t: real,
      f: real_function): bool =
    f(1) - 2 * f(2 / 3) + f(1 / 3)
      >= t * (f(2 / 3) - 2 * f(1 / 3) + f(0))

  in_function_class(t: real, f: real_function): bool =
    nonnegative_on_unit_interval(f)
      AND strictly_increasing_on_unit_interval(f)
      AND convex_on_unit_interval(f)
      AND continuous_on_unit_interval(f)
      AND finite_difference_condition(t, f)

  pointwise_product(
      f, g: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real): f(x) * g(x)

  closed_under_multiplication(t: real): bool =
    FORALL (f, g: real_function):
      (in_function_class(t, f)
        AND in_function_class(t, g))
      IMPLIES
        in_function_class(t, pointwise_product(f, g))

  putnam_1980_b5: bool =
    FORALL (t: real):
      t >= 0 IMPLIES
        (closed_under_multiplication(t) IFF t <= 1)
END putnam_1980_b5

import Mathlib

open Set

/--
For integers $d, n$ with $1 \le d \le n$, let $G(1, n) = \frac{1}{n}$ and $G(d, n) = \frac{d}{n}\sum_{i=d}^{n}G(d - 1, i - 1)$ for all $d > 1$. If $1 < d \le p$ for some prime $p$, prove that the reduced denominator of $G(d, p)$ is not divisible by $p$.
-/
theorem putnam_1980_b6
(G : ℤ × ℤ → ℚ)
(hG : ∀ d n : ℕ, d ≤ n → (d = 1 → G (d, n) = 1/(n : ℚ)) ∧ (d > 1 → G (d, n) = (d/(n : ℚ))*∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc d n, G ((d : ℤ) - 1, (i : ℤ) - 1)))
: ∀ d p : ℕ, 1 < d ∧ d ≤ p ∧ Prime p → ¬p ∣ (G (d, p)).den :=

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1980_b6:
  nondivisibility by a prime of the reduced denominator of the recursively
  defined rational number G(d,p). This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let rat_value =
     \q:int#num. real_of_int (FST q) / &(SND q) in
   let reduced =
     \q:int#num.
       0 < SND q /\ coprime (num_of_int (abs (FST q)),SND q) in
   !G:(int#int)->(int#num).
     (!x:int#int. reduced (G x)) /\
     (!d n:num.
        d <= n
        ==>
        ((d = 1
          ==> rat_value (G ((&d:int),(&n:int))) = &1 / &n) /\
         (d > 1
          ==> rat_value (G ((&d:int),(&n:int))) =
              (&d / &n) *
              sum (d..n)
                (\i:num.
                   rat_value
                     (G (((&d:int) - &1),((&i:int) - &1)))))))
     ==>
     !d p:num.
       1 < d /\ d <= p /\ prime p
       ==> ~(p divides SND (G ((&d:int),(&p:int))))`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1980_b6:
;; the reduced denominator of the recursively defined rational G(d,p) is not
;; divisible by the prime p when 1 < d <= p. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; E(K,M) is the K-th elementary symmetric sum of 1, 1/2, ..., 1/M.
;; Splitting subsets according to whether they contain M gives its exact
;; recursion below.
(defun putnam-1980-b6-elementary-symmetric (k m)
  (declare (xargs :measure (+ (nfix k) (nfix m))))
  (cond
   ((not (and (natp k) (natp m))) 0)
   ((zp k) 1)
   ((zp m) 0)
   (t
    (+ (putnam-1980-b6-elementary-symmetric k (- m 1))
       (* (/ 1 m)
          (putnam-1980-b6-elementary-symmetric
           (- k 1) (- m 1)))))))

(defun putnam-1980-b6-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (or (not (natp n)) (zp n))
      1
    (* n (putnam-1980-b6-factorial (- n 1)))))

;; The source recurrence uniquely determines every value used in its
;; conclusion. Its solution on 1 <= D <= N is
;;
;;   G(D,N) = D! / N * E(D-1,N-1).
;;
;; Indeed the D=1 case is 1/N. For D>1, substituting the formula for D-1
;; makes the source sum telescope via
;;
;;   E(K,M) - E(K,M-1) = E(K-1,M-1)/M.
;;
;; Conversely induction on D in the source recurrence gives this formula,
;; so eliminating the external G and its recurrence hypothesis is
;; bidirectionally equivalent. Values at other integer pairs are irrelevant
;; and may be extended arbitrarily.
(defun putnam-1980-b6-g (d n)
  (if (and (natp d)
           (natp n)
           (< 0 d)
           (<= d n))
      (* (/ (putnam-1980-b6-factorial d) n)
         (putnam-1980-b6-elementary-symmetric
          (- d 1) (- n 1)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1980-b6-no-divisor-from-p (n d)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix (- n d))))
  (if (and (natp n)
           (natp d)
           (<= 2 d)
           (< d n))
      (and
       (not (equal (mod n d) 0))
       (putnam-1980-b6-no-divisor-from-p n (+ d 1)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1980-b6-primep (n)
  (and (natp n)
       (< 1 n)
       (putnam-1980-b6-no-divisor-from-p n 2)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1980-b6-statement (d p)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp d)
    (natp p)
    (< 1 d)
    (<= d p)
    (putnam-1980-b6-primep p))
   (not
    (equal
     (mod
      (denominator (putnam-1980-b6-g d p))
      p)
     0))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1980_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1980_b6:
-- the reduced denominator of the recursively defined rational value G(d,p)
-- is not divisible by the prime p when 1 < d <= p. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<N_ _~Q_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

record Pair (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    first-coordinate  : A
    second-coordinate : B

pred : Nat -> Nat
pred zero =
  zero
pred (suc n) =
  n

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

subtractInt : Int -> Int -> Int
subtractInt x y =
  addInt x (negateInt y)

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

scaleInt : Int -> Nat -> Int
scaleInt z n =
  multiplyInt z (pos n)

absInt : Int -> Nat
absInt (pos n) =
  n
absInt (negsuc n) =
  suc n

record Rational : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator             : Int
    denominator-minus-one : Nat

open Rational

denominator : Rational -> Nat
denominator q =
  suc (denominator-minus-one q)

_~Q_ : Rational -> Rational -> Set
x ~Q y =
  scaleInt (numerator x) (denominator y) ==
  scaleInt (numerator y) (denominator x)

zeroQ : Rational
zeroQ =
  fraction (pos zero) zero

addQ : Rational -> Rational -> Rational
addQ x y =
  fraction
    (addInt
      (scaleInt (numerator x) (denominator y))
      (scaleInt (numerator y) (denominator x)))
    (pred (denominator x * denominator y))

multiplyQ : Rational -> Rational -> Rational
multiplyQ x y =
  fraction
    (multiplyInt (numerator x) (numerator y))
    (pred (denominator x * denominator y))

naturalRatio : Nat -> Nat -> Rational
naturalRatio numerator-value denominator-value =
  fraction
    (pos numerator-value)
    (pred denominator-value)

naturalDiv : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalDiv numerator-value zero =
  zero
naturalDiv numerator-value (suc denominator-value) =
  div-helper
    zero
    denominator-value
    numerator-value
    denominator-value

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator-value zero =
  zero
naturalMod numerator-value (suc denominator-value) =
  mod-helper
    zero
    denominator-value
    numerator-value
    denominator-value

gcdWithFuel : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat
gcdWithFuel zero a b =
  a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a zero =
  a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a (suc b) =
  gcdWithFuel fuel (suc b) (naturalMod a (suc b))

naturalGCD : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalGCD a b =
  gcdWithFuel (suc (a + b)) a b

reducedDenominator : Rational -> Nat
reducedDenominator q =
  naturalDiv
    (denominator q)
    (naturalGCD (absInt (numerator q)) (denominator q))

Divides : Nat -> Nat -> Set
Divides divisor number =
  Exists Nat
    (\ factor -> divisor * factor == number)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

Prime : Nat -> Set
Prime number =
  twoN <=N number
  and
  ((divisor : Nat) ->
    Divides divisor number ->
    divisor == oneN or divisor == number)

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos oneN

sumFrom :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> Rational) ->
  Rational
sumFrom start zero term =
  zeroQ
sumFrom start (suc count) term =
  addQ
    (sumFrom start count term)
    (term (start + count))

sumInclusive :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> Rational) ->
  Rational
sumInclusive lower upper term =
  sumFrom lower (suc upper - lower) term

Recurrence :
  (Pair Int Int -> Rational) ->
  Set
Recurrence G =
  (d n : Nat) ->
  d <=N n ->
  ((d == oneN ->
    G (pair (pos d) (pos n)) ~Q
    naturalRatio oneN n)
  and
  (oneN <N d ->
    G (pair (pos d) (pos n)) ~Q
    multiplyQ
      (naturalRatio d n)
      (sumInclusive d n
        (\ i ->
          G
            (pair
              (subtractInt (pos d) oneZ)
              (subtractInt (pos i) oneZ))))))

putnam-1980-b6 : Set
putnam-1980-b6 =
  (G : Pair Int Int -> Rational) ->
  Recurrence G ->
  (d p : Nat) ->
  (oneN <N d and d <=N p and Prime p) ->
  Not
    (Divides p
      (reducedDenominator
        (G (pair (pos d) (pos p)))))

(*

  a recursively defined rational sum has reduced denominator not divisible
  by the prime endpoint. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory dividesTheory pred_setTheory ratTheory;

val putnam_1980_b6 =
  ``!G : num # num -> rat.
      (!d n : num.
         d <= n
         ==>
         (d = 1 ==> G (d, n) = 1q / rat_of_num n) /\
         (1 < d ==>
          G (d, n) =
            (rat_of_num d / rat_of_num n) *
            ITSET
              (\i : num. \acc : rat. rat_add (G (d - 1, i - 1)) acc)
              {i : num | d <= i /\ i <= n}
              0q))
      ==>
      !d p : num.
        1 < d /\ d <= p /\ prime p
        ==>
        ~divides p (RATD (G (d, p)))``;

$(

  through n. SetMM's denom is the positive denominator of the unique reduced

                d = 1
                ->

              /\
              p e. Prime

content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1980_b6:
% the reduced denominator of a value defined by the stated rational recurrence
% is not divisible by the prime indexing that value. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1980_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  rational_array: TYPE = [int, int -> rat]

  nat_subtract(n, k: nat): nat =
    IF k <= n THEN n - k ELSE 0 ENDIF

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(p: nat): bool =
    p >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: nat):
        nat_divides(divisor, p)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = p

  reduced_fraction(
      value: rat,
      numerator: int,
      denominator: posnat): bool =
    value = numerator / denominator
      AND (FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        ((EXISTS (integer_quotient: int):
            numerator = divisor * integer_quotient)
          AND (EXISTS (natural_quotient: nat):
            denominator = divisor * natural_quotient))
        IMPLIES divisor = 1)

  has_reduced_denominator(value: rat, denominator: posnat): bool =
    EXISTS (numerator: int):
      reduced_fraction(value, numerator, denominator)

  recurrence_sum(
      G: rational_array,
      d, term_count: nat): RECURSIVE rat =
    IF term_count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      recurrence_sum(G, d, term_count - 1)
        + G(
            (d :: int) - 1,
            (d :: int) + (term_count :: int) - 2)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE term_count

  putnam_1980_b6: bool =
    FORALL (G: rational_array):
      (FORALL (d, n: nat):
        d <= n IMPLIES
          ((d = 1 IMPLIES
              G(d :: int, n :: int) = 1 / (n :: rat))
            AND (d > 1 IMPLIES
              G(d :: int, n :: int)
                = ((d :: rat) / (n :: rat))
                    * recurrence_sum(
                        G, d, nat_subtract(n, d) + 1))))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (d, p: nat):
          (1 < d AND d <= p AND prime_nat(p))
          IMPLIES
            EXISTS (denominator: posnat):
              has_reduced_denominator(
                G(d :: int, p :: int), denominator)
                AND NOT nat_divides(p, denominator)
END putnam_1980_b6

/--

    (P : ℕ → ℕ → Prop)

    (E : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hE : ∀ n ∈ Ici 1, P n (E n) ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, P n k → k ≤ E n) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ((E n) : ℝ)/n^2) atTop (𝓝 putnam_1981_a1_solution) :=

  the limiting normalized greatest exponent of 5 dividing the weighted

title: putnam_1981_a1
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1981_a1:
;; the exponent of 5 in 1^1*2^2*...*n^n, divided by n^2, tends to 1/8.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; V5-AUX computes the exponent of 5 in a positive integer.  The fuel is
;; initialized to the integer itself, which exceeds the number of successive
;; divisions by 5, so it does not bound or approximate the valuation.
(defun putnam-1981-a1-v5-aux (value fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      0
    (if (and (posp value)
             (equal (mod value 5) 0))
        (+ 1
           (putnam-1981-a1-v5-aux
            (floor value 5)
            (- fuel 1)))
      0)))

(defun putnam-1981-a1-v5 (value)
  (if (posp value)
      (putnam-1981-a1-v5-aux value value)
    0))

;; Additivity of prime valuations gives
;;   v_5(product_(m=1)^n m^m) = sum_(m=1)^n m*v_5(m).
;; Thus this is exactly the greatest k for which 5^k divides the source
;; product, rather than a replacement sequence.
(defun putnam-1981-a1-exponent (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1981-a1-exponent (- n 1))
       (* n (putnam-1981-a1-v5 n)))))

(defun putnam-1981-a1-normalized-exponent (n)
  (if (posp n)
      (/ (putnam-1981-a1-exponent n)
         (* n n))
    0))

;; Positive rational tolerances are cofinal in the positive reals, so this is
;; the epsilon definition of convergence to the real number 1/8.
(defun-sk putnam-1981-a1-tail-p (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (<= cutoff n))
     (< (abs
         (- (putnam-1981-a1-normalized-exponent n)
            1/8))
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1981-a1-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (putnam-1981-a1-tail-p epsilon cutoff))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1981-a1-statement (epsilon)
  (implies
   (and (rationalp epsilon)
        (< 0 epsilon))
   (putnam-1981-a1-cutoff-exists-p epsilon)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1981_a1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1981_a1:
-- the greatest exponent E(n) such that 5^E(n) divides 1^1 * 2^2 * ... * n^n
-- has E(n) / n^2 converging to 1 / 8. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _divides_
infixr 8 _^_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record _divides_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    equation : divisor * quotient == dividend

_^_ : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
base ^ zero =
  1
base ^ suc exponent =
  base * (base ^ exponent)

weightedProduct : Nat -> Nat
weightedProduct zero =
  1
weightedProduct (suc n) =
  weightedProduct n * ((suc n) ^ (suc n))

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc (suc (suc (suc oneN)))

eightN : Nat
eightN =
  suc (suc (suc fiveN))

GreatestExponent : (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat -> Set
GreatestExponent E n =
  ((fiveN ^ (E n)) divides weightedProduct n)
  and
  ((k : Nat) ->
    (fiveN ^ k) divides weightedProduct n ->
    k <=N E n)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    addR multiplyR : R -> R -> R
    negateR inverseR : R -> R
    lessOrEqualR : R -> R -> Set
    fromNatR : Nat -> R

    oneR-not-zeroR :
      oneR != zeroR

    addR-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> addR x y == addR y x
    addR-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> addR (addR x y) z == addR x (addR y z)
    addR-zero :
      (x : R) -> addR x zeroR == x
    addR-inverse :
      (x : R) -> addR x (negateR x) == zeroR

    multiplyR-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiplyR x y == multiplyR y x
    multiplyR-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiplyR (multiplyR x y) z == multiplyR x (multiplyR y z)
    multiplyR-one :
      (x : R) -> multiplyR x oneR == x
    multiplyR-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiplyR x zeroR == zeroR
    distributeR :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiplyR x (addR y z) ==
      addR (multiplyR x y) (multiplyR x z)
    inverseR-zero :
      inverseR zeroR == zeroR
    multiplyR-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiplyR x (inverseR x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqualR x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR y z ->
      lessOrEqualR x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y or lessOrEqualR y x
    addR-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR x y ->
      lessOrEqualR (addR z x) (addR z y)
    multiplyR-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqualR zeroR (multiplyR x y)
    zeroR-less-than-oneR :
      lessOrEqualR zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNatR-zero :
      fromNatR zero == zeroR
    fromNatR-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNatR (suc n) == addR (fromNatR n) oneR
    fromNatR-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNatR (m + n) == addR (fromNatR m) (fromNatR n)
    fromNatR-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNatR (m * n) == multiplyR (fromNatR m) (fromNatR n)
    fromNatR-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNatR m == fromNatR n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqualR x (fromNatR n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqualR x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqualR x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqualR x upper) ->
            lessOrEqualR supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  addR reals x (negateR reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiplyR reals x (inverseR reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqualR reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals (subtract reals center radius) x
  and
  StrictLess reals x (addR reals center radius)

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SequentialLimit {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

normalizedExponent :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Nat ->
  R
normalizedExponent reals E n =
  divide reals
    (fromNatR reals (E n))
    (multiplyR reals
      (fromNatR reals n)
      (fromNatR reals n))

oneEighth :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
oneEighth reals =
  divide reals
    (oneR reals)
    (fromNatR reals eightN)

putnam-1981-a1 : Set1
putnam-1981-a1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (E : Nat -> Nat) ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    oneN <=N n ->
    GreatestExponent E n) ->
  SequentialLimit reals
    (normalizedExponent reals E)
    (oneEighth reals)

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1981_a1:
% the greatest exponent E(n) for which 5^E(n) divides the weighted product
% 1^1 * 2^2 * ... * n^n satisfies E(n) / n^2 -> 1/8. This file contains no
% proof.

putnam_1981_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  weighted_product(n: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      weighted_product(n - 1) * n ^ n
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  exponent_property(n, k: nat): bool =
    nat_divides(5 ^ k, weighted_product(n))

  is_greatest_exponent_function(E: natural_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n > 0 IMPLIES
        exponent_property(n, E(n))
          AND (FORALL (k: nat):
            exponent_property(n, k) IMPLIES k <= E(n))

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  normalized_exponent(E: natural_sequence): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (n: nat):
      safe_div(E(n) :: real, (n :: real) ^ 2)

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  putnam_1981_a1: bool =
    FORALL (E: natural_sequence):
      is_greatest_exponent_function(E) IMPLIES
        converges_to(
          normalized_exponent(E),
          (1 :: real) / 8)
END putnam_1981_a1

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1981_a3:
;; nonexistence of a finite real limit for an exponential times an iterated
;; real integral. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The interfaces below present the real numbers as an arbitrary complete
;; ordered field.  Formula-specific DEFUN-SK binders supply the mathematical
;; quantifiers; no finite carrier, table of values, or sampled approximation
;; is used.

(defstub p81a3-real-p (r-type value) t)
(defstub p81a3-zero (r-type) t)
(defstub p81a3-one (r-type) t)
(defstub p81a3-add (r-type left right) t)
(defstub p81a3-mul (r-type left right) t)
(defstub p81a3-neg (r-type value) t)
(defstub p81a3-inv (r-type value) t)
(defstub p81a3-lt (r-type left right) t)
(defstub p81a3-set-member-p (r-type set value) t)

;; These three operations are constrained below by exact definitions:
;; the exponential by its real power series and the two integral operations
;; by convergence of uniform midpoint Riemann sums.

(defstub p81a3-exp (r-type value) t)
(defstub p81a3-inner-integral (r-type time y) t)
(defstub p81a3-outer-integral (r-type time) t)

(defun p81a3-sub (r-type x y)
  (p81a3-add r-type x (p81a3-neg r-type y)))

(defun p81a3-div (r-type x y)
  (p81a3-mul r-type x (p81a3-inv r-type y)))

(defun p81a3-le (r-type x y)
  (not (p81a3-lt r-type y x)))

(defun p81a3-abs (r-type x)
  (if (p81a3-lt r-type x (p81a3-zero r-type))
      (p81a3-neg r-type x)
    x))

(defun p81a3-in-closed-interval-p (r-type a b x)
  (and (p81a3-real-p r-type x)
       (p81a3-le r-type a x)
       (p81a3-le r-type x b)))

;; Complete ordered-field laws for the real carrier.

(defun-sk p81a3-operation-closure-p (r-type)
  (forall (x y)
    (and
     (p81a3-real-p r-type (p81a3-zero r-type))
     (p81a3-real-p r-type (p81a3-one r-type))
     (implies
      (p81a3-real-p r-type x)
      (and
       (p81a3-real-p r-type (p81a3-neg r-type x))
       (p81a3-real-p r-type (p81a3-inv r-type x))))
     (implies
      (and (p81a3-real-p r-type x)
           (p81a3-real-p r-type y))
      (and
       (p81a3-real-p r-type (p81a3-add r-type x y))
       (p81a3-real-p r-type (p81a3-mul r-type x y)))))))

(defun-sk p81a3-unary-field-laws-p (r-type)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p81a3-real-p r-type x)
     (let ((zero (p81a3-zero r-type))
           (one (p81a3-one r-type)))
       (and
        (equal (p81a3-add r-type zero x) x)
        (equal (p81a3-add r-type x zero) x)
        (equal (p81a3-add r-type x (p81a3-neg r-type x)) zero)
        (equal (p81a3-add r-type (p81a3-neg r-type x) x) zero)
        (equal (p81a3-mul r-type one x) x)
        (equal (p81a3-mul r-type x one) x)
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (and
          (equal (p81a3-mul r-type x (p81a3-inv r-type x)) one)
          (equal (p81a3-mul r-type (p81a3-inv r-type x) x) one))))))))

(defun-sk p81a3-binary-field-laws-p (r-type)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and (p81a3-real-p r-type x)
          (p81a3-real-p r-type y))
     (and
      (equal (p81a3-add r-type x y)
             (p81a3-add r-type y x))
      (equal (p81a3-mul r-type x y)
             (p81a3-mul r-type y x))))))

(defun-sk p81a3-ternary-field-laws-p (r-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and (p81a3-real-p r-type x)
          (p81a3-real-p r-type y)
          (p81a3-real-p r-type z))
     (and
      (equal
       (p81a3-add r-type (p81a3-add r-type x y) z)
       (p81a3-add r-type x (p81a3-add r-type y z)))
      (equal
       (p81a3-mul r-type (p81a3-mul r-type x y) z)
       (p81a3-mul r-type x (p81a3-mul r-type y z)))
      (equal
       (p81a3-mul r-type x (p81a3-add r-type y z))
       (p81a3-add
        r-type
        (p81a3-mul r-type x y)
        (p81a3-mul r-type x z)))))))

(defun-sk p81a3-order-laws-p (r-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and (p81a3-real-p r-type x)
          (p81a3-real-p r-type y)
          (p81a3-real-p r-type z))
     (and
      (not (p81a3-lt r-type x x))
      (implies
       (and (p81a3-lt r-type x y)
            (p81a3-lt r-type y z))
       (p81a3-lt r-type x z))
      (or (p81a3-lt r-type x y)
          (equal x y)
          (p81a3-lt r-type y x))
      (implies
       (p81a3-lt r-type x y)
       (p81a3-lt
        r-type
        (p81a3-add r-type x z)
        (p81a3-add r-type y z)))
      (implies
       (and (p81a3-lt r-type (p81a3-zero r-type) x)
            (p81a3-lt r-type (p81a3-zero r-type) y))
       (p81a3-lt
        r-type
        (p81a3-zero r-type)
        (p81a3-mul r-type x y)))))))

(defun-sk p81a3-valid-real-set-p (r-type set)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p81a3-set-member-p r-type set x)
     (p81a3-real-p r-type x))))

(defun-sk p81a3-set-nonempty-p (r-type set)
  (exists (x)
    (and (p81a3-real-p r-type x)
         (p81a3-set-member-p r-type set x))))

(defun-sk p81a3-upper-bound-p (r-type set bound)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p81a3-set-member-p r-type set x)
     (p81a3-le r-type x bound))))

(defun-sk p81a3-set-bounded-above-p (r-type set)
  (exists (bound)
    (and (p81a3-real-p r-type bound)
         (p81a3-upper-bound-p r-type set bound))))

(defun-sk p81a3-least-upper-bound-p (r-type set supremum)
  (forall (bound)
    (and
     (p81a3-real-p r-type supremum)
     (p81a3-upper-bound-p r-type set supremum)
     (implies
      (and (p81a3-real-p r-type bound)
           (p81a3-upper-bound-p r-type set bound))
      (p81a3-le r-type supremum bound)))))

(defun-sk p81a3-supremum-exists-p (r-type set)
  (exists (supremum)
    (and (p81a3-real-p r-type supremum)
         (p81a3-least-upper-bound-p r-type set supremum))))

(defun-sk p81a3-dedekind-complete-p (r-type)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and (p81a3-valid-real-set-p r-type set)
          (p81a3-set-nonempty-p r-type set)
          (p81a3-set-bounded-above-p r-type set))
     (p81a3-supremum-exists-p r-type set))))

(defun p81a3-real-structure-p (r-type)
  (and
   (p81a3-operation-closure-p r-type)
   (p81a3-unary-field-laws-p r-type)
   (p81a3-binary-field-laws-p r-type)
   (p81a3-ternary-field-laws-p r-type)
   (p81a3-order-laws-p r-type)
   (not (equal (p81a3-zero r-type) (p81a3-one r-type)))
   (p81a3-lt r-type (p81a3-zero r-type) (p81a3-one r-type))
   (p81a3-dedekind-complete-p r-type)))

;; Natural numerals, powers, factorials, and partial sums are interpreted
;; inside the presented real field.  The exponential interface is exactly
;; the limit of sum_{k < n} x^k/k!, not an uninterpreted token.

(defun p81a3-real-nat (r-type n)
  (if (zp n)
      (p81a3-zero r-type)
    (p81a3-add r-type
               (p81a3-one r-type)
               (p81a3-real-nat r-type (1- n)))))

(defun-sk p81a3-archimedean-witness-p (r-type x)
  (exists (n)
    (and
     (natp n)
     (p81a3-lt
      r-type x (p81a3-real-nat r-type n)))))

(defun-sk p81a3-archimedean-p (r-type)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p81a3-real-p r-type x)
     (p81a3-archimedean-witness-p r-type x))))

(defun p81a3-power (r-type x n)
  (if (zp n)
      (p81a3-one r-type)
    (p81a3-mul r-type x (p81a3-power r-type x (1- n)))))

(defun p81a3-factorial (r-type n)
  (if (zp n)
      (p81a3-one r-type)
    (p81a3-mul
     r-type
     (p81a3-real-nat r-type n)
     (p81a3-factorial r-type (1- n)))))

(defun p81a3-exp-prefix (r-type x n)
  (if (zp n)
      (p81a3-zero r-type)
    (let ((k (1- n)))
      (p81a3-add
       r-type
       (p81a3-exp-prefix r-type x k)
       (p81a3-div
        r-type
        (p81a3-power r-type x k)
        (p81a3-factorial r-type k))))))

(defun-sk p81a3-exp-tail-p (r-type x epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and (natp n)
          (<= cutoff n))
     (p81a3-lt
      r-type
      (p81a3-abs
       r-type
       (p81a3-sub
        r-type
        (p81a3-exp-prefix r-type x n)
        (p81a3-exp r-type x)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p81a3-exp-cutoff-exists-p (r-type x epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and (natp cutoff)
         (p81a3-exp-tail-p r-type x epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk p81a3-exp-operation-p (r-type)
  (forall (x epsilon)
    (and
     (implies
      (p81a3-real-p r-type x)
      (p81a3-real-p r-type (p81a3-exp r-type x)))
     (implies
      (and (p81a3-real-p r-type x)
           (p81a3-real-p r-type epsilon)
           (p81a3-lt r-type (p81a3-zero r-type) epsilon))
      (p81a3-exp-cutoff-exists-p r-type x epsilon)))))

;; Lean's totalized real division makes the displayed quotient zero on the
;; diagonal.  This definition records that value explicitly.

(defun p81a3-divided-difference (r-type x y)
  (if (equal x y)
      (p81a3-zero r-type)
    (p81a3-div
     r-type
     (p81a3-sub r-type
                (p81a3-exp r-type x)
                (p81a3-exp r-type y))
     (p81a3-sub r-type x y))))

;; Uniform midpoint sums give a concrete, nonvacuous Cauchy name for each
;; compact-interval integral. The isolated diagonal value changes no limit.

(defun p81a3-midpoint
    (r-type a b index subdivisions)
  (p81a3-add
   r-type
   a
   (p81a3-mul
    r-type
    (p81a3-sub r-type b a)
    (p81a3-div
     r-type
     (p81a3-real-nat r-type (+ (* 2 index) 1))
     (p81a3-real-nat r-type (* 2 subdivisions))))))

(defun p81a3-inner-midpoint-sum-aux
    (r-type time y remaining subdivisions)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      (p81a3-zero r-type)
    (let* ((index (- remaining 1))
           (x (p81a3-midpoint
               r-type
               (p81a3-zero r-type)
               time
               index
               subdivisions))
           (width
            (p81a3-div
             r-type
             time
             (p81a3-real-nat r-type subdivisions))))
      (p81a3-add
       r-type
       (p81a3-mul
        r-type
        (p81a3-divided-difference r-type x y)
        width)
       (p81a3-inner-midpoint-sum-aux
        r-type time y index subdivisions)))))

(defun p81a3-inner-riemann-sum
    (r-type time y subdivisions)
  (if (posp subdivisions)
      (p81a3-inner-midpoint-sum-aux
       r-type time y subdivisions subdivisions)
    (p81a3-zero r-type)))

(defun-sk p81a3-inner-sums-tail-p
    (r-type time y integral epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (subdivisions)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp subdivisions)
      (<= cutoff subdivisions))
     (p81a3-lt
      r-type
      (p81a3-abs
       r-type
       (p81a3-sub
        r-type
        (p81a3-inner-riemann-sum
         r-type time y subdivisions)
        integral))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p81a3-inner-cutoff-exists-p
    (r-type time y integral epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (posp cutoff)
     (p81a3-inner-sums-tail-p
      r-type time y integral epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk p81a3-inner-sums-converge-p
    (r-type time y integral)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (p81a3-real-p r-type epsilon)
      (p81a3-lt r-type (p81a3-zero r-type) epsilon))
     (p81a3-inner-cutoff-exists-p
      r-type time y integral epsilon))))

(defun p81a3-has-inner-integral-p
    (r-type time y integral)
  (and
   (p81a3-real-p r-type integral)
   (p81a3-inner-sums-converge-p
    r-type time y integral)))

(defun-sk p81a3-inner-integral-operation-p (r-type)
  (forall (time y)
    (implies
     (and
      (p81a3-in-closed-interval-p
       r-type (p81a3-zero r-type) time y))
     (and
      (p81a3-real-p r-type (p81a3-inner-integral r-type time y))
      (p81a3-has-inner-integral-p
       r-type time y (p81a3-inner-integral r-type time y))))))

(defun p81a3-outer-midpoint-sum-aux
    (r-type time remaining subdivisions)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      (p81a3-zero r-type)
    (let* ((index (- remaining 1))
           (y (p81a3-midpoint
               r-type
               (p81a3-zero r-type)
               time
               index
               subdivisions))
           (width
            (p81a3-div
             r-type
             time
             (p81a3-real-nat r-type subdivisions))))
      (p81a3-add
       r-type
       (p81a3-mul
        r-type
        (p81a3-inner-integral r-type time y)
        width)
       (p81a3-outer-midpoint-sum-aux
        r-type time index subdivisions)))))

(defun p81a3-outer-riemann-sum
    (r-type time subdivisions)
  (if (posp subdivisions)
      (p81a3-outer-midpoint-sum-aux
       r-type time subdivisions subdivisions)
    (p81a3-zero r-type)))

(defun-sk p81a3-outer-sums-tail-p
    (r-type time integral epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (subdivisions)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp subdivisions)
      (<= cutoff subdivisions))
     (p81a3-lt
      r-type
      (p81a3-abs
       r-type
       (p81a3-sub
        r-type
        (p81a3-outer-riemann-sum
         r-type time subdivisions)
        integral))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p81a3-outer-cutoff-exists-p
    (r-type time integral epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (posp cutoff)
     (p81a3-outer-sums-tail-p
      r-type time integral epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk p81a3-outer-sums-converge-p
    (r-type time integral)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (p81a3-real-p r-type epsilon)
      (p81a3-lt r-type (p81a3-zero r-type) epsilon))
     (p81a3-outer-cutoff-exists-p
      r-type time integral epsilon))))

(defun p81a3-has-outer-integral-p
    (r-type time integral)
  (and
   (p81a3-real-p r-type integral)
   (p81a3-outer-sums-converge-p
    r-type time integral)))

(defun-sk p81a3-outer-integral-operation-p (r-type)
  (forall (time)
    (implies
     (and
      (p81a3-real-p r-type time)
      (p81a3-le r-type (p81a3-zero r-type) time))
     (and
      (p81a3-real-p r-type (p81a3-outer-integral r-type time))
      (p81a3-has-outer-integral-p
       r-type time (p81a3-outer-integral r-type time))))))

;; On each compact interval these midpoint limits agree with the source
;; interval integrals for the displayed bounded integrands. The isolated
;; diagonal value is immaterial. For negative t the Lean half-open intervals
;; are empty; this branch therefore has value zero.

(defun p81a3-function-value (r-type time)
  (if (and
       (p81a3-real-p r-type time)
       (p81a3-le r-type (p81a3-zero r-type) time))
      (p81a3-mul
       r-type
       (p81a3-exp r-type (p81a3-neg r-type time))
       (p81a3-outer-integral r-type time))
    (p81a3-zero r-type)))

;; This is the ordinary epsilon definition of convergence to a finite real
;; limit as t tends to +infinity.  Both the candidate limit and the tail
;; threshold remain internally existential, as in the source proposition.

(defun-sk p81a3-limit-tail-p (r-type limit epsilon threshold)
  (forall (time)
    (implies
     (and
      (p81a3-real-p r-type time)
      (p81a3-le r-type threshold time))
     (p81a3-lt
      r-type
      (p81a3-abs
       r-type
       (p81a3-sub
        r-type
        (p81a3-function-value r-type time)
        limit))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p81a3-limit-threshold-exists-p
    (r-type limit epsilon)
  (exists (threshold)
    (and
     (p81a3-real-p r-type threshold)
     (p81a3-limit-tail-p
      r-type limit epsilon threshold))))

(defun-sk p81a3-tends-to-at-top-p (r-type limit)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (p81a3-real-p r-type epsilon)
      (p81a3-lt r-type (p81a3-zero r-type) epsilon))
     (p81a3-limit-threshold-exists-p
      r-type limit epsilon))))

(defun-sk p81a3-finite-limit-exists-p (r-type)
  (exists (limit)
    (and
     (p81a3-real-p r-type limit)
     (p81a3-tends-to-at-top-p r-type limit))))

(defun p81a3-analysis-context-p (r-type)
  (and
   (p81a3-real-structure-p r-type)
   (p81a3-archimedean-p r-type)
   (p81a3-exp-operation-p r-type)
   (p81a3-inner-integral-operation-p r-type)
   (p81a3-outer-integral-operation-p r-type)))

;; The cataloged solution proposition is False.  Keeping the biconditional
;; explicit preserves the source statement rather than replacing it by a
;; preselected numerical witness or an asymptotic estimate.

(defun-sk putnambench-acl2-putnam-1981-a3-statement ()
  (forall (r-type)
    (implies
     (p81a3-analysis-context-p r-type)
     (iff (p81a3-finite-limit-exists-p r-type)
          nil))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)

:q
