end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1986_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1986_a5:
% a real vector field on a positive-dimensional Euclidean space whose
% second partial derivatives are continuous and whose skew first-partial
% differences are constant admits a scalar correction making every
% component real-linear. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1986_a5[n: posnat]: THEORY
BEGIN
  coordinate: TYPE = below(n)
  vector: TYPE = [coordinate -> real]
  scalar_field: TYPE = [vector -> real]
  vector_field: TYPE = [coordinate -> scalar_field]
  constant_matrix: TYPE = [coordinate, coordinate -> real]

  zero_vector: vector =
    LAMBDA (i: coordinate): 0

  vector_add(x, y: vector): vector =
    LAMBDA (i: coordinate): x(i) + y(i)

  scalar_multiply(a: real, x: vector): vector =
    LAMBDA (i: coordinate): a * x(i)

  replace_coordinate(
      x: vector,
      i: coordinate,
      value: real): vector =
    LAMBDA (j: coordinate):
      IF j = i THEN value ELSE x(j) ENDIF

  vectors_close(x, y: vector, radius: real): bool =
    FORALL (i: coordinate):
      abs(x(i) - y(i)) < radius

  continuous_at(f: scalar_field, x: vector): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (y: vector):
          vectors_close(y, x, delta)
            IMPLIES abs(f(y) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  continuous_field(f: scalar_field): bool =
    FORALL (x: vector):
      continuous_at(f, x)

  has_partial_derivative_at(
      f: scalar_field,
      i: coordinate,
      derivative: real,
      x: vector): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (value: real):
          (value /= x(i)
            AND abs(value - x(i)) < delta)
          IMPLIES
            abs(
              f(replace_coordinate(x, i, value)) - f(x)
                - derivative * (value - x(i)))
              < epsilon_value * abs(value - x(i))

  partial_differentiable_at(
      f: scalar_field,
      i: coordinate,
      x: vector): bool =
    EXISTS (derivative: real):
      has_partial_derivative_at(f, i, derivative, x)

  partial_derivative_value(
      f: scalar_field,
      i: coordinate,
      x: vector): real =
    IF partial_differentiable_at(f, i, x) THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (derivative: real):
          has_partial_derivative_at(f, i, derivative, x))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  first_partial(
      f: scalar_field,
      i: coordinate): scalar_field =
    LAMBDA (x: vector):
      partial_derivative_value(f, i, x)

  second_partial(
      f: scalar_field,
      i, j: coordinate): scalar_field =
    first_partial(first_partial(f, i), j)

  continuously_twice_partially_differentiable(
      f: scalar_field): bool =
    continuous_field(f)
      AND (FORALL (i: coordinate), (x: vector):
        partial_differentiable_at(f, i, x))
      AND (FORALL (i, j: coordinate), (x: vector):
        partial_differentiable_at(first_partial(f, i), j, x))
      AND (FORALL (i: coordinate):
        continuous_field(first_partial(f, i)))
      AND (FORALL (i, j: coordinate):
        continuous_field(second_partial(f, i, j)))

  has_continuous_second_partials(f: vector_field): bool =
    FORALL (i: coordinate):
      continuously_twice_partially_differentiable(f(i))

  has_constant_skew_partial_differences(
      f: vector_field): bool =
    EXISTS (c: constant_matrix):
      FORALL (i, j: coordinate), (x: vector):
        partial_derivative_value(f(i), j, x)
          - partial_derivative_value(f(j), i, x)
          = c(i, j)

  real_linear(f: scalar_field): bool =
    (FORALL (x, y: vector):
      f(vector_add(x, y)) = f(x) + f(y))
      AND (FORALL (a: real), (x: vector):
        f(scalar_multiply(a, x)) = a * f(x))

  putnam_1986_a5: bool =
    FORALL (f: vector_field):
      (has_continuous_second_partials(f)
        AND has_constant_skew_partial_differences(f))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (g: scalar_field):
          FORALL (i: coordinate):
            real_linear(
              LAMBDA (x: vector):
                f(i)(x)
                  + partial_derivative_value(g, i, x))
END putnam_1986_a5

title: putnam_1986_a6
content:
import Mathlib

open  Real Equiv

noncomputable abbrev putnam_1986_a6_solution : (ℕ → ℕ) → ℕ → ℝ := sorry
-- fun b n ↦ (∏ i : Finset.Icc 1 n, b i) / Nat.factorial n
/--
Let $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ be real numbers, and let $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ be distinct positive integers. Suppose that there is a polynomial $f(x)$ satisfying the identity
\[
(1-x)^n f(x) = 1 + \sum_{i=1}^n a_i x^{b_i}.
\]
Find a simple expression (not involving any sums) for $f(1)$ in terms of $b_1, b_2, \dots, b_n$ and $n$ (but independent of $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$).
-/
theorem putnam_1986_a6
(n : ℕ)
(npos : n > 0)
(a : ℕ → ℝ)
(b : ℕ → ℕ)
(bpos : ∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, b i > 0)
(binj : ∀ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, ∀ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, b i = b j → i = j)
(f : Polynomial ℝ)
(hf : ∀ x : ℝ, (1 - x) ^ n * f.eval x = 1 + ∑ i : Finset.Icc 1 n, (a i) * x ^ (b i))
: (f.eval 1 = putnam_1986_a6_solution b n) :=
sorry

title: putnam_1986_a6
content:
From mathcomp Require Import all_algebra all_ssreflect.
From mathcomp Require Import reals.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.

Variable R : realType.
Definition putnam_1986_a6_solution : (nat -> nat) -> nat -> R := fun b n => (\prod_(1 <= i < n.+1) (b i)%:R) / n`!%:R.
Theorem putnam_1986_a6
    (n : nat)
    (npos : gt n 0)
    (a : nat -> R)
    (b : nat -> nat)
    (bpos : forall i : nat, (1 <= i < n.+1)%nat -> gt (b i) 0)
    (binj : forall i j : nat,
      (1 <= i < n.+1)%nat ->
      (1 <= j < n.+1)%nat ->
      b i = b j ->
      i = j)
    (f : {poly R})
    (hf : forall x : R, (1 - x) ^ n * f.[x] = 1 + \sum_(1 <= i < n.+1) ((a i) * x ^ (b i)))
    : f.[1] = putnam_1986_a6_solution b n.
Proof. Admitted.

theory putnam_1986_a6 imports Complex_Main "HOL-Computational_Algebra.Polynomial"
begin

definition putnam_1986_a6_solution::"(nat\<Rightarrow>nat) \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> real" where "putnam_1986_a6_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* \<lambda>b. \<lambda>n. (\<Prod>i=1..n. b i) / fact n *)
theorem putnam_1986_a6:
  fixes n::nat and a::"nat\<Rightarrow>real" and b::"nat\<Rightarrow>nat" and f::"real poly"
  assumes npos : "n > 0"
    and bpos : "\<forall>i \<in> {1..n::nat}. b i > 0"
    and binj : "\<forall>i \<in> {1..n::nat}. \<forall>j \<in> {1..n::nat}. b i = b j \<longrightarrow> i = j"
    and hf : "\<forall>x::real. (1 - x) ^ n * (poly f x) = 1 + (\<Sum>i=1..n. (a i) * x ^ (b i))"
  shows "poly f 1 = putnam_1986_a6_solution b n"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_1986_a6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_a6:
  the value at 1 of a real polynomial satisfying the given sparse identity
  is the product of its distinct positive exponents divided by n factorial.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `!n:num. !a:num->real. !b:num->num. !f:real->real.
     0 < n /\
     (!i:num. i IN (1..n) ==> 0 < b i) /\
     (!i j:num.
        i IN (1..n) /\ j IN (1..n) /\ b i = b j ==> i = j) /\
     polynomial_function f /\
     (!x:real.
        (&1 - x) pow n * f x =
        &1 + sum (1..n) (\i:num. a i * x pow (b i)))
     ==> f (&1) =
         product (1..n) (\i:num. &(b i)) / &(FACT n)`;;

title: putnam_1986_a6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_a6:
;; the value at 1 of a real polynomial constrained by a sparse power identity
;; is the product of the distinct positive exponents divided by n factorial.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Lists A and B contain exactly a_1,...,a_n and b_1,...,b_n. Polynomials use
;; ascending coefficient order. This loses no function data because the source
;; statement refers only to these n entries, and every polynomial has a finite
;; coefficient list.
;;
;; Standard ACL2 has exact rationals rather than a primitive real sort. For
;; fixed N and B, coefficientwise expansion of the source identity is an
;; affine linear system with integer coefficients in A and the coefficients
;; of F; failure of the conclusion is one affine linear disequality with a
;; rational constant. Any real counterexample therefore has a rational
;; counterexample, by rational row reduction and a rational choice outside the
;; resulting hyperplane. Conversely, rational data embeds in the reals.
;; Hence universal closure of this rational coefficient formulation is
;; bidirectionally equivalent to the source theorem over real coefficients.

(defun putnam-1986-a6-rational-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and (rationalp (car values))
           (putnam-1986-a6-rational-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-1986-a6-positive-nat-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and (posp (car values))
           (putnam-1986-a6-positive-nat-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-1986-a6-poly-normalize (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (let ((rest
             (putnam-1986-a6-poly-normalize (cdr polynomial))))
        (if (and (endp rest)
                 (equal (car polynomial) 0))
            nil
          (cons (car polynomial) rest)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1986-a6-poly-add (left right)
  (cond
   ((consp left)
    (cons (+ (car left)
             (if (consp right) (car right) 0))
          (putnam-1986-a6-poly-add
           (cdr left)
           (if (consp right) (cdr right) nil))))
   ((consp right) right)
   (t nil)))

(defun putnam-1986-a6-poly-scale (scalar polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons (* scalar (car polynomial))
            (putnam-1986-a6-poly-scale scalar (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1986-a6-poly-mul (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (putnam-1986-a6-poly-add
       (putnam-1986-a6-poly-scale (car left) right)
       (cons 0
             (putnam-1986-a6-poly-mul (cdr left) right)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1986-a6-poly-pow (polynomial exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      (list 1)
    (putnam-1986-a6-poly-mul
     polynomial
     (putnam-1986-a6-poly-pow polynomial (- exponent 1)))))

(defun putnam-1986-a6-monomial (coefficient exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      (list coefficient)
    (cons 0
          (putnam-1986-a6-monomial coefficient (- exponent 1)))))

(defun putnam-1986-a6-sparse-polynomial (coefficients exponents)
  (if (and (consp coefficients)
           (consp exponents))
      (putnam-1986-a6-poly-add
       (putnam-1986-a6-monomial
        (car coefficients) (car exponents))
       (putnam-1986-a6-sparse-polynomial
        (cdr coefficients) (cdr exponents)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1986-a6-poly-at-one (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (+ (car polynomial)
         (putnam-1986-a6-poly-at-one (cdr polynomial)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1986-a6-product (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (* (car values)
         (putnam-1986-a6-product (cdr values)))
    1))

(defun putnam-1986-a6-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n (putnam-1986-a6-factorial (- n 1)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1986-a6-statement
    (n coefficients exponents polynomial)
  (implies
   (and
    (posp n)
    (putnam-1986-a6-rational-list-p coefficients)
    (equal (len coefficients) n)
    (putnam-1986-a6-positive-nat-list-p exponents)
    (equal (len exponents) n)
    (no-duplicatesp-equal exponents)
    (putnam-1986-a6-rational-list-p polynomial)
    (equal
     (putnam-1986-a6-poly-normalize
      (putnam-1986-a6-poly-mul

title: putnam_1986_a6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_a6:
-- a polynomial identity with distinct positive integer exponents determines
-- f(1) as their product divided by n factorial. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

InOneTo :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Set
InOneTo i n =
  Positive i and i <=N n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial :
  Nat ->
  Nat
factorial zero =
  suc zero
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumOneTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
sumOneTo reals term zero =
  zeroR reals
sumOneTo reals term (suc n) =
  add reals
    (sumOneTo reals term n)
    (term (suc n))

productOneTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
productOneTo reals term zero =
  oneR reals
productOneTo reals term (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (productOneTo reals term n)
    (term (suc n))

Polynomial :
  Set ->
  Set
Polynomial R =
  List R

evaluate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  R ->
  R
evaluate reals [] x =
  zeroR reals
evaluate reals (coefficient ∷ coefficients) x =
  add reals
    coefficient
    (multiply reals x (evaluate reals coefficients x))

putnam-1986-a6-solution :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Nat ->
  R
putnam-1986-a6-solution reals b n =
  divide reals
    (productOneTo reals (\ i -> fromNat reals (b i)) n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

putnam-1986-a6 : Set1
putnam-1986-a6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  (a : Nat -> R) ->
  (b : Nat -> Nat) ->
  ((i : Nat) ->
    InOneTo i n ->
    Positive (b i)) ->
  ((i j : Nat) ->
    InOneTo i n ->
    InOneTo j n ->
    b i == b j ->
    i == j) ->
  (f : Polynomial R) ->
  ((x : R) ->
    multiply reals
      (naturalPower reals
        (subtract reals (oneR reals) x)
        n)
      (evaluate reals f x)
    ==
    add reals
      (oneR reals)
      (sumOneTo reals
        (\ i ->
          multiply reals
            (a i)
            (naturalPower reals x (b i)))
        n)) ->
  evaluate reals f (oneR reals) ==
  putnam-1986-a6-solution reals b n

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_a6:
  the value at one of a real polynomial satisfying the given sparse
  polynomial identity is the product of its distinct positive exponents
  divided by n factorial. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory combinatoricsTheory listTheory pred_setTheory realTheory
     real_sigmaTheory polyTheory;

val putnam_1986_a6 =
  ``!n : num. !a : num -> real. !b : num -> num. !f : real list.
      0 < n /\
      (!i : num.
         i IN IMAGE SUC (count n)
         ==>
         0 < b i) /\
      (!i j : num.
         i IN IMAGE SUC (count n) /\
         j IN IMAGE SUC (count n) /\
         b i = b j
         ==>
         i = j) /\
      (!x : real.
         (1 - x) pow n * poly f x =
           1 +
           SIGMA
             (\i : num. a i * x pow (b i))
             (IMAGE SUC (count n)))
      ==>
      poly f 1 =
        REAL_PROD_IMAGE
          (\i : num. &(b i))
          (IMAGE SUC (count n)) /
        &(FACT n)``;

$(

  putnam_1986_a6: the value at one of a real polynomial constrained by a
  finite sparse-power identity is the product of its distinct positive
  exponents divided by n factorial. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  RR ^m NN0 and NN0 ^m NN0 retain the source's arbitrary real-valued and
  natural-valued functions on all natural indices. The assumptions restrict
  positivity and pairwise distinctness of the exponent values only on the
  inclusive interval 1 ... n, exactly where the finite sum uses them.

  Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) is set.mm's ring of finite-support univariate
  real polynomials, and eval1 is polynomial evaluation. The conclusion
  inlines the explicit solution from the Rocq source and the solution
  annotations in the Isabelle and Lean sources. The final declaration is
  the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p
  proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d a b f i j n x $.

  putnambench-putnam-1986-a6 $a |-
    A. n e. NN
      A. a e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
        A. b e. ( NN0 ^m NN0 )
          A. f e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
            (
              (
                (
                  A. i e. ( 1 ... n )
                    0 < ( b ` i )
                  /\
                  A. i e. ( 1 ... n )
                    A. j e. ( 1 ... n )
                      (
                        ( b ` i ) = ( b ` j )
                        ->
                        i = j
                      )
                )
                /\
                A. x e. RR
                  (
                    ( ( 1 - x ) ^ n )
                    x.
                    ( ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` f ) ` x )
                  )
                  =
                  (
                    1
                    +
                    sum_ i e. ( 1 ... n )
                      (
                        ( a ` i )
                        x.
                        ( x ^ ( b ` i ) )
                      )
                  )
              )
              ->
              (
                ( ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` f ) ` 1 )
                =
                (
                  (
                    prod_ i e. ( 1 ... n )
                      ( b ` i )
                  )
                  /
                  ( ! ` n )
                )
              )
            )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1986_a6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_a6:
% a real polynomial satisfying the stated identity for distinct positive
% integer exponents has value at one equal to their product divided by n
% factorial. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1986_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  polynomial_value(
      polynomial: list[real],
      x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: 0,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        coefficient + x * polynomial_value(tail, x)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  coefficient_sum(
      a: real_sequence,
      b: natural_sequence,
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      coefficient_sum(a, b, x, count - 1)
        + a(count) * x ^ b(count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  exponent_product(
      b: natural_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      exponent_product(b, count - 1) * b(count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  nat_factorial(n: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      n * nat_factorial(n - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  putnam_1986_a6_solution(
      b: natural_sequence,
      n: nat): real =
    safe_div(
      exponent_product(b, n) :: real,
      nat_factorial(n) :: real)

  putnam_1986_a6: bool =
    FORALL
        (n: nat),
        (a: real_sequence),
        (b: natural_sequence),
        (f: list[real]):
      (n > 0
        AND (FORALL (i: nat):
          (1 <= i AND i <= n) IMPLIES b(i) > 0)
        AND (FORALL (i, j: nat):
          (1 <= i AND i <= n
            AND 1 <= j AND j <= n
            AND b(i) = b(j))
          IMPLIES i = j)
        AND (FORALL (x: real):
          (1 - x) ^ n * polynomial_value(f, x)
            = 1 + coefficient_sum(a, b, x, n)))
      IMPLIES
        polynomial_value(f, 1)
          = putnam_1986_a6_solution(b, n)
END putnam_1986_a6

-- 2 / 5
/--
Inscribe a rectangle of base $b$ and height $h$ and an isosceles triangle of base $b$ (against a corresponding side of the rectangle and pointed in the other direction) in a circle of radius one. For what value of $h$ do the rectangle and triangle have the same area?
-/

(b h : ℝ)
(hbh : b > 0 ∧ h > 0 ∧ b ^ 2 + h ^ 2 = 2 ^ 2)
(areaeq : b * h = 0.5 * b * (1 - h / 2))

(defun-sk putnam-1986-b1-order-laws-p (real-type)

       (and

        (or

-- positive real dimensions satisfying the circle and equal-area equations
-- force the common height to be 2/5. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc (suc (suc twoN))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

module Putnam1986B1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  Positive : R -> Set
  Positive x =
    lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x
    and
    x != zeroR reals

  circleEquation : R -> R -> Set
  circleEquation b h =
    add reals
      (naturalPower reals b twoN)
      (naturalPower reals h twoN)
    ==
    naturalPower reals (fromNat reals twoN) twoN

  areaEquation : R -> R -> Set
  areaEquation b h =
    multiply reals b h
    ==
    multiply reals
      (multiply reals
        (divide reals (oneR reals) (fromNat reals twoN))
        b)
      (subtract reals
        (oneR reals)
        (divide reals h (fromNat reals twoN)))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (b h : R) ->
    Positive b ->
    Positive h ->
    circleEquation b h ->
    areaEquation b h ->
    h ==
    divide reals
      (fromNat reals twoN)
      (fromNat reals fiveN)

putnam-1986-b1 : Set1
putnam-1986-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1986B1Statement.proposition reals

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_b2:
;; the complex difference triples arising from the given symmetric quadratic
;; equations are exactly four specified triples. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Write a = x-y, b = y-z, and c = z-x. Then c = -(a+b), and subtracting
;; consecutive source equations gives
;;
;;   a(a+2b-1) = 0 and b(-2a-b-1) = 0.
;;
;; Conversely, these three equations give source witnesses x=a+b, y=b, z=0,
;; so this eliminates the source's internal existential quantifier in both
;; directions.
;;
;; ACL2 numbers are Gaussian rationals rather than arbitrary complex numbers.
;; This does not narrow this particular statement. Over the complex numbers,
;; the two product equations split into a=0 or a+2b=1, and b=0 or
;; 2a+b=-1. The four cases force (a,b,c) respectively to be
;; (0,0,0), (0,-1,1), (1,0,-1), or (-1,1,0). Thus every possible complex
;; output triple already has integer coordinates. Conversely, Gaussian
;; rationals embed in the complex numbers and the displayed witnesses realize
;; every target-side equation triple. Hence universal closure of the
;; componentwise ACL2 predicate is bidirectionally equivalent to equality of
;; the two source sets over all complex triples.

(defun putnam-1986-b2-listed-solution-p (a b c)
  (or (and (equal a 0)
           (equal b 0)
           (equal c 0))
      (and (equal a 0)
           (equal b -1)
           (equal c 1))
      (and (equal a 1)
           (equal b 0)
           (equal c -1))
      (and (equal a -1)
           (equal b 1)
           (equal c 0))))

(defun putnam-1986-b2-difference-equations-p (a b c)
  (and (equal c (- (+ a b)))
       (equal (* a (- (+ a (* 2 b)) 1)) 0)
       (equal (* b (- (- (+ (* 2 a) b)) 1)) 0)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1986-b2-statement (a b c)
  (implies
   (and (acl2-numberp a)
        (acl2-numberp b)
        (acl2-numberp c))
   (iff (putnam-1986-b2-listed-solution-p a b c)
        (putnam-1986-b2-difference-equations-p a b c))))

      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

record Complex (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor complex
  field
    realPart      : R
    imaginaryPart : R

open Complex

complexZero :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R
complexZero reals =
  complex (zeroR reals) (zeroR reals)

complexOne :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R
complexOne reals =
  complex (oneR reals) (zeroR reals)

complexNegate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexNegate reals z =
  complex
    (negate reals (realPart z))
    (negate reals (imaginaryPart z))

complexAdd :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexAdd reals z w =
  complex
    (add reals (realPart z) (realPart w))
    (add reals (imaginaryPart z) (imaginaryPart w))

complexSubtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexSubtract reals z w =
  complexAdd reals z (complexNegate reals w)

complexMultiply :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexMultiply reals z w =
  complex
    (add reals
      (multiply reals (realPart z) (realPart w))
      (negate reals
        (multiply reals (imaginaryPart z) (imaginaryPart w))))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals (realPart z) (imaginaryPart w))
      (multiply reals (imaginaryPart z) (realPart w)))

complexTwo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R
complexTwo reals =
  complexAdd reals (complexOne reals) (complexOne reals)

record Triple (A : Set) : Set where
  constructor triple
  field
    firstCoordinate  : A
    secondCoordinate : A
    thirdCoordinate  : A

module Putnam1986B2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  C : Set
  C =
    Complex R

  zeroC : C
  zeroC =
    complexZero reals

  oneC : C
  oneC =
    complexOne reals

  minusOneC : C
  minusOneC =
    complexNegate reals oneC

  equationValue : C -> C -> C -> C
  equationValue x y z =
    complexAdd reals
      (complexMultiply reals x (complexSubtract reals x oneC))
      (complexMultiply reals
        (complexMultiply reals (complexTwo reals) y)
        z)

  differenceTriple : C -> C -> C -> Triple C
  differenceTriple x y z =
    triple
      (complexSubtract reals x y)
      (complexSubtract reals y z)
      (complexSubtract reals z x)

  ListedSolution : Triple C -> Set
  ListedSolution T =
    T == triple zeroC zeroC zeroC
    or
    (T == triple zeroC minusOneC oneC
    or
    (T == triple oneC zeroC minusOneC
    or
    T == triple minusOneC oneC zeroC))

  Attainable : Triple C -> Set
  Attainable T =
    Exists C
      (\ x ->
        Exists C
          (\ y ->
            Exists C
              (\ z ->
                T == differenceTriple x y z
                and
                (equationValue x y z == equationValue y z x
                and
                equationValue y z x == equationValue z x y))))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (T : Triple C) ->
    Iff (ListedSolution T) (Attainable T)

putnam-1986-b2 : Set1
putnam-1986-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1986B2Statement.proposition reals

  exactly four specified triples. This file contains no proof.

val putnam_1986_b2 =
  ``!T : (complex # complex) # complex.
      (T = ((0, 0), 0) \/
       T = ((0, ~1), 1) \/
       T = ((1, 0), ~1) \/
       T = ((~1, 1), 0))
      <=>
      ?x y z : complex.
        T = ((x - y, y - z), z - x) /\
        x * (x - 1) + 2 * y * z =
          y * (y - 1) + 2 * z * x /\
        y * (y - 1) + 2 * z * x =
          z * (z - 1) + 2 * x * y``;

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_b2:
% the ordered complex triples (x-y, y-z, z-x) arising from the given symmetric
% polynomial system are exactly four listed triples. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1986_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  complex: TYPE = [# real_part: real, imag_part: real #]

  complex_triple: TYPE =
    [# first_component: complex,
       second_component: complex,
       third_component: complex #]

  complex_of_real(value: real): complex =
    (# real_part := value, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_neg(value: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := -real_part(value),
       imag_part := -imag_part(value) #)

  complex_add(left, right: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := real_part(left) + real_part(right),
       imag_part := imag_part(left) + imag_part(right) #)

  complex_sub(left, right: complex): complex =
    complex_add(left, complex_neg(right))

  complex_mul(left, right: complex): complex =
    (# real_part :=
         real_part(left) * real_part(right)
           - imag_part(left) * imag_part(right),
       imag_part :=
         real_part(left) * imag_part(right)
           + imag_part(left) * real_part(right) #)

  make_triple(first_value, second_value, third_value: complex):
      complex_triple =
    (# first_component := first_value,
       second_component := second_value,
       third_component := third_value #)

  system_value(x, y, z: complex): complex =
    complex_add(
      complex_mul(
        x,
        complex_sub(x, complex_of_real(1))),
      complex_mul(
        complex_mul(complex_of_real(2), y),
        z))

  system_holds(x, y, z: complex): bool =
    system_value(x, y, z) = system_value(y, z, x)
      AND system_value(y, z, x) = system_value(z, x, y)

  difference_triple(x, y, z: complex): complex_triple =
    make_triple(
      complex_sub(x, y),
      complex_sub(y, z),
      complex_sub(z, x))

  putnam_1986_b2_solution(T: complex_triple): bool =
    T = make_triple(
          complex_of_real(0),
          complex_of_real(0),
          complex_of_real(0))
      OR T = make_triple(
          complex_of_real(1),
          complex_of_real(0),
          complex_of_real(-1))
      OR T = make_triple(
          complex_of_real(-1),
          complex_of_real(1),
          complex_of_real(0))
      OR T = make_triple(
          complex_of_real(0),
          complex_of_real(-1),
          complex_of_real(1))

  putnam_1986_b2: bool =
    FORALL (T: complex_triple):
      putnam_1986_b2_solution(T)
        IFF
      EXISTS (x, y, z: complex):
        T = difference_triple(x, y, z)
          AND system_holds(x, y, z)
END putnam_1986_b2

import Mathlib

open  Real Equiv Polynomial

/--
Let $\Gamma$ consist of all polynomials in $x$ with integer coefficients. For $f$ and $g$ in $\Gamma$ and $m$ a positive integer, let $f \equiv g \pmod{m}$ mean that every coefficient of $f-g$ is an integral multiple of $m$. Let $n$ and $p$ be positive integers with $p$ prime. Given that $f,g,h,r$ and $s$ are in $\Gamma$ with $rf+sg\equiv 1 \pmod{p}$ and $fg \equiv h \pmod{p}$, prove that there exist $F$ and $G$ in $\Gamma$ with $F \equiv f \pmod{p}$, $G \equiv g \pmod{p}$, and $FG \equiv h \pmod{p^n}$.
-/
theorem putnam_1986_b3
    (n p : ℕ)
    (nppos : n > 0 ∧ p > 0)
    (pprime : Nat.Prime p)
    (cong : Polynomial ℤ → Polynomial ℤ → ℤ → Prop)
    (hcong : ∀ f g m, cong f g m ↔ ∀ i : ℕ, m ∣ (f - g).coeff i)
    (f g h r s : Polynomial ℤ)
    (hcoprime : cong (r * f + s * g) 1 p)
    (hprod : cong (f * g) h p)
    : (∃ F G : Polynomial ℤ, cong F f p ∧ cong G g p ∧ cong (F * G) h (p ^ n)) :=
  sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1986_b3:
   lifting a factorization of an integer polynomial modulo a prime to a
   factorization modulo an arbitrary positive power. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith Znumtheory Lists.List Arith.

Import ListNotations.

Definition putnam_1986_b3_polynomial : Type := list Z.

Definition putnam_1986_b3_coefficient
    (f : putnam_1986_b3_polynomial) (i : nat) : Z :=
  nth i f 0%Z.

Fixpoint putnam_1986_b3_add
    (f g : putnam_1986_b3_polynomial) :
    putnam_1986_b3_polynomial :=
  match f, g with
  | [], _ => g
  | _, [] => f
  | a :: f', b :: g' =>
      (a + b)%Z :: putnam_1986_b3_add f' g'
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_1986_b3_scale
    (a : Z) (f : putnam_1986_b3_polynomial) :
    putnam_1986_b3_polynomial :=
  match f with
  | [] => []
  | b :: f' => (a * b)%Z :: putnam_1986_b3_scale a f'
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_1986_b3_mul
    (f g : putnam_1986_b3_polynomial) :
    putnam_1986_b3_polynomial :=
  match f with
  | [] => []
  | a :: f' =>
      putnam_1986_b3_add
        (putnam_1986_b3_scale a g)
        (0%Z :: putnam_1986_b3_mul f' g)
  end.

Definition putnam_1986_b3_congruent
    (f g : putnam_1986_b3_polynomial) (m : Z) : Prop :=
  forall i : nat,
    exists k : Z,
      (putnam_1986_b3_coefficient f i -
       putnam_1986_b3_coefficient g i = m * k)%Z.

Theorem putnam_1986_b3
    (n p : nat)
    (nppos : (0 < n)%nat /\ (0 < p)%nat)
    (pprime : prime (Z.of_nat p))
    (f g h r s : putnam_1986_b3_polynomial)
    (hcoprime :
      putnam_1986_b3_congruent
        (putnam_1986_b3_add
          (putnam_1986_b3_mul r f)
          (putnam_1986_b3_mul s g))
        [1%Z]
        (Z.of_nat p))
    (hprod :
      putnam_1986_b3_congruent
        (putnam_1986_b3_mul f g) h (Z.of_nat p)) :
  exists F G : putnam_1986_b3_polynomial,
    putnam_1986_b3_congruent F f (Z.of_nat p) /\
    putnam_1986_b3_congruent G g (Z.of_nat p) /\
    putnam_1986_b3_congruent
      (putnam_1986_b3_mul F G) h (Z.of_nat (Nat.pow p n)).
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_b3:
  lifting a factorization of an integer-coefficient polynomial modulo a prime
  to a factorization modulo an arbitrary positive power of that prime. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let polynomial =
     \f:num->int. ?d:num. !i:num. d < i ==> f i = &0 in
   let padd =
     \f g:num->int. \i:num. f i + g i in
   let pmul =
     \f g:num->int. \k:num.
       isum (0..k) (\i:num. f i * g (k - i)) in
   let pone =
     \i:num. if i = 0 then &1 else &0 in
   let pcong =
     \f g:num->int. \m:int.
       !i:num. (f i == g i) (mod m) in
   !n p:num. !f g h r s:num->int.
     0 < n /\
     0 < p /\
     prime p /\
     polynomial f /\
     polynomial g /\
     polynomial h /\
     polynomial r /\
     polynomial s /\
     pcong (padd (pmul r f) (pmul s g)) pone (&p) /\
     pcong (pmul f g) h (&p)
     ==> ?F G:num->int.
           polynomial F /\
           polynomial G /\
           pcong F f (&p) /\
           pcong G g (&p) /\
           pcong (pmul F G) h (&(p EXP n))`;;

title: putnam_1986_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_b3:
;; existence of integer-polynomial factors lifting a coprime factorization
;; from modulo p to modulo p^n. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Integer polynomials are canonical finite lists of coefficients in ascending
;; degree order. The zero polynomial is NIL; every nonzero polynomial has a
;; nonzero final coefficient. This is a bijective representation of Z[x].
(defun putnam-1986-b3-integer-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and (integerp (car values))
           (putnam-1986-b3-integer-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-1986-b3-poly-normalize (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (let ((tail
             (putnam-1986-b3-poly-normalize
              (cdr coefficients))))
        (if (and (equal (car coefficients) 0)
                 (endp tail))
            nil
          (cons (car coefficients) tail)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1986-b3-integer-polynomial-p (polynomial)
  (and
   (putnam-1986-b3-integer-list-p polynomial)
   (equal
    (putnam-1986-b3-poly-normalize polynomial)
    polynomial)))

(defun putnam-1986-b3-poly-add-raw (left right)
  (cond
   ((consp left)
    (cons
     (+ (car left)
        (if (consp right) (car right) 0))
     (putnam-1986-b3-poly-add-raw
      (cdr left)
      (if (consp right) (cdr right) nil))))
   ((consp right) right)
   (t nil)))

(defun putnam-1986-b3-poly-add (left right)
  (putnam-1986-b3-poly-normalize
   (putnam-1986-b3-poly-add-raw left right)))

(defun putnam-1986-b3-poly-scale (scalar polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (putnam-1986-b3-poly-normalize
       (cons
        (* scalar (car polynomial))
        (putnam-1986-b3-poly-scale
         scalar (cdr polynomial))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1986-b3-poly-multiply (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (putnam-1986-b3-poly-add
       (putnam-1986-b3-poly-scale (car left) right)
       (cons
        0
        (putnam-1986-b3-poly-multiply
         (cdr left) right)))
    nil))

;; This recursive check is exactly coefficientwise polynomial congruence.
;; Missing list entries denote the zero coefficients above the degree.
(defun putnam-1986-b3-poly-congruent-p (left right modulus)
  (declare
   (xargs
    :measure
    (+ (acl2-count left)
       (acl2-count right))))
  (if (or (consp left) (consp right))
      (and
       (equal
        (mod
         (-
          (if (consp left) (car left) 0)
          (if (consp right) (car right) 0))
         modulus)
        0)
       (putnam-1986-b3-poly-congruent-p
        (if (consp left) (cdr left) nil)
        (if (consp right) (cdr right) nil)
        modulus))
    t))

(defun putnam-1986-b3-no-divisor-from-p (number candidate)
  (declare
   (xargs
    :measure
    (nfix (- number candidate))))
  (if (and
       (natp number)
       (natp candidate)
       (<= 2 candidate)
       (< candidate number))
      (and
       (not (equal (mod number candidate) 0))
       (putnam-1986-b3-no-divisor-from-p
        number (+ candidate 1)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1986-b3-prime-p (number)
  (and
   (natp number)
   (< 1 number)
   (putnam-1986-b3-no-divisor-from-p number 2)))

(defun-sk putnam-1986-b3-lifts-exist-p
    (n p f g h)
  (exists (f-lifted g-lifted)
    (and
     (putnam-1986-b3-integer-polynomial-p f-lifted)
     (putnam-1986-b3-integer-polynomial-p g-lifted)
     (putnam-1986-b3-poly-congruent-p
      f-lifted f p)
     (putnam-1986-b3-poly-congruent-p
      g-lifted g p)
     (putnam-1986-b3-poly-congruent-p
      (putnam-1986-b3-poly-multiply
       f-lifted g-lifted)
      h
      (expt p n)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1986-b3-statement
    (n p f g h r s)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp n)
    (< 0 n)
    (natp p)
    (< 0 p)
    (putnam-1986-b3-prime-p p)
    (putnam-1986-b3-integer-polynomial-p f)
    (putnam-1986-b3-integer-polynomial-p g)
    (putnam-1986-b3-integer-polynomial-p h)
    (putnam-1986-b3-integer-polynomial-p r)
    (putnam-1986-b3-integer-polynomial-p s)
    (putnam-1986-b3-poly-congruent-p
     (putnam-1986-b3-poly-add
      (putnam-1986-b3-poly-multiply r f)
      (putnam-1986-b3-poly-multiply s g))
     (list 1)
     p)
    (putnam-1986-b3-poly-congruent-p
     (putnam-1986-b3-poly-multiply f g)
     h
     p))
   (putnam-1986-b3-lifts-exist-p
    n p f g h)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- integer-polynomial factorization modulo a prime lifts compatibly to every
-- positive prime power under a Bezout congruence. This file contains no proof.

open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)

infix 4 _<=N_ _dividesN_ _dividesZ_
infixr 8 _^N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record _dividesN_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    equation : dividend == divisor * quotient

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Prime (p : Nat) : Set where
  field
    at-least-two :
      suc (suc zero) <=N p
    only-trivial-divisors :
      (d : Nat) ->
      d dividesN p ->
      (d == suc zero) or (d == p)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

_^N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
base ^N zero =
  oneN
base ^N (suc exponent) =
  (base ^N exponent) * base

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

record _dividesZ_ (divisor dividend : Int) : Set where
  field
    integer-quotient : Int
    integer-equation :
      dividend == multiplyInt divisor integer-quotient

Polynomial : Set
Polynomial =
  List Int

coefficientAt : Polynomial -> Nat -> Int
coefficientAt [] index =
  pos zero
coefficientAt (coefficient ∷ coefficients) zero =
  coefficient
coefficientAt (coefficient ∷ coefficients) (suc index) =
  coefficientAt coefficients index

addPolynomial : Polynomial -> Polynomial -> Polynomial
addPolynomial [] q =
  q
addPolynomial p [] =
  p
addPolynomial (coefficientP ∷ coefficientsP)
              (coefficientQ ∷ coefficientsQ) =
  addInt coefficientP coefficientQ
  ∷ addPolynomial coefficientsP coefficientsQ

negatePolynomial : Polynomial -> Polynomial
negatePolynomial [] =
  []
negatePolynomial (coefficient ∷ coefficients) =
  negateInt coefficient ∷ negatePolynomial coefficients

subtractPolynomial : Polynomial -> Polynomial -> Polynomial
subtractPolynomial p q =
  addPolynomial p (negatePolynomial q)

scalePolynomial : Int -> Polynomial -> Polynomial
scalePolynomial scalar [] =
  []
scalePolynomial scalar (coefficient ∷ coefficients) =
  multiplyInt scalar coefficient
  ∷ scalePolynomial scalar coefficients

shiftPolynomial : Polynomial -> Polynomial
shiftPolynomial coefficients =
  pos zero ∷ coefficients

multiplyPolynomial : Polynomial -> Polynomial -> Polynomial
multiplyPolynomial [] q =
  []
multiplyPolynomial (coefficient ∷ coefficients) q =
  addPolynomial
    (scalePolynomial coefficient q)
    (shiftPolynomial (multiplyPolynomial coefficients q))

onePolynomial : Polynomial
onePolynomial =
  pos oneN ∷ []

Congruent : Polynomial -> Polynomial -> Nat -> Set
Congruent f g modulus =
  (index : Nat) ->
  pos modulus dividesZ
    coefficientAt (subtractPolynomial f g) index

putnam-1986-b3 : Set
putnam-1986-b3 =
  (n p : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  Positive p ->
  Prime p ->
  (f g h r s : Polynomial) ->
  Congruent
    (addPolynomial
      (multiplyPolynomial r f)
      (multiplyPolynomial s g))
    onePolynomial
    p ->
  Congruent (multiplyPolynomial f g) h p ->
  Exists Polynomial
    (\ F ->
      Exists Polynomial
        (\ G ->
          Congruent F f p
          and
          Congruent G g p
          and
          Congruent
            (multiplyPolynomial F G)
            h
            (p ^N n)))

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_b3:
  coefficientwise Hensel lifting of a factorization of an integer polynomial
  from a prime modulus to an arbitrary positive prime power. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_1986_b3 =
  ``let integer_polynomials =
      {f : num -> int | FINITE {k : num | f k <> 0}};
      poly_one =
        (\k : num. if k = 0 then (1 : int) else 0);
      poly_add =
        (\f g : num -> int.
           \k : num. f k + g k);
      poly_mul =
        (\f g : num -> int.
           \k : num.
             ITSET
               (\i acc. f i * g (k - i) + acc)
               (count (SUC k))
               (0 : int));
      poly_cong =
        (\f g : num -> int.
           \m : int.
             !k : num. m int_divides (f k - g k))
    in
      !n p : num.
      !f g h r s : num -> int.
        0 < n /\
        0 < p /\
        prime p /\
        f IN integer_polynomials /\
        g IN integer_polynomials /\
        h IN integer_polynomials /\
        r IN integer_polynomials /\
        s IN integer_polynomials /\
        poly_cong
          (poly_add (poly_mul r f) (poly_mul s g))
          poly_one
          (int_of_num p) /\
        poly_cong (poly_mul f g) h (int_of_num p)
        ==>
        ?F G : num -> int.
          F IN integer_polynomials /\
          G IN integer_polynomials /\
          poly_cong F f (int_of_num p) /\
          poly_cong G g (int_of_num p) /\
          poly_cong
            (poly_mul F G)
            h
            ((int_of_num p) ** n)``;

title: putnam_1986_b3
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1986_b3: a coprime factorization of an integer polynomial modulo a
  prime lifts to a factorization modulo every positive power of that prime.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P86B3Poly is the class of all finite-support functions from NN0 to ZZ, a
  coefficient representation bidirectionally equivalent to arbitrary
  integer-coefficient polynomials. Polynomial multiplication is inlined as
  the finite convolution sum over 0 ... i.

  Divisibility of every coefficient difference is exactly the source
  congruence relation. The coefficient if ( i = 0 , 1 , 0 ) represents the
  constant polynomial one. Thus the two hypotheses are r*f + s*g congruent
  to 1 modulo p and f*g congruent to h modulo p, while the conclusion retains
  internally existential polynomials F and G and lifts only the product
  congruence to p^n.

  All declarations below are unproved $a statement encodings; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P86B3Poly $.

p86b3-poly-syntax $a class P86B3Poly $.

${
  $d A i $.

  p86b3-poly-definition $a |- P86B3Poly =
    {
      A e. ( ZZ ^m NN0 ) |
        { i e. NN0 | ( A ` i ) =/= 0 } e. Fin
    }
  $.
$}

${
  $d F G f g h i k n p r s $.

  putnambench-putnam-1986-b3 $a |-
    A. n e. NN
      A. p e. Prime
        A. f e. P86B3Poly
          A. g e. P86B3Poly
            A. h e. P86B3Poly
              A. r e. P86B3Poly
                A. s e. P86B3Poly
                  (
                    (
                      A. i e. NN0
                        p
                        ||
                        (
                          (
                            (
                              sum_ k e. ( 0 ... i )
                                ( ( r ` k ) x. ( f ` ( i - k ) ) )
                            )
                            +
                            (
                              sum_ k e. ( 0 ... i )
                                ( ( s ` k ) x. ( g ` ( i - k ) ) )
                            )
                          )
                          -
                          if ( i = 0 , 1 , 0 )
                        )
                      /\
                      A. i e. NN0
                        p
                        ||
                        (
                          (
                            sum_ k e. ( 0 ... i )
                              ( ( f ` k ) x. ( g ` ( i - k ) ) )
                          )
                          -
                          ( h ` i )
                        )
                    )
                    ->
                    E. F e. P86B3Poly
                      E. G e. P86B3Poly
                        (
                          (
                            A. i e. NN0
                              p || ( ( F ` i ) - ( f ` i ) )
                            /\
                            A. i e. NN0
                              p || ( ( G ` i ) - ( g ` i ) )
                          )
                          /\
                          A. i e. NN0
                            ( p ^ n )
                            ||
                            (
                              (
                                sum_ k e. ( 0 ... i )
                                  ( ( F ` k ) x. ( G ` ( i - k ) ) )
                              )
                              -
                              ( h ` i )
                            )
                        )
                  )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1986_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_b3:
% coefficientwise congruence of integer polynomials and lifting a coprime
% factorization modulo a prime to a factorization modulo its powers. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1986_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  polynomial_coefficient(
      polynomial: list[int],
      degree: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: 0,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        IF degree = 0 THEN
          coefficient
        ELSE
          polynomial_coefficient(tail, degree - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  polynomial_add(
      left, right: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES left OF
      null: right,
      cons(left_coefficient, left_tail):
        CASES right OF
          null: left,
          cons(right_coefficient, right_tail):
            cons(
              left_coefficient + right_coefficient,
              polynomial_add(left_tail, right_tail))
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE left BY <<

  polynomial_scale(
      scalar: int,
      polynomial: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: null,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        cons(
          scalar * coefficient,
          polynomial_scale(scalar, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  polynomial_multiply(
      left, right: list[int]): RECURSIVE list[int] =
    CASES left OF
      null: null,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        polynomial_add(
          polynomial_scale(coefficient, right),
          cons(0, polynomial_multiply(tail, right)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE left BY <<

  constant_polynomial(value: int): list[int] =
    cons(value, null)

  int_divides(divisor, value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: int): value = divisor * quotient

  polynomial_congruent(
      left, right: list[int],
      modulus: int): bool =
    FORALL (degree: nat):
      int_divides(
        modulus,
        polynomial_coefficient(left, degree)
          - polynomial_coefficient(right, degree))

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: nat):
        (EXISTS (quotient: nat): value = divisor * quotient)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value

  putnam_1986_b3: bool =
    FORALL
        (n, p: nat),
        (f, g, h, r, s: list[int]):
      (n > 0
        AND p > 0
        AND prime_nat(p)
        AND polynomial_congruent(
          polynomial_add(
            polynomial_multiply(r, f),
            polynomial_multiply(s, g)),
          constant_polynomial(1),
          (p :: int))
        AND polynomial_congruent(
          polynomial_multiply(f, g),
          h,
          (p :: int)))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (F, G: list[int]):
          polynomial_congruent(F, f, (p :: int))
            AND polynomial_congruent(G, g, (p :: int))
            AND polynomial_congruent(
              polynomial_multiply(F, G),
              h,
              ((p ^ n) :: int))
END putnam_1986_b3

title: putnam_1986_b4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_b4:
;; asymptotic approximation of large real numbers by square roots of integers
;; of the form m^2 + 2*n^2. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The inequalities below are equivalent to
;;
;;   |R - sqrt(M^2 + 2*N^2)| < EPSILON.
;;
;; Splitting at R-EPSILON avoids introducing a square-root function into
;; ordinary ACL2. The radicand is nonnegative because M and N are integers.
(defun putnam-1986-b4-close-square-p (r epsilon m n)
  (let* ((lower (- r epsilon))
         (upper (+ r epsilon))
         (radicand (+ (* m m) (* 2 n n))))
    (and
     (rationalp r)
     (rationalp epsilon)
     (< 0 epsilon)
     (integerp m)
     (integerp n)
     (< 0 upper)
     (or (< lower 0)
         (< (* lower lower) radicand))
     (< radicand (* upper upper)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1986-b4-close-value-exists-p (r epsilon)
  (exists (m n)
    (putnam-1986-b4-close-square-p r epsilon m n)))

(defun-sk putnam-1986-b4-tail-p (epsilon threshold)
  (forall (r)
    (implies
     (and (rationalp r)
          (<= threshold r))
     (putnam-1986-b4-close-value-exists-p r epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1986-b4-epsilon-tail-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (threshold)
    (and (rationalp threshold)
         (putnam-1986-b4-tail-p epsilon threshold))))

;; For each fixed real R, the source minimum exists and is less than EPSILON
;; exactly when the existential predicate above holds. Positive rational
;; tolerances are cofinal in the positive reals. Rational R are dense, and
;; distance to a fixed set is 1-Lipschitz, so this rational epsilon-tail
;; statement is equivalent to Tendsto G atTop (nhds 0). In particular, no
;; convergence threshold is supplied by the statement.
(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-1986-b4-statement ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and (rationalp epsilon)
          (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-1986-b4-epsilon-tail-exists-p epsilon))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1986_b4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_b4:
-- the minimum distance from a real number r to a value sqrt(m^2 + 2*n^2),
-- over arbitrary integers m and n, tends to zero as r tends to infinity.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1986B4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse absoluteValue squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    absolute-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (absoluteValue x)
    absolute-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      absoluteValue x == x
    absolute-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      absoluteValue x == negate x

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

magnitude : Int -> Nat
magnitude (pos n) =
  n
magnitude (negsuc n) =
  suc n

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

radicand : Int -> Int -> Nat
radicand m n =
  magnitude m * magnitude m +
  twoN * (magnitude n * magnitude n)

Distance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  R
Distance reals r m n =
  absoluteValue reals
    (subtract reals
      r
      (squareRoot reals
        (fromNat reals (radicand m n))))

MinimumDistanceFunction :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
MinimumDistanceFunction {R} reals G =
  ((r : R) ->
    Exists Int
      (\ m ->
        Exists Int
          (\ n ->
            G r == Distance reals r m n)))
  and
  ((r : R) ->
    (m n : Int) ->
    lessOrEqual reals
      (G r)
      (Distance reals r m n))

LimitAtPositiveInfinity :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
LimitAtPositiveInfinity {R} reals function limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ cutoff ->
      (r : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals cutoff r ->
      StrictLess reals
        (absoluteValue reals
          (subtract reals (function r) limit))
        epsilon)

putnam-1986-b4-solution : Set
putnam-1986-b4-solution =
  Top

putnam-1986-b4 : Set1
putnam-1986-b4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (G : R -> R) ->
  MinimumDistanceFunction reals G ->
  Iff
    (LimitAtPositiveInfinity reals G (zeroR reals))
    putnam-1986-b4-solution

  sqrt(m^2 + 2 n^2), for integers m and n, tends to zero as the real

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  G ranges over total real-valued functions on the reals. The first
  hypothesis says that G(r) is attained by some integer pair (m,n), and the
  second says that it is a lower bound for the corresponding distance for
  every integer pair. Together these state exactly that G(r) is the source
  minimum for every real r.

  Set.mm's complex modulus abs agrees with real absolute value here, and its
  principal square root is applied to the nonnegative real integer expression
  m^2 + 2 n^2. The relation ~~>r is the limit at positive infinity for a
  real-indexed function. The Rocq ground truth defines the solution predicate
  as True, so its biconditional is equivalent to this limit assertion.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d G m n r $.

  putnambench-putnam-1986-b4 $a |- A. G e. ( RR ^m RR )
    (
      (
        A. r e. RR
          E. m e. ZZ E. n e. ZZ
            (
              ( G ` r )
              =
              (
                abs
                `
                (
                  r
                  -
                  (

                    `
                    (

                      +

                    )
                  )
                )
              )
            )
        /\

            <_

                -

title: putnam_1986_b4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_b4:
% the minimum distance from a large real number to a value sqrt(m^2 + 2*n^2),
% for integers m and n, tends to zero. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1986_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  integer_radicand(m, n: int): int =
    m ^ 2 + 2 * n ^ 2

  sqrt_value(root, radicand: real): bool =
    root >= 0 AND root * root = radicand

  distance_value(
      distance, r: real,
      m, n: int): bool =
    EXISTS (root: real):
      sqrt_value(root, (integer_radicand(m, n) :: real))
        AND distance = abs(r - root)

  is_minimum_distance_function(G: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (r: real):
      (EXISTS (m, n: int), (distance: real):
        distance_value(distance, r, m, n)
          AND G(r) = distance)
      AND
      (FORALL (m, n: int), (distance: real):
        distance_value(distance, r, m, n)
          IMPLIES G(r) <= distance)

  tends_to_zero_at_real_top(G: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: real):
        FORALL (r: real):
          cutoff <= r IMPLIES abs(G(r)) < epsilon_value

  putnam_1986_b4_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_1986_b4: bool =
    FORALL (G: real_function):
      is_minimum_distance_function(G)
        IMPLIES
          (tends_to_zero_at_real_top(G)
            IFF putnam_1986_b4_solution)
END putnam_1986_b4

open  Real Equiv Polynomial Filter Topology MvPolynomial

-- False
/--
Let $f(x,y,z) = x^2+y^2+z^2+xyz$. Let $p(x,y,z), q(x,y,z)$, $r(x,y,z)$ be polynomials with real coefficients satisfying
\[
f(p(x,y,z), q(x,y,z), r(x,y,z)) = f(x,y,z).
\]
Prove or disprove the assertion that the sequence $p,q,r$ consists of some permutation of $\pm x, \pm y, \pm z$, where the number of minus signs is $0$ or $2$.
-/
theorem putnam_1986_b5
    (f : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℝ)
    (perms : Set (Set (MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℝ)))
    (hf : f = (X 0) ^ 2 + (X 1) ^ 2 + (X 2) ^ 2 + (X 0) * (X 1) * (X 2))
    (hperms : perms = {{X 0, X 1, X 2}, {X 0, -X 1, -X 2}, {-X 0, X 1, -X 2}, {-X 0, -X 1, X 2}}) :
    putnam_1986_b5_solution ↔ (∀ pqr : Fin 3 → MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℝ,
      (∀ xyz : Fin 3 → ℝ, MvPolynomial.eval (fun i ↦ MvPolynomial.eval xyz (pqr i)) f = MvPolynomial.eval xyz f) →
      ({pqr 0, pqr 1, pqr 2} ∈ perms)) :=

title: putnam_1986_b5
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1986_b5:
   real trivariate polynomial substitutions preserving
   x^2 + y^2 + z^2 + xyz and the four permitted sign patterns, up to
   permutation. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals Arith.PeanoNat Bool.

Open Scope R_scope.

Record putnam_1986_b5_polynomial : Type := {
  putnam_1986_b5_raw_coefficient : nat -> nat -> nat -> R;
  putnam_1986_b5_x_bound : nat;
  putnam_1986_b5_y_bound : nat;
  putnam_1986_b5_z_bound : nat
}.

Definition putnam_1986_b5_coefficient
    (p : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial) (i j k : nat) : R :=
  if andb
       (Nat.leb i (putnam_1986_b5_x_bound p))
       (andb
          (Nat.leb j (putnam_1986_b5_y_bound p))
          (Nat.leb k (putnam_1986_b5_z_bound p)))
  then putnam_1986_b5_raw_coefficient p i j k
  else 0.

Definition putnam_1986_b5_polynomial_eq
    (p q : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial) : Prop :=
  forall i j k : nat,
    putnam_1986_b5_coefficient p i j k =
    putnam_1986_b5_coefficient q i j k.

Fixpoint putnam_1986_b5_sum_to
    (n : nat) (term : nat -> R) : R :=
  match n with
  | O => term O
  | S m => putnam_1986_b5_sum_to m term + term (S m)
  end.

Definition putnam_1986_b5_eval
    (p : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial) (x y z : R) : R :=
  putnam_1986_b5_sum_to
    (putnam_1986_b5_x_bound p)
    (fun i : nat =>
      putnam_1986_b5_sum_to
        (putnam_1986_b5_y_bound p)
        (fun j : nat =>
          putnam_1986_b5_sum_to
            (putnam_1986_b5_z_bound p)
            (fun k : nat =>
              putnam_1986_b5_coefficient p i j k *
              x ^ i * y ^ j * z ^ k))).

Definition putnam_1986_b5_monomial
    (i j k : nat) (coefficient : R) :
    putnam_1986_b5_polynomial :=
  {|
    putnam_1986_b5_raw_coefficient :=
      fun a b c : nat =>
        if andb
             (Nat.eqb a i)
             (andb (Nat.eqb b j) (Nat.eqb c k))
        then coefficient
        else 0;
    putnam_1986_b5_x_bound := i;
    putnam_1986_b5_y_bound := j;
    putnam_1986_b5_z_bound := k
  |}.

Definition putnam_1986_b5_x : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial :=
  putnam_1986_b5_monomial 1%nat 0%nat 0%nat 1.

Definition putnam_1986_b5_y : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial :=
  putnam_1986_b5_monomial 0%nat 1%nat 0%nat 1.

Definition putnam_1986_b5_z : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial :=
  putnam_1986_b5_monomial 0%nat 0%nat 1%nat 1.

Definition putnam_1986_b5_neg_x : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial :=
  putnam_1986_b5_monomial 1%nat 0%nat 0%nat (-1).

Definition putnam_1986_b5_neg_y : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial :=
  putnam_1986_b5_monomial 0%nat 1%nat 0%nat (-1).

Definition putnam_1986_b5_neg_z : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial :=
  putnam_1986_b5_monomial 0%nat 0%nat 1%nat (-1).

Definition putnam_1986_b5_f (x y z : R) : R :=
  x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 + z ^ 2 + x * y * z.

Definition putnam_1986_b5_same_unordered_triple
    (p q r a b c : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial) : Prop :=
  forall s : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial,
    (putnam_1986_b5_polynomial_eq s p \/
     putnam_1986_b5_polynomial_eq s q \/
     putnam_1986_b5_polynomial_eq s r) <->
    (putnam_1986_b5_polynomial_eq s a \/
     putnam_1986_b5_polynomial_eq s b \/
     putnam_1986_b5_polynomial_eq s c).

Definition putnam_1986_b5_permitted
    (p q r : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial) : Prop :=
  putnam_1986_b5_same_unordered_triple
    p q r
    putnam_1986_b5_x putnam_1986_b5_y putnam_1986_b5_z \/
  putnam_1986_b5_same_unordered_triple
    p q r
    putnam_1986_b5_x putnam_1986_b5_neg_y putnam_1986_b5_neg_z \/
  putnam_1986_b5_same_unordered_triple
    p q r
    putnam_1986_b5_neg_x putnam_1986_b5_y putnam_1986_b5_neg_z \/
  putnam_1986_b5_same_unordered_triple
    p q r
    putnam_1986_b5_neg_x putnam_1986_b5_neg_y putnam_1986_b5_z.

Definition putnam_1986_b5_solution : Prop := False.

Theorem putnam_1986_b5 :
  putnam_1986_b5_solution <->
  forall p q r : putnam_1986_b5_polynomial,
    (forall x y z : R,
      putnam_1986_b5_f
        (putnam_1986_b5_eval p x y z)
        (putnam_1986_b5_eval q x y z)
        (putnam_1986_b5_eval r x y z) =
      putnam_1986_b5_f x y z) ->
    putnam_1986_b5_permitted p q r.
Admitted.

  defines "f \<equiv> [:[:[: 0, 0, 1:], 0, 1:], [:0, [:0, 1:]:], 1:]" (* x^2 + y^2 + z^2 + xyz = ((0 + 0z + z^2) + 0y + y^2) + (0 + (0 + z)y) x + x^2 *)

    }"

  shows "(\<forall>p q r::real poly poly poly. (\<forall>x y z::real. eval f x y z = eval f (eval p x y z) (eval q x y z) (eval r x y z)) \<longrightarrow> ({p, q, r} \<in> perms)) \<longleftrightarrow> putnam_1986_b5_solution"

end

     \p:(num#num#num)->real. FINITE {m | ~(p m = &0)} in

       sum {m | ~(p m = &0)}
         (\m.

            x pow (FST m) *
            y pow (FST (SND m)) *

   let xpoly =
     \m:num#num#num. if m = (1,0,0) then &1 else &0 in
   let ypoly =
     \m:num#num#num. if m = (0,1,0) then &1 else &0 in
   let zpoly =
     \m:num#num#num. if m = (0,0,1) then &1 else &0 in
   let negp =
     \p:(num#num#num)->real. \m:num#num#num. --(p m) in
   let f =
     \x y z:real. x pow 2 + y pow 2 + z pow 2 + x * y * z in
   let allowed =
     \p:(num#num#num)->real.
      \q:(num#num#num)->real.
       \r:(num#num#num)->real.
        p INSERT q INSERT r INSERT {} =
          xpoly INSERT ypoly INSERT zpoly INSERT {} \/
        p INSERT q INSERT r INSERT {} =
          xpoly INSERT negp ypoly INSERT negp zpoly INSERT {} \/
        p INSERT q INSERT r INSERT {} =
          negp xpoly INSERT ypoly INSERT negp zpoly INSERT {} \/
        p INSERT q INSERT r INSERT {} =
          negp xpoly INSERT negp ypoly INSERT zpoly INSERT {} in
   ((!p:(num#num#num)->real.
      !q:(num#num#num)->real.
      !r:(num#num#num)->real.
       polynomial p /\
       polynomial q /\
       polynomial r /\

title: putnam_1986_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1986_b5:
;; the Vieta involution (x,y,z) -> (x,y,-z-xy) preserves
;; x^2+y^2+z^2+xyz but is not a permutation of signed coordinate
;; polynomials with zero or two minus signs. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A term is (EX EY EZ COEFFICIENT), and a polynomial is a list of nonzero
;; terms in strictly increasing lexicographic exponent order. This is a
;; canonical sparse representation of a polynomial in X, Y, and Z.

(defun putnam-1986-b5-term-ex (term)
  (nth 0 term))

(defun putnam-1986-b5-term-ey (term)
  (nth 1 term))

(defun putnam-1986-b5-term-ez (term)
  (nth 2 term))

(defun putnam-1986-b5-term-coefficient (term)
  (nth 3 term))

(defun putnam-1986-b5-term-p (term)
  (and
   (true-listp term)
   (equal (len term) 4)
   (natp (putnam-1986-b5-term-ex term))
   (natp (putnam-1986-b5-term-ey term))
   (natp (putnam-1986-b5-term-ez term))
   (rationalp (putnam-1986-b5-term-coefficient term))
   (not (equal (putnam-1986-b5-term-coefficient term) 0))))

(defun putnam-1986-b5-same-exponents-p (left right)
  (and
   (equal (putnam-1986-b5-term-ex left)
          (putnam-1986-b5-term-ex right))
   (equal (putnam-1986-b5-term-ey left)
          (putnam-1986-b5-term-ey right))
   (equal (putnam-1986-b5-term-ez left)
          (putnam-1986-b5-term-ez right))))

(defun putnam-1986-b5-exponents-less-p (left right)
  (or
   (< (putnam-1986-b5-term-ex left)
      (putnam-1986-b5-term-ex right))
   (and
    (equal (putnam-1986-b5-term-ex left)
           (putnam-1986-b5-term-ex right))
    (or
     (< (putnam-1986-b5-term-ey left)
        (putnam-1986-b5-term-ey right))
     (and
      (equal (putnam-1986-b5-term-ey left)
             (putnam-1986-b5-term-ey right))
      (< (putnam-1986-b5-term-ez left)
         (putnam-1986-b5-term-ez right)))))))

(defun putnam-1986-b5-polynomial-p (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (and
       (putnam-1986-b5-term-p (car polynomial))
       (or
        (endp (cdr polynomial))
        (and
         (putnam-1986-b5-term-p (cadr polynomial))
         (putnam-1986-b5-exponents-less-p
          (car polynomial)
          (cadr polynomial))))
       (putnam-1986-b5-polynomial-p (cdr polynomial)))

  (list
   (putnam-1986-b5-term-ex term)
   (putnam-1986-b5-term-ey term)
   (putnam-1986-b5-term-ez term)
   coefficient))
