theory putnam_1989_b1 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Finite_Cartesian_Product"
"HOL-Analysis.Lebesgue_Measure"
begin

definition putnam_1989_b1_solution :: "int \<times> int \<times> int \<times> int" where
  "putnam_1989_b1_solution \<equiv> (4, 2, -5, 3)"
(* (4, 2, -5, 3) *)
theorem putnam_1989_b1:
  fixes square :: "(real^2) set"
    and edges :: "(real^2) set"
    and center :: "real^2"
    and Scloser :: "(real^2) set"
  defines "square \<equiv> {p :: real^2. \<forall> i :: 2. p$i \<in> {0..1}}"
    and "edges \<equiv> {p \<in> square. p$0 = 0 \<or> p$0 = 1 \<or> p$1 = 0 \<or> p$1 = 1}"
    and "center \<equiv> \<chi> i :: 2. (1 :: real) / 2"
    and "Scloser \<equiv> {p \<in> square. \<forall> q \<in> edges. dist p center < dist p q}"
  shows "let (a, b, c, d) = putnam_1989_b1_solution in b > 0 \<and> d > 0 \<and> (\<not>(\<exists> n :: int. n^2 = b)) \<and>
  measure lebesgue Scloser / measure lebesgue square = (a * sqrt (real_of_int b) + c) / d"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_1989_b1
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1989_b1:
  the area probability that a point in a square is closer to its center than
  to every point on an edge. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let square =
     {p:real#real |
        &0 <= FST p /\ FST p <= &1 /\
        &0 <= SND p /\ SND p <= &1} in
   let edges =
     {p:real#real |
        p IN square /\
        (FST p = &0 \/ FST p = &1 \/
         SND p = &0 \/ SND p = &1)} in
   let center = (&1 / &2,&1 / &2) in
   let squared_distance =
     \(p:real#real) (q:real#real).
       (FST p - FST q) pow 2 + (SND p - SND q) pow 2 in
   let closer =
     {p:real#real |
        p IN square /\
        !q:real#real.
          q IN edges
          ==> squared_distance p center < squared_distance p q} in
   let cover_bound =
     \(s:(real#real)->bool) (B:real).
       &0 <= B /\
       ?left right bottom top:num->real.
         (!k. left k <= right k /\ bottom k <= top k) /\
         (!p. p IN s
              ==> ?k.
                    left k < FST p /\ FST p < right k /\
                    bottom k < SND p /\ SND p < top k) /\
         (!N.
            sum (0..N)
              (\k. (right k - left k) * (top k - bottom k))
            <= B) in
   let outer_area =
     \(s:(real#real)->bool). inf {B:real | cover_bound s B} in
   outer_area closer / outer_area square =
   (&4 * sqrt (&2) - &5) / &3`;;

title: putnam_1989_b1
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1989_b1:
;; the unit-square area probability of points nearer the center than every
;; edge is (4*sqrt(2)-5)/3. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For an N by N midpoint grid, X and Y are the centered coordinates scaled
;; by 2*N. The four strict inequalities say that the squared distance to the
;; center is smaller than the squared distance to each edge. Since the nearest
;; point on an edge is its perpendicular projection, this is exactly the
;; source predicate "nearer to the center than to any edge."
(defun putnam-1989-b1-grid-point-closer-p (row column subdivisions)
  (and
   (posp subdivisions)
   (natp row)
   (< row subdivisions)
   (natp column)
   (< column subdivisions)
   (let* ((x (- (+ (* 2 column) 1) subdivisions))
          (y (- (+ (* 2 row) 1) subdivisions))
          (radius-squared (+ (* x x) (* y y)))
          (left-distance (+ subdivisions x))
          (right-distance (- subdivisions x))
          (bottom-distance (+ subdivisions y))
          (top-distance (- subdivisions y)))
     (and
      (< radius-squared (* left-distance left-distance))
      (< radius-squared (* right-distance right-distance))
      (< radius-squared (* bottom-distance bottom-distance))
      (< radius-squared (* top-distance top-distance))))))

(defun putnam-1989-b1-row-count
    (row remaining-columns subdivisions)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-columns)))
  (if (zp remaining-columns)
      0
    (+ (if (putnam-1989-b1-grid-point-closer-p
            row (- remaining-columns 1) subdivisions)
           1
         0)
       (putnam-1989-b1-row-count
        row (- remaining-columns 1) subdivisions))))

(defun putnam-1989-b1-grid-count
    (remaining-rows subdivisions)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-rows)))
  (if (zp remaining-rows)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1989-b1-row-count
        (- remaining-rows 1) subdivisions subdivisions)
       (putnam-1989-b1-grid-count
        (- remaining-rows 1) subdivisions))))

;; This exact rational midpoint sum converges to the Lebesgue area of the
;; semialgebraic closer-point subset. Its boundary is contained in finitely
;; many algebraic curves and therefore has planar measure zero.
(defun putnam-1989-b1-area-approx (subdivisions)
  (if (posp subdivisions)
      (/ (putnam-1989-b1-grid-count
          subdivisions subdivisions)
         (* subdivisions subdivisions))
    0))

(defun putnam-1989-b1-isqrt-down (number candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (zp candidate)
      0
    (if (<= (* candidate candidate) number)
        candidate
      (putnam-1989-b1-isqrt-down
       number (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-1989-b1-isqrt (number)
  (let ((number (nfix number)))
    (putnam-1989-b1-isqrt-down number number)))

;; floor(sqrt(2*N^2))/N is an exact rational lower approximation to sqrt(2)
;; with error less than 1/N.
(defun putnam-1989-b1-sqrt-two-approx (subdivisions)
  (if (posp subdivisions)
      (/ (putnam-1989-b1-isqrt
          (* 2 subdivisions subdivisions))
         subdivisions)
    0))

(defun putnam-1989-b1-solution-approx (subdivisions)
  (/ (- (* 4
           (putnam-1989-b1-sqrt-two-approx subdivisions))
        5)
     3))

(defun putnam-1989-b1-error (subdivisions)
  (abs
   (- (putnam-1989-b1-area-approx subdivisions)
      (putnam-1989-b1-solution-approx subdivisions))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b1-limit-tail-p (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (subdivisions)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp subdivisions)
      (<= cutoff subdivisions))
     (< (putnam-1989-b1-error subdivisions)
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b1-limit-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (posp cutoff)
     (putnam-1989-b1-limit-tail-p epsilon cutoff))))

;; Positive rational tolerances are cofinal among positive real tolerances.
;; Thus equality of these two rational limits is bidirectionally equivalent
;; to the source equality between the Lebesgue-area ratio and
;; (4*sqrt(2)-5)/3. The square has area one, so the ratio is this area.
(defun-sk putnam-1989-b1-area-identity-p ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-1989-b1-limit-cutoff-exists-p epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b1-two-is-nonsquare-p ()
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (integerp n)
     (not (equal (* n n) 2)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1989-b1-statement ()
  (and
   (< 0 2)
   (< 0 3)
   (putnam-1989-b1-two-is-nonsquare-p)
   (putnam-1989-b1-area-identity-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_1989_b1): the area probability that a point in
-- the unit square is nearer its center than every boundary point, expressed
-- as (4 * sqrt 2 - 5) / 3. This file contains no proof.

module Putnam1989B1 where

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set

x != y =

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where

    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc threeN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc fourN

negativeNat : Nat -> Int
negativeNat zero =
  pos zero
negativeNat (suc n) =
  negsuc n

differenceNat : Nat -> Nat -> Int
differenceNat zero zero =
  pos zero
differenceNat (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
differenceNat zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
differenceNat (suc m) (suc n) =
  differenceNat m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  differenceNat m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  differenceNat n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negativeNat (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negativeNat (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms total =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    total

record StandardSquareRoot
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    squareRoot : R -> R

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      square reals (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals x (zeroR reals) ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR reals
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) y ->
      square reals y == x ->
      squareRoot x == y

open StandardSquareRoot

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

Region : Set -> Set1
Region R =
  Point R -> Set

record Rectangle (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor rectangle
  field
    lower-x : R
    upper-x : R
    lower-y : R
    upper-y : R

open Rectangle

ValidRectangle :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Rectangle R ->
  Set
ValidRectangle reals box =
  lessOrEqual reals (lower-x box) (upper-x box)
  and
  lessOrEqual reals (lower-y box) (upper-y box)

RectangleContains :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Rectangle R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
RectangleContains reals box p =
  lessOrEqual reals (lower-x box) (x-coordinate p)
  and
  lessOrEqual reals (x-coordinate p) (upper-x box)
  and
  lessOrEqual reals (lower-y box) (y-coordinate p)
  and
  lessOrEqual reals (y-coordinate p) (upper-y box)

rectangleArea :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Rectangle R ->
  R
rectangleArea reals box =
  multiply reals
    (subtract reals (upper-x box) (lower-x box))
    (subtract reals (upper-y box) (lower-y box))

RectangleCover : Set -> Set
RectangleCover R =
  Nat -> Rectangle R

ValidCover :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  RectangleCover R ->
  Set
ValidCover reals cover =
  (n : Nat) ->
  ValidRectangle reals (cover n)

Covers :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  RectangleCover R ->
  Region R ->
  Set
Covers {R} reals cover region =
  (p : Point R) ->
  region p ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ n -> RectangleContains reals (cover n) p)

CoverHasCost :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  RectangleCover R ->
  R ->
  Set
CoverHasCost reals cover total =
  SeriesHasSum reals
    (\ n -> rectangleArea reals (cover n))
    total

CoverCost :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Region R ->
  R ->
  Set
CoverCost {R} reals region total =
  Exists (RectangleCover R)
    (\ cover ->
      ValidCover reals cover
      and
      Covers reals cover region
      and
      CoverHasCost reals cover total)

LowerBound :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> Set) ->
  R ->
  Set
LowerBound {R} reals values bound =
  (value : R) ->
  values value ->
  lessOrEqual reals bound value

GreatestLowerBound :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> Set) ->
  R ->
  Set
GreatestLowerBound {R} reals values infimum =
  LowerBound reals values infimum
  and
  ((bound : R) ->
    LowerBound reals values bound ->
    lessOrEqual reals bound infimum)

LebesgueOuterArea :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Region R ->
  R ->
  Set
LebesgueOuterArea reals region area =
  GreatestLowerBound reals (CoverCost reals region) area

BoundedRegion :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Region R ->
  Set
BoundedRegion {R} reals region =
  Exists R
    (\ bound ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) bound
      and
      ((p : Point R) ->
        region p ->
        lessOrEqual reals
          (negate reals bound)
          (x-coordinate p)
        and
        lessOrEqual reals
          (x-coordinate p)
          bound
        and
        lessOrEqual reals
          (negate reals bound)
          (y-coordinate p)
        and
        lessOrEqual reals
          (y-coordinate p)
          bound))

record StandardLebesguePlane
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    area : Region R -> R
    area-characterization :
      (region : Region R) ->
      BoundedRegion reals region ->
      LebesgueOuterArea reals region (area region)

open StandardLebesguePlane

squaredDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
squaredDistance reals p q =
  add reals
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q)))
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)))

distance :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardSquareRoot reals ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
distance reals roots p q =
  squareRoot roots (squaredDistance reals p q)

record Quadruple (A : Set) : Set where
  constructor quadruple
  field
    first-coordinate  : A
    second-coordinate : A
    third-coordinate  : A
    fourth-coordinate : A

open Quadruple

PositiveInt : Int -> Set
PositiveInt (pos zero) =
  Bottom
PositiveInt (pos (suc n)) =
  Top
PositiveInt (negsuc n) =
  Bottom

IntDivides : Int -> Int -> Set
IntDivides divisor dividend =
  Exists Int
    (\ factor -> multiplyInt divisor factor == dividend)

IsIntegerSquare : Int -> Set
IsIntegerSquare z =
  Exists Int
    (\ root -> multiplyInt root root == z)

IsUnit : Int -> Set
IsUnit (pos oneN) =
  Top
IsUnit (negsuc zero) =
  Top
IsUnit _ =
  Bottom

CoprimeTriple : Int -> Int -> Int -> Set
CoprimeTriple a c d =
  (common : Int) ->
  IntDivides common a ->
  IntDivides common c ->
  IntDivides common d ->
  IsUnit common

module Putnam1989B1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (roots : StandardSquareRoot reals)
  (lebesgue : StandardLebesguePlane reals) where

  half : R
  half =
    divide reals
      (oneR reals)
      (fromNat reals twoN)

  center : Point R
  center =
    point half half

  unitSquare : Region R
  unitSquare p =
    lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (x-coordinate p)
    and
    lessOrEqual reals (x-coordinate p) (oneR reals)
    and
    lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (y-coordinate p)
    and
    lessOrEqual reals (y-coordinate p) (oneR reals)

  boundary : Region R
  boundary p =
    unitSquare p
    and
    ((x-coordinate p == zeroR reals)
      or
      (x-coordinate p == oneR reals)
      or
      (y-coordinate p == zeroR reals)
      or
      (y-coordinate p == oneR reals))

  closerToCenter : Region R
  closerToCenter p =
    unitSquare p
    and
    ((q : Point R) ->
      boundary q ->
      StrictLess reals
        (distance reals roots p center)
        (distance reals roots p q))

  solution : Quadruple Int
  solution =
    quadruple
      (pos fourN)
      (pos twoN)
      (negsuc fourN)
      (pos threeN)

  normalizedSolution : Set
  normalizedSolution =
    PositiveInt (second-coordinate solution)
    and
    PositiveInt (fourth-coordinate solution)
    and
    Not (IsIntegerSquare (second-coordinate solution))
    and
    CoprimeTriple
      (first-coordinate solution)
      (third-coordinate solution)
      (fourth-coordinate solution)

  answer : R
  answer =
    divide reals
      (add reals
        (multiply reals
          (fromInt reals (first-coordinate solution))
          (squareRoot roots
            (fromInt reals (second-coordinate solution))))
        (fromInt reals (third-coordinate solution)))
      (fromInt reals (fourth-coordinate solution))

  probability : R
  probability =
    divide reals
      (area lebesgue closerToCenter)
      (area lebesgue unitSquare)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    normalizedSolution
    and
    probability == answer

putnam-1989-b1 : Set1
putnam-1989-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (roots : StandardSquareRoot reals) ->
  (lebesgue : StandardLebesguePlane reals) ->
  Putnam1989B1Statement.proposition reals roots lebesgue

title: putnam_1989_b1
putnam_1989_b1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1989_b1: the area probability that a point in the unit square is
  nearer its center than every boundary point, expressed in normalized
  quadratic-irrational form. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P89B1R2 is the real coordinate plane on the index set {1,2}.
  P89B1Square is the closed unit square, P89B1Boundary is its four-edge
  boundary, and P89B1Center is the constant coordinate function 1/2.
  P89B1Dist is Euclidean distance and P89B1Closer is the set of square
  points strictly nearer the center than every boundary point.

  P89B1Area is planar Lebesgue measure through set.mm's finite-dimensional
  volume function voln. P89B1Solution is the annotated source quadruple
  (4,2,-5,3). P89B1Normalized states positivity of b and d, that b is not
  an integer square, and gcd(a,c,d) = 1.

  The final unproved $a assertion states the normalization conditions and
  the exact ratio of the two planar areas. The definitions eliminate the
  source parameters constrained by square_def, perimeter_def, center_def,
  and hScloser. This root file declares no $p proof statement; the included
  set.mm library supplies the standard mathematical vocabulary.
$)

$c P89B1I P89B1R2 P89B1Square P89B1Boundary P89B1Center $.
$c P89B1Dist P89B1Closer P89B1Area $.
$c P89B1A P89B1B P89B1C P89B1D P89B1Solution P89B1Normalized $.

p89b1-index-syntax $a class P89B1I $.
p89b1-plane-syntax $a class P89B1R2 $.
p89b1-square-syntax $a class P89B1Square $.
p89b1-boundary-syntax $a class P89B1Boundary $.
p89b1-center-syntax $a class P89B1Center $.
p89b1-distance-syntax $a class ( P89B1Dist p q ) $.
p89b1-closer-syntax $a class P89B1Closer $.
p89b1-area-syntax $a class ( P89B1Area A ) $.
p89b1-a-syntax $a class P89B1A $.
p89b1-b-syntax $a class P89B1B $.
p89b1-c-syntax $a class P89B1C $.
p89b1-d-syntax $a class P89B1D $.
p89b1-solution-syntax $a class P89B1Solution $.
p89b1-normalized-syntax $a wff P89B1Normalized $.

p89b1-index-definition $a |- P89B1I = ( 1 ... 2 ) $.

p89b1-plane-definition $a |- P89B1R2 = ( RR ^m P89B1I ) $.

${
  $d j p $.

  p89b1-square-definition $a |- P89B1Square = {
    p e. P89B1R2 |
    A. j e. P89B1I
      (
        0 <_ ( p ` j )
        /\
        ( p ` j ) <_ 1
      )
  } $.
$}

${
  p89b1-boundary-definition $a |- P89B1Boundary = {
    p e. P89B1Square |
    (
      ( p ` 1 ) = 0
      \/
      (
        ( p ` 1 ) = 1
        \/
        (
          ( p ` 2 ) = 0
          \/
          ( p ` 2 ) = 1
        )
      )
    )
  } $.
$}

p89b1-center-definition $a |- P89B1Center =
  ( j e. P89B1I |-> ( 1 / 2 ) ) $.

${
  $d j p q $.

  p89b1-distance-definition $a |- (
    P89B1Dist p q
  ) = (
    sqrt
    `
    (
      sum_ j e. P89B1I
        ( ( ( p ` j ) - ( q ` j ) ) ^ 2 )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d p q $.

  p89b1-closer-definition $a |- P89B1Closer = {
    p e. P89B1Square |
    A. q e. P89B1Boundary
      ( P89B1Dist p P89B1Center )
      <
      ( P89B1Dist p q )
  } $.
$}

p89b1-area-definition $a |- (
  P89B1Area A
) = (
  ( voln ` P89B1I ) ` A
) $.

p89b1-a-definition $a |- P89B1A = 4 $.
p89b1-b-definition $a |- P89B1B = 2 $.
p89b1-c-definition $a |- P89B1C = ( -u 5 ) $.
p89b1-d-definition $a |- P89B1D = 3 $.

p89b1-solution-definition $a |- P89B1Solution =
  <.
    P89B1A
    ,
    <.
      P89B1B
      ,
      <. P89B1C , P89B1D >.
    >.
  >. $.

${
  p89b1-normalized-definition $a |- (
    P89B1Normalized
    <->
    (
      0 < P89B1B
      /\
      (
        0 < P89B1D
        /\
        (
          -. E. n e. ZZ ( n ^ 2 ) = P89B1B
          /\
          ( ( P89B1A gcd P89B1C ) gcd P89B1D ) = 1
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

putnambench-putnam-1989-b1 $a |- (
  P89B1Normalized
  /\
  (
    ( P89B1Area P89B1Closer )
    /
    ( P89B1Area P89B1Square )
  )
  =
  (
    (
      ( P89B1A x. ( sqrt ` P89B1B ) )
      +
      P89B1C
    )
    /
    P89B1D
  )
) $.

title: putnam_1989_b1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1989_b1:
% the area probability that a point in the unit square is nearer its center
% than every boundary point, expressed as (4 * sqrt(2) - 5) / 3.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_1989_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]
  planar_region: TYPE = [point -> bool]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  box: TYPE =
    [# left: real, right: real, bottom: real, top: real #]
  box_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> box]

  solution_quadruple: TYPE =
    [# a: int, b: int, c: int, d: int #]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  squared_distance(p, q: point): real =
    (x_coord(p) - x_coord(q)) ^ 2
      + (y_coord(p) - y_coord(q)) ^ 2

  unit_square: planar_region =
    LAMBDA (p: point):
      0 <= x_coord(p) AND x_coord(p) <= 1
        AND 0 <= y_coord(p) AND y_coord(p) <= 1

  boundary: planar_region =
    LAMBDA (p: point):
      unit_square(p)
        AND (x_coord(p) = 0
          OR x_coord(p) = 1
          OR y_coord(p) = 0
          OR y_coord(p) = 1)

  center: point =
    (# x_coord := 1 / 2, y_coord := 1 / 2 #)

  closer_to_center: planar_region =
    LAMBDA (p: point):
      unit_square(p)
        AND FORALL (q: point):
          boundary(q) IMPLIES
            squared_distance(p, center)
              < squared_distance(p, q)

  in_open_box(p: point, rectangle: box): bool =
    left(rectangle) < x_coord(p)
      AND x_coord(p) < right(rectangle)
      AND bottom(rectangle) < y_coord(p)
      AND y_coord(p) < top(rectangle)

  box_area(rectangle: box): real =
    IF left(rectangle) < right(rectangle)
        AND bottom(rectangle) < top(rectangle)
    THEN
      (right(rectangle) - left(rectangle))
        * (top(rectangle) - bottom(rectangle))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  partial_box_area(
      boxes: box_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_box_area(boxes, count - 1)
        + box_area(boxes(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  covers(region: planar_region, boxes: box_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (p: point):
      region(p) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (index: nat):
          in_open_box(p, boxes(index))

  cover_has_total_area(
      region: planar_region,
      boxes: box_sequence,
      total: real): bool =
    covers(region, boxes)
      AND converges_to(
        LAMBDA (count: nat):
          partial_box_area(boxes, count),
        total)

  has_lebesgue_outer_area(
      region: planar_region,
      area: real): bool =
    0 <= area
      AND (FORALL (boxes: box_sequence), (total: real):
        cover_has_total_area(region, boxes, total)
          IMPLIES area <= total)
      AND (FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (boxes: box_sequence), (total: real):
          cover_has_total_area(region, boxes, total)
            AND total < area + epsilon_value)

  int_divides(divisor, value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: int):
      value = divisor * quotient

  not_integer_square(value: int): bool =
    NOT EXISTS (root: int):
      root * root = value

  no_nonunit_square_divisor(value: int): bool =
    FORALL (root: int):
      (root > 1 OR root < -1) IMPLIES
        NOT int_divides(root * root, value)

  coprime_triple(first, second, third: int): bool =
    FORALL (common: int):
      (int_divides(common, first)
        AND int_divides(common, second)
        AND int_divides(common, third))
      IMPLIES common = 1 OR common = -1

  putnam_1989_b1_solution: solution_quadruple =
    (# a := 4, b := 2, c := -5, d := 3 #)

  normalized_solution: bool =
    b(putnam_1989_b1_solution) > 0
      AND d(putnam_1989_b1_solution) > 0
      AND not_integer_square(b(putnam_1989_b1_solution))
      AND no_nonunit_square_divisor(
        b(putnam_1989_b1_solution))
      AND coprime_triple(
        a(putnam_1989_b1_solution),
        c(putnam_1989_b1_solution),
        d(putnam_1989_b1_solution))

  sqrt_value(root, radicand: real): bool =
    0 <= root AND root * root = radicand

  solution_value(sqrt_two: real): real =
    safe_div(
      (a(putnam_1989_b1_solution) :: real) * sqrt_two
        + (c(putnam_1989_b1_solution) :: real),
      d(putnam_1989_b1_solution) :: real)

  putnam_1989_b1: bool =
    EXISTS (square_area, closer_area, sqrt_two: real):
      has_lebesgue_outer_area(unit_square, square_area)
        AND has_lebesgue_outer_area(
          closer_to_center, closer_area)
        AND sqrt_value(sqrt_two, 2)
        AND normalized_solution
        AND safe_div(closer_area, square_area)
          = solution_value(sqrt_two)
END putnam_1989_b1

title: putnam_1989_b2
content:
import Mathlib

open Nat

-- Note: This formalization uses "Type" rather than "Type*" as the underlying structure for a semigroup.
abbrev putnam_1989_b2_solution : Prop := sorry
-- True
/--
Let $S$ be a non-empty set with an associative operation that is left and right cancellative ($xy=xz$ implies $y=z$, and $yx=zx$ implies $y=z$). Assume that for every $a$ in $S$ the set $\{a^n:\,n=1, 2, 3, \ldots\}$ is finite. Must $S$ be a group?
-/
theorem putnam_1989_b2 :
    (∀ (S : Type) [Nonempty S] [Semigroup S] [IsCancelMul S]
      (h_fin : ∀ a : S, {(a * ·)^[n] a | n : ℕ}.Finite),
      ∃ e : S, ∀ x, e * x = x ∧ x * e = x ∧ ∃ y, x * y = e ∧ y * x = e) ↔
    putnam_1989_b2_solution :=
  sorry

title: putnam_1989_b2
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1989_b2:
   every nonempty left- and right-cancellative semigroup whose positive powers
   of each element form a finite set is a group; this file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Ensembles Finite_sets.

Record putnam_1989_b2_semigroup (S : Type) : Type := {
  putnam_1989_b2_mul : S -> S -> S;
  putnam_1989_b2_assoc :
    forall x y z : S,
      putnam_1989_b2_mul x (putnam_1989_b2_mul y z) =
      putnam_1989_b2_mul (putnam_1989_b2_mul x y) z
}.

Arguments putnam_1989_b2_mul {S} _ _ _.

Definition putnam_1989_b2_cancellative
    {S : Type}
    (sg : putnam_1989_b2_semigroup S) : Prop :=
  forall x y z : S,
    (putnam_1989_b2_mul sg x y =
       putnam_1989_b2_mul sg x z ->
     y = z) /\
    (putnam_1989_b2_mul sg y x =
       putnam_1989_b2_mul sg z x ->
     y = z).

Fixpoint putnam_1989_b2_positive_power
    {S : Type}
    (sg : putnam_1989_b2_semigroup S)
    (a : S)
    (n : nat) : S :=
  match n with
  | O => a
  | S k =>
      putnam_1989_b2_mul sg a
        (putnam_1989_b2_positive_power sg a k)
  end.

Definition putnam_1989_b2_finite_positive_powers
    {S : Type}
    (sg : putnam_1989_b2_semigroup S) : Prop :=
  forall a : S,
    Finite S
      (fun x : S =>
        exists n : nat,
          x = putnam_1989_b2_positive_power sg a n).

Definition putnam_1989_b2_is_group
    {S : Type}
    (sg : putnam_1989_b2_semigroup S) : Prop :=
  exists e : S,
    forall x : S,
      putnam_1989_b2_mul sg e x = x /\
      putnam_1989_b2_mul sg x e = x /\
      exists y : S,
        putnam_1989_b2_mul sg x y = e /\
        putnam_1989_b2_mul sg y x = e.

Definition putnam_1989_b2_solution : Prop := True.

Theorem putnam_1989_b2 :
  (forall (S : Type) (sg : putnam_1989_b2_semigroup S),
    (exists a : S, True) ->
    putnam_1989_b2_cancellative sg ->
    putnam_1989_b2_finite_positive_powers sg ->
    putnam_1989_b2_is_group sg) <->
  putnam_1989_b2_solution.
Admitted.

title: putnam_1989_b2

theory putnam_1989_b2 imports
Complex_Main
"HOL-Algebra.Complete_Lattice"
"HOL-Library.FuncSet"
begin

(* Isabelle/HOL cannot quantify over carrier types directly, so a semigroup is
   represented by a carrier set and a binary operation on a fixed ambient type. *)
definition putnam_1989_b2_solution :: bool where
  "putnam_1989_b2_solution \<equiv> True"
(* True *)
theorem putnam_1989_b2:
  shows "(\<forall>S :: 'a set. \<forall>mult :: 'a \<Rightarrow> 'a \<Rightarrow> 'a.
    (S \<noteq> {}
      \<and> (\<forall>x \<in> S. \<forall>y \<in> S. mult x y \<in> S)
      \<and> (\<forall>x \<in> S. \<forall>y \<in> S. \<forall>z \<in> S.
        mult (mult x y) z = mult x (mult y z))
      \<and> (\<forall>x \<in> S. \<forall>y \<in> S. \<forall>z \<in> S.
        (mult x y = mult x z \<longrightarrow> y = z)
        \<and> (mult y x = mult z x \<longrightarrow> y = z))
      \<and> (\<forall>a \<in> S. finite {x \<in> S.
        \<exists>n :: nat. x = foldr mult (replicate n a) a}))
    \<longrightarrow> (\<exists>e \<in> S. \<forall>x \<in> S.
      mult x e = x \<and> mult e x = x
      \<and> (\<exists>y \<in> S. mult x y = e \<and> mult y x = e)))
    \<longleftrightarrow> putnam_1989_b2_solution"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1989_b2:
  every nonempty cancellative semigroup in which each element has only
  finitely many positive powers is a group. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `!carrier:A->bool mul:A->A->A.
     (?w:A. w IN carrier) /\
     (!x y:A.
        x IN carrier /\ y IN carrier
        ==> mul x y IN carrier) /\
     (!x y z:A.
        x IN carrier /\ y IN carrier /\ z IN carrier
        ==> mul (mul x y) z = mul x (mul y z)) /\
     (!x y z:A.
        x IN carrier /\ y IN carrier /\ z IN carrier
        ==>
        (mul x y = mul x z ==> y = z) /\
        (mul y x = mul z x ==> y = z)) /\
     (!a:A.
        a IN carrier
        ==>
        FINITE
          {x:A |
             ?n:num powers:num->A.
               powers 0 = a /\
               (!k:num. powers (SUC k) = mul a (powers k)) /\
               powers n = x})
     ==>
     ?e:A.
       e IN carrier /\
       !x:A.
         x IN carrier
         ==>
         mul e x = x /\
         mul x e = x /\
         ?y:A.
           y IN carrier /\
           mul x y = e /\
           mul y x = e`;;

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1989_b2:
;; every nonempty cancellative semigroup in which each element has a finite
;; positive-power orbit has a two-sided identity and two-sided inverses. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; DEFSTUB is ACL2's conservative mechanism for a generic function symbol.
;; These declarations therefore range over an arbitrary carrier predicate and
;; binary operation, rather than the restricted class of APPLY$-tame objects.

(defstub putnam-1989-b2-carrier (x) t)
(defstub putnam-1989-b2-multiply (x y) t)

(defun putnam-1989-b2-member-p (x)
  (if (putnam-1989-b2-carrier x) t nil))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b2-nonempty-p ()
  (exists (x)
    (putnam-1989-b2-member-p x)))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b2-closed-p ()
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1989-b2-member-p x)
      (putnam-1989-b2-member-p y))
     (putnam-1989-b2-member-p
      (putnam-1989-b2-multiply x y)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b2-associative-p ()
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1989-b2-member-p x)
      (putnam-1989-b2-member-p y)
      (putnam-1989-b2-member-p z))
     (equal
      (putnam-1989-b2-multiply
       (putnam-1989-b2-multiply x y)
       z)
      (putnam-1989-b2-multiply
       x
       (putnam-1989-b2-multiply y z))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b2-cancellative-p ()
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1989-b2-member-p x)
      (putnam-1989-b2-member-p y)
      (putnam-1989-b2-member-p z))
     (and
      (implies
       (equal
        (putnam-1989-b2-multiply x y)
        (putnam-1989-b2-multiply x z))
       (equal y z))
      (implies
       (equal
        (putnam-1989-b2-multiply y x)
        (putnam-1989-b2-multiply z x))
       (equal y z))))))

;; POWER(A,N) is the source's a^(N+1), defined without assuming an identity:
;; POWER(A,0)=A and POWER(A,N+1)=A*POWER(A,N).

(defun putnam-1989-b2-power (a n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      a
    (putnam-1989-b2-multiply
     a
     (putnam-1989-b2-power a (- n 1)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b2-power-representative-exists-p
    (a n bound)
  (exists (k)
    (and
     (natp k)
     (< k bound)
     (equal
      (putnam-1989-b2-power a n)
      (putnam-1989-b2-power a k)))))

;; A sequence has finite range iff some finite initial segment contains every
;; value. BOUND remains an internal existential witness.

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b2-power-orbit-covered-p
    (a bound)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (natp n)
     (putnam-1989-b2-power-representative-exists-p
      a n bound))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b2-finite-power-orbit-p (a)
  (exists (bound)
    (and
     (posp bound)
     (putnam-1989-b2-power-orbit-covered-p
      a bound))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b2-all-power-orbits-finite-p ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (putnam-1989-b2-member-p a)
     (putnam-1989-b2-finite-power-orbit-p a))))

(defun putnam-1989-b2-semigroup-hypotheses-p ()
  (and
   (putnam-1989-b2-nonempty-p)
   (putnam-1989-b2-closed-p)
   (putnam-1989-b2-associative-p)
   (putnam-1989-b2-cancellative-p)
   (putnam-1989-b2-all-power-orbits-finite-p)))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b2-inverse-exists-p (e x)
  (exists (y)
    (and
     (putnam-1989-b2-member-p y)
     (equal
      (putnam-1989-b2-multiply x y)
      e)
     (equal
      (putnam-1989-b2-multiply y x)
      e))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b2-identity-and-inverses-p (e)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (putnam-1989-b2-member-p x)
     (and
      (equal
       (putnam-1989-b2-multiply e x)
       x)
      (equal
       (putnam-1989-b2-multiply x e)
       x)
      (putnam-1989-b2-inverse-exists-p e x)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b2-group-witness-exists-p ()
  (exists (e)
    (and
     (putnam-1989-b2-member-p e)
     (putnam-1989-b2-identity-and-inverses-p e))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1989-b2-statement ()
  (implies
   (putnam-1989-b2-semigroup-hypotheses-p)
   (putnam-1989-b2-group-witness-exists-p)))

:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1989_b2:
-- every nonempty associative left- and right-cancellative semigroup in which
-- each element has only finitely many positive powers is a group.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data Member {A : Set} (x : A) : List A -> Set where
  at-head : {xs : List A} -> Member x (x ∷ xs)
  in-tail :
    {y : A} ->
    {xs : List A} ->
    Member x xs ->
    Member x (y ∷ xs)

record Nonempty (A : Set) : Set where
  field
    element : A

record Semigroup (S : Set) : Set where
  field
    multiply : S -> S -> S
    associative :
      (x y z : S) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)

open Semigroup

record Cancellative
  {S : Set}
  (algebra : Semigroup S) :
  Set where

  field
    left-cancel :
      (x y z : S) ->
      multiply algebra x y == multiply algebra x z ->
      y == z
    right-cancel :
      (x y z : S) ->
      multiply algebra y x == multiply algebra z x ->
      y == z

positivePower :
  {S : Set} ->
  Semigroup S ->
  S ->
  Nat ->
  S
positivePower algebra a zero =
  a
positivePower algebra a (suc n) =
  multiply algebra a (positivePower algebra a n)

FiniteImage :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set
FiniteImage {A} {B} function =
  Exists (List B)
    (\ values ->
      (x : A) ->
      Member (function x) values)

record IsGroup
  {S : Set}
  (algebra : Semigroup S) :
  Set where

  field
    identity : S
    left-identity :
      (x : S) ->
      multiply algebra identity x == x
    right-identity :
      (x : S) ->
      multiply algebra x identity == x
    inverse :
      (x : S) ->
      Exists S
        (\ y ->
          Both
            (multiply algebra x y == identity)
            (multiply algebra y x == identity))

putnam-1989-b2 : Set1
putnam-1989-b2 =
  (S : Set) ->
  Nonempty S ->
  (algebra : Semigroup S) ->
  Cancellative algebra ->
  ((a : S) -> FiniteImage (positivePower algebra a)) ->
  IsGroup algebra

             ==>
             (mul x y = mul x z ==> y = z) /\
             (mul y x = mul z x ==> y = z)) /\
          (!a : 'a.
             a IN carrier
             ==>
             FINITE
               (IMAGE
                  (\n : num. FUNPOW (mul a) n a)
                  (UNIV : num set)))
          ==>
          ?e : 'a.
            e IN carrier /\
            !x : 'a.
              x IN carrier
              ==>
              mul e x = x /\
              mul x e = x /\
              ?y : 'a.
                y IN carrier /\
                mul x y = e /\
                mul y x = e)
       <=>
       putnam_1989_b2_solution)``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1989_b2: every nonempty cancellative semigroup in which each
  element has only finitely many positive powers is a group, identified
  with the source's solution proposition. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The arbitrary carrier is the set s, and f is an arbitrary total binary
  operation from s X. s to s. The antecedent states nonemptiness,
  associativity, and both cancellation laws.

  For each a in s, the internally existential sequence p has p(0) = a and
  p(n+1) = f(a,p(n)). Its range is therefore exactly the set of positive
  powers of a, with the same indexing as the Lean and Isabelle sources, and
  requiring ran p to be finite preserves their finiteness hypothesis.

  The resolved answer is True, so the statement directly asserts the group
  conclusion. The identity and inverse witnesses remain inside the
  conclusion for each arbitrary semigroup. The final declaration is the
  single unproved $a corpus statement; this statement file contributes no
  $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a e f n p s x y z $.

  putnambench-putnam-1989-b2 $a |-
      A. s
        A. f e. ( s ^m ( s X. s ) )
          (
            (
              (
                s =/= (/)
                /\
                A. x e. s A. y e. s A. z e. s
                  ( f ` <. ( f ` <. x , y >. ) , z >. )
                  =
                  ( f ` <. x , ( f ` <. y , z >. ) >. )
              )
              /\
              A. x e. s A. y e. s A. z e. s
                (
                  (
                    ( f ` <. x , y >. ) = ( f ` <. x , z >. )
                    ->
                    y = z
                  )
                  /\
                  (
                    ( f ` <. y , x >. ) = ( f ` <. z , x >. )
                    ->
                    y = z
                  )
                )
              /\
              A. a e. s
                E. p e. ( s ^m NN0 )
                  (
                    (
                      ( p ` 0 ) = a
                      /\
                      A. n e. NN0
                        ( p ` ( n + 1 ) )
                        =
                        ( f ` <. a , ( p ` n ) >. )
                    )
                    /\
                    ran p e. Fin
                  )
            )
            ->
            E. e e. s
              A. x e. s
                (
                  (
                    ( f ` <. e , x >. ) = x
                    /\
                    ( f ` <. x , e >. ) = x
                  )
                  /\
                  E. y e. s
                    (
                      ( f ` <. x , y >. ) = e
                      /\
                      ( f ` <. y , x >. ) = e
                    )
                )
          )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1989_b2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1989_b2:
% every cancellative semigroup whose positive-power set is finite for each
% element is a group. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1989_b2[S: TYPE+]: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[S]

  operation: TYPE = [S, S -> S]

  associative(op: operation): bool =
    FORALL (x, y, z: S):
      op(op(x, y), z) = op(x, op(y, z))

  cancellative(op: operation): bool =
    FORALL (x, y, z: S):
      (op(x, y) = op(x, z) IMPLIES y = z)
        AND (op(y, x) = op(z, x) IMPLIES y = z)

  positive_power(op: operation, a: S, offset: nat): RECURSIVE S =
    IF offset = 0 THEN
      a
    ELSE
      op(a, positive_power(op, a, offset - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE offset

  has_finite_positive_powers(op: operation, a: S): bool =
    EXISTS (powers: finite_set[S]):
      FORALL (x: S):
        powers(x) IFF
          EXISTS (offset: nat):
            x = positive_power(op, a, offset)

  is_group(op: operation): bool =
    EXISTS (identity: S):
      FORALL (x: S):
        op(identity, x) = x
          AND op(x, identity) = x
          AND EXISTS (inverse: S):
            op(x, inverse) = identity
              AND op(inverse, x) = identity

  putnam_1989_b2_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_1989_b2: bool =
    (FORALL (op: operation):
      (associative(op)
        AND cancellative(op)
        AND FORALL (a: S):
          has_finite_positive_powers(op, a))
      IMPLIES is_group(op))
    IFF putnam_1989_b2_solution
END putnam_1989_b2

title: putnam_1989_b3
content:
import Mathlib

open Nat Filter Topology

noncomputable abbrev putnam_1989_b3_solution : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ := sorry
-- fun n c ↦ c * n ! / (3 ^ n * ∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc (1 : ℤ) n, (1 - 2 ^ (-m)))
/--
Let $f$ be a function on $[0,\infty)$, differentiable and satisfying
\[
f'(x)=-3f(x)+6f(2x)
\]
for $x>0$. Assume that $|f(x)|\le e^{-\sqrt{x}}$ for $x\ge 0$ (so that $f(x)$ tends rapidly to $0$ as $x$ increases). For $n$ a non-negative integer, define
\[
\mu_n=\int_0^\infty x^n f(x)\,dx
\]
(sometimes called the $n$th moment of $f$).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[a)] Express $\mu_n$ in terms of $\mu_0$.
\item[b)] Prove that the sequence $\{\mu_n \frac{3^n}{n!}\}$ always converges, and that the limit is $0$ only if $\mu_0=0$.
\end{enumerate}
-/
theorem putnam_1989_b3
    (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hfdiff : Differentiable ℝ f)
    (hfderiv : ∀ x > 0, deriv f x = -3 * f x + 6 * f (2 * x))
    (hdecay : ∀ x ≥ 0, |f x| ≤ Real.exp (- √x))
    (μ : ℕ → ℝ)
    (μ_def : ∀ n, μ n = ∫ x in Set.Ioi 0, x ^ n * f x) :
    (∀ n, μ n = putnam_1989_b3_solution n (μ 0)) ∧
    (∃ L, Tendsto (fun n ↦ (μ n) * 3 ^ n / n !) atTop (𝓝 L)) ∧
    (Tendsto (fun n ↦ (μ n) * 3 ^ n / n !) atTop (𝓝 0) → μ 0 = 0) :=
  sorry

title: putnam_1989_b3
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1989_b3:
   moments of a rapidly decaying solution of a dilation differential equation,
   their closed form, and convergence of their factorial normalization; this
   file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals ClassicalEpsilon Arith.Factorial.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_1989_b3_nonnegative_derivative
    (f : R -> R) (x d : R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    epsilon > 0 ->
    exists delta : R,
      delta > 0 /\
      forall y : R,
        0 <= y ->
        y <> x ->
        Rabs (y - x) < delta ->
        Rabs ((f y - f x) / (y - x) - d) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_1989_b3_derivative
    (f : R -> R) (x : R) : R :=
  epsilon (inhabits (0 : R))
    (fun d : R => putnam_1989_b3_nonnegative_derivative f x d).

Fixpoint putnam_1989_b3_product (n : nat) : R :=
  match n with
  | O => 1
  | S k =>
      putnam_1989_b3_product k *
      (1 - / (2 ^ (S k)))
  end.

Definition putnam_1989_b3_solution
    (n : nat) (c : R) : R :=
  c * INR (fact n) /
  (3 ^ n * putnam_1989_b3_product n).

Definition putnam_1989_b3_tends_to_at_pos_infty
    (g : R -> R) (limit : R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    epsilon > 0 ->
    exists M : R,
      forall b : R,
        b >= M ->
        Rabs (g b - limit) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_1989_b3_moment
    (f : R -> R) (n : nat) (value : R) : Prop :=
  exists partial_integral : R -> R,
    (forall b : R,
      0 <= b ->
      exists integrable :
        Riemann_integrable
          (fun x : R => x ^ n * f x) 0 b,
        partial_integral b = RiemannInt integrable) /\
    putnam_1989_b3_tends_to_at_pos_infty
      partial_integral value.

Definition putnam_1989_b3_sequence_converges_to
    (u : nat -> R) (limit : R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    epsilon > 0 ->
    exists N : nat,
      forall n : nat,
        (N <= n)%nat ->
        Rabs (u n - limit) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_1989_b3_normalized_moment
    (mu : nat -> R) (n : nat) : R :=
  mu n * 3 ^ n / INR (fact n).

Theorem putnam_1989_b3
    (f : R -> R)
    (hfdiff :
      forall x : R,
        0 <= x ->
        putnam_1989_b3_nonnegative_derivative
          f x (putnam_1989_b3_derivative f x))
    (hfderiv :
      forall x : R,
        x > 0 ->
        putnam_1989_b3_derivative f x =
        -3 * f x + 6 * f (2 * x))
    (hdecay :
      forall x : R,
        x >= 0 ->
        Rabs (f x) <= exp (- sqrt x))
    (mu : nat -> R)
    (mu_def :
      forall n : nat,
        putnam_1989_b3_moment f n (mu n)) :
  (forall n : nat,
    mu n = putnam_1989_b3_solution n (mu 0%nat)) /\
  (exists limit : R,
    putnam_1989_b3_sequence_converges_to
      (putnam_1989_b3_normalized_moment mu) limit) /\
  (putnam_1989_b3_sequence_converges_to
      (putnam_1989_b3_normalized_moment mu) 0 ->
    mu 0%nat = 0).
Admitted.

title: putnam_1989_b3
content:
theory putnam_1989_b3 imports
Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Interval_Integral"
begin

definition putnam_1989_b3_solution :: "nat \<Rightarrow> real \<Rightarrow> real" where "putnam_1989_b3_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* \<lambda> n c. c * fact n / (3 ^ n * (\<Prod> m = 1..n. 1 - 2 powi (-m))) *)
theorem putnam_1989_b3:
  fixes f :: "real \<Rightarrow> real"
  and \<mu> :: "nat \<Rightarrow> real"
  defines "\<mu> \<equiv> \<lambda> n. interval_lebesgue_integral lebesgue 0 \<infinity> (\<lambda> x. x ^ n * f x)"
  assumes hfdiff: "f differentiable_on {0..}"
  and hfderiv: "\<forall> x > 0. deriv f x = -3 * f x + 6 * f (2 * x)"
  and hdecay: "\<forall> x \<ge> 0. \<bar>f x\<bar> \<le> exp (-sqrt x)"
  shows "(\<forall> n :: nat. \<mu> n = putnam_1989_b3_solution n (\<mu> 0)) \<and> convergent (\<lambda> n :: nat. \<mu> n * 3 ^ n / fact n) \<and> (((\<lambda> n :: nat. \<mu> n * 3 ^ n / fact n) \<longlonglongrightarrow> 0) \<longrightarrow> (\<mu> 0 = 0))"
  sorry

end
