theory putnam_1989_b6 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Finite_Cartesian_Product"
"HOL-Analysis.Lebesgue_Measure"
"HOL-Analysis.Set_Integral"
"HOL-Analysis.Interval_Integral"
"HOL-Computational_Algebra.Polynomial"
begin

theorem putnam_1989_b6:
  fixes n :: "nat"
    and Sx :: "(real^'n) set"
    and fprop :: "(real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
    and xext :: "(real^'n) \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> real)"
    and fxsum :: "(real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> (real^'n) \<Rightarrow> real"
    and fEV :: "(real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> real"
    and bij :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'n"
  defines "Sx \<equiv> {x :: real^'n. (\<forall> i :: 'n. x$i \<in> {0<..<1}) \<and> (\<forall> j \<in> {1..n-1}. x$(bij (j + 1)) > x$(bij j))}"
    and "fprop \<equiv> \<lambda> f :: real \<Rightarrow> real. continuous_on {0..1} f \<and> f 1 = 0"
    and "fxsum \<equiv> \<lambda> (f :: real \<Rightarrow> real) (x :: real^'n). (\<Sum> i \<in> {0..n}. ((xext x) (i + 1) - (xext x) i) * f ((xext x) (i + 1)))"
    and "fEV \<equiv>  \<lambda> f :: real \<Rightarrow> real. (set_lebesgue_integral lebesgue Sx (fxsum f)) / (set_lebesgue_integral lebesgue Sx (\<lambda> x :: real^'n. 1))"
  assumes hcard : "CARD('n) = n"
    and hbij : "bij_betw bij {1..n} (UNIV :: 'n set)"
    and npos : "n \<ge> 1"
    and hext : "\<forall> x :: real^'n. xext x 0 = 0 \<and> xext x (n + 1) = 1 \<and> (\<forall> i \<in> {1..n}. xext x i = x$(bij i))"
  shows "\<exists> P :: real poly. degree P = n \<and> (\<forall> t \<in> {0..1}. poly P t \<in> {0..1}) \<and> (\<forall> f :: real \<Rightarrow> real. fprop f \<longrightarrow> fEV f = (interval_lebesgue_integral lebesgue 0 1 (\<lambda> t :: real. f t * poly P t)))"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_1989_b6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1989_b6:
  the expected right-endpoint Riemann sum over the uniformly sampled ordered
  simplex is integration against a bounded degree-n polynomial independent of
  the continuous function. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let grid =
     \n m. {q:num list |
              LENGTH q = n /\
              (!i. i < n ==> 0 < EL i q /\ EL i q < m) /\
              (!i. i + 1 < n ==> EL i q < EL (i + 1) q)} in
   let coordinate =
     \n m (q:num list) i.
       if i = 0 then &0
       else if i = n + 1 then &1
       else &(EL (i - 1) q) / &m in
   let right_sum =
     \n m (f:real->real) (q:num list).
       sum (0..n)
         (\i. (coordinate n m q (i + 1) -
               coordinate n m q i) *
              f (coordinate n m q (i + 1))) in
   let polynomial =
     \n (p:real list) t.
       sum (0..n) (\k. EL k p * t pow k) in
   let simplex_average =
     \n (f:real->real) m.
       sum (grid n m) (\q. right_sum n m f q) /
       &(CARD (grid n m)) in
   let interval_average =
     \n (p:real list) (f:real->real) m.
       sum (0..m - 1)
         (\j. f (&(j + 1) / &m) *
              polynomial n p (&(j + 1) / &m)) /
       &m in
   let tends_to =
     \(u:num->real) L.
       !e. &0 < e
           ==> ?M. !m. M <= m ==> abs (u m - L) < e in
   let continuous_on_unit =
     \f:real->real.
       !x. &0 <= x /\ x <= &1
           ==> !e. &0 < e
                   ==> ?d. &0 < d /\
                           !y. &0 <= y /\ y <= &1 /\ abs (y - x) < d
                               ==> abs (f y - f x) < e in
   !n:num.
     1 <= n
     ==> ?p:real list.
           LENGTH p = n + 1 /\
           ~(LAST p = &0) /\
           (!t. &0 <= t /\ t <= &1
                ==> &0 <= polynomial n p t /\
                    polynomial n p t <= &1) /\
           (!f:real->real.
              continuous_on_unit f /\
              f (&1) = &0
              ==>
              ?L. tends_to (simplex_average n f) L /\
                  tends_to (interval_average n p f) L)`;;

title: putnam_1989_b6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1989_b6:
;; the expected right-endpoint Riemann sum over uniformly ordered points in
;; (0,1) is integration against a degree-n polynomial bounded by 0 and 1.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Polynomials are finite lists of rational coefficients in ascending degree
;; order.  These test functions are not a restriction of the source domain:
;; rational polynomials vanishing at 1 are uniformly dense in the continuous
;; real functions on [0,1] that vanish at 1.  Both the expected-sum functional
;; and integration against the bounded polynomial below are continuous in the
;; uniform norm, so equality on these tests is equivalent in both directions
;; to equality for every source function.

(defun putnam-1989-b6-rational-polynomial-p (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and (rationalp (car coefficients))
           (putnam-1989-b6-rational-polynomial-p
            (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun putnam-1989-b6-polynomial-value (coefficients x)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (+ (car coefficients)
         (* x
            (putnam-1989-b6-polynomial-value
             (cdr coefficients) x)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1989-b6-last-coefficient (coefficients)
  (if (consp (cdr coefficients))
      (putnam-1989-b6-last-coefficient (cdr coefficients))
    (if (consp coefficients) (car coefficients) 0)))

(defun putnam-1989-b6-degree-n-p (coefficients n)
  (and
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (putnam-1989-b6-rational-polynomial-p coefficients)
   (equal (len coefficients) (+ n 1))
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-1989-b6-last-coefficient coefficients)
     0))))

(defun putnam-1989-b6-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n (putnam-1989-b6-factorial (- n 1)))))

;; Midpoint coordinate number INDEX in a SUBDIVISIONS-grid of [0,1].
(defun putnam-1989-b6-grid-coordinate
    (code index subdivisions)
  (if (posp subdivisions)
      (/ (+ (* 2
               (mod
                (floor code
                       (expt subdivisions index))
                subdivisions))
            1)
         (* 2 subdivisions))
    0))

(defun putnam-1989-b6-ordered-grid-point-p
    (code index remaining subdivisions)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (or (zp remaining)
          (equal remaining 1))
      t
    (and
     (< (putnam-1989-b6-grid-coordinate
         code index subdivisions)
        (putnam-1989-b6-grid-coordinate
         code (+ index 1) subdivisions))
     (putnam-1989-b6-ordered-grid-point-p
      code (+ index 1) (- remaining 1)
      subdivisions))))

;; The source right-endpoint sum, including the final interval to 1.
(defun putnam-1989-b6-right-sum-aux
    (function-coefficients code index remaining
                           subdivisions previous)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      (* (- 1 previous)
         (putnam-1989-b6-polynomial-value
          function-coefficients 1))
    (let ((current
           (putnam-1989-b6-grid-coordinate
            code index subdivisions)))
      (+ (* (- current previous)
            (putnam-1989-b6-polynomial-value
             function-coefficients current))
         (putnam-1989-b6-right-sum-aux
          function-coefficients code (+ index 1)
          (- remaining 1) subdivisions current)))))

(defun putnam-1989-b6-simplex-summand
    (function-coefficients code n subdivisions)
  (if (putnam-1989-b6-ordered-grid-point-p
       code 0 n subdivisions)
      (putnam-1989-b6-right-sum-aux
       function-coefficients code 0 n subdivisions 0)
    0))

(defun putnam-1989-b6-simplex-grid-sum
    (function-coefficients remaining n subdivisions)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1989-b6-simplex-summand
        function-coefficients (- remaining 1)
        n subdivisions)
       (putnam-1989-b6-simplex-grid-sum
        function-coefficients (- remaining 1)
        n subdivisions))))

;; The ordered simplex has volume 1/n!, so multiplying its cube Riemann sum
;; by n! gives expectation under the source uniform distribution.
(defun putnam-1989-b6-expected-sum-approx
    (function-coefficients n subdivisions)
  (if (and (posp n)
           (posp subdivisions))
      (* (/ (putnam-1989-b6-factorial n)
            (expt subdivisions n))
         (putnam-1989-b6-simplex-grid-sum
          function-coefficients
          (expt subdivisions n)
          n subdivisions))
    0))

;; Exact integral of t^degree times the polynomial.
(defun putnam-1989-b6-shifted-integral
    (coefficients degree)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (+ (/ (car coefficients) (+ degree 1))
         (putnam-1989-b6-shifted-integral
          (cdr coefficients) (+ degree 1)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1989-b6-product-integral-aux
    (function-coefficients witness-coefficients degree)
  (if (consp function-coefficients)
      (+ (* (car function-coefficients)
            (putnam-1989-b6-shifted-integral
             witness-coefficients degree))
         (putnam-1989-b6-product-integral-aux
          (cdr function-coefficients)
          witness-coefficients
          (+ degree 1)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1989-b6-product-integral
    (function-coefficients witness-coefficients)
  (putnam-1989-b6-product-integral-aux
   function-coefficients
   witness-coefficients
   0))

;; The simplex indicator is discontinuous only on finitely many hyperplanes,
;; so these midpoint sums converge to the normalized simplex integral.
(defun-sk putnam-1989-b6-expectation-tail-p
    (n function-coefficients witness-coefficients
       epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (subdivisions)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp subdivisions)
      (<= cutoff subdivisions))
     (< (abs
         (- (putnam-1989-b6-expected-sum-approx
             function-coefficients n subdivisions)
            (putnam-1989-b6-product-integral
             function-coefficients
             witness-coefficients)))
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b6-cutoff-exists-p
    (n function-coefficients witness-coefficients epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (posp cutoff)
     (putnam-1989-b6-expectation-tail-p
      n function-coefficients witness-coefficients
      epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnam-1989-b6-witness-bounds-p
    (witness-coefficients)
  (forall (t-value)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp t-value)
      (<= 0 t-value)
      (<= t-value 1))
     (let ((value
            (putnam-1989-b6-polynomial-value
             witness-coefficients t-value)))
       (and
        (<= 0 value)
        (<= value 1))))))

;; Rational polynomials vanishing at 1 are uniformly dense in the source
;; continuous function space. Both sides are bounded linear functionals in
;; the uniform norm, so equality on this test class is equivalent to equality
;; for every source function.
(defun-sk putnam-1989-b6-witness-equality-p
    (n witness-coefficients)
  (forall (function-coefficients epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1989-b6-rational-polynomial-p
       function-coefficients)
      (equal
       (putnam-1989-b6-polynomial-value
        function-coefficients 1)
       0)
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-1989-b6-cutoff-exists-p
      n function-coefficients witness-coefficients
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-1989-b6-statement (n)
  (exists (witness-coefficients)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (< 0 n))
     (and
      (putnam-1989-b6-degree-n-p
       witness-coefficients n)
      (putnam-1989-b6-witness-bounds-p
       witness-coefficients)
      (putnam-1989-b6-witness-equality-p
       n witness-coefficients)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1989_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1989_b6:
-- the expected right-endpoint Riemann sum over the ordered unit simplex is a
-- unit-interval integral against a bounded polynomial of degree n. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1989B6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

Between :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
Between reals lower upper x =
  lessOrEqual reals lower x
  and
  lessOrEqual reals x upper

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ContinuousOn :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
ContinuousOn {R} reals lower upper function =
  (x : R) ->
  Between reals lower upper x ->
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((y : R) ->
        Between reals lower upper y ->
        CloseTo reals x delta y ->
        CloseTo reals (function x) epsilon (function y)))

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

midpointRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
midpointRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
    halfStep =
      divide reals
        step
        (fromNat reals twoN)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (add reals
              (multiply reals
                (fromNat reals i)
                step)
              halfStep)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function value =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      midpointRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

Vector : Set -> Nat -> Set
Vector A n =
  Fin n -> A

emptyVector :
  {A : Set} ->
  Vector A zero
emptyVector ()

castSucc :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin (suc n)
castSucc fzero =
  fzero
castSucc (fsuc i) =
  fsuc (castSucc i)

snoc :
  {A : Set} ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Vector A n ->
  A ->
  Vector A (suc n)
snoc {n = zero} vector last fzero =
  last
snoc {n = suc n} vector last fzero =
  vector fzero
snoc {n = suc n} vector last (fsuc i) =
  snoc
    (\ j -> vector (fsuc j))
    last
    i

extendedCoordinate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Vector R n ->
  Fin (suc (suc n)) ->
  R
extendedCoordinate reals {zero} vector fzero =
  zeroR reals
extendedCoordinate reals {zero} vector (fsuc fzero) =
  oneR reals
extendedCoordinate reals {suc n} vector fzero =
  zeroR reals
extendedCoordinate reals {suc n} vector (fsuc fzero) =
  vector fzero
extendedCoordinate reals {suc n} vector (fsuc (fsuc i)) =
  extendedCoordinate reals
    (\ j -> vector (fsuc j))
    (fsuc i)

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} terms =
  add reals
    (terms fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> terms (fsuc i)))

rightEndpointSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Vector R n ->
  R
rightEndpointSum reals {n} function point =
  sumFin reals
    (\ i ->
      let
        leftEndpoint =
          extendedCoordinate reals point (castSucc i)
        rightEndpoint =
          extendedCoordinate reals point (fsuc i)
      in
      multiply reals
        (subtract reals rightEndpoint leftEndpoint)
        (function rightEndpoint))

data OrderedSimplexIntegralValue
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  {n : Nat} ->
  R ->
  (Vector R n -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set where

  zero-dimensional :
    {upper : R} ->
    {function : Vector R zero -> R} ->
    {value : R} ->
    function emptyVector == value ->
    OrderedSimplexIntegralValue reals
      upper function value

  successor-dimensional :
    {n : Nat} ->
    {upper : R} ->
    {function : Vector R (suc n) -> R} ->
    {value : R} ->
    (innerValues : R -> R) ->
    ((t : R) ->
      Between reals (zeroR reals) upper t ->
      OrderedSimplexIntegralValue reals
        t
        (\ point -> function (snoc point t))
        (innerValues t)) ->
    IntervalIntegralValue reals
      (zeroR reals)
      upper
      innerValues
      value ->
    OrderedSimplexIntegralValue reals
      upper function value

record Polynomial (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor polynomial
  field
    coefficient : Nat -> R
    cutoff : Nat

open Polynomial

PolynomialRepresentation :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Set
PolynomialRepresentation reals P =
  (k : Nat) ->
  cutoff P <N k ->
  coefficient P k == zeroR reals

HasDegree :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Nat ->
  Set
HasDegree reals P n =
  coefficient P n != zeroR reals
  and
  ((k : Nat) ->
    n <N k ->
    coefficient P k == zeroR reals)

evaluatePolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  R ->
  R
evaluatePolynomial reals P x =
  sumFirst reals
    (suc (cutoff P))
    (\ k ->
      multiply reals
        (coefficient P k)
        (naturalPower reals x k))

BoundedOnUnitInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Set
BoundedOnUnitInterval {R} reals P =
  (t : R) ->
  Between reals (zeroR reals) (oneR reals) t ->
  Between reals
    (zeroR reals)
    (oneR reals)
    (evaluatePolynomial reals P t)

module Putnam1989B6Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (n : Nat) where

  constantOne :
    Vector R n ->
    R
  constantOne _ =
    oneR reals

  weightedIntegrand :
    (R -> R) ->
    Polynomial R ->
    R ->
    R
  weightedIntegrand function P t =
    multiply reals
      (function t)
      (evaluatePolynomial reals P t)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    n != zero ->
    Exists (Polynomial R)
      (\ P ->
        PolynomialRepresentation reals P
        and
        (HasDegree reals P n
        and
        (BoundedOnUnitInterval reals P
        and
        Exists R
          (\ simplexVolume ->
            OrderedSimplexIntegralValue reals
              (oneR reals)
              constantOne
              simplexVolume
            and
            ((function : R -> R) ->
              function (oneR reals) == zeroR reals ->
              ContinuousOn reals
                (zeroR reals)
                (oneR reals)
                function ->
              Exists R
                (\ sumIntegral ->
                  OrderedSimplexIntegralValue reals
                    (oneR reals)
                    (rightEndpointSum reals {n = n} function)
                    sumIntegral
                  and
                  Exists R
                    (\ weightedIntegral ->
                      IntervalIntegralValue reals
                        (zeroR reals)
                        (oneR reals)
                        (weightedIntegrand function P)
                        weightedIntegral
                      and
                      divide reals
                        sumIntegral
                        simplexVolume
                      == weightedIntegral)))))))

putnam-1989-b6 : Set1
putnam-1989-b6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  Putnam1989B6Statement.proposition reals n

title: putnam_1989_b6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1989_b6:
  the expected right-endpoint Riemann sum over the ordered unit simplex is
  represented by integration against a bounded degree-n polynomial.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory pred_setTheory fcpTheory realTheory;
open real_sigmaTheory real_topologyTheory integrationTheory polyTheory;

val putnam_1989_b6 =
  ``let xrepl =
      \x : real['N].
      \i : num.
      \t : real.
        FCP k. if k = i then t else x ' k
    in
    let cube_integral =
      \n : num.
      \g : real['N] -> real.
        FOLDL
          (\J : (real['N] -> real) -> real.
           \i : num.
           \h : real['N] -> real.
             integration$integral (interval [0, 1])
               (\t : real.
                  J (\x : real['N]. h (xrepl x i t))))
          (\h : real['N] -> real. h (FCP i. 0))
          (GENLIST (\i : num. i) n)
          g
    in
    let ordered =
      \n : num.
      \x : real['N].
        (!i : num.
           i < n ==> 0 < x ' i /\ x ' i < 1) /\
        (!i : num.
           SUC i < n ==> x ' i < x ' (SUC i))
    in
    let xext =
      \n : num.
      \x : real['N].
      \i : num.
        if i = 0 then 0
        else if i = n + 1 then 1
        else x ' (i - 1)
    in
    let rsum =
      \n : num.
      \f : real -> real.
      \x : real['N].
        SIGMA
          (\i : num.
             (xext n x (i + 1) - xext n x i) *
             f (xext n x (i + 1)))
          (count (n + 1))
    in
      !n : num.
        0 < n /\
        dimindex (:'N) = n
        ==>
        ?P : real list.
          degree P = n /\
          (!t : real.
             t IN interval [0, 1]
             ==>
             0 <= poly P t /\ poly P t <= 1) /\
          !f : real -> real.
            f continuous_on interval [0, 1] /\
            f 1 = 0
            ==>
            cube_integral n
              (\x : real['N].
                 if ordered n x then rsum n f x else 0) /
              cube_integral n
                (\x : real['N].
                   if ordered n x then 1 else 0) =
            integration$integral (interval [0, 1])
              (\t : real. f t * poly P t)``;

title: putnam_1989_b6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1989_b6: the expected right-endpoint Riemann sum over uniformly
  ordered points in the unit interval is represented by integration against
  a degree-n polynomial bounded between zero and one. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P89B6Index(n) is {1,...,n}, and P89B6Region(n) is the full open region of
  strictly increasing real coordinate functions on that index set.
  P89B6Ext(X,n) extends X by x_0 = 0 and x_(n+1) = 1.

  P89B6Integrand(F,n) is the source right-endpoint Riemann sum on the ordered
  region and zero off that region. Its Bochner integral against voln divided
  by the volume of the region is therefore exactly the source uniform
  expectation. Poly, deg, and function application are set.mm's native real
  polynomial representation, exact degree, and evaluation.

  The polynomial witness is quantified before F, so it is independent of
  the continuous function. Every declaration is an unproved $a statement;
  this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P89B6Index P89B6Region P89B6Ext P89B6Sum $.
$c P89B6Integrand P89B6Expectation $.

p89b6-index-syntax $a class ( P89B6Index n ) $.
p89b6-region-syntax $a class ( P89B6Region n ) $.
p89b6-ext-syntax $a class ( P89B6Ext X n ) $.
p89b6-sum-syntax $a class ( P89B6Sum F X n ) $.
p89b6-integrand-syntax $a class ( P89B6Integrand F n ) $.
p89b6-expectation-syntax $a class ( P89B6Expectation F n ) $.

p89b6-index-definition $a |- (
  P89B6Index n
) = (
  1 ... n
) $.

${
  $d X i j n $.

  p89b6-region-definition $a |- (
    P89B6Region n
  ) = {
    X e. ( RR ^m ( P89B6Index n ) ) |
      (
        A. i e. ( P89B6Index n )
          (
            0 < ( X ` i )
            /\
            ( X ` i ) < 1
          )
        /\
        A. i e. ( P89B6Index n )
          A. j e. ( P89B6Index n )
            (
              i < j
              ->
              ( X ` i ) < ( X ` j )
            )
      )
  } $.
$}

${
  $d X i n $.

  p89b6-ext-definition $a |- (
    P89B6Ext X n
  ) = (
    i e. ( 0 ... ( n + 1 ) ) |->
      if (
        i = 0 ,
        0 ,
        if (
          i = ( n + 1 ) ,
          1 ,
          ( X ` i )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d F X i n $.

  p89b6-sum-definition $a |- (
    P89B6Sum F X n
  ) = (
    sum_ i e. ( 0 ... n )
      (
        (
          (
            ( P89B6Ext X n )
            `
            ( i + 1 )
          )
          -
          (
            ( P89B6Ext X n )
            `
            i
          )
        )
        x.
        (
          F
          `
          (
            ( P89B6Ext X n )
            `
            ( i + 1 )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d F X n $.

  p89b6-integrand-definition $a |- (
    P89B6Integrand F n
  ) = (
    X e. ( RR ^m ( P89B6Index n ) ) |->
      if (
        X e. ( P89B6Region n ) ,
        ( P89B6Sum F X n ) ,
        0
      )
  ) $.
$}

p89b6-expectation-definition $a |- (
  P89B6Expectation F n
) = (
  (
    (
      RRfld
      itgm
      ( voln ` ( P89B6Index n ) )
    )
    `
    ( P89B6Integrand F n )
  )
  /
  (
    ( voln ` ( P89B6Index n ) )
    `
    ( P89B6Region n )
  )
) $.

${
  $d F P n t $.

  putnambench-putnam-1989-b6 $a |-
    A. n e. NN
      E. P e. ( Poly ` RR )
        (
          ( deg ` P ) = n
          /\
          (
            A. t e. ( 0 [,] 1 )
              (
                0 <_ ( P ` t )
                /\
                ( P ` t ) <_ 1
              )
            /\
            A. F e. ( RR ^m RR )
              (
                (
                  ( F ` 1 ) = 0
                  /\
                  (
                    ( F |` ( 0 [,] 1 ) )
                    e.
                    ( ( 0 [,] 1 ) -cn-> RR )
                  )
                )
                ->
                (
                  P89B6Expectation F n
                )
                =
                S. ( 0 [,] 1 )
                  (
                    ( F ` t )
                    x.
                    ( P ` t )
                  )
                  _d t
              )
          )
        )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1989_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1989_b6:
% the expected right-endpoint Riemann sum for uniformly distributed ordered
% points in (0,1) is integration against a bounded degree-n polynomial
% independent of the continuous function. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1989_b6[n: posnat]: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [below(n) -> real]
  point_function: TYPE = [point -> real]
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  polynomial: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  quotient_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      0
    ELSE
      1
        + quotient_aux(
            numerator - denominator,
            denominator,
            fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  remainder_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      numerator
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator - denominator,
        denominator,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  safe_ndiv(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    quotient_aux(
      numerator,
      denominator,
      numerator + 1)

  safe_mod(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator,
        denominator,
        numerator + 1)
    ENDIF

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  continuous_on_unit_interval(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      (0 <= x AND x <= 1) IMPLIES
        FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
          EXISTS (delta: posreal):
            FORALL (y: real):
              (0 <= y
                AND y <= 1
                AND abs(y - x) < delta)
              IMPLIES
                abs(f(y) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  ordered_simplex(x: point): bool =
    (FORALL (index: below(n)):
      0 < x(index) AND x(index) < 1)
      AND (FORALL (left, right: below(n)):
        left < right IMPLIES x(left) < x(right))

  extended_coordinate(x: point, index: nat): real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSIF index = n + 1 THEN
      1
    ELSIF index <= n THEN
      x(index - 1)
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  right_endpoint_sum(
      f: real_function,
      x: point,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      right_endpoint_sum(f, x, count - 1)
        + (extended_coordinate(x, count)
            - extended_coordinate(x, count - 1))
          * f(extended_coordinate(x, count))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  grid_coordinate(
      code: nat,
      index: below(n),
      mesh: nat): real =
    IF mesh = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      ((safe_mod(
          safe_ndiv(code, mesh ^ index), mesh) + 1) :: real)
        / (mesh :: real)
    ENDIF

  grid_point(code, mesh: nat): point =
    LAMBDA (index: below(n)):
      grid_coordinate(code, index, mesh)

  finite_simplex_grid_sum(
      function_value: point_function,
      mesh, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET sample: point = grid_point(count - 1, mesh) IN
        finite_simplex_grid_sum(
          function_value, mesh, count - 1)
          + IF ordered_simplex(sample) THEN
              function_value(sample)
            ELSE
              0
            ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  simplex_grid_integral(
      function_value: point_function,
      mesh: nat): real =
    IF mesh = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      safe_div(
        finite_simplex_grid_sum(
          function_value, mesh, mesh ^ n),
        (mesh ^ n) :: real)
    ENDIF

  has_simplex_integral(
      function_value: point_function,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (mesh: nat):
        simplex_grid_integral(function_value, mesh),
      integral_value)

  simplex_integral(function_value: point_function): real =
    IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
        has_simplex_integral(function_value, integral_value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
          has_simplex_integral(
            function_value, integral_value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  finite_unit_grid_sum(
      function_value: real_function,
      mesh, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      finite_unit_grid_sum(
        function_value, mesh, count - 1)
        + function_value(
            safe_div(count :: real, mesh :: real))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  unit_grid_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      mesh: nat): real =
    IF mesh = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      safe_div(
        finite_unit_grid_sum(
          function_value, mesh, mesh),
        mesh :: real)
    ENDIF

  has_unit_interval_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (mesh: nat):
        unit_grid_integral(function_value, mesh),
      integral_value)

  unit_interval_integral(function_value: real_function): real =
    IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
        has_unit_interval_integral(
          function_value, integral_value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
          has_unit_interval_integral(
            function_value, integral_value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  polynomial_partial_value(
      coefficients: polynomial,
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET degree: nat = count - 1 IN
        polynomial_partial_value(
          coefficients, x, count - 1)
          + coefficients(degree) * x ^ degree
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_exact_degree(
      coefficients: polynomial,
      degree: nat): bool =
    coefficients(degree) /= 0
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        degree < index IMPLIES coefficients(index) = 0

  polynomial_value(
      coefficients: polynomial,
      x: real,
      degree: nat): real =
    polynomial_partial_value(coefficients, x, degree + 1)

  expected_right_endpoint_sum(f: real_function): real =
    safe_div(
      simplex_integral(
        LAMBDA (x: point):
          right_endpoint_sum(f, x, n + 1)),
      simplex_integral(
        LAMBDA (x: point): 1))

  putnam_1989_b6: bool =
    EXISTS (P: polynomial):
      has_exact_degree(P, n)
        AND (FORALL (t: real):
          (0 <= t AND t <= 1) IMPLIES
            (0 <= polynomial_value(P, t, n)
              AND polynomial_value(P, t, n) <= 1))
        AND (FORALL (f: real_function):
          (continuous_on_unit_interval(f) AND f(1) = 0)
          IMPLIES
            expected_right_endpoint_sum(f)
              = unit_interval_integral(
                  LAMBDA (t: real):
                    f(t) * polynomial_value(P, t, n)))
END putnam_1989_b6

title: putnam_1990_a1

import Mathlib

open Filter Topology Nat

abbrev putnam_1990_a1_solution : (ℕ → ℤ) × (ℕ → ℤ) := sorry
-- (fun n : ℕ => (n)!, fun n : ℕ => 2 ^ n)
/--
Let $T_0=2,T_1=3,T_2=6$, and for $n \geq 3$, $T_n=(n+4)T_{n-1}-4nT_{n-2}+(4n-8)T_{n-3}$. The first few terms are $2,3,6,14,40,152,784,5168,40576$. Find, with proof, a formula for $T_n$ of the form $T_n=A_n+B_n$, where $\{A_n\}$ and $\{B_n\}$ are well-known sequences.
-/
theorem putnam_1990_a1
    (T : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hT012 : T 0 = 2 ∧ T 1 = 3 ∧ T 2 = 6)
    (hTn : ∀ n, T (n + 3) = (n + 7) * T (n + 2) - 4 * (n + 3) * T (n + 1) + (4 * n + 4) * T n) :
    T = putnam_1990_a1_solution.1 + putnam_1990_a1_solution.2 :=
  sorry

title: putnam_1990_a1
content:
Require Import Nat Factorial Coquelicot.Coquelicot.
Definition putnam_1990_a1_solution := (fun n => fact n, fun n => pow 2 n).
Theorem putnam_1990_a1
    (A := fix a (n: nat) : nat :=
        match n with
        | O => 2
        | S O => 3
        | S (S O) => 6
        | S (S (S n''' as n'') as n') => (n + 4) * a n' - 4 * n * a n'' + (4 * n - 8) * a n'''
    end)
    : let (b,c) := putnam_1990_a1_solution in forall (n: nat), A n = b n + c n.
Proof. Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_a1:
;; the integer sequence with initial values 2, 3, 6 and the given third-order
;; recurrence has closed form n! + 2^n. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-1990-a1-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n
       (putnam-1990-a1-factorial (- n 1)))))

;; The source assumptions uniquely determine T at every natural index.

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_a1:
-- the integer sequence with the specified third-order recurrence equals
-- n factorial plus 2 to the nth power. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

subtractInt : Int -> Int -> Int
subtractInt x y =
  addInt x (negateInt y)

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  1
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

twoPower : Nat -> Nat
twoPower zero =
  1
twoPower (suc n) =
  2 * twoPower n

closedForm : Nat -> Int
closedForm n =
  addInt
    (pos (factorial n))
    (pos (twoPower n))

record InitialValues (T : Nat -> Int) : Set where
  field
    value-zero : T 0 == pos 2
    value-one  : T 1 == pos 3
    value-two  : T 2 == pos 6

recurrenceRightHandSide :
  (Nat -> Int) ->
  Nat ->
  Int
recurrenceRightHandSide T n =
  addInt
    (subtractInt
      (multiplyInt
        (pos (n + 7))
        (T (n + 2)))
      (multiplyInt
        (multiplyInt
          (pos 4)
          (pos (n + 3)))
        (T (n + 1))))
    (multiplyInt
      (pos (4 * n + 4))
      (T n))

Recurrence : (Nat -> Int) -> Set
Recurrence T =
  (n : Nat) ->
  T (n + 3) == recurrenceRightHandSide T n

putnam-1990-a1 : Set
putnam-1990-a1 =
  (T : Nat -> Int) ->
  InitialValues T ->
  Recurrence T ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  T n == closedForm n

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1990_a1: the integer sequence with initial values 2, 3, and 6 and
  the specified third-order recurrence equals n factorial plus 2 to the n
  for every nonnegative integer n. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  ZZ ^m NN0 is set.mm's class of all integer-valued sequences indexed by
  the nonnegative integers. The recurrence is shifted from indices n >= 3
  to n + 3 for n in NN0, exactly as in the Lean ground truth, so no truncated
  subtraction is introduced. Set.mm's ! and ^ are factorial and natural
  exponentiation.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d T n $.

  putnambench-putnam-1990-a1 $a |- A. T e. ( ZZ ^m NN0 )
    (
      (
        (
          ( T ` 0 ) = 2
          /\
          (
            ( T ` 1 ) = 3
            /\
            ( T ` 2 ) = 6
          )
        )
        /\
        A. n e. NN0
          ( T ` ( n + 3 ) )
          =
          (
            (
              ( ( n + 7 ) x. ( T ` ( n + 2 ) ) )
              -
              ( ( 4 x. ( n + 3 ) ) x. ( T ` ( n + 1 ) ) )
            )
            +
            ( ( ( 4 x. n ) + 4 ) x. ( T ` n ) )
          )
      )
      ->
      A. n e. NN0
        ( T ` n )
        =
        (
          ( ! ` n )
          +
          ( 2 ^ n )
        )
    )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_a1:
% the integer sequence with the stated third-order recurrence has closed form
% n! + 2^n. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1990_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> int]

  nat_factorial(n: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      n * nat_factorial(n - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  putnam_1990_a1: bool =
    FORALL (T: integer_sequence):
      (T(0) = 2
        AND T(1) = 3
        AND T(2) = 6
        AND (FORALL (n: nat):
          T(n + 3) =
            ((n :: int) + 7) * T(n + 2)
              - 4 * ((n :: int) + 3) * T(n + 1)
              + (4 * (n :: int) + 4) * T(n)))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (n: nat):
          T(n) =
            (nat_factorial(n) :: int) + (2 :: int) ^ n
END putnam_1990_a1

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_a2:
;; existence of a sequence of differences of nonnegative integer cube roots
;; converging to the real number sqrt(2). This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A real number lies in the closure of the set of cube-root differences
;; exactly when every positive rational epsilon contains such a difference.
;; From a convergent source sequence this follows by taking a sufficiently
;; late term. Conversely, choosing a term within 1/(k+1) for each k gives the
;; source sequence. Thus this closure formulation preserves the source's
;; internal existential sequence without exposing it as a statement argument.
;;
;; The existential witness consists of n, m, a positive rational precision,
;; and rational lower brackets for cube-root(n), cube-root(m), and sqrt(2).
;; Each root lies within 1/precision of its bracket. Monotonicity of square
;; and cube on the nonnegative reals then bounds the combined error by
;; 3/precision.
(defun putnam-1990-a2-approximation-witness-p
    (epsilon n m precision n-root m-root two-root)
  (let* ((delta (/ precision))
         (n-root-upper (+ n-root delta))
         (m-root-upper (+ m-root delta))
         (two-root-upper (+ two-root delta)))
    (and
     (natp n)
     (natp m)
     (posp precision)
     (rationalp n-root)
     (<= 0 n-root)
     (rationalp m-root)
     (<= 0 m-root)
     (rationalp two-root)
     (<= 0 two-root)
     (<= (expt n-root 3) n)
     (< n (expt n-root-upper 3))
     (<= (expt m-root 3) m)
     (< m (expt m-root-upper 3))
     (<= (expt two-root 2) 2)
     (< 2 (expt two-root-upper 2))
     (< (+ (abs (- (- n-root m-root) two-root))
           (* 3 delta))
        epsilon))))

;; DEFUN-SK supplies the source-level existential witnesses internally; the
;; statement predicate exposes only the universally quantified tolerance.
(defun-sk putnam-1990-a2-approximation-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (n m precision n-root m-root two-root)
    (putnam-1990-a2-approximation-witness-p
     epsilon n m precision n-root m-root two-root)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1990-a2-statement (epsilon)
  (implies
   (and (rationalp epsilon)
        (< 0 epsilon))
   (putnam-1990-a2-approximation-exists-p epsilon)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_a2:
-- sqrt(2) is the limit of a real sequence whose terms are differences of
-- cube roots of nonnegative integers. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

cube :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
cube reals x =
  multiply reals x (multiply reals x x)

record StandardSquareAndCubeRoots
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    squareRoot cubeRoot : R -> R

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (squareRoot x)

    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      square reals (squareRoot x) == x

    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) y ->
      square reals y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

    cube-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (cubeRoot x)

    cube-root-cube :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      cube reals (cubeRoot x) == x

    cube-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) y ->
      cube reals y == x ->
      y == cubeRoot x

open StandardSquareAndCubeRoots

NumForm :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardSquareAndCubeRoots reals ->
  R ->
  Set
NumForm reals roots x =
  Exists Nat
    (\ n ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ m ->
          x ==
          subtract reals
            (cubeRoot roots (fromNat reals n))
            (cubeRoot roots (fromNat reals m))))

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

putnam-1990-a2 : Set1
putnam-1990-a2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (roots : StandardSquareAndCubeRoots reals) ->
  Exists (Nat -> R)
    (\ sequence ->
      ((i : Nat) ->
        NumForm reals roots (sequence i))
      and
      ConvergesTo reals
        sequence
        (squareRoot roots (fromNat reals twoN)))

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_a2:
% sqrt(2) is the limit of a sequence whose terms are differences of cube roots
% of nonnegative integers. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1990_a2: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  cube_root_value(root: real, radicand: nat): bool =
    root >= 0 AND root ^ 3 = (radicand :: real)

  square_root_value(root, radicand: real): bool =
    root >= 0 AND root ^ 2 = radicand

  numform(x: real): bool =
    EXISTS (n, m: nat), (n_root, m_root: real):
      cube_root_value(n_root, n)
        AND cube_root_value(m_root, m)
        AND x = n_root - m_root

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  putnam_1990_a2_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_1990_a2: bool =
    (EXISTS (sqrt_two: real), (sequence: real_sequence):
      square_root_value(sqrt_two, 2)
        AND (FORALL (index: nat): numform(sequence(index)))
        AND converges_to(sequence, sqrt_two))
      IFF putnam_1990_a2_solution
END putnam_1990_a2

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_a5:
-- the assertion that ABAB = 0 implies BABA = 0 for all positive-size square
-- real matrices is false. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 1 _iff_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

Matrix :
  Set ->
  Nat ->
  Set
Matrix R n =
  Fin n -> Fin n -> R

MatrixEqual :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Set
MatrixEqual {n = n} A B =
  (i j : Fin n) ->
  A i j == B i j

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

zeroMatrix :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n
zeroMatrix reals i j =
  zeroR reals

matrixMultiply :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n
matrixMultiply reals A B i j =
  sumFin reals
    (\ k -> multiply reals (A i k) (B k j))

fourfoldProduct :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n
fourfoldProduct reals A B =
  matrixMultiply reals
    (matrixMultiply reals
      (matrixMultiply reals A B)
      A)
    B

UniversalImplication :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Set
UniversalImplication {R} reals =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  (A B : Matrix R n) ->
  MatrixEqual
    (fourfoldProduct reals A B)
    (zeroMatrix reals) ->
  MatrixEqual
    (fourfoldProduct reals B A)
    (zeroMatrix reals)

putnam-1990-a5-solution : Set
putnam-1990-a5-solution =
  Bottom

putnam-1990-a5 : Set1
putnam-1990-a5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  UniversalImplication reals iff putnam-1990-a5-solution

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_a5:
% the proposed implication from ABAB = 0 to BABA = 0 for positive-dimensional
% real square matrices is false. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1990_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  matrix(n: posnat): TYPE = [below(n), below(n) -> real]

  bounded_real_sum(
      n: posnat,
      values: [below(n) -> real],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      bounded_real_sum(n, values, count - 1)
        + IF count <= n THEN
            values(count - 1)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  zero_matrix(n: posnat): matrix(n) =
    LAMBDA (row, column: below(n)): 0

  matrix_multiply(n: posnat)(A, B: matrix(n)): matrix(n) =
    LAMBDA (row, column: below(n)):
      bounded_real_sum(
        n,
        LAMBDA (inner: below(n)):
          A(row, inner) * B(inner, column),
        n)

  putnam_1990_a5_solution: bool = FALSE

  putnam_1990_a5: bool =
    (FORALL (n: posnat), (A, B: matrix(n)):
      matrix_multiply(
        n)(
        matrix_multiply(
          n)(
          matrix_multiply(n)(A, B),
          A),
        B)
        = zero_matrix(n)
      IMPLIES
        matrix_multiply(
          n)(
          matrix_multiply(
            n)(
            matrix_multiply(n)(B, A),
            B),
          A)
          = zero_matrix(n))
      IFF putnam_1990_a5_solution
END putnam_1990_a5

abbrev putnam_1990_a6_solution : ℕ := sorry
-- 17711
/--
If $X$ is a finite set, let $|X|$ denote the number of elements in $X$. Call an ordered pair $(S,T)$ of subsets of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ \emph{admissible} if $s>|T|$ for each $s \in S$, and $t>|S|$ for each $t \in T$. How many admissible ordered pairs of subsets of $\{1,2,\dots,10\}$ are there? Prove your answer.
-/
theorem putnam_1990_a6 :
    ((Finset.univ : Finset <| Finset (Set.Icc 1 10) × Finset (Set.Icc 1 10)).filter
      fun ⟨S, T⟩ ↦ (∀ s ∈ S, T.card < s) ∧ (∀ t ∈ T, S.card < t)).card =
    putnam_1990_a6_solution :=

    (ST : {set 'I_10} * {set 'I_10}) : bool :=

  #|putnam_1990_a6_admissible_pairs| = putnam_1990_a6_solution.

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_a6:
;; exactly 17,711 ordered pairs of subsets of {1,...,10} are admissible when
;; every element of either subset exceeds the cardinality of the other.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A subset of {1,...,10} is represented by its 10-bit characteristic
;; number. Codes from 0 through 2^10 - 1 are therefore in bijection with all
;; source subsets, and the recursion through the ten bits gives the exact
;; subset cardinality.
(defun putnam-1990-a6-mask-member-p (element mask)
  (and
   (posp element)
   (<= element 10)
   (natp mask)
   (< mask (expt 2 10))
   (equal
    (mod (floor mask (expt 2 (- element 1))) 2)
    1)))

(defun putnam-1990-a6-cardinality-through
    (mask remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+
     (if (putnam-1990-a6-mask-member-p remaining mask)
         1
       0)
     (putnam-1990-a6-cardinality-through
      mask (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-1990-a6-members-exceed-p
    (mask other-cardinality remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (and
     (or
      (not (putnam-1990-a6-mask-member-p remaining mask))
      (< other-cardinality remaining))
     (putnam-1990-a6-members-exceed-p
      mask other-cardinality (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-1990-a6-admissible-p (s-code t-code)
  (and
   (natp s-code)
   (< s-code (expt 2 10))
   (natp t-code)
   (< t-code (expt 2 10))
   (let ((s-cardinality
          (putnam-1990-a6-cardinality-through s-code 10))
         (t-cardinality
          (putnam-1990-a6-cardinality-through t-code 10)))
     (and
      (putnam-1990-a6-members-exceed-p
       s-code t-cardinality 10)
      (putnam-1990-a6-members-exceed-p
       t-code s-cardinality 10)))))

(defun putnam-1990-a6-count-t-codes
    (s-code remaining-t-codes)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-t-codes)))
  (if (zp remaining-t-codes)
      0
    (let ((t-code (- remaining-t-codes 1)))
      (+
       (if (putnam-1990-a6-admissible-p s-code t-code)
           1
         0)
       (putnam-1990-a6-count-t-codes s-code t-code)))))

(defun putnam-1990-a6-count-s-codes
    (remaining-s-codes)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-s-codes)))
  (if (zp remaining-s-codes)
      0
    (let ((s-code (- remaining-s-codes 1)))
      (+
       (putnam-1990-a6-count-t-codes
        s-code (expt 2 10))
       (putnam-1990-a6-count-s-codes s-code)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1990-a6-statement ()
  (equal
   (putnam-1990-a6-count-s-codes (expt 2 10))
   17711))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- exactly 17711 ordered pairs of subsets of {1,...,10} are admissible, where
-- every element of either subset exceeds the size of the other subset.

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _<N_

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

data _<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<sucN : {n : Nat} -> zero <N suc n
  suc<sucN  : {m n : Nat} -> m <N n -> suc m <N suc n

one two three four five six seven eight nine ten : Nat
one =
  suc zero
two =
  suc one
three =
  suc two
four =
  suc three
five =
  suc four
six =
  suc five
seven =
  suc six
eight =
  suc seven
nine =
  suc eight
ten =
  suc nine

finToNat :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc index) =
  suc (finToNat index)

elementValue :
  Fin ten ->
  Nat
elementValue index =
  suc (finToNat index)

Subset : Set
Subset =
  Fin ten -> Bool

countTrue :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Bool) ->
  Nat
countTrue {zero} membership =
  zero
countTrue {suc n} membership with membership fzero
... | false =
  countTrue (\ index -> membership (fsuc index))
... | true =
  suc (countTrue (\ index -> membership (fsuc index)))

subsetCardinality :
  Subset ->
  Nat
subsetCardinality =
  countTrue

record OrderedPair : Set where
  constructor orderedPair
  field
    firstSubset  : Subset
    secondSubset : Subset

open OrderedPair

record Admissible (pair : OrderedPair) : Set where
  field
    first-elements-large :
      (index : Fin ten) ->
      firstSubset pair index == true ->
      subsetCardinality (secondSubset pair) <N elementValue index

    second-elements-large :
      (index : Fin ten) ->
      secondSubset pair index == true ->
      subsetCardinality (firstSubset pair) <N elementValue index

record AdmissibleOrderedPair : Set where
  constructor admissibleOrderedPair
  field
    pair          : OrderedPair
    admissibility : Admissible pair

open AdmissibleOrderedPair

record SameOrderedPair (left right : OrderedPair) : Set where
  field
    same-first-subset :
      (index : Fin ten) ->
      firstSubset left index == firstSubset right index

    same-second-subset :
      (index : Fin ten) ->
      secondSubset left index == secondSubset right index

SameAdmissibleOrderedPair :
  AdmissibleOrderedPair ->
  AdmissibleOrderedPair ->
  Set
SameAdmissibleOrderedPair left right =
  SameOrderedPair (pair left) (pair right)

record HasExtensionalCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (equivalent : A -> A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A

    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> equivalent item (enumerate index))

    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      equivalent (enumerate left-index) (enumerate right-index) ->
      left-index == right-index

putnam-1990-a6-solution : Nat
putnam-1990-a6-solution =
  17711

putnam-1990-a6 : Set
putnam-1990-a6 =
  HasExtensionalCardinality
    SameAdmissibleOrderedPair
    putnam-1990-a6-solution

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_a6:
% exactly 17711 ordered pairs of subsets of {1,...,10} satisfy the two
% cardinality bounds defining admissibility. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1990_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  subset_limit: posnat = 2 ^ 10
  ordered_pair_limit: nat = subset_limit ^ 2

  selected(subset_code, index: nat): bool =
    mod(ndiv(subset_code, 2 ^ index), 2) = 1

  count_below(limit: nat, property: [nat -> bool]): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_below(limit - 1, property)
        + IF property(limit - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  subset_cardinality(subset_code: nat): nat =
    count_below(
      10,
      LAMBDA (index: nat): selected(subset_code, index))

  admissible_pair(left_code, right_code: nat): bool =
    left_code < subset_limit
      AND right_code < subset_limit
      AND
        (FORALL (index: below(10)):
          selected(left_code, index)
            IMPLIES subset_cardinality(right_code) < index + 1)
      AND
        (FORALL (index: below(10)):
          selected(right_code, index)
            IMPLIES subset_cardinality(left_code) < index + 1)

  admissible_ordered_pair(pair_code: nat): bool =
    pair_code < ordered_pair_limit
      AND admissible_pair(
        mod(pair_code, subset_limit),
        ndiv(pair_code, subset_limit))

  putnam_1990_a6_solution: nat = 17711

  putnam_1990_a6: bool =
    count_below(
      ordered_pair_limit,
      admissible_ordered_pair)
      = putnam_1990_a6_solution
END putnam_1990_a6
