;; These conservative generic functions are arbitrary rational Cauchy names
;; for the source reals x, z, and P(j).  The hypotheses in the root predicate
;; explicitly require rational values and the regular Cauchy law.  Every real
;; has such a name, so this is an exact presentation of the real domain rather
;; than a restriction to rational values.

(defstub p90b2-x-approx (index) t)
(defstub p90b2-z-approx (index) t)
(defstub p90b2-p-approx (j index) t)

(defun p90b2-positive-rational-p (value)
  (and (rationalp value)
       (< 0 value)))

(defun p90b2-cauchy-radius (index)
  (/ 1 (+ 1 (nfix index))))

(defun-sk p90b2-x-rational-values-p ()
  (forall (index)
    (implies (natp index)
             (rationalp (p90b2-x-approx index)))))

(defun-sk p90b2-z-rational-values-p ()
  (forall (index)
    (implies (natp index)
             (rationalp (p90b2-z-approx index)))))

(defun-sk p90b2-p-rational-values-p ()
  (forall (j index)
    (implies (and (posp j)
                  (natp index))
             (rationalp (p90b2-p-approx j index)))))

(defun-sk p90b2-x-regular-cauchy-p ()
  (forall (left-index right-index)
    (implies
     (and (natp left-index)
          (natp right-index))
     (<=
      (abs
       (- (p90b2-x-approx left-index)
          (p90b2-x-approx right-index)))
      (+ (p90b2-cauchy-radius left-index)
         (p90b2-cauchy-radius right-index))))))

(defun-sk p90b2-z-regular-cauchy-p ()
  (forall (left-index right-index)
    (implies
     (and (natp left-index)
          (natp right-index))
     (<=
      (abs
       (- (p90b2-z-approx left-index)
          (p90b2-z-approx right-index)))
      (+ (p90b2-cauchy-radius left-index)
         (p90b2-cauchy-radius right-index))))))

(defun-sk p90b2-p-regular-cauchy-p ()
  (forall (j left-index right-index)
    (implies
     (and (posp j)
          (natp left-index)
          (natp right-index))
     (<=
      (abs
       (- (p90b2-p-approx j left-index)
          (p90b2-p-approx j right-index)))
      (+ (p90b2-cauchy-radius left-index)
         (p90b2-cauchy-radius right-index))))))

;; Strict inequalities between represented reals use an eventual rational
;; margin.  For regular Cauchy names these predicates are exactly |x| < 1 and
;; |z| > 1.

(defun-sk p90b2-x-inside-unit-tail-p (margin cutoff)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (and (natp index)
          (<= cutoff index))
     (< (abs (p90b2-x-approx index))
        (- 1 margin)))))

(defun-sk p90b2-x-inside-unit-p ()
  (exists (margin cutoff)
    (and (p90b2-positive-rational-p margin)
         (< margin 1)
         (natp cutoff)
         (p90b2-x-inside-unit-tail-p
          margin cutoff))))

(defun-sk p90b2-z-outside-unit-tail-p (margin cutoff)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (and (natp index)
          (<= cutoff index))
     (< (+ 1 margin)
        (abs (p90b2-z-approx index))))))

(defun-sk p90b2-z-outside-unit-p ()
  (exists (margin cutoff)
    (and (p90b2-positive-rational-p margin)
         (natp cutoff)
         (p90b2-z-outside-unit-tail-p
          margin cutoff))))

;; At each approximation index these are the source finite products
;;
;;   product_(i=0)^(j-1) (1-z*x^i)
;;   product_(i=1)^j     (z-x^i).
;;
;; Their quotient converges to the corresponding quotient of represented
;; reals.  The source bounds make its denominator nonzero in the real limit.

(defun p90b2-numerator-approx (j index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix j)))
  (if (zp j)
      1
    (let ((i (- j 1)))
      (*
       (p90b2-numerator-approx i index)
       (- 1
          (* (p90b2-z-approx index)
             (expt (p90b2-x-approx index) i)))))))

(defun p90b2-denominator-approx (j index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix j)))
  (if (zp j)
      1
    (*
     (p90b2-denominator-approx (- j 1) index)
     (- (p90b2-z-approx index)
        (expt (p90b2-x-approx index) j)))))

(defun p90b2-product-quotient-approx (j index)
  (/ (p90b2-numerator-approx j index)
     (p90b2-denominator-approx j index)))

;; Equality of two represented reals is equality of their limits.  Thus the
;; following unbounded epsilon-tail condition states P(j) equal to the exact
;; finite-product quotient for every source index j >= 1.

(defun-sk p90b2-p-formula-tail-p
    (j epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (and (natp index)
          (<= cutoff index))
     (<
      (abs
       (- (p90b2-p-approx j index)
          (p90b2-product-quotient-approx
           j index)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p90b2-p-formula-cutoff-exists-p
    (j epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and (natp cutoff)
         (p90b2-p-formula-tail-p
          j epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk p90b2-p-formula-at-j-p (j)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p90b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (p90b2-p-formula-cutoff-exists-p
      j epsilon))))

(defun-sk p90b2-p-formula-p ()
  (forall (j)
    (implies (posp j)
             (p90b2-p-formula-at-j-p j))))

;; This is the rational Cauchy approximation to
;;
;;   1 + sum_(j=1)^terms (1+x^j) P(j).
;;
;; No telescoping identity or convergence rate is assumed in its definition.

(defun p90b2-partial-sum-approx (terms index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      1
    (+
     (p90b2-partial-sum-approx
      (- terms 1) index)
     (*
      (+ 1
         (expt (p90b2-x-approx index)
               terms))
      (p90b2-p-approx terms index)))))

;; For a fixed number of terms, this predicate says that the exact represented
;; partial sum has absolute value below EPSILON.  The internal rational margin
;; is equivalent to strict real inequality and is not an approximation.

(defun-sk p90b2-partial-sum-below-tail-p
    (terms margin cutoff)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (and (natp index)
          (<= cutoff index))
     (< (abs
         (p90b2-partial-sum-approx
          terms index))
        margin))))

(defun-sk p90b2-partial-sum-below-p
    (terms epsilon)
  (exists (margin cutoff)
    (and (p90b2-positive-rational-p margin)
         (< margin epsilon)
         (natp cutoff)
         (p90b2-partial-sum-below-tail-p
          terms margin cutoff))))

;; The source infinite-sum conclusion is precisely the unbounded epsilon-N
;; assertion that these real partial sums tend to zero.

(defun-sk p90b2-series-tail-p (epsilon start)
  (forall (terms)
    (implies
     (and (natp terms)
          (<= start terms))
     (p90b2-partial-sum-below-p
      terms epsilon))))

(defun-sk p90b2-series-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (start)
    (and (natp start)
         (p90b2-series-tail-p
          epsilon start))))

(defun-sk p90b2-series-converges-to-zero-p ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p90b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (p90b2-series-cutoff-exists-p epsilon))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1990-b2-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (p90b2-x-rational-values-p)
    (p90b2-z-rational-values-p)
    (p90b2-p-rational-values-p)
    (p90b2-x-regular-cauchy-p)
    (p90b2-z-regular-cauchy-p)
    (p90b2-p-regular-cauchy-p)
    (p90b2-x-inside-unit-p)
    (p90b2-z-outside-unit-p)
    (p90b2-p-formula-p))
   (p90b2-series-converges-to-zero-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1990_b2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b2:
-- the finite-product coefficients P_j give a real series whose sum, after
-- adding one, is zero when |x| < 1 and |z| > 1. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

maximum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
maximum reals x y with order-total reals x y
... | left _ =
  y
... | right _ =
  x

absoluteValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
absoluteValue reals x =
  maximum reals x (negate reals x)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

productFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
productFirst reals zero factors =
  oneR reals
productFirst reals (suc n) factors =
  multiply reals
    (productFirst reals n factors)
    (factors n)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

module Putnam1990B2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (x z : R)
  (P : Nat -> R) where

  numerator : Nat -> R
  numerator j =
    productFirst reals j
      (\ i ->
        subtract reals
          (oneR reals)
          (multiply reals
            z
            (naturalPower reals x i)))

  denominator : Nat -> R
  denominator j =
    productFirst reals j
      (\ i ->
        subtract reals
          z
          (naturalPower reals x (suc i)))

  coefficientFormula : Set
  coefficientFormula =
    (j : Nat) ->
    oneN <=N j ->
    P j ==
    divide reals
      (numerator j)
      (denominator j)

  summand : Nat -> R
  summand i =
    multiply reals
      (add reals
        (oneR reals)
        (naturalPower reals x (suc i)))
      (P (suc i))

  partialExpression : Nat -> R
  partialExpression n =
    add reals
      (oneR reals)
      (sumFirst reals n summand)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    StrictLess reals
      (absoluteValue reals x)
      (oneR reals) ->
    StrictLess reals
      (oneR reals)
      (absoluteValue reals z) ->
    coefficientFormula ->
    ConvergesTo reals
      partialExpression
      (zeroR reals)

putnam-1990-b2 : Set1
putnam-1990-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (x z : R) ->
  (P : Nat -> R) ->
  Putnam1990B2Statement.proposition reals x z P

title: putnam_1990_b2
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b2:
  a real series built from the stated finite-product coefficients has sum
  negative one when |x| < 1 and |z| > 1. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;
open real_topologyTheory;

val putnam_1990_b2 =
  ``!x z : real. !P : num -> real.
      abs x < 1 /\
      1 < abs z /\
      (!j : num.
         1 <= j
         ==>
         P j =
           REAL_PROD_IMAGE
             (\i : num. 1 - z * x pow i)
             (count j) /
           REAL_PROD_IMAGE
             (\i : num. z - x pow i)
             (IMAGE SUC (count j)))
      ==>
      ((\n : num.
          1 +
          SIGMA
            (\j : num. (1 + x pow j) * P j)
            (IMAGE SUC (count n))) -->
        0)
      sequentially``;

title: putnam_1990_b2
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1990_b2: evaluation of an infinite real series whose terms use a
  quotient of two finite products, under absolute-value conditions on its
  two real parameters. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P ranges over all real-valued sequences indexed by NN0. For positive j,
  0 ..^ j is the half-open natural interval from 0 through j - 1, while
  1 ... j is the inclusive interval from 1 through j. Thus the defining
  hypothesis for P is exactly

    P_j = product_(0 <= i < j) (1 - z x^i)
          / product_(1 <= i <= j) (z - x^i).

  The sum over NN is set.mm's convergent infinite real-series sum, matching
  the direct infinite sums in the Lean and Isabelle sources and equivalently
  the limit of partial sums in the Rocq source. The final declaration is the
  single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

${
  $d P i j x z $.

  putnambench-putnam-1990-b2 $a |-
    A. x e. RR
      A. z e. RR
        A. P e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
          (
            (
              (
                ( abs ` x ) < 1
                /\
                1 < ( abs ` z )
              )
              /\
              A. j e. NN
                ( P ` j )
                =
                (
                  (
                    prod_ i e. ( 0 ..^ j )
                      ( 1 - ( z x. ( x ^ i ) ) )
                  )
                  /
                  (
                    prod_ i e. ( 1 ... j )
                      ( z - ( x ^ i ) )
                  )
                )
            )
            ->
            (
              1
              +
              sum_ j e. NN
                (
                  ( 1 + ( x ^ j ) )
                  x.
                  ( P ` j )
                )
            )
            =
            0
          )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1990_b2
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1990_b2:
:: for real x,z with |x| < 1 and |z| > 1, a series built from ratios of
:: specified finite products converges to -1. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    NUMBERS, XREAL_0, COMPLEX1, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3,
    REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, NEWTON, PREPOWER,
    SEQ_1, SEQ_2, ORDINAL2, XXREAL_2, SEQ_4, POWER, ABIAN, ORDINAL1,
    SERIES_1, RVSUM_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_4, FINSEQOP,
    ZFMISC_1, CARD_3, XCMPLX_0, SETWISEO, SETWOP_2, FINSOP_1,
    FUNCOP_1, BINOP_1, BINOP_2;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ZFMISC_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    REAL_1, INT_1, COMPLEX1, XXREAL_0, NEWTON, NAT_1, NAT_D, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_4, SEQ_1, SEQ_2, COMSEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4,
    PREPOWER, ABIAN, XXREAL_2, POWER, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, BINOP_1,
    BINOP_2, SETWISEO, FUNCOP_1, FINSOP_1, FINSEQOP, SETWOP_2,
    RVSUM_1, SERIES_1;
  constructors FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1, REAL_1, COMPLEX1,
    INT_1, XXREAL_0, NEWTON, NAT_1, NAT_D, SEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4, PREPOWER,
    ABIAN, BINOP_1, BINOP_2, COMSEQ_2, POWER, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_4,
    VALUED_1, FINSEQOP, FINSOP_1, SETWOP_2, RVSUM_1, SERIES_1,
    SETWISEO;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0, VALUED_1,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, NAT_1, INT_1, NEWTON, PREPOWER,
    SEQ_4, ABIAN, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_4, RVSUM_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for x,z being Real,
      P being Real_Sequence st
    |.x.| < 1 &
    |.z.| > 1 &
    (for j being Nat st 1 <= j holds
      ex a,b being FinSequence of REAL st
        len a = j &
        len b = j &
        (for k being Nat st k in Seg j holds
          a.k = 1 - z * (x |^ (k-'1)) &
          b.k = z - (x |^ k)) &
        P.j = (Product a) / (Product b))
  holds
    ex s being Real_Sequence st
      s.0 = 1 &
      (for j being Nat st 1 <= j holds
        s.j = (1 + x |^ j) * P.j) &
      Partial_Sums(s) is convergent &
      lim Partial_Sums(s) = 0
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1990_b2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b2:
% a finite-product quotient sequence yields an infinite real series summing
% to negative one when the two parameters satisfy the stated absolute-value
% bounds. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1990_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  numerator_product(x, z: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      numerator_product(x, z, count - 1)
        * (1 - z * x ^ (count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  denominator_product(x, z: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      denominator_product(x, z, count - 1)
        * (z - x ^ count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_product_quotients(
      x, z: real,
      P: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (j: nat):
      j >= 1 IMPLIES
        P(j) =
          safe_div(
            numerator_product(x, z, j),
            denominator_product(x, z, j))

  series_partial_sum(
      x: real,
      P: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      series_partial_sum(x, P, count - 1)
        + (1 + x ^ count) * P(count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to_zero(
      x: real,
      P: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(series_partial_sum(x, P, count))
              < epsilon_value

  putnam_1990_b2: bool =
    FORALL
        (x, z: real),
        (P: real_sequence):
      (abs(x) < 1
        AND abs(z) > 1
        AND has_product_quotients(x, z, P))
      IMPLIES converges_to_zero(x, P)
END putnam_1990_b2

title: putnam_1990_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b3:
;; a sufficiently large set of 2 by 2 natural-number matrices whose entries
;; are integer squares at most 200 contains two distinct commuting matrices.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Each admissible entry belongs to a finite set, so every source set S is
;; finite. A duplicate-free list is therefore an extensional enumeration of S,
;; and every such list determines a source set with the same cardinality.
;; The downward search is equivalent to the source existential square witness:
;; for natural X, any integer M satisfying M^2 = X yields the natural witness
;; |M| <= X, while every natural witness is also an integer witness.

(defun putnam-1990-b3-square-witness-down-p (x candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (zp candidate)
      (equal x 0)
    (or
     (equal x (* candidate candidate))
     (putnam-1990-b3-square-witness-down-p
      x (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-1990-b3-entry-p (x)
  (and
   (natp x)
   (<= x 200)
   (putnam-1990-b3-square-witness-down-p x x)))

;; A matrix is stored in row-major order as (a_00 a_01 a_10 a_11).

(defun putnam-1990-b3-matrix-p (matrix)
  (and
   (true-listp matrix)
   (equal (len matrix) 4)
   (putnam-1990-b3-entry-p (nth 0 matrix))
   (putnam-1990-b3-entry-p (nth 1 matrix))
   (putnam-1990-b3-entry-p (nth 2 matrix))
   (putnam-1990-b3-entry-p (nth 3 matrix))))

(defun putnam-1990-b3-matrix-set-p (matrices)
  (if (consp matrices)
      (and
       (putnam-1990-b3-matrix-p (car matrices))
       (not (member-equal (car matrices) (cdr matrices)))
       (putnam-1990-b3-matrix-set-p (cdr matrices)))
    (equal matrices nil)))

(defun putnam-1990-b3-matrix-multiply (left right)
  (let ((a (nth 0 left))
        (b (nth 1 left))
        (c (nth 2 left))
        (d (nth 3 left))
        (e (nth 0 right))
        (f (nth 1 right))
        (g (nth 2 right))
        (h (nth 3 right)))
    (list
     (+ (* a e) (* b g))
     (+ (* a f) (* b h))
     (+ (* c e) (* d g))
     (+ (* c f) (* d h)))))

(defun putnam-1990-b3-commute-p (left right)
  (equal
   (putnam-1990-b3-matrix-multiply left right)
   (putnam-1990-b3-matrix-multiply right left)))

;; These two searches are exactly the nested existential quantifiers over
;; distinct members A and B of S; no witnesses are external parameters.

(defun putnam-1990-b3-commutes-with-some-p (matrix matrices)
  (if (consp matrices)
      (or
       (and
        (not (equal matrix (car matrices)))
        (putnam-1990-b3-commute-p matrix (car matrices)))
       (putnam-1990-b3-commutes-with-some-p
        matrix (cdr matrices)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1990-b3-commuting-pair-exists-p (matrices)
  (if (consp matrices)
      (or
       (putnam-1990-b3-commutes-with-some-p
        (car matrices) (cdr matrices))
       (putnam-1990-b3-commuting-pair-exists-p
        (cdr matrices)))
    nil))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1990-b3-statement (matrices)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-1990-b3-matrix-set-p matrices)
    (< 50387 (len matrices)))
   (putnam-1990-b3-commuting-pair-exists-p matrices)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b3:
-- a sufficiently large set of 2 by 2 natural-number matrices with square
-- entries at most 200 contains two distinct commuting matrices. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not proposition =
  proposition -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record Matrix2 : Set where
  constructor matrix
  field
    entry00 : Nat
    entry01 : Nat
    entry10 : Nat
    entry11 : Nat

open Matrix2

MatrixEqual : Matrix2 -> Matrix2 -> Set
MatrixEqual A B =
  entry00 A == entry00 B
  and
  entry01 A == entry01 B
  and
  entry10 A == entry10 B
  and
  entry11 A == entry11 B

MatrixDistinct : Matrix2 -> Matrix2 -> Set
MatrixDistinct A B =
  Not (MatrixEqual A B)

matrixMultiply : Matrix2 -> Matrix2 -> Matrix2
matrixMultiply A B =
  matrix
    (entry00 A * entry00 B + entry01 A * entry10 B)
    (entry00 A * entry01 B + entry01 A * entry11 B)
    (entry10 A * entry00 B + entry11 A * entry10 B)
    (entry10 A * entry01 B + entry11 A * entry11 B)

SquareAtMost : Nat -> Set
SquareAtMost n =
  Exists Nat (\ root -> n == root * root)
  and
  n <=N 200

AdmissibleMatrix : Matrix2 -> Set
AdmissibleMatrix A =
  SquareAtMost (entry00 A)
  and
  SquareAtMost (entry01 A)
  and
  SquareAtMost (entry10 A)
  and
  SquareAtMost (entry11 A)

record HasMoreThan
  (member : Matrix2 -> Set)
  (lowerBound : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin (suc lowerBound) ->
      Matrix2
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin (suc lowerBound)) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin (suc lowerBound)) ->
      MatrixEqual (enumerate left-index) (enumerate right-index) ->
      left-index == right-index

CommutingDistinctMembers :
  (Matrix2 -> Set) ->
  Set
CommutingDistinctMembers member =
  Exists Matrix2
    (\ A ->
      member A
      and
      Exists Matrix2
        (\ B ->
          member B
          and
          MatrixDistinct A B
          and
          MatrixEqual
            (matrixMultiply A B)
            (matrixMultiply B A)))

putnam-1990-b3 : Set1
putnam-1990-b3 =
  (S : Matrix2 -> Set) ->
  ((A : Matrix2) ->
    S A ->
    AdmissibleMatrix A) ->
  HasMoreThan S 50387 ->
  CommutingDistinctMembers S

content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1990_b3:
% more than 50387 two-by-two natural matrices with square entries bounded by
% 200 contain two distinct matrices that commute. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1990_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  matrix: TYPE =
    [# entry_00: nat,
       entry_01: nat,
       entry_10: nat,
       entry_11: nat #]

  matrix_set: TYPE = [matrix -> bool]

  square_bounded(value: nat): bool =
    (EXISTS (root: nat): value = root ^ 2)
      AND value <= 200

  admissible_matrix(A: matrix): bool =
    square_bounded(entry_00(A))
      AND square_bounded(entry_01(A))
      AND square_bounded(entry_10(A))
      AND square_bounded(entry_11(A))

  matrix_multiply(A, B: matrix): matrix =
    (# entry_00 :=
         entry_00(A) * entry_00(B) + entry_01(A) * entry_10(B),
       entry_01 :=
         entry_00(A) * entry_01(B) + entry_01(A) * entry_11(B),
       entry_10 :=
         entry_10(A) * entry_00(B) + entry_11(A) * entry_10(B),
       entry_11 :=
         entry_10(A) * entry_01(B) + entry_11(A) * entry_11(B) #)

  has_more_than_50387_elements(S: matrix_set): bool =
    EXISTS (enumeration: [below(50388) -> matrix]):
      (FORALL (index: below(50388)): S(enumeration(index)))
        AND
          (FORALL (left, right: below(50388)):
            enumeration(left) = enumeration(right)
              IMPLIES left = right)

  putnam_1990_b3: bool =
    FORALL (S: matrix_set):
      (FORALL (A: matrix):
        S(A) IMPLIES admissible_matrix(A))
      IMPLIES
        has_more_than_50387_elements(S)
          IMPLIES
            EXISTS (A, B: matrix):
              S(A)
                AND S(B)
                AND A /= B
                AND matrix_multiply(A, B) = matrix_multiply(B, A)
END putnam_1990_b3

import Mathlib

open Filter Topology Nat

-- Note: uses (ℕ → G) instead of (Fin (2 * n) → G)
abbrev putnam_1990_b4_solution : Prop := True
/--
Let $G$ be a finite group of order $n$ generated by $a$ and $b$. Prove or disprove: there is a sequence $g_1,g_2,g_3,\dots,g_{2n}$ such that
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)] every element of $G$ occurs exactly twice, and
\item[(2)] $g_{i+1}$ equals $g_ia$ or $g_ib$ for $i=1,2,\dots,2n$. (Interpret $g_{2n+1}$ as $g_1$.)
\end{itemize}
-/
theorem putnam_1990_b4
: (∀ (G : Type*) (_ : Fintype G) (_ : Group G) (n : ℕ) (a b : G),
    (n = Fintype.card G ∧ Subgroup.closure {a, b} = ⊤ ∧
      Subgroup.closure {a} ≠ ⊤ ∧ Subgroup.closure {b} ≠ ⊤) →
    (∃ g : ℕ → G, (∀ x : G, {i : Fin (2 * n) | g i = x}.encard = 2)
  ∧ (∀ i : Fin (2 * n), (g ((i + 1) % (2 * n)) = g i * a) ∨ (g ((i + 1) % (2 * n)) = g i * b))) ↔ putnam_1990_b4_solution) :=
sorry

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1990_b4:
   a cyclic walk of length twice the order of a finite two-generated group,
   using right multiplication by either generator and visiting every element
   exactly twice. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Arith.PeanoNat.

Record putnam_1990_b4_group (G : Type) : Type := {
  putnam_1990_b4_mul : G -> G -> G;
  putnam_1990_b4_one : G;
  putnam_1990_b4_inv : G -> G;
  putnam_1990_b4_assoc :
    forall x y z : G,
      putnam_1990_b4_mul x (putnam_1990_b4_mul y z) =
      putnam_1990_b4_mul (putnam_1990_b4_mul x y) z;
  putnam_1990_b4_left_identity :
    forall x : G, putnam_1990_b4_mul putnam_1990_b4_one x = x;
  putnam_1990_b4_right_identity :
    forall x : G, putnam_1990_b4_mul x putnam_1990_b4_one = x;
  putnam_1990_b4_left_inverse :
    forall x : G,
      putnam_1990_b4_mul (putnam_1990_b4_inv x) x =
      putnam_1990_b4_one;
  putnam_1990_b4_right_inverse :
    forall x : G,
      putnam_1990_b4_mul x (putnam_1990_b4_inv x) =
      putnam_1990_b4_one
}.

Arguments putnam_1990_b4_mul {G} _ _ _.
Arguments putnam_1990_b4_one {G} _.
Arguments putnam_1990_b4_inv {G} _ _.

Inductive putnam_1990_b4_generated
    {G : Type}
    (grp : putnam_1990_b4_group G)
    (S : G -> Prop) : G -> Prop :=
  | putnam_1990_b4_generated_one :
      putnam_1990_b4_generated grp S (putnam_1990_b4_one grp)
  | putnam_1990_b4_generated_member :
      forall x : G,
        S x ->
        putnam_1990_b4_generated grp S x
  | putnam_1990_b4_generated_mul :
      forall x y : G,
        putnam_1990_b4_generated grp S x ->
        putnam_1990_b4_generated grp S y ->
        putnam_1990_b4_generated grp S
          (putnam_1990_b4_mul grp x y)
  | putnam_1990_b4_generated_inv :
      forall x : G,
        putnam_1990_b4_generated grp S x ->
        putnam_1990_b4_generated grp S
          (putnam_1990_b4_inv grp x).

Definition putnam_1990_b4_exactly_twice
    {G : Type}
    (n : nat)
    (g : nat -> G)
    (x : G) : Prop :=
  exists i j : nat,
    (i < 2 * n)%nat /\
    (j < 2 * n)%nat /\
    i <> j /\
    g i = x /\
    g j = x /\
    forall k : nat,
      (k < 2 * n)%nat ->
      g k = x ->
      k = i \/ k = j.

Definition putnam_1990_b4_solution : Prop := True.

Theorem putnam_1990_b4 :
  (forall
      (G : Type)
      (grp : putnam_1990_b4_group G)
      (enumeration : list G)
      (n : nat)
      (a b : G),
    NoDup enumeration ->
    (forall x : G, In x enumeration) ->
    n = length enumeration ->
    (forall x : G,
      putnam_1990_b4_generated grp (fun y => y = a \/ y = b) x) ->
    ~ (forall x : G,
      putnam_1990_b4_generated grp (fun y => y = a) x) ->
    ~ (forall x : G,
      putnam_1990_b4_generated grp (fun y => y = b) x) ->
    exists g : nat -> G,
      (forall x : G, putnam_1990_b4_exactly_twice n g x) /\
      forall i : nat,
        (i < 2 * n)%nat ->
        g ((S i) mod (2 * n)) = putnam_1990_b4_mul grp (g i) a \/
        g ((S i) mod (2 * n)) = putnam_1990_b4_mul grp (g i) b)
  <-> putnam_1990_b4_solution.
Admitted.

title: putnam_1990_b4
content:
theory putnam_1990_b4 imports Complex_Main "HOL-Algebra.Multiplicative_Group" 
begin

definition putnam_1990_b4_solution :: bool where
  "putnam_1990_b4_solution \<equiv> True"

theorem putnam_1990_b4:
  assumes pacard: "\<exists> pamap :: 'a \<Rightarrow> nat. surj pamap"
  shows "(\<forall> (G :: 'a monoid) (n :: nat) (a :: 'a) (b :: 'a). Group.group G \<and> finite (carrier G) \<and> card (carrier G) = n \<and> 
    a \<in> carrier G \<and> b \<in> carrier G \<and>
    (generate G {a, b} = carrier G \<and> generate G {a} \<noteq> carrier G \<and> generate G {b} \<noteq> carrier G) \<longrightarrow> 
    (\<exists>g::nat\<Rightarrow>'a. (\<forall>x \<in> carrier G. card {i::nat. i < 2 * n \<and> g i = x} = 2) \<and>
    (\<forall>i \<in> {0..<(2*n)}. (g ((i+1) mod (2*n)) = g i \<otimes>\<^bsub>G\<^esub> a) \<or> (g ((i+1) mod (2*n)) = g i \<otimes>\<^bsub>G\<^esub> b)))) \<longleftrightarrow> putnam_1990_b4_solution"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_1990_b4
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b4:
  a finite group generated by two elements, but by neither element alone,
  admits a cyclic sequence in which every group element occurs exactly twice
  and each step is right multiplication by one of the generators. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let putnam_1990_b4_solution = T in
   let is_group =
     \(mul:G->G->G) (identity:G) (ginv:G->G).
       (!x y z:G. mul (mul x y) z = mul x (mul y z)) /\
       (!x:G. mul identity x = x /\ mul x identity = x) /\
       (!x:G.
          mul (ginv x) x = identity /\ mul x (ginv x) = identity) in
   let is_subgroup =
     \(mul:G->G->G) (identity:G) (ginv:G->G) (H:G->bool).
       identity IN H /\
       (!x:G. x IN H ==> ginv x IN H) /\
       (!x y:G. x IN H /\ y IN H ==> mul x y IN H) in
   let generated_by =
     \(mul:G->G->G) (identity:G) (ginv:G->G) (S:G->bool).
       !H:G->bool.
         is_subgroup mul identity ginv H /\ S SUBSET H
         ==> H = (UNIV:G->bool) in
   ((!mul:G->G->G. !identity:G. !ginv:G->G. !n:num. !a b:G.
       FINITE (UNIV:G->bool) /\
       CARD (UNIV:G->bool) = n /\
       is_group mul identity ginv /\
       generated_by mul identity ginv {a,b} /\
       ~(generated_by mul identity ginv {a}) /\
       ~(generated_by mul identity ginv {b})
       ==>
       ?g:num->G.
         (!x:G. CARD {i:num | i < 2 * n /\ g i = x} = 2) /\
         (!i:num.
            i < 2 * n
            ==> g ((i + 1) MOD (2 * n)) = mul (g i) a \/
                g ((i + 1) MOD (2 * n)) = mul (g i) b))
     <=> putnam_1990_b4_solution)`;;

title: putnam_1990_b4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b4:
;; every finite group generated by a and b, but by neither one alone, has a
;; cyclic length-2n sequence visiting each element twice using right
;; multiplication by a or b. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A duplicate-free carrier and a complete multiplication table represent an
;; arbitrary finite group extensionally. Every finite group has such a
;; presentation, and the group axioms below recover exactly the represented
;; multiplication without restricting the group's isomorphism type.

(defun putnam-1990-b4-set-list-p (xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (not (member-equal (car xs) (cdr xs)))
       (putnam-1990-b4-set-list-p (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-binary-table-p (table carrier)
  (if (consp table)
      (let* ((entry (car table))
             (arguments (car entry))
             (value (cdr entry)))
        (and
         (consp entry)
         (true-listp arguments)
         (equal (len arguments) 2)
         (member-equal (car arguments) carrier)
         (member-equal (cadr arguments) carrier)
         (member-equal value carrier)
         (not (assoc-equal arguments (cdr table)))
         (putnam-1990-b4-binary-table-p
          (cdr table) carrier)))
    (equal table nil)))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-multiply (left right table)
  (cdr (assoc-equal (list left right) table)))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-associative-z-p
    (zs x y table)
  (if (endp zs)
      t
    (let* ((z (car zs))
           (xy (putnam-1990-b4-multiply x y table))
           (yz (putnam-1990-b4-multiply y z table)))
      (and
       (equal
        (putnam-1990-b4-multiply xy z table)
        (putnam-1990-b4-multiply x yz table))
       (putnam-1990-b4-associative-z-p
        (cdr zs) x y table)))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-group-y-axioms-p
    (ys carrier x table)
  (if (endp ys)
      t
    (let ((y (car ys)))
      (and
       (assoc-equal (list x y) table)
       (putnam-1990-b4-associative-z-p
        carrier x y table)
       (putnam-1990-b4-group-y-axioms-p
        (cdr ys) carrier x table)))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-inverse-exists-p
    (x candidates one table)
  (if (endp candidates)
      nil
    (or
     (and
      (equal
       (putnam-1990-b4-multiply x (car candidates) table)
       one)
      (equal
       (putnam-1990-b4-multiply (car candidates) x table)
       one))
     (putnam-1990-b4-inverse-exists-p
      x (cdr candidates) one table))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-group-x-axioms-p
    (xs carrier one table)
  (if (endp xs)
      t
    (let ((x (car xs)))
      (and
       (equal
        (putnam-1990-b4-multiply one x table)
        x)
       (equal
        (putnam-1990-b4-multiply x one table)
        x)
       (putnam-1990-b4-inverse-exists-p
        x carrier one table)
       (putnam-1990-b4-group-y-axioms-p
        carrier carrier x table)
       (putnam-1990-b4-group-x-axioms-p
        (cdr xs) carrier one table)))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-finite-group-p
    (carrier one table)
  (and
   (putnam-1990-b4-set-list-p carrier)
   (consp carrier)
   (member-equal one carrier)
   (putnam-1990-b4-binary-table-p table carrier)
   (putnam-1990-b4-group-x-axioms-p
    carrier carrier one table)))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-adjoin-equal (x xs)
  (if (member-equal x xs)
      xs
    (cons x xs)))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-add-generator-products
    (elements generator table result)
  (if (endp elements)
      result
    (putnam-1990-b4-add-generator-products
     (cdr elements)
     generator
     table
     (putnam-1990-b4-adjoin-equal
      (putnam-1990-b4-multiply
       (car elements) generator table)
      result))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-add-all-generator-products
    (generators elements table result)
  (if (endp generators)
      result
    (putnam-1990-b4-add-all-generator-products
     (cdr generators)
     elements
     table
     (putnam-1990-b4-add-generator-products
      elements (car generators) table result))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-closure-step
    (elements generators table)
  (putnam-1990-b4-add-all-generator-products
   generators elements table elements))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-closure-iterate
    (fuel elements generators table)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (zp fuel)
      elements
    (putnam-1990-b4-closure-iterate
     (- fuel 1)
     (putnam-1990-b4-closure-step
      elements generators table)
     generators
     table)))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-subset-p (xs ys)
  (if (endp xs)
      t
    (and
     (member-equal (car xs) ys)
     (putnam-1990-b4-subset-p (cdr xs) ys))))

;; In a group of order n, right-multiplication paths of length at most n
;; suffice to reach every element reachable by an arbitrary generator word.
;; Thus this finite search is exactly subgroup generation, not a bound on the
;; source group or on its possible generators.

(defun putnam-1990-b4-generates-carrier-p
    (carrier one generators table)
  (putnam-1990-b4-subset-p
   carrier
   (putnam-1990-b4-closure-iterate
    (len carrier) (list one) generators table)))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-prepend-to-sequences
    (element sequences)
  (if (endp sequences)
      nil
    (cons
     (cons element (car sequences))
     (putnam-1990-b4-prepend-to-sequences
      element (cdr sequences)))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-extend-sequences
    (elements sequences)
  (if (endp elements)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-1990-b4-prepend-to-sequences
      (car elements) sequences)
     (putnam-1990-b4-extend-sequences
      (cdr elements) sequences))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-all-sequences
    (carrier length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix length)))
  (if (zp length)
      (list nil)
    (putnam-1990-b4-extend-sequences
     carrier
     (putnam-1990-b4-all-sequences
      carrier (- length 1)))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-sequence-in-carrier-p
    (sequence carrier)
  (if (endp sequence)
      t
    (and
     (member-equal (car sequence) carrier)
     (putnam-1990-b4-sequence-in-carrier-p
      (cdr sequence) carrier))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-count-equal (x sequence)
  (if (endp sequence)
      0
    (+
     (if (equal x (car sequence)) 1 0)
     (putnam-1990-b4-count-equal x (cdr sequence)))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-each-element-twice-p
    (elements sequence)
  (if (endp elements)
      t
    (and
     (equal
      (putnam-1990-b4-count-equal
       (car elements) sequence)
      2)
     (putnam-1990-b4-each-element-twice-p
      (cdr elements) sequence))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-next-index
    (index length)
  (if (zp length)
      0
    (mod (+ index 1) length)))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-transitions-p
    (index remaining sequence table a b)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (let* ((length (len sequence))
           (current (nth index sequence))
           (next
            (nth
             (putnam-1990-b4-next-index index length)
             sequence)))
      (and
       (or
        (equal
         next
         (putnam-1990-b4-multiply current a table))
        (equal
         next
         (putnam-1990-b4-multiply current b table)))
       (putnam-1990-b4-transitions-p
        (+ index 1)
        (- remaining 1)
        sequence
        table
        a
        b)))))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-valid-sequence-p
    (sequence carrier table n a b)
  (and
   (true-listp sequence)
   (equal (len sequence) (* 2 n))
   (putnam-1990-b4-sequence-in-carrier-p
    sequence carrier)
   (putnam-1990-b4-each-element-twice-p
    carrier sequence)
   (putnam-1990-b4-transitions-p
    0 (len sequence) sequence table a b)))

(defun putnam-1990-b4-valid-sequence-exists-p
    (sequences carrier table n a b)
  (if (endp sequences)
      nil
    (or
     (putnam-1990-b4-valid-sequence-p
      (car sequences) carrier table n a b)
     (putnam-1990-b4-valid-sequence-exists-p
      (cdr sequences) carrier table n a b))))

;; Exhaustive search over all carrier-valued lists of length 2n is the source
;; existential quantifier over the relevant finite prefix of g : nat -> G.
;; Hence the witness is internal rather than an extra universally quantified
;; parameter.

(defun putnam-1990-b4-sequence-exists-p
    (carrier table n a b)
  (putnam-1990-b4-valid-sequence-exists-p
   (putnam-1990-b4-all-sequences carrier (* 2 n))
   carrier
   table
   n
   a
   b))

;; The supplied PutnamBench solution is True, so its defining biconditional is
;; exactly the universally quantified implication encoded by this predicate.

(defun putnambench-putnam-1990-b4-statement
    (carrier one table n a b)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-1990-b4-finite-group-p
     carrier one table)
    (natp n)
    (equal n (len carrier))
    (member-equal a carrier)
    (member-equal b carrier)
    (putnam-1990-b4-generates-carrier-p
     carrier one (list a b) table)
    (not
     (putnam-1990-b4-generates-carrier-p
      carrier one (list a) table))
    (not
     (putnam-1990-b4-generates-carrier-p
      carrier one (list b) table)))
   (putnam-1990-b4-sequence-exists-p
    carrier table n a b)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1990_b4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b4:
-- every finite group generated by two elements, but by neither element alone,
-- has a cyclic generator-step sequence visiting every group element twice,
-- equivalently to the catalogued solution True. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)
open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc; _⊔_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

record Top : Set where
  constructor truth

Not :
  {a : Level} ->
  Set a ->
  Set a
Not proposition =
  proposition -> Bottom

_!=_ :
  {a : Level} ->
  {A : Set a} ->
  A ->
  A ->
  Set a
left != right =
  Not (left == right)

record _and_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists
  {a p : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (property : A -> Set p) :
  Set (a ⊔ p) where

  constructor witness
  field
    value     : A
    satisfies : property value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record Bijection
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  field
    to      : A -> B
    from    : B -> A
    from-to : (x : A) -> from (to x) == x
    to-from : (y : B) -> to (from y) == y

record HasCardinality
  {a p : Level}
  {A : Set a}
  (property : A -> Set p)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set (a ⊔ p) where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      property (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (x : A) ->
      property x ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> x == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

record Group
  {ell : Level}
  (G : Set ell) :
  Set ell where

  field
    identity       : G
    inverse        : G -> G
    multiply       : G -> G -> G
    associative    : (x y z : G) ->
                     multiply (multiply x y) z ==
                     multiply x (multiply y z)
    identity-left  : (x : G) -> multiply identity x == x
    identity-right : (x : G) -> multiply x identity == x
    inverse-left   : (x : G) -> multiply (inverse x) x == identity
    inverse-right  : (x : G) -> multiply x (inverse x) == identity

open Group

data Sign : Set where
  positive negative : Sign

data TwoGeneratorLetter : Set where
  first-positive first-negative : TwoGeneratorLetter
  second-positive second-negative : TwoGeneratorLetter

signedValue :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  Group G ->
  G ->
  Sign ->
  G
signedValue structure generator positive =
  generator
signedValue structure generator negative =
  inverse structure generator

twoGeneratorValue :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  Group G ->
  G ->
  G ->
  TwoGeneratorLetter ->
  G
twoGeneratorValue structure a b first-positive =
  a
twoGeneratorValue structure a b first-negative =
  inverse structure a
twoGeneratorValue structure a b second-positive =
  b
twoGeneratorValue structure a b second-negative =
  inverse structure b

evaluateOne :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  Group G ->
  G ->
  List Sign ->
  G
evaluateOne structure generator [] =
  identity structure
evaluateOne structure generator (letter ∷ rest) =
  multiply structure
    (signedValue structure generator letter)
    (evaluateOne structure generator rest)

evaluateTwo :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  Group G ->
  G ->
  G ->
  List TwoGeneratorLetter ->
  G
evaluateTwo structure a b [] =
  identity structure
evaluateTwo structure a b (letter ∷ rest) =
  multiply structure
    (twoGeneratorValue structure a b letter)
    (evaluateTwo structure a b rest)

GeneratesOne :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  Group G ->
  G ->
  Set ell
GeneratesOne {G = G} structure generator =
  (x : G) ->
  Exists (List Sign)
    (\ word -> evaluateOne structure generator word == x)

GeneratesTwo :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  Group G ->
  G ->
  G ->
  Set ell
GeneratesTwo {G = G} structure a b =
  (x : G) ->
  Exists (List TwoGeneratorLetter)
    (\ word -> evaluateTwo structure a b word == x)

weakenFin :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin (suc n)
weakenFin fzero =
  fzero
weakenFin (fsuc index) =
  fsuc (weakenFin index)

lastFin :
  (n : Nat) ->
  Fin (suc n)
lastFin zero =
  fzero
lastFin (suc n) =
  fsuc (lastFin n)

data CyclicSuccessor :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n ->
  Set where

  successor-step :
    {n : Nat} ->
    (index : Fin n) ->
    CyclicSuccessor {suc n}
      (weakenFin index)
      (fsuc index)

  successor-wrap :
    {n : Nat} ->
    CyclicSuccessor {suc n}
      (lastFin n)
      fzero

two : Nat
two =
  suc (suc zero)

EveryElementTwice :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  {length : Nat} ->
  (Fin length -> G) ->
  Set ell
EveryElementTwice {G = G} sequence =
  (x : G) ->
  HasCardinality
    (\ index -> sequence index == x)
    two

FollowsGenerators :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  {length : Nat} ->
  Group G ->
  G ->
  G ->
  (Fin length -> G) ->
  Set ell
FollowsGenerators {length = length} structure a b sequence =
  (current next : Fin length) ->
  CyclicSuccessor current next ->
  sequence next == multiply structure (sequence current) a
  or
  sequence next == multiply structure (sequence current) b

ValidSequence :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {G : Set ell} ->
  Group G ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  G ->
  G ->
  Set ell
ValidSequence {G = G} structure n a b =
  Exists (Fin (two * n) -> G)
    (\ sequence ->
      EveryElementTwice sequence
      and
      FollowsGenerators structure a b sequence)

putnam-1990-b4-solution : Set
putnam-1990-b4-solution =
  Top

putnam-1990-b4 :
  (ell : Level) ->
  Set (lsuc ell)
putnam-1990-b4 ell =
  Iff
    ((G : Set ell) ->
      (structure : Group G) ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      (a b : G) ->
      Bijection G (Fin n) ->
      GeneratesTwo structure a b ->
      Not (GeneratesOne structure a) ->
      Not (GeneratesOne structure b) ->
      ValidSequence structure n a b)
    putnam-1990-b4-solution

title: putnam_1990_b4
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b4:
  every finite group generated by two elements, neither of which generates
  alone, admits a cyclic length-2n sequence visiting each element twice by
  right multiplication by one of the generators. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory groupTheory;

val putnam_1990_b4 =
  ``let putnam_1990_b4_solution = T
    in
      ((!(g : 'a group) (n : num) (a b : 'a).
          FiniteGroup g /\
          CARD g.carrier = n /\
          (Generated_subset g {a; b}).carrier = g.carrier /\
          (Generated_subset g {a}).carrier <> g.carrier /\
          (Generated_subset g {b}).carrier <> g.carrier
          ==>
          ?walk : num -> 'a.
            (!x : 'a.
               x IN g.carrier
               ==>
               CARD {i : num | i < 2 * n /\ walk i = x} = 2) /\
            (!i : num.
               i < 2 * n
               ==>
               (walk ((i + 1) MOD (2 * n)) = g.op (walk i) a \/
                walk ((i + 1) MOD (2 * n)) = g.op (walk i) b)))
       <=>
       putnam_1990_b4_solution)``;

title: putnam_1990_b4
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1990_b4: every finite group irredundantly generated by two elements
  has a cyclic sequence of twice its order in which every group element
  occurs twice and each step right-multiplies by a generator. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  In SetMM, G e. Grp supplies an arbitrary group, Base ` G is its carrier,
  +g ` G is its group operation, and the Moore closure in SubGrp ` G is
  subgroup generation. Thus the three closure conditions say that a and b
  generate G together but neither generates G alone.

  The ordinal 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) represents Fin (2*n). The witness g is a
  function on exactly this finite cyclic index set. Restricting the source
  witness NN0 --> Base ` G to these indices gives this representation, and
  every such finite function extends to NN0 because a group carrier is
  nonempty, so the existential statements are equivalent. Fiber cardinality
  two expresses that every carrier element occurs exactly twice, and mod

title: putnam_1990_b4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b4:
% every finite group generated by two individually non-generating elements
% has the stated cyclic double-occurrence sequence. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1990_b4[Element: TYPE+]: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[Element]

  element_set: TYPE = finite_set[Element]
  sequence: TYPE = [nat -> Element]

  subset_of(A, B: element_set): bool =
    FORALL (x: Element):
      A(x) IMPLIES B(x)

  finite_group(
      carrier: element_set,
      one: Element,
      inverse: [Element -> Element],
      multiply: [Element, Element -> Element]): bool =
    carrier(one)
      AND
        (FORALL (x, y: Element):
          carrier(x) AND carrier(y) IMPLIES
            carrier(multiply(x, y)))
      AND
        (FORALL (x: Element):
          carrier(x) IMPLIES carrier(inverse(x)))
      AND
        (FORALL (x, y, z: Element):
          carrier(x) AND carrier(y) AND carrier(z) IMPLIES
            multiply(multiply(x, y), z)
              = multiply(x, multiply(y, z)))
      AND
        (FORALL (x: Element):
          carrier(x) IMPLIES
            multiply(one, x) = x
              AND multiply(x, one) = x)
      AND
        (FORALL (x: Element):
          carrier(x) IMPLIES
            multiply(inverse(x), x) = one
              AND multiply(x, inverse(x)) = one)

  is_subgroup(
      subgroup, carrier: element_set,
      one: Element,
      inverse: [Element -> Element],
      multiply: [Element, Element -> Element]): bool =
    subset_of(subgroup, carrier)
      AND subgroup(one)
      AND
        (FORALL (x, y: Element):
          subgroup(x) AND subgroup(y) IMPLIES
            subgroup(multiply(x, y)))
      AND
        (FORALL (x: Element):
          subgroup(x) IMPLIES subgroup(inverse(x)))

  generated_by_two(
      carrier: element_set,
      one: Element,
      inverse: [Element -> Element],
      multiply: [Element, Element -> Element],
      a, b: Element): bool =
    carrier(a)
      AND carrier(b)
      AND
        (FORALL (subgroup: element_set):
          (is_subgroup(
              subgroup, carrier, one, inverse, multiply)
            AND subgroup(a)
            AND subgroup(b))
          IMPLIES subset_of(carrier, subgroup))

  generated_by_one(
      carrier: element_set,
      one: Element,
      inverse: [Element -> Element],
      multiply: [Element, Element -> Element],
      a: Element): bool =
    carrier(a)
      AND
        (FORALL (subgroup: element_set):
          (is_subgroup(
              subgroup, carrier, one, inverse, multiply)
            AND subgroup(a))
          IMPLIES subset_of(carrier, subgroup))

  occurs_exactly_twice(
      g: sequence,
      x: Element,
      n: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (first, second: nat):
      first < 2 * n
        AND second < 2 * n
        AND first /= second
        AND g(first) = x
        AND g(second) = x
        AND
          (FORALL (index: nat):
            index < 2 * n AND g(index) = x IMPLIES
              index = first OR index = second)

  has_cyclic_successor_value(
      g: sequence,
      index, n: nat,
      value: Element): bool =
    (index + 1 < 2 * n AND g(index + 1) = value)
      OR
    (index + 1 = 2 * n AND g(0) = value)

  has_cyclic_double_occurrence_sequence(
      carrier: element_set,
      multiply: [Element, Element -> Element],
      n: nat,
      a, b: Element): bool =
    EXISTS (g: sequence):
      (FORALL (x: Element):
        carrier(x) IMPLIES occurs_exactly_twice(g, x, n))
      AND
        (FORALL (index: nat):
          index < 2 * n IMPLIES
            has_cyclic_successor_value(
              g, index, n, multiply(g(index), a))
              OR has_cyclic_successor_value(
                g, index, n, multiply(g(index), b)))

  putnam_1990_b4_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_1990_b4: bool =
    (FORALL (carrier: element_set),
            (one: Element),
            (inverse: [Element -> Element]),
            (multiply: [Element, Element -> Element]),
            (n: nat),
            (a, b: Element):
      (finite_group(carrier, one, inverse, multiply)
        AND n = card(carrier)
        AND generated_by_two(
          carrier, one, inverse, multiply, a, b)
        AND NOT generated_by_one(
          carrier, one, inverse, multiply, a)
        AND NOT generated_by_one(
          carrier, one, inverse, multiply, b))
      IMPLIES
        has_cyclic_double_occurrence_sequence(
          carrier, multiply, n, a, b))
    IFF putnam_1990_b4_solution
END putnam_1990_b4

import Mathlib

open Filter Polynomial Topology Nat

abbrev putnam_1990_b5_solution : Prop := sorry
-- True
/--
Is there an infinite sequence $a_0,a_1,a_2,\dots$ of nonzero real numbers such that for $n=1,2,3,\dots$ the polynomial $p_n(x)=a_0+a_1x+a_2x^2+\cdots+a_nx^n$ has exactly $n$ distinct real roots?
-/
theorem putnam_1990_b5 :
    (∃ a : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ i, a i ≠ 0) ∧
      (∀ n ≥ 1, (∑ i ∈ Finset.Iic n, a i • X ^ i : Polynomial ℝ).roots.toFinset.card = n)) ↔
    putnam_1990_b5_solution :=
  sorry

title: putnam_1990_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b5:
;; existence of an infinite sequence of nonzero real coefficients whose
;; degree-n partial polynomial has exactly n distinct real roots for every
;; positive n. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The real scalar domain is presented as a real-closed ordered field. This
;; suffices because the statement concerns polynomial arithmetic, order, and
;; roots. APPLY$ objects represent the field operations and sequence, while
;; DEFUN-SK keeps the sequence and all root-list witnesses existentially
;; quantified inside the statement.

(defun p90b5-apply1 (function argument)
  (apply$ function (list argument)))

(defun p90b5-apply2 (function left right)
  (apply$ function (list left right)))

(defun p90b5-carrier-p (ctx value)
  (if (p90b5-apply1 (nth 0 ctx) value) t nil))

(defun p90b5-zero (ctx) (nth 1 ctx))
(defun p90b5-one (ctx) (nth 2 ctx))
(defun p90b5-add-operation (ctx) (nth 3 ctx))
(defun p90b5-multiply-operation (ctx) (nth 4 ctx))
(defun p90b5-negate-operation (ctx) (nth 5 ctx))
(defun p90b5-inverse-operation (ctx) (nth 6 ctx))
(defun p90b5-less-operation (ctx) (nth 7 ctx))

(defun p90b5-add (ctx left right)
  (p90b5-apply2
   (p90b5-add-operation ctx) left right))

(defun p90b5-multiply (ctx left right)
  (p90b5-apply2
   (p90b5-multiply-operation ctx) left right))

(defun p90b5-negate (ctx value)
  (p90b5-apply1
   (p90b5-negate-operation ctx) value))

(defun p90b5-inverse (ctx value)
  (p90b5-apply1
   (p90b5-inverse-operation ctx) value))

(defun p90b5-less-p (ctx left right)
  (if (p90b5-apply2
       (p90b5-less-operation ctx) left right)
      t nil))

(defun-sk p90b5-field-laws-p (ctx)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p90b5-carrier-p ctx x)
      (p90b5-carrier-p ctx y)
      (p90b5-carrier-p ctx z))
     (let* ((zero (p90b5-zero ctx))
            (one (p90b5-one ctx))
            (x-plus-y (p90b5-add ctx x y))
            (y-plus-z (p90b5-add ctx y z))
            (x-times-y (p90b5-multiply ctx x y))
            (y-times-z (p90b5-multiply ctx y z))
            (minus-x (p90b5-negate ctx x))
            (inverse-x (p90b5-inverse ctx x)))
       (and
        (p90b5-carrier-p ctx x-plus-y)
        (p90b5-carrier-p ctx x-times-y)
        (p90b5-carrier-p ctx minus-x)
        (p90b5-carrier-p ctx inverse-x)
        (equal
         (p90b5-add ctx x-plus-y z)
         (p90b5-add ctx x y-plus-z))
        (equal x-plus-y (p90b5-add ctx y x))
        (equal (p90b5-add ctx x zero) x)
        (equal (p90b5-add ctx x minus-x) zero)
        (equal
         (p90b5-multiply ctx x-times-y z)
         (p90b5-multiply ctx x y-times-z))
        (equal x-times-y (p90b5-multiply ctx y x))
        (equal (p90b5-multiply ctx x one) x)
        (implies
         (equal x zero)
         (equal inverse-x zero))
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (equal
          (p90b5-multiply ctx x inverse-x)
          one))
        (equal
         (p90b5-multiply ctx x y-plus-z)
         (p90b5-add
          ctx
          (p90b5-multiply ctx x y)
          (p90b5-multiply ctx x z))))))))

(defun-sk p90b5-order-laws-p (ctx)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p90b5-carrier-p ctx x)
      (p90b5-carrier-p ctx y)
      (p90b5-carrier-p ctx z))
     (let ((zero (p90b5-zero ctx)))
       (and
        (not (p90b5-less-p ctx x x))
        (or
         (p90b5-less-p ctx x y)
         (equal x y)
         (p90b5-less-p ctx y x))
        (implies
         (and
          (p90b5-less-p ctx x y)
          (p90b5-less-p ctx y z))
         (p90b5-less-p ctx x z))
        (implies
         (p90b5-less-p ctx x y)
         (p90b5-less-p
          ctx
          (p90b5-add ctx x z)
          (p90b5-add ctx y z)))
        (implies
         (and
          (p90b5-less-p ctx zero x)
          (p90b5-less-p ctx zero y))
         (p90b5-less-p
          ctx
          zero
          (p90b5-multiply ctx x y))))))))

(defun p90b5-coefficient-list-p (ctx coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and
       (p90b5-carrier-p ctx (car coefficients))
       (p90b5-coefficient-list-p
        ctx (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun p90b5-polynomial-p (ctx coefficients)
  (and
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (consp coefficients)
   (p90b5-coefficient-list-p ctx coefficients)
   (not
    (equal
     (car (last coefficients))
     (p90b5-zero ctx)))))

(defun p90b5-polynomial-evaluate (ctx coefficients x)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (p90b5-add
       ctx
       (car coefficients)
       (p90b5-multiply
        ctx
        x
        (p90b5-polynomial-evaluate
         ctx (cdr coefficients) x)))
    (p90b5-zero ctx)))

(defun-sk p90b5-positive-square-root-exists-p
    (ctx value)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (p90b5-carrier-p ctx root)
     (equal
      (p90b5-multiply ctx root root)
      value))))

(defun-sk p90b5-positive-square-root-law-p (ctx)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (and
      (p90b5-carrier-p ctx value)
      (p90b5-less-p
       ctx (p90b5-zero ctx) value))
     (p90b5-positive-square-root-exists-p
      ctx value))))

(defun-sk p90b5-odd-polynomial-root-exists-p
    (ctx coefficients)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (p90b5-carrier-p ctx root)
     (equal
      (p90b5-polynomial-evaluate
       ctx coefficients root)
      (p90b5-zero ctx)))))

(defun-sk p90b5-odd-polynomial-root-law-p (ctx)
  (forall (coefficients)
    (implies
     (and
      (p90b5-polynomial-p ctx coefficients)
      (evenp (len coefficients)))
     (p90b5-odd-polynomial-root-exists-p
      ctx coefficients))))

(defun p90b5-real-closed-field-p (ctx)
  (and
   (true-listp ctx)
   (equal (len ctx) 8)
   (tamep-functionp (nth 0 ctx))
   (tamep-functionp (nth 3 ctx))
   (tamep-functionp (nth 4 ctx))
   (tamep-functionp (nth 5 ctx))
   (tamep-functionp (nth 6 ctx))
   (tamep-functionp (nth 7 ctx))
   (p90b5-carrier-p ctx (p90b5-zero ctx))
   (p90b5-carrier-p ctx (p90b5-one ctx))
   (not (equal (p90b5-zero ctx) (p90b5-one ctx)))
   (p90b5-field-laws-p ctx)
   (p90b5-order-laws-p ctx)
   (p90b5-less-p
    ctx (p90b5-zero ctx) (p90b5-one ctx))
   (p90b5-positive-square-root-law-p ctx)
   (p90b5-odd-polynomial-root-law-p ctx)))

(defun p90b5-sequence-value (sequence index)
  (p90b5-apply1 sequence index))

(defun-sk p90b5-sequence-values-p (ctx sequence)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (natp index)
     (and
      (p90b5-carrier-p
       ctx
       (p90b5-sequence-value sequence index))
      (not
       (equal
        (p90b5-sequence-value sequence index)
        (p90b5-zero ctx)))))))

;; Horner evaluation of
;; a_index + a_(index+1)x + ... + a_(index+count-1)x^(count-1).

(defun p90b5-partial-polynomial-evaluate
    (ctx sequence index count x)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      (p90b5-zero ctx)
    (p90b5-add
     ctx
     (p90b5-sequence-value sequence index)
     (p90b5-multiply
      ctx
      x
      (p90b5-partial-polynomial-evaluate
       ctx sequence (+ index 1) (- count 1) x)))))

(defun p90b5-root-p (ctx sequence degree value)
  (and
   (p90b5-carrier-p ctx value)
   (equal
    (p90b5-partial-polynomial-evaluate
     ctx sequence 0 (+ degree 1) value)
    (p90b5-zero ctx))))

(defun p90b5-listed-roots-p
    (ctx sequence degree roots)
  (if (consp roots)
      (and
       (p90b5-root-p
        ctx sequence degree (car roots))
       (p90b5-listed-roots-p
        ctx sequence degree (cdr roots)))
    (equal roots nil)))

(defun-sk p90b5-all-roots-listed-p
    (ctx sequence degree roots)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (p90b5-root-p ctx sequence degree value)
     (member-equal value roots))))

(defun p90b5-exact-root-list-p
    (ctx sequence degree roots)
  (and
   (true-listp roots)
   (equal (len roots) degree)
   (no-duplicatesp-equal roots)
   (p90b5-listed-roots-p
    ctx sequence degree roots)
   (p90b5-all-roots-listed-p
    ctx sequence degree roots)))

(defun-sk p90b5-exact-root-list-exists-p
    (ctx sequence degree)
  (exists (roots)
    (p90b5-exact-root-list-p
     ctx sequence degree roots)))

(defun-sk p90b5-all-partial-polynomials-p
    (ctx sequence)
  (forall (degree)
    (implies
     (posp degree)
     (p90b5-exact-root-list-exists-p
      ctx sequence degree))))

(defun p90b5-sequence-witness-p (ctx sequence)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp sequence)
   (p90b5-sequence-values-p ctx sequence)
   (p90b5-all-partial-polynomials-p
    ctx sequence)))

(defun-sk p90b5-sequence-exists-p (ctx)
  (exists (sequence)
    (p90b5-sequence-witness-p ctx sequence)))

(defun p90b5-solution ()
  t)

(defun putnambench-putnam-1990-b5-statement (ctx)
  (implies
   (p90b5-real-closed-field-p ctx)
   (iff
    (p90b5-sequence-exists-p ctx)
    (p90b5-solution))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (P : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      P (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      P item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> item == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

module Putnam1990B5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  polynomialValue :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    R ->
    R
  polynomialValue coefficients n x =
    sumFirst reals (suc n)
      (\ i ->
        multiply reals
          (coefficients i)
          (naturalPower reals x i))

  IsRoot :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    R ->
    Set
  IsRoot coefficients n x =
    polynomialValue coefficients n x == zeroR reals

  HasExactlyNRoots :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    Set
  HasExactlyNRoots coefficients n =
    HasCardinality (IsRoot coefficients n) n

  desiredSequenceExists : Set
  desiredSequenceExists =
    Exists (Nat -> R)
      (\ coefficients ->
        ((i : Nat) ->
          coefficients i != zeroR reals)
        and
        ((n : Nat) ->
          oneN <=N n ->
          HasExactlyNRoots coefficients n))

  solution : Set
  solution =
    Top

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    Iff desiredSequenceExists solution

putnam-1990-b5 : Set1
putnam-1990-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1990B5Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b5:
  existence of a nonzero real coefficient sequence whose degree-n
  truncation has exactly n distinct real roots for every positive n.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;

val putnam_1990_b5 =
  ``let real_roots =
      \a : num -> real.
      \n : num.
        {x : real |
           SIGMA
             (\i : num. a i * x pow i)
             (count (n + 1)) =
           0}
    in
    let putnam_1990_b5_solution = T
    in
      ((?a : num -> real.
          (!i : num. a i <> 0) /\
          (!n : num.
             1 <= n
             ==>
             FINITE (real_roots a n) /\
             CARD (real_roots a n) = n))
       <=>
       putnam_1990_b5_solution)``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1990_b5: existence of an infinite sequence of nonzero real
  coefficients whose nth truncation has exactly n distinct real roots for
  every positive integer n. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  RR ^m NN0 is set.mm's class of all real-valued sequences indexed by the
  nonnegative integers. For each positive n, the finite sum is exactly the
  polynomial a_0 + a_1 x + ... + a_n x^n, and the cardinality expression
  counts its distinct real roots.

  The Rocq source expresses the same root condition by exhibiting n distinct
  roots. Since the coefficient at n is nonzero, the polynomial has degree n
  and therefore has at most n roots, making that formulation equivalent to
  the exact-cardinality formulation below. The annotated solution is True,
  so the source biconditional is equivalent to this existence assertion.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d A i n x $.

  putnambench-putnam-1990-b5 $a |-
    E. A e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
      (
        A. i e. NN0
          ( A ` i ) =/= 0
        /\
        A. n e. NN
          (
            #
            `
            {
              x e. RR |
              (
                sum_ i e. ( 0 ... n )
                  (
                    ( A ` i )
                    x.
                    ( x ^ i )
                  )
              )
              =
              0
            }
          )
          =
          n
      )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1990_b5:
% there exists an infinite sequence of nonzero real coefficients whose degree-n
% truncation has exactly n distinct real roots for every n >= 1. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1990_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[real]

  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  polynomial_value(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      degree: nat,
      x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    IF degree = 0 THEN
      coefficients(0)
    ELSE
      polynomial_value(coefficients, degree - 1, x)
        + coefficients(degree) * x ^ degree
    ENDIF
  MEASURE degree

  has_exactly_n_distinct_real_roots(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      degree: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (roots: finite_set[real]):
      card(roots) = degree
        AND (FORALL (x: real):
          roots(x) IFF polynomial_value(coefficients, degree, x) = 0)

  putnam_1990_b5_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_1990_b5: bool =
    (EXISTS (coefficients: real_sequence):
      (FORALL (i: nat): coefficients(i) /= 0)
        AND (FORALL (n: nat):
          n >= 1 IMPLIES
            has_exactly_n_distinct_real_roots(coefficients, n)))
      IFF putnam_1990_b5_solution
END putnam_1990_b5

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_a2:
   nonexistence of distinct real square matrices satisfying two cubic
   identities whose sum of squares is invertible. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Vectors.Fin Reals.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_1991_a2_matrix (n : nat) : Type :=
  Fin.t n -> Fin.t n -> R.

Definition putnam_1991_a2_matrix_eq
    {n : nat}
    (A B : putnam_1991_a2_matrix n) : Prop :=
  forall i j, A i j = B i j.

Fixpoint putnam_1991_a2_indices (n : nat) : list (Fin.t n) :=
  match n with
  | O => []
  | S k => Fin.F1 :: map Fin.FS (putnam_1991_a2_indices k)
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_1991_a2_sum (xs : list R) : R :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0
  | x :: rest => x + putnam_1991_a2_sum rest
  end.

Definition putnam_1991_a2_mul
    {n : nat}
    (A B : putnam_1991_a2_matrix n) :
    putnam_1991_a2_matrix n :=
  fun i j =>
    putnam_1991_a2_sum
      (map
        (fun k => A i k * B k j)
        (putnam_1991_a2_indices n)).

Definition putnam_1991_a2_add
    {n : nat}
    (A B : putnam_1991_a2_matrix n) :
    putnam_1991_a2_matrix n :=
  fun i j => A i j + B i j.

Definition putnam_1991_a2_identity
    (n : nat) : putnam_1991_a2_matrix n :=
  fun i j =>
    if Fin.eq_dec i j then 1 else 0.

Definition putnam_1991_a2_invertible
    {n : nat} (A : putnam_1991_a2_matrix n) : Prop :=
  exists B : putnam_1991_a2_matrix n,
    putnam_1991_a2_matrix_eq
      (putnam_1991_a2_mul A B)
      (putnam_1991_a2_identity n) /\
    putnam_1991_a2_matrix_eq
      (putnam_1991_a2_mul B A)
      (putnam_1991_a2_identity n).

Definition putnam_1991_a2_solution : Prop := False.

Theorem putnam_1991_a2
    (n : nat)
    (hn : (1 <= n)%nat) :
  putnam_1991_a2_solution <->
  exists A B : putnam_1991_a2_matrix n,
    ~ putnam_1991_a2_matrix_eq A B /\
    putnam_1991_a2_matrix_eq
      (putnam_1991_a2_mul (putnam_1991_a2_mul A A) A)
      (putnam_1991_a2_mul (putnam_1991_a2_mul B B) B) /\
    putnam_1991_a2_matrix_eq
      (putnam_1991_a2_mul (putnam_1991_a2_mul A A) B)
      (putnam_1991_a2_mul (putnam_1991_a2_mul B B) A) /\
    putnam_1991_a2_invertible
      (putnam_1991_a2_add
        (putnam_1991_a2_mul A A)
        (putnam_1991_a2_mul B B)).
Admitted.
