Definition putnam_1991_a6_has_cardinality
    {X : Type} (P : X -> Prop) (cardinality : nat) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list X,
    NoDup enumeration /\
    length enumeration = cardinality /\
    forall x : X, In x enumeration <-> P x.

Definition putnam_1991_a6_composition
    (n : nat) (terms : list nat) : Prop :=
  terms <> nil /\
  Forall (fun term : nat => 0 < term) terms /\
  fold_right Nat.add 0 terms = n.

Definition putnam_1991_a6_agt (terms : list nat) : Prop :=
  (forall i : nat,
      i + 2 < length terms ->
      nth i terms 0 >
        nth (i + 1) terms 0 + nth (i + 2) terms 0) /\
  (1 < length terms ->
    nth (length terms - 2) terms 0 >
      nth (length terms - 1) terms 0).

Definition putnam_1991_a6_bge (terms : list nat) : Prop :=
  forall i : nat,
    i + 1 < length terms ->
    nth i terms 0 >= nth (i + 1) terms 0.

Definition putnam_1991_a6_bg1
    (g : nat -> nat) (terms : list nat) : Prop :=
  forall term : nat,
    In term terms ->
    exists j : nat, term = g j.

Definition putnam_1991_a6_bg2
    (g : nat -> nat) (terms : list nat) : Prop :=
  exists k : nat,
    nth 0 terms 0 = g k /\
    forall j : nat,
      j <= k ->
      In (g j) terms.

Definition putnam_1991_a6_A_member
    (n : nat) (terms : list nat) : Prop :=
  putnam_1991_a6_composition n terms /\
  putnam_1991_a6_agt terms.

Definition putnam_1991_a6_B_member
    (g : nat -> nat) (n : nat) (terms : list nat) : Prop :=
  putnam_1991_a6_composition n terms /\
  putnam_1991_a6_bge terms /\
  putnam_1991_a6_bg1 g terms /\
  putnam_1991_a6_bg2 g terms.

Definition putnam_1991_a6_recurrence (g : nat -> nat) : Prop :=
  g 0 = 1 /\
  g 1 = 2 /\
  forall j : nat,
    2 <= j ->
    g j = g (j - 1) + g (j - 2) + 1.

Theorem putnam_1991_a6 :
  forall A g B : nat -> nat,
    putnam_1991_a6_recurrence g ->
    (forall n : nat,
        1 <= n ->
        putnam_1991_a6_has_cardinality
          (putnam_1991_a6_A_member n) (A n)) ->
    (forall n : nat,
        1 <= n ->
        putnam_1991_a6_has_cardinality
          (putnam_1991_a6_B_member g n) (B n)) ->
    forall n : nat, 1 <= n -> A n = B n.
Admitted.

title: putnam_1991_a6
content:
theory putnam_1991_a6 imports
Complex_Main
begin

(* uses (nat \<rightarrow> nat) instead of (Fin r \<rightarrow> nat) and (Fin s \<rightarrow> nat) *)
theorem putnam_1991_a6:
  fixes nabsum :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and agt :: "nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and A :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
  and bge :: "nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and g :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
  and bg1 :: "nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and bg2 :: "nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and B :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
  defines "nabsum \<equiv> \<lambda> (n :: nat) (ab :: nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat)). (fst ab) \<ge> 1 \<and> (\<forall> i < fst ab. (snd ab) i > 0) \<and> (\<forall> i \<ge> fst ab. (snd ab) i = 0) \<and> (\<Sum> i = 0 .. fst ab - 1. (snd ab) i) = n"
  and "agt \<equiv> \<lambda> a :: nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat). (\<forall> i \<in> {0 .. fst a - 3}. (snd a) i > (snd a) (i + 1) + (snd a) (i + 2)) \<and> (1 < fst a \<longrightarrow> (snd a) (fst a - 2) > (snd a) (fst a - 1))"
  and "A \<equiv> \<lambda> n :: nat. card {a :: nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat). nabsum n a \<and> agt a}"
  and "bge \<equiv> \<lambda> b :: nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat). \<forall> i \<in> {0 .. fst b - 2}. (snd b) i \<ge> (snd b) (i + 1)"
  and "bg1 \<equiv> \<lambda> b :: nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat). \<forall> i \<in> {0 .. fst b - 1}. \<exists> j :: nat. (snd b) i = g j"
  and "bg2 \<equiv> \<lambda> b :: nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat). \<exists> k :: nat. (snd b) 0 = g k \<and> (\<forall> j \<le> k. \<exists> i \<in> {0 .. fst b - 1}. (snd b) i = g j)"
  and "B \<equiv> \<lambda> n :: nat. card {b :: nat \<times> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat). nabsum n b \<and> bge b \<and> bg1 b \<and> bg2 b}"
  assumes hg: "g 0 = 1 \<and> g 1 = 2 \<and> (\<forall> j \<ge> 2. g j = g (j - 1) + g (j - 2) + 1)"
  shows "\<forall> n \<ge> 1. A n = B n"
  sorry
  
end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_a6:
  equality of the counts of two families of positive-integer compositions,
  defined respectively by strong gap and recurrence-prefix conditions. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let nabsum =
     \n:num. \ab:num#(num->num).
       1 <= FST ab /\
       (!i:num. i < FST ab ==> 0 < SND ab i) /\
       (!i:num. FST ab <= i ==> SND ab i = 0) /\
       nsum (0..FST ab - 1) (\i. SND ab i) = n in
   let A =
     \n:num.
       CARD
         {a:num#(num->num) |
            nabsum n a /\
            (!i:num.
               i + 2 < FST a
               ==> SND a i > SND a (i + 1) + SND a (i + 2)) /\
            (1 < FST a
             ==> SND a (FST a - 2) > SND a (FST a - 1))} in
   let B =
     \g:num->num. \n:num.
       CARD
         {b:num#(num->num) |
            nabsum n b /\
            (!i:num.
               i + 1 < FST b
               ==> SND b i >= SND b (i + 1)) /\
            (!i:num.
               i < FST b
               ==> ?j:num. SND b i = g j) /\
            (?k:num.
               SND b 0 = g k /\
               (!j:num.
                  j <= k
                  ==> ?i:num. i < FST b /\ SND b i = g j))} in
   !g:num->num.
     g 0 = 1 /\
     g 1 = 2 /\
     (!j:num.
        2 <= j
        ==> g j = g (j - 1) + g (j - 2) + 1)
     ==>
     !n:num. 1 <= n ==> A n = B g n`;;

title: putnam_1991_a6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_a6:
;; two classes of positive-integer compositions of every n >= 1, one defined
;; by strict two-step inequalities and the other by a recurrence sequence with
;; prefix coverage, have equal cardinalities. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A mask below 2^(n-1) records the separator choices between n unit symbols.
;; This is a bijection with the nonempty finite sequences of positive integers
;; having sum n, hence with the finite positive prefixes of the source
;; eventually-zero functions.
(defun putnam-1991-a6-mask-to-composition-aux
    (units mask current-part reversed-parts)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix units)))
  (if (zp units)
      (reverse reversed-parts)
    (if (equal units 1)
        (reverse (cons current-part reversed-parts))
      (if (equal (mod mask 2) 1)
          (putnam-1991-a6-mask-to-composition-aux
           (- units 1)
           (floor mask 2)
           1
           (cons current-part reversed-parts))
        (putnam-1991-a6-mask-to-composition-aux
         (- units 1)
         (floor mask 2)
         (+ current-part 1)
         reversed-parts)))))

(defun putnam-1991-a6-mask-to-composition (n mask)
  (if (and (posp n)
           (natp mask)
           (< mask (expt 2 (- n 1))))
      (putnam-1991-a6-mask-to-composition-aux
       n mask 1 nil)
    nil))

;; This is exactly a_i > a_(i+1)+a_(i+2) at every available triple,
;; together with the final condition a_(r-1) > a_r.
(defun putnam-1991-a6-a-valid-p (composition)
  (cond
   ((endp composition) nil)
   ((endp (cdr composition)) t)
   ((endp (cddr composition))
    (> (car composition) (cadr composition)))
   (t
    (and
     (> (car composition)
        (+ (cadr composition) (caddr composition)))
     (putnam-1991-a6-a-valid-p (cdr composition))))))

(defun putnam-1991-a6-g (index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (cond
   ((zp index) 1)
   ((equal index 1) 2)
   (t
    (+ (putnam-1991-a6-g (- index 1))
       (putnam-1991-a6-g (- index 2))
       1))))

;; Since g_j >= j+1, searching indices from VALUE down to zero is unbounded
;; in the source parameter yet contains every possible witness to g_j=VALUE.
(defun putnam-1991-a6-g-value-p (value index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (equal value (putnam-1991-a6-g index))
      t
    (if (zp index)
        nil
      (putnam-1991-a6-g-value-p value (- index 1)))))

(defun putnam-1991-a6-all-g-values-p (composition)
  (if (consp composition)
      (and
       (putnam-1991-a6-g-value-p
        (car composition) (car composition))
       (putnam-1991-a6-all-g-values-p (cdr composition)))
    (equal composition nil)))

(defun putnam-1991-a6-nonincreasing-p (composition)
  (if (and (consp composition)
           (consp (cdr composition)))
      (and
       (>= (car composition) (cadr composition))
       (putnam-1991-a6-nonincreasing-p (cdr composition)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1991-a6-member-p (value composition)
  (if (consp composition)
      (or (equal value (car composition))
          (putnam-1991-a6-member-p value (cdr composition)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1991-a6-g-prefix-covered-p (composition index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (and
   (putnam-1991-a6-member-p
    (putnam-1991-a6-g index) composition)
   (if (zp index)
       t
     (putnam-1991-a6-g-prefix-covered-p
      composition (- index 1)))))

;; This bounded search is exactly the source existential k: if the first part
;; is g_k, then k is below that positive first part because g_k >= k+1.
(defun putnam-1991-a6-leading-prefix-p
    (composition index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (equal (car composition)
             (putnam-1991-a6-g index))
      (putnam-1991-a6-g-prefix-covered-p composition index)
    (if (zp index)
        nil
      (putnam-1991-a6-leading-prefix-p
       composition (- index 1)))))

(defun putnam-1991-a6-b-valid-p (composition)
  (and
   (consp composition)
   (putnam-1991-a6-nonincreasing-p composition)
   (putnam-1991-a6-all-g-values-p composition)
   (putnam-1991-a6-leading-prefix-p
    composition (car composition))))

(defun putnam-1991-a6-count-a-codes
    (n remaining-codes)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-codes)))
  (if (zp remaining-codes)
      0
    (let* ((code (- remaining-codes 1))
           (composition
            (putnam-1991-a6-mask-to-composition n code)))
      (+
       (if (putnam-1991-a6-a-valid-p composition) 1 0)
       (putnam-1991-a6-count-a-codes n code)))))

(defun putnam-1991-a6-count-b-codes
    (n remaining-codes)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-codes)))
  (if (zp remaining-codes)
      0
    (let* ((code (- remaining-codes 1))
           (composition
            (putnam-1991-a6-mask-to-composition n code)))
      (+
       (if (putnam-1991-a6-b-valid-p composition) 1 0)
       (putnam-1991-a6-count-b-codes n code)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1991-a6-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (<= 1 n))
   (equal
    (putnam-1991-a6-count-a-codes
     n (expt 2 (- n 1)))
    (putnam-1991-a6-count-b-codes
     n (expt 2 (- n 1))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1991_a6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
-- putnambench__agda__putnam_1991_a6: equality of two counts of positive
-- integer compositions governed by gap and recurrence conditions.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1991A6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_)

infix 4 _<N_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finToNat :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc index) =
  suc (finToNat index)

sumFin :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Nat) ->
  Nat
sumFin {zero} terms =
  zero
sumFin {suc n} terms =
  terms fzero + sumFin (\ index -> terms (fsuc index))

record Composition : Set where
  constructor composition
  field
    length : Nat
    terms  : Nat -> Nat

open Composition

record SameComposition
  (left right : Composition) :
  Set where

  field
    same-length :
      length left == length right
    same-terms :
      (index : Nat) ->
      terms left index == terms right index

record HasExtensionalCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (equivalent : A -> A -> Set)
  (member : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> equivalent item (enumerate index))
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      equivalent (enumerate left-index) (enumerate right-index) ->
      left-index == right-index

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

PositiveCompositionOf :
  Nat ->
  Composition ->
  Set
PositiveCompositionOf n parts =
  one <=N length parts
  and
  ((index : Nat) ->
    index <N length parts ->
    zero <N terms parts index)
  and
  ((index : Nat) ->
    length parts <=N index ->
    terms parts index == zero)
  and
  sumFin {n = length parts}
    (\ index ->
      terms parts (finToNat index))
  == n

StrongGap :
  Composition ->
  Set
StrongGap parts =
  ((index : Nat) ->
    index <N (length parts - two) ->
    terms parts (index + one) + terms parts (index + two)
      <N terms parts index)
  and
  (one <N length parts ->
    terms parts (length parts - one)
      <N terms parts (length parts - two))

Nonincreasing :
  Composition ->
  Set
Nonincreasing parts =
  (index : Nat) ->
  index <N (length parts - one) ->
  terms parts (index + one) <=N terms parts index

UsesSequence :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Composition ->
  Set
UsesSequence g parts =
  (index : Nat) ->
  index <N length parts ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ sequence-index ->
      terms parts index == g sequence-index)

CoversInitialSegment :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Composition ->
  Set
CoversInitialSegment g parts =
  Exists Nat
    (\ largest-index ->
      terms parts zero == g largest-index
      and
      ((sequence-index : Nat) ->
        sequence-index <=N largest-index ->
        Exists Nat
          (\ part-index ->
            part-index <N length parts
            and
            terms parts part-index == g sequence-index)))

FirstFamily :
  Nat ->
  Composition ->
  Set
FirstFamily n parts =
  PositiveCompositionOf n parts
  and
  StrongGap parts

SecondFamily :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Nat ->
  Composition ->
  Set
SecondFamily g n parts =
  PositiveCompositionOf n parts
  and
  Nonincreasing parts
  and
  UsesSequence g parts
  and
  CoversInitialSegment g parts

RecurrenceSequence :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Set
RecurrenceSequence g =
  g zero == one
  and
  g one == two
  and
  ((index : Nat) ->
    two <=N index ->
    g index ==
      g (index - one) + g (index - two) + one)

FirstFamilyCount :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Set
FirstFamilyCount A =
  (n : Nat) ->
  one <=N n ->
  HasExtensionalCardinality
    SameComposition
    (FirstFamily n)
    (A n)

SecondFamilyCount :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Set
SecondFamilyCount g B =
  (n : Nat) ->
  one <=N n ->
  HasExtensionalCardinality
    SameComposition
    (SecondFamily g n)
    (B n)

putnam-1991-a6 : Set
putnam-1991-a6 =
  (A g B : Nat -> Nat) ->
  FirstFamilyCount A ->
  RecurrenceSequence g ->
  SecondFamilyCount g B ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  one <=N n ->
  A n == B n

title: putnam_1991_a6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_a6:
  equality between the number of strict-gap compositions of each positive
  integer and the number of ordered compositions using every required term
  of the recurrence 1, 2, 4, ... . This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_1991_a6 =
  ``let nabsum =
      \n (ab : num # (num -> num)).
        1 <= FST ab /\
        (!i : num. i < FST ab ==> 0 < SND ab i) /\
        (!i : num. FST ab <= i ==> SND ab i = 0) /\
        SIGMA (SND ab) (count (FST ab)) = n
    in
    let agt =
      \a : num # (num -> num).
        (!i : num.
           i + 2 < FST a
           ==>
           SND a i > SND a (i + 1) + SND a (i + 2)) /\
        (1 < FST a
         ==>
         SND a (FST a - 2) > SND a (FST a - 1))
    in
    let A =
      \n : num.
        CARD
          {a : num # (num -> num) |
             nabsum n a /\ agt a}
    in
    let bge =
      \b : num # (num -> num).
        !i : num.
          i + 1 < FST b
          ==>
          SND b i >= SND b (i + 1)
    in
    let bg1 =
      \g (b : num # (num -> num)).
        !i : num.
          i < FST b
          ==>
          ?j : num. SND b i = g j
    in
    let bg2 =
      \g (b : num # (num -> num)).
        ?k : num.
          SND b 0 = g k /\
          !j : num.
            j <= k
            ==>
            ?i : num. i < FST b /\ SND b i = g j
    in
    let B =
      \g n.
        CARD
          {b : num # (num -> num) |
             nabsum n b /\ bge b /\ bg1 g b /\ bg2 g b}
    in
      !g : num -> num.
        (g 0 = 1 /\
         g 1 = 2 /\
         (!j : num.
            2 <= j
            ==>
            g j = g (j - 1) + g (j - 2) + 1))
        ==>
        !n : num. 1 <= n ==> A n = B g n``;

title: putnam_1991_a6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1991_a6: equality between two counts of positive-integer
  compositions, one defined by strict next-term inequalities and the other
  by a nonincreasing recurrence-valued representation using every recurrence
  value through its largest term. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  A composition is represented exactly as in the sources by a pair p whose
  first component is its positive length and whose second component is a
  total NN0-indexed NN0-valued function. P91A6Base requires positive entries
  before the length, a zero tail, and the prescribed finite sum.

  P91A6A is the source agt condition. P91A6B combines the source bge, bg1,
  and bg2 conditions: the entries are nonincreasing, every entry is a value
  of g, and if the first entry is g(k), every g(j) for j at most k occurs.
  The final assertion inlines the source definitions of A and B and equates
  the cardinalities for every positive n and every natural-valued g satisfying
  the stated recurrence. All declarations are unproved $a statement
  encodings; this database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c P91A6Base P91A6A P91A6B $.

p91a6-base-syntax $a wff ( P91A6Base n p ) $.
p91a6-a-syntax $a wff ( P91A6A p ) $.
p91a6-b-syntax $a wff ( P91A6B g p ) $.

${
  $d i n p $.

  p91a6-base-definition $a |- (
    P91A6Base n p
  ) <->
  (
    (
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( 1st ` p ) )
        0 < ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` i )
      /\
      A. i e. NN0
        (
          ( 1st ` p ) <_ i
          ->
          ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` i ) = 0
        )
    )
    /\
    (
      sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ ( 1st ` p ) )
        ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` i )
    )
    =
    n
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d i p $.

  p91a6-a-definition $a |- (
    P91A6A p
  ) <->
  (
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( ( 1st ` p ) - 2 ) )
      (
        (
          ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` ( i + 1 ) )
          +
          ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` ( i + 2 ) )
        )
        <
        ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` i )
      )
    /\
    (
      1 < ( 1st ` p )
      ->
      (
        ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` ( ( 1st ` p ) - 1 ) )
        <
        ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` ( ( 1st ` p ) - 2 ) )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d g i j k p $.

  p91a6-b-definition $a |- (
    P91A6B g p
  ) <->
  (
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( ( 1st ` p ) - 1 ) )
      (
        ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` ( i + 1 ) )
        <_
        ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` i )
      )
    /\
    (
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( 1st ` p ) )
        E. j e. NN0
          ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` i ) = ( g ` j )
      /\
      E. k e. NN0
        (
          ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` 0 ) = ( g ` k )
          /\
          A. j e. ( 0 ... k )
            E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( 1st ` p ) )
              ( ( 2nd ` p ) ` i ) = ( g ` j )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d g j n p $.

  putnambench-putnam-1991-a6 $a |-
    A. g e. ( NN0 ^m NN0 )
      (
        (
          ( g ` 0 ) = 1
          /\
          (
            ( g ` 1 ) = 2
            /\
            A. j e. NN0
              (
                2 <_ j
                ->
                ( g ` j )
                =
                (
                  ( ( g ` ( j - 1 ) ) + ( g ` ( j - 2 ) ) )
                  +
                  1
                )
              )
          )
        )
        ->
        A. n e. NN
          (
            #
            `
            {
              p e. ( NN X. ( NN0 ^m NN0 ) ) |

title: putnam_1991_a6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_a6:
% equality between counts of restricted positive-integer compositions and
% recurrence-valued nonincreasing compositions. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1991_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  composition: TYPE =
    [# part_count: nat, parts: natural_sequence #]
  composition_set: TYPE = [composition -> bool]
  composition_enumeration: TYPE = [nat -> composition]

  prefix_sum(values: natural_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      prefix_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  is_positive_sum(n: nat, value: composition): bool =
    part_count(value) >= 1
      AND
        (FORALL (index: nat):
          index < part_count(value) IMPLIES
            parts(value)(index) > 0)
      AND
        (FORALL (index: nat):
          index >= part_count(value) IMPLIES
            parts(value)(index) = 0)
      AND prefix_sum(parts(value), part_count(value)) = n

  satisfies_a_inequalities(value: composition): bool =
    (FORALL (index: nat):
      index < part_count(value) - 2 IMPLIES
        parts(value)(index)
          > parts(value)(index + 1) + parts(value)(index + 2))
      AND
        (part_count(value) > 1 IMPLIES
          parts(value)(part_count(value) - 2)
            > parts(value)(part_count(value) - 1))

  a_compositions(n: nat): composition_set =
    LAMBDA (value: composition):
      is_positive_sum(n, value)
        AND satisfies_a_inequalities(value)

  recurrence_sequence(g: natural_sequence): bool =
    g(0) = 1
      AND g(1) = 2
      AND
        (FORALL (index: nat):
          index >= 2 IMPLIES
            g(index) = g(index - 1) + g(index - 2) + 1)

  is_nonincreasing(value: composition): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < part_count(value) - 1 IMPLIES
        parts(value)(index) >= parts(value)(index + 1)

  uses_recurrence_values(
      g: natural_sequence,
      value: composition): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < part_count(value) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (sequence_index: nat):
          parts(value)(index) = g(sequence_index)

  contains_initial_recurrence_segment(
      g: natural_sequence,
      value: composition): bool =
    EXISTS (largest_index: nat):
      parts(value)(0) = g(largest_index)
        AND
          (FORALL (sequence_index: nat):
            sequence_index <= largest_index IMPLIES
              EXISTS (part_index: nat):
                part_index < part_count(value)
                  AND parts(value)(part_index) = g(sequence_index))

  b_compositions(
      g: natural_sequence,
      n: nat): composition_set =
    LAMBDA (value: composition):
      is_positive_sum(n, value)
        AND is_nonincreasing(value)
        AND uses_recurrence_values(g, value)
        AND contains_initial_recurrence_segment(g, value)

  injective_below(
      enumeration: composition_enumeration,
      cardinality: nat): bool =
    FORALL (left_index, right_index: nat):
      left_index < cardinality
        AND right_index < cardinality
        AND enumeration(left_index) = enumeration(right_index)
      IMPLIES left_index = right_index

  enumerates_exactly(
      enumeration: composition_enumeration,
      values: composition_set,
      cardinality: nat): bool =
    FORALL (value: composition):
      values(value)
        IFF
          EXISTS (position: nat):
            position < cardinality
              AND enumeration(position) = value

  has_cardinality(
      values: composition_set,
      cardinality: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (enumeration: composition_enumeration):
      injective_below(enumeration, cardinality)
        AND enumerates_exactly(enumeration, values, cardinality)

  same_finite_cardinality(
      left_values, right_values: composition_set): bool =
    EXISTS (cardinality: nat):
      has_cardinality(left_values, cardinality)
        AND has_cardinality(right_values, cardinality)

  putnam_1991_a6: bool =
    FORALL (g: natural_sequence):
      recurrence_sequence(g) IMPLIES
        FORALL (n: nat):
          n >= 1 IMPLIES
            same_finite_cardinality(
              a_compositions(n),
              b_compositions(g, n))
END putnam_1991_a6

import Mathlib

open Filter Topology

abbrev putnam_1991_b1_solution : Set ℤ := sorry
-- {A : ℤ | ∃ x > 0, A = x ^ 2}
/--
For each integer $n \geq 0$, let $S(n)=n-m^2$, where $m$ is the greatest integer with $m^2 \leq n$. Define a sequence $(a_k)_{k=0}^\infty$ by $a_0=A$ and $a_{k+1}=a_k+S(a_k)$ for $k \geq 0$. For what positive integers $A$ is this sequence eventually constant?
-/
theorem putnam_1991_b1
  (m S : ℤ → ℤ)
  (A : ℤ)
  (a : ℕ → ℤ)
  (hm : ∀ n, 0 ≤ n → (m n) ^ 2 ≤ n ∧ (∀ m' : ℤ, m' ^ 2 ≤ n → m' ≤ m n))
  (hS : ∀ n, 0 ≤ n → S n = n - (m n) ^ 2)
  (ha : a 0 = A ∧ (∀ k, a (k + 1) = a k + S (a k)))
  (hA : A > 0) :
  (∃ (K : ℕ) (c : ℕ), ∀ k ≥ K, a k = c) ↔ A ∈ putnam_1991_b1_solution :=
sorry

Require Import Nat.
Open Scope nat_scope.
Definition putnam_1991_b1_solution (A: nat) := exists (m: nat), A = pow m 2.
Theorem putnam_1991_b1
    (eS : nat -> nat := fun n => sub n (pow (sqrt n) 2))
    (a_seq := fix a (A k: nat) :=
        match k with
        | O => A
        | S k' => a A k' + eS (a A k')
    end)
    (A : nat)
    (hA : gt A 0)
    : (exists K c : nat, forall k : nat, k >= K -> a_seq A k = c) <-> putnam_1991_b1_solution A.
Proof. Admitted.

Complex_Main
begin

definition putnam_1991_b1_solution :: "nat set" where "putnam_1991_b1_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* {A :: nat. \<exists> x > 0. A = x ^ 2} *)
theorem putnam_1991_b1:
  fixes m :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
    and S :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
    and A :: nat
    and a :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
  defines "m \<equiv> \<lambda> n. GREATEST M :: nat. M ^ 2 \<le> n"
    and "S \<equiv> \<lambda> n. n - (m n) ^ 2"
  assumes ha : "a 0 = A \<and> (\<forall> k :: nat. a (k + 1) = a k + S (a k))"
    and hA : "A > 0"  
  shows "(\<exists> K c :: nat. \<forall> k \<ge> K. a k = c) \<longleftrightarrow> A \<in> putnam_1991_b1_solution"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_1991_b1

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b1:
;; the positive initial values whose square-remainder recurrence is eventually
;; constant are exactly the perfect squares. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; This is floor(sqrt(N)) for natural N, hence the greatest natural M with
;; M^2 <= N.
(defun putnam-1991-b1-floor-sqrt-down (n candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (zp candidate)
      0
    (if (<= (* candidate candidate) n)
        candidate
      (putnam-1991-b1-floor-sqrt-down
       n (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-1991-b1-floor-sqrt (n)
  (if (natp n)
      (putnam-1991-b1-floor-sqrt-down n n)
    0))

(defun putnam-1991-b1-square-remainder (n)
  (if (natp n)
      (let ((root (putnam-1991-b1-floor-sqrt n)))
        (- n (* root root)))
    0))

;; The source assumptions uniquely determine the sequence from A, so this
;; recursion eliminates the arbitrary source functions m, S, and a
;; bidirectionally.
(defun putnam-1991-b1-sequence-value (a index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (or (not (natp a))
          (not (natp index)))
      0
    (if (zp index)
        a
      (let ((previous
             (putnam-1991-b1-sequence-value
              a (- index 1))))
        (+ previous
           (putnam-1991-b1-square-remainder previous))))))

;; For a positive natural value, this is equivalent to the source solution-set
;; condition that the value is the square of a positive integer.
(defun putnam-1991-b1-perfect-square-p (value)
  (and
   (natp value)
   (let ((root (putnam-1991-b1-floor-sqrt value)))
     (equal (* root root) value))))

(defun putnam-1991-b1-fixed-step-p (a index)
  (equal
   (putnam-1991-b1-sequence-value a (+ index 1))
   (putnam-1991-b1-sequence-value a index)))

;; Because the recurrence is deterministic, it is eventually constant iff
;; some consecutive pair is equal. The first implication is the universal
;; form of "(exists K, fixed-step(A,K)) implies square(A)"; K is not an
;; external existential witness. The reverse implication uses the canonical
;; internal witness K=0, since a square has zero square remainder.
(defun putnambench-putnam-1991-b1-statement (a k)
  (implies
   (and (posp a)
        (natp k))
   (and
    (implies
     (putnam-1991-b1-fixed-step-p a k)
     (putnam-1991-b1-perfect-square-p a))
    (implies
     (putnam-1991-b1-perfect-square-p a)
     (putnam-1991-b1-fixed-step-p a 0)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b1:
-- a positive-integer square-remainder recurrence is eventually constant
-- exactly when its initial value is a perfect square. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

GreatestSquareRootFunction : (Nat -> Nat) -> Set
GreatestSquareRootFunction m =
  (n : Nat) ->
  ((m n * m n) <=N n)
  and
  ((r : Nat) ->
    (r * r) <=N n ->
    r <=N m n)

SquareRemainderFunction :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Set
SquareRemainderFunction m S =
  (n : Nat) ->
  S n == n - (m n * m n)

FollowsRecurrence :
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Set
FollowsRecurrence A S a =
  a zero == A
  and
  ((k : Nat) ->
    a (suc k) == a k + S (a k))

EventuallyConstant : (Nat -> Nat) -> Set
EventuallyConstant a =
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ constant ->
          (k : Nat) ->
          cutoff <=N k ->
          a k == constant))

PerfectSquare : Nat -> Set
PerfectSquare A =
  Exists Nat
    (\ root ->
      A == root * root)

putnam-1991-b1 : Set
putnam-1991-b1 =
  (m S : Nat -> Nat) ->
  (A : Nat) ->
  (a : Nat -> Nat) ->
  GreatestSquareRootFunction m ->
  SquareRemainderFunction m S ->
  FollowsRecurrence A S a ->
  Positive A ->
  Iff
    (EventuallyConstant a)
    (PerfectSquare A)

content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b1:
% the positive initial values for which the square-remainder recurrence is
% eventually constant are exactly the perfect squares. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1991_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  greatest_square_root(m: natural_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      m(n) ^ 2 <= n
        AND FORALL (root: nat):
          root ^ 2 <= n IMPLIES root <= m(n)

  square_remainder(
      m, remainder: natural_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n = m(n) ^ 2 + remainder(n)

  follows_recurrence(
      remainder: natural_sequence,
      initial: nat,
      a: natural_sequence): bool =
    a(0) = initial
      AND FORALL (k: nat):
        a(k + 1) = a(k) + remainder(a(k))

  eventually_constant(a: natural_sequence): bool =
    EXISTS (cutoff, value: nat):
      FORALL (k: nat):
        cutoff <= k IMPLIES a(k) = value

  perfect_square(value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (root: nat):
      value = root ^ 2

  putnam_1991_b1: bool =
    FORALL
        (m, remainder: natural_sequence),
        (initial: nat),
        (a: natural_sequence):
      (greatest_square_root(m)
        AND square_remainder(m, remainder)
        AND follows_recurrence(remainder, initial, a)
        AND initial > 0)
      IMPLIES
        (eventually_constant(a) IFF perfect_square(initial))
END putnam_1991_b1

    (fgdiff : forall x : R, ex_derive f x /\ ex_derive g x)
    (fadd : forall x y : R, f (x + y) = f x * f y - g x * g y)
    (gadd : forall x y : R, g (x + y) = f x * g y + g x * f y)
    : Derive f 0 = 0 -> forall x : R, pow (f x) 2 + pow (g x) 2 = 1.
Proof. Admitted.

theory putnam_1991_b2 imports
Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Derivative"
begin

theorem putnam_1991_b2:
  fixes f g :: "real \<Rightarrow> real"
  assumes fgnconst: "\<not>(\<exists> c :: real. f = (\<lambda> x. c) \<or> g = (\<lambda> x. c))"
  and fgdiff: "f differentiable_on UNIV \<and> g differentiable_on UNIV"
  and fadd: "\<forall> x y :: real. f (x + y) = f x * f y - g x * g y"
  and gadd: "\<forall> x y :: real. g (x + y) = f x * g y + g x * f y"

title: putnam_1991_b2
putnam_1991_b2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b2:
;; two nonconstant differentiable real functions satisfying the sine-cosine
;; addition laws have f(x)^2 + g(x)^2 = 1 for every real x when f'(0) = 0.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The scalar context is a Dedekind-complete ordered field, hence the real
;; field up to ordered-field isomorphism. Arbitrary subsets and real-valued
;; functions are tame APPLY$ function objects. DEFUN-SK keeps every unbounded
;; universal and existential quantifier internal to the statement. The
;; derivative predicate is the usual epsilon-delta definition, so under the
;; explicit differentiability assumption its zero derivative clause is
;; equivalent to the source's totalized deriv f 0 = 0.

(defun p91b2-member-p (carrier x)
  (if (apply$ carrier (list x)) t nil))

(defun p91b2-unary-value (function x)
  (apply$ function (list x)))

(defun p91b2-binary-value (function x y)
  (apply$ function (list x y)))

(defun-sk p91b2-valid-set-p (carrier set)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (apply$ set (list x))
     (p91b2-member-p carrier x))))

(defun-sk p91b2-real-function-p (carrier function)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p91b2-member-p carrier x)
     (p91b2-member-p
      carrier
      (p91b2-unary-value function x)))))

(defun-sk p91b2-field-laws-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p91b2-member-p carrier x)
      (p91b2-member-p carrier y)
      (p91b2-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (p91b2-member-p carrier
                    (p91b2-binary-value add x y))
      (p91b2-member-p carrier
                    (p91b2-binary-value multiply x y))
      (p91b2-member-p carrier
                    (p91b2-unary-value negate x))
      (p91b2-member-p carrier
                    (p91b2-unary-value inverse x))
      (equal
       (p91b2-binary-value
        add (p91b2-binary-value add x y) z)
       (p91b2-binary-value
        add x (p91b2-binary-value add y z)))
      (equal (p91b2-binary-value add x y)
             (p91b2-binary-value add y x))
      (equal (p91b2-binary-value add x zero) x)
      (equal
       (p91b2-binary-value
        add x (p91b2-unary-value negate x))
       zero)
      (equal
       (p91b2-binary-value
        multiply (p91b2-binary-value multiply x y) z)
       (p91b2-binary-value
        multiply x (p91b2-binary-value multiply y z)))
      (equal (p91b2-binary-value multiply x y)
             (p91b2-binary-value multiply y x))
      (equal (p91b2-binary-value multiply x one) x)
      (implies
       (equal x zero)
       (equal (p91b2-unary-value inverse x) zero))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal
        (p91b2-binary-value
         multiply x (p91b2-unary-value inverse x))
        one))
      (equal
       (p91b2-binary-value
        multiply x (p91b2-binary-value add y z))
       (p91b2-binary-value
        add
        (p91b2-binary-value multiply x y)
        (p91b2-binary-value multiply x z)))))))

(defun-sk p91b2-order-laws-p
    (carrier add multiply zero less)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p91b2-member-p carrier x)
      (p91b2-member-p carrier y)
      (p91b2-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (not (p91b2-binary-value less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (p91b2-binary-value less x y)
       (p91b2-binary-value less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (p91b2-binary-value less x y)
        (p91b2-binary-value less y z))
       (p91b2-binary-value less x z))
      (implies
       (p91b2-binary-value less x y)
       (p91b2-binary-value
        less
        (p91b2-binary-value add x z)
        (p91b2-binary-value add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (p91b2-binary-value less zero x)
        (p91b2-binary-value less zero y))
       (p91b2-binary-value
        less zero (p91b2-binary-value multiply x y)))))))

(defun-sk p91b2-set-nonempty-p (carrier set)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (p91b2-member-p carrier x)
     (apply$ set (list x)))))

(defun-sk p91b2-upper-bound-p
    (carrier less set bound)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (p91b2-member-p carrier x)
      (apply$ set (list x)))
     (not (p91b2-binary-value less bound x)))))

(defun-sk p91b2-bounded-above-p
    (carrier less set)
  (exists (bound)
    (and
     (p91b2-member-p carrier bound)
     (p91b2-upper-bound-p
      carrier less set bound))))

(defun-sk p91b2-least-upper-bound-p
    (carrier less set supremum)
  (forall (bound)
    (implies
     (and
      (p91b2-member-p carrier bound)
      (p91b2-upper-bound-p carrier less set bound))
     (not (p91b2-binary-value less bound supremum)))))

(defun p91b2-supremum-p
    (carrier less set supremum)
  (and
   (p91b2-member-p carrier supremum)
   (p91b2-upper-bound-p carrier less set supremum)
   (p91b2-least-upper-bound-p
    carrier less set supremum)))

(defun-sk p91b2-has-supremum-p
    (carrier less set)
  (exists (supremum)
    (p91b2-supremum-p
     carrier less set supremum)))

(defun-sk p91b2-dedekind-complete-p
    (carrier less)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (tamep-functionp set)
      (p91b2-valid-set-p carrier set)
      (p91b2-set-nonempty-p carrier set)
      (p91b2-bounded-above-p carrier less set))
     (p91b2-has-supremum-p carrier less set))))

(defun p91b2-real-field-p
    (carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse less)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp add)
   (tamep-functionp multiply)
   (tamep-functionp negate)
   (tamep-functionp inverse)
   (tamep-functionp less)
   (p91b2-member-p carrier zero)
   (p91b2-member-p carrier one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (p91b2-field-laws-p
    carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one)
   (p91b2-order-laws-p
    carrier add multiply zero less)
   (p91b2-binary-value less zero one)
   (p91b2-dedekind-complete-p carrier less)))

;; The outer context contains one eight-entry real-field presentation.

(defun p91b2-field-context (ctx)
  (car ctx))

(defun p91b2-r-carrier (ctx)
  (nth 0 (p91b2-field-context ctx)))

(defun p91b2-r-zero (ctx)
  (nth 1 (p91b2-field-context ctx)))

(defun p91b2-r-one (ctx)
  (nth 2 (p91b2-field-context ctx)))

(defun p91b2-r-add (ctx)
  (nth 3 (p91b2-field-context ctx)))

(defun p91b2-r-mul (ctx)
  (nth 4 (p91b2-field-context ctx)))

(defun p91b2-r-neg (ctx)
  (nth 5 (p91b2-field-context ctx)))

(defun p91b2-r-inv (ctx)
  (nth 6 (p91b2-field-context ctx)))

(defun p91b2-r-lt (ctx)
  (nth 7 (p91b2-field-context ctx)))

(defun p91b2-field-context-p (field-context)
  (and
   (true-listp field-context)
   (equal (len field-context) 8)
   (p91b2-real-field-p
    (nth 0 field-context)
    (nth 1 field-context)
    (nth 2 field-context)
    (nth 3 field-context)
    (nth 4 field-context)
    (nth 5 field-context)
    (nth 6 field-context)
    (nth 7 field-context))))

(defun p91b2-r-add-value (ctx x y)
  (p91b2-binary-value (p91b2-r-add ctx) x y))

(defun p91b2-r-neg-value (ctx x)
  (p91b2-unary-value (p91b2-r-neg ctx) x))

(defun p91b2-r-sub-value (ctx x y)
  (p91b2-r-add-value
   ctx x (p91b2-r-neg-value ctx y)))

(defun p91b2-r-mul-value (ctx x y)
  (p91b2-binary-value (p91b2-r-mul ctx) x y))

(defun p91b2-r-lt-p (ctx x y)
  (if (p91b2-binary-value (p91b2-r-lt ctx) x y)
      t nil))

(defun p91b2-r-le-p (ctx x y)
  (not (p91b2-r-lt-p ctx y x)))

(defun p91b2-r-abs-value (ctx x)
  (if (p91b2-r-lt-p ctx x (p91b2-r-zero ctx))
      (p91b2-r-neg-value ctx x)
    x))

(defun p91b2-positive-real-p (ctx x)
  (and
   (p91b2-member-p (p91b2-r-carrier ctx) x)
   (p91b2-r-lt-p ctx (p91b2-r-zero ctx) x)))

;; HasDerivAt in epsilon-delta form:
;; |f(z)-f(x)-d(z-x)| <= epsilon |z-x| near x.

(defun-sk p91b2-derivative-neighborhood-p
    (ctx function derivative x epsilon radius)
  (forall (z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p91b2-member-p (p91b2-r-carrier ctx) z)
      (p91b2-r-lt-p
       ctx
       (p91b2-r-abs-value
        ctx (p91b2-r-sub-value ctx z x))
       radius))
     (p91b2-r-le-p
      ctx
      (p91b2-r-abs-value
       ctx
       (p91b2-r-sub-value
        ctx
        (p91b2-r-sub-value
         ctx
         (p91b2-unary-value function z)
         (p91b2-unary-value function x))
        (p91b2-r-mul-value
         ctx derivative
         (p91b2-r-sub-value ctx z x))))
      (p91b2-r-mul-value
       ctx epsilon
       (p91b2-r-abs-value
        ctx (p91b2-r-sub-value ctx z x)))))))

(defun-sk p91b2-derivative-radius-exists-p
    (ctx function derivative x epsilon)
  (exists (radius)
    (and
     (p91b2-positive-real-p ctx radius)
     (p91b2-derivative-neighborhood-p
      ctx function derivative x epsilon radius))))

(defun-sk p91b2-has-derivative-at-p
    (ctx function derivative x)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p91b2-positive-real-p ctx epsilon)
     (p91b2-derivative-radius-exists-p
      ctx function derivative x epsilon))))

(defun-sk p91b2-derivative-exists-at-p
    (ctx function x)
  (exists (derivative)
    (and
     (p91b2-member-p
      (p91b2-r-carrier ctx) derivative)
     (p91b2-has-derivative-at-p
      ctx function derivative x))))

(defun-sk p91b2-differentiable-p (ctx function)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p91b2-member-p (p91b2-r-carrier ctx) x)
     (p91b2-derivative-exists-at-p
      ctx function x))))

(defun p91b2-context-p (ctx)
  (and
   (true-listp ctx)
   (equal (len ctx) 1)
   (p91b2-field-context-p (p91b2-field-context ctx))))

(defun-sk p91b2-constant-with-value-p
    (ctx function constant)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p91b2-member-p (p91b2-r-carrier ctx) x)
     (equal
      (p91b2-unary-value function x)
      constant))))

(defun-sk p91b2-constant-function-p (ctx function)
  (exists (constant)
    (and
     (p91b2-member-p
      (p91b2-r-carrier ctx) constant)
     (p91b2-constant-with-value-p
      ctx function constant))))

(defun-sk p91b2-addition-laws-p (ctx f g)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (p91b2-member-p (p91b2-r-carrier ctx) x)
      (p91b2-member-p (p91b2-r-carrier ctx) y))
     (and
      (equal
       (p91b2-unary-value
        f (p91b2-r-add-value ctx x y))
       (p91b2-r-sub-value
        ctx
        (p91b2-r-mul-value
         ctx
         (p91b2-unary-value f x)
         (p91b2-unary-value f y))
        (p91b2-r-mul-value
         ctx
         (p91b2-unary-value g x)
         (p91b2-unary-value g y))))
      (equal
       (p91b2-unary-value
        g (p91b2-r-add-value ctx x y))
       (p91b2-r-add-value
        ctx
        (p91b2-r-mul-value
         ctx
         (p91b2-unary-value f x)
         (p91b2-unary-value g y))
        (p91b2-r-mul-value
         ctx
         (p91b2-unary-value g x)
         (p91b2-unary-value f y))))))))

(defun-sk p91b2-unit-circle-identity-p (ctx f g)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p91b2-member-p (p91b2-r-carrier ctx) x)
     (equal
      (p91b2-r-add-value
       ctx
       (p91b2-r-mul-value
        ctx
        (p91b2-unary-value f x)
        (p91b2-unary-value f x))
       (p91b2-r-mul-value
        ctx
        (p91b2-unary-value g x)
        (p91b2-unary-value g x)))
      (p91b2-r-one ctx)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1991-b2-statement (ctx f g)
  (implies
   (and
    (p91b2-context-p ctx)
    (tamep-functionp f)
    (tamep-functionp g)
    (p91b2-real-function-p
     (p91b2-r-carrier ctx) f)
    (p91b2-real-function-p
     (p91b2-r-carrier ctx) g)
    (not (p91b2-constant-function-p ctx f))
    (not (p91b2-constant-function-p ctx g))
    (p91b2-differentiable-p ctx f)
    (p91b2-differentiable-p ctx g)
    (p91b2-addition-laws-p ctx f g)
    (p91b2-has-derivative-at-p
     ctx f (p91b2-r-zero ctx) (p91b2-r-zero ctx)))
   (p91b2-unit-circle-identity-p ctx f g)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1991_b2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b2:
-- nonconstant differentiable real functions satisfying the complex addition
-- laws have unit squared norm when the derivative of f at zero is zero.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
differenceQuotient reals function point x =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals (function x) (function point))
    (subtract reals x point)

DerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeAt {R} reals function point derivative =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        x != point ->
        CloseTo reals derivative epsilon
          (differenceQuotient reals function point x)))

Differentiable :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
Differentiable {R} reals function =
  (x : R) ->
  Exists R
    (\ derivative ->
      DerivativeAt reals function x derivative)

Constant :
  {R : Set} ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
Constant {R} function constant =
  (x : R) ->
  function x == constant

NonconstantPair :
  {R : Set} ->
  (R -> R) ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
NonconstantPair {R} f g =
  Not
    (Exists R
      (\ constant ->
        Constant f constant
        or
        Constant g constant))

module Putnam1991B2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  AdditionLaws :
    (R -> R) ->
    (R -> R) ->
    Set
  AdditionLaws f g =
    ((x y : R) ->
      f (add reals x y) ==
      subtract reals
        (multiply reals (f x) (f y))
        (multiply reals (g x) (g y)))
    and
    ((x y : R) ->
      g (add reals x y) ==
      add reals
        (multiply reals (f x) (g y))
        (multiply reals (g x) (f y)))

  UnitSquaredNorm :
    (R -> R) ->
    (R -> R) ->
    Set
  UnitSquaredNorm f g =
    (x : R) ->
    add reals
      (square reals (f x))
      (square reals (g x))
    ==
    oneR reals

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (f g : R -> R) ->
    NonconstantPair f g ->
    (Differentiable reals f and Differentiable reals g) ->
    AdditionLaws f g ->
    DerivativeAt reals f (zeroR reals) (zeroR reals) ->
    UnitSquaredNorm f g

putnam-1991-b2 : Set1
putnam-1991-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1991B2Statement.proposition reals

(*

  nonconstant differentiable real functions satisfying the complex addition
  laws have unit squared norm everywhere when the derivative of the first
  function vanishes at zero. This file contains no proof.

open realTheory limTheory;

val putnam_1991_b2 =
  ``!f g : real -> real.
      ~(?c : real.
          f = (\x : real. c) \/
          g = (\x : real. c)) /\
      (!x : real.
         f differentiable x /\
         g differentiable x) /\
      (!x y : real.
         f (x + y) = f x * f y - g x * g y) /\
      (!x y : real.
         g (x + y) = f x * g y + g x * f y)

       ==>
       !x : real. f x pow 2 + g x pow 2 = 1)``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1991_b2: globally differentiable nonconstant real functions obeying
  the complex multiplication addition laws have unit squared norm everywhere
  when the derivative of the first function at zero is zero. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  RR ^m RR is the class of total real-valued functions. Containment of RR in
  dom ( RR _D f ) and dom ( RR _D g ) expresses differentiability everywhere.
  Equality with x e. RR |-> c is equality with a constant real function, so
  the negated existential says that neither f nor g is constant. The two
  addition identities and the unit-norm conclusion are stated pointwise over
  all real inputs. The final declaration is one unproved $a statement.
$)

${
  $d c f g x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-1991-b2 $a |-
    A. f e. ( RR ^m RR )
    A. g e. ( RR ^m RR )
      (
        (
          (
            -. E. c e. RR
              (
                f = ( x e. RR |-> c )
                \/
                g = ( x e. RR |-> c )
              )
            /\
            (
              RR C_ dom ( RR _D f )
              /\
              RR C_ dom ( RR _D g )
            )
          )
          /\
          (
            A. x e. RR A. y e. RR
              ( f ` ( x + y ) )
              =
              (
                ( ( f ` x ) x. ( f ` y ) )
                -
                ( ( g ` x ) x. ( g ` y ) )
              )
            /\
            A. x e. RR A. y e. RR
              ( g ` ( x + y ) )
              =
              (
                ( ( f ` x ) x. ( g ` y ) )
                +
                ( ( g ` x ) x. ( f ` y ) )
              )
          )
        )
        ->
        (
          ( ( RR _D f ) ` 0 ) = 0
          ->
          A. x e. RR
            (
              ( ( f ` x ) ^ 2 )
              +
              ( ( g ` x ) ^ 2 )
            )
            =
            1
        )
      )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b2:
% nonconstant globally differentiable real functions satisfying the complex
% addition formulas have unit squared modulus everywhere if f'(0) is zero.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_1991_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  has_derivative_at(
      function_value: real_function,
      derivative, point: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (increment: real):
          (NOT (increment = 0) AND abs(increment) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                function_value(point + increment)
                  - function_value(point)
                  - derivative * increment)
                < epsilon_value * abs(increment)

  differentiable_at(
      function_value: real_function,
      point: real): bool =
    EXISTS (derivative: real):
      has_derivative_at(function_value, derivative, point)

  differentiable(function_value: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (point: real):
      differentiable_at(function_value, point)

  derivative_value(
      function_value: real_function,
      point: real): real =
    IF differentiable_at(function_value, point) THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (derivative: real):
          has_derivative_at(
            function_value, derivative, point))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  putnam_1991_b2: bool =
    FORALL (f, g: real_function):
      ((NOT EXISTS (constant_value: real):
          f = (LAMBDA (x: real): constant_value)
            OR g = (LAMBDA (x: real): constant_value))
        AND differentiable(f)
        AND differentiable(g)
        AND (FORALL (x, y: real):
          f(x + y) = f(x) * f(y) - g(x) * g(y))
        AND (FORALL (x, y: real):
          g(x + y) = f(x) * g(y) + g(x) * f(y)))
      IMPLIES
        (derivative_value(f, 0) = 0
          IMPLIES
            FORALL (x: real):
              f(x) ^ 2 + g(x) ^ 2 = 1)
END putnam_1991_b2

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b4:
;; for every odd prime p, a binomial sum from 0 through p is congruent to
;; 2^p + 1 modulo p^2. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-1991-b4-no-divisor-through-p (p candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (or (not (natp candidate))
          (<= candidate 1))
      t
    (and
     (not (equal (mod p candidate) 0))
     (putnam-1991-b4-no-divisor-through-p
      p (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-1991-b4-prime-p (p)
  (and
   (natp p)
   (< 1 p)
   (putnam-1991-b4-no-divisor-through-p
    p (- p 1))))

;; Pascal recursion represents the natural-number binomial coefficient.
(defun putnam-1991-b4-binomial-coefficient (n k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (or (zp k)
          (zp n))
      (if (zp k) 1 0)
    (+ (putnam-1991-b4-binomial-coefficient (- n 1) k)
       (putnam-1991-b4-binomial-coefficient
        (- n 1) (- k 1)))))

;; Sum choose(p,j) * choose(p+j,j) for j = 0,...,term-count-1.
(defun putnam-1991-b4-binomial-sum (p term-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix term-count)))
  (if (zp term-count)
      0
    (let ((j (- term-count 1)))
      (+
       (*
        (putnam-1991-b4-binomial-coefficient p j)
        (putnam-1991-b4-binomial-coefficient (+ p j) j))
       (putnam-1991-b4-binomial-sum p j)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1991-b4-statement (p)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp p)
    (putnam-1991-b4-prime-p p)
    (equal (mod p 2) 1))
   (equal
    (mod
     (putnam-1991-b4-binomial-sum p (+ p 1))
     (expt p 2))
    (mod
     (+ (expt 2 p) 1)
     (expt p 2)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1991_b4

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b4:
-- for every odd prime p, the sum from j = 0 through p of C(p,j) C(p+j,j)
-- is congruent to 2^p + 1 modulo p^2. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1991B4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; mod-helper)

infix 4 _<=_ _divides_
infixr 2 _or_

data _<=_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<= : {n : Nat} -> zero <= n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> suc m <= suc n

record _divides_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    division-equation : dividend == divisor * quotient

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

record Odd (n : Nat) : Set where
  field
    half : Nat
    odd-equation : n == two * half + one

record Prime (p : Nat) : Set where
  field
    at-least-two : two <= p
    only-trivial-divisors :
      (d : Nat) ->
      d divides p ->
      (d == one) or (d == p)

choose : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
choose n zero =
  one
choose zero (suc k) =
  zero
choose (suc n) (suc k) =
  choose n (suc k) + choose n k

sumThrough : Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat
sumThrough zero term =
  term zero
sumThrough (suc n) term =
  sumThrough n term + term (suc n)

power : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
power base zero =
  one
power base (suc exponent) =
  base * power base exponent

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero =
  numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

ModEq : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Set
ModEq modulus lhs rhs =
  naturalMod lhs modulus == naturalMod rhs modulus

binomialSum : Nat -> Nat
binomialSum p =
  sumThrough p
    (\ j -> choose p j * choose (p + j) j)

putnam-1991-b4 : Set
putnam-1991-b4 =
  (p : Nat) ->
  Odd p ->
  Prime p ->
  ModEq
    (power p two)
    (binomialSum p)
    (power two p + one)

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b4:
% for every odd prime p, a finite sum of products of binomial coefficients
% has residue 2^p + 1 modulo p^2. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1991_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  nat_divides(divisor: posnat, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat): value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value

  nat_congruent(left, right, modulus: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (offset: int):
      (left :: int) - (right :: int) = (modulus :: int) * offset

  binomial_coefficient(n, k: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF k = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSIF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k - 1)
        + binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  binomial_product_sum(p, count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET j: nat = count - 1 IN
        binomial_product_sum(p, count - 1)
          + binomial_coefficient(p, j)
              * binomial_coefficient(p + j, j)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  putnam_1991_b4: bool =
    FORALL (p: nat):
      (prime_nat(p) AND mod(p, 2) = 1)
        IMPLIES
          nat_congruent(
            binomial_product_sum(p, p + 1),
            2 ^ p + 1,
            p ^ 2)
END putnam_1991_b4

Theorem putnam_1991_b5 
    (p: nat)
    (hp : odd p = true /\ prime (Z.of_nat p))
    (A: Ensemble Z := fun z => exists (m: 'I_p), z = Z.of_nat (pow (nat_of_ord m) 2) mod (Z.of_nat p))

    (C : Ensemble Z := Intersection Z A B)
    : cardinal Z C (putnam_1991_b5_solution p).

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b5:
;; for an odd prime p, the intersection of the quadratic residues modulo p
;; with their translates by one has floor(p/4) + 1 elements. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Every element of ZMod p has a unique representative in {0,...,p-1}.
;; The searches below therefore express the two internal existential
;; witnesses, and the final recursion counts exactly the source intersection.

(defun putnam-1991-b5-no-divisor-through-p (p candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (or (not (natp candidate))
          (<= candidate 1))
      t
    (and
     (not (equal (mod p candidate) 0))
     (putnam-1991-b5-no-divisor-through-p
      p (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-1991-b5-prime-p (p)
  (and
   (natp p)
   (< 1 p)
   (putnam-1991-b5-no-divisor-through-p
    p (- p 1))))

;; Search x = 0,...,p-1 for z = x^2 + OFFSET modulo p.
(defun putnam-1991-b5-residue-witness-p
    (z p offset witness-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix witness-count)))
  (if (or (not (posp p))
          (zp witness-count))
      nil
    (let ((x (- witness-count 1)))
      (or
       (equal z (mod (+ (* x x) offset) p))
       (putnam-1991-b5-residue-witness-p
        z p offset x)))))

(defun putnam-1991-b5-intersection-member-p (z p)
  (and
   (natp z)
   (< z p)
   (putnam-1991-b5-residue-witness-p z p 0 p)
   (putnam-1991-b5-residue-witness-p z p 1 p)))

(defun putnam-1991-b5-intersection-count-through
    (p residue-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix residue-count)))
  (if (or (not (posp p))
          (zp residue-count))
      0
    (let ((z (- residue-count 1)))
      (+
       (if (putnam-1991-b5-intersection-member-p z p)
           1
         0)
       (putnam-1991-b5-intersection-count-through p z)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1991-b5-statement (p)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp p)
    (putnam-1991-b5-prime-p p)
    (equal (mod p 2) 1))
   (equal
    (putnam-1991-b5-intersection-count-through p p)
    (+ (floor p 4) 1))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b5:
-- for every odd prime p, the residue classes modulo p that are both a square
-- and one more than a square have cardinality p / 4 + 1. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)

infix 4 _<=_ _<_ _divides_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <= n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> suc m <= suc n

_<_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m < n =
  suc m <= n

record _divides_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    division-equation : dividend == divisor * quotient

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

three : Nat
three =
  suc two

four : Nat
four =
  suc three

record Odd (n : Nat) : Set where
  field
    half : Nat
    odd-equation : n == two * half + one

record Prime (p : Nat) : Set where
  field
    at-least-two : two <= p
    only-trivial-divisors :
      (d : Nat) ->
      d divides p ->
      (d == one) or (d == p)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> item == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

naturalDiv : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero =
  zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero =
  numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

ModEq : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Set
ModEq modulus lhs rhs =
  naturalMod lhs modulus == naturalMod rhs modulus

IsSquareResidue : Nat -> Nat -> Set
IsSquareResidue p z =
  Exists Nat
    (\ x ->
      x < p
      and
      ModEq p z (x * x))

IsOneMoreThanSquareResidue : Nat -> Nat -> Set
IsOneMoreThanSquareResidue p z =
  Exists Nat
    (\ y ->
      y < p
      and
      ModEq p z (y * y + one))

QuadraticIntersection : Nat -> Nat -> Set
QuadraticIntersection p z =
  z < p
  and
  IsSquareResidue p z
  and
  IsOneMoreThanSquareResidue p z

putnam-1991-b5-solution : Nat -> Nat
putnam-1991-b5-solution p =
  naturalDiv p four + one

putnam-1991-b5 : Set
putnam-1991-b5 =
  (p : Nat) ->
  Odd p ->
  Prime p ->
  HasCardinality
    (QuadraticIntersection p)
    (putnam-1991-b5-solution p)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1991_b5:
  the number of residue classes modulo an odd prime that are both a square
  and one more than a square. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_1991_b5 =
  ``!p : num.
      ODD p /\ prime p
      ==>
      CARD
        ({z : num |
            z < p /\
            ?x : num. x < p /\ z = (x EXP 2) MOD p}
         INTER
         {z : num |
            z < p /\
            ?y : num. y < p /\ z = (y EXP 2 + 1) MOD p}) =
      p DIV 4 + 1``;

title: putnam_1991_b5

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1991_b5: the number of residue classes modulo an odd prime that
  are both a square and one more than a square. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  Prime is SetMM's class of natural primes, and ( 0 ..^ p ) is the standard
  set of representatives {0,...,p-1}. The two restricted classes therefore
  represent exactly the square residues and the residues that are one more
  than a square. This is the representative-set presentation used directly
  by Isabelle and Rocq, and reduction to standard representatives gives a
  bijection with Lean's ZMod p presentation.

  For odd p, floor(p/4) + 1 equals ceiling(p/4), so the right side is the
  explicit Rocq solution and the solution described in the Lean and Isabelle
  source comments. The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus
  statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d p x y z $.

  putnambench-putnam-1991-b5 $a |- A. p e. Prime
    (
      ( p mod 2 ) = 1
      ->
      (
        #
        `
        (
          {
            z e. ( 0 ..^ p ) |
            E. x e. ( 0 ..^ p )
              z = ( ( x ^ 2 ) mod p )
          }
          i^i
          {
            z e. ( 0 ..^ p ) |
            E. y e. ( 0 ..^ p )
              z = ( ( ( y ^ 2 ) + 1 ) mod p )
          }
        )
      )
      =
      ( ( |_ ` ( p / 4 ) ) + 1 )
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1991_b5

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1991_b5:
% for every odd prime p, the common residues of a square and one more than a
% square modulo p have cardinality floor(p / 4) + 1. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1991_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[nat]

  nat_divides(divisor: posnat, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat): value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value

  odd_nat(value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (half: nat): value = 2 * half + 1

  nat_congruent(left, right, modulus: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (offset: int):
      (left :: int) - (right :: int) = (modulus :: int) * offset

  common_quadratic_residue(p, z: nat): bool =
    z < p
      AND EXISTS (x: nat):
        x < p
          AND nat_congruent(z, x ^ 2, p)
      AND EXISTS (y: nat):
        y < p
          AND nat_congruent(z, y ^ 2 + 1, p)

  putnam_1991_b5_solution(p: nat): nat =
    ndiv(p, 4) + 1

  putnam_1991_b5: bool =
    FORALL (p: nat):
      (prime_nat(p) AND odd_nat(p))
        IMPLIES
          EXISTS (solutions: finite_set[nat]):
            card(solutions) = putnam_1991_b5_solution(p)
              AND (FORALL (z: nat):
                solutions(z) IFF common_quadratic_residue(p, z))
END putnam_1991_b5

title: putnam_1991_b6

import Mathlib

open Filter Topology

noncomputable abbrev putnam_1991_b6_solution : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ := sorry
-- (fun a b : ℝ => |Real.log (a / b)|)
/--
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive numbers. Find the largest number $c$, in terms of $a$ and $b$, such that $a^xb^{1-x} \leq a\frac{\sinh ux}{\sinh u}+b\frac{\sinh u(1-x)}{\sinh u}$ for all $u$ with $0<|u| \leq c$ and for all $x$, $0< x<1$. (Note: $\sinh u=(e^u-e^{-u})/2$.)
-/
theorem putnam_1991_b6
  (a b : ℝ)
  (abpos : a > 0 ∧ b > 0) :
  IsGreatest {c | ∀ u,
    (0 < |u| ∧ |u| ≤ c) →
    (∀ x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1, a ^ x * b ^ (1 - x) ≤ a * (Real.sinh (u * x) / Real.sinh u) + b * (Real.sinh (u * (1 - x)) / Real.sinh u))}
  (putnam_1991_b6_solution a b) :=
sorry

Require Import Reals Coquelicot.Coquelicot.
Open Scope R.
Definition putnam_1991_b6_solution (a b : R) := Rabs (ln (a / b)). 
Theorem putnam_1991_b6 
    (a b: R)
    (hab : a > 0 /\ b > 0)
    (ineq_holds : R -> Prop := fun c => forall (u x: R), 0 < Rabs u <= c /\ 0 < x < 1 -> Rpower a x * Rpower b (1 - x) <= a * sinh (u * x) / sinh u + b * sinh (u * (1 - x)) / sinh u)
    (c: R)
    (hc : ineq_holds c)
    (hcub : forall (x: R), ineq_holds x -> x <= c)
    : c = putnam_1991_b6_solution a b.
Proof. Admitted.

definition putnam_1991_b6_solution :: "real \<Rightarrow> real \<Rightarrow> real" where "putnam_1991_b6_solution \<equiv> undefined"

theorem putnam_1991_b6:

  and cle :: "real \<Rightarrow> bool"
  defines "cle \<equiv> \<lambda> c :: real. \<forall> u :: real. (0 < \<bar>u\<bar> \<and> \<bar>u\<bar> \<le> c) \<longrightarrow> (\<forall> x \<in> {0 <..< 1}. a powr x * b powr (1 - x) \<le> a * (sinh (u * x) / sinh u) + b * (sinh (u * (1 - x)) / sinh u))"
