(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a1:
   the value of a horizontal line for which two areas cut from the cubic
   y = 2x - 3x^3 are equal. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals RiemannInt.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_1993_a1_solution : R := 4 / 9.

Definition putnam_1993_a1_left_integrand (x : R) : R :=
  Rmax 0 (putnam_1993_a1_solution - (2 * x - 3 * x ^ 3)).

Definition putnam_1993_a1_right_integrand (x : R) : R :=
  Rmax 0 ((2 * x - 3 * x ^ 3) - putnam_1993_a1_solution).

Theorem putnam_1993_a1 :
  0 < putnam_1993_a1_solution /\
  putnam_1993_a1_solution < 4 * sqrt 2 / 9 /\
  exists left_integrable :
      Riemann_integrable
        putnam_1993_a1_left_integrand 0 (sqrt 2 / 3),
    exists right_integrable :
        Riemann_integrable
          putnam_1993_a1_right_integrand 0 (sqrt 6 / 3),
      RiemannInt left_integrable = RiemannInt right_integrable.
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a1:
;; for c = 4/9, the horizontal line y = c cuts y = 2*x - 3*x^3 so that the
;; two specified first-quadrant shaded areas are equal. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-1993-a1-isqrt-search (x candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (or (not (natp x))
          (not (natp candidate)))
      0
    (if (<= (* candidate candidate) x)
        candidate
      (putnam-1993-a1-isqrt-search
       x (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-1993-a1-isqrt (x)
  (if (natp x)
      (putnam-1993-a1-isqrt-search x x)
    0))

;; A rational upper approximation to sqrt(X), converging as SCALE grows.
(defun putnam-1993-a1-sqrt-upper (x scale)
  (if (and (rationalp x)
           (<= 0 x)
           (posp scale))
      (/ (+ 1
            (putnam-1993-a1-isqrt
             (floor (* x scale scale) 1)))
         scale)
    0))

(defun putnam-1993-a1-solution ()
  4/9)

(defun putnam-1993-a1-cubic (x)
  (- (* 2 x) (* 3 (expt x 3))))

(defun putnam-1993-a1-positive-part (x)
  (if (< 0 x) x 0))

(defun putnam-1993-a1-midpoint
    (upper index subdivisions)
  (/ (* upper (- (* 2 index) 1))
     (* 2 subdivisions)))

(defun putnam-1993-a1-integrand
    (c x left-p)
  (if left-p
      (putnam-1993-a1-positive-part
       (- c (putnam-1993-a1-cubic x)))
    (putnam-1993-a1-positive-part
     (- (putnam-1993-a1-cubic x) c))))

(defun putnam-1993-a1-integral-sum
    (c upper remaining subdivisions left-p)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1993-a1-integrand
        c
        (putnam-1993-a1-midpoint
         upper remaining subdivisions)
        left-p)
       (putnam-1993-a1-integral-sum
        c upper (- remaining 1)
        subdivisions left-p))))

;; Direct midpoint approximation to one of the two source positive-part
;; integrals. RADICAND is 2 on the left and 6 on the right.
(defun putnam-1993-a1-integral-approx
    (c radicand precision left-p)
  (if (posp precision)
      (let ((upper
             (/ (putnam-1993-a1-sqrt-upper
                 radicand precision)
                3)))
        (* (/ upper precision)
           (putnam-1993-a1-integral-sum
            c upper precision precision left-p)))
    0))

;; With c positive, c < 4*sqrt(2)/9 is equivalent to 81*c^2 < 32.
(defun putnam-1993-a1-below-cubic-maximum-p (c)
  (and (rationalp c)
       (< 0 c)
       (< (* 81 c c) 32)))

;; The endpoint approximations and midpoint sums converge jointly to the two
;; source integrals. The positive-part integrands are continuous, so no roots
;; or antiderivative computations are embedded in the statement.
(defun-sk putnam-1993-a1-area-tail-p
    (c epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (precision)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp precision)
      (<= cutoff precision))
     (< (abs
         (- (putnam-1993-a1-integral-approx
             c 2 precision t)
            (putnam-1993-a1-integral-approx
             c 6 precision nil)))
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a1-area-cutoff-exists-p
    (c epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (posp cutoff)
     (putnam-1993-a1-area-tail-p
      c epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a1-areas-equal-p (c)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-1993-a1-area-cutoff-exists-p
      c epsilon))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1993-a1-statement ()
  (let ((c (putnam-1993-a1-solution)))
    (and
     (< 0 c)
     (putnam-1993-a1-below-cubic-maximum-p c)
     (putnam-1993-a1-areas-equal-p c))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- the constant 4/9 lies in the stated range and makes the two positive-part

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc threeN

sixN : Nat
sixN =
  threeN + threeN

nineN : Nat
nineN =
  threeN * threeN

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

maximum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
maximum reals x y with order-total reals x y
... | left _ =
  y
... | right _ =
  x

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

midpointRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
midpointRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
    halfStep =
      divide reals
        step
        (fromNat reals twoN)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (add reals
              (multiply reals
                (fromNat reals i)
                step)
              halfStep)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function integralValue =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      midpointRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    integralValue

module Putnam1993A1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  solution : R
  solution =
    divide reals
      (fromNat reals fourN)
      (fromNat reals nineN)

  squareRootTwo : R
  squareRootTwo =
    squareRoot reals (fromNat reals twoN)

  squareRootSix : R
  squareRootSix =
    squareRoot reals (fromNat reals sixN)

  polynomial : R -> R
  polynomial x =
    subtract reals
      (multiply reals
        (fromNat reals twoN)
        x)
      (multiply reals
        (fromNat reals threeN)
        (naturalPower reals x threeN))

  leftIntegrand : R -> R
  leftIntegrand x =
    maximum reals
      (zeroR reals)
      (subtract reals solution (polynomial x))

  rightIntegrand : R -> R
  rightIntegrand x =
    maximum reals
      (zeroR reals)
      (subtract reals (polynomial x) solution)

  leftUpperEndpoint : R
  leftUpperEndpoint =
    divide reals
      squareRootTwo
      (fromNat reals threeN)

  rightUpperEndpoint : R
  rightUpperEndpoint =
    divide reals
      squareRootSix
      (fromNat reals threeN)

  solutionUpperBound : R
  solutionUpperBound =
    divide reals
      (multiply reals
        (fromNat reals fourN)
        squareRootTwo)
      (fromNat reals nineN)

  EqualAreaIntegrals : Set
  EqualAreaIntegrals =
    Exists R
      (\ commonValue ->
        IntervalIntegralValue reals
          (zeroR reals)
          leftUpperEndpoint
          leftIntegrand
          commonValue
        and
        IntervalIntegralValue reals
          (zeroR reals)
          rightUpperEndpoint
          rightIntegrand
          commonValue)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) solution
    and
    StrictLess reals solution solutionUpperBound
    and
    EqualAreaIntegrals

putnam-1993-a1 : Set1
putnam-1993-a1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1993A1Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a1:
  the equal-area horizontal line for the first-quadrant cubic
  y = 2x - 3x^3 has height 4/9. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory realTheory transcTheory integrationTheory;

val putnam_1993_a1 =
  ``let solution = (4 / 9 : real)
    in
      0 < solution /\
      solution < 4 * sqrt 2 / 9 /\
      integration$integral (interval [0, sqrt 2 / 3])
        (\x : real.
           max (solution - (2 * x - 3 * x pow 3)) 0) =
      integration$integral (interval [0, sqrt 6 / 3])
        (\x : real.
           max ((2 * x - 3 * x pow 3) - solution) 0)``;

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(

title: putnam_1993_a1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a1:
% a positive horizontal level below 4*sqrt(2)/9 equalizes the two Lebesgue
% areas determined by y = 2*x - 3*x^3. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1993_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_set: TYPE = [real -> bool]
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  real_set_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real_set]

  finite_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      finite_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(values: real_sequence, limit: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(values(count) - limit) < epsilon_value

  open_interval(left_endpoint, right_endpoint: real): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      left_endpoint < x AND x < right_endpoint

  set_intersection(left_set, right_set: real_set): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      left_set(x) AND right_set(x)

  set_difference(left_set, right_set: real_set): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      left_set(x) AND NOT right_set(x)

  set_subset(left_set, right_set: real_set): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      left_set(x) IMPLIES right_set(x)

  bounded(covered: real_set): bool =
    EXISTS (bound: nonneg_real):
      FORALL (x: real):
        covered(x) IMPLIES abs(x) <= bound

  interval_length(left_endpoint, right_endpoint: real): real =
    IF left_endpoint < right_endpoint THEN
      right_endpoint - left_endpoint
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  open_interval_cover(
      covered: real_set,
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      covered(x) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (index: nat):
          left_endpoints(index) < x
            AND x < right_endpoints(index)

  cover_partial_length(
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence,
      count: nat): real =
    finite_sum(
      LAMBDA (index: nat):
        interval_length(
          left_endpoints(index),
          right_endpoints(index)),
      count)

  cover_has_total_length(
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence,
      total: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat):
        cover_partial_length(
          left_endpoints, right_endpoints, count),
      total)

  has_outer_measure(
      covered: real_set,
      measure_value: real): bool =
    bounded(covered)
      AND measure_value >= 0
      AND (FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS
            (left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence),
            (total: real):
          open_interval_cover(
            covered, left_endpoints, right_endpoints)
            AND cover_has_total_length(
              left_endpoints, right_endpoints, total)
            AND total < measure_value + epsilon_value)
      AND (FORALL
          (left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence),
          (total: real):
        (open_interval_cover(
            covered, left_endpoints, right_endpoints)
          AND cover_has_total_length(
            left_endpoints, right_endpoints, total))
        IMPLIES measure_value <= total)

  lebesgue_measurable(measured_set: real_set): bool =
    bounded(measured_set)
      AND FORALL (test_set: real_set):
        bounded(test_set) IMPLIES
          EXISTS (whole, inside, outside: real):
            has_outer_measure(test_set, whole)
              AND has_outer_measure(
                set_intersection(test_set, measured_set),
                inside)
              AND has_outer_measure(
                set_difference(test_set, measured_set),
                outside)
              AND whole = inside + outside

  outer_measure_value(measured_set: real_set): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (measure_value: real):
        has_outer_measure(measured_set, measure_value))

  measurable_nonnegative_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set): bool =
    lebesgue_measurable(domain)
      AND (FORALL (x: real):
        domain(x) IMPLIES 0 <= function_value(x))
      AND FORALL (level: real):
        lebesgue_measurable(
          LAMBDA (x: real):
            domain(x) AND level < function_value(x))

  pairwise_disjoint_below(
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (left_index, right_index: nat):
      left_index < count
        AND right_index < count
        AND left_index /= right_index
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (x: real):
          NOT (pieces(left_index)(x)
            AND pieces(right_index)(x))

  simple_value(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat,
      x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      simple_value(coefficients, pieces, count - 1, x)
        + IF pieces(count - 1)(x)
            THEN coefficients(count - 1)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  simple_integral(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      simple_integral(coefficients, pieces, count - 1)
        + coefficients(count - 1)
            * outer_measure_value(pieces(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  valid_simple_minorant(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set,
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    pairwise_disjoint_below(pieces, count)
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          coefficients(index) >= 0
            AND lebesgue_measurable(pieces(index))
            AND set_subset(pieces(index), domain))
      AND FORALL (x: real):
        domain(x) IMPLIES
          simple_value(coefficients, pieces, count, x)
            <= function_value(x)

  finite_nonnegative_lebesgue_integral_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    measurable_nonnegative_on(function_value, domain)
      AND integral_value >= 0
      AND (FORALL
          (coefficients: real_sequence),
          (pieces: real_set_sequence),
          (count: nat):
        valid_simple_minorant(
          function_value, domain,
          coefficients, pieces, count)
        IMPLIES
          simple_integral(coefficients, pieces, count)
            <= integral_value)
      AND (FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS
            (coefficients: real_sequence),
            (pieces: real_set_sequence),
            (count: nat):
          valid_simple_minorant(
            function_value, domain,
            coefficients, pieces, count)
            AND integral_value - epsilon_value
              < simple_integral(coefficients, pieces, count))

  lebesgue_integral_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set): real =
    IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
        finite_nonnegative_lebesgue_integral_on(
          function_value, domain, integral_value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
          finite_nonnegative_lebesgue_integral_on(
            function_value, domain, integral_value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  nonnegative_square_root(value: real): real =
    IF 0 <= value THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (root: real):
          0 <= root AND root * root = value)
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  nonnegative_part(value: real): real =
    IF 0 <= value THEN value ELSE 0 ENDIF

  curve(x: real): real =
    2 * x - 3 * x ^ 3

  lower_area_integrand(c: real): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      nonnegative_part(c - curve(x))

  upper_area_integrand(c: real): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      nonnegative_part(curve(x) - c)

  solution_condition(c: real): bool =
    c > 0
      AND c < 4 * nonnegative_square_root(2) / 9
      AND lebesgue_integral_on(
            lower_area_integrand(c),
            open_interval(
              0, nonnegative_square_root(2) / 3))
          =
          lebesgue_integral_on(
            upper_area_integrand(c),
            open_interval(
              0, nonnegative_square_root(6) / 3))

  putnam_1993_a1_solution: real = 4 / 9

  putnam_1993_a1: bool =
    solution_condition(putnam_1993_a1_solution)
END putnam_1993_a1

import Mathlib

/--
Let $(x_n)_{n \geq 0}$ be a sequence of nonzero real numbers such that $x_n^2-x_{n-1}x_{n+1}=1$ for $n=1,2,3,\dots$. Prove there exists a real number $a$ such that $x_{n+1}=ax_n-x_{n-1}$ for all $n \geq 1$.
-/
theorem putnam_1993_a2
(x : ℕ → ℝ)
(xnonzero : ∀ n : ℕ, x n ≠ 0)
(hx : ∀ n ≥ 1, (x n) ^ 2 - x (n - 1) * x (n + 1) = 1)
: ∃ a : ℝ, ∀ n ≥ 1, x (n + 1) = a * x n - x (n - 1) :=

content:
Require Import Reals Coquelicot.Coquelicot.
Open Scope R.
Theorem putnam_1993_a2 
    (x : nat -> R)

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1993_a2:
;; a nonzero sequence with constant adjacent determinant has a common
;; second-order recurrence coefficient. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The theorem is algebraic. X is an arbitrary sequence in an arbitrary
;; field, represented by ACL2's conservative generic-symbol mechanism.
(defstub p1993a2-carrier (x) t)
(defstub p1993a2-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub p1993a2-multiply-op (x y) t)
(defstub p1993a2-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub p1993a2-inverse-op (x) t)
(defstub p1993a2-x (n) t)

(defun p1993a2-member-p (x)
  (if (p1993a2-carrier x) t nil))

(defun p1993a2-add (x y)
  (p1993a2-add-op x y))

(defun p1993a2-mul (x y)
  (p1993a2-multiply-op x y))

(defun p1993a2-neg (x)
  (p1993a2-negate-op x))

(defun p1993a2-sub (x y)
  (p1993a2-add x (p1993a2-neg y)))

(defun p1993a2-inv (x)
  (p1993a2-inverse-op x))

(defun-sk p1993a2-field-laws-p (zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p1993a2-member-p x)
      (p1993a2-member-p y)
      (p1993a2-member-p z))
     (and
      (p1993a2-member-p (p1993a2-add x y))
      (p1993a2-member-p (p1993a2-mul x y))
      (p1993a2-member-p (p1993a2-neg x))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (p1993a2-member-p (p1993a2-inv x)))
      (equal (p1993a2-add (p1993a2-add x y) z)
             (p1993a2-add x (p1993a2-add y z)))
      (equal (p1993a2-add x y)
             (p1993a2-add y x))
      (equal (p1993a2-add x zero) x)
      (equal (p1993a2-add x (p1993a2-neg x)) zero)
      (equal (p1993a2-mul (p1993a2-mul x y) z)
             (p1993a2-mul x (p1993a2-mul y z)))
      (equal (p1993a2-mul x y)
             (p1993a2-mul y x))
      (equal (p1993a2-mul x one) x)
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal (p1993a2-mul x (p1993a2-inv x)) one))
      (equal
       (p1993a2-mul x (p1993a2-add y z))
       (p1993a2-add (p1993a2-mul x y)
                    (p1993a2-mul x z)))))))

(defun p1993a2-field-p (zero one)
  (and
   (p1993a2-member-p zero)
   (p1993a2-member-p one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (p1993a2-field-laws-p zero one)))

(defun-sk p1993a2-sequence-p (zero)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (natp n)
     (and
      (p1993a2-member-p (p1993a2-x n))
      (not (equal (p1993a2-x n) zero))))))

(defun-sk p1993a2-determinant-condition-p (one)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and (natp n)
          (<= 1 n))
     (equal
      (p1993a2-sub
       (p1993a2-mul (p1993a2-x n)
                    (p1993a2-x n))
       (p1993a2-mul (p1993a2-x (- n 1))
                    (p1993a2-x (+ n 1))))
      one))))

(defun-sk p1993a2-recurrence-p (coefficient)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and (natp n)
          (<= 1 n))
     (equal
      (p1993a2-x (+ n 1))
      (p1993a2-sub
       (p1993a2-mul coefficient (p1993a2-x n))
       (p1993a2-x (- n 1)))))))

(defun-sk p1993a2-has-coefficient-p ()
  (exists (coefficient)
    (and
     (p1993a2-member-p coefficient)
     (p1993a2-recurrence-p coefficient))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1993-a2-statement (zero one)
  (implies
   (and
    (p1993a2-field-p zero one)
    (p1993a2-sequence-p zero)
    (p1993a2-determinant-condition-p one))
   (p1993a2-has-coefficient-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a2:
-- a nonzero real sequence satisfying x_n^2 - x_(n-1) x_(n+1) = 1 admits a
-- constant-coefficient second-order recurrence. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

module Putnam1993A2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (x : Nat -> R) ->
    ((n : Nat) ->
      x n != zeroR reals) ->
    ((n : Nat) ->
      oneN <=N n ->
      subtract reals
        (square reals (x n))
        (multiply reals
          (x (n - oneN))
          (x (suc n)))
      ==
      oneR reals) ->
    Exists R
      (\ a ->
        (n : Nat) ->
        oneN <=N n ->
        x (suc n)
        ==
        subtract reals
          (multiply reals a (x n))
          (x (n - oneN)))

putnam-1993-a2 : Set1
putnam-1993-a2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1993A2Statement.proposition reals

   counting intersection-preserving maps from the subsets of an n-element set

From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect.

Definition putnam_1993_a3_admissible {n m : nat}
    (f : {ffun {set 'I_n} -> 'I_m}) : bool :=
  [forall A : {set 'I_n},
    [forall B : {set 'I_n},

        putnam_1993_a3_admissible f]| =
    \sum_(1 <= j < m.+1) j ^ n.

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a3:
;; the number of functions from the subsets of an n-element set to
;; {1,...,m} that send intersections to minima is sum_{j=1}^m j^n.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Subsets of {1,...,n} are represented by their n-bit characteristic
;; numbers, exactly the naturals below 2^n. A function on this power set is
;; represented by the 2^n base-m digits of a natural below m^(2^n), with
;; digit d corresponding to source value d+1. These encodings are bijective,
;; and adding one preserves both equality and minimum, so the predicates
;; below count exactly the source function space rather than an approximation.

(defun putnam-1993-a3-function-value
    (function-code subset-code m)
  (mod
   (floor function-code (expt m subset-code))
   m))

(defun putnam-1993-a3-subset-intersection
    (left right remaining-bits)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-bits)))
  (if (zp remaining-bits)
      0
    (+
     (if (and (equal (mod left 2) 1)
              (equal (mod right 2) 1))
         1
       0)
     (*
      2
      (putnam-1993-a3-subset-intersection
       (floor left 2)
       (floor right 2)
       (- remaining-bits 1))))))

(defun putnam-1993-a3-pairs-for-left-p
    (function-code left remaining-right m n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-right)))
  (if (zp remaining-right)
      t
    (let* ((right (- remaining-right 1))
           (left-value
            (putnam-1993-a3-function-value
             function-code left m))
           (right-value
            (putnam-1993-a3-function-value
             function-code right m))
           (intersection
            (putnam-1993-a3-subset-intersection
             left right n))
           (intersection-value
            (putnam-1993-a3-function-value
             function-code intersection m)))
      (and
       (equal
        intersection-value
        (if (< left-value right-value)
            left-value
          right-value))
       (putnam-1993-a3-pairs-for-left-p
        function-code left right m n)))))

(defun putnam-1993-a3-meet-preserving-p
    (function-code remaining-left subset-count m n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-left)))
  (if (zp remaining-left)
      t
    (let ((left (- remaining-left 1)))
      (and
       (putnam-1993-a3-pairs-for-left-p
        function-code left subset-count m n)
       (putnam-1993-a3-meet-preserving-p
        function-code left subset-count m n)))))

(defun putnam-1993-a3-count-functions
    (remaining-functions subset-count m n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-functions)))
  (if (zp remaining-functions)
      0
    (let ((function-code (- remaining-functions 1)))
      (+
       (if (putnam-1993-a3-meet-preserving-p
            function-code subset-count subset-count m n)
           1
         0)
       (putnam-1993-a3-count-functions
        function-code subset-count m n)))))

(defun putnam-1993-a3-power-sum (n upper)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix upper)))
  (if (zp upper)
      0
    (+
     (expt upper n)
     (putnam-1993-a3-power-sum n (- upper 1)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1993-a3-statement (n m)
  (implies
   (and
    (posp n)
    (posp m))
   (let ((subset-count (expt 2 n)))
     (equal
      (putnam-1993-a3-count-functions
       (expt m subset-count)
       subset-count
       m
       n)
      (putnam-1993-a3-power-sum n m)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a3:
-- the number of intersection-preserving maps from the power set of an
-- n-element set to an m-element chain equals the sum of j^n for 1 <= j <= m.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

data FiniteSubset : Nat -> Set where
  emptySubset : FiniteSubset zero
  addBit      : {n : Nat} -> Bool -> FiniteSubset n -> FiniteSubset (suc n)

boolAnd : Bool -> Bool -> Bool
boolAnd false right = false
boolAnd true right = right

intersection :
  {n : Nat} ->
  FiniteSubset n ->
  FiniteSubset n ->
  FiniteSubset n
intersection emptySubset emptySubset =
  emptySubset
intersection (addBit left leftTail) (addBit right rightTail) =
  addBit
    (boolAnd left right)
    (intersection leftTail rightTail)

minFin :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n
minFin fzero right =
  fzero
minFin (fsuc left) fzero =
  fzero
minFin (fsuc left) (fsuc right) =
  fsuc (minFin left right)

record MeetPreservingMap (n m : Nat) : Set where
  field
    function :
      FiniteSubset n ->
      Fin m

    preserves-intersection :
      (left right : FiniteSubset n) ->
      function (intersection left right) ==
      minFin (function left) (function right)

open MeetPreservingMap

SameMeetPreservingMap :
  {n m : Nat} ->
  MeetPreservingMap n m ->
  MeetPreservingMap n m ->
  Set
SameMeetPreservingMap {n} left right =
  (subset : FiniteSubset n) ->
  function left subset == function right subset

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  field
    witness  : A
    property : P witness

record HasExtensionalCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (equivalent : A -> A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A

    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> equivalent item (enumerate index))

    enumeration-injective :
      (leftIndex rightIndex : Fin cardinality) ->
      equivalent (enumerate leftIndex) (enumerate rightIndex) ->
      leftIndex == rightIndex

MeetPreservingFamilyHasCardinality :
  (n m cardinality : Nat) ->
  Set
MeetPreservingFamilyHasCardinality n m cardinality =
  HasExtensionalCardinality
    {A = MeetPreservingMap n m}
    SameMeetPreservingMap
    cardinality

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

power : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
power base zero =
  one
power base (suc exponent) =
  power base exponent * base

sumPowersThrough : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
sumPowersThrough exponent zero =
  zero
sumPowersThrough exponent (suc bound) =
  sumPowersThrough exponent bound +
  power (suc bound) exponent

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

putnam-1993-a3 : Set
putnam-1993-a3 =
  (c : Nat -> Nat -> Nat) ->
  ((n m : Nat) ->
    Positive n ->
    Positive m ->
    MeetPreservingFamilyHasCardinality n m (c n m)) ->
  (n m : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  Positive m ->
  c n m == sumPowersThrough n m

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a3:
  the number of intersection-preserving functions from the subsets of
  {1,...,n} to {1,...,m} equals the sum of the nth powers from 1 to m. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_1993_a3 =
  ``let pown =
      \n : num. POW (IMAGE SUC (count n))
    in
    let c =
      \n m : num.
        CARD
          {f : num set -> num |
             (!s : num set.
                s IN pown n
                ==>
                f s IN IMAGE SUC (count m)) /\
             (!s : num set.
                s NOTIN pown n
                ==>
                f s = 0) /\
             (!A B : num set.
                A IN pown n /\ B IN pown n
                ==>
                f (A INTER B) = MIN (f A) (f B))}
    in
      !n m : num.
        1 <= n /\ 1 <= m
        ==>
        c n m =
          SIGMA
            (\j : num. j EXP n)
            (IMAGE SUC (count m))``;

$(

  putnam_1993_a3: the number of intersection-to-minimum preserving maps from
  the power set of an n-element set to an m-element chain is the sum of the
  nth powers of the integers from 1 through m. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For positive natural n and m, ~P ( 1 ... n ) is the full power set of an
  n-element set, and ( 1 ... m ) ^m ~P ( 1 ... n ) is the class of all total
  functions from that power set to the m-element chain.

  For natural-valued f, the two order implications in the restricted class
  are equivalent to

    f ( A intersection B ) = min ( f A , f B ).

  Thus the left side is exactly the source count c(n,m), with its defining
  equation substituted into the conclusion. The final declaration is the
  single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

${
  $d A B f j m n $.

  putnambench-putnam-1993-a3 $a |- A. n e. NN A. m e. NN
    (
      #
      `
      {
        f e.
          (
            ( 1 ... m )
            ^m
            ( ~P ( 1 ... n ) )
          )
        |
        A. A e. ( ~P ( 1 ... n ) )
          A. B e. ( ~P ( 1 ... n ) )
            (
              (
                ( f ` A ) <_ ( f ` B )
                ->
                ( f ` ( A i^i B ) ) = ( f ` A )
              )
              /\
              (
                ( f ` B ) <_ ( f ` A )
                ->
                ( f ` ( A i^i B ) ) = ( f ` B )
              )
            )
      }
      =
      sum_ j e. ( 1 ... m ) ( j ^ n )
    )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1993_a3:
% the number of intersection-minimum-preserving functions from the subsets
% of an n-element set to an m-element chain is the sum of the nth powers
% from 1 through m. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1993_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  subset_intersection(
      left, right, bit_count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF bit_count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      (IF mod(left, 2) = 1 AND mod(right, 2) = 1 THEN
         1
       ELSE
         0
       ENDIF)
        + 2 * subset_intersection(
            ndiv(left, 2),
            ndiv(right, 2),
            bit_count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE bit_count

  function_code_count(n, m: posnat): nat =
    m ^ (2 ^ n)

  function_value(
      function_code, subset_code: nat,
      m: posnat): nat =
    mod(
      ndiv(function_code, m ^ subset_code),
      m)

  nat_min(left, right: nat): nat =
    IF left <= right THEN left ELSE right ENDIF

  preserves_intersection_minimum(
      function_code: nat,
      n, m: posnat): bool =
    FORALL (left_subset, right_subset: nat):
      (left_subset < 2 ^ n AND right_subset < 2 ^ n)
        IMPLIES
          function_value(
            function_code,
            subset_intersection(
              left_subset, right_subset, n),
            m)
            = nat_min(
                function_value(
                  function_code, left_subset, m),
                function_value(
                  function_code, right_subset, m))

  count_below(
      limit: nat,
      property: [nat -> bool]): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_below(limit - 1, property)
        + IF property(limit - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  intersection_minimum_function_count(
      n, m: posnat): nat =
    count_below(
      function_code_count(n, m),
      LAMBDA (function_code: nat):
        preserves_intersection_minimum(
          function_code, n, m))

  power_sum(n, upper: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF upper = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      power_sum(n, upper - 1) + upper ^ n
    ENDIF
  MEASURE upper

  putnam_1993_a3: bool =
    FORALL (n, m: posnat):
      intersection_minimum_function_count(n, m)
        = power_sum(n, m)
END putnam_1993_a3

(defun putnam-1993-a4-positive-bounded-list-p
    (values remaining bound)

     (< 0 (car values))
     (<= (car values) bound)

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a4:
-- bounded positive integer sequences of lengths 19 and 93 have equal subset
-- sums with the subset of the first sequence nonempty. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1993A4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

Subset : Nat -> Set
Subset n =
  Fin n -> Bool

Nonempty :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Subset n ->
  Set
Nonempty {n} subset =
  Exists (Fin n) (\ index -> subset index == true)

selectedSum :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Nat) ->
  Subset n ->
  Nat
selectedSum {zero} values subset =
  zero
selectedSum {suc n} values subset with subset fzero
... | false =
  selectedSum
    (\ index -> values (fsuc index))
    (\ index -> subset (fsuc index))
... | true =
  values fzero +
  selectedSum
    (\ index -> values (fsuc index))
    (\ index -> subset (fsuc index))

BoundedPositive :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Nat) ->
  Nat ->
  Set
BoundedPositive {n} values upper =
  (index : Fin n) ->
  Positive (values index)
  and
  values index <=N upper

putnam-1993-a4 : Set
putnam-1993-a4 =
  (x : Fin 19 -> Nat) ->
  (y : Fin 93 -> Nat) ->
  BoundedPositive x 93 ->
  BoundedPositive y 19 ->
  Exists (Subset 19)
    (\ is ->
      Exists (Subset 93)
        (\ js ->
          Nonempty is
          and
          selectedSum x is == selectedSum y js))

          (EXISTS (i: nat): i < 19 AND is(i))
            AND selected_sum(x, is, 19)

(defun putnam-1993-a5-integrand (x)
  (let* ((numerator (- (* x x) x))
         (denominator (+ (* x x x) (* -3 x) 1))
         (quotient (/ numerator denominator)))
    (* quotient quotient)))

(defun putnam-1993-a5-grid-point
    (left right index subdivisions)
  (+ left
     (/ (* (- right left) index)
        subdivisions)))

(defun putnam-1993-a5-riemann-sum-aux
    (left right subdivisions remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1993-a5-integrand
        (putnam-1993-a5-grid-point
         left right remaining subdivisions))
       (putnam-1993-a5-riemann-sum-aux
        left right subdivisions (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-1993-a5-integral-approx
    (left right subdivisions)
  (if (posp subdivisions)
      (* (/ (- right left) subdivisions)
         (putnam-1993-a5-riemann-sum-aux
          left right subdivisions subdivisions))
    0))

;; These are the summed uniform right-endpoint Riemann approximations for
;; exactly the three source intervals. The rational function is continuous on
;; those intervals, so their limit is the source sum of definite integrals.
(defun putnam-1993-a5-three-integral-approx
    (subdivisions)
  (+ (putnam-1993-a5-integral-approx
      -100 -10 subdivisions)
     (putnam-1993-a5-integral-approx
      (/ 1 101) (/ 1 11) subdivisions)
     (putnam-1993-a5-integral-approx
      (/ 101 100) (/ 11 10) subdivisions)))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a5-limit-tail-p
    (limit epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (subdivisions)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp subdivisions)
      (<= cutoff subdivisions))
     (< (abs
         (- (putnam-1993-a5-three-integral-approx
             subdivisions)
            limit))
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a5-limit-cutoff-exists-p
    (limit epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (posp cutoff)
     (putnam-1993-a5-limit-tail-p
      limit epsilon cutoff))))

;; Positive rational tolerances are cofinal among positive real tolerances.
(defun-sk putnam-1993-a5-converges-to-p (limit)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-1993-a5-limit-cutoff-exists-p
      limit epsilon))))

;; The rational value is existentially quantified inside the proposition.
(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-1993-a5-statement ()
  (exists (limit)
    (and
     (rationalp limit)
     (putnam-1993-a5-converges-to-p limit))))

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a5:
-- the sum of three specified definite integrals of a squared rational function
-- is a rational number. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

rightRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
rightRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals (suc i))
              step)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function integralValue =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      rightRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    integralValue

record Rational : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator             : Int
    denominator-minus-one : Nat

open Rational

denominator : Rational -> Nat
denominator q =
  suc (denominator-minus-one q)

rationalValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Rational ->
  R
rationalValue reals q =
  divide reals
    (fromInt reals (numerator q))
    (fromNat reals (denominator q))

IsRational :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
IsRational reals x =
  Exists Rational
    (\ q -> x == rationalValue reals q)

module Putnam1993A5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  integrand : R -> R
  integrand x =
    let
      xSquared =
        naturalPower reals x 2
      xCubed =
        naturalPower reals x 3
      numeratorValue =
        subtract reals xSquared x
      denominatorValue =
        add reals
          (subtract reals
            xCubed
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals 3)
              x))
          (oneR reals)
      quotient =
        divide reals numeratorValue denominatorValue
    in
    naturalPower reals quotient 2

  negativeHundred : R
  negativeHundred =
    negate reals (fromNat reals 100)

  negativeTen : R
  negativeTen =
    negate reals (fromNat reals 10)

  oneOverHundredOne : R
  oneOverHundredOne =
    divide reals
      (oneR reals)
      (fromNat reals 101)

  oneOverEleven : R
  oneOverEleven =
    divide reals
      (oneR reals)
      (fromNat reals 11)

  hundredOneOverHundred : R
  hundredOneOverHundred =
    divide reals
      (fromNat reals 101)
      (fromNat reals 100)

  elevenOverTen : R
  elevenOverTen =
    divide reals
      (fromNat reals 11)
      (fromNat reals 10)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    Exists R
      (\ firstIntegral ->
        IntervalIntegralValue reals
          negativeHundred
          negativeTen
          integrand
          firstIntegral
        and
        Exists R
          (\ secondIntegral ->
            IntervalIntegralValue reals
              oneOverHundredOne
              oneOverEleven
              integrand
              secondIntegral
            and
            Exists R
              (\ thirdIntegral ->
                IntervalIntegralValue reals
                  hundredOneOverHundred
                  elevenOverTen
                  integrand
                  thirdIntegral
                and
                IsRational reals
                  (add reals
                    (add reals firstIntegral secondIntegral)
                    thirdIntegral))))

putnam-1993-a5 : Set1
putnam-1993-a5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1993A5Statement.proposition reals

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a5:
% the sum of three definite integrals of the stated squared rational function
% is a rational number. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1993_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  integrand(x: real): real =
    safe_div(
      x ^ 2 - x,
      x ^ 3 - 3 * x + 1) ^ 2

  valid_tagged_partition(
      left, right: real,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = left
      AND points(count) = right
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          (points(index) < points(index + 1)
            AND points(index) <= tags(index)
            AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1))

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      f: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count - 1)
        + f(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_interval_integral(
      f: real_function,
      left, right, integral_value: real): bool =
    left < right
      AND FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
          FORALL
              (points, tags: real_sequence),
              (count: nat):
            (valid_tagged_partition(
                left, right, points, tags, count)
              AND mesh_less_than(points, count, mesh_bound))
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count)
                  - integral_value)
                < epsilon_value

  interval_integral(
      f: real_function,
      left, right: real): real =
    IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
        has_interval_integral(f, left, right, integral_value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
          has_interval_integral(
            f, left, right, integral_value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  putnam_1993_a5: bool =
    rational?(
      interval_integral(integrand, -100, -10)
        + interval_integral(
            integrand,
            safe_div(1, 101),
            safe_div(1, 11))
        + interval_integral(
            integrand,
            safe_div(101, 100),
            safe_div(11, 10)))
END putnam_1993_a5

title: putnam_1993_a6

import Mathlib

/--
The infinite sequence of $2$'s and $3$'s $2,3,3,2,3,3,3,2,3,3,3,2,3,3,2,3,3,3,2,3,3,3,2,3,3,3,2,3,3,2,3,3,3,2,\dots$ has the property that, if one forms a second sequence that records the number of $3$'s between successive $2$'s, the result is identical to the given sequence. Show that there exists a real number $r$ such that, for any $n$, the $n$th term of the sequence is $2$ if and only if $n=1+\lfloor rm \rfloor$ for some nonnegative integer $m$. (Note: $\lfloor x \rfloor$ denotes the largest integer less than or equal to $x$.)
-/
theorem putnam_1993_a6
(seq : ℕ → ℤ)
(hseq23 : ∀ n, seq n = 2 ∨ seq n = 3)
(hseq2inds : ∀ n, seq n = 2 ↔ (∃ N : ℕ, n = ∑ i : Fin N, (seq i + 1)))
: ∃ r : ℝ, ∀ n, seq n = 2 ↔ (∃ m : ℤ, n + 1 = 1 + Int.floor (r * m)) :=
sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1993_a6:
   a self-describing sequence of 2s and 3s has its 2-valued positions
   represented by a real floor sequence. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals ZArith.

Fixpoint putnam_1993_a6_prefix_sum
    (seq : nat -> nat) (N : nat) : nat :=
  match N with
  | O => O
  | S N' => putnam_1993_a6_prefix_sum seq N' + (seq N' + 1)
  end.

Theorem putnam_1993_a6 :
  forall seq : nat -> nat,
    (forall n : nat, seq n = 2 \/ seq n = 3) ->
    (forall n : nat,
        seq n = 2 <->
        exists N : nat, n = putnam_1993_a6_prefix_sum seq N) ->
    exists r : R,
      forall n : nat,
        seq n = 2 <->
        exists m : nat,
          Z.of_nat (n + 1) = (1 + Zfloor (r * INR m))%Z.
Admitted.
