;; Standard ACL2 has no primitive real carrier. Following the repository's
;; statement-only convention, these conservative symbols present an arbitrary
;; Archimedean Dedekind-complete ordered field, hence the real numbers up to
;; ordered-field isomorphism. Every carrier, field, order, completeness, and
;; Archimedean law used by the statement is explicit below.

(defstub putnam-1993-a6-real-p (real-type value) t)
(defstub putnam-1993-a6-zero (real-type) t)
(defstub putnam-1993-a6-one (real-type) t)
(defstub putnam-1993-a6-add (real-type left right) t)
(defstub putnam-1993-a6-multiply (real-type left right) t)
(defstub putnam-1993-a6-negate (real-type value) t)
(defstub putnam-1993-a6-inverse (real-type value) t)
(defstub putnam-1993-a6-less (real-type left right) t)
(defstub putnam-1993-a6-supremum (real-type set) t)

;; The source sequence remains an arbitrary function on the natural numbers.
(defstub putnam-1993-a6-sequence (index) t)

(defun putnam-1993-a6-leq (real-type left right)
  (not (putnam-1993-a6-less real-type right left)))

(defun putnam-1993-a6-set-member-p (set value)
  (if (apply$ set (list value)) t nil))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-field-laws-p (real-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type x)
      (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type y)
      (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type z))
     (let* ((zero (putnam-1993-a6-zero real-type))
            (one (putnam-1993-a6-one real-type))
            (xy-add (putnam-1993-a6-add real-type x y))
            (yz-add (putnam-1993-a6-add real-type y z))
            (xy-mul (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type x y))
            (yz-mul (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type y z))
            (neg-x (putnam-1993-a6-negate real-type x))
            (inv-x (putnam-1993-a6-inverse real-type x)))
       (and
        (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type xy-add)
        (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type xy-mul)
        (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type neg-x)
        (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type inv-x)
        (equal
         (putnam-1993-a6-add real-type xy-add z)
         (putnam-1993-a6-add real-type x yz-add))
        (equal
         (putnam-1993-a6-add real-type x y)
         (putnam-1993-a6-add real-type y x))
        (equal
         (putnam-1993-a6-add real-type x zero)
         x)
        (equal
         (putnam-1993-a6-add real-type x neg-x)
         zero)
        (equal
         (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type xy-mul z)
         (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type x yz-mul))
        (equal
         (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type x y)
         (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type y x))
        (equal
         (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type x one)
         x)
        (implies
         (equal x zero)
         (equal inv-x zero))
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (equal
          (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type x inv-x)
          one))
        (equal
         (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type x yz-add)
         (putnam-1993-a6-add
          real-type
          (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type x y)
          (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type x z))))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-order-laws-p (real-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type x)
      (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type y)
      (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type z))
     (let ((zero (putnam-1993-a6-zero real-type)))
       (and
        (not (putnam-1993-a6-less real-type x x))
        (or
         (equal x y)
         (putnam-1993-a6-less real-type x y)
         (putnam-1993-a6-less real-type y x))
        (implies
         (and
          (putnam-1993-a6-less real-type x y)
          (putnam-1993-a6-less real-type y z))
         (putnam-1993-a6-less real-type x z))
        (implies
         (putnam-1993-a6-less real-type x y)
         (putnam-1993-a6-less
          real-type
          (putnam-1993-a6-add real-type x z)
          (putnam-1993-a6-add real-type y z)))
        (implies
         (and
          (putnam-1993-a6-less real-type zero x)
          (putnam-1993-a6-less real-type zero y))
         (putnam-1993-a6-less
          real-type
          zero
          (putnam-1993-a6-multiply real-type x y))))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-valid-real-set-p (real-type set)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (putnam-1993-a6-set-member-p set value)
     (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type value))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-upper-bound-p
    (real-type set upper)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type value)
      (putnam-1993-a6-set-member-p set value))
     (putnam-1993-a6-leq real-type value upper))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-set-nonempty-p (real-type set)
  (exists (value)
    (and
     (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type value)
     (putnam-1993-a6-set-member-p set value))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-set-bounded-above-p
    (real-type set)
  (exists (upper)
    (and
     (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type upper)
     (putnam-1993-a6-upper-bound-p
      real-type set upper))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-least-upper-bound-p
    (real-type set supremum)
  (forall (upper)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type upper)
      (putnam-1993-a6-upper-bound-p
       real-type set upper))
     (putnam-1993-a6-leq
      real-type supremum upper))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-complete-p (real-type)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (tamep-functionp set)
      (putnam-1993-a6-valid-real-set-p real-type set)
      (putnam-1993-a6-set-nonempty-p real-type set)
      (putnam-1993-a6-set-bounded-above-p real-type set))
     (let ((supremum
            (putnam-1993-a6-supremum real-type set)))
       (and
        (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type supremum)
        (putnam-1993-a6-upper-bound-p
         real-type set supremum)
        (putnam-1993-a6-least-upper-bound-p
         real-type set supremum))))))

(defun putnam-1993-a6-real-nat (real-type n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (putnam-1993-a6-zero real-type)
    (putnam-1993-a6-add
     real-type
     (putnam-1993-a6-one real-type)
     (putnam-1993-a6-real-nat real-type (1- n)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-archimedean-bound-exists-p
    (real-type value)
  (exists (n)
    (and
     (natp n)
     (putnam-1993-a6-less
      real-type
      value
      (putnam-1993-a6-real-nat real-type n)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-archimedean-p (real-type)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type value)
     (putnam-1993-a6-archimedean-bound-exists-p
      real-type value))))

(defun putnam-1993-a6-real-field-p (real-type)
  (let ((zero (putnam-1993-a6-zero real-type))
        (one (putnam-1993-a6-one real-type)))
    (and
     (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type zero)
     (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type one)
     (not (equal zero one))
     (putnam-1993-a6-field-laws-p real-type)
     (putnam-1993-a6-order-laws-p real-type)
     (putnam-1993-a6-less real-type zero one)
     (putnam-1993-a6-complete-p real-type)
     (putnam-1993-a6-archimedean-p real-type))))

;; Sum of seq(i)+1 over 0 <= i < count, exactly as in the source hypothesis.
(defun putnam-1993-a6-prefix-sum (count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      0
    (let ((index (1- count)))
      (+
       (putnam-1993-a6-prefix-sum index)
       (+ (putnam-1993-a6-sequence index) 1)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-prefix-index-exists-p (index)
  (exists (count)
    (and
     (natp count)
     (equal
      index
      (putnam-1993-a6-prefix-sum count)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-values-are-two-or-three-p ()
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (natp index)
     (or
      (equal (putnam-1993-a6-sequence index) 2)
      (equal (putnam-1993-a6-sequence index) 3)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-self-referential-p ()
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (natp index)
     (iff
      (equal (putnam-1993-a6-sequence index) 2)
      (putnam-1993-a6-prefix-index-exists-p index)))))

;; floor(r*m) = n is represented without approximation by the equivalent
;; ordered-field inequalities n <= r*m < n+1.
(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-beatty-index-p
    (real-type r index)
  (exists (m)
    (and
     (natp m)
     (let ((product
            (putnam-1993-a6-multiply
             real-type
             r
             (putnam-1993-a6-real-nat real-type m))))
       (and
        (putnam-1993-a6-leq
         real-type
         (putnam-1993-a6-real-nat real-type index)
         product)
        (putnam-1993-a6-less
         real-type
         product
         (putnam-1993-a6-real-nat
          real-type (+ index 1))))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-beatty-representation-p
    (real-type r)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (natp index)
     (iff
      (equal (putnam-1993-a6-sequence index) 2)
      (putnam-1993-a6-beatty-index-p
       real-type r index)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-a6-real-witness-exists-p
    (real-type)
  (exists (r)
    (and
     (putnam-1993-a6-real-p real-type r)
     (putnam-1993-a6-beatty-representation-p
      real-type r))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1993-a6-statement (real-type)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-1993-a6-real-field-p real-type)
    (putnam-1993-a6-values-are-two-or-three-p)
    (putnam-1993-a6-self-referential-p))
   (putnam-1993-a6-real-witness-exists-p
    real-type)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1993_a6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a6:
-- a self-describing infinite sequence of 2s and 3s is characterized by the
-- floor values of multiples of a real number. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

negativeNat : Nat -> Int
negativeNat zero =
  pos zero
negativeNat (suc n) =
  negsuc n

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

successorInt : Int -> Int
successorInt (pos n) =
  pos (suc n)
successorInt (negsuc zero) =
  pos zero
successorInt (negsuc (suc n)) =
  negsuc n

record StandardFloor
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    floor : R -> Int

    floor-lower :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals
        (fromInt reals (floor x))
        x
    floor-upper :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals
        x
        (fromInt reals (successorInt (floor x)))
    floor-unique :
      (x : R) ->
      (z : Int) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (fromInt reals z) x ->
      StrictLess reals x (fromInt reals (successorInt z)) ->
      floor x == z

open StandardFloor

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

sumFirst : Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat
sumFirst zero term =
  zero
sumFirst (suc n) term =
  sumFirst n term + term n

module Putnam1993A6Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (flooring : StandardFloor reals) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (seq : Nat -> Nat) ->
    ((n : Nat) ->
      (seq n == twoN) or (seq n == threeN)) ->
    ((n : Nat) ->
      Iff
        (seq n == twoN)
      (Exists Nat
        (\ N ->
          n ==
          sumFirst N
            (\ i -> seq i + oneN)))) ->
    Exists R
      (\ r ->
        (n : Nat) ->
        Iff
          (seq n == twoN)
        (Exists Nat
          (\ m ->
            pos (suc n) ==
            successorInt
              (floor flooring
                (multiply reals r (fromNat reals m))))))

putnam-1993-a6 : Set1
putnam-1993-a6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (flooring : StandardFloor reals) ->
  Putnam1993A6Statement.proposition reals flooring

title: putnam_1993_a6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a6:
  a self-describing sequence of twos and threes has a real floor-sequence
  characterization of the positions of its twos. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory realTheory intrealTheory;

val putnam_1993_a6 =
  ``!seq : num -> num.
      (!n : num. seq n = 2 \/ seq n = 3) /\
      (!n : num.
         seq n = 2 <=>
         ?N : num. n = SIGMA (\i : num. seq i + 1) (count N))
      ==>
      ?r : real.
        !n : num.
          seq n = 2 <=>
          ?m : num.
            int_of_num (n + 1) =
            1 + INT_FLOOR (r * (&m : real))``;

title: putnam_1993_a6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1993_a6: a self-indexing sequence of 2s and 3s has its positions
  occupied by 2 characterized by a real Beatty-type floor sequence. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  A ranges over integer-valued sequences indexed by NN0. The first antecedent
  forces every value to be 2 or 3, so this is equivalent to the natural-valued
  sequence type in the Isabelle source. The set 0 ..^ N consists exactly of
  the N indices 0 through N - 1, matching both source prefix sums.

  The witness m ranges over NN0, preserving the nonnegative witness specified
  by Isabelle and by the problem statement. This is also equivalent to Lean's
  integer witness: the antecedent gives A(0) = 2 and then A(3) = 2, so any
  parameter satisfying the conclusion is nonzero; replacing it by its
  absolute value and replacing an integer witness by its absolute value
  preserves every nonnegative floor value. Conversely, for a positive
  parameter, a negative integer witness cannot produce a nonnegative floor
  value, while NN0 is contained in ZZ.

  Set.mm's |_ is the floor function on the reals. The final declaration is
  the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

${
  $d A N i m n r $.

  putnambench-putnam-1993-a6 $a |- A. A e. ( ZZ ^m NN0 )
    (
      (
        A. n e. NN0
          (
            ( A ` n ) = 2
            \/
            ( A ` n ) = 3
          )
        /\
        A. n e. NN0
          (
            ( A ` n ) = 2
            <->
            E. N e. NN0
              n
              =
              (
                sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ N )
                  ( ( A ` i ) + 1 )
              )
          )
      )
      ->
      E. r e. RR
        A. n e. NN0
          (
            ( A ` n ) = 2
            <->
            E. m e. NN0
              ( n + 1 )
              =
              ( 1 + ( |_ ` ( r x. m ) ) )
          )
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1993_a6
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a6:
:: a self-describing sequence of 2s and 3s has its 2-valued positions given
:: by a Beatty sequence for some real parameter. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies NUMBERS, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, TARSKI, CARD_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, REAL_1, ORDINAL1, INT_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, CARD_3,
    VALUED_0, VALUED_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, REAL_1, INT_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, FINSEQ_1, RVSUM_1, FINSEQ_2, NAT_1, NAT_D;
  constructors REAL_1, NAT_D, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, RVSUM_1,
    FINSEQOP;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1,
    NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XREAL_0, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, RVSUM_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, CARD_1, MEMBERED;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for seq being Function of NAT,NAT st
    (for n being Nat holds seq.n = 2 or seq.n = 3) &
    (for n being Nat holds
      (seq.n = 2 iff
        ex N being Nat, terms being FinSequence of NAT st
          len terms = N &
          (for i being Nat st i < N holds
            terms.(i + 1) = seq.i + 1) &
          n = Sum terms))
  holds
    ex r being Real st
      for n being Nat holds
        (seq.n = 2 iff
          ex m being Nat st
            ((n + 1) qua Integer) =
              1 + [\ r * (m qua Real) /])
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1993_a6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_a6:
% a self-describing sequence of 2s and 3s has its 2-valued positions given by
% the floors of multiples of a real number. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1993_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  prefix_sum(sequence: natural_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      prefix_sum(sequence, count - 1)
        + sequence(count - 1) + 1
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  putnam_1993_a6: bool =
    FORALL (sequence: natural_sequence):
      ((FORALL (n: nat):
          sequence(n) = 2 OR sequence(n) = 3)
        AND (FORALL (n: nat):
          sequence(n) = 2
            IFF EXISTS (count: nat):
              n = prefix_sum(sequence, count)))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (r: real):
          FORALL (n: nat):
            sequence(n) = 2
              IFF EXISTS (m: nat):
                floor(r * (m :: real)) = (n :: int)
END putnam_1993_a6

title: putnam_1993_b1

import Mathlib

abbrev putnam_1993_b1_solution : ℕ := sorry
-- 3987
/--
Find the smallest positive integer $n$ such that for every integer $m$ with $0< m<1993$, there exists an integer $k$ for which $\frac{m}{1993}<\frac{k}{n}<\frac{m+1}{1994}$.
-/
theorem putnam_1993_b1 :
    IsLeast
    {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧
      ∀ m ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℤ) (1993), ∃ k : ℤ,
      (m / 1993 < (k : ℝ) / n) ∧ ((k : ℝ) / n < (m + 1) / 1994) }
    putnam_1993_b1_solution :=
  sorry

title: putnam_1993_b1
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b1:
;; 3987 is the least positive integer n such that every integer m with
;; 0 < m < 1993 admits an integer k strictly between the specified rational
;; bounds m/1993 and (m+1)/1994 after division by n. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For positive n and 0 < m < 1993, any integer k satisfying the source
;; inequalities must have 0 < k < n: the lower bound is positive and the upper
;; bound is less than one. Conversely every possible source witness is
;; therefore included in this finite search. ACL2's rational comparisons agree
;; with the same inequalities after embedding these rational values in R.
(defun putnam-1993-b1-witness-through-p (n m candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (and (posp n)
           (natp m)
           (natp candidate))
      (or (and (< (/ m 1993)
                  (/ candidate n))
               (< (/ candidate n)
                  (/ (+ m 1) 1994)))
          (and (not (zp candidate))
               (putnam-1993-b1-witness-through-p
                n m (- candidate 1))))
    nil))

;; Called with m=1992, this is the universal quantifier over exactly the
;; integers 0 < m < 1993, with each existential k kept internal.
(defun putnam-1993-b1-all-m-through-p (n m)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix m)))
  (if (and (posp n)
           (natp m))
      (if (zp m)
          t
        (and (putnam-1993-b1-witness-through-p
              n m (- n 1))
             (putnam-1993-b1-all-m-through-p
              n (- m 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1993-b1-condition-p (n)
  (and (posp n)
       (putnam-1993-b1-all-m-through-p n 1992)))

;; Since the condition itself requires positivity, the assertion that every
;; solution is at least 3987 is equivalent to checking that none of the
;; positive integers through 3986 satisfies it.
(defun putnam-1993-b1-no-solution-through-p (candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (natp candidate)
      (if (zp candidate)
          t
        (and (not (putnam-1993-b1-condition-p candidate))
             (putnam-1993-b1-no-solution-through-p
              (- candidate 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1993-b1-statement ()
  (and (putnam-1993-b1-condition-p 3987)
       (putnam-1993-b1-no-solution-through-p 3986)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- satisfying the stated rational interval condition. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1993B1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

bound : Nat
bound =
  1993

next-bound : Nat
next-bound =
  1994

solution : Nat
solution =
  3987

Qualifies : Nat -> Set
Qualifies n =
  zero <N n
  and
  ((m : Nat) ->
    zero <N m ->
    m <N bound ->
    Exists Nat
      (\ k ->
        (m * n <N k * bound)
        and
        (k * next-bound <N (m + one) * n)))

record IsLeastQualifying (least : Nat) : Set where
  field
    qualifies :
      Qualifies least
    least-bound :
      (n : Nat) ->
      Qualifies n ->
      least <=N n

putnam-1993-b1 : Set
putnam-1993-b1 =
  IsLeastQualifying solution

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b1:
% 3987 is the least positive integer n satisfying the stated real interval
% condition for every integer m with 0 < m < 1993. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1993_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  admissible(n: nat): bool =
    n > 0
      AND FORALL (m: int):
        (0 < m AND m < 1993)
          IMPLIES
            EXISTS (k: int):
              safe_div(m :: real, 1993)
                < safe_div(k :: real, n :: real)
                AND safe_div(k :: real, n :: real)
                  < safe_div((m + 1) :: real, 1994)

  putnam_1993_b1_solution: nat = 3987

  putnam_1993_b1_statement: bool =
    admissible(putnam_1993_b1_solution)
      AND FORALL (n: nat):
        admissible(n) IMPLIES putnam_1993_b1_solution <= n
END putnam_1993_b1

import Mathlib

abbrev putnam_1993_b3_solution : ℚ × ℚ := sorry
-- (5 / 4, -1 / 4)
/--
Two real numbers $x$ and $y$ are chosen at random in the interval $(0,1)$ with respect to the uniform distribution. What is the probability that the closest integer to $x/y$ is even? Express the answer in the form $r+s\pi$, where $r$ and $s$ are rational numbers.
-/
theorem putnam_1993_b3 :
  let (r, s) := putnam_1993_b3_solution;
  (MeasureTheory.volume
    {p : Fin 2 → ℝ | 0 < p ∧ p < 1 ∧ Even (round (p 0 / p 1))}
  ).toReal
  = r + s * Real.pi :=
sorry

title: putnam_1993_b3
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b3:
   the planar probability that the nearest integer to x/y is even for
   uniformly chosen x,y in the open unit interval. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals ZArith QArith.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_1993_b3_point := (R * R)%type.
Definition putnam_1993_b3_point_set := putnam_1993_b3_point -> Prop.

Definition putnam_1993_b3_solution : (Q * Q)%type :=
  ((5 / 4)%Q, (-1 / 4)%Q).

Definition putnam_1993_b3_nearest_integer (t : R) : Z :=
  Int_part (t + 1 / 2).

Definition putnam_1993_b3_event : putnam_1993_b3_point_set :=
  fun p : putnam_1993_b3_point =>
    0 < fst p /\
    fst p < 1 /\
    0 < snd p /\
    snd p < 1 /\
    Z.even
      (putnam_1993_b3_nearest_integer (fst p / snd p)) = true.

Record putnam_1993_b3_open_rectangle : Type := {
  putnam_1993_b3_x_lower : R;
  putnam_1993_b3_x_upper : R;
  putnam_1993_b3_y_lower : R;
  putnam_1993_b3_y_upper : R
}.

Definition putnam_1993_b3_in_open_rectangle
    (rectangle : putnam_1993_b3_open_rectangle)
    (p : putnam_1993_b3_point) : Prop :=
  putnam_1993_b3_x_lower rectangle < fst p <
    putnam_1993_b3_x_upper rectangle /\
  putnam_1993_b3_y_lower rectangle < snd p <
    putnam_1993_b3_y_upper rectangle.

Definition putnam_1993_b3_rectangle_area
    (rectangle : putnam_1993_b3_open_rectangle) : R :=
  Rmax 0
    (putnam_1993_b3_x_upper rectangle -
     putnam_1993_b3_x_lower rectangle) *
  Rmax 0
    (putnam_1993_b3_y_upper rectangle -
     putnam_1993_b3_y_lower rectangle).

Definition putnam_1993_b3_rectangles_cover
    (S : putnam_1993_b3_point_set)
    (rectangles : nat -> putnam_1993_b3_open_rectangle) : Prop :=
  forall p : putnam_1993_b3_point,
    S p ->
    exists n : nat,
      putnam_1993_b3_in_open_rectangle (rectangles n) p.

Fixpoint putnam_1993_b3_partial_rectangle_area
    (rectangles : nat -> putnam_1993_b3_open_rectangle)
    (n : nat) : R :=
  match n with
  | O => 0
  | S k =>
      putnam_1993_b3_partial_rectangle_area rectangles k +
      putnam_1993_b3_rectangle_area (rectangles k)
  end.

(* The countable-open-rectangle characterization of finite planar Lebesgue
   outer measure, equal here to Lebesgue measure because the event is Borel. *)
Definition putnam_1993_b3_has_planar_lebesgue_measure
    (S : putnam_1993_b3_point_set) (area : R) : Prop :=
  0 <= area /\
  (forall rectangles : nat -> putnam_1993_b3_open_rectangle,
    putnam_1993_b3_rectangles_cover S rectangles ->
    forall lower : R,
      lower < area ->
      exists n : nat,
        lower <
          putnam_1993_b3_partial_rectangle_area rectangles n) /\
  (forall epsilon : R,
    0 < epsilon ->
    exists rectangles : nat -> putnam_1993_b3_open_rectangle,
      putnam_1993_b3_rectangles_cover S rectangles /\
      forall n : nat,
        putnam_1993_b3_partial_rectangle_area rectangles n <
          area + epsilon).

Theorem putnam_1993_b3 :
  putnam_1993_b3_has_planar_lebesgue_measure
    putnam_1993_b3_event
    (Q2R (fst putnam_1993_b3_solution) +
     Q2R (snd putnam_1993_b3_solution) * PI).
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b3:
  the probability that the nearest integer to x/y is even for a uniformly
  chosen point (x,y) in the open unit square is 5/4 - pi/4. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

needs "Library/transc.ml";;

let statement =
  `let cover_bound =
     \(s:(real#real)->bool) (B:real).
       &0 <= B /\
       ?xl xu yl yu:num->real.
         (!k:num. xl k <= xu k /\ yl k <= yu k) /\
         (!p:real#real.
            p IN s
            ==> ?k:num.
                  xl k < FST p /\ FST p < xu k /\
                  yl k < SND p /\ SND p < yu k) /\
         (!N:num.
            sum (0..N)
              (\k:num. (xu k - xl k) * (yu k - yl k)) <= B) in
   let lebesgue_outer_measure =
     \(s:(real#real)->bool).
       inf {B:real | cover_bound s B} in
   let nearest_integer =
     \x:real.
       @z:int.
         real_of_int z - &1 / &2 <= x /\
         x < real_of_int z + &1 / &2 in
   let putnam_1993_b3_solution =
     (&5 / &4,--(&1 / &4)) in
   lebesgue_outer_measure
     {p:real#real |
        &0 < FST p /\ FST p < &1 /\
        &0 < SND p /\ SND p < &1 /\
        (?k:int.
           nearest_integer (FST p / SND p) = (&2:int) * k)} =
   FST putnam_1993_b3_solution +
   SND putnam_1993_b3_solution * pi`;;

title: putnam_1993_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b3:
;; the probability that the nearest integer to the ratio of two independent
;; uniform points in (0,1) is even equals 5/4 - pi/4. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-1993-b3-midpoint (index subdivisions)
  (/ (- (* 2 index) 1)
     (* 2 subdivisions)))

;; FLOOR(x/y + 1/2) is a nearest integer away from the half-integer tie
;; lines. Those countably many lines have planar measure zero.
(defun putnam-1993-b3-event-p (x y)
  (and
   (< 0 x)
   (< x 1)
   (< 0 y)
   (< y 1)
   (evenp (floor (+ (/ x y) 1/2) 1))))

(defun putnam-1993-b3-row-count
    (x remaining subdivisions)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+ (if
           (putnam-1993-b3-event-p
            x
            (putnam-1993-b3-midpoint
             remaining subdivisions))
           1
         0)
       (putnam-1993-b3-row-count
        x (- remaining 1) subdivisions))))

(defun putnam-1993-b3-event-count
    (remaining subdivisions)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1993-b3-row-count
        (putnam-1993-b3-midpoint
         remaining subdivisions)
        subdivisions subdivisions)
       (putnam-1993-b3-event-count
        (- remaining 1) subdivisions))))

;; Direct midpoint sum of the original unit-square event indicator.
(defun putnam-1993-b3-area-approx (subdivisions)
  (if (posp subdivisions)
      (/ (putnam-1993-b3-event-count
          subdivisions subdivisions)
         (* subdivisions subdivisions))
    0))

;; Exact rational Taylor prefixes for arctan(z), used in the independent
;; Machin Cauchy name pi = 16*arctan(1/5) - 4*arctan(1/239).
(defun putnam-1993-b3-arctan-prefix (z terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (exponent (+ (* 2 index) 1))
           (sign (if (equal (mod index 2) 0) 1 -1)))
      (+ (putnam-1993-b3-arctan-prefix z index)
         (/ (* sign (expt z exponent))
            exponent)))))

(defun putnam-1993-b3-pi-prefix (terms)
  (- (* 16
        (putnam-1993-b3-arctan-prefix 1/5 terms))
     (* 4
        (putnam-1993-b3-arctan-prefix 1/239 terms))))

;; The rational pair (5/4,-1/4) from the source specifies this real value.
(defun putnam-1993-b3-solution-prefix (pi-terms)
  (- 5/4
     (/ (putnam-1993-b3-pi-prefix pi-terms) 4)))

;; The event boundary is a countable union of line segments together with
;; y=0, hence has area zero. The midpoint sums therefore converge to its
;; Lebesgue measure. Existential cutoffs add no proof-specific rate.
(defun-sk putnam-1993-b3-tail-p (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (precision)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp precision)
      (<= cutoff precision))
     (< (abs
         (- (putnam-1993-b3-area-approx precision)
            (putnam-1993-b3-solution-prefix precision)))
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1993-b3-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (posp cutoff)
     (putnam-1993-b3-tail-p epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-1993-b3-statement ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-1993-b3-cutoff-exists-p epsilon))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc threeN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc fourN

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

alternatingUnit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingUnit reals zero =
  oneR reals
alternatingUnit reals (suc n) =
  negate reals (alternatingUnit reals n)

oddNatural : Nat -> Nat
oddNatural n =
  suc (n + n)

leibnizTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
leibnizTerm reals n =
  divide reals
    (alternatingUnit reals n)
    (fromNat reals (oddNatural n))

piApproximation :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
piApproximation reals n =
  multiply reals
    (fromNat reals fourN)
    (sumFirst reals (suc n) (leibnizTerm reals))

record StandardRealAnalysis (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    algebra : CompleteOrderedRealField R
    pi : R
    pi-leibniz-limit :
      ConvergesTo algebra
        (piApproximation algebra)
        pi

open StandardRealAnalysis

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    firstCoordinate  : R
    secondCoordinate : R

open Point

Region : Set -> Set1
Region R =
  Point R -> Set

Empty :
  {R : Set} ->
  Region R
Empty _ =
  Bottom

Complement :
  {R : Set} ->
  Region R ->
  Region R
Complement body p =
  Not (body p)

Intersect :
  {R : Set} ->
  Region R ->
  Region R ->
  Region R
Intersect leftBody rightBody p =
  leftBody p and rightBody p

UnionAll :
  {R : Set} ->
  (Nat -> Region R) ->
  Region R
UnionAll bodies p =
  Exists Nat (\ n -> bodies n p)

Disjoint :
  {R : Set} ->
  Region R ->
  Region R ->
  Set
Disjoint {R} leftBody rightBody =
  (p : Point R) ->
  leftBody p ->
  rightBody p ->
  Bottom

PairwiseDisjoint :
  {R : Set} ->
  (Nat -> Region R) ->
  Set
PairwiseDisjoint bodies =
  (m n : Nat) ->
  m != n ->
  Disjoint (bodies m) (bodies n)

addPoint :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R
addPoint reals p q =
  point
    (add reals
      (firstCoordinate p)
      (firstCoordinate q))
    (add reals
      (secondCoordinate p)
      (secondCoordinate q))

translateRegion :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Region R ->
  Region R
translateRegion {R} reals offset body p =
  Exists (Point R)
    (\ q ->
      body q
      and
      p == addPoint reals offset q)

HalfOpenBox :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Region R
HalfOpenBox reals lower upper p =
  (lessOrEqual reals
    (firstCoordinate lower)
    (firstCoordinate p)
  and
  StrictLess reals
    (firstCoordinate p)
    (firstCoordinate upper))
  and
  (lessOrEqual reals
    (secondCoordinate lower)
    (secondCoordinate p)
  and
  StrictLess reals
    (secondCoordinate p)
    (secondCoordinate upper))

data ExtendedNonnegative (R : Set) : Set where
  finite   : R -> ExtendedNonnegative R
  infinity : ExtendedNonnegative R

data ExtendedLessOrEqual
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  ExtendedNonnegative R ->
  ExtendedNonnegative R ->
  Set where

  finite<=finite :
    {x y : R} ->
    lessOrEqual reals x y ->
    ExtendedLessOrEqual reals (finite x) (finite y)

  finite<=infinity :
    {x : R} ->
    ExtendedLessOrEqual reals (finite x) infinity

  infinity<=infinity :
    ExtendedLessOrEqual reals infinity infinity

addExtended :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  ExtendedNonnegative R ->
  ExtendedNonnegative R ->
  ExtendedNonnegative R
addExtended reals infinity rightValue =
  infinity
addExtended reals (finite x) infinity =
  infinity
addExtended reals (finite x) (finite y) =
  finite (add reals x y)

sumFirstExtended :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> ExtendedNonnegative R) ->
  ExtendedNonnegative R
sumFirstExtended reals zero term =
  finite (zeroR reals)
sumFirstExtended reals (suc n) term =
  addExtended reals
    (sumFirstExtended reals n term)
    (term n)

UpperBoundExtended :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> ExtendedNonnegative R) ->
  ExtendedNonnegative R ->
  Set
UpperBoundExtended reals values bound =
  (n : Nat) ->
  ExtendedLessOrEqual reals (values n) bound

LeastUpperBoundExtended :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> ExtendedNonnegative R) ->
  ExtendedNonnegative R ->
  Set
LeastUpperBoundExtended reals values supremum =
  UpperBoundExtended reals values supremum
  and
  ((upper : ExtendedNonnegative _) ->
    UpperBoundExtended reals values upper ->
    ExtendedLessOrEqual reals supremum upper)

record StandardPlaneLebesgueMeasure
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    measurable : Region R -> Set
    volume : Region R -> ExtendedNonnegative R

    measurable-empty :
      measurable Empty
    measurable-complement :
      (body : Region R) ->
      measurable body ->
      measurable (Complement body)
    measurable-countable-union :
      (bodies : Nat -> Region R) ->
      ((n : Nat) -> measurable (bodies n)) ->
      measurable (UnionAll bodies)
    measurable-intersection :
      (leftBody rightBody : Region R) ->
      measurable leftBody ->
      measurable rightBody ->
      measurable (Intersect leftBody rightBody)
    measurable-translation :
      (offset : Point R) ->
      (body : Region R) ->
      measurable body ->
      measurable (translateRegion reals offset body)
    measurable-box :
      (lower upper : Point R) ->
      measurable (HalfOpenBox reals lower upper)

    volume-congruent :
      (leftBody rightBody : Region R) ->
      ((p : Point R) ->
        Iff (leftBody p) (rightBody p)) ->
      volume leftBody == volume rightBody
    volume-empty :
      volume Empty == finite (zeroR reals)
    volume-nonnegative :
      (body : Region R) ->
      measurable body ->
      ExtendedLessOrEqual reals
        (finite (zeroR reals))
        (volume body)
    volume-countable-additive :
      (bodies : Nat -> Region R) ->
      ((n : Nat) -> measurable (bodies n)) ->
      PairwiseDisjoint bodies ->
      LeastUpperBoundExtended reals
        (\ count ->
          sumFirstExtended reals count
            (\ n -> volume (bodies n)))
        (volume (UnionAll bodies))
    volume-translation-invariant :
      (offset : Point R) ->
      (body : Region R) ->
      measurable body ->
      volume (translateRegion reals offset body) ==
      volume body
    volume-box :
      (lower upper : Point R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals
        (firstCoordinate lower)
        (firstCoordinate upper) ->
      lessOrEqual reals
        (secondCoordinate lower)
        (secondCoordinate upper) ->
      volume (HalfOpenBox reals lower upper) ==
      finite
        (multiply reals
          (subtract reals
            (firstCoordinate upper)
            (firstCoordinate lower))
          (subtract reals
            (secondCoordinate upper)
            (secondCoordinate lower)))

open StandardPlaneLebesgueMeasure

EvenNearestInteger :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
EvenNearestInteger reals value =
  Exists Nat
    (\ k ->
      let evenInteger = fromNat reals (k + k)
          half = divide reals
            (oneR reals)
            (fromNat reals twoN)
      in
      lessOrEqual reals
        (subtract reals evenInteger half)
        value
      and
      StrictLess reals
        value
        (add reals evenInteger half))

module Putnam1993B3Statement
  {R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (lebesgue : StandardPlaneLebesgueMeasure (algebra analysis)) where

  reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R
  reals =
    algebra analysis

  favorableRegion : Region R
  favorableRegion p =
    StrictLess reals
      (zeroR reals)
      (firstCoordinate p)
    and
    StrictLess reals
      (firstCoordinate p)
      (oneR reals)
    and
    StrictLess reals
      (zeroR reals)
      (secondCoordinate p)
    and
    StrictLess reals
      (secondCoordinate p)
      (oneR reals)
    and
    EvenNearestInteger reals
      (divide reals
        (firstCoordinate p)
        (secondCoordinate p))

  solution : R
  solution =
    subtract reals
      (divide reals
        (fromNat reals fiveN)
        (fromNat reals fourN))
      (divide reals
        (pi analysis)
        (fromNat reals fourN))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    volume lebesgue favorableRegion ==
    finite solution

putnam-1993-b3 : Set1
putnam-1993-b3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R) ->
  (lebesgue : StandardPlaneLebesgueMeasure (algebra analysis)) ->
  Putnam1993B3Statement.proposition analysis lebesgue

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b3:
  the probability that the nearest integer to the ratio of two independent
  uniform points in the open unit interval is even equals 5/4 - pi/4. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory transcTheory;
open extrealTheory measureTheory lebesgue_measureTheory martingaleTheory;

val putnam_1993_b3 =
  ``measure
      (prod_measure_space lebesgue lebesgue)
      {p : real # real |
        0 < FST p /\ FST p < 1 /\
        0 < SND p /\ SND p < 1 /\
        EVEN (NUM_FLOOR (FST p / SND p + 1 / 2))} =
    Normal (5 / 4 - pi / 4)``;

title: putnam_1993_b3
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1993_b3: the planar Lebesgue
  measure of points in the open unit square for which the nearest
  integer to the coordinate ratio is even is expressed by a rational
  pair and pi.  This file contains no proof.

  The two coordinates are indexed by { 0 , 1 }, corresponding to the
  source type Fin 2.  Nearest-integer rounding is rendered as
  floor ( x + 1 / 2 ), and evenness is rendered by an internally
  quantified integer multiplier. The resolved rational pair is substituted
  directly as ( 5 / 4 , -1 / 4 ).
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$c P93B3I P93B3Plane P93B3Event P93B3Area $.

p93b3-index-syntax $a class P93B3I $.
p93b3-plane-syntax $a class P93B3Plane $.
p93b3-event-syntax $a class P93B3Event $.
p93b3-area-syntax $a class P93B3Area $.

p93b3-index-definition $a
  |- P93B3I = ( 0 ... 1 ) $.

p93b3-plane-definition $a
  |- P93B3Plane = ( RR ^m P93B3I ) $.

${
  $d i k p $.
  p93b3-event-definition $a
    |- P93B3Event =
        { p e. P93B3Plane |
          ( A. i e. P93B3I
              ( 0 < ( p ` i ) /\ ( p ` i ) < 1 )
            /\
            E. k e. ZZ
              ( |_ ` ( ( ( p ` 0 ) / ( p ` 1 ) ) + ( 1 / 2 ) ) )
                =
              ( 2 x. k ) ) } $.
$}

p93b3-area-definition $a
  |- P93B3Area = ( ( voln ` P93B3I ) ` P93B3Event ) $.

putnambench-putnam-1993-b3 $a
  |- P93B3Area =
      ( ( 5 / 4 ) + ( ( -u 1 / 4 ) x. _pi ) ) $.

title: putnam_1993_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b3:
% the probability that the nearest integer to x/y is even for independent
% uniform x,y in (0,1) is 5/4 - pi/4. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1993_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]
  planar_region: TYPE = [point -> bool]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  box: TYPE =
    [# left: real, right: real, bottom: real, top: real #]
  box_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> box]

  solution_pair: TYPE =
    [# rational_part: rat, pi_coefficient: rat #]

  putnam_1993_b3_solution: solution_pair =
    (# rational_part := 5 / 4,
       pi_coefficient := -1 / 4 #)

  nearest_integer(value: real): int =
    floor(value + 1 / 2)

  integer_even(value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (factor: int):
      value = 2 * factor

  event_region: planar_region =
    LAMBDA (p: point):
      0 < x_coord(p)
        AND x_coord(p) < 1
        AND 0 < y_coord(p)
        AND y_coord(p) < 1
        AND integer_even(
          nearest_integer(x_coord(p) / y_coord(p)))

  in_open_box(p: point, rectangle: box): bool =
    left(rectangle) < x_coord(p)
      AND x_coord(p) < right(rectangle)
      AND bottom(rectangle) < y_coord(p)
      AND y_coord(p) < top(rectangle)

  box_area(rectangle: box): real =
    IF left(rectangle) < right(rectangle)
        AND bottom(rectangle) < top(rectangle)
    THEN
      (right(rectangle) - left(rectangle))
        * (top(rectangle) - bottom(rectangle))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  partial_box_area(
      boxes: box_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_box_area(boxes, count - 1)
        + box_area(boxes(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  covers(region: planar_region, boxes: box_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (p: point):
      region(p) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (index: nat):
          in_open_box(p, boxes(index))

  cover_has_total_area(
      region: planar_region,
      boxes: box_sequence,
      total: real): bool =
    covers(region, boxes)
      AND converges_to(
        LAMBDA (count: nat):
          partial_box_area(boxes, count),
        total)

  has_lebesgue_outer_area(
      region: planar_region,
      area: real): bool =
    0 <= area
      AND (FORALL (boxes: box_sequence), (total: real):
        cover_has_total_area(region, boxes, total)
          IMPLIES area <= total)
      AND (FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (boxes: box_sequence), (total: real):
          cover_has_total_area(region, boxes, total)
            AND total < area + epsilon_value)

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  leibniz_partial_sum(count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        leibniz_partial_sum(count - 1)
          + alternating_sign(index)
              / ((2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  is_pi(value: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat):
        4 * leibniz_partial_sum(count),
      value)

  pi: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        is_pi(value))

  solution_value: real =
    (rational_part(putnam_1993_b3_solution) :: real)
      + (pi_coefficient(putnam_1993_b3_solution) :: real)
          * pi

  putnam_1993_b3: bool =
    has_lebesgue_outer_area(event_region, solution_value)
END putnam_1993_b3

content:
import Mathlib

/--
The function $K(x,y)$ is positive and continuous for $0 \leq x \leq 1,0 \leq y \leq 1$, and the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are positive and continuous for $0 \leq x \leq 1$. Suppose that for all $x$, $0 \leq x \leq 1$, $\int_0^1 f(y)K(x,y)\,dy=g(x)$ and $\int_0^1 g(y)K(x,y)\,dy=f(x)$. Show that $f(x)=g(x)$ for $0 \leq x \leq 1$.
-/
theorem putnam_1993_b4
(K : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ)
(f g : ℝ → ℝ)
(Kpos : ∀ x y : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, K (x, y) > 0)
(Kcont : ContinuousOn K {(x, y) : ℝ × ℝ | x ∈ Set.Icc 0 1 ∧ y ∈ Set.Icc 0 1})
(fgpos : ∀ x : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, f x > 0 ∧ g x > 0)
(fgcont : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧ ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc 0 1))
(fgint : ∀ x : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, (∫ y in Set.Ioo 0 1, f y * K (x, y)) = g x ∧ (∫ y in Set.Ioo 0 1, g y * K (x, y)) = f x)
: ∀ x : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, f x = g x :=
sorry

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b4:
  positive continuous real functions and a positive continuous kernel on the
  unit interval satisfying reciprocal integral equations are equal there.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let transc_output = open_out "/dev/null";;
let transc_formatter = Format.formatter_of_out_channel transc_output;;
let previous_file_loader = !Hol_loader.file_loader;;
Hol_loader.file_loader :=
  (fun path -> Toploop.use_file transc_formatter path);;
let transc_loaded =
  Toploop.use_file transc_formatter "Library/transc.ml";;
Hol_loader.file_loader := previous_file_loader;;
Format.pp_print_flush transc_formatter ();;
close_out transc_output;;
if not transc_loaded then failwith "failed to load Library/transc.ml";;

let statement =
  `let unit_interval = {x:real | &0 <= x /\ x <= &1} in
   let continuous_on_interval =
     \(h:real->real).
       !x:real.
         x IN unit_interval
         ==> !e:real.
               &0 < e
               ==> ?d:real.
                     &0 < d /\
                     !y:real.
                       y IN unit_interval /\ abs (y - x) < d
                       ==> abs (h y - h x) < e in
   let continuous_on_rectangle =
     \(K:(real#real)->real).
       !x y:real.
         x IN unit_interval /\ y IN unit_interval
         ==> !e:real.
               &0 < e
               ==> ?d:real.
                     &0 < d /\
                     !x' y':real.
                       x' IN unit_interval /\
                       y' IN unit_interval /\
                       abs (x' - x) < d /\
                       abs (y' - y) < d
                       ==> abs (K (x',y') - K (x,y)) < e in
   !K:(real#real)->real. !f g:real->real.
     ((!x y:real.
         x IN unit_interval /\ y IN unit_interval
         ==> &0 < K (x,y)) /\
      continuous_on_rectangle K /\
      (!x:real.
         x IN unit_interval
         ==> &0 < f x /\ &0 < g x) /\
      continuous_on_interval f /\
      continuous_on_interval g /\
      (!x:real.
         x IN unit_interval
         ==> integral(&0,&1) (\y:real. f y * K (x,y)) = g x /\
             integral(&0,&1) (\y:real. g y * K (x,y)) = f x))
     ==>
     !x:real. x IN unit_interval ==> f x = g x`;;

title: putnam_1993_b4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b4:
;; positive continuous real functions coupled by a positive continuous kernel
;; on the unit interval through two integral equations are equal there. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; FUNCTION(x,epsilon) and KERNEL(x,y,epsilon) are rational regular Cauchy
;; names for exact real values at rational points of [0,1]. Internal moduli
;; give their unique continuous extensions to the compact interval and square.
;; Since only these restrictions occur in the source proposition, this is
;; equivalent to its total real-function presentation.
;;
;; Strict positivity on a compact domain is equivalently expressed by an
;; internally existential uniform positive rational lower bound. The integral
;; equations use the double limit of rational right Riemann sums as the mesh
;; and value precision tend to zero. For the continuous source integrands this
;; limit is exactly the stated Lebesgue interval integral. Equality on the
;; dense rational points then extends to every real point of [0,1].

(defun p93b4-abs (x)
  (if (< x 0) (- x) x))

(defun p93b4-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and (rationalp x) (< 0 x)))

(defun p93b4-unit-rational-p (x)
  (and (rationalp x) (<= 0 x) (<= x 1)))

(defun p93b4-function-value (function x precision)
  (apply$ function (list x precision)))

(defun p93b4-kernel-value (kernel x y precision)
  (apply$ kernel (list x y precision)))

(defun-sk p93b4-function-name-p (function)
  (forall (x epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p x)
      (p93b4-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (p93b4-positive-rational-p eta))
     (and
      (rationalp
       (p93b4-function-value function x epsilon))
      (rationalp
       (p93b4-function-value function x eta))
      (<=
       (p93b4-abs
        (-
         (p93b4-function-value function x epsilon)
         (p93b4-function-value function x eta)))
       (+ epsilon eta))))))

(defun-sk p93b4-kernel-name-p (kernel)
  (forall (x y epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p x)
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p y)
      (p93b4-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (p93b4-positive-rational-p eta))
     (and
      (rationalp
       (p93b4-kernel-value kernel x y epsilon))
      (rationalp
       (p93b4-kernel-value kernel x y eta))
      (<=
       (p93b4-abs
        (-
         (p93b4-kernel-value kernel x y epsilon)
         (p93b4-kernel-value kernel x y eta)))
       (+ epsilon eta))))))

(defun-sk p93b4-function-modulus-p (function modulus)
  (forall (x y epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p x)
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p y)
      (p93b4-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (let ((delta (apply$ modulus (list epsilon))))
       (and
        (p93b4-positive-rational-p delta)
        (implies
         (< (p93b4-abs (- x y)) delta)
         (<=
          (p93b4-abs
           (-
            (p93b4-function-value
             function x (/ epsilon 4))
            (p93b4-function-value
             function y (/ epsilon 4))))
          epsilon)))))))

(defun-sk p93b4-function-continuous-p (function)
  (exists (modulus)
    (and
     (tamep-functionp modulus)
     (p93b4-function-modulus-p function modulus))))

(defun-sk p93b4-kernel-modulus-p (kernel modulus)
  (forall (x1 y1 x2 y2 epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p x1)
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p y1)
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p x2)
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p y2)
      (p93b4-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (let ((delta (apply$ modulus (list epsilon))))
       (and
        (p93b4-positive-rational-p delta)
        (implies
         (<
          (+
           (p93b4-abs (- x1 x2))
           (p93b4-abs (- y1 y2)))
          delta)
         (<=
          (p93b4-abs
           (-
            (p93b4-kernel-value
             kernel x1 y1 (/ epsilon 4))
            (p93b4-kernel-value
             kernel x2 y2 (/ epsilon 4))))
          epsilon)))))))

(defun-sk p93b4-kernel-continuous-p (kernel)
  (exists (modulus)
    (and
     (tamep-functionp modulus)
     (p93b4-kernel-modulus-p kernel modulus))))

(defun-sk p93b4-function-positive-bound-p
    (function lower)
  (forall (x epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p x)
      (p93b4-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (<=
      lower
      (+ (p93b4-function-value function x epsilon)
         epsilon)))))

(defun-sk p93b4-function-positive-p (function)
  (exists (lower)
    (and
     (p93b4-positive-rational-p lower)
     (p93b4-function-positive-bound-p
      function lower))))

(defun-sk p93b4-kernel-positive-bound-p
    (kernel lower)
  (forall (x y epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p x)
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p y)
      (p93b4-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (<=
      lower
      (+ (p93b4-kernel-value
          kernel x y epsilon)
         epsilon)))))

(defun-sk p93b4-kernel-positive-p (kernel)
  (exists (lower)
    (and
     (p93b4-positive-rational-p lower)
     (p93b4-kernel-positive-bound-p
      kernel lower))))

(defun p93b4-riemann-numerator
    (index pieces x precision function kernel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (zp index)
      0
    (let ((y (/ index pieces)))
      (+
       (*
        (p93b4-function-value function y precision)
        (p93b4-kernel-value kernel x y precision))
       (p93b4-riemann-numerator
        (- index 1)
        pieces
        x
        precision
        function
        kernel)))))

(defun p93b4-riemann-sum
    (pieces x precision function kernel)
  (if (posp pieces)
      (/
       (p93b4-riemann-numerator
        pieces pieces x precision function kernel)
       pieces)
    0))

(defun-sk p93b4-integral-tail-p
    (function kernel result x epsilon cutoff precision-cutoff)
  (forall (pieces precision)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp pieces)
      (posp cutoff)
      (<= cutoff pieces)
      (p93b4-positive-rational-p precision)
      (p93b4-positive-rational-p precision-cutoff)
      (<= precision precision-cutoff))
     (<=
      (p93b4-abs
       (-
        (p93b4-riemann-sum
         pieces x precision function kernel)
        (p93b4-function-value result x precision)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p93b4-integral-tail-exists-p
    (function kernel result x epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff precision-cutoff)
    (and
     (posp cutoff)
     (p93b4-positive-rational-p precision-cutoff)
     (p93b4-integral-tail-p
      function kernel result x epsilon
      cutoff precision-cutoff))))

(defun-sk p93b4-integral-equation-at-p
    (function kernel result x)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p93b4-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (p93b4-integral-tail-exists-p
      function kernel result x epsilon))))

(defun-sk p93b4-integral-equations-p
    (kernel f g)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p93b4-unit-rational-p x)
     (and
      (p93b4-integral-equation-at-p f kernel g x)
      (p93b4-integral-equation-at-p g kernel f x)))))

(defun-sk p93b4-equal-on-unit-p (f g)
  (forall (x epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (p93b4-unit-rational-p x)
      (p93b4-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (<=
      (p93b4-abs
       (-
        (p93b4-function-value f x epsilon)
        (p93b4-function-value g x epsilon)))
      (* 2 epsilon)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1993-b4-statement
    (kernel f g)
  (implies
   (and
    (tamep-functionp kernel)
    (tamep-functionp f)
    (tamep-functionp g)
    (p93b4-kernel-name-p kernel)
    (p93b4-function-name-p f)
    (p93b4-function-name-p g)
    (p93b4-kernel-continuous-p kernel)
    (p93b4-function-continuous-p f)
    (p93b4-function-continuous-p g)
    (p93b4-kernel-positive-p kernel)
    (p93b4-function-positive-p f)
    (p93b4-function-positive-p g)
    (p93b4-integral-equations-p kernel f g))
   (p93b4-equal-on-unit-p f g)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1993_b4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_1993_b4): positive continuous functions on the
-- unit interval satisfying two reciprocal integral equations are equal.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record Pair (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    fst : A
    snd : B

open Pair

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

UnitInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
UnitInterval reals x =
  lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x
  and
  lessOrEqual reals x (oneR reals)

UnitSquare :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Pair R R ->
  Set
UnitSquare reals point =
  UnitInterval reals (fst point)
  and
  UnitInterval reals (snd point)

ContinuousOn :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> Set) ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
ContinuousOn {R} reals domain function =
  (point : R) ->
  domain point ->
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        domain x ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function point)
          epsilon
          (function x)))

JointlyContinuousOn :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Pair R R -> Set) ->
  (Pair R R -> R) ->
  Set
JointlyContinuousOn {R} reals domain function =
  (point : Pair R R) ->
  domain point ->
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((other : Pair R R) ->
        domain other ->
        CloseTo reals (fst point) delta (fst other) ->
        CloseTo reals (snd point) delta (snd other) ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function point)
          epsilon
          (function other)))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

rightRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
rightRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals (suc i))
              step)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function integralValue =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      rightRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    integralValue

module Putnam1993B4Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (K : Pair R R -> R)
  (f g : R -> R) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    ((x y : R) ->
      UnitInterval reals x ->
      UnitInterval reals y ->
      StrictLess reals
        (zeroR reals)
        (K (pair x y))) ->
    JointlyContinuousOn reals (UnitSquare reals) K ->
    ((x : R) ->
      UnitInterval reals x ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (f x)
      and
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (g x)) ->
    ContinuousOn reals (UnitInterval reals) f ->
    ContinuousOn reals (UnitInterval reals) g ->
    ((x : R) ->
      UnitInterval reals x ->
      IntervalIntegralValue reals
        (zeroR reals)
        (oneR reals)
        (\ y ->
          multiply reals
            (f y)
            (K (pair x y)))
        (g x)
      and
      IntervalIntegralValue reals
        (zeroR reals)
        (oneR reals)
        (\ y ->
          multiply reals
            (g y)
            (K (pair x y)))
        (f x)) ->
    (x : R) ->
    UnitInterval reals x ->
    f x == g x

putnam-1993-b4 : Set1
putnam-1993-b4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (K : Pair R R -> R) ->
  (f g : R -> R) ->
  Putnam1993B4Statement.proposition reals K f g

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b4:
  positive continuous functions coupled by a positive continuous kernel on
  the unit square through reciprocal integral equations are equal on the
  unit interval. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pairTheory pred_setTheory metricTheory topologyTheory realTheory;
open real_topologyTheory integrationTheory;

val putnam_1993_b4 =
  ``let unit_interval = interval [0, 1]
    in
    let unit_square =
      {p : real # real |
         FST p IN unit_interval /\ SND p IN unit_interval}
    in
      !K : real # real -> real.
      !f g : real -> real.
        (!x y : real.
           x IN unit_interval /\ y IN unit_interval
           ==>
           0 < K (x, y)) /\
        continuous_map
          (subtopology (mtop mr2) unit_square, euclidean) K /\
        (!x : real.
           x IN unit_interval
           ==>
           0 < f x /\ 0 < g x) /\
        f continuous_on unit_interval /\
        g continuous_on unit_interval /\
        (!x : real.
           x IN unit_interval
           ==>
           integration$integral unit_interval
             (\y : real. f y * K (x, y)) = g x /\
           integration$integral unit_interval
             (\y : real. g y * K (x, y)) = f x)
        ==>
        !x : real. x IN unit_interval ==> f x = g x``;

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  K ranges over all real-valued functions on RR X. RR, while f and g range
  over all total real-valued functions on RR. Joint continuity of K on the
  unit square is expanded in relative epsilon-delta form; coordinatewise
  delta neighborhoods induce the standard product topology. Continuity of f
  and g is asserted for their restrictions to [0,1].

  Set.mm's S. binder is the real Lebesgue integral. Endpoint inclusion does
  not affect these integrals, so the closed interval notation agrees with the
  open-interval and interval-integral formulations in the ground truths.
  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d K d e f g u v x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-1993-b4 $a |-
    A. K e. ( RR ^m ( RR X. RR ) )
    A. f e. ( RR ^m RR )
    A. g e. ( RR ^m RR )
      (
        (
          A. x e. ( 0 [,] 1 ) A. y e. ( 0 [,] 1 )
            0 < ( K ` <. x , y >. )
          /\
          (
            A. x e. ( 0 [,] 1 ) A. y e. ( 0 [,] 1 ) A. e e. RR
              (
                0 < e
                ->
                E. d e. RR
                  (
                    0 < d
                    /\
                    A. u e. ( 0 [,] 1 ) A. v e. ( 0 [,] 1 )
                      (
                        (
                          ( abs ` ( u - x ) ) < d
                          /\
                          ( abs ` ( v - y ) ) < d
                        )
                        ->
                        (
                          abs
                          `
                          (
                            ( K ` <. u , v >. )
                            -
                            ( K ` <. x , y >. )
                          )
                        )
                        < e
                      )
                  )
              )
            /\
            (
              A. x e. ( 0 [,] 1 )
                (
                  0 < ( f ` x )
                  /\
                  0 < ( g ` x )
                )
              /\
              (
                (
                  ( f |` ( 0 [,] 1 ) )
                  e. ( ( 0 [,] 1 ) -cn-> RR )
                  /\
                  ( g |` ( 0 [,] 1 ) )
                  e. ( ( 0 [,] 1 ) -cn-> RR )
                )
                /\
                A. x e. ( 0 [,] 1 )
                  (
                    (
                      S. ( 0 [,] 1 )
                        (
                          ( f ` y )
                          x.
                          ( K ` <. x , y >. )
                        )
