title: putnam_1993_b4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b4:
% equality of positive continuous real functions satisfying mutually coupled
% unit-interval integral equations with a positive continuous kernel. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1993_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  bivariate_function: TYPE = [real, real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  in_closed_unit_interval(x: real): bool =
    0 <= x AND x <= 1

  positive_on_unit_interval(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      in_closed_unit_interval(x) IMPLIES f(x) > 0

  continuous_on_unit_interval(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      in_closed_unit_interval(x) IMPLIES
        FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
          EXISTS (delta: posreal):
            FORALL (z: real):
              (in_closed_unit_interval(z)
                AND abs(z - x) < delta)
              IMPLIES
                abs(f(z) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  positive_on_unit_square(K: bivariate_function): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: real):
      (in_closed_unit_interval(x)
        AND in_closed_unit_interval(y))
      IMPLIES K(x, y) > 0

  continuous_on_unit_square(K: bivariate_function): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: real):
      (in_closed_unit_interval(x)
        AND in_closed_unit_interval(y))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
          EXISTS (delta: posreal):
            FORALL (u, v: real):
              (in_closed_unit_interval(u)
                AND in_closed_unit_interval(v)
                AND abs(u - x) < delta
                AND abs(v - y) < delta)
              IMPLIES
                abs(K(u, v) - K(x, y)) < epsilon_value

  valid_partition(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = 0
      AND points(count) = 1
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          points(index) < points(index + 1)

  valid_tags(
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index) <= tags(index)
          AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1)

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      f: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count - 1)
        + f(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_unit_interval_integral(
      f: real_function,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
        FORALL
            (points, tags: real_sequence),
            (count: nat):
          (valid_partition(points, count)
            AND valid_tags(points, tags, count)
            AND mesh_less_than(points, count, mesh_bound))
          IMPLIES
            abs(
              riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count)
                - integral_value)
              < epsilon_value

  kernel_product(
      K: bivariate_function,
      f: real_function,
      x: real): real_function =
    LAMBDA (y: real): f(y) * K(x, y)

  putnam_1993_b4: bool =
    FORALL
        (K: bivariate_function),
        (f, g: real_function):
      (positive_on_unit_square(K)
        AND continuous_on_unit_square(K)
        AND positive_on_unit_interval(f)
        AND positive_on_unit_interval(g)
        AND continuous_on_unit_interval(f)
        AND continuous_on_unit_interval(g)
        AND FORALL (x: real):
          in_closed_unit_interval(x) IMPLIES
            (has_unit_interval_integral(
                kernel_product(K, f, x), g(x))
              AND has_unit_interval_integral(
                kernel_product(K, g, x), f(x))))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (x: real):
          in_closed_unit_interval(x) IMPLIES f(x) = g(x)
END putnam_1993_b4

title: putnam_1993_b5
putnam_1993_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b5:
;; no four points in the real Euclidean plane have all six pairwise distances
;; equal to odd integers. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; For fixed integer distance witnesses, existence of the four points is a
;; first-order condition over real closed fields. Hence a real configuration
;; exists exactly when one exists over the real algebraic numbers. Every
;; finite tuple of real algebraic coordinates lies in Q(alpha) for one real
;; algebraic alpha, so rational polynomials in alpha encode all four points
;; without restricting the source's arbitrary real domain.
;;
;; A distance equal to an odd integer is necessarily a positive odd integer,
;; and for a positive integer k it is equivalent to squared distance = k^2.
;; The source has only six unordered pairs. Moving those six existential
;; integer witnesses and the four points across the outer negation gives the
;; explicit DEFUN-SK universal closure below by exact finite quantifier
;; duality.

;; Rational polynomials in alpha use descending coefficient order.

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-p (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (and (rationalp (car p))
           (putnam-1993-b5-rp-p (cdr p)))
    (equal p nil)))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (if (equal (car p) 0)
          (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize (cdr p))
        p)
    nil))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-negate (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (cons (- (car p))
            (putnam-1993-b5-rp-negate (cdr p)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-add-raw (p q)
  (declare (xargs :measure (+ (acl2-count p) (acl2-count q))))
  (cond
   ((endp p) q)
   ((endp q) p)
   ((< (len p) (len q))
    (cons (car q)
          (putnam-1993-b5-rp-add-raw p (cdr q))))
   ((< (len q) (len p))
    (cons (car p)
          (putnam-1993-b5-rp-add-raw (cdr p) q)))
   (t
    (cons (+ (car p) (car q))
          (putnam-1993-b5-rp-add-raw (cdr p) (cdr q))))))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-add (p q)
  (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize
   (putnam-1993-b5-rp-add-raw p q)))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-subtract (p q)
  (putnam-1993-b5-rp-add
   p (putnam-1993-b5-rp-negate q)))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-scale (coefficient p)
  (if (consp p)
      (cons (* coefficient (car p))
            (putnam-1993-b5-rp-scale coefficient (cdr p)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-zeroes (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (cons 0 (putnam-1993-b5-zeroes (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-scale-shift (coefficient p shift)
  (append
   (putnam-1993-b5-rp-scale coefficient p)
   (putnam-1993-b5-zeroes shift)))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-multiply-raw (p q)
  (if (consp p)
      (putnam-1993-b5-rp-add
       (putnam-1993-b5-rp-scale-shift
        (car p) q (len (cdr p)))
       (putnam-1993-b5-rp-multiply-raw (cdr p) q))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-multiply (p q)
  (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize
   (putnam-1993-b5-rp-multiply-raw p q)))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-square (p)
  (putnam-1993-b5-rp-multiply p p))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-eval-aux (p x accumulator)
  (if (consp p)
      (putnam-1993-b5-rp-eval-aux
       (cdr p) x (+ (* accumulator x) (car p)))
    accumulator))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-eval (p x)
  (putnam-1993-b5-rp-eval-aux p x 0))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-derivative-aux (p degree)
  (if (consp p)
      (if (zp degree)
          nil
        (cons (* degree (car p))
              (putnam-1993-b5-rp-derivative-aux
               (cdr p) (- degree 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-derivative (p)
  (let ((normalized (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize p)))
    (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize
     (putnam-1993-b5-rp-derivative-aux
      normalized
      (nfix (- (len normalized) 1))))))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-remainder-fuel (p q fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((p (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize p))
        (q (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize q)))
    (if (or (zp fuel)
            (endp q)
            (< (len p) (len q)))
        p
      (putnam-1993-b5-rp-remainder-fuel
       (putnam-1993-b5-rp-subtract
        p
        (putnam-1993-b5-rp-scale-shift
         (/ (car p) (car q))
         q
         (- (len p) (len q))))
       q
       (- fuel 1)))))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-remainder (p q)
  (putnam-1993-b5-rp-remainder-fuel
   p q (+ 1 (len (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize p)))))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-sturm-tail (previous current fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((current (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize current)))
    (if (or (zp fuel) (endp current))
        nil
      (cons
       current
       (putnam-1993-b5-rp-sturm-tail
        current
        (putnam-1993-b5-rp-negate
         (putnam-1993-b5-rp-remainder previous current))
        (- fuel 1))))))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-sturm-sequence (p q)
  (let ((p (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize p))
        (q (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize q)))
    (if (endp p)
        nil
      (cons
       p
       (if (endp q)
           nil
         (cons
          q
          (putnam-1993-b5-rp-sturm-tail
           p q (+ 1 (len p) (len q)))))))))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rational-sign (x)
  (cond ((< x 0) -1)
        ((< 0 x) 1)
        (t 0)))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-variations-aux
    (polynomials x previous-sign)
  (if (consp polynomials)
      (let ((sign
             (putnam-1993-b5-rational-sign
              (putnam-1993-b5-rp-eval
               (car polynomials) x))))
        (if (equal sign 0)
            (putnam-1993-b5-rp-variations-aux
             (cdr polynomials) x previous-sign)
          (+ (if (and (not (equal previous-sign 0))
                      (not (equal sign previous-sign)))
                 1
               0)
             (putnam-1993-b5-rp-variations-aux
              (cdr polynomials) x sign))))
    0))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-variations (polynomials x)
  (putnam-1993-b5-rp-variations-aux polynomials x 0))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-cauchy-index (p q lower upper)
  (let ((sequence
         (putnam-1993-b5-rp-sturm-sequence p q)))
    (- (putnam-1993-b5-rp-variations sequence lower)
       (putnam-1993-b5-rp-variations sequence upper))))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-rp-root-count (p lower upper)
  (putnam-1993-b5-rp-cauchy-index
   p (putnam-1993-b5-rp-derivative p) lower upper))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-primitive-p (primitive lower upper)
  (and
   (putnam-1993-b5-rp-p primitive)
   (consp (putnam-1993-b5-rp-normalize primitive))
   (rationalp lower)
   (rationalp upper)
   (< lower upper)
   (not (equal
         (putnam-1993-b5-rp-eval primitive lower) 0))
   (not (equal
         (putnam-1993-b5-rp-eval primitive upper) 0))
   (equal
    (putnam-1993-b5-rp-root-count primitive lower upper)
    1)
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-1993-b5-rp-cauchy-index
      primitive
      (putnam-1993-b5-rp-multiply
       (putnam-1993-b5-rp-derivative primitive)
       (putnam-1993-b5-rp-derivative primitive))
      lower
      upper)
     0))))

;; For the isolated simple root alpha, this Sturm-Tarski query is the sign of
;; VALUE(alpha).
(defun putnam-1993-b5-algebraic-sign
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (putnam-1993-b5-rp-cauchy-index
   primitive
   (putnam-1993-b5-rp-multiply
    (putnam-1993-b5-rp-derivative primitive)
    value)
   lower
   upper))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-zero-at-alpha-p
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (equal
   (putnam-1993-b5-algebraic-sign
    primitive lower upper value)
   0))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-point-code-p (point)
  (and
   (true-listp point)
   (equal (len point) 2)
   (putnam-1993-b5-rp-p (nth 0 point))
   (putnam-1993-b5-rp-p (nth 1 point))))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-distance-squared (left right)
  (putnam-1993-b5-rp-add
   (putnam-1993-b5-rp-square
    (putnam-1993-b5-rp-subtract
     (nth 0 left) (nth 0 right)))
   (putnam-1993-b5-rp-square
    (putnam-1993-b5-rp-subtract
     (nth 1 left) (nth 1 right)))))

(defun putnam-1993-b5-distance-is-p
    (primitive lower upper left right distance)
  (putnam-1993-b5-zero-at-alpha-p
   primitive
   lower
   upper
   (putnam-1993-b5-rp-subtract

-- there do not exist four points in the Euclidean plane whose six pairwise
-- distances are all odd integers. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

open CompleteOrderedRealField

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

squaredDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
squaredDistance reals p q =
  add reals
    (square reals
      (subtract reals
        (x-coordinate p)
        (x-coordinate q)))
    (square reals
      (subtract reals
        (y-coordinate p)
        (y-coordinate q)))

distance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
distance reals p q =
  squareRoot reals (squaredDistance reals p q)

data Odd : Int -> Set where
  positive-odd :
    (k : Nat) ->
    Odd (pos (suc (k + k)))
  negative-odd :
    (k : Nat) ->
    Odd (negsuc (k + k))

OddIntegerDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
OddIntegerDistance reals p q =
  Exists Int
    (\ n ->
      distance reals p q == fromInt reals n
      and
      Odd n)

record PairwiseOddIntegerDistances
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (A B C D : Point R) :
  Set where

  field
    distance-AB : OddIntegerDistance reals A B
    distance-AC : OddIntegerDistance reals A C
    distance-AD : OddIntegerDistance reals A D
    distance-BC : OddIntegerDistance reals B C
    distance-BD : OddIntegerDistance reals B D
    distance-CD : OddIntegerDistance reals C D

module Putnam1993B5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    Not
      (Exists (Point R)
        (\ A ->
          Exists (Point R)
            (\ B ->
              Exists (Point R)
                (\ C ->
                  Exists (Point R)
                    (\ D ->
                      PairwiseOddIntegerDistances
                        reals A B C D)))))

putnam-1993-b5 : Set1
putnam-1993-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1993B5Statement.proposition reals

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b5:
% no four points in the Euclidean plane have all six pairwise distances equal
% to odd integers. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1993_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]
  point_index: TYPE = below(4)
  point_configuration: TYPE = [point_index -> point]

  squared_distance(P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q)) ^ 2
      + (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q)) ^ 2

  is_euclidean_distance(distance: real, P, Q: point): bool =
    distance >= 0
      AND distance * distance = squared_distance(P, Q)

  is_odd_integer(value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (half: int):
      value = 2 * half + 1

  has_odd_integer_distance(P, Q: point): bool =
    EXISTS (distance: real), (value: int):
      is_euclidean_distance(distance, P, Q)
        AND distance = (value :: real)
        AND is_odd_integer(value)

  putnam_1993_b5: bool =
    NOT EXISTS (points: point_configuration):
      FORALL (i, j: point_index):
        i /= j
          IMPLIES has_odd_integer_distance(points(i), points(j))
END putnam_1993_b5

    (initial : putnam_1993_b6_state)
    (transform :
      putnam_1993_b6_index ->

    (initial_positive :

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b6:
;; every positive triple of natural numbers can reach a triple containing zero
;; by finitely many allowed doubling-and-subtraction moves. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A state is the exact Fin 3 -> Nat object from the source, represented by
;; its three values. For distinct indices, the source hypothesis on F uniquely
;; determines F I J STATE: if STATE[I] <= STATE[J], double the former entry and
;; subtract it from the latter; otherwise leave the state unchanged. Since the
;; conclusion only uses distinct indices, eliminating F in favor of this
;; canonical operation is bidirectionally equivalent to the source statement.

(defun putnam-1993-b6-state-p (triple)
  (and
   (true-listp triple)
   (equal (len triple) 3)
   (natp (nth 0 triple))
   (natp (nth 1 triple))
   (natp (nth 2 triple))))

(defun putnam-1993-b6-zero-state-p (triple)
  (or
   (equal (nth 0 triple) 0)
   (equal (nth 1 triple) 0)
   (equal (nth 2 triple) 0)))

(defun putnam-1993-b6-step (triple i j)
  (if
      (and
       (putnam-1993-b6-state-p triple)
       (natp i)
       (< i 3)
       (natp j)
       (< j 3)
       (not (equal i j))
       (<= (nth i triple) (nth j triple)))
      (update-nth
       j
       (- (nth j triple) (nth i triple))
       (update-nth i (* 2 (nth i triple)) triple))
    triple))

;; This recursion is the internal existential quantifier over all finite
;; sequences of ordered, distinct index pairs. It is true exactly when some
;; allowed path of length at most FUEL reaches a zero state.

(defun putnam-1993-b6-reachable-p (triple fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (putnam-1993-b6-zero-state-p triple)
      t
    (if (zp fuel)
        nil
      (let ((next-fuel (- fuel 1)))
        (or
         (putnam-1993-b6-reachable-p
          (putnam-1993-b6-step triple 0 1) next-fuel)
         (putnam-1993-b6-reachable-p
          (putnam-1993-b6-step triple 0 2) next-fuel)
         (putnam-1993-b6-reachable-p
          (putnam-1993-b6-step triple 1 0) next-fuel)
         (putnam-1993-b6-reachable-p
          (putnam-1993-b6-step triple 1 2) next-fuel)
         (putnam-1993-b6-reachable-p
          (putnam-1993-b6-step triple 2 0) next-fuel)
         (putnam-1993-b6-reachable-p
          (putnam-1993-b6-step triple 2 1) next-fuel))))))

;; Every move preserves the natural-valued state and its sum. For initial sum
;; TOTAL, every reachable coordinate is at most TOTAL, so there are at most
;; (TOTAL+1)^3 reachable candidate states. Any path to zero can have loops
;; removed, making this finite bound exactly equivalent to the source's

(defun putnam-1993-b6-path-bound (triple)

   (+ 1
      (nth 0 triple)
      (nth 1 triple)
      (nth 2 triple))
   3))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1993-b6-statement (s0 s1 s2)
  (implies
   (and
    (posp s0)
    (posp s1)
    (posp s2))
   (let ((initial-state (list s0 s1 s2)))
     (putnam-1993-b6-reachable-p
      initial-state
      (putnam-1993-b6-path-bound initial-state)))))

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b6:
-- three positive natural numbers can be transformed until one is zero by
-- repeatedly replacing an ordered pair x <= y with 2x and y - x. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

toNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
toNat fzero =
  zero
toNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (toNat i)

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

lessOrEqualBool : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
lessOrEqualBool zero n =
  true
lessOrEqualBool (suc m) zero =
  false
lessOrEqualBool (suc m) (suc n) =
  lessOrEqualBool m n

If : Bool -> Set -> Set -> Set
If true when-true when-false =
  when-true
If false when-true when-false =
  when-false

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

three : Nat
three =
  suc two

Fin3 : Set
Fin3 =
  Fin three

State : Set
State =
  Fin3 -> Nat

StateEqual : State -> State -> Set
StateEqual A B =
  (i : Fin3) ->
  A i == B i

UpdateFunction : Set
UpdateFunction =
  Fin3 -> Fin3 -> State -> State

PairwiseDistinct : Fin3 -> Fin3 -> Fin3 -> Set
PairwiseDistinct i j k =
  i != j and i != k and j != k

UpdateAtPair :
  UpdateFunction ->
  Fin3 ->
  Fin3 ->
  Fin3 ->
  State ->
  Set
UpdateAtPair f i j k S' =
  ((f i j S') i == two * S' i)
  and
  ((f i j S') j == S' j - S' i)
  and
  ((f i j S') k == S' k)

UpdateSpecification : UpdateFunction -> Set
UpdateSpecification f =
  (i j k : Fin3) ->
  PairwiseDistinct i j k ->
  (S' : State) ->
  If
    (lessOrEqualBool (S' i) (S' j))
    (UpdateAtPair f i j k S')
    (StateEqual (f i j S') S')

FiniteTrajectory :
  State ->
  UpdateFunction ->
  Set
FiniteTrajectory S f =
  Exists (Nat -> State)
    (\ Ss ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ N ->
          StateEqual (Ss zero) S
          and
          Exists Fin3
            (\ i -> Ss N i == zero)
          and
          ((n : Fin N) ->
            Exists Fin3
              (\ i ->
                Exists Fin3
                  (\ j ->
                    i != j
                    and
                    StateEqual
                      (f i j (Ss (toNat n)))
                      (Ss (suc (toNat n))))))))

putnam-1993-b6 : Set
putnam-1993-b6 =
  (S : State) ->
  (f : UpdateFunction) ->
  ((i : Fin3) -> Positive (S i)) ->
  UpdateSpecification f ->
  FiniteTrajectory S f

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b6:
  three positive natural numbers can be transformed to include zero by
  finitely many applications of the stated doubling-and-subtraction rule.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory;

val putnam_1993_b6 =
  ``!S : num -> num.
    !f : num -> num -> (num -> num) -> (num -> num).
      (!i : num. i < 3 ==> 0 < S i) /\
      (!i j k : num.
         i < 3 /\ j < 3 /\ k < 3 /\
         i <> j /\ i <> k /\ j <> k
         ==>
         !S' : num -> num.
           if S' i <= S' j then
             f i j S' i = 2 * S' i /\
             f i j S' j = S' j - S' i /\
             f i j S' k = S' k
           else
             f i j S' = S')
      ==>
      ?Ss : num -> num -> num.
        ?N : num.
          Ss 0 = S /\
          (?i : num. i < 3 /\ Ss N i = 0) /\
          (!n : num.
             n < N
             ==>
             ?i j : num.
               i < 3 /\ j < 3 /\ i <> j /\
               f i j (Ss n) = Ss (n + 1))``;

theorem
  for S being Function of NAT,NAT,
      f being Function of
        [:NAT,NAT,Funcs(NAT,NAT):],Funcs(NAT,NAT) st
    (for i being Nat st i < 3 holds 0 < S.i) &

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1993_b6:
% a finite sequence of the stipulated conditional two-entry updates from a
% positive natural-number triple reaches a triple containing zero. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1993_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  index: TYPE = below(3)
  configuration: TYPE = [index -> nat]
  move_function: TYPE =
    [index, index, configuration -> configuration]
  configuration_history: TYPE = [nat -> configuration]

  putnam_1993_b6: bool =
    FORALL (S: configuration), (f: move_function):
      ((FORALL (i: index):
          S(i) > 0)
        AND
          (FORALL (i, j, k: index):
            (i /= j AND i /= k AND j /= k)
              IMPLIES
                (FORALL (S_prime: configuration):
                  IF S_prime(i) <= S_prime(j) THEN
                    f(i, j, S_prime)(i) = 2 * S_prime(i)
                      AND f(i, j, S_prime)(j) =
                        S_prime(j) - S_prime(i)
                      AND f(i, j, S_prime)(k) = S_prime(k)
                  ELSE
                    f(i, j, S_prime) = S_prime
                  ENDIF)))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (Ss: configuration_history), (N: nat):
          Ss(0) = S
            AND (EXISTS (i: index):
              Ss(N)(i) = 0)
            AND (FORALL (n: nat):
              n < N IMPLIES
                EXISTS (i, j: index):
                  i /= j
                    AND f(i, j, Ss(n)) = Ss(n + 1))
END putnam_1993_b6

/--
Suppose that a sequence $a_1,a_2,a_3,\dots$ satisfies $0< a_n \leq a_{2n}+a_{2n+1}$ for all $n \geq 1$. Prove that the series $\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n$ diverges.

theorem putnam_1994_a1
    (a : ℕ → ℝ)
    (ha : ∀ n ≥ 1, 0 < a n ∧ a n ≤ a (2 * n) + a (2 * n + 1)) :
    Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => ∑ n : Set.Icc 1 N, a n) atTop atTop :=
  sorry

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1994_a1:
;; if 0 < a(n) <= a(2n)+a(2n+1) for n >= 1, then the partial sums
;; of a diverge to positive infinity. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The source sequence is represented by an arbitrary conservative ACL2
;; function symbol. Both directions of the Archimedean property are explicit:
;; rational upper bounds are cofinal, and every positive scalar dominates
;; some positive reciprocal integer. The second clause rules out positive
;; infinitesimals, which would make the source conclusion false.
(defstub p1994a1-scalar-p (x) t)
(defstub p1994a1-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub p1994a1-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub p1994a1-less-op (x y) t)
(defstub p1994a1-rational-embed (q) t)
(defstub p1994a1-arch-bound (x) t)
(defstub p1994a1-reciprocal-bound (x) t)
(defstub p1994a1-a (n) t)

(defun p1994a1-add (x y)
  (p1994a1-add-op x y))

(defun p1994a1-neg (x)
  (p1994a1-negate-op x))

(defun p1994a1-less (x y)
  (if (p1994a1-less-op x y) t nil))

(defun p1994a1-less-equal (x y)
  (not (p1994a1-less y x)))

(defun-sk p1994a1-additive-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p1994a1-scalar-p x)
      (p1994a1-scalar-p y)
      (p1994a1-scalar-p z))
     (and
      (p1994a1-scalar-p (p1994a1-add x y))
      (p1994a1-scalar-p (p1994a1-neg x))
      (equal (p1994a1-add (p1994a1-add x y) z)
             (p1994a1-add x (p1994a1-add y z)))
      (equal (p1994a1-add x y)
             (p1994a1-add y x))
      (equal (p1994a1-add x zero) x)
      (equal (p1994a1-add x (p1994a1-neg x)) zero)))))

(defun-sk p1994a1-order-laws-p ()
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p1994a1-scalar-p x)
      (p1994a1-scalar-p y)
      (p1994a1-scalar-p z))
     (and
      (not (p1994a1-less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (p1994a1-less x y)
       (p1994a1-less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (p1994a1-less x y)
        (p1994a1-less y z))
       (p1994a1-less x z))
      (implies
       (p1994a1-less x y)
       (p1994a1-less
        (p1994a1-add x z)
        (p1994a1-add y z)))))))

(defun-sk p1994a1-rational-embedding-laws-p ()
  (forall (a b)
    (implies
     (and (rationalp a) (rationalp b))
     (and
      (p1994a1-scalar-p (p1994a1-rational-embed a))
      (equal
       (p1994a1-rational-embed (+ a b))
       (p1994a1-add
        (p1994a1-rational-embed a)
        (p1994a1-rational-embed b)))
      (iff
       (< a b)
       (p1994a1-less
        (p1994a1-rational-embed a)
        (p1994a1-rational-embed b)))))))

(defun-sk p1994a1-archimedean-p ()
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p1994a1-scalar-p x)
     (and
      (natp (p1994a1-arch-bound x))
      (p1994a1-less
       x
       (p1994a1-rational-embed
        (p1994a1-arch-bound x)))
      (implies
       (p1994a1-less
        (p1994a1-rational-embed 0)
        x)
       (and
        (posp (p1994a1-reciprocal-bound x))
        (p1994a1-less
         (p1994a1-rational-embed
          (/ 1 (p1994a1-reciprocal-bound x)))
         x)))))))

(defun p1994a1-real-additive-structure-p (zero)
  (and
   (p1994a1-scalar-p zero)
   (equal (p1994a1-rational-embed 0) zero)
   (p1994a1-additive-laws-p zero)
   (p1994a1-order-laws-p)
   (p1994a1-rational-embedding-laws-p)
   (p1994a1-archimedean-p)))

(defun-sk p1994a1-sequence-hypotheses-p (zero)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and (natp n) (<= 1 n))
     (and
      (p1994a1-scalar-p (p1994a1-a n))
      (p1994a1-less zero (p1994a1-a n))
      (p1994a1-less-equal
       (p1994a1-a n)
       (p1994a1-add
        (p1994a1-a (* 2 n))
        (p1994a1-a (+ (* 2 n) 1))))))))

(defun p1994a1-partial-sum (n zero)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      zero
    (p1994a1-add
     (p1994a1-partial-sum (- n 1) zero)
     (p1994a1-a n))))

(defun-sk p1994a1-above-bound-tail-p
    (bound cutoff zero)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and (natp n) (<= cutoff n))
     (p1994a1-less
      (p1994a1-rational-embed bound)
      (p1994a1-partial-sum n zero)))))

(defun-sk p1994a1-above-bound-cutoff-exists-p
    (bound zero)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (p1994a1-above-bound-tail-p
      bound cutoff zero))))

(defun-sk p1994a1-partial-sums-diverge-p (zero)
  (forall (bound)
    (implies
     (rationalp bound)
     (p1994a1-above-bound-cutoff-exists-p
      bound zero))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1994-a1-statement (zero)
  (implies
   (and
    (p1994a1-real-additive-structure-p zero)
    (p1994a1-sequence-hypotheses-p zero))
   (p1994a1-partial-sums-diverge-p zero)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a1:
-- every positive real sequence satisfying a_n <= a_(2n) + a_(2n+1) has
-- partial sums from 1 through N tending to positive infinity. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

partialSumFromOne :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
partialSumFromOne reals a zero =
  zeroR reals
partialSumFromOne reals a (suc n) =
  add reals
    (partialSumFromOne reals a n)
    (a (suc n))

GrowsWithoutBound :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Set
GrowsWithoutBound {R} reals sequence =
  (bound : R) ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      lessOrEqual reals bound (sequence n))

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

putnam-1994-a1 : Set1
putnam-1994-a1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (a : Nat -> R) ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    oneN <=N n ->
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (a n)
    and
    lessOrEqual reals
      (a n)
      (add reals
        (a (twoN * n))
        (a (twoN * n + oneN)))) ->
  GrowsWithoutBound reals (partialSumFromOne reals a)

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1994_a1: every positive real sequence satisfying the binary-tree
  inequality has partial sums tending to positive infinity. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  A ranges over all real-valued sequences indexed by the nonnegative
  integers. Quantification over NN in the hypothesis is exactly
  quantification over natural indices n >= 1.

  The conclusion expands convergence of the partial sums to positive
  infinity: for every real bound b, all sums from k = 1 through N exceed
  that bound once N is past a natural threshold. This is the restricted-
  quantifier form of the atTop-to-atTop limit in the Lean and Isabelle
  sources. Positivity makes it consistent with the Rocq formulation as
  nonexistence of a finite limit.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d A N b k m n $.

  putnambench-putnam-1994-a1 $a |- A. A e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
    (
      A. n e. NN
        (
          0 < ( A ` n )
          /\
          ( A ` n )
          <_
          (
            ( A ` ( 2 x. n ) )
            +
            ( A ` ( ( 2 x. n ) + 1 ) )
          )
        )
      ->
      A. b e. RR
        E. m e. NN0
          A. N e. NN0
            (
              m <_ N
              ->
              b
              <_
              (
                sum_ k e. ( 1 ... N )
                  ( A ` k )
              )
            )
    )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a1:
% a positive real sequence satisfying the binary-branching inequality has its
% partial sums from 1 through N tend to positive infinity. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1994_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  partial_sum(sequence: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_sum(sequence, count - 1) + sequence(count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  tends_to_positive_infinity(sequence: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (bound: real):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES bound <= sequence(count)

  putnam_1994_a1: bool =
    FORALL (a: real_sequence):
      (FORALL (n: nat):
        n >= 1 IMPLIES
          0 < a(n)
            AND a(n) <= a(2 * n) + a(2 * n + 1))
      IMPLIES
        tends_to_positive_infinity(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): partial_sum(a, count))
END putnam_1994_a1

Show that if the points of an isosceles right triangle of side length $1$ are each colored with one of four colors, then there must be two points of the same color which are at least a distance $2-\sqrt{2}$ apart.

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a3:
   a four-coloring of the closed unit isosceles right triangle has two
   same-colored points at distance at least 2 minus sqrt 2.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_1994_a3_point : Type := (R * R)%type.

Inductive putnam_1994_a3_color : Type :=
| putnam_1994_a3_color0
| putnam_1994_a3_color1
| putnam_1994_a3_color2
| putnam_1994_a3_color3.

Definition putnam_1994_a3_in_triangle
    (p : putnam_1994_a3_point) : Prop :=
  0 <= fst p /\
  0 <= snd p /\
  fst p + snd p <= 1.

Definition putnam_1994_a3_distance
    (p q : putnam_1994_a3_point) : R :=
  sqrt ((fst p - fst q) ^ 2 + (snd p - snd q) ^ 2).

Theorem putnam_1994_a3
    (T : putnam_1994_a3_point -> Prop)
    (T_def :
      forall p : putnam_1994_a3_point,
        T p <-> putnam_1994_a3_in_triangle p)
    (Tcolors : putnam_1994_a3_point -> putnam_1994_a3_color) :
  exists p q : putnam_1994_a3_point,
    T p /\
    T q /\
    Tcolors p = Tcolors q /\
    2 - sqrt 2 <= putnam_1994_a3_distance p q.
Admitted.

title: putnam_1994_a3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1994_a3:
;; every four-coloring of the closed unit isosceles right triangle has two
;; same-colored points at distance at least 2 - sqrt(2). This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The theorem uses only ordered-field arithmetic, one positive square root
;; of two, and an arbitrary coloring. Conservative generic symbols are the
;; standard ACL2 presentation of those universally quantified objects; no
;; completeness axiom or restricted APPLY$ function universe is needed.
(defstub p1994a3-scalar-p (x) t)
(defstub p1994a3-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub p1994a3-multiply-op (x y) t)
(defstub p1994a3-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub p1994a3-inverse-op (x) t)
(defstub p1994a3-less-op (x y) t)
(defstub p1994a3-color (point) t)

(defun p1994a3-add (x y)
  (p1994a3-add-op x y))

(defun p1994a3-mul (x y)
  (p1994a3-multiply-op x y))

(defun p1994a3-neg (x)
  (p1994a3-negate-op x))

(defun p1994a3-inv (x)
  (p1994a3-inverse-op x))

(defun p1994a3-sub (x y)
  (p1994a3-add x (p1994a3-neg y)))

(defun p1994a3-less (x y)
  (if (p1994a3-less-op x y) t nil))

(defun p1994a3-less-equal (x y)
  (not (p1994a3-less y x)))

(defun p1994a3-square (x)
  (p1994a3-mul x x))

(defun-sk p1994a3-field-laws-p (zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p1994a3-scalar-p x)
      (p1994a3-scalar-p y)
      (p1994a3-scalar-p z))
     (and
      (p1994a3-scalar-p (p1994a3-add x y))
      (p1994a3-scalar-p (p1994a3-mul x y))
      (p1994a3-scalar-p (p1994a3-neg x))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (p1994a3-scalar-p (p1994a3-inv x)))
      (equal (p1994a3-add (p1994a3-add x y) z)
             (p1994a3-add x (p1994a3-add y z)))
      (equal (p1994a3-add x y)
             (p1994a3-add y x))
      (equal (p1994a3-add x zero) x)
      (equal (p1994a3-add x (p1994a3-neg x)) zero)
      (equal (p1994a3-mul (p1994a3-mul x y) z)
             (p1994a3-mul x (p1994a3-mul y z)))
      (equal (p1994a3-mul x y)
             (p1994a3-mul y x))
      (equal (p1994a3-mul x one) x)
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal (p1994a3-mul x (p1994a3-inv x)) one))
      (equal
       (p1994a3-mul x (p1994a3-add y z))
       (p1994a3-add (p1994a3-mul x y)
                    (p1994a3-mul x z)))))))

(defun-sk p1994a3-order-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p1994a3-scalar-p x)
      (p1994a3-scalar-p y)
      (p1994a3-scalar-p z))
     (and
      (not (p1994a3-less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (p1994a3-less x y)
       (p1994a3-less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (p1994a3-less x y)
        (p1994a3-less y z))
       (p1994a3-less x z))
      (implies
       (p1994a3-less x y)
       (p1994a3-less
        (p1994a3-add x z)
        (p1994a3-add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (p1994a3-less zero x)
        (p1994a3-less zero y))
       (p1994a3-less zero (p1994a3-mul x y)))))))

(defun p1994a3-ordered-field-p (zero one)
  (and
   (p1994a3-scalar-p zero)
   (p1994a3-scalar-p one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (p1994a3-less zero one)
   (p1994a3-field-laws-p zero one)
   (p1994a3-order-laws-p zero)))

(defun p1994a3-point-p (point)
  (and
   (true-listp point)
   (equal (len point) 2)
   (p1994a3-scalar-p (nth 0 point))
   (p1994a3-scalar-p (nth 1 point))))

(defun p1994a3-triangle-point-p (point zero one)
  (and
   (p1994a3-point-p point)
   (p1994a3-less-equal zero (nth 0 point))
   (p1994a3-less-equal zero (nth 1 point))
   (p1994a3-less-equal
    (p1994a3-add (nth 0 point) (nth 1 point))
    one)))

(defun p1994a3-color-p (color)
  (and (natp color) (< color 4)))

(defun-sk p1994a3-coloring-p (zero one)
  (forall (point)
    (implies
     (p1994a3-triangle-point-p point zero one)
     (p1994a3-color-p (p1994a3-color point)))))

(defun p1994a3-sqrt-two-p (sqrt-two zero one)
  (let ((two (p1994a3-add one one)))
    (and
     (p1994a3-scalar-p sqrt-two)
     (p1994a3-less zero sqrt-two)
     (p1994a3-less sqrt-two two)
     (equal (p1994a3-square sqrt-two) two))))

(defun p1994a3-distance-squared (left right)
  (let ((dx (p1994a3-sub (nth 0 left) (nth 0 right)))
        (dy (p1994a3-sub (nth 1 left) (nth 1 right))))
    (p1994a3-add
     (p1994a3-square dx)
     (p1994a3-square dy))))

(defun p1994a3-bound-squared (sqrt-two one)
  (let ((two (p1994a3-add one one)))
    (p1994a3-square (p1994a3-sub two sqrt-two))))

(defun-sk p1994a3-separated-pair-exists-p
    (sqrt-two zero one)
  (exists (left right)
    (and
     (p1994a3-triangle-point-p left zero one)
     (p1994a3-triangle-point-p right zero one)
     (equal (p1994a3-color left)
            (p1994a3-color right))
     (p1994a3-less-equal
      (p1994a3-bound-squared sqrt-two one)
      (p1994a3-distance-squared left right)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1994-a3-statement
    (sqrt-two zero one)
  (implies
   (and
    (p1994a3-ordered-field-p zero one)
    (p1994a3-sqrt-two-p sqrt-two zero one)
    (p1994a3-coloring-p zero one))
   (p1994a3-separated-pair-exists-p
    sqrt-two zero one)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a3:
-- every four-coloring of the closed unit isosceles right triangle has two
-- same-colored points at distance at least 2 - sqrt 2. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

two :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
two reals =
  add reals (oneR reals) (oneR reals)

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

InTriangle :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
InTriangle reals p =
  lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (x-coordinate p)
  and
  lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (y-coordinate p)
  and
  lessOrEqual reals
    (add reals (x-coordinate p) (y-coordinate p))
    (oneR reals)

squaredDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
squaredDistance reals p q =
  add reals
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q)))
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)))

distance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
distance reals p q =
  squareRoot reals (squaredDistance reals p q)

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc (suc (suc (suc zero)))

record TriangleColoring
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set where

  field
    colorAt :
      (p : Point R) ->
      InTriangle reals p ->
      Fin fourN

    membership-proof-independent :
      (p : Point R) ->
      (first-membership second-membership : InTriangle reals p) ->
      colorAt p first-membership == colorAt p second-membership

open TriangleColoring

record SameColorFarApart
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (coloring : TriangleColoring reals) :
  Set where

  field
    p q : Point R
    p-in-triangle : InTriangle reals p
    q-in-triangle : InTriangle reals q
    same-color :
      colorAt coloring p p-in-triangle ==
      colorAt coloring q q-in-triangle
    far-apart :
      lessOrEqual reals
        (subtract reals
          (two reals)
          (squareRoot reals (two reals)))
        (distance reals p q)

putnam-1994-a3 : Set1
putnam-1994-a3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (coloring : TriangleColoring reals) ->
  SameColorFarApart reals coloring

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a3:
  every four-coloring of the closed unit isosceles right triangle has two
  same-colored points at least 2 - sqrt 2 apart. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_1994_a3 =
  ``let triangle =
      {p : real # real |
         0 <= FST p /\ 0 <= SND p /\ FST p + SND p <= 1}
    in
    let dist =
      \p q : real # real.
        sqrt ((FST p - FST q) pow 2 + (SND p - SND q) pow 2)
    in
      !color : (real # real) -> num.
        (!p : real # real. p IN triangle ==> color p < 4)
        ==>
        ?p q : real # real.
          p IN triangle /\
          q IN triangle /\
          color p = color q /\
          2 - sqrt 2 <= dist p q``;

title: putnam_1994_a3
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1994_a3: every four-coloring of the closed isosceles right
  triangle with vertices (0,0), (1,0), and (0,1) has two same-colored
  points at distance at least 2 - sqrt(2). This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P94A3R2 is the full real coordinate plane. P94A3Triangle is the closed
  triangle x_1 >= 0, x_2 >= 0, x_1 + x_2 <= 1. This is exactly the convex
  hull in the sources: the barycentric weights of (0,0), (1,0), and (0,1)
  are 1 - x_1 - x_2, x_1, and x_2. P94A3Dist is ordinary Euclidean
  distance.

  C ranges over every total function from this triangle to the four-element
  ordinal 4, which is bijective with Fin 4; colors are observed only through
  equality. This directly matches the Lean domain. It is also equivalent to
  Isabelle's plane-domain coloring restricted to the triangle: restriction
  gives one direction, and every triangle coloring extends to the plane
  because the color carrier is nonempty. The two point witnesses remain
  internally existentially quantified.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P94A3I P94A3R2 P94A3Triangle P94A3Dist $.

p94a3-index-syntax $a class P94A3I $.
p94a3-plane-syntax $a class P94A3R2 $.
p94a3-triangle-syntax $a class P94A3Triangle $.
p94a3-distance-syntax $a class ( P94A3Dist A B ) $.

p94a3-index-definition $a |- P94A3I = ( 1 ... 2 ) $.

p94a3-plane-definition $a |- P94A3R2 = ( RR ^m P94A3I ) $.

p94a3-triangle-definition $a |- P94A3Triangle = {
  x e. P94A3R2 |
  (
    0 <_ ( x ` 1 )
    /\
    (
      0 <_ ( x ` 2 )
      /\
      ( ( x ` 1 ) + ( x ` 2 ) ) <_ 1
    )
  )
} $.

${
  $d A B k $.

  p94a3-distance-definition $a |- (
    P94A3Dist A B
  ) = (
    sqrt
    `
    (
      sum_ k e. P94A3I
        ( ( ( A ` k ) - ( B ` k ) ) ^ 2 )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d C p q $.

  putnambench-putnam-1994-a3 $a |-
    A. C e. ( 4 ^m P94A3Triangle )
      E. p e. P94A3Triangle E. q e. P94A3Triangle
        (
          ( C ` p ) = ( C ` q )
          /\
          ( 2 - ( sqrt ` 2 ) ) <_ ( P94A3Dist p q )
        )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1994_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a3:
% every four-coloring of the closed unit isosceles right triangle has two
% same-colored points at distance at least 2 minus sqrt(2). This file contains
% no proof.

putnam_1994_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]
  coloring: TYPE = [point -> below(4)]

  in_triangle(p: point): bool =
    x_coord(p) >= 0
      AND y_coord(p) >= 0
      AND x_coord(p) + y_coord(p) <= 1

  squared_distance(p, q: point): real =
    (x_coord(p) - x_coord(q)) ^ 2
      + (y_coord(p) - y_coord(q)) ^ 2

  sqrt_value(root, radicand: real): bool =
    0 <= root AND root * root = radicand

  putnam_1994_a3: bool =
    FORALL (color: coloring):
      EXISTS (p, q: point), (distance, sqrt_two: real):
        in_triangle(p)
          AND in_triangle(q)
          AND color(p) = color(q)
          AND sqrt_value(distance, squared_distance(p, q))
          AND sqrt_value(sqrt_two, 2)
          AND distance >= 2 - sqrt_two
END putnam_1994_a3

import Mathlib

open Filter Topology

/--
Let $A$ and $B$ be $2 \times 2$ matrices with integer entries such that $A$, $A+B$, $A+2B$, $A+3B$, and $A+4B$ are all invertible matrices whose inverses have integer entries. Show that $A+5B$ is invertible and that its inverse has integer entries.
-/
theorem putnam_1994_a4
  (A B : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ)
  (ABinv : Nonempty (Invertible A) ∧
    Nonempty (Invertible (A + B)) ∧
    Nonempty (Invertible (A + 2 * B)) ∧
    Nonempty (Invertible (A + 3 * B)) ∧
    Nonempty (Invertible (A + 4 * B)))
  : Nonempty (Invertible (A + 5 * B)) :=
sorry

title: putnam_1994_a4
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a4:
   invertibility over the integers of the first five matrices in an affine
   sequence of 2 by 2 matrices implies invertibility of the sixth; this file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith Vectors.Fin.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition putnam_1994_a4_matrix : Type :=
  Fin.t 2 -> Fin.t 2 -> Z.

Definition putnam_1994_a4_matrix_eq
    (A B : putnam_1994_a4_matrix) : Prop :=
  forall i j, A i j = B i j.

Fixpoint putnam_1994_a4_fin_sum
    (n : nat) : (Fin.t n -> Z) -> Z :=
  match n as k return (Fin.t k -> Z) -> Z with
  | O => fun _ => 0
  | S k =>
      fun f =>
        f Fin.F1 +
        putnam_1994_a4_fin_sum k (fun i => f (Fin.FS i))
  end.

Definition putnam_1994_a4_add
    (A B : putnam_1994_a4_matrix) : putnam_1994_a4_matrix :=
  fun i j => A i j + B i j.

Definition putnam_1994_a4_scale
    (c : Z) (A : putnam_1994_a4_matrix) : putnam_1994_a4_matrix :=
  fun i j => c * A i j.

Definition putnam_1994_a4_mul
    (A B : putnam_1994_a4_matrix) : putnam_1994_a4_matrix :=
  fun i j =>
    putnam_1994_a4_fin_sum 2 (fun k => A i k * B k j).

Definition putnam_1994_a4_identity : putnam_1994_a4_matrix :=
  fun i j => if Fin.eq_dec i j then 1 else 0.

Definition putnam_1994_a4_invertible
    (A : putnam_1994_a4_matrix) : Prop :=
  exists Ainv : putnam_1994_a4_matrix,
    putnam_1994_a4_matrix_eq
      (putnam_1994_a4_mul A Ainv)
      putnam_1994_a4_identity /\
    putnam_1994_a4_matrix_eq
      (putnam_1994_a4_mul Ainv A)
      putnam_1994_a4_identity.

Theorem putnam_1994_a4
    (A B : putnam_1994_a4_matrix)
    (ABinv :
      putnam_1994_a4_invertible A /\
      putnam_1994_a4_invertible
        (putnam_1994_a4_add A B) /\
      putnam_1994_a4_invertible
        (putnam_1994_a4_add A (putnam_1994_a4_scale 2 B)) /\
      putnam_1994_a4_invertible
        (putnam_1994_a4_add A (putnam_1994_a4_scale 3 B)) /\
      putnam_1994_a4_invertible
        (putnam_1994_a4_add A (putnam_1994_a4_scale 4 B))) :
  putnam_1994_a4_invertible
    (putnam_1994_a4_add A (putnam_1994_a4_scale 5 B)).
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a4:
  integer 2 by 2 matrices A + kB that are invertible over the integers for
  k = 0 through 4 force A + 5B to be invertible over the integers. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let matrix_mul =
     \A:int^2^2. \B:int^2^2.
       (lambda i j.
          isum (1..2) (\k. A$i$k * B$k$j)):int^2^2 in
   let identity_matrix =
     (lambda i j. if i = j then &1 else &0):int^2^2 in
   let matrix_unit =
     \M:int^2^2.
       ?C:int^2^2.
         matrix_mul M C = identity_matrix /\
         matrix_mul C M = identity_matrix in
   let affine_matrix =
     \k:num. \A:int^2^2. \B:int^2^2.
       (lambda i j. A$i$j + &k * B$i$j):int^2^2 in
   !A:int^2^2. !B:int^2^2.
     matrix_unit (affine_matrix 0 A B) /\
     matrix_unit (affine_matrix 1 A B) /\
     matrix_unit (affine_matrix 2 A B) /\
     matrix_unit (affine_matrix 3 A B) /\
     matrix_unit (affine_matrix 4 A B)
     ==> matrix_unit (affine_matrix 5 A B)`;;

title: putnam_1994_a4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a4:
;; arbitrary 2 by 2 integer matrices A and B for which A+kB is invertible
;; over the integers for k=0,1,2,3,4 have A+5B invertible over the integers.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A 2 by 2 integer matrix is invertible with an integer-entry inverse exactly
;; when its determinant is a unit of the integers, namely 1 or -1. Thus the
;; entrywise determinant predicates below are bidirectionally equivalent to
;; the source matrix invertibility assertions.

(defun putnam-1994-a4-determinant-at
    (a00 a01 a10 a11 b00 b01 b10 b11 k)
  (- (* (+ a00 (* k b00))
        (+ a11 (* k b11)))
     (* (+ a01 (* k b01))
        (+ a10 (* k b10)))))

(defun putnam-1994-a4-invertible-at-p
    (a00 a01 a10 a11 b00 b01 b10 b11 k)
  (let ((determinant
         (putnam-1994-a4-determinant-at
          a00 a01 a10 a11 b00 b01 b10 b11 k)))
    (or (equal determinant 1)
        (equal determinant -1))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1994-a4-statement
    (a00 a01 a10 a11 b00 b01 b10 b11)
  (implies
   (and
    (integerp a00)
    (integerp a01)
    (integerp a10)
    (integerp a11)
    (integerp b00)
    (integerp b01)
    (integerp b10)
    (integerp b11)
    (putnam-1994-a4-invertible-at-p
     a00 a01 a10 a11 b00 b01 b10 b11 0)
    (putnam-1994-a4-invertible-at-p
     a00 a01 a10 a11 b00 b01 b10 b11 1)
    (putnam-1994-a4-invertible-at-p
     a00 a01 a10 a11 b00 b01 b10 b11 2)
    (putnam-1994-a4-invertible-at-p
     a00 a01 a10 a11 b00 b01 b10 b11 3)
    (putnam-1994-a4-invertible-at-p
     a00 a01 a10 a11 b00 b01 b10 b11 4))
   (putnam-1994-a4-invertible-at-p
    a00 a01 a10 a11 b00 b01 b10 b11 5)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1994_a4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a4:
-- integer 2 by 2 matrices A, A+B, ..., A+4B having integer matrix inverses
-- imply that A+5B also has an integer matrix inverse. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

data Fin2 : Set where
  i0 i1 : Fin2

Matrix : Set
Matrix =
  Fin2 -> Fin2 -> Int

MatrixEqual : Matrix -> Matrix -> Set
MatrixEqual A B =
  (i j : Fin2) ->
  A i j == B i j

matrixAdd : Matrix -> Matrix -> Matrix
matrixAdd A B i j =
  addInt (A i j) (B i j)

scaleMatrix : Int -> Matrix -> Matrix
scaleMatrix scalar A i j =
  multiplyInt scalar (A i j)

matrixMultiply : Matrix -> Matrix -> Matrix
matrixMultiply A B i j =
  addInt
    (multiplyInt (A i i0) (B i0 j))
    (multiplyInt (A i i1) (B i1 j))

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc threeN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc fourN

identityMatrix : Matrix
identityMatrix i0 i0 =
  pos oneN
identityMatrix i0 i1 =
  pos zero
identityMatrix i1 i0 =
  pos zero
identityMatrix i1 i1 =
  pos oneN

Invertible : Matrix -> Set
Invertible A =
  Exists Matrix
    (\ AInverse ->
      MatrixEqual
        (matrixMultiply A AInverse)
        identityMatrix
      and
      MatrixEqual
        (matrixMultiply AInverse A)
        identityMatrix)

affineMatrix : Matrix -> Matrix -> Nat -> Matrix
affineMatrix A B coefficient =
  matrixAdd A (scaleMatrix (pos coefficient) B)

putnam-1994-a4 : Set
putnam-1994-a4 =
  (A B : Matrix) ->
  Invertible A
  and
  Invertible (affineMatrix A B oneN)
  and
  Invertible (affineMatrix A B twoN)
  and
  Invertible (affineMatrix A B threeN)
  and
  Invertible (affineMatrix A B fourN) ->
  Invertible (affineMatrix A B fiveN)

title: putnam_1994_a4
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a4:
  integer-entry 2 by 2 matrices whose first five affine combinations are
  invertible over the integers have an invertible sixth combination. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory fcpTheory;

val putnam_1994_a4 =
  ``let matrix_add =
      \A B : int['N]['N].
        ((FCP i j. A ' i ' j + B ' i ' j) : int['N]['N])
    in
    let matrix_scale =
      \k : int. \A : int['N]['N].
        ((FCP i j. k * A ' i ' j) : int['N]['N])
    in
    let matrix_mul =
      \A B : int['N]['N].
        ((FCP i j.
            A ' i ' 0 * B ' 0 ' j + A ' i ' 1 * B ' 1 ' j) :
          int['N]['N])
    in
    let matrix_one =
      ((FCP i j. if i = j then 1 else 0) : int['N]['N])
    in
    let matrix_invertible =
      \A : int['N]['N].
        ?C : int['N]['N].
          matrix_mul A C = matrix_one /\
          matrix_mul C A = matrix_one
    in
      !A B : int['N]['N].
        dimindex (:'N) = 2 /\
        matrix_invertible A /\
        matrix_invertible (matrix_add A B) /\
        matrix_invertible (matrix_add A (matrix_scale 2 B)) /\
        matrix_invertible (matrix_add A (matrix_scale 3 B)) /\
        matrix_invertible (matrix_add A (matrix_scale 4 B))
        ==>
        matrix_invertible (matrix_add A (matrix_scale 5 B))``;

title: putnam_1994_a4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a4:
% integer 2-by-2 matrices A through A + 4B having integer matrix inverses
% imply that A + 5B also has an integer matrix inverse. This file contains no
% proof.

putnam_1994_a4: THEORY
BEGIN
  index: TYPE = below(2)
  integer_matrix: TYPE = [index, index -> int]

  bounded_integer_sum(
      values: [index -> int],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      bounded_integer_sum(values, count - 1)
        + IF count <= 2 THEN
            values(count - 1)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  identity_matrix: integer_matrix =
    LAMBDA (row, column: index):
      IF row = column THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF

  matrix_add_multiple(
      A, B: integer_matrix,
      coefficient: int): integer_matrix =
    LAMBDA (row, column: index):
      A(row, column) + coefficient * B(row, column)

  matrix_multiply(
      A, B: integer_matrix): integer_matrix =
    LAMBDA (row, column: index):
      bounded_integer_sum(
        LAMBDA (inner: index):
          A(row, inner) * B(inner, column),
        2)

  has_integer_matrix_inverse(A: integer_matrix): bool =
    EXISTS (inverse: integer_matrix):
      matrix_multiply(A, inverse) = identity_matrix
        AND matrix_multiply(inverse, A) = identity_matrix

  putnam_1994_a4: bool =
    FORALL (A, B: integer_matrix):
      (has_integer_matrix_inverse(A)
        AND has_integer_matrix_inverse(matrix_add_multiple(A, B, 1))
        AND has_integer_matrix_inverse(matrix_add_multiple(A, B, 2))
        AND has_integer_matrix_inverse(matrix_add_multiple(A, B, 3))
        AND has_integer_matrix_inverse(matrix_add_multiple(A, B, 4)))
      IMPLIES
        has_integer_matrix_inverse(matrix_add_multiple(A, B, 5))
END putnam_1994_a4

import Mathlib

open Filter Topology

/--
Let $(r_n)_{n \geq 0}$ be a sequence of positive real numbers such that $\lim_{n \to \infty} r_n=0$. Let $S$ be the set of numbers representable as a sum $r_{i_1}+r_{i_2}+\cdots+r_{i_{1994}}$, with $i_1< i_2<\cdots< i_{1994}$. Show that every nonempty interval $(a,b)$ contains a nonempty subinterval $(c,d)$ that does not intersect $S$.
-/
theorem putnam_1994_a5
  (r : ℕ → ℝ)
  (S : Set ℝ)
  (rpos : ∀ n, r n > 0)
  (rlim : Tendsto r atTop (𝓝 0))
  (hS : S = {x | ∃ i : Fin 1994 → ℕ, (∀ j k : Fin 1994, j < k → i j < i k) ∧ (x = ∑ j : Fin 1994, r (i j))}) :
  ∀ a b : ℝ, a < b → (∃ c d : ℝ, a ≤ c ∧ c < d ∧ d ≤ b ∧ (Set.Ioo c d) ∩ S = ∅) :=
sorry

title: putnam_1994_a5

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a5:
   positive real sequences tending to zero and gaps in the set of sums over
   1994 strictly increasing indices. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals Ensembles SeqSeries.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_1994_a5_sum
    (r : nat -> R) (i : nat -> nat) : R :=
  sum_f_R0 (fun j : nat => r (i j)) 1993.

Definition putnam_1994_a5_representable
    (r : nat -> R) : Ensemble R :=
  fun x : R =>
    exists i : nat -> nat,
      (forall j k : nat,
        (j < 1994)%nat ->
        (k < 1994)%nat ->
        (j < k)%nat ->
        (i j < i k)%nat) /\
      x = putnam_1994_a5_sum r i.

Theorem putnam_1994_a5
    (r : nat -> R)
    (S : Ensemble R)
    (rpos : forall n : nat, 0 < r n)
    (rlim : Un_cv r 0)
    (hS : Same_set R S (putnam_1994_a5_representable r)) :
  forall a b : R,
    a < b ->
    exists c d : R,
      a <= c /\
      c < d /\
      d <= b /\
      forall x : R, c < x /\ x < d -> ~ S x.
Admitted.
