putnam_1994_a5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a5:
;; every nonempty real interval contains a nonempty subinterval avoiding all
;; sums of 1994 distinct terms of a positive null sequence. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; SEQUENCE is an ACL2 function object. At natural index N and positive
;; rational precision EPSILON, component 0 is a rational Cauchy approximation
;; to r_N, component 1 at precision 1 is a positive rational lower bound for
;; r_N, and component 2 at index 0 is a convergence cutoff. The matrices below
;; make this a name for an arbitrary positive real sequence tending to zero.
;;
;; The set parameter S is eliminated by substituting its defining equality.
;; It is equivalent to test rational A<B: every real interval contains a
;; rational subinterval, and a gap in that subinterval is a gap in the original
;; interval. The internal witness is (C D CUTOFF TAIL-BOUND PRECISION).
;; CUTOFF reduces each increasing 1994-tuple to its finite prefix below the
;; cutoff. The remaining terms are bounded by TAIL-BOUND, while rational
;; Cauchy approximations bound the prefix. The finite ALWAYS$+ check therefore
;; certifies that every represented sum is at most C or at least D.
;;
;; Conversely, the closure of the source sum set consists of sums of at most
;; 1994 terms with distinct indices, with missing terms equal to the sole limit
;; value 0. A closed rational subinterval of any source gap has positive
;; distance from this compact closure. Sufficiently small tail and Cauchy
;; bounds then give exactly such a finite certificate. Thus the certificate
;; formulation is bidirectionally equivalent and keeps C and D existential.

(defun putnam-1994-a5-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'cons
       (car terms)
       (putnam-1994-a5-term-list (cdr terms)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-apply-term (function arguments)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-1994-a5-quoted function)
   (putnam-1994-a5-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-component-term
    (sequence component index precision)
  (list
   'nth
   (putnam-1994-a5-quoted component)
   (putnam-1994-a5-apply-term
    sequence
    (list index precision))))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-nth-term (index value)
  (list 'nth (putnam-1994-a5-quoted index) value))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-list-term (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'cons
       (car terms)
       (putnam-1994-a5-list-term (cdr terms)))
    (putnam-1994-a5-quoted nil)))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'if
       (car terms)
       (putnam-1994-a5-and-terms (cdr terms))
       (putnam-1994-a5-quoted nil))
    (putnam-1994-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-or-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'if
       (car terms)
       (putnam-1994-a5-quoted t)
       (putnam-1994-a5-or-terms (cdr terms)))
    (putnam-1994-a5-quoted nil)))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list
   'if
   hypothesis
   conclusion
   (putnam-1994-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-negate-term (value)
  (list 'unary-- value))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-subtract-term (left right)
  (putnam-1994-a5-add-term
   left
   (putnam-1994-a5-negate-term right)))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-multiply-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-* left right))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-divide-term (left right)
  (putnam-1994-a5-multiply-term
   left
   (list 'unary-/ right)))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-absolute-term (value)
  (list
   'if
   (list '< value (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 0))
   (putnam-1994-a5-negate-term value)
   value))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-less-equal-term (left right)
  (list
   'if
   (list '< right left)
   (putnam-1994-a5-quoted nil)
   (putnam-1994-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-positive-rational-term (value)
  (putnam-1994-a5-and-terms
   (list
    (list 'rationalp value)
    (list '< (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 0) value))))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-range-term (upper)
  (list
   'from-to-by
   (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 0)
   upper
   (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 1)))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-true-function (formals)
  (list
   'lambda
   formals
   (putnam-1994-a5-quoted t)))

;; A regular rational Cauchy name determines one real at every natural index.
(defun putnam-1994-a5-cauchy-function (sequence)
  (let* ((at-epsilon
          (putnam-1994-a5-component-term
           sequence 0 'n 'epsilon))
         (at-eta
          (putnam-1994-a5-component-term
           sequence 0 'n 'eta))
         (distance
          (putnam-1994-a5-absolute-term
           (putnam-1994-a5-subtract-term
            at-epsilon at-eta))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(n epsilon eta)
     (putnam-1994-a5-implies-term
      (putnam-1994-a5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'natp 'n)
        (putnam-1994-a5-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
        (putnam-1994-a5-positive-rational-term 'eta)))
      (putnam-1994-a5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp at-epsilon)
        (list 'rationalp at-eta)
        (putnam-1994-a5-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-1994-a5-add-term
          'epsilon 'eta))))))))

;; A positive rational lower bound valid at every precision is equivalent to
;; strict positivity of the represented real.
(defun putnam-1994-a5-positive-function (sequence)
  (let ((lower
         (putnam-1994-a5-component-term
          sequence 1 'n (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 1)))
        (value
         (putnam-1994-a5-component-term
          sequence 0 'n 'epsilon)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(n epsilon)
     (putnam-1994-a5-implies-term
      (putnam-1994-a5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'natp 'n)
        (putnam-1994-a5-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)))
      (putnam-1994-a5-and-terms
       (list
        (putnam-1994-a5-positive-rational-term lower)
        (list 'rationalp value)
        (putnam-1994-a5-less-equal-term
         lower
         (putnam-1994-a5-add-term
          value 'epsilon))))))))

;; For every positive tolerance, component 2 supplies an internal natural
;; cutoff after which the represented real values have absolute value below
;; that tolerance. The strict 3/4 approximation bound leaves 1/4 for the
;; Cauchy-name error and is equivalent to convergence to zero.
(defun putnam-1994-a5-zero-limit-function (sequence)
  (let* ((cutoff
          (putnam-1994-a5-component-term
           sequence 2
           (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 0)
           'epsilon))
         (quarter-epsilon
          (putnam-1994-a5-divide-term
           'epsilon
           (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 4)))
         (value
          (putnam-1994-a5-component-term
           sequence 0 'n quarter-epsilon))
         (three-quarters
          (putnam-1994-a5-multiply-term
           (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 3)
           quarter-epsilon)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon n)
     (putnam-1994-a5-implies-term
      (putnam-1994-a5-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
      (putnam-1994-a5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'natp cutoff)
        (putnam-1994-a5-implies-term
         (putnam-1994-a5-and-terms
          (list
           (list 'natp 'n)
           (putnam-1994-a5-less-equal-term
            cutoff 'n)))
         (putnam-1994-a5-and-terms
          (list
           (list 'rationalp value)
           (list '<
                 (putnam-1994-a5-absolute-term value)
                 three-quarters))))))))))

;; CODE is the base-(CUTOFF+1) encoding of 1994 entries. A qualifying code is
;; a strictly increasing prefix below CUTOFF followed only by the sentinel
;; CUTOFF. It represents every possible finite prefix of an increasing source
;; index tuple.
(defun putnam-1994-a5-digit-term
    (code cutoff position)
  (let ((base
         (putnam-1994-a5-add-term
          cutoff
          (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 1))))
    (list
     'mod
     (list
      'floor
      code
      (list 'expt base position))
     base)))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-prefix-valid-function ()
  (let* ((cutoff
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 0 'globals))
         (code
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 1 'globals))
         (digit
          (putnam-1994-a5-digit-term
           code cutoff 'position))
         (previous-position
          (putnam-1994-a5-subtract-term
           'position
           (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 1)))
         (previous-digit
          (putnam-1994-a5-digit-term
           code cutoff previous-position)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(globals position)
     (list
      'if
      (list '< digit cutoff)
      (putnam-1994-a5-or-terms
       (list
        (list 'equal
              'position
              (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 0))
        (list '< previous-digit digit)))
      (list 'equal digit cutoff)))))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-prefix-count-function ()
  (let* ((cutoff
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 0 'globals))
         (code
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 1 'globals))
         (digit
          (putnam-1994-a5-digit-term
           code cutoff 'position)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(globals position)
     (list
      'if
      (list '< digit cutoff)
      (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 1)
      (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 0)))))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-prefix-sum-function (sequence)
  (let* ((cutoff
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 0 'globals))
         (code
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 1 'globals))
         (precision
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 2 'globals))
         (digit
          (putnam-1994-a5-digit-term
           code cutoff 'position))
         (value
          (putnam-1994-a5-component-term
           sequence 0 digit precision)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(globals position)
     (list
      'if
      (list '< digit cutoff)
      value
      (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 0)))))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-prefix-certificate-function
    (sequence)
  (let* ((cutoff
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 0 'globals))
         (tail-bound
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 1 'globals))
         (precision
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 2 'globals))
         (c
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 3 'globals))
         (d
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 4 'globals))
         (position-upper
          (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 1993))
         (prefix-globals
          (putnam-1994-a5-list-term
           (list cutoff 'code)))
         (sum-globals
          (putnam-1994-a5-list-term
           (list cutoff 'code precision)))
         (valid-function
          (putnam-1994-a5-prefix-valid-function))
         (count-function
          (putnam-1994-a5-prefix-count-function))
         (sum-function
          (putnam-1994-a5-prefix-sum-function sequence))
         (valid
          (list
           'always$+
           (putnam-1994-a5-quoted valid-function)
           prefix-globals
           (putnam-1994-a5-range-term
            position-upper)))
         (prefix-count
          (list
           'sum$+
           (putnam-1994-a5-quoted count-function)
           prefix-globals
           (putnam-1994-a5-range-term
            position-upper)))
         (approximate-sum
          (list
           'sum$+
           (putnam-1994-a5-quoted sum-function)
           sum-globals
           (putnam-1994-a5-range-term
            position-upper)))
         (prefix-error
          (putnam-1994-a5-multiply-term
           prefix-count precision))
         (tail-count
          (putnam-1994-a5-subtract-term
           (putnam-1994-a5-quoted 1994)
           prefix-count))
         (tail-error
          (putnam-1994-a5-multiply-term
           tail-count tail-bound))
         (upper
          (putnam-1994-a5-add-term
           (putnam-1994-a5-add-term
            approximate-sum prefix-error)
           tail-error))
         (lower
          (putnam-1994-a5-subtract-term
           approximate-sum prefix-error)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(globals code)
     (putnam-1994-a5-implies-term
      valid
      (putnam-1994-a5-or-terms
       (list
        (putnam-1994-a5-less-equal-term upper c)
        (putnam-1994-a5-less-equal-term d lower)))))))

(defun putnam-1994-a5-gap-witness-failure-function
    (sequence a b)
  (let* ((c
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 0 'witness))
         (d
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 1 'witness))
         (cutoff
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 2 'witness))
         (tail-bound
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 3 'witness))
         (precision
          (putnam-1994-a5-nth-term 4 'witness))
         (modulus
          (putnam-1994-a5-component-term

title: putnam_1994_a5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a5:
-- every nonempty real interval contains a nonempty open subinterval disjoint
-- from the set of sums of 1994 positive sequence terms at increasing indices.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

NatStrictLess : Nat -> Nat -> Set
NatStrictLess m n =
  suc m <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finToNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (finToNat i)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

Predicate : Set -> Set1
Predicate A =
  A -> Set

record SetEqual
  {A : Set}
  (S T : Predicate A) :
  Set where

  constructor same-set
  field
    membership :
      (x : A) ->
      Iff (S x) (T x)

OpenInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Predicate R
OpenInterval reals lower upper x =
  StrictLess reals lower x
  and
  StrictLess reals x upper

StrictlyIncreasing :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Nat) ->
  Set
StrictlyIncreasing indices =
  (j k : _) ->
  NatStrictLess (finToNat j) (finToNat k) ->
  NatStrictLess (indices j) (indices k)

Representable :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Predicate R
Representable reals sequence x =
  Exists (Fin 1994 -> Nat)
    (\ indices ->
      StrictlyIncreasing indices
      and
      x == sumFin reals
        (\ j -> sequence (indices j)))

module Putnam1994A5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (r : Nat -> R)
  (S : Predicate R) where

  positiveTerms : Set
  positiveTerms =
    (n : Nat) ->
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (r n)

  tendsToZero : Set
  tendsToZero =
    ConvergesTo reals r (zeroR reals)

  exactSumSet : Set
  exactSumSet =
    SetEqual S (Representable reals r)

  hasAvoidingSubinterval : Set
  hasAvoidingSubinterval =
    (a b : R) ->
    StrictLess reals a b ->
    Exists R
      (\ c ->
        Exists R
          (\ d ->
            lessOrEqual reals a c
            and
            StrictLess reals c d
            and
            lessOrEqual reals d b
            and
            ((x : R) ->
              OpenInterval reals c d x ->
              Not (S x))))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    positiveTerms ->
    tendsToZero ->
    exactSumSet ->
    hasAvoidingSubinterval

putnam-1994-a5 : Set1
putnam-1994-a5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (r : Nat -> R) ->
  (S : Predicate R) ->
  Putnam1994A5Statement.proposition reals r S

  sums of 1994 terms at strictly increasing indices from a positive real
  sequence tending to zero leave a nonempty gap in every nonempty open
  interval. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;
open real_topologyTheory;

val putnam_1994_a5 =
  ``!r : num -> real. !S : real set.
      (!n : num. 0 < r n) /\
      ((r --> 0) sequentially) /\
      S =
        {x : real |
           ?i : num -> num.
             (!j k : num.
                j IN count 1994 /\ k IN count 1994 /\ j < k
                ==>
                i j < i k) /\
             x = SIGMA (\j : num. r (i j)) (count 1994)}
      ==>
      !a b : real.
        a < b
        ==>
        ?c d : real.
          a <= c /\
          c < d /\
          d <= b /\
          {x : real | c < x /\ x < d} INTER S = {}``;

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The sequence r ranges over all functions from NN0 to RR, and S ranges over
  all subsets of RR. The epsilon-threshold clause is the atTop limit of r at
  zero. The index set 0 ... 1993 has exactly 1994 elements, so functions i
  from that set to NN0 with the displayed strict-order condition are exactly
  the increasing index selections in the source.

  The equality defining S preserves the source set of all corresponding
  finite sums. The conclusion uses set.mm's open real interval and requires
  its intersection with S to be empty. The final declaration is the single
  unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.

${
  $d N S a b c d e i j k n r x $.

  putnambench-putnam-1994-a5 $a |-
    A. r e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
    A. S e. ~P RR
      (

                    (

                      ->
                      ( abs ` ( r ` n ) ) < e
                    )
              )
            /\
            S
            =
            {
              x e. RR |
              E. i e.
                ( NN0 ^m ( 0 ... ; ; ; 1 9 9 3 ) )
                (
                  A. j e. ( 0 ... ; ; ; 1 9 9 3 )
                    A. k e. ( 0 ... ; ; ; 1 9 9 3 )
                      (
                        j < k
                        ->
                        ( i ` j ) < ( i ` k )
                      )
                  /\
                  x
                  =
                  (
                    sum_ j e. ( 0 ... ; ; ; 1 9 9 3 )
                      ( r ` ( i ` j ) )
                  )

            }

                (

                  /\

                    d <_ b
                    /\

title: putnam_1994_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a5:
% sums of exactly 1994 terms at strictly increasing indices from a positive
% real sequence tending to zero leave an open gap in every nonempty interval.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_1994_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]
  real_set: TYPE = [real -> bool]

  converges_to_zero(sequence: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index)) < epsilon_value

  selected_sum(
      sequence: real_sequence,
      indices: natural_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      selected_sum(sequence, indices, count - 1)
        + sequence(indices(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  strictly_increasing_prefix(
      indices: natural_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (j, k: nat):
      (j < count AND k < count AND j < k)
        IMPLIES indices(j) < indices(k)

  is_sum_of_1994_terms(
      sequence: real_sequence,
      value: real): bool =
    EXISTS (indices: natural_sequence):
      strictly_increasing_prefix(indices, 1994)
        AND value = selected_sum(sequence, indices, 1994)

  is_representable_set(
      sequence: real_sequence,
      S: real_set): bool =
    FORALL (value: real):
      S(value) IFF is_sum_of_1994_terms(sequence, value)

  contains_open_gap_in_every_interval(S: real_set): bool =
    FORALL (a, b: real):
      a < b IMPLIES
        EXISTS (c, d: real):
          a <= c
            AND c < d
            AND d <= b
            AND (FORALL (value: real):
              (c < value AND value < d) IMPLIES NOT S(value))

  putnam_1994_a5: bool =
    FORALL (sequence: real_sequence), (S: real_set):
      ((FORALL (index: nat): sequence(index) > 0)
        AND converges_to_zero(sequence)
        AND is_representable_set(sequence, S))
      IMPLIES contains_open_gap_in_every_interval(S)
END putnam_1994_a5

title: putnam_1994_a6

import Mathlib

open Classical Filter Topology

-- Note: uses (ℕ → Fin 10) instead of (Fin m → Fin 10)
/--
Let $f_1,\dots,f_{10}$ be bijections of the set of integers such that for each integer $n$, there is some composition $f_{i_1} \circ f_{i_2} \circ \cdots \circ f_{i_m}$ of these functions (allowing repetitions) which maps 0 to $n$. Consider the set of $1024$ functions $\mathcal{F}=\{f_1^{e_1} \circ f_2^{e_2} \circ \cdots \circ f_{10}^{e_{10}}\}$, $e_i=0$ or $1$ for $1 \leq i \leq 10$. ($f_i^0$ is the identity function and $f_i^1=f_i$.) Show that if $A$ is any nonempty finite set of integers, then at most $512$ of the functions in $\mathcal{F}$ map $A$ to itself.
-/
theorem putnam_1994_a6
(f : Fin 10 → Equiv.Perm ℤ)
(mijcomp : ℕ → (ℕ → Fin 10) → ℕ → (ℤ → ℤ))
(F : Finset (ℤ → ℤ))
(hf: ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ m : ℕ, ∃ i : ℕ → Fin 10, m ≥ 1 ∧ (mijcomp m i 0) 0 = n)
(hmijcomp : ∀ m ≥ 1, ∀ (i : ℕ → Fin 10) (j : Fin m), mijcomp m i j = if (j = m - 1) then (f (i j) : ℤ → ℤ) else (f (i j) ∘ mijcomp m i (j + 1)))
(hF : F = {g : ℤ → ℤ | ∃ e : Fin 10 → Fin 2, g = (f 0)^[e 0] ∘ (f 1)^[e 1] ∘ (f 2)^[e 2] ∘ (f 3)^[e 3] ∘ (f 4)^[e 4] ∘ (f 5)^[e 5] ∘ (f 6)^[e 6] ∘ (f 7)^[e 7] ∘ (f 8)^[e 8] ∘ (f 9)^[e 9]})
: ∀ A : Finset ℤ, A.Nonempty → {g ∈ F | g '' A = A}.card ≤ 512 :=
sorry

title: putnam_1994_a6
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a6:
   ten permutations of the integers whose finite compositions act transitively
   have at most 512 optional ordered compositions stabilizing any nonempty
   finite set of integers. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List ZArith Arith.PeanoNat.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Inductive putnam_1994_a6_index : Type :=
| putnam_1994_a6_i0
| putnam_1994_a6_i1
| putnam_1994_a6_i2
| putnam_1994_a6_i3
| putnam_1994_a6_i4
| putnam_1994_a6_i5
| putnam_1994_a6_i6
| putnam_1994_a6_i7
| putnam_1994_a6_i8
| putnam_1994_a6_i9.

Definition putnam_1994_a6_bijective (h : Z -> Z) : Prop :=
  (forall x y : Z, h x = h y -> x = y) /\
  (forall y : Z, exists x : Z, h x = y).

Fixpoint putnam_1994_a6_apply_word
    (f : putnam_1994_a6_index -> Z -> Z)
    (word : list putnam_1994_a6_index)
    (x : Z) : Z :=
  match word with
  | nil => x
  | i :: rest => f i (putnam_1994_a6_apply_word f rest x)
  end.

Definition putnam_1994_a6_apply_optional
    (choice : bool) (h : Z -> Z) (x : Z) : Z :=
  if choice then h x else x.

Definition putnam_1994_a6_optional_composition
    (f : putnam_1994_a6_index -> Z -> Z)
    (e : putnam_1994_a6_index -> bool) : Z -> Z :=
  fun x : Z =>
    putnam_1994_a6_apply_optional
      (e putnam_1994_a6_i0) (f putnam_1994_a6_i0)
      (putnam_1994_a6_apply_optional
        (e putnam_1994_a6_i1) (f putnam_1994_a6_i1)
        (putnam_1994_a6_apply_optional
          (e putnam_1994_a6_i2) (f putnam_1994_a6_i2)
          (putnam_1994_a6_apply_optional
            (e putnam_1994_a6_i3) (f putnam_1994_a6_i3)
            (putnam_1994_a6_apply_optional
              (e putnam_1994_a6_i4) (f putnam_1994_a6_i4)
              (putnam_1994_a6_apply_optional
                (e putnam_1994_a6_i5) (f putnam_1994_a6_i5)
                (putnam_1994_a6_apply_optional
                  (e putnam_1994_a6_i6) (f putnam_1994_a6_i6)
                  (putnam_1994_a6_apply_optional
                    (e putnam_1994_a6_i7) (f putnam_1994_a6_i7)
                    (putnam_1994_a6_apply_optional
                      (e putnam_1994_a6_i8) (f putnam_1994_a6_i8)
                      (putnam_1994_a6_apply_optional
                        (e putnam_1994_a6_i9) (f putnam_1994_a6_i9)
                        x))))))))).

Definition putnam_1994_a6_finite_set (A : Z -> Prop) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list Z,
    NoDup enumeration /\
    forall x : Z, In x enumeration <-> A x.

Definition putnam_1994_a6_nonempty_set (A : Z -> Prop) : Prop :=
  exists x : Z, A x.

Definition putnam_1994_a6_image
    (g : Z -> Z) (A : Z -> Prop) : Z -> Prop :=
  fun y : Z => exists x : Z, A x /\ y = g x.

Definition putnam_1994_a6_maps_set_to_itself
    (g : Z -> Z) (A : Z -> Prop) : Prop :=
  forall y : Z,
    putnam_1994_a6_image g A y <-> A y.

Definition putnam_1994_a6_has_at_most_cardinality
    {X : Type} (P : X -> Prop) (bound : nat) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list X,
    NoDup enumeration /\
    (length enumeration <= bound)%nat /\
    forall x : X, In x enumeration <-> P x.

Theorem putnam_1994_a6
    (f : putnam_1994_a6_index -> Z -> Z)
    (hfperm :
      forall i : putnam_1994_a6_index,
        putnam_1994_a6_bijective (f i))
    (hfcomp :
      forall n : Z,
        exists word : list putnam_1994_a6_index,
          word <> nil /\
          putnam_1994_a6_apply_word f word 0 = n) :
  forall A : Z -> Prop,
    putnam_1994_a6_finite_set A ->
    putnam_1994_a6_nonempty_set A ->
    putnam_1994_a6_has_at_most_cardinality
      (fun g : Z -> Z =>
        (exists e : putnam_1994_a6_index -> bool,
          g = putnam_1994_a6_optional_composition f e) /\
        putnam_1994_a6_maps_set_to_itself g A)
      512%nat.
Admitted.

theory putnam_1994_a6 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Combinatorics.Permutations"
begin

(* uses (nat \<Rightarrow> (int \<Rightarrow> int)) instead of (Fin 10 \<Rightarrow> (int \<Rightarrow> int)) and (nat \<Rightarrow> nat) instead of (Fin m \<Rightarrow> Fin 10) and (Fin 10 \<Rightarrow> Fin 2) *)
theorem putnam_1994_a6:
  fixes f :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (int \<Rightarrow> int)"
  and mijcomp :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> (int \<Rightarrow> int)"
  and F :: "(int \<Rightarrow> int) set"
  assumes hfperm: "\<forall>i::nat\<in>{0..9}. (f i) permutes UNIV"
  and hfcomp: "\<forall>n::int. \<exists>m::nat\<ge>1. \<exists>i::nat\<Rightarrow>nat. (\<forall>j::nat\<in>{0..(m-1)}. i j \<in> {0..9}) \<and> (mijcomp m i 0) 0 = n"
  and hmijcomp: "\<forall>m::nat\<ge>1. \<forall>(i::nat\<Rightarrow>nat). \<forall>j::nat\<in>{0..(m-1)}. mijcomp m i j = (if (j = m-1) then (f (i j)) else (f (i j) \<circ> mijcomp m i (j+1)))"
  and hF: "F \<equiv> {g::int\<Rightarrow>int. (\<exists>e::nat\<Rightarrow>nat. (\<forall>i::nat\<in>{0..9}. e i = 0 \<or> e i = 1) \<and> (g = (f 0)^^(e 0) \<circ> (f 1)^^(e 1) \<circ> (f 2)^^(e 2) \<circ> (f 3)^^(e 3) \<circ> (f 4)^^(e 4) \<circ> (f 5)^^(e 5) \<circ> (f 6)^^(e 6) \<circ> (f 7)^^(e 7) \<circ> (f 8)^^(e 8) \<circ> (f 9)^^(e 9)))}"
  shows "\<forall>A::int set. (finite A \<and> A \<noteq> {}) \<longrightarrow> (card {g\<in>F. g ` A = A} \<le> 512)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a6:
  at most half of the 0/1 ordered compositions of ten integer permutations
  can preserve any given finite nonempty set of integers. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

needs "Library/iter.ml";;

let statement =
  `!f:num->int->int.
   !mijcomp:num->(num->num)->num->int->int.
   !fam:(int->int)->bool.
     (!i:num. i < 10 ==> BIJ (f i) (:int) (:int)) /\
     (!n:int.
        ?m:num. ?i:num->num.
          1 <= m /\
          (!j:num. j < m ==> i j < 10) /\
          mijcomp m i 0 (&0) = n) /\
     (!m:num. !i:num->num. !j:num.
        1 <= m /\ j < m
        ==> mijcomp m i j =
            if j = m - 1 then
              f (i j)
            else
              f (i j) o mijcomp m i (j + 1)) /\
     fam =
       {g:int->int |
          ?e:num->num.
            (!i:num. i < 10 ==> e i = 0 \/ e i = 1) /\
            g =
              (ITER (e 0) (f 0)) o
              (ITER (e 1) (f 1)) o
              (ITER (e 2) (f 2)) o
              (ITER (e 3) (f 3)) o
              (ITER (e 4) (f 4)) o
              (ITER (e 5) (f 5)) o
              (ITER (e 6) (f 6)) o
              (ITER (e 7) (f 7)) o
              (ITER (e 8) (f 8)) o
              (ITER (e 9) (f 9))}
     ==>
     !A:int->bool.
       FINITE A /\ ~(A = {})
       ==> CARD {g:int->int | g IN fam /\ IMAGE g A = A} <= 512`;;

title: putnam_1994_a6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a6:
;; ten integer permutations whose nonempty finite compositions reach every
;; integer from zero have at most 512 distinct optional ordered compositions
;; stabilizing any nonempty finite integer set. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A conservative DEFSTUB supplies ten arbitrary unary functions through the
;; first argument. Proving the resulting theorem permits ordinary ACL2
;; functional instantiation for any concrete family of ten functions.
(defstub p94a6-generator (index x) t)

(defun p94a6-apply (index x)
  (p94a6-generator index x))

(defun-sk p94a6-integer-function-values-p (index)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (integerp x)
     (integerp (p94a6-apply index x)))))

(defun-sk p94a6-injective-on-integers-p (index)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (integerp x)
      (integerp y)
      (equal (p94a6-apply index x)
             (p94a6-apply index y)))
     (equal x y))))

(defun-sk p94a6-integer-preimage-exists-p (index y)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (integerp x)
     (equal (p94a6-apply index x) y))))

(defun-sk p94a6-surjective-on-integers-p (index)
  (forall (y)
    (implies
     (integerp y)
     (p94a6-integer-preimage-exists-p index y))))

(defun p94a6-integer-permutation-p (index)
  (and
   (natp index)
   (< index 10)
   (p94a6-integer-function-values-p index)
   (p94a6-injective-on-integers-p index)
   (p94a6-surjective-on-integers-p index)))

(defun p94a6-index-word-p (word)
  (if (endp word)
      (equal word nil)
    (and
     (natp (car word))
     (< (car word) 10)
     (p94a6-index-word-p (cdr word)))))

;; The head of WORD is the outermost function, matching
;; f_i1 o f_i2 o ... o f_im.
(defun p94a6-apply-word (word x)
  (if (endp word)
      x
    (p94a6-apply
     (car word)
     (p94a6-apply-word (cdr word) x))))

(defun-sk p94a6-reaching-word-exists-p (n)
  (exists (word)
    (and
     (consp word)
     (true-listp word)
     (p94a6-index-word-p word)
     (equal (p94a6-apply-word word 0) n))))

(defun-sk p94a6-zero-orbit-is-all-integers-p ()
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (integerp n)
     (p94a6-reaching-word-exists-p n))))

(defun p94a6-mask-bit-p (mask index)
  (equal
   (mod (floor mask (expt 2 index)) 2)
   1))

(defun p94a6-apply-optional-composition (mask x)
  (let*
      ((x9 (if (p94a6-mask-bit-p mask 9)
               (p94a6-apply 9 x)
             x))
       (x8 (if (p94a6-mask-bit-p mask 8)
               (p94a6-apply 8 x9)
             x9))
       (x7 (if (p94a6-mask-bit-p mask 7)
               (p94a6-apply 7 x8)
             x8))
       (x6 (if (p94a6-mask-bit-p mask 6)
               (p94a6-apply 6 x7)
             x7))
       (x5 (if (p94a6-mask-bit-p mask 5)
               (p94a6-apply 5 x6)
             x6))
       (x4 (if (p94a6-mask-bit-p mask 4)
               (p94a6-apply 4 x5)
             x5))
       (x3 (if (p94a6-mask-bit-p mask 3)
               (p94a6-apply 3 x4)
             x4))
       (x2 (if (p94a6-mask-bit-p mask 2)
               (p94a6-apply 2 x3)
             x3))
       (x1 (if (p94a6-mask-bit-p mask 1)
               (p94a6-apply 1 x2)
             x2))
       (x0 (if (p94a6-mask-bit-p mask 0)
               (p94a6-apply 0 x1)
             x1)))
    x0))

(defun p94a6-integer-list-p (list)
  (if (endp list)
      (equal list nil)
    (and
     (integerp (car list))
     (p94a6-integer-list-p (cdr list)))))

(defun p94a6-valid-finite-set-p (set)
  (and
   (consp set)
   (true-listp set)
   (p94a6-integer-list-p set)
   (no-duplicatesp-equal set)))

(defun-sk p94a6-image-contains-p (mask set y)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (integerp x)
     (member-equal x set)
     (equal y (p94a6-apply-optional-composition mask x)))))

(defun-sk p94a6-stabilizes-p (mask set)
  (forall (y)
    (implies
     (integerp y)
     (iff
      (p94a6-image-contains-p mask set y)
      (member-equal y set)))))

(defun-sk p94a6-optional-functions-differ-p (left-mask right-mask)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (integerp x)
     (not
      (equal
       (p94a6-apply-optional-composition left-mask x)
       (p94a6-apply-optional-composition right-mask x))))))

(defun p94a6-valid-mask-p (mask)
  (and
   (natp mask)
   (< mask 1024)))

(defun p94a6-all-masks-stabilize-p (masks set)
  (if (endp masks)
      (equal masks nil)
    (and
     (p94a6-valid-mask-p (car masks))
     (p94a6-stabilizes-p (car masks) set)
     (p94a6-all-masks-stabilize-p (cdr masks) set))))

(defun p94a6-mask-differs-from-list-p (mask masks)
  (if (endp masks)
      (equal masks nil)
    (and
     (p94a6-optional-functions-differ-p mask (car masks))
     (p94a6-mask-differs-from-list-p mask (cdr masks)))))

(defun p94a6-pairwise-distinct-functions-p (masks)
  (if (endp masks)
      (equal masks nil)
    (and
     (p94a6-mask-differs-from-list-p (car masks) (cdr masks))
     (p94a6-pairwise-distinct-functions-p (cdr masks)))))

;; A family has cardinality at most 512 exactly when it has no list of 513
;; pairwise extensionally distinct members.
(defun-sk p94a6-513-distinct-stabilizers-exist-p (set)
  (exists (masks)
    (and
     (true-listp masks)
     (equal (len masks) 513)
     (p94a6-all-masks-stabilize-p masks set)
     (p94a6-pairwise-distinct-functions-p masks))))

(defun p94a6-at-most-512-stabilizers-p (set)
  (not (p94a6-513-distinct-stabilizers-exist-p set)))

(defun p94a6-all-generators-are-permutations-p (index)
  (if (zp index)
      t
    (and
     (p94a6-integer-permutation-p (- index 1))
     (p94a6-all-generators-are-permutations-p (- index 1)))))

(defun p94a6-hypotheses-p ()
  (and
   (p94a6-all-generators-are-permutations-p 10)
   (p94a6-zero-orbit-is-all-integers-p)))

(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-1994-a6-statement ()
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (p94a6-hypotheses-p)
      (p94a6-valid-finite-set-p set))
     (p94a6-at-most-512-stabilizers-p set))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1994_a6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_1994_a6): among the distinct functions formed
-- by binary ordered compositions of ten integer permutations generating every
-- integer from zero, at most 512 stabilize any nonempty finite integer set.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

data Fin10 : Set where
  i0 i1 i2 i3 i4 i5 i6 i7 i8 i9 : Fin10

data NonemptyList {A : Set} : List A -> Set where
  nonempty : (x : A) -> (xs : List A) -> NonemptyList (x ∷ xs)

record Permutation (A : Set) : Set where
  field
    apply         : A -> A
    inverse       : A -> A
    inverse-apply : (x : A) -> inverse (apply x) == x
    apply-inverse : (x : A) -> apply (inverse x) == x

open Permutation

FunctionEqual :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set
FunctionEqual left right =
  (x : _) ->
  left x == right x

SetEqual :
  {A : Set} ->
  (A -> Set) ->
  (A -> Set) ->
  Set
SetEqual left right =
  (x : _) ->
  Iff (left x) (right x)

record HasExtensionalCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (equivalent : A -> A -> Set)
  (member : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> equivalent item (enumerate index))
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      equivalent (enumerate left-index) (enumerate right-index) ->
      left-index == right-index

FiniteSet :
  {A : Set} ->
  (A -> Set) ->
  Set
FiniteSet member =
  Exists Nat
    (\ cardinality ->
      HasExtensionalCardinality _==_ member cardinality)

NonemptySet :
  {A : Set} ->
  (A -> Set) ->
  Set
NonemptySet member =
  Exists _
    (\ item -> member item)

CardinalityAtMost :
  {A : Set} ->
  (A -> A -> Set) ->
  (A -> Set) ->
  Nat ->
  Set
CardinalityAtMost equivalent member bound =
  Exists Nat
    (\ cardinality ->
      HasExtensionalCardinality equivalent member cardinality
      and
      cardinality <=N bound)

composeWord :
  (Fin10 -> Permutation Int) ->
  List Fin10 ->
  Int ->
  Int
composeWord f [] x =
  x
composeWord f (index ∷ rest) x =
  apply (f index) (composeWord f rest x)

GeneratesIntegersFromZero :
  (Fin10 -> Permutation Int) ->
  Set
GeneratesIntegersFromZero f =
  (n : Int) ->
  Exists (List Fin10)
    (\ indices ->
      NonemptyList indices
      and
      composeWord f indices (pos zero) == n)

selectPower :
  Bool ->
  Permutation Int ->
  Int ->
  Int
selectPower false permutation x =
  x
selectPower true permutation x =
  apply permutation x

binaryComposition :
  (Fin10 -> Permutation Int) ->
  (Fin10 -> Bool) ->
  Int ->
  Int
binaryComposition f exponent x =
  selectPower (exponent i0) (f i0)
    (selectPower (exponent i1) (f i1)
      (selectPower (exponent i2) (f i2)
        (selectPower (exponent i3) (f i3)
          (selectPower (exponent i4) (f i4)
            (selectPower (exponent i5) (f i5)
              (selectPower (exponent i6) (f i6)
                (selectPower (exponent i7) (f i7)
                  (selectPower (exponent i8) (f i8)
                    (selectPower (exponent i9) (f i9) x)))))))))

InBinaryFamily :
  (Fin10 -> Permutation Int) ->
  (Int -> Int) ->
  Set
InBinaryFamily f g =
  Exists (Fin10 -> Bool)
    (\ exponent ->
      FunctionEqual g (binaryComposition f exponent))

Image :
  (Int -> Int) ->
  (Int -> Set) ->
  Int ->
  Set
Image g member y =
  Exists Int
    (\ x ->
      member x
      and
      g x == y)

Stabilizes :
  (Int -> Int) ->
  (Int -> Set) ->
  Set
Stabilizes g member =
  SetEqual (Image g member) member

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

fiveHundredTwelveN : Nat
fiveHundredTwelveN =
  twoN * twoN * twoN * twoN * twoN * twoN * twoN * twoN * twoN

putnam-1994-a6 : Set1
putnam-1994-a6 =
  (f : Fin10 -> Permutation Int) ->
  GeneratesIntegersFromZero f ->
  (A : Int -> Set) ->
  FiniteSet A ->
  NonemptySet A ->
  CardinalityAtMost
    FunctionEqual
    (\ g ->
      InBinaryFamily f g
      and
      Stabilizes g A)
    fiveHundredTwelveN

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a6:
  ten bijections of the integers whose finite nonempty compositions reach
  every integer from zero have at most 512 binary-exponent composites
  stabilizing any finite nonempty integer set. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_1994_a6 =
  ``!(f : num -> int -> int)
     (mijcomp : num -> (num -> num) -> num -> int -> int)
     (F : (int -> int) set).
      (!k : num.
         k < 10
         ==>
         BIJ (f k) (UNIV : int set) (UNIV : int set)) /\
      (!n : int.
         ?m : num.
           1 <= m /\
           ?i : num -> num.
             (!j : num. j < m ==> i j < 10) /\
             mijcomp m i 0 0 = n) /\
      (!m : num.
         1 <= m
         ==>
         !i : num -> num. !j : num.
           j < m
           ==>
           mijcomp m i j =
             if j = m - 1 then
               f (i j)
             else
               \x : int. f (i j) (mijcomp m i (j + 1) x)) /\
      F =
        {g : int -> int |
           ?e : num -> num.
             (!k : num. k < 10 ==> (e k = 0 \/ e k = 1)) /\
             g =
               \x : int.
                 FUNPOW (f 0) (e 0)
                   (FUNPOW (f 1) (e 1)
                     (FUNPOW (f 2) (e 2)
                       (FUNPOW (f 3) (e 3)
                         (FUNPOW (f 4) (e 4)
                           (FUNPOW (f 5) (e 5)
                             (FUNPOW (f 6) (e 6)
                               (FUNPOW (f 7) (e 7)
                                 (FUNPOW (f 8) (e 8)
                                   (FUNPOW (f 9) (e 9) x))))))))))}
      ==>
      !A : int set.
        FINITE A /\ A <> {}
        ==>
        CARD {g : int -> int | g IN F /\ IMAGE g A = A} <= 512``;

title: putnam_1994_a6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1994_a6: ten bijections of the integers whose finite compositions
  reach every integer from zero have at most 512 binary-exponent compositions
  stabilizing any nonempty finite set of integers. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The index set 0 ... 9 represents the ten source bijections. A nonempty word
  w over these indices, together with the state sequence s, records successive
  applications beginning at zero and ending at an arbitrary integer n.
  Reversing w converts this left-to-right path convention to the source's
  right-associated composition convention, so the reachability hypothesis is
  bidirectionally equivalent to the source hypothesis.

  In the conclusion, e ranges over all functions from 0 ... 9 to { 0 , 1 }.
  Each conditional factor is f_i when e_i = 1 and the identity on ZZ when
  e_i = 0. The displayed right-associated relation composition is therefore
  exactly f_0^e_0 o ... o f_9^e_9. The restricted class counts the distinct
  resulting functions whose image of A is A. The final declaration is the
  single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

${
  $d A e f g i j n s w $.

  putnambench-putnam-1994-a6 $a |-
    A. f e. ( ( ZZ ^m ZZ ) ^m ( 0 ... 9 ) )
      (
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ... 9 )
            ( f ` i ) : ZZ -1-1-onto-> ZZ
          /\
          A. n e. ZZ
            E. w e. ( Word ( 0 ... 9 ) \ { (/) } )
              E. s e. ( ZZ ^m ( 0 ... ( # ` w ) ) )
                (
                  (
                    ( s ` 0 ) = 0
                    /\
                    ( s ` ( # ` w ) ) = n
                  )
                  /\
                  A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` w ) )
                    ( s ` ( j + 1 ) )
                    =
                    ( ( f ` ( w ` j ) ) ` ( s ` j ) )
                )
        )
        ->
        A. A e. ( Fin i^i ~P ZZ )
          (
            A =/= (/)
            ->
            (
              #
              `
              { g e. ( ZZ ^m ZZ ) |
                (
                  E. e e. ( { 0 , 1 } ^m ( 0 ... 9 ) )
                    g
                    =
                    (
                      if
                        (
                          ( e ` 0 ) = 1 ,
                          ( f ` 0 ) ,
                          ( _I |` ZZ )
                        )

title: putnam_1994_a6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_a6:
% ten bijections of the integers act transitively from zero, and at most half
% of their ordered binary-exponent compositions stabilize any nonempty finite
% set of integers. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1994_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  digit: TYPE = {index: nat | index < 10}
  integer_function: TYPE = [int -> int]
  generator_family: TYPE = [digit -> integer_function]
  word: TYPE = [nat -> digit]
  composition_table: TYPE =
    [nat, word, nat -> integer_function]
  exponent_selection: TYPE = [digit -> bool]

  IMPORTING finite_sets[int], finite_sets[integer_function]

  integer_set: TYPE = finite_set[int]
  function_family: TYPE = finite_set[integer_function]

  injective(g: integer_function): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: int):
      g(x) = g(y) IMPLIES x = y

  surjective(g: integer_function): bool =
    FORALL (y: int):
      EXISTS (x: int):
        g(x) = y

  all_bijections(f: generator_family): bool =
    FORALL (index: digit):
      injective(f(index)) AND surjective(f(index))

  composition_specification(
      f: generator_family,
      mijcomp: composition_table): bool =
    FORALL (length: nat):
      length >= 1 IMPLIES
        FORALL (indices: word), (position: nat):
          position < length IMPLIES
            FORALL (x: int):
              mijcomp(length, indices, position)(x) =
                IF position = length - 1 THEN
                  f(indices(position))(x)
                ELSE
                  f(indices(position))(
                    mijcomp(length, indices, position + 1)(x))
                ENDIF

  transitive_from_zero(mijcomp: composition_table): bool =
    FORALL (target: int):
      EXISTS (length: nat), (indices: word):
        length >= 1
          AND mijcomp(length, indices, 0)(0) = target

  optional_apply(
      g: integer_function,
      selected: bool,
      x: int): int =
    IF selected THEN g(x) ELSE x ENDIF

  selected_composition(
      f: generator_family,
      exponents: exponent_selection): integer_function =
    LAMBDA (x: int):
      optional_apply(f(0), exponents(0),
        optional_apply(f(1), exponents(1),
          optional_apply(f(2), exponents(2),
            optional_apply(f(3), exponents(3),
              optional_apply(f(4), exponents(4),
                optional_apply(f(5), exponents(5),
                  optional_apply(f(6), exponents(6),
                    optional_apply(f(7), exponents(7),
                      optional_apply(f(8), exponents(8),
                        optional_apply(
                          f(9), exponents(9), x))))))))))

  is_binary_composition_family(
      f: generator_family,
      F: function_family): bool =
    FORALL (g: integer_function):
      F(g) IFF
        EXISTS (exponents: exponent_selection):
          g = selected_composition(f, exponents)

  maps_set_to_itself(
      g: integer_function,
      A: integer_set): bool =
    FORALL (y: int):
      A(y) IFF
        EXISTS (x: int):
          A(x) AND g(x) = y

  is_stabilizer_family(
      stabilizers, F: function_family,
      A: integer_set): bool =
    FORALL (g: integer_function):
      stabilizers(g) IFF
        F(g) AND maps_set_to_itself(g, A)

  putnam_1994_a6: bool =
    FORALL (f: generator_family),
           (mijcomp: composition_table),
           (F: function_family):
      (all_bijections(f)
        AND transitive_from_zero(mijcomp)
        AND composition_specification(f, mijcomp)
        AND is_binary_composition_family(f, F))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (A: integer_set):
          card(A) > 0 IMPLIES
            EXISTS (stabilizers: function_family):
              is_stabilizer_family(stabilizers, F, A)
                AND card(stabilizers) <= 512
END putnam_1994_a6

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_b1:
;; the positive integers within 250 of exactly 15 natural-number squares are
;; precisely 315 through 325 and 332 through 350. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For positive integer n, every natural m satisfying |n - m^2| <= 250 has
;; m^2 <= n + 250, hence m <= n + 250. Thus this recursion counts the entire
;; source set of natural-number square roots, including m = 0.
(defun putnam-1994-b1-square-count-through (n m)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix m)))
  (if (and (integerp n)
           (natp m))
      (if (zp m)
          (if (<= (abs n) 250)
              1
            0)
        (+ (if (<= (abs (- n (* m m))) 250)
               1
             0)
           (putnam-1994-b1-square-count-through
            n (- m 1))))
    0))

(defun putnam-1994-b1-solution-p (n)
  (and
   (integerp n)
   (or (and (<= 315 n)
            (<= n 325))
       (and (<= 332 n)
            (<= n 350)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1994-b1-statement (n)
  (implies
   (integerp n)
   (iff
    (putnam-1994-b1-solution-p n)
    (and
     (< 0 n)
     (equal
      (putnam-1994-b1-square-count-through
       n (+ n 250))
      15)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_b1:
-- the positive integers lying within 250 of exactly 15 natural-number
-- perfect squares are precisely two stated intervals. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1994B1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<=Z_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data _<=Z_ : Int -> Int -> Set where
  negative<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    negsuc m <=Z pos n
  positive<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    m <=N n ->
    pos m <=Z pos n
  negative<=negative :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    n <=N m ->
    negsuc m <=Z negsuc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> item == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

subtractSquare : Int -> Nat -> Int
subtractSquare (pos n) m =
  difference n (m * m)
subtractSquare (negsuc n) m =
  negsuc (n + m * m)

absoluteValue : Int -> Nat
absoluteValue (pos n) =
  n
absoluteValue (negsuc n) =
  suc n

data PositiveInteger : Int -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> PositiveInteger (pos (suc n))

Within250OfSquare : Int -> Nat -> Set
Within250OfSquare n m =
  absoluteValue (subtractSquare n m) <=N 250

ExactlyFifteenNearbySquares : Int -> Set
ExactlyFifteenNearbySquares n =
  HasCardinality (Within250OfSquare n) 15

putnam-1994-b1-solution : Int -> Set
putnam-1994-b1-solution n =
  ((pos 315 <=Z n) and (n <=Z pos 325))
  or
  ((pos 332 <=Z n) and (n <=Z pos 350))

putnam-1994-b1 : Set
putnam-1994-b1 =
  (n : Int) ->
  Iff
    (putnam-1994-b1-solution n)
    (PositiveInteger n and ExactlyFifteenNearbySquares n)

(defstub p94b2-multiply (real-type left right) t)
(defstub p94b2-negate (real-type value) t)
(defstub p94b2-inverse (real-type value) t)
(defstub p94b2-less (real-type left right) t)

(defun p94b2-r-add (real-type left right)
  (p94b2-add real-type left right))

(defun p94b2-r-multiply (real-type left right)
  (p94b2-multiply real-type left right))

(defun p94b2-r-negate (real-type value)
  (p94b2-negate real-type value))

(defun p94b2-r-inverse (real-type value)
  (p94b2-inverse real-type value))

(defun p94b2-r-subtract (real-type left right)
  (p94b2-r-add
   real-type left (p94b2-r-negate real-type right)))

(defun p94b2-r-divide (real-type numerator denominator)
  (p94b2-r-multiply
   real-type numerator (p94b2-r-inverse real-type denominator)))

(defun p94b2-leq (real-type left right)
  (not (p94b2-less real-type right left)))

(defun p94b2-square (real-type value)
  (p94b2-r-multiply real-type value value))

(defun p94b2-cube (real-type value)
  (p94b2-r-multiply
   real-type (p94b2-square real-type value) value))

(defun p94b2-fourth-power (real-type value)
  (p94b2-square real-type (p94b2-square real-type value)))

(defun p94b2-r-nat (real-type n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (p94b2-zero real-type)
    (p94b2-r-add
     real-type
     (p94b2-one real-type)
     (p94b2-r-nat real-type (1- n)))))

(defun-sk p94b2-field-laws-p (real-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p94b2-member-p real-type x)
      (p94b2-member-p real-type y)
      (p94b2-member-p real-type z))
     (let* ((zero (p94b2-zero real-type))
            (one (p94b2-one real-type))
            (xy-add (p94b2-r-add real-type x y))
            (yz-add (p94b2-r-add real-type y z))
            (xy-mul (p94b2-r-multiply real-type x y))
            (yz-mul (p94b2-r-multiply real-type y z))
            (neg-x (p94b2-r-negate real-type x))
            (inv-x (p94b2-r-inverse real-type x)))
       (and
        (p94b2-member-p real-type xy-add)
        (p94b2-member-p real-type xy-mul)
        (p94b2-member-p real-type neg-x)
        (p94b2-member-p real-type inv-x)
        (equal
         (p94b2-r-add real-type xy-add z)
         (p94b2-r-add real-type x yz-add))
        (equal xy-add (p94b2-r-add real-type y x))
        (equal (p94b2-r-add real-type x zero) x)
        (equal (p94b2-r-add real-type x neg-x) zero)
        (equal
         (p94b2-r-multiply real-type xy-mul z)
         (p94b2-r-multiply real-type x yz-mul))
        (equal xy-mul (p94b2-r-multiply real-type y x))
        (equal (p94b2-r-multiply real-type x one) x)
        (implies
         (equal x zero)
         (equal inv-x zero))
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (equal
          (p94b2-r-multiply real-type x inv-x)
          one))
        (equal
         (p94b2-r-multiply real-type x yz-add)
         (p94b2-r-add
          real-type
          (p94b2-r-multiply real-type x y)
          (p94b2-r-multiply real-type x z))))))))

(defun-sk p94b2-order-laws-p (real-type)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p94b2-member-p real-type x)
      (p94b2-member-p real-type y)
      (p94b2-member-p real-type z))
     (let ((zero (p94b2-zero real-type)))
       (and
        (not (p94b2-less real-type x x))
        (or
         (p94b2-less real-type x y)
         (equal x y)
         (p94b2-less real-type y x))
        (implies
         (and
          (p94b2-less real-type x y)
          (p94b2-less real-type y z))
         (p94b2-less real-type x z))
        (implies
         (p94b2-less real-type x y)
         (p94b2-less
          real-type
          (p94b2-r-add real-type x z)
          (p94b2-r-add real-type y z)))
        (implies
         (and
          (p94b2-less real-type zero x)
          (p94b2-less real-type zero y))
         (p94b2-less
          real-type
          zero
          (p94b2-r-multiply real-type x y))))))))

;; A standard first-order characterization of real-closed ordered fields:
;; every nonnegative element is a square, and every odd-degree polynomial has
;; a root. Coefficient lists below are constant-term first.

(defun p94b2-polynomial-p (real-type coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and
       (p94b2-member-p real-type (car coefficients))
       (p94b2-polynomial-p real-type (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun p94b2-leading-coefficient (coefficients)
  (if (consp (cdr coefficients))
      (p94b2-leading-coefficient (cdr coefficients))
    (car coefficients)))

(defun p94b2-polynomial-value
    (real-type coefficients value)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (p94b2-r-add
       real-type
       (car coefficients)
       (p94b2-r-multiply
        real-type
        value
        (p94b2-polynomial-value
         real-type (cdr coefficients) value)))
    (p94b2-zero real-type)))

(defun p94b2-odd-degree-polynomial-p
    (real-type coefficients)
  (and
   (consp coefficients)
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (p94b2-polynomial-p real-type coefficients)
   (oddp (1- (len coefficients)))
   (not
    (equal
     (p94b2-leading-coefficient coefficients)
     (p94b2-zero real-type)))))

(defun-sk p94b2-nonnegative-square-root-exists-p
    (real-type value)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (p94b2-member-p real-type root)
     (equal
      (p94b2-square real-type root)
      value))))

(defun-sk p94b2-nonnegative-elements-are-squares-p
    (real-type)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (and
      (p94b2-member-p real-type value)
      (p94b2-leq
       real-type (p94b2-zero real-type) value))
     (p94b2-nonnegative-square-root-exists-p
      real-type value))))

(defun-sk p94b2-polynomial-root-exists-p
    (real-type coefficients)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (p94b2-member-p real-type root)
     (equal
      (p94b2-polynomial-value
       real-type coefficients root)
      (p94b2-zero real-type)))))

(defun-sk p94b2-odd-polynomials-have-roots-p
    (real-type)
  (forall (coefficients)
    (implies
     (p94b2-odd-degree-polynomial-p
      real-type coefficients)
     (p94b2-polynomial-root-exists-p
      real-type coefficients))))

(defun p94b2-real-closed-field-p (real-type)
  (let ((zero (p94b2-zero real-type))
        (one (p94b2-one real-type)))
    (and
     (p94b2-member-p real-type zero)
     (p94b2-member-p real-type one)
     (not (equal zero one))
     (p94b2-field-laws-p real-type)
     (p94b2-order-laws-p real-type)
     (p94b2-less real-type zero one)
     (p94b2-nonnegative-elements-are-squares-p real-type)
     (p94b2-odd-polynomials-have-roots-p real-type))))

(defun p94b2-curve-value (real-type c x)
  (let ((nine (p94b2-r-nat real-type 9))
        (four (p94b2-r-nat real-type 4)))
    (p94b2-r-add
     real-type
     (p94b2-fourth-power real-type x)
     (p94b2-r-add
      real-type
      (p94b2-r-multiply
       real-type nine (p94b2-cube real-type x))
      (p94b2-r-add
       real-type
       (p94b2-r-multiply
        real-type c (p94b2-square real-type x))
       (p94b2-r-add
        real-type
        (p94b2-r-multiply real-type nine x)
        four))))))

(defun p94b2-line-value (real-type m b x)
  (p94b2-r-add
   real-type
   (p94b2-r-multiply real-type m x)
   b))

(defun p94b2-intersection-p (real-type c m b x)
  (and
   (p94b2-member-p real-type x)
   (equal
    (p94b2-line-value real-type m b x)
    (p94b2-curve-value real-type c x))))

(defun p94b2-four-distinct-p (x1 x2 x3 x4)
  (and
   (not (equal x1 x2))
   (not (equal x1 x3))
   (not (equal x1 x4))
   (not (equal x2 x3))
   (not (equal x2 x4))
   (not (equal x3 x4))))

(defun-sk p94b2-all-intersections-listed-p
    (real-type c m b x1 x2 x3 x4)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p94b2-intersection-p real-type c m b x)
     (or
      (equal x x1)
      (equal x x2)
      (equal x x3)
      (equal x x4)))))

(defun p94b2-exactly-four-intersections-witness-p
    (real-type c m b x1 x2 x3 x4)
  (and
   (p94b2-member-p real-type m)
   (p94b2-member-p real-type b)
   (p94b2-member-p real-type x1)
   (p94b2-member-p real-type x2)
   (p94b2-member-p real-type x3)
   (p94b2-member-p real-type x4)
   (p94b2-four-distinct-p x1 x2 x3 x4)
   (p94b2-intersection-p real-type c m b x1)
   (p94b2-intersection-p real-type c m b x2)
   (p94b2-intersection-p real-type c m b x3)
   (p94b2-intersection-p real-type c m b x4)
   (p94b2-all-intersections-listed-p
    real-type c m b x1 x2 x3 x4)))

(defun-sk p94b2-line-with-exactly-four-intersections-exists-p
    (real-type c)
  (exists (m b x1 x2 x3 x4)
    (p94b2-exactly-four-intersections-witness-p
     real-type c m b x1 x2 x3 x4)))

(defun p94b2-solution-p (real-type c)
  (p94b2-less
   real-type
   c
   (p94b2-r-divide
    real-type
    (p94b2-r-nat real-type 243)
    (p94b2-r-nat real-type 8))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1994-b2-statement
    (real-type c)
  (implies
   (and
    (p94b2-real-closed-field-p real-type)
    (p94b2-member-p real-type c))
   (iff
    (p94b2-line-with-exactly-four-intersections-exists-p
     real-type c)
    (p94b2-solution-p real-type c))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1994_b2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_b2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_1994_b2): a real coefficient admits a straight
-- line intersecting the stated quartic in exactly four distinct points
-- exactly when it is less than 243/8. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (P : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      P (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      P item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> item == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc threeN

eightN : Nat
eightN =
  fourN + fourN

nineN : Nat
nineN =
  suc eightN

twoHundredFortyThreeN : Nat
twoHundredFortyThreeN =
  243

module Putnam1994B2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  lineValue :
    R ->
    R ->
    R ->
    R
  lineValue slope intercept x =
    add reals
      (multiply reals slope x)
      intercept

  quarticValue :
    R ->
    R ->
    R
  quarticValue c x =
    add reals
      (add reals
        (add reals
          (add reals
            (naturalPower reals x fourN)
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals nineN)
              (naturalPower reals x threeN)))
          (multiply reals
            c
            (naturalPower reals x twoN)))
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals nineN)
          x))
      (fromNat reals fourN)

  IsIntersectionAbscissa :
    R ->
    R ->
    R ->
    R ->
    Set
  IsIntersectionAbscissa c slope intercept x =
    lineValue slope intercept x ==
    quarticValue c x

  IntersectsInExactlyFourPoints :
    R ->
    Set
  IntersectsInExactlyFourPoints c =
    Exists R
      (\ slope ->
        Exists R
          (\ intercept ->
            HasCardinality
              (IsIntersectionAbscissa c slope intercept)
              fourN))

  solution :
    R ->
    Set
  solution c =
    StrictLess reals
      c
      (divide reals
        (fromNat reals twoHundredFortyThreeN)
        (fromNat reals eightN))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (c : R) ->
    Iff
      (IntersectsInExactlyFourPoints c)
      (solution c)

putnam-1994-b2 : Set1
putnam-1994-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam1994B2Statement.proposition reals

title: putnam_1994_b2

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_b2:
  a real parameter admits a straight line intersecting the corresponding
  quartic in exactly four distinct real points if and only if it is less than
  243/8. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory;

val putnam_1994_b2 =
  ``!c : real.
      ((?m b : real.
          let intersections =
            {x : real |
               m * x + b =
                 x pow 4 + 9 * x pow 3 + c * x pow 2 + 9 * x + 4}
          in
            FINITE intersections /\ CARD intersections = 4)
       <=>
       c < 243 / 8)``;

$(

  putnam_1994_b2: a real line intersects the quartic
  x^4 + 9x^3 + cx^2 + 9x + 4 in four distinct real points exactly when
  c is less than 243/8. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The real parameters m and b describe the source line y = mx + b. The
  restricted class is exactly the set of real x-coordinates at which that
  line meets the graph of the quartic. Since the curve is a function of x,
  cardinality four is equivalent to four distinct intersection points.

  The right side expands the solution set identified in the Rocq source and
  in the Lean and Isabelle annotations. The final declaration is the single
  unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d b c m x $.

  putnambench-putnam-1994-b2 $a |-
    A. c e. RR
      (
        (
          E. m e. RR E. b e. RR
            (
              #
              `
              {
                x e. RR
                |
                (
                  ( ( m x. x ) + b )
                  =
                  (
                    (
                      (
                        (
                          ( x ^ 4 )
                          +
                          ( 9 x. ( x ^ 3 ) )
                        )
                        +
                        ( c x. ( x ^ 2 ) )
                      )
                      +
                      ( 9 x. x )
                    )
                    +
                    4
                  )
                )
              }
            )
            =
            4
        )
        <->
        c < ( ( ; ; 2 4 3 ) / 8 )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1994_b2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1994_b2:
% a real line intersects x^4 + 9*x^3 + c*x^2 + 9*x + 4 in exactly four
% distinct real points exactly when c < 243/8. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1994_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[real]

  quartic(c, x: real): real =
    x ^ 4 + 9 * x ^ 3 + c * x ^ 2 + 9 * x + 4

  has_four_distinct_intersections(c: real): bool =
    EXISTS (m, b: real), (roots: finite_set[real]):
      card(roots) = 4
        AND (FORALL (x: real):
          roots(x) IFF m * x + b = quartic(c, x))

  putnam_1994_b2_solution(c: real): bool =
    c < 243 / 8

  putnam_1994_b2_statement: bool =
    FORALL (c: real):
      has_four_distinct_intersections(c)
        IFF putnam_1994_b2_solution(c)
END putnam_1994_b2

-- Set.Iio 1

Find the set of all real numbers $k$ with the following property: For any positive, differentiable function $f$ that satisfies $f'(x)>f(x)$ for all $x$, there is some number $N$ such that $f(x)>e^{kx}$ for all $x>N$.
-/
theorem putnam_1994_b3 :
    {k | ∀ f (hf : (∀ x, 0 < f x ∧ f x < deriv f x) ∧ Differentiable ℝ f),
      ∃ N, ∀ x > N, Real.exp (k * x) < f x} = putnam_1994_b3_solution :=
