content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
-- putnambench__agda__putnam_1995_a2: the improper integral from b to
-- positive infinity of the difference of the two nested square-root terms
-- converges exactly when the positive real parameters a and b are equal.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1995A2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_ _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

open CompleteOrderedRealField

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

LimitAtPositiveInfinity :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
LimitAtPositiveInfinity {R} reals function limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ threshold ->
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals threshold x ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (function x))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

midpointRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
midpointRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
    halfStep =
      divide reals
        step
        (fromNat reals twoN)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (add reals
              (multiply reals
                (fromNat reals i)
                step)
              halfStep)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function integralValue =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      midpointRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    integralValue

putnamIntegrand :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
putnamIntegrand reals a b x =
  subtract reals
    (squareRoot reals
      (subtract reals
        (squareRoot reals (add reals x a))
        (squareRoot reals x)))
    (squareRoot reals
      (subtract reals
        (squareRoot reals x)
        (squareRoot reals (subtract reals x b))))

IntegralAssignment :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
IntegralAssignment {R} reals a b integralValues =
  (t : R) ->
  lessOrEqual reals b t ->
  IntervalIntegralValue reals
    b
    t
    (putnamIntegrand reals a b)
    (integralValues t)

ImproperIntegralConverges :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
ImproperIntegralConverges {R} reals a b =
  Exists (R -> R)
    (\ integralValues ->
      IntegralAssignment reals a b integralValues
      and
      Exists R
        (\ limit ->
          LimitAtPositiveInfinity reals integralValues limit))

putnam-1995-a2 : Set1
putnam-1995-a2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (a b : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) a
  and
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) b ->
  ImproperIntegralConverges reals a b iff a == b

  characterization of the positive real pairs for which the given improper
  integral involving nested square roots converges. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory realTheory transcTheory integrationTheory;

val putnam_1995_a2 =
  ``!a b : real.
      0 < a /\ 0 < b
      ==>
      ((?limit : real.
          !e : real.
            0 < e
            ==>
            ?T : real.
              !t : real.
                T <= t
                ==>
                abs
                  (integration$integral (interval [b, t])
                     (\x : real.
                        sqrt (sqrt (x + a) - sqrt x) -
                        sqrt (sqrt x - sqrt (x - b))) -
                   limit) < e)
       <=>
       a = b)``;

title: putnam_1995_a2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a2:
% the improper integral with nested square-root differences converges for
% positive parameters a and b exactly when a = b. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1995_a2: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_set: TYPE = [real -> bool]
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  real_set_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real_set]

  finite_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      finite_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(values: real_sequence, limit_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(values(count) - limit_value) < epsilon_value

  interval_length(left_endpoint, right_endpoint: real): real =
    IF left_endpoint < right_endpoint THEN
      right_endpoint - left_endpoint
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  closed_interval(left_endpoint, right_endpoint: real): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      left_endpoint <= x AND x <= right_endpoint

  open_interval_cover(
      covered: real_set,
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      covered(x) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (index: nat):
          left_endpoints(index) < x
            AND x < right_endpoints(index)

  cover_partial_length(
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence,
      count: nat): real =
    finite_sum(
      LAMBDA (index: nat):
        interval_length(
          left_endpoints(index),
          right_endpoints(index)),
      count)

  cover_has_total_length(
      left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence,
      total: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat):
        cover_partial_length(
          left_endpoints, right_endpoints, count),
      total)

  has_outer_measure(
      covered: real_set,
      measure_value: real): bool =
    measure_value >= 0
      AND (FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS
            (left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence),
            (total: real):
          open_interval_cover(
            covered, left_endpoints, right_endpoints)
            AND cover_has_total_length(
              left_endpoints, right_endpoints, total)
            AND total < measure_value + epsilon_value)
      AND (FORALL
          (left_endpoints, right_endpoints: real_sequence),
          (total: real):
        (open_interval_cover(
            covered, left_endpoints, right_endpoints)
          AND cover_has_total_length(
            left_endpoints, right_endpoints, total))
        IMPLIES measure_value <= total)

  set_intersection(left_set, right_set: real_set): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      left_set(x) AND right_set(x)

  set_difference(left_set, right_set: real_set): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      left_set(x) AND NOT right_set(x)

  set_subset(left_set, right_set: real_set): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      left_set(x) IMPLIES right_set(x)

  lebesgue_measurable(measured_set: real_set): bool =
    FORALL
        (test_set: real_set),
        (test_measure, inside_measure, outside_measure: real):
      (has_outer_measure(test_set, test_measure)
        AND has_outer_measure(
          set_intersection(test_set, measured_set),
          inside_measure)
        AND has_outer_measure(
          set_difference(test_set, measured_set),
          outside_measure))
      IMPLIES
        test_measure = inside_measure + outside_measure

  lebesgue_measure(measured_set: real_set): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (measure_value: real):
        has_outer_measure(measured_set, measure_value))

  sublevel_set_on(
      domain: real_set,
      function_value: real_function,
      bound: real): real_set =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      domain(x) AND function_value(x) <= bound

  measurable_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set): bool =
    FORALL (bound: real):
      lebesgue_measurable(
        sublevel_set_on(domain, function_value, bound))

  pairwise_disjoint_below(
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (left_index, right_index: nat):
      left_index < count
        AND right_index < count
        AND left_index /= right_index
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (x: real):
          NOT (pieces(left_index)(x)
            AND pieces(right_index)(x))

  simple_value(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat,
      x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      simple_value(coefficients, pieces, count - 1, x)
        + IF pieces(count - 1)(x)
            THEN coefficients(count - 1)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  simple_integral(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      simple_integral(coefficients, pieces, count - 1)
        + coefficients(count - 1)
            * lebesgue_measure(pieces(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  nonnegative_simple_minorant_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set,
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      pieces: real_set_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    pairwise_disjoint_below(pieces, count)
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          coefficients(index) >= 0
            AND lebesgue_measurable(pieces(index))
            AND set_subset(pieces(index), domain))
      AND (FORALL (x: real):
        domain(x) IMPLIES
          0 <= simple_value(
            coefficients, pieces, count, x)
          AND simple_value(
            coefficients, pieces, count, x)
              <= function_value(x))

  nonnegative_integral_upper_bound_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set,
      upper_bound: real): bool =
    FORALL
        (coefficients: real_sequence),
        (pieces: real_set_sequence),
        (count: nat):
      nonnegative_simple_minorant_on(
        function_value, domain,
        coefficients, pieces, count)
      IMPLIES
        simple_integral(coefficients, pieces, count)
          <= upper_bound

  has_nonnegative_integral_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    measurable_on(function_value, domain)
      AND (FORALL (x: real):
        domain(x) IMPLIES function_value(x) >= 0)
      AND integral_value >= 0
      AND nonnegative_integral_upper_bound_on(
        function_value, domain, integral_value)
      AND (FORALL (upper_bound: real):
        nonnegative_integral_upper_bound_on(
          function_value, domain, upper_bound)
        IMPLIES integral_value <= upper_bound)

  positive_part(function_value: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      IF function_value(x) >= 0
      THEN function_value(x)
      ELSE 0
      ENDIF

  negative_part(function_value: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      IF function_value(x) <= 0
      THEN -function_value(x)
      ELSE 0
      ENDIF

  has_integral_on(
      function_value: real_function,
      domain: real_set,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    measurable_on(function_value, domain)
      AND EXISTS (positive_integral, negative_integral: real):
        has_nonnegative_integral_on(
          positive_part(function_value),
          domain,
          positive_integral)
          AND has_nonnegative_integral_on(
            negative_part(function_value),
            domain,
            negative_integral)
          AND integral_value =
            positive_integral - negative_integral

  interval_lebesgue_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      left_endpoint, right_endpoint: real): real =
    IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
        has_integral_on(
          function_value,
          closed_interval(left_endpoint, right_endpoint),
          integral_value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
          has_integral_on(
            function_value,
            closed_interval(left_endpoint, right_endpoint),
            integral_value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  nonnegative_square_root(value: real): real =
    IF 0 <= value THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (root: real):
          0 <= root AND root * root = value)
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  integrand(a, b: real): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      nonnegative_square_root(
        nonnegative_square_root(x + a)
          - nonnegative_square_root(x))
        - nonnegative_square_root(
            nonnegative_square_root(x)
              - nonnegative_square_root(x - b))

  truncated_integral(a, b, t: real): real =
    interval_lebesgue_integral(
      integrand(a, b), b, t)

  converges_at_real_top(
      function_value: real_function,
      limit_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: real):
        FORALL (t: real):
          cutoff <= t IMPLIES
            abs(function_value(t) - limit_value)
              < epsilon_value

  improper_integral_converges(a, b: real): bool =
    EXISTS (limit_value: real):
      converges_at_real_top(
        LAMBDA (t: real):
          truncated_integral(a, b, t),
        limit_value)

  putnam_1995_a2_solution(a, b: real): bool =
    a = b

  putnam_1995_a2: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: real):
      (a > 0 AND b > 0)
        IMPLIES
          (improper_integral_converges(a, b)
            IFF putnam_1995_a2_solution(a, b))
END putnam_1995_a2

title: putnam_1995_a3

import Mathlib

open Filter Topology Real

/--
The number $d_{1}d_{2}\dots d_{9}$ has nine (not necessarily distinct) decimal digits. The number $e_{1}e_{2}\dots e_{9}$ is such that each of the nine 9-digit numbers formed by replacing just one of the digits $d_{i}$ is $d_{1}d_{2}\dots d_{9}$ by the corresponding digit $e_{i}$ ($1 \leq i \leq 9$) is divisible by 7. The number $f_{1}f_{2}\dots f_{9}$ is related to $e_{1}e_{2}\dots e_{9}$ is the same way: that is, each of the nine numbers formed by replacing one of the $e_{i}$ by the corresponding $f_{i}$ is divisible by 7. Show that, for each $i$, $d_{i}-f_{i}$ is divisible by 7. [For example, if $d_{1}d_{2}\dots d_{9} = 199501996$, then $e_{6}$ may be 2 or 9, since $199502996$ and $199509996$ are multiples of 7.]
-/
theorem putnam_1995_a3
(relation : (Fin 9 → ℤ) → (Fin 9 → ℤ) → Prop)
(digits_to_num : (Fin 9 → ℤ) → ℤ)
(hdigits_to_num : digits_to_num = fun dig => ∑ i : Fin 9, (dig i) * 10^i.1)
(hrelation : ∀ d e : (Fin 9 → ℤ), relation d e ↔ (∀ i : Fin 9, d i < 10 ∧ d i ≥ 0 ∧ e i < 10 ∧ e i ≥ 0) ∧ (∀ i : Fin 9, 7 ∣ (digits_to_num (fun j : Fin 9 => if j = i then e j else d j))))
: ∀ d e f : (Fin 9 → ℤ), ((relation d e) ∧ (relation e f)) → (∀ i : Fin 9, 7 ∣ d i - f i) :=
sorry

title: putnam_1995_a3
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1995_a3:
   divisibility by seven after successive coordinatewise replacements in
   nine-digit decimal numbers forces corresponding outer digits to be
   congruent modulo seven. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith Vectors.Fin.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition putnam_1995_a3_digits : Type :=
  Fin.t 9 -> Z.

Fixpoint putnam_1995_a3_fin_sum
    (n : nat) : (Fin.t n -> Z) -> Z :=
  match n as k return (Fin.t k -> Z) -> Z with
  | O => fun _ => 0
  | S k =>
      fun u =>
        u Fin.F1 +
        putnam_1995_a3_fin_sum k (fun i => u (Fin.FS i))
  end.

Definition putnam_1995_a3_index_value
    {n : nat} (i : Fin.t n) : nat :=
  proj1_sig (Fin.to_nat i).

Definition putnam_1995_a3_decimal_value
    (digits : putnam_1995_a3_digits) : Z :=
  putnam_1995_a3_fin_sum 9
    (fun i =>
      digits i *
      Z.pow 10 (Z.of_nat (putnam_1995_a3_index_value i))).

Theorem putnam_1995_a3
    (relation :
      putnam_1995_a3_digits ->
      putnam_1995_a3_digits ->
      Prop)
    (digits_to_num : putnam_1995_a3_digits -> Z)
    (hdigits_to_num :
      digits_to_num = putnam_1995_a3_decimal_value)
    (hrelation :
      forall d e : putnam_1995_a3_digits,
        relation d e <->
        (forall i : Fin.t 9,
          0 <= d i < 10 /\
          0 <= e i < 10) /\
        (forall i : Fin.t 9,
          Z.divide 7
            (digits_to_num
              (fun j : Fin.t 9 =>
                if Fin.eq_dec j i then e j else d j)))) :
  forall d e f : putnam_1995_a3_digits,
    relation d e /\
    relation e f ->
    forall i : Fin.t 9,
      Z.divide 7 (d i - f i).
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a3:
  nine decimal digit replacements divisible by seven in two successive steps
  force each original-to-final digit difference to be divisible by seven.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `!relation:(num->int)->(num->int)->bool.
   !digits_to_num:(num->int)->int.
     digits_to_num =
       (\dig:num->int.
          isum (0..8) (\i. dig i * ((&10:int) pow i))) /\
     (!d e:num->int.
        relation d e <=>

title: putnam_1995_a3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a3:
;; two successive nine-digit replacement relations force every corresponding
;; first-and-third digit difference to be divisible by 7. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A nine-element integer list is exactly a function Fin 9 -> Z, represented
;; by its values at indices 0 through 8. The source definitions uniquely
;; determine DIGITS_TO_NUM and RELATION, so substituting the definitions below
;; is bidirectionally equivalent to quantifying over those defined symbols.

(defun putnam-1995-a3-decimal-digit-list-p (digits)
  (if (consp digits)
      (and
       (integerp (car digits))
       (<= 0 (car digits))
       (< (car digits) 10)
       (putnam-1995-a3-decimal-digit-list-p (cdr digits)))
    (equal digits nil)))

(defun putnam-1995-a3-digit-vector-p (digits)
  (and
   (true-listp digits)
   (equal (len digits) 9)
   (putnam-1995-a3-decimal-digit-list-p digits)))

(defun putnam-1995-a3-digits-to-num (digits)
  (+ (nth 0 digits)
     (* (nth 1 digits) 10)
     (* (nth 2 digits) (expt 10 2))
     (* (nth 3 digits) (expt 10 3))
     (* (nth 4 digits) (expt 10 4))
     (* (nth 5 digits) (expt 10 5))
     (* (nth 6 digits) (expt 10 6))
     (* (nth 7 digits) (expt 10 7))
     (* (nth 8 digits) (expt 10 8))))

(defun putnam-1995-a3-replacement-divisible-p
    (digits replacements index)
  (equal
   (mod
    (putnam-1995-a3-digits-to-num
     (update-nth
      index
      (nth index replacements)
      digits))
    7)
   0))

(defun putnam-1995-a3-relation-p (digits replacements)

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a3:
-- digitwise replacement divisibility by 7 for two successive nine-digit
-- integer vectors forces corresponding endpoint digits to agree modulo 7.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<N_ _dividesZ_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<sucN : {n : Nat} -> zero <N suc n
  suc<sucN  : {m n : Nat} -> m <N n -> suc m <N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finToNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (finToNat i)

finEqual : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin n -> Bool
finEqual fzero fzero =
  true
finEqual fzero (fsuc j) =
  false
finEqual (fsuc i) fzero =
  false
finEqual (fsuc i) (fsuc j) =
  finEqual i j

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

subtractInt : Int -> Int -> Int
subtractInt x y =
  addInt x (negateInt y)

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

record _dividesZ_ (divisor dividend : Int) : Set where
  field
    integer-quotient : Int
    integer-equation :
      dividend == multiplyInt divisor integer-quotient

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

sevenN : Nat
sevenN =
  suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc oneN)))))

nineN : Nat
nineN =
  suc (suc sevenN)

tenN : Nat
tenN =
  suc nineN

powerNat : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
powerNat base zero =
  oneN
powerNat base (suc exponent) =
  powerNat base exponent * base

sumFin : {n : Nat} -> (Fin n -> Int) -> Int
sumFin {zero} terms =
  pos zero
sumFin {suc n} terms =
  addInt
    (terms fzero)
    (sumFin (\ i -> terms (fsuc i)))

Index : Set
Index =
  Fin nineN

Digits : Set
Digits =
  Index -> Int

data DecimalDigit : Int -> Set where
  decimal-digit :
    {n : Nat} ->
    n <N tenN ->
    DecimalDigit (pos n)

replaceDigit : Digits -> Digits -> Index -> Digits
replaceDigit d e replaced j with finEqual j replaced
... | true =
  e j
... | false =
  d j

digitsToNumberDefinition : Digits -> Int
digitsToNumberDefinition digits =
  sumFin
    (\ i ->
      multiplyInt
        (digits i)
        (pos (powerNat tenN (finToNat i))))

RelationMeaning :
  (Digits -> Int) ->
  Digits ->
  Digits ->
  Set
RelationMeaning digitsToNumber d e =
  ((i : Index) ->
    DecimalDigit (d i)
    and
    DecimalDigit (e i))
  and
  ((i : Index) ->
    pos sevenN dividesZ
    digitsToNumber (replaceDigit d e i))

putnam-1995-a3 : Set1
putnam-1995-a3 =
  (relation : Digits -> Digits -> Set) ->
  (digitsToNumber : Digits -> Int) ->
  digitsToNumber == digitsToNumberDefinition ->
  ((d e : Digits) ->
    Iff
      (relation d e)
      (RelationMeaning digitsToNumber d e)) ->
  (d e f : Digits) ->
  (relation d e and relation e f) ->
  (i : Index) ->
  pos sevenN dividesZ subtractInt (d i) (f i)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a3:
  divisibility modulo 7 for digit differences after two successive
  single-digit replacement relations on nine decimal digits. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_1995_a3 =
  ``!(relation : (num -> int) -> (num -> int) -> bool).
    !(digits_to_num : (num -> int) -> int).
      digits_to_num =
        (\dig : num -> int.
           ITSET
             (\i acc. dig i * (10 : int) ** i + acc)
             (count 9)
             (0 : int)) /\
      (!d e : num -> int.
         relation d e <=>
           ((!i : num.
               i IN count 9
               ==>
               d i < 10 /\ 0 <= d i /\
               e i < 10 /\ 0 <= e i) /\
            (!i : num.
               i IN count 9
               ==>
               (7 : int) int_divides
                 digits_to_num
                   (\j : num. if j = i then e j else d j))))
      ==>
      !d e f : num -> int.
        relation d e /\ relation e f
        ==>
        !i : num.
          i IN count 9
          ==>
          (7 : int) int_divides (d i - f i)``;

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a3:
% two successive digit-replacement divisibility relations force corresponding
% original and final decimal digits to differ by a multiple of 7. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1995_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  digit_index: TYPE = below(9)
  digit_vector: TYPE = [digit_index -> int]
  digit_number_function: TYPE = [digit_vector -> int]
  digit_relation: TYPE = [digit_vector, digit_vector -> bool]

  integer_divides(divisor, value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: int):
      value = divisor * quotient

  decimal_value(digits: digit_vector): int =
    digits(0) * (10 :: int) ^ 0
      + digits(1) * (10 :: int) ^ 1
      + digits(2) * (10 :: int) ^ 2
      + digits(3) * (10 :: int) ^ 3
      + digits(4) * (10 :: int) ^ 4
      + digits(5) * (10 :: int) ^ 5
      + digits(6) * (10 :: int) ^ 6
      + digits(7) * (10 :: int) ^ 7
      + digits(8) * (10 :: int) ^ 8

  replace_digit(
      original, replacement: digit_vector,
      position: digit_index): digit_vector =
    LAMBDA (index: digit_index):
      IF index = position THEN
        replacement(index)
      ELSE
        original(index)
      ENDIF

  digit_number_spec(
      digits_to_num: digit_number_function): bool =
    FORALL (digits: digit_vector):
      digits_to_num(digits) = decimal_value(digits)

  digit_relation_spec(
      relation: digit_relation,
      digits_to_num: digit_number_function): bool =
    FORALL (original, replacement: digit_vector):
      relation(original, replacement)
        IFF
          ((FORALL (index: digit_index):
              0 <= original(index)
                AND original(index) < 10
                AND 0 <= replacement(index)
                AND replacement(index) < 10)
            AND (FORALL (position: digit_index):
              integer_divides(
                7,
                digits_to_num(
                  replace_digit(
                    original, replacement, position)))))

  putnam_1995_a3: bool =
    FORALL
        (relation: digit_relation),
        (digits_to_num: digit_number_function):
      (digit_number_spec(digits_to_num)
        AND digit_relation_spec(relation, digits_to_num))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (d, e, f: digit_vector):
          (relation(d, e) AND relation(e, f))
          IMPLIES
            FORALL (index: digit_index):
              integer_divides(7, d(index) - f(index))
END putnam_1995_a3

Require Import Nat ZArith Coquelicot.Coquelicot.
Open Scope Z_scope.
Fixpoint Z_sum (a : nat -> Z) (k : nat) : Z := 
    match k with
    | O => a O
    | S k' => a k + Z_sum a k'
    end.
Theorem putnam_1995_a4
    (n : nat)
    (hn : gt n 0)
    (necklace : nat -> Z)
    (hnecklacesum : Z_sum necklace (n - 1) = (Z.of_nat n) - 1)
    : exists cut : nat, le cut (n-1) /\ (forall k : nat, le k (n-1) -> (Z_sum (fun i => necklace (Nat.modulo (cut + i) n)) k) <= Z.of_nat k).
Proof. Admitted.

;; a cyclic necklace of n integer labels with total n - 1 has a cut at which
;; every nonempty initial sum is at most its zero-based endpoint. This file

;; An integer true list of length n is bijective with a function Fin n -> Z.

(defun putnam-1995-a4-integer-list-p (values)

      (and

       (putnam-1995-a4-integer-list-p (cdr values)))

    (necklace cut count)

    (necklace cut)

  (or
   (putnam-1995-a4-all-prefix-bounds-p

    (posp n)
    (true-listp necklace)
    (equal (len necklace) n)
    (putnam-1995-a4-integer-list-p necklace)
    (equal (putnam-1995-a4-list-sum necklace)

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a4:
-- a cyclic integer-labeled necklace of positive length and total label sum n - 1
-- has a cut whose every nonempty prefix sum is at most its length minus one.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; mod-helper)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<=Z_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data _<=Z_ : Int -> Int -> Set where
  negative<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    negsuc m <=Z pos n
  positive<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    m <=N n ->
    pos m <=Z pos n
  negative<=negative :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    n <=N m ->
    negsuc m <=Z negsuc n

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

sumThrough : (Nat -> Int) -> Nat -> Int
sumThrough term zero =
  term zero
sumThrough term (suc n) =
  addInt (sumThrough term n) (term (suc n))

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero =
  zero
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

putnam-1995-a4 : Set
putnam-1995-a4 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  (necklace : Nat -> Int) ->
  sumThrough necklace (n - 1) == difference n 1 ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cut ->
      (cut <=N (n - 1))
      and
      ((k : Nat) ->
        k <=N (n - 1) ->
        sumThrough
          (\ i -> necklace (naturalMod (cut + i) n))
          k
        <=Z
        pos k))

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1995_a4: a cyclic integer necklace of positive length and total
  label sum n minus one has a cut after which every nonempty prefix sum is
  at most its zero-based final index. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The ordinal interval 0 ..^ n is the n-element carrier representing Fin n.
  Thus a e. ( ZZ ^m ( 0 ..^ n ) ) is an arbitrary integer labeling of the
  necklace. For k in that carrier, 0 ... k indexes the first k+1 labels
  after the cut, and reduction modulo n implements cyclic wraparound.

  The existential cut remains internal to the conclusion. The final
  declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a c i k n $.

  putnambench-putnam-1995-a4 $a |- A. n e. NN
    A. a e. ( ZZ ^m ( 0 ..^ n ) )
      (
        (
          sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ n ) ( a ` i )
        )
        =
        ( n - 1 )
        ->
        E. c e. ( 0 ..^ n )
          A. k e. ( 0 ..^ n )
            (
              sum_ i e. ( 0 ... k )
                (
                  a
                  `
                  ( ( c + i ) mod n )
                )
            )
            <_
            k
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1995_a4
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a4:
:: an integer-labeled cyclic necklace with n > 0 beads and total label
:: sum n-1 has a cut for which every nonempty prefix sum is at most its
:: length minus one. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies NUMBERS, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, TARSKI, CARD_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, ORDINAL1, INT_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, CARD_3, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    FINSEQ_1, RVSUM_1, FINSEQ_2, NAT_1, NAT_D;
  constructors REAL_1, NAT_D, RELSET_1, NUMBERS, RVSUM_1, FINSEQOP,
    FUNCT_2;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XREAL_0, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2,
    RVSUM_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, CARD_1, MEMBERED;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat,
      necklace being FinSequence of INT st
    0 < n &
    len necklace = n &
    Sum necklace = (n qua Integer) - 1
  holds
    ex cut being Nat,
       rotated being FinSequence of INT st
      cut < n &
      len rotated = n &
      (for i being Nat st i in Seg n holds
        rotated.i =
          necklace.(((cut + (i -' 1)) mod n) + 1)) &
      (for k being Nat st k in Seg n holds
        ex terms being FinSequence of INT st
          len terms = k &
          (for i being Nat st i in Seg k holds
            terms.i = rotated.i) &
          Sum terms <= (k qua Integer) - 1)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1995_a4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a4:
% an integer-labeled cyclic necklace of positive length and total label sum
% n - 1 admits a cut whose nonempty prefix sums have the stated bounds.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_1995_a4: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> int]

  prefix_sum(
      values: integer_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      prefix_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  remainder_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      numerator
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator - denominator,
        denominator,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  safe_mod(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator,
        denominator,
        numerator + 1)
    ENDIF

  rotated(
      necklace: integer_sequence,
      length, cut: nat): integer_sequence =
    LAMBDA (index: nat):
      necklace(safe_mod(cut + index, length))

  putnam_1995_a4: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (necklace: integer_sequence):
      (n > 0
        AND prefix_sum(necklace, n) = (n :: int) - 1)
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (cut: nat):
          cut < n
            AND FORALL (k: nat):
              k < n IMPLIES
                prefix_sum(rotated(necklace, n, cut), k + 1)
                  <= (k :: int)
END putnam_1995_a4

title: putnam_1995_a5
content:
import Mathlib

open Filter Topology Real

abbrev putnam_1995_a5_solution : Prop := sorry
-- True
/--
Let $x_{1},x_{2},\dots,x_{n}$ be differentiable (real-valued) functions of a single variable $f$ which satisfy \begin{align*} \frac{dx_{1}}{dt} &= a_{11}x_{1} + a_{12}x_{2} + \cdots + a_{1n}x_{n} \ \frac{dx_{2}}{dt} &= a_{21}x_{1} + a_{22}x_{2} + \cdots + a_{2n}x_{n} \ \vdots && \vdots \ \frac{dx_{n}}{dt} &= a_{n1}x_{1} + a_{n2}x_{2} + \cdots + a_{nn}x_{n} \end{align*} for some constants $a_{ij}>0$. Suppose that for all $i$, $x_{i}(t) \to 0$ as $t \to \infty$. Are the functions $x_{1},x_{2},\dots,x_{n}$ necessarily linearly dependent?
-/
theorem putnam_1995_a5 :
  putnam_1995_a5_solution ↔
  (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → (ℝ → ℝ)) (a : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ),
    (0 < n) →
    (∀ i, Differentiable ℝ (x i)) →
    (∀ i j, a i j > 0) →
    (∀ t i, (deriv (x i)) t = ∑ j : Fin n, (a i j) * ((x j) t)) →
    (∀ i, Tendsto (x i) atTop (𝓝 0)) →
    ¬(∀ b : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ t : ℝ, ∑ i : Fin n, (b i) * ((x i) t) = 0) →
      (∀ i, b i = 0))) :=
  sorry

title: putnam_1995_a5
content:
Require Import Nat Reals Coquelicot.Coquelicot. From mathcomp Require Import fintype.
Definition putnam_1995_a5_solution : Prop := True.
Theorem putnam_1995_a5
    (hdiffx := fun (n : nat) (x : nat -> (R -> R)) => forall (i : nat) (t : R), le i (Nat.sub n 1) -> ex_derive (x i) t)
    (ha := fun (n : nat) (a : nat -> nat -> R) => forall i j : nat, le i (Nat.sub n 1) /\ le j (Nat.sub n 1) -> a i j > 0)
    (hcomb := fun (n : nat) (x : nat -> (R -> R)) (a : nat -> nat -> R) => (forall t : R, forall i : nat, le i (Nat.sub n 1) -> Derive (x i) t = sum_n (fun j => a i j * ((x j) t)) (n - 1)))
    (hxlim := fun (n : nat) (x : nat -> (R -> R)) => (forall i : nat, le i (Nat.sub n 1) -> filterlim (x i) (Rbar_locally p_infty) (locally 0)))
    : putnam_1995_a5_solution <-> (forall (n : nat) (x : nat -> (R -> R)) (a : nat -> nat -> R), (gt n 0 /\ hdiffx n x /\ ha n a /\ hcomb n x a /\ hxlim n x) -> ~(forall b : nat -> R, (forall t : R, 0 = sum_n (fun i => (b i) * ((x i) t)) (n - 1)) -> (forall i : nat, le i (Nat.sub n 1) -> b i = 0))).
Proof. Admitted.

title: putnam_1995_a5
content:
theory putnam_1995_a5 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Derivative"
begin

(* uses (nat \<Rightarrow> (real \<Rightarrow> real)) instead of (Fin n \<Rightarrow> (real \<Rightarrow> real)) and (nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> real) instead of (Fin n \<Rightarrow> Fin n \<Rightarrow> real) *)
definition putnam_1995_a5_solution :: bool where "putnam_1995_a5_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* True *)
theorem putnam_1995_a5:
  fixes hdiffx :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> (real \<Rightarrow> real)) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and ha :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and hcomb :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> (real \<Rightarrow> real)) \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and hxlim :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> (real \<Rightarrow> real)) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  defines "hdiffx \<equiv> (\<lambda>(n::nat)(x::nat\<Rightarrow>(real\<Rightarrow>real)). (\<forall>i::nat\<in>{0..(n-1)}. (x i) differentiable_on UNIV))"
  and "ha \<equiv> (\<lambda>(n::nat)(a::nat\<Rightarrow>nat\<Rightarrow>real). (\<forall>i::nat\<in>{0..(n-1)}. \<forall>j::nat\<in>{0..(n-1)}. a i j > 0))"
  and "hcomb \<equiv> (\<lambda>(n::nat)(x::nat\<Rightarrow>(real\<Rightarrow>real))(a::nat\<Rightarrow>nat\<Rightarrow>real). (\<forall>t::real. \<forall>i::nat\<in>{0..(n-1)}. deriv (x i) t = (\<Sum>j::nat=0..(n-1). (a i j) * ((x j) t))))"
  and "hxlim \<equiv> (\<lambda>(n::nat)(x::nat\<Rightarrow>(real\<Rightarrow>real)). (\<forall>i::nat\<in>{0..(n-1)}. filterlim (x i) (nhds 0) at_top))"
  shows "putnam_1995_a5_solution \<longleftrightarrow> (\<forall>(n::nat)(x::nat\<Rightarrow>(real\<Rightarrow>real))(a::nat\<Rightarrow>nat\<Rightarrow>real). (n > 0 \<and> hdiffx n x \<and> ha n a \<and> hcomb n x a \<and> hxlim n x) \<longrightarrow> \<not>(\<forall>b::nat\<Rightarrow>real. (\<forall>t::real. (\<Sum>i::nat=0..(n-1). (b i) * ((x i) t)) = 0) \<longrightarrow> (\<forall>i::nat\<in>{0..(n-1)}. b i = 0)))"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_1995_a5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a5:
  linear dependence of finite families of differentiable real solutions of a
  positive-coefficient constant linear differential system that vanish at
  positive infinity. This file contains no proof.
*)

let analysis_output = open_out "/dev/null";;
let analysis_formatter = Format.formatter_of_out_channel analysis_output;;
let analysis_loaded =
  Toploop.use_file analysis_formatter "Library/analysis.ml";;
Format.pp_print_flush analysis_formatter ();;
close_out analysis_output;;
if not analysis_loaded then failwith "failed to load Library/analysis.ml";;

let statement =
  `let deriv =
     \(f:real->real) (t:real). @d:real. (f diffl d) t in
   let tends_at_posinfinity =
     \(f:real->real) (l:real).
       !e:real.
         &0 < e
         ==> ?B:real.
               !t:real. B <= t ==> abs (f t - l) < e in
   let putnam_1995_a5_solution = T in
   putnam_1995_a5_solution <=>
   (!n:num. !x:num->real->real. !a:num->num->real.
      0 < n /\
      (!i:num. i < n ==> !t:real. (x i) differentiable t) /\
      (!i j:num. i < n /\ j < n ==> &0 < a i j) /\
      (!t:real. !i:num.
         i < n
         ==> deriv (x i) t =
             sum (0..n - 1) (\j:num. a i j * x j t)) /\
      (!i:num. i < n ==> tends_at_posinfinity (x i) (&0))
      ==>
      ~(!b:num->real.
          (!t:real.
             sum (0..n - 1) (\i:num. b i * x i t) = &0)
          ==>
          (!i:num. i < n ==> b i = &0)))`;;

title: putnam_1995_a5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a5:
;; differentiable real functions satisfying a positive-coefficient linear
;; differential system and tending to zero at positive infinity are linearly
;; dependent. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The scalar parameters describe a Dedekind-complete ordered field, hence a
;; presentation of the real field. The derivative and limit predicates below
;; are their epsilon-delta definitions. Tame APPLY$ function objects represent
;; the arbitrary trajectories, coefficient matrices, and dependence vectors.

(defun putnam-1995-a5-member-p (carrier value)
  (if (apply$ carrier (list value)) t nil))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-unary (operation value)
  (apply$ operation (list value)))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-binary (operation left right)
  (apply$ operation (list left right)))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-field-laws-p
    (carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier x)
      (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier y)
      (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier z))
     (let* ((xy-add
             (putnam-1995-a5-binary add x y))
            (yz-add
             (putnam-1995-a5-binary add y z))
            (xy-multiply
             (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply x y))
            (yz-multiply
             (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply y z))
            (negative-x
             (putnam-1995-a5-unary negate x))
            (inverse-x
             (putnam-1995-a5-unary inverse x)))
       (and
        (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier xy-add)
        (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier xy-multiply)
        (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier negative-x)
        (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier inverse-x)
        (equal
         (putnam-1995-a5-binary add xy-add z)
         (putnam-1995-a5-binary add x yz-add))
        (equal xy-add
               (putnam-1995-a5-binary add y x))
        (equal
         (putnam-1995-a5-binary add x zero)
         x)
        (equal
         (putnam-1995-a5-binary add x negative-x)
         zero)
        (equal
         (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply xy-multiply z)
         (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply x yz-multiply))
        (equal
         xy-multiply
         (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply y x))
        (equal
         (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply x one)
         x)
        (implies
         (equal x zero)
         (equal inverse-x zero))
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (equal
          (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply x inverse-x)
          one))
        (equal
         (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply x yz-add)
         (putnam-1995-a5-binary
          add
          (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply x y)
          (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply x z))))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-order-laws-p
    (carrier zero add multiply less)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier x)
      (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier y)
      (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (not (putnam-1995-a5-binary less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (putnam-1995-a5-binary less x y)
       (putnam-1995-a5-binary less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (putnam-1995-a5-binary less x y)
        (putnam-1995-a5-binary less y z))
       (putnam-1995-a5-binary less x z))
      (implies
       (putnam-1995-a5-binary less x y)
       (putnam-1995-a5-binary
        less
        (putnam-1995-a5-binary add x z)
        (putnam-1995-a5-binary add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (putnam-1995-a5-binary less zero x)
        (putnam-1995-a5-binary less zero y))
       (putnam-1995-a5-binary
        less
        zero
        (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply x y)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-valid-set-p (carrier set)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (apply$ set (list x))
     (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier x))))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-set-nonempty-p (carrier set)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier x)
     (apply$ set (list x)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-upper-bound-p
    (carrier less set bound)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier x)
      (apply$ set (list x)))
     (not
      (putnam-1995-a5-binary less bound x)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-bounded-above-p
    (carrier less set)
  (exists (bound)
    (and
     (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier bound)
     (putnam-1995-a5-upper-bound-p
      carrier less set bound))))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-least-upper-bound-p
    (carrier less set supremum)
  (forall (bound)
    (and
     (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier supremum)
     (putnam-1995-a5-upper-bound-p
      carrier less set supremum)
     (implies
      (and
       (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier bound)
       (putnam-1995-a5-upper-bound-p
        carrier less set bound))
      (not
       (putnam-1995-a5-binary
        less bound supremum))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-has-supremum-p
    (carrier less set)
  (exists (supremum)
    (putnam-1995-a5-least-upper-bound-p
     carrier less set supremum)))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-dedekind-complete-p
    (carrier less)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (tamep-functionp set)
      (putnam-1995-a5-valid-set-p carrier set)
      (putnam-1995-a5-set-nonempty-p carrier set)
      (putnam-1995-a5-bounded-above-p
       carrier less set))
     (putnam-1995-a5-has-supremum-p
      carrier less set))))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-real-field-p
    (carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse less)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp add)
   (tamep-functionp multiply)
   (tamep-functionp negate)
   (tamep-functionp inverse)
   (tamep-functionp less)
   (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier zero)
   (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (putnam-1995-a5-field-laws-p
    carrier zero one add multiply negate inverse)
   (putnam-1995-a5-order-laws-p
    carrier zero add multiply less)
   (putnam-1995-a5-binary less zero one)
   (putnam-1995-a5-dedekind-complete-p
    carrier less)))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-r-add (add left right)
  (putnam-1995-a5-binary add left right))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-r-multiply (multiply left right)
  (putnam-1995-a5-binary multiply left right))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-r-negate (negate value)
  (putnam-1995-a5-unary negate value))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-r-subtract (add negate left right)
  (putnam-1995-a5-r-add
   add left (putnam-1995-a5-r-negate negate right)))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-r-less-p (less left right)
  (if (putnam-1995-a5-binary less left right) t nil))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-r-less-equal-p (less left right)
  (not (putnam-1995-a5-r-less-p less right left)))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-r-absolute-value
    (zero negate less value)
  (if (putnam-1995-a5-r-less-p less value zero)
      (putnam-1995-a5-r-negate negate value)
    value))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-positive-real-p
    (carrier zero less value)
  (and
   (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier value)
   (putnam-1995-a5-r-less-p less zero value)))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-index-p (n index)
  (and
   (natp index)
   (< index n)))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-x-value (trajectory index time)
  (apply$ trajectory (list index time)))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-a-value
    (coefficients row column)
  (apply$ coefficients (list row column)))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-b-value
    (dependence-vector index)
  (apply$ dependence-vector (list index)))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-trajectory-typed-p
    (carrier n trajectory)
  (forall (index time)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1995-a5-index-p n index)
      (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier time))
     (putnam-1995-a5-member-p
      carrier
      (putnam-1995-a5-x-value
       trajectory index time)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-coefficients-typed-p
    (carrier n coefficients)
  (forall (row column)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1995-a5-index-p n row)
      (putnam-1995-a5-index-p n column))
     (putnam-1995-a5-member-p
      carrier
      (putnam-1995-a5-a-value
       coefficients row column)))))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-positive-coefficients-p
    (zero less n coefficients)
  (forall (row column)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1995-a5-index-p n row)
      (putnam-1995-a5-index-p n column))
     (putnam-1995-a5-r-less-p
      less
      zero
      (putnam-1995-a5-a-value
       coefficients row column)))))

(defun putnam-1995-a5-system-sum
    (zero add multiply coefficients trajectory
     row time column count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      zero
    (putnam-1995-a5-r-add
     add
     (putnam-1995-a5-r-multiply
      multiply
      (putnam-1995-a5-a-value
       coefficients row column)
      (putnam-1995-a5-x-value
       trajectory column time))
     (putnam-1995-a5-system-sum
      zero add multiply coefficients trajectory
      row time (+ 1 column) (- count 1)))))

;; The error form
;; |x(y)-x(t)-d*(y-t)| <= epsilon*|y-t|
;; is equivalent to the usual one-variable derivative definition.

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-derivative-neighborhood-p
    (carrier zero add multiply negate less
     trajectory index point derivative epsilon radius)
  (forall (nearby)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-1995-a5-member-p carrier nearby)
      (putnam-1995-a5-r-less-p
       less
       (putnam-1995-a5-r-absolute-value
        zero
        negate
        less
        (putnam-1995-a5-r-subtract
         add negate nearby point))
       radius))
     (putnam-1995-a5-r-less-equal-p
      less
      (putnam-1995-a5-r-absolute-value
       zero
       negate
       less
       (putnam-1995-a5-r-subtract
        add
        negate
        (putnam-1995-a5-r-subtract
         add
         negate
         (putnam-1995-a5-x-value
          trajectory index nearby)
         (putnam-1995-a5-x-value
          trajectory index point))
        (putnam-1995-a5-r-multiply
         multiply
         derivative
         (putnam-1995-a5-r-subtract
          add negate nearby point))))
      (putnam-1995-a5-r-multiply
       multiply
       epsilon
       (putnam-1995-a5-r-absolute-value
        zero
        negate
        less
        (putnam-1995-a5-r-subtract
         add negate nearby point)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-derivative-radius-exists-p
    (carrier zero add multiply negate less
     trajectory index point derivative epsilon)
  (exists (radius)
    (and
     (putnam-1995-a5-positive-real-p
      carrier zero less radius)
     (putnam-1995-a5-derivative-neighborhood-p
      carrier zero add multiply negate less
      trajectory index point derivative epsilon radius))))

(defun-sk putnam-1995-a5-has-derivative-at-p
    (carrier zero add multiply negate less

title: putnam_1995_a5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_1995_a5): linear dependence of real solutions
-- of positive-coefficient linear ODE systems that converge to zero. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record Truth : Set where
  constructor truth

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

data _<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<sucN : {n : Nat} -> zero <N suc n
  suc<sucN  : {m n : Nat} -> m <N n -> suc m <N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals numerator denominator =
  multiply reals numerator (inverse reals denominator)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
differenceQuotient reals function point x =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals (function x) (function point))
    (subtract reals x point)

DerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeAt {R} reals function point derivative =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        x != point ->
        CloseTo reals derivative epsilon
          (differenceQuotient reals function point x)))

TendsToZeroAtPositiveInfinity :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
TendsToZeroAtPositiveInfinity {R} reals function =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ cutoff ->
      (t : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals cutoff t ->
      CloseTo reals
        (zeroR reals)
        epsilon
        (function t))

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} terms =
  add reals
    (terms fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> terms (fsuc i)))

PositiveCoefficients :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Fin n -> R) ->
  Set
PositiveCoefficients {R} reals {n} coefficients =
  (i j : Fin n) ->
  StrictLess reals
    (zeroR reals)
    (coefficients i j)

SatisfiesDifferentialSystem :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R -> R) ->
  (Fin n -> Fin n -> R) ->
  Set
SatisfiesDifferentialSystem {R} reals {n} functions coefficients =
  (i : Fin n) ->
  (t : R) ->
  DerivativeAt reals
    (functions i)
    t
    (sumFin reals
      (\ j ->
        multiply reals
          (coefficients i j)
          (functions j t)))

AllFunctionsTendToZero :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R -> R) ->
  Set
AllFunctionsTendToZero reals {n} functions =
  (i : Fin n) ->
  TendsToZeroAtPositiveInfinity reals (functions i)

LinearlyIndependent :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R -> R) ->
  Set
LinearlyIndependent {R} reals {n} functions =
  (coefficients : Fin n -> R) ->
  ((t : R) ->
    sumFin reals
      (\ i ->
        multiply reals
          (coefficients i)
          (functions i t))
    == zeroR reals) ->
  (i : Fin n) ->
  coefficients i == zeroR reals

EveryAdmissibleSystemIsDependent :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Set
EveryAdmissibleSystemIsDependent {R} reals =
  (n : Nat) ->
  (functions : Fin n -> R -> R) ->
  (coefficients : Fin n -> Fin n -> R) ->
  zero <N n ->
  PositiveCoefficients reals coefficients ->
  SatisfiesDifferentialSystem reals functions coefficients ->
  AllFunctionsTendToZero reals functions ->
  Not (LinearlyIndependent reals functions)

putnam-1995-a5-solution : Set
putnam-1995-a5-solution =
  Truth

putnam-1995-a5 : Set1
putnam-1995-a5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Iff
    putnam-1995-a5-solution
    (EveryAdmissibleSystemIsDependent reals)

title: putnam_1995_a5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a5:
  linear dependence of a finite system of differentiable real functions
  satisfying a constant-coefficient linear ODE with strictly positive
  coefficients and tending componentwise to zero. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;
open real_topologyTheory limTheory;

val putnam_1995_a5 =
  ``let putnam_1995_a5_solution = T
    in
      putnam_1995_a5_solution <=>
      !n : num.
      !x : num -> real -> real.
      !a : num -> num -> real.
        0 < n /\
        (!i : num.
           i < n
           ==>
           !t : real. x i differentiable t) /\
        (!i j : num.
           i < n /\ j < n
           ==>
           0 < a i j) /\
        (!t : real.
         !i : num.
           i < n
           ==>
           diffn 1 (x i) t =
             SIGMA (\j : num. a i j * x j t) (count n)) /\
        (!i : num.
           i < n
           ==>
           (x i --> 0) at_posinfinity)
        ==>
        ~(!b : num -> real.
            (!t : real.
               SIGMA (\i : num. b i * x i t) (count n) = 0)
            ==>
            (!i : num. i < n ==> b i = 0))``;

title: putnam_1995_a5
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1995_a5: every positive-dimensional family of differentiable real
  functions satisfying a constant linear ODE system with strictly positive
  coefficients and tending to zero at positive infinity is linearly
  dependent. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The ordinal interval 0 ..^ n is the n-element carrier representing Fin n.
  Thus x ranges over arbitrary n-indexed families of total real functions,
  and a ranges over arbitrary n by n real coefficient families. Containment
  of RR in each derivative domain expresses differentiability at every real
  point, and the displayed finite sum is the source ODE system.

  The epsilon-threshold clause is convergence of every x_i(t) to zero as the
  real variable t tends to positive infinity. The conclusion is exactly the
  negation of linear independence: it negates the assertion that every real
  coefficient family whose pointwise linear combination is zero has all
  coefficients zero. The source solution is True, so its biconditional with
  this universal property is equivalent to the property asserted below. The
  final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d M a b e i j n t x $.

  putnambench-putnam-1995-a5 $a |- A. n e. NN
    A. x e. ( ( RR ^m RR ) ^m ( 0 ..^ n ) )
    A. a e.
      (
        ( RR ^m ( 0 ..^ n ) )
        ^m
        ( 0 ..^ n )
      )
      (
        (
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
            RR C_ dom ( RR _D ( x ` i ) )
          /\
          (
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
              A. j e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                0 < ( ( a ` i ) ` j )
            /\
            (
              A. t e. RR
                A. i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                  (
                    ( ( RR _D ( x ` i ) ) ` t )
                    =
                    (
                      sum_ j e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                        (
                          ( ( a ` i ) ` j )
                          x.
                          ( ( x ` j ) ` t )
                        )
                    )
                  )
              /\
              A. i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                A. e e. RR
                  (
                    0 < e
                    ->
                    E. M e. RR
                      A. t e. RR
                        (
                          M <_ t
                          ->
                          ( abs ` ( ( x ` i ) ` t ) ) < e
                        )
                  )
            )
          )
        )
        ->
        -.
        A. b e. ( RR ^m ( 0 ..^ n ) )
          (
            A. t e. RR
              (
                sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                  (
                    ( b ` i )
                    x.
                    ( ( x ` i ) ` t )
                  )
              )
              =
              0
            ->
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ n ) ( b ` i ) = 0
          )
      )
  $.
$}

content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1995_a5:
:: every finite positive-coefficient real linear differential system whose
:: differentiable components tend to zero has linearly dependent component
:: functions. This file contains no proof.

environ

  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    PARTFUN1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, COMPLEX1, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1,

    SEQ_1, SEQ_2, SEQ_4, RCOMP_1, FDIFF_1, LIMFUNC1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, RVSUM_1, ZFMISC_1, BINOP_1, BINOP_2, FUNCOP_1,
    FINSEQOP, SETWISEO, SETWOP_2, FINSOP_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ZFMISC_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, REAL_1, COMPLEX1, XXREAL_0, NAT_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1,
    SEQ_1, SEQ_2, SEQ_4, RCOMP_1, FDIFF_1, LIMFUNC1, BINOP_1,
    BINOP_2, SETWISEO, FUNCOP_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_4,
    FINSOP_1, FINSEQOP, SETWOP_2, RVSUM_1;
  constructors FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1, REAL_1,
    COMPLEX1, NAT_1, SEQ_2, SEQ_4, RCOMP_1, PARTFUN2, RFUNCT_2,
    LIMFUNC1, FDIFF_1, VALUED_1, XXREAL_2, BINOP_1, SETWISEO,
    BINOP_2, FINSEQOP, FINSEQ_4, FINSOP_1, SETWOP_2, FINSEQ_2,
    RVSUM_1, ZFMISC_1, COMSEQ_2;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0, VALUED_1,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, NAT_1, RCOMP_1, FDIFF_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_4, RVSUM_1, BINOP_2, FUNCOP_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat,
      x being Function of Seg n,Funcs(REAL,REAL),
      a being Function of [:Seg n,Seg n:],REAL st
    0 < n &
    (for i being Nat st i in Seg n holds
      ex xi being Function of REAL,REAL st
        xi = x.i & xi is_differentiable_on [#]REAL) &
    (for i,j being Nat st i in Seg n & j in Seg n holds
      0 < a.(i,j)) &
    (for t being Real, i being Nat st i in Seg n holds
      ex xi being Function of REAL,REAL,
         terms,partials being FinSequence of REAL st
        xi = x.i &
        len terms = n &
        len partials = n &
        (for j being Nat st j in Seg n holds
          ex xj being Function of REAL,REAL st
            xj = x.j & terms.j = a.(i,j) * xj.t) &
        partials.1 = terms.1 &
        (for j being Nat st 1 < j & j <= n holds
          partials.j = partials.(j-'1) + terms.j) &
        diff(xi,t) = partials.n) &
    (for i being Nat st i in Seg n holds
      ex xi being Function of REAL,REAL st
        xi = x.i &
        xi is convergent_in+infty &
        lim_in+infty xi = 0)
  holds
    not (for b being FinSequence of REAL st len b = n holds
      ((for t being Real holds
          ex terms,partials being FinSequence of REAL st
            len terms = n &
            len partials = n &
            (for i being Nat st i in Seg n holds
              ex xi being Function of REAL,REAL st
                xi = x.i & terms.i = b.i * xi.t) &
            partials.1 = terms.1 &
            (for i being Nat st 1 < i & i <= n holds
              partials.i = partials.(i-'1) + terms.i) &
            partials.n = 0)
        implies
          for i being Nat st i in Seg n holds b.i = 0))
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1995_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a5:
% finite systems of differentiable real functions satisfying a constant
% linear ODE with strictly positive coefficients and tending to zero at
% positive infinity are linearly dependent. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1995_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_function_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real_function]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  real_matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> real]

  finite_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      finite_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_derivative_at(
      f: real_function,
      derivative, point: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (h: real):
          (h /= 0 AND abs(h) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                f(point + h) - f(point)
                  - derivative * h)
                < epsilon_value * abs(h)

  differentiable(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (point: real):
      EXISTS (derivative: real):
        has_derivative_at(f, derivative, point)

  derivative_value(
      f: real_function,
      point: real): real =
    IF EXISTS (derivative: real):
        has_derivative_at(f, derivative, point)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (derivative: real):
          has_derivative_at(f, derivative, point))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  tends_to_zero_at_positive_infinity(
      f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (threshold: real):
        FORALL (point: real):
          threshold <= point IMPLIES
            abs(f(point)) < epsilon_value

  positive_coefficients(
      n: nat,
      coefficients: real_matrix): bool =
    FORALL (row, column: nat):
      (row < n AND column < n)
        IMPLIES coefficients(row, column) > 0

  satisfies_system(
      n: nat,
      functions: real_function_sequence,
      coefficients: real_matrix): bool =
    FORALL (point: real), (row: nat):
      row < n IMPLIES
        derivative_value(functions(row), point)
          =
            finite_sum(
              LAMBDA (column: nat):
                coefficients(row, column)
                  * functions(column)(point),
              n)

  linearly_independent(
      n: nat,
      functions: real_function_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (weights: real_sequence):
      (FORALL (point: real):
        finite_sum(
          LAMBDA (index: nat):
            weights(index) * functions(index)(point),
          n)
          = 0)
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (index: nat):
          index < n IMPLIES weights(index) = 0

  putnam_1995_a5_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_1995_a5: bool =
    putnam_1995_a5_solution IFF
      FORALL
          (n: nat),
          (functions: real_function_sequence),
          (coefficients: real_matrix):
        (n > 0
          AND (FORALL (index: nat):
            index < n IMPLIES differentiable(functions(index)))
          AND positive_coefficients(n, coefficients)
          AND satisfies_system(n, functions, coefficients)
          AND (FORALL (index: nat):
            index < n IMPLIES
              tends_to_zero_at_positive_infinity(functions(index))))
        IMPLIES
          NOT linearly_independent(n, functions)
END putnam_1995_a5

title: putnam_1995_a6
content:
import Mathlib

open Filter Topology Real

/--
Suppose that each of $n$ people writes down the numbers $1,2,3$ in random order in one column of a $3 \times n$ matrix, with all orders equally likely and with the orders for different columns independent of each other. Let the row sums $a,b,c$ of the resulting matrix be rearranged (if necessary) so that $a \leq b \leq c$. Show that for some $n \geq 1995$, it is at least four times as likely that both $b=a+1$ and $c=a+2$ as that $a=b=c$.
-/
theorem putnam_1995_a6
(SM : (n : ℕ) → Set (Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin n) ℤ))
(Srowsums : (n : ℕ) → Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin n) ℤ → Set ℤ)
(sumsprog : (Set ℤ) → Prop)
(hSM : ∀ n, SM n = {M : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin n) ℤ | ∀ j : Fin n, {M i j | i : Fin 3} = {1, 2, 3}})
(hSrowsums : ∀ n M, Srowsums n M = {∑ j : Fin n, M i j | i : Fin 3})
(hsumsprog : ∀ sums, sumsprog sums ↔ sums.encard = 3 ∧ (∃ a b c : ℤ, {a, b, c} = sums ∧ b = a + 1 ∧ c = a + 2))
: ∃ n ≥ 1995, {M : (SM n) | sumsprog (Srowsums n M)}.encard ≥ 4 * {M : (SM n) | (Srowsums n M).encard = 1}.encard :=
sorry

title: putnam_1995_a6
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1995_a6:
   counting 3 by n integer matrices whose columns are permutations of
   1, 2, 3, comparing consecutive row sums with equal row sums; this file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith.
From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Definition putnam_1995_a6_entry {n : nat}
    (M : {ffun 'I_n -> 'I_6}) (i : 'I_3) (j : 'I_n) : Z :=
  let row := nat_of_ord i in
  match nat_of_ord (M j) with
  | O =>
      Z.of_nat (S row)
  | S O =>
      match row with
      | O => 1%Z
      | S O => 3%Z
      | _ => 2%Z
      end
  | S (S O) =>
      match row with
      | O => 2%Z
      | S O => 1%Z
      | _ => 3%Z
      end
  | S (S (S O)) =>
      match row with
      | O => 2%Z
      | S O => 3%Z
      | _ => 1%Z
      end
  | S (S (S (S O))) =>
      match row with
      | O => 3%Z
      | S O => 1%Z
      | _ => 2%Z
      end
  | _ =>
      match row with
      | O => 3%Z
      | S O => 2%Z
      | _ => 1%Z
      end
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_1995_a6_sum_columns {n : nat}
    (M : {ffun 'I_n -> 'I_6}) (i : 'I_3)
    (columns : seq 'I_n) : Z :=
  match columns with
  | [::] => 0%Z
  | j :: remaining =>
      (putnam_1995_a6_entry M i j +
       putnam_1995_a6_sum_columns M i remaining)%Z
  end.

Definition putnam_1995_a6_row_sum {n : nat}
    (M : {ffun 'I_n -> 'I_6}) (i : 'I_3) : Z :=
  putnam_1995_a6_sum_columns M i (enum 'I_n).

Definition putnam_1995_a6_ordered_consecutive (a b c : Z) : bool :=
  Z.eqb b (a + 1)%Z && Z.eqb c (a + 2)%Z.

Definition putnam_1995_a6_consecutive {n : nat}
    (M : {ffun 'I_n -> 'I_6}) : bool :=
  let a := putnam_1995_a6_row_sum M (inord 0) in
  let b := putnam_1995_a6_row_sum M (inord 1) in
  let c := putnam_1995_a6_row_sum M (inord 2) in
  putnam_1995_a6_ordered_consecutive a b c ||
  putnam_1995_a6_ordered_consecutive a c b ||
  putnam_1995_a6_ordered_consecutive b a c ||
  putnam_1995_a6_ordered_consecutive b c a ||
  putnam_1995_a6_ordered_consecutive c a b ||
  putnam_1995_a6_ordered_consecutive c b a.

Definition putnam_1995_a6_equal {n : nat}
    (M : {ffun 'I_n -> 'I_6}) : bool :=
  [forall i : 'I_3,
    Z.eqb
      (putnam_1995_a6_row_sum M i)
      (putnam_1995_a6_row_sum M (inord 0))].

Theorem putnam_1995_a6 :
  exists n : nat,
    (1995 <= n)%nat /\
    (4 *
       #|[pred M : {ffun 'I_n -> 'I_6} |
           putnam_1995_a6_equal M]| <=
     #|[pred M : {ffun 'I_n -> 'I_6} |
         putnam_1995_a6_consecutive M]|)%nat.
Admitted.

title: putnam_1995_a6
