-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_1996_a1): the least area of a positive rectangle
-- that can pack every positive unit-sum-of-squares pair of side lengths is
-- (1 + sqrt 2) / 2. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record StandardReal (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) -> Either (lessOrEqual x y) (lessOrEqual y x)
    add-monotone :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-or-equal-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n
    fromNat-nonnegative :
      (n : Nat) -> lessOrEqual zeroR (fromNat n)

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      squareRoot x == y

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          Both
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
            ((upper : R) ->
              ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
              lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open StandardReal

maximum :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
maximum reals x y with order-total reals x y
... | left x-le-y =
  y
... | right y-le-x =
  x

minimum :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
minimum reals x y with order-total reals x y
... | left x-le-y =
  x
... | right y-le-x =
  y

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  Both
    (lessOrEqual reals x y)
    (x != y)

solution :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  R
solution reals =
  divide reals
    (add reals
      (oneR reals)
      (squareRoot reals (fromNat reals 2)))
    (fromNat reals 2)

Packable :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
Packable reals n1 n2 a1 a2 =
  Both
    (lessOrEqual reals
      (add reals n1 n2)
      (maximum reals a1 a2))
    (lessOrEqual reals
      (maximum reals n1 n2)
      (minimum reals a1 a2))

AProperty :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  R ->
  Set
AProperty {R} reals area =
  (n1 n2 : R) ->
  Both
    (StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) n1)
    (Both
      (StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) n2)
      (add reals
        (square reals n1)
        (square reals n2)
        == oneR reals)) ->
  Exists R
    (\ a1 ->
      Exists R
        (\ a2 ->
          Both
            (StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) a1)
            (Both
              (StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) a2)
              (Both
                (multiply reals a1 a2 == area)
                (Packable reals n1 n2 a1 a2)))))

putnam-1996-a1 : Set1
putnam-1996-a1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : StandardReal R) ->
  Both
    (AProperty reals (solution reals))
    ((area : R) ->
      AProperty reals area ->
      lessOrEqual reals (solution reals) area)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a1:
  the least area admitting positive rectangle sides that pack every positive
  real pair on the unit circle is (1 + sqrt 2) / 2. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open realTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_1996_a1 =
  ``let putnam_1996_a1_solution = (1 + sqrt 2) / 2
    in
    let packable =
      \n1 n2 a1 a2 : real.
        n1 + n2 <= max a1 a2 /\ max n1 n2 <= min a1 a2
    in
    let Aprop =
      \A : real.
        !n1 n2 : real.
          0 < n1 /\ 0 < n2 /\ n1 pow 2 + n2 pow 2 = 1
          ==>
          ?a1 a2 : real.
            0 < a1 /\ 0 < a2 /\ a1 * a2 = A /\
            packable n1 n2 a1 a2
    in
      Aprop putnam_1996_a1_solution /\
      (!A : real.
         Aprop A
         ==>
         putnam_1996_a1_solution <= A)``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1996_a1: the least area of a positive rectangle satisfying the
  stated max/min packing inequalities for every positive real pair whose
  squared lengths sum to one is (1 + sqrt 2) / 2. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P96A1Property A is definitionally the source predicate Aprop A. The four
  side variables remain arbitrary reals, the rectangle sides remain internal
  existential witnesses, and the if-expressions are the real maximum and
  minimum functions. The final conjunction states both feasibility at the
  displayed area and its minimality among every real A satisfying the same
  property.

  All declarations below are unproved $a statement encodings; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P96A1Property $.

p96a1-property-syntax $a wff ( P96A1Property A ) $.

${
  $d A a b x y $.

  p96a1-property-definition $a |- (
    ( P96A1Property A )
    <->
    A. x e. RR
      A. y e. RR
        (
          (
            (
              0 < x
              /\
              0 < y
            )
            /\
            ( ( x ^ 2 ) + ( y ^ 2 ) ) = 1
          )
          ->
          E. a e. RR
            E. b e. RR
              (
                (
                  (
                    0 < a
                    /\
                    0 < b
                  )
                  /\
                  ( a x. b ) = A
                )
                /\
                (
                  ( x + y )
                  <_
                  if ( a <_ b , b , a )
                  /\
                  if ( x <_ y , y , x )
                  <_
                  if ( a <_ b , a , b )
                )
              )
        )
  ) $.
$}

putnambench-putnam-1996-a1 $a |- (
  (
    P96A1Property
      ( ( 1 + ( sqrt ` 2 ) ) / 2 )
  )
  /\
  A. A e. RR
    (
      ( P96A1Property A )
      ->
      ( ( 1 + ( sqrt ` 2 ) ) / 2 ) <_ A
    )
) $.

:: the least area of positive rectangle dimensions satisfying the stated
:: min-max packing inequalities for every positive normalized pair is
:: (1 + sqrt(2))/2. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    NUMBERS, XREAL_0, XCMPLX_0, COMPLEX1, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1,
    ARYTM_3, SQUARE_1, REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1, VALUED_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, REAL_1, INT_1,
    COMPLEX1, SQUARE_1, XXREAL_0;
  constructors FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, REAL_1, SQUARE_1, COMPLEX1,
    INT_1, XXREAL_0;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0, VALUED_1,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, SQUARE_1, ORDINAL1, NAT_1, INT_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  (for n1,n2 being Real st
    n1 > 0 & n2 > 0 & n1^2 + n2^2 = 1
  holds
    ex a1,a2 being Real st
      a1 > 0 & a2 > 0 &
      a1 * a2 = (1 + sqrt 2) / 2 &
      n1 + n2 <= max(a1,a2) &
      max(n1,n2) <= min(a1,a2)) &
  (for A being Real st
    (for n1,n2 being Real st
      n1 > 0 & n2 > 0 & n1^2 + n2^2 = 1
    holds
      ex a1,a2 being Real st
        a1 > 0 & a2 > 0 &
        a1 * a2 = A &
        n1 + n2 <= max(a1,a2) &
        max(n1,n2) <= min(a1,a2))
  holds
    A >= (1 + sqrt 2) / 2)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1996_a1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a1:
% the least rectangle area that can pack every pair of positive square side
% lengths whose squared lengths sum to one. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1996_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_max(left, right: real): real =
    IF left >= right THEN left ELSE right ENDIF

  real_min(left, right: real): real =
    IF left <= right THEN left ELSE right ENDIF

  square_root_value(root, radicand: real): bool =
    0 <= root AND root ^ 2 = radicand

  packable(n1, n2, a1, a2: real): bool =
    n1 + n2 <= real_max(a1, a2)
      AND real_max(n1, n2) <= real_min(a1, a2)

  admissible_area(area: real): bool =
    FORALL (n1, n2: real):
      (n1 > 0 AND n2 > 0 AND n1 ^ 2 + n2 ^ 2 = 1)
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (a1, a2: real):
          a1 > 0
            AND a2 > 0
            AND a1 * a2 = area
            AND packable(n1, n2, a1, a2)

  solution_value(sqrt_two: real): real =
    (1 + sqrt_two) / 2

  putnam_1996_a1: bool =
    EXISTS (sqrt_two: real):
      square_root_value(sqrt_two, 2)
        AND admissible_area(solution_value(sqrt_two))
        AND (FORALL (area: real):
          admissible_area(area)
            IMPLIES area >= solution_value(sqrt_two))
END putnam_1996_a1

import Mathlib

open Metric

abbrev putnam_1996_a2_solution : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) → (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) := sorry
-- (fun O1 O2 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) => {p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) | dist p (midpoint ℝ O1 O2) ≥ 1 ∧ dist p (midpoint ℝ O1 O2) ≤ 2})
/--
Let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be circles whose centers are $10$ units apart, and whose radii are $1$ and $3$. Find, with proof, the locus of all points $M$ for which there exist points $X$ on $C_1$ and $Y$ on $C_2$ such that $M$ is the midpoint of the line segment $XY$.
-/
theorem putnam_1996_a2
(O1 O2 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
(C1 C2 : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))
(hC1 : C1 = sphere O1 1)
(hC2 : C2 = sphere O2 3)
(hO1O2 : dist O1 O2 = 10)
: {M : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) | ∃ X Y, X ∈ C1 ∧ Y ∈ C2 ∧ M = midpoint ℝ X Y} = putnam_1996_a2_solution O1 O2 :=
sorry

title: putnam_1996_a2
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a2:
   the locus of midpoints of pairs of points on two circles of radii one and
   three is a closed annulus about the midpoint of their centers. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_1996_a2_point : Type :=
  (R * R)%type.

Definition putnam_1996_a2_point_set : Type :=
  putnam_1996_a2_point -> Prop.

Definition putnam_1996_a2_distance
    (p q : putnam_1996_a2_point) : R :=
  sqrt ((fst p - fst q) ^ 2 + (snd p - snd q) ^ 2).

Definition putnam_1996_a2_midpoint
    (p q : putnam_1996_a2_point) : putnam_1996_a2_point :=
  ((fst p + fst q) / 2, (snd p + snd q) / 2).

Definition putnam_1996_a2_circle
    (center : putnam_1996_a2_point) (radius : R) :
    putnam_1996_a2_point_set :=
  fun p : putnam_1996_a2_point =>
    putnam_1996_a2_distance p center = radius.

Definition putnam_1996_a2_locus
    (C1 C2 : putnam_1996_a2_point_set) :
    putnam_1996_a2_point_set :=
  fun M : putnam_1996_a2_point =>
    exists X Y : putnam_1996_a2_point,
      C1 X /\
      C2 Y /\
      M = putnam_1996_a2_midpoint X Y.

Definition putnam_1996_a2_solution
    (O1 O2 : putnam_1996_a2_point) :
    putnam_1996_a2_point_set :=
  fun p : putnam_1996_a2_point =>
    1 <=
      putnam_1996_a2_distance p
        (putnam_1996_a2_midpoint O1 O2) /\
    putnam_1996_a2_distance p
      (putnam_1996_a2_midpoint O1 O2) <= 2.

Theorem putnam_1996_a2
    (O1 O2 : putnam_1996_a2_point)
    (C1 C2 : putnam_1996_a2_point_set)
    (hC1 : C1 = putnam_1996_a2_circle O1 1)
    (hC2 : C2 = putnam_1996_a2_circle O2 3)
    (hO1O2 : putnam_1996_a2_distance O1 O2 = 10) :
  forall M : putnam_1996_a2_point,
    putnam_1996_a2_locus C1 C2 M <->
    putnam_1996_a2_solution O1 O2 M.
Admitted.

"HOL-Analysis.Finite_Cartesian_Product"

definition putnam_1996_a2_solution :: "(real^2) \<Rightarrow> (real^2) \<Rightarrow> ((real^2) set)" where "putnam_1996_a2_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* \<lambda> O1 O2 :: real^2. {p :: real^2. dist p (midpoint O1 O2) \<in> {1..2}} *)
theorem putnam_1996_a2:
  fixes O1 O2 :: "real^2"
    and C1 C2 :: "(real^2) set"
  defines "C1 \<equiv> {p :: real^2. dist p O1 = 1}"
    and "C2 \<equiv> {p :: real^2. dist p O2 = 3}"

  shows "{M :: real^2. \<exists> X \<in> C1. \<exists> Y \<in> C2. M = midpoint X Y} = putnam_1996_a2_solution O1 O2"

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a2:
  the locus of midpoints of segments joining points on two circles with
  radii 1 and 3 whose centers are 10 units apart. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let edist =
     \(x:real#real) (y:real#real).
       sqrt ((FST x - FST y) pow 2 + (SND x - SND y) pow 2) in
   let midpoint =
     \(x:real#real) (y:real#real).
       ((FST x + FST y) / &2, (SND x + SND y) / &2) in
   !O1 O2:real#real.
     edist O1 O2 = &10
     ==>
     !M:real#real.
       ((?X Y:real#real.
           edist X O1 = &1 /\
           edist Y O2 = &3 /\
           M = midpoint X Y) <=>
        &1 <= edist M (midpoint O1 O2) /\
        edist M (midpoint O1 O2) <= &2)`;;

title: putnam_1996_a2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a2:
;; the midpoint locus for points chosen on two circles of radii 1 and 3 is
;; the closed annulus of radii 1 and 2 about the midpoint of their centers.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Put d=O2-O1, w=2*M-O1-O2, u=X-O1, and v=Y-O2. Then the source statement is
;;
;;   |d|^2=100 implies
;;   ((exists u,v, |u|^2=1 and |v|^2=9 and w=u+v)
;;      iff 4 <= |w|^2 <= 16).
;;
;; The defun-sk predicate below retains the source's existential circle
;; witnesses. Its new primitive element beta may generate a finite algebraic
;; extension of Q(alpha), so witnesses such as square roots need not already
;; be polynomials in the input primitive alpha. A polynomial alpha-code(beta)
;; is required to be the unique input root in its isolating interval, and the
;; original coordinates are transported by polynomial composition. Thus the
;; circle witnesses are internal rather than additional statement parameters.
;;
;; Every finite tuple of real algebraic numbers lies in Q(alpha). A rational
;; polynomial and isolating interval represent alpha, and rational polynomials
;; in alpha represent all coordinates under discussion. Sturm-Tarski queries
;; decide their signs exactly. Each clause is first-order over real closed
;; fields with rational coefficients, so a real counterexample exists exactly
;; when a real-algebraic one exists. Thus the universal closure below covers
;; arbitrary real-plane points without narrowing the domain to ACL2's rationals.

;; Rational polynomials in alpha use descending coefficient order.

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-p (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (and (rationalp (car polynomial))
           (putnam-1996-a2-rp-p (cdr polynomial)))
    (equal polynomial nil)))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-normalize (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (if (equal (car polynomial) 0)
          (putnam-1996-a2-rp-normalize (cdr polynomial))
        polynomial)
    nil))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-neg (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons (- (car polynomial))
            (putnam-1996-a2-rp-neg (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-add-raw (left right)
  (declare
   (xargs :measure (+ (acl2-count left) (acl2-count right))))
  (cond
   ((endp left) right)
   ((endp right) left)
   ((< (len left) (len right))
    (cons (car right)
          (putnam-1996-a2-rp-add-raw left (cdr right))))
   ((< (len right) (len left))
    (cons (car left)
          (putnam-1996-a2-rp-add-raw (cdr left) right)))
   (t
    (cons (+ (car left) (car right))
          (putnam-1996-a2-rp-add-raw
           (cdr left) (cdr right))))))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-add (left right)
  (putnam-1996-a2-rp-normalize
   (putnam-1996-a2-rp-add-raw left right)))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-sub (left right)
  (putnam-1996-a2-rp-add
   left (putnam-1996-a2-rp-neg right)))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-scale (scalar polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons (* scalar (car polynomial))
            (putnam-1996-a2-rp-scale scalar (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-zeroes (count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons 0 (putnam-1996-a2-zeroes (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-scale-shift
    (scalar polynomial shift)
  (append
   (putnam-1996-a2-rp-scale scalar polynomial)
   (putnam-1996-a2-zeroes shift)))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-mul-raw (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (putnam-1996-a2-rp-add
       (putnam-1996-a2-rp-scale-shift
        (car left) right (len (cdr left)))
       (putnam-1996-a2-rp-mul-raw (cdr left) right))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-mul (left right)
  (putnam-1996-a2-rp-normalize
   (putnam-1996-a2-rp-mul-raw left right)))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-square (polynomial)
  (putnam-1996-a2-rp-mul polynomial polynomial))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-compose-aux
    (outer inner accumulator)
  (if (consp outer)
      (putnam-1996-a2-rp-compose-aux
       (cdr outer)
       inner
       (putnam-1996-a2-rp-add
        (putnam-1996-a2-rp-mul accumulator inner)
        (list (car outer))))
    accumulator))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-compose (outer inner)
  (putnam-1996-a2-rp-compose-aux outer inner nil))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-eval-aux
    (polynomial value accumulator)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (putnam-1996-a2-rp-eval-aux
       (cdr polynomial)
       value
       (+ (* accumulator value) (car polynomial)))
    accumulator))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-eval (polynomial value)
  (putnam-1996-a2-rp-eval-aux polynomial value 0))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-derivative-aux
    (polynomial degree)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (if (zp degree)
          nil
        (cons
         (* degree (car polynomial))

    (putnam-1996-a2-rp-normalize

  (let ((dividend
         (putnam-1996-a2-rp-normalize dividend))
        (divisor
         (putnam-1996-a2-rp-normalize divisor)))

        dividend
        (putnam-1996-a2-rp-scale-shift

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-sturm-tail

  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((current
         (putnam-1996-a2-rp-normalize current)))
    (if (or (zp fuel) (endp current))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-sturm-sequence

        (second
         (putnam-1996-a2-rp-normalize second)))

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rational-sign (value)

(defun putnam-1996-a2-rp-variations-aux
    (polynomials value previous-sign)
  (if (consp polynomials)
      (let ((sign
             (putnam-1996-a2-rational-sign
              (putnam-1996-a2-rp-eval
               (car polynomials) value))))
        (if (equal sign 0)
            (putnam-1996-a2-rp-variations-aux

    (putnam-1996-a2-rp-derivative primitive)

(defun putnam-1996-a2-alg-positive-p

title: putnam_1996_a2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_1996_a2): the midpoint locus determined by
-- circles of radii 1 and 3 whose centers are 10 units apart is the closed
-- annulus of radii 1 and 2 about the centers' midpoint. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record Both (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

_and_ : Set -> Set -> Set
A and B =
  Both A B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record StandardReal (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) -> Either (lessOrEqual x y) (lessOrEqual y x)
    add-monotone :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and oneR != zeroR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) -> fromNat m == fromNat n -> m == n
    fromNat-nonnegative :
      (n : Nat) -> lessOrEqual zeroR (fromNat n)

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      squareRoot x == y

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open StandardReal

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

half :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  R
half reals =
  inverse reals (fromNat reals 2)

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

Subset :
  (R : Set) ->
  Set1
Subset R =
  Point R -> Set

SameSubset :
  {R : Set} ->
  Subset R ->
  Subset R ->
  Set
SameSubset {R} A B =
  (p : Point R) ->
  Iff (A p) (B p)

squaredDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
squaredDistance reals p q =
  add reals
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q)))
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)))

distance :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
distance reals p q =
  squareRoot reals (squaredDistance reals p q)

midpoint :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R
midpoint reals p q =
  point
    (multiply reals
      (add reals (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q))
      (half reals))
    (multiply reals
      (add reals (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q))
      (half reals))

Circle :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  Point R ->
  R ->
  Subset R
Circle reals center radius p =
  distance reals p center == radius

MidpointLocus :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  Subset R ->
  Subset R ->
  Subset R
MidpointLocus {R} reals C1 C2 M =
  Exists (Point R)
    (\ X ->
      Exists (Point R)
        (\ Y ->
          C1 X
          and
          C2 Y
          and
          M == midpoint reals X Y))

SolutionAnnulus :
  {R : Set} ->
  StandardReal R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Subset R
SolutionAnnulus reals O1 O2 p =
  lessOrEqual reals
    (fromNat reals 1)
    (distance reals p (midpoint reals O1 O2))
  and
  lessOrEqual reals
    (distance reals p (midpoint reals O1 O2))
    (fromNat reals 2)

module Putnam1996A2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : StandardReal R) where

  proposition : Set1
  proposition =
    (O1 O2 : Point R) ->
    (C1 C2 : Subset R) ->
    SameSubset C1
      (Circle reals O1 (fromNat reals 1)) ->
    SameSubset C2
      (Circle reals O2 (fromNat reals 3)) ->
    distance reals O1 O2 == fromNat reals 10 ->
    SameSubset
      (MidpointLocus reals C1 C2)
      (SolutionAnnulus reals O1 O2)

putnam-1996-a2 : Set1
putnam-1996-a2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : StandardReal R) ->
  Putnam1996A2Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a2:
  the midpoint locus determined by circles of radii 1 and 3 whose centers are
  10 units apart is a closed annulus about the centers' midpoint. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_1996_a2 =
  ``let dist =
      \P Q : real # real.
        sqrt ((FST P - FST Q) pow 2 + (SND P - SND Q) pow 2)
    in
    let midpoint =
      \P Q : real # real.
        ((FST P + FST Q) / 2, (SND P + SND Q) / 2)
    in
      !(O1 O2 : real # real). !(C1 C2 : (real # real) set).
        C1 = {P : real # real | dist P O1 = 1} /\
        C2 = {P : real # real | dist P O2 = 3} /\
        dist O1 O2 = 10
        ==>
        {M : real # real |
           ?X Y : real # real.
             X IN C1 /\ Y IN C2 /\ M = midpoint X Y} =
        {P : real # real |
           1 <= dist P (midpoint O1 O2) /\
           dist P (midpoint O1 O2) <= 2}``;

$(

  putnam_1996_a2: the midpoint locus determined by circles of radii 1 and 3
  whose centers are 10 units apart is the closed annulus of radii 1 and 2
  centered at the midpoint of the circle centers. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P96A2I is the two-coordinate index set, P96A2R2 is the full real
  Euclidean plane, P96A2Dist is coordinate Euclidean distance, and P96A2Mid
  is coordinatewise midpoint.

  Circle membership and the source solution set are inlined definitionally
  in the final assertion. Both centers remain universally quantified over
  the real plane, and the points on the two circles remain internal
  existential witnesses. The final declaration is the single unproved $a
  corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P96A2I P96A2R2 P96A2Dist P96A2Mid $.

p96a2-index-syntax $a class P96A2I $.
p96a2-plane-syntax $a class P96A2R2 $.
p96a2-distance-syntax $a class ( P96A2Dist A B ) $.
p96a2-midpoint-syntax $a class ( P96A2Mid A B ) $.

p96a2-index-definition $a |- P96A2I = ( 1 ... 2 ) $.

p96a2-plane-definition $a |- P96A2R2 = ( RR ^m P96A2I ) $.

${
  $d A B j $.

  p96a2-distance-definition $a |- (
    P96A2Dist A B
  ) = (
    sqrt
    `
    (
      sum_ j e. P96A2I
        ( ( ( A ` j ) - ( B ` j ) ) ^ 2 )
    )
  ) $.

  p96a2-midpoint-definition $a |- (
    P96A2Mid A B
  ) = (
    j e. P96A2I |->
      (
        ( ( A ` j ) + ( B ` j ) )
        /
        2
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d M O P X Y $.

  putnambench-putnam-1996-a2 $a |-
    A. O e. P96A2R2
    A. P e. P96A2R2
      (
        ( P96A2Dist O P ) = ; 1 0
        ->
        {
          M e. P96A2R2 |
          E. X e. P96A2R2 E. Y e. P96A2R2
            (
              (
                ( P96A2Dist X O ) = 1
                /\
                ( P96A2Dist Y P ) = 3
              )
              /\
              M = ( P96A2Mid X Y )
            )
        }
        =
        {
          M e. P96A2R2 |
          (
            1 <_ ( P96A2Dist M ( P96A2Mid O P ) )
            /\
            ( P96A2Dist M ( P96A2Mid O P ) ) <_ 2
          )
        }
      )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a2:
% the midpoint locus determined by circles of radii one and three whose
% centers are ten units apart is the closed annulus of radii one and two
% centered at the midpoint of the centers. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1996_a2: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]
  point_set: TYPE = [point -> bool]

  squared_distance(P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q)) ^ 2
      + (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q)) ^ 2

  midpoint(P, Q: point): point =
    (# x_coord := (x_coord(P) + x_coord(Q)) / 2,
       y_coord := (y_coord(P) + y_coord(Q)) / 2 #)

  circle(center: point, radius: real): point_set =
    LAMBDA (P: point):
      squared_distance(P, center) = radius ^ 2

  midpoint_locus(C1, C2: point_set): point_set =
    LAMBDA (M: point):
      EXISTS (X, Y: point):
        C1(X) AND C2(Y) AND M = midpoint(X, Y)

  putnam_1996_a2_solution(O1, O2: point): point_set =
    LAMBDA (P: point):
      1 <= squared_distance(P, midpoint(O1, O2))
        AND squared_distance(P, midpoint(O1, O2)) <= 4

  putnam_1996_a2: bool =
    FORALL (O1, O2: point), (C1, C2: point_set):
      (C1 = circle(O1, 1)
        AND C2 = circle(O2, 3)
        AND squared_distance(O1, O2) = 100)
      IMPLIES

title: putnam_1996_a3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a3:
;; the universal claim that every assignment of subsets of six courses to
;; twenty students has five students and two courses that all five either
;; take together or omit together is false. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A student's chosen course set is its 6-bit characteristic number. A full
;; choice function is the 20-digit base-64 number whose digit at position S is
;; student S's course set. These are bijections with Set (Fin 6) and with all
;; functions Fin 20 -> Set (Fin 6), respectively.

(defun putnam-1996-a3-choice-set
    (choices-code student)
  (mod
   (floor choices-code (expt 64 student))
   64))

(defun putnam-1996-a3-member-p
    (set-code element)
  (equal
   (mod
    (floor set-code (expt 2 element))
    2)
   1))

(defun putnam-1996-a3-cardinality
    (set-code width)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix width)))
  (if (zp width)
      0
    (+
     (mod set-code 2)
     (putnam-1996-a3-cardinality
      (floor set-code 2)
      (- width 1)))))

;; MODE is true for "chosen" and false for "not chosen." This checks every
;; selected course for one student.
(defun putnam-1996-a3-student-agrees-p
    (choices-code student course-set course-count mode)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix course-count)))
  (if (zp course-count)
      t
    (let* ((course (- course-count 1))
           (course-selected
            (putnam-1996-a3-member-p course-set course))
           (course-chosen
            (putnam-1996-a3-member-p
             (putnam-1996-a3-choice-set
              choices-code student)
             course)))
      (and
       (or
        (not course-selected)
        (equal course-chosen mode))
       (putnam-1996-a3-student-agrees-p
        choices-code
        student
        course-set
        course
        mode)))))

;; This checks that every selected student agrees with MODE on both selected
;; courses.
(defun putnam-1996-a3-students-agree-p
    (choices-code student-set course-set student-count mode)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix student-count)))
  (if (zp student-count)
      t
    (let ((student (- student-count 1)))
      (and
       (or
        (not
         (putnam-1996-a3-member-p
          student-set student))
        (putnam-1996-a3-student-agrees-p
         choices-code student course-set 6 mode))
       (putnam-1996-a3-students-agree-p
        choices-code
        student-set
        course-set
        student
        mode)))))

;; Search all subsets of the six courses for a two-course witness.
(defun putnam-1996-a3-course-witness-p
    (choices-code student-set course-candidates)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix course-candidates)))
  (if (zp course-candidates)
      nil
    (let ((course-set (- course-candidates 1)))
      (or
       (and
        (equal
         (putnam-1996-a3-cardinality course-set 6)
         2)
        (or
         (putnam-1996-a3-students-agree-p
          choices-code student-set course-set 20 t)
         (putnam-1996-a3-students-agree-p
          choices-code student-set course-set 20 nil)))
       (putnam-1996-a3-course-witness-p
        choices-code student-set course-set)))))

;; Search all subsets of the twenty students for a five-student witness.
(defun putnam-1996-a3-student-witness-p
    (choices-code student-candidates)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix student-candidates)))
  (if (zp student-candidates)
      nil
    (let ((student-set (- student-candidates 1)))
      (or
       (and
        (equal
         (putnam-1996-a3-cardinality student-set 20)
         5)
        (putnam-1996-a3-course-witness-p
         choices-code student-set (expt 2 6)))
       (putnam-1996-a3-student-witness-p
        choices-code student-set)))))

(defun putnam-1996-a3-choice-property-p
    (choices-code)
  (putnam-1996-a3-student-witness-p
   choices-code (expt 2 20)))

;; This is the source's universal quantifier over the complete finite function
;; space, not a sample or bounded approximation.
(defun putnam-1996-a3-all-choice-functions-p
    (choice-function-candidates)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix choice-function-candidates)))
  (if (zp choice-function-candidates)
      t
    (let ((choices-code (- choice-function-candidates 1)))
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a3-choice-property-p choices-code)
       (putnam-1996-a3-all-choice-functions-p
        choices-code)))))

;; The designated solution is False, so the source biconditional is exactly
;; the negation of the universal claim above.
(defun putnambench-putnam-1996-a3-statement ()
  (not
   (putnam-1996-a3-all-choice-functions-p
    (expt 64 20))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- the universal assertion that every assignment of subsets of six courses to

-- choose both courses or omit both courses is false. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)
open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; _⊔_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : {a : Level} -> Set a -> Set a
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists
  {a p : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (P : A -> Set p) :
  Set (a ⊔ p) where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

one two three four five six : Nat
one =
  suc zero
two =
  suc one
three =
  suc two
four =
  suc three
five =
  suc four
six =
  suc five

seven eight nine ten eleven twelve thirteen fourteen fifteen : Nat
seven =
  suc six
eight =
  suc seven
nine =
  suc eight
ten =
  suc nine
eleven =
  suc ten
twelve =
  suc eleven
thirteen =
  suc twelve
fourteen =
  suc thirteen
fifteen =
  suc fourteen

sixteen seventeen eighteen nineteen twenty : Nat
sixteen =
  suc fifteen
seventeen =
  suc sixteen
eighteen =
  suc seventeen
nineteen =
  suc eighteen
twenty =
  suc nineteen

Student : Set
Student =
  Fin twenty

Course : Set
Course =
  Fin six

ChoiceAssignment : Set1
ChoiceAssignment =
  Student -> Course -> Set

Injective :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set
Injective {A} function =
  (x y : A) ->
  function x == function y ->
  x == y

AllChosen :
  ChoiceAssignment ->
  (Fin five -> Student) ->
  (Fin two -> Course) ->
  Set
AllChosen choices students courses =
  (student-index : Fin five) ->
  (course-index : Fin two) ->
  choices
    (students student-index)
    (courses course-index)

AllOmitted :
  ChoiceAssignment ->
  (Fin five -> Student) ->
  (Fin two -> Course) ->
  Set
AllOmitted choices students courses =
  (student-index : Fin five) ->
  (course-index : Fin two) ->
  Not
    (choices
      (students student-index)
      (courses course-index))

SelectionPrinciple : Set1
SelectionPrinciple =
  (choices : ChoiceAssignment) ->
  Exists (Fin five -> Student)
    (\ students ->
      Injective students
      and
      Exists (Fin two -> Course)
        (\ courses ->
          Injective courses
          and
          (AllChosen choices students courses
           or
           AllOmitted choices students courses)))

putnam-1996-a3-solution : Set
putnam-1996-a3-solution =
  Bottom

putnam-1996-a3 : Set1
putnam-1996-a3 =
  Iff SelectionPrinciple putnam-1996-a3-solution

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a3:
% the universal assertion that every assignment of six courses to twenty students
% admits five students uniformly choosing or omitting the same two courses is false.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_1996_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  student: TYPE = below(20)
  course: TYPE = below(6)

  IMPORTING finite_sets[student], finite_sets[course]

  student_set: TYPE = finite_set[student]
  course_set: TYPE = finite_set[course]
  course_choices: TYPE = [student -> [course -> bool]]

  all_choose(
      choices: course_choices,
      students: student_set,
      courses: course_set): bool =
    FORALL (s: student), (c: course):
      students(s) AND courses(c) IMPLIES choices(s)(c)

  all_omit(
      choices: course_choices,
      students: student_set,
      courses: course_set): bool =
    FORALL (s: student), (c: course):
      students(s) AND courses(c) IMPLIES NOT choices(s)(c)

  has_uniform_students(choices: course_choices): bool =
    EXISTS (students: student_set), (courses: course_set):
      card(students) = 5
        AND card(courses) = 2
        AND
          (all_choose(choices, students, courses)
            OR all_omit(choices, students, courses))

  putnam_1996_a3_solution: bool = FALSE

  putnam_1996_a3: bool =
    (FORALL (choices: course_choices):
      has_uniform_students(choices))
      IFF putnam_1996_a3_solution
END putnam_1996_a3

title: putnam_1996_a4

import Mathlib

open Function

/--
Let $S$ be a set of ordered triples $(a, b, c)$ of distinct elements of a finite set $A$. Suppose that \begin{enumerate} \item $(a,b,c) \in S$ if and only if $(b,c,a) \in S$; \item $(a,b,c) \in S$ if and only if $(c,b,a) \notin S$; \item $(a,b,c)$ and $(c,d,a)$ are both in $S$ if and only if $(b,c,d)$ and $(d,a,b)$ are both in $S$. \end{enumerate} Prove that there exists a one-to-one function $g$ from $A$ to $\R$ such that $g(a) < g(b) < g(c)$ implies $(a,b,c) \in S$.
-/
theorem putnam_1996_a4
(A : Type*)
[Finite A]
(S : Set (A × A × A))
(hSdistinct : ∀ a b c : A, ⟨a, b, c⟩ ∈ S → a ≠ b ∧ b ≠ c ∧ a ≠ c)
(hS1 : ∀ a b c : A, [a,b,c].Pairwise (· ≠ ·) → (⟨a, b, c⟩ ∈ S ↔ ⟨b, c, a⟩ ∈ S))
(hS2 : ∀ a b c : A, [a,b,c].Pairwise (· ≠ ·) → (⟨a, b, c⟩ ∈ S ↔ ⟨c, b, a⟩ ∉ S))
(hS3 : ∀ a b c d : A, [a,b,c,d].Pairwise (· ≠ ·) → ((⟨a, b, c⟩ ∈ S ∧ ⟨c, d, a⟩ ∈ S) ↔ (⟨b,c,d⟩ ∈ S ∧ ⟨d,a,b⟩ ∈ S)))
: ∃ g : A → ℝ, Injective g ∧ (∀ a b c : A, g a < g b ∧ g b < g c → ⟨a,b,c⟩ ∈ S) :=
sorry

    (hSdistinct: forall a b c : A, In _ SS (a, b, c) -> a <> b /\ b <> c /\ c <> a)
    (hS1 : forall a b c : A,
      a <> b /\ b <> c /\ c <> a ->

    (hS2 : forall a b c : A,

      ((In _ SS (a, b, c) /\ In _ SS (c, d, a)) <->

    : exists g : A -> R, Injective g /\ (forall a b c : A, g a < g b /\ g b < g c -> In _ SS (a, b, c)).

title: putnam_1996_a4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a4:
;; a finite ternary orientation satisfying cyclic, reversal, and four-point
;; axioms admits an injective real ranking compatible with every increasing
;; triple. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; CARRIER is a duplicate-free enumeration of the arbitrary finite source
;; type, and RELATION is a duplicate-free enumeration of S. Thus the lists
;; represent the finite sets extensionally without restricting their elements.
;; The distinctness guards on the three structural axioms are the explicit,
;; non-vacuous formulation in the Lean source and in the mathematical problem.
;;
;; Every injective real-valued map on a finite carrier orders its elements by
;; increasing image. Conversely, any permutation of the carrier defines such
;; a map by assigning each element its integer position. Therefore the finite
;; permutation search below is bidirectionally equivalent to the source's
;; internal existential quantifier over g; no witness is an external parameter.

(defun putnam-1996-a4-set-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (not (member-equal (car values) (cdr values)))
       (putnam-1996-a4-set-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-triple-p (triple carrier)
  (and
   (true-listp triple)
   (equal (len triple) 3)
   (member-equal (car triple) carrier)
   (member-equal (cadr triple) carrier)
   (member-equal (caddr triple) carrier)))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-relation-p (relation carrier)
  (if (consp relation)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-triple-p (car relation) carrier)
       (not (member-equal (car relation) (cdr relation)))
       (putnam-1996-a4-relation-p (cdr relation) carrier))
    (equal relation nil)))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-pairwise-distinct-3-p (a b c)
  (and
   (not (equal a b))
   (not (equal b c))
   (not (equal a c))))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-pairwise-distinct-4-p (a b c d)
  (and
   (not (equal a b))
   (not (equal a c))
   (not (equal a d))
   (not (equal b c))
   (not (equal b d))
   (not (equal c d))))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-relation-distinct-p (relation)
  (if (consp relation)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-pairwise-distinct-3-p
        (caar relation)
        (cadar relation)
        (caddar relation))
       (putnam-1996-a4-relation-distinct-p (cdr relation)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-in-s-p (a b c relation)
  (if (member-equal (list a b c) relation)
      t
    nil))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-cyclic-c-p (a b cs relation)
  (if (consp cs)
      (let ((c (car cs)))
        (and
         (implies
          (putnam-1996-a4-pairwise-distinct-3-p a b c)
          (iff
           (putnam-1996-a4-in-s-p a b c relation)
           (putnam-1996-a4-in-s-p b c a relation)))
         (putnam-1996-a4-cyclic-c-p
          a b (cdr cs) relation)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-cyclic-b-p (a bs carrier relation)
  (if (consp bs)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-cyclic-c-p
        a (car bs) carrier relation)
       (putnam-1996-a4-cyclic-b-p
        a (cdr bs) carrier relation))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-cyclic-p (as carrier relation)
  (if (consp as)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-cyclic-b-p
        (car as) carrier carrier relation)
       (putnam-1996-a4-cyclic-p
        (cdr as) carrier relation))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-reversal-c-p (a b cs relation)
  (if (consp cs)
      (let ((c (car cs)))
        (and
         (implies
          (putnam-1996-a4-pairwise-distinct-3-p a b c)
          (iff
           (putnam-1996-a4-in-s-p a b c relation)
           (not
            (putnam-1996-a4-in-s-p c b a relation))))
         (putnam-1996-a4-reversal-c-p
          a b (cdr cs) relation)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-reversal-b-p (a bs carrier relation)
  (if (consp bs)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-reversal-c-p
        a (car bs) carrier relation)
       (putnam-1996-a4-reversal-b-p
        a (cdr bs) carrier relation))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-reversal-p (as carrier relation)
  (if (consp as)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-reversal-b-p
        (car as) carrier carrier relation)
       (putnam-1996-a4-reversal-p
        (cdr as) carrier relation))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-four-point-d-p
    (a b c ds relation)
  (if (consp ds)
      (let ((d (car ds)))
        (and
         (implies
          (putnam-1996-a4-pairwise-distinct-4-p a b c d)
          (iff
           (and
            (putnam-1996-a4-in-s-p a b c relation)
            (putnam-1996-a4-in-s-p c d a relation))
           (and
            (putnam-1996-a4-in-s-p b c d relation)
            (putnam-1996-a4-in-s-p d a b relation))))
         (putnam-1996-a4-four-point-d-p
          a b c (cdr ds) relation)))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-four-point-c-p
    (a b cs carrier relation)
  (if (consp cs)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-four-point-d-p
        a b (car cs) carrier relation)
       (putnam-1996-a4-four-point-c-p
        a b (cdr cs) carrier relation))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-four-point-b-p
    (a bs carrier relation)
  (if (consp bs)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-four-point-c-p
        a (car bs) carrier carrier relation)
       (putnam-1996-a4-four-point-b-p
        a (cdr bs) carrier relation))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-four-point-p
    (as carrier relation)
  (if (consp as)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-four-point-b-p
        (car as) carrier carrier relation)
       (putnam-1996-a4-four-point-p
        (cdr as) carrier relation))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-compatible-after-two-p
    (a b remaining relation)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-in-s-p
        a b (car remaining) relation)
       (putnam-1996-a4-compatible-after-two-p
        a b (cdr remaining) relation))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-compatible-after-one-p
    (a remaining relation)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-compatible-after-two-p
        a (car remaining) (cdr remaining) relation)
       (putnam-1996-a4-compatible-after-one-p
        a (cdr remaining) relation))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-compatible-order-p (order relation)
  (if (consp order)
      (and
       (putnam-1996-a4-compatible-after-one-p
        (car order) (cdr order) relation)
       (putnam-1996-a4-compatible-order-p
        (cdr order) relation))
    t))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-prepend-each (value lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (cons
     (cons value (car lists))
     (putnam-1996-a4-prepend-each value (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-insert-everywhere (value values)
  (if (endp values)
      (list (list value))
    (cons
     (cons value values)
     (putnam-1996-a4-prepend-each
      (car values)
      (putnam-1996-a4-insert-everywhere
       value (cdr values))))))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-insert-into-permutations
    (value permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-1996-a4-insert-everywhere
      value (car permutations))
     (putnam-1996-a4-insert-into-permutations
      value (cdr permutations)))))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-permutations (values)
  (if (endp values)
      (list nil)
    (putnam-1996-a4-insert-into-permutations
     (car values)
     (putnam-1996-a4-permutations (cdr values)))))

(defun putnam-1996-a4-compatible-order-exists-p
    (orders relation)
  (if (consp orders)
      (or
       (putnam-1996-a4-compatible-order-p
        (car orders) relation)
       (putnam-1996-a4-compatible-order-exists-p
        (cdr orders) relation))
    nil))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1996-a4-statement
    (carrier relation)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-1996-a4-set-list-p carrier)
    (putnam-1996-a4-relation-p relation carrier)
    (putnam-1996-a4-relation-distinct-p relation)
    (putnam-1996-a4-cyclic-p carrier carrier relation)
    (putnam-1996-a4-reversal-p carrier carrier relation)
    (putnam-1996-a4-four-point-p carrier carrier relation))
   (putnam-1996-a4-compatible-order-exists-p
    (putnam-1996-a4-permutations carrier)
    relation)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1996_a4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a4:
-- a consistent orientation of the distinct triples of a finite set admits an
-- injective real-valued ordering whose increasing triples have that orientation.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam1996A4 where

open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc; _⊔_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not :
  {a : Level} ->
  Set a ->
  Set a
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ :
  {a : Level} ->
  {A : Set a} ->
  A ->
  A ->
  Set a
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Iff
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists
  {a p : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (P : A -> Set p) :
  Set (a ⊔ p) where

  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record Finite
  {a : Level}
  (A : Set a) :
  Set a where

  field
    cardinality : Nat
    to-fin       : A -> Fin cardinality
    from-fin     : Fin cardinality -> A
    from-to      : (x : A) -> from-fin (to-fin x) == x
    to-from      : (i : Fin cardinality) -> to-fin (from-fin i) == i

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

StrictlyLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictlyLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y
  and
  x != y

Injective :
  {a b : Level} ->
  {A : Set a} ->
  {B : Set b} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set (a ⊔ b)
Injective {A = A} f =
  (x y : A) ->
  f x == f y ->
  x == y

PairwiseDistinct3 :
  {a : Level} ->
  {A : Set a} ->
  A ->
  A ->
  A ->
  Set a
PairwiseDistinct3 a b c =
  a != b
  and
  b != c
  and
  a != c

PairwiseDistinct4 :
  {a : Level} ->
  {A : Set a} ->
  A ->
  A ->
  A ->
  A ->
  Set a
PairwiseDistinct4 a b c d =
  a != b
  and
  a != c
  and
  a != d
  and
  b != c
  and
  b != d
  and
  c != d

putnam-1996-a4 :
  {a : Level} ->
  Set (lsuc a)
putnam-1996-a4 {a} =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (A : Set a) ->
  Finite A ->
  (S : A -> A -> A -> Set a) ->
  ((x y z : A) ->
    S x y z ->
    PairwiseDistinct3 x y z) ->
  ((a b c : A) ->
    PairwiseDistinct3 a b c ->
    Iff
      (S a b c)
      (S b c a)) ->
  ((a b c : A) ->
    PairwiseDistinct3 a b c ->
    Iff
      (S a b c)
      (Not (S c b a))) ->
  ((a b c d : A) ->
    PairwiseDistinct4 a b c d ->
    Iff
      (S a b c and S c d a)
      (S b c d and S d a b)) ->
  Exists (A -> R)
    (\ g ->
      Injective g
      and
      ((a b c : A) ->
        StrictlyLess reals (g a) (g b)
        and
        StrictlyLess reals (g b) (g c) ->
        S a b c))

title: putnam_1996_a4
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a4:
  a ternary orientation relation on a finite set satisfying cyclic, reversal,
  and four-point compatibility conditions admits a compatible injective
  real-valued ordering. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory realTheory;

val putnam_1996_a4 =
  ``!S : ('a # 'a # 'a) -> bool.
      FINITE (UNIV : 'a set) /\
      (!a b c : 'a.
         S (a, b, c)
         ==>
         a <> b /\ b <> c /\ a <> c) /\
      (!a b c : 'a.
         a <> b /\ b <> c /\ a <> c
         ==>
         (S (a, b, c) <=> S (b, c, a))) /\
      (!a b c : 'a.
         a <> b /\ b <> c /\ a <> c
         ==>
         (S (a, b, c) <=> ~S (c, b, a))) /\
      (!a b c d : 'a.
         a <> b /\ a <> c /\ a <> d /\
         b <> c /\ b <> d /\ c <> d
         ==>
         ((S (a, b, c) /\ S (c, d, a)) <=>
          (S (b, c, d) /\ S (d, a, b))))
      ==>
      ?g : 'a -> real.
        (!a b : 'a. g a = g b ==> a = b) /\
        (!a b c : 'a.
           g a < g b /\ g b < g c
           ==>
           S (a, b, c))``;

title: putnam_1996_a4
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1996_a4: a consistent orientation of the distinct triples of a
  finite set admits an injective real-valued ordering whose increasing
  triples have that orientation. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  An arbitrary A e. Fin is the source finite carrier. The powerset of
  ( A X. A ) X. A contains every ternary relation on A when SetMM's ordered
  triple <. a , b , c >. is used. The explicit inequalities retain the
  pairwise-distinct scopes of the nontrivial distinct-element formulation.

  The witness g remains existential and SetMM's -1-1-> notation requires it
  to be an injective total function from A into RR. The final declaration is
  the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

${
  $d A S a b c d g $.

  putnambench-putnam-1996-a4 $a |- A. A e. Fin
    A. S e. ~P ( ( A X. A ) X. A )
      (
        (
          A. a e. A A. b e. A A. c e. A
            (
              <. a , b , c >. e. S
              ->
              (
                a =/= b
                /\
                (
                  b =/= c
                  /\
                  a =/= c
                )
              )
            )
          /\
          (
            A. a e. A A. b e. A A. c e. A
              (
                (
                  a =/= b
                  /\
                  (
                    b =/= c
                    /\
                    a =/= c
                  )
                )
                ->
                (
                  <. a , b , c >. e. S
                  <->
                  <. b , c , a >. e. S
                )
              )
            /\
            (
              A. a e. A A. b e. A A. c e. A
                (
                  (
                    a =/= b
                    /\
                    (
                      b =/= c
                      /\
                      a =/= c
                    )
                  )
                  ->
                  (
                    <. a , b , c >. e. S
                    <->
                    -. <. c , b , a >. e. S
                  )
                )
              /\
              A. a e. A A. b e. A A. c e. A A. d e. A
                (
                  (
                    a =/= b
                    /\
                    (
                      a =/= c
                      /\
                      (
                        a =/= d
                        /\
                        (
                          b =/= c
                          /\
                          (
                            b =/= d
                            /\
                            c =/= d
                          )
                        )
                      )
                    )
                  )
                  ->
                  (
                    (
                      <. a , b , c >. e. S
                      /\
                      <. c , d , a >. e. S
                    )
                    <->
                    (
                      <. b , c , d >. e. S
                      /\
                      <. d , a , b >. e. S
                    )
                  )
                )
            )
          )
        )
        ->
        E. g
          (
            g : A -1-1-> RR
            /\
            A. a e. A A. b e. A A. c e. A
              (
                (
                  ( g ` a ) < ( g ` b )
                  /\
                  ( g ` b ) < ( g ` c )
                )
                ->
                <. a , b , c >. e. S
              )
          )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1996_a4
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a4:
:: a cyclic orientation relation on distinct triples of a finite set satisfying
:: the four-point compatibility law admits an injective real ordering consistent
:: with every increasing triple. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, FINSET_1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, XCMPLX_0, CARD_1, XXREAL_0,
    ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1, ORDINAL1, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, PARTFUN1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, XTUPLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1,
    FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, FINSET_1, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS,
    XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, REAL_1, NAT_1, INT_1;
  constructors ZFMISC_1, XTUPLE_0, FINSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, XCMPLX_0, REAL_1, NAT_1, INT_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, FINSET_1, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, MEMBERED, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, NAT_1, INT_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, ZFMISC_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for A being finite set, S being Subset of [:A,A,A:] st
    (for a,b,c being Element of A st [a,b,c] in S holds
      a <> b & b <> c & a <> c) &
    (for a,b,c being Element of A st
      a <> b & b <> c & a <> c
     holds
      ([a,b,c] in S iff [b,c,a] in S)) &
    (for a,b,c being Element of A st
      a <> b & b <> c & a <> c
     holds
      ([a,b,c] in S iff not [c,b,a] in S)) &
    (for a,b,c,d being Element of A st
      a <> b & a <> c & a <> d &
      b <> c & b <> d & c <> d
     holds
      ([a,b,c] in S & [c,d,a] in S iff
       [b,c,d] in S & [d,a,b] in S))
  holds
    ex g being Function of A,REAL st
      g is one-to-one &
      for a,b,c being Element of A st
        g/.a < g/.b & g/.b < g/.c
      holds [a,b,c] in S
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1996_a4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a4:
% a ternary orientation relation on distinct triples of a finite set satisfying
% cyclic, reversal, and four-point compatibility conditions admits a compatible
% injective real-valued ordering. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1996_a4[Element: TYPE+]: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[Element]

  ternary_relation: TYPE = [Element, Element, Element -> bool]

  pairwise_distinct_3(a, b, c: Element): bool =
    a /= b AND b /= c AND a /= c

  pairwise_distinct_4(a, b, c, d: Element): bool =
    a /= b
      AND a /= c
      AND a /= d
      AND b /= c
      AND b /= d
      AND c /= d

  injective_on(
      A: finite_set[Element],
      g: [Element -> real]): bool =
    FORALL (a, b: Element):
      A(a) AND A(b) AND g(a) = g(b)
        IMPLIES a = b

  putnam_1996_a4: bool =
    FORALL (A: finite_set[Element]), (S: ternary_relation):
      ((FORALL (a, b, c: Element):
          A(a) AND A(b) AND A(c) AND S(a, b, c)
            IMPLIES pairwise_distinct_3(a, b, c))
        AND
          (FORALL (a, b, c: Element):
            A(a)
              AND A(b)
              AND A(c)
              AND pairwise_distinct_3(a, b, c)
            IMPLIES (S(a, b, c) IFF S(b, c, a)))
        AND
          (FORALL (a, b, c: Element):
            A(a)
              AND A(b)
              AND A(c)
              AND pairwise_distinct_3(a, b, c)
            IMPLIES (S(a, b, c) IFF NOT S(c, b, a)))
        AND
          (FORALL (a, b, c, d: Element):
            A(a)
              AND A(b)
              AND A(c)
              AND A(d)
              AND pairwise_distinct_4(a, b, c, d)
            IMPLIES
              ((S(a, b, c) AND S(c, d, a))
                IFF (S(b, c, d) AND S(d, a, b)))))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (g: [Element -> real]):
          injective_on(A, g)
            AND
              (FORALL (a, b, c: Element):
                A(a)
                  AND A(b)
                  AND A(c)
                  AND g(a) < g(b)
                  AND g(b) < g(c)
                IMPLIES S(a, b, c))
END putnam_1996_a4

putnam_1996_a5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a5:
;; for every prime natural p greater than 3, the sum of choose(p,i) from
;; i = 1 through floor(2*p/3) is divisible by p^2. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Trial division through p-1 is exactly primality for natural p > 1.
(defun putnam-1996-a5-no-divisor-through-p (p candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (or (not (natp candidate))
          (<= candidate 1))
      t
    (and
     (not (equal (mod p candidate) 0))
     (putnam-1996-a5-no-divisor-through-p
      p (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-1996-a5-prime-p (p)
  (and
   (natp p)
   (< 1 p)
   (putnam-1996-a5-no-divisor-through-p
    p (- p 1))))

;; Pascal recursion represents the natural-number binomial coefficient.
(defun putnam-1996-a5-binomial-coefficient (n i)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (or (zp i)
          (zp n))
      (if (zp i) 1 0)
    (+ (putnam-1996-a5-binomial-coefficient (- n 1) i)
       (putnam-1996-a5-binomial-coefficient
        (- n 1) (- i 1)))))

;; Inclusive sum of choose(p,i) for i = 1,...,upper.
(defun putnam-1996-a5-binomial-sum-through (p upper)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix upper)))
  (if (zp upper)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1996-a5-binomial-sum-through
        p (- upper 1))
       (putnam-1996-a5-binomial-coefficient p upper))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1996-a5-statement (p k)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp p)
    (natp k)
    (putnam-1996-a5-prime-p p)
    (> p 3)
    (equal k (floor (* 2 p) 3)))
   (equal
    (mod
     (putnam-1996-a5-binomial-sum-through p k)
     (expt p 2))
    0)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a5:
-- for every prime natural p greater than 3, the sum of the binomial
-- coefficients C(p,i) from i = 1 through floor(2p/3) is divisible by p^2.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; div-helper)

infix 4 _<=_ _<_ _divides_
infixr 2 _or_

data _<=_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<= : {n : Nat} -> zero <= n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> suc m <= suc n

_<_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m < n =
  suc m <= n

record _divides_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    division-equation : dividend == divisor * quotient

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

three : Nat
three =
  suc two

record Prime (p : Nat) : Set where
  field
    at-least-two : two <= p
    only-trivial-divisors :
      (d : Nat) ->
      d divides p ->
      (d == one) or (d == p)

naturalDiv : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero =
  zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

choose : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
choose n zero =
  one
choose zero (suc k) =
  zero
choose (suc n) (suc k) =
  choose n (suc k) + choose n k

sumFromOne : Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat
sumFromOne zero term =
  zero
sumFromOne (suc bound) term =
  sumFromOne bound term + term (suc bound)

cutoff : Nat -> Nat
cutoff p =
  naturalDiv (two * p) three

binomialSum : Nat -> Nat
binomialSum p =
  sumFromOne (cutoff p) (\ i -> choose p i)

square : Nat -> Nat
square n =
  n * n

putnam-1996-a5 : Set
putnam-1996-a5 =
  (p : Nat) ->
  Prime p ->
  three < p ->
  square p divides binomialSum p

title: putnam_1996_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_a5:
% for every prime p greater than 3, the sum of the binomial coefficients
% (p choose i) from i = 1 through floor(2p/3) is divisible by p^2.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_1996_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat): value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value

  binomial_coefficient(n, k: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF k = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSIF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k - 1)
        + binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  binomial_partial_sum(p, upper: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF upper = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      binomial_partial_sum(p, upper - 1)
        + binomial_coefficient(p, upper)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE upper

  two_thirds_floor(p: nat): nat =
    ndiv(2 * p, 3)

  putnam_1996_a5: bool =
    FORALL (p: nat):
      (prime_nat(p) AND p > 3)
        IMPLIES
          nat_divides(
            p ^ 2,
            binomial_partial_sum(p, two_thirds_floor(p)))
END putnam_1996_a5

Let $c>0$ be a constant. Give a complete description, with proof, of the set of all continuous functions $f:\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $f(x)=f(x^2+c)$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.
-/
theorem putnam_1996_a6
(c : ℝ)
(f : ℝ → ℝ)
(cgt0 : c > 0)
: (Continuous f ∧ ∀ x : ℝ, f x = f (x ^ 2 + c)) ↔ f ∈ putnam_1996_a6_solution c :=

Definition putnam_1996_a6_solution (c: R) (f: R -> R) :=  if Rle_dec c (1/4) then (exists (d: R), f = (fun _ => d)) else ((forall (x: R), 0 <= x <= c -> continuity_pt f x) /\ f 0 = f c /\ (forall (x: R), x > 0 -> f x = f (pow x 2 + c)) /\ (forall (x: R), x < 0 -> f x = f (-x))).
Theorem putnam_1996_a6
    (c: R)
    (hc : c > 0)
    : forall (f: R -> R), (continuity f /\ (forall (x: R), f x = f (pow x 2 + c))) <-> putnam_1996_a6_solution c f.
Proof. Admitted.
