    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  matrix_zero: matrix =
    LAMBDA (i, j: coordinate): 0

  matrix_identity: matrix =
    LAMBDA (i, j: coordinate):
      IF i = j THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF

  matrix_add(A, B: matrix): matrix =
    LAMBDA (i, j: coordinate):
      A(i, j) + B(i, j)

  matrix_scale(c: real, A: matrix): matrix =
    LAMBDA (i, j: coordinate):
      c * A(i, j)

  matrix_multiply(A, B: matrix): matrix =
    LAMBDA (i, j: coordinate):
      A(i, 0) * B(0, j) + A(i, 1) * B(1, j)

  matrix_power(A: matrix, exponent: nat): RECURSIVE matrix =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      matrix_identity
    ELSE
      matrix_multiply(A, matrix_power(A, exponent - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  sine_series_term(A: matrix, index: nat): matrix =
    matrix_scale(
      safe_div(
        (-1 :: real) ^ index,
        nat_factorial(2 * index + 1) :: real),
      matrix_power(A, 2 * index + 1))

  matrix_sine_partial(A: matrix, count: nat): RECURSIVE matrix =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      matrix_zero
    ELSE
      matrix_add(
        matrix_sine_partial(A, count - 1),
        sine_series_term(A, count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  matrix_converges_to(
      sequence: matrix_sequence,
      value: matrix): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat), (i, j: coordinate):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index)(i, j) - value(i, j))
              < epsilon_value

  mat1996: matrix =
    LAMBDA (i, j: coordinate):
      IF i = 0 THEN
        IF j = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 1996 ENDIF
      ELSE
        IF j = 0 THEN 0 ELSE 1 ENDIF
      ENDIF

  putnam_1996_b4_solution: bool = FALSE

  putnam_1996_b4: bool =
    (EXISTS (A: matrix):
      matrix_converges_to(
        LAMBDA (count: nat):
          matrix_sine_partial(A, count),
        mat1996))
      IFF putnam_1996_b4_solution
END putnam_1996_b4

import Mathlib

open Function Nat

abbrev putnam_1996_b5_solution : ℕ → ℕ := sorry
-- (fun n : ℕ ↦ 2 ^ ⌊(n + 2) / 2⌋₊ + 2 ^ ⌊(n + 1) / 2⌋₊ - 2)

/--
Given a finite string $S$ of symbols $X$ and $O$, we write $\Delta(S)$ for the number of $X$'s in $S$ minus the number of $O$'s. For example, $\Delta(XOOXOOX)=-1$. We call a string $S$ \emph{balanced} if every substring $T$ of (consecutive symbols of) $S$ has $-2 \leq \Delta(T) \leq 2$. Thus, $XOOXOOX$ is not balanced, since it contains the substring $OOXOO$. Find, with proof, the number of balanced strings of length $n$.
-/
theorem putnam_1996_b5
    (n : ℕ)
    (Δ : (Fin n → ℤˣ) → Fin n → Fin n → ℤ)
    (balanced : (Fin n → ℤˣ) → Prop)
    (hΔ : ∀ S, ∀ a b, a ≤ b → Δ S a b = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc a b, (S i : ℤ))
    (hbalanced : ∀ S, balanced S ↔ ∀ a b, a ≤ b → |Δ S a b| ≤ 2) :
    {S : Fin n → ℤˣ | balanced S}.ncard = putnam_1996_b5_solution n :=
  sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_b5:
   the number of two-symbol strings whose every consecutive substring has
   symbol-count imbalance between -2 and 2. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Bool.Bool Lists.List Vectors.Fin
  ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_1996_b5_fin_sum
    (n : nat) : (Fin.t n -> Z) -> Z :=
  match n as m return (Fin.t m -> Z) -> Z with
  | O => fun _ => 0
  | S k =>
      fun f =>
        f Fin.F1 +
        putnam_1996_b5_fin_sum k (fun i => f (Fin.FS i))
  end.

Definition putnam_1996_b5_index
    {n : nat} (i : Fin.t n) : nat :=
  proj1_sig (Fin.to_nat i).

Definition putnam_1996_b5_delta
    {n : nat} (S : Fin.t n -> bool) (a b : Fin.t n) : Z :=
  putnam_1996_b5_fin_sum n
    (fun i =>
      if andb
           (Nat.leb (putnam_1996_b5_index a)
                    (putnam_1996_b5_index i))
           (Nat.leb (putnam_1996_b5_index i)
                    (putnam_1996_b5_index b))
      then if S i then 1 else -1
      else 0).

Definition putnam_1996_b5_balanced
    {n : nat} (S : Fin.t n -> bool) : Prop :=
  forall a b : Fin.t n,
    (putnam_1996_b5_index a <= putnam_1996_b5_index b)%nat ->
    (-2 <= putnam_1996_b5_delta S a b /\
     putnam_1996_b5_delta S a b <= 2)%Z.

Definition putnam_1996_b5_string_eq
    {n : nat} (S T : Fin.t n -> bool) : Prop :=
  forall i : Fin.t n, S i = T i.

Fixpoint putnam_1996_b5_distinct_representatives
    {n : nat} (strings : list (Fin.t n -> bool)) : Prop :=
  match strings with
  | nil => True
  | head :: remaining =>
      (forall T : Fin.t n -> bool,
          In T remaining ->
          ~ putnam_1996_b5_string_eq head T) /\
      putnam_1996_b5_distinct_representatives remaining
  end.

Definition putnam_1996_b5_has_cardinality
    (n : nat)
    (P : (Fin.t n -> bool) -> Prop)
    (cardinality : nat) : Prop :=
  exists representatives : list (Fin.t n -> bool),
    length representatives = cardinality /\
    putnam_1996_b5_distinct_representatives representatives /\
    forall S : Fin.t n -> bool,
      P S <->
      exists T : Fin.t n -> bool,
        In T representatives /\
        putnam_1996_b5_string_eq S T.

Definition putnam_1996_b5_solution (n : nat) : nat :=
  (Nat.pow 2 (Nat.div (n + 2) 2) +
   Nat.pow 2 (Nat.div (n + 1) 2) - 2)%nat.

Theorem putnam_1996_b5 (n : nat) :
  putnam_1996_b5_has_cardinality
    n
    (fun S => putnam_1996_b5_balanced S)
    (putnam_1996_b5_solution n).
Admitted.

theorem putnam_1996_b5:

  and "Sbalanced \<equiv> \<lambda> (S :: nat \<Rightarrow> bool). \<forall> T1 \<in> {0 .. n - 1}. \<forall> T2 \<in> {0 .. n - 1}. T1 \<le> T2 \<longrightarrow> (-2 \<le> STdelta S T1 T2 \<and> STdelta S T1 T2 \<le> 2)"

title: putnam_1996_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_b5:
;; the number of length-n two-symbol strings whose every contiguous substring
;; has symbol imbalance between -2 and 2. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A length-n string is encoded by its unique mask in [0,2^n), with bit i
;; representing the symbol at position i. Mapping a set bit to 1 and a clear
;; bit to -1 is a bijection with both source encodings (integer units or
;; Booleans), and interval sums are exactly the source imbalance function.

(defun putnam-1996-b5-symbol-value (code index)
  (if (equal
       (mod (floor code (expt 2 (nfix index))) 2)
       1)
      1
    -1))

(defun putnam-1996-b5-interval-delta
    (code start remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+
     (putnam-1996-b5-symbol-value code start)
     (putnam-1996-b5-interval-delta
      code
      (+ 1 (nfix start))
      (- remaining 1)))))

;; For a fixed start, check all nonempty intervals beginning there. The
;; initial remaining value is n-start, so the tested lengths are precisely
;; 1,...,n-start.
(defun putnam-1996-b5-balanced-lengths-p
    (code start remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (let ((delta
           (putnam-1996-b5-interval-delta
            code start remaining)))
      (and
       (<= -2 delta)
       (<= delta 2)
       (putnam-1996-b5-balanced-lengths-p
        code start (- remaining 1))))))

;; Check every start in 0,...,n-1.
(defun putnam-1996-b5-balanced-starts-p
    (code n remaining-starts)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-starts)))
  (if (zp remaining-starts)
      t
    (let ((start (- remaining-starts 1)))
      (and
       (putnam-1996-b5-balanced-lengths-p
        code start (- n start))
       (putnam-1996-b5-balanced-starts-p
        code n start)))))

(defun putnam-1996-b5-balanced-code-p (code n)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (natp code)
   (< code (expt 2 n))
   (putnam-1996-b5-balanced-starts-p code n n)))

;; Count all masks below code-count; at 2^n this is the cardinality of the
;; complete source space of length-n strings satisfying balanced.
(defun putnam-1996-b5-balanced-count
    (n code-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix code-count)))
  (if (zp code-count)
      0
    (let ((code (- code-count 1)))
      (+
       (if (putnam-1996-b5-balanced-code-p code n)
           1
         0)
       (putnam-1996-b5-balanced-count n code)))))

(defun putnam-1996-b5-solution (n)
  (-
   (+
    (expt 2 (floor (+ n 2) 2))
    (expt 2 (floor (+ n 1) 2)))
   2))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1996-b5-statement (n)
  (implies
   (natp n)
   (equal
    (putnam-1996-b5-balanced-count n (expt 2 n))
    (putnam-1996-b5-solution n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_1996_b5): the number of length-n X/O strings
-- whose every consecutive substring has symbol-count difference at most two.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_; div-helper)

infixr 5 _++_
infixr 4 _and_

data Symbol : Set where
  X O : Symbol

_and_ : Bool -> Bool -> Bool
true and condition = condition
false and condition = false

lessOrEqual : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
lessOrEqual zero n = true
lessOrEqual (suc m) zero = false
lessOrEqual (suc m) (suc n) = lessOrEqual m n

_++_ :
  {A : Set} ->
  List A ->
  List A ->
  List A
[] ++ ys = ys
(x ∷ xs) ++ ys = x ∷ (xs ++ ys)

mapList :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  List A ->
  List B
mapList function [] = []
mapList function (x ∷ xs) =
  function x ∷ mapList function xs

prependX : List Symbol -> List Symbol
prependX string =
  X ∷ string

prependO : List Symbol -> List Symbol
prependO string =
  O ∷ string

allStrings : Nat -> List (List Symbol)
allStrings zero =
  [] ∷ []
allStrings (suc n) =
  mapList prependX (allStrings n) ++
  mapList prependO (allStrings n)

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

withinTwo :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Bool
withinTwo x-count o-count =
  lessOrEqual x-count (o-count + two) and
  lessOrEqual o-count (x-count + two)

allPrefixesWithinTwoFrom :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  List Symbol ->
  Bool
allPrefixesWithinTwoFrom x-count o-count [] =
  true
allPrefixesWithinTwoFrom x-count o-count (X ∷ string) =
  withinTwo (suc x-count) o-count and
  allPrefixesWithinTwoFrom (suc x-count) o-count string
allPrefixesWithinTwoFrom x-count o-count (O ∷ string) =
  withinTwo x-count (suc o-count) and
  allPrefixesWithinTwoFrom x-count (suc o-count) string

allPrefixesWithinTwo :
  List Symbol ->
  Bool
allPrefixesWithinTwo =
  allPrefixesWithinTwoFrom zero zero

balanced : List Symbol -> Bool
balanced [] =
  true
balanced string@(_ ∷ tail) =
  allPrefixesWithinTwo string and
  balanced tail

filterList :
  {A : Set} ->
  (A -> Bool) ->
  List A ->
  List A
filterList predicate [] =
  []
filterList predicate (x ∷ xs) with predicate x
... | true =
  x ∷ filterList predicate xs
... | false =
  filterList predicate xs

length :
  {A : Set} ->
  List A ->
  Nat
length [] =
  zero
length (_ ∷ xs) =
  suc (length xs)

numberOfBalancedStrings :
  Nat ->
  Nat
numberOfBalancedStrings n =
  length (filterList balanced (allStrings n))

naturalDiv : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero =
  zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

power : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
power base zero =
  one
power base (suc exponent) =
  base * power base exponent

putnam-1996-b5-solution :
  Nat ->
  Nat
putnam-1996-b5-solution n =
  power two (naturalDiv (n + two) two) +
  power two (naturalDiv (n + one) two) -
  two

putnam-1996-b5 : Set
putnam-1996-b5 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  numberOfBalancedStrings n == putnam-1996-b5-solution n

  the number of length-n two-symbol strings whose every consecutive substring
  has symbol-count imbalance at most two. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_1996_b5 =

      let balanced =
        \s : num -> bool.
          !a b : num.
            a < n /\ b < n /\ a <= b
            ==>
            (CARD {i : num | a <= i /\ i <= b /\ s i} <=
               CARD {i : num | a <= i /\ i <= b /\ ~s i} + 2 /\

      in

          {s : num -> bool |

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1996_b5: the number of length-n sign strings whose every consecutive
  substring has signed sum between negative two and two. This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The ordinal interval 0 ..^ n is the n-element carrier representing Fin n,
  and { -u 1 , 1 } is the integer-unit codomain representing the symbols O
  and X. For endpoints a <= b, the inclusive interval a ... b and the finite
  sum give exactly the source value Delta(S[a..b]).

  The restricted class therefore contains exactly the balanced strings from
  the Lean source. It is also in bijection with the Isabelle representation
  by extending each finite string with False outside 0 ..^ n. The right-hand
  side is the resolved closed form recorded in the Lean annotation and stated
  explicitly in the Rocq source. The final declaration is an unproved $a
  statement, and this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a b i n s $.

  putnambench-putnam-1996-b5 $a |- A. n e. NN0
    (
      #
      `
      {
        s e. ( { -u 1 , 1 } ^m ( 0 ..^ n ) ) |
        A. a e. ( 0 ..^ n ) A. b e. ( 0 ..^ n )
          (
            a <_ b
            ->
            (
              ( -u 2 )
              <_
              sum_ i e. ( a ... b ) ( s ` i )
              /\
              (
                sum_ i e. ( a ... b ) ( s ` i )
              )
              <_
              2
            )
          )
      }
    )
    =
    (
      (
        ( 2 ^ ( |_ ` ( ( n + 2 ) / 2 ) ) )
        +
        ( 2 ^ ( |_ ` ( ( n + 1 ) / 2 ) ) )
      )
      -
      2
    )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1996_b5:
% the number of length-n Boolean strings whose every consecutive substring has
% symbol imbalance between -2 and 2 has the stated formula. This file contains
% no proof.

putnam_1996_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  bit_string: TYPE = [nat -> bool]

  IMPORTING finite_sets[bit_string]

  interval_delta(
      S: bit_string,
      start, count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      interval_delta(S, start, count - 1)
        + IF S(start + count - 1) THEN 1 ELSE -1 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  zero_extended_to_length(S: bit_string, n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index >= n IMPLIES NOT S(index)

  balanced_to_length(S: bit_string, n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (first, last: nat):
      first <= last AND last < n IMPLIES
        -2 <= interval_delta(S, first, last - first + 1)
          AND interval_delta(S, first, last - first + 1) <= 2

  nat_subtract(n, k: nat): nat =
    IF n >= k THEN n - k ELSE 0 ENDIF

  putnam_1996_b5_solution(n: nat): nat =
    nat_subtract(
      2 ^ ndiv(n + 2, 2) + 2 ^ ndiv(n + 1, 2),
      2)

  putnam_1996_b5: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      EXISTS (solutions: finite_set[bit_string]):
        card(solutions) = putnam_1996_b5_solution(n)
          AND (FORALL (S: bit_string):
            solutions(S) IFF
              balanced_to_length(S, n)
                AND zero_extended_to_length(S, n))
END putnam_1996_b5

Theorem putnam_1997_a3
    (evenfact := fix even_fact (n : nat) : R :=
        match n with
        | O => 1 
        | S n' => (2 * INR n) * even_fact n'
    end)

    (f : R -> R := fun x => Series (fun n => pow (-1) n * pow x (2 * n + 1) / evenfact n))
    (g : R -> R := fun x => Series (fun n => pow x (2 * n) / evenfactsqr n))
    : Lim_seq (fun t : nat => RInt (fun x => f x * g x) 0 (INR t)) = putnam_1997_a3_solution.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_a3:
;; the improper integral of the product of the specified two real power
;; series converges to sqrt(exp(1)). This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

(defun putnam-1997-a3-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n
       (putnam-1997-a3-factorial (- n 1)))))

;; These exact rational prefixes are the two source power series. Their
;; denominators are respectively
;;
;;   product_(i<n) 2(i+1)       = 2^n n!
;;   product_(i<n) (2(i+1))^2   = (2^n n!)^2.

(defun putnam-1997-a3-series1-prefix (x terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let ((index (- terms 1)))
      (+ (putnam-1997-a3-series1-prefix x index)
         (/ (* (expt -1 index)
               (expt x (+ (* 2 index) 1)))
            (* (expt 2 index)
               (putnam-1997-a3-factorial index)))))))

(defun putnam-1997-a3-series2-prefix (x terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (even-factorial
            (* (expt 2 index)
               (putnam-1997-a3-factorial index))))
      (+ (putnam-1997-a3-series2-prefix x index)
         (/ (expt x (* 2 index))
            (* even-factorial even-factorial))))))

(defun putnam-1997-a3-integrand-prefix (x terms)
  (* (putnam-1997-a3-series1-prefix x terms)
     (putnam-1997-a3-series2-prefix x terms)))

;; A midpoint sum with rational endpoint UPPER. As PARTITIONS and TERMS tend
;; to infinity, compact-uniform convergence of the two power series makes
;; this converge to the source integral on [0, UPPER].

(defun putnam-1997-a3-midpoint-sum-aux
    (upper partitions terms points)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix points)))
  (if (zp points)
      0
    (let* ((index (- points 1))
           (midpoint
            (/ (* upper (+ (* 2 index) 1))
               (* 2 partitions))))
      (+ (putnam-1997-a3-midpoint-sum-aux
          upper partitions terms index)
         (putnam-1997-a3-integrand-prefix
          midpoint terms)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a3-integral-prefix
    (upper partitions terms)
  (if (and (rationalp upper)
           (posp partitions)
           (natp terms))
      (* (/ upper partitions)
         (putnam-1997-a3-midpoint-sum-aux
          upper partitions terms partitions))
    0))

;; The Rocq ground truth identifies the answer as sqrt(exp(1)). Its positive
;; value is exp(1/2), represented here by exact rational Taylor prefixes.

(defun putnam-1997-a3-solution-prefix (terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let ((index (- terms 1)))
      (+ (putnam-1997-a3-solution-prefix index)
         (/ (expt (/ 1 2) index)
            (putnam-1997-a3-factorial index))))))

;; For a fixed rational upper endpoint, this is the simultaneous tail
;; condition for the midpoint partitions, the two source power-series
;; prefixes (which share SERIES-TERMS), and the exp(1/2) solution prefix.
;; It is not a bounded approximation: every index at or beyond CUTOFF is
;; universally quantified.  Thus this is the epsilon definition that the
;; three rational Cauchy nets have one common real limit.

(defun-sk putnam-1997-a3-approximation-tail-p
    (epsilon upper cutoff)
  (forall (partitions series-terms solution-terms)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp partitions)
      (natp cutoff)
      (<= cutoff partitions)
      (natp series-terms)
      (<= cutoff series-terms)
      (natp solution-terms)
      (<= cutoff solution-terms))
     (<
      (abs
       (- (putnam-1997-a3-integral-prefix
           upper partitions series-terms)
          (putnam-1997-a3-solution-prefix
           solution-terms)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-1997-a3-approximation-cutoff-exists-p
    (epsilon upper)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (putnam-1997-a3-approximation-tail-p
      epsilon upper cutoff))))

;; Positive rational tolerances are cofinal in the positive reals. Rational
;; upper endpoints are cofinal at +infinity, and continuity of the integrand
;; makes their improper-integral limit equivalent to the source real-endpoint
;; limit. The quantifier order below is the nested source limit: after choosing
;; an eventual upper threshold, each later endpoint has its own eventual
;; approximation threshold.  The exp(1/2) prefix is an exact Cauchy
;; representative of sqrt(exp(1)), not a replacement by one finite prefix.

(defun-sk putnam-1997-a3-improper-tail-p
    (epsilon upper-cutoff)
  (forall (upper)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp upper)
      (<= upper-cutoff upper))
     (putnam-1997-a3-approximation-cutoff-exists-p
      epsilon upper))))

(defun-sk putnam-1997-a3-improper-cutoff-exists-p
    (epsilon)
  (exists (upper-cutoff)
    (and
     (rationalp upper-cutoff)
     (putnam-1997-a3-improper-tail-p
      epsilon upper-cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-1997-a3-statement ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-1997-a3-improper-cutoff-exists-p
      epsilon))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_a3:
-- the improper integral of the product of two specified real power series
-- equals the nonnegative square root of exp(1). This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  suc zero
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

alternatingPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingPower reals n =
  naturalPower reals
    (negate reals (oneR reals))
    n

evenFactor :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
evenFactor reals zero =
  oneR reals
evenFactor reals (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (fromNat reals (twoN * suc n))
    (evenFactor reals n)

evenFactorSquare :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
evenFactorSquare reals zero =
  oneR reals
evenFactorSquare reals (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals
      (fromNat reals (twoN * suc n))
      twoN)
    (evenFactorSquare reals n)

firstSeriesTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
firstSeriesTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (suc (twoN * n))))
    (evenFactor reals n)

secondSeriesTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
secondSeriesTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x (twoN * n))
    (evenFactorSquare reals n)

exponentialTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

record StandardRealAnalysis
  (R : Set) :
  Set1 where

  field
    algebra :
      CompleteOrderedRealField R
    exponential squareRoot :
      R -> R

    exponential-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum algebra
        (exponentialTerm algebra x)
        (exponential x)
    exponential-positive :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess algebra
        (zeroR algebra)
        (exponential x)

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) x ->
      lessOrEqual algebra
        (zeroR algebra)
        (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual algebra (zeroR algebra) x ->
      multiply algebra
        (squareRoot x)
        (squareRoot x)
      ==
      x

open StandardRealAnalysis

rightRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
rightRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals (suc i))
              step)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function value =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      rightRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    value

ImproperIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ImproperIntegralValue {R} reals function limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ threshold ->
      (upper : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals threshold upper ->
      Exists R
        (\ integralValue ->
          IntervalIntegralValue reals
            (zeroR reals)
            upper
            function
            integralValue
          and
          CloseTo reals limit epsilon integralValue))

module Putnam1997A3Statement
  {R : Set}
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R)
  (series1 series2 : R -> R) where

  reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R
  reals =
    algebra analysis

  integrand : R -> R
  integrand x =
    multiply reals
      (series1 x)
      (series2 x)

  solution : R
  solution =
    squareRoot analysis
      (exponential analysis (oneR reals))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    ((x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (firstSeriesTerm reals x)
        (series1 x))
    ->
    ((x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (secondSeriesTerm reals x)
        (series2 x))
    ->
    ImproperIntegralValue reals
      integrand
      solution

putnam-1997-a3 : Set1
putnam-1997-a3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis R) ->
  (series1 series2 : R -> R) ->
  Putnam1997A3Statement.proposition
    analysis
    series1
    series2

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_a3:
  the improper integral of the product of two specified real power series
  equals the square root of exp 1. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_topologyTheory seqTheory;
open transcTheory integrationTheory;

val putnam_1997_a3 =
  ``let even_factorial =
      \n : num. (2 : real) pow n * &(FACT n)
    in
    let series1 =
      \x : real.
        suminf
          (\n : num.
             (~1 : real) pow n * x pow (2 * n + 1) /
             even_factorial n)
    in
    let series2 =
      \x : real.
        suminf
          (\n : num.
             x pow (2 * n) / (even_factorial n) pow 2)
    in
      ((\t : real.
          integration$integral (interval [0, t])
            (\x : real. series1 x * series2 x)) -->
        sqrt (exp 1))
        at_posinfinity``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1997_a3: evaluation of the improper real integral of the product of
  two factorial-denominator power series as sqrt(exp(1)). This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  f and g are arbitrary total real functions constrained to be the two
  source power series. The half-open index set 0 ..^ n is {0,...,n-1}, so
  the finite products are respectively 2 * 4 * ... * (2n) and its
  termwise square, including the empty product at n = 0.

  The sum over NN0 is set.mm's convergent infinite real-series sum, and S.
  is its real Lebesgue integral. The epsilon-threshold conclusion is the
  real at-positive-infinity limit of the integrals over [0,t]. Its target is
  the explicit Rocq solution and the value recorded in the Lean and Isabelle
  annotations. The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus
  statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d e f g i m n t x $.

  putnambench-putnam-1997-a3 $a |-
    A. f e. ( RR ^m RR )
    A. g e. ( RR ^m RR )
      (
        (
          f
          =
          (
            x e. RR |->
              sum_ n e. NN0
                (
                  (
                    ( ( -u 1 ) ^ n )
                    x.
                    ( x ^ ( ( 2 x. n ) + 1 ) )
                  )
                  /
                  (
                    prod_ i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                      ( 2 x. ( i + 1 ) )
                  )
                )
          )
          /\
          g
          =
          (
            x e. RR |->
              sum_ n e. NN0
                (
                  ( x ^ ( 2 x. n ) )
                  /
                  (
                    prod_ i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                      ( ( 2 x. ( i + 1 ) ) ^ 2 )
                  )
                )
          )
        )
        ->
        A. e e. RR
          (
            0 < e
            ->
            E. m e. RR
              A. t e. RR
                (
                  m <_ t
                  ->
                  (
                    abs
                    `
                    (
                      (
                        S. ( 0 [,] t )
                          ( ( f ` x ) x. ( g ` x ) )
                          _d x
                      )
                      -
                      ( sqrt ` ( exp ` 1 ) )
                    )
                  )
                  <
                  e
                )
          )
      )
  $.
$}

:: the improper integral of the product of two specified real power series
:: converges to sqrt(exp(1)). This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    PARTFUN1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, COMPLEX1, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1,

    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    REAL_1, COMPLEX1, SQUARE_1, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1, XXREAL_3,
    NEWTON, NAT_1, SEQ_1, SEQ_2, COMSEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4, PREPOWER,
    SERIES_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, SIN_COS, SUPINF_2, MEASURE1,
    MESFUNC1, MESFUNC5, MESFUNC6, MEASUR12, INTEGRA5, EXTREAL1,
    LIMFUNC1;
  constructors FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1, REAL_1, COMPLEX1,
    SQUARE_1, NAT_1, NEWTON, SEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4, PREPOWER,
    COMSEQ_2, SERIES_1, SIN_COS, MESFUNC1, MESFUNC5, MESFUNC6,
    MEASUR12, INTEGRA5, EXTREAL1, LIMFUNC1, BINOP_2;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, NAT_1, NEWTON, PREPOWER,
    SEQ_4, SQUARE_1, XXREAL_3, MEASURE1, MEASUR12, SIN_COS;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  definitions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0;
  expansions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for evenfact,evenfactsqr being Real_Sequence,
      series1,series2,F being Function of REAL,REAL st
    evenfact.0 = 1 &
    (for n being Nat holds
      evenfact.(n+1) =
        (2 * ((n+1) qua Real)) * evenfact.n) &
    evenfactsqr.0 = 1 &
    (for n being Nat holds
      evenfactsqr.(n+1) =
        ((2 * ((n+1) qua Real)) |^ 2) * evenfactsqr.n) &
    (for x being Real holds
      ex s being Real_Sequence st
        (for n being Nat holds
          s.n =
            (((-1) qua Real) |^ n) * (x |^ (2*n+1)) /
              evenfact.n) &
        series1.x = lim Partial_Sums(s)) &
    (for x being Real holds
      ex s being Real_Sequence st
        (for n being Nat holds
          s.n = (x |^ (2*n)) / evenfactsqr.n) &
        series2.x = lim Partial_Sums(s)) &
    (for t being Real st 0 <= t holds
      ex I being Subset of REAL,
         h being Function of REAL,REAL st
        I = {x where x is Real : 0 <= x & x <= t} &
        (for x being Real st x in I holds
          h.x = series1.x * series2.x) &
        F.t = Integral(L-Meas,h|I))
  holds
    F is convergent_in+infty &
    lim_in+infty F = sqrt (exp_R.1)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_1997_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_a3:
% the improper integral of the product of two specified real power series
% equals the nonnegative square root of exp(1). This file contains no proof.

putnam_1997_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  even_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      2 * (index :: real) * even_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  even_factorial_squared(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      (2 * (index :: real)) ^ 2
        * even_factorial_squared(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  first_series_term(x: real, index: nat): real =
    safe_div(
      alternating_sign(index) * x ^ (2 * index + 1),
      even_factorial(index))

  second_series_term(x: real, index: nat): real =
    safe_div(
      x ^ (2 * index),
      even_factorial_squared(index))

  first_series_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      first_series_partial(x, count - 1)
        + first_series_term(x, count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  second_series_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      second_series_partial(x, count - 1)
        + second_series_term(x, count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  first_power_series(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            first_series_partial(x, count),
          value))

  second_power_series(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            second_series_partial(x, count),
          value))

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  nonnegative_square_root(x: real): real =
    IF x >= 0 THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (root: real):
          root >= 0 AND root * root = x)
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  valid_tagged_partition(
      left, right: real,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = left
      AND points(count) = right
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          (points(index) < points(index + 1)
            AND points(index) <= tags(index)
            AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1))

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      function_value: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(
        function_value, points, tags, count - 1)
        + function_value(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_interval_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      left, right, integral_value: real): bool =
    left < right
      AND FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
          FORALL
              (points, tags: real_sequence),
              (count: nat):
            (valid_tagged_partition(
                left, right, points, tags, count)
              AND mesh_less_than(
                points, count, mesh_bound))
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                riemann_sum(
                  function_value, points, tags, count)
                  - integral_value)
                < epsilon_value

  interval_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      left, right: real): real =
    IF left = right THEN
      0
    ELSIF left < right THEN
      IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
          has_interval_integral(
            function_value, left, right, integral_value)
      THEN
        epsilon(
          LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
            has_interval_integral(
              function_value, left, right, integral_value))
      ELSE
        0
      ENDIF
    ELSE
      IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
          has_interval_integral(
            function_value, right, left, integral_value)
      THEN
        -epsilon(
          LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
            has_interval_integral(
              function_value, right, left, integral_value))
      ELSE
        0
      ENDIF
    ENDIF

  truncated_integral(
      series1, series2: real_function,
      t: real): real =
    interval_integral(
      LAMBDA (x: real): series1(x) * series2(x),
      0,
      t)

  converges_at_real_top(
      function_value: real_function,
      limit_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: real):
        FORALL (t: real):
          cutoff <= t IMPLIES
            abs(function_value(t) - limit_value)
              < epsilon_value

  putnam_1997_a3_solution: real =
    nonnegative_square_root(real_exponential(1))

  putnam_1997_a3: bool =
    FORALL (series1, series2: real_function):
      ((FORALL (x: real):
          series1(x) = first_power_series(x))
        AND (FORALL (x: real):
          series2(x) = second_power_series(x)))
      IMPLIES
        converges_at_real_top(
          LAMBDA (t: real):
            truncated_integral(series1, series2, t),
          putnam_1997_a3_solution)
END putnam_1997_a3

title: putnam_1997_a4
content:
(* Statement-only formalization over an arbitrary group. *)

Record putnam_1997_a4_group (G : Type) : Type := {
  putnam_1997_a4_mul : G -> G -> G;
  putnam_1997_a4_one : G;
  putnam_1997_a4_inv : G -> G;
  putnam_1997_a4_assoc :
    forall x y z : G,
      putnam_1997_a4_mul x (putnam_1997_a4_mul y z) =
      putnam_1997_a4_mul (putnam_1997_a4_mul x y) z;
  putnam_1997_a4_left_identity :
    forall x : G, putnam_1997_a4_mul putnam_1997_a4_one x = x;
  putnam_1997_a4_right_identity :
    forall x : G, putnam_1997_a4_mul x putnam_1997_a4_one = x;
  putnam_1997_a4_left_inverse :
    forall x : G,
      putnam_1997_a4_mul (putnam_1997_a4_inv x) x =
      putnam_1997_a4_one;
  putnam_1997_a4_right_inverse :
    forall x : G,
      putnam_1997_a4_mul x (putnam_1997_a4_inv x) =
      putnam_1997_a4_one
}.

Arguments putnam_1997_a4_mul {G} _ _ _.
Arguments putnam_1997_a4_one {G} _.

Theorem putnam_1997_a4
    (G : Type)
    (grp : putnam_1997_a4_group G)
    (f : G -> G)
    (hf : forall g1 g2 g3 h1 h2 h3 : G,
      (putnam_1997_a4_mul grp
         (putnam_1997_a4_mul grp g1 g2) g3 =
         putnam_1997_a4_one grp /\
       putnam_1997_a4_mul grp
         (putnam_1997_a4_mul grp h1 h2) h3 =
         putnam_1997_a4_one grp) ->
      putnam_1997_a4_mul grp
        (putnam_1997_a4_mul grp (f g1) (f g2)) (f g3) =
      putnam_1997_a4_mul grp
        (putnam_1997_a4_mul grp (f h1) (f h2)) (f h3)) :
  exists a : G,
    let psi := fun g => putnam_1997_a4_mul grp a (f g) in
    forall x y : G,
      psi (putnam_1997_a4_mul grp x y) =
      putnam_1997_a4_mul grp (psi x) (psi y).
Admitted.

title: putnam_1997_a4
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_a4:
  a triple-product invariance condition on a self-map of an arbitrary group
  implies that a left translate of the map is a homomorphism. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let is_group =
     \(mul:G->G->G) (identity:G) (ginv:G->G).
       (!x y z:G. mul (mul x y) z = mul x (mul y z)) /\
       (!x:G. mul identity x = x /\ mul x identity = x) /\
       (!x:G.
          mul (ginv x) x = identity /\ mul x (ginv x) = identity) in
   !mul:G->G->G identity:G ginv:G->G phi:G->G.
     is_group mul identity ginv /\
     (!g1 g2 g3 h1 h2 h3:G.
        mul (mul g1 g2) g3 = identity /\
        mul (mul h1 h2) h3 = identity
        ==> mul (mul (phi g1) (phi g2)) (phi g3) =
            mul (mul (phi h1) (phi h2)) (phi h3))
     ==> ?a:G.
           !x y:G.
             mul a (phi (mul x y)) =
             mul (mul a (phi x)) (mul a (phi y))`;;

title: putnam_1997_a4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_a4:
;; a function on an arbitrary group whose triple product is constant on
;; triples multiplying to the identity can be left-translated into a group
;; homomorphism. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; CARRIER, OP, INV, and PHI are ACL2 function objects. Generated predicate
;; lambdas return T outside CARRIER, so FN-EQUAL against a constant-T lambda
;; expresses universal quantification over exactly the represented group.

(defun putnam-1997-a4-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-1997-a4-quoted function)
        (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-1997-a4-quoted function)
        (list 'cons left
              (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-1997-a4-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-operation-term (op left right)
  (putnam-1997-a4-apply2-term op left right))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-inverse-term (inv element)
  (putnam-1997-a4-apply1-term inv element))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-phi-term (phi element)
  (putnam-1997-a4-apply1-term phi element))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-all-in-carrier-term
    (carrier variables)
  (if (endp variables)
      (putnam-1997-a4-quoted t)
    (list 'if
          (putnam-1997-a4-carrier-term
           carrier (car variables))
          (putnam-1997-a4-all-in-carrier-term
           carrier (cdr variables))
          (putnam-1997-a4-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-restricted-predicate-term
    (carrier variables proposition)
  (list 'if
        (putnam-1997-a4-all-in-carrier-term
         carrier variables)
        proposition
        (putnam-1997-a4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-and-term (left right)
  (list 'if left right (putnam-1997-a4-quoted nil)))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list 'if hypothesis conclusion (putnam-1997-a4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda formals (putnam-1997-a4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-operation-closure-function (carrier op)
  (let ((op-xy
         (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op 'x 'y)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y)
     (putnam-1997-a4-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x y)
      (putnam-1997-a4-carrier-term carrier op-xy)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-inverse-closure-function (carrier inv)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(x)
   (putnam-1997-a4-restricted-predicate-term
    carrier
    '(x)
    (putnam-1997-a4-carrier-term
     carrier
     (putnam-1997-a4-inverse-term inv 'x)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-associative-function (carrier op)
  (let* ((op-xy
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op 'x 'y))
         (op-yz
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op 'y 'z)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y z)
     (putnam-1997-a4-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x y z)
      (list
       'equal
       (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op op-xy 'z)
       (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op 'x op-yz))))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-identity-function (carrier op one)
  (let ((left
         (list
          'equal
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term
           op (putnam-1997-a4-quoted one) 'x)
          'x))
        (right
         (list
          'equal
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term
           op 'x (putnam-1997-a4-quoted one))
          'x)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-1997-a4-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x)
      (putnam-1997-a4-and-term left right)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-inverse-law-function
    (carrier op inv one)
  (let* ((inv-x
          (putnam-1997-a4-inverse-term inv 'x))
         (left
          (list
           'equal
           (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op inv-x 'x)
           (putnam-1997-a4-quoted one)))
         (right
          (list
           'equal
           (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op 'x inv-x)
           (putnam-1997-a4-quoted one))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-1997-a4-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x)
      (putnam-1997-a4-and-term left right)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-phi-closure-function (carrier phi)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(x)
   (putnam-1997-a4-restricted-predicate-term
    carrier
    '(x)
    (putnam-1997-a4-carrier-term
     carrier
     (putnam-1997-a4-phi-term phi 'x)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-member-p (carrier element)
  (apply$ carrier (list element)))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-group-p (carrier op inv one)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp op)
   (tamep-functionp inv)
   (putnam-1997-a4-member-p carrier one)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1997-a4-operation-closure-function carrier op)
    (putnam-1997-a4-true-function '(x y)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1997-a4-inverse-closure-function carrier inv)
    (putnam-1997-a4-true-function '(x)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1997-a4-associative-function carrier op)
    (putnam-1997-a4-true-function '(x y z)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1997-a4-identity-function carrier op one)
    (putnam-1997-a4-true-function '(x)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1997-a4-inverse-law-function carrier op inv one)
    (putnam-1997-a4-true-function '(x)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-phi-closed-p (carrier phi)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp phi)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-1997-a4-phi-closure-function carrier phi)
    (putnam-1997-a4-true-function '(x)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-triple-invariance-function
    (carrier op one phi)
  (let* ((g12
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op 'g1 'g2))
         (g123
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op g12 'g3))
         (h12
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op 'h1 'h2))
         (h123
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op h12 'h3))
         (phi-g1
          (putnam-1997-a4-phi-term phi 'g1))
         (phi-g2
          (putnam-1997-a4-phi-term phi 'g2))
         (phi-g3
          (putnam-1997-a4-phi-term phi 'g3))
         (phi-h1
          (putnam-1997-a4-phi-term phi 'h1))
         (phi-h2
          (putnam-1997-a4-phi-term phi 'h2))
         (phi-h3
          (putnam-1997-a4-phi-term phi 'h3))
         (phi-g12
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term
           op phi-g1 phi-g2))
         (phi-g123
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term
           op phi-g12 phi-g3))
         (phi-h12
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term
           op phi-h1 phi-h2))
         (phi-h123
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term
           op phi-h12 phi-h3))
         (both-products-one
          (putnam-1997-a4-and-term
           (list 'equal
                 g123
                 (putnam-1997-a4-quoted one))
           (list 'equal
                 h123
                 (putnam-1997-a4-quoted one)))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(g1 g2 g3 h1 h2 h3)
     (putnam-1997-a4-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(g1 g2 g3 h1 h2 h3)
      (putnam-1997-a4-implies-term
       both-products-one
       (list 'equal phi-g123 phi-h123))))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-triple-invariance-p
    (carrier op one phi)
  (fn-equal
   (putnam-1997-a4-triple-invariance-function
    carrier op one phi)
   (putnam-1997-a4-true-function
    '(g1 g2 g3 h1 h2 h3))))

;; If x |-> a*PHI(x) is a homomorphism, its value at the identity is the
;; identity, so necessarily a = inverse(PHI(one)). Thus the source existential
;; is equivalent to checking the following uniquely determined witness.

(defun putnam-1997-a4-homomorphism-function
    (carrier op inv one phi)
  (let* ((phi-one
          (putnam-1997-a4-phi-term
           phi (putnam-1997-a4-quoted one)))
         (a
          (putnam-1997-a4-inverse-term inv phi-one))
         (xy
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op 'x 'y))
         (phi-xy
          (putnam-1997-a4-phi-term phi xy))
         (phi-x
          (putnam-1997-a4-phi-term phi 'x))
         (phi-y
          (putnam-1997-a4-phi-term phi 'y))
         (left
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op a phi-xy))
         (translated-x
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op a phi-x))
         (translated-y
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term op a phi-y))
         (right
          (putnam-1997-a4-operation-term
           op translated-x translated-y)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y)
     (putnam-1997-a4-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(x y)
      (list 'equal left right)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a4-explicit-witness-homomorphism-p
    (carrier op inv one phi)
  (fn-equal
   (putnam-1997-a4-homomorphism-function
    carrier op inv one phi)
   (putnam-1997-a4-true-function '(x y))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1997-a4-statement
    (carrier op inv one phi)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-1997-a4-group-p carrier op inv one)
    (putnam-1997-a4-phi-closed-p carrier phi)
    (putnam-1997-a4-triple-invariance-p
     carrier op one phi))
   (putnam-1997-a4-explicit-witness-homomorphism-p
    carrier op inv one phi)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1997_a4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_a4:
-- a function on an arbitrary group whose triple products agree whenever both
-- input triples multiply to the identity can be left-translated into a group
-- homomorphism. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc; _⊔_)

infixr 3 _and_

record _and_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists
  {a p : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (property : A -> Set p) :
  Set (a ⊔ p) where

  constructor witness
  field
    value     : A
    satisfies : property value

record Group
  {ell : Level}
  (G : Set ell) :
  Set ell where

  field
    identity       : G
    inverse        : G -> G
    multiply       : G -> G -> G
    associative    : (x y z : G) ->
                     multiply (multiply x y) z ==
                     multiply x (multiply y z)
    identity-left  : (x : G) -> multiply identity x == x

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1997_a4:
% an arbitrary group and a self-map whose product is constant on triples
% with identity product admit a left translate that is a homomorphism.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_1997_a4[
  Element: TYPE+,
  multiply: [Element, Element -> Element],
  inverse: [Element -> Element],
  one: Element,
  phi: [Element -> Element]
]: THEORY
BEGIN
  group_laws: bool =
    (FORALL (x, y, z: Element):
      multiply(multiply(x, y), z)
        = multiply(x, multiply(y, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x: Element):
        multiply(one, x) = x
          AND multiply(x, one) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x: Element):
        multiply(inverse(x), x) = one
          AND multiply(x, inverse(x)) = one)

  triple_product_invariant: bool =
    FORALL (g1, g2, g3, h1, h2, h3: Element):
      (multiply(multiply(g1, g2), g3) = one
        AND multiply(multiply(h1, h2), h3) = one)
      IMPLIES
        multiply(multiply(phi(g1), phi(g2)), phi(g3))
          = multiply(multiply(phi(h1), phi(h2)), phi(h3))

  putnam_1997_a4: bool =
    (group_laws AND triple_product_invariant)
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (a: Element):
          FORALL (x, y: Element):
            multiply(a, phi(multiply(x, y)))
              = multiply(
                  multiply(a, phi(x)),
                  multiply(a, phi(y)))
END putnam_1997_a4

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_a5:
;; the number of ordered 10-tuples of positive integers whose reciprocals sum
;; to one is odd. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-1997-a5-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (natp n)
      (if (zp n)
          1
        (* n
           (putnam-1997-a5-factorial (- n 1))))
    1))

;; Every ordered solution has a unique nondecreasing rearrangement. If K
;; entries remain and their reciprocal sum is R, the next denominator A in a
;; nondecreasing tuple satisfies R <= K/A, hence A <= floor(K/R). The search
;; therefore enumerates every sorted solution exactly once without imposing
;; an external finite cutoff. SYMMETRY-DIVISOR is the product of factorials
;; of the multiplicities seen so far, so each leaf contributes exactly the
;; number 10!/SYMMETRY-DIVISOR of distinct ordered rearrangements.
(defun putnam-1997-a5-count-sorted-range
    (remaining slots previous candidate maximum
               run-length symmetry-divisor)
  (declare
   (xargs
    :measure
    (make-ord
     1
     (+ 1 (nfix slots))
     (nfix (+ 1 (- maximum candidate))))
    :well-founded-relation o<))
  (if (and (rationalp remaining)
           (natp slots)
           (natp previous)
           (posp candidate)
           (natp maximum)
           (natp run-length)
           (posp symmetry-divisor))
      (if (zp slots)
          (if (equal remaining 0)
              (/ (putnam-1997-a5-factorial 10)
                 symmetry-divisor)
            0)
        (if (or (<= remaining 0)
                (> candidate maximum))
            0
          (let* ((next-remaining
                  (- remaining (/ candidate)))
                 (next-slots (- slots 1))
                 (same-denominator
                  (equal candidate previous))
                 (next-run-length
                  (if same-denominator
                      (+ run-length 1)
                    1))
                 (next-symmetry-divisor
                  (if same-denominator
                      (* symmetry-divisor
                         (+ run-length 1))
                    symmetry-divisor))
                 (next-maximum
                  (if (and (posp next-slots)
                           (< 0 next-remaining))
                      (floor next-slots next-remaining)
                    0)))
            (+
             (putnam-1997-a5-count-sorted-range
              next-remaining
              next-slots
              candidate
              candidate
              next-maximum
              next-run-length
              next-symmetry-divisor)
             (putnam-1997-a5-count-sorted-range
              remaining
              slots
              previous
              (+ candidate 1)
              maximum
              run-length
              symmetry-divisor)))))
    0))

(defun putnam-1997-a5-ordered-solution-count ()
  (putnam-1997-a5-count-sorted-range
   1 10 0 1 10 0 1))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1997-a5-statement ()
  (equal
   (mod (putnam-1997-a5-ordered-solution-count) 2)
   1))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
-- putnambench__agda__putnam_1997_a5: the set of ordered ten-tuples of positive
-- integers whose reciprocals sum to one has odd cardinality. This file contains
-- no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    left-proof  : A
    right-proof : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> item == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

data PositiveNat : Set where
  positive : Nat -> PositiveNat

positiveValue : PositiveNat -> Nat
positiveValue (positive predecessor) =
  suc predecessor

record Tuple10 : Set where
  constructor tuple10
  field
    entry1  : PositiveNat
    entry2  : PositiveNat
    entry3  : PositiveNat
    entry4  : PositiveNat
    entry5  : PositiveNat
    entry6  : PositiveNat
    entry7  : PositiveNat
    entry8  : PositiveNat
    entry9  : PositiveNat
    entry10 : PositiveNat

open Tuple10

record FractionExpression : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator   : Nat
    denominator : Nat

open FractionExpression

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

oneFraction : FractionExpression
oneFraction =
  fraction oneN oneN

reciprocal : PositiveNat -> FractionExpression
reciprocal denominatorValue =
  fraction oneN (positiveValue denominatorValue)

addFraction :
  FractionExpression ->
  FractionExpression ->
  FractionExpression
addFraction left right =
  fraction
    (numerator left * denominator right
     + numerator right * denominator left)
    (denominator left * denominator right)

EquivalentFraction :
  FractionExpression ->
  FractionExpression ->
  Set
EquivalentFraction left right =
  numerator left * denominator right
  ==
  numerator right * denominator left

reciprocalSum : Tuple10 -> FractionExpression
reciprocalSum tuple =
  addFraction
    (reciprocal (entry1 tuple))
    (addFraction
      (reciprocal (entry2 tuple))
      (addFraction
        (reciprocal (entry3 tuple))
        (addFraction
          (reciprocal (entry4 tuple))
          (addFraction
            (reciprocal (entry5 tuple))
            (addFraction
              (reciprocal (entry6 tuple))
              (addFraction
                (reciprocal (entry7 tuple))
                (addFraction
                  (reciprocal (entry8 tuple))
                  (addFraction
                    (reciprocal (entry9 tuple))
                    (reciprocal (entry10 tuple))))))))))

ReciprocalsSumToOne : Tuple10 -> Set
ReciprocalsSumToOne tuple =
  EquivalentFraction
    (reciprocalSum tuple)
    oneFraction

Odd : Nat -> Set
Odd cardinality =
  Exists Nat
    (\ k -> cardinality == suc (twoN * k))

OddCardinality :
  {A : Set} ->
  (A -> Set) ->
  Set
OddCardinality member =
  Exists Nat
    (\ cardinality ->
      HasCardinality member cardinality
      and
      Odd cardinality)

putnam-1997-a5 : Set
putnam-1997-a5 =
  OddCardinality ReciprocalsSumToOne

    : forall (k: nat), (le 1 k /\ le k n) -> X maxc k = putnam_1997_a6_solution n k.
Proof. Admitted.

theory putnam_1997_a6 imports Complex_Main

begin

definition putnam_1997_a6_solution :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> real" where
"putnam_1997_a6_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* \<lambda> n k. (n-1) choose (k-1) *)
theorem putnam_1997_a6:
  fixes n :: "nat"
    and C :: "real"
    and x :: "real \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> real)"
    and S :: "real set"
  defines "S \<equiv> {c :: real. x c (n + 1) = 0}"
  assumes hx0 : "\<forall> c :: real. x c 0 = 0"
    and hx1 : "\<forall> c :: real. x c 1 = 1"
    and hxk : "\<forall> (c :: real) (k :: nat). x c (k + 2) = (c * (x c (k+1)) - (n-k) * (x c k))/(k+1)"
    and hC : "C = (GREATEST s. s \<in> S)"
    and hn : "n > 0"
  shows "\<forall> k \<in> {1..n}. x C k = putnam_1997_a6_solution n k"
  sorry

end

putnam_1997_a6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_a6:
;; the recurrence at the greatest real zero of its (n+1)-st term has values
;; choose(n-1,k-1) for 1 <= k <= n. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; For fixed positive natural N, every recurrence term is a rational
;; polynomial in the real parameter c. The source sequence is uniquely
;; determined by x_0=0, x_1=1, and the recurrence, so these polynomials are a
;; definitional encoding of the arbitrary source function x.
;;
;; Every zero of the (N+1)-st polynomial is real algebraic. PRIMITIVE and the
;; rational interval (LOWER,UPPER) represent its isolated algebraic value
;; alpha. Sturm-Tarski queries decide polynomial signs at alpha exactly, while
;; Sturm root counts and a strict Cauchy bound state that alpha is the greatest
;; real zero. Thus this representation ranges over the source's real maximum,
;; not merely ACL2's executable rationals.

;; Rational polynomials use descending coefficient order.

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-p (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (and (rationalp (car polynomial))
           (putnam-1997-a6-rp-p (cdr polynomial)))
    (equal polynomial nil)))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (if (equal (car polynomial) 0)
          (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize (cdr polynomial))
        polynomial)
    nil))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-neg (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons (- (car polynomial))
            (putnam-1997-a6-rp-neg (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-add-raw (left right)
  (declare
   (xargs :measure (+ (acl2-count left) (acl2-count right))))
  (cond
   ((endp left) right)
   ((endp right) left)
   ((< (len left) (len right))
    (cons (car right)
          (putnam-1997-a6-rp-add-raw left (cdr right))))
   ((< (len right) (len left))
    (cons (car left)
          (putnam-1997-a6-rp-add-raw (cdr left) right)))
   (t
    (cons (+ (car left) (car right))
          (putnam-1997-a6-rp-add-raw
           (cdr left) (cdr right))))))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-add (left right)
  (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize
   (putnam-1997-a6-rp-add-raw left right)))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-sub (left right)
  (putnam-1997-a6-rp-add
   left (putnam-1997-a6-rp-neg right)))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-scale (scalar polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons (* scalar (car polynomial))
            (putnam-1997-a6-rp-scale scalar (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-zeroes (count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons 0 (putnam-1997-a6-zeroes (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-scale-shift
    (scalar polynomial shift)
  (append
   (putnam-1997-a6-rp-scale scalar polynomial)
   (putnam-1997-a6-zeroes shift)))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-mul-raw (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (putnam-1997-a6-rp-add
       (putnam-1997-a6-rp-scale-shift
        (car left) right (len (cdr left)))
       (putnam-1997-a6-rp-mul-raw (cdr left) right))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-mul (left right)
  (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize
   (putnam-1997-a6-rp-mul-raw left right)))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-eval-aux
    (polynomial value accumulator)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (putnam-1997-a6-rp-eval-aux
       (cdr polynomial)
       value
       (+ (* accumulator value) (car polynomial)))
    accumulator))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-eval (polynomial value)
  (putnam-1997-a6-rp-eval-aux polynomial value 0))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-derivative-aux
    (polynomial degree)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (if (zp degree)
          nil
        (cons
         (* degree (car polynomial))
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-derivative-aux
          (cdr polynomial) (- degree 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-derivative (polynomial)
  (let ((polynomial
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize polynomial)))
    (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize
     (putnam-1997-a6-rp-derivative-aux
      polynomial
      (nfix (- (len polynomial) 1))))))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-rem-fuel
    (dividend divisor fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((dividend
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize dividend))
        (divisor
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize divisor)))
    (if (or (zp fuel)
            (endp divisor)
            (< (len dividend) (len divisor)))
        dividend
      (putnam-1997-a6-rp-rem-fuel
       (putnam-1997-a6-rp-sub
        dividend
        (putnam-1997-a6-rp-scale-shift
         (/ (car dividend) (car divisor))
         divisor
         (- (len dividend) (len divisor))))
       divisor
       (- fuel 1)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-rem (dividend divisor)
  (putnam-1997-a6-rp-rem-fuel
   dividend
   divisor
   (+ 1 (len (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize dividend)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-sturm-tail
    (previous current fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((current
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize current)))
    (if (or (zp fuel) (endp current))
        nil
      (cons
       current
       (putnam-1997-a6-rp-sturm-tail
        current
        (putnam-1997-a6-rp-neg
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-rem previous current))
        (- fuel 1))))))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-sturm-sequence
    (polynomial second)
  (let ((polynomial
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize polynomial))
        (second
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize second)))
    (if (endp polynomial)
        nil
      (cons
       polynomial
       (if (endp second)
           nil
         (cons
          second
          (putnam-1997-a6-rp-sturm-tail
           polynomial
           second
           (+ 1 (len polynomial) (len second)))))))))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rational-sign (value)
  (cond ((< value 0) -1)
        ((< 0 value) 1)
        (t 0)))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-variations-aux
    (polynomials value previous-sign)
  (if (consp polynomials)
      (let ((sign
             (putnam-1997-a6-rational-sign
              (putnam-1997-a6-rp-eval
               (car polynomials) value))))
        (if (equal sign 0)
            (putnam-1997-a6-rp-variations-aux
             (cdr polynomials) value previous-sign)
          (+ (if (and (not (equal previous-sign 0))
                      (not (equal sign previous-sign)))
                 1
               0)
             (putnam-1997-a6-rp-variations-aux
              (cdr polynomials) value sign))))
    0))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-variations
    (polynomials value)
  (putnam-1997-a6-rp-variations-aux
   polynomials value 0))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-cauchy-index
    (polynomial second lower upper)
  (let ((sequence
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-sturm-sequence
          polynomial second)))
    (- (putnam-1997-a6-rp-variations sequence lower)
       (putnam-1997-a6-rp-variations sequence upper))))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-root-count
    (polynomial lower upper)
  (putnam-1997-a6-rp-cauchy-index
   polynomial
   (putnam-1997-a6-rp-derivative polynomial)
   lower
   upper))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-primitive-p
    (primitive lower upper)
  (and
   (putnam-1997-a6-rp-p primitive)
   (consp (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize primitive))
   (rationalp lower)
   (rationalp upper)
   (< lower upper)
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-1997-a6-rp-eval primitive lower)
     0))
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-1997-a6-rp-eval primitive upper)
     0))
   (equal
    (putnam-1997-a6-rp-root-count
     primitive lower upper)
    1)
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-1997-a6-rp-cauchy-index
      primitive
      (putnam-1997-a6-rp-mul
       (putnam-1997-a6-rp-derivative primitive)
       (putnam-1997-a6-rp-derivative primitive))
      lower
      upper)
     0))))

;; For the isolated simple root alpha, this Sturm-Tarski query is the sign of
;; POLYNOMIAL(alpha).
(defun putnam-1997-a6-alg-sign
    (primitive lower upper polynomial)
  (putnam-1997-a6-rp-cauchy-index
   primitive
   (putnam-1997-a6-rp-mul
    (putnam-1997-a6-rp-derivative primitive)
    polynomial)
   lower
   upper))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-alg-zero-p
    (primitive lower upper polynomial)
  (equal
   (putnam-1997-a6-alg-sign
    primitive lower upper polynomial)
   0))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-max-ratio
    (coefficients leading maximum)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (let ((ratio (abs (/ (car coefficients) leading))))
        (putnam-1997-a6-rp-max-ratio
         (cdr coefficients)
         leading
         (if (< maximum ratio) ratio maximum)))
    maximum))

;; Every real zero of a nonconstant nonzero polynomial lies strictly between
;; the negative and positive values of this Cauchy bound.
(defun putnam-1997-a6-rp-root-bound (polynomial)
  (let ((polynomial
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-normalize polynomial)))
    (if (or (endp polynomial) (endp (cdr polynomial)))
        1
      (+ 1
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-max-ratio
          (cdr polynomial) (car polynomial) 0)))))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-recurrence-polynomial (n index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (not (natp index))
      nil
    (cond
     ((equal index 0) nil)
     ((equal index 1) (list 1))
     (t
      (let ((k (- index 2)))
        (putnam-1997-a6-rp-scale
         (/ 1 (+ k 1))
         (putnam-1997-a6-rp-sub
          (putnam-1997-a6-rp-scale-shift
           1
           (putnam-1997-a6-recurrence-polynomial
            n (- index 1))
           1)
          (putnam-1997-a6-rp-scale
           (- n k)
           (putnam-1997-a6-recurrence-polynomial
            n (- index 2))))))))))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-binomial (n k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (cond
   ((or (not (natp n))
        (not (natp k))
        (< n k))
    0)
   ((equal k 0) 1)
   ((equal n 0) 0)
   (t
    (+ (putnam-1997-a6-binomial (- n 1) k)
       (putnam-1997-a6-binomial (- n 1) (- k 1))))))

(defun putnam-1997-a6-greatest-root-p
    (n primitive lower upper)
  (let* ((polynomial
          (putnam-1997-a6-recurrence-polynomial
           n (+ n 1)))
         (bound
          (putnam-1997-a6-rp-root-bound polynomial)))
    (and
     (putnam-1997-a6-primitive-p primitive lower upper)
     (putnam-1997-a6-alg-zero-p
      primitive lower upper polynomial)
     (not
      (equal
       (putnam-1997-a6-rp-eval polynomial lower)
       0))
     (not
      (equal
       (putnam-1997-a6-rp-eval polynomial upper)
       0))
     (equal
      (putnam-1997-a6-rp-root-count
       polynomial lower upper)
      1)
     (< upper bound)
     (not
      (equal
       (putnam-1997-a6-rp-eval polynomial bound)
       0))
     (equal
      (putnam-1997-a6-rp-root-count
       polynomial upper bound)
      0))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1997-a6-statement
    (n k primitive lower upper)
  (implies
   (and
    (posp n)
    (natp k)
    (<= 1 k)
    (<= k n)
    (putnam-1997-a6-greatest-root-p
     n primitive lower upper))
   (putnam-1997-a6-alg-zero-p
    primitive
    lower
    upper
    (putnam-1997-a6-rp-sub
     (putnam-1997-a6-recurrence-polynomial n k)
     (list
      (putnam-1997-a6-binomial
       (- n 1) (- k 1)))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q
