content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_a6:
-- the sequence defined by a real recurrence, at its greatest root parameter,
-- has binomial-coefficient values from index one through n. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  oneN <=N n

InClosedNatInterval : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Set
InClosedNatInterval lower upper k =
  lower <=N k and k <=N upper

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

choose : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
choose n zero =
  oneN
choose zero (suc k) =
  zero
choose (suc n) (suc k) =
  choose n (suc k) + choose n k

putnam-1997-a6-solution :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  R
putnam-1997-a6-solution reals n k =
  fromNat reals (choose (n - oneN) (k - oneN))

putnamSequence :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
putnamSequence reals n c zero =
  zeroR reals
putnamSequence reals n c (suc zero) =
  oneR reals
putnamSequence reals n c (suc (suc k)) =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals
      (multiply reals c
        (putnamSequence reals n c (suc k)))
      (multiply reals
        (fromNat reals (n - k))
        (putnamSequence reals n c k)))
    (fromNat reals (suc k))

IsGreatestRootParameter :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  Set
IsGreatestRootParameter {R} reals n greatest =
  putnamSequence reals n greatest (suc n) == zeroR reals
  and
  ((c : R) ->
    putnamSequence reals n c (suc n) == zeroR reals ->
    lessOrEqual reals c greatest)

putnam-1997-a6 : Set1
putnam-1997-a6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  (greatest : R) ->
  IsGreatestRootParameter reals n greatest ->
  (k : Nat) ->
  InClosedNatInterval oneN n k ->
  putnamSequence reals n greatest k
  ==
  putnam-1997-a6-solution reals n k

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_a6:
  the recursively defined real sequence at the largest root of its terminal
  term has binomial-coefficient values. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory combinatoricsTheory realTheory;

val putnam_1997_a6 =
  ``!n : num. !x : real -> num -> real. !C : real.
      0 < n /\
      (!c : real. x c 0 = 0) /\
      (!c : real. x c 1 = 1) /\
      (!c : real. !k : num.
         x c (k + 2) =
           (c * x c (k + 1) - &(n - k) * x c k) / &(k + 1)) /\
      x C (n + 1) = 0 /\
      (!c : real. x c (n + 1) = 0 ==> c <= C)
      ==>
      !k : num.
        1 <= k /\ k <= n
        ==>
        x C k = (&(binomial (n - 1) (k - 1)) : real)``;

title: putnam_1997_a6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1997_a6: a recursively defined real sequence at the greatest
  parameter making its (n+1)-st term zero has binomial-coefficient values.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The family x ranges over arbitrary total maps from real parameters to
  NN0-indexed real sequences. The recurrence uses ordinary real subtraction,
  multiplication, and division, with n and k canonically embedded in RR.

  The two conditions on r say that r is itself a parameter making the
  (n+1)-st term zero and that every such real parameter is at most r. Thus r
  is exactly the greatest member of the source root set, equivalently the
  source largest-value/supremum formulation under its greatest-root
  hypothesis. The conclusion uses set.mm's inclusive natural interval and
  _C binomial-coefficient operation.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d c k n r x $.

  putnambench-putnam-1997-a6 $a |-
    A. n e. NN
      A. x e. ( ( RR ^m NN0 ) ^m RR )
        A. r e. RR
          (
            (
              (
                (
                  A. c e. RR
                    (
                      ( ( x ` c ) ` 0 ) = 0
                      /\
                      ( ( x ` c ) ` 1 ) = 1
                    )
                  /\
                  A. c e. RR
                    A. k e. NN0
                      ( ( x ` c ) ` ( k + 2 ) )
                      =
                      (
                        (
                          c x. ( ( x ` c ) ` ( k + 1 ) )
                        )
                        -
                        (
                          ( n - k ) x. ( ( x ` c ) ` k )
                        )
                      )
                      /
                      ( k + 1 )
                )
                /\
                ( ( x ` r ) ` ( n + 1 ) ) = 0
              )
              /\
              A. c e. RR
                (
                  ( ( x ` c ) ` ( n + 1 ) ) = 0
                  ->
                  c <_ r
                )
            )
            ->
            A. k e. ( 1 ... n )
              ( ( x ` r ) ` k )
              =
              ( ( n - 1 ) _C ( k - 1 ) )
          )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_1997_a6:
% the recursively defined sequence at its greatest root parameter equals
% the corresponding binomial coefficients. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1997_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence_family: TYPE = [real -> [nat -> real]]

  binomial_coefficient(n, k: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF k = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSIF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k - 1)
        + binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  putnam_1997_a6: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (x: real_sequence_family), (maxc: real):
      n > 0
        AND (FORALL (c: real): x(c)(0) = 0)
        AND (FORALL (c: real): x(c)(1) = 1)
        AND (FORALL (c: real), (k: nat):
          x(c)(k + 2)
            = (c * x(c)(k + 1)
                - ((n - k) :: real) * x(c)(k))
              / ((k + 1) :: real))
        AND x(maxc)(n + 1) = 0
        AND (FORALL (c: real):
          x(c)(n + 1) = 0 IMPLIES c <= maxc)
      IMPLIES
        (FORALL (k: nat):
          1 <= k AND k <= n IMPLIES
            x(maxc)(k)
              = (binomial_coefficient(n - 1, k - 1) :: real))
END putnam_1997_a6

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b1:
;; for every positive integer n, the sum from m = 1 through 6n-1 of the
;; minimum nearest-integer distances of m/(6n) and m/(3n) equals n. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-1997-b1-min (left right)
  (if (<= left right)
      left
    right))

;; Every argument used below is rational. ACL2's exact rational FLOOR gives
;; the two adjacent integers, so the smaller absolute difference is exactly
;; the source's distance to the nearest integer, including half-integer ties.
(defun putnam-1997-b1-distance-to-integer (x)
  (let ((lower (floor x 1))
        (upper (floor (+ x 1) 1)))
    (putnam-1997-b1-min
     (abs (- x lower))
     (abs (- x upper)))))

(defun putnam-1997-b1-sum-through (n m)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix m)))
  (if (zp m)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1997-b1-sum-through n (- m 1))
       (putnam-1997-b1-min
        (putnam-1997-b1-distance-to-integer
         (/ m (* 6 n)))
        (putnam-1997-b1-distance-to-integer
         (/ m (* 3 n)))))))

;; Substituting the source hypothesis that defines F yields this equivalent
;; pointwise identity.
(defun putnambench-putnam-1997-b1-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (< 0 n))
   (equal
    (putnam-1997-b1-sum-through n (- (* 6 n) 1))
    n)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1997_b1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b1:
-- the sum from 1 through 6n - 1 of the smaller nearest-integer distance of
-- m/(6n) and m/(3n) equals n for every positive natural n. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

minimum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
minimum reals x y with order-total reals x y
... | left _ =
  x
... | right _ =
  y

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

sumOneThrough :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumOneThrough reals n terms =
  sumFirst reals n (\ i -> terms (suc i))

record StandardIntegerParts
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    floor ceiling : R -> Int

    floor-lower :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals
        (fromInt reals (floor x))
        x
    floor-greatest :
      (x : R) ->
      (z : Int) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (fromInt reals z) x ->
      lessOrEqual reals
        (fromInt reals z)
        (fromInt reals (floor x))

    ceiling-upper :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals
        x
        (fromInt reals (ceiling x))
    ceiling-least :
      (x : R) ->
      (z : Int) ->
      lessOrEqual reals x (fromInt reals z) ->
      lessOrEqual reals
        (fromInt reals (ceiling x))
        (fromInt reals z)

open StandardIntegerParts

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc (suc oneN)

sixN : Nat
sixN =
  threeN + threeN

module Putnam1997B1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (integerParts : StandardIntegerParts reals) where

  nearestIntegerDistance : R -> R
  nearestIntegerDistance x =
    minimum reals
      (subtract reals
        x
        (fromInt reals (floor integerParts x)))
      (subtract reals
        (fromInt reals (ceiling integerParts x))
        x)

  summand : Nat -> Nat -> R
  summand n m =
    minimum reals
      (nearestIntegerDistance
        (divide reals
          (fromNat reals m)
          (fromNat reals (sixN * n))))
      (nearestIntegerDistance
        (divide reals
          (fromNat reals m)
          (fromNat reals (threeN * n))))

  finiteSum : Nat -> R
  finiteSum n =
    sumOneThrough reals
      (sixN * n - oneN)
      (summand n)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (n : Nat) ->
    oneN <=N n ->
    finiteSum n == fromNat reals n

putnam-1997-b1 : Set1
putnam-1997-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (integerParts : StandardIntegerParts reals) ->
  Putnam1997B1Statement.proposition reals integerParts

  minima of distances to the nearest integer equals n. This file contains
  no proof.

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P97B1Dist(x) is the distance from a real x to the nearest integer. For a
  noninteger x, floor(x)+1 is its ceiling; for an integer x, the first branch
  is zero. Thus the conditional is exactly

    min(x - floor(x), ceiling(x) - x).

  The outer conditional is min(P97B1Dist(m/(6n)), P97B1Dist(m/(3n))).
  The interval 1 ... 6n-1 is inclusive, so the sum and the positive-integer
  quantifier are exactly those in the sources. Inlining F is definitionally
  equivalent to the Lean and Isabelle defining equations, while the Rocq
  source identifies the solution value as n. The final declaration is the
  single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

$c P97B1Dist $.

p97b1-distance-syntax $a class ( P97B1Dist A ) $.

p97b1-distance-definition $a |- (
  ( P97B1Dist A )
  =
  if (
    ( A - ( |_ ` A ) ) <_ ( ( ( |_ ` A ) + 1 ) - A ) ,
    ( A - ( |_ ` A ) ) ,
    ( ( ( |_ ` A ) + 1 ) - A )
  )
) $.

${

          ( P97B1Dist ( m / ( 6 x. n ) ) ) ,

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b1:
% evaluating a finite sum of minimum distances to the nearest integer for every
% positive integer n. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1997_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_subtract(minuend, subtrahend: nat): nat =
    IF subtrahend <= minuend THEN
      minuend - subtrahend
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  nearest_integer_distance(x: real): real =
    LET lower_distance: real =
          x - (floor(x) :: real),
        upper_distance: real =
          ((-floor(-x)) :: real) - x
    IN
      IF lower_distance <= upper_distance THEN
        lower_distance
      ELSE
        upper_distance
      ENDIF

  summand(n, m: nat): real =
    LET first_distance: real =
          nearest_integer_distance(
            safe_div(m :: real, 6 * (n :: real))),
        second_distance: real =
          nearest_integer_distance(
            safe_div(m :: real, 3 * (n :: real)))
    IN
      IF first_distance <= second_distance THEN
        first_distance
      ELSE
        second_distance
      ENDIF

  finite_sum(n, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      finite_sum(n, count - 1) + summand(n, count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  putnam_1997_b1_solution(n: nat): real =
    n :: real

  putnam_1997_b1: bool =
    FORALL (F: real_sequence):
      F = (LAMBDA (n: nat):
        finite_sum(n, nat_subtract(6 * n, 1)))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (n: nat):
          n > 0 IMPLIES
            F(n) = putnam_1997_b1_solution(n)
END putnam_1997_b1

  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b3:
  the positive integers for which the reduced denominator of the harmonic
  sum from 1 through n is not divisible by 5. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let solution =
     \n:num.
       (1 <= n /\ n <= 4) \/
       (20 <= n /\ n <= 24) \/
       (100 <= n /\ n <= 104) \/
       (120 <= n /\ n <= 124) in
   !n p q:num.
     0 < n /\
     0 < p /\
     0 < q /\
     coprime(p,q) /\
     sum (1..n) (\m:num. &1 / &m) = &p / &q
     ==> (~(5 divides q) <=> solution n)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b3:
;; the positive integers whose exact harmonic sum has reduced denominator not
;; divisible by 5 are exactly 1 through 4, 20 through 24, 100 through 104,
;; and 120 through 124. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-1997-b3-harmonic-sum (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1997-b3-harmonic-sum (- n 1))
       (/ 1 n))))

(defun putnam-1997-b3-listed-solution-p (n)
  (or (and (<= 1 n)
           (<= n 4))
      (and (<= 20 n)
           (<= n 24))
      (and (<= 100 n)
           (<= n 104))
      (and (<= 120 n)
           (<= n 124))))

;; ACL2 represents every rational in canonical reduced form, with a positive
;; denominator. Thus DENOMINATOR applied to this exact finite sum is q_n from
;; the source statement.
(defun putnambench-putnam-1997-b3-statement (n)
  (implies
   (posp n)
   (iff
    (putnam-1997-b3-listed-solution-p n)
    (not
     (equal
      (mod (denominator (putnam-1997-b3-harmonic-sum n)) 5)
      0)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b3:
-- the positive integers whose harmonic sum has reduced denominator not
-- divisible by 5 are exactly four specified intervals. This file contains no
-- proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : (n : Nat) -> Positive (suc n)

pred : Nat -> Nat
pred zero =
  zero
pred (suc n) =
  n

record Rational : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator             : Nat
    denominator-minus-one : Nat

open Rational

denominator : Rational -> Nat
denominator q =
  suc (denominator-minus-one q)

zeroQ : Rational
zeroQ =
  fraction zero zero

addQ : Rational -> Rational -> Rational
addQ x y =
  fraction
    ((numerator x * denominator y)
      + (numerator y * denominator x))
    (pred (denominator x * denominator y))

naturalRatio : Nat -> Nat -> Rational
naturalRatio numerator-value denominator-value =
  fraction numerator-value (pred denominator-value)

naturalDiv : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalDiv numerator-value zero =
  zero
naturalDiv numerator-value (suc denominator-value) =
  div-helper
    zero
    denominator-value
    numerator-value
    denominator-value

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator-value zero =
  zero
naturalMod numerator-value (suc denominator-value) =
  mod-helper
    zero
    denominator-value
    numerator-value
    denominator-value

gcdWithFuel : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat
gcdWithFuel zero a b =
  a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a zero =
  a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a (suc b) =
  gcdWithFuel fuel (suc b) (naturalMod a (suc b))

naturalGCD : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalGCD a b =
  gcdWithFuel (suc (a + b)) a b

reducedDenominator : Rational -> Nat
reducedDenominator q =
  naturalDiv
    (denominator q)
    (naturalGCD (numerator q) (denominator q))

Divides : Nat -> Nat -> Set
Divides divisor number =
  Exists Nat
    (\ factor -> divisor * factor == number)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  5

harmonicSum : Nat -> Rational
harmonicSum zero =
  zeroQ
harmonicSum (suc n) =
  addQ
    (harmonicSum n)
    (naturalRatio oneN (suc n))

Between : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Set
Between lower upper n =
  lower <=N n and n <=N upper

putnam-1997-b3-solution : Nat -> Set
putnam-1997-b3-solution n =
  Between 1 4 n
  or
  Between 20 24 n
  or
  Between 100 104 n
  or
  Between 120 124 n

putnam-1997-b3 : Set
putnam-1997-b3 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  Iff
    (putnam-1997-b3-solution n)
    (Not
      (Divides fiveN
        (reducedDenominator (harmonicSum n))))

val putnam_1997_b3 =

        (20 <= n /\ n <= 24) \/
        (100 <= n /\ n <= 104) \/
        (120 <= n /\ n <= 124)) <=>

  denominator not divisible by 5 are exactly 1 through 4, 20 through 24,
  100 through 104, and 120 through 124. This file contains no proof.

$(
  NN is set.mm's class of positive integers. The sum binder ranges over the
  inclusive interval 1 ... n, and denom gives the positive denominator of
  the unique reduced rational representation of that harmonic sum. Thus
  nondivisibility by 5 is exactly the denominator condition in the sources.

  The four inclusive intervals inline the solution set defined in the Rocq
  source and documented in the Lean and Isabelle sources. The final
  declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d m n $.

  putnambench-putnam-1997-b3 $a |- A. n e. NN
    (
      (
        n e. ( 1 ... 4 )
        \/
        (
          n e. ( ; 2 0 ... ; 2 4 )
          \/
          (
            n e. ( ; ; 1 0 0 ... ; ; 1 0 4 )
            \/
            n e. ( ; ; 1 2 0 ... ; ; 1 2 4 )
          )
        )
      )
      <->
      -. 5 ||
        (
          denom
          `
          (
            sum_ m e. ( 1 ... n ) ( 1 / m )
          )
        )
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1997_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b3:
% the positive integers whose reduced harmonic-sum denominator is not
% divisible by 5 are exactly four specified intervals. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1997_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  safe_div(numerator, denominator: rat): rat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  harmonic_sum(n: nat): RECURSIVE rat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      harmonic_sum(n - 1) + safe_div(1, n :: rat)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  nat_divides(divisor: posnat, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  coprime_nat(left, right: nat): bool =
    FORALL (divisor: posnat):
      nat_divides(divisor, left) AND nat_divides(divisor, right)
        IMPLIES divisor = 1

  putnam_1997_b3_solution(n: nat): bool =
    (1 <= n AND n <= 4)
      OR (20 <= n AND n <= 24)
      OR (100 <= n AND n <= 104)
      OR (120 <= n AND n <= 124)

  putnam_1997_b3: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n > 0 IMPLIES
        (putnam_1997_b3_solution(n)
          IFF
            EXISTS (p, q: nat):
              p > 0
                AND q > 0
                AND coprime_nat(p, q)
                AND harmonic_sum(n)
                  = safe_div(p :: rat, q :: rat)
                AND mod(q, 5) /= 0)
END putnam_1997_b3

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b4:
   an alternating sum of coefficients of powers of 1 + x + x^2 lies between
   zero and one. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_1997_b4_coefficient (m n : nat) : Z :=
  match m with
  | O =>
      match n with
      | O => 1
      | S _ => 0
      end
  | S m' =>
      putnam_1997_b4_coefficient m' n +
      match n with
      | O => 0
      | S n' => putnam_1997_b4_coefficient m' n'
      end +
      match n with
      | O => 0
      | S O => 0
      | S (S n') => putnam_1997_b4_coefficient m' n'
      end
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_1997_b4_sign (i : nat) : Z :=
  match i with
  | O => 1
  | S i' => - putnam_1997_b4_sign i'
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_1997_b4_sum
    (a : nat -> nat -> Z) (k count : nat) : Z :=
  match count with
  | O => 0
  | S i =>
      putnam_1997_b4_sum a k i +
      putnam_1997_b4_sign i * a (k - i)%nat i
  end.

Theorem putnam_1997_b4 :
  forall a : nat -> nat -> Z,
    (forall m n : nat,
      a m n = putnam_1997_b4_coefficient m n) ->
    forall k : nat,
      let total :=
        putnam_1997_b4_sum a k (S (Nat.div (2 * k) 3)) in
      (0 <= total <= 1)%Z.
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b4:
;; coefficients of (1+x+x^2)^m give an alternating finite sum between zero
;; and one for every natural k. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; This recurrence is exactly the coefficient of x^n in (1+x+x^2)^m.
(defun putnam-1997-b4-trinomial-coefficient (m n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix m)))
  (if (or (not (natp m))
          (not (natp n)))
      0
    (if (zp m)
        (if (zp n) 1 0)
      (+ (putnam-1997-b4-trinomial-coefficient (- m 1) n)
         (putnam-1997-b4-trinomial-coefficient
          (- m 1) (- n 1))
         (putnam-1997-b4-trinomial-coefficient
          (- m 1) (- n 2))))))

;; Inclusive sum from i = 0 through upper of
;; (-1)^i times the coefficient of x^i in (1+x+x^2)^(k-i).
(defun putnam-1997-b4-alternating-sum (k upper)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix upper)))
  (if (zp upper)
      (putnam-1997-b4-trinomial-coefficient k 0)
    (+ (putnam-1997-b4-alternating-sum k (- upper 1))
       (* (expt -1 upper)
          (putnam-1997-b4-trinomial-coefficient
           (- k upper) upper)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1997-b4-statement (k)
  (implies
   (natp k)
   (let ((sum
          (putnam-1997-b4-alternating-sum
           k (floor (* 2 k) 3))))
     (and (<= 0 sum)
          (<= sum 1)))))

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b4:
-- coefficients of powers of 1 + x + x^2 satisfy an alternating-sum bound
-- between zero and one. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_; div-helper)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<=Z_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data _<=Z_ : Int -> Int -> Set where
  negative<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    negsuc m <=Z pos n
  positive<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    m <=N n ->
    pos m <=Z pos n
  negative<=negative :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    n <=N m ->
    negsuc m <=Z negsuc n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

negativeNat : Nat -> Int
negativeNat zero =
  pos zero
negativeNat (suc n) =
  negsuc n

differenceNat : Nat -> Nat -> Int
differenceNat zero zero =
  pos zero
differenceNat (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
differenceNat zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
differenceNat (suc m) (suc n) =
  differenceNat m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  differenceNat m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  differenceNat n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negativeNat (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negativeNat (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

powerInt : Int -> Nat -> Int
powerInt x zero =
  pos oneN
powerInt x (suc n) =
  multiplyInt x (powerInt x n)

naturalDiv : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero =
  zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

trinomialCoefficient : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
trinomialCoefficient zero zero =
  oneN
trinomialCoefficient zero (suc n) =
  zero
trinomialCoefficient (suc m) zero =
  trinomialCoefficient m zero
trinomialCoefficient (suc m) (suc zero) =
  trinomialCoefficient m (suc zero)
  + trinomialCoefficient m zero
trinomialCoefficient (suc m) (suc (suc n)) =
  trinomialCoefficient m (suc (suc n))
  + trinomialCoefficient m (suc n)
  + trinomialCoefficient m n

CoefficientSpecification :
  (Nat -> Nat -> Int) ->
  Set
CoefficientSpecification a =
  (m n : Nat) ->
  a m n == pos (trinomialCoefficient m n)

sumThroughInt :
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> Int) ->
  Int
sumThroughInt zero term =
  term zero
sumThroughInt (suc n) term =
  addInt
    (sumThroughInt n term)
    (term (suc n))

alternatingCoefficientSum :
  (Nat -> Nat -> Int) ->
  Nat ->
  Int
alternatingCoefficientSum a k =
  sumThroughInt
    (naturalDiv (twoN * k) threeN)
    (\ i ->
      multiplyInt
        (powerInt (negsuc zero) i)
        (a (k - i) i))

InZeroOne : Int -> Set
InZeroOne value =
  pos zero <=Z value
  and
  value <=Z pos oneN

putnam-1997-b4 : Set
putnam-1997-b4 =
  (a : Nat -> Nat -> Int) ->
  CoefficientSpecification a ->
  (k : Nat) ->
  InZeroOne (alternatingCoefficientSum a k)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b4:
  coefficients of powers of 1 + x + x^2 satisfy an alternating finite-sum
  bound between zero and one. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_1997_b4 =
  ``!(a : num -> num -> int).
      let base =
        \i : num. if i <= 2 then 1 else 0
      in
      let multiply =
        \p q : num -> num.
          \n : num.
            SIGMA
              (\i : num. p i * q (n - i))
              (count (SUC n))
      in
      let one =
        \i : num. if i = 0 then 1 else 0
      in
        (!m n : num.
           a m n =
             int_of_num
               (FUNPOW
                  (\p : num -> num. multiply p base)
                  m
                  one
                  n))
        ==>
        !k : num.
          let alternating_sum =
            FOLDL
              (\acc : int. \i : num.
                 acc + (~1 : int) ** i * a (k - i) i)
              0
              (GENLIST
                 (\i : num. i)
                 (SUC ((2 * k) DIV 3)))
          in
            0 <= alternating_sum /\ alternating_sum <= 1``;

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b4:
% the alternating sum through floor(2*k/3) of coefficients of
% (1 + x + x^2)^(k-i) lies between zero and one. This file contains no proof.

putnam_1997_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  coefficient_table: TYPE = [nat, nat -> int]

  trinomial_coefficient(m, n: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF m = 0 THEN
      IF n = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ELSE
      trinomial_coefficient(m - 1, n)
        + IF n >= 1 THEN
            trinomial_coefficient(m - 1, n - 1)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
        + IF n >= 2 THEN
            trinomial_coefficient(m - 1, n - 2)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE m

  coefficient_specification(a: coefficient_table): bool =
    FORALL (m, n: nat):
      a(m, n) = trinomial_coefficient(m, n)

  nat_subtract(minuend, subtrahend: nat): nat =
    IF subtrahend <= minuend THEN
      minuend - subtrahend
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  alternating_coefficient_sum(
      a: coefficient_table,
      k, count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        alternating_coefficient_sum(a, k, count - 1)
          + alternating_sign(index)
              * a(nat_subtract(k, index), index)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  two_thirds_floor(k: nat): nat =
    ndiv(2 * k, 3)

  putnam_1997_b4: bool =
    FORALL (a: coefficient_table):
      coefficient_specification(a)
        IMPLIES
          FORALL (k: nat):
            LET value: int =
                  alternating_coefficient_sum(
                    a, k, two_thirds_floor(k) + 1)
            IN
              0 <= value AND value <= 1
END putnam_1997_b4

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1997_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_1997_b5): for every natural n at least 2,
-- the height-n and height-(n-1) towers of 2 are congruent modulo n.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _-_; _*_; mod-helper)

infix 4 _<=N_

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

naturalPower : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalPower base zero =
  oneN
naturalPower base (suc exponent) =
  base * naturalPower base exponent

tetration : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
tetration base zero =
  oneN
tetration base (suc height) =
  naturalPower base (tetration base height)

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero =
  zero
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

putnam-1997-b5 : Set
putnam-1997-b5 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  twoN <=N n ->
  naturalMod (tetration twoN n) n
  ==
  naturalMod (tetration twoN (n - oneN)) n

import Mathlib

/--
Let $s$ be any arc of the unit circle lying entirely in the first quadrant. Let $A$ be the area of the region lying below $s$ and above the $x$-axis and let $B$ be the area of the region lying to the right of the $y$-axis and to the left of $s$. Prove that $A+B$ depends only on the arc length, and not on the position, of $s$.
-/
theorem putnam_1998_a2
(quadrant : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) → Prop)
(isarc : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) → (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) → Prop)
(hquadrant : ∀ P, quadrant P ↔ P 0 > 0 ∧ P 1 > 0 ∧ dist 0 P = 1)
(hisarc : ∀ P Q, isarc P Q ↔ quadrant P ∧ quadrant Q ∧ P 0 > Q 0)
(arc : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) → (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) → Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))
(harc : arc = fun P Q ↦ {R : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) | quadrant R ∧ P 0 > R 0 ∧ R 0 > Q 0})
(A B : (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) → (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) → ℝ)
(hA : A = fun P Q ↦ (MeasureTheory.volume {S : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) | ∃ R ∈ arc P Q, R 0 = S 0 ∧ R 1 > S 1 ∧ S 1 > 0}).toReal)
(hB : B = fun P Q ↦ (MeasureTheory.volume {S : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) | ∃ R ∈ arc P Q, R 1 = S 1 ∧ R 0 > S 0 ∧ S 0 > 0}).toReal)
: (∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, ∀ P Q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), isarc P Q → A P Q + B P Q = f (InnerProductGeometry.angle P Q)) :=

title: putnam_1998_a2
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1998_a2:
   for a first-quadrant unit-circle arc, the sum of the area below the arc and
   the area between the y-axis and the arc depends only on its angular length.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_1998_a2_point : Type := (R * R)%type.
Definition putnam_1998_a2_point_set : Type :=
  putnam_1998_a2_point -> Prop.

Definition putnam_1998_a2_distance
    (p q : putnam_1998_a2_point) : R :=
  sqrt ((fst p - fst q) ^ 2 + (snd p - snd q) ^ 2).

Record putnam_1998_a2_open_rectangle : Type := {
  putnam_1998_a2_x_lower : R;
  putnam_1998_a2_x_upper : R;
  putnam_1998_a2_y_lower : R;
  putnam_1998_a2_y_upper : R
}.

Definition putnam_1998_a2_in_open_rectangle
    (rectangle : putnam_1998_a2_open_rectangle)
    (p : putnam_1998_a2_point) : Prop :=
  putnam_1998_a2_x_lower rectangle < fst p <
    putnam_1998_a2_x_upper rectangle /\
  putnam_1998_a2_y_lower rectangle < snd p <
    putnam_1998_a2_y_upper rectangle.

Definition putnam_1998_a2_rectangle_area
    (rectangle : putnam_1998_a2_open_rectangle) : R :=
  Rmax 0
    (putnam_1998_a2_x_upper rectangle -
     putnam_1998_a2_x_lower rectangle) *
  Rmax 0
    (putnam_1998_a2_y_upper rectangle -
     putnam_1998_a2_y_lower rectangle).

Definition putnam_1998_a2_rectangles_cover
    (region : putnam_1998_a2_point_set)
    (rectangles : nat -> putnam_1998_a2_open_rectangle) : Prop :=
  forall p : putnam_1998_a2_point,
    region p ->
    exists n : nat,
      putnam_1998_a2_in_open_rectangle (rectangles n) p.

Fixpoint putnam_1998_a2_partial_rectangle_area
    (rectangles : nat -> putnam_1998_a2_open_rectangle)
    (n : nat) : R :=
  match n with
  | O => 0
  | S k =>
      putnam_1998_a2_partial_rectangle_area rectangles k +
      putnam_1998_a2_rectangle_area (rectangles k)
  end.

(* Equality with finite planar Lebesgue outer measure, expressed through
   countable open-rectangle covers. *)
Definition putnam_1998_a2_has_planar_lebesgue_measure
    (region : putnam_1998_a2_point_set) (area : R) : Prop :=
  0 <= area /\
  (forall rectangles : nat -> putnam_1998_a2_open_rectangle,
    putnam_1998_a2_rectangles_cover region rectangles ->
    forall lower : R,
      lower < area ->
      exists n : nat,
        lower <
        putnam_1998_a2_partial_rectangle_area rectangles n) /\
  (forall epsilon : R,
    0 < epsilon ->
    exists rectangles : nat -> putnam_1998_a2_open_rectangle,
      putnam_1998_a2_rectangles_cover region rectangles /\
      forall n : nat,
        putnam_1998_a2_partial_rectangle_area rectangles n <
        area + epsilon).

Theorem putnam_1998_a2
    (quadrant : putnam_1998_a2_point -> Prop)
    (isarc :
      putnam_1998_a2_point -> putnam_1998_a2_point -> Prop)
    (arc :
      putnam_1998_a2_point -> putnam_1998_a2_point ->
      putnam_1998_a2_point_set)
    (A B :
      putnam_1998_a2_point -> putnam_1998_a2_point -> R)
    (hquadrant :
      forall P : putnam_1998_a2_point,
        quadrant P <->
        fst P > 0 /\
        snd P > 0 /\
        putnam_1998_a2_distance (0, 0) P = 1)
    (hisarc :
      forall P Q : putnam_1998_a2_point,
        isarc P Q <->
        quadrant P /\ quadrant Q /\ fst P > fst Q)
    (harc :
      forall P Q R : putnam_1998_a2_point,
        arc P Q R <->
        quadrant R /\ fst P > fst R /\ fst R > fst Q)
    (hA :
      forall P Q : putnam_1998_a2_point,
        putnam_1998_a2_has_planar_lebesgue_measure
          (fun S : putnam_1998_a2_point =>
            exists R : putnam_1998_a2_point,
              arc P Q R /\
              fst R = fst S /\
              snd R > snd S /\
              snd S > 0)
          (A P Q))
    (hB :
      forall P Q : putnam_1998_a2_point,
        putnam_1998_a2_has_planar_lebesgue_measure
          (fun S : putnam_1998_a2_point =>
            exists R : putnam_1998_a2_point,
              arc P Q R /\
              snd R = snd S /\
              fst R > fst S /\
              fst S > 0)
          (B P Q)) :
  exists f : R -> R,
    forall P Q : putnam_1998_a2_point,
      isarc P Q ->
      A P Q + B P Q =
      f (atan (snd Q / fst Q) - atan (snd P / fst P)).
Admitted.
