content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1999_b5:
;; the determinant of the identity plus the n-by-n cosine matrix at equally
;; spaced angles has value 1 - n^2/4. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Let zeta = exp(2*pi*i/n).  It is a primitive n-th root of unity, and
;;
;;   cos((j+k+2)*2*pi/n)
;;     = (zeta^(j+k+2) + zeta^(-(j+k+2)))/2.
;;
;; The polynomial matrix below replaces zeta by X and reduces exponents
;; modulo n using zeta^n = 1.  Its determinant polynomial D_n therefore
;; evaluates at zeta to the source determinant.  Since Phi_n is the minimal
;; polynomial of zeta over the rationals,
;;
;;   D_n(zeta) = 1 - n^2/4
;;
;; holds exactly when Phi_n divides D_n(X) - (1 - n^2/4).  Thus this
;; rational-polynomial encoding is bidirectionally equivalent to the real
;; cosine statement; it does not restrict the source values to rationals.
;; The zero-based rows and columns below correspond to the source indices
;; 1 through n.  The Isabelle index bijection only reorders both matrix axes,
;; which leaves the determinant unchanged.

;; Polynomials are rational coefficient lists in ascending degree order.

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (let ((tail
             (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize
              (cdr coefficients))))
        (if (and (equal (car coefficients) 0)
                 (not (consp tail)))
            nil
          (cons (car coefficients) tail)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-add (left right)
  (cond
   ((consp left)
    (if (consp right)
        (cons (+ (car left) (car right))
              (putnam-1999-b5-poly-add
               (cdr left) (cdr right)))
      left))
   (t right)))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-scale (scalar polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons (* scalar (car polynomial))
            (putnam-1999-b5-poly-scale
             scalar (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-negate (polynomial)
  (putnam-1999-b5-poly-scale -1 polynomial))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-subtract (left right)
  (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize
   (putnam-1999-b5-poly-add
    left
    (putnam-1999-b5-poly-negate right))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-multiply (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize
       (putnam-1999-b5-poly-add
        (putnam-1999-b5-poly-scale (car left) right)
        (cons 0
              (putnam-1999-b5-poly-multiply
               (cdr left) right))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-zero-list (count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons 0
          (putnam-1999-b5-zero-list (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-monomial (coefficient degree)
  (if (equal coefficient 0)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-1999-b5-zero-list degree)
     (list coefficient))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-degree (polynomial)
  (let ((normalized
         (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize polynomial)))
    (if (consp normalized)
        (- (len normalized) 1)
      0)))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-leading-coefficient (polynomial)
  (let ((normalized
         (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize polynomial)))
    (if (consp normalized)
        (nth (putnam-1999-b5-poly-degree normalized)
             normalized)
      0)))

;; The step bound exceeds the number of degree reductions required by
;; polynomial long division with a nonzero divisor.
(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-divmod-steps
    (remainder divisor quotient steps)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix steps)))
  (if (zp steps)
      (cons (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize quotient)
            (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize remainder))
    (let* ((normalized-remainder
            (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize remainder))
           (normalized-divisor
            (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize divisor)))
      (if (or (not (consp normalized-remainder))
              (not (consp normalized-divisor))
              (< (putnam-1999-b5-poly-degree
                  normalized-remainder)
                 (putnam-1999-b5-poly-degree
                  normalized-divisor)))
          (cons (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize quotient)
                normalized-remainder)
        (let* ((degree-difference
                (- (putnam-1999-b5-poly-degree
                    normalized-remainder)
                   (putnam-1999-b5-poly-degree
                    normalized-divisor)))
               (coefficient
                (/ (putnam-1999-b5-poly-leading-coefficient
                    normalized-remainder)
                   (putnam-1999-b5-poly-leading-coefficient
                    normalized-divisor)))
               (term
                (putnam-1999-b5-poly-monomial
                 coefficient degree-difference)))
          (putnam-1999-b5-poly-divmod-steps
           (putnam-1999-b5-poly-subtract
            normalized-remainder
            (putnam-1999-b5-poly-multiply
             term normalized-divisor))
           normalized-divisor
           (putnam-1999-b5-poly-add quotient term)
           (- steps 1)))))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-divmod (dividend divisor)
  (putnam-1999-b5-poly-divmod-steps
   dividend
   divisor
   nil
   (+ 1
      (len (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize dividend)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-quotient (dividend divisor)
  (car (putnam-1999-b5-poly-divmod dividend divisor)))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-poly-remainder (dividend divisor)
  (cdr (putnam-1999-b5-poly-divmod dividend divisor)))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-x-to-n-minus-one (n)
  (putnam-1999-b5-poly-add
   (list -1)
   (putnam-1999-b5-poly-monomial 1 n)))

;; The list PRECEDING contains Phi_1 through Phi_(n-1).
(defun putnam-1999-b5-proper-divisor-product
    (n divisor preceding)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix divisor)))
  (if (zp divisor)
      (list 1)
    (let ((remaining
           (putnam-1999-b5-proper-divisor-product
            n (- divisor 1) preceding)))
      (if (equal (mod n divisor) 0)
          (putnam-1999-b5-poly-multiply
           (nth (- divisor 1) preceding)
           remaining)
        remaining))))

;; Phi_n = (X^n - 1) / product_(d | n, d < n) Phi_d.
(defun putnam-1999-b5-cyclotomic-list (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (let* ((preceding
            (putnam-1999-b5-cyclotomic-list (- n 1)))
           (proper-divisor-product
            (putnam-1999-b5-proper-divisor-product
             n (- n 1) preceding))
           (phi-n
            (putnam-1999-b5-poly-quotient
             (putnam-1999-b5-x-to-n-minus-one n)
             proper-divisor-product)))
      (append
       preceding
       (list (putnam-1999-b5-poly-normalize phi-n))))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-cyclotomic-polynomial (n)
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (nth (- n 1)
         (putnam-1999-b5-cyclotomic-list n))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-indices (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (cons (- n 1)
          (putnam-1999-b5-indices (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-prepend-each (value lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (cons
     (cons value (car lists))
     (putnam-1999-b5-prepend-each
      value (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-insert-everywhere (value values)
  (if (endp values)
      (list (list value))
    (cons
     (cons value values)
     (putnam-1999-b5-prepend-each
      (car values)
      (putnam-1999-b5-insert-everywhere
       value (cdr values))))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-insert-into-permutations
    (value permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-1999-b5-insert-everywhere
      value (car permutations))
     (putnam-1999-b5-insert-into-permutations
      value (cdr permutations)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-permutations (values)
  (if (endp values)
      (list nil)
    (putnam-1999-b5-insert-into-permutations
     (car values)
     (putnam-1999-b5-permutations (cdr values)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-smaller-count (value values)
  (if (endp values)
      0
    (+ (if (< (car values) value) 1 0)
       (putnam-1999-b5-smaller-count
        value (cdr values)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-inversion-count (permutation)
  (if (endp permutation)
      0
    (+ (putnam-1999-b5-smaller-count
        (car permutation) (cdr permutation))
       (putnam-1999-b5-inversion-count
        (cdr permutation)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-permutation-sign (permutation)
  (if (equal
       (mod (putnam-1999-b5-inversion-count permutation) 2)
       0)
      1
    -1))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-entry (n row column)
  (let* ((angle-index (+ row column 2))
         (positive-exponent (mod angle-index n))
         (negative-exponent (mod (- angle-index) n))
         (cosine-polynomial
          (putnam-1999-b5-poly-add
           (putnam-1999-b5-poly-monomial
            1/2 positive-exponent)
           (putnam-1999-b5-poly-monomial
            1/2 negative-exponent))))
    (if (equal row column)
        (putnam-1999-b5-poly-add
         (list 1) cosine-polynomial)
      cosine-polynomial)))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-determinant-product
    (n row permutation)
  (if (endp permutation)
      (list 1)
    (putnam-1999-b5-poly-multiply
     (putnam-1999-b5-entry
      n row (car permutation))
     (putnam-1999-b5-determinant-product
      n (+ row 1) (cdr permutation)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-determinant-sum
    (n permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      nil
    (putnam-1999-b5-poly-add
     (putnam-1999-b5-poly-scale
      (putnam-1999-b5-permutation-sign
       (car permutations))
      (putnam-1999-b5-determinant-product
       n 0 (car permutations)))
     (putnam-1999-b5-determinant-sum
      n (cdr permutations)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-determinant-polynomial (n)
  (putnam-1999-b5-determinant-sum
   n
   (putnam-1999-b5-permutations
    (putnam-1999-b5-indices n))))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-solution (n)
  (- 1 (/ (* n n) 4)))

(defun putnam-1999-b5-equation-polynomial (n)
  (putnam-1999-b5-poly-subtract
   (putnam-1999-b5-determinant-polynomial n)
   (list (putnam-1999-b5-solution n))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1999-b5-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (<= 3 n))
   (equal
    (putnam-1999-b5-poly-remainder
     (putnam-1999-b5-equation-polynomial n)
     (putnam-1999-b5-cyclotomic-polynomial n))
    nil)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1999_b5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1999_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_1999_b5): the determinant of the identity plus
-- the n by n cosine matrix with angles j theta + k theta, theta = 2 pi / n,
-- equals 1 - n squared / 4 for n at least 3. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finToNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (finToNat i)

sameFin : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin n -> Bool
sameFin fzero fzero =
  true
sameFin fzero (fsuc j) =
  false
sameFin (fsuc i) fzero =
  false
sameFin (fsuc i) (fsuc j) =
  sameFin i j

ifBool : {A : Set} -> Bool -> A -> A -> A
ifBool true whenTrue whenFalse =
  whenTrue
ifBool false whenTrue whenFalse =
  whenFalse

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc threeN

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

alternatingPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingPower reals n =
  naturalPower reals
    (negate reals (oneR reals))
    n

cosineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
cosineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (twoN * n)))
    (fromNat reals (factorial (twoN * n)))

leibnizTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
leibnizTerm reals n =
  divide reals
    (alternatingPower reals n)
    (fromNat reals (suc (twoN * n)))

record StandardCosine
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) : Set1 where
  field
    cosine : R -> R
    pi : R
    cosine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (cosineTerm reals x)
        (cosine x)
    pi-positive :
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) pi
    pi-leibniz-series :
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (leibnizTerm reals)
        (divide reals pi (fromNat reals fourN))

open StandardCosine

Matrix : Set -> Nat -> Set
Matrix R n =
  Fin n -> Fin n -> R

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

skip :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin (suc n)
skip {zero} column ()
skip {suc n} fzero k =
  fsuc k
skip {suc n} (fsuc column) fzero =
  fzero
skip {suc n} (fsuc column) (fsuc k) =
  fsuc (skip column k)

firstRowMinor :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R (suc n) ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Matrix R n
firstRowMinor A column i j =
  A (fsuc i) (skip column j)

alternatingSign :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  R
alternatingSign reals fzero =
  oneR reals
alternatingSign reals (fsuc i) =
  negate reals (alternatingSign reals i)

determinant :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  R
determinant reals {zero} A =
  oneR reals
determinant reals {suc n} A =
  sumFin reals
    (\ column ->
      multiply reals
        (alternatingSign reals column)
        (multiply reals
          (A fzero column)
          (determinant reals (firstRowMinor A column))))

identityMatrix :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n
identityMatrix reals i j =
  ifBool
    (sameFin i j)
    (oneR reals)
    (zeroR reals)

matrixAdd :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n
matrixAdd reals A B i j =
  add reals (A i j) (B i j)

theta :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardCosine reals ->
  Nat ->
  R
theta reals trigonometry n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (fromNat reals twoN)
      (pi trigonometry))
    (fromNat reals n)

putnamMatrix :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardCosine reals ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  Matrix R n
putnamMatrix reals trigonometry n i j =
  let
    angleStep = theta reals trigonometry n
    rowAngle =
      multiply reals
        (fromNat reals (suc (finToNat i)))
        angleStep
    columnAngle =
      multiply reals
        (fromNat reals (suc (finToNat j)))
        angleStep
  in
  cosine trigonometry
    (add reals rowAngle columnAngle)

solution :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
solution reals n =
  subtract reals
    (oneR reals)
    (divide reals
      (naturalPower reals
        (fromNat reals n)
        twoN)
      (fromNat reals fourN))

putnam-1999-b5 : Set1
putnam-1999-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (trigonometry : StandardCosine reals) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  threeN <=N n ->
  determinant reals
    (matrixAdd reals
      (identityMatrix reals)
      (putnamMatrix reals trigonometry n))
  ==
  solution reals n

title: putnam_1999_b5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1999_b5:
  the determinant of the n by n real matrix I + A, where
  A_jk = cos(j theta + k theta) and theta = 2 pi / n, is
  1 - n squared / 4. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory permutesTheory realTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_1999_b5 =
  ``let determinant =
      \n : num. \M : num -> num -> real.
        ITSET
          (\p : num -> num. \sum : real.
             (if evenperm p then
                ITSET
                  (\i : num. \acc : real. M i (p i) * acc)
                  (count n)
                  1
              else
                -(ITSET
                    (\i : num. \acc : real. M i (p i) * acc)
                    (count n)
                    1)) +
             sum)
          {p : num -> num | p permutes count n}
          0
    in
      !n : num. !theta : real. !A : num -> num -> real.
        3 <= n /\
        theta = 2 * pi / (&n : real) /\
        (!i j : num.
           i < n /\ j < n
           ==>
           A i j =
             cos ((&(SUC i) : real) * theta +
                  (&(SUC j) : real) * theta))
        ==>
        determinant n
          (\i j.
             (if i = j then 1 else 0) + A i j) =
        1 - (&n : real) pow 2 / 4``;

title: putnam_1999_b5
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_1999_b5: evaluation of the determinant of an n-by-n real
  cosine matrix plus the identity. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The carrier 0 ..^ n has exactly n elements. Its zero-based indices i,j
  are shifted to i+1,j+1, so the displayed binary map is the source matrix
  I+A with theta definitionally replaced by 2*pi/n. SetMM's maDet over
  RRfld is the determinant of this real matrix.

  Inlining theta and the uniquely specified matrix eliminates only
  definitional parameters. The right side is the solution 1-n^2/4
  annotated in both ground-truth sources. The final declaration is the
  single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

${
  $d i j n $.

  putnambench-putnam-1999-b5 $a |- A. n e. NN0
    (
      3 <_ n
      ->
      (
        (
          ( ( 0 ..^ n ) maDet RRfld )
          `
          (
            i e. ( 0 ..^ n ) , j e. ( 0 ..^ n ) |->
              (
                if ( i = j , 1 , 0 )
                +
                (
                  cos
                  `
                  (
                    (
                      ( i + 1 )
                      x.
                      ( ( 2 x. _pi ) / n )
                    )
                    +
                    (
                      ( j + 1 )
                      x.
                      ( ( 2 x. _pi ) / n )
                    )
                  )
                )
              )
          )
        )
        =
        (
          1
          -
          ( ( n ^ 2 ) / 4 )
        )
      )
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_1999_b5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1999_b5:
% for n at least 3, the determinant of the identity plus the n-by-n real
% matrix with (j,k)-entry cos(j*theta+k*theta), theta=2*pi/n, is 1-n^2/4.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_1999_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  cosine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index),
              factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  cosine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): cosine_partial(x, count),
          value))

  pi: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        3 < value
          AND value < 4
          AND cosine(value / 2) = 0)

  quotient_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      0
    ELSE
      1
        + quotient_aux(
            numerator - denominator,
            denominator,
            fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  remainder_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      numerator
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator - denominator,
        denominator,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  safe_ndiv(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    quotient_aux(
      numerator,
      denominator,
      numerator + 1)

  safe_mod(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator,
        denominator,
        numerator + 1)
    ENDIF

  function_code_count(n: nat): nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN 1 ELSE n ^ n ENDIF

  permutation_entry(code, row, n: nat): nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      safe_mod(safe_ndiv(code, n ^ row), n)
    ENDIF

  permutation_code(code, n: nat): bool =
    code < function_code_count(n)
      AND (FORALL (row_1, row_2: nat):
        (row_1 < n
          AND row_2 < n
          AND permutation_entry(code, row_1, n)
            = permutation_entry(code, row_2, n))
        IMPLIES row_1 = row_2)

  pair_row(pair, n: nat): nat =
    safe_ndiv(pair, n)

  pair_column(pair, n: nat): nat =
    safe_mod(pair, n)

  inversion_at(code, pair, n: nat): bool =
    pair_row(pair, n) < n
      AND pair_column(pair, n) < n
      AND pair_row(pair, n) < pair_column(pair, n)
      AND permutation_entry(code, pair_row(pair, n), n)
        > permutation_entry(code, pair_column(pair, n), n)

  count_true(
      property: [nat -> bool],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_true(property, count - 1)
        + IF property(count - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  inversion_count(code, n: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      (LAMBDA (pair: nat): inversion_at(code, pair, n)),
      n * n)

  permutation_sign(code, n: nat): real =
    IF mod(inversion_count(code, n), 2) = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -1
    ENDIF

  permutation_product(
      A: matrix,
      code, n, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      permutation_product(A, code, n, count - 1)
        * A(
            count - 1,
            permutation_entry(code, count - 1, n))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  determinant_sum(
      A: matrix,
      n, limit: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET code: nat = limit - 1 IN
        determinant_sum(A, n, limit - 1)
          + IF permutation_code(code, n) THEN
              permutation_sign(code, n)
                * permutation_product(A, code, n, n)
            ELSE
              0
            ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  determinant(A: matrix, n: nat): real =
    determinant_sum(A, n, function_code_count(n))

  identity_plus(A: matrix): matrix =
    LAMBDA (row, column: nat):
      (IF row = column THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF) + A(row, column)

  has_cosine_entries(
      A: matrix,
      n: nat,
      theta: real): bool =
    FORALL (row, column: nat):
      row < n AND column < n IMPLIES
        A(row, column)
          = cosine(
              ((row + 1) :: real) * theta
                + ((column + 1) :: real) * theta)

  putnam_1999_b5_solution(n: nat): real =
    1 - (n :: real) ^ 2 / 4

  putnam_1999_b5: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (theta: real), (A: matrix):
      (n >= 3
        AND theta = safe_div(2 * pi, n :: real)
        AND has_cosine_entries(A, n, theta))
      IMPLIES
        determinant(identity_plus(A), n)
          = putnam_1999_b5_solution(n)
END putnam_1999_b5

title: putnam_1999_b6

import Mathlib

open Filter Topology Metric

/--
Let $S$ be a finite set of integers, each greater than 1.  Suppose that for each integer $n$ there is some $s\in S$ such that $\gcd(s,n)=1$ or $\gcd(s,n)=s$.  Show that there exist $s,t\in S$ such that $\gcd(s,t)$ is prime.
-/
theorem putnam_1999_b6
  (S : Finset ℤ)
  (hSgt : ∀ s, s ∈ S → s > 1)
  (hSgcd : ∀ n, ∃ s ∈ S, Int.gcd s n = 1 ∨ Int.gcd s n = s) :
  ∃ᵉ (s ∈ S) (t ∈ S), Prime (Int.gcd s t) :=
sorry

Theorem putnam_1999_b6
    (A : list Z)
    (Age1 : forall (x: Z), In x A -> x > 1)
    (hgcd : forall (n: Z), exists (s: Z), In s A /\ (Zis_gcd s n 1 \/ Zis_gcd s n s))
    : exists (s: Z) (t: Z) (p: Z), In s A /\ In t A /\ Zis_gcd s t p /\ prime p.
Proof. Admitted.

title: putnam_1999_b6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1999_b6:
;; a finite set of integers greater than one satisfying the stated gcd
;; covering condition contains two elements whose gcd is prime. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A duplicate-free true list is a bijective enumeration of the source finite
;; set. Since every element is greater than one, the product below is positive
;; and is a common multiple of every element.

(defun putnam-1999-b6-all-greater-than-one-p (elements)
  (if (consp elements)
      (and
       (integerp (car elements))
       (< 1 (car elements))
       (putnam-1999-b6-all-greater-than-one-p
        (cdr elements)))
    (equal elements nil)))

(defun putnam-1999-b6-product (elements)
  (if (consp elements)
      (* (car elements)
         (putnam-1999-b6-product (cdr elements)))
    1))

(defun putnam-1999-b6-gcd (left right)
  (declare (xargs :measure (+ (nfix left) (nfix right))))
  (if (and (natp left) (natp right))
      (cond
       ((equal left 0) right)
       ((equal right 0) left)
       ((< left right)
        (putnam-1999-b6-gcd left (- right left)))
       (t
        (putnam-1999-b6-gcd (- left right) right)))
    0))

(defun putnam-1999-b6-residue-covered-p (elements residue)
  (if (consp elements)
      (let* ((s (car elements))
             (common-divisor
              (putnam-1999-b6-gcd s residue)))
        (or
         (equal common-divisor 1)
         (equal common-divisor s)
         (putnam-1999-b6-residue-covered-p
          (cdr elements) residue)))
    nil))

;; For each positive s in the list, gcd(s,n) depends only on n modulo s.
;; The list product is divisible by every s, so checking its complete residue
;; system is equivalent to the source hypothesis quantified over all integers.
(defun putnam-1999-b6-all-residues-covered-p
    (elements remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (let ((residue (- remaining 1)))
      (and
       (putnam-1999-b6-residue-covered-p
        elements residue)
       (putnam-1999-b6-all-residues-covered-p
        elements residue)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b6-no-divisor-through-p
    (number candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (or
       (not (natp candidate))
       (<= candidate 1))
      t
    (and
     (not (equal (mod number candidate) 0))
     (putnam-1999-b6-no-divisor-through-p
      number (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-1999-b6-prime-p (number)
  (and
   (natp number)
   (< 1 number)
   (putnam-1999-b6-no-divisor-through-p
    number (- number 1))))

(defun putnam-1999-b6-prime-gcd-with-some-p
    (s candidates)
  (if (consp candidates)
      (or
       (putnam-1999-b6-prime-p
        (putnam-1999-b6-gcd s (car candidates)))
       (putnam-1999-b6-prime-gcd-with-some-p
        s (cdr candidates)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-1999-b6-prime-gcd-pair-p
    (remaining elements)
  (if (consp remaining)
      (or
       (putnam-1999-b6-prime-gcd-with-some-p
        (car remaining) elements)
       (putnam-1999-b6-prime-gcd-pair-p
        (cdr remaining) elements))
    nil))

(defun putnambench-putnam-1999-b6-statement (elements)
  (implies
   (and
    (true-listp elements)
    (no-duplicatesp-equal elements)
    (putnam-1999-b6-all-greater-than-one-p elements)
    (let ((period (putnam-1999-b6-product elements)))
      (putnam-1999-b6-all-residues-covered-p
       elements period)))
   (putnam-1999-b6-prime-gcd-pair-p
    elements elements)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_1999_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1999_b6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_1999_b6): a finite set of integers greater than
-- one satisfying a universal gcd dichotomy contains two elements whose gcd
-- is prime. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; mod-helper)

infix 4 _member_ _<=N_ _divides_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _member_ {A : Set} (x : A) : List A -> Set where
  here  : {xs : List A} -> x member (x ∷ xs)
  there : {y : A} {xs : List A} ->
          x member xs ->
          x member (y ∷ xs)

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record _divides_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    division-equation : dividend == divisor * quotient

data IntegerGreaterThanOne : Int -> Set where
  positive-at-least-two :
    (k : Nat) ->
    IntegerGreaterThanOne (pos (suc (suc k)))

absInt : Int -> Nat
absInt (pos n) =
  n
absInt (negsuc n) =
  suc n

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero =
  zero
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

gcdWithFuel : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat
gcdWithFuel zero a b =
  a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a zero =
  a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a (suc b) =
  gcdWithFuel fuel (suc b) (naturalMod a (suc b))

naturalGCD : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalGCD a b =
  gcdWithFuel (suc (a + b)) a b

integerGCD : Int -> Int -> Nat
integerGCD x y =
  naturalGCD (absInt x) (absInt y)

record Prime (p : Nat) : Set where
  field
    at-least-two :
      suc (suc zero) <=N p
    only-trivial-divisors :
      (d : Nat) ->
      d divides p ->
      (d == suc zero) or (d == p)

putnam-1999-b6 : Set
putnam-1999-b6 =
  (S : List Int) ->
  ((s : Int) ->
    s member S ->
    IntegerGreaterThanOne s) ->
  ((n : Int) ->
    Exists Int
      (\ s ->
        s member S
        and
        ((integerGCD s n == suc zero)
        or
        (integerGCD s n == absInt s)))) ->
  Exists Int
    (\ s ->
      s member S
      and
      Exists Int
        (\ t ->
          t member S
          and
          Prime (integerGCD s t)))

  greatest-common-divisor selection property contains two members whose

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(

  The first restricted universal quantifier states that every member is
  greater than one. The second retains the source quantifier over every
  integer n and its internally existential choice of s in S.

                \/
                ( s gcd n ) = s

      E. s e. S E. t e. S ( s gcd t ) e. Prime

title: putnam_1999_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_1999_b6:
% a finite set of integers greater than one satisfying the stated gcd
% selection property contains two elements whose gcd is prime. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_1999_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[int]

  int_divides(divisor, value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: int):
      value = divisor * quotient

  is_nonnegative_gcd(gcd_value, left, right: int): bool =
    gcd_value >= 0
      AND int_divides(gcd_value, left)
      AND int_divides(gcd_value, right)
      AND (FORALL (common_divisor: int):
        int_divides(common_divisor, left)
          AND int_divides(common_divisor, right)
          IMPLIES int_divides(common_divisor, gcd_value))

  prime_int(value: int): bool =
    value > 1
      AND (FORALL (divisor: int):
        divisor > 0
          AND int_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value)

  putnam_1999_b6: bool =
    FORALL (S: finite_set[int]):
      ((FORALL (s: int):
          S(s) IMPLIES s > 1)
        AND (FORALL (n: int):
          EXISTS (s: int):
            S(s)
              AND (is_nonnegative_gcd(1, s, n)
                OR is_nonnegative_gcd(s, s, n))))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (s, t, gcd_value: int):
          S(s)
            AND S(t)
            AND is_nonnegative_gcd(gcd_value, s, t)
            AND prime_int(gcd_value)
END putnam_1999_b6

import Mathlib

open Topology Filter

abbrev putnam_2000_a1_solution : ℝ → Set ℝ := sorry
-- (fun A : ℝ => Set.Ioo 0 (A ^ 2))
/--
Let $A$ be a positive real number. What are the possible values of $\sum_{j=0}^\infty x_j^2$, given that $x_0,x_1,\ldots$ are positive numbers for which $\sum_{j=0}^\infty x_j=A$?
-/
theorem putnam_2000_a1
(A : ℝ)
(Apos : A > 0)
: {S : ℝ |
    ∃ x : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ j : ℕ, x j > 0) ∧
      (∑' j : ℕ, x j) = A ∧
      (∑' j : ℕ, (x j) ^ 2) = S}
  = putnam_2000_a1_solution A :=
sorry

Require Import Reals Coquelicot.Coquelicot.
Definition putnam_2000_a1_solution : R -> (R -> Prop) := (fun A : R => (fun x : R => 0 < x < A ^ 2)).
Theorem putnam_2000_a1
    (A: R)
    (hA : A > 0)
    : forall SS : R, ((exists x : nat -> R, (forall j : nat, x j > 0) /\ Series x = A /\ Series (fun j => (x j) ^ 2) = SS) <-> (putnam_2000_a1_solution A) SS).
Proof. Admitted.

title: putnam_2000_a1
putnam_2000_a1
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_a1:
;; for positive real A, the squared sums of positive real sequences summing
;; to A are exactly the real numbers strictly between 0 and A^2. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A real is represented by a rational regular Cauchy name: at each positive
;; rational precision it returns a rational approximation. A sequence name
;; returns a pair whose CAR is such an approximation to x_j and whose CDR at
;; precision 1 is a positive rational lower bound for x_j. These names retain
;; arbitrary real values and an arbitrary function on the naturals; they are
;; neither rational-valued restrictions nor finite tables.
;;
;; The source existential sequence stays internal. Its witness is a list of
;; three function objects: the sequence and convergence moduli for its sum and
;; squared sum. Negated FN-EQUAL quantifies over that complete witness object.
;; The two limit matrices are the Cauchy definitions of
;;
;;   sum_j x_j = A  and  sum_j x_j^2 = S.
;;
;; The final IFF is the pointwise form of the source set equality. Strict
;; positivity is represented by an internal positive rational margin. For
;; A^2-S the approximations use an adaptive precision bounded from a
;; precision-1 approximation to A, so no real input is narrowed to ACL2's
;; rational number domain.

(defun putnam-2000-a1-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'cons
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2000-a1-term-list (cdr terms)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-apply-term (function arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2000-a1-quoted function)
        (putnam-2000-a1-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'if
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms (cdr terms))
            (putnam-2000-a1-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2000-a1-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list 'if
        hypothesis
        conclusion
        (putnam-2000-a1-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-negate-term (value)
  (list 'unary-- value))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-subtract-term (left right)
  (putnam-2000-a1-add-term
   left
   (putnam-2000-a1-negate-term right)))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-multiply-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-* left right))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-divide-term (numerator denominator)
  (putnam-2000-a1-multiply-term
   numerator
   (list 'unary-/ denominator)))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-absolute-term (value)
  (list 'if
        (list '< value 0)
        (putnam-2000-a1-negate-term value)
        value))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-less-equal-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        (list '< right left)
        (putnam-2000-a1-quoted nil)
        (putnam-2000-a1-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-minimum-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        (list '< left right)
        left
        right))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-positive-rational-term (value)
  (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms
   (list
    (list 'rationalp value)
    (list '< 0 value))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda
        formals
        (putnam-2000-a1-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-real-value-term (name precision)
  (putnam-2000-a1-apply-term name (list precision)))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-real-cauchy-function (name)
  (let* ((left
          (putnam-2000-a1-real-value-term name 'epsilon))
         (right
          (putnam-2000-a1-real-value-term name 'eta))
         (distance
          (putnam-2000-a1-absolute-term
           (putnam-2000-a1-subtract-term left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon eta)
     (putnam-2000-a1-implies-term
      (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms
       (list
        (putnam-2000-a1-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
        (putnam-2000-a1-positive-rational-term 'eta)))
      (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2000-a1-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2000-a1-add-term
          'epsilon 'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-real-name-p (name)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2000-a1-real-cauchy-function name)
    (putnam-2000-a1-true-function
     '(epsilon eta)))))

;; LOWER is a strict positive margin for the real denoted by NAME.
(defun putnam-2000-a1-positive-margin-function (name lower)
  (let ((value
         (putnam-2000-a1-real-value-term name 'epsilon)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2000-a1-implies-term
      (putnam-2000-a1-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
      (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp value)
        (putnam-2000-a1-less-equal-term
         (putnam-2000-a1-quoted lower)
         (putnam-2000-a1-add-term
          value 'epsilon))))))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-positive-margin-p (name lower)
  (and
   (rationalp lower)
   (< 0 lower)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2000-a1-positive-margin-function
     name lower)
    (putnam-2000-a1-true-function '(epsilon)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-positive-margin-failure-function (name)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(lower)
   (list
    'if
    (list
     'putnam-2000-a1-positive-margin-p
     (putnam-2000-a1-quoted name)
     'lower)
    (putnam-2000-a1-quoted nil)
    (putnam-2000-a1-quoted t))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-positive-real-p (name)
  (let ((failure-function
         (putnam-2000-a1-positive-margin-failure-function
          name))
        (true-function
         (putnam-2000-a1-true-function '(lower))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp failure-function)
     (tamep-functionp true-function)
     (not (fn-equal failure-function true-function)))))

;; This matrix gives a strict positive margin for A^2-S. If a1 approximates A
;; at precision 1, then 2+|a1| bounds both A and every A-approximation taken
;; below at precision at most 1. The adaptive DELTA therefore controls the
;; squaring error uniformly.
(defun putnam-2000-a1-square-gap-margin-function
    (a s lower)
  (let* ((a-at-one
          (putnam-2000-a1-real-value-term a 1))
         (bound
          (putnam-2000-a1-add-term
           2
           (putnam-2000-a1-absolute-term a-at-one)))
         (candidate-delta
          (putnam-2000-a1-divide-term
           'epsilon
           (putnam-2000-a1-multiply-term 4 bound)))
         (delta
          (putnam-2000-a1-minimum-term
           1 candidate-delta))
         (a-value
          (putnam-2000-a1-real-value-term a delta))
         (s-value
          (putnam-2000-a1-real-value-term s 'epsilon))
         (gap-approximation
          (putnam-2000-a1-subtract-term
           (putnam-2000-a1-multiply-term
            a-value a-value)
           s-value)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2000-a1-implies-term
      (putnam-2000-a1-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
      (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp a-at-one)
        (list 'rationalp a-value)
        (list 'rationalp s-value)
        (putnam-2000-a1-less-equal-term
         (putnam-2000-a1-quoted lower)
         (putnam-2000-a1-add-term
          gap-approximation
          (putnam-2000-a1-multiply-term
           2 'epsilon)))))))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-square-gap-margin-p
    (a s lower)
  (and
   (rationalp lower)
   (< 0 lower)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2000-a1-square-gap-margin-function
     a s lower)
    (putnam-2000-a1-true-function '(epsilon)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-square-gap-failure-function (a s)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(lower)
   (list
    'if
    (list
     'putnam-2000-a1-square-gap-margin-p
     (putnam-2000-a1-quoted a)
     (putnam-2000-a1-quoted s)
     'lower)
    (putnam-2000-a1-quoted nil)
    (putnam-2000-a1-quoted t))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-square-gap-positive-p (a s)
  (let ((failure-function
         (putnam-2000-a1-square-gap-failure-function
          a s))
        (true-function
         (putnam-2000-a1-true-function '(lower))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp failure-function)
     (tamep-functionp true-function)
     (not (fn-equal failure-function true-function)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-in-solution-interval-p (a s)
  (and
   (putnam-2000-a1-positive-real-p s)
   (putnam-2000-a1-square-gap-positive-p a s)))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-sequence-component-term
    (sequence component index precision)
  (list component
        (putnam-2000-a1-apply-term
         sequence
         (list index precision))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-sequence-cauchy-function (sequence)
  (let* ((left
          (putnam-2000-a1-sequence-component-term
           sequence 'car 'n 'epsilon))
         (right
          (putnam-2000-a1-sequence-component-term
           sequence 'car 'n 'eta))
         (distance
          (putnam-2000-a1-absolute-term
           (putnam-2000-a1-subtract-term left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(n epsilon eta)
     (putnam-2000-a1-implies-term
      (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'natp 'n)
        (putnam-2000-a1-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
        (putnam-2000-a1-positive-rational-term 'eta)))
      (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2000-a1-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2000-a1-add-term
          'epsilon 'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-sequence-positive-function (sequence)
  (let ((lower
         (putnam-2000-a1-sequence-component-term
          sequence 'cdr 'n 1))
        (value
         (putnam-2000-a1-sequence-component-term
          sequence 'car 'n 'epsilon)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(n epsilon)
     (putnam-2000-a1-implies-term
      (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'natp 'n)
        (putnam-2000-a1-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)))
      (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms
       (list
        (putnam-2000-a1-positive-rational-term lower)
        (list 'rationalp value)
        (putnam-2000-a1-less-equal-term
         lower
         (putnam-2000-a1-add-term
          value 'epsilon))))))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-positive-sequence-p (sequence)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp sequence)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2000-a1-sequence-cauchy-function sequence)
    (putnam-2000-a1-true-function
     '(n epsilon eta)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2000-a1-sequence-positive-function sequence)
    (putnam-2000-a1-true-function
     '(n epsilon)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-modulus-function (modulus)
  (let ((cutoff
         (putnam-2000-a1-apply-term modulus '(epsilon))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2000-a1-implies-term
      (putnam-2000-a1-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
      (list 'natp cutoff)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-modulus-p (modulus)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp modulus)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2000-a1-modulus-function modulus)
    (putnam-2000-a1-true-function '(epsilon)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-sequence-value
    (sequence index precision)
  (car (apply$ sequence (list index precision))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-partial-sum
    (sequence terms precision)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let ((index (- (nfix terms) 1)))
      (+ (putnam-2000-a1-partial-sum
          sequence index precision)
         (putnam-2000-a1-sequence-value
          sequence index precision)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-square-precision
    (sequence index terms epsilon)
  (let* ((at-one
          (putnam-2000-a1-sequence-value
           sequence index 1))
         (bound (+ 2 (abs at-one)))
         (candidate
          (/ epsilon
             (* 4 (+ (nfix terms) 1) bound))))
    (if (< candidate 1)
        candidate
      1)))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-partial-square-sum
    (sequence remaining terms epsilon)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (let* ((index (- (nfix remaining) 1))
           (precision
            (putnam-2000-a1-square-precision
             sequence index terms epsilon))
           (value
            (putnam-2000-a1-sequence-value
             sequence index precision)))
      (+ (putnam-2000-a1-partial-square-sum
          sequence index terms epsilon)
         (* value value)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-series-limit-function
    (sequence modulus target squaredp)
  (let* ((cutoff
          (putnam-2000-a1-apply-term
           modulus '(epsilon)))
         (target-value
          (putnam-2000-a1-real-value-term
           target 'epsilon))
         (term-precision
          (putnam-2000-a1-divide-term
           'epsilon
           (putnam-2000-a1-add-term 'terms 1)))
         (partial-sum
          (if squaredp
              (list
               'putnam-2000-a1-partial-square-sum
               (putnam-2000-a1-quoted sequence)
               'terms
               'terms
               'epsilon)
            (list
             'putnam-2000-a1-partial-sum
             (putnam-2000-a1-quoted sequence)
             'terms
             term-precision)))
         (distance
          (putnam-2000-a1-absolute-term
           (putnam-2000-a1-subtract-term
            partial-sum target-value))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon terms)
     (putnam-2000-a1-implies-term
      (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms
       (list
        (putnam-2000-a1-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
        (list 'natp 'terms)
        (putnam-2000-a1-less-equal-term
         cutoff 'terms)))
      (putnam-2000-a1-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp partial-sum)
        (list 'rationalp target-value)
        (putnam-2000-a1-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2000-a1-multiply-term
          4 'epsilon))))))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-series-limit-p
    (sequence modulus target squaredp)
  (and
   (putnam-2000-a1-modulus-p modulus)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2000-a1-series-limit-function
     sequence modulus target squaredp)
    (putnam-2000-a1-true-function
     '(epsilon terms)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-attainment-witness-p
    (witness a s)
  (and
   (true-listp witness)
   (equal (len witness) 3)
   (let ((sequence (nth 0 witness))
         (sum-modulus (nth 1 witness))
         (square-modulus (nth 2 witness)))
     (and
      (putnam-2000-a1-positive-sequence-p sequence)
      (putnam-2000-a1-series-limit-p
       sequence sum-modulus a nil)
      (putnam-2000-a1-series-limit-p
       sequence square-modulus s t)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-attainment-failure-function (a s)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(witness)
   (list
    'if
    (list
     'putnam-2000-a1-attainment-witness-p
     'witness
     (putnam-2000-a1-quoted a)
     (putnam-2000-a1-quoted s))
    (putnam-2000-a1-quoted nil)
    (putnam-2000-a1-quoted t))))

(defun putnam-2000-a1-attainable-p (a s)
  (let ((failure-function
         (putnam-2000-a1-attainment-failure-function
          a s))
        (true-function
         (putnam-2000-a1-true-function '(witness))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp failure-function)
     (tamep-functionp true-function)
     (not (fn-equal failure-function true-function)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2000-a1-statement (a s)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2000-a1-real-name-p a)
    (putnam-2000-a1-real-name-p s)
    (putnam-2000-a1-positive-real-p a))
   (iff
    (putnam-2000-a1-attainable-p a s)
    (putnam-2000-a1-in-solution-interval-p a s))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2000_a1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_a1:
-- the square-sums of positive real sequences with fixed positive infinite sum
-- are exactly the values strictly between zero and its square. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_
infix 1 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

module Putnam2000A1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  square : R -> R
  square x =
    multiply reals x x

  PositiveSequence : (Nat -> R) -> Set
  PositiveSequence x =
    (j : Nat) ->
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (x j)

  AttainableSquareSum : R -> R -> Set
  AttainableSquareSum A S =
    Exists (Nat -> R)
      (\ x ->
        PositiveSequence x
        and
        (SeriesHasSum reals x A
        and
        SeriesHasSum reals
          (\ j -> square (x j))
          S))

  Solution : R -> R -> Set
  Solution A S =
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) S
    and
    StrictLess reals S (square A)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (A : R) ->
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) A ->
    (S : R) ->
    AttainableSquareSum A S
    iff
    Solution A S

putnam-2000-a1 : Set1
putnam-2000-a1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2000A1Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_a1:
  for positive A, the possible sums of squares of positive real sequences
  with sum A form the open interval from 0 to A squared. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory seqTheory;

val putnam_2000_a1 =
  ``!A : real.
      0 < A
      ==>
      {s : real |
         ?x : num -> real.
           (!j : num. 0 < x j) /\
           x sums A /\
           (\j : num. (x j) pow 2) sums s} =
      {s : real | 0 < s /\ s < A pow 2}``;

title: putnam_2000_a1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2000_a1: the possible sums of squares of a positive real sequence
  with prescribed positive total are exactly the reals strictly between zero
  and the square of that total. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  RR ^m NN0 is the class of all real-valued sequences indexed by the
  nonnegative integers. The two sum_ expressions are set.mm's unbounded
  real-series sums, matching the total infinite sums in the source
  formalizations. The sequence witness remains internally existentially
  quantified for each possible value S.

  The right side inlines the explicit Rocq solution and the open-interval
  solution annotated in the Lean and Isabelle sources. The final declaration
  is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p
  proof statement.
$)

${
  $d A S j x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2000-a1 $a |- A. A e. RR
    (
      0 < A
      ->
      {
        S e. RR |
        E. x e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
          (
            (
              A. j e. NN0
                0 < ( x ` j )
            )
            /\
            (
              (
                sum_ j e. NN0
                  ( x ` j )
              )
              =
              A
              /\
              (
                sum_ j e. NN0
                  ( ( x ` j ) ^ 2 )
              )
              =
              S
            )
          )
      }
      =
      {
        S e. RR |
        (
          0 < S
          /\
          S < ( A ^ 2 )
        )
      }
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2000_a1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_a1:
% the possible sums of squares of a strictly positive real sequence with
% prescribed positive sum form the open interval from zero to its square.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2000_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  partial_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  series_sum(values: real_sequence, total: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat): partial_sum(values, count),
      total)

  putnam_2000_a1: bool =
    FORALL (A, S: real):
      A > 0 IMPLIES
        ((EXISTS (x: real_sequence):
            (FORALL (index: nat): x(index) > 0)
              AND series_sum(x, A)
              AND series_sum(
                LAMBDA (index: nat): x(index) ^ 2,
                S))
          IFF (0 < S AND S < A ^ 2))
END putnam_2000_a1

import Mathlib

open Topology Filter

/--
Prove that there exist infinitely many integers $n$ such that $n,n+1,n+2$ are each the sum of the squares of two integers.
-/
theorem putnam_2000_a2 :
  ∀ n : ℕ,
    ∃ N : ℤ,
      ∃ i : Fin 6 → ℕ,
        N > n ∧
        N = (i 0)^2 + (i 1)^2 ∧
        N + 1 = (i 2)^2 + (i 3)^2 ∧
        N + 2 = (i 4)^2 + (i 5)^2 :=
  sorry

title: putnam_2000_a2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_a2:
;; arbitrarily large integers begin triples of consecutive integers, each a
;; sum of two integer squares. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; LOWER is the universally quantified integer lower bound.  The source's
;; existential integers m,a,b,c,d,e,f are kept internal as a seven-element
;; tuple.  FN-EQUAL compares the failure predicate with the constant-T
;; function on every ACL2 object, so its negation says exactly that some
;; integer tuple satisfies the strict bound and the three square-sum equations.

(defun putnam-2000-a2-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2000-a2-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'if
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2000-a2-and-terms (cdr terms))
       (putnam-2000-a2-quoted nil))

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_a2:
-- arbitrarily large integers begin three consecutive sums of two integer
-- squares. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<Z_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data _<Z_ : Int -> Int -> Set where
  negative<positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    negsuc m <Z pos n
  positive<positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    suc m <=N n ->
    pos m <Z pos n
  negative<negative :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    suc n <=N m ->
    negsuc m <Z negsuc n

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

squareInt : Int -> Int
squareInt (pos n) =
  pos (n * n)
squareInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n * suc n)

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos (suc zero)

twoZ : Int
twoZ =
  pos (suc (suc zero))

SumOfTwoSquares : Int -> Set
SumOfTwoSquares n =
  Exists Int
    (\ a ->
      Exists Int
        (\ b ->
          n == addInt (squareInt a) (squareInt b)))

putnam-2000-a2 : Set
putnam-2000-a2 =
  (lower : Int) ->
  Exists Int
    (\ n ->
      (lower <Z n)
      and
      SumOfTwoSquares n
      and
      SumOfTwoSquares (addInt n oneZ)
      and
      SumOfTwoSquares (addInt n twoZ))

$(

  putnam_2000_a2: above every integer cutoff, three consecutive integers
  exist that are each sums of two integer squares. This file contains no
  proof.

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(

  the three consecutive values, and all six square witnesses in ZZ. This is

  witnesses: absolute values replace integer square witnesses by natural
  ones, and the case of cutoff zero supplies a positive triple above every
  negative integer cutoff. It is also equivalent to Rocq's non-strict cutoff
  form by shifting the universally quantified cutoff by one.

  Every witness remains internally existentially quantified. The final
  declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.

${
  $d a b c d e f m n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2000-a2 $a |- A. n e. ZZ
    E. m e. ZZ
      (

        /\

            E. e e. ZZ E. f e. ZZ

$}

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_a4:
;; convergence of the improper real integral of sin(x)*sin(x^2) from zero
;; to an upper endpoint tending to positive infinity. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; For rational UPPER >= 0 and positive integer STAGE, the value below is a
;; rational midpoint sum on [0,UPPER]. Both sine factors are evaluated by
;; Maclaurin prefixes whose length tends to infinity with STAGE. For each
;; fixed rational UPPER these values converge to
;;
;;   integral_0^UPPER sin(x)*sin(x^2) dx.
;;
;; Thus this is a Cauchy name for the source finite real integral, not a fixed
;; quadrature or a rational-valued replacement for it.

(defun putnam-2000-a4-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n
       (putnam-2000-a4-factorial (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a4-sine-prefix (x terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (degree (+ (* 2 index) 1))
           (sign (if (equal (mod index 2) 0)
                     1
                   -1)))
      (+ (putnam-2000-a4-sine-prefix x index)
         (/ (* sign (expt x degree))
            (putnam-2000-a4-factorial degree))))))

(defun putnam-2000-a4-midpoint
    (index upper subdivisions)
  (* upper
     (/ (+ (* 2 index) 1)
        (* 2 subdivisions))))

(defun putnam-2000-a4-midpoint-sum
    (remaining upper subdivisions terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (let* ((index (- remaining 1))
           (x (putnam-2000-a4-midpoint
               index upper subdivisions))
           (sine-x
            (putnam-2000-a4-sine-prefix x terms))
           (sine-x-squared
            (putnam-2000-a4-sine-prefix
             (* x x) terms)))
      (+ (* sine-x sine-x-squared)
         (putnam-2000-a4-midpoint-sum
          index upper subdivisions terms)))))

(defun putnam-2000-a4-integral-approx (upper stage)
  (if (and (rationalp upper)
           (<= 0 upper)
           (posp stage))
      (* (/ upper stage)
         (putnam-2000-a4-midpoint-sum
          stage upper stage stage))
    0))

;; The source limit exists exactly when its finite-integral values satisfy the
;; Cauchy criterion at positive infinity. Nonnegative rational endpoints are
;; enough: they are cofinal and dense in the reals, and the finite-integral
;; function is continuous in its endpoint. Completeness of the reals then
;; recovers the source's internal existential limit.
;;
;; The source asserts convergence, not a particular quantitative rate.
;; Therefore every tail and approximation modulus below is existential. The
;; quantifier order is the Cauchy criterion for the endpoint-indexed finite
;; integrals, with each finite integral itself represented by its convergent
;; midpoint/Maclaurin approximation sequence.

(defun-sk putnam-2000-a4-stage-tail-p
    (epsilon left-upper right-upper
             left-cutoff right-cutoff)
  (forall (left-stage right-stage)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp left-stage)
      (<= left-cutoff left-stage)
      (natp right-stage)
      (<= right-cutoff right-stage))
     (< (abs
         (- (putnam-2000-a4-integral-approx
             left-upper left-stage)
            (putnam-2000-a4-integral-approx
             right-upper right-stage)))
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-a4-stage-cutoffs-exist-p
    (epsilon left-upper right-upper)
  (exists (left-cutoff right-cutoff)
    (and
     (posp left-cutoff)
     (posp right-cutoff)
     (putnam-2000-a4-stage-tail-p
      epsilon left-upper right-upper
      left-cutoff right-cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-a4-endpoint-tail-p
    (epsilon endpoint-cutoff)
  (forall (left-upper right-upper)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp left-upper)
      (<= endpoint-cutoff left-upper)
      (rationalp right-upper)
      (<= endpoint-cutoff right-upper))
     (putnam-2000-a4-stage-cutoffs-exist-p
      epsilon left-upper right-upper))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-a4-endpoint-cutoff-exists-p
    (epsilon)
  (exists (endpoint-cutoff)
    (and
     (rationalp endpoint-cutoff)
     (<= 0 endpoint-cutoff)
     (putnam-2000-a4-endpoint-tail-p
      epsilon endpoint-cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-2000-a4-statement ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-2000-a4-endpoint-cutoff-exists-p
      epsilon))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
