/--
Let $f(t)=\sum_{j=1}^N a_j \sin(2\pi jt)$, where each $a_j$ is real and $a_N$ is not equal to $0$. Let $N_k$ denote the number of zeroes (including multiplicities) of $\frac{d^k f}{dt^k}$. Prove that
\[
N_0\leq N_1\leq N_2\leq \cdots \mbox{ and } \lim_{k\to\infty} N_k = 2N.
\]
-/
theorem putnam_2000_b3
  (N : ℕ) (hN : N > 0)
  (a : Icc 1 N → ℝ)
  (f : ℝ → ℝ)
  (mult : (ℝ → ℝ) → ℝ → ℕ)
  (M : ℕ → ℕ)
  (haN : a ⟨N, by simp; omega⟩ ≠ 0)
  (hf : ∀ t, f t = ∑ j : Icc 1 N, a j * Real.sin (2 * Real.pi * j * t))
  (hmult : ∀ g : ℝ → ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, (∃ c : ℕ, iteratedDeriv c g t ≠ 0) → (iteratedDeriv (mult g t) g t ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ k < (mult g t), iteratedDeriv k g t = 0))
  (hM : ∀ k, M k = ∑' t : Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, mult (iteratedDeriv k f) t) :
  ((∀ i j : ℕ, i ≤ j → M i ≤ M j) ∧ Tendsto M atTop (𝓝 (2 * N))) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2000_b3
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_2000_b3:
   multiplicity-weighted zero counts of successive derivatives of a real
   trigonometric polynomial are nondecreasing and tend to twice its highest
   frequency. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import
  Reals Lists.List Arith.PeanoNat
  ClassicalDescription ClassicalEpsilon.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2000_b3_total_derivative
    (f : R -> R) (x : R) : R :=
  match excluded_middle_informative
          (exists d : R, derivable_pt_lim f x d) with
  | left _ =>
      epsilon (inhabits (0 : R))
        (fun d : R => derivable_pt_lim f x d)
  | right _ => 0
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2000_b3_iterated_derivative
    (n : nat) (f : R -> R) : R -> R :=
  match n with
  | O => f
  | S k =>
      putnam_2000_b3_total_derivative
        (putnam_2000_b3_iterated_derivative k f)
  end.

Definition putnam_2000_b3_trigonometric_sum
    (N : nat) (a : nat -> R) (t : R) : R :=
  fold_right Rplus 0
    (map
      (fun j : nat =>
        a j * sin (2 * PI * INR j * t))
      (seq 1 N)).

Definition putnam_2000_b3_weighted_zero_count
    (mult : (R -> R) -> R -> nat)
    (g : R -> R)
    (total : nat) : Prop :=
  exists zeros : list R,
    NoDup zeros /\
    (forall t : R,
      In t zeros <->
        0 <= t /\ t < 1 /\ mult g t <> O) /\
    total =
      fold_right Nat.add O (map (mult g) zeros).

Theorem putnam_2000_b3
    (N : nat)
    (a : nat -> R)
    (f : R -> R)
    (mult : (R -> R) -> R -> nat)
    (M : nat -> nat)
    (Npos : (O < N)%nat)
    (haN : a N <> 0)
    (hf : forall t : R,
      f t = putnam_2000_b3_trigonometric_sum N a t)
    (hmult : forall (g : R -> R) (t : R),
      (exists c : nat,
        putnam_2000_b3_iterated_derivative c g t <> 0) ->
      putnam_2000_b3_iterated_derivative (mult g t) g t <> 0 /\
      forall k : nat,
        (k < mult g t)%nat ->
        putnam_2000_b3_iterated_derivative k g t = 0)
    (hM : forall k : nat,
      putnam_2000_b3_weighted_zero_count
        mult (putnam_2000_b3_iterated_derivative k f) (M k)) :
  (forall i j : nat,
    (i <= j)%nat ->
    (M i <= M j)%nat) /\
  exists K : nat,
    forall k : nat,
      (K <= k)%nat ->
      M k = (2 * N)%nat.
Admitted.

title: putnam_2000_b3
content:
theory putnam_2000_b3 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Derivative"
begin

(* uses (nat \<Rightarrow> real) instead of (Fin (N + 1) \<Rightarrow> real) *)
theorem putnam_2000_b3:
  fixes N :: nat
  and a :: "nat \<Rightarrow> real"
  and f :: "real \<Rightarrow> real"
  and mult :: "(real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> real \<Rightarrow> nat"
  and M :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
  assumes Npos: "N > 0"
  and haN: "a N \<noteq> 0"
  defines "f \<equiv> (\<lambda>t::real. (\<Sum>j::nat=1..N. a j * sin (2*pi*j*t)))"
  assumes hmult: "\<forall>(g::real\<Rightarrow>real)(t::real). ((\<exists>c::nat. (deriv^^c) g t \<noteq> 0) \<longrightarrow> mult g t = (LEAST k::nat. (deriv^^k) g t \<noteq> 0))"
  defines "M \<equiv> (\<lambda>k::nat. (\<Sum>\<^sub>\<infinity>t::real\<in>{0..<1}. mult ((deriv^^k) f) t))"
  shows "(\<forall>i j::nat. (i \<le> j \<longrightarrow> M i \<le> M j)) \<and> filterlim M (nhds (2*N)) at_top"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_2000_b3
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b3:
  monotonicity and convergence to twice the highest frequency of the total
  zero multiplicities of successive derivatives of a finite sine polynomial.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let transc_output = open_out "/dev/null";;
let transc_formatter = Format.formatter_of_out_channel transc_output;;
let previous_file_loader = !Hol_loader.file_loader;;
Hol_loader.file_loader :=
  (fun path -> Toploop.use_file transc_formatter path);;
let transc_loaded =
  Toploop.use_file transc_formatter "Library/transc.ml";;
Hol_loader.file_loader := previous_file_loader;;
Format.pp_print_flush transc_formatter ();;
close_out transc_output;;
if not transc_loaded then failwith "failed to load Library/transc.ml";;

let statement =
  `let deriv =
     \(g:real->real) (x:real). @d:real. (g diffl d) x in
   let iterated_deriv =
     \(n:num) (g:real->real).
       (@D:num->real->real.
          D 0 = g /\
          (!k:num. D (SUC k) = deriv (D k))) n in
   !N:num.
   !a:num->real.
   !f:real->real.
   !mult:(real->real)->real->num.
   !M:num->num.
     0 < N /\
     ~(a N = &0) /\
     (!t:real.
        f t =
        sum (1..N) (\j:num. a j * sin (&2 * pi * &j * t))) /\
     (!g:real->real. !t:real.
        (?c:num. ~(iterated_deriv c g t = &0))
        ==> ~(iterated_deriv (mult g t) g t = &0) /\
            (!k:num.
               k < mult g t
               ==> iterated_deriv k g t = &0)) /\
     (!k:num.
        M k =
        nsum {t:real | &0 <= t /\ t < &1}
          (\t:real. mult (iterated_deriv k f) t))
     ==> (!i j:num. i <= j ==> M i <= M j) /\
         (?K:num. !k:num. K <= k ==> M k = 2 * N)`;;

title: putnam_2000_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b3:
;; zero counts with multiplicity for successive derivatives of a finite real
;; sine sum are nondecreasing and converge to twice the highest nonzero
;; frequency. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Conservative generic symbols present an arbitrary ordered field. The final
;; predicate explicitly requires the Archimedean real-closed-field laws.
;; Every finite tuple of source coefficients and every algebraic unit-circle
;; root lies in such a real-closed subfield of the reals, while every such
;; field embeds order-preservingly in the reals.

(defstub putnam-2000-b3-real-p (x) t)
(defstub putnam-2000-b3-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub putnam-2000-b3-mul-op (x y) t)
(defstub putnam-2000-b3-neg-op (x) t)
(defstub putnam-2000-b3-inv-op (x) t)
(defstub putnam-2000-b3-less-op (x y) t)

(defun putnam-2000-b3-member-p (x)
  (if (putnam-2000-b3-real-p x) t nil))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-add (x y)
  (putnam-2000-b3-add-op x y))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-mul (x y)
  (putnam-2000-b3-mul-op x y))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-neg (x)
  (putnam-2000-b3-neg-op x))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-inv (x)
  (putnam-2000-b3-inv-op x))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-less (x y)
  (if (putnam-2000-b3-less-op x y) t nil))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-field-laws-p (zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2000-b3-member-p x)
      (putnam-2000-b3-member-p y)
      (putnam-2000-b3-member-p z))
     (and
      (putnam-2000-b3-member-p
       (putnam-2000-b3-add x y))
      (putnam-2000-b3-member-p
       (putnam-2000-b3-mul x y))
      (putnam-2000-b3-member-p
       (putnam-2000-b3-neg x))
      (putnam-2000-b3-member-p
       (putnam-2000-b3-inv x))
      (equal
       (putnam-2000-b3-add
        (putnam-2000-b3-add x y) z)
       (putnam-2000-b3-add
        x (putnam-2000-b3-add y z)))
      (equal
       (putnam-2000-b3-add x y)
       (putnam-2000-b3-add y x))
      (equal (putnam-2000-b3-add x zero) x)
      (equal
       (putnam-2000-b3-add x (putnam-2000-b3-neg x))
       zero)
      (equal
       (putnam-2000-b3-mul
        (putnam-2000-b3-mul x y) z)
       (putnam-2000-b3-mul
        x (putnam-2000-b3-mul y z)))
      (equal
       (putnam-2000-b3-mul x y)
       (putnam-2000-b3-mul y x))
      (equal (putnam-2000-b3-mul x one) x)
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal
        (putnam-2000-b3-mul
         x (putnam-2000-b3-inv x))
        one))
      (equal
       (putnam-2000-b3-mul
        x (putnam-2000-b3-add y z))
       (putnam-2000-b3-add
        (putnam-2000-b3-mul x y)
        (putnam-2000-b3-mul x z)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-order-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2000-b3-member-p x)
      (putnam-2000-b3-member-p y)
      (putnam-2000-b3-member-p z))
     (and
      (not (putnam-2000-b3-less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (putnam-2000-b3-less x y)
       (putnam-2000-b3-less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (putnam-2000-b3-less x y)
        (putnam-2000-b3-less y z))
       (putnam-2000-b3-less x z))
      (implies
       (putnam-2000-b3-less x y)
       (putnam-2000-b3-less
        (putnam-2000-b3-add x z)
        (putnam-2000-b3-add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (putnam-2000-b3-less zero x)
        (putnam-2000-b3-less zero y))
       (putnam-2000-b3-less
        zero
        (putnam-2000-b3-mul x y)))))))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-coefficient-list-p (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and
       (putnam-2000-b3-member-p (car coefficients))
       (putnam-2000-b3-coefficient-list-p
        (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-polynomial-evaluate
    (coefficients x zero)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (putnam-2000-b3-add
       (car coefficients)
       (putnam-2000-b3-mul
        x
        (putnam-2000-b3-polynomial-evaluate
         (cdr coefficients) x zero)))
    zero))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-odd-degree-polynomial-p
    (coefficients zero)
  (and
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (consp coefficients)
   (putnam-2000-b3-coefficient-list-p coefficients)
   (not (equal (car (last coefficients)) zero))
   (evenp (len coefficients))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-square-root-exists-p (x)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (putnam-2000-b3-member-p root)
     (equal (putnam-2000-b3-mul root root) x))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-nonnegative-square-roots-p (zero)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2000-b3-member-p x)
      (not (putnam-2000-b3-less x zero)))
     (putnam-2000-b3-square-root-exists-p x))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-polynomial-root-exists-p
    (coefficients zero)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (putnam-2000-b3-member-p root)
     (equal
      (putnam-2000-b3-polynomial-evaluate
       coefficients root zero)
      zero))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-odd-polynomial-roots-p (zero)
  (forall (coefficients)
    (implies
     (putnam-2000-b3-odd-degree-polynomial-p
      coefficients zero)
     (putnam-2000-b3-polynomial-root-exists-p
      coefficients zero))))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-embed-natural (n zero one)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      zero
    (putnam-2000-b3-add
     one
     (putnam-2000-b3-embed-natural
      (- n 1) zero one))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-natural-bound-exists-p
    (x zero one)
  (exists (n)
    (and
     (natp n)
     (putnam-2000-b3-less
      x
      (putnam-2000-b3-embed-natural
       n zero one)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-archimedean-p (zero one)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (putnam-2000-b3-member-p x)
     (putnam-2000-b3-natural-bound-exists-p
      x zero one))))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-real-field-p (zero one)
  (and
   (putnam-2000-b3-member-p zero)
   (putnam-2000-b3-member-p one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (putnam-2000-b3-less zero one)
   (putnam-2000-b3-field-laws-p zero one)
   (putnam-2000-b3-order-laws-p zero)
   (putnam-2000-b3-nonnegative-square-roots-p zero)
   (putnam-2000-b3-odd-polynomial-roots-p zero)
   (putnam-2000-b3-archimedean-p zero one)))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-power (base exponent one)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      one
    (putnam-2000-b3-mul
     base
     (putnam-2000-b3-power
      base (- exponent 1) one))))

;; If (x,y)=(cos theta,sin theta), this recurrence returns
;; (cos(j*theta),sin(j*theta)).

(defun putnam-2000-b3-harmonic-pair
    (j x y zero one)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix j)))
  (if (zp j)
      (cons one zero)
    (let* ((previous
            (putnam-2000-b3-harmonic-pair
             (- j 1) x y zero one))
           (cosine (car previous))
           (sine (cdr previous)))
      (cons
       (putnam-2000-b3-add
        (putnam-2000-b3-mul cosine x)
        (putnam-2000-b3-neg
         (putnam-2000-b3-mul sine y)))
       (putnam-2000-b3-add
        (putnam-2000-b3-mul cosine y)
        (putnam-2000-b3-mul sine x))))))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-phase-value
    (derivative-order harmonic-pair)
  (case (mod derivative-order 4)
    (0 (cdr harmonic-pair))
    (1 (car harmonic-pair))
    (2 (putnam-2000-b3-neg (cdr harmonic-pair)))
    (otherwise
     (putnam-2000-b3-neg (car harmonic-pair)))))

;; This is the kth derivative divided by the nonzero common factor
;; (2*pi)^k. Removing that factor preserves every zero and multiplicity.

(defun putnam-2000-b3-derivative-value-aux
    (coefficients harmonic derivative-order x y
                  zero one)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (let* ((pair
              (putnam-2000-b3-harmonic-pair
               harmonic x y zero one))
             (harmonic-value
              (putnam-2000-b3-embed-natural
               harmonic zero one))
             (scale
              (putnam-2000-b3-power
               harmonic-value derivative-order one))
             (term
              (putnam-2000-b3-mul
               (car coefficients)
               (putnam-2000-b3-mul
                scale
                (putnam-2000-b3-phase-value
                 derivative-order pair)))))
        (putnam-2000-b3-add
         term
         (putnam-2000-b3-derivative-value-aux
          (cdr coefficients)
          (+ harmonic 1)
          derivative-order x y zero one)))
    zero))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-derivative-value
    (coefficients derivative-order x y zero one)
  (putnam-2000-b3-derivative-value-aux
   coefficients 1 derivative-order x y zero one))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-unit-circle-p (x y one)
  (and
   (putnam-2000-b3-member-p x)
   (putnam-2000-b3-member-p y)
   (equal
    (putnam-2000-b3-add
     (putnam-2000-b3-mul x x)
     (putnam-2000-b3-mul y y))
    one)))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-lower-derivatives-zero-p
    (coefficients derivative-order multiplicity
                  x y zero one)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix multiplicity)))
  (if (zp multiplicity)
      t
    (and
     (equal
      (putnam-2000-b3-derivative-value
       coefficients derivative-order x y zero one)
      zero)
     (putnam-2000-b3-lower-derivatives-zero-p
      coefficients
      (+ derivative-order 1)
      (- multiplicity 1)
      x y zero one))))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-multiplicity-p
    (coefficients derivative-order x y multiplicity
                  zero one)
  (and
   (posp multiplicity)
   (putnam-2000-b3-lower-derivatives-zero-p
    coefficients derivative-order multiplicity
    x y zero one)
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-2000-b3-derivative-value
      coefficients
      (+ derivative-order multiplicity)
      x y zero one)
     zero))))

;; A root entry is the list (x y multiplicity).

(defun putnam-2000-b3-root-entry-p
    (entry coefficients derivative-order zero one)
  (and
   (true-listp entry)
   (equal (len entry) 3)
   (putnam-2000-b3-unit-circle-p
    (nth 0 entry) (nth 1 entry) one)
   (putnam-2000-b3-multiplicity-p
    coefficients derivative-order
    (nth 0 entry) (nth 1 entry) (nth 2 entry)
    zero one)))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-point-not-in-entries-p
    (x y entries)
  (if (consp entries)
      (and
       (not
        (and
         (equal x (nth 0 (car entries)))
         (equal y (nth 1 (car entries)))))
       (putnam-2000-b3-point-not-in-entries-p
        x y (cdr entries)))
    (equal entries nil)))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-root-entries-p
    (entries coefficients derivative-order zero one)
  (if (consp entries)
      (and
       (putnam-2000-b3-root-entry-p
        (car entries) coefficients derivative-order
        zero one)
       (putnam-2000-b3-point-not-in-entries-p
        (nth 0 (car entries))
        (nth 1 (car entries))
        (cdr entries))
       (putnam-2000-b3-root-entries-p
        (cdr entries) coefficients derivative-order
        zero one))
    (equal entries nil)))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-point-in-entries-p (x y entries)
  (if (consp entries)
      (or
       (and
        (equal x (nth 0 (car entries)))
        (equal y (nth 1 (car entries))))
       (putnam-2000-b3-point-in-entries-p
        x y (cdr entries)))
    nil))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-all-roots-listed-p
    (entries coefficients derivative-order zero one)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2000-b3-unit-circle-p x y one)
      (equal
       (putnam-2000-b3-derivative-value
        coefficients derivative-order x y zero one)
       zero))
     (putnam-2000-b3-point-in-entries-p
      x y entries))))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-exact-root-list-p
    (entries coefficients derivative-order zero one)
  (and
   (true-listp entries)
   (putnam-2000-b3-root-entries-p
    entries coefficients derivative-order zero one)
   (putnam-2000-b3-all-roots-listed-p
    entries coefficients derivative-order zero one)))

(defun putnam-2000-b3-total-multiplicity (entries)
  (if (consp entries)
      (+
       (nth 2 (car entries))
       (putnam-2000-b3-total-multiplicity
        (cdr entries)))
    0))

;; The existential list is only a finite presentation of the source's root
;; set, not a choice of its cardinality. ROOT-ENTRIES-P admits no duplicate
;; point, ALL-ROOTS-LISTED-P makes the list complete, and MULTIPLICITY-P fixes
;; the unique first derivative order that is nonzero at each point. Hence any
;; two exact root lists differ only in ordering and have the same total.

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-root-count-is-p
    (coefficients derivative-order count zero one)
  (exists (entries)
    (and
     (natp count)
     (putnam-2000-b3-exact-root-list-p
      entries coefficients derivative-order zero one)
     (equal
      (putnam-2000-b3-total-multiplicity entries)
      count))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-count-comparison-p
    (coefficients i j zero one)
  (exists (count-i count-j)
    (and
     (putnam-2000-b3-root-count-is-p
      coefficients i count-i zero one)
     (putnam-2000-b3-root-count-is-p
      coefficients j count-j zero one)
     (<= count-i count-j))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-nondecreasing-p
    (coefficients zero one)
  (forall (i j)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (natp j)
      (<= i j))
     (putnam-2000-b3-count-comparison-p
      coefficients i j zero one))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-tail-equals-twice-frequency-p
    (coefficients cutoff zero one)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp k)
      (<= cutoff k))
     (putnam-2000-b3-root-count-is-p
      coefficients
      k
      (* 2 (len coefficients))
      zero one))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b3-eventually-twice-frequency-p
    (coefficients zero one)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (putnam-2000-b3-tail-equals-twice-frequency-p
      coefficients cutoff zero one))))

;; The coefficient list is (a_1,...,a_N), so its nonempty length is N and its
;; last entry is the source assumption a_N != 0. The half-open interval [0,1)
;; maps bijectively to the unit circle by t |-> (cos(2*pi*t),sin(2*pi*t)).
;; Exact duplicate-free root lists therefore define the same M(k) internally.
;; Since M is natural-valued, convergence to 2N is equivalent to eventual
;; equality with 2N.
;;
;; The real-field antecedent is a structure hypothesis on ACL2's arbitrary
;; defstub operations, not an existentially chosen witness. The resulting
;; implication is uniform over every interpretation satisfying the laws, and
;; the ordinary real numbers supply a concrete satisfying interpretation.

(defun putnambench-putnam-2000-b3-statement
    (coefficients zero one)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2000-b3-real-field-p zero one)
    (true-listp coefficients)
    (consp coefficients)
    (putnam-2000-b3-coefficient-list-p coefficients)
    (not
     (equal (car (last coefficients)) zero)))
   (and
    (putnam-2000-b3-nondecreasing-p
     coefficients zero one)
    (putnam-2000-b3-eventually-twice-frequency-p
     coefficients zero one))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2000_b3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2000_b3): zero counts with multiplicity for
-- successive derivatives of a finite real sine sum are nondecreasing and
-- converge to twice its top frequency. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  twoN + twoN

PositiveNat : Nat -> Set
PositiveNat n =
  oneN <=N n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

sumFinNat :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Nat) ->
  Nat
sumFinNat {zero} terms =
  zero
sumFinNat {suc n} terms =
  terms fzero +
  sumFinNat (\ i -> terms (fsuc i))

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

alternatingPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingPower reals n =
  naturalPower reals
    (negate reals (oneR reals))
    n

sineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
sineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (suc (twoN * n))))
    (fromNat reals (factorial (suc (twoN * n))))

leibnizTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
leibnizTerm reals n =
  divide reals
    (alternatingPower reals n)
    (fromNat reals (suc (twoN * n)))

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
differenceQuotient reals function point x =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals (function x) (function point))
    (subtract reals x point)

DerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeAt {R} reals function point derivativeValue =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        x != point ->
        CloseTo reals derivativeValue epsilon
          (differenceQuotient reals function point x)))

record StandardRealAnalysis
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) : Set1 where
  field
    sine : R -> R
    pi : R

    sine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (sineTerm reals x)
        (sine x)
    pi-positive :
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) pi
    pi-leibniz-series :
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (leibnizTerm reals)
        (divide reals pi (fromNat reals fourN))

    derivative : (R -> R) -> R -> R
    derivative-correct :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      (point derivativeValue : R) ->
      DerivativeAt reals function point derivativeValue ->
      derivative function point == derivativeValue
    derivative-totalized-at-zero :
      (function : R -> R) ->
      (point : R) ->
      Not (Exists R (DerivativeAt reals function point)) ->
      derivative function point == zeroR reals

open StandardRealAnalysis

iteratedDerivative :
  {R : Set} ->
  {reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R} ->
  StandardRealAnalysis reals ->
  Nat ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
iteratedDerivative analysis zero function =
  function
iteratedDerivative analysis (suc n) function =
  derivative analysis
    (iteratedDerivative analysis n function)

trigonometricPolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardRealAnalysis reals ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
trigonometricPolynomial reals analysis N a t =
  sumFirst reals N
    (\ offset ->
      let j = suc offset
      in
      multiply reals
        (a j)
        (sine analysis
          (multiply reals
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals twoN)
              (pi analysis))
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals j)
              t))))

UnitHalfOpen :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
UnitHalfOpen reals t =
  lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) t
  and
  StrictLess reals t (oneR reals)

record FiniteSupportSum
  {A : Set}
  (domain : A -> Set)
  (term : A -> Nat)
  (total : Nat) : Set where
  field
    size : Nat
    points : Fin size -> A

    points-in-domain :
      (i : Fin size) ->
      domain (points i)
    points-nonzero :
      (i : Fin size) ->
      term (points i) != zero
    points-injective :
      (i j : Fin size) ->
      points i == points j ->
      i == j
    support-complete :
      (x : A) ->
      domain x ->
      term x != zero ->
      Exists (Fin size)
        (\ i -> x == points i)
    sum-correct :
      sumFinNat
        (\ i -> term (points i))
      ==
      total

HasFiniteSupport :
  {A : Set} ->
  (A -> Set) ->
  (A -> Nat) ->
  Set
HasFiniteSupport domain term =
  Exists Nat
    (\ total ->
      FiniteSupportSum domain term total)

TotalizedUnorderedNatSum :
  {A : Set} ->
  (A -> Set) ->
  (A -> Nat) ->
  Nat ->
  Set
TotalizedUnorderedNatSum domain term total =
  FiniteSupportSum domain term total
  or
  (Not (HasFiniteSupport domain term)
  and
  total == zero)

MultiplicityCorrect :
  {R : Set} ->
  {reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R} ->
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis reals) ->
  ((R -> R) -> R -> Nat) ->
  Set
MultiplicityCorrect {R} {reals} analysis mult =
  (g : R -> R) ->
  (t : R) ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ c ->
      iteratedDerivative analysis c g t !=
      zeroR reals) ->
  (iteratedDerivative analysis (mult g t) g t !=
    zeroR reals)
  and
  ((k : Nat) ->
    k <N mult g t ->
    iteratedDerivative analysis k g t ==
    zeroR reals)

MonotoneNat :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Set
MonotoneNat M =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  i <=N j ->
  M i <=N M j

NatSequenceConvergesTo :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Nat ->
  Set
NatSequenceConvergesTo sequence limit =
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      sequence n == limit)

putnam-2000-b3 : Set1
putnam-2000-b3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis reals) ->
  (N : Nat) ->
  PositiveNat N ->
  (a : Nat -> R) ->
  a N != zeroR reals ->
  (f : R -> R) ->
  ((t : R) ->
    f t ==
    trigonometricPolynomial reals analysis N a t) ->
  (mult : (R -> R) -> R -> Nat) ->
  MultiplicityCorrect analysis mult ->
  (M : Nat -> Nat) ->
  ((k : Nat) ->
    TotalizedUnorderedNatSum
      (UnitHalfOpen reals)
      (\ t ->
        mult
          (iteratedDerivative analysis k f)
          t)
      (M k)) ->
  MonotoneNat M
  and
  NatSequenceConvergesTo M (twoN * N)

title: putnam_2000_b3
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b3:
  monotonicity and convergence to twice the degree of the zero counts, with
  multiplicity, of successive derivatives of a real trigonometric polynomial.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory limTheory
     transcTheory;

val putnam_2000_b3 =
  ``let nat_tsum_on =
      \(s : real -> bool) (h : real -> num).
        if FINITE {x : real | x IN s /\ h x <> 0}
        then SIGMA h {x : real | x IN s /\ h x <> 0}
        else 0
    in
      !N : num.
      !a : num -> real.
      !f : real -> real.
      !mult : (real -> real) -> real -> num.
      !M : num -> num.
        0 < N /\
        a N <> 0 /\
        (!t : real.
           f t =
             SIGMA
               (\j : num. a j * sin (2 * pi * &j * t))
               (IMAGE SUC (count N))) /\
        (!g : real -> real.
         !t : real.
           (?c : num. diffn c g t <> 0)
           ==>
           diffn (mult g t) g t <> 0 /\
           !k : num. k < mult g t ==> diffn k g t = 0) /\
        (!k : num.
           M k =
             nat_tsum_on
               {t : real | 0 <= t /\ t < 1}
               (\t : real. mult (diffn k f) t))
        ==>
        (!i j : num. i <= j ==> M i <= M j) /\
        ?K : num. !k : num. K <= k ==> M k = 2 * N``;

title: putnam_2000_b3
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2000_b3: monotonicity and limiting value of the total zero
  multiplicities of the iterated derivatives of a finite real sine
  polynomial. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The coefficient function has exact domain 1 ... N, matching the Lean
  subtype; extending it arbitrarily outside that interval gives the
  equivalent total sequence used by Isabelle. P00B3Deriv is the total real
  derivative, with value zero where set.mm's partial derivative is undefined.
  IterComp therefore matches Lean's total iteratedDeriv, including order zero.

  The multiplicity hypothesis says that whenever some iterated derivative is
  nonzero, U(g)(t) is nonzero at that order and every smaller order vanishes.
  Over NN0 this is equivalent to Isabelle's least-order definition. The
  arbitrary-index nonnegative sum is indexed by the real half-open interval
  0 [,) 1, exactly matching the source subtype/index set. It is the supremum
  of all finite subsums when those subsums have a natural upper bound, and is
  zero otherwise. For NN0-valued families this is exactly the totalized
  infinite sum used by Lean and Isabelle. Since M is NN0-valued, set.mm
  sequence convergence to 2 x. N is equivalent to convergence in the discrete
  topology on NN0 used by the sources.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement. This
  extension file introduces no $p proof statement; the included set.mm
  library retains its existing verified proofs.
$)

$c P00B3Deriv P00B3IterDeriv P00B3FiniteSums P00B3NNSum $.

p00b3-deriv-syntax $a class P00B3Deriv $.
p00b3-iter-deriv-syntax $a class ( P00B3IterDeriv n A ) $.
p00b3-finite-sums-syntax $a class ( P00B3FiniteSums I H ) $.
p00b3-nnsum-syntax $a class ( P00B3NNSum I H ) $.

${
  $d A x $.

  p00b3-deriv-definition $a |- P00B3Deriv =
    (
      A e. ( RR ^m RR ) |->
        (
          x e. RR |->
            if (
              x e. dom ( RR _D A ) ,
              ( ( RR _D A ) ` x ) ,
              0
            )
        )
    ) $.
$}

p00b3-iter-deriv-definition $a |- ( P00B3IterDeriv n A ) =
  (
    ( ( IterComp ` P00B3Deriv ) ` n )
    `
    A
  ) $.

${
  $d H I s t z $.

  p00b3-finite-sums-definition $a |- ( P00B3FiniteSums I H ) =
    {
      z e. NN0 |
        E. s e. ( ~P I i^i Fin )
          z = sum_ t e. s ( H ` t )
    } $.
$}

${
  $d H I b z $.

  p00b3-nnsum-definition $a |- ( P00B3NNSum I H ) =
    if (
      E. b e. NN0
        A. z e. ( P00B3FiniteSums I H )
          z <_ b ,
      sup ( ( P00B3FiniteSums I H ) , NN0 , < ) ,
      0
    ) $.
$}

${
  $d A F M N U c g i j k t $.

  putnambench-putnam-2000-b3 $a |-
    A. N e. NN0
    A. A e. ( RR ^m ( 1 ... N ) )
    A. F e. ( RR ^m RR )
    A. U e. ( ( NN0 ^m RR ) ^m ( RR ^m RR ) )
    A. M e. ( NN0 ^m NN0 )
      (
        (
          (
            (
              (
                0 < N
                /\
                ( A ` N ) =/= 0
              )
              /\
              F =
                (
                  t e. RR |->
                    sum_ j e. ( 1 ... N )
                      (
                        ( A ` j )
                        x.
                        (
                          sin
                          `
                          (
                            (
                              ( 2 x. _pi )
                              x.
                              j
                            )
                            x.
                            t
                          )
                        )
                      )
                )
            )
            /\
            A. g e. ( RR ^m RR ) A. t e. RR
              (
                E. c e. NN0
                  ( ( P00B3IterDeriv c g ) ` t ) =/= 0
                ->
                (
                  (
                    (
                      P00B3IterDeriv
                        ( ( U ` g ) ` t )
                        g
                    )
                    `
                    t
                  )
                  =/= 0
                  /\
                  A. k e. NN0
                    (
                      k < ( ( U ` g ) ` t )
                      ->
                      ( ( P00B3IterDeriv k g ) ` t ) = 0
                    )
                )
              )
          )
          /\
          A. k e. NN0
            ( M ` k )
            =
            ( P00B3NNSum
              ( 0 [,) 1 )
              (
                t e. ( 0 [,) 1 ) |->
                  (
                    (
                      U
                      `
                      ( P00B3IterDeriv k F )
                    )
                    `
                    t
                  )
              )
            )
        )
        ->
        (
          A. i e. NN0 A. j e. NN0
            (
              i <_ j
              ->
              ( M ` i ) <_ ( M ` j )
            )
          /\
          M ~~> ( 2 x. N )
        )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2000_b3
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b3:
:: the zero counts with multiplicity on [0,1) of successive derivatives of
:: a nonzero finite real sine sum are nondecreasing and converge to twice its
:: highest frequency. This file contains no proof.

environ

  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, PARTFUN1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, COMPLEX1, CARD_1, XXREAL_0,
    XXREAL_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, REAL_1, NAT_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1,
    ORDINAL1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, RVSUM_1, RCOMP_1, FDIFF_1,
    TAYLOR_1, SIN_COS, SEQ_1, SEQ_2, REALSET1, INT_1, CARD_3,
    NEWTON;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    RELSET_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0,
    XREAL_0, REAL_1, COMPLEX1, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1,
    NAT_D, NEWTON, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, RVSUM_1,
    RCOMP_1, FDIFF_1, SIN_COS, TAYLOR_1;
  constructors FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1, REAL_1,
    COMPLEX1, INT_1, NAT_1, NAT_D, NEWTON, NUMBERS, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, RVSUM_1, RCOMP_1, RFUNCT_2, FDIFF_1, SIN_COS,
    TAYLOR_1, VALUED_1, ZFMISC_1, BINOP_2, FINSEQOP;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, NAT_1, INT_1, FINSEQ_1,
    FINSEQ_2, RVSUM_1, NEWTON, RCOMP_1, FDIFF_1, SIN_COS;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  definitions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0;
  equalities XCMPLX_0, VALUED_1, SUBSET_1;
  expansions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for N being Nat,
      a being Function of NAT,REAL,
      f being Function of REAL,REAL,
      D being Function of [:Funcs(REAL,REAL),NAT:],Funcs(REAL,REAL),
      mult being Function of [:Funcs(REAL,REAL),REAL:],NAT,
      M being Function of NAT,NAT st
    0 < N &
    a.N <> 0 &
    (for t being Real holds
      ex terms being FinSequence of REAL st
        len terms = N &
        (for j being Nat st j in Seg N holds
          terms.j =
            a.j * sin(2 * PI * (j qua Real) * t)) &
        f.t = Sum terms) &
    (for g being Function of REAL,REAL holds
      ex p being Element of [:Funcs(REAL,REAL),NAT:],
         d being Function of REAL,REAL st
        p = [g,0] & d = D.p & d = g) &
    (for g being Function of REAL,REAL,
         k being Nat holds
      ex p,q being Element of [:Funcs(REAL,REAL),NAT:],
         d,e being Function of REAL,REAL st
        p = [g,k] & q = [g,k+1] &
        d = D.p & e = D.q &
        (for t being Real holds
          (d is_differentiable_in t & e.t = diff(d,t)) or
          (not d is_differentiable_in t & e.t = 0))) &
    (for g being Function of REAL,REAL,
         t being Real st
      ex c being Nat,
         pc being Element of [:Funcs(REAL,REAL),NAT:],
         dc being Function of REAL,REAL st
        pc = [g,c] & dc = D.pc & dc.t <> 0
    holds
      ex pgt being Element of [:Funcs(REAL,REAL),REAL:],
         m being Nat,
         pm being Element of [:Funcs(REAL,REAL),NAT:],
         dm being Function of REAL,REAL st
        pgt = [g,t] & m = mult.pgt &
        pm = [g,m] & dm = D.pm & dm.t <> 0 &
        (for k being Nat st k < m holds
          ex pk being Element of [:Funcs(REAL,REAL),NAT:],
             dk being Function of REAL,REAL st
            pk = [g,k] & dk = D.pk & dk.t = 0)) &
    (for k being Nat holds
      ex pk being Element of [:Funcs(REAL,REAL),NAT:],
         fk being Function of REAL,REAL st
        pk = [f,k] & fk = D.pk &
        M.k =
          card {[t,r] where t is Real, r is Nat :
            0 <= t & t < 1 & 1 <= r &
            ex p being Element of [:Funcs(REAL,REAL),REAL:] st
              p = [fk,t] & r <= mult.p})
  holds
    (for i,j being Nat st i <= j holds M.i <= M.j) &
    (for e being Real st 0 < e holds
      ex n being Nat st
        for m being Nat st n <= m holds
          |.(M.m qua Real) - ((2 * N) qua Real).| < e)

end;

title: putnam_2000_b3

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b3:
% zero multiplicities of successive derivatives of a real sine polynomial are
% nondecreasing in total on [0, 1) and eventually total twice its degree. This
% file contains no proof.

putnam_2000_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  real_enumeration: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  real_nat_function: TYPE = [real -> nat]
  real_set: TYPE = [real -> bool]
  multiplicity_function: TYPE =
    [real_function -> [real -> nat]]
  nat_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  sine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        sine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index)
                * x ^ (2 * index + 1),
              nat_factorial(2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  cosine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index)
                * x ^ (2 * index),
              nat_factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  sine(x: real): real =
    IF EXISTS (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): sine_partial(x, count),
          value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (value: real):
          converges_to(
            LAMBDA (count: nat): sine_partial(x, count),
            value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  cosine(x: real): real =
    IF EXISTS (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): cosine_partial(x, count),
          value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (value: real):
          converges_to(
            LAMBDA (count: nat): cosine_partial(x, count),
            value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  pi: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        3 < value
          AND value < 4
          AND cosine(value / 2) = 0)

  trigonometric_sum(
      coefficients: [nat -> real],
      t: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      trigonometric_sum(coefficients, t, count - 1)
        + coefficients(count)
            * sine(
                2 * pi * (count :: real) * t)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_derivative_at(
      f: real_function,
      derivative, x: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (h: real):
          (NOT (h = 0) AND abs(h) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                f(x + h) - f(x)
                  - derivative * h)
                < epsilon_value * abs(h)

  differentiable_at(f: real_function, x: real): bool =
    EXISTS (derivative: real):
      has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x)

  derivative_value(f: real_function, x: real): real =
    IF differentiable_at(f, x) THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (derivative: real):
          has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  derivative_function(f: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real): derivative_value(f, x)

  iterated_derivative(
      f: real_function,
      order: nat): RECURSIVE real_function =
    IF order = 0 THEN
      f
    ELSE
      derivative_function(
        iterated_derivative(f, order - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE order

  injective_below(
      points: real_enumeration,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      i < count
        AND j < count
        AND points(i) = points(j)
      IMPLIES i = j

  enumerates_positive_support(
      points: real_enumeration,
      count: nat,
      domain: real_set,
      term: real_nat_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      (domain(x) AND term(x) > 0)
        IFF
          EXISTS (index: nat):
            index < count AND points(index) = x

  enumerated_nat_sum(
      points: real_enumeration,
      term: real_nat_function,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      enumerated_nat_sum(points, term, count - 1)
        + term(points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_nat_sum(
      domain: real_set,
      term: real_nat_function,
      total: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (points: real_enumeration), (count: nat):
      injective_below(points, count)
        AND enumerates_positive_support(
          points, count, domain, term)
        AND total = enumerated_nat_sum(points, term, count)

  nat_tsum(
      domain: real_set,
      term: real_nat_function): nat =
    IF EXISTS (total: nat):
        has_nat_sum(domain, term, total)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (total: nat):
          has_nat_sum(domain, term, total))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  unit_half_open_interval: real_set =
    LAMBDA (t: real): 0 <= t AND t < 1

  nat_converges_to(
      sequence: nat_sequence,
      limit_value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
      FORALL (index: nat):
        cutoff <= index IMPLIES
          sequence(index) = limit_value

  putnam_2000_b3: bool =
    FORALL
        (N: nat),
        (a: [nat -> real]),
        (f: real_function),
        (mult: multiplicity_function),
        (M: nat_sequence):
      (N > 0
        AND a(N) /= 0
        AND (FORALL (t: real):
          f(t) = trigonometric_sum(a, t, N))
        AND (FORALL (g: real_function), (t: real):
          (EXISTS (order: nat):
            iterated_derivative(g, order)(t) /= 0)
          IMPLIES
            (iterated_derivative(
                g, mult(g)(t))(t) /= 0
              AND FORALL (order: nat):
                order < mult(g)(t) IMPLIES
                  iterated_derivative(g, order)(t) = 0))
        AND (FORALL (order: nat):
          M(order) =
            nat_tsum(
              unit_half_open_interval,
              LAMBDA (t: real):
                mult(iterated_derivative(f, order))(t))))
      IMPLIES
        ((FORALL (i, j: nat):
          i <= j IMPLIES M(i) <= M(j))
          AND nat_converges_to(M, 2 * N))
END putnam_2000_b3

title: putnam_2000_b4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b4:
;; every continuous real function satisfying f(2*x^2-1) = 2*x*f(x) on the
;; real line vanishes on the closed interval [-1,1]. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; F-APPROX(x,epsilon) is a rational approximation to f(x), for rational x
;; and positive rational epsilon. DEFSTUB makes this an arbitrary function
;; symbol, rather than an APPLY$ code or a finite table.
;;
;; The regular Cauchy condition determines one exact real value at every
;; rational x. Uniform continuity on each bounded rational interval is
;; equivalent to a unique continuous extension to the full real line, and
;; every continuous real function supplies such rational approximation data.
;; The functional equation is imposed on the dense rational inputs using
;; exact Cauchy-name equality; continuity extends it to every real input.
;; Likewise, exact zero values on the rational points of [-1,1] are equivalent
;; to vanishing on the full real interval.

(defstub putnam-2000-b4-f-approx (x epsilon) t)

(defun putnam-2000-b4-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and (rationalp x)
       (< 0 x)))

(defun putnam-2000-b4-rational-in-bound-p (x bound)
  (and
   (rationalp x)
   (<= (- bound) x)
   (<= x bound)))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b4-regular-cauchy-data-p ()
  (forall (x epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (putnam-2000-b4-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2000-b4-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((left
            (putnam-2000-b4-f-approx x epsilon))
           (right
            (putnam-2000-b4-f-approx x eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<= (abs (- left right))
            (+ epsilon eta)))))))

;; This predicate states that the exact represented values at x and y differ
;; by at most MARGIN. Approximation errors are included explicitly.

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b4-value-distance-at-most-p
    (x y margin)
  (forall (epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2000-b4-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2000-b4-positive-rational-p eta))
     (<=
      (abs
       (-
        (putnam-2000-b4-f-approx x epsilon)
        (putnam-2000-b4-f-approx y eta)))
      (+ margin epsilon eta)))))

;; For exact represented reals, distance < EPSILON iff there is a rational
;; MARGIN < EPSILON that is an upper bound for their distance.

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b4-value-distance-below-p
    (x y epsilon)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (rationalp margin)
     (<= 0 margin)
     (< margin epsilon)
     (putnam-2000-b4-value-distance-at-most-p
      x y margin))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b4-uniform-radius-p
    (bound epsilon delta)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2000-b4-rational-in-bound-p x bound)
      (putnam-2000-b4-rational-in-bound-p y bound)
      (< (abs (- x y)) delta))
     (putnam-2000-b4-value-distance-below-p
      x y epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b4-uniform-radius-exists-p
    (bound epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (putnam-2000-b4-positive-rational-p delta)
     (putnam-2000-b4-uniform-radius-p
      bound epsilon delta))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b4-continuous-extension-p ()
  (forall (bound epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp bound)
      (putnam-2000-b4-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (putnam-2000-b4-uniform-radius-exists-p
      bound epsilon))))

;; Equality of the two represented real values in the functional equation.
;; The right approximation error is scaled by |2*x|.

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b4-functional-equation-p ()
  (forall (x epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (putnam-2000-b4-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2000-b4-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let* ((factor (* 2 x))
            (transformed (- (* 2 x x) 1))
            (left
             (putnam-2000-b4-f-approx
              transformed epsilon))
            (right
             (* factor
                (putnam-2000-b4-f-approx x eta))))
       (<=
        (abs (- left right))
        (+ epsilon (* (abs factor) eta)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2000-b4-zero-on-unit-interval-p ()
  (forall (x epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (<= -1 x)
      (<= x 1)
      (putnam-2000-b4-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (<=
      (abs (putnam-2000-b4-f-approx x epsilon))
      epsilon))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2000-b4-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2000-b4-regular-cauchy-data-p)
    (putnam-2000-b4-continuous-extension-p)
    (putnam-2000-b4-functional-equation-p))
   (putnam-2000-b4-zero-on-unit-interval-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2000_b4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2000_b4): a continuous real function satisfying
-- f(2x^2 - 1) = 2x f(x) for every real x vanishes on the interval [-1,1].
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ContinuousAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ContinuousAt {R} reals function point =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function point)
          epsilon
          (function x)))

Continuous :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
Continuous {R} reals function =
  (point : R) ->
  ContinuousAt reals function point

functionalArgument :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
functionalArgument reals x =
  subtract reals
    (multiply reals
      (fromNat reals twoN)
      (multiply reals x x))
    (oneR reals)

functionalValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
functionalValue reals f x =
  multiply reals
    (multiply reals
      (fromNat reals twoN)
      x)
    (f x)

putnam-2000-b4 : Set1
putnam-2000-b4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (f : R -> R) ->
  Continuous reals f ->
  ((x : R) ->
    f (functionalArgument reals x) ==
    functionalValue reals f x) ->
  (x : R) ->
  lessOrEqual reals (negate reals (oneR reals)) x ->
  lessOrEqual reals x (oneR reals) ->
  f x == zeroR reals

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b4:
% every continuous real function satisfying f(2x^2 - 1) = 2x f(x) for all
% real x vanishes on the closed interval [-1, 1]. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2000_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  continuous(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real), (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (y: real):
          abs(y - x) < delta IMPLIES
            abs(f(y) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  putnam_2000_b4: bool =
    FORALL (f: real_function):
      (continuous(f)
        AND (FORALL (x: real):
          f(2 * x ^ 2 - 1) = 2 * x * f(x)))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (x: real):
          (-1 <= x AND x <= 1) IMPLIES f(x) = 0
END putnam_2000_b4

import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Nat Set Function

/--
Let $S_0$ be a finite set of positive integers. We define finite sets $S_1,S_2,\ldots$ of positive integers as follows: the integer $a$ is in $S_{n+1}$ if and only if exactly one of $a-1$ or $a$ is in $S_n$. Show that there exist infinitely many integers $N$ for which $S_N=S_0\cup\{N+a: a\in S_0\}$.
-/
theorem putnam_2000_b5
(S : ℕ → Set ℤ)
(hSfin : ∀ n, Set.Finite (S n))
(hSpos : ∀ n, ∀ s ∈ S n, s > 0)
(hSdef : ∀ n, ∀ a, a ∈ S (n + 1) ↔ Xor' (a - 1 ∈ S n) (a ∈ S n))
: (∀ n, ∃ N ≥ n, S N = S 0 ∪ {M : ℤ | M - N ∈ S 0}) :=
sorry

    (hSSfin : forall n : nat, exists m : nat, cardinal _ (SS n) m)
    (hSSpos : forall n : nat, forall s : Z, In _ (SS n) s -> Z.gt s 0)
    (hSSdef : forall n : nat, forall a : Z, (In _ (SS (n + 1)) a) <-> ((In _ (SS n) (Z.sub a 1) /\ ~ (In _ (SS n) a)) \/ (In _ (SS n) a /\ ~ (In _ (SS n) (Z.sub a 1)))))
    : forall n : nat, exists N : nat, N >= n /\ Same_set _ (SS N) (Union _ (SS 0) (fun i : Z => exists a : Z, In _ (SS 0) a /\ i = Z.add a (Z.of_nat N))).

(*

  finite positive-integer sets evolving by exclusive membership of adjacent
  integers recur as the union of the initial set and one of its translates.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `!S:num->int->bool.
     (!n:num. FINITE (S n)) /\
     (!n:num. !s:int. s IN S n ==> &0 < s) /\
     (!n:num. !a:int.
        a IN S (n + 1) <=>
        ((a - &1 IN S n /\ ~(a IN S n)) \/
         (a IN S n /\ ~(a - &1 IN S n))))

title: putnam_2000_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b5:
;; a finite positive-integer set sequence evolving by symmetric difference
;; with its unit shift has arbitrarily late terms equal to the union of its
;; initial set and an index-translate of that set. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; SEQUENCE is an ACL2 function object whose value at (n,a), for natural n
;; and integer a, is membership of a in S_n. Its otherwise unused value at
;; (nil,nil) carries a natural upper bound for S_0. This decorated function
;; representation is bidirectionally equivalent to a sequence of finite sets:
;; forget the out-of-domain value in one direction, and store any bound for
;; the finite positive set S_0 in the other. APPLY$ and FN-EQUAL retain the
;; arbitrary source membership function and quantify extensionally over its
;; typed arguments; no finite table replaces the infinite sequence.

(defun putnam-2000-b5-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'cons
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2000-b5-term-list (cdr terms)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-apply-term (function arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2000-b5-quoted function)
        (putnam-2000-b5-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'if
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2000-b5-and-terms (cdr terms))
            (putnam-2000-b5-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2000-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list 'if
        hypothesis
        conclusion
        (putnam-2000-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-less-equal-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        (list '< right left)
        (putnam-2000-b5-quoted nil)
        (putnam-2000-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda
        formals
        (putnam-2000-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-member-term
    (sequence index element)
  (list 'if
        (putnam-2000-b5-apply-term
         sequence (list index element))
        (putnam-2000-b5-quoted t)
        (putnam-2000-b5-quoted nil)))

;; This exact function object is the canonical executable representation of
;; the all-empty sequence. Recognizing it only normalizes a concrete model;
;; every other sequence is checked by the full extensional matrices below.

(defun putnam-2000-b5-empty-sequence-p (sequence)
  (equal sequence
         '(lambda (n a) 'nil)))

;; Because every source member is a positive integer, S_0 is finite exactly
;; when it has a natural upper bound. The recurrence propagates finite support,
;; so checking the represented bound for S_0 is equivalent to the source
;; assumption that every S_n is finite.

(defun putnam-2000-b5-support-bound (sequence)
  (nfix (apply$ sequence (list nil nil))))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-initial-bound-function
    (sequence bound)
  (let ((member
         (putnam-2000-b5-member-term
          sequence
          (putnam-2000-b5-quoted 0)
          'a)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(a)
     (putnam-2000-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2000-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'integerp 'a)
        member))
      (putnam-2000-b5-less-equal-term
       'a bound)))))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-finite-initial-p (sequence)
  (if (putnam-2000-b5-empty-sequence-p sequence)
      t
    (let* ((bound
            (putnam-2000-b5-support-bound sequence))
           (bound-function
            (putnam-2000-b5-initial-bound-function
             sequence (putnam-2000-b5-quoted bound)))
           (true-function
            (putnam-2000-b5-true-function '(a))))
      (and
       (tamep-functionp bound-function)
       (tamep-functionp true-function)
       (fn-equal bound-function true-function)))))

;; These two FN-EQUAL matrices are the source assumptions
;;
;;   all members of every S_n are positive integers, and
;;   a in S_(n+1) iff exactly one of a-1 and a belongs to S_n.

(defun putnam-2000-b5-positive-function (sequence)
  (let ((member
         (putnam-2000-b5-member-term
          sequence 'n 'a)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(n a)
     (putnam-2000-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2000-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'natp 'n)
        (list 'integerp 'a)
        member))
      (list '<
            (putnam-2000-b5-quoted 0)
            'a)))))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-positive-p (sequence)
  (if (putnam-2000-b5-empty-sequence-p sequence)
      t
    (let ((positive-function
           (putnam-2000-b5-positive-function sequence))
          (true-function
           (putnam-2000-b5-true-function '(n a))))
      (and
       (tamep-functionp positive-function)
       (tamep-functionp true-function)
       (fn-equal positive-function true-function)))))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-recurrence-function (sequence)
  (let* ((next-index
          (list
           'binary-+
           'n
           (putnam-2000-b5-quoted 1)))
         (previous-element
          (list
           'binary-+
           'a
           (putnam-2000-b5-quoted -1)))
         (next-member
          (putnam-2000-b5-member-term
           sequence next-index 'a))
         (previous-member
          (putnam-2000-b5-member-term
           sequence 'n previous-element))
         (current-member
          (putnam-2000-b5-member-term
           sequence 'n 'a))
         (exclusive-member
          (list
           'if
           (list 'equal previous-member current-member)
           (putnam-2000-b5-quoted nil)
           (putnam-2000-b5-quoted t))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(n a)
     (putnam-2000-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2000-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'natp 'n)
        (list 'integerp 'a)))
      (list 'equal next-member exclusive-member)))))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-recurrence-p (sequence)
  (if (putnam-2000-b5-empty-sequence-p sequence)
      t
    (let ((recurrence-function
           (putnam-2000-b5-recurrence-function sequence))
          (true-function
           (putnam-2000-b5-true-function '(n a))))
      (and
       (tamep-functionp recurrence-function)
       (tamep-functionp true-function)
       (fn-equal recurrence-function true-function)))))

;; If B bounds S_0, the recurrence and positivity assumptions imply that S_N
;; and S_0 union {M : M-N is in S_0} are both supported in [1,B+N].
;; Consequently their equality over all integers is equivalent to equality on
;; that finite interval. FROM-TO-BY enumerates the interval, COLLECT$ wraps
;; each integer as the argument list expected by ALWAYS$+, and N is carried in
;; ALWAYS$+'s globals list.

(defun putnam-2000-b5-singleton-function ()
  '(lambda (m)
     (cons m 'nil)))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-index-range-term (upper)
  (list
   'from-to-by
   (putnam-2000-b5-quoted 1)
   upper
   (putnam-2000-b5-quoted 1)))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-membership-equality-function
    (sequence)
  (let* ((index
          (list 'car 'globals))
         (element
          (list 'car 'entry))
         (left-member
          (putnam-2000-b5-member-term
           sequence index element))
         (initial-member
          (putnam-2000-b5-member-term
           sequence
           (putnam-2000-b5-quoted 0)
           element))
         (shifted-element
          (list
           'binary-+
           element
           (list 'unary-- index)))
         (shifted-member
          (putnam-2000-b5-member-term
           sequence
           (putnam-2000-b5-quoted 0)
           shifted-element))
         (union-member
          (list
           'if
           initial-member
           (putnam-2000-b5-quoted t)
           shifted-member)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(globals entry)
     (list 'equal left-member union-member))))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-finite-equality-term
    (equality-function singleton-function support-bound)
  (let* ((upper
          (list 'binary-+ support-bound 'n))
         (range
          (putnam-2000-b5-index-range-term upper))
         (wrapped-range
          (list
           'collect$
           (putnam-2000-b5-quoted singleton-function)
           range))
         (globals
          (putnam-2000-b5-term-list (list 'n))))
    (list
     'always$+
     (putnam-2000-b5-quoted equality-function)
     globals
     wrapped-range)))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-success-function
    (sequence lower-bound)
  (let* ((support-bound
          (putnam-2000-b5-quoted
           (putnam-2000-b5-support-bound sequence)))
         (equality-function
          (putnam-2000-b5-membership-equality-function
           sequence))
         (singleton-function
          (putnam-2000-b5-singleton-function))
         (finite-equality
          (putnam-2000-b5-finite-equality-term
           equality-function
           singleton-function
           support-bound)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(n)
     (putnam-2000-b5-and-terms
      (list
       (list 'natp 'n)
       (putnam-2000-b5-less-equal-term
        (putnam-2000-b5-quoted lower-bound)
        'n)
       finite-equality)))))

(defun putnam-2000-b5-false-function ()
  '(lambda (n) 'nil))

;; For a natural LOWER-BOUND, SUCCESS-FUNCTION is true exactly at the natural
;; indices N at least LOWER-BOUND satisfying the required set equality.
;; Negated FN-EQUAL against the constantly false unary function is therefore
;; the source's internal unbounded existential quantifier over N.

(defun putnam-2000-b5-conclusion-p (sequence lower-bound)
  (if (putnam-2000-b5-empty-sequence-p sequence)
      t
    (let ((equality-function
           (putnam-2000-b5-membership-equality-function
            sequence))
          (singleton-function
           (putnam-2000-b5-singleton-function))
          (success-function
           (putnam-2000-b5-success-function
            sequence lower-bound))
          (false-function
           (putnam-2000-b5-false-function)))
      (and
       (tamep-functionp equality-function)
       (tamep-functionp singleton-function)
       (tamep-functionp success-function)
       (tamep-functionp false-function)
       (not
        (fn-equal success-function false-function))))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2000-b5-statement
    (sequence lower-bound)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp lower-bound)
    (tamep-functionp sequence)
    (putnam-2000-b5-finite-initial-p sequence)
    (putnam-2000-b5-positive-p sequence)
    (putnam-2000-b5-recurrence-p sequence))
   (putnam-2000-b5-conclusion-p
    sequence lower-bound)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2000_b5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2000_b5): finite positive-integer sets evolving
-- by exclusive membership under a unit shift recur as the union of the
-- initial set with its translation. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2000B5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record HasCardinality
  (member : Int -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      Int
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (x : Int) ->
      member x ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> x == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

Finite :
  (Int -> Set) ->
  Set
Finite member =
  Exists Nat
    (\ cardinality ->
      HasCardinality member cardinality)

data PositiveInteger : Int -> Set where
  positive :
    {n : Nat} ->
    PositiveInteger (pos (suc n))

predecessor : Int -> Int
predecessor (pos zero) =
  negsuc zero
predecessor (pos (suc n)) =
  pos n
predecessor (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc n)

subtractNat : Int -> Nat -> Int
subtractNat x zero =
  x
subtractNat x (suc n) =
  subtractNat (predecessor x) n

Exclusive : Set -> Set -> Set
Exclusive A B =
  (A and Not B) or (B and Not A)

ExtensionalEqual :
  (Int -> Set) ->
  (Int -> Set) ->
  Set
ExtensionalEqual left-set right-set =
  (x : Int) ->
  Iff (left-set x) (right-set x)

putnam-2000-b5 : Set1
putnam-2000-b5 =
  (S : Nat -> Int -> Set) ->
  ((n : Nat) -> Finite (S n)) ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    (s : Int) ->
    S n s ->
    PositiveInteger s) ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    (a : Int) ->
    Iff
      (S (suc n) a)
      (Exclusive
        (S n (predecessor a))
        (S n a))) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ N ->
      (n <=N N)
      and
      ExtensionalEqual
        (S N)
        (\ M ->
          (S zero M)
          or
          (S zero (subtractNat M N))))

  exclusive-or recur arbitrarily often as the union of the initial set and
  its translate by the time index. This file contains no proof.

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2000_b5 =

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2000_b5: finite sets of positive integers evolving by exclusive
  membership with their unit shift recur arbitrarily late as the union of
  the initial set and its index translate. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The function space ( ( ~P ZZ ) ^m NN0 ) quantifies arbitrary sequences of
  sets of integers. Finiteness and positivity are imposed pointwise. The
  recurrence expands exclusive-or into its two disjoint cases, preserving
  exactly the source membership condition.

  For N in NN0, the restricted class
  { M e. ZZ | ( M - N ) e. ( S ` 0 ) } is exactly the translate
  { N + a | a e. ( S ` 0 ) }. The quantifier
  A. n e. NN0 E. N e. NN0 ( n <_ N /\ ... ) states that such indices are
  arbitrarily large. The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus
  statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d M N S a n s $.

  putnambench-putnam-2000-b5 $a |-
    A. S e. ( ( ~P ZZ ) ^m NN0 )
      (
        (
          (
            A. n e. NN0
              ( S ` n ) e. Fin
            /\
            A. n e. NN0 A. s e. ( S ` n )
              0 < s
          )
          /\
          A. n e. NN0 A. a e. ZZ
            (
              a e. ( S ` ( n + 1 ) )
              <->
              (
                (
                  ( a - 1 ) e. ( S ` n )
                  /\
                  -. a e. ( S ` n )
                )
                \/
                (
                  a e. ( S ` n )
                  /\
                  -. ( a - 1 ) e. ( S ` n )
                )
              )
            )
        )
        ->
        A. n e. NN0 E. N e. NN0
          (
            n <_ N
            /\
            ( S ` N )
            =
            (
              ( S ` 0 )
              u.
              { M e. ZZ | ( M - N ) e. ( S ` 0 ) }
            )
          )
      )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2000_b5:
% finite sets of positive integers evolving by exclusive adjacent membership
% recur arbitrarily late as the initial set union its index-translate. This
% file contains no proof.

putnam_2000_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[int]

  integer_set: TYPE = finite_set[int]
  integer_set_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> integer_set]

  exclusive_or(left, right: bool): bool =
    (left AND NOT right) OR (right AND NOT left)

  positive_integer_set(S: integer_set): bool =
    FORALL (value: int):
      S(value) IMPLIES value > 0

  evolves_by_exclusive_membership(
      S: integer_set_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (a: int):
      S(n + 1)(a) IFF
        exclusive_or(S(n)(a - 1), S(n)(a))

  equals_initial_union_translate(
      S: integer_set_sequence,
      N: nat): bool =
    FORALL (M: int):
      S(N)(M) IFF
        (S(0)(M) OR S(0)(M - (N :: int)))

  putnam_2000_b5: bool =
    FORALL (S: integer_set_sequence):
      ((FORALL (n: nat):
          positive_integer_set(S(n)))
        AND evolves_by_exclusive_membership(S))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (n: nat):
          EXISTS (N: nat):
            N >= n
              AND equals_initial_union_translate(S, N)
END putnam_2000_b5
