;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_a1:
;; an involutive law for an arbitrary binary operation implies its reversed
;; involutive law. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; CARRIER and OP are ACL2 function objects. The generated predicate lambdas
;; return T outside CARRIER, so FN-EQUAL against a constant-T lambda expresses
;; universal quantification over exactly the represented type. Closure is the
;; explicit ACL2 counterpart of the source's typed binary operation.

(defun putnam-2001-a1-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2001-a1-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2001-a1-quoted function)
        (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-2001-a1-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2001-a1-quoted function)
        (list 'cons left
              (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-2001-a1-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-2001-a1-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-2001-a1-operation-term (op left right)
  (putnam-2001-a1-apply2-term op left right))

(defun putnam-2001-a1-all-in-carrier-term
    (carrier variables)
  (if (endp variables)
      (putnam-2001-a1-quoted t)
    (list 'if
          (putnam-2001-a1-carrier-term
           carrier (car variables))
          (putnam-2001-a1-all-in-carrier-term
           carrier (cdr variables))
          (putnam-2001-a1-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-2001-a1-restricted-predicate-term
    (carrier variables proposition)
  (list 'if
        (putnam-2001-a1-all-in-carrier-term
         carrier variables)
        proposition
        (putnam-2001-a1-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2001-a1-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda formals (putnam-2001-a1-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2001-a1-closure-function (carrier op)
  (let ((op-ab
         (putnam-2001-a1-operation-term op 'a 'b)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(a b)
     (putnam-2001-a1-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(a b)
      (putnam-2001-a1-carrier-term carrier op-ab)))))

(defun putnam-2001-a1-hypothesis-function (carrier op)
  (let ((op-ab
         (putnam-2001-a1-operation-term op 'a 'b)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(a b)
     (putnam-2001-a1-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(a b)
      (list
       'equal
       (putnam-2001-a1-operation-term op op-ab 'a)
       'b)))))

(defun putnam-2001-a1-conclusion-function (carrier op)
  (let ((op-ba
         (putnam-2001-a1-operation-term op 'b 'a)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(a b)
     (putnam-2001-a1-restricted-predicate-term
      carrier
      '(a b)
      (list
       'equal
       (putnam-2001-a1-operation-term op 'a op-ba)
       'b)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2001-a1-statement (carrier op)
  (implies
   (and
    (tamep-functionp carrier)
    (tamep-functionp op)
    (fn-equal
     (putnam-2001-a1-closure-function carrier op)
     (putnam-2001-a1-true-function '(a b)))
    (fn-equal
     (putnam-2001-a1-hypothesis-function carrier op)
     (putnam-2001-a1-true-function '(a b))))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2001-a1-conclusion-function carrier op)
    (putnam-2001-a1-true-function '(a b)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

For each integer $m$, consider the polynomial
\[P_m(x)=x^4-(2m+4)x^2+(m-2)^2.\] For what values of $m$ is $P_m(x)$

  classification of the integers for which a specified quartic factors into
  two nonconstant polynomials with integer coefficients. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let eval =
     \p:int list. \x:int.
       ITLIST (\c acc. c + x * acc) p (&0) in
   let nonconstant =
     \p:int list.
       ?i:num. 0 < i /\ i < LENGTH p /\ ~(EL i p = &0) in
   !m:int.
     ((?a b:int list.
         nonconstant a /\

title: putnam_2001_a3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_a3:
;; the integer parameters for which x^4-(2m+4)x^2+(m-2)^2 factors as a
;; product of two nonconstant integer-coefficient polynomials are exactly the
;; integer squares and twice the integer squares. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For a monic quartic, any nontrivial factorization over the integers can be
;; normalized to have a monic factor of degree one or two. If
;; C=(m-2)^2 is nonzero, that factor's constant coefficient divides C and
;; therefore has absolute value at most |C|. If C=0, x is already a factor.
;;
;; For a monic quadratic factor x^2+a*x+b, coefficient comparison forces the
;; other factor to be x^2-a*x+d, where
;;   d = -(2m+4)-b+a^2,
;;   b*d = C, and a*(d-b) = 0.
;; When a is nonzero, d=b and hence
;;   a^2 = 2b+(2m+4).
;; Thus |a| <= 2|C|+|2m+4|. The searches below are consequently equivalent
;; to the source existential quantification over all nonconstant integer
;; polynomial factors; no factor coefficients are external parameters.

(defun putnam-2001-a3-integer-abs (x)
  (if (< x 0) (- x) x))

(defun putnam-2001-a3-constant (m)
  (* (- m 2) (- m 2)))

(defun putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-coefficient (m)
  (- (+ (* 2 m) 4)))

;; The condition says that x+a divides the displayed quartic. Its monic cubic
;; cofactor is forced coefficient by coefficient.
(defun putnam-2001-a3-linear-factor-p (m a)
  (let* ((q (putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-coefficient m))
         (c (putnam-2001-a3-constant m))
         (cubic-linear (+ q (* a a)))
         (cubic-constant (- (* a cubic-linear))))
    (and
     (integerp m)
     (integerp a)
     (equal (* a cubic-constant) c))))

(defun putnam-2001-a3-linear-through-index-p
    (m bound index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (and (integerp m)
           (natp bound)
           (natp index))
      (or
       (putnam-2001-a3-linear-factor-p
        m (- index bound))
       (and
        (not (zp index))
        (putnam-2001-a3-linear-through-index-p
         m bound (- index 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2001-a3-linear-factor-exists-p (m)
  (if (integerp m)
      (let ((bound
             (putnam-2001-a3-integer-abs
              (putnam-2001-a3-constant m))))
        (putnam-2001-a3-linear-through-index-p
         m bound (* 2 bound)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-factor-p (m a b)
  (let* ((q (putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-coefficient m))
         (c (putnam-2001-a3-constant m))
         (d (+ q (- b) (* a a))))
    (and
     (integerp m)
     (integerp a)
     (integerp b)
     (equal (* b d) c)
     (equal (* a (- d b)) 0))))

(defun putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-a-through-index-p
    (m b a-bound a-index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix a-index)))
  (if (and (integerp m)
           (integerp b)
           (natp a-bound)
           (natp a-index))
      (or
       (putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-factor-p
        m (- a-index a-bound) b)
       (and
        (not (zp a-index))
        (putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-a-through-index-p
         m b a-bound (- a-index 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-b-through-index-p
    (m b-bound a-bound b-index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix b-index)))
  (if (and (integerp m)
           (natp b-bound)
           (natp a-bound)
           (natp b-index))
      (or
       (putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-a-through-index-p
        m
        (- b-index b-bound)
        a-bound
        (* 2 a-bound))
       (and
        (not (zp b-index))
        (putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-b-through-index-p
         m b-bound a-bound (- b-index 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-factor-exists-p (m)
  (if (integerp m)
      (let* ((b-bound
              (putnam-2001-a3-integer-abs
               (putnam-2001-a3-constant m)))
             (a-bound
              (+ (* 2 b-bound)
                 (putnam-2001-a3-integer-abs
                  (putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-coefficient m)))))
        (putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-b-through-index-p
         m b-bound a-bound (* 2 b-bound)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2001-a3-factorization-exists-p (m)
  (and
   (integerp m)
   (or
    (putnam-2001-a3-linear-factor-exists-p m)
    (putnam-2001-a3-quadratic-factor-exists-p m))))

;; For nonnegative m, any integer k with k^2=m or 2*k^2=m satisfies
;; |k| <= m, including the case m=0. Hence this bounded search is exactly the
;; source existential integer witness.
(defun putnam-2001-a3-scaled-square-through-index-p
    (m scale bound index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (and (integerp m)
           (posp scale)
           (natp bound)
           (natp index))
      (let ((k (- index bound)))
        (or
         (equal m (* scale k k))
         (and
          (not (zp index))
          (putnam-2001-a3-scaled-square-through-index-p
           m scale bound (- index 1)))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2001-a3-solution-p (m)
  (and
   (integerp m)
   (<= 0 m)
   (or
    (putnam-2001-a3-scaled-square-through-index-p
     m 1 m (* 2 m))
    (putnam-2001-a3-scaled-square-through-index-p
     m 2 m (* 2 m)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2001-a3-statement (m)
  (implies
   (integerp m)
   (equal
    (putnam-2001-a3-factorization-exists-p m)
    (putnam-2001-a3-solution-p m))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_a3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2001_a3): the integer parameters for which the
-- prescribed quartic factors into two nonconstant integer polynomials are
-- exactly the squares and twice the squares. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _iff_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos zero) =
  pos zero
negateInt (pos (suc n)) =
  negsuc n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

subtractInt : Int -> Int -> Int
subtractInt x y =
  addInt x (negateInt y)

squareInt : Int -> Int
squareInt x =
  multiplyInt x x

zeroZ : Int
zeroZ =
  pos zero

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  twoN + twoN

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos oneN

twoZ : Int
twoZ =
  pos twoN

fourZ : Int
fourZ =
  pos fourN

Polynomial : Set
Polynomial =
  List Int

coefficient : Polynomial -> Nat -> Int
coefficient [] n =
  zeroZ
coefficient (c ∷ coefficients) zero =
  c
coefficient (c ∷ coefficients) (suc n) =
  coefficient coefficients n

PolynomialEqual : Polynomial -> Polynomial -> Set
PolynomialEqual p q =
  (n : Nat) ->
  coefficient p n == coefficient q n

addPolynomials : Polynomial -> Polynomial -> Polynomial
addPolynomials [] ys =
  ys
addPolynomials xs [] =
  xs
addPolynomials (x ∷ xs) (y ∷ ys) =
  addInt x y ∷ addPolynomials xs ys

scalePolynomial : Int -> Polynomial -> Polynomial
scalePolynomial scalar [] =
  []
scalePolynomial scalar (coefficient ∷ coefficients) =
  multiplyInt scalar coefficient ∷
  scalePolynomial scalar coefficients

multiplyPolynomials : Polynomial -> Polynomial -> Polynomial
multiplyPolynomials [] ys =
  []
multiplyPolynomials (x ∷ xs) [] =
  []
multiplyPolynomials (x ∷ xs) (y ∷ ys) =
  addPolynomials
    (scalePolynomial x (y ∷ ys))
    (zeroZ ∷ multiplyPolynomials xs (y ∷ ys))

Nonconstant : Polynomial -> Set
Nonconstant polynomial =
  Exists Nat
    (\ degree ->
      Positive degree
      and
      coefficient polynomial degree != zeroZ)

putnamPolynomial : Int -> Polynomial
putnamPolynomial m =
  squareInt (subtractInt m twoZ)
  ∷ zeroZ
  ∷ negateInt (addInt (multiplyInt twoZ m) fourZ)
  ∷ zeroZ
  ∷ oneZ
  ∷ []

Factorable : Int -> Set
Factorable m =
  Exists Polynomial
    (\ a ->
      Exists Polynomial
        (\ b ->
          PolynomialEqual
            (putnamPolynomial m)
            (multiplyPolynomials a b)
          and
          Nonconstant a
          and
          Nonconstant b))

Solution : Int -> Set
Solution m =
  Exists Int
    (\ k ->
      m == squareInt k
      or
      m == multiplyInt twoZ (squareInt k))

putnam-2001-a3 : Set
putnam-2001-a3 =
  (m : Int) ->
  Factorable m iff Solution m

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_a3:
  classification of the integer parameters for which the specified quartic
  factors into two nonconstant integer-coefficient polynomials. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2001_a3 =
  ``let integer_polynomials =
      {f : num -> int | FINITE {k : num | f k <> 0}};
      poly_mul =
        (\f g : num -> int.
           \k : num.
             ITSET
               (\i acc. f i * g (k - i) + acc)
               (count (SUC k))
               (0 : int));
      P =
        (\m : int.
           \k : num.
             if k = 4 then (1 : int)
             else if k = 2 then -(2 * m + 4)
             else if k = 0 then (m - 2) * (m - 2)
             else 0);
      factorable =
        (\m : int.
           ?a b : num -> int.
             a IN integer_polynomials /\
             b IN integer_polynomials /\
             (?i : num. 0 < i /\ a i <> 0) /\
             (?i : num. 0 < i /\ b i <> 0) /\
             poly_mul a b = P m);
      solution =
        (\m : int.
           ?k : int. m = k * k \/ m = 2 * (k * k))
    in
      !m : int. factorable m <=> solution m``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2001_a3: classification of the integer parameters for which
  x^4 - (2m + 4)x^2 + (m - 2)^2 factors into two nonconstant
  integer-coefficient polynomials. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  Base ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) is SetMM's ring of all finite-support
  univariate polynomials over the integers, var1 is its indeterminate,
  algSc embeds integer constants, and coe1 is the complete
  nonnegative-integer-indexed coefficient function.

  A factor is nonconstant exactly when one of its coefficients at a
  positive index is nonzero. Thus the two existential coefficient
  conditions preserve the source degree-positive requirements without
  choosing an external degree bound.

  The pointwise biconditional over every integer m is equivalent to the
  source equality of the factorable-parameter set with the set of integer
  squares and twice integer squares. All factor and square witnesses remain
  internally existentially quantified. The final declaration is the single
  unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a b i j k m $.

  putnambench-putnam-2001-a3 $a |-
    A. m e. ZZ
      (
        E. a e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) )
          E. b e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) )
            (
              (
                (
                  (
                    4
                    ( .g ` ( mulGrp ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) ) )
                    ( var1 ` ZZring )
                  )
                  ( -g ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) )
                  (
                    ( ( algSc ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) ) ` ( ( 2 x. m ) + 4 ) )
                    ( .r ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) )
                    (
                      2
                      ( .g ` ( mulGrp ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) ) )
                      ( var1 ` ZZring )
                    )
                  )
                )
                ( +g ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) )
                ( ( algSc ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) ) ` ( ( m - 2 ) ^ 2 ) )
              )
              =
              (
                a
                ( .r ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) )
                b
              )
              /\
              (
                E. i e. NN ( ( coe1 ` a ) ` i ) =/= 0
                /\
                E. j e. NN ( ( coe1 ` b ) ` j ) =/= 0
              )
            )
        <->
        E. k e. ZZ
          (
            m = ( k ^ 2 )
            \/
            m = ( 2 x. ( k ^ 2 ) )
          )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2001_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_a3:
% the integer parameters for which x^4 - (2m + 4)x^2 + (m - 2)^2 factors
% into two nonconstant integer polynomials. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2001_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_polynomial: TYPE = list[int]

  polynomial_coefficient(
      polynomial: integer_polynomial,
      degree: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: 0,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        IF degree = 0 THEN
          coefficient
        ELSE
          polynomial_coefficient(tail, degree - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  polynomial_equal(
      left, right: integer_polynomial): bool =
    FORALL (degree: nat):
      polynomial_coefficient(left, degree)
        = polynomial_coefficient(right, degree)

  polynomial_add(
      left, right: integer_polynomial): RECURSIVE integer_polynomial =
    CASES left OF
      null: right,
      cons(left_coefficient, left_tail):
        CASES right OF
          null: left,
          cons(right_coefficient, right_tail):
            cons(
              left_coefficient + right_coefficient,
              polynomial_add(left_tail, right_tail))
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE left BY <<

  polynomial_scale(
      scalar: int,
      polynomial: integer_polynomial): RECURSIVE integer_polynomial =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: null,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        cons(
          scalar * coefficient,
          polynomial_scale(scalar, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  polynomial_multiply(
      left, right: integer_polynomial): RECURSIVE integer_polynomial =
    CASES left OF
      null: null,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        polynomial_add(
          polynomial_scale(coefficient, right),
          cons(0, polynomial_multiply(tail, right)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE left BY <<

  nonconstant(polynomial: integer_polynomial): bool =
    EXISTS (degree: nat):
      degree > 0
        AND polynomial_coefficient(polynomial, degree) /= 0

  quartic(m: int): integer_polynomial =
    cons[int](
      (m - 2) * (m - 2),
      cons[int](
        0,
        cons[int](
          -(2 * m + 4),
          cons[int](0, cons[int](1, null[int])))))

  factorable(m: int): bool =
    EXISTS (left, right: integer_polynomial):
      polynomial_equal(
        quartic(m),
        polynomial_multiply(left, right))
        AND nonconstant(left)
        AND nonconstant(right)

  putnam_2001_a3_solution(m: int): bool =
    EXISTS (k: int):
      m = k * k OR m = 2 * k * k

  putnam_2001_a3: bool =
    FORALL (m: int):
      factorable(m) IFF putnam_2001_a3_solution(m)
END putnam_2001_a3

(defun putnam-2001-a5-and-terms (terms)

    (putnam-2001-a5-quoted t)))

      (list 'integerp a)

      (list 'equal

    (putnam-2001-a5-quoted nil)

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_a5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2001_a5): existence and uniqueness of positive
-- integers a and n satisfying a^(n+1) - (a+1)^n = 2001. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record ExistsUnique (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor unique-witness
  field
    value      : A
    property   : P value
    uniqueness : (other : A) -> P other -> other == value

data PositiveNatural : Nat -> Set where
  positive-natural :
    {n : Nat} ->
    PositiveNatural (suc n)

data PositiveInteger : Int -> Set where
  positive-integer :
    {n : Nat} ->
    PositiveInteger (pos (suc n))

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

subtractInt : Int -> Int -> Int
subtractInt x y =
  addInt x (negateInt y)

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos (suc zero)

naturalPower : Int -> Nat -> Int
naturalPower base zero =
  oneZ
naturalPower base (suc exponent) =
  multiplyInt base (naturalPower base exponent)

record IntegerNaturalPair : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    integer-coordinate : Int
    natural-coordinate : Nat

open IntegerNaturalPair

SatisfiesEquation : IntegerNaturalPair -> Set
SatisfiesEquation candidate =
  subtractInt
    (naturalPower
      (integer-coordinate candidate)
      (suc (natural-coordinate candidate)))
    (naturalPower
      (addInt (integer-coordinate candidate) oneZ)
      (natural-coordinate candidate))
  ==
  pos 2001

PositiveSolution : IntegerNaturalPair -> Set
PositiveSolution candidate =
  PositiveInteger (integer-coordinate candidate)
  and
  PositiveNatural (natural-coordinate candidate)
  and
  SatisfiesEquation candidate

putnam-2001-a5 : Set
putnam-2001-a5 =
  ExistsUnique IntegerNaturalPair PositiveSolution

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_a5:
% existence and uniqueness of positive integers a and n satisfying
% a^(n+1) - (a+1)^n = 2001. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2001_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  solution(a: int, n: nat): bool =
    a > 0
      AND n > 0
      AND a ^ (n + 1) - (a + 1) ^ n = 2001

  putnam_2001_a5: bool =
    EXISTS (a: int):
      EXISTS (n: nat):
        solution(a, n)
          AND
            (FORALL (other_a: int):
              FORALL (other_n: nat):
                solution(other_a, other_n)

| putnam_2001_b1_black.

    (n : nat) (f : nat -> nat) : nat :=

Theorem putnam_2001_b1
    (n : nat)

    (colors : nat -> nat -> putnam_2001_b1_color)
    (hn : Nat.lt 0 n)

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b1:
;; balanced two-colorings of a row-major numbered even square grid have equal
;; sums of the labels in the two color classes. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; COLORS is an exact n-by-n list representation of the source function on
;; Fin n x Fin n. Each entry is 0 or 1. The source function NUMS is uniquely
;; fixed by its hypothesis, so the weighted sums use row*n+column+1 directly.
;; For n bit entries with even n, sum n/2 equivalently says that both colors
;; occur n/2 times, matching the two ground-truth balance formulations.

(defun putnam-2001-b1-bit-row-p (row remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      (endp row)
    (and
     (consp row)
     (or (equal (car row) 0)
         (equal (car row) 1))
     (putnam-2001-b1-bit-row-p
      (cdr row) (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-2001-b1-grid-p (colors n remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      (endp colors)
    (and
     (consp colors)
     (putnam-2001-b1-bit-row-p (car colors) n)
     (putnam-2001-b1-grid-p
      (cdr colors) n (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-2001-b1-row-sum (row)
  (if (endp row)
      0
    (+ (car row)
       (putnam-2001-b1-row-sum (cdr row)))))

(defun putnam-2001-b1-rows-balanced-p (colors half)
  (if (endp colors)
      t
    (and
     (equal (putnam-2001-b1-row-sum (car colors))
            half)
     (putnam-2001-b1-rows-balanced-p
      (cdr colors) half))))

(defun putnam-2001-b1-column-sum (colors column)
  (if (endp colors)
      0
    (+ (nth column (car colors))
       (putnam-2001-b1-column-sum
        (cdr colors) column))))

(defun putnam-2001-b1-columns-balanced-p
    (colors column remaining half)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (and
     (equal (putnam-2001-b1-column-sum colors column)
            half)
     (putnam-2001-b1-columns-balanced-p
      colors (+ column 1) (- remaining 1) half))))

(defun putnam-2001-b1-weighted-row-sum
    (row row-index column-index n color)
  (if (endp row)
      0
    (+ (if (equal (car row) color)
           (+ (* row-index n) column-index 1)
         0)
       (putnam-2001-b1-weighted-row-sum
        (cdr row) row-index (+ column-index 1) n color))))

(defun putnam-2001-b1-weighted-grid-sum
    (colors row-index n color)
  (if (endp colors)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2001-b1-weighted-row-sum
        (car colors) row-index 0 n color)
       (putnam-2001-b1-weighted-grid-sum
        (cdr colors) (+ row-index 1) n color))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2001-b1-statement (n colors)
  (implies
   (and
    (posp n)
    (evenp n)
    (putnam-2001-b1-grid-p colors n n)
    (putnam-2001-b1-rows-balanced-p colors (/ n 2))
    (putnam-2001-b1-columns-balanced-p
     colors 0 n (/ n 2)))
   (equal
    (putnam-2001-b1-weighted-grid-sum colors 0 n 0)
    (putnam-2001-b1-weighted-grid-sum colors 0 n 1))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2001_b1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2001_b1): equality of the red- and black-square
-- sums in an evenly colored row-major numbered grid. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data Even : Nat -> Set where
  even-zero : Even zero
  even-step : {n : Nat} -> Even n -> Even (suc (suc n))

half : Nat -> Nat
half zero =
  zero
half (suc zero) =
  zero
half (suc (suc n)) =
  suc (half n)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finToNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (finToNat i)

data Color : Set where
  red   : Color
  black : Color

redCount : Color -> Nat
redCount red =
  suc zero
redCount black =
  zero

redContribution : Color -> Int -> Int
redContribution red value =
  value
redContribution black value =
  pos zero

blackContribution : Color -> Int -> Int
blackContribution red value =
  pos zero
blackContribution black value =
  value

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

sumFinNat : {n : Nat} -> (Fin n -> Nat) -> Nat
sumFinNat {zero} terms =
  zero
sumFinNat {suc n} terms =
  terms fzero + sumFinNat (\ i -> terms (fsuc i))

sumFinInt : {n : Nat} -> (Fin n -> Int) -> Int
sumFinInt {zero} terms =
  pos zero
sumFinInt {suc n} terms =
  addInt
    (terms fzero)
    (sumFinInt (\ i -> terms (fsuc i)))

putnam-2001-b1 : Set
putnam-2001-b1 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  Even n ->
  (nums : Fin n -> Fin n -> Int) ->
  (colors : Fin n -> Fin n -> Color) ->
  ((k l : Fin n) ->
    nums k l ==
    pos (suc (finToNat k * n + finToNat l))) ->
  ((k : Fin n) ->
    sumFinNat (\ l -> redCount (colors k l)) ==
    half n) ->
  ((l : Fin n) ->
    sumFinNat (\ k -> redCount (colors k l)) ==
    half n) ->
  sumFinInt
    (\ k ->
      sumFinInt
        (\ l ->
          redContribution
            (colors k l)
            (nums k l)))
  ==
  sumFinInt
    (\ k ->
      sumFinInt
        (\ l ->
          blackContribution
            (colors k l)
            (nums k l)))

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b1:
  equal sums in the two color classes of a row-major numbered even square
  grid when each row and column contains equally many squares of each color.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2001_b1 =
  ``!n : num.
      !nums : num -> num -> int.
      !colors : num -> num -> bool.
        0 < n /\
        EVEN n /\
        (!k l : num.
           k < n /\ l < n
           ==>
           nums k l = int_of_num (k * n + l + 1)) /\
        (!k : num.
           k < n
           ==>
           CARD {l : num | l < n /\ ~colors k l} = n DIV 2) /\
        (!l : num.
           l < n
           ==>
           CARD {k : num | k < n /\ ~colors k l} = n DIV 2)
        ==>
        ITSET
          (\k : num. \total : int.
             ITSET
               (\l : num. \row_total : int.
                  (if ~colors k l then nums k l else 0) + row_total)
               (count n)
               0 +
             total)
          (count n)
          0 =
        ITSET
          (\k : num. \total : int.
             ITSET
               (\l : num. \row_total : int.
                  (if colors k l then nums k l else 0) + row_total)
               (count n)
               0 +
             total)
          (count n)
          0``;

$(

  The label equation is the source row-major enumeration k*n+l+1.

  The row and column cardinalities are exactly the source sums of zero-color
  indicators. Since 2 divides n, the field quotient n/2 equals the natural

  are precisely the sums of labels on colors 0 and 1.

  database contains no $p proof statement.

title: putnam_2001_b1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b1:
% in a positive even square grid with row-major integer labels and a balanced
% two-coloring in every row and column, the two color sums are equal. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_2001_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_grid: TYPE = [nat, nat -> int]
  natural_grid: TYPE = [nat, nat -> nat]

  row_color_count(
      colors: natural_grid,
      color, row, count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      row_color_count(colors, color, row, count - 1)
        + (IF colors(row, count - 1) = color THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  column_color_count(
      colors: natural_grid,
      color, column, count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      column_color_count(colors, color, column, count - 1)
        + (IF colors(count - 1, column) = color THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  weighted_row_color_sum(
      nums: integer_grid,
      colors: natural_grid,
      color, row, count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      weighted_row_color_sum(nums, colors, color, row, count - 1)
        + (IF colors(row, count - 1) = color
           THEN nums(row, count - 1)
           ELSE 0
           ENDIF)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  weighted_color_sum(
      nums: integer_grid,
      colors: natural_grid,
      color, row_count, column_count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF row_count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      weighted_color_sum(
        nums, colors, color, row_count - 1, column_count)
        + weighted_row_color_sum(
            nums, colors, color, row_count - 1, column_count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE row_count

  row_major_labels(nums: integer_grid, n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (row, column: nat):
      (row < n AND column < n)
        IMPLIES
          nums(row, column) = ((row * n + column + 1) :: int)

  binary_coloring(colors: natural_grid, n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (row, column: nat):
      (row < n AND column < n)
        IMPLIES
          (colors(row, column) = 0 OR colors(row, column) = 1)

  balanced_rows(colors: natural_grid, n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (row: nat):
      row < n
        IMPLIES row_color_count(colors, 0, row, n) = ndiv(n, 2)

  balanced_columns(colors: natural_grid, n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (column: nat):
      column < n
        IMPLIES column_color_count(colors, 0, column, n) = ndiv(n, 2)

  putnam_2001_b1: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (nums: integer_grid), (colors: natural_grid):
      (n > 0
        AND mod(n, 2) = 0
        AND row_major_labels(nums, n)
        AND binary_coloring(colors, n)
        AND balanced_rows(colors, n)
        AND balanced_columns(colors, n))
      IMPLIES
        weighted_color_sum(nums, colors, 0, n, n)
          = weighted_color_sum(nums, colors, 1, n, n)
END putnam_2001_b1

\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{2y}&=(x^2+3y^2)(3x^2+y^2) \\
\frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{2y}&=2(y^4-x^4).
\end{align*}

theorem putnam_2001_b2
    (x y : ℝ)
    (hx : x ≠ 0)
    (hy : y ≠ 0)
    (eq1 eq2 : Prop)
    (heq1 : eq1 ↔ (1 / x + 1 / (2 * y) = (x ^ 2 + 3 * y ^ 2) * (3 * x ^ 2 + y ^ 2)))

title: putnam_2001_b2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b2:
;; the real solutions of a two-equation reciprocal polynomial system form the
;; singleton determined by the positive real fifth root of 3. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source quantifies over arbitrary real x and y.  The parameters below
;; present a real closed ordered field, rather than replacing the reals by
;; ACL2's rational numbers.  FN-EQUAL against a constant-T function expresses
;; the universal field, order, and real-closure laws over the whole carrier.
;;
;; If r is the unique real root of r^5 = 3, the source solution
;; ((r+1)/2,(r-1)/2) is equivalently characterized by
;;
;;   x - y = 1  and  (x + y)^5 = 3.
;;
;; Odd fifth powers are injective in every ordered field, so this eliminates
;; the named irrational without changing the singleton or introducing an
;; external witness.  The reciprocal equations themselves are retained
;; directly using the field inverse operation.

(defun putnam-2001-b2-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2001-b2-quoted function)
   (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2001-b2-quoted function)
   (list 'cons left (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-and-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2001-b2-quoted t)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2001-b2-and-term (cdr terms))
     (putnam-2001-b2-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-or-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2001-b2-quoted nil)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2001-b2-quoted t)
     (putnam-2001-b2-or-term (cdr terms)))))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-not-term (term)
  (list
   'if
   term
   (putnam-2001-b2-quoted nil)
   (putnam-2001-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-implies-term (antecedent consequent)
  (list
   'if
   antecedent
   consequent
   (putnam-2001-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-true-function (formals)
  (list
   'lambda
   formals
   (putnam-2001-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-2001-b2-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-operation-term (operation left right)
  (putnam-2001-b2-apply2-term operation left right))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-all-coefficients-function (carrier)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)
   (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term
    carrier 'loop$-ivars)))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-all-coefficients-term
    (carrier coefficients)
  (list
   'always$+
   (putnam-2001-b2-quoted
    (putnam-2001-b2-all-coefficients-function
     carrier))
   (putnam-2001-b2-quoted nil)
   coefficients))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-polynomial-term
    (carrier zero coefficients)
  (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
   (list
    (list 'true-listp coefficients)
    (list 'consp coefficients)
    (putnam-2001-b2-all-coefficients-term
     carrier coefficients)
    (putnam-2001-b2-or-term
     (list
      (list 'equal
            (list 'len coefficients)
            (putnam-2001-b2-quoted 1))
      (putnam-2001-b2-not-term
       (list 'equal
             (list 'car (list 'last coefficients))
             (putnam-2001-b2-quoted zero))))))))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-field-laws-function
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (y 'y)
         (z 'z)
         (qzero (putnam-2001-b2-quoted zero))
         (qone (putnam-2001-b2-quoted one))
         (add-xy
          (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term add x y))
         (add-yz
          (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term add y z))
         (mul-xy
          (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul x y))
         (mul-yz
          (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul y z))
         (neg-x
          (putnam-2001-b2-apply1-term neg x))
         (inv-x
          (putnam-2001-b2-apply1-term inv x))
         (domain
          (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier y)
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier z))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier add-xy)
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier mul-xy)
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier neg-x)
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier inv-x)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term add add-xy z)
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term add x add-yz))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul mul-xy z)
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul x mul-yz))
            (list
             'equal
             add-xy
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term add y x))
            (list
             'equal
             mul-xy
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul y x))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term add x qzero)
             x)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term add x neg-x)
             qzero)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul x qone)
             x)
            (putnam-2001-b2-implies-term
             (list 'equal x qzero)
             (list 'equal inv-x qzero))
            (putnam-2001-b2-implies-term
             (putnam-2001-b2-not-term
              (list 'equal x qzero))
             (list
              'equal
              (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul x inv-x)
              qone))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul x add-yz)
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term
              add
              (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul x y)
              (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul x z)))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y z)
     (putnam-2001-b2-implies-term domain laws))))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-order-laws-function
    (carrier zero add mul lt)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (y 'y)
         (z 'z)
         (qzero (putnam-2001-b2-quoted zero))
         (lt-xy
          (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term lt x y))
         (lt-yx
          (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term lt y x))
         (lt-yz
          (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term lt y z))
         (lt-xz
          (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term lt x z))
         (domain
          (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier y)
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier z))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2001-b2-not-term
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term lt x x))
            (putnam-2001-b2-or-term
             (list
              lt-xy
              (list 'equal x y)
              lt-yx))
            (putnam-2001-b2-implies-term
             (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
              (list lt-xy lt-yz))
             lt-xz)
            (putnam-2001-b2-implies-term
             lt-xy
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term
              lt
              (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term add x z)
              (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term add y z)))
            (putnam-2001-b2-implies-term
             (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
              (list
               (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term lt qzero x)
               (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term lt qzero y)))
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term
              lt
              qzero
              (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul x y)))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y z)
     (putnam-2001-b2-implies-term domain laws))))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-square-root-laws-function
    (carrier zero mul lt square-root)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (qzero (putnam-2001-b2-quoted zero))
         (root
          (putnam-2001-b2-apply1-term square-root x))
         (domain
          (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2001-b2-not-term
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term lt x qzero)))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier root)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term mul root root)
             x)))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-2001-b2-implies-term domain laws))))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-evaluation-laws-function
    (carrier zero add mul evaluate)
  (let* ((coefficient 'coefficient)
         (rest 'rest)
         (x 'x)
         (qzero (putnam-2001-b2-quoted zero))
         (domain
          (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term
             carrier coefficient)
            (list 'true-listp rest)
            (putnam-2001-b2-all-coefficients-term
             carrier rest)
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier x))))
         (empty-law
          (putnam-2001-b2-implies-term
           (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier x)
           (list
            'equal
            (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term
             evaluate
             (putnam-2001-b2-quoted nil)
             x)
            qzero)))
         (recursive-value
          (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term
           add
           coefficient
           (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term
            mul
            x
            (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term
             evaluate rest x))))
         (recursive-law
          (putnam-2001-b2-implies-term
           domain
           (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
            (list
             (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term
              carrier
              (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term
               evaluate
               (list 'cons coefficient rest)
               x))
             (list
              'equal
              (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term
               evaluate
               (list 'cons coefficient rest)
               x)
              recursive-value))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(coefficient rest x)
     (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
      (list empty-law recursive-law)))))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-odd-root-laws-function
    (carrier zero evaluate odd-root)
  (let* ((coefficients 'coefficients)
         (root
          (putnam-2001-b2-apply1-term
           odd-root coefficients))
         (domain
          (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2001-b2-polynomial-term
             carrier zero coefficients)
            (list 'evenp (list 'len coefficients)))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2001-b2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2001-b2-carrier-term carrier root)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2001-b2-operation-term
              evaluate coefficients root)
             (putnam-2001-b2-quoted zero))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(coefficients)
     (putnam-2001-b2-implies-term domain laws))))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-real-closed-field-p
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv lt square-root odd-root evaluate)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp add)
   (tamep-functionp mul)
   (tamep-functionp neg)
   (tamep-functionp inv)
   (tamep-functionp lt)
   (tamep-functionp square-root)
   (tamep-functionp odd-root)
   (tamep-functionp evaluate)
   (apply$ carrier (list zero))
   (apply$ carrier (list one))
   (not (equal zero one))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2001-b2-field-laws-function
     carrier zero one add mul neg inv)
    (putnam-2001-b2-true-function '(x y z)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2001-b2-order-laws-function
     carrier zero add mul lt)
    (putnam-2001-b2-true-function '(x y z)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2001-b2-square-root-laws-function
     carrier zero mul lt square-root)
    (putnam-2001-b2-true-function '(x)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2001-b2-evaluation-laws-function
     carrier zero add mul evaluate)
    (putnam-2001-b2-true-function
     '(coefficient rest x)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2001-b2-odd-root-laws-function
     carrier zero evaluate odd-root)
    (putnam-2001-b2-true-function
     '(coefficients)))))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-add (add left right)
  (apply$ add (list left right)))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-mul (mul left right)
  (apply$ mul (list left right)))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-neg (neg value)
  (apply$ neg (list value)))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-inv (inv value)
  (apply$ inv (list value)))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-sub (add neg left right)
  (putnam-2001-b2-add
   add left (putnam-2001-b2-neg neg right)))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-power (mul one value exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      one
    (putnam-2001-b2-mul
     mul
     value
     (putnam-2001-b2-power
      mul one value (- exponent 1)))))

(defun putnam-2001-b2-system-p
    (one add mul neg inv x y)
  (let* ((two
          (putnam-2001-b2-add add one one))
         (three
          (putnam-2001-b2-add add two one))
         (x2
          (putnam-2001-b2-power mul one x 2))
         (y2
          (putnam-2001-b2-power mul one y 2))
         (x4
          (putnam-2001-b2-power mul one x 4))
         (y4
          (putnam-2001-b2-power mul one y 4))
         (two-y
          (putnam-2001-b2-mul mul two y))
         (left1
          (putnam-2001-b2-add
           add
           (putnam-2001-b2-inv inv x)
           (putnam-2001-b2-inv inv two-y)))
         (right1
          (putnam-2001-b2-mul
           mul
           (putnam-2001-b2-add
            add
            x2
            (putnam-2001-b2-mul mul three y2))

            add

          (putnam-2001-b2-sub

           (putnam-2001-b2-inv inv x)

         (right2
          (putnam-2001-b2-mul

           two

    (and
     (equal left1 right1)

(defun putnam-2001-b2-solution-p
    (one add mul neg x y)
  (let* ((two
          (putnam-2001-b2-add add one one))
         (three
          (putnam-2001-b2-add add two one))
         (difference
          (putnam-2001-b2-sub add neg x y))
         (sum

(defun putnambench-putnam-2001-b2-statement
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv lt square-root odd-root

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2001_b2): the real solutions of a system of two
-- rational polynomial equations form a specified singleton. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_
infix 1 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  twoN + twoN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc fourN

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

module Putnam2001B2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  equationOne :
    R ->
    R ->
    Set
  equationOne x y =
    add reals
      (divide reals (oneR reals) x)
      (divide reals
        (oneR reals)
        (multiply reals (fromNat reals twoN) y))
    ==
    multiply reals
      (add reals
        (naturalPower reals x twoN)
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals threeN)
          (naturalPower reals y twoN)))
      (add reals
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals threeN)
          (naturalPower reals x twoN))
        (naturalPower reals y twoN))

  equationTwo :
    R ->
    R ->
    Set
  equationTwo x y =
    subtract reals
      (divide reals (oneR reals) x)
      (divide reals
        (oneR reals)
        (multiply reals (fromNat reals twoN) y))
    ==
    multiply reals
      (fromNat reals twoN)
      (subtract reals
        (naturalPower reals y fourN)
        (naturalPower reals x fourN))

  isPositiveFifthRootOfThree :
    R ->
    Set
  isPositiveFifthRootOfThree root =
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) root
    and
    naturalPower reals root fiveN == fromNat reals threeN

  isSolutionPair :
    R ->
    R ->
    Set
  isSolutionPair x y =
    Exists R
      (\ root ->
        isPositiveFifthRootOfThree root
        and
        (x ==
          divide reals
            (add reals root (oneR reals))
            (fromNat reals twoN)
        and
        y ==
          divide reals
            (subtract reals root (oneR reals))
            (fromNat reals twoN)))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (x y : R) ->
    x != zeroR reals ->
    y != zeroR reals ->
    (equationOne x y and equationTwo x y)
      iff
    isSolutionPair x y

putnam-2001-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2001B2Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b2:
  the nonzero real solutions of the stated reciprocal polynomial system
  consist exactly of the pair determined by the positive fifth root of 3.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open realTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2001_b2 =
  ``!x y : real.
      ~(x = 0) /\ ~(y = 0)
      ==>
      let r = (3 : real) powr (1 / 5)
      in
        (1 / x + 1 / (2 * y) =
           (x pow 2 + 3 * y pow 2) * (3 * x pow 2 + y pow 2) /\
         1 / x - 1 / (2 * y) =
           2 * (y pow 4 - x pow 4)
         <=>
         x = (r + 1) / 2 /\ y = (r - 1) / 2)``;

  putnam_2001_b2: the real solutions of a two-equation reciprocal and
  quartic system form one explicit pair involving the fifth root of three.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The variables x and y range over all real numbers. The source hypotheses
  x != 0 and y != 0 remain explicit, and both source equations occur together
  on the left side of the biconditional.

  Since 3 is positive and 1 / 5 is real, set.mm's complex-power expression
  3 ^c ( 1 / 5 ) is the positive real fifth root used by the source
  solution. The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement;
  this root file declares no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-2001-b2 $a |-
    A. x e. RR A. y e. RR
      (
        (
          x =/= 0
          /\
          y =/= 0
        )
        ->
        (
          (
            (
              ( ( 1 / x ) + ( 1 / ( 2 x. y ) ) )
              =
              (
                ( ( x ^ 2 ) + ( 3 x. ( y ^ 2 ) ) )
                x.
                ( ( 3 x. ( x ^ 2 ) ) + ( y ^ 2 ) )

            /\

              ( ( 1 / x ) - ( 1 / ( 2 x. y ) ) )
              =
              ( 2 x. ( ( y ^ 4 ) - ( x ^ 4 ) ) )

          )
          <->
          (
            x = ( ( ( 3 ^c ( 1 / 5 ) ) + 1 ) / 2 )
            /\
            y = ( ( ( 3 ^c ( 1 / 5 ) ) - 1 ) / 2 )
          )
        )
      )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b2:
% the real solutions of a two-equation reciprocal polynomial system form the
% stated singleton involving the real fifth root of three. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2001_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  fifth_root_of_three(root: real): bool =
    root ^ 5 = 3

  putnam_2001_b2_solution(x, y: real): bool =
    EXISTS (root: real):
      fifth_root_of_three(root)
        AND x = safe_div(root + 1, 2)
        AND y = safe_div(root - 1, 2)

  satisfies_system(x, y: real): bool =
    safe_div(1, x) + safe_div(1, 2 * y)
        = (x ^ 2 + 3 * y ^ 2) * (3 * x ^ 2 + y ^ 2)
      AND
    safe_div(1, x) - safe_div(1, 2 * y)
        = 2 * (y ^ 4 - x ^ 4)

  putnam_2001_b2: bool =
    FORALL (x, y: real):
      (x /= 0 AND y /= 0)
        IMPLIES
          (satisfies_system(x, y)
            IFF putnam_2001_b2_solution(x, y))
END putnam_2001_b2

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b3:
;; the infinite real series whose nth term uses the nearest integer to sqrt(n)
;; in the exponents of 2 converges to 3. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; For integral n there is no half-integer tie in rounding sqrt(n). The nearest
;; integer k is characterized by k*(k-1) < n <= k*(k+1). The recurrence below
;; computes exactly that k without replacing the square root by an approximation.
(defun putnam-2001-b3-nearest-sqrt (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      0
    (let ((previous
           (putnam-2001-b3-nearest-sqrt (- n 1))))
      (if (< (* previous (+ previous 1)) n)
          (+ previous 1)
        previous))))

(defun putnam-2001-b3-term (n)
  (if (posp n)
      (let* ((nearest
              (putnam-2001-b3-nearest-sqrt n))
             (power
              (expt 2 nearest)))
        (/ (+ power (/ 1 power))
           (expt 2 n)))
    0))

;; The exact rational sum of the source terms indexed from 1 through TERMS.
(defun putnam-2001-b3-prefix (terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2001-b3-prefix (- terms 1))
       (putnam-2001-b3-term terms))))

;; Positive rational tolerances are cofinal in the positive reals. Since the
;; source series has rational terms and rational limit 3, quantifying over
;; positive rational tolerances gives exactly its real epsilon convergence.
(defun-sk putnam-2001-b3-tail-p (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (terms)
    (implies
     (and (natp terms)
          (<= cutoff terms))
     (< (abs (- (putnam-2001-b3-prefix terms) 3))
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b3-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and (natp cutoff)
         (putnam-2001-b3-tail-p epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-2001-b3-statement ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and (rationalp epsilon)
          (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-2001-b3-cutoff-exists-p epsilon))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2001_b3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2001_b3): the infinite real series whose nth
-- exponent is the closest integer to sqrt(n) has value 3. This file contains
-- no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2001B3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

successorInt : Int -> Int
successorInt (pos n) =
  pos (suc n)
successorInt (negsuc zero) =
  pos zero
successorInt (negsuc (suc n)) =
  negsuc n

intToNat : Int -> Nat
intToNat (pos n) =
  n
intToNat (negsuc n) =
  zero

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms total =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    total

record StandardFloor
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    floor : R -> Int

    floor-lower :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals
        (fromInt reals (floor x))
        x
    floor-upper :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals
        x
        (fromInt reals (successorInt (floor x)))
    floor-unique :
      (x : R) ->
      (z : Int) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (fromInt reals z) x ->
      StrictLess reals x (fromInt reals (successorInt z)) ->
      floor x == z

open StandardFloor

module Putnam2001B3Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (flooring : StandardFloor reals) where

  closestIntegerToSquareRoot : Nat -> Nat
  closestIntegerToSquareRoot n =
    intToNat
      (floor flooring
        (add reals
          (squareRoot reals (fromNat reals n))
          (inverse reals (fromNat reals twoN))))

  term : Nat -> R
  term index =
    let
      n = suc index
      exponent = closestIntegerToSquareRoot n
      twoToExponent =
        naturalPower reals (fromNat reals twoN) exponent
    in
    divide reals
      (add reals
        twoToExponent
        (inverse reals twoToExponent))
      (naturalPower reals (fromNat reals twoN) n)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    SeriesHasSum reals term (fromNat reals threeN)

putnam-2001-b3 : Set1
putnam-2001-b3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (flooring : StandardFloor reals) ->
  Putnam2001B3Statement.proposition reals flooring

title: putnam_2001_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b3:
% the series formed from powers of two indexed by the nearest integer to each
% positive integer's square root converges to 3. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2001_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  nearest_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nearest_integer_to_sqrt(n, k: nat): bool =
    (2 * (k :: real) - 1) ^ 2 <= 4 * (n :: real)
      AND 4 * (n :: real) < (2 * (k :: real) + 1) ^ 2

  is_nearest_sqrt_sequence(nearest: nearest_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n > 0 IMPLIES nearest_integer_to_sqrt(n, nearest(n))

  power_of_two(exponent: nat): real =
    (2 :: real) ^ exponent

  series_terms(nearest: nearest_sequence): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (index: nat):
      LET n: nat = index + 1,
          k: nat = nearest(n)
      IN
        safe_div(
          power_of_two(k) + safe_div(1, power_of_two(k)),
          power_of_two(n))

  partial_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  series_sums_to(values: real_sequence, total: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(partial_sum(values, count) - total) < epsilon_value

  putnam_2001_b3_solution: real = 3

  putnam_2001_b3: bool =
    EXISTS (nearest: nearest_sequence):
      is_nearest_sqrt_sequence(nearest)
        AND series_sums_to(
          series_terms(nearest),
          putnam_2001_b3_solution)
END putnam_2001_b3

Require Import QArith.

Open Scope Q_scope.

Definition putnam_2001_b4_in_domain (x : Q) : Prop :=
  ~ (Qeq x (-1) \/ Qeq x 0 \/ Qeq x 1).

Definition putnam_2001_b4_image (f : Q -> Q) (y : Q) : Prop :=
  exists x : Q,
    putnam_2001_b4_in_domain x /\
    Qeq (f x) y.

Fixpoint putnam_2001_b4_compose_n (f : Q -> Q) (n : nat) : Q -> Q :=
  match n with
  | O => fun x => x
  | S n' => fun x => f (putnam_2001_b4_compose_n f n' x)
  end.

Definition putnam_2001_b4_solution : Prop := True.

Theorem putnam_2001_b4
    (f : Q -> Q := fun x => x - 1 / x) :
  (~ exists x : Q,
      putnam_2001_b4_in_domain x /\
      forall n : nat,
        (n >= 1)%nat ->
        putnam_2001_b4_image (putnam_2001_b4_compose_n f n) x) <->
  putnam_2001_b4_solution.
Proof. Admitted.

title: putnam_2001_b4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b4:
;; emptiness of the intersection of all positive iterated images of the
;; rational map f(x) = x - 1/x on Q minus {-1,0,1}. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

(defun putnam-2001-b4-in-s-p (x)
  (and
   (rationalp x)
   (not (equal x -1))
   (not (equal x 0))
   (not (equal x 1))))

(defun putnam-2001-b4-f (x)
  (- x (/ x)))

(defun putnam-2001-b4-iterate (n x)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      x
    (putnam-2001-b4-iterate
     (- n 1)
     (putnam-2001-b4-f x))))

;; Membership of X in the nth image of S is expressed with an internal
;; preimage witness Y in S.

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b4-in-image-p (x n)
  (exists (y)
    (and
     (putnam-2001-b4-in-s-p y)
     (equal
      (putnam-2001-b4-iterate n y)
      x))))

;; X lies in every positive iterated image.

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b4-in-all-positive-images-p (x)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (<= 1 n))
     (putnam-2001-b4-in-image-p x n))))

;; Since f maps S to S, the intersection is nonempty exactly when some
;; element of S lies in every positive iterated image.

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b4-intersection-nonempty-p ()
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (putnam-2001-b4-in-s-p x)
     (putnam-2001-b4-in-all-positive-images-p x))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2001-b4-statement ()
  (not (putnam-2001-b4-intersection-nonempty-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2001_b4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2001_b4): emptiness of the intersection of all
-- positive iterated images of x -> x - 1/x on rationals other than -1, 0,
-- and 1. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2001B4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

record Top : Set where
  constructor truth

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : (n : Nat) -> Positive (suc n)

record RationalField (Q : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroQ oneQ : Q
    add multiply : Q -> Q -> Q
    negate inverse : Q -> Q
    fromNat : Nat -> Q
    fromInt : Int -> Q

    one-not-zero :
      oneQ != zeroQ

    add-commutative :
      (x y : Q) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : Q) -> add x zeroQ == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : Q) -> add x (negate x) == zeroQ

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : Q) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : Q) -> multiply x oneQ == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : Q) -> multiply x zeroQ == zeroQ
    distribute :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroQ == zeroQ
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : Q) ->
      x != zeroQ ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneQ

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroQ
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneQ
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    fromInt-positive :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromInt (pos n) == fromNat n
    fromInt-negative :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromInt (negsuc n) == negate (fromNat (suc n))

    fraction-surjective :
      (x : Q) ->
      Exists Int
        (\ numerator ->
          Exists Nat
            (\ denominator-minus-one ->
              x ==
              multiply
                (fromInt numerator)
                (inverse
                  (fromNat (suc denominator-minus-one)))))

open RationalField

subtract :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q ->
  Q ->
  Q
subtract rationals x y =
  add rationals x (negate rationals y)

divide :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q ->
  Q ->
  Q
divide rationals x y =
  multiply rationals x (inverse rationals y)

negativeOne :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q
negativeOne rationals =
  negate rationals (oneQ rationals)

InS :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q ->
  Set
InS rationals x =
  (x != negativeOne rationals)
  and
  ((x != zeroQ rationals)
  and
  (x != oneQ rationals))

record SElement {Q : Set} (rationals : RationalField Q) : Set where
  constructor element
  field
    rationalValue : Q
    belongsToS    : InS rationals rationalValue

open SElement

SameElement :
  {Q : Set} ->
  {rationals : RationalField Q} ->
  SElement rationals ->
  SElement rationals ->
  Set
SameElement x y =
  rationalValue x == rationalValue y

iterate :
  {A : Set} ->
  (A -> A) ->
  Nat ->
  A ->
  A
iterate f zero x =
  x
iterate f (suc n) x =
  f (iterate f n x)

putnamMap :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q ->
  Q
putnamMap rationals x =
  subtract rationals x
    (divide rationals (oneQ rationals) x)

HasPutnamFormula :
  {Q : Set} ->
  (rationals : RationalField Q) ->
  (SElement rationals -> SElement rationals) ->
  Set
HasPutnamFormula rationals f =
  (x : SElement rationals) ->
  rationalValue (f x) ==
  putnamMap rationals (rationalValue x)

InIteratedImage :
  {Q : Set} ->
  {rationals : RationalField Q} ->
  (SElement rationals -> SElement rationals) ->
  Nat ->
  SElement rationals ->
  Set
InIteratedImage {rationals = rationals} f n y =
  Exists (SElement rationals)
    (\ x -> SameElement (iterate f n x) y)

EmptyPositiveIteratedIntersection :
  {Q : Set} ->
  {rationals : RationalField Q} ->
  (SElement rationals -> SElement rationals) ->
  Set
EmptyPositiveIteratedIntersection
  {rationals = rationals} f =
  Not
    (Exists (SElement rationals)
      (\ y ->
        (n : Nat) ->
        Positive n ->
        InIteratedImage f n y))

putnam-2001-b4 : Set1
putnam-2001-b4 =
  (Q : Set) ->
  (rationals : RationalField Q) ->
  (f : SElement rationals -> SElement rationals) ->
  HasPutnamFormula rationals f ->
  EmptyPositiveIteratedIntersection f iff Top

  putnam_2001_b4: emptiness of the intersection of all positive iterate
  images of the rational map x |-> x - 1/x away from -1, 0, and 1.
  This file contains no proof.

$(

  endofunctions of S satisfying the specified formula. IterComp is set.mm's
  native finite-iteration operator. Thus the final negated existential says
  that no y in S has, for every positive integer n, a preimage in S under
  the n-fold iterate of F. This is exactly emptiness of the intersection of
  the positive iterate images.

  database contains no $p proof statement.

  putnambench-putnam-2001-b4 $a |- A. S
    A. F e. ( S ^m S )
      (

          S = ( QQ \ { -u 1 , 0 , 1 } )
          /\
          A. x e. S
            ( F ` x ) = ( x - ( 1 / x ) )
        )
        ->
        -. E. y e. S A. n e. NN E. x e. S
          (
            (
              ( ( IterComp ` F ) ` n )
              `
              x
            )
            =
            y
          )
      )
  $.
$}

% the intersection of the positive iterate images of the rationals other than

putnam_2001_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  in_S(x: rat): bool =
    x /= -1 AND x /= 0 AND x /= 1

  reciprocal_on_S(x: rat): rat =
    IF x = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      1 / x
    ENDIF

  f(x: rat): rat =
    x - reciprocal_on_S(x)

  iterate_f(x: rat, count: nat): RECURSIVE rat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      x
    ELSE
      f(iterate_f(x, count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  in_iterate_image(value: rat, count: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (start: rat):
      in_S(start) AND iterate_f(start, count) = value

  positive_iterate_intersection_empty: bool =
    NOT EXISTS (value: rat):
      FORALL (count: nat):
        count >= 1 IMPLIES in_iterate_image(value, count)

  putnam_2001_b4_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_2001_b4: bool =
    positive_iterate_intersection_empty
      IFF putnam_2001_b4_solution
END putnam_2001_b4
