;; These conservative symbols provide arbitrary rational regular Cauchy names
;; for a, b, and the value g(x) at each rational x. They are not APPLY$ codes
;; or finite tables. Regular names cover every real number, and compact
;; uniform continuity on the rational line is equivalent to a unique
;; continuous extension g : R -> R.
;;
;; The functional equation is equality of the limits of its rational
;; approximations. It is imposed at every rational x and hence, by continuity,
;; at every real x. The conclusion uses the forced slope g(1): a function of
;; the form g(x)=c*x has c=g(1), so this is equivalent in both directions to
;; the source conclusion that some real c works for every real x.

(defstub putnam-2001-b5-a-approx (epsilon) t)
(defstub putnam-2001-b5-b-approx (epsilon) t)
(defstub putnam-2001-b5-g-approx (x epsilon) t)

(defun putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and
   (rationalp x)
   (< 0 x)))

(defun putnam-2001-b5-rational-in-bound-p (x bound)
  (and
   (rationalp x)
   (<= (- bound) x)
   (<= x bound)))

(defun putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-approx (which epsilon)
  (if (equal which :a)
      (putnam-2001-b5-a-approx epsilon)
    (putnam-2001-b5-b-approx epsilon)))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-real-name-p (which)
  (forall (epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((left
            (putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-approx
             which epsilon))
           (right
            (putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-approx
             which eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<= (abs (- left right))
            (+ epsilon eta)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-lower-bound-p
    (which lower)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (<=
      lower
      (+ (putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-approx
          which epsilon)
         epsilon)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-half-gap-p
    (which gap)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (<=
      gap
      (+ (- 1/2
            (putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-approx
             which epsilon))
         epsilon)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-in-open-half-p (which)
  (exists (lower gap)
    (and
     (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p lower)
     (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p gap)
     (putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-lower-bound-p
      which lower)
     (putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-half-gap-p
      which gap))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-function-real-name-p ()
  (forall (x epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((left
            (putnam-2001-b5-g-approx x epsilon))
           (right
            (putnam-2001-b5-g-approx x eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<= (abs (- left right))
            (+ epsilon eta)))))))

;; Exact distance at most MARGIN between the represented values g(x), g(y).

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-value-distance-at-most-p
    (x y margin)
  (forall (epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p eta))
     (<=
      (abs
       (-
        (putnam-2001-b5-g-approx x epsilon)
        (putnam-2001-b5-g-approx y eta)))
      (+ margin epsilon eta)))))

;; Rational density makes this equivalent to exact distance below EPSILON.

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-value-distance-below-p
    (x y epsilon)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (rationalp margin)
     (<= 0 margin)
     (< margin epsilon)
     (putnam-2001-b5-value-distance-at-most-p
      x y margin))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-uniform-radius-p
    (bound epsilon delta)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2001-b5-rational-in-bound-p x bound)
      (putnam-2001-b5-rational-in-bound-p y bound)
      (< (abs (- x y)) delta))
     (putnam-2001-b5-value-distance-below-p
      x y epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-uniform-radius-exists-p
    (bound epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p delta)
     (putnam-2001-b5-uniform-radius-p
      bound epsilon delta))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-continuous-extension-p ()
  (forall (bound epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp bound)
      (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (putnam-2001-b5-uniform-radius-exists-p
      bound epsilon))))

;; For fixed rational x, these expressions converge respectively to
;; g(g(x)) and a*g(x)+b*x. Requiring arbitrarily fine residuals is therefore
;; exact equality of the represented real limits.

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-equation-precision-exists-p
    (x epsilon)
  (exists (precision)
    (and
     (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p precision)
     (< precision epsilon)
     (<
      (abs
       (-
        (putnam-2001-b5-g-approx
         (putnam-2001-b5-g-approx x precision)
         precision)
        (+
         (*
          (putnam-2001-b5-a-approx precision)
          (putnam-2001-b5-g-approx x precision))
         (*
          (putnam-2001-b5-b-approx precision)
          x))))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-functional-equation-p ()
  (forall (x epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (putnam-2001-b5-equation-precision-exists-p
      x epsilon))))

;; The exact represented equality g(x)=g(1)*x on all rational x extends by
;; continuity to all real x.

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-linear-precision-exists-p
    (x epsilon)
  (exists (precision)
    (and
     (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p precision)
     (< precision epsilon)
     (<
      (abs
       (-
        (putnam-2001-b5-g-approx x precision)
        (*
         (putnam-2001-b5-g-approx 1 precision)
         x)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b5-linear-through-origin-p ()
  (forall (x epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (putnam-2001-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (putnam-2001-b5-linear-precision-exists-p
      x epsilon))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2001-b5-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-real-name-p :a)
    (putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-real-name-p :b)
    (putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-in-open-half-p :a)
    (putnam-2001-b5-coefficient-in-open-half-p :b)
    (putnam-2001-b5-function-real-name-p)
    (putnam-2001-b5-continuous-extension-p)
    (putnam-2001-b5-functional-equation-p))
   (putnam-2001-b5-linear-through-origin-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2001_b5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2001_b5): every continuous real function whose
-- second iterate is a fixed linear combination of the function and its input,
-- with both coefficients in (0, 1/2), is scalar multiplication. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2001B5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ContinuousAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ContinuousAt {R} reals function point =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function point)
          epsilon
          (function x)))

Continuous :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
Continuous {R} reals function =
  (point : R) ->
  ContinuousAt reals function point

module Putnam2001B5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  two : R
  two =
    fromNat reals (suc (suc zero))

  oneHalf : R
  oneHalf =
    divide reals (oneR reals) two

  InOpenHalfInterval : R -> Set
  InOpenHalfInterval x =
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) x
    and
    StrictLess reals x oneHalf

  SatisfiesEquation :
    R ->
    R ->
    (R -> R) ->
    Set
  SatisfiesEquation a b g =
    (x : R) ->
    g (g x) ==
      add reals
        (multiply reals a (g x))
        (multiply reals b x)

  IsScalarMultiplication : (R -> R) -> Set
  IsScalarMultiplication g =
    Exists R
      (\ c ->
        (x : R) ->
        g x == multiply reals c x)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (a b : R) ->
    (g : R -> R) ->
    InOpenHalfInterval a ->
    InOpenHalfInterval b ->
    Continuous reals g ->
    SatisfiesEquation a b g ->
    IsScalarMultiplication g

putnam-2001-b5 : Set1
putnam-2001-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2001B5Statement.proposition reals

(*

  a continuous real function satisfying the stated linear self-composition
  equation is scalar multiplication. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory realTheory real_topologyTheory;

val putnam_2001_b5 =
  ``!a b : real. !g : real -> real.
      0 < a /\ a < 1 / 2 /\
      0 < b /\ b < 1 / 2 /\
      g continuous_on UNIV /\
      (!x : real. g (g x) = a * g x + b * x)
      ==>
      ?c : real. !x : real. g x = c * x``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2001_b5: a continuous real function satisfying
  g(g(x)) = a g(x) + b x for real parameters a,b in (0,1/2) is a scalar
  multiple of the identity function. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  F ranges over all total real-valued functions, and membership in
  ( RR -cn-> RR ) is set.mm's native assertion of global continuity.
  The parameters a and b range over the full open interval (0,1/2), the
  functional equation retains its universal scope over RR, and the scalar c
  remains internally existential.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d F a b c x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2001-b5 $a |-
    A. a e. RR
      A. b e. RR
        A. F e. ( RR ^m RR )
          (
            (
              (
                ( 0 < a /\ a < ( 1 / 2 ) )
                /\
                ( 0 < b /\ b < ( 1 / 2 ) )
              )
              /\
              (
                F e. ( RR -cn-> RR )
                /\
                A. x e. RR
                  ( F ` ( F ` x ) )
                  =
                  (
                    ( a x. ( F ` x ) )
                    +
                    ( b x. x )
                  )
              )
            )
            ->
            E. c e. RR
              A. x e. RR
                ( F ` x ) = ( c x. x )
          )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2001_b5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b5:
% every continuous real function satisfying the stated second-iterate equation
% with coefficients in (0, 1/2) is a scalar multiple of the identity. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_2001_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  continuous(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real), (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (y: real):
          abs(y - x) < delta IMPLIES
            abs(f(y) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  putnam_2001_b5: bool =
    FORALL (a, b: real), (g: real_function):
      ((0 < a AND a < 1 / 2 AND 0 < b AND b < 1 / 2)
        AND continuous(g)
        AND (FORALL (x: real):
          g(g(x)) = a * g(x) + b * x))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (c: real):
          FORALL (x: real):
            g(x) = c * x
END putnam_2001_b5

import Mathlib

-- Note: uses (ℤ → ℝ) instead of (Set.Ici 1 → ℝ)

-- True
/--
Assume that $(a_n)_{n \geq 1}$ is an increasing sequence of positive real numbers such that $\lim a_n/n=0$. Must there exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $a_{n-i}+a_{n+i}<2a_n$ for $i=1,2,\ldots,n-1$?
-/
theorem putnam_2001_b6 :
  (∀ a : ℤ → ℝ,
    (∀ n ≥ 1, a n > 0 ∧ a n < a (n + 1)) →
    (Tendsto (fun n : ℤ => a (n + 1) / (n + 1)) atTop (𝓝 0)) →
    {n : ℤ | n > 0 ∧ (∀ i ∈ Set.Icc 1 (n - 1), a (n - i) + a (n + i) < 2 * a n)}.Infinite)
  ↔ putnam_2001_b6_solution :=
sorry

Definition putnam_2001_b6_solution : Prop := True.
Theorem putnam_2001_b6
    (aposinc : (nat -> R) -> Prop := (fun a : nat -> R => forall n : nat, ge n 1 -> (a n > 0 /\ a n < a (add n 1))))
    (alim : (nat -> R) -> Prop := (fun a : nat -> R => Lim_seq (fun n : nat => a (add n 1) / INR (add n 1)) = 0))
    : (forall a : nat -> R, (aposinc a /\ alim a) -> forall m : nat, exists n : nat, gt n m /\ (forall i : nat, (le 1 i /\ le i (n - 1)) -> a (sub n i) + a (add n i) < 2 * a n)) <-> putnam_2001_b6_solution.
Proof. Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b6:
;; every positive strictly increasing real sequence with a_n/n tending to zero
;; has infinitely many strict midpoint-concavity indices. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; This conservative generic symbol supplies a rational regular Cauchy name
;; for a_n at every natural n.  It is an arbitrary function symbol, not an
;; APPLY$ code or a finite table.  Every real sequence admits such a name, and
;; every name satisfying PUTNAM-2001-B6-REGULAR-NAME-P determines a unique real
;; sequence, so this presentation is bidirectionally equivalent to quantifying
;; over all functions from the naturals to the reals.
;;
;; Strict inequalities are expressed by positive rational margins valid at
;; every precision.  The limit cutoff and the unbounded good-index witness are
;; existentially quantified inside DEFUN-SK predicates.  For each fixed n,
;; only finitely many midpoint gaps occur, so separate positive margins for
;; those gaps are equivalent to the source's strict inequalities.

(defstub putnam-2001-b6-a-approx (n epsilon) t)

(defun putnam-2001-b6-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and
   (rationalp x)
   (< 0 x)))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-regular-name-p ()
  (forall (n epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (putnam-2001-b6-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2001-b6-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((left
            (putnam-2001-b6-a-approx n epsilon))
           (right
            (putnam-2001-b6-a-approx n eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<= (abs (- left right))
            (+ epsilon eta)))))))

;; MARGIN <= a_n, expressed through every regular-name approximation.

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-positive-margin-p (n margin)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2001-b6-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (<=
      margin
      (+ (putnam-2001-b6-a-approx n epsilon)
         epsilon)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-positive-value-p (n)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (putnam-2001-b6-positive-rational-p margin)
     (putnam-2001-b6-positive-margin-p n margin))))

;; MARGIN <= a_(n+1)-a_n.

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-increase-margin-p (n margin)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2001-b6-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (<=
      margin
      (+
       (-
        (putnam-2001-b6-a-approx (+ n 1) epsilon)
        (putnam-2001-b6-a-approx n epsilon))
       (* 2 epsilon))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-increase-positive-p (n)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (putnam-2001-b6-positive-rational-p margin)
     (putnam-2001-b6-increase-margin-p n margin))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-positive-increasing-p ()
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (posp n)
     (and
      (putnam-2001-b6-positive-value-p n)
      (putnam-2001-b6-increase-positive-p n)))))

;; At name precision PRECISION*(n+1), division by n+1 introduces at most
;; PRECISION approximation error.  Requiring the exact quotient to be at most
;; EPSILON eventually, for every positive rational EPSILON, is equivalent
;; after rescaling EPSILON to convergence to zero.

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-limit-tail-p
    (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (n precision)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (<= cutoff n)
      (putnam-2001-b6-positive-rational-p precision))
     (let* ((denominator (+ n 1))
            (name-precision (* precision denominator))
            (sample
             (putnam-2001-b6-a-approx
              denominator name-precision)))
       (and
        (rationalp sample)
        (<=
         (abs (/ sample denominator))
         (+ epsilon precision)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-limit-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (putnam-2001-b6-limit-tail-p
      epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-limit-zero-p ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2001-b6-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (putnam-2001-b6-limit-cutoff-exists-p
      epsilon))))

;; MARGIN <= 2*a_n-a_(n-i)-a_(n+i).

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-midpoint-margin-p
    (n i margin)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2001-b6-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (<=
      margin
      (+
       (-
        (-
         (* 2
            (putnam-2001-b6-a-approx n epsilon))
         (putnam-2001-b6-a-approx
          (- n i) epsilon))
        (putnam-2001-b6-a-approx
         (+ n i) epsilon))
       (* 4 epsilon))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-midpoint-gap-positive-p
    (n i)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (putnam-2001-b6-positive-rational-p margin)
     (putnam-2001-b6-midpoint-margin-p
      n i margin))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-good-index-p (n)
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp i)
      (<= 1 i)
      (<= i (- n 1)))
     (putnam-2001-b6-midpoint-gap-positive-p
      n i))))

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-good-index-above-p (m)
  (exists (n)
    (and
     (posp n)
     (< m n)
     (putnam-2001-b6-good-index-p n))))

;; An infinite subset of the naturals is equivalently unbounded.

(defun-sk putnam-2001-b6-unbounded-good-indices-p ()
  (forall (m)
    (implies
     (natp m)
     (putnam-2001-b6-good-index-above-p m))))

;; The benchmark's catalogued answer is True, so the source equivalence with
;; that answer reduces to the universally generic implication below.

(defun putnambench-putnam-2001-b6-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2001-b6-regular-name-p)
    (putnam-2001-b6-positive-increasing-p)
    (putnam-2001-b6-limit-zero-p))
   (putnam-2001-b6-unbounded-good-indices-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2001_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2001_b6): every positive strictly increasing
-- real sequence with a_n / n tending to zero has infinitely many indices
-- satisfying the stated strict midpoint inequality. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2001B6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

NatStrictLess : Nat -> Nat -> Set
NatStrictLess m n =
  suc m <=N n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

module Putnam2001B6Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  PositiveStrictlyIncreasing : (Nat -> R) -> Set
  PositiveStrictlyIncreasing a =
    (n : Nat) ->
    oneN <=N n ->
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (a n)
    and
    StrictLess reals (a n) (a (suc n))

  Sublinear : (Nat -> R) -> Set
  Sublinear a =
    ConvergesTo reals
      (\ n ->
        divide reals
          (a (suc n))
          (fromNat reals (suc n)))
      (zeroR reals)

  MidpointInequality :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    Set
  MidpointInequality a n =
    oneN <=N n
    and
    ((i : Nat) ->
      oneN <=N i ->
      i <=N (n - oneN) ->
      StrictLess reals
        (add reals
          (a (n - i))
          (a (n + i)))
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals twoN)
          (a n)))

  InfinitelyManyMidpointIndices : (Nat -> R) -> Set
  InfinitelyManyMidpointIndices a =
    (m : Nat) ->
    Exists Nat
      (\ n ->
        NatStrictLess m n
        and
        MidpointInequality a n)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (a : Nat -> R) ->
    PositiveStrictlyIncreasing a ->
    Sublinear a ->
    InfinitelyManyMidpointIndices a

putnam-2001-b6 : Set1
putnam-2001-b6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2001B6Statement.proposition reals

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;

val putnam_2001_b6 =

        (!n : num.
           1 <= n
           ==>
           0 < a n /\ a n < a (n + 1)) /\
        (((\n : num. a (n + 1) / &(n + 1)) --> 0) sequentially)
        ==>

          {n : num |

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2001_b6: infinitely many strict midpoint inequalities in every
  positive increasing real sequence that grows sublinearly. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN is the class of positive integers, so a ranges over exactly the
  positive-indexed real sequences in the published problem. The Lean source
  extends a to all integers, but its hypotheses and conclusion observe only
  positive indices; the Isabelle and Rocq sources use natural indices with
  the same positive-indexed content.

  The sequence n |-> a(n)/n is the index-shifted form of the source sequence
  n |-> a(n+1)/(n+1), and therefore has the same limit. Non-membership of the
  displayed subset of NN in Fin states that infinitely many positive n
  satisfy every inequality for i from 1 through n-1. The source solution is
  True, so its biconditional with the displayed proposition is logically
  equivalent to the proposition itself.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a i n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2001-b6 $a |-
    A. a e. ( RR ^m NN )
      (
        (
          A. n e. NN
            (
              0 < ( a ` n )
              /\
              ( a ` n ) < ( a ` ( n + 1 ) )
            )
          /\
          (
            n e. NN |->
              ( ( a ` n ) / n )
          )
          ~~>
          0
        )
        ->
        {
          n e. NN
          |
          A. i e. ( 1 ... ( n - 1 ) )
            (
              ( ( a ` ( n - i ) ) + ( a ` ( n + i ) ) )
              <
              ( 2 x. ( a ` n ) )
            )
        }
        e/
        Fin
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2001_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2001_b6:
% every positive strictly increasing real sequence with a_n / n tending to zero
% has infinitely many indices satisfying all stated strict midpoint inequalities.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2001_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  sublinear_growth(a: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(
              a(index + 1) / ((index + 1) :: real))
              < epsilon_value

  positive_strictly_increasing(a: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index >= 1 IMPLIES
        a(index) > 0
          AND a(index) < a(index + 1)

  midpoint_index(a: real_sequence, n: nat): bool =
    n > 0
      AND FORALL (i: nat):
        (1 <= i AND i <= n - 1) IMPLIES
          a(n - i) + a(n + i) < 2 * a(n)

  putnam_2001_b6: bool =
    FORALL (a: real_sequence):
      (positive_strictly_increasing(a)
        AND sublinear_growth(a))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (bound: nat):
          EXISTS (n: nat):
            bound < n AND midpoint_index(a, n)
END putnam_2001_b6

import Mathlib

open Nat

abbrev putnam_2002_a1_solution : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ := sorry
-- (fun k n : ℕ => (-k) ^ n * (n)!)
/--
Let $k$ be a fixed positive integer. The $n$-th derivative of $\frac{1}{x^k-1}$ has the form $\frac{P_n(x)}{(x^k-1)^{n+1}}$ where $P_n(x)$ is a polynomial. Find $P_n(1)$.
-/
theorem putnam_2002_a1
(k : ℕ)
(P : ℕ → Polynomial ℝ)
(kpos : k > 0)
(Pderiv : ∀ n x, iteratedDeriv n (fun x' : ℝ => 1 / (x' ^ k - 1)) x = ((P n).eval x) / ((x ^ k - 1) ^ (n + 1)))
: ∀ n, (P n).eval 1 = putnam_2002_a1_solution k n :=
sorry

From mathcomp Require Import all_algebra all_ssreflect.
From mathcomp Require Import reals normedtype sequences topology derive.
From mathcomp Require Import classical_sets.
Import numFieldNormedType.Exports.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.
Local Open Scope classical_set_scope.

Variable R : realType.
Definition putnam_2002_a1_solution : nat -> nat -> R := fun k n : nat => (-k%:R) ^ n * n`!%:R.
Theorem putnam_2002_a1
    (k : nat)
    (P : nat -> {poly R})
    (kpos : gt k 0)
    (Pderiv : forall n : nat, forall x : R, derive1n n (fun x' : R => 1/(x' ^ k - 1)) x = (P n).[x] / ((x ^ k - 1) ^ (n.+1)))
    : forall n : nat, (P n).[1] = putnam_2002_a1_solution k n.
Proof. Admitted.

theory putnam_2002_a1 imports Complex_Main "HOL-Computational_Algebra.Polynomial" "HOL-Analysis.Derivative"
begin

definition putnam_2002_a1_solution :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> real" where
  "putnam_2002_a1_solution \<equiv> (\<lambda>k n. (- real k)^n * fact n)"
(* \<lambda>k. \<lambda>n. (-k) ^n * fact n *)
theorem putnam_2002_a1:
  fixes k::nat and P::"nat \<Rightarrow> (real poly)"
  assumes kpos : "k > 0"
    and Pderiv : "\<forall>n::nat. \<forall>x::real. x^k \<noteq> 1 \<longrightarrow>
      (deriv^^n) (\<lambda>x'::real. 1 / (x' ^ k - 1)) x =
      poly (P n) x / ((x^k - 1) ^ (n+1))"
  shows "\<forall>n::nat. (poly (P n) 1) = putnam_2002_a1_solution k n"
  sorry

end

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a1:
;; the numerator polynomial in the nth derivative of 1/(x^k-1), evaluated at
;; x=1, is (-k)^n*n! for every positive integer k. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; ACL2 has no first-class function quantifiers. This unconstrained function
;; symbol is the standard ACL2 representation of the source's arbitrary
;; polynomial family P.

(defstub putnam-2002-a1-p (n) t)

;; Polynomials use canonical nonempty integer coefficient lists in ascending
;; degree order. Writing D=X^k-1, the source derivative identity is equivalent
;; to the explicit hypotheses
;;
;;   P_0 = 1,
;;   P_(n+1) = P_n' D - (n+1) P_n D'.
;;
;; Differentiating P_n/D^(n+1) gives the forward implication. Conversely, the
;; recurrence reconstructs every iterated derivative identity. Equality away
;; from the finitely many roots of D is polynomial equality, so every source
;; real-polynomial family is uniquely this integer-coefficient family. Using
;; integer coefficient lists therefore does not narrow the admissible P.

(defun putnam-2002-a1-integer-list-p (values)
  (if (endp values)
      (equal values nil)
    (and
     (integerp (car values))
     (putnam-2002-a1-integer-list-p (cdr values)))))

(defun putnam-2002-a1-polynomial-p (polynomial)
  (and
   (true-listp polynomial)
   (consp polynomial)
   (putnam-2002-a1-integer-list-p polynomial)
   (or
    (equal (len polynomial) 1)
    (not (equal (car (last polynomial)) 0)))))

(defun putnam-2002-a1-trim-zero-tail (polynomial)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      nil
    (let ((rest
           (putnam-2002-a1-trim-zero-tail
            (cdr polynomial))))
      (if (and (endp rest)
               (equal (car polynomial) 0))
          nil
        (cons (car polynomial) rest)))))

(defun putnam-2002-a1-canonicalize (polynomial)
  (let ((trimmed
         (putnam-2002-a1-trim-zero-tail polynomial)))
    (if (endp trimmed)
        (list 0)
      trimmed)))

(defun putnam-2002-a1-poly-add (left right)
  (cond
   ((endp left) right)
   ((endp right) left)
   (t
    (cons
     (+ (car left) (car right))
     (putnam-2002-a1-poly-add
      (cdr left) (cdr right))))))

(defun putnam-2002-a1-poly-negate (polynomial)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      nil
    (cons
     (- (car polynomial))
     (putnam-2002-a1-poly-negate
      (cdr polynomial)))))

(defun putnam-2002-a1-poly-subtract (left right)
  (putnam-2002-a1-poly-add
   left
   (putnam-2002-a1-poly-negate right)))

(defun putnam-2002-a1-poly-scale (scalar polynomial)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      nil
    (cons
     (* scalar (car polynomial))
     (putnam-2002-a1-poly-scale
      scalar (cdr polynomial)))))

(defun putnam-2002-a1-poly-multiply (left right)
  (if (endp left)
      nil
    (putnam-2002-a1-poly-add
     (putnam-2002-a1-poly-scale (car left) right)
     (cons
      0
      (putnam-2002-a1-poly-multiply
       (cdr left) right)))))

(defun putnam-2002-a1-poly-derivative-aux
    (polynomial degree)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      nil
    (cons
     (* degree (car polynomial))
     (putnam-2002-a1-poly-derivative-aux
      (cdr polynomial) (+ degree 1)))))

(defun putnam-2002-a1-poly-derivative (polynomial)
  (if (endp polynomial)
      (list 0)
    (putnam-2002-a1-canonicalize

title: putnam_2002_a1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2002_a1): the numerator polynomial in the nth
-- derivative of 1 / (x^k - 1) has value (-k)^n n! at one. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2002A1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<suc : {n : Nat} -> zero <N suc n
  suc<suc  : {m n : Nat} -> m <N n -> suc m <N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse absoluteValue : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    absolute-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (absoluteValue x)
    absolute-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      absoluteValue x == x
    absolute-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      absoluteValue x == negate x

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals (naturalPower reals x n) x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  suc zero
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

record Polynomial
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) : Set where
  constructor polynomial
  field
    coefficient : Nat -> R
    degreeBound : Nat
    zeroAbove :
      (n : Nat) ->
      degreeBound <N n ->
      coefficient n == zeroR reals

open Polynomial

evaluate :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Polynomial reals ->
  R ->
  R
evaluate reals polynomialValue x =
  sumFirst reals
    (suc (degreeBound polynomialValue))
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (coefficient polynomialValue i)
        (naturalPower reals x i))

HasDerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
HasDerivativeAt {R} reals function point derivative =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((increment : R) ->
        StrictLess reals
          (absoluteValue reals increment)
          delta ->
        increment != zeroR reals ->
        StrictLess reals
          (absoluteValue reals
            (subtract reals
              (divide reals
                (subtract reals
                  (function (add reals point increment))
                  (function point))
                increment)
              derivative))
          epsilon))

DerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeAt {R} reals function point derivative =
  HasDerivativeAt reals function point derivative
  or
  (Not
    (Exists R
      (\ value ->
        HasDerivativeAt reals function point value))
  and
  derivative == zeroR reals)

IteratedDerivativeValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
IteratedDerivativeValue reals zero function point value =
  value == function point
IteratedDerivativeValue {R} reals (suc n) function point value =
  Exists (R -> R)
    (\ derivativeFunction ->
      ((x : R) ->
        DerivativeAt reals function x (derivativeFunction x))
      and
      IteratedDerivativeValue reals n derivativeFunction point value)

putnamFunction :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  R
putnamFunction reals k x =
  divide reals
    (oneR reals)
    (subtract reals
      (naturalPower reals x k)
      (oneR reals))

derivativeNumeratorQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Nat ->
  Polynomial reals ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  R
derivativeNumeratorQuotient reals k polynomialValue n x =
  divide reals
    (evaluate reals polynomialValue x)
    (naturalPower reals
      (subtract reals
        (naturalPower reals x k)
        (oneR reals))
      (suc n))

putnamSolution :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  R
putnamSolution reals k n =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals
      (negate reals (fromNat reals k))
      n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

putnam-2002-a1 : Set1
putnam-2002-a1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (k : Nat) ->
  (P : Nat -> Polynomial reals) ->
  zero <N k ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    (x : R) ->
    IteratedDerivativeValue reals n
      (putnamFunction reals k)
      x
      (derivativeNumeratorQuotient reals k (P n) n x)) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  evaluate reals (P n) (oneR reals) ==
    putnamSolution reals k n

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a1:
  the numerator polynomial in the nth derivative of 1 / (x^k - 1),
  evaluated at x = 1, is (-k)^n times n factorial. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory realTheory polyTheory derivativeTheory;

val putnam_2002_a1 =
  ``let deriv0 =
      \f : real -> real.
        \x : real.
          if f differentiable (at x) then vector_derivative f (at x) else 0
    in
      !k : num. !P : num -> real list.
        0 < k /\
        (!n : num. !x : real.
           FUNPOW deriv0 n (\x' : real. 1 / (x' pow k - 1)) x =
             poly (P n) x / ((x pow k - 1) pow (n + 1)))
        ==>
        !n : num.
          poly (P n) 1 =
            (~(&k : real)) pow n * &(FACT n)``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2002_a1: the numerator polynomial in the nth derivative of
  1 / (x^k - 1), evaluated at one, equals (-k)^n times n factorial.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  Poly1 ` RRfld is set.mm's ring of finite-support univariate real
  polynomials, and eval1 is its polynomial evaluation map. P ranges over
  all NN0-indexed families in this ring.

  P02A1Deriv totalizes set.mm's partial real derivative by assigning zero
  where the derivative does not exist. IterComp therefore agrees with the
  total iterated derivative operators in the source formalizations, including
  derivative order zero. Quantifying k over NN is equivalent to the source
  assumptions that k is a natural number and k > 0.

  Both divisions are explicitly zero at x^k = 1, matching the totalized field
  division used by the Lean and Rocq sources. The antecedent retains the
  derivative identity for every n in NN0 and every real x. The conclusion
  evaluates the same polynomial p(n) at one and gives the explicit Rocq value
  (-k)^n n!. The declarations below are unproved $a statement encodings; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P02A1Deriv P02A1IterDeriv $.

p02a1-deriv-syntax $a class P02A1Deriv $.
p02a1-iter-deriv-syntax $a class ( P02A1IterDeriv n A ) $.

${
  $d A x $.

  p02a1-deriv-definition $a |- P02A1Deriv =
    (
      A e. ( RR ^m RR ) |->
        (
          x e. RR |->
            if (
              x e. dom ( RR _D A ) ,
              ( ( RR _D A ) ` x ) ,
              0
            )
        )
    ) $.
$}

p02a1-iter-deriv-definition $a |- ( P02A1IterDeriv n A ) =
  (
    ( ( IterComp ` P02A1Deriv ) ` n )
    `
    A
  ) $.

${
  $d A k n p x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2002-a1 $a |-
    A. k e. NN
    A. p e. ( ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) ) ^m NN0 )
      (
        (
          A. n e. NN0 A. x e. RR
            (
              (
                P02A1IterDeriv
                  n
                  (
                    x e. RR |->
                      if (
                        ( x ^ k ) = 1 ,
                        0 ,
                        (
                          1
                          /
                          (
                            ( x ^ k )
                            -
                            1
                          )
                        )
                      )
                  )
              )
              `
              x
            )
            =
            (
              if (
                ( x ^ k ) = 1 ,
                0 ,
                (
                  (
                    (
                      ( eval1 ` RRfld )
                      `
                      ( p ` n )
                    )
                    `
                    x
                  )
                  /
                  (
                    (
                      ( x ^ k )
                      -
                      1
                    )
                    ^
                    ( n + 1 )
                  )
                )
              )
            )
        )
        ->
        A. n e. NN0
          (
            (
              (
                ( eval1 ` RRfld )
                `
                ( p ` n )
              )
              `
              1
            )
            =
            (
              ( ( -u k ) ^ n )
              x.
              ( ! ` n )
            )
          )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2002_a1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a1:
% the value at 1 of the polynomial numerator in each iterated derivative of
% 1/(x^k - 1) is (-k)^n n! for every positive natural k. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2002_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  polynomial: TYPE = list[real]
  polynomial_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> polynomial]
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  polynomial_value(p: polynomial, x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    CASES p OF
      null: 0,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        coefficient + x * polynomial_value(tail, x)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE p BY <<

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  has_derivative_at(
      f: real_function,
      derivative, x: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (h: real):
          (h /= 0 AND abs(h) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(f(x + h) - f(x) - derivative * h)
                < epsilon_value * abs(h)

  differentiable_at(f: real_function, x: real): bool =
    EXISTS (derivative: real):
      has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x)

  derivative_value(f: real_function, x: real): real =
    IF differentiable_at(f, x) THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (derivative: real):
          has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  derivative_function(f: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      derivative_value(f, x)

  iterated_derivative(
      f: real_function,
      order: nat): RECURSIVE real_function =
    IF order = 0 THEN
      f
    ELSE
      derivative_function(
        iterated_derivative(f, order - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE order

  rational_function(k: nat): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      safe_div(1, x ^ k - 1)

  nat_factorial(n: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      n * nat_factorial(n - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  putnam_2002_a1_solution(k, n: nat): real =
    (0 - (k :: real)) ^ n * (nat_factorial(n) :: real)

  derivative_representation(
      k: nat,
      P: polynomial_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (x: real):
      iterated_derivative(rational_function(k), n)(x)
        =
      safe_div(
        polynomial_value(P(n), x),
        (x ^ k - 1) ^ (n + 1))

  putnam_2002_a1: bool =
    FORALL (k: nat), (P: polynomial_sequence):
      (k > 0 AND derivative_representation(k, P))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (n: nat):
          polynomial_value(P(n), 1)
            = putnam_2002_a1_solution(k, n)
END putnam_2002_a1

import Mathlib

open Nat Metric

/--

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a2:
-- among any five points on the unit sphere in real three-space, four lie in
-- one closed hemisphere. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

three : Nat
three =
  suc (suc (suc zero))

four : Nat
four =
  suc three

five : Nat
five =
  suc four

Point :
  Set ->
  Set
Point R =
  Fin three -> R

Subset :
  Set ->
  Set1
Subset A =
  A -> Set

ContainedIn :
  {A : Set} ->
  Subset A ->
  Subset A ->
  Set
ContainedIn S T =
  (x : _) ->
  S x ->
  T x

Intersection :
  {A : Set} ->
  Subset A ->
  Subset A ->
  Subset A
Intersection S T x =
  S x and T x

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> item == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

record HasAtLeastCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

VectorEqual :
  {R : Set} ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
VectorEqual u v =
  (i : Fin three) ->
  u i == v i

ZeroVector :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R
ZeroVector reals i =
  zeroR reals

VectorNonzero :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
VectorNonzero reals v =
  Not (VectorEqual v (ZeroVector reals))

dot :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
dot reals u v =
  add reals
    (multiply reals (u fzero) (v fzero))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals (u (fsuc fzero)) (v (fsuc fzero)))
      (multiply reals
        (u (fsuc (fsuc fzero)))
        (v (fsuc (fsuc fzero)))))

UnitSphere :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Subset (Point R)
UnitSphere reals point =
  dot reals point point == oneR reals

ClosedHemisphere :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Subset (Point R)
ClosedHemisphere reals normal point =
  lessOrEqual reals
    (zeroR reals)
    (dot reals point normal)

putnam-2002-a2 : Set1
putnam-2002-a2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (S : Subset (Point R)) ->
  ContainedIn S (UnitSphere reals) ->
  HasCardinality S five ->
  Exists (Point R)
    (\ normal ->
      VectorNonzero reals normal
      and
      HasAtLeastCardinality
        (Intersection S (ClosedHemisphere reals normal))
        four)

title: putnam_2002_a2

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a2:
% every five points on the unit sphere in real three-space have four points
% in a closed hemisphere. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2002_a2: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE =
    [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real, z_coord: real #]

  IMPORTING finite_sets[point]

  zero_vector: point =
    (# x_coord := 0, y_coord := 0, z_coord := 0 #)

  dot_product(P, V: point): real =
    x_coord(P) * x_coord(V)
      + y_coord(P) * y_coord(V)
      + z_coord(P) * z_coord(V)

  on_unit_sphere(P: point): bool =
    dot_product(P, P) = 1

  in_closed_hemisphere(P, V: point): bool =
    dot_product(P, V) >= 0

  hemisphere_points(
      S: finite_set[point],
      V: point): finite_set[point] =
    intersection(
      S,
      {P: point | in_closed_hemisphere(P, V)})

  putnam_2002_a2: bool =
    FORALL (S: finite_set[point]):
      (card(S) = 5
        AND (FORALL (P: point):
          S(P) IMPLIES on_unit_sphere(P)))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (V: point):
          V /= zero_vector
            AND card(hemisphere_points(S, V)) >= 4
END putnam_2002_a2

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a3:
   parity of the number of nonempty subsets of an initial integer interval
   whose average is an integer. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals List Sorting.Sorted ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_2002_a3_sum (xs : list Z) : Z :=
  match xs with
  | nil => 0
  | cons x tail => x + putnam_2002_a3_sum tail
  end.

Definition putnam_2002_a3_qualifying_subset
    (n : Z) (xs : list Z) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Z.lt xs /\
  xs <> nil /\
  Forall (fun x : Z => 1 <= x <= n) xs /\
  exists k : Z,
    (IZR (putnam_2002_a3_sum xs) / INR (length xs))%R = IZR k.

Definition putnam_2002_a3_has_integer_cardinality
    (P : list Z -> Prop) (cardinality : Z) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list (list Z),
    NoDup enumeration /\
    (forall xs : list Z, In xs enumeration <-> P xs) /\
    cardinality = Z.of_nat (length enumeration).

Theorem putnam_2002_a3
    (n Tn : Z)
    (hn : 2 <= n)
    (hTn :
      putnam_2002_a3_has_integer_cardinality
        (putnam_2002_a3_qualifying_subset n) Tn) :
  Z.Even (Tn - n).
Admitted.

title: putnam_2002_a3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a3:
;; for every integer n at least 2, the number Tn of nonempty subsets of
;; {1,...,n} having integer average satisfies that Tn-n is even. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Each branch makes the next interval element absent or present. At a leaf,
;; CHOSEN-COUNT and CHOSEN-SUM are exactly the cardinality and sum of one
;; subset. For a nonempty integer subset, its real average is an integer
;; exactly when its cardinality divides its sum.

(defun putnam-2002-a3-count-integer-average-subsets
    (next remaining chosen-count chosen-sum)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      (if (and (< 0 chosen-count)
               (equal (mod chosen-sum chosen-count) 0))
          1
        0)
    (+
     (putnam-2002-a3-count-integer-average-subsets
      (+ next 1)
      (- remaining 1)
      chosen-count
      chosen-sum)
     (putnam-2002-a3-count-integer-average-subsets
      (+ next 1)
      (- remaining 1)
      (+ chosen-count 1)
      (+ chosen-sum next)))))

(defun putnam-2002-a3-tn (n)
  (putnam-2002-a3-count-integer-average-subsets
   1 n 0 0))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2002-a3-statement (n tn)
  (implies
   (and
    (integerp n)
    (integerp tn)
    (<= 2 n)
    (equal tn (putnam-2002-a3-tn n)))
   (equal (mod (- tn n) 2) 0)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2002_a3): the number of nonempty subsets of
-- {1,...,n} with integer average differs from n by an even integer. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2002A3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; negsuc; pos)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 3 _andB_

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

_andB_ : Bool -> Bool -> Bool
true andB right =
  right
false andB right =
  false

natEqual : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
natEqual zero zero =
  true
natEqual zero (suc right) =
  false
natEqual (suc left) zero =
  false
natEqual (suc left) (suc right) =
  natEqual left right

Subset : Nat -> Set
Subset n =
  Fin n -> Bool

emptySubset : Subset zero
emptySubset ()

prepend :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Bool ->
  Subset n ->
  Subset (suc n)
prepend choice tail fzero =
  choice
prepend choice tail (fsuc index) =
  tail index

countWhere :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Subset n -> Bool) ->
  Nat
countWhere {zero} predicate with predicate emptySubset
... | true =
  one
... | false =
  zero
countWhere {suc n} predicate =
  countWhere {n} (\ tail -> predicate (prepend false tail))
  +
  countWhere {n} (\ tail -> predicate (prepend true tail))

subsetCardinality :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Subset n ->
  Nat
subsetCardinality {zero} subset =
  zero
subsetCardinality {suc n} subset with subset fzero
... | true =
  suc (subsetCardinality (\ index -> subset (fsuc index)))
... | false =
  subsetCardinality (\ index -> subset (fsuc index))

subsetSumFrom :
  Nat ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Subset n ->
  Nat
subsetSumFrom offset {zero} subset =
  zero
subsetSumFrom offset {suc n} subset with subset fzero
... | true =
  suc offset
  +
  subsetSumFrom
    (suc offset)
    (\ index -> subset (fsuc index))
... | false =
  subsetSumFrom
    (suc offset)
    (\ index -> subset (fsuc index))

subsetSum :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Subset n ->
  Nat
subsetSum =
  subsetSumFrom zero

searchQuotient :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Bool
searchQuotient divisor dividend zero =
  natEqual (divisor * zero) dividend
searchQuotient divisor dividend (suc quotient) with
  natEqual (divisor * suc quotient) dividend
... | true =
  true
... | false =
  searchQuotient divisor dividend quotient

hasNaturalQuotient :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Bool
hasNaturalQuotient divisor dividend =
  searchQuotient divisor dividend dividend

nonzero : Nat -> Bool
nonzero zero =
  false
nonzero (suc n) =
  true

hasIntegralAverage :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Subset n ->
  Bool
hasIntegralAverage subset =
  nonzero (subsetCardinality subset)
  andB
  hasNaturalQuotient
    (subsetCardinality subset)
    (subsetSum subset)

qualifyingSubsetCount : Nat -> Nat
qualifyingSubsetCount n =
  countWhere {n} hasIntegralAverage

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc left) zero =
  pos (suc left)
difference zero (suc right) =
  negsuc right
difference (suc left) (suc right) =
  difference left right

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos left) (pos right) =
  pos (left + right)
addInt (pos left) (negsuc right) =
  difference left (suc right)
addInt (negsuc left) (pos right) =
  difference right (suc left)
addInt (negsuc left) (negsuc right) =
  negsuc (suc (left + right))

record Even (integer : Int) : Set where
  constructor even
  field
    half     : Int
    equation : addInt half half == integer

putnam-2002-a3 : Set
putnam-2002-a3 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  two <=N n ->
  Even (difference (qualifyingSubsetCount n) n)

title: putnam_2002_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a3:
% the number of nonempty subsets of the integers from 1 through n whose
% average is an integer differs from n by an even integer. This file contains
% no proof.

putnam_2002_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING
    finite_sets[int],
    finite_sets_of_sets[int]

  integer_set: TYPE = finite_set[int]
  integer_set_family: TYPE = finite_set[integer_set]

  distinct_entries(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(value, tail):
        NOT member(value, tail) AND distinct_entries(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  integer_list_sum(values: list[int]): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES values OF
      null: 0,
      cons(value, tail):
        value + integer_list_sum(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  enumerates_set(values: list[int], S: integer_set): bool =
    distinct_entries(values)
      AND FORALL (value: int):
        S(value) IFF member(value, values)

  is_one_through_n(universe: integer_set, n: int): bool =
    FORALL (value: int):
      universe(value) IFF (1 <= value AND value <= n)

  has_integer_average(S: integer_set): bool =
    card(S) > 0
      AND EXISTS (values: list[int]), (average: int):
        enumerates_set(values, S)
          AND integer_list_sum(values)
            = average * (card(S) :: int)

  qualifying_subsets(
      universe: integer_set): integer_set_family =
    intersection(
      powerset(universe),
      {S: integer_set | has_integer_average(S)})

  integer_even(value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (factor: int):
      value = 2 * factor

  putnam_2002_a3: bool =
    FORALL (n, Tn: int):
      (n >= 2
        AND EXISTS (universe: integer_set):
          is_one_through_n(universe, n)
            AND Tn
              = (card(qualifying_subsets(universe)) :: int))
      IMPLIES integer_even(Tn - n)
END putnam_2002_a3

  the binary-recursive rational sequence yields every positive rational as

;; every positive rational occurs as a consecutive-term ratio in any rational
;; sequence satisfying the stated Stern recurrence. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; DEFSTUB supplies the arbitrary source sequence a : N -> Q.  The predicates
;; below state its codomain and recurrence explicitly; no particular sequence
;; or witness is built into the formalization.
(defstub putnam-2002-a5-a (n) t)

(defun-sk putnam-2002-a5-rational-valued-p ()
  (forall
   (n)
   (implies
    (natp n)
    (rationalp (putnam-2002-a5-a n)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2002-a5-recurrence-p ()
  (forall
   (n)
   (implies
    (natp n)
    (and
     (equal
      (putnam-2002-a5-a (+ (* 2 n) 1))
      (putnam-2002-a5-a n))
     (equal
      (putnam-2002-a5-a (+ (* 2 n) 2))
      (+ (putnam-2002-a5-a n)
         (putnam-2002-a5-a (+ n 1))))))))

(defun putnam-2002-a5-valid-sequence-p ()
  (and
   (putnam-2002-a5-rational-valued-p)
   (equal (putnam-2002-a5-a 0) 1)
   (putnam-2002-a5-recurrence-p)))

;; ACL2 division is totalized, as it is for rationals in the source provers.
;; Since q is positive, an index with a zero denominator cannot satisfy the
;; displayed equality and therefore needs no separate side condition.
(defun-sk putnam-2002-a5-witness-exists-p (q)
  (exists
   (n)
   (and
    (natp n)
    (<= 1 n)
    (equal
     q
     (/ (putnam-2002-a5-a (- n 1))
        (putnam-2002-a5-a n))))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2002-a5-statement (q)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2002-a5-valid-sequence-p)
    (rationalp q)
    (< 0 q))
   (putnam-2002-a5-witness-exists-p q)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)

:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2002_a5): the Stern recurrence enumerates every
-- positive rational as a quotient of consecutive terms. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2002A5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record RationalField (Q : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroQ oneQ : Q
    add multiply : Q -> Q -> Q
    negate inverse : Q -> Q
    lessOrEqual : Q -> Q -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> Q
    fromInt : Int -> Q

    one-not-zero :
      oneQ != zeroQ

    add-commutative :
      (x y : Q) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : Q) -> add x zeroQ == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : Q) -> add x (negate x) == zeroQ

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : Q) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : Q) -> multiply x oneQ == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : Q) -> multiply x zeroQ == zeroQ
    distribute :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroQ == zeroQ
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : Q) ->
      x != zeroQ ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneQ

    order-reflexive :
      (x : Q) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroQ x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroQ y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroQ (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroQ oneQ and zeroQ != oneQ

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroQ
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneQ
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    fromInt-nonnegative :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromInt (pos n) == fromNat n
    fromInt-negative :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromInt (negsuc n) == negate (fromNat (suc n))

    every-element-is-ratio :
      (x : Q) ->
      Exists Int
        (\ numerator ->
          Exists Nat
            (\ denominator-minus-one ->
              x ==
              multiply
                (fromInt numerator)
                (inverse
                  (fromNat (suc denominator-minus-one)))))

open RationalField

divide :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q ->
  Q ->
  Q
divide rationals x y =
  multiply rationals x (inverse rationals y)

StrictLess :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q ->
  Q ->
  Set
StrictLess rationals x y =
  lessOrEqual rationals x y and x != y

SternRecurrence :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  (Nat -> Q) ->
  Set
SternRecurrence rationals a =
  a zero == oneQ rationals
  and
  ((n : Nat) ->
    a (suc (n + n)) == a n
    and
    a (suc (suc (n + n))) ==
      add rationals (a n) (a (suc n)))

OccursAsConsecutiveQuotient :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  (Nat -> Q) ->
  Q ->
  Set
OccursAsConsecutiveQuotient rationals a q =
  Exists Nat
    (\ n ->
      suc zero <=N n
      and
      divide rationals (a (n - suc zero)) (a n) == q)

putnam-2002-a5 : Set1
putnam-2002-a5 =
  (Q : Set) ->
  (rationals : RationalField Q) ->
  (a : Nat -> Q) ->
  SternRecurrence rationals a ->
  (q : Q) ->
  StrictLess rationals (zeroQ rationals) q ->
  OccursAsConsecutiveQuotient rationals a q

$(

  putnam_2002_a5: every positive rational occurs as the ratio of consecutive
  terms of the specified recursively defined rational sequence. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The class QQ ^m NN0 is the class of rational-valued sequences indexed by
  the nonnegative integers. The antecedent states the initial value and both
  recursion rules for every nonnegative integer n.

  Set.mm's NN is the class of positive integers. Thus the internally
  quantified m in the conclusion ranges over exactly the source indices
  m >= 1, and m - 1 remains a nonnegative sequence index.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a m n q $.

  putnambench-putnam-2002-a5 $a |- A. a e. ( QQ ^m NN0 )
    (
      (
        ( a ` 0 ) = 1
        /\
        A. n e. NN0
          (
            ( a ` ( ( 2 x. n ) + 1 ) ) = ( a ` n )
            /\
            ( a ` ( ( 2 x. n ) + 2 ) )
            =
            ( ( a ` n ) + ( a ` ( n + 1 ) ) )
          )
      )
      ->
      A. q e. QQ
        (
          0 < q
          ->
          E. m e. NN
            q
            =
            (
              ( a ` ( m - 1 ) )
              /
              ( a ` m )
            )
        )
    )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a5:
% a rational sequence defined by the stated binary recurrences enumerates every
% positive rational as a ratio of consecutive terms. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2002_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  rational_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> rat]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: rat): rat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  putnam_2002_a5: bool =
    FORALL (a: rational_sequence):
      (a(0) = 1
        AND (FORALL (n: nat):
          a(2 * n + 1) = a(n)
            AND a(2 * n + 2) = a(n) + a(n + 1)))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (q: rat):
          q > 0 IMPLIES
            EXISTS (n: nat):
              n >= 1
                AND q = safe_div(a(n - 1), a(n))
END putnam_2002_a5

import Mathlib

open Nat Set Topology Filter

abbrev putnam_2002_a6_solution : Set ℕ := sorry
-- {2}
/--
Fix an integer $b \geq 2$. Let $f(1) = 1$, $f(2) = 2$, and for each
$n \geq 3$, define $f(n) = n f(d)$, where $d$ is the number of
base-$b$ digits of $n$. For which values of $b$ does
\[
\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{f(n)}
\]
converge?
-/
theorem putnam_2002_a6
(f : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ)
(hf : ∀ b : ℕ, f b 1 = 1 ∧ f b 2 = 2 ∧ ∀ n ∈ Ici 3, f b n = n * f b (Nat.digits b n).length)
: {b ∈ Ici 2 | ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, 1/(f b n)) atTop (𝓝 L)} = putnam_2002_a6_solution :=
sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a6:
   convergence of a recursively defined reciprocal series according to the
   base-b digit length, with exactly base 2 qualifying; this file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals Arith.PeanoNat SeqSeries.

Open Scope R_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_2002_a6_digit_length_fuel
    (fuel b n : nat) : nat :=
  match fuel with
  | O => O
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb n b
      then 1%nat
      else S (putnam_2002_a6_digit_length_fuel
                fuel' b (Nat.div n b))
  end.

Definition putnam_2002_a6_digit_length
    (b n : nat) : nat :=
  if Nat.ltb b 2
  then O
  else putnam_2002_a6_digit_length_fuel (S n) b n.

Fixpoint putnam_2002_a6_partial_sum
    (f : nat -> nat -> R) (b m : nat) : R :=
  match m with
  | O => 0
  | S m' =>
      putnam_2002_a6_partial_sum f b m' + 1 / f b (S m')
  end.

Definition putnam_2002_a6_converges
    (f : nat -> nat -> R) (b : nat) : Prop :=
  exists limit : R,
    Un_cv (fun m : nat => putnam_2002_a6_partial_sum f b m) limit.

Definition putnam_2002_a6_solution (b : nat) : Prop :=
  b = 2%nat.

Theorem putnam_2002_a6 :
  forall f : nat -> nat -> R,
    (forall b : nat,
      f b 1%nat = 1 /\
      f b 2%nat = 2 /\
      forall n : nat,
        (3 <= n)%nat ->
        f b n =
          INR n * f b (putnam_2002_a6_digit_length b n)) ->
    forall b : nat,
      (2 <= b)%nat ->
      (putnam_2002_a6_converges f b <->
       putnam_2002_a6_solution b).
Admitted.

  the recursively defined real series converges exactly for base 2 among
  integer bases at least 2. This file contains no proof.

let analysis_formatter = Format.formatter_of_out_channel analysis_output;;
