;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a6:
;; the reciprocal series generated by the base-b digit-length recurrence
;; converges exactly for b = 2. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; For b >= 2 this is the length of Nat.digits b n. Fuel n makes the
;; definition total; every recursive argument is smaller for the relevant
;; bases.
(defun putnam-2002-a6-digit-length-aux
    (b n fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (or (zp fuel) (zp n))
      0
    (+ 1
       (putnam-2002-a6-digit-length-aux
        b (floor n b) (- fuel 1)))))

(defun putnam-2002-a6-digit-length (b n)
  (if (and (natp b)
           (natp n)
           (<= 2 b))
      (putnam-2002-a6-digit-length-aux b n n)
    0))

;; On every relevant base, the source recurrence forces f(b,n) to be a
;; positive integer embedded in R. Representing those forced values by exact
;; ACL2 rationals loses no source functions and avoids a surrogate real sort.
(defun-sk putnam-2002-a6-recurrence-p (function)
  (forall (b n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp b)
      (<= 2 b)
      (natp n)
      (<= 1 n))
     (and
      (rationalp (apply$ function (list b n)))
      (implies
       (equal n 1)
       (equal (apply$ function (list b n)) 1))
      (implies
       (equal n 2)
       (equal (apply$ function (list b n)) 2))
      (implies
       (<= 3 n)
       (equal
        (apply$ function (list b n))
        (* n
           (apply$
            function
            (list
             b
             (putnam-2002-a6-digit-length b n))))))))))

(defun putnam-2002-a6-partial-sum
    (function b m)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix m)))
  (if (zp m)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2002-a6-partial-sum
        function b (- m 1))
       (/ 1
          (apply$ function (list b m))))))

;; These partial sums are increasing because the recurrence makes every
;; denominator positive. An increasing rational sequence converges in R
;; exactly when it is bounded above, so this predicate is equivalent to the
;; source's existential real limit without introducing a proposed limit or
;; convergence rate.
(defun-sk putnam-2002-a6-bounded-by-p
    (function b bound)
  (forall (m)
    (implies
     (natp m)
     (<= (putnam-2002-a6-partial-sum
          function b m)
         bound))))

(defun-sk putnam-2002-a6-partial-sums-bounded-p
    (function b)
  (exists (bound)
    (and
     (rationalp bound)
     (putnam-2002-a6-bounded-by-p
      function b bound))))

;; Pointwise extensional equality with the source solution set {2}.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2002-a6-statement
    (function b)
  (implies
   (and
    (tamep-functionp function)
    (putnam-2002-a6-recurrence-p function))
   (iff
    (and
     (natp b)
     (<= 2 b)
     (putnam-2002-a6-partial-sums-bounded-p
      function b))
    (equal b 2))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- the reciprocal series defined by the base-b digit-length recurrence converges
-- exactly for base 2. This file contains no proof.

module Putnam2002A6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

NatStrictLess : Nat -> Nat -> Set
NatStrictLess m n =
  suc m <=N n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

naturalPowerNat : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalPowerNat b zero =
  oneN
naturalPowerNat b (suc exponent) =
  naturalPowerNat b exponent * b

BaseDigitCount : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Set
BaseDigitCount b n d =
  Exists Nat
    (\ predecessor ->
      d == suc predecessor
      and
      naturalPowerNat b predecessor <=N n
      and
      NatStrictLess n (naturalPowerNat b d))

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    add-associative :

    add-zero :

    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :

    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->

    multiply-one :

    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

module Putnam2002A6Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  partialSum :
    (Nat -> Nat -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    Nat ->
    R
  partialSum f b zero =
    zeroR reals
  partialSum f b (suc m) =
    add reals
      (partialSum f b m)
      (divide reals
        (oneR reals)
        (f b (suc m)))

  SeriesConverges :
    (Nat -> Nat -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    Set
  SeriesConverges f b =
    Exists R
      (\ limit ->
        ConvergesTo reals
          (partialSum f b)
          limit)

  FollowsDigitRecurrence :
    (Nat -> Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  FollowsDigitRecurrence f =
    (b : Nat) ->
    twoN <=N b ->
    f b oneN == oneR reals
    and
    f b twoN == fromNat reals twoN
    and
    ((n : Nat) ->
      threeN <=N n ->
      (d : Nat) ->
      BaseDigitCount b n d ->
      f b n ==
      multiply reals
        (fromNat reals n)
        (f b d))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (f : Nat -> Nat -> R) ->
    FollowsDigitRecurrence f ->
    (b : Nat) ->
    Iff
      (twoN <=N b and SeriesConverges f b)
      (b == twoN)

putnam-2002-a6 : Set1
putnam-2002-a6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2002A6Statement.proposition reals

title: putnam_2002_a6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a6:
  the reciprocal series defined by the base-b digit-length recurrence converges
  exactly for base 2 among natural-number bases at least 2. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;
open real_topologyTheory;

val putnam_2002_a6 =
  ``let digitlength =
      \b n : num.
        if b < 2 then 0
        else LEAST k : num. n < b EXP k
    in
      !f : num -> num -> real.
        (!b : num.
           f b 1 = 1 /\
           f b 2 = 2 /\
           (!n : num.
              3 <= n
              ==>
              f b n = &n * f b (digitlength b n)))
        ==>
        {b : num |
           2 <= b /\
           ?L : real.
             ((\m : num.
                 SIGMA
                   (\n : num. 1 / f b n)
                   (IMAGE SUC (count m))) --> L)
             sequentially} =
        {b : num | b = 2}``;

title: putnam_2002_a6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2002_a6: the bases for which the reciprocal series generated by
  the base-digit-length recurrence converges are exactly the singleton
  containing base 2. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The function f is an arbitrary real-valued family indexed by a base and a
  nonnegative integer. For every base b at least 2, its initial values are 1
  and 2. For n at least 3, the internally existential positive integer d is
  characterized by

    b^(d-1) <= n < b^d,

  which for b >= 2 uniquely says that d is the number of base-b digits of n.
  The recurrence then has exactly the source form f(b,n) = n f(b,d).

  For m in NN0, 1 ... m is the inclusive finite interval, empty when m is
  zero, so the mapped finite sum is the source sequence of real partial sums.
  Its real limit L remains existentially quantified inside the set-builder.
  Equality with { 2 } inlines the solution value recorded by the sources.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d b d f L m n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2002-a6 $a
    |- A. f e. ( RR ^m ( NN0 X. NN0 ) )
      (
        (
          A. b e. NN
            (
              2 <_ b
              ->
              (
                (
                  ( f ` <. b , 1 >. ) = 1
                  /\
                  ( f ` <. b , 2 >. ) = 2
                )
                /\
                A. n e. NN
                  (
                    3 <_ n
                    ->
                    E. d e. NN
                      (
                        (
                          ( b ^ ( d - 1 ) ) <_ n
                          /\
                          n < ( b ^ d )
                        )
                        /\
                        ( f ` <. b , n >. )
                        =
                        ( n x. ( f ` <. b , d >. ) )
                      )
                  )
              )
            )
          ->
          {
            b e. NN |
            (
              2 <_ b
              /\
              E. L e. RR
                (
                  m e. NN0 |->
                    sum_ n e. ( 1 ... m )
                      ( 1 / ( f ` <. b , n >. ) )
                )
                ~~>
                L
            )
          }
          =
          { 2 }
        )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2002_a6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_a6:
% the reciprocal series for the base-b digit-length recurrence converges
% exactly when the integer base b is 2. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2002_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  recurrence_function: TYPE = [nat, nat -> real]

  base_digit_count_is(
      base, value, digit_count: nat): bool =
    digit_count > 0
      AND base ^ (digit_count - 1) <= value
      AND value < base ^ digit_count

  satisfies_recurrence(f: recurrence_function): bool =
    FORALL (base: nat):
      base >= 2 IMPLIES
        (f(base, 1) = 1
          AND f(base, 2) = 2
          AND FORALL (value: nat):
            value >= 3 IMPLIES
              EXISTS (digit_count: nat):
                base_digit_count_is(
                  base, value, digit_count)
                  AND f(base, value) =
                    (value :: real)
                      * f(base, digit_count))

  safe_reciprocal(value: real): real =
    IF value = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      1 / value
    ENDIF

  partial_sum(
      f: recurrence_function,
      base, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_sum(f, base, count - 1)
        + safe_reciprocal(f(base, count))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  series_converges(
      f: recurrence_function,
      base: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (limit_value: real):
      FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
          FORALL (count: nat):
            cutoff <= count IMPLIES
              abs(
                partial_sum(f, base, count)
                  - limit_value)
                < epsilon_value

  putnam_2002_a6: bool =
    FORALL (f: recurrence_function):
      satisfies_recurrence(f) IMPLIES
        FORALL (base: nat):
          base >= 2 IMPLIES
            (series_converges(f, base)
              IFF base = 2)
END putnam_2002_a6

putnam_2002_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b3:
;; the two-sided error bounds for (1-1/n)^n as an approximation to 1/e for
;; every integer n greater than one. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-2002-b3-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2002-b3-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'if
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2002-b3-and-terms (cdr terms))
       (putnam-2002-b3-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2002-b3-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2002-b3-true-function ()
  (list 'lambda '(witness)
        (putnam-2002-b3-quoted t)))

;; (CAR LOOP$-IVARS) is an index j and (CAR LOOP$-GVARS) is a proposed finite
;; list of Taylor terms. This fully tame function checks term_0 = 1 and
;; term_j = term_(j-1)/j for every positive j.
(defun putnam-2002-b3-taylor-entry-function ()
  '(lambda (loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)
     (if (equal (car loop$-ivars) '0)
         (equal
          (nth (car loop$-ivars) (car loop$-gvars))
          '1)
       (equal
        (nth (car loop$-ivars) (car loop$-gvars))
        (binary-*
         (nth
          (binary-+ (car loop$-ivars) '-1)
          (car loop$-gvars))
         (unary-/ (car loop$-ivars)))))))

(defun putnam-2002-b3-singleton-index-function ()
  '(lambda (index)
     (cons index 'nil)))

(defun putnam-2002-b3-taylor-prefix-valid-term (terms)
  (let* ((range
          (list
           'from-to-by
           (putnam-2002-b3-quoted 0)
           (list
            'binary-+
            (list 'len terms)
            (putnam-2002-b3-quoted -1))
           (putnam-2002-b3-quoted 1)))
         (wrapped-range
          (list
           'collect$
           (putnam-2002-b3-quoted
            (putnam-2002-b3-singleton-index-function))
           range)))
    (list
     'always$+
     (putnam-2002-b3-quoted
      (putnam-2002-b3-taylor-entry-function))
     (list
      'cons
      terms
      (putnam-2002-b3-quoted nil))
     wrapped-range)))

(defun putnam-2002-b3-taylor-prefix-sum-term (terms)
  (list
   'sum$
   (putnam-2002-b3-quoted 'identity)
   terms))

;; The witness is the complete list 1/0!,...,1/k!. The tame recurrence check
;; makes its SUM$ value exactly the degree-k Taylor prefix. The function
;; differs from constant true exactly when a prefix exceeds THRESHOLD, so
;; NOT/FN-EQUAL keeps k and its finite certificate internal and expresses
;; THRESHOLD < exp(1).
(defun putnam-2002-b3-not-below-e-function (threshold)
  (let* ((witness 'witness)
         (qualification
          (putnam-2002-b3-and-terms
           (list
            (list 'true-listp witness)
            (list 'consp witness)
            (putnam-2002-b3-taylor-prefix-valid-term
             witness)
            (list
             '<
             (putnam-2002-b3-quoted threshold)
             (putnam-2002-b3-taylor-prefix-sum-term
              witness))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(witness)
     (list
      'if
      qualification
      (putnam-2002-b3-quoted nil)
      (putnam-2002-b3-quoted t)))))

(defun putnam-2002-b3-less-than-e-p (threshold)
  (let ((failure-function
         (putnam-2002-b3-not-below-e-function threshold))
        (true-function
         (putnam-2002-b3-true-function)))
    (and
     (rationalp threshold)
     (tamep-functionp failure-function)
     (tamep-functionp true-function)
     (not
      (fn-equal failure-function true-function)))))

;; For positive k, the exponential-series tail after degree k is strictly
;; smaller than 1/(k*k!). Thus prefix_k + term_k/k is a rational upper bound
;; cofinal with exp(1). The function differs from constant true exactly when
;; one fully validated upper bound is below THRESHOLD, so NOT/FN-EQUAL
;; expresses exp(1) < THRESHOLD with an internal Taylor witness.
(defun putnam-2002-b3-not-above-e-function (threshold)
  (let* ((witness 'witness)
         (degree
          (list
           'binary-+
           (list 'len witness)
           (putnam-2002-b3-quoted -1)))
         (last-term
          (list 'nth degree witness))
         (upper-bound
          (list
           'binary-+
           (putnam-2002-b3-taylor-prefix-sum-term
            witness)
           (list
            'binary-*
            last-term
            (list 'unary-/ degree))))
         (qualification
          (putnam-2002-b3-and-terms
           (list
            (list 'true-listp witness)
            (list 'consp (list 'cdr witness))
            (putnam-2002-b3-taylor-prefix-valid-term
             witness)
            (list
             '<
             upper-bound
             (putnam-2002-b3-quoted threshold))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(witness)
     (list
      'if
      qualification
      (putnam-2002-b3-quoted nil)
      (putnam-2002-b3-quoted t)))))

(defun putnam-2002-b3-e-less-than-p (threshold)
  (let ((failure-function
         (putnam-2002-b3-not-above-e-function threshold))
        (true-function
         (putnam-2002-b3-true-function)))
    (and
     (rationalp threshold)
     (tamep-functionp failure-function)
     (tamep-functionp true-function)
     (not
      (fn-equal failure-function true-function)))))

(defun putnam-2002-b3-power-approximation (n)
  (expt (- 1 (/ 1 n)) n))

;; Since n>1, both exp(1) and (1-1/n)^n are positive. Multiplying the source
;; inequalities by exp(1) and dividing by the rational power shows that they
;; are respectively equivalent to
;;
;;   (1-1/n)/(1-1/n)^n < exp(1)
;;   exp(1) < (1-1/(2*n))/(1-1/n)^n.
;;
;; The two comparison predicates above are the exact strict order on this
;; computable real, not fixed-precision numerical approximations.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2002-b3-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and (integerp n)
        (< 1 n))
   (let ((power (putnam-2002-b3-power-approximation n)))
     (and
      (putnam-2002-b3-less-than-e-p
       (/ (- 1 (/ 1 n))
          power))
      (putnam-2002-b3-e-less-than-p
       (/ (- 1 (/ 1 (* 2 n)))
          power))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2002_b3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2002_b3): the two strict bounds for the error
-- between 1/e and (1 - 1/n)^n for every integer n greater than one. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2002B3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data IntegerGreaterThanOne : Int -> Set where
  positive-at-least-two :
    (k : Nat) ->
    IntegerGreaterThanOne (pos (suc (suc k)))

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

integerPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Int ->
  R
integerPower reals x (pos n) =
  naturalPower reals x n
integerPower reals x (negsuc n) =
  naturalPower reals (inverse reals x) (suc n)

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

exponentialTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

ExponentialValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
ExponentialValue reals x value =
  SeriesHasSum reals
    (exponentialTerm reals x)
    value

record StandardExponential
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    exponential : R -> R
    exponential-series :
      (x : R) ->
      ExponentialValue reals x (exponential x)

open StandardExponential

module Putnam2002B3Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (realExp : StandardExponential reals) where

  eulerNumber : R
  eulerNumber =
    exponential realExp (oneR reals)

  putnamFunction : Int -> R
  putnamFunction n =
    subtract reals
      (divide reals (oneR reals) eulerNumber)
      (integerPower reals
        (subtract reals
          (oneR reals)
          (divide reals
            (oneR reals)
            (fromInt reals n)))
        n)

  lowerBound : Int -> R -> R
  lowerBound n e =
    divide reals
      (oneR reals)
      (multiply reals
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals twoN)
          (fromInt reals n))
        e)

  upperBound : Int -> R -> R
  upperBound n e =
    divide reals
      (oneR reals)
      (multiply reals
        (fromInt reals n)
        e)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (e : R) ->
    e == eulerNumber ->
    (f : Int -> R) ->
    f == putnamFunction ->
    (n : Int) ->
    IntegerGreaterThanOne n ->
    StrictLess reals (lowerBound n e) (f n)
    and
    StrictLess reals (f n) (upperBound n e)

putnam-2002-b3 : Set1
putnam-2002-b3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (realExp : StandardExponential reals) ->
  Putnam2002B3Statement.proposition reals realExp

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b3:
% for every integer n greater than one, 1/e - (1 - 1/n)^n lies strictly
% between 1/(2ne) and 1/(ne). This file contains no proof.

putnam_2002_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  putnam_2002_b3: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n > 1 IMPLIES
        LET n_real: real = n,
            e: real = real_exponential(1),
            difference: real =
              safe_div(1, e)
                - (1 - safe_div(1, n_real)) ^ n
        IN
          safe_div(1, 2 * n_real * e) < difference
            AND difference < safe_div(1, n_real * e)
END putnam_2002_b3

import Mathlib

open Nat Set Topology Filter

/--
A palindrome in base $b$ is a positive integer whose base-$b$
digits read the same backwards and forwards; for example,
$2002$ is a 4-digit palindrome in base 10. Note that 200 is not
a palindrome in base 10, but it is the 3-digit palindrome
242 in base 9, and 404 in base 7. Prove that there is an integer
which is a 3-digit palindrome in base $b$ for at least 2002
different values of $b$.
-/
theorem putnam_2002_b5
: ∃ n : ℕ, {b : ℕ | b ≥ 1 ∧ (Nat.digits b n).length = 3 ∧ List.Palindrome (Nat.digits b n)}.ncard ≥ 2002 :=

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b5:
   some natural number has a three-digit palindromic expansion in at least
   2002 different bases. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List.

Import ListNotations.

Fixpoint putnam_2002_b5_digits_fuel
    (fuel base n : nat) : list nat :=
  match fuel with
  | O => []
  | S fuel' =>
      if Nat.ltb base 2
      then repeat 1 n
      else
        if Nat.eqb n O
        then []
        else
          Nat.modulo n base ::
          putnam_2002_b5_digits_fuel
            fuel' base (Nat.div n base)
  end.

Definition putnam_2002_b5_digits
    (base n : nat) : list nat :=
  putnam_2002_b5_digits_fuel (S n) base n.

Definition putnam_2002_b5_three_digit_palindrome
    (n base : nat) : Prop :=
  (1 <= base)%nat /\
  length (putnam_2002_b5_digits base n) = 3%nat /\
  putnam_2002_b5_digits base n =
    rev (putnam_2002_b5_digits base n).

Definition putnam_2002_b5_has_cardinality_at_least
    (P : nat -> Prop) (minimum : nat) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list nat,
    NoDup enumeration /\
    (forall b : nat, In b enumeration <-> P b) /\
    (minimum <= length enumeration)%nat.

Theorem putnam_2002_b5 :
  exists n : nat,
    putnam_2002_b5_has_cardinality_at_least
      (putnam_2002_b5_three_digit_palindrome n)
      2002%nat.
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b5:
;; existence of a natural number that is a three-digit palindrome in at
;; least 2002 distinct natural-number bases. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For b >= 2, write q1 = floor(n/b) and q2 = floor(q1/b). The source digit
;; list has length three exactly when q1 >= b and q2 < b, and then its first
;; and last digits are mod(n,b) and q2. For b = 1, the source definition gives
;; n copies of 1, so it is a three-digit palindrome exactly when n = 3.

(defun putnam-2002-b5-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2002-b5-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'if
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2002-b5-and-terms (cdr terms))
       (putnam-2002-b5-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2002-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2002-b5-or-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'if
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2002-b5-quoted t)
       (putnam-2002-b5-or-terms (cdr terms)))
    (putnam-2002-b5-quoted nil)))

(defun putnam-2002-b5-less-equal-term (left right)
  (list
   'if
   (list '< right left)
   (putnam-2002-b5-quoted nil)
   (putnam-2002-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2002-b5-palindromic-base-function ()
  (let* ((n (list 'car 'globals))
         (q1
          (list
           'floor
           n
           'b))
         (q2
          (list
           'floor
           q1
           'b))
         (base-one-case
          (putnam-2002-b5-and-terms
           (list
            (list
             'equal
             'b
             (putnam-2002-b5-quoted 1))
            (list
             'equal
             n
             (putnam-2002-b5-quoted 3)))))
         (ordinary-base-case
          (putnam-2002-b5-and-terms
           (list
            (putnam-2002-b5-less-equal-term
             (putnam-2002-b5-quoted 2)
             'b)
            (putnam-2002-b5-less-equal-term
             'b
             q1)
            (list '< q2 'b)
            (list
             'equal
             (list 'mod n 'b)
             q2))))
         (qualification
          (putnam-2002-b5-or-terms
           (list base-one-case ordinary-base-case))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(globals b)
     (list
      'if
      qualification
      (putnam-2002-b5-quoted 1)
      (putnam-2002-b5-quoted 0)))))

;; No base b > n can satisfy the ordinary-base case: its digit list is [n].
;; Hence this sum is exactly the cardinality of the source set of all natural
;; bases b >= 1, rather than a bounded approximation to that cardinality.
(defun putnam-2002-b5-palindromic-base-count-term (n)
  (list
   'sum$+
   (putnam-2002-b5-quoted
    (putnam-2002-b5-palindromic-base-function))
   (list
    'cons
    n
    (putnam-2002-b5-quoted nil))
   (list
    'from-to-by
    (putnam-2002-b5-quoted 1)
    n
    (putnam-2002-b5-quoted 1))))

;; This function is false exactly at natural witnesses having at least 2002
;; qualifying bases. Negated FN-EQUAL therefore expresses the source's
;; unbounded existential quantifier without making its witness a parameter.
(defun putnam-2002-b5-witness-failure-function ()
  (let ((qualification
         (putnam-2002-b5-and-terms
          (list
           (list 'natp 'n)
           (putnam-2002-b5-less-equal-term
            (putnam-2002-b5-quoted 2002)
            (putnam-2002-b5-palindromic-base-count-term
             'n))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(n)
     (list
      'if
      qualification
      (putnam-2002-b5-quoted nil)
      (putnam-2002-b5-quoted t)))))

(defun putnam-2002-b5-true-function ()
  '(lambda (n) 't))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2002-b5-statement ()
  (let ((base-function
         (putnam-2002-b5-palindromic-base-function))
        (failure-function
         (putnam-2002-b5-witness-failure-function))
        (true-function
         (putnam-2002-b5-true-function)))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp base-function)
     (tamep-functionp failure-function)
     (tamep-functionp true-function)
     (not
      (fn-equal failure-function true-function)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b5:
-- some natural number is a three-digit palindrome in at least 2002 distinct
-- natural-number bases. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module putnam-2002-b5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=_ _<_

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

data _<=_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <= n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> suc m <= suc n

_<_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m < n =
  suc m <= n

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

record ThreeDigitPalindrome (base number : Nat) : Set where
  field
    base-at-least-one : one <= base
    outer-digit       : Nat
    middle-digit      : Nat
    outer-positive    : zero < outer-digit
    outer-below-base  : outer-digit < base
    middle-below-base : middle-digit < base
    base-expansion    :
      number
      ==
      outer-digit
      + base * middle-digit
      + (base * base) * outer-digit

record AtLeastPalindromicBases (number count : Nat) : Set where
  field
    base :
      Fin count ->
      Nat
    palindromic :
      (index : Fin count) ->
      ThreeDigitPalindrome (base index) number
    distinct :
      (left-index right-index : Fin count) ->
      base left-index == base right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

putnam-2002-b5 : Set
putnam-2002-b5 =
  Exists Nat
    (\ number ->
      AtLeastPalindromicBases number 2002)

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2002_b5: existence of a natural number that is a three-digit
  palindrome in at least 2002 integer bases. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For b >= 2, a least-significant-digit-first base-b expansion has length
  three and is palindromic exactly when its digits are a,d,a, where
  1 <= a < b and 0 <= d < b. The displayed positional-value equation
  expresses precisely that condition. For b = 1, the sources define the
  digit list as n copies of 1, so it has length three and is palindromic
  exactly when n = 3.

  Thus the restricted class is exactly the source set of qualifying natural

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b5:
% some natural number is a three-digit palindrome in at least 2002 distinct
% integer bases. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2002_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  three_digit_palindrome(number, base: nat): bool =
    base >= 2
      AND EXISTS (outer_digit, middle_digit: nat):
        outer_digit >= 1
          AND outer_digit < base
          AND middle_digit < base
          AND number =
            outer_digit * base * base
              + middle_digit * base
              + outer_digit

  distinct_bases(bases: [below(2002) -> nat]): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: below(2002)):
      bases(i) = bases(j) IMPLIES i = j

  putnam_2002_b5: bool =
    EXISTS (number: nat), (bases: [below(2002) -> nat]):
      distinct_bases(bases)
        AND (FORALL (i: below(2002)):
          three_digit_palindrome(number, bases(i)))
END putnam_2002_b5

import Mathlib

open Nat Set Topology Filter Matrix MvPolynomial

/--
Let $p$ be a prime number. Prove that the determinant of the matrix
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
x & y & z \\
x^p & y^p & z^p \\
x^{p^2} & y^{p^2} & z^{p^2}
\end{pmatrix}
\]
is congruent modulo $p$ to a product of polynomials of the form
$ax+by+cz$, where $a,b,c$ are integers. (We say two integer
polynomials are congruent modulo $p$ if corresponding coefficients
are congruent modulo $p$.)
-/
theorem putnam_2002_b6
(p : ℕ)
(hp : Nat.Prime p)
(M : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) (MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℤ))
(hM : M = fun (r c : Fin 3) => ((X c)^(p^(r : ℕ)) : MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℤ))
(cong : ℕ → MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℤ × MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℤ → Prop)
(hcong : cong = fun p : ℕ => fun (f, g) => ∀ n : Fin 3 →₀ ℕ, Int.ModEq p (f.coeff n) (g.coeff n))
: ∃ S : Finset (MvPolynomial (Fin 3) ℤ), cong p ((det M), (∏ s ∈ S, s)) ∧ ∀ s ∈ S, (∃ a b c : ℤ, s = (C a)*(X 0) + (C b)*(X 1) + (C c)*(X 2)) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2002_b6
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b6:
   coefficientwise congruence modulo a prime between a three-variable
   polynomial determinant and a finite product of integer linear forms.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith List Arith.PeanoNat Bool.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Record putnam_2002_b6_monomial : Type := {
  putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent : nat;
  putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent : nat;
  putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent : nat;
  putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient : Z
}.

Definition putnam_2002_b6_polynomial : Type :=
  list putnam_2002_b6_monomial.

Fixpoint putnam_2002_b6_coefficient
    (p : putnam_2002_b6_polynomial) (i j k : nat) : Z :=
  match p with
  | [] => 0
  | m :: p' =>
      let rest := putnam_2002_b6_coefficient p' i j k in
      if andb
           (Nat.eqb (putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent m) i)
           (andb
              (Nat.eqb (putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent m) j)
              (Nat.eqb (putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent m) k))
      then putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient m + rest
      else rest
  end.

Definition putnam_2002_b6_monomial_product
    (m n : putnam_2002_b6_monomial) :
    putnam_2002_b6_monomial :=
  {|
    putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent :=
      (putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent m +
       putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent n)%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent :=
      (putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent m +
       putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent n)%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent :=
      (putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent m +
       putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent n)%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient :=
      putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient m *
      putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient n
  |}.

Definition putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_add
    (p q : putnam_2002_b6_polynomial) :
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  p ++ q.

Definition putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_neg
    (p : putnam_2002_b6_polynomial) :
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  map
    (fun m =>
      {|
        putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent :=
          putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent m;
        putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent :=
          putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent m;
        putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent :=
          putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent m;
        putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient :=
          - putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient m
      |})
    p.

Definition putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_sub
    (p q : putnam_2002_b6_polynomial) :
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_add
    p (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_neg q).

Definition putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul
    (p q : putnam_2002_b6_polynomial) :
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  flat_map
    (fun m => map (putnam_2002_b6_monomial_product m) q)
    p.

Definition putnam_2002_b6_one :
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  [{|
    putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent := 0%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent := 0%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent := 0%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient := 1
  |}].

Fixpoint putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_pow
    (p : putnam_2002_b6_polynomial) (n : nat) :
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  match n with
  | O => putnam_2002_b6_one
  | S n' =>
      putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul
        p (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_pow p n')
  end.

Definition putnam_2002_b6_x :
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  [{|
    putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent := 1%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent := 0%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent := 0%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient := 1
  |}].

Definition putnam_2002_b6_y :
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  [{|
    putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent := 0%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent := 1%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent := 0%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient := 1
  |}].

Definition putnam_2002_b6_z :
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  [{|
    putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent := 0%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent := 0%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent := 1%nat;
    putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient := 1
  |}].

Definition putnam_2002_b6_determinant
    (p : nat) : putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  let xp :=
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_pow putnam_2002_b6_x p in
  let yp :=
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_pow putnam_2002_b6_y p in
  let zp :=
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_pow putnam_2002_b6_z p in
  let xp2 :=
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_pow
      putnam_2002_b6_x (Nat.pow p 2) in
  let yp2 :=
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_pow
      putnam_2002_b6_y (Nat.pow p 2) in
  let zp2 :=
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_pow
      putnam_2002_b6_z (Nat.pow p 2) in
  putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_add
    (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_sub
      (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul
        putnam_2002_b6_x
        (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_sub
          (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul yp zp2)
          (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul zp yp2)))
      (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul
        putnam_2002_b6_y
        (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_sub
          (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul xp zp2)
          (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul zp xp2))))
    (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul
      putnam_2002_b6_z
      (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_sub
        (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul xp yp2)
        (putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul yp xp2))).

Record putnam_2002_b6_linear_coefficients : Type := {
  putnam_2002_b6_linear_x_coefficient : Z;
  putnam_2002_b6_linear_y_coefficient : Z;
  putnam_2002_b6_linear_z_coefficient : Z
}.

Definition putnam_2002_b6_linear_form
    (c : putnam_2002_b6_linear_coefficients) :
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  [
    {|
      putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent := 1%nat;
      putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent := 0%nat;
      putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent := 0%nat;
      putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient :=
        putnam_2002_b6_linear_x_coefficient c
    |};
    {|
      putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent := 0%nat;
      putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent := 1%nat;
      putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent := 0%nat;
      putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient :=
        putnam_2002_b6_linear_y_coefficient c
    |};
    {|
      putnam_2002_b6_x_exponent := 0%nat;
      putnam_2002_b6_y_exponent := 0%nat;
      putnam_2002_b6_z_exponent := 1%nat;
      putnam_2002_b6_monomial_coefficient :=
        putnam_2002_b6_linear_z_coefficient c
    |}
  ].

Fixpoint putnam_2002_b6_linear_product
    (factors : list putnam_2002_b6_linear_coefficients) :
    putnam_2002_b6_polynomial :=
  match factors with
  | [] => putnam_2002_b6_one
  | c :: factors' =>
      putnam_2002_b6_polynomial_mul
        (putnam_2002_b6_linear_form c)
        (putnam_2002_b6_linear_product factors')
  end.

Definition putnam_2002_b6_prime (p : nat) : Prop :=
  (2 <= p)%nat /\
  forall d : nat,
    (exists q : nat, p = (d * q)%nat) ->
    d = 1%nat \/ d = p.

Definition putnam_2002_b6_mod_eq
    (p : nat) (a b : Z) : Prop :=
  exists q : Z, a - b = Z.of_nat p * q.

Theorem putnam_2002_b6 :
  forall p : nat,
    putnam_2002_b6_prime p ->
    exists factors : list putnam_2002_b6_linear_coefficients,
      forall i j k : nat,
        putnam_2002_b6_mod_eq p
          (putnam_2002_b6_coefficient
            (putnam_2002_b6_determinant p) i j k)
          (putnam_2002_b6_coefficient
            (putnam_2002_b6_linear_product factors) i j k).
Admitted.

content:
theory putnam_2002_b6 imports
Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Finite_Cartesian_Product"
"HOL-Analysis.Determinants"
"HOL-Number_Theory.Cong"
"HOL-Computational_Algebra.Primes"
"HOL-Computational_Algebra.Polynomial"
begin

theorem putnam_2002_b6:
  fixes p :: nat
  and lincomb :: "int \<times> int \<times> int \<Rightarrow> int poly poly poly"
  and M :: "(int poly poly poly)^3^3"
  and cong :: "nat \<Rightarrow> int poly poly poly \<times> int poly poly poly \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and idx :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 3"
  defines "lincomb \<equiv> \<lambda> (a, b, c). monom (monom (monom a 0) 0) 1 + monom (monom (monom b 0) 1) 0 + monom (monom (monom c 1) 0) 0"
  and "cong \<equiv> \<lambda> p (f, g). \<forall> r s t :: nat. [coeff (coeff (coeff f r) s) t = coeff (coeff (coeff g r) s) t] (mod (int p))"
  assumes idxbij: "\<forall> s :: 3. \<exists>! r \<in> {0..2}. idx r = s"
  and hp: "prime p"
  and hM: "\<forall> r \<in> {0..2}. M$(idx r)$(idx 0) = monom (monom (monom 1 0) 0) (p ^ r) \<and> M$(idx r)$(idx 1) = monom (monom (monom 1 0) (p ^ r)) 0 \<and> M$(idx r)$(idx 2) = monom (monom (monom 1 (p ^ r)) 0) 0"
  shows "\<exists> L :: (int \<times> int \<times> int) list. cong p (det M, foldr (\<lambda> t q. (lincomb t) * q) L 1)"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_2002_b6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b6:
  modulo a prime, the determinant of the three-variable Frobenius-power
  matrix is coefficientwise congruent to a finite product of integer linear
  forms. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let pmul =
     \f g:(num#num#num)->int.
      \(i,j,k):num#num#num.
       isum (0..i)
         (\a:num.
            isum (0..j)
              (\b:num.
                 isum (0..k)
                   (\c:num.
                      f (a,b,c) * g (i - a,j - b,k - c)))) in
   let padd =
     \f g:(num#num#num)->int.
      \m:num#num#num. f m + g m in
   let psub =
     \f g:(num#num#num)->int.
      \m:num#num#num. f m - g m in
   let pone =
     \m:num#num#num. if m = (0,0,0) then &1 else &0 in
   let monomial =
     \e:num#num#num.
      \m:num#num#num. if m = e then &1 else &0 in
   let linear =
     \(a,b,c):int#int#int.
      \m:num#num#num.
       if m = (1,0,0) then a
       else if m = (0,1,0) then b
       else if m = (0,0,1) then c
       else &0 in
   let detpoly =
     \p:num.
       psub
         (padd
           (padd
             (pmul (monomial (1,0,0))
               (pmul (monomial (0,p,0))
                     (monomial (0,0,p EXP 2))))
             (pmul (monomial (0,1,0))
               (pmul (monomial (0,0,p))
                     (monomial (p EXP 2,0,0)))))
           (pmul (monomial (0,0,1))
             (pmul (monomial (p,0,0))
                   (monomial (0,p EXP 2,0)))))
         (padd
           (padd
             (pmul (monomial (0,0,1))
               (pmul (monomial (0,p,0))
                     (monomial (p EXP 2,0,0))))
             (pmul (monomial (0,1,0))
               (pmul (monomial (p,0,0))
                     (monomial (0,0,p EXP 2)))))
           (pmul (monomial (1,0,0))
             (pmul (monomial (0,0,p))
                   (monomial (0,p EXP 2,0))))) in
   !p:num.
     prime p
     ==>
     ?L:(int#int#int)list.
       !m:num#num#num.
         (detpoly p m ==
          ITLIST (\abc acc. pmul (linear abc) acc) L pone m)
         (mod (&p:int))`;;

title: putnam_2002_b6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b6:
;; for every prime p, the determinant of the matrix with rows (x,y,z),
;; (x^p,y^p,z^p), and (x^(p^2),y^(p^2),z^(p^2)) is coefficientwise
;; congruent modulo p to a finite product of integer linear forms. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

(defun putnam-2002-b6-no-divisor-through-p (p divisor)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix divisor)))
  (if (and (natp p) (natp divisor))
      (if (< divisor 2)
          t
        (and
         (not (equal (mod p divisor) 0))
         (putnam-2002-b6-no-divisor-through-p
          p (- divisor 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2002-b6-prime-p (p)
  (and
   (natp p)
   (<= 2 p)
   (putnam-2002-b6-no-divisor-through-p p (- p 1))))

;; A triple (a b c) denotes the integer polynomial ax+by+cz. A true list of
;; such triples denotes its finite product. Neither the list length nor any
;; coefficient is bounded.
(defun putnam-2002-b6-integer-triple-p (triple)
  (and
   (true-listp triple)
   (equal (len triple) 3)
   (integerp (nth 0 triple))
   (integerp (nth 1 triple))
   (integerp (nth 2 triple))))

(defun putnam-2002-b6-linear-form-list-p (linear-forms)
  (cond
   ((equal linear-forms nil) t)
   ((consp linear-forms)
    (and
     (putnam-2002-b6-integer-triple-p (car linear-forms))
     (putnam-2002-b6-linear-form-list-p (cdr linear-forms))))
   (t nil)))

;; This is the coefficient of x^i y^j z^k in the product represented by
;; LINEAR-FORMS. The empty product has constant coefficient one.
(defun putnam-2002-b6-product-coefficient
    (linear-forms i j k)
  (if (endp linear-forms)
      (if (and (equal i 0)
               (equal j 0)
               (equal k 0))
          1
        0)
    (let ((linear-form (car linear-forms))
          (remaining (cdr linear-forms)))
      (+
       (if (and (natp i) (< 0 i))
           (* (nth 0 linear-form)
              (putnam-2002-b6-product-coefficient
               remaining (- i 1) j k))
         0)
       (if (and (natp j) (< 0 j))
           (* (nth 1 linear-form)
              (putnam-2002-b6-product-coefficient
               remaining i (- j 1) k))
         0)
       (if (and (natp k) (< 0 k))
           (* (nth 2 linear-form)
              (putnam-2002-b6-product-coefficient
               remaining i j (- k 1)))
         0)))))

(defun putnam-2002-b6-monomial-indicator
    (i j k x-exponent y-exponent z-exponent)
  (if (and (equal i x-exponent)
           (equal j y-exponent)
           (equal k z-exponent))
      1
    0))

;; The six signed Leibniz terms give the coefficient of the source
;; determinant, including any coincident terms by integer addition.
(defun putnam-2002-b6-determinant-coefficient (p i j k)
  (let ((p2 (expt p 2)))
    (+
     (putnam-2002-b6-monomial-indicator i j k 1 p p2)
     (- (putnam-2002-b6-monomial-indicator i j k 1 p2 p))
     (- (putnam-2002-b6-monomial-indicator i j k p 1 p2))
     (putnam-2002-b6-monomial-indicator i j k p2 1 p)
     (putnam-2002-b6-monomial-indicator i j k p p2 1)
     (- (putnam-2002-b6-monomial-indicator i j k p2 p 1)))))

;; Universal quantification over all natural exponent triples is exactly
;; coefficientwise congruence of the two integer polynomials modulo p.
(defun-sk putnam-2002-b6-coefficientwise-congruent-p
    (p linear-forms)
  (forall (i j k)
    (implies
     (and (natp i) (natp j) (natp k))
     (equal
      (mod (putnam-2002-b6-determinant-coefficient p i j k) p)
      (mod (putnam-2002-b6-product-coefficient
            linear-forms i j k)
           p)))))

;; The source witness remains an internal, unbounded existential over all
;; finite lists of integer linear forms.
(defun-sk putnam-2002-b6-factorization-exists-p (p)
  (exists (linear-forms)
    (and
     (putnam-2002-b6-linear-form-list-p linear-forms)
     (putnam-2002-b6-coefficientwise-congruent-p
      p linear-forms))))

(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-2002-b6-statement ()
  (forall (p)
    (implies
     (putnam-2002-b6-prime-p p)
     (putnam-2002-b6-factorization-exists-p p))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2002_b6): the determinant of the three-variable
-- Frobenius-power matrix modulo a prime is a finite product of integer linear
-- forms. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2002B6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; true; false)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _≤_ _∣_

data _≤_ : Nat → Nat → Set where
  zero≤   : {n : Nat} → zero ≤ n
  suc≤suc : {m n : Nat} → m ≤ n → suc m ≤ suc n

record _∣_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat

data _∨_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A → A ∨ B
  right : B → A ∨ B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A → Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

one : Nat
one = suc zero

two : Nat
two = suc one

record Prime (p : Nat) : Set where
  field
    at-least-two : two ≤ p
    only-trivial-divisors :
      (d : Nat) →
      d ∣ p →
      (d ≡ one) ∨ (d ≡ p)

negative : Nat → Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

difference : Nat → Nat → Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int → Int → Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

negateInt : Int → Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

multiplyInt : Int → Int → Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

sameNat : Nat → Nat → Bool
sameNat zero zero =
  true
sameNat zero (suc n) =
  false
sameNat (suc m) zero =
  false
sameNat (suc m) (suc n) =
  sameNat m n

andBool : Bool → Bool → Bool
andBool true b =
  b
andBool false b =
  false

ifInt : Bool → Int → Int → Int
ifInt true when-true when-false =
  when-true
ifInt false when-true when-false =
  when-false

record Monomial : Set where
  constructor monomial
  field
    coefficient : Int
    x-exponent  : Nat
    y-exponent  : Nat
    z-exponent  : Nat

open Monomial

Polynomial : Set
Polynomial =
  List Monomial

coefficientAt : Polynomial → Nat → Nat → Nat → Int
coefficientAt [] i j k =
  pos zero
coefficientAt (term ∷ terms) i j k =
  addInt
    (ifInt
      (andBool
        (sameNat (x-exponent term) i)
        (andBool
          (sameNat (y-exponent term) j)
          (sameNat (z-exponent term) k)))
      (coefficient term)
      (pos zero))
    (coefficientAt terms i j k)

appendPolynomial : Polynomial → Polynomial → Polynomial
appendPolynomial [] q =
  q
appendPolynomial (term ∷ terms) q =
  term ∷ appendPolynomial terms q

negatePolynomial : Polynomial → Polynomial
negatePolynomial [] =
  []
negatePolynomial (term ∷ terms) =
  monomial
    (negateInt (coefficient term))
    (x-exponent term)
    (y-exponent term)
    (z-exponent term)
  ∷ negatePolynomial terms

subtractPolynomial : Polynomial → Polynomial → Polynomial
subtractPolynomial p q =
  appendPolynomial p (negatePolynomial q)

multiplyMonomial : Monomial → Monomial → Monomial
multiplyMonomial p q =
  monomial
    (multiplyInt (coefficient p) (coefficient q))
    (x-exponent p + x-exponent q)
    (y-exponent p + y-exponent q)
    (z-exponent p + z-exponent q)

multiplyByMonomial : Monomial → Polynomial → Polynomial
multiplyByMonomial term [] =
  []
multiplyByMonomial term (factor ∷ factors) =
  multiplyMonomial term factor ∷
  multiplyByMonomial term factors

multiplyPolynomial : Polynomial → Polynomial → Polynomial
multiplyPolynomial [] q =
  []
multiplyPolynomial (term ∷ terms) q =
  appendPolynomial
    (multiplyByMonomial term q)
    (multiplyPolynomial terms q)

constantPolynomial : Int → Polynomial
constantPolynomial c =
  monomial c zero zero zero ∷ []

onePolynomial : Polynomial
onePolynomial =
  constantPolynomial (pos one)

scalePolynomial : Int → Polynomial → Polynomial
scalePolynomial c [] =
  []
scalePolynomial c (term ∷ terms) =
  monomial
    (multiplyInt c (coefficient term))
    (x-exponent term)
    (y-exponent term)
    (z-exponent term)
  ∷ scalePolynomial c terms

powerPolynomial : Polynomial → Nat → Polynomial
powerPolynomial p zero =
  onePolynomial
powerPolynomial p (suc n) =
  multiplyPolynomial p (powerPolynomial p n)

data Index3 : Set where
  first  : Index3
  second : Index3
  third  : Index3

variablePolynomial : Index3 → Polynomial
variablePolynomial first =
  monomial (pos one) one zero zero ∷ []
variablePolynomial second =
  monomial (pos one) zero one zero ∷ []
variablePolynomial third =
  monomial (pos one) zero zero one ∷ []

Matrix3 : Set
Matrix3 =
  Index3 → Index3 → Polynomial

putnamMatrix : Nat → Matrix3
putnamMatrix p first column =
  variablePolynomial column
putnamMatrix p second column =
  powerPolynomial (variablePolynomial column) p
putnamMatrix p third column =
  powerPolynomial (variablePolynomial column) (p * p)

determinant3 : Matrix3 → Polynomial
determinant3 M =
  appendPolynomial
    (subtractPolynomial
      (multiplyPolynomial
        (M first first)
        (multiplyPolynomial (M second second) (M third third)))
      (multiplyPolynomial
        (M first first)
        (multiplyPolynomial (M second third) (M third second))))
    (appendPolynomial
      (subtractPolynomial
        (multiplyPolynomial
          (M first second)
          (multiplyPolynomial (M second third) (M third first)))
        (multiplyPolynomial
          (M first second)
          (multiplyPolynomial (M second first) (M third third))))
      (subtractPolynomial
        (multiplyPolynomial
          (M first third)
          (multiplyPolynomial (M second first) (M third second)))
        (multiplyPolynomial
          (M first third)
          (multiplyPolynomial (M second second) (M third first)))))

record IntModEq (modulus : Nat) (left-value right-value : Int) : Set where
  field
    multiple : Int
    equation :
      left-value ≡
      addInt right-value (multiplyInt (pos modulus) multiple)

PolynomialCongruent : Nat → Polynomial → Polynomial → Set
PolynomialCongruent modulus f g =
  (i j k : Nat) →
  IntModEq modulus
    (coefficientAt f i j k)
    (coefficientAt g i j k)

record LinearCoefficients : Set where
  constructor coefficients
  field
    a : Int
    b : Int
    c : Int

open LinearCoefficients

linearForm : LinearCoefficients → Polynomial
linearForm values =
  appendPolynomial
    (scalePolynomial (a values) (variablePolynomial first))
    (appendPolynomial
      (scalePolynomial (b values) (variablePolynomial second))
      (scalePolynomial (c values) (variablePolynomial third)))

productOfLinearForms : List LinearCoefficients → Polynomial
productOfLinearForms [] =
  onePolynomial
productOfLinearForms (values ∷ rest) =
  multiplyPolynomial
    (linearForm values)
    (productOfLinearForms rest)

putnam-2002-b6 : Set
putnam-2002-b6 =
  (p : Nat) →
  Prime p →
  Exists (List LinearCoefficients)
    (λ factors →
      PolynomialCongruent p
        (determinant3 (putnamMatrix p))
        (productOfLinearForms factors))

title: putnam_2002_b6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b6:
  for a prime p, the determinant of the 3 by 3 matrix whose rows contain
  x, y, z and their p-th and p-squared powers is coefficientwise congruent
  modulo p to a finite product of integer linear forms ax + by + cz. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2002_b6 =
  ``let poly_one =
        (\i j k : num.
           if i = 0 /\ j = 0 /\ k = 0 then (1 : int) else 0);
      poly_add =
        (\f g : num -> num -> num -> int.
           \i j k : num. f i j k + g i j k);
      poly_neg =
        (\f : num -> num -> num -> int.
           \i j k : num. ~(f i j k));
      poly_mul =
        (\f g : num -> num -> num -> int.
           \i j k : num.
             ITSET
               (\a acc_i.
                  ITSET
                    (\b acc_j.
                       ITSET
                         (\c acc_k.
                            f a b c * g (i - a) (j - b) (k - c) + acc_k)
                         (count (SUC k))
                         (0 : int) +
                       acc_j)
                    (count (SUC j))
                    (0 : int) +
                  acc_i)
               (count (SUC i))
               (0 : int));
      x_power =
        (\e i j k : num.
           if i = e /\ j = 0 /\ k = 0 then (1 : int) else 0);
      y_power =
        (\e i j k : num.
           if i = 0 /\ j = e /\ k = 0 then (1 : int) else 0);
      z_power =
        (\e i j k : num.
           if i = 0 /\ j = 0 /\ k = e then (1 : int) else 0);
      matrix_entry =
        (\p r c : num.
           if c = 0 then x_power (p ** r)
           else if c = 1 then y_power (p ** r)
           else z_power (p ** r));
      determinant_term =
        (\p c0 c1 c2 : num.
           poly_mul
             (matrix_entry p 0 c0)
             (poly_mul (matrix_entry p 1 c1) (matrix_entry p 2 c2)));
      determinant =
        (\p : num.
           poly_add
             (poly_add
                (poly_add
                   (determinant_term p 0 1 2)
                   (determinant_term p 1 2 0))
                (determinant_term p 2 0 1))
             (poly_add
                (poly_neg (determinant_term p 2 1 0))
                (poly_add
                   (poly_neg (determinant_term p 1 0 2))
                   (poly_neg (determinant_term p 0 2 1)))));
      linear_form =
        (\abc : int # (int # int).
           \i j k : num.
             if i = 1 /\ j = 0 /\ k = 0 then FST abc
             else if i = 0 /\ j = 1 /\ k = 0 then FST (SND abc)
             else if i = 0 /\ j = 0 /\ k = 1 then SND (SND abc)
             else 0);
      product_of_linear_forms =
        (\L : (int # (int # int)) list.
           FOLDR
             (\abc acc. poly_mul (linear_form abc) acc)
             poly_one
             L);
      poly_cong =
        (\p : num. \f g : num -> num -> num -> int.
           !i j k : num.
             int_of_num p int_divides (f i j k - g i j k))
    in
      !p : num.
        prime p
        ==>
        ?L : (int # (int # int)) list.
          poly_cong p (determinant p) (product_of_linear_forms L)``;

title: putnam_2002_b6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2002_b6: modulo a prime, the determinant of the three-by-three
  matrix whose rows are the p-power iterates of three variables is a finite
  product of integer linear forms in those variables. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P02B6Poly is SetMM's ring of finite-support polynomials over ZZ in the
  three variables indexed by the integer interval 0 ... 2, and P02B6Vars is
  its canonical variable
  map. P02B6Matrix p has entry X_c^(p^r), with ring exponentiation in
  P02B6Poly, so P02B6Det p is exactly the source determinant.

  P02B6Lin a b c is the polynomial ax + by + cz, with integer constants
  embedded into the polynomial ring. P02B6Prod S is the finite
  multiplicative product of the polynomial set S. P02B6Cong compares the
  coefficient functions at every exponent vector in NN0 ^m (0 ... 2), using
  equality of integer remainders modulo p. Thus it is exactly
  coefficientwise polynomial congruence modulo p.

  The finite-set witness and all integer coefficients remain existentially
  quantified inside the quantifier over the prime. The final declaration is
  the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

$c P02B6Poly P02B6Vars P02B6Matrix P02B6Det P02B6Lin P02B6Prod
   P02B6Cong $.

p02b6-poly-syntax $a class P02B6Poly $.
p02b6-vars-syntax $a class P02B6Vars $.
p02b6-matrix-syntax $a class ( P02B6Matrix p ) $.
p02b6-det-syntax $a class ( P02B6Det p ) $.
p02b6-lin-syntax $a class ( P02B6Lin a b c ) $.
p02b6-prod-syntax $a class ( P02B6Prod S ) $.
p02b6-cong-syntax $a wff ( P02B6Cong p F G ) $.

p02b6-poly-definition $a |- P02B6Poly =
  ( ( 0 ... 2 ) mPoly ZZring ) $.

p02b6-vars-definition $a |- P02B6Vars =
  ( ( 0 ... 2 ) mVar ZZring ) $.

${
  $d c p r $.

  p02b6-matrix-definition $a |- ( P02B6Matrix p ) =
    (
      r e. ( 0 ... 2 ) , c e. ( 0 ... 2 ) |->
        (
          ( p ^ r )
          ( .g ` ( mulGrp ` P02B6Poly ) )
          ( P02B6Vars ` c )
        )
    ) $.
$}

p02b6-det-definition $a |- ( P02B6Det p ) =
  ( ( ( 0 ... 2 ) maDet P02B6Poly ) ` ( P02B6Matrix p ) ) $.

${
  $d a b c $.

  p02b6-lin-definition $a |- ( P02B6Lin a b c ) =
    (
      (
        (
          ( ( algSc ` P02B6Poly ) ` a )
          ( .r ` P02B6Poly )
          ( P02B6Vars ` 0 )
        )
        ( +g ` P02B6Poly )
        (
          ( ( algSc ` P02B6Poly ) ` b )
          ( .r ` P02B6Poly )
          ( P02B6Vars ` 1 )
        )
      )
      ( +g ` P02B6Poly )
      (
        ( ( algSc ` P02B6Poly ) ` c )
        ( .r ` P02B6Poly )
        ( P02B6Vars ` 2 )
      )
    ) $.
$}

${
  $d S s $.

  p02b6-prod-definition $a |- ( P02B6Prod S ) =
    (
      ( mulGrp ` P02B6Poly )
      gsum
      ( s e. S |-> s )
    ) $.
$}

${
  $d F G n p $.

  p02b6-cong-definition $a |- (
    ( P02B6Cong p F G )
    <->
    A. n e. ( NN0 ^m ( 0 ... 2 ) )
      ( ( F ` n ) mod p ) = ( ( G ` n ) mod p )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d a b c p u v $.

  putnambench-putnam-2002-b6 $a |-
    A. p e. Prime
      E. u e. Fin
        (
          u C_ ( Base ` P02B6Poly )
          /\
          (
            A. v e. u
              E. a e. ZZ E. b e. ZZ E. c e. ZZ
                v = ( P02B6Lin a b c )
            /\
            ( P02B6Cong p ( P02B6Det p ) ( P02B6Prod u ) )
          )
        )
  $.
$}

    cx = <%vx%> &
    vy = <%0.(Polynom-Ring INT.Ring),1.(Polynom-Ring INT.Ring)%> &

    Y = <%vy%> &

    M*(2,1) = X |^ p & M*(2,2) = Y |^ p & M*(2,3) = Z |^ p &
    M*(3,1) = X |^ (p * p) &
    M*(3,2) = Y |^ (p * p) &
    M*(3,3) = Z |^ (p * p)
  holds

        the carrier of
          Polynom-Ring (Polynom-Ring (Polynom-Ring INT.Ring)) st
      (for n being Nat st n in dom factors holds
        ex a,b,c being Element of INT.Ring,
           a0,b0,c0 being Element of Polynom-Ring INT.Ring,
           a1,b1,c1 being
             Element of Polynom-Ring (Polynom-Ring INT.Ring),
           A,B,C being
             Element of
               Polynom-Ring (Polynom-Ring (Polynom-Ring INT.Ring)) st
          a0 = <%a%> & b0 = <%b%> & c0 = <%c%> &
          a1 = <%a0%> & b1 = <%b0%> & c1 = <%c0%> &
          A = <%a1%> & B = <%b1%> & C = <%c1%> &
          factors/.n = A * X + B * Y + C * Z) &
      ex D,E being
          Polynomial of Polynom-Ring (Polynom-Ring INT.Ring) st
        D = Det M & E = Product factors &
        for i,j,k being Nat holds
          ex Di,Ei being Polynomial of Polynom-Ring INT.Ring st
            Di = D.i & Ei = E.i &
            ex Dij,Eij being Polynomial of INT.Ring st
              Dij = Di.j & Eij = Ei.j &
              ex d,e being Integer st
                d = Dij.k & e = Eij.k &
                (p qua Integer) divides (d - e)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2002_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2002_b6:
% for every prime p, the determinant of the 3 by 3 matrix with rows
% (x, y, z), (x^p, y^p, z^p), and (x^(p^2), y^(p^2), z^(p^2)) is
% coefficientwise congruent modulo p to a finite product of integer linear
% forms a*x + b*y + c*z. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2002_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  exponent: TYPE =
    [# x_degree: nat, y_degree: nat, z_degree: nat #]

  polynomial: TYPE = [exponent -> int]
  matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> polynomial]

  linear_coefficients: TYPE =
    [# x_coefficient: int,
       y_coefficient: int,
       z_coefficient: int #]

  zero_polynomial: polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (powers: exponent): 0)

  one_polynomial: polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (powers: exponent):
      IF x_degree(powers) = 0
          AND y_degree(powers) = 0
          AND z_degree(powers) = 0
      THEN 1
      ELSE 0
      ENDIF)

  polynomial_add(left, right: polynomial): polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (powers: exponent):
      left(powers) + right(powers))

  polynomial_negate(value: polynomial): polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (powers: exponent): -value(powers))

  natural_difference(left, right: nat): nat =
    IF right <= left THEN left - right ELSE 0 ENDIF

  convolution_z(
      left, right: polynomial,
      powers: exponent,
      left_x, left_y, count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET left_z: nat = count - 1 IN
        convolution_z(
          left, right, powers, left_x, left_y, count - 1)
          + left(
              (# x_degree := left_x,
                 y_degree := left_y,
                 z_degree := left_z #))
            * right(
                (# x_degree :=
                     natural_difference(x_degree(powers), left_x),
                   y_degree :=
                     natural_difference(y_degree(powers), left_y),
                   z_degree :=
                     natural_difference(z_degree(powers), left_z) #))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  convolution_y(
      left, right: polynomial,
      powers: exponent,
      left_x, count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET left_y: nat = count - 1 IN
        convolution_y(
          left, right, powers, left_x, count - 1)
          + convolution_z(
              left,
              right,
              powers,
              left_x,
              left_y,
              z_degree(powers) + 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  convolution_x(
      left, right: polynomial,
      powers: exponent,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET left_x: nat = count - 1 IN
        convolution_x(left, right, powers, count - 1)
          + convolution_y(
              left,
              right,
              powers,
              left_x,
              y_degree(powers) + 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  polynomial_multiply(left, right: polynomial): polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (powers: exponent):
      convolution_x(
        left, right, powers, x_degree(powers) + 1))

  variable_power(variable, degree: nat): polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (powers: exponent):
      IF variable = 0
          AND x_degree(powers) = degree
          AND y_degree(powers) = 0
          AND z_degree(powers) = 0
      THEN
        1
      ELSIF variable = 1
          AND x_degree(powers) = 0
          AND y_degree(powers) = degree
          AND z_degree(powers) = 0
      THEN
        1
      ELSIF variable = 2
          AND x_degree(powers) = 0
          AND y_degree(powers) = 0
          AND z_degree(powers) = degree
      THEN
        1
      ELSE
        0
      ENDIF)

  putnam_matrix(p: nat): matrix =
    (LAMBDA (row, column: nat):
      IF row < 3 AND column < 3 THEN
        variable_power(column, p ^ row)
      ELSE
        zero_polynomial
      ENDIF)

  determinant_3(value: matrix): polynomial =
    polynomial_add(
      polynomial_add(
        polynomial_multiply(
          value(0, 0),
          polynomial_multiply(value(1, 1), value(2, 2))),
        polynomial_multiply(
          value(0, 1),
          polynomial_multiply(value(1, 2), value(2, 0)))),
      polynomial_add(
        polynomial_multiply(
          value(0, 2),
          polynomial_multiply(value(1, 0), value(2, 1))),
        polynomial_negate(
          polynomial_add(
            polynomial_add(
              polynomial_multiply(
                value(0, 2),
                polynomial_multiply(value(1, 1), value(2, 0))),
              polynomial_multiply(
                value(0, 1),
                polynomial_multiply(value(1, 0), value(2, 2)))),
            polynomial_multiply(
              value(0, 0),
              polynomial_multiply(value(1, 2), value(2, 1)))))))

  linear_form(coefficients: linear_coefficients): polynomial =
    (LAMBDA (powers: exponent):
      IF x_degree(powers) = 1
          AND y_degree(powers) = 0
          AND z_degree(powers) = 0
      THEN
        x_coefficient(coefficients)
      ELSIF x_degree(powers) = 0
          AND y_degree(powers) = 1
          AND z_degree(powers) = 0
      THEN
        y_coefficient(coefficients)
      ELSIF x_degree(powers) = 0
          AND y_degree(powers) = 0
          AND z_degree(powers) = 1
      THEN
        z_coefficient(coefficients)
      ELSE
        0
      ENDIF)

  product_of_linear_forms(
      factors: list[linear_coefficients]): RECURSIVE polynomial =
    CASES factors OF
      null: one_polynomial,
      cons(factor, tail):
        polynomial_multiply(
          linear_form(factor),
          product_of_linear_forms(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE factors BY <<

  int_divides(divisor, value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: int): value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(p: nat): bool =
    p >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        int_divides(divisor :: int, p :: int)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = p

  coefficient_congruent(
      left, right: int,
      modulus: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (offset: int):
      left - right = (modulus :: int) * offset

  polynomial_congruent(
      left, right: polynomial,
      modulus: nat): bool =
    FORALL (powers: exponent):
      coefficient_congruent(
        left(powers), right(powers), modulus)

  putnam_2002_b6_statement: bool =
    FORALL (p: nat):
      prime_nat(p) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (factors: list[linear_coefficients]):
          polynomial_congruent(
            determinant_3(putnam_matrix(p)),
            product_of_linear_forms(factors),
            p)
END putnam_2002_b6

import Mathlib

open MvPolynomial

-- Note: uses (ℕ → ℤ) instead of (Fin k → ℤ)
abbrev putnam_2003_a1_solution : ℕ → ℕ := sorry
-- fun n => n
/--
Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer. How many ways are there to write $n$ as a sum of positive integers, \[ n = a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_k, \] with $k$ an arbitrary positive integer and $a_1 \leq a_2 \leq \dots \leq a_k \leq a_1 + 1$? For example, with $n = 4$, there are four ways: $4, 2 + 2, 1 + 1 + 2, 1 + 1 + 1 + 1$
-/
theorem putnam_2003_a1
(n : ℕ) (hn : n > 0)
: Set.encard {a : ℕ → ℤ |
  ∃ k > 0, (∑ i : Fin k, a i = n) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin k, a i > 0) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin (k - 1), a i ≤ a (i + 1)) ∧
    a (k - 1) ≤ a 0 + 1 ∧ (∀ i ≥ k, a i = 0)}
  = putnam_2003_a1_solution n :=
sorry

Require Import Nat List Ensembles Finite_sets Coquelicot.Coquelicot.
Definition putnam_2003_a1_solution : nat -> nat := (fun n : nat => n).
Theorem putnam_2003_a1
    (n: nat)
    (hn : n > 0)
    (E: Ensemble (list nat) := fun l => fold_left add l 0 = n /\ (forall i : nat, i < length l -> nth i l 0 > 0) /\ (forall (i j: nat), i < length l /\ j < length l /\ i < j -> nth i l 0 <= nth j l 0) /\ last l 0 <= hd 0 l + 1)
    : cardinal (list nat) E (putnam_2003_a1_solution n).
Proof. Admitted.

theorem putnam_2003_a1:
