import Mathlib

open MvPolynomial Set

/--
A Dyck $n$-path is a lattice path of $n$ upsteps $(1,1)$ and $n$ downsteps $(1,-1)$ that starts at the origin $O$ and never dips below the $x$-axis. A return is a maximal sequence of contiguous downsteps that terminates on the $x$-axis. Show that there is a one-to-one correspondence between the Dyck $n$-paths with no return of even length and the Dyck $(n-1)$-paths.
-/
theorem putnam_2003_a5
(n : ℕ) (npos : n > 0)
(dyckpath : (m : ℕ) → Set ((Fin (2 * m)) → ℤ))
(hdyckpath : dyckpath = fun m ↦ {p |
      range p ⊆ {-1, 1} ∧ ∑ k, p k = 0 ∧ ∀ j, ∑ k, ite (k ≤ j) (p k) 0 ≥ 0})
(noevenreturn : (m : ℕ) → Set ((Fin (2 * m)) → ℤ))
(hnoevenreturn : noevenreturn = fun m ↦ {p |
      ¬∃ i j, i < j ∧ p i = 1 ∧ (∀ k ∈ Ioc i j, p k = -1) ∧
            Even (j.1 - i.1) ∧ ∑ k, ite (k ≤ j) (p k) 0 = 0})
      : ∃ f : ((Fin (2 * n)) → ℤ) → (Fin (2 * (n - 1)) → ℤ),
            ∀ y ∈ dyckpath (n - 1), ∃! x, x ∈ dyckpath n ∩ noevenreturn n ∧ f x = y :=
sorry

title: putnam_2003_a5
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_a5:
   a one-to-one correspondence between Dyck n-paths with no even-length return
   and Dyck (n-1)-paths; this file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith Arith.PeanoNat Vectors.Fin.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition putnam_2003_a5_path (m : nat) : Type :=
  Fin.t (2 * m) -> Z.

Fixpoint putnam_2003_a5_fin_sum
    (m : nat) : (Fin.t m -> Z) -> Z :=
  match m as k return (Fin.t k -> Z) -> Z with
  | O => fun _ => 0
  | S k =>
      fun p =>
        p Fin.F1 +
        putnam_2003_a5_fin_sum k (fun i => p (Fin.FS i))
  end.

Definition putnam_2003_a5_index
    {m : nat} (i : Fin.t m) : nat :=
  proj1_sig (Fin.to_nat i).

Definition putnam_2003_a5_prefix_sum
    {m : nat} (p : Fin.t m -> Z) (j : Fin.t m) : Z :=
  putnam_2003_a5_fin_sum m
    (fun k =>
      if Nat.leb (putnam_2003_a5_index k) (putnam_2003_a5_index j)
      then p k
      else 0).

Definition putnam_2003_a5_dyckpath
    (m : nat) (p : putnam_2003_a5_path m) : Prop :=
  (forall k : Fin.t (2 * m), p k = 1 \/ p k = -1) /\
  putnam_2003_a5_fin_sum (2 * m) p = 0 /\
  forall j : Fin.t (2 * m),
    0 <= putnam_2003_a5_prefix_sum p j.

Definition putnam_2003_a5_no_even_return
    (m : nat) (p : putnam_2003_a5_path m) : Prop :=
  ~ exists i j : Fin.t (2 * m),
      (putnam_2003_a5_index i < putnam_2003_a5_index j)%nat /\
      p i = 1 /\
      (forall k : Fin.t (2 * m),
        (putnam_2003_a5_index i < putnam_2003_a5_index k)%nat ->
        (putnam_2003_a5_index k <= putnam_2003_a5_index j)%nat ->
        p k = -1) /\
      Nat.Even
        (putnam_2003_a5_index j - putnam_2003_a5_index i) /\
      putnam_2003_a5_prefix_sum p j = 0.

Definition putnam_2003_a5_eligible
    (m : nat) (p : putnam_2003_a5_path m) : Prop :=
  putnam_2003_a5_dyckpath m p /\
  putnam_2003_a5_no_even_return m p.

Theorem putnam_2003_a5
    (n : nat)
    (npos : (0 < n)%nat) :
  exists f :
      putnam_2003_a5_path n ->
      putnam_2003_a5_path (n - 1),
    forall y : putnam_2003_a5_path (n - 1),
      putnam_2003_a5_dyckpath (n - 1) y ->
      exists! x : putnam_2003_a5_path n,
        putnam_2003_a5_eligible n x /\ f x = y.
Admitted.

theory putnam_2003_a5 imports Complex_Main
begin

(* uses (nat \<Rightarrow> int) instead of (Fin (2*m) \<Rightarrow> int) *)
theorem putnam_2003_a5:
  fixes n :: nat
  and dyckpath :: "nat \<Rightarrow> ((nat \<Rightarrow> int) set)"
  and noevenreturn :: "nat \<Rightarrow> ((nat \<Rightarrow> int) set)"
  assumes npos: "n > 0"
  defines "dyckpath \<equiv> (\<lambda>m::nat. {p::nat\<Rightarrow>int. (\<forall>k::nat\<ge>2*m. p k = 0) \<and>
  p ` {0..<(2*m)} \<subseteq> {-1, 1} \<and> (\<Sum>k::nat\<in>{0..<(2*m)}. p k) = 0 \<and>
  (\<forall>j::nat\<in>{0..<(2*m)}. (\<Sum>k::nat\<in>{0..j}. p k) \<ge> 0)})"
  and "noevenreturn \<equiv> (\<lambda>m::nat. {p::nat\<Rightarrow>int. (\<forall>k::nat\<ge>2*m. p k = 0) \<and>
  \<not>(\<exists>i::nat\<in>{0..<(2*m)}. \<exists>j::nat\<in>{0..<(2*m)}. i < j \<and> p i = 1 \<and>
    (\<forall>k::nat\<in>{(i+1)..j}. p k = -1) \<and> even (j - i) \<and>
    (\<Sum>k::nat\<in>{0..j}. p k) = 0)})"
  shows "\<exists>f::(nat\<Rightarrow>int)\<Rightarrow>(nat\<Rightarrow>int).
    bij_betw f (dyckpath n \<inter> noevenreturn n) (dyckpath (n-1))"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_a5:
  a bijection between Dyck n-paths with no even-length return and Dyck
  (n-1)-paths. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let dyckpath =
     \m:num. \p:int list.
       LENGTH p = 2 * m /\
       (!k:num.
          k < LENGTH p
          ==> EL k p = &1 \/ EL k p = -- &1) /\
       isum {k:num | k < LENGTH p} (\k. EL k p) = &0 /\
       (!j:num.
          j < LENGTH p
          ==> &0 <= isum {k:num | k <= j} (\k. EL k p)) in
   let noevenreturn =
     \m:num. \p:int list.
       LENGTH p = 2 * m /\
       ~(?i j:num.
           i < j /\
           j < LENGTH p /\
           EL i p = &1 /\
           (!k:num.
              i < k /\ k <= j
              ==> EL k p = -- &1) /\
           EVEN (j - i) /\
           isum {k:num | k <= j} (\k. EL k p) = &0) in
   !n:num.
     0 < n
     ==> ?f:int list->int list.
           (!x:int list.
              LENGTH x = 2 * n
              ==> LENGTH (f x) = 2 * (n - 1)) /\
           (!y:int list.
              dyckpath (n - 1) y
              ==> ?!x:int list.
                    dyckpath n x /\
                    noevenreturn n x /\
                    f x = y)`;;

title: putnam_2003_a5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_a5:
;; the published bijection between Dyck n-paths with no even-length return and
;; Dyck (n-1)-paths, expressed by equality of their finite cardinalities.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A path of length L whose values lie in {-1,1} is represented bijectively by
;; an L-bit natural number. Thus the searches below enumerate exactly the
;; finite-function objects that can satisfy the source Dyck-path definitions.

(defun putnam-2003-a5-step (code index)
  (if (equal
       (mod (floor code (expt 2 index)) 2)
       1)
      1
    -1))

(defun putnam-2003-a5-prefix-sum (code count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2003-a5-prefix-sum code (- count 1))
       (putnam-2003-a5-step code (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2003-a5-dyck-prefixes-p
    (code remaining index height)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      (equal height 0)
    (let ((next-height
           (+ height
              (putnam-2003-a5-step code index))))
      (and
       (<= 0 next-height)
       (putnam-2003-a5-dyck-prefixes-p
        code
        (- remaining 1)
        (+ index 1)
        next-height)))))

(defun putnam-2003-a5-dyck-path-p (code length)
  (and
   (natp code)
   (natp length)
   (< code (expt 2 length))
   (putnam-2003-a5-dyck-prefixes-p
    code length 0 0)))

(defun putnam-2003-a5-all-downsteps-p
    (code index count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      t
    (and
     (equal (putnam-2003-a5-step code index) -1)
     (putnam-2003-a5-all-downsteps-p
      code
      (+ index 1)
      (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2003-a5-even-return-at-index-p
    (code index down-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix down-count)))
  (if (zp down-count)
      nil
    (or
     (and
      (equal (putnam-2003-a5-step code index) 1)
      (putnam-2003-a5-all-downsteps-p
       code
       (+ index 1)
       down-count)
      (equal (mod down-count 2) 0)
      (equal
       (putnam-2003-a5-prefix-sum
        code
        (+ index down-count 1))
       0))
     (putnam-2003-a5-even-return-at-index-p
      code index (- down-count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2003-a5-has-even-return-p
    (code index-count length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index-count)))
  (if (zp index-count)
      nil
    (let* ((index (- index-count 1))
           (available-downsteps (- (- length index) 1)))
      (or
       (putnam-2003-a5-even-return-at-index-p
        code index available-downsteps)
       (putnam-2003-a5-has-even-return-p
        code (- index-count 1) length)))))

(defun putnam-2003-a5-no-even-return-p
    (code length)
  (not
   (putnam-2003-a5-has-even-return-p
    code length length)))

(defun putnam-2003-a5-count-dyck-paths
    (candidate-count length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate-count)))
  (if (zp candidate-count)
      0
    (let ((code (- candidate-count 1)))
      (+
       (if (putnam-2003-a5-dyck-path-p code length)
           1
         0)
       (putnam-2003-a5-count-dyck-paths
        code length)))))

(defun putnam-2003-a5-count-no-even-return-dyck-paths
    (candidate-count length)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate-count)))
  (if (zp candidate-count)
      0
    (let ((code (- candidate-count 1)))
      (+
       (if (and
            (putnam-2003-a5-dyck-path-p code length)
            (putnam-2003-a5-no-even-return-p
             code length))
           1
         0)
       (putnam-2003-a5-count-no-even-return-dyck-paths
        code length)))))

;; For finite sets A and B, the published one-to-one correspondence is
;; equivalent in both directions to |A| = |B|. The exact counts below therefore
;; preserve the bijection claim for every positive n without externalizing a
;; function witness.

;; The Lean source tests every k in (i,j] for p(k)=-1. This is the intended
;; no-even-return condition described by the problem statement.

(defun putnambench-putnam-2003-a5-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and (natp n) (< 0 n))
   (let* ((source-length (* 2 n))
          (target-length (* 2 (- n 1)))
          (source-count
           (putnam-2003-a5-count-no-even-return-dyck-paths
            (expt 2 source-length)
            source-length))
          (target-count
           (putnam-2003-a5-count-dyck-paths
            (expt 2 target-length)
            target-length)))
     (equal source-count target-count))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2003_a5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_a5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2003_a5): Dyck n-paths with no even-length
-- return are in one-to-one correspondence with Dyck (n-1)-paths. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2003A5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _<F_ _<=F_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not proposition =
  proposition -> Bottom

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive :
    {n : Nat} ->
    Positive (suc n)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero :
    {n : Nat} ->
    Fin (suc n)
  fsuc :
    {n : Nat} ->
    Fin n ->
    Fin (suc n)

finToNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (finToNat i)

data _<F_ : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin n -> Set where
  fzero<fsuc :
    {n : Nat} {j : Fin n} ->
    fzero <F fsuc j
  fsuc<fsuc :
    {n : Nat} {i j : Fin n} ->
    i <F j ->
    fsuc i <F fsuc j

data _<=F_ : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin n -> Set where
  fzero<= :
    {n : Nat} {j : Fin (suc n)} ->
    fzero <=F j
  fsuc<=fsuc :
    {n : Nat} {i j : Fin n} ->
    i <=F j ->
    fsuc i <=F fsuc j

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

zeroZ : Int
zeroZ =
  pos zero

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos (suc zero)

minusOneZ : Int
minusOneZ =
  negsuc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc (suc zero)

data Step : Int -> Set where
  up-step :
    Step oneZ
  down-step :
    Step minusOneZ

data Nonnegative : Int -> Set where
  nonnegative :
    {n : Nat} ->
    Nonnegative (pos n)

data Even : Nat -> Set where
  even-zero :
    Even zero
  even-plus-two :
    {n : Nat} ->
    Even n ->
    Even (suc (suc n))

Path : Nat -> Set
Path m =
  Fin (two * m) -> Int

sumFin :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Int) ->
  Int
sumFin {zero} terms =
  zeroZ
sumFin {suc n} terms =
  addInt
    (terms fzero)
    (sumFin (\ i -> terms (fsuc i)))

prefixSum :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Int) ->
  Fin n ->
  Int
prefixSum {suc n} path fzero =
  path fzero
prefixSum {suc n} path (fsuc j) =
  addInt
    (path fzero)
    (prefixSum (\ i -> path (fsuc i)) j)

PathEqual :
  {m : Nat} ->
  Path m ->
  Path m ->
  Set
PathEqual {m} left right =
  (i : Fin (two * m)) ->
  left i == right i

record IsDyckPath (m : Nat) (path : Path m) : Set where
  field
    unit-steps :
      (i : Fin (two * m)) ->
      Step (path i)
    balanced :
      sumFin path == zeroZ
    nonnegative-prefixes :
      (j : Fin (two * m)) ->
      Nonnegative (prefixSum path j)

record HasEvenReturn (m : Nat) (path : Path m) : Set where
  field
    preceding-index :
      Fin (two * m)
    return-index :
      Fin (two * m)
    precedes-return :
      preceding-index <F return-index
    preceding-up-step :
      path preceding-index == oneZ
    contiguous-down-steps :
      (k : Fin (two * m)) ->
      preceding-index <F k ->
      k <=F return-index ->
      path k == minusOneZ
    even-return-length :
      Even
        (finToNat return-index - finToNat preceding-index)
    returns-to-axis :
      prefixSum path return-index == zeroZ

NoEvenReturn :
  (m : Nat) ->
  Path m ->
  Set
NoEvenReturn m path =
  Not (HasEvenReturn m path)

record IsSpecialDyckPath (m : Nat) (path : Path m) : Set where
  field
    is-dyck-path :
      IsDyckPath m path
    has-no-even-return :
      NoEvenReturn m path

record DyckPathBijection (n : Nat) : Set where
  field
    forward :
      Path n ->
      Path (n - suc zero)
    backward :
      Path (n - suc zero) ->
      Path n
    forward-preserves-membership :
      (path : Path n) ->
      IsSpecialDyckPath n path ->
      IsDyckPath (n - suc zero) (forward path)
    backward-preserves-membership :
      (path : Path (n - suc zero)) ->
      IsDyckPath (n - suc zero) path ->
      IsSpecialDyckPath n (backward path)
    backward-after-forward :
      (path : Path n) ->
      IsSpecialDyckPath n path ->
      PathEqual {m = n} (backward (forward path)) path
    forward-after-backward :
      (path : Path (n - suc zero)) ->
      IsDyckPath (n - suc zero) path ->
      PathEqual {m = n - suc zero} (forward (backward path)) path

putnam-2003-a5 : Set
putnam-2003-a5 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  DyckPathBijection n

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_a5:
  a one-to-one correspondence between Dyck n-paths with no even-length return
  and Dyck (n - 1)-paths. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2003_a5 =
  ``let path_sum =
      \p : num -> int. \r : num.
        ITSET
          (\k : num. \acc : int. p k + acc)
          (count r)
          (0 : int)
    in
    let dyckpath =
      \m : num. \p : num -> int.
        (!k : num. 2 * m <= k ==> p k = 0) /\
        (!k : num. k < 2 * m ==> p k = 1 \/ p k = ~1) /\
        path_sum p (2 * m) = 0 /\
        (!j : num. j < 2 * m ==> 0 <= path_sum p (SUC j))
    in
    let noevenreturn =
      \m : num. \p : num -> int.
        ~(?i j : num.
            i < j /\
            j < 2 * m /\
            p i = 1 /\
            (!k : num. i < k /\ k <= j ==> p k = ~1) /\
            EVEN (j - i) /\
            path_sum p (SUC j) = 0)
    in
      !n : num.
        0 < n
        ==>
        ?f : (num -> int) -> (num -> int).
          !y : num -> int.
            dyckpath (n - 1) y
            ==>
            ?!x : num -> int.
              dyckpath n x /\
              noevenreturn n x /\
              f x = y``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2003_a5: Dyck n-paths with no return of even length are in
  one-to-one correspondence with Dyck (n-1)-paths. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For m e. NN0, the carrier 0 ..^ (2*m) is SetMM's canonical copy of
  Fin (2*m), and ZZ ^m (0 ..^ (2*m)) is the full set of integer-valued
  paths on that carrier. The range, total-sum, and prefix-sum conditions
  define Dyck paths exactly as in the primary formal source.

  On the left, i is the upstep immediately preceding a contiguous block of
  downsteps through j. Requiring the prefix sum through j to be zero makes
  that block a return, and 2 || (j-i) says that its length is even. Negating
  the existential condition therefore states that no return has even length.

  SetMM's equipollence relation ~~ means that a bijection exists between the
  two displayed path classes. The final declaration is the single unproved
  $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d i j k n p q $.

  putnambench-putnam-2003-a5 $a |- A. n e. NN
    (
      {
        p e. ( ZZ ^m ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) ) ) |
        (
          (
            (
              ran p C_ { -u 1 , 1 }
              /\
              (
                sum_ k e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
                  ( p ` k )
              )
              =
              0
            )
            /\
            A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
              0
              <_
              (
                sum_ k e. ( 0 ... j )
                  ( p ` k )
              )
          )
          /\
          -.
          E. i e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
            E. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
              (
                i < j
                /\
                (
                  ( p ` i ) = 1
                  /\
                  (
                    A. k e. ( ( i + 1 ) ... j )
                      ( p ` k ) = ( -u 1 )
                    /\
                    (
                      2 || ( j - i )
                      /\
                      (
                        sum_ k e. ( 0 ... j )
                          ( p ` k )
                      )
                      =
                      0
                    )
                  )
                )
              )
        )
      }
      ~~
      {
        q e.
          (
            ZZ
            ^m
            ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. ( n - 1 ) ) )
          )
        |
        (
          (
            ran q C_ { -u 1 , 1 }
            /\
            (
              sum_ k e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. ( n - 1 ) ) )
                ( q ` k )
            )
            =
            0
          )
          /\
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. ( n - 1 ) ) )
            0
            <_
            (
              sum_ k e. ( 0 ... j )
                ( q ` k )
            )
        )
      }
    )
  $.
$}

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat st 0 < n holds
    {p where p is FinSequence of INT :
      len p = 2*n &

      Sum p = 0 &
      (for j being Nat st j in Seg (2*n) holds

        i in Seg (2*n) & j in Seg (2*n) & i < j &
        p.i = 1 &

        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          len s = j &
          (for k being Nat st k in Seg j holds s.k = p.k) &
          Sum s = 0},
    {q where q is FinSequence of INT :
      len q = 2*(n -' 1) &
      (for k being Nat st k in Seg (2*(n -' 1)) holds
        q.k = -1 or q.k = 1) &
      Sum q = 0 &
      (for j being Nat st j in Seg (2*(n -' 1)) holds
        ex s being FinSequence of INT st
          len s = j &
          (for k being Nat st k in Seg j holds s.k = q.k) &

proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2003_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_a5:
% Dyck n-paths with no return of even length correspond one-to-one with Dyck
% (n - 1)-paths for every positive n. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2003_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> int]
  sequence_map: TYPE = [integer_sequence -> integer_sequence]

  prefix_sum(path: integer_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      prefix_sum(path, count - 1) + path(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  canonical_path(path: integer_sequence, semilength: nat): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      2 * semilength <= index IMPLIES path(index) = 0

  dyck_path(path: integer_sequence, semilength: nat): bool =
    canonical_path(path, semilength)
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        index < 2 * semilength
          IMPLIES (path(index) = -1 OR path(index) = 1))
      AND prefix_sum(path, 2 * semilength) = 0
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        index < 2 * semilength
          IMPLIES 0 <= prefix_sum(path, index + 1))

  even_nat(value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (half: nat):
      value = 2 * half

  no_even_return(path: integer_sequence, semilength: nat): bool =
    canonical_path(path, semilength)
      AND NOT EXISTS (first, last: nat):
        first < last
          AND last < 2 * semilength
          AND path(first) = 1
          AND (FORALL (index: nat):
            (first < index AND index <= last)
              IMPLIES path(index) = -1)
          AND even_nat(last - first)
          AND prefix_sum(path, last + 1) = 0

  putnam_2003_a5: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n > 0 IMPLIES
        EXISTS (correspondence: sequence_map):
          FORALL (target: integer_sequence):
            dyck_path(target, n - 1) IMPLIES
              (EXISTS (source: integer_sequence):
                dyck_path(source, n)
                  AND no_even_return(source, n)
                  AND correspondence(source) = target)
              AND (FORALL (left, right: integer_sequence):
                ((dyck_path(left, n)
                    AND no_even_return(left, n)
                    AND correspondence(left) = target)
                  AND (dyck_path(right, n)
                    AND no_even_return(right, n)
                    AND correspondence(right) = target))
                  IMPLIES left = right)
END putnam_2003_a5

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_a6:
   a partition of the nonnegative integers into two sets with equal numbers
   of ordered distinct-pair representations of every sum; this file contains
   no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List ClassicalDescription.

Definition putnam_2003_a6_pairs (n : nat) : list (nat * nat) :=
  flat_map
    (fun s1 : nat =>
      map (fun s2 : nat => (s1, s2)) (seq 0 (Nat.succ n)))
    (seq 0 (Nat.succ n)).

Definition putnam_2003_a6_representation_pairb
    (S : nat -> Prop) (n : nat) (pair : nat * nat) : bool :=
  if excluded_middle_informative
       (S (fst pair) /\
        S (snd pair) /\
        fst pair <> snd pair /\
        (fst pair + snd pair = n)%nat)
  then true
  else false.

Definition putnam_2003_a6_representation_count
    (S : nat -> Prop) (n : nat) : nat :=
  length
    (filter
      (putnam_2003_a6_representation_pairb S n)
      (putnam_2003_a6_pairs n)).

Definition putnam_2003_a6_solution : Prop := True.

Theorem putnam_2003_a6 :
  (exists A B : nat -> Prop,
      (forall n : nat, A n \/ B n) /\
      (forall n : nat, ~ (A n /\ B n)) /\
      (forall n : nat,
        putnam_2003_a6_representation_count A n =
        putnam_2003_a6_representation_count B n))
  <-> putnam_2003_a6_solution.
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_a6:
;; existence of a partition of the nonnegative integers into two sets having
;; equal ordered distinct-pair representation counts for every sum. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Sets of naturals are represented by tame unary characteristic-function
;; objects. Every such object determines a source set. Conversely, the source
;; existence assertion has tame Thue-Morse characteristic-function witnesses,
;; so this representation is equivalent for this existential proposition and
;; does not replace either set by a finite carrier or table.

(defun putnam-2003-a6-member-p (set n)
  (if (apply$ set (list n))
      t
    nil))

;; REMAINING ranges over s1 = n,n-1,...,0. For each s1, the only possible
;; second summand is s2 = n-s1, so every ordered pair is counted exactly once.
(defun putnam-2003-a6-representation-count-aux
    (set n remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (let* ((s1 (- remaining 1))
           (s2 (- n s1)))
      (+
       (if (and
            (not (equal s1 s2))
            (putnam-2003-a6-member-p set s1)
            (putnam-2003-a6-member-p set s2))
           1
         0)
       (putnam-2003-a6-representation-count-aux
        set n (- remaining 1))))))

(defun putnam-2003-a6-representation-count (set n)
  (if (natp n)
      (putnam-2003-a6-representation-count-aux
       set n (+ n 1))
    0))

(defun putnam-2003-a6-partition-and-count-at-p (a b n)
  (and
   ;; Exclusive membership is pointwise equivalent to union UNIV and empty
   ;; intersection.
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-2003-a6-member-p a n)
     (putnam-2003-a6-member-p b n)))
   (equal
    (putnam-2003-a6-representation-count a n)
    (putnam-2003-a6-representation-count b n))))

(defun-sk putnam-2003-a6-partition-and-counts-agree-p (a b)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (natp n)
     (putnam-2003-a6-partition-and-count-at-p a b n))))

(defun-sk putnam-2003-a6-partition-exists-p ()
  (exists (a b)
    (and
     (tamep-functionp a)
     (tamep-functionp b)
     (putnam-2003-a6-partition-and-counts-agree-p a b))))

;; The supplied PutnamBench solution is True, so the source biconditional is
;; exactly the internally quantified existence assertion above.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2003-a6-statement ()
  (putnam-2003-a6-partition-exists-p))

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_a6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2003_a6): existence of a partition of the
-- nonnegative integers whose two parts have equal ordered distinct-pair
-- representation counts for every sum. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2003A6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; suc; _+_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not :
  Set ->
  Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ :
  {A : Set} ->
  A ->
  A ->
  Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_
  (A B : Set) :
  Set where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_
  (A B : Set) :
  Set where

  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists
  (A : Set)
  (P : A -> Set) :
  Set where

  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record Pair : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    first-coordinate  : Nat
    second-coordinate : Nat

open Pair

Subset : Set1
Subset =
  Nat -> Set

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (P : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (i : Fin cardinality) ->
      P (enumerate i)
    enumeration-complete :
      (x : A) ->
      P x ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ i -> enumerate i == x)
    enumeration-injective :
      (i j : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate i == enumerate j ->
      i == j

Representation :
  Subset ->
  Nat ->
  Pair ->
  Set
Representation S n p =
  S (first-coordinate p)
  and
  S (second-coordinate p)
  and
  first-coordinate p != second-coordinate p
  and
  first-coordinate p + second-coordinate p == n

EqualRepresentationCount :
  Subset ->
  Subset ->
  Nat ->
  Set
EqualRepresentationCount A B n =
  Exists Nat
    (\ cardinality ->
      HasCardinality
        (Representation A n)
        cardinality
      and
      HasCardinality
        (Representation B n)
        cardinality)

record IsPartition
  (A B : Subset) :
  Set where

  field
    covers-all :
      (n : Nat) ->
      A n or B n
    disjoint :
      (n : Nat) ->
      A n ->
      B n ->
      Bottom

record Putnam2003A6Witness : Set1 where
  field
    A B :
      Subset
    partition :
      IsPartition A B
    equal-representation-counts :
      (n : Nat) ->
      EqualRepresentationCount A B n

putnam-2003-a6 : Set1
putnam-2003-a6 =
  Putnam2003A6Witness

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_a6:
% the nonnegative integers can be partitioned into two sets having equally many
% ordered distinct-summand representations of every natural number. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_2003_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_set: TYPE = [nat -> bool]

  row_representation_count(
      S: natural_set,
      n, first, second_count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF second_count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      row_representation_count(S, n, first, second_count - 1)
        + IF S(first)
            AND S(second_count - 1)
            AND first /= second_count - 1
            AND first + second_count - 1 = n THEN
            1
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE second_count

  bounded_representation_count(
      S: natural_set,
      n, first_count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF first_count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      bounded_representation_count(S, n, first_count - 1)
        + row_representation_count(S, n, first_count - 1, n + 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE first_count

  representation_count(S: natural_set, n: nat): nat =
    bounded_representation_count(S, n, n + 1)

  partitions_naturals(A, B: natural_set): bool =
    (FORALL (x: nat): A(x) OR B(x))
      AND (FORALL (x: nat): NOT (A(x) AND B(x)))

  equal_representation_counts(A, B: natural_set): bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      representation_count(A, n) = representation_count(B, n)

  putnam_2003_a6_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_2003_a6: bool =
    (EXISTS (A, B: natural_set):
      partitions_naturals(A, B)
        AND equal_representation_counts(A, B))
      IFF putnam_2003_a6_solution
END putnam_2003_a6

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b1:
;; nonexistence of four real univariate polynomials whose two separated
;; products sum identically to 1 + x*y + x^2*y^2. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Since the supplied solution is False, the source biconditional is the
;; universal assertion that no four real polynomials satisfy the identity.
;; A failure of that assertion is a finite system of polynomial equations
;; over the reals, so it has a real solution iff it has a real-algebraic
;; solution. Every finite tuple of real algebraic coefficients lies in
;; Q(alpha) for one real algebraic alpha. Rational polynomials in alpha, with
;; alpha specified by a rational isolating interval, therefore preserve the
;; arbitrary real domain rather than restricting coefficients to rationals.
;;
;; Source polynomials are arbitrary finite coefficient lists in ascending
;; degree order. Coefficientwise comparison is equivalent to identity for all
;; real x and y, and the list lengths remain unbounded.

;; Rational polynomials in alpha use descending coefficient order.

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-p (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (and (rationalp (car p))
           (putnam-2003-b1-rp-p (cdr p)))
    (equal p nil)))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (if (equal (car p) 0)
          (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize (cdr p))
        p)
    nil))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-neg (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (cons (- (car p))
            (putnam-2003-b1-rp-neg (cdr p)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-add-raw (p q)
  (declare (xargs :measure (+ (acl2-count p) (acl2-count q))))
  (cond
   ((endp p) q)
   ((endp q) p)
   ((< (len p) (len q))
    (cons (car q)
          (putnam-2003-b1-rp-add-raw p (cdr q))))
   ((< (len q) (len p))
    (cons (car p)
          (putnam-2003-b1-rp-add-raw (cdr p) q)))
   (t
    (cons (+ (car p) (car q))
          (putnam-2003-b1-rp-add-raw (cdr p) (cdr q))))))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-add (p q)
  (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize
   (putnam-2003-b1-rp-add-raw p q)))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-sub (p q)
  (putnam-2003-b1-rp-add
   p (putnam-2003-b1-rp-neg q)))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-scale (coefficient p)
  (if (consp p)
      (cons (* coefficient (car p))
            (putnam-2003-b1-rp-scale coefficient (cdr p)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-zeroes (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (cons 0 (putnam-2003-b1-zeroes (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-scale-shift (coefficient p shift)
  (append
   (putnam-2003-b1-rp-scale coefficient p)
   (putnam-2003-b1-zeroes shift)))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-mul-raw (p q)
  (if (consp p)
      (putnam-2003-b1-rp-add
       (putnam-2003-b1-rp-scale-shift
        (car p) q (len (cdr p)))
       (putnam-2003-b1-rp-mul-raw (cdr p) q))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-mul (p q)
  (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize
   (putnam-2003-b1-rp-mul-raw p q)))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-eval-aux (p x accumulator)
  (if (consp p)
      (putnam-2003-b1-rp-eval-aux
       (cdr p) x (+ (* accumulator x) (car p)))
    accumulator))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-eval (p x)
  (putnam-2003-b1-rp-eval-aux p x 0))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-derivative-aux (p degree)
  (if (consp p)
      (if (zp degree)
          nil
        (cons (* degree (car p))
              (putnam-2003-b1-rp-derivative-aux
               (cdr p) (- degree 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-derivative (p)
  (let ((p (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize p)))
    (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize
     (putnam-2003-b1-rp-derivative-aux
      p (nfix (- (len p) 1))))))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-rem-fuel (p q fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((p (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize p))
        (q (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize q)))
    (if (or (zp fuel)
            (endp q)
            (< (len p) (len q)))
        p
      (putnam-2003-b1-rp-rem-fuel
       (putnam-2003-b1-rp-sub
        p
        (putnam-2003-b1-rp-scale-shift
         (/ (car p) (car q))
         q
         (- (len p) (len q))))
       q
       (- fuel 1)))))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-rem (p q)
  (putnam-2003-b1-rp-rem-fuel
   p q (+ 1 (len (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize p)))))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-sturm-tail (previous current fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((current (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize current)))
    (if (or (zp fuel) (endp current))
        nil
      (cons
       current
       (putnam-2003-b1-rp-sturm-tail
        current
        (putnam-2003-b1-rp-neg
         (putnam-2003-b1-rp-rem previous current))
        (- fuel 1))))))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-sturm-sequence (p q)
  (let ((p (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize p))
        (q (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize q)))
    (if (endp p)
        nil
      (cons
       p
       (if (endp q)
           nil
         (cons
          q
          (putnam-2003-b1-rp-sturm-tail
           p q (+ 1 (len p) (len q)))))))))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rational-sign (x)
  (cond ((< x 0) -1)
        ((< 0 x) 1)
        (t 0)))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-rp-variations-aux
    (polynomials x previous-sign)
  (if (consp polynomials)
      (let ((sign
             (putnam-2003-b1-rational-sign
              (putnam-2003-b1-rp-eval
               (car polynomials) x))))

             (cdr polynomials) x previous-sign)
          (+ (if (and (not (equal previous-sign 0))
                      (not (equal sign previous-sign)))
                 1

              (cdr polynomials) x sign))))
    0))

  (putnam-2003-b1-rp-variations-aux polynomials x 0))

  (let ((sequence
         (putnam-2003-b1-rp-sturm-sequence p q)))
    (- (putnam-2003-b1-rp-variations sequence lower)
       (putnam-2003-b1-rp-variations sequence upper))))

   (putnam-2003-b1-rp-p primitive)
   (consp (putnam-2003-b1-rp-normalize primitive))
   (rationalp lower)
   (rationalp upper)
   (< lower upper)
   (not (equal
         (putnam-2003-b1-rp-eval primitive lower) 0))
   (not (equal
         (putnam-2003-b1-rp-eval primitive upper) 0))
   (equal
    (putnam-2003-b1-rp-root-count primitive lower upper)
    1)
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-2003-b1-rp-cauchy-index
      primitive
      (putnam-2003-b1-rp-mul
       (putnam-2003-b1-rp-derivative primitive)
       (putnam-2003-b1-rp-derivative primitive))
      lower
      upper)

(defun putnam-2003-b1-algebraic-sign
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (putnam-2003-b1-rp-cauchy-index
   primitive
   (putnam-2003-b1-rp-mul
    (putnam-2003-b1-rp-derivative primitive)
    value)

   upper))

    (primitive lower upper left right)

    primitive lower upper
    (putnam-2003-b1-rp-sub left right))

  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and
       (putnam-2003-b1-rp-p (car coefficients))

    (primitive lower upper a b c d x-degree y-degree)

   primitive lower upper
   (putnam-2003-b1-rp-add
    (putnam-2003-b1-rp-mul
     (nth x-degree a)

  (if (< left right) right left))

(defun putnam-2003-b1-coefficient-identity-p (primitive lower upper a b c d)

           3

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2003_b1): nonexistence of four real univariate
-- polynomials expressing 1 + xy + x^2 y^2 as a sum of two separated products.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2003B1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

Polynomial : Set -> Set
Polynomial R =
  List R

evaluatePolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  R ->
  R
evaluatePolynomial reals [] x =
  zeroR reals
evaluatePolynomial reals (coefficient ∷ coefficients) x =
  add reals
    coefficient
    (multiply reals
      x
      (evaluatePolynomial reals coefficients x))

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

module Putnam2003B1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  targetPolynomial : R -> R -> R
  targetPolynomial x y =
    add reals
      (oneR reals)
      (add reals
        (multiply reals x y)
        (multiply reals
          (square reals x)
          (square reals y)))

  IsSeparatedRepresentation :
    Polynomial R ->
    Polynomial R ->
    Polynomial R ->
    Polynomial R ->
    Set
  IsSeparatedRepresentation a b c d =
    (x y : R) ->
    targetPolynomial x y ==
      add reals
        (multiply reals
          (evaluatePolynomial reals a x)
          (evaluatePolynomial reals c y))
        (multiply reals
          (evaluatePolynomial reals b x)
          (evaluatePolynomial reals d y))

  SeparatedRepresentationExists : Set
  SeparatedRepresentationExists =
    Exists (Polynomial R)
      (\ a ->
        Exists (Polynomial R)
          (\ b ->
            Exists (Polynomial R)
              (\ c ->
                Exists (Polynomial R)
                  (\ d ->
                    IsSeparatedRepresentation a b c d))))

  putnam-2003-b1-solution : Set
  putnam-2003-b1-solution =
    Bottom

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    Iff
      SeparatedRepresentationExists
      putnam-2003-b1-solution

putnam-2003-b1 : Set1
putnam-2003-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2003B1Statement.proposition reals

  putnam_2003_b1: nonexistence of four real univariate polynomials whose
  two-product sum is identically 1 + xy + x^2 y^2. This file contains no

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) is set.mm's ring of all finite-support
  univariate real polynomials, and eval1 evaluates such a polynomial at an
  arbitrary real input. Thus a, b, c, and d range over exactly the source
  polynomial objects, while x and y retain their universal real domains.

  equivalent to the negation of the full existential polynomial identity
  below. The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement;
  this database contains no $p proof declaration.

${
  $d a b c d x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-2003-b1 $a |- -.
    E. a e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
      E. b e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
        E. c e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
          E. d e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
            A. x e. RR

                    x.

                  +
                  (
                    ( ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` b ) ` x )
                    x.
                    ( ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` d ) ` y )

  $.
$}

  polynomial: TYPE = list[real]

import Mathlib

open MvPolynomial Set

-- uses (ℕ → ℕ → ℚ) instead of (Fin n → Icc 1 n → ℚ)
/--
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Starting with the sequence $$1, \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{3}, \dots, \frac{1}{n},$$ form a new sequence of $n-1$ entries $$\frac{3}{4}, \frac{5}{12}, \dots, \frac{2n-1}{2n(n-1)}$$ by taking the averages of two consecutive entries in the first sequence. Repeat the averaging of neighbors on the second sequence to obtain a third sequence of $n-2$ entries, and continue until the final sequence produced consists of a single number $x_n$. Show that $x_n < 2/n$.
-/
theorem putnam_2003_b2
  (n : ℕ)
  (hn : n > 0)
  (seq : ℕ → ℕ → ℚ)
  (hinit : ∀ j ∈ Icc 1 n, seq 0 j = 1 / j)
  (havg : ∀ᵉ (k ∈ Icc 1 (n - 1)) (j ∈ Icc 1 (n - k)),
    seq k j = (seq (k - 1) j + seq (k - 1) (j + 1)) / 2) :
  (seq (n - 1) 1 < 2 / n) :=
sorry

Theorem putnam_2003_b2
    (n : nat)

    (seq : nat -> nat -> Q)

  seq (n - 1)%nat 1%nat < 2 / inject_Z (Z.of_nat n).
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b2:
;; the final value obtained by repeatedly averaging adjacent terms of
;; 1, 1/2, ..., 1/n is strictly less than 2/n. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; SEQUENCE is a total tame binary function object on natural indices, with
;; rational codomain enforced below by FN-EQUAL. The source hypotheses and
;; conclusion inspect only the finite triangle
;;
;;   0 <= k < n,  1 <= j <= n-k.
;;
;; Every source sequence restricts on this triangle to values represented by
;; a tame nested-IF function (with rational default zero), and every qualifying
;; target function gives a source sequence. Thus restricting the representing
;; function object to tame functions is bidirectionally equivalent for this
;; proposition and does not replace the sequence by a finite table.

(defun putnam-2003-b2-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2003-b2-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'cons
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2003-b2-term-list (cdr terms)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2003-b2-apply-term (function arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2003-b2-quoted function)
        (putnam-2003-b2-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2003-b2-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'if
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2003-b2-and-terms (cdr terms))
            (putnam-2003-b2-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2003-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2003-b2-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list 'if
        hypothesis
        conclusion
        (putnam-2003-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2003-b2-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda formals (putnam-2003-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2003-b2-codomain-function (sequence)
  (let ((value
         (putnam-2003-b2-apply-term
          sequence '(k j))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(k j)
     (putnam-2003-b2-implies-term
      (putnam-2003-b2-and-terms
       (list (list 'natp 'k)
             (list 'natp 'j)))
      (list 'rationalp value)))))

(defun putnam-2003-b2-rational-sequence-p (sequence)
  (let ((codomain
         (putnam-2003-b2-codomain-function sequence))
        (true-on-two
         (putnam-2003-b2-true-function '(k j))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp sequence)
     (tamep-functionp codomain)
     (tamep-functionp true-on-two)
     (fn-equal codomain true-on-two))))

(defun putnam-2003-b2-sequence-value (sequence k j)
  (apply$ sequence (list k j)))

(defun putnam-2003-b2-initial-p (sequence j)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix j)))
  (if (zp j)
      t
    (and
     (equal
      (putnam-2003-b2-sequence-value sequence 0 j)
      (/ 1 j))
     (putnam-2003-b2-initial-p sequence (- j 1)))))

(defun putnam-2003-b2-averaging-row-p
    (sequence k j)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix j)))
  (if (zp j)
      t
    (and
     (equal
      (putnam-2003-b2-sequence-value sequence k j)
      (/

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2003_b2): repeated averaging of the rational
-- sequence 1, 1/2, ..., 1/n yields a final value less than 2/n.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2003B2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<N_ _~Q_ _<Q_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

data Top : Set where
  top : Top

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : (n : Nat) -> Positive (suc n)

pred : Nat -> Nat
pred zero =
  zero
pred (suc n) =
  n

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

scaleInt : Int -> Nat -> Int
scaleInt z n =
  multiplyInt z (pos n)

IntStrictLess : Int -> Int -> Set
IntStrictLess (pos m) (pos n) =
  m <N n
IntStrictLess (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  Bottom
IntStrictLess (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  Top
IntStrictLess (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  n <N m

record Rational : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator             : Int
    denominator-minus-one : Nat

open Rational

denominator : Rational -> Nat
denominator q =
  suc (denominator-minus-one q)

_~Q_ : Rational -> Rational -> Set
x ~Q y =
  scaleInt (numerator x) (denominator y) ==
  scaleInt (numerator y) (denominator x)

_<Q_ : Rational -> Rational -> Set
x <Q y =
  IntStrictLess
    (scaleInt (numerator x) (denominator y))
    (scaleInt (numerator y) (denominator x))

zeroQ : Rational
zeroQ =
  fraction (pos zero) zero

addQ : Rational -> Rational -> Rational
addQ x y =
  fraction
    (addInt
      (scaleInt (numerator x) (denominator y))
      (scaleInt (numerator y) (denominator x)))
    (pred (denominator x * denominator y))

divideByNat : Rational -> Nat -> Rational
divideByNat q zero =
  zeroQ
divideByNat q (suc n) =
  fraction
    (numerator q)
    (pred (denominator q * suc n))

naturalRatio : Nat -> Nat -> Rational
naturalRatio numerator-value zero =
  zeroQ
naturalRatio numerator-value (suc denominator-minus-one-value) =
  fraction
    (pos numerator-value)
    denominator-minus-one-value

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

InClosedNatInterval :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Set
InClosedNatInterval lower upper value =
  lower <=N value
  and
  value <=N upper

averageQ : Rational -> Rational -> Rational
averageQ x y =
  divideByNat (addQ x y) twoN

putnam-2003-b2 : Set
putnam-2003-b2 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  (seq : Nat -> Nat -> Rational) ->
  ((j : Nat) ->
    InClosedNatInterval oneN n j ->
    seq zero j ~Q naturalRatio oneN j) ->
  ((k : Nat) ->
    InClosedNatInterval oneN (n - oneN) k ->
    (j : Nat) ->
    InClosedNatInterval oneN (n - k) j ->
    seq k j ~Q
      averageQ
        (seq (k - oneN) j)
        (seq (k - oneN) (j + oneN))) ->
  seq (n - oneN) oneN <Q naturalRatio twoN n

open arithmeticTheory ratTheory;

val putnam_2003_b2 =

  putnam_2003_b2: repeated adjacent averaging of the rational sequence
  1, 1/2, ..., 1/n yields a final value strictly less than 2/n.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  NN is set.mm's class of positive integers, so quantifying n over NN is
  equivalent to the source's natural-number parameter together with n > 0.
  The class ( QQ ^m NN0 ) ^m NN0 contains exactly the total curried
  rational-valued functions on pairs of nonnegative integer indices used by
  the Lean and Isabelle sources. Values outside the displayed triangular
  ranges are intentionally unconstrained, as they are in those sources.

  The first conjunct is the reciprocal initialization on 1 ... n. The second
  is the adjacent-average recurrence at every stage k from 1 through n - 1
  and every valid position j from 1 through n - k. The conclusion is the
  source inequality for the sole entry at the last stage.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d F j k n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2003-b2 $a |-
    A. n e. NN
      A. F e. ( ( QQ ^m NN0 ) ^m NN0 )
        (
          (
            A. j e. ( 1 ... n )
              ( ( F ` 0 ) ` j ) = ( 1 / j )
            /\
            A. k e. ( 1 ... ( n - 1 ) )
              A. j e. ( 1 ... ( n - k ) )
                ( ( F ` k ) ` j )
                =
                (
                  (
                    ( ( F ` ( k - 1 ) ) ` j )
                    +
                    ( ( F ` ( k - 1 ) ) ` ( j + 1 ) )
                  )
                  /
                  2
                )
          )
          ->
          ( ( F ` ( n - 1 ) ) ` 1 ) < ( 2 / n )
        )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b2:
% repeated averaging of adjacent terms of 1, 1/2, ..., 1/n yields a final
% rational value strictly less than 2/n. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2003_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  rational_array: TYPE = [nat, nat -> rat]

  nat_sub(n, k: nat): nat =
    IF k <= n THEN n - k ELSE 0 ENDIF

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: rat): rat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  putnam_2003_b2: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (seq: rational_array):
      (n > 0
        AND (FORALL (j: nat):
          (1 <= j AND j <= n) IMPLIES
            seq(0, j) = safe_div(1, j :: rat))
        AND (FORALL (k: nat):
          (1 <= k AND k <= nat_sub(n, 1)) IMPLIES
            (FORALL (j: nat):
              (1 <= j AND j <= nat_sub(n, k)) IMPLIES
                seq(k, j) =
                  safe_div(
                    seq(nat_sub(k, 1), j)
                      + seq(nat_sub(k, 1), j + 1),
                    2))))
      IMPLIES
        seq(nat_sub(n, 1), 1)
          < safe_div(2, n :: rat)
END putnam_2003_b2

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2003_b3): the factorial identity expressing n!
-- as a product of least common multiples of initial natural-number intervals.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

naturalDiv : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero =
  zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero =
  zero
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

gcdWithFuel : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat
gcdWithFuel zero a b =
  a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a zero =
  a
gcdWithFuel (suc fuel) a (suc b) =
  gcdWithFuel fuel (suc b) (naturalMod a (suc b))

naturalGCD : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalGCD a b =
  gcdWithFuel (suc (a + b)) a b

naturalLCM : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalLCM a b =
  naturalDiv (a * b) (naturalGCD a b)

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  one
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

lcmThrough : Nat -> Nat
lcmThrough zero =
  one
lcmThrough (suc n) =
  naturalLCM (lcmThrough n) (suc n)

quotientLcmProduct : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
quotientLcmProduct n zero =
  one
quotientLcmProduct n (suc i) =
  quotientLcmProduct n i *
  lcmThrough (naturalDiv n (suc i))

putnam-2003-b3 : Set
putnam-2003-b3 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  factorial n == quotientLcmProduct n n

$(

$}

title: putnam_2003_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b3:
% for every positive integer n, n factorial is the product over i from 1 to n
% of the least common multiple of the integers from 1 through floor(n / i).
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2003_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  nat_factorial(n: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      n * nat_factorial(n - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  is_lcm_through(lcm_value, bound: nat): bool =
    (FORALL (value: nat):
      1 <= value AND value <= bound IMPLIES
        nat_divides(value, lcm_value))
      AND (FORALL (common_multiple: nat):
        (FORALL (value: nat):
          1 <= value AND value <= bound IMPLIES
            nat_divides(value, common_multiple))
        IMPLIES nat_divides(lcm_value, common_multiple))

  indexed_product(values: [nat -> nat], count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      indexed_product(values, count - 1) * values(count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  putnam_2003_b3: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n > 0 IMPLIES
        EXISTS (lcm_values: [nat -> nat]):
          (FORALL (i: nat):
            1 <= i AND i <= n IMPLIES
              is_lcm_through(lcm_values(i), ndiv(n, i)))
            AND nat_factorial(n) = indexed_product(lcm_values, n)
END putnam_2003_b3

import Mathlib

open MvPolynomial Set Nat

/--
Let $f(z)=az^4+bz^3+cz^2+dz+e=a(z-r_1)(z-r_2)(z-r_3)(z-r_4)$ where $a,b,c,d,e$ are integers, $a \neq 0$. Show that if $r_1+r_2$ is a rational number and $r_1+r_2 \neq r_3+r_4$, then $r_1r_2$ is a rational number.
-/
theorem putnam_2003_b4
  (f : ℝ → ℝ)
  (a b c d e : ℤ)
  (r1 r2 r3 r4 : ℝ)
  (ane0 : a ≠ 0)
  (hf1 : ∀ z, f z = a * z ^ 4 + b * z ^ 3 + c * z ^ 2 + d * z + e)
  (hf2 : ∀ z, f z = a * (z - r1) * (z - r2) * (z - r3) * (z - r4)) :
  (¬Irrational (r1 + r2) ∧ r1 + r2 ≠ r3 + r4) → ¬Irrational (r1 * r2) :=
sorry
