(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b4:
  rationality of the product of two roots of an integer-coefficient real
  quartic when their sum is rational and differs from the other roots' sum.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let is_rational =
     \x:real.
       ?p q:int.
         ~(q = (&0:int)) /\
         x = real_of_int p / real_of_int q in
   !f:real->real.
   !a b c d e:int.
   !r1 r2 r3 r4:real.
     ~(a = &0) /\
     (!z:real.
        f z =
        real_of_int a * z pow 4 +
        real_of_int b * z pow 3 +
        real_of_int c * z pow 2 +
        real_of_int d * z +
        real_of_int e) /\
     (!z:real.
        f z =
        real_of_int a *
        (z - r1) * (z - r2) * (z - r3) * (z - r4))
     ==>
     (is_rational (r1 + r2) /\ ~(r1 + r2 = r3 + r4)
      ==> is_rational (r1 * r2))`;;

title: putnam_2003_b4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b4:
;; rationality of the sum of two roots of an integer quartic, when distinct
;; from the other two roots' sum, forces their product to be rational. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Every root of the nonzero integer quartic is real algebraic. Every finite
;; tuple of real algebraic numbers lies in Q(alpha) for one real algebraic
;; alpha. A rational polynomial and rational isolating interval encode alpha,
;; and rational polynomials in alpha encode the four roots. Sturm-Tarski
;; queries decide equality exactly, so this covers all source root tuples
;; without restricting them to rational roots.
;;
;; Expanding a*(z-r1)*(z-r2)*(z-r3)*(z-r4) gives the four Vieta identities
;; used below, which are equivalent to the source's universal polynomial
;; identity. If s=r1+r2 is rational and t=r3+r4 differs from s, then
;;
;;   u = c/a-s*t = r1*r2+r3*r4,
;;   v = -d/a   = (r1*r2)*t+(r3*r4)*s,
;;   r1*r2      = (v-s*u)/(t-s).
;;
;; The rational witness s occurs universally in the ACL2 statement:
;; forall s, (s rational and s=r1+r2) implies the conclusion. This is
;; logically equivalent to the source implication whose antecedent says that
;; r1+r2 is rational. The conclusion keeps its rational witness existentially
;; quantified inside a separate predicate.

;; Rational polynomials use descending coefficient order.

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-p (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (and (rationalp (car p))
           (putnam-2003-b4-rp-p (cdr p)))
    (equal p nil)))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (if (equal (car p) 0)
          (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize (cdr p))
        p)
    nil))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-neg (p)
  (if (consp p)
      (cons (- (car p))
            (putnam-2003-b4-rp-neg (cdr p)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-add-raw (p q)
  (declare (xargs :measure (+ (acl2-count p) (acl2-count q))))
  (cond
   ((endp p) q)
   ((endp q) p)
   ((< (len p) (len q))
    (cons (car q)
          (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add-raw p (cdr q))))
   ((< (len q) (len p))
    (cons (car p)
          (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add-raw (cdr p) q)))
   (t
    (cons (+ (car p) (car q))
          (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add-raw (cdr p) (cdr q))))))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-add (p q)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize
   (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add-raw p q)))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-sub (p q)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add p (putnam-2003-b4-rp-neg q)))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-scale (c p)
  (if (consp p)
      (cons (* c (car p))
            (putnam-2003-b4-rp-scale c (cdr p)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-zeroes (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (cons 0 (putnam-2003-b4-zeroes (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-scale-shift (c p shift)
  (append (putnam-2003-b4-rp-scale c p)
          (putnam-2003-b4-zeroes shift)))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul-raw (p q)
  (if (consp p)
      (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
       (putnam-2003-b4-rp-scale-shift
        (car p) q (len (cdr p)))
       (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul-raw (cdr p) q))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul (p q)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize
   (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul-raw p q)))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-eval-aux (p x accumulator)
  (if (consp p)
      (putnam-2003-b4-rp-eval-aux
       (cdr p) x (+ (* accumulator x) (car p)))
    accumulator))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-eval (p x)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-eval-aux p x 0))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-derivative-aux (p degree)
  (if (consp p)
      (if (zp degree)
          nil
        (cons (* degree (car p))
              (putnam-2003-b4-rp-derivative-aux
               (cdr p) (- degree 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-derivative (p)
  (let ((p (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize p)))
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-derivative-aux
      p (nfix (- (len p) 1))))))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-rem-fuel (p q fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((p (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize p))
        (q (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize q)))
    (if (or (zp fuel)
            (endp q)
            (< (len p) (len q)))
        p
      (putnam-2003-b4-rp-rem-fuel
       (putnam-2003-b4-rp-sub
        p
        (putnam-2003-b4-rp-scale-shift
         (/ (car p) (car q))
         q
         (- (len p) (len q))))
       q
       (- fuel 1)))))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-rem (p q)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-rem-fuel
   p q (+ 1 (len (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize p)))))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-sturm-tail (previous current fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((current (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize current)))
    (if (or (zp fuel) (endp current))
        nil
      (cons
       current
       (putnam-2003-b4-rp-sturm-tail
        current
        (putnam-2003-b4-rp-neg
         (putnam-2003-b4-rp-rem previous current))
        (- fuel 1))))))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-sturm-sequence (p q)
  (let ((p (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize p))
        (q (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize q)))
    (if (endp p)
        nil
      (cons
       p
       (if (endp q)
           nil
         (cons
          q
          (putnam-2003-b4-rp-sturm-tail
           p q (+ 1 (len p) (len q)))))))))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rational-sign (x)
  (cond ((< x 0) -1)
        ((< 0 x) 1)
        (t 0)))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-variations-aux
    (polynomials x previous-sign)
  (if (consp polynomials)
      (let ((sign
             (putnam-2003-b4-rational-sign
              (putnam-2003-b4-rp-eval (car polynomials) x))))
        (if (equal sign 0)
            (putnam-2003-b4-rp-variations-aux
             (cdr polynomials) x previous-sign)
          (+ (if (and (not (equal previous-sign 0))
                      (not (equal sign previous-sign)))
                 1
               0)
             (putnam-2003-b4-rp-variations-aux
              (cdr polynomials) x sign))))
    0))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-variations (polynomials x)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-variations-aux polynomials x 0))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-cauchy-index (p q lower upper)
  (let ((sequence
         (putnam-2003-b4-rp-sturm-sequence p q)))
    (- (putnam-2003-b4-rp-variations sequence lower)
       (putnam-2003-b4-rp-variations sequence upper))))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-rp-root-count (p lower upper)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-cauchy-index
   p (putnam-2003-b4-rp-derivative p) lower upper))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-primitive-p (primitive lower upper)
  (and
   (putnam-2003-b4-rp-p primitive)
   (consp (putnam-2003-b4-rp-normalize primitive))
   (rationalp lower)
   (rationalp upper)
   (< lower upper)
   (not (equal (putnam-2003-b4-rp-eval primitive lower) 0))
   (not (equal (putnam-2003-b4-rp-eval primitive upper) 0))
   (equal
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-root-count primitive lower upper)
    1)
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-cauchy-index
      primitive
      (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul
       (putnam-2003-b4-rp-derivative primitive)
       (putnam-2003-b4-rp-derivative primitive))
      lower
      upper)
     0))))

;; For the isolated simple root alpha, this query is sign(g(alpha)).
(defun putnam-2003-b4-alg-sign (primitive lower upper g)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-cauchy-index
   primitive
   (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-derivative primitive)
    g)
   lower
   upper))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-alg-equal-p
    (primitive lower upper left right)
  (equal
   (putnam-2003-b4-alg-sign
    primitive lower upper
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-sub left right))
   0))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-root-sum (r1 r2 r3 r4)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
   r1
   (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
    r2 (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add r3 r4))))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-pair-sum (r1 r2 r3 r4)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
   (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r1 r2)
   (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r1 r3)
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r1 r4)
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
      (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r2 r3)
      (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
       (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r2 r4)
       (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r3 r4)))))))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-triple-sum (r1 r2 r3 r4)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
   (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r1 r2) r3)
   (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r1 r2) r4)
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul
      (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r1 r3) r4)
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul
      (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r2 r3) r4)))))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-root-product (r1 r2 r3 r4)
  (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul
   (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r1 r2)
   (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r3 r4)))

(defun putnam-2003-b4-vieta-p
    (primitive lower upper a b c d e r1 r2 r3 r4)
  (and
   (putnam-2003-b4-alg-equal-p
    primitive lower upper
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-scale
      a (putnam-2003-b4-root-sum r1 r2 r3 r4))
     (list b))
    nil)
   (putnam-2003-b4-alg-equal-p
    primitive lower upper
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-sub
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-scale
      a (putnam-2003-b4-pair-sum r1 r2 r3 r4))
     (list c))
    nil)
   (putnam-2003-b4-alg-equal-p
    primitive lower upper
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-scale
      a (putnam-2003-b4-triple-sum r1 r2 r3 r4))
     (list d))
    nil)
   (putnam-2003-b4-alg-equal-p
    primitive lower upper
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-sub
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-scale
      a (putnam-2003-b4-root-product r1 r2 r3 r4))
     (list e))
    nil)))

(defun-sk putnam-2003-b4-rational-product-p
    (primitive lower upper product)
  (exists
   (q)
   (and
    (rationalp q)
    (putnam-2003-b4-alg-equal-p
     primitive lower upper product (list q)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2003-b4-statement
    (primitive lower upper a b c d e r1 r2 r3 r4 s)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2003-b4-primitive-p primitive lower upper)
    (integerp a)
    (integerp b)
    (integerp c)
    (integerp d)
    (integerp e)
    (not (equal a 0))
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-p r1)
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-p r2)
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-p r3)
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-p r4)
    (putnam-2003-b4-vieta-p
     primitive lower upper a b c d e r1 r2 r3 r4)
    (rationalp s)
    (putnam-2003-b4-alg-equal-p
     primitive lower upper
     (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add r1 r2)
     (list s))
    (not
     (putnam-2003-b4-alg-equal-p
      primitive lower upper
      (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add r1 r2)
      (putnam-2003-b4-rp-add r3 r4))))
   (putnam-2003-b4-rational-product-p
    primitive lower upper
    (putnam-2003-b4-rp-mul r1 r2))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2003_b4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2003_b4): rationality of the product of two
-- roots of a quartic with integer coefficients under a rational root-sum
-- hypothesis. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

power :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
power reals x zero =
  oneR reals
power reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals x (power reals x n)

quarticValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  R ->
  R
quarticValue reals a b c d e z =
  add reals
    (add reals
      (add reals
        (add reals
          (multiply reals (fromInt reals a) (power reals z 4))
          (multiply reals (fromInt reals b) (power reals z 3)))
        (multiply reals (fromInt reals c) (power reals z 2)))
      (multiply reals (fromInt reals d) z))
    (fromInt reals e)

factorizedValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
factorizedValue reals a r1 r2 r3 r4 z =
  multiply reals
    (multiply reals
      (multiply reals
        (multiply reals
          (fromInt reals a)
          (subtract reals z r1))
        (subtract reals z r2))
      (subtract reals z r3))
    (subtract reals z r4)

IsRational :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
IsRational reals x =
  Exists Int
    (\ numerator ->
      Exists Int
        (\ denominator ->
          denominator != pos zero
          and
          x ==
          divide reals
            (fromInt reals numerator)
            (fromInt reals denominator)))

putnam-2003-b4 : Set1
putnam-2003-b4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (f : R -> R) ->
  (a b c d e : Int) ->
  (r1 r2 r3 r4 : R) ->
  a != pos zero ->
  ((z : R) ->
    f z == quarticValue reals a b c d e z) ->
  ((z : R) ->
    f z == factorizedValue reals a r1 r2 r3 r4 z) ->
  (IsRational reals (add reals r1 r2)
  and
  add reals r1 r2 != add reals r3 r4) ->
  IsRational reals (multiply reals r1 r2)

title: putnam_2003_b4
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b4:
  an integer-coefficient quartic with four real roots has rational pair-product
  when the corresponding pair-sum is rational and differs from the other
  pair-sum. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open integerTheory realTheory intrealTheory;

val putnam_2003_b4 =
  ``let rational =
      \x : real.
        ?p q : int.
          q <> 0 /\
          x = real_of_int p / real_of_int q
    in
      !a b c d e : int. !r1 r2 r3 r4 : real.
        a <> 0 /\
        (!z : real.
           real_of_int a * z pow 4 +
             real_of_int b * z pow 3 +
             real_of_int c * z pow 2 +
             real_of_int d * z +
             real_of_int e =
           real_of_int a *
             (z - r1) * (z - r2) * (z - r3) * (z - r4))
        ==>
        (rational (r1 + r2) /\ r1 + r2 <> r3 + r4
         ==>
         rational (r1 * r2))``;

title: putnam_2003_b4
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2003_b4: rationality of the product of two roots of an
  integer-coefficient quartic when their sum is rational and differs from
  the sum of the other two roots. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The integer coefficients a through e and real roots p, q, r, s correspond
  to a, b, c, d, e and r1, r2, r3, r4 in the ground-truth statements. The
  pointwise equality directly identifies the quartic polynomial with its
  four-real-root factorization. This eliminates the auxiliary function f
  definitionally: either source pair of equations implies this equality, and
  this equality recovers the source equations by taking f to be the displayed
  polynomial.

  Membership in QQ is exactly rationality of the real sum or product. The
  final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a b c d e p q r s x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2003-b4 $a |-
    A. a e. ZZ A. b e. ZZ A. c e. ZZ
      A. d e. ZZ A. e e. ZZ
        A. p e. RR A. q e. RR A. r e. RR A. s e. RR
          (
            (
              a =/= 0
              /\
              A. x e. RR
                (
                  (
                    (
                      (
                        (
                          ( a x. ( x ^ 4 ) )
                          +
                          ( b x. ( x ^ 3 ) )
                        )
                        +
                        ( c x. ( x ^ 2 ) )
                      )
                      +
                      ( d x. x )
                    )
                    +
                    e
                  )
                  =
                  (
                    (
                      (
                        ( a x. ( x - p ) )
                        x.
                        ( x - q )
                      )
                      x.
                      ( x - r )
                    )
                    x.
                    ( x - s )
                  )
                )
            )
            ->
            (
              (
                ( p + q ) e. QQ
                /\
                ( p + q ) =/= ( r + s )
              )
              ->
              ( p x. q ) e. QQ
            )
          )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2003_b4
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b4:
:: an integer-coefficient real quartic with four real roots has rational
:: pair-product when the corresponding pair-sum is rational and differs from
:: the complementary pair-sum. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    NUMBERS, XREAL_0, XCMPLX_0, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3,
    REAL_1, INT_1, NAT_1, ORDINAL1, NEWTON, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, RAT_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, REAL_1,
    NAT_1, INT_1, NEWTON, RAT_1;
  constructors RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, REAL_1, NAT_1, INT_1, NEWTON, RAT_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, NAT_1,
    INT_1, NEWTON, RAT_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for f being Function of REAL,REAL,
      a,b,c,d,e being Integer,
      r1,r2,r3,r4 being Real st
    a <> 0 &
    (for z being Real holds
      f.z =
        (a qua Real) * (z |^ 4) +
        (b qua Real) * (z |^ 3) +
        (c qua Real) * (z |^ 2) +
        (d qua Real) * z +
        (e qua Real)) &
    (for z being Real holds
      f.z =
        (a qua Real) * (z - r1) * (z - r2) * (z - r3) * (z - r4))
  holds
    (r1 + r2 in RAT & r1 + r2 <> r3 + r4)
      implies r1 * r2 in RAT
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2003_b4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b4:
% an integer-coefficient quartic with four real roots has rational root
% product r1*r2 when the pair sum r1+r2 is rational and differs from r3+r4.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2003_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  putnam_2003_b4: bool =
    FORALL
        (f: real_function),
        (a, b, c, d, e: int),
        (r1, r2, r3, r4: real):
      (a /= 0
        AND (FORALL (z: real):
          f(z) =
            a * z ^ 4
              + b * z ^ 3
              + c * z ^ 2
              + d * z
              + e)
        AND (FORALL (z: real):
          f(z) =
            a * (z - r1) * (z - r2)
              * (z - r3) * (z - r4))
        AND rational?(r1 + r2)
        AND r1 + r2 /= r3 + r4)
      IMPLIES rational?(r1 * r2)
END putnam_2003_b4

title: putnam_2003_b5
content:
import Mathlib

open MvPolynomial Set Nat

/--
Let $A,B$, and $C$ be equidistant points on the circumference of a circle of unit radius centered at $O$, and let $P$ be any point in the circle's interior. Let $a, b, c$ be the distance from $P$ to $A, B, C$, respectively. Show that there is a triangle with side lengths $a, b, c$, and that the area of this triangle depends only on the distance from $P$ to $O$.
-/
theorem putnam_2003_b5
(A B C : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
(hABC : dist 0 A = 1 ∧ dist 0 B = 1 ∧ dist 0 C = 1 ∧ dist A B = dist A C ∧ dist A B = dist B C ∧ dist A B ≠ 0)
: (∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, ∀ P : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), dist 0 P < 1 → ∃ X Y Z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2),
      dist X Y = dist P A ∧ dist Y Z = dist P B ∧ dist X Z = dist P C ∧
      (MeasureTheory.volume (convexHull ℝ {X, Y, Z})).toReal = f (dist 0 P)) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2003_b5
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b5:
   for a point inside the unit circle and three distinct pairwise equidistant
   points on its circumference, the distances to those points are the side
   lengths of a triangle whose area depends only on the point's distance from
   the center. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2003_b5_point : Type := (R * R)%type.

Definition putnam_2003_b5_origin : putnam_2003_b5_point := (0, 0).

Definition putnam_2003_b5_distance
    (p q : putnam_2003_b5_point) : R :=
  sqrt ((fst p - fst q) ^ 2 + (snd p - snd q) ^ 2).

Definition putnam_2003_b5_signed_twice_area
    (a b c : putnam_2003_b5_point) : R :=
  (fst b - fst a) * (snd c - snd a) -
  (snd b - snd a) * (fst c - fst a).

Definition putnam_2003_b5_triangle_area
    (a b c : putnam_2003_b5_point) : R :=
  Rabs (putnam_2003_b5_signed_twice_area a b c) / 2.

Theorem putnam_2003_b5
    (A B C : putnam_2003_b5_point)
    (hABC :
      putnam_2003_b5_distance putnam_2003_b5_origin A = 1 /\
      putnam_2003_b5_distance putnam_2003_b5_origin B = 1 /\
      putnam_2003_b5_distance putnam_2003_b5_origin C = 1 /\
      putnam_2003_b5_distance A B = putnam_2003_b5_distance A C /\
      putnam_2003_b5_distance A B = putnam_2003_b5_distance B C /\
      putnam_2003_b5_distance A B <> 0) :
  exists f : R -> R,
    forall P : putnam_2003_b5_point,
      putnam_2003_b5_distance putnam_2003_b5_origin P < 1 ->
      exists X Y Z : putnam_2003_b5_point,
        putnam_2003_b5_distance X Y = putnam_2003_b5_distance P A /\
        putnam_2003_b5_distance Y Z = putnam_2003_b5_distance P B /\
        putnam_2003_b5_distance X Z = putnam_2003_b5_distance P C /\
        putnam_2003_b5_triangle_area X Y Z =
          f (putnam_2003_b5_distance putnam_2003_b5_origin P).
Admitted.

  shows "\<exists>f::real\<Rightarrow>real. \<forall>P::real^2. dist 0 P < 1 \<longrightarrow> (\<exists>X Y Z::real^2.
  dist X Y = dist P A \<and> dist Y Z = dist P B \<and> dist X Z = dist P C \<and>

title: putnam_2003_b5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b5:
  a triangle whose side lengths are the distances from an interior point to
  the vertices of a unit-circle equilateral triangle has area depending only
  on the point's distance from the center. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let edist =
     \(p:real#real) (q:real#real).
       sqrt ((FST p - FST q) pow 2 + (SND p - SND q) pow 2) in
   let triangle_area =
     \(x:real#real) (y:real#real) (z:real#real).
       abs ((FST y - FST x) * (SND z - SND x) -
            (SND y - SND x) * (FST z - FST x)) / &2 in
   !A B C:real#real.
     edist (&0,&0) A = &1 /\
     edist (&0,&0) B = &1 /\
     edist (&0,&0) C = &1 /\
     edist A B = edist A C /\
     edist A B = edist B C /\
     ~(edist A B = &0)
     ==> ?f:real->real.
           !P:real#real.
             edist (&0,&0) P < &1
             ==> ?X Y Z:real#real.
                   edist X Y = edist P A /\
                   edist Y Z = edist P B /\
                   edist X Z = edist P C /\
                   triangle_area X Y Z = f (edist (&0,&0) P)`;;

title: putnam_2003_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b5:
;; for three equidistant noncoincident points on the unit circle, the
;; distances from an interior point are the side lengths of a triangle whose
;; area depends only on the point's distance from the origin. This file
;; contains no proof and does not prescribe the area function or a triangle.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The scalar symbols present an arbitrary real-closed ordered field. The
;; theorem is semialgebraic after eliminating the auxiliary area function as
;; explained below, so completeness of real-closed fields makes this
;; presentation equivalent to the statement over the real numbers.

(defstub p2003b5-scalar-p (x) t)
(defstub p2003b5-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub p2003b5-multiply-op (x y) t)
(defstub p2003b5-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub p2003b5-inverse-op (x) t)
(defstub p2003b5-less-op (x y) t)
(defstub p2003b5-zero () t)
(defstub p2003b5-one () t)

(defun p2003b5-add (x y)
  (p2003b5-add-op x y))

(defun p2003b5-multiply (x y)
  (p2003b5-multiply-op x y))

(defun p2003b5-negate (x)
  (p2003b5-negate-op x))

(defun p2003b5-inverse (x)
  (p2003b5-inverse-op x))

(defun p2003b5-subtract (x y)
  (p2003b5-add x (p2003b5-negate y)))

(defun p2003b5-less (x y)
  (if (p2003b5-less-op x y) t nil))

(defun p2003b5-nonnegative-p (x)
  (and
   (p2003b5-scalar-p x)
   (not (p2003b5-less x (p2003b5-zero)))))

(defun p2003b5-positive-p (x)
  (and
   (p2003b5-scalar-p x)
   (p2003b5-less (p2003b5-zero) x)))

(defun-sk p2003b5-field-laws-p ()
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p2003b5-scalar-p x)
      (p2003b5-scalar-p y)
      (p2003b5-scalar-p z))
     (and
      (p2003b5-scalar-p (p2003b5-add x y))
      (p2003b5-scalar-p (p2003b5-multiply x y))
      (p2003b5-scalar-p (p2003b5-negate x))
      (implies
       (not (equal x (p2003b5-zero)))
       (p2003b5-scalar-p (p2003b5-inverse x)))
      (equal
       (p2003b5-add (p2003b5-add x y) z)
       (p2003b5-add x (p2003b5-add y z)))
      (equal
       (p2003b5-add x y)
       (p2003b5-add y x))
      (equal
       (p2003b5-add x (p2003b5-zero))
       x)
      (equal
       (p2003b5-add x (p2003b5-negate x))
       (p2003b5-zero))
      (equal
       (p2003b5-multiply
        (p2003b5-multiply x y) z)
       (p2003b5-multiply
        x (p2003b5-multiply y z)))
      (equal
       (p2003b5-multiply x y)
       (p2003b5-multiply y x))
      (equal
       (p2003b5-multiply x (p2003b5-one))
       x)
      (implies
       (not (equal x (p2003b5-zero)))
       (equal
        (p2003b5-multiply x (p2003b5-inverse x))
        (p2003b5-one)))
      (equal
       (p2003b5-multiply x (p2003b5-add y z))
       (p2003b5-add
        (p2003b5-multiply x y)
        (p2003b5-multiply x z)))))))

(defun-sk p2003b5-order-laws-p ()
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p2003b5-scalar-p x)
      (p2003b5-scalar-p y)
      (p2003b5-scalar-p z))
     (and
      (not (p2003b5-less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (p2003b5-less x y)
       (p2003b5-less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (p2003b5-less x y)
        (p2003b5-less y z))
       (p2003b5-less x z))
      (implies
       (p2003b5-less x y)
       (p2003b5-less
        (p2003b5-add x z)
        (p2003b5-add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (p2003b5-less (p2003b5-zero) x)
        (p2003b5-less (p2003b5-zero) y))
       (p2003b5-less
        (p2003b5-zero)
        (p2003b5-multiply x y)))))))

(defun p2003b5-carrier-list-p (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and
       (p2003b5-scalar-p (car coefficients))
       (p2003b5-carrier-list-p (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

;; Coefficients are stored in increasing degree order.
(defun p2003b5-polynomial-value (coefficients x)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (p2003b5-add
       (car coefficients)
       (p2003b5-multiply
        x
        (p2003b5-polynomial-value
         (cdr coefficients) x)))
    (p2003b5-zero)))

(defun p2003b5-polynomial-p (coefficients)
  (and
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (p2003b5-carrier-list-p coefficients)))

(defun p2003b5-odd-degree-polynomial-p (coefficients)
  (and
   (p2003b5-polynomial-p coefficients)
   (consp coefficients)
   ;; Degree LEN-1 is odd exactly when LEN is even.
   (evenp (len coefficients))
   (not
    (equal
     (car (last coefficients))
     (p2003b5-zero)))))

(defun-sk p2003b5-square-root-exists-p (x)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (p2003b5-scalar-p root)
     (equal
      (p2003b5-multiply root root)
      x))))

(defun-sk p2003b5-positive-square-roots-p ()
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p2003b5-positive-p x)
     (p2003b5-square-root-exists-p x))))

(defun-sk p2003b5-polynomial-root-exists-p (coefficients)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (p2003b5-scalar-p root)
     (equal
      (p2003b5-polynomial-value coefficients root)
      (p2003b5-zero)))))

(defun-sk p2003b5-odd-polynomial-roots-p ()
  (forall (coefficients)
    (implies
     (p2003b5-odd-degree-polynomial-p coefficients)
     (p2003b5-polynomial-root-exists-p
      coefficients))))

(defun p2003b5-real-closed-field-p ()
  (and
   (p2003b5-scalar-p (p2003b5-zero))
   (p2003b5-scalar-p (p2003b5-one))
   (not (equal (p2003b5-zero) (p2003b5-one)))
   (p2003b5-less (p2003b5-zero) (p2003b5-one))
   (p2003b5-field-laws-p)
   (p2003b5-order-laws-p)
   (p2003b5-positive-square-roots-p)
   (p2003b5-odd-polynomial-roots-p)))

(defun p2003b5-square (x)
  (p2003b5-multiply x x))

(defun p2003b5-two ()
  (p2003b5-add
   (p2003b5-one)
   (p2003b5-one)))

(defun p2003b5-point-p (point)
  (and
   (true-listp point)
   (equal (len point) 2)
   (p2003b5-scalar-p (nth 0 point))
   (p2003b5-scalar-p (nth 1 point))))

(defun p2003b5-point-subtract (left right)
  (list
   (p2003b5-subtract
    (nth 0 left) (nth 0 right))
   (p2003b5-subtract
    (nth 1 left) (nth 1 right))))

(defun p2003b5-dot (left right)
  (p2003b5-add
   (p2003b5-multiply
    (nth 0 left) (nth 0 right))
   (p2003b5-multiply
    (nth 1 left) (nth 1 right))))

(defun p2003b5-norm-squared (point)
  (p2003b5-dot point point))

(defun p2003b5-distance-squared (left right)
  (p2003b5-norm-squared
   (p2003b5-point-subtract left right)))

(defun p2003b5-cross (left right)
  (p2003b5-subtract
   (p2003b5-multiply
    (nth 0 left) (nth 1 right))
   (p2003b5-multiply
    (nth 1 left) (nth 0 right))))

(defun p2003b5-twice-oriented-area (x y z)
  (p2003b5-cross
   (p2003b5-point-subtract y x)
   (p2003b5-point-subtract z x)))

(defun p2003b5-configuration-p (a b c)
  (and
   (p2003b5-point-p a)
   (p2003b5-point-p b)
   (p2003b5-point-p c)
   (equal
    (p2003b5-norm-squared a)
    (p2003b5-one))
   (equal
    (p2003b5-norm-squared b)
    (p2003b5-one))
   (equal
    (p2003b5-norm-squared c)
    (p2003b5-one))
   (equal
    (p2003b5-distance-squared a b)
    (p2003b5-distance-squared a c))
   (equal
    (p2003b5-distance-squared a b)
    (p2003b5-distance-squared b c))
   (not
    (equal
     (p2003b5-distance-squared a b)
     (p2003b5-zero)))))

(defun p2003b5-triangle-witness-p
    (a b c p area x y z)
  (and
   (p2003b5-point-p x)
   (p2003b5-point-p y)
   (p2003b5-point-p z)
   (p2003b5-scalar-p area)
   (p2003b5-nonnegative-p area)
   (equal
    (p2003b5-distance-squared x y)
    (p2003b5-distance-squared p a))
   (equal
    (p2003b5-distance-squared y z)
    (p2003b5-distance-squared p b))
   (equal
    (p2003b5-distance-squared x z)
    (p2003b5-distance-squared p c))
   ;; Euclidean triangle area is |cross(y-x,z-x)| / 2. Both sides are
   ;; nonnegative, so equality of their squares is exactly area equality.
   (equal
    (p2003b5-square
     (p2003b5-multiply
      (p2003b5-two) area))
    (p2003b5-square
     (p2003b5-twice-oriented-area x y z)))))

(defun-sk p2003b5-triangle-exists-p
    (a b c p area)
  (exists (x y z)
    (p2003b5-triangle-witness-p
     a b c p area x y z)))

(defun-sk p2003b5-area-valid-for-radius-squared-p
    (a b c radius-squared area)
  (forall (p)
    (implies
     (and
      (p2003b5-point-p p)
      (equal
       (p2003b5-norm-squared p)
       radius-squared))
     (p2003b5-triangle-exists-p
      a b c p area))))

(defun p2003b5-area-witness-p
    (a b c radius-squared area)
  (and
   (p2003b5-scalar-p area)
   (p2003b5-nonnegative-p area)
   (p2003b5-area-valid-for-radius-squared-p
    a b c radius-squared area)))

(defun-sk p2003b5-area-exists-for-radius-squared-p
    (a b c radius-squared)
  (exists (area)
    (p2003b5-area-witness-p
     a b c radius-squared area)))

;; Replacing radius r by radius-squared rho is exact on 0 <= r < 1 because
;; r |-> r^2 is a bijection there. Thus
;;
;;   exists f, forall P, exists triangle with area f(||P||)
;;
;; is equivalent (using ordinary choice) to the first-order statement below:
;; for every rho in [0,1), one common area works for every P with ||P||^2=rho.
;; This preserves the source quantifiers without hard-coding the solved area.

(defun-sk p2003b5-all-interior-radii-p (a b c)
  (forall (radius-squared)
    (implies
     (and
      (p2003b5-scalar-p radius-squared)
      (p2003b5-nonnegative-p radius-squared)
      (p2003b5-less
       radius-squared
       (p2003b5-one)))
     (p2003b5-area-exists-for-radius-squared-p
      a b c radius-squared))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2003-b5-statement (a b c)
  (implies
   (and
    (p2003b5-real-closed-field-p)
    (p2003b5-configuration-p a b c))
   (p2003b5-all-interior-radii-p a b c)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2003_b5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2003_b5): existence of a triangle whose side
-- lengths are the distances from an interior point to three equally spaced
-- unit-circle points, with area depending only on the point's radius.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

record StandardSquareRoot
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    squareRoot : R -> R

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      square reals (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals x (zeroR reals) ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR reals
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) y ->
      square reals y == x ->
      squareRoot x == y

open StandardSquareRoot

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

origin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R
origin reals =
  point (zeroR reals) (zeroR reals)

squaredDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
squaredDistance reals p q =
  add reals
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q)))
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)))

distance :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardSquareRoot reals ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
distance reals roots p q =
  squareRoot roots (squaredDistance reals p q)

two :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
two reals =
  fromNat reals (suc (suc zero))

half :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
half reals =
  inverse reals (two reals)

doubleSignedArea :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
doubleSignedArea reals a b c =
  subtract reals
    (multiply reals
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate b) (x-coordinate a))
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate c) (y-coordinate a)))
    (multiply reals
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate b) (y-coordinate a))
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate c) (x-coordinate a)))

triangleArea :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardSquareRoot reals ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
triangleArea reals roots a b c =
  multiply reals
    (half reals)
    (squareRoot roots
      (square reals (doubleSignedArea reals a b c)))

module Putnam2003B5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (roots : StandardSquareRoot reals) where

  EquilateralUnitCircleConfiguration :
    Point R ->
    Point R ->
    Point R ->
    Set
  EquilateralUnitCircleConfiguration A B C =
    distance reals roots (origin reals) A == oneR reals
    and
    distance reals roots (origin reals) B == oneR reals
    and
    distance reals roots (origin reals) C == oneR reals
    and
    distance reals roots A B == distance reals roots A C
    and
    distance reals roots A B == distance reals roots B C
    and
    distance reals roots A B != zeroR reals

  HasRequiredTriangle :
    Point R ->
    Point R ->
    Point R ->
    (R -> R) ->
    Point R ->
    Set
  HasRequiredTriangle A B C f P =
    Exists (Point R)
      (\ X ->
        Exists (Point R)
          (\ Y ->
            Exists (Point R)
              (\ Z ->
                distance reals roots X Y == distance reals roots P A
                and
                distance reals roots Y Z == distance reals roots P B
                and
                distance reals roots X Z == distance reals roots P C
                and
                triangleArea reals roots X Y Z ==
                  f (distance reals roots (origin reals) P))))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (A B C : Point R) ->
    EquilateralUnitCircleConfiguration A B C ->
    Exists (R -> R)
      (\ f ->
        (P : Point R) ->
        StrictLess reals
          (distance reals roots (origin reals) P)
          (oneR reals) ->
        HasRequiredTriangle A B C f P)

putnam-2003-b5 : Set1
putnam-2003-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (roots : StandardSquareRoot reals) ->
  Putnam2003B5Statement.proposition reals roots

title: putnam_2003_b5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b5:
  a triangle whose side lengths are the distances from an interior point to
  three equidistant points on the unit circle has area depending only on the
  interior point's distance from the center. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pairTheory realTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2003_b5 =
  ``let origin = (0, 0) : real # real in
    let dist =
      \P Q : real # real.
        sqrt ((FST P - FST Q) pow 2 + (SND P - SND Q) pow 2)
    in
    let triangle_area =
      \X Y Z : real # real.
        abs
          ((FST Y - FST X) * (SND Z - SND X) -
           (SND Y - SND X) * (FST Z - FST X)) / 2
    in
      !A B C : real # real.
        dist origin A = 1 /\
        dist origin B = 1 /\
        dist origin C = 1 /\
        dist A B = dist A C /\
        dist A B = dist B C /\
        dist A B <> 0
        ==>
        ?f : real -> real.
          !P : real # real.
            dist origin P < 1
            ==>
            ?X Y Z : real # real.
              dist X Y = dist P A /\
              dist Y Z = dist P B /\
              dist X Z = dist P C /\
              triangle_area X Y Z = f (dist origin P)``;

title: putnam_2003_b5
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2003_b5: distances from an interior point to the vertices of a
  nondegenerate equilateral triangle on the unit circle are side lengths of
  a triangle whose area depends only on the point's distance from the center.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P03B5R2 is the real Euclidean plane, P03B5Zero is its origin, and
  P03B5Dist is ordinary Euclidean distance. P03B5Hull is exactly the convex
  hull of three points through nonnegative barycentric coordinates, and
  P03B5Area is its two-dimensional Lebesgue measure via set.mm's voln.

  The final assertion universally quantifies A, B, and C, retains their
  unit-circle, equal-distance, and nondegeneracy assumptions, and internally
  quantifies the total real function f. For every point P in the open unit
  disk, X, Y, and Z remain existentially quantified and realize the three
  prescribed side lengths, with area equal to f at the radial distance of P.
  Every declaration below is an unproved $a statement; there is no $p proof.
$)

$c P03B5I P03B5R2 P03B5Zero P03B5Dist P03B5Hull P03B5Area $.

p03b5-index-syntax $a class P03B5I $.
p03b5-plane-syntax $a class P03B5R2 $.
p03b5-zero-syntax $a class P03B5Zero $.
p03b5-distance-syntax $a class ( P03B5Dist A B ) $.
p03b5-hull-syntax $a class ( P03B5Hull A B C ) $.
p03b5-area-syntax $a class ( P03B5Area A B C ) $.

p03b5-index-definition $a |- P03B5I = ( 1 ... 2 ) $.

p03b5-plane-definition $a |- P03B5R2 = ( RR ^m P03B5I ) $.

p03b5-zero-definition $a |- P03B5Zero =
  ( j e. P03B5I |-> 0 )
$.

${
  $d A B j $.

  p03b5-distance-definition $a |- (
    P03B5Dist A B
  ) = (
    sqrt
    `
    (
      sum_ j e. P03B5I
        ( ( ( A ` j ) - ( B ` j ) ) ^ 2 )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d A B C j u v w x $.

  p03b5-hull-definition $a |- (
    P03B5Hull A B C
  ) = {
    x e. P03B5R2 |
    E. u e. RR E. v e. RR E. w e. RR
      (
        (
          0 <_ u
          /\
          (
            0 <_ v
            /\
            0 <_ w
          )
        )
        /\
        (
          ( ( u + v ) + w ) = 1
          /\
          x =
            (
              j e. P03B5I |->
                (
                  (
                    ( u x. ( A ` j ) )
                    +
                    ( v x. ( B ` j ) )
                  )
                  +
                  ( w x. ( C ` j ) )
                )
            )
        )
      )
  } $.
$}

p03b5-area-definition $a |- (
  P03B5Area A B C
) = (
  ( voln ` P03B5I )
  `
  ( P03B5Hull A B C )
) $.

${
  $d A B C P X Y Z f $.

  putnambench-putnam-2003-b5 $a |- (
    A. A e. P03B5R2
    A. B e. P03B5R2
    A. C e. P03B5R2
      (
        (
          (
            ( P03B5Dist P03B5Zero A ) = 1
            /\
            (
              ( P03B5Dist P03B5Zero B ) = 1
              /\
              ( P03B5Dist P03B5Zero C ) = 1
            )
          )
          /\
          (
            ( P03B5Dist A B ) = ( P03B5Dist A C )
            /\
            (
              ( P03B5Dist A B ) = ( P03B5Dist B C )
              /\
              ( P03B5Dist A B ) =/= 0
            )
          )
        )
        ->
        E. f e. ( RR ^m RR )
          A. P e. P03B5R2
            (
              ( P03B5Dist P03B5Zero P ) < 1
              ->
              E. X e. P03B5R2
              E. Y e. P03B5R2
              E. Z e. P03B5R2
                (
                  ( P03B5Dist X Y ) = ( P03B5Dist P A )
                  /\
                  (
                    ( P03B5Dist Y Z ) = ( P03B5Dist P B )
                    /\
                    (
                      ( P03B5Dist X Z ) = ( P03B5Dist P C )
                      /\
                      ( P03B5Area X Y Z )
                      =
                      ( f ` ( P03B5Dist P03B5Zero P ) )
                    )
                  )
                )
            )
      )
  ) $.
$}

title: putnam_2003_b5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b5:
% triangle side lengths given by distances from an interior point to the
% vertices of a unit-circle equilateral triangle, with area depending only on
% the point's distance from the center. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2003_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]

  zero_point: point =
    (# x_coord := 0, y_coord := 0 #)

  squared_distance(P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q)) ^ 2
      + (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q)) ^ 2

  distance(P, Q: point): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (length: real):
        0 <= length
          AND length * length = squared_distance(P, Q))

  cross_from(P, Q, R: point): real =
    (x_coord(Q) - x_coord(P)) * (y_coord(R) - y_coord(P))
      - (y_coord(Q) - y_coord(P)) * (x_coord(R) - x_coord(P))

  triangle_area(P, Q, R: point): real =
    abs(cross_from(P, Q, R)) / 2

  unit_equilateral(A, B, C: point): bool =
    distance(zero_point, A) = 1
      AND distance(zero_point, B) = 1
      AND distance(zero_point, C) = 1
      AND distance(A, B) = distance(A, C)
      AND distance(A, B) = distance(B, C)
      AND distance(A, B) /= 0

  putnam_2003_b5: bool =
    FORALL (A, B, C: point):
      unit_equilateral(A, B, C)
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (area_by_radius: [real -> real]):
          FORALL (P: point):
            distance(zero_point, P) < 1
            IMPLIES
              EXISTS (X, Y, Z: point):
                distance(X, Y) = distance(P, A)
                  AND distance(Y, Z) = distance(P, B)
                  AND distance(X, Z) = distance(P, C)
                  AND triangle_area(X, Y, Z)
                    = area_by_radius(distance(zero_point, P))
END putnam_2003_b5

import Mathlib

open MvPolynomial Set Nat

/--
Let  $f(x)$  be  a continuous real-valued function defined on the interval $[0,1]$. Show that \[ \int_0^1 \int_0^1 | f(x) + f(y) |\,dx\,dy \geq \int_0^1 |f(x)|\,dx. \]
-/
theorem putnam_2003_b6
(f : ℝ → ℝ)
(hf : Continuous f)
: (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..1, (∫ y in (0 : ℝ)..1, |f x + f y|)) ≥ (∫ x in (0 : ℝ)..1, |f x|) :=
sorry

putnam_2003_b6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b6:
;; every continuous real-valued function on the unit interval satisfies the
;; stated lower bound comparing a double integral of |f(x)+f(y)| with the
;; integral of |f(x)|. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A code is a rational polygonal function on [0,1], with strictly increasing
;; rational knots beginning at 0 and ending at 1. Extending it constantly
;; outside [0,1] gives a globally continuous real function, as required by the
;; ground-truth statements.
;;
;; This is an exact counterexample-preserving encoding, not a restriction to
;; a fixed grid or a finite table. Rational polygonal functions with arbitrary
;; finite knot lists are uniformly dense in the continuous real functions on
;; [0,1]. If ||f-g||_infinity <= delta, then
;;
;;   | integral integral |f(x)+f(y)| - integral integral |g(x)+g(y)| |
;;     <= 2*delta
;;
;; and
;;
;;   | integral |f(x)| - integral |g(x)| | <= delta.
;;
;; Hence any strict failure of the source inequality survives a sufficiently
;; close rational polygonal approximation. Conversely, every code denotes a
;; source function. Thus universal validity for these codes is bidirectionally
;; equivalent to universal validity for the source continuous functions.
;;
;; All integrals below are exact rational integrals of the denoted polygonal
;; functions. On a pair of knot intervals, f(x)+f(y) is affine in (x,y).
;; The mixed second derivative of |z|^3 is 6*|z|, which gives the exact
;; four-corner formula used for a rectangle when both slopes are nonzero.

(defun putnam-2003-b6-point-p (point)
  (and
   (true-listp point)
   (equal (len point) 2)
   (rationalp (car point))
   (rationalp (cadr point))))

(defun putnam-2003-b6-point-x (point)
  (car point))

(defun putnam-2003-b6-point-y (point)
  (cadr point))

(defun putnam-2003-b6-last-point (points)
  (if (consp (cdr points))
      (putnam-2003-b6-last-point (cdr points))
    (car points)))

(defun putnam-2003-b6-points-p (points)
  (if (consp points)
      (and
       (putnam-2003-b6-point-p (car points))
       (putnam-2003-b6-points-p (cdr points)))
    (equal points nil)))

(defun putnam-2003-b6-strict-knots-p (points)
  (if (consp (cdr points))
      (and
       (< (putnam-2003-b6-point-x (car points))
          (putnam-2003-b6-point-x (cadr points)))
       (putnam-2003-b6-strict-knots-p (cdr points)))
    t))

(defun putnam-2003-b6-polygon-p (points)
  (and
   (true-listp points)
   (consp points)
   (consp (cdr points))
   (putnam-2003-b6-points-p points)
   (equal (putnam-2003-b6-point-x (car points)) 0)
   (equal
    (putnam-2003-b6-point-x
     (putnam-2003-b6-last-point points))
    1)

title: putnam_2003_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2003_b6): every continuous real function
-- satisfies the stated absolute-value integral inequality on the unit square.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

maximum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
maximum reals x y with order-total reals x y
... | left _ =
  y
... | right _ =
  x

absoluteValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
absoluteValue reals x =
  maximum reals x (negate reals x)

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ContinuousAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ContinuousAt {R} reals function point =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function point)
          epsilon
          (function x)))

Continuous :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
Continuous {R} reals function =
  (point : R) ->
  ContinuousAt reals function point

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

midpointRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
midpointRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
    halfStep =
      divide reals
        step
        (fromNat reals twoN)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (add reals
              (multiply reals
                (fromNat reals i)
                step)
              halfStep)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function value =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      midpointRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    value

record StandardIntervalIntegration
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    intervalIntegral :
      R ->
      R ->
      (R -> R) ->
      R

    interval-integral-is-riemann :
      (lower upper : R) ->
      (function : R -> R) ->
      Exists R
        (\ value ->
          IntervalIntegralValue reals
            lower
            upper
            function
            value) ->
      IntervalIntegralValue reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (intervalIntegral lower upper function)

open StandardIntervalIntegration

module Putnam2003B6Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (integration : StandardIntervalIntegration reals) where

  innerIntegrand :
    (R -> R) ->
    R ->
    R ->
    R
  innerIntegrand f x y =
    absoluteValue reals
      (add reals (f x) (f y))

  innerIntegral :
    (R -> R) ->
    R ->
    R
  innerIntegral f x =
    intervalIntegral integration
      (zeroR reals)
      (oneR reals)
      (innerIntegrand f x)

  doubleIntegral :
    (R -> R) ->
    R
  doubleIntegral f =
    intervalIntegral integration
      (zeroR reals)
      (oneR reals)
      (innerIntegral f)

  singleIntegral :
    (R -> R) ->
    R
  singleIntegral f =
    intervalIntegral integration
      (zeroR reals)
      (oneR reals)
      (\ x -> absoluteValue reals (f x))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (f : R -> R) ->
    Continuous reals f ->
    lessOrEqual reals
      (singleIntegral f)
      (doubleIntegral f)

putnam-2003-b6 : Set1
putnam-2003-b6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (integration : StandardIntervalIntegration reals) ->
  Putnam2003B6Statement.proposition
    reals
    integration

content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2003_b6:
% an integral inequality for the absolute value of the sum of two values of
% a continuous real function on the unit interval. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2003_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  continuous(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real), (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (y: real):
          abs(y - x) < delta IMPLIES
            abs(f(y) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  valid_unit_partition(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = 0
      AND points(count) = 1
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          points(index) < points(index + 1)

  valid_tags(
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index) <= tags(index)
          AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1)

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      f: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count - 1)
        + f(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_unit_interval_integral(
      f: real_function,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
        FORALL
            (points, tags: real_sequence),
            (count: nat):
          (valid_unit_partition(points, count)
            AND valid_tags(points, tags, count)
            AND mesh_less_than(points, count, mesh_bound))
          IMPLIES
            abs(
              riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count)
                - integral_value)
              < epsilon_value

  unit_interval_integral(f: real_function): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
        has_unit_interval_integral(f, integral_value))

  putnam_2003_b6: bool =
    FORALL (f: real_function):
      continuous(f) IMPLIES
        unit_interval_integral(
          LAMBDA (x: real):
            unit_interval_integral(
              LAMBDA (y: real):
                abs(f(x) + f(y))))
          >= unit_interval_integral(
            LAMBDA (x: real): abs(f(x)))
END putnam_2003_b6

title: putnam_2004_a1

import Mathlib

open Nat Topology Filter

abbrev putnam_2004_a1_solution : Prop := sorry
-- True
/--
Basketball star Shanille O'Keal's team statistician keeps track of the number, $S(N)$, of successful free throws she has made in her first $N$ attempts of the season. Early in the season, $S(N)$ was less than $80\%$ of $N$, but by the end of the season, $S(N)$ was more than $80\%$ of $N$. Was there necessarily a moment in between when $S(N)$ was exactly $80\%$ of $N$?
-/
theorem putnam_2004_a1
  (S : (ℕ → Fin 2) → ℕ → ℝ)
  (hS : ∀ attempts, ∀ N ≥ 1, S attempts N = (∑ i : Fin N, (attempts i).1) / N) :
  (∀ attempts a b,
    (1 ≤ a ∧ a < b ∧ S attempts a < 0.8 ∧ S attempts b > 0.8) →
      (∃ c : ℕ, a < c ∧ c < b ∧ S attempts c = 0.8))
  ↔ putnam_2004_a1_solution :=
sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_a1:
   a free-throw success rate crossing 80 percent between two attempt counts
   must equal 80 percent at an intermediate count. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals Arith.PeanoNat.

Open Scope R_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_2004_a1_successes
    (attempts : nat -> bool) (N : nat) : R :=
  match N with
  | O => 0
  | S n =>
      putnam_2004_a1_successes attempts n +
      if attempts n then 1 else 0
  end.

Definition putnam_2004_a1_solution : Prop := True.

Theorem putnam_2004_a1
    (S : (nat -> bool) -> nat -> R)
    (hS :
      forall (attempts : nat -> bool) (N : nat),
        (1 <= N)%nat ->
        S attempts N =
          putnam_2004_a1_successes attempts N / INR N) :
  (forall (attempts : nat -> bool) (a b : nat),
      (1 <= a)%nat /\
      (a < b)%nat /\
      S attempts a < 4 / 5 /\
      S attempts b > 4 / 5 ->
      exists c : nat,
        (a < c)%nat /\
        (c < b)%nat /\
        S attempts c = 4 / 5) <->
  putnam_2004_a1_solution.
Admitted.

title: putnam_2004_a1
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_a1:
;; a finite prefix of free-throw attempts whose success rate rises from below
;; 80 percent to above 80 percent has an intermediate prefix with success rate
;; exactly 80 percent. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For fixed a < b, the source proposition reads an attempt sequence only at
;; indices below b. ATTEMPTS therefore records exactly that length-b binary
;; prefix. Restricting any infinite Boolean (or Fin 2) sequence gives such a
;; list, and every such list extends to an infinite sequence by appending
;; zeros, so this is a bidirectional finite-prefix encoding rather than a
;; restriction to finite sequences.
;;
;; The hypothesis hS uniquely defines S at every positive index used here.
;; If C(N) is the number of successes in the first N attempts, comparison of
;; S(N) = C(N)/N with 0.8 = 4/5 is exactly comparison of 5*C(N) with 4*N.
;; Thus the integer formulas below definitionally eliminate both S and the
;; real-valued divisions without changing any inequality or equality.

(defun putnam-2004-a1-binary-prefix-p (attempts)
  (if (consp attempts)
      (and (or (equal (car attempts) 0)
               (equal (car attempts) 1))
           (putnam-2004-a1-binary-prefix-p (cdr attempts)))
    (equal attempts nil)))

(defun putnam-2004-a1-success-count (attempts terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (+ (if (equal (nth (- (nfix terms) 1) attempts) 1)
           1
         0)
       (putnam-2004-a1-success-count
        attempts (- (nfix terms) 1)))))

(defun putnam-2004-a1-rate-below-four-fifths-p
    (attempts terms)
  (< (* 5 (putnam-2004-a1-success-count attempts terms))
     (* 4 terms)))

(defun putnam-2004-a1-rate-above-four-fifths-p
    (attempts terms)
  (< (* 4 terms)
     (* 5 (putnam-2004-a1-success-count attempts terms))))

(defun putnam-2004-a1-rate-equals-four-fifths-p
    (attempts terms)
  (equal
   (* 5 (putnam-2004-a1-success-count attempts terms))
   (* 4 terms)))

;; Search every c with a < c < b. The existential witness stays internal to
;; the statement predicate.
(defun putnam-2004-a1-intermediate-through-p
    (attempts a candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (and (natp a)
           (natp candidate)
           (< a candidate))
      (or
       (putnam-2004-a1-rate-equals-four-fifths-p
        attempts candidate)
       (putnam-2004-a1-intermediate-through-p
        attempts a (- candidate 1)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2004-a1-intermediate-exists-p
    (attempts a b)
  (and (natp a)
       (natp b)
       (< a b)
       (putnam-2004-a1-intermediate-through-p
        attempts a (- b 1))))

;; The root predicate is universally closed over ATTEMPTS, A, and B by the
;; ACL2 statement-corpus convention. Since the annotated solution is True,
;; this implication is exactly the source's universally quantified
;; proposition iff its solution.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2004-a1-statement
    (attempts a b)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp a)
    (natp b)
    (<= 1 a)
    (< a b)
    (putnam-2004-a1-binary-prefix-p attempts)
    (equal (len attempts) b)
    (putnam-2004-a1-rate-below-four-fifths-p attempts a)
    (putnam-2004-a1-rate-above-four-fifths-p attempts b))
   (putnam-2004-a1-intermediate-exists-p attempts a b)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2004_a1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_a1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2004_a1): a basketball free-throw prefix success
-- rate that crosses 80 percent must equal 80 percent at an intermediate
-- attempt count. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2004A1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record Top : Set where
  constructor true

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

NatStrictLess : Nat -> Nat -> Set
NatStrictLess m n =
  suc m <=N n

data Bit : Set where
  zeroBit oneBit : Bit

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  twoN * twoN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc fourN

attemptValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Bit ->
  R
attemptValue reals zeroBit =
  zeroR reals
attemptValue reals oneBit =
  oneR reals

module Putnam2004A1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (S : (Nat -> Bit) -> Nat -> R) where

  fourFifths : R
  fourFifths =
    divide reals
      (fromNat reals fourN)
      (fromNat reals fiveN)

  rateDefinition : Set
  rateDefinition =
    (attempts : Nat -> Bit) ->
    (N : Nat) ->
    oneN <=N N ->
    S attempts N ==
      divide reals
        (sumFirst reals N
          (\ i -> attemptValue reals (attempts i)))
        (fromNat reals N)

  crossingProperty : Set
  crossingProperty =
    (attempts : Nat -> Bit) ->
    (a b : Nat) ->
    (oneN <=N a
    and
    (NatStrictLess a b
    and
    (StrictLess reals (S attempts a) fourFifths
    and
    StrictLess reals fourFifths (S attempts b)))) ->
    Exists Nat
      (\ c ->
        NatStrictLess a c
        and
        (NatStrictLess c b
        and
        S attempts c == fourFifths))

  solution : Set
  solution =
    Top

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    rateDefinition ->
    Iff crossingProperty solution

putnam-2004-a1 : Set1
putnam-2004-a1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (S : (Nat -> Bit) -> Nat -> R) ->
  Putnam2004A1Statement.proposition reals S

  attempt count. This file contains no proof.

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The class { 0 , 1 } ^m NN0 consists of all infinite binary attempt
  sequences, bijectively representing both the Lean Fin 2-valued sequences
  and the Isabelle Boolean-valued sequences. F assigns a real-valued rate
  sequence to every such attempt sequence. Its antecedent is exactly the
  source definition at every positive index: the numerator is the finite
  prefix sum over indices 0 through n - 1, and 4 / 5 is the real number 0.8.

  Binding a, b, and c over NN incorporates the source condition 1 <= a;
  under a < c < b all three indices are positive. The source solution
  proposition is annotated True, so its biconditional with the universally
  quantified crossing property is equivalent to the assertion below. The
  final declaration is a single unproved $a statement, with no $p proof.
$)

${
  $d A F a b c i n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2004-a1 $a |-
    A. F e.
      ( ( RR ^m NN0 ) ^m ( { 0 , 1 } ^m NN0 ) )
      (
        A. A e. ( { 0 , 1 } ^m NN0 )
          A. n e. NN
            (
              ( ( F ` A ) ` n )
              =
              (
                (
                  sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                    ( A ` i )
                )
                /
                n
              )
            )
        ->
        A. A e. ( { 0 , 1 } ^m NN0 )
          A. a e. NN
            A. b e. NN

                  a < b
                  /\
                  (
                    ( ( F ` A ) ` a ) < ( 4 / 5 )
                    /\
                    ( 4 / 5 ) < ( ( F ` A ) ` b )
                  )
                )
                ->
                E. c e. NN
                  (
                    a < c
                    /\
                    (

                      /\
