:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_a6
:: (putnambench__mizar__putnam_2004_a6): the two squared marginal integrals
:: of a continuous real-valued function on the unit square satisfy the stated
:: inequality involving its total integral and the integral of its square.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ

 vocabularies NUMBERS, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
      FUNCT_2, PARTFUN1, CARD_1, ORDINAL1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1,
      XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, REAL_1,
      COMPLEX1, SUPINF_2, MEASURE1, MESFUNC1, MESFUNC5, MEASUR12,
      INTEGRA5, RCOMP_1, SQUARE_1;
 notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ZFMISC_1, XTUPLE_0, RELAT_1,
      RELSET_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS,
      XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1, XXREAL_3, VALUED_0,
      VALUED_1, COMPLEX1, SUPINF_2, MEASURE1, MESFUNC1, MESFUNC5,
      MESFUNC6, MEASUR12, INTEGRA5, EXTREAL1, RCOMP_1, SQUARE_1;
 constructors RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, REAL_1, COMPLEX1, MESFUNC1, MESFUNC5,
      MESFUNC6, MEASUR12, INTEGRA5, EXTREAL1, ZFMISC_1, XTUPLE_0,
      BINOP_2, RCOMP_1, SQUARE_1;
 registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_1,
      FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, VALUED_0,
      VALUED_1, XXREAL_3, MEASURE1, MEASUR12, MEMBERED, RCOMP_1,
      SQUARE_1;
 requirements BOOLE, SUBSET, NUMERALS, REAL, ARITHM;
 definitions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0;
 equalities SQUARE_1;
 expansions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for f being Function of [:REAL,REAL:],REAL,
      I being Element of L-Field st
    I = {t where t is Real : 0 <= t & t <= 1} &
    (for x,y being Real st x in I & y in I holds
      for epsilon being Real st 0 < epsilon holds
        ex delta being Real st 0 < delta &
          for u,v being Real st
            u in I & v in I &
            |.u-x.| < delta & |.v-y.| < delta
          holds |.f.([u,v])-f.([x,y]).| < epsilon)
  holds
    ex rowSquares,columnSquares,totalRows,columnValues,squareRows
        being Function of REAL,REAL,
       totalIntegral being Real st
      (for y being Real st y in I holds
        ex row,squareRow being Function of REAL,REAL st
          (for x being Real st x in I holds
            row.x = f.([x,y]) &
            squareRow.x = (f.([x,y]))^2) &
          totalRows.y = Integral(L-Meas,row|I) &
          rowSquares.y = (totalRows.y)^2 &
          squareRows.y = Integral(L-Meas,squareRow|I)) &
      (for x being Real st x in I holds
        ex column being Function of REAL,REAL st
          (for y being Real st y in I holds
            column.y = f.([x,y])) &
          columnValues.x = Integral(L-Meas,column|I) &
          columnSquares.x = (columnValues.x)^2) &
      totalIntegral = Integral(L-Meas,totalRows|I) &
      Integral(L-Meas,rowSquares|I) +
          Integral(L-Meas,columnSquares|I)
        <= totalIntegral^2 +
          Integral(L-Meas,squareRows|I)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2004_a6

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_a6:
% the sum of the squared marginal integrals of a continuous real-valued
% function on the unit square satisfies the stated integral inequality.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2004_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  bivariate_function: TYPE = [real, real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  in_closed_unit_interval(x: real): bool =
    0 <= x AND x <= 1

  continuous_on_unit_square(f: bivariate_function): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: real):
      (in_closed_unit_interval(x)
        AND in_closed_unit_interval(y))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
          EXISTS (delta: posreal):
            FORALL (u, v: real):
              (in_closed_unit_interval(u)
                AND in_closed_unit_interval(v)
                AND abs(u - x) < delta
                AND abs(v - y) < delta)
              IMPLIES
                abs(f(u, v) - f(x, y)) < epsilon_value

  valid_partition(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = 0
      AND points(count) = 1
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          points(index) < points(index + 1)

  valid_tags(
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index) <= tags(index)
          AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1)

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      f: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count - 1)
        + f(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_unit_interval_integral(
      f: real_function,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
        FORALL
            (points, tags: real_sequence),
            (count: nat):
          (valid_partition(points, count)
            AND valid_tags(points, tags, count)
            AND mesh_less_than(points, count, mesh_bound))
          IMPLIES
            abs(
              riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count)
                - integral_value)
              < epsilon_value

  unit_interval_integral(f: real_function): real =
    IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
        has_unit_interval_integral(f, integral_value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
          has_unit_interval_integral(f, integral_value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  integral_in_x(f: bivariate_function, y: real): real =
    unit_interval_integral(
      LAMBDA (x: real): f(x, y))

  integral_in_y(f: bivariate_function, x: real): real =
    unit_interval_integral(
      LAMBDA (y: real): f(x, y))

  iterated_integral(f: bivariate_function): real =
    unit_interval_integral(
      LAMBDA (y: real): integral_in_x(f, y))

  iterated_integral_of_square(f: bivariate_function): real =
    unit_interval_integral(
      LAMBDA (y: real):
        unit_interval_integral(
          LAMBDA (x: real): f(x, y) ^ 2))

  putnam_2004_a6: bool =
    FORALL (f: bivariate_function):
      continuous_on_unit_square(f)
        IMPLIES
          unit_interval_integral(
            LAMBDA (y: real): integral_in_x(f, y) ^ 2)
            + unit_interval_integral(
                LAMBDA (x: real):
                  integral_in_y(f, x) ^ 2)
          <= iterated_integral(f) ^ 2
              + iterated_integral_of_square(f)
END putnam_2004_a6

import Mathlib

open Nat Topology Filter

/--
Let $P(x)=c_nx^n+c_{n-1}x^{n-1}+\cdots+c_0$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients. Suppose that $r$ is a rational number such that $P(r)=0$. Show that the $n$ numbers $c_nr,\,c_nr^2+c_{n-1}r,\,c_nr^3+c_{n-1}r^2+c_{n-2}r,\dots,\,c_nr^n+c_{n-1}r^{n-1}+\cdots+c_1r$ are integers.
-/
theorem putnam_2004_b1
(n : ℕ)
(P : Polynomial ℤ)
(r : ℚ)
(Pdeg : P.degree = n)
(Preq0 : Polynomial.aeval r P = 0)
: ∀ i ∈ Finset.range n, ∃ m : ℤ, m = ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (i + 1), (P.coeff (n - j) * r ^ (i + 1 - j)) :=

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b1:
  partial sums formed from the leading coefficients of an integer polynomial
  at a rational root are integers. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let is_rational =
     \x:real.
       ?p q:int.
         ~(q = (&0:int)) /\
         x = real_of_int p / real_of_int q in
   !c:int list n:num r:real.
     LENGTH c = n + 1 /\
     ~(LAST c = (&0:int)) /\
     is_rational r /\
     sum (0..n)
       (\k:num. real_of_int (EL k c) * r pow k) = &0
     ==>
     !i:num.
       i < n
       ==> ?m:int.
             sum (0..i)
               (\j:num.
                  real_of_int (EL (n - j) c) *
                  r pow (i + 1 - j)) =
             real_of_int m`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b1:
;; integer-valued leading-coefficient partial sums at a rational root of an
;; integer polynomial. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Coefficients are stored in ascending degree order. A proper integer list
;; of length n+1 with nonzero nth entry represents exactly a degree-n
;; polynomial over the integers. Since ACL2 rationals are exact, INTEGERP of
;; each displayed rational sum is equivalent to the source's existential
;; equality with an integer.

(defun putnam-2004-b1-integer-coefficient-list-p (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and (integerp (car coefficients))
           (putnam-2004-b1-integer-coefficient-list-p
            (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun putnam-2004-b1-polynomial-evaluate (coefficients r)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (+ (car coefficients)
         (* r
            (putnam-2004-b1-polynomial-evaluate
             (cdr coefficients) r)))
    0))

;; For i >= 0, this is
;; c_n*r^(i+1) + c_(n-1)*r^i + ... + c_(n-i)*r.
(defun putnam-2004-b1-leading-partial-sum
    (coefficients n r i)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix i)))
  (if (zp i)
      (* (nth n coefficients) r)
    (* r
       (+ (putnam-2004-b1-leading-partial-sum
           coefficients n r (- i 1))
          (nth (- n i) coefficients)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2004-b1-statement
    (coefficients n r i)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (rationalp r)
        (natp i)
        (true-listp coefficients)
        (putnam-2004-b1-integer-coefficient-list-p coefficients)
        (equal (len coefficients) (+ n 1))
        (not (equal (nth n coefficients) 0))
        (equal
         (putnam-2004-b1-polynomial-evaluate coefficients r)
         0)
        (< i n))
   (integerp
    (putnam-2004-b1-leading-partial-sum
     coefficients n r i))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2004_b1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2004_b1): integer-coefficient polynomials at
-- rational roots have integer leading partial sums. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<N_ _~Q_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

predNat : Nat -> Nat
predNat zero =
  zero
predNat (suc n) =
  n

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

intDifference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
intDifference zero zero =
  pos zero
intDifference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
intDifference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
intDifference (suc m) (suc n) =
  intDifference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  intDifference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  intDifference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

scaleInt : Int -> Nat -> Int
scaleInt z n =
  multiplyInt z (pos n)

record Rational : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator             : Int
    denominator-minus-one : Nat

open Rational

denominator : Rational -> Nat
denominator q =
  suc (denominator-minus-one q)

_~Q_ : Rational -> Rational -> Set
p ~Q q =
  scaleInt (numerator p) (denominator q) ==
  scaleInt (numerator q) (denominator p)

zeroQ : Rational
zeroQ =
  fraction (pos zero) zero

oneQ : Rational
oneQ =
  fraction (pos (suc zero)) zero

integerQ : Int -> Rational
integerQ z =
  fraction z zero

addQ : Rational -> Rational -> Rational
addQ p q =
  fraction
    (addInt
      (scaleInt (numerator p) (denominator q))
      (scaleInt (numerator q) (denominator p)))
    (predNat (denominator p * denominator q))

multiplyQ : Rational -> Rational -> Rational
multiplyQ p q =
  fraction
    (multiplyInt (numerator p) (numerator q))
    (predNat (denominator p * denominator q))

powerQ : Rational -> Nat -> Rational
powerQ q zero =
  oneQ
powerQ q (suc n) =
  multiplyQ q (powerQ q n)

sumFirst : Nat -> (Nat -> Rational) -> Rational
sumFirst zero term =
  zeroQ
sumFirst (suc n) term =
  addQ
    (sumFirst n term)
    (term n)

record DegreeExactly (coefficients : Nat -> Int) (n : Nat) : Set where
  constructor exactDegree
  field
    leading-nonzero :
      Not (coefficients n == pos zero)
    coefficients-above-zero :
      (k : Nat) ->
      n <N k ->
      coefficients k == pos zero

polynomialValue :
  (Nat -> Int) ->
  Nat ->
  Rational ->
  Rational
polynomialValue coefficients n r =
  sumFirst (suc n)
    (\ j ->
      multiplyQ
        (integerQ (coefficients j))
        (powerQ r j))

leadingPartialSum :
  (Nat -> Int) ->
  Nat ->
  Rational ->
  Nat ->
  Rational
leadingPartialSum coefficients n r i =
  sumFirst (suc i)
    (\ j ->
      multiplyQ
        (integerQ (coefficients (n - j)))
        (powerQ r (suc i - j)))

IsIntegerQ : Rational -> Set
IsIntegerQ q =
  Exists Int
    (\ z -> integerQ z ~Q q)

putnam-2004-b1 : Set
putnam-2004-b1 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  (coefficients : Nat -> Int) ->
  (r : Rational) ->
  DegreeExactly coefficients n ->
  polynomialValue coefficients n r ~Q zeroQ ->
  (i : Nat) ->
  i <N n ->
  IsIntegerQ (leadingPartialSum coefficients n r i)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b1:
  a degree-n polynomial with integer coefficients and a rational root has
  integer-valued partial Horner sums through every index below n. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory ratTheory;

val putnam_2004_b1 =
  ``let rat_sum =
      \f : num -> rat.
      \N : num.
        ITSET
          (\k : num. \acc : rat. f k + acc)
          (count N)
          0q
    in
      !n : num. !c : num -> int. !r : rat.
        c n <> 0 /\
        (!k : num. n < k ==> c k = 0) /\
        rat_sum
          (\k : num. rat_of_int (c k) * rat_expn r k)
          (n + 1) = 0q
        ==>
        !i : num.
          i < n
          ==>
          ?m : int.
            rat_of_int m =
              rat_sum
                (\j : num.
                   rat_of_int (c (n - j)) *
                   rat_expn r (i + 1 - j))
                (i + 1)``;

title: putnam_2004_b1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2004_b1: partial sums formed from the reversed coefficients of an
  integer polynomial at a rational root are integers. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For n in NN0, the inclusive interval 0 ... n indexes every coefficient of
  a polynomial of degree n. The function c has integer values on this
  interval, and ( c ` n ) =/= 0 makes the degree exactly n. Conversely, every
  integer polynomial of exact degree n determines exactly one such
  coefficient function, so this finite coefficient representation is
  bidirectionally equivalent to the source polynomial object.

  The root assumption is the usual evaluation sum from degree zero through
  n. The half-open interval 0 ..^ n indexes exactly the source's n
  conclusions, and each conclusion directly asserts membership of the
  reversed-coefficient partial sum in ZZ. All coefficient, root, and index
  domains and all quantifiers remain explicit.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d c i j k n r $.

  putnambench-putnam-2004-b1 $a |-
    A. n e. NN0
      A. c e. ( ZZ ^m ( 0 ... n ) )
        A. r e. QQ
          (
            (
              ( c ` n ) =/= 0
              /\
              (
                sum_ k e. ( 0 ... n )
                  ( ( c ` k ) x. ( r ^ k ) )
              )
              =
              0
            )
            ->
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
              (
                sum_ j e. ( 0 ... i )
                  (
                    ( c ` ( n - j ) )
                    x.
                    ( r ^ ( ( i + 1 ) - j ) )
                  )
              )
              e. ZZ
          )
  $.
$}

::$P-

      c being FinSequence of INT,
      x being Real st

      b <> 0 &
      (b qua Real) * x = (a qua Real)) &

      Sum rootTerms = 0)
  holds
    for k being Nat st k in Seg n holds
      ex terms being FinSequence of REAL st
        len terms = k &
        (for j being Nat st j in Seg k holds

            (c.(n + 2 -' j) qua Real) *
            (x |^ (k + 1 -' j))) &
        Sum terms in INT
proof
end;

content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b1:
% an integer-coefficient polynomial with a rational root has integer-valued
% truncated leading-coefficient sums at that root. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2004_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  coefficient_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> int]

  nat_subtract(left, right: nat): nat =
    IF right <= left THEN left - right ELSE 0 ENDIF

  polynomial_value(
      coefficients: coefficient_sequence,
      x: rat,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE rat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        polynomial_value(coefficients, x, count - 1)
          + (coefficients(index) :: rat) * x ^ index
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  leading_sum(
      coefficients: coefficient_sequence,
      degree: nat,
      x: rat,
      index: nat,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE rat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET offset: nat = count - 1 IN
        leading_sum(coefficients, degree, x, index, count - 1)
          + (coefficients(nat_subtract(degree, offset)) :: rat)
              * x ^ nat_subtract(index + 1, offset)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  putnam_2004_b1: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (coefficients: coefficient_sequence), (r: rat):
      (coefficients(n) /= 0
        AND polynomial_value(coefficients, r, n + 1) = 0)
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (i: nat):
          i < n IMPLIES
            EXISTS (m: int):
              leading_sum(coefficients, n, r, i, i + 1) = (m :: rat)
END putnam_2004_b1

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2004_b2): the strict factorial-ratio inequality
-- for two positive integers. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2004B2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  suc zero <=N n

record RationalField (Q : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroQ oneQ : Q
    add multiply : Q -> Q -> Q
    negate inverse : Q -> Q
    lessOrEqual : Q -> Q -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> Q
    fromInt : Int -> Q

    one-not-zero :
      oneQ != zeroQ

    add-commutative :
      (x y : Q) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : Q) -> add x zeroQ == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : Q) -> add x (negate x) == zeroQ

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : Q) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : Q) -> multiply x oneQ == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : Q) -> multiply x zeroQ == zeroQ
    distribute :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroQ == zeroQ
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : Q) ->
      x != zeroQ ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneQ

    order-reflexive :
      (x : Q) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroQ x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroQ y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroQ (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroQ oneQ and zeroQ != oneQ

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroQ
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneQ
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    fromInt-nonnegative :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromInt (pos n) == fromNat n
    fromInt-negative :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromInt (negsuc n) == negate (fromNat (suc n))

    every-element-is-ratio :
      (x : Q) ->
      Exists Int
        (\ numerator ->
          Exists Nat
            (\ denominator-minus-one ->
              x ==
              multiply
                (fromInt numerator)
                (inverse
                  (fromNat (suc denominator-minus-one)))))

open RationalField

divide :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q ->
  Q ->
  Q
divide rationals x y =
  multiply rationals x (inverse rationals y)

StrictLess :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q ->
  Q ->
  Set
StrictLess rationals x y =
  lessOrEqual rationals x y and x != y

naturalPower :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q ->
  Nat ->
  Q
naturalPower rationals x zero =
  oneQ rationals
naturalPower rationals x (suc n) =
  multiply rationals
    (naturalPower rationals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  suc zero
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

factorialRatio :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Nat ->
  Q
factorialRatio rationals n =
  divide rationals
    (fromNat rationals (factorial n))
    (naturalPower rationals (fromNat rationals n) n)

putnam-2004-b2 : Set1
putnam-2004-b2 =
  (Q : Set) ->
  (rationals : RationalField Q) ->
  (m n : Nat) ->
  Positive m ->
  Positive n ->
  StrictLess rationals
    (factorialRatio rationals (m + n))
    (multiply rationals
      (factorialRatio rationals m)
      (factorialRatio rationals n))

BEGIN
  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE

            ((m + n) :: real) ^ (m + n))

              safe_div(
                nat_factorial(m) :: real,
                (m :: real) ^ m)
                * safe_div(
                    nat_factorial(n) :: real,
                    (n :: real) ^ n)

abbrev putnam_2004_b4_solution : ℕ → ℂ → ℂ := sorry
-- fun n z ↦ z + n
/--
Let $n$ be a positive integer, $n \ge 2$, and put $\theta = 2 \pi / n$. Define points $P_k = (k,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, for $k = 1, 2, \dots, n$. Let $R_k$ be the map that rotates the plane counterclockwise by the angle $\theta$ about the point $P_k$. Let $R$ denote the map obtained by applying, in order, $R_1$, then $R_2, \dots$, then $R_n$. For an arbitrary point $(x,y)$, find, and simplify, the coordinates of $R(x,y)$.
-/
theorem putnam_2004_b4
(n : ℕ)
(nge2 : n ≥ 2)
(R Rk : ℕ → ℂ → ℂ)
(hR : R 0 = id ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, R (k + 1) = Rk (k + 1) ∘ R k)
(hRk : Rk = fun (k : ℕ) (Q : ℂ) ↦ k + Complex.exp (Complex.I * 2 * Real.pi / n) * (Q - k))
: (R n = putnam_2004_b4_solution n) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2004_b4

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b4:
   the composition of equally angled rotations about consecutive points on
   the real axis is a translation by n. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2004_b4_complex := (R * R)%type.

Definition putnam_2004_b4_of_real
    (x : R) : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  (x, 0).

Definition putnam_2004_b4_of_nat
    (n : nat) : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  putnam_2004_b4_of_real (INR n).

Definition putnam_2004_b4_i : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  (0, 1).

Definition putnam_2004_b4_add
    (z w : putnam_2004_b4_complex) : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  (fst z + fst w, snd z + snd w).

Definition putnam_2004_b4_neg
    (z : putnam_2004_b4_complex) : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  (- fst z, - snd z).

Definition putnam_2004_b4_sub
    (z w : putnam_2004_b4_complex) : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  putnam_2004_b4_add z (putnam_2004_b4_neg w).

Definition putnam_2004_b4_mul
    (z w : putnam_2004_b4_complex) : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  (fst z * fst w - snd z * snd w,
   fst z * snd w + snd z * fst w).

Definition putnam_2004_b4_inv
    (z : putnam_2004_b4_complex) : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  (fst z / (fst z ^ 2 + snd z ^ 2),
   - snd z / (fst z ^ 2 + snd z ^ 2)).

Definition putnam_2004_b4_div
    (z w : putnam_2004_b4_complex) : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  putnam_2004_b4_mul z (putnam_2004_b4_inv w).

Definition putnam_2004_b4_exp
    (z : putnam_2004_b4_complex) : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  (exp (fst z) * cos (snd z),
   exp (fst z) * sin (snd z)).

Definition putnam_2004_b4_rotation
    (n k : nat)
    (Q : putnam_2004_b4_complex) : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  putnam_2004_b4_add
    (putnam_2004_b4_of_nat k)
    (putnam_2004_b4_mul
      (putnam_2004_b4_exp
        (putnam_2004_b4_div
          (putnam_2004_b4_mul
            (putnam_2004_b4_mul
              putnam_2004_b4_i
              (putnam_2004_b4_of_real 2))
            (putnam_2004_b4_of_real PI))
          (putnam_2004_b4_of_nat n)))
      (putnam_2004_b4_sub Q (putnam_2004_b4_of_nat k))).

Definition putnam_2004_b4_solution
    (n : nat)
    (z : putnam_2004_b4_complex) : putnam_2004_b4_complex :=
  putnam_2004_b4_add z (putnam_2004_b4_of_nat n).

Theorem putnam_2004_b4
    (n : nat)
    (nge2 : (2 <= n)%nat)
    (R Rk : nat -> putnam_2004_b4_complex -> putnam_2004_b4_complex)
    (hR :
      R 0%nat = (fun Q => Q) /\
      forall k : nat,
        R (k + 1)%nat =
          (fun Q => Rk (k + 1)%nat (R k Q)))
    (hRk : Rk = putnam_2004_b4_rotation n) :
  R n = putnam_2004_b4_solution n.
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b4:
;; composing the rotations through angle 2*pi/n about (1,0), ..., (n,0)
;; translates every complex point by n. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Put zeta = exp(2*pi*i/n).  Each source rotation is the affine map
;;
;;   Q |-> zeta*Q + (1-zeta)*k.
;;
;; The polynomial pair (A,B) below represents Q |-> A(zeta)*Q+B(zeta).
;; Starting from the identity and composing the rotations for k=1,...,n
;; therefore gives exactly the source map R n.  The claimed translation is
;; Q |-> Q+n, so equality as functions on all complex Q is equivalent to
;; A(zeta)=1 and B(zeta)=n.
;;
;; Since zeta is a primitive n-th root of unity, its minimal polynomial over
;; the rationals is Phi_n.  Each coefficient equality holds exactly when its
;; polynomial difference is divisible by Phi_n.  Thus the two remainder
;; tests preserve the arbitrary complex domain and are bidirectionally
;; equivalent to the source function equality; they do not replace complex
;; values by ACL2's complex rationals.  The source parameters R and Rk are
;; eliminated only by unfolding the hypotheses that uniquely define them.

;; Polynomials use rational coefficient lists in ascending degree order.

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (let ((tail
             (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize
              (cdr coefficients))))
        (if (and (equal (car coefficients) 0)
                 (not (consp tail)))
            nil
          (cons (car coefficients) tail)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-add (left right)
  (cond
   ((consp left)
    (if (consp right)
        (cons (+ (car left) (car right))
              (putnam-2004-b4-poly-add
               (cdr left) (cdr right)))
      left))
   (t right)))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-scale (scalar polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons (* scalar (car polynomial))
            (putnam-2004-b4-poly-scale
             scalar (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-negate (polynomial)
  (putnam-2004-b4-poly-scale -1 polynomial))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-subtract (left right)
  (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize
   (putnam-2004-b4-poly-add
    left
    (putnam-2004-b4-poly-negate right))))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-multiply (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize
       (putnam-2004-b4-poly-add
        (putnam-2004-b4-poly-scale (car left) right)
        (cons 0
              (putnam-2004-b4-poly-multiply
               (cdr left) right))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-zero-list (count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons 0
          (putnam-2004-b4-zero-list (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-monomial (coefficient degree)
  (if (equal coefficient 0)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-2004-b4-zero-list degree)
     (list coefficient))))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-degree (polynomial)
  (let ((normalized
         (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize polynomial)))
    (if (consp normalized)
        (- (len normalized) 1)
      0)))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-leading-coefficient (polynomial)
  (let ((normalized
         (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize polynomial)))
    (if (consp normalized)
        (nth (putnam-2004-b4-poly-degree normalized)
             normalized)
      0)))

;; The step bound exceeds the number of degree reductions required by
;; polynomial long division with a nonzero divisor.
(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-divmod-steps
    (remainder divisor quotient steps)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix steps)))
  (if (zp steps)
      (cons (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize quotient)
            (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize remainder))
    (let* ((normalized-remainder
            (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize remainder))
           (normalized-divisor
            (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize divisor)))
      (if (or (not (consp normalized-remainder))
              (not (consp normalized-divisor))
              (< (putnam-2004-b4-poly-degree
                  normalized-remainder)
                 (putnam-2004-b4-poly-degree
                  normalized-divisor)))
          (cons (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize quotient)
                normalized-remainder)
        (let* ((degree-difference
                (- (putnam-2004-b4-poly-degree
                    normalized-remainder)
                   (putnam-2004-b4-poly-degree
                    normalized-divisor)))
               (coefficient
                (/ (putnam-2004-b4-poly-leading-coefficient
                    normalized-remainder)
                   (putnam-2004-b4-poly-leading-coefficient
                    normalized-divisor)))
               (term
                (putnam-2004-b4-poly-monomial
                 coefficient degree-difference)))
          (putnam-2004-b4-poly-divmod-steps
           (putnam-2004-b4-poly-subtract
            normalized-remainder
            (putnam-2004-b4-poly-multiply
             term normalized-divisor))
           normalized-divisor
           (putnam-2004-b4-poly-add quotient term)
           (- steps 1)))))))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-divmod (dividend divisor)
  (putnam-2004-b4-poly-divmod-steps
   dividend
   divisor
   nil
   (+ 1
      (len (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize dividend)))))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-quotient (dividend divisor)
  (car (putnam-2004-b4-poly-divmod dividend divisor)))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-poly-remainder (dividend divisor)
  (cdr (putnam-2004-b4-poly-divmod dividend divisor)))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-x-to-n-minus-one (n)
  (putnam-2004-b4-poly-add
   (list -1)
   (putnam-2004-b4-poly-monomial 1 n)))

;; The list PRECEDING contains Phi_1 through Phi_(n-1).
(defun putnam-2004-b4-proper-divisor-product
    (n divisor preceding)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix divisor)))
  (if (zp divisor)
      (list 1)
    (let ((remaining
           (putnam-2004-b4-proper-divisor-product
            n (- divisor 1) preceding)))
      (if (equal (mod n divisor) 0)
          (putnam-2004-b4-poly-multiply
           (nth (- divisor 1) preceding)
           remaining)
        remaining))))

;; Phi_n = (X^n - 1) / product_(d | n, d < n) Phi_d.
(defun putnam-2004-b4-cyclotomic-list (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (let* ((preceding
            (putnam-2004-b4-cyclotomic-list (- n 1)))
           (proper-divisor-product
            (putnam-2004-b4-proper-divisor-product
             n (- n 1) preceding))
           (phi-n
            (putnam-2004-b4-poly-quotient
             (putnam-2004-b4-x-to-n-minus-one n)
             proper-divisor-product)))
      (append
       preceding
       (list (putnam-2004-b4-poly-normalize phi-n))))))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-cyclotomic-polynomial (n)
  (if (zp n)
      nil
    (nth (- n 1)
         (putnam-2004-b4-cyclotomic-list n))))

;; AFFINE is (A B), representing Q |-> A(zeta)*Q+B(zeta).
(defun putnam-2004-b4-compose-rotations
    (remaining k affine)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      affine
    (let* ((x-polynomial (list 0 1))
           (one-minus-x (list 1 -1))
           (a (car affine))
           (b (cadr affine))
           (next-a
            (putnam-2004-b4-poly-multiply
             x-polynomial a))
           (next-b
            (putnam-2004-b4-poly-add
             (putnam-2004-b4-poly-multiply
              x-polynomial b)
             (putnam-2004-b4-poly-scale
              k one-minus-x))))
      (putnam-2004-b4-compose-rotations
       (- remaining 1)
       (+ k 1)
       (list next-a next-b)))))

(defun putnam-2004-b4-composition-affine (n)
  (putnam-2004-b4-compose-rotations
   n 1 (list (list 1) nil)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2004-b4-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (<= 2 n))
   (let* ((affine
           (putnam-2004-b4-composition-affine n))
          (a-difference
           (putnam-2004-b4-poly-subtract
            (car affine) (list 1)))
          (b-difference
           (putnam-2004-b4-poly-subtract
            (cadr affine) (list n)))
          (phi-n
           (putnam-2004-b4-cyclotomic-polynomial n)))
     (and
      (equal
       (putnam-2004-b4-poly-remainder
        a-difference phi-n)
       nil)
      (equal
       (putnam-2004-b4-poly-remainder
        b-difference phi-n)
       nil)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2004_b4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2004_b4): composing rotations through angle
-- 2*pi/n about (1,0),...,(n,0) gives translation by (n,0). This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2004B4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  twoN + twoN

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

alternatingPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingPower reals n =
  naturalPower reals
    (negate reals (oneR reals))
    n

sineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
sineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (suc (twoN * n))))
    (fromNat reals (factorial (suc (twoN * n))))

cosineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
cosineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (twoN * n)))
    (fromNat reals (factorial (twoN * n)))

leibnizTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
leibnizTerm reals n =
  divide reals
    (alternatingPower reals n)
    (fromNat reals (suc (twoN * n)))

SineValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
SineValue reals x value =
  SeriesHasSum reals
    (sineTerm reals x)
    value

CosineValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CosineValue reals x value =
  SeriesHasSum reals
    (cosineTerm reals x)
    value

record PiValue
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (value : R) : Set where
  field
    positive :
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) value
    leibniz-series :
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (leibnizTerm reals)
        (divide reals value (fromNat reals fourN))

record StandardTrigonometry
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) : Set1 where
  field
    sine cosine : R -> R
    pi : R
    sine-value :
      (x : R) ->
      SineValue reals x (sine x)
    cosine-value :
      (x : R) ->
      CosineValue reals x (cosine x)
    pi-value :
      PiValue reals pi

open StandardTrigonometry

record Complex (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor complex
  field
    realPart      : R
    imaginaryPart : R

open Complex

complexFromNat :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  Complex R
complexFromNat reals n =
  complex
    (fromNat reals n)
    (zeroR reals)

complexAdd :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexAdd reals z w =
  complex
    (add reals (realPart z) (realPart w))
    (add reals (imaginaryPart z) (imaginaryPart w))

complexNegate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexNegate reals z =
  complex
    (negate reals (realPart z))
    (negate reals (imaginaryPart z))

complexSubtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexSubtract reals z w =
  complexAdd reals z (complexNegate reals w)

complexMultiply :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexMultiply reals z w =
  complex
    (add reals
      (multiply reals (realPart z) (realPart w))
      (negate reals
        (multiply reals (imaginaryPart z) (imaginaryPart w))))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals (realPart z) (imaginaryPart w))
      (multiply reals (imaginaryPart z) (realPart w)))

FunctionEqual :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set
FunctionEqual {A} f g =
  (x : A) ->
  f x == g x

compose :
  {A B C : Set} ->
  (B -> C) ->
  (A -> B) ->
  A ->
  C
compose g f x =
  g (f x)

identity :
  {A : Set} ->
  A ->
  A
identity x =
  x

module Putnam2004B4Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (trigonometry : StandardTrigonometry reals) where

  angle : Nat -> R
  angle n =
    divide reals
      (multiply reals
        (fromNat reals twoN)
        (pi trigonometry))
      (fromNat reals n)

  rotationFactor : Nat -> Complex R
  rotationFactor n =
    complex
      (cosine trigonometry (angle n))
      (sine trigonometry (angle n))

  rotateAbout :
    Nat ->
    Nat ->
    Complex R ->
    Complex R
  rotateAbout n k point =
    let
      center = complexFromNat reals k
    in
    complexAdd reals center
      (complexMultiply reals
        (rotationFactor n)
        (complexSubtract reals point center))

  translateByN :
    Nat ->
    Complex R ->
    Complex R
  translateByN n point =
    complexAdd reals point (complexFromNat reals n)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (n : Nat) ->
    twoN <=N n ->
    (Rk composite : Nat -> Complex R -> Complex R) ->
    FunctionEqual (composite zero) identity ->
    ((k : Nat) ->
      FunctionEqual
        (composite (suc k))
        (compose (Rk (suc k)) (composite k))) ->
    ((k : Nat) ->
      FunctionEqual
        (Rk k)
        (rotateAbout n k)) ->
    FunctionEqual
      (composite n)
      (translateByN n)

putnam-2004-b4 : Set1
putnam-2004-b4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (trigonometry : StandardTrigonometry reals) ->
  Putnam2004B4Statement.proposition reals trigonometry

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b4:
  composing equal-angle counterclockwise rotations about the consecutive
  real-axis points 1 through n translates every complex point by n.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory realTheory transcTheory complexTheory;

val putnam_2004_b4 =
  ``!n : num.
      !R Rk : num -> complex -> complex.
        2 <= n /\
        R 0 = (\z : complex. z) /\
        (!k : num.
           R (k + 1) =
             (\z : complex. Rk (k + 1) (R k z))) /\
        Rk =
          (\k : num.
           \Q : complex.
             complex_of_real (&k) +
             complex_exp (i * (2 * pi / &n)) *
               (Q - complex_of_real (&k)))
        ==>
        R n = (\z : complex. z + complex_of_real (&n))``;

title: putnam_2004_b4
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2004_b4: the ordered composition of equal-angle rotations about the
  points 1 through n translates every complex point by n. This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The natural number n remains in NN0 with the explicit assumption n >= 2.
  The family R ranges over all NN0-indexed complex self-maps. Its initial
  value is the identity, and the displayed pointwise recurrence is exactly
  R_(k+1) = Rk_(k+1) composed with R_k after the source definition

    Rk_j(Q) = j + exp(i * 2 * pi / n) * (Q - j)

  is substituted. Thus the auxiliary family Rk is eliminated definitionally,
  while the universal quantification over R and every complex input is
  preserved. Equality of the resulting complex self-maps is expressed
  pointwise, equivalently to the function equality in the ground truth.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d R k n z $.

  putnambench-putnam-2004-b4 $a |-
    A. n e. NN0
      (
        2 <_ n
        ->
        A. R e. ( ( CC ^m CC ) ^m NN0 )
          (
            (
              A. z e. CC
                ( ( R ` 0 ) ` z ) = z
              /\
              A. k e. NN0 A. z e. CC
                ( ( R ` ( k + 1 ) ) ` z )
                =
                (
                  ( k + 1 )
                  +
                  (
                    (
                      exp
                      `
                      (
                        ( ( _i x. 2 ) x. _pi )
                        /
                        n
                      )
                    )
                    x.
                    (
                      ( ( R ` k ) ` z )
                      -
                      ( k + 1 )
                    )
                  )
                )
            )
            ->
            A. z e. CC
              ( ( R ` n ) ` z ) = ( z + n )
          )
      )
  $.
$}

environ

    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, BINOP_2, SETWISEO, FUNCT_2, BINOP_1,

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat,
      R,Rk being Function of NAT,Funcs(COMPLEX,COMPLEX) st
    n >= 2 &
    (for z being Complex holds (R.0).z = z) &
    (for k being Nat, z being Complex holds
      (R.(k + 1)).z = (Rk.(k + 1)).((R.k).z)) &

title: putnam_2004_b4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b4:
% composing the rotations through angle 2*pi/n about (k,0), for k from 1
% through n, translates every complex point z to z + n. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2004_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  complex: TYPE = [# real_part: real, imag_part: real #]
  complex_function: TYPE = [complex -> complex]
  complex_function_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> complex_function]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  complex_of_nat(value: nat): complex =
    (# real_part := value, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_neg(value: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := -real_part(value),
       imag_part := -imag_part(value) #)

  complex_add(left, right: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := real_part(left) + real_part(right),
       imag_part := imag_part(left) + imag_part(right) #)

  complex_sub(left, right: complex): complex =
    complex_add(left, complex_neg(right))

  complex_mul(left, right: complex): complex =
    (# real_part :=
         real_part(left) * real_part(right)
           - imag_part(left) * imag_part(right),
       imag_part :=
         real_part(left) * imag_part(right)
           + imag_part(left) * real_part(right) #)

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  sine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        sine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index) * x ^ (2 * index + 1),
              factorial(2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  cosine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index) * x ^ (2 * index),
              factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  leibniz_partial_sum(count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        leibniz_partial_sum(count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index),
              (2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  sine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): sine_partial(x, count),
          value))

  cosine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): cosine_partial(x, count),
          value))

  pi: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            4 * leibniz_partial_sum(count),
          value))

  rotation_angle(n: nat): real =
    safe_div(2 * pi, n :: real)

  rotation_multiplier(n: nat): complex =
    (# real_part := cosine(rotation_angle(n)),
       imag_part := sine(rotation_angle(n)) #)

  rotation_map(n, k: nat, point: complex): complex =
    complex_add(
      complex_of_nat(k),
      complex_mul(
        rotation_multiplier(n),
        complex_sub(point, complex_of_nat(k))))

  putnam_2004_b4_solution(n: nat): complex_function =
    LAMBDA (point: complex):
      complex_add(point, complex_of_nat(n))

  putnam_2004_b4: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat),
      (R, Rk: complex_function_sequence):
      (n >= 2
        AND (FORALL (k: nat), (point: complex):
          Rk(k)(point) = rotation_map(n, k, point))
        AND (FORALL (point: complex):
          R(0)(point) = point)
        AND (FORALL (k: nat), (point: complex):
          R(k + 1)(point) = Rk(k + 1)(R(k)(point))))
      IMPLIES
        R(n) = putnam_2004_b4_solution(n)
END putnam_2004_b4

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b5:
;; the left limit at 1 of the stated infinite product is 2 / exp(1).
;; This file contains no proof.
;;
;; For 0 < x < 1, taking logarithms and summing by parts rewrites the
;; logarithm of the first N factors as
;;
;;   -log 2
;;   + (1-x) * sum_{m=1}^{N-1} x^(m-1) log(1+x^m)
;;   + x^(N-1) log(1+x^N).
;;
;; The middle term is a geometric Riemann sum for
;; integral_0^1 log(1+t) dt = 2 log 2 - 1.  Thus the product limit has
;; logarithm log 2 - 1, equivalently the product is 2 / exp(1).
;; PUTNAM-2004-B5-LOG-APPROX is the standard rational atanh series for
;; log. Rational epsilon and x form cofinal and dense presentations of the
;; corresponding real conditions.
;; The product hypothesis uniquely determines xprod on 0 < x < 1, so
;; eliminating that auxiliary function is bidirectionally equivalent to
;; the source statement; the inclusive Isabelle indexing differs only by
;; one term and has the same infinite product.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

(defun putnam-2004-b5-log-series-aux (u power odd remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+ (/ power odd)
       (putnam-2004-b5-log-series-aux
        u
        (* power u u)
        (+ odd 2)
        (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-2004-b5-log-approx (base terms)
  (if (and (rationalp base)
           (< 0 base)
           (natp terms))
      (let ((u (/ (- base 1) (+ base 1))))
        (* 2
           (putnam-2004-b5-log-series-aux u u 1 terms)))
    0))

(defun putnam-2004-b5-weighted-log-prefix (x upper log-terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix upper)))
  (if (zp upper)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2004-b5-weighted-log-prefix
        x (- upper 1) log-terms)
       (* (expt x (- upper 1))
          (putnam-2004-b5-log-approx
           (+ 1 (expt x upper))
           log-terms)))))

(defun putnam-2004-b5-log-product-approx (x terms log-terms)
  (if (and (rationalp x)
           (< 0 x)
           (< x 1)
           (posp terms)
           (natp log-terms))
      (+ (- (putnam-2004-b5-log-approx 2 log-terms))
         (* (- 1 x)
            (putnam-2004-b5-weighted-log-prefix
             x (- terms 1) log-terms))
         (* (expt x (- terms 1))
            (putnam-2004-b5-log-approx
             (+ 1 (expt x terms))
             log-terms)))
    0))

(defun putnam-2004-b5-log-solution-approx (log-terms)
  (- (putnam-2004-b5-log-approx 2 log-terms) 1))

;; The source gives no convergence rates. The quantifiers below state the
;; left-limit definition directly: every tolerance has a left neighborhood,
;; and at every rational point in that neighborhood the finite-product and
;; logarithm approximations eventually remain within the tolerance.

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b5-approximation-tail-p
    (epsilon x product-cutoff log-cutoff)
  (forall (terms log-terms)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp terms)
      (<= product-cutoff terms)
      (natp log-terms)
      (<= log-cutoff log-terms))
     (< (abs
         (- (putnam-2004-b5-log-product-approx
             x terms log-terms)
            (putnam-2004-b5-log-solution-approx
             log-terms)))
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b5-approximation-cutoffs-exist-p
    (epsilon x)
  (exists (product-cutoff log-cutoff)
    (and
     (posp product-cutoff)
     (posp log-cutoff)
     (putnam-2004-b5-approximation-tail-p
      epsilon x product-cutoff log-cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b5-left-neighborhood-p
    (epsilon delta)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (< 0 x)
      (< x 1)
      (< (- 1 x) delta))
     (putnam-2004-b5-approximation-cutoffs-exist-p
      epsilon x))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b5-delta-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (rationalp delta)
     (< 0 delta)
     (putnam-2004-b5-left-neighborhood-p
      epsilon delta))))

(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-2004-b5-statement ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-2004-b5-delta-exists-p epsilon))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)

:q

title: putnam_2004_b5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2004_b5): the left-hand limit at 1 of an
-- infinite product with real exponents is 2 / exp(1). This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2004B5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SequentialLimit {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

LeftLimit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
LeftLimit {R} reals function limit point =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        StrictLess reals
          (subtract reals point delta)
          x ->
        StrictLess reals x point ->
        CloseTo reals limit epsilon (function x)))

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

productFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
productFirst reals zero terms =
  oneR reals
productFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  multiply reals
    (productFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

exponentialTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

ExponentialValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
ExponentialValue reals x value =
  SequentialLimit reals
    (\ n ->
      sumFirst reals n
        (exponentialTerm reals x))
    value

record StandardRealAnalysis
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    exponential naturalLogarithm : R -> R

    exponential-is-power-series :
      (x : R) ->
      ExponentialValue reals x (exponential x)

    exponential-positive :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals
        (zeroR reals)
        (exponential x)

    logarithm-of-exponential :
      (x : R) ->
      naturalLogarithm (exponential x) == x

    exponential-of-logarithm :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      exponential (naturalLogarithm x) == x

open StandardRealAnalysis

realPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardRealAnalysis reals ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
realPower reals analysis base exponent =
  exponential analysis
    (multiply reals
      exponent
      (naturalLogarithm analysis base))

module Putnam2004B5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis reals) where

  productTerm : R -> Nat -> R
  productTerm x n =
    realPower reals analysis
      (divide reals
        (add reals
          (oneR reals)
          (naturalPower reals x (suc n)))
        (add reals
          (oneR reals)
          (naturalPower reals x n)))
      (naturalPower reals x n)

  partialProduct : R -> Nat -> R
  partialProduct x n =
    productFirst reals n (productTerm x)

  solution : R
  solution =
    divide reals
      (fromNat reals twoN)
      (exponential analysis (oneR reals))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (xprod : R -> R) ->
    ((x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      StrictLess reals x (oneR reals) ->
      SequentialLimit reals
        (partialProduct x)
        (xprod x)) ->
    LeftLimit reals
      xprod
      solution
      (oneR reals)

putnam-2004-b5 : Set1
putnam-2004-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (analysis : StandardRealAnalysis reals) ->
  Putnam2004B5Statement.proposition reals analysis

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b5:
  evaluation of a real infinite product as its parameter approaches 1 from
  below, with limit 2 / exp 1. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory
     real_topologyTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2004_b5 =
  ``!xprod : real -> real.
      (!x : real.
         0 < x /\ x < 1
         ==>
         ((\N : num.
             REAL_PROD_IMAGE
               (\n : num.
                  ((1 + x pow (n + 1)) / (1 + x pow n)) powr
                    (x pow n))
               (count N)) -->
          xprod x)
           sequentially)
      ==>
      (xprod --> 2 / exp 1)
        (at 1 within {x : real | x < 1})``;

title: putnam_2004_b5
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2004_b5: evaluation of the left-hand limit at one of an infinite
  product with real exponents as two divided by exp(1). This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  F ranges over arbitrary real-valued functions. For each real x in the open
  unit interval, its value is assumed to be the limit of the finite products
  indexed by 0 ..^ N, namely the indices 0 through N - 1. This is exactly the
  exclusive partial-product convention of the Lean and Rocq sources; the
  inclusive Isabelle convention is the same sequence with an index shift.

  Every ratio base is positive on 0 < x < 1, so set.mm's complex-power
  operation ^c agrees with the source real power
  exp((x^n) log((1+x^(n+1))/(1+x^n))). The relation ~~> is standard
  sequence convergence. The conclusion expands the left-hand limit at one
  into its epsilon-delta definition and uses the explicit solution 2/exp(1).

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d F N d e n x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2004-b5 $a |- A. F e. ( RR ^m RR )
    (
      (
        A. x e. RR
          (
            (
              0 < x
              /\
              x < 1
            )
            ->
            (
              (
                N e. NN0 |->
                  prod_ n e. ( 0 ..^ N )
                    (
                      (
                        (
                          1
                          +
                          ( x ^ ( n + 1 ) )
                        )
                        /
                        (
                          1
                          +
                          ( x ^ n )
                        )
                      )
                      ^c
                      ( x ^ n )
                    )
              )
              ~~>
              ( F ` x )
            )
          )
      )
      ->
      A. e e. RR
        (
          0 < e
          ->
          E. d e. RR
            (
              0 < d
              /\
              A. x e. RR
                (
                  (
                    x < 1
                    /\
                    ( abs ` ( x - 1 ) ) < d
                  )
                  ->
                  (
                    abs
                    `
                    (
                      ( F ` x )
                      -
                      ( 2 / ( exp ` 1 ) )
                    )
                  )
                  < e
                )
            )
        )
    )
  $.
$}

content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b5:
% the left-hand limit at one of a real infinite product with factors
% ((1 + x^(n+1)) / (1 + x^n))^(x^n) is 2 / exp(1). This file contains no proof.

putnam_2004_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  natural_log(x: real): real =
    IF x > 0 THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (value: real):
          real_exponential(value) = x)
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  real_power(base, exponent: real): real =
    IF base > 0 THEN
      real_exponential(exponent * natural_log(base))
    ELSIF base = 0 AND exponent = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  product_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        product_partial(x, count - 1)
          * real_power(
              safe_div(
                1 + x ^ (index + 1),
                1 + x ^ index),
              x ^ index)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  infinite_product_value(x, value: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat):
        product_partial(x, count),
      value)

  left_tends_to_at(
      f: real_function,
      limit, point: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (x: real):
          (0 < point - x AND point - x < delta)
            IMPLIES abs(f(x) - limit) < epsilon_value

  putnam_2004_b5_solution: real =
    safe_div(2, real_exponential(1))

  putnam_2004_b5: bool =
    FORALL (xprod: real_function):
      (FORALL (x: real):
        (0 < x AND x < 1)
          IMPLIES infinite_product_value(x, xprod(x)))
      IMPLIES
        left_tends_to_at(
          xprod,
          putnam_2004_b5_solution,
          1)
END putnam_2004_b5

import Mathlib

open Nat Topology Filter

/--
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a non-empty set of positive integers, and let $N(x)$ denote the number of elements of $\mathcal{A}$ not exceeding $x$. Let $\mathcal{B}$ denote the set of positive integers $b$ that can be written in the form $b=a-a'$ with $a \in \mathcal{A}$ and $a' \in \mathcal{A}$. Let $b_1< b_2<\cdots$ be the members of $\mathcal{B}$, listed in increasing order. Show that if the sequence $b_{i+1}-b_i$ is unbounded, then $\lim_{x \to\infty} N(x)/x=0$.
-/
theorem putnam_2004_b6
  (A B : Set ℕ)
  (N : ℝ → ℕ)
  (b : ℕ → ℕ)
  (Anempty : A.Nonempty)
  (Apos : ∀ a ∈ A, a > 0)
  (hN : ∀ x : ℝ, N x = Set.encard {a : A | a ≤ x})
  (hB : B = {b' > 0 | ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ a' ∈ A, b' = a - a'})
  (hbB : Set.range b = B ∧ ∀ i : ℕ, b i < b (i + 1)) :
  (∀ r : ℕ, ∃ i : ℕ, (b (i + 1) - b i) ≥ r) → Tendsto (fun x => N x / x) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
sorry

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b6:
  unbounded consecutive gaps in the increasing positive-difference set of a
  nonempty set of positive integers force its counting density to tend to zero.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals List Arith.PeanoNat.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2004_b6_has_cardinality
    (P : nat -> Prop) (n : nat) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list nat,
    NoDup enumeration /\
    length enumeration = n /\
    forall a : nat, In a enumeration <-> P a.

Definition putnam_2004_b6_tends_to_zero_at_pos_infinity
    (f : R -> R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    0 < epsilon ->
    exists cutoff : R,
      forall x : R,
        cutoff <= x ->
        Rabs (f x - 0) < epsilon.

Theorem putnam_2004_b6
    (A B : nat -> Prop)
    (N : R -> nat)
    (b : nat -> nat)
    (Anempty : exists a : nat, A a)
    (Apos : forall a : nat, A a -> (0 < a)%nat)
    (hN :
      forall x : R,
        putnam_2004_b6_has_cardinality
          (fun a : nat => A a /\ INR a <= x)
          (N x))
    (hB :
      forall d : nat,
        B d <->
        (0 < d)%nat /\
        exists a a' : nat,
          A a /\ A a' /\ d = (a - a')%nat)
    (hbB :
      forall d : nat,
        B d <-> exists i : nat, b i = d)
    (hbasc :
      forall i : nat, (b i < b (S i))%nat) :
  (forall r : nat,
      exists i : nat, (r <= b (S i) - b i)%nat) ->
  putnam_2004_b6_tends_to_zero_at_pos_infinity
    (fun x : R => INR (N x) / x).
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2004_b6:
;; a positive-integer set whose increasing positive-difference enumeration has
;; unbounded successive gaps has counting-function density tending to zero.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; These conservative generic symbols represent the arbitrary characteristic
;; predicate of A and the arbitrary sequence b. DEFSTUB imposes no
;; executability or finiteness restriction. Every domain condition and every
;; source quantifier is stated explicitly below with DEFUN-SK.
(defstub putnam-2004-b6-a-member (n) t)
(defstub putnam-2004-b6-b (i) t)

(defun putnam-2004-b6-member-p (n)
  (if (putnam-2004-b6-a-member n) t nil))

(defun putnam-2004-b6-nat-subtract (left right)
  (if (< left right)
      0
    (- left right)))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b6-set-nonempty-p ()
  (exists (a)
    (and
     (natp a)
     (putnam-2004-b6-member-p a))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b6-positive-set-p ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp a)
      (putnam-2004-b6-member-p a))
     (< 0 a))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b6-increasing-natural-sequence-p ()
  (forall (i)
    (implies
     (natp i)
     (and
      (natp (putnam-2004-b6-b i))
      (natp (putnam-2004-b6-b (+ i 1)))
      (< (putnam-2004-b6-b i)
         (putnam-2004-b6-b (+ i 1)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b6-in-sequence-range-p (value)
  (exists (i)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (equal (putnam-2004-b6-b i) value))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b6-positive-difference-p (value)
  (exists (a a-prime)
    (and
     (natp value)
     (< 0 value)
     (natp a)
     (natp a-prime)
     (putnam-2004-b6-member-p a)
     (putnam-2004-b6-member-p a-prime)
     (equal
      value
      (putnam-2004-b6-nat-subtract a a-prime)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b6-exact-difference-range-p ()
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (natp value)
     (iff
      (putnam-2004-b6-in-sequence-range-p value)
      (putnam-2004-b6-positive-difference-p value)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b6-gap-at-least-exists-p (bound)
  (exists (i)
    (and
     (natp i)
     (<=
      bound
      (putnam-2004-b6-nat-subtract
       (putnam-2004-b6-b (+ i 1))
       (putnam-2004-b6-b i))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b6-unbounded-gaps-p ()
  (forall (bound)
    (implies
     (natp bound)
     (putnam-2004-b6-gap-at-least-exists-p bound))))

;; This is exactly the cardinality of {a in A | a <= n}.
(defun putnam-2004-b6-count-through (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (if (putnam-2004-b6-member-p 0)
          1
        0)
    (+ (if (putnam-2004-b6-member-p n)
           1
         0)
       (putnam-2004-b6-count-through (- n 1)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b6-limit-from-cutoff-p
    (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (<= cutoff n))
     (<
      (* (putnam-2004-b6-count-through n)
         (/ n))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b6-limit-at-tolerance-p (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (< 0 cutoff)
     (putnam-2004-b6-limit-from-cutoff-p
      epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnam-2004-b6-density-tends-to-zero-p ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-2004-b6-limit-at-tolerance-p epsilon))))

;; B and N are eliminated by their source definitions. For real x >= 1 and
;; n=floor(x), the count is constant on [n,n+1), and
;; count(n)/x <= count(n)/n; natural arguments are cofinal in the reals.
;; Thus the source real limit is equivalent to the natural-argument limit
;; above. Positive rational tolerances are cofinal among positive real ones.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2004-b6-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2004-b6-set-nonempty-p)
    (putnam-2004-b6-positive-set-p)
    (putnam-2004-b6-increasing-natural-sequence-p)
    (putnam-2004-b6-exact-difference-range-p))
   (implies
    (putnam-2004-b6-unbounded-gaps-p)
    (putnam-2004-b6-density-tends-to-zero-p))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
