-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_a5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2006_a5): the quotient of the finite sum and
-- product of tan(theta + k*pi/n), for positive odd n and irrational theta/pi,
-- equals n or -n according as n is 1 or 3 modulo 4. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2006A5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

toNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
toNat fzero =
  zero
toNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (toNat i)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  twoN + twoN

record Odd (n : Nat) : Set where
  field
    half : Nat
    odd-equation : n == twoN * half + oneN

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

alternatingPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingPower reals n =
  naturalPower reals
    (negate reals (oneR reals))
    n

sineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
sineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (suc (twoN * n))))
    (fromNat reals (factorial (suc (twoN * n))))

cosineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
cosineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (twoN * n)))
    (fromNat reals (factorial (twoN * n)))

leibnizTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
leibnizTerm reals n =
  divide reals
    (alternatingPower reals n)
    (fromNat reals (suc (twoN * n)))

record PiValue
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (value : R) : Set where
  field
    positive :
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) value
    leibniz-series :
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (leibnizTerm reals)
        (divide reals value (fromNat reals fourN))

record StandardTrigonometry
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) : Set1 where
  field
    sine cosine : R -> R
    pi : R

    sine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (sineTerm reals x)
        (sine x)
    cosine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (cosineTerm reals x)
        (cosine x)
    pi-value :
      PiValue reals pi

open StandardTrigonometry

tangent :
  {R : Set} ->
  {reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R} ->
  StandardTrigonometry reals ->
  R ->
  R
tangent {reals = reals} trigonometry x =
  divide reals
    (sine trigonometry x)
    (cosine trigonometry x)

IsRational :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
IsRational reals x =
  Exists Int
    (\ numerator ->
      Exists Int
        (\ denominator ->
          denominator != pos zero
          and
          x ==
          divide reals
            (fromInt reals numerator)
            (fromInt reals denominator)))

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

productFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
productFin reals {zero} term =
  oneR reals
productFin reals {suc n} term =
  multiply reals
    (term fzero)
    (productFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

data RemainderFour : Set where
  remainder0 remainder1 remainder2 remainder3 : RemainderFour

nextRemainder : RemainderFour -> RemainderFour
nextRemainder remainder0 =
  remainder1
nextRemainder remainder1 =
  remainder2
nextRemainder remainder2 =
  remainder3
nextRemainder remainder3 =
  remainder0

remainderFour : Nat -> RemainderFour
remainderFour zero =
  remainder0
remainderFour (suc n) =
  nextRemainder (remainderFour n)

solutionValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
solutionValue reals n with remainderFour n
... | remainder1 =
  fromNat reals n
... | remainder0 =
  negate reals (fromNat reals n)
... | remainder2 =
  negate reals (fromNat reals n)
... | remainder3 =
  negate reals (fromNat reals n)

module Putnam2006A5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (trigonometry : StandardTrigonometry reals) where

  angle : {n : Nat} -> R -> Fin n -> R
  angle {n} theta index =
    add reals theta
      (divide reals
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals (suc (toNat index)))
          (pi trigonometry))
        (fromNat reals n))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (n : Nat) ->
    Odd n ->
    (theta : R) ->
    Not
      (IsRational reals
        (divide reals theta (pi trigonometry))) ->
    (a : Fin n -> R) ->
    ((index : Fin n) ->
      a index ==
      tangent trigonometry (angle theta index)) ->
    divide reals
      (sumFin reals a)
      (productFin reals a)
    ==
    solutionValue reals n

putnam-2006-a5 : Set1
putnam-2006-a5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (trigonometry : StandardTrigonometry reals) ->
  Putnam2006A5Statement.proposition reals trigonometry

title: putnam_2006_a5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_a5:
  the quotient of the sum and product of tangent values at n equally spaced
  angles, for odd n and an irrational theta/pi, is n or -n according to n
  modulo four. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_of_ratTheory
     real_sigmaTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2006_a5 =
  ``!n : num. !theta : real. !a : num -> real.
      ODD n /\
      theta / pi NOTIN q_set /\
      (!k : num.
         k IN (count (SUC n) DIFF count 1)
         ==>
         a k = tan (theta + (&k * pi) / &n))
      ==>
      REAL_SUM_IMAGE a (count (SUC n) DIFF count 1) /
        REAL_PROD_IMAGE a (count (SUC n) DIFF count 1) =
      (if n MOD 4 = 1 then (&n : real) else ~(&n : real))``;

title: putnam_2006_a5
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2006_a5: the ratio of the sum to the product of the tangent
  values tan(theta + k*pi/n), for odd positive n and irrational theta/pi,
  equals n or -n according to n modulo four. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  NN and Odd restrict n to the positive odd integers. The class
  RR ^m ( 1 ... n ) contains exactly the real-valued functions on the
  source index interval. Nonmembership of t / _pi in QQ is precisely the
  irrationality assumption on theta / pi.

  The finite sum and product use the same inclusive interval 1 ... n.
  The conditional inlines the explicit source solution: n when n is
  congruent to one modulo four, and -n otherwise. The final declaration
  is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no
  $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a k n t $.

  putnambench-putnam-2006-a5 $a |-
    A. n e. NN
      A. t e. RR
        A. a e. ( RR ^m ( 1 ... n ) )
          (
            (
              (
                n e. Odd
                /\
                ( t / _pi ) e/ QQ
              )
              /\
              A. k e. ( 1 ... n )
                ( a ` k )
                =
                (
                  tan
                  `
                  (
                    t
                    +
                    (
                      ( k x. _pi )
                      /
                      n
                    )
                  )
                )
            )
            ->
            (
              (
                sum_ k e. ( 1 ... n )
                  ( a ` k )
              )
              /
              (
                prod_ k e. ( 1 ... n )
                  ( a ` k )
              )
            )
            =
            if (
              ( n mod 4 ) = 1 ,
              n ,
              ( -u n )
            )
          )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2006_a5
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_a5:
:: for positive odd n and irrational theta/PI, the sum-to-product ratio of
:: tan(theta + k*PI/n), k=1,...,n, is n or -n according to n modulo 4.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies NUMBERS, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_4,
    VALUED_0, VALUED_1, CARD_1, CARD_3, RELAT_1, SUBSET_1, XBOOLE_0,
    FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2, TARSKI, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, ORDINAL1, ORDINAL4,
    BINOP_1, BINOP_2, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, FUNCOP_1, REAL_1, FINSEQOP,
    ZFMISC_1, XCMPLX_0, SETWISEO, SETWOP_2, FINSOP_1, RVSUM_1,
    INT_1, PARTFUN1, SIN_COS, SIN_COS4, RAT_1, IRRAT_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ZFMISC_1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1,
    NUMBERS, VALUED_0, XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XREAL_0, REAL_1, RELAT_1,
    FUNCT_1, PARTFUN1, BINOP_2, SETWISEO, FUNCT_2, BINOP_1, FUNCOP_1,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_4, VALUED_1, NAT_1, NAT_D, INT_1,
    FINSOP_1, FINSEQOP, SETWOP_2, RVSUM_1, SIN_COS, SIN_COS4, RAT_1,
    IRRAT_1;
  constructors PARTFUN1, BINOP_1, SETWISEO, NAT_1, NAT_D, BINOP_2,
    VALUED_1, FINSEQOP, FINSEQ_4, FINSOP_1, SETWOP_2, RELSET_1,
    XXREAL_1, REAL_1, FINSEQ_2, RVSUM_1, SIN_COS, SIN_COS4, RAT_1,
    IRRAT_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, FUNCT_1, ORDINAL1, FUNCT_2,
    FUNCOP_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, NAT_1, BINOP_2,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, RELAT_1, FINSEQ_4, CARD_1,
    RVSUM_1, SIN_COS, RELSET_1, MEMBERED, INT_1, RAT_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat,
      theta being Real,
      a being FinSequence of REAL st
    n mod 2 = 1 &
    theta / PI is irrational &
    len a = n &
    (for k being Nat st k in Seg n holds
      a.k = tan(theta + (k qua Real) * PI / (n qua Real)))
  holds
    (n mod 4 = 1 &
      (Sum a) / (Product a) = (n qua Real)) or
    (n mod 4 <> 1 &
      (Sum a) / (Product a) = -(n qua Real))
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2006_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_a5:
% for positive odd n and irrational theta/pi, the sum of tan(theta + k*pi/n)
% for k from 1 through n divided by their product equals n when n is 1
% modulo 4, and equals -n otherwise. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2006_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  sine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        sine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index + 1),
              nat_factorial(2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  cosine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index),
              nat_factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  sine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): sine_partial(x, count),
          value))

  cosine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat): cosine_partial(x, count),
          value))

  tangent(x: real): real =
    safe_div(sine(x), cosine(x))

  pi: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        3 < value
          AND value < 4
          AND cosine(value / 2) = 0)

  indexed_sum(a: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      indexed_sum(a, count - 1) + a(count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  indexed_product(a: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      indexed_product(a, count - 1) * a(count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  putnam_2006_a5_solution(n: nat): int =
    IF mod(n, 4) = 1 THEN
      n :: int
    ELSE
      -(n :: int)
    ENDIF

  putnam_2006_a5: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (theta: real), (a: real_sequence):
      (mod(n, 2) = 1
        AND NOT rational?(safe_div(theta, pi))
        AND (FORALL (k: nat):
          1 <= k AND k <= n IMPLIES
            a(k) =
              tangent(
                theta
                  + safe_div(
                      (k :: real) * pi,
                      n :: real))))
      IMPLIES
        safe_div(indexed_sum(a, n), indexed_product(a, n))
          = (putnam_2006_a5_solution(n) :: real)
END putnam_2006_a5

title: putnam_2006_b1
content:
import Mathlib

noncomputable abbrev putnam_2006_b1_solution : ℝ := sorry
-- 3 * Real.sqrt 3 / 2
/--
Show that the curve $x^3 + 3xy + y^3 = 1$ contains only one set of three distinct points, $A$, $B$, and $C$, which are vertices of an equilateral triangle, and find its area.
-/
theorem putnam_2006_b1
  (curve : Set (ℝ × ℝ))
  (hcurve : curve = {(x, y) | x ^ 3 + 3 * x * y + y ^ 3 = 1})
  (equilateral : Set (ℝ × ℝ) → Prop)
  (hequilateral : ∀ S, equilateral S ↔ S.encard = 3 ∧
    ∃ d : ℝ, ∀ P ∈ S, ∀ Q ∈ S, P ≠ Q →
    Real.sqrt ((P.1 - Q.1)^2 + (P.2 - Q.2)^2) = d) :
  (∃! S : Set (ℝ × ℝ), S ⊆ curve ∧ equilateral S) ∧
  (∃ S : Set (ℝ × ℝ), S ⊆ curve ∧ equilateral S ∧ (MeasureTheory.volume (convexHull ℝ S)).toReal = putnam_2006_b1_solution) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2006_b1
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_b1:
   the cubic curve x^3 + 3xy + y^3 = 1 contains a unique three-point
   equilateral triangle, whose convex hull has area 3 * sqrt(3) / 2.
   This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals List.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition point := (R * R)%type.
Definition point_set := point -> Prop.

Definition putnam_2006_b1_curve : point_set :=
  fun p : point =>
    fst p ^ 3 + 3 * fst p * snd p + snd p ^ 3 = 1.

Definition putnam_2006_b1_distance (p q : point) : R :=
  sqrt ((fst p - fst q) ^ 2 + (snd p - snd q) ^ 2).

Definition putnam_2006_b1_subset
    (A B : point_set) : Prop :=
  forall p : point, A p -> B p.

Definition putnam_2006_b1_same_set
    (A B : point_set) : Prop :=
  forall p : point, A p <-> B p.

Definition putnam_2006_b1_has_cardinality
    (S : point_set) (n : nat) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list point,
    NoDup enumeration /\
    length enumeration = n /\
    forall p : point, In p enumeration <-> S p.

Definition putnam_2006_b1_equilateral
    (S : point_set) : Prop :=
  putnam_2006_b1_has_cardinality S 3%nat /\
  exists d : R,
    forall P Q : point,
      S P ->
      S Q ->
      P <> Q ->
      putnam_2006_b1_distance P Q = d.

Definition putnam_2006_b1_affine_combination
    (t : R) (p q : point) : point :=
  ((1 - t) * fst p + t * fst q,
   (1 - t) * snd p + t * snd q).

Definition putnam_2006_b1_convex
    (S : point_set) : Prop :=
  forall (p q : point) (t : R),
    S p ->
    S q ->
    0 <= t <= 1 ->
    S (putnam_2006_b1_affine_combination t p q).

Definition putnam_2006_b1_convex_hull
    (S : point_set) : point_set :=
  fun p : point =>
    forall C : point_set,
      putnam_2006_b1_convex C ->
      putnam_2006_b1_subset S C ->
      C p.

Record putnam_2006_b1_open_rectangle : Type := {
  putnam_2006_b1_x_lower : R;
  putnam_2006_b1_x_upper : R;
  putnam_2006_b1_y_lower : R;
  putnam_2006_b1_y_upper : R
}.

Definition putnam_2006_b1_in_open_rectangle
    (rectangle : putnam_2006_b1_open_rectangle)
    (p : point) : Prop :=
  putnam_2006_b1_x_lower rectangle < fst p <
    putnam_2006_b1_x_upper rectangle /\
  putnam_2006_b1_y_lower rectangle < snd p <
    putnam_2006_b1_y_upper rectangle.

Definition putnam_2006_b1_rectangle_area
    (rectangle : putnam_2006_b1_open_rectangle) : R :=
  Rmax 0
    (putnam_2006_b1_x_upper rectangle -
     putnam_2006_b1_x_lower rectangle) *
  Rmax 0
    (putnam_2006_b1_y_upper rectangle -
     putnam_2006_b1_y_lower rectangle).

Definition putnam_2006_b1_rectangles_cover
    (S : point_set)
    (rectangles : nat -> putnam_2006_b1_open_rectangle) : Prop :=
  forall p : point,
    S p ->
    exists n : nat,
      putnam_2006_b1_in_open_rectangle (rectangles n) p.

Fixpoint putnam_2006_b1_partial_rectangle_area
    (rectangles : nat -> putnam_2006_b1_open_rectangle)
    (n : nat) : R :=
  match n with
  | O => 0
  | S k =>
      putnam_2006_b1_partial_rectangle_area rectangles k +
      putnam_2006_b1_rectangle_area (rectangles k)
  end.

(* The countable-open-rectangle characterization of planar Lebesgue outer
   measure, which equals Lebesgue measure on this finite convex hull. *)
Definition putnam_2006_b1_has_planar_lebesgue_measure
    (S : point_set) (area : R) : Prop :=
  0 <= area /\
  (forall rectangles : nat -> putnam_2006_b1_open_rectangle,
    putnam_2006_b1_rectangles_cover S rectangles ->
    forall lower : R,
      lower < area ->
      exists n : nat,
        lower <
          putnam_2006_b1_partial_rectangle_area rectangles n) /\
  (forall epsilon : R,
    0 < epsilon ->
    exists rectangles : nat -> putnam_2006_b1_open_rectangle,
      putnam_2006_b1_rectangles_cover S rectangles /\
      forall n : nat,
        putnam_2006_b1_partial_rectangle_area rectangles n <
          area + epsilon).

Definition putnam_2006_b1_solution : R :=
  3 * sqrt 3 / 2.

Definition putnam_2006_b1_unique_triangle : Prop :=
  exists S : point_set,
    putnam_2006_b1_subset S putnam_2006_b1_curve /\
    putnam_2006_b1_equilateral S /\
    forall T : point_set,
      putnam_2006_b1_subset T putnam_2006_b1_curve /\
      putnam_2006_b1_equilateral T ->
      putnam_2006_b1_same_set T S.

Theorem putnam_2006_b1 :
  putnam_2006_b1_unique_triangle /\
  exists S : point_set,
    putnam_2006_b1_subset S putnam_2006_b1_curve /\
    putnam_2006_b1_equilateral S /\
    putnam_2006_b1_has_planar_lebesgue_measure
      (putnam_2006_b1_convex_hull S)
      putnam_2006_b1_solution.
Admitted.

theory putnam_2006_b1 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Lebesgue_Measure"
"HOL-Analysis.Finite_Cartesian_Product"
begin

definition putnam_2006_b1_solution :: "real" where
"putnam_2006_b1_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* 3 * sqrt 3 / 2 *)
theorem putnam_2006_b1:
  fixes curve :: "(real^2) set"
    and equilateral :: "(real^2) set \<Rightarrow> bool"
  defines "curve \<equiv> {p :: real^2. (p$1)^3 + 3 * (p$1) * (p$2) + (p$2)^3 = 1}"
    and "equilateral \<equiv> \<lambda> S :: (real^2) set. card S = 3 \<and> (\<exists> d :: real. \<forall> P \<in> S. \<forall> Q \<in> S. P \<noteq> Q \<longrightarrow> dist P Q = d)"
  shows "((\<exists>! S :: (real^2) set. S \<subseteq> curve \<and> equilateral S) \<and> (\<exists> S :: (real^2) set. S \<subseteq> curve \<and> equilateral S \<and> emeasure lebesgue (convex hull S) = putnam_2006_b1_solution))"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_2006_b1
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_b1:
  uniqueness of an equilateral three-point subset of the cubic curve
  x^3 + 3xy + y^3 = 1, whose triangle has area 3 sqrt(3) / 2. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let edist =
     \(P:real#real) (Q:real#real).
       sqrt ((FST P - FST Q) pow 2 + (SND P - SND Q) pow 2) in
   let curve =
     {P:real#real |
        FST P pow 3 + &3 * FST P * SND P + SND P pow 3 = &1} in
   let equilateral =
     \(S:(real#real)->bool).
       S HAS_SIZE 3 /\
       ?d:real.
         !P Q:real#real.
           P IN S /\ Q IN S /\ ~(P = Q)
           ==> edist P Q = d in
   let triangle_area =
     \(A:real#real) (B:real#real) (C:real#real).
       abs ((FST B - FST A) * (SND C - SND A) -
            (SND B - SND A) * (FST C - FST A)) / &2 in
   let putnam_2006_b1_solution = &3 * sqrt (&3) / &2 in
   (?!S:(real#real)->bool.
       S SUBSET curve /\ equilateral S) /\
   (?S:(real#real)->bool. ?A B C:real#real.
      S SUBSET curve /\
      equilateral S /\
      S = {A,B,C} /\
      triangle_area A B C = putnam_2006_b1_solution)`;;

title: putnam_2006_b1
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_b1:
;; the cubic curve x^3 + 3xy + y^3 = 1 has a unique three-point equilateral
;; subset, and its convex-hull area is 3*sqrt(3)/2. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The conservative operations below present an arbitrary real closed ordered
;; field. Real closed fields have the same first-order theory as the reals.
;; The named square-root operation is fixed by its nonnegative-root law, so the
;; displayed answer denotes exactly 3*sqrt(3)/2.
;;
;; A three-element set is represented extensionally by three pairwise distinct
;; points. Equality of such sets is membership in both directions, so coordinate
;; order is irrelevant. Equal squared side lengths are equivalent to the source
;; distance definition of equilateral. For three distinct equilateral points,
;; the Lebesgue measure of their convex hull is the standard triangle area
;; |det(B-A,C-A)|/2, used explicitly below.
;;
;; The final existential packages the source conjunction equivalently: it gives
;; an area-qualified triangle and says that every other equilateral triple on
;; the curve enumerates the same set. All point and competitor quantifiers remain
;; internal to DEFUN-SK.

(defstub p06b1-real-p (ctx value) t)
(defstub p06b1-zero (ctx) t)
(defstub p06b1-one (ctx) t)
(defstub p06b1-add-op (ctx left right) t)
(defstub p06b1-mul-op (ctx left right) t)
(defstub p06b1-neg-op (ctx value) t)
(defstub p06b1-inv-op (ctx value) t)
(defstub p06b1-less-op (ctx left right) t)
(defstub p06b1-sqrt-op (ctx value) t)

(defun p06b1-add (ctx left right)
  (p06b1-add-op ctx left right))

(defun p06b1-mul (ctx left right)
  (p06b1-mul-op ctx left right))

(defun p06b1-neg (ctx value)
  (p06b1-neg-op ctx value))

(defun p06b1-inv (ctx value)
  (p06b1-inv-op ctx value))

(defun p06b1-less-p (ctx left right)
  (if (p06b1-less-op ctx left right) t nil))

(defun p06b1-sqrt (ctx value)
  (p06b1-sqrt-op ctx value))

(defun p06b1-sub (ctx left right)
  (p06b1-add ctx left (p06b1-neg ctx right)))

(defun p06b1-div (ctx numerator denominator)
  (p06b1-mul ctx numerator (p06b1-inv ctx denominator)))

(defun p06b1-square (ctx value)
  (p06b1-mul ctx value value))

(defun p06b1-cube (ctx value)
  (p06b1-mul ctx (p06b1-square ctx value) value))

(defun p06b1-two (ctx)
  (p06b1-add ctx (p06b1-one ctx) (p06b1-one ctx)))

(defun p06b1-three (ctx)
  (p06b1-add ctx (p06b1-two ctx) (p06b1-one ctx)))

(defun p06b1-abs (ctx value)
  (if (p06b1-less-p ctx value (p06b1-zero ctx))
      (p06b1-neg ctx value)
    value))

(defun-sk p06b1-field-laws-p (ctx)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p06b1-real-p ctx x)
      (p06b1-real-p ctx y)
      (p06b1-real-p ctx z))
     (and
      (p06b1-real-p ctx (p06b1-add ctx x y))
      (p06b1-real-p ctx (p06b1-mul ctx x y))
      (p06b1-real-p ctx (p06b1-neg ctx x))
      (p06b1-real-p ctx (p06b1-inv ctx x))
      (equal
       (p06b1-add ctx (p06b1-add ctx x y) z)
       (p06b1-add ctx x (p06b1-add ctx y z)))
      (equal
       (p06b1-add ctx x y)
       (p06b1-add ctx y x))
      (equal
       (p06b1-add ctx x (p06b1-zero ctx))
       x)
      (equal
       (p06b1-add ctx x (p06b1-neg ctx x))
       (p06b1-zero ctx))
      (equal
       (p06b1-mul ctx (p06b1-mul ctx x y) z)
       (p06b1-mul ctx x (p06b1-mul ctx y z)))
      (equal
       (p06b1-mul ctx x y)
       (p06b1-mul ctx y x))
      (equal
       (p06b1-mul ctx x (p06b1-one ctx))
       x)
      (implies
       (equal x (p06b1-zero ctx))
       (equal
        (p06b1-inv ctx x)
        (p06b1-zero ctx)))
      (implies
       (not (equal x (p06b1-zero ctx)))
       (equal
        (p06b1-mul ctx x (p06b1-inv ctx x))
        (p06b1-one ctx)))
      (equal
       (p06b1-mul ctx x (p06b1-add ctx y z))
       (p06b1-add
        ctx
        (p06b1-mul ctx x y)
        (p06b1-mul ctx x z)))))))

(defun-sk p06b1-order-laws-p (ctx)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p06b1-real-p ctx x)
      (p06b1-real-p ctx y)
      (p06b1-real-p ctx z))
     (and
      (not (p06b1-less-p ctx x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (p06b1-less-p ctx x y)
       (p06b1-less-p ctx y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (p06b1-less-p ctx x y)
        (p06b1-less-p ctx y z))
       (p06b1-less-p ctx x z))
      (implies
       (p06b1-less-p ctx x y)
       (p06b1-less-p
        ctx
        (p06b1-add ctx x z)
        (p06b1-add ctx y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (p06b1-less-p ctx (p06b1-zero ctx) x)
        (p06b1-less-p ctx (p06b1-zero ctx) y))
       (p06b1-less-p
        ctx
        (p06b1-zero ctx)
        (p06b1-mul ctx x y)))))))

(defun p06b1-real-list-p (values ctx)
  (if (endp values)
      (equal values nil)
    (and
     (p06b1-real-p ctx (car values))
     (p06b1-real-list-p (cdr values) ctx))))

(defun p06b1-polynomial-p (coefficients ctx)
  (and
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (consp coefficients)
   (p06b1-real-list-p coefficients ctx)
   (or
    (equal (len coefficients) 1)
    (not
     (equal
      (car (last coefficients))
      (p06b1-zero ctx))))))

(defun p06b1-polynomial-eval (ctx coefficients value)
  (if (endp coefficients)
      (p06b1-zero ctx)
    (p06b1-add
     ctx
     (car coefficients)
     (p06b1-mul
      ctx
      value
      (p06b1-polynomial-eval
       ctx (cdr coefficients) value)))))

(defun-sk p06b1-odd-polynomial-root-exists-p
    (ctx coefficients)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (p06b1-real-p ctx root)
     (equal
      (p06b1-polynomial-eval ctx coefficients root)
      (p06b1-zero ctx)))))

(defun-sk p06b1-square-root-laws-p (ctx)
  (forall (value)
    (implies
     (and
      (p06b1-real-p ctx value)
      (not
       (p06b1-less-p ctx value (p06b1-zero ctx))))
     (let ((root (p06b1-sqrt ctx value)))
       (and
        (p06b1-real-p ctx root)
        (not
         (p06b1-less-p ctx root (p06b1-zero ctx)))
        (equal
         (p06b1-square ctx root)
         value))))))

(defun-sk p06b1-odd-root-laws-p (ctx)
  (forall (coefficients)
    (implies
     (and
      (p06b1-polynomial-p coefficients ctx)
      (evenp (len coefficients)))
     (p06b1-odd-polynomial-root-exists-p
      ctx coefficients))))

(defun p06b1-real-closed-field-p (ctx)
  (and
   (p06b1-real-p ctx (p06b1-zero ctx))
   (p06b1-real-p ctx (p06b1-one ctx))
   (not
    (equal
     (p06b1-zero ctx)
     (p06b1-one ctx)))
   (p06b1-field-laws-p ctx)
   (p06b1-order-laws-p ctx)
   (p06b1-less-p
    ctx (p06b1-zero ctx) (p06b1-one ctx))
   (p06b1-square-root-laws-p ctx)
   (p06b1-odd-root-laws-p ctx)))

(defun p06b1-point-p (ctx x y)
  (and
   (p06b1-real-p ctx x)
   (p06b1-real-p ctx y)))

(defun p06b1-curve-point-p (ctx x y)
  (and
   (p06b1-point-p ctx x y)
   (equal
    (p06b1-add
     ctx
     (p06b1-cube ctx x)
     (p06b1-add
      ctx
      (p06b1-mul
       ctx
       (p06b1-three ctx)
       (p06b1-mul ctx x y))
      (p06b1-cube ctx y)))
    (p06b1-one ctx))))

(defun p06b1-same-point-p (ax ay bx by)
  (and
   (equal ax bx)
   (equal ay by)))

(defun p06b1-distinct-points-p (ax ay bx by)
  (not (p06b1-same-point-p ax ay bx by)))

(defun p06b1-squared-distance
    (ctx ax ay bx by)
  (p06b1-add
   ctx
   (p06b1-square ctx (p06b1-sub ctx ax bx))
   (p06b1-square ctx (p06b1-sub ctx ay by))))

(defun p06b1-equilateral-triple-p
    (ctx ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (let ((ab
         (p06b1-squared-distance
          ctx ax ay bx by))
        (ac
         (p06b1-squared-distance
          ctx ax ay cx cy))
        (bc
         (p06b1-squared-distance
          ctx bx by cx cy)))
    (and
     (p06b1-distinct-points-p ax ay bx by)
     (p06b1-distinct-points-p ax ay cx cy)
     (p06b1-distinct-points-p bx by cx cy)
     (equal ab ac)
     (equal ac bc))))

(defun p06b1-triangle-on-curve-p
    (ctx ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (and
   (p06b1-curve-point-p ctx ax ay)
   (p06b1-curve-point-p ctx bx by)
   (p06b1-curve-point-p ctx cx cy)
   (p06b1-equilateral-triple-p
    ctx ax ay bx by cx cy)))

(defun p06b1-point-in-triple-p
    (px py ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (or
   (p06b1-same-point-p px py ax ay)
   (p06b1-same-point-p px py bx by)
   (p06b1-same-point-p px py cx cy)))

(defun p06b1-same-triangle-set-p
    (ax ay bx by cx cy dx dy ex ey fx fy)
  (and
   (p06b1-point-in-triple-p
    ax ay dx dy ex ey fx fy)
   (p06b1-point-in-triple-p
    bx by dx dy ex ey fx fy)
   (p06b1-point-in-triple-p
    cx cy dx dy ex ey fx fy)
   (p06b1-point-in-triple-p
    dx dy ax ay bx by cx cy)
   (p06b1-point-in-triple-p
    ex ey ax ay bx by cx cy)
   (p06b1-point-in-triple-p
    fx fy ax ay bx by cx cy)))

(defun p06b1-determinant
    (ctx ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (p06b1-sub
   ctx
   (p06b1-mul
    ctx
    (p06b1-sub ctx bx ax)
    (p06b1-sub ctx cy ay))
   (p06b1-mul
    ctx
    (p06b1-sub ctx by ay)
    (p06b1-sub ctx cx ax))))

(defun p06b1-triangle-area
    (ctx ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (p06b1-div
   ctx
   (p06b1-abs
    ctx
    (p06b1-determinant
     ctx ax ay bx by cx cy))
   (p06b1-two ctx)))

(defun p06b1-answer (ctx)
  (p06b1-div
   ctx
   (p06b1-mul
    ctx
    (p06b1-three ctx)
    (p06b1-sqrt ctx (p06b1-three ctx)))
   (p06b1-two ctx)))

(defun p06b1-area-is-answer-p
    (ctx ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (equal
   (p06b1-triangle-area
    ctx ax ay bx by cx cy)
   (p06b1-answer ctx)))

(defun-sk p06b1-all-triangles-are-this-set-p
    (ctx ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (forall (dx dy ex ey fx fy)
    (implies
     (p06b1-triangle-on-curve-p
      ctx dx dy ex ey fx fy)
     (p06b1-same-triangle-set-p
      ax ay bx by cx cy
      dx dy ex ey fx fy))))

(defun-sk p06b1-unique-area-triangle-exists-p (ctx)
  (exists (ax ay bx by cx cy)
    (and
     (p06b1-triangle-on-curve-p
      ctx ax ay bx by cx cy)
     (p06b1-area-is-answer-p
      ctx ax ay bx by cx cy)
     (p06b1-all-triangles-are-this-set-p
      ctx ax ay bx by cx cy))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2006-b1-statement (ctx)
  (implies
   (p06b1-real-closed-field-p ctx)
   (p06b1-unique-area-triangle-exists-p ctx)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2006_b1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_b1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2006_b1): the real cubic x^3 + 3xy + y^3 = 1
-- has a unique equilateral three-point subset, of area 3 sqrt(3) / 2.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

cube :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
cube reals x =
  multiply reals (square reals x) x

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

absolute :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
absolute reals x =
  squareRoot reals (square reals x)

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

PointEqual :
  {R : Set} ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
PointEqual p q =
  x-coordinate p == x-coordinate q
  and
  y-coordinate p == y-coordinate q

PointSet : Set -> Set1
PointSet R =
  Point R -> Set

SetEqual :
  {R : Set} ->
  PointSet R ->
  PointSet R ->
  Set
SetEqual {R} S T =
  (p : Point R) ->
  Iff (S p) (T p)

Subset :
  {R : Set} ->
  PointSet R ->
  PointSet R ->
  Set
Subset {R} S T =
  (p : Point R) ->
  S p ->
  T p

squaredDistance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
squaredDistance reals p q =
  add reals
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q)))
    (square reals
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)))

distance :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
distance reals p q =
  squareRoot reals (squaredDistance reals p q)

determinant :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
determinant reals a b c =
  subtract reals
    (multiply reals
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate b) (x-coordinate a))
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate c) (y-coordinate a)))
    (multiply reals
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate b) (y-coordinate a))
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate c) (x-coordinate a)))

triangleArea :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
triangleArea reals a b c =
  divide reals
    (absolute reals (determinant reals a b c))
    (fromNat reals 2)

record EnumeratesThree
  {R : Set}
  (S : PointSet R) :
  Set where

  field
    first-point second-point third-point : Point R

    first-member  : S first-point
    second-member : S second-point
    third-member  : S third-point

    first-second-distinct :
      Not (PointEqual first-point second-point)
    first-third-distinct :
      Not (PointEqual first-point third-point)
    second-third-distinct :
      Not (PointEqual second-point third-point)

    complete :
      (p : Point R) ->
      S p ->
      PointEqual p first-point
      or PointEqual p second-point
      or PointEqual p third-point

open EnumeratesThree

record Equilateral
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (S : PointSet R) :
  Set where

  field
    three-points : EnumeratesThree S
    side-length  : R
    equal-distances :
      (p q : Point R) ->
      S p ->
      S q ->
      Not (PointEqual p q) ->
      distance reals p q == side-length

record HasArea
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (S : PointSet R)
  (area : R) :
  Set where

  field
    enumeration : EnumeratesThree S
    area-equality :
      triangleArea reals
        (first-point enumeration)
        (second-point enumeration)
        (third-point enumeration)
      ==
      area

module Putnam2006B1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  curve : PointSet R
  curve p =
    add reals
      (add reals
        (cube reals (x-coordinate p))
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals 3)
          (multiply reals
            (x-coordinate p)
            (y-coordinate p))))
      (cube reals (y-coordinate p))
    ==
    oneR reals

  Qualifies : PointSet R -> Set
  Qualifies S =
    Subset S curve
    and
    Equilateral reals S

  record UniqueEquilateralSet : Set1 where
    field
      set        : PointSet R
      property   : Qualifies set
      uniqueness :
        (other : PointSet R) ->
        Qualifies other ->
        SetEqual other set

  solution-area : R
  solution-area =
    divide reals
      (multiply reals
        (fromNat reals 3)
        (squareRoot reals (fromNat reals 3)))
      (fromNat reals 2)

  record AreaWitness : Set1 where
    field
      set         : PointSet R
      lies-on-curve : Subset set curve
      equilateral : Equilateral reals set
      has-area    : HasArea reals set solution-area

  record Conclusion : Set1 where
    field
      unique-equilateral-set : UniqueEquilateralSet
      area-witness           : AreaWitness

putnam-2006-b1 : Set1
putnam-2006-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2006B1Statement.Conclusion reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_b1:
  the cubic plane curve x^3 + 3xy + y^3 = 1 contains a unique three-point
  equilateral triangle, whose area is 3 * sqrt 3 / 2. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory transcTheory;
open extrealTheory measureTheory lebesgue_measureTheory martingaleTheory;

val putnam_2006_b1 =
  ``let cubic_curve =
      {P : real # real |
         FST P pow 3 + 3 * FST P * SND P + SND P pow 3 = 1}
    in
    let dist =
      \P Q : real # real.
        sqrt ((FST P - FST Q) pow 2 + (SND P - SND Q) pow 2)
    in
    let equilateral =
      \S : (real # real) set.
        FINITE S /\
        CARD S = 3 /\
        ?d : real.
          !P Q : real # real.
            P IN S /\ Q IN S /\ P <> Q ==> dist P Q = d
    in
    let in_convex_hull =
      \S : (real # real) set.
      \X : real # real.
        ?w : (real # real) -> real.
          (!P : real # real. P IN S ==> 0 <= w P) /\
          SIGMA w S = 1 /\
          X =
            (SIGMA (\P : real # real. w P * FST P) S,
             SIGMA (\P : real # real. w P * SND P) S)
    in
    let area =
      measure (prod_measure_space lebesgue lebesgue)
    in
      (?!S : (real # real) set.
         S SUBSET cubic_curve /\ equilateral S) /\
      (?S : (real # real) set.
         S SUBSET cubic_curve /\
         equilateral S /\
         area (in_convex_hull S) = Normal (3 * sqrt 3 / 2))``;

title: putnam_2006_b1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2006_b1: uniqueness of an equilateral three-point subset of the
  cubic curve x^3 + 3xy + y^3 = 1, whose triangle has area
  3 * sqrt(3) / 2. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P06B1R2 is the real coordinate plane and P06B1Dist is Euclidean distance.
  P06B1Curve is the stated cubic curve. P06B1Equilateral requires exactly
  three points and one common distance between every two distinct points.
  P06B1Hull is the convex hull of a finite set through internally existential
  nonnegative barycentric weights, and P06B1Area is its planar Lebesgue
  measure through set.mm's finite-dimensional volume function voln.

  The final declaration preserves the unique existential set and the separate
  existential area assertion from the formal sources, while inlining their
  annotated solution value. It is an unproved $a statement. This root candidate
  file declares no $p statement; the included set.mm library contains proofs.
$)

$c P06B1I P06B1R2 P06B1Dist P06B1Curve $.
$c P06B1Equilateral P06B1Hull P06B1Area $.

p06b1-index-syntax $a class P06B1I $.
p06b1-plane-syntax $a class P06B1R2 $.
p06b1-distance-syntax $a class ( P06B1Dist A B ) $.
p06b1-curve-syntax $a class P06B1Curve $.
p06b1-equilateral-syntax $a wff ( P06B1Equilateral S ) $.
p06b1-hull-syntax $a class ( P06B1Hull S ) $.
p06b1-area-syntax $a class ( P06B1Area S ) $.

p06b1-index-definition $a |- P06B1I = ( 1 ... 2 ) $.

p06b1-plane-definition $a |- P06B1R2 = ( RR ^m P06B1I ) $.

${
  $d A B k $.

  p06b1-distance-definition $a |- (
    P06B1Dist A B
  ) = (
    sqrt
    `
    (
      sum_ k e. P06B1I
        ( ( ( A ` k ) - ( B ` k ) ) ^ 2 )
    )
  ) $.
$}

p06b1-curve-definition $a |- P06B1Curve = {
  p e. P06B1R2 |
  (
    (
      (
        ( p ` 1 ) ^ 3
      )
      +
      (
        ( 3 x. ( p ` 1 ) )
        x.
        ( p ` 2 )
      )
    )
    +
    ( ( p ` 2 ) ^ 3 )
  )
  =
  1
} $.

${
  $d P Q S d $.

  p06b1-equilateral-definition $a |- (
    ( P06B1Equilateral S )
    <->
    (
      ( # ` S ) = 3
      /\
      E. d e. RR
        A. P e. S A. Q e. S
          (
            P =/= Q
            ->
            ( P06B1Dist P Q ) = d
          )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d S i w x z $.

  p06b1-hull-definition $a |- (
    P06B1Hull S
  ) = {
    z e. P06B1R2 |
    E. w
      (
        (
          w : S --> RR
          /\
          A. x e. S 0 <_ ( w ` x )
        )
        /\
        (
          ( sum_ x e. S ( w ` x ) ) = 1
          /\
          z =
            (
              i e. P06B1I |->
                sum_ x e. S
                  (
                    ( w ` x )
                    x.
                    ( x ` i )
                  )
            )
        )
      )
  } $.
$}

p06b1-area-definition $a |- (
  P06B1Area S
) = (
  ( voln ` P06B1I )
  `
  ( P06B1Hull S )
) $.

putnambench-putnam-2006-b1 $a |- (
  E! S e. ~P P06B1R2
    (
      S C_ P06B1Curve
      /\
      ( P06B1Equilateral S )
    )
  /\
  E. S e. ~P P06B1R2
    (
      (
        S C_ P06B1Curve
        /\
        ( P06B1Equilateral S )
      )
      /\
      ( P06B1Area S )
      =
      ( ( 3 x. ( sqrt ` 3 ) ) / 2 )
    )
) $.

title: putnam_2006_b1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_2006_b1:
% the cubic curve x^3 + 3*x*y + y^3 = 1 contains a unique three-point
% equilateral triangle, whose convex-hull area is 3*sqrt(3)/2. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_2006_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]
  point_set: TYPE = [point -> bool]

  squared_distance(P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q)) ^ 2
      + (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q)) ^ 2

  distance(P, Q: point): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (length: real):
        0 <= length
          AND length * length = squared_distance(P, Q))

  curve: point_set =
    LAMBDA (P: point):
      x_coord(P) ^ 3
        + 3 * x_coord(P) * y_coord(P)
        + y_coord(P) ^ 3
        = 1

  point_subset(A, B: point_set): bool =
    FORALL (P: point):
      A(P) IMPLIES B(P)

  exactly_three(S: point_set): bool =
    EXISTS (A, B, C: point):
      A /= B
        AND A /= C
        AND B /= C
        AND FORALL (P: point):
          S(P) IFF (P = A OR P = B OR P = C)

  equilateral(S: point_set): bool =
    exactly_three(S)
      AND EXISTS (side_length: real):
        FORALL (P, Q: point):
          S(P) AND S(Q) AND P /= Q
            IMPLIES distance(P, Q) = side_length

  triangle_area(A, B, C: point): real =
    abs(
      (x_coord(B) - x_coord(A)) * (y_coord(C) - y_coord(A))
        - (y_coord(B) - y_coord(A)) * (x_coord(C) - x_coord(A)))
      / 2

  has_convex_hull_area(S: point_set, area: real): bool =
    EXISTS (A, B, C: point):
      A /= B
        AND A /= C
        AND B /= C
        AND (FORALL (P: point):
          S(P) IFF (P = A OR P = B OR P = C))
        AND area = triangle_area(A, B, C)

  sqrt_three: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (root: real):
        0 <= root AND root * root = 3)

  putnam_2006_b1_solution: real =
    3 * sqrt_three / 2

  putnam_2006_b1: bool =
    (EXISTS (S: point_set):
      point_subset(S, curve)
        AND equilateral(S)
        AND FORALL (T: point_set):
          point_subset(T, curve) AND equilateral(T)
            IMPLIES T = S)
      AND EXISTS (S: point_set):
        point_subset(S, curve)
          AND equilateral(S)
          AND has_convex_hull_area(S, putnam_2006_b1_solution)
END putnam_2006_b1

    (n : nat)
    (hn : gt n 0)
    (X : seq R)

title: putnam_2006_b2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_b2:
;; every nonempty finite set of real numbers has a nonempty subset whose sum,
;; after adding an integer, has absolute value at most 1/(n+1). This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A real number is represented by a function object that maps every positive
;; rational precision to a rational approximation. The Cauchy condition below
;; makes the approximation at precision EPSILON lie within EPSILON of a unique
;; real limit. Conversely, every real number has such a rational Cauchy name,
;; so this does not restrict the source domain to rational values.

(defun putnam-2006-b2-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'cons
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2006-b2-term-list (cdr terms)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-apply-term (function arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2006-b2-quoted function)
        (putnam-2006-b2-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'if
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2006-b2-and-terms (cdr terms))
            (putnam-2006-b2-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2006-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list 'if
        hypothesis
        conclusion
        (putnam-2006-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-negate-term (value)
  (list 'unary-- value))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-subtract-term (left right)
  (putnam-2006-b2-add-term
   left
   (putnam-2006-b2-negate-term right)))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-multiply-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-* left right))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-reciprocal-term (value)
  (list 'unary-/ value))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-divide-term (numerator denominator)
  (putnam-2006-b2-multiply-term
   numerator
   (putnam-2006-b2-reciprocal-term denominator)))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-absolute-term (value)
  (list 'if
        (list '<
              value
              (putnam-2006-b2-quoted 0))
        (putnam-2006-b2-negate-term value)
        value))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-less-equal-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        (list '< right left)
        (putnam-2006-b2-quoted nil)
        (putnam-2006-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-positive-rational-term (value)
  (putnam-2006-b2-and-terms
   (list
    (list 'rationalp value)
    (list '<
          (putnam-2006-b2-quoted 0)
          value))))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda
        formals
        (putnam-2006-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-cauchy-function (name)
  (let* ((at-epsilon
          (putnam-2006-b2-apply-term
           name
           (list 'epsilon)))
         (at-eta
          (putnam-2006-b2-apply-term
           name
           (list 'eta)))
         (distance
          (putnam-2006-b2-absolute-term
           (putnam-2006-b2-subtract-term
            at-epsilon at-eta))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon eta)
     (putnam-2006-b2-implies-term
      (putnam-2006-b2-and-terms
       (list
        (putnam-2006-b2-positive-rational-term
         'epsilon)
        (putnam-2006-b2-positive-rational-term
         'eta)))
      (putnam-2006-b2-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp at-epsilon)
        (list 'rationalp at-eta)
        (putnam-2006-b2-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2006-b2-add-term
          'epsilon 'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-real-name-p (name)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2006-b2-cauchy-function name)
    (putnam-2006-b2-true-function
     '(epsilon eta)))))

;; Two valid Cauchy names denote the same real exactly when their values at
;; every positive rational EPSILON differ by at most 2*EPSILON.

(defun putnam-2006-b2-real-equality-function
    (left-name right-name)
  (let* ((left
          (putnam-2006-b2-apply-term
           left-name
           (list 'epsilon)))
         (right
          (putnam-2006-b2-apply-term
           right-name
           (list 'epsilon)))
         (distance
          (putnam-2006-b2-absolute-term
           (putnam-2006-b2-subtract-term
            left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2006-b2-implies-term
      (putnam-2006-b2-positive-rational-term
       'epsilon)
      (putnam-2006-b2-less-equal-term
       distance
       (putnam-2006-b2-multiply-term
        (putnam-2006-b2-quoted 2)
        'epsilon))))))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-real-equal-p
    (left-name right-name)
  (fn-equal
   (putnam-2006-b2-real-equality-function
    left-name right-name)
   (putnam-2006-b2-true-function
    '(epsilon))))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-distinct-from-list-p
    (name names)
  (if (consp names)
      (and
       (not
        (putnam-2006-b2-real-equal-p
         name (car names)))
       (putnam-2006-b2-distinct-from-list-p
        name (cdr names)))
    (equal names nil)))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-real-finset-list-p (names)
  (if (consp names)
      (and
       (putnam-2006-b2-real-name-p (car names))
       (putnam-2006-b2-distinct-from-list-p
        (car names) (cdr names))
       (putnam-2006-b2-real-finset-list-p
        (cdr names)))
    (equal names nil)))

;; A nonzero MASK below 2^(LEN NAMES) selects a nonempty subset of the
;; semantically distinct real values in NAMES. This is a bijective encoding of
;; the source subsets, not a finite restriction on the elements themselves.

(defun putnam-2006-b2-mask-cardinality (names mask)
  (if (consp names)
      (+ (mod mask 2)
         (putnam-2006-b2-mask-cardinality
          (cdr names)
          (floor mask 2)))
    0))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-selected-sum-term
    (names mask precision)
  (if (consp names)
      (let ((rest
             (putnam-2006-b2-selected-sum-term
              (cdr names)
              (floor mask 2)
              precision)))
        (if (equal (mod mask 2) 1)
            (putnam-2006-b2-add-term
             (putnam-2006-b2-apply-term
              (car names)
              (list precision))
             rest)
          rest))
    (putnam-2006-b2-quoted 0)))

;; If K elements are selected, each is sampled at EPSILON/K. The total
;; approximation error is at most EPSILON. Therefore the universal precision
;; inequality below is equivalent in both directions to
;;
;;   |M + sum(S)| <= 1/(N+1)
;;
;; for the represented real limits.

(defun putnam-2006-b2-subset-bound-function
    (names n mask m)
  (let* ((count
          (putnam-2006-b2-mask-cardinality
           names mask))
         (precision
          (putnam-2006-b2-divide-term
           'epsilon
           (putnam-2006-b2-quoted count)))
         (sum
          (putnam-2006-b2-selected-sum-term
           names mask precision))
         (absolute-total
          (putnam-2006-b2-absolute-term
           (putnam-2006-b2-add-term
            (putnam-2006-b2-quoted m)
            sum)))
         (bound
          (/ 1 (+ n 1))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2006-b2-implies-term
      (putnam-2006-b2-positive-rational-term
       'epsilon)
      (putnam-2006-b2-less-equal-term
       absolute-total
       (putnam-2006-b2-add-term
        (putnam-2006-b2-quoted bound)
        'epsilon))))))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-subset-bound-holds-p
    (names n mask m)
  (let ((bound-function
         (putnam-2006-b2-subset-bound-function
          names n mask m))
        (true-function
         (putnam-2006-b2-true-function
          '(epsilon))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp bound-function)
     (tamep-functionp true-function)
     (fn-equal bound-function true-function))))

;; At precision 1, a valid Cauchy name differs from its represented real by at
;; most 1. Hence every subset sum has absolute value at most the sum below.
;; If an integer M satisfies the requested inequality, then
;;
;;   |M| <= 1 + sum_i (1 + |name_i(1)|).
;;
;; The numerator of this nonnegative rational is at least the rational itself.
;; Thus the integer search bound is complete, not an approximation. Together
;; with the finite mask search, this keeps both source witnesses internal
;; without placing an unbadged user function in a generated lambda.

(defun putnam-2006-b2-real-magnitude-bound (names)
  (if (consp names)
      (+ 1
         (abs
          (apply$ (car names) (list 1)))
         (putnam-2006-b2-real-magnitude-bound
          (cdr names)))
    0))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-integer-search-bound (names)
  (+ 1
     (numerator
      (putnam-2006-b2-real-magnitude-bound
       names))))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-integer-witness-in-list-p
    (names n mask integers)
  (if (consp integers)
      (let ((m (car integers)))
      (or
       (putnam-2006-b2-subset-bound-holds-p
        names n mask m)
       (putnam-2006-b2-integer-witness-in-list-p
        names n mask (cdr integers))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2006-b2-subset-witness-in-list-p
    (names n integer-bound masks)
  (if (consp masks)
      (let ((mask (car masks)))
      (or
       (putnam-2006-b2-integer-witness-in-list-p
         names
         n
         mask
         (from-to-by
          (- integer-bound)
          integer-bound
          1))
       (putnam-2006-b2-subset-witness-in-list-p
        names n integer-bound (cdr masks))))
    nil))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2006-b2-statement
    (n names)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp n)
    (< 0 n)
    (putnam-2006-b2-real-finset-list-p names)
    (equal (len names) n))
   (let ((integer-bound
          (putnam-2006-b2-integer-search-bound
           names)))
     (putnam-2006-b2-subset-witness-in-list-p
      names
      n
      integer-bound
      (from-to-by
       1
       (- (expt 2 (len names)) 1)
       1)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2006_b2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_b2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2006_b2): every nonempty finite set of n real
-- numbers has a nonempty subset whose sum differs from an integer by at most
-- 1 / (n + 1). This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2006B2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<_ _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<suc : {n : Nat} -> zero < suc n
  suc<suc  : {m n : Nat} -> m < n -> suc m < suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

Injective :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set
Injective function =
  (x y : _) ->
  function x == function y ->
  x == y

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

maximum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
maximum reals x y with order-total reals x y
... | left _ =
  y
... | right _ =
  x

absoluteValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
absoluteValue reals x =
  maximum reals x (negate reals x)

integerToReal :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
integerToReal reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
integerToReal reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (terms fzero)
    (sumFin reals n (\ i -> terms (fsuc i)))

module Putnam2006B2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  SubsetBound :
    {n : Nat} ->
    (Fin n -> R) ->
    Set
  SubsetBound {n} elements =
    Exists Nat
      (\ k ->
        zero < k
        and
        Exists (Fin k -> Fin n)
          (\ select ->
            Injective select
            and
            Exists Int
              (\ integer ->
                lessOrEqual reals
                  (absoluteValue reals
                    (add reals
                      (integerToReal reals integer)
                      (sumFin reals k
                        (\ i -> elements (select i)))))
                  (divide reals
                    (oneR reals)
                    (fromNat reals (suc n))))))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (n : Nat) ->
    zero < n ->
    (elements : Fin n -> R) ->
    Injective elements ->
    SubsetBound elements

putnam-2006-b2 : Set1
putnam-2006-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2006B2Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_b2:
  every finite set of n real numbers, for positive n, has a nonempty subset
  whose sum is within 1 / (n + 1) of an integer. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory realTheory intrealTheory
  real_sigmaTheory;

val putnam_2006_b2 =
  ``!n : num. !X : real set.
      0 < n /\
      FINITE X /\
      CARD X = n
      ==>
      ?S : real set. ?m : int.
        S SUBSET X /\
        S <> {} /\
        abs (real_of_int m + SIGMA (\s : real. s) S) <=
          1 / (&n + 1)``;

$(

  putnam_2006_b2: every finite set of n real numbers, for positive n, has a
  nonempty subset whose sum is within 1 / (n + 1) of an integer. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN is the class of positive integers. The conditions X C_ RR and
  ( # ` X ) = n represent an arbitrary n-element set of real numbers; the
  finite cardinality equality also ensures that X is finite. The witness S
  ranges over the full powerset of X and is required to be nonempty.

  The finite sum over S is added to the internally existential integer m,
  and its absolute value is bounded by 1 / (n + 1), exactly as in the source
  statements. The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus
  statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d m n s S X $.

  putnambench-putnam-2006-b2 $a |- A. n e. NN A. X
    (
      (
        X C_ RR
        /\
        ( # ` X ) = n
      )
      ->
      E. S e. ~P X
        (
          S =/= (/)
          /\
          E. m e. ZZ
            (
              abs
              `
              (
                m
                +
                ( sum_ s e. S s )
              )
            )
            <_
            ( 1 / ( n + 1 ) )
        )
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2006_b2

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_b2:
% every finite set of n real numbers, for positive n, has a nonempty subset
% whose sum is within 1/(n+1) of an integer. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2006_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets@finite_sets_sum_real[real]

  finite_subset(S, X: finite_set[real]): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      S(x) IMPLIES X(x)

  putnam_2006_b2: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (X: finite_set[real]):
      (n > 0 AND card(X) = n)
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (S: finite_set[real]), (m: int):
          finite_subset(S, X)
            AND card(S) > 0
            AND abs(
              (m :: real)
                + sum(S, (LAMBDA (s: real): s)))
              <= 1 / ((n :: real) + 1)
END putnam_2006_b2

title: putnam_2006_b3

import Mathlib

abbrev putnam_2006_b3_solution : ℕ → ℕ := sorry
-- (fun n : ℕ => (Nat.choose n 2) + 1)
/--
Let $S$ be a finite set of points in the plane. A linear partition of $S$ is an unordered pair $\{A,B\}$ of subsets of $S$ such that $A \cup B=S$, $A \cap B=\emptyset$, and $A$ and $B$ lie on opposite sides of some straight line disjoint from $S$ ($A$ or $B$ may be empty). Let $L_S$ be the number of linear partitions of $S$. For each positive integer $n$, find the maximum of $L_S$ over all sets $S$ of $n$ points.
-/
theorem putnam_2006_b3
    (IsLinearPartition : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ) → Finset (Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ)) → Prop)
    (IsLinearPartition_def : ∀ S AB, IsLinearPartition S AB ↔
      (AB.card = 2 ∧ ∃ A ∈ AB, ∃ B ∈ AB,
        A ≠ B ∧ (A ∪ B = S) ∧ (A ∩ B = ∅) ∧
        (∃ m b : ℝ,
          (∀ p ∈ A, p 1 > m * p 0 + b) ∧
          (∀ p ∈ B, p 1 < m * p 0 + b))))
    (L : Finset (Fin 2 → ℝ) → ℕ)
    (hL : ∀ S, L S = {AB | IsLinearPartition S AB}.encard)
    (n : ℕ) (npos : 0 < n) :
    IsGreatest {L S | (S) (hS : S.card = n)} (putnam_2006_b3_solution n) :=
  sorry

title: putnam_2006_b3
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2006_b3:
   the maximum number of unordered linear partitions of an n-point subset of
   the real plane is binomial(n, 2) + 1. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals Lists.List.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2006_b3_point := (R * R)%type.
Definition putnam_2006_b3_point_set := putnam_2006_b3_point -> Prop.

Definition putnam_2006_b3_same_set
    (A B : putnam_2006_b3_point_set) : Prop :=
  forall p : putnam_2006_b3_point, A p <-> B p.

Definition putnam_2006_b3_has_cardinality
    (S : putnam_2006_b3_point_set) (n : nat) : Prop :=
  exists points : list putnam_2006_b3_point,
    NoDup points /\
    length points = n /\
    forall p : putnam_2006_b3_point, In p points <-> S p.

Definition putnam_2006_b3_partition :=
  (putnam_2006_b3_point_set * putnam_2006_b3_point_set)%type.

Definition putnam_2006_b3_same_unordered_partition
    (P Q : putnam_2006_b3_partition) : Prop :=
  (putnam_2006_b3_same_set (fst P) (fst Q) /\
   putnam_2006_b3_same_set (snd P) (snd Q)) \/
  (putnam_2006_b3_same_set (fst P) (snd Q) /\
   putnam_2006_b3_same_set (snd P) (fst Q)).

Definition putnam_2006_b3_separated_by_a_line
    (A B : putnam_2006_b3_point_set) : Prop :=
  exists m b : R,
    ((forall p : putnam_2006_b3_point,
        A p -> snd p > m * fst p + b) /\
     (forall p : putnam_2006_b3_point,
        B p -> snd p < m * fst p + b)) \/
    ((forall p : putnam_2006_b3_point,
        B p -> snd p > m * fst p + b) /\
     (forall p : putnam_2006_b3_point,
        A p -> snd p < m * fst p + b)).

Definition putnam_2006_b3_linear_partition
    (S : putnam_2006_b3_point_set)
    (P : putnam_2006_b3_partition) : Prop :=
  ~ putnam_2006_b3_same_set (fst P) (snd P) /\
  (forall p : putnam_2006_b3_point,
    S p <-> fst P p \/ snd P p) /\
  (forall p : putnam_2006_b3_point,
    ~ (fst P p /\ snd P p)) /\
  putnam_2006_b3_separated_by_a_line (fst P) (snd P).

Fixpoint putnam_2006_b3_no_duplicate_partitions
    (partitions : list putnam_2006_b3_partition) : Prop :=
  match partitions with
  | nil => True
  | P :: rest =>
      (forall Q : putnam_2006_b3_partition,
        In Q rest ->
        ~ putnam_2006_b3_same_unordered_partition P Q) /\
      putnam_2006_b3_no_duplicate_partitions rest
  end.

Definition putnam_2006_b3_enumerates_linear_partitions
    (S : putnam_2006_b3_point_set)
    (partitions : list putnam_2006_b3_partition) : Prop :=
  putnam_2006_b3_no_duplicate_partitions partitions /\
  (forall P : putnam_2006_b3_partition,
    In P partitions ->
    putnam_2006_b3_linear_partition S P) /\
  (forall P : putnam_2006_b3_partition,
    putnam_2006_b3_linear_partition S P ->
    exists Q : putnam_2006_b3_partition,
      In Q partitions /\
      putnam_2006_b3_same_unordered_partition P Q).

Definition putnam_2006_b3_linear_partition_count
    (S : putnam_2006_b3_point_set) (k : nat) : Prop :=
  exists partitions : list putnam_2006_b3_partition,
    putnam_2006_b3_enumerates_linear_partitions S partitions /\
    length partitions = k.

Definition putnam_2006_b3_is_greatest
    (values : nat -> Prop) (maximum : nat) : Prop :=
  values maximum /\
  forall value : nat, values value -> (value <= maximum)%nat.

Fixpoint putnam_2006_b3_binomial (n k : nat) : nat :=
  match n, k with
  | _, O => 1%nat
  | O, S _ => 0%nat
  | S n', S k' =>
      (putnam_2006_b3_binomial n' k' +
       putnam_2006_b3_binomial n' (S k'))%nat
  end.

Definition putnam_2006_b3_solution (n : nat) : nat :=
  (putnam_2006_b3_binomial n 2 + 1)%nat.

Theorem putnam_2006_b3 :
  forall n : nat,
    (0 < n)%nat ->
    putnam_2006_b3_is_greatest
      (fun k : nat =>
        exists S : putnam_2006_b3_point_set,
          putnam_2006_b3_has_cardinality S n /\
          putnam_2006_b3_linear_partition_count S k)
      (putnam_2006_b3_solution n).
Admitted.
