title: putnam_2007_a2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a2:
% the least area of a convex plane set meeting both branches of each of the
% hyperbolas x*y = 1 and x*y = -1 is 4. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2007_a2: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]
  region: TYPE = [point -> bool]

  box: TYPE =
    [# left: real, right: real, bottom: real, top: real #]
  box_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> box]

  measure_value: TYPE =
    [# infinite_flag: bool, finite_part: real #]

  canonical_measure_value(value: measure_value): bool =
    IF infinite_flag(value) THEN
      finite_part(value) = 0
    ELSE
      0 <= finite_part(value)
    ENDIF

  finite_measure_value(value: nonneg_real): measure_value =
    (# infinite_flag := FALSE, finite_part := value #)

  infinite_measure_value: measure_value =
    (# infinite_flag := TRUE, finite_part := 0 #)

  measure_value_le(left_value, right_value: measure_value): bool =
    canonical_measure_value(left_value)
      AND canonical_measure_value(right_value)
      AND IF infinite_flag(right_value) THEN
        TRUE
      ELSIF infinite_flag(left_value) THEN
        FALSE
      ELSE
        finite_part(left_value) <= finite_part(right_value)
      ENDIF

  affine_combination(t: real, p, q: point): point =
    (# x_coord :=
         t * x_coord(p) + (1 - t) * x_coord(q),
       y_coord :=
         t * y_coord(p) + (1 - t) * y_coord(q) #)

  convex(S: region): bool =
    FORALL (p, q: point), (t: real):
      (S(p) AND S(q) AND 0 <= t AND t <= 1)
        IMPLIES S(affine_combination(t, p, q))

  meets_positive_hyperbola_branches(S: region): bool =
    (EXISTS (p: point):
      S(p)
        AND 0 < x_coord(p)
        AND 0 < y_coord(p)
        AND x_coord(p) * y_coord(p) = 1)
      AND
    (EXISTS (p: point):
      S(p)
        AND x_coord(p) < 0
        AND y_coord(p) < 0
        AND x_coord(p) * y_coord(p) = 1)

  meets_negative_hyperbola_branches(S: region): bool =
    (EXISTS (p: point):
      S(p)
        AND x_coord(p) < 0
        AND 0 < y_coord(p)
        AND x_coord(p) * y_coord(p) = -1)
      AND
    (EXISTS (p: point):
      S(p)
        AND 0 < x_coord(p)
        AND y_coord(p) < 0
        AND x_coord(p) * y_coord(p) = -1)

  admissible(S: region): bool =
    convex(S)
      AND meets_positive_hyperbola_branches(S)
      AND meets_negative_hyperbola_branches(S)

  in_open_box(p: point, rectangle: box): bool =
    left(rectangle) < x_coord(p)
      AND x_coord(p) < right(rectangle)
      AND bottom(rectangle) < y_coord(p)
      AND y_coord(p) < top(rectangle)

  box_area(rectangle: box): real =
    IF left(rectangle) < right(rectangle)
        AND bottom(rectangle) < top(rectangle) THEN
      (right(rectangle) - left(rectangle))
        * (top(rectangle) - bottom(rectangle))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  partial_box_area(
      boxes: box_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_box_area(boxes, count - 1)
        + box_area(boxes(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  covers(S: region, boxes: box_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (p: point):
      S(p) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (index: nat):
          in_open_box(p, boxes(index))

  has_finite_lebesgue_outer_area(
      S: region,
      area: nonneg_real): bool =
    (FORALL (boxes: box_sequence):
      covers(S, boxes) IMPLIES
        FORALL (lower_bound: real):
          lower_bound < area IMPLIES
            EXISTS (count: nat):
              lower_bound < partial_box_area(boxes, count))
      AND
    (FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (boxes: box_sequence):
        covers(S, boxes)
          AND FORALL (count: nat):
            partial_box_area(boxes, count)
              <= area + epsilon_value)

  has_infinite_lebesgue_outer_area(S: region): bool =
    FORALL (boxes: box_sequence):
      covers(S, boxes) IMPLIES
        FORALL (bound: real):
          EXISTS (count: nat):
            bound < partial_box_area(boxes, count)

  has_lebesgue_outer_area(
      S: region,
      area: measure_value): bool =
    canonical_measure_value(area)
      AND IF infinite_flag(area) THEN
        has_infinite_lebesgue_outer_area(S)
      ELSE
        has_finite_lebesgue_outer_area(S, finite_part(area))
      ENDIF

  attainable_area(area: measure_value): bool =
    EXISTS (S: region):
      admissible(S)
        AND has_lebesgue_outer_area(S, area)

  is_least(
      values: [measure_value -> bool],
      candidate: measure_value): bool =
    values(candidate)
      AND FORALL (value: measure_value):
        values(value) IMPLIES
          measure_value_le(candidate, value)

  putnam_2007_a2_statement: bool =
    is_least(
      attainable_area,
      finite_measure_value(4))
END putnam_2007_a2

import Mathlib

open Set
open scoped Nat

abbrev putnam_2007_a3_solution : ℕ → ℚ := sorry
-- fun k ↦ (k)! * (k + 1)! / ((3 * k + 1) * (2 * k)!)
/--
Let $k$ be a positive integer. Suppose that the integers $1, 2, 3, \dots, 3k+1$ are written down in random order. What is the probability that at no time during this process, the sum of the integers that have been written up to that time is a positive integer divisible by $3$? Your answer should be in closed form, but may include factorials.
-/
theorem putnam_2007_a3
(k : ℕ)
(kpos : k > 0)
(perms : Set (Fin (3 * k + 1) → ℤ))
(goodperms : Set (Fin (3 * k + 1) → ℤ))
(hgoodperms : goodperms = {f ∈ perms | ¬∃ j : Fin (3 * k + 1), 3 ∣ ∑ i : Fin (3 * k + 1), ite (i ≤ j) (f i) 0})
(hperms : perms = {f : Fin (3 * k + 1) → ℤ | ∀ y ∈ Icc 1 (3 * k + 1), ∃! x : Fin (3 * k + 1), f x = y})
: (goodperms.ncard = perms.ncard * (putnam_2007_a3_solution k)) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2007_a3
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a3:
   the probability that no prefix sum of a random ordering of the integers
   1 through 3k+1 is divisible by 3. This file contains no proof. *)

From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Fixpoint putnam_2007_a3_factorial (n : nat) : nat :=
  match n with
  | O => 1
  | S m => S m * putnam_2007_a3_factorial m
  end.

Definition putnam_2007_a3_partial_sum {n : nat}
    (p : {ffun 'I_n -> 'I_n}) (j : 'I_n) : nat :=
  \sum_(i : 'I_n | i <= j) (nat_of_ord (p i) + 1).

Definition putnam_2007_a3_is_permutation {n : nat}
    (p : {ffun 'I_n -> 'I_n}) : bool :=
  [forall i : 'I_n,
    [forall j : 'I_n, (p i == p j) ==> (i == j)]].

Definition putnam_2007_a3_good {n : nat}
    (p : {ffun 'I_n -> 'I_n}) : bool :=
  [forall j : 'I_n,
    putnam_2007_a3_partial_sum p j %% 3 != 0].

Definition putnam_2007_a3_good_count (n : nat) : nat :=
  #|[pred p : {ffun 'I_n -> 'I_n} |
      putnam_2007_a3_is_permutation p && putnam_2007_a3_good p]|.

Theorem putnam_2007_a3 :
  forall k : nat,
    (0 < k)%nat ->
    ((3 * k + 1) *
       putnam_2007_a3_factorial (2 * k) *
       putnam_2007_a3_good_count (3 * k + 1) =
     putnam_2007_a3_factorial k *
       putnam_2007_a3_factorial (k + 1) *
       putnam_2007_a3_factorial (3 * k + 1))%nat.
Admitted.

theory putnam_2007_a3 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Combinatorics.Permutations"
begin

(* Note: Boosts domain from Fin 3k+1 to nat, adding condition to keep sequence count finite *)
definition putnam_2007_a3_solution :: "nat \<Rightarrow> real" where
  "putnam_2007_a3_solution \<equiv> (\<lambda>k.
    real (fact k) * real (fact (k + 1)) /
      (real (3 * k + 1) * real (fact (2 * k))))"
(* \<lambda> k. (fact k) * (fact (k + 1)) / ((3 * k + 1 :: real) * (fact (2 * k))) *)
theorem putnam_2007_a3:
  fixes k :: "nat"
    and perms goodperms :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> nat) set"
  assumes kpos: "k > 0"
  defines "perms \<equiv> {f :: nat \<Rightarrow> nat. f permutes {1..3*k+1}}"
    and "goodperms \<equiv> {f :: nat \<Rightarrow> nat. f \<in> perms \<and>
      (\<not>(\<exists>j \<in> {1..3*k+1}. 3 dvd (\<Sum>i \<in> {1..j}. f i)))}"
  shows "card goodperms = (card perms) * (putnam_2007_a3_solution k)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a3:
  the probability that a uniformly ordered listing of 1 through 3k+1 has no
  prefix sum divisible by 3, together with its factorial closed form. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `!k:num.
     0 < k
     ==>
     let n = 3 * k + 1 in
     let permutations =
       {p:num->num |
          BIJ p (1..n) (1..n) /\
          (!i:num. ~(i IN (1..n)) ==> p i = 0)} in
     let good_permutations =
       {p:num->num |
          p IN permutations /\
          (!j:num.
             j IN (1..n)
             ==> ~(3 divides nsum (1..j) p))} in
     &(CARD good_permutations) / &(CARD permutations) =
     &(FACT k) * &(FACT (k + 1)) /
     (&(3 * k + 1) * &(FACT (2 * k)))`;;

title: putnam_2007_a3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a3:
;; for every positive integer k, the proportion of permutations of the
;; integers 1 through 3k+1 having no prefix sum divisible by 3 is
;; k!(k+1)!/((3k+1)(2k)!). This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A permutation of the finite integer interval is represented by its image
;; list. Since the interval has no duplicates, insertion at every position
;; enumerates every permutation exactly once.
(defun putnam-2007-a3-range-from (start count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons start
          (putnam-2007-a3-range-from
           (+ start 1) (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2007-a3-prefix-each (value lists)
  (if (consp lists)
      (cons (cons value (car lists))
            (putnam-2007-a3-prefix-each value (cdr lists)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2007-a3-insert-everywhere (value values)
  (if (consp values)
      (cons
       (cons value values)
       (putnam-2007-a3-prefix-each
        (car values)
        (putnam-2007-a3-insert-everywhere
         value (cdr values))))
    (list (list value))))

(defun putnam-2007-a3-insert-into-each (value permutations)
  (if (consp permutations)
      (append
       (putnam-2007-a3-insert-everywhere
        value (car permutations))
       (putnam-2007-a3-insert-into-each
        value (cdr permutations)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2007-a3-permutations (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (putnam-2007-a3-insert-into-each
       (car values)
       (putnam-2007-a3-permutations (cdr values)))
    (list nil)))

(defun putnam-2007-a3-good-prefixes-from-p
    (values partial-sum)
  (if (consp values)
      (let ((next-sum (+ partial-sum (car values))))
        (and
         (not (equal (mod next-sum 3) 0))
         (putnam-2007-a3-good-prefixes-from-p
          (cdr values) next-sum)))
    t))

(defun putnam-2007-a3-good-permutation-p (values)
  (putnam-2007-a3-good-prefixes-from-p values 0))

(defun putnam-2007-a3-count-good (permutations)
  (if (consp permutations)
      (+ (if (putnam-2007-a3-good-permutation-p
              (car permutations))
             1
           0)
         (putnam-2007-a3-count-good (cdr permutations)))
    0))

(defun putnam-2007-a3-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* (nfix n)
       (putnam-2007-a3-factorial (- (nfix n) 1)))))

;; Cross multiplication states
;;
;;   good-count / all-count = k!(k+1)! / ((3k+1)(2k)!)
;;
;; using only exact integers. The generated finite lists are bijective with
;; the Fin-indexed permutation functions in the source.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2007-a3-statement (k)
  (implies
   (posp k)
   (let* ((entry-count (+ (* 3 k) 1))
          (entries
           (putnam-2007-a3-range-from 1 entry-count))
          (permutations
           (putnam-2007-a3-permutations entries))
          (good-count
           (putnam-2007-a3-count-good permutations))
          (all-count (len permutations)))
     (equal
      (* good-count
         entry-count
         (putnam-2007-a3-factorial (* 2 k)))
      (* all-count
         (putnam-2007-a3-factorial k)
         (putnam-2007-a3-factorial (+ k 1)))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2007_a3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2007_a3): the probability that no prefix sum
-- of a random ordering of 1 through 3k+1 is divisible by 3.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2007A3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_ _divides_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  oneN <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

toNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
toNat fzero =
  zero
toNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (toNat i)

record Bijection (A B : Set) : Set where
  field
    to      : A -> B
    from    : B -> A
    from-to : (x : A) -> from (to x) == x
    to-from : (y : B) -> to (from y) == y

open Bijection

Permutation : Nat -> Set
Permutation n =
  Bijection (Fin n) (Fin n)

PermutationEqual :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Permutation n ->
  Permutation n ->
  Set
PermutationEqual left right =
  (i : _) ->
  to left i == to right i

valueAt :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Permutation n ->
  Fin n ->
  Nat
valueAt permutation position =
  suc (toNat (to permutation position))

prefixSum :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Nat) ->
  Fin n ->
  Nat
prefixSum {suc n} values fzero =
  values fzero
prefixSum {suc n} values (fsuc last) =
  values fzero
  + prefixSum
      (\ position -> values (fsuc position))
      last

record _divides_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    equation : divisor * quotient == dividend

record GoodPermutation (n : Nat) : Set where
  field
    permutation : Permutation n
    no-divisible-prefix :
      (last : Fin n) ->
      Not
        (threeN divides
          prefixSum
            (valueAt permutation)
            last)

open GoodPermutation

GoodPermutationEqual :
  {n : Nat} ->
  GoodPermutation n ->
  GoodPermutation n ->
  Set
GoodPermutationEqual left right =
  PermutationEqual
    (permutation left)
    (permutation right)

record HasExtensionalCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (equivalent : A -> A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> equivalent item (enumerate index))
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      equivalent (enumerate left-index) (enumerate right-index) ->
      left-index == right-index

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

numberOfEntries : Nat -> Nat
numberOfEntries k =
  threeN * k + oneN

probabilityNumerator : Nat -> Nat
probabilityNumerator k =
  factorial k * factorial (suc k)

probabilityDenominator : Nat -> Nat
probabilityDenominator k =
  numberOfEntries k * factorial (twoN * k)

putnam-2007-a3 : Set
putnam-2007-a3 =
  (k : Nat) ->
  Positive k ->
  (permutationCount goodPermutationCount : Nat) ->
  HasExtensionalCardinality
    (PermutationEqual {numberOfEntries k})
    permutationCount ->
  HasExtensionalCardinality
    (GoodPermutationEqual {numberOfEntries k})
    goodPermutationCount ->
  probabilityDenominator k * goodPermutationCount
  ==
  permutationCount * probabilityNumerator k

(*

  the probability that no nonempty prefix sum of a random ordering of the
  integers from 1 through 3k+1 is divisible by 3. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory dividesTheory pred_setTheory permutesTheory realTheory;

val putnam_2007_a3 =
  ``!k : num.
      0 < k
      ==>
      let n = 3 * k + 1
      in
        &(CARD
            {p : num -> num |
               p permutes count n /\
               !j : num.
                 j < n
                 ==>
                 ~divides 3
                    (SIGMA (\i : num. p i + 1) (count (j + 1)))}) /
        &(CARD {p : num -> num | p permutes count n}) =
        (&(FACT k) * &(FACT (k + 1))) /
        ((&(3 * k + 1) : real) * &(FACT (2 * k)))``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2007_a3: the probability that no prefix sum of a uniformly ordered
  permutation of 1 through 3k+1 is divisible by three has the stated
  factorial closed form. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For positive k, Base ` SymGrp ` (1 ... (3k+1)) is the finite set of all
  orders of the integers 1 through 3k+1. The restricted class in the
  numerator consists exactly of those orders for which every nonempty prefix
  sum has nonzero remainder modulo 3. Since all entries are positive, this is
  equivalent to excluding positive prefix sums divisible by 3.

  The quotient of the two finite cardinalities is therefore the uniform
  probability in the problem, and the right side is

                 k! (k+1)!
             ------------------- .
             (3k+1) (2k)!

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d f i k m $.

  putnambench-putnam-2007-a3 $a |- A. k e. NN
    (
      (
        #
        `
        {
          f e. ( Base ` ( SymGrp ` ( 1 ... ( ( 3 x. k ) + 1 ) ) ) ) |
          A. m e. ( 1 ... ( ( 3 x. k ) + 1 ) )
            (
              (
                sum_ i e. ( 1 ... m )
                  ( f ` i )
              )
              mod 3
            )
            =/= 0
        }
      )
      /
      (
        #
        `
        ( Base ` ( SymGrp ` ( 1 ... ( ( 3 x. k ) + 1 ) ) ) )
      )
      =
      (
        (
          ( ! ` k )
          x.
          ( ! ` ( k + 1 ) )
        )
        /
        (
          ( ( 3 x. k ) + 1 )
          x.
          ( ! ` ( 2 x. k ) )
        )
      )
    )
  $.
$}

theorem

    goodperms =

        for j being Nat st j in Seg (3 * k + 1) holds
          ex partial being FinSequence of NAT st
            len partial = j &
            (for i being Nat st i in Seg j holds partial.i = p.i) &
            not ex q being Nat st Sum partial = 3 * q}
  holds
    (card goodperms qua Real) =
      (card perms qua Real) *
        (((k !) qua Real) * (((k + 1) !) qua Real) /
          (((3 * k + 1) qua Real) * (((2 * k) !) qua Real)))
proof
end;

title: putnam_2007_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a3:
% the probability that no nonempty prefix sum of a permutation of 1 through
% 3*k+1 is divisible by 3 has the stated factorial closed form. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_2007_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> int]

  IMPORTING finite_sets[integer_sequence]

  nat_factorial(n: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      n * nat_factorial(n - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  prefix_sum(
      values: integer_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      prefix_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  int_divides(divisor, value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: int):
      value = divisor * quotient

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN 0 ELSE numerator / denominator ENDIF

  appears_exactly_once(
      values: integer_sequence,
      length: nat,
      value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (index: nat):
      index < length
        AND values(index) = value
        AND (FORALL (other: nat):
          (other < length AND values(other) = value)
            IMPLIES other = index)

  permutation_of_first_n(
      values: integer_sequence,
      length: nat): bool =
    (FORALL (index: nat):
      index < length IMPLIES
        1 <= values(index)
          AND values(index) <= (length :: int))
      AND
    (FORALL (value: int):
      (1 <= value AND value <= (length :: int))
        IMPLIES appears_exactly_once(values, length, value))
      AND
    (FORALL (index: nat):
      index >= length IMPLIES values(index) = 0)

  admissible_permutation(
      values: integer_sequence,
      k: posnat): bool =
    permutation_of_first_n(values, 3 * k + 1)

  good_permutation(
      values: integer_sequence,
      k: posnat): bool =
    admissible_permutation(values, k)
      AND NOT EXISTS (last_index: nat):
        last_index < 3 * k + 1
          AND int_divides(
            3,
            prefix_sum(values, last_index + 1))

  putnam_2007_a3_solution(k: posnat): real =
    safe_div(
      (nat_factorial(k) :: real)
        * (nat_factorial(k + 1) :: real),
      ((3 * k + 1) :: real)
        * (nat_factorial(2 * k) :: real))

  putnam_2007_a3: bool =
    FORALL (k: posnat):
      EXISTS (perms, goodperms: finite_set[integer_sequence]):
        (FORALL (values: integer_sequence):
          perms(values) IFF admissible_permutation(values, k))
          AND
        (FORALL (values: integer_sequence):
          goodperms(values) IFF good_permutation(values, k))
          AND
        (card(goodperms) :: real)
          = (card(perms) :: real) * putnam_2007_a3_solution(k)
END putnam_2007_a3

title: putnam_2007_a4
content:
import Mathlib

open Set Nat

abbrev putnam_2007_a4_solution : Set (Polynomial ℝ) := sorry
-- {f : Polynomial ℝ | ∃ d : ℕ, ∃ c ≥ (1 : ℤ) - d, ∀ n : ℝ, f.eval n = (1 / 9) * ((10 ^ c) * (9 * n + 1) ^ d - 1)}
/--
A \emph{repunit} is a positive integer whose digits in base 10 are all ones. Find all polynomials $f$ with real coefficients such that if $n$ is a repunit, then so is $f(n)$.
-/
theorem putnam_2007_a4
(S : Set (Polynomial ℝ))
(repunit : ℝ → Prop)
(hrepunit : ∀ x, repunit x ↔ x > 0 ∧ x = floor x ∧ ∀ d ∈ (digits 10 (floor x)), d = 1)
(hS : ∀ f, f ∈ S ↔ (∀ n : ℝ, repunit n → repunit (f.eval n)))
: (S = putnam_2007_a4_solution) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2007_a4
content:
Require Import Reals Zpower Coquelicot.Coquelicot.

Definition putnam_2007_a4_solution (f : R -> R) : Prop :=
  exists (c : Z) (d : nat),
    (1 - Z.of_nat d <= c)%Z /\
    forall x : R,
      f x = (powerRZ 10 c * (9 * x + 1) ^ d - 1) / 9.

Theorem putnam_2007_a4
    (repunit : R -> Prop := fun n => n = IZR (floor n) /\ n > 0 /\ exists (m: nat), n = sum_n (fun i => 10 ^ i) m)
    (c: nat -> R)
    (n: nat)
    (f : R -> R := fun x => sum_n (fun i => c i * x ^ i) n)
    : (forall (n: nat), repunit (INR n) -> repunit (f (INR n))) <-> putnam_2007_a4_solution f.
Proof. Admitted.

title: putnam_2007_a4
content:
theory putnam_2007_a4 imports
Complex_Main
"HOL-Computational_Algebra.Polynomial"
begin

definition putnam_2007_a4_solution :: "(real poly) set" where "putnam_2007_a4_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* {f :: real poly. \<exists> d :: nat. \<exists> c :: int. c \<ge> 1 - d \<and> (\<forall> n :: real. poly f n = (1 / 9) * ((10 powr c) * (9 * n + 1) ^ d - 1))} *)
theorem putnam_2007_a4:
  fixes repunit :: "real \<Rightarrow> bool"
  defines "repunit \<equiv> \<lambda> x :: real. x > 0 \<and> x = real_of_int (floor x) \<and> (\<forall> i :: nat. (10 ^ i \<le> floor x) \<longrightarrow> ((floor x) div (10 ^ i)) mod 10 = 1)"
  shows "{f :: real poly. \<forall> n :: real. repunit n \<longrightarrow> repunit (poly f n)} = putnam_2007_a4_solution"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_2007_a4
putnam_2007_a4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a4:
;; the real-coefficient polynomials that map every base-10 repunit to a
;; repunit are exactly the stated family indexed by a natural degree and an
;; integer power of 10. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A coefficient is a rational regular-Cauchy name for an arbitrary real, and
;; a polynomial is its canonical finite coefficient list in ascending degree
;; order. Thus the representation neither restricts coefficients to rationals
;; nor replaces a polynomial by a finite table of sampled values.
;;
;; At each input repunit, a fixed 1/4-accurate polynomial approximation
;; uniquely identifies the only possible integral output. The preservation
;; matrix then checks, at every positive rational precision, exact equality
;; to that integer and checks its decimal digits with the tame ALWAYS$+ scion.
;; This is definitionally equivalent to the source's nested
;; forall-input/exists-output-repunit scope, without externalizing a witness.
;;
;; The solution-family predicate keeps the source's existential natural d and
;; integer c, including c >= 1-d, and checks coefficientwise equality with
;; (10^c*(9*x+1)^d-1)/9 over the represented reals. Every generated quantified
;; lambda contains only tame ACL2 primitives, APPLY$, and tame loop scions.

(defun putnam-2007-a4-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'cons
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2007-a4-term-list (cdr terms)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-apply-term (function arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2007-a4-quoted function)
        (putnam-2007-a4-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'if
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2007-a4-and-terms (cdr terms))
            (putnam-2007-a4-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2007-a4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list 'if
        hypothesis
        conclusion
        (putnam-2007-a4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-multiply-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-* left right))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-negate-term (value)
  (list 'unary-- value))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-subtract-term (left right)
  (putnam-2007-a4-add-term
   left
   (putnam-2007-a4-negate-term right)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-divide-term (numerator denominator)
  (putnam-2007-a4-multiply-term
   numerator
   (list 'unary-/ denominator)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-absolute-term (value)
  (list 'if
        (list '< value (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 0))
        (putnam-2007-a4-negate-term value)
        value))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-less-equal-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        (list '< right left)
        (putnam-2007-a4-quoted nil)
        (putnam-2007-a4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-positive-rational-term (value)
  (putnam-2007-a4-and-terms
   (list
    (list 'rationalp value)
    (list '< (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 0) value))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda
        formals
        (putnam-2007-a4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-real-name-cauchy-function (name)
  (let* ((left
          (putnam-2007-a4-apply-term name '(epsilon)))
         (right
          (putnam-2007-a4-apply-term name '(eta)))
         (distance
          (putnam-2007-a4-absolute-term
           (putnam-2007-a4-subtract-term left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon eta)
     (putnam-2007-a4-implies-term
      (putnam-2007-a4-and-terms
       (list
        (putnam-2007-a4-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
        (putnam-2007-a4-positive-rational-term 'eta)))
      (putnam-2007-a4-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2007-a4-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2007-a4-add-term
          'epsilon 'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-real-name-p (name)
  (let ((matrix
         (putnam-2007-a4-real-name-cauchy-function name))
        (always-true
         (putnam-2007-a4-true-function
          '(epsilon eta))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp name)
     (tamep-functionp matrix)
     (tamep-functionp always-true)
     (fn-equal matrix always-true))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-real-equal-rational-function
    (name rational)
  (let* ((value
          (putnam-2007-a4-apply-term name '(epsilon)))
         (distance
          (putnam-2007-a4-absolute-term
           (putnam-2007-a4-subtract-term
            value
            (putnam-2007-a4-quoted rational)))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2007-a4-implies-term
      (putnam-2007-a4-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
      (putnam-2007-a4-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp value)
        (putnam-2007-a4-less-equal-term
         distance 'epsilon)))))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-real-equal-rational-p
    (name rational)
  (let ((matrix
         (putnam-2007-a4-real-equal-rational-function
          name rational))
        (always-true
         (putnam-2007-a4-true-function '(epsilon))))
    (and
     (rationalp rational)
     (tamep-functionp matrix)
     (tamep-functionp always-true)
     (fn-equal matrix always-true))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-real-coefficient-list-p
    (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (and
       (putnam-2007-a4-real-name-p (car polynomial))
       (putnam-2007-a4-real-coefficient-list-p
        (cdr polynomial)))
    (equal polynomial nil)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-real-polynomial-p (polynomial)
  (and
   (true-listp polynomial)
   (consp polynomial)
   (putnam-2007-a4-real-coefficient-list-p polynomial)
   (or
    (equal (len polynomial) 1)
    (not
     (putnam-2007-a4-real-equal-rational-p
      (car (last polynomial))
      0)))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-rational-zero-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (equal (car values) 0)
       (putnam-2007-a4-rational-zero-list-p
        (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-polynomial-equal-rationals-p
    (polynomial rationals)
  (cond
   ((consp polynomial)
    (and
     (putnam-2007-a4-real-equal-rational-p
      (car polynomial)
      (if (consp rationals)
          (car rationals)
        0))
     (putnam-2007-a4-polynomial-equal-rationals-p
      (cdr polynomial)
      (if (consp rationals)
          (cdr rationals)
        nil))))
   ((consp rationals)
    (putnam-2007-a4-rational-zero-list-p rationals))
   (t
    (and
     (equal polynomial nil)
     (equal rationals nil)))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-binomial (n k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (cond
   ((or (not (natp n))
        (not (natp k))
        (< n k))
    0)
   ((equal k 0)
    1)
   ((equal n 0)
    0)
   (t
    (+ (putnam-2007-a4-binomial (- n 1) (- k 1))
       (putnam-2007-a4-binomial (- n 1) k)))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-integer-power-of-ten (c)
  (if (and (integerp c) (< c 0))
      (/ (expt 10 (- c)))
    (expt 10 (nfix c))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-solution-coefficient (d c i)
  (let ((power-of-ten
         (putnam-2007-a4-integer-power-of-ten c)))
    (if (equal i 0)
        (/ (- power-of-ten 1) 9)
      (* power-of-ten
         (putnam-2007-a4-binomial d i)
         (expt 9 (- i 1))))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-solution-coefficients-aux
    (d c i remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      nil
    (cons
     (putnam-2007-a4-solution-coefficient d c i)
     (putnam-2007-a4-solution-coefficients-aux
      d c (+ i 1) (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-solution-coefficients (d c)
  (putnam-2007-a4-solution-coefficients-aux
   d c 0 (+ 1 (nfix d))))

(defun-sk putnam-2007-a4-solution-p (polynomial)
  (exists
   (d c)
   (and
    (natp d)
    (integerp c)
    (<= (- 1 d) c)
    (putnam-2007-a4-polynomial-equal-rationals-p
     polynomial
     (putnam-2007-a4-solution-coefficients d c)))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-repunit-term (index-term)
  (putnam-2007-a4-divide-term
   (putnam-2007-a4-subtract-term
    (list
     'expt
     (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 10)
     (putnam-2007-a4-add-term
      (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 1)
      index-term))
    (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 1))
   (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 9)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-polynomial-weight-term
    (polynomial value-term)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (putnam-2007-a4-add-term
       (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 1)
       (putnam-2007-a4-multiply-term
        (putnam-2007-a4-absolute-term value-term)
        (putnam-2007-a4-polynomial-weight-term
         (cdr polynomial) value-term)))
    (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 0)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-evaluation-precision-term
    (polynomial value-term epsilon-term)
  (let ((weight
         (putnam-2007-a4-polynomial-weight-term
          polynomial value-term)))
    (putnam-2007-a4-divide-term
     epsilon-term
     (list
      'if
      (list '< (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 0) weight)
      weight
      (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 1)))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-polynomial-approximation-term
    (polynomial value-term precision-term)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (putnam-2007-a4-add-term
       (putnam-2007-a4-apply-term
        (car polynomial)
        (list precision-term))
       (putnam-2007-a4-multiply-term
        value-term
        (putnam-2007-a4-polynomial-approximation-term
         (cdr polynomial)
         value-term
         precision-term)))
    (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 0)))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-singleton-function ()
  (list
   'lambda
   '(value)
   (putnam-2007-a4-term-list (list 'value))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-index-tuples-term (last-term)
  (list
   'collect$
   (putnam-2007-a4-quoted
    (putnam-2007-a4-singleton-function))
   (list
    'from-to-by
    (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 0)
    last-term
    (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 1))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-digit-function ()
  (let* ((candidate
          (list 'car 'globals))
         (exponent
          (list 'car 'exponent-tuple))
         (place
          (list
           'expt
           (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 10)
           exponent))
         (digit
          (list
           'mod
           (list 'floor candidate place)
           (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 10))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(globals exponent-tuple)
     (list
      'if
      (list '< candidate place)
      (putnam-2007-a4-quoted t)
      (list
       'equal
       digit
       (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 1))))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-decimal-repunit-term
    (candidate-term)
  (putnam-2007-a4-and-terms
   (list
    (list 'integerp candidate-term)
    (list
     '<
     (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 0)
     candidate-term)
    (list
     'always$+
     (putnam-2007-a4-quoted
      (putnam-2007-a4-digit-function))
     (putnam-2007-a4-term-list
      (list candidate-term))
     (putnam-2007-a4-index-tuples-term
      candidate-term)))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-preservation-function
    (polynomial)
  (let* ((input-index 'input-index)
         (epsilon 'epsilon)
         (input-value
          (putnam-2007-a4-repunit-term input-index))
         (fixed-precision
          (putnam-2007-a4-evaluation-precision-term
           polynomial
           input-value
           (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 1/4)))
         (fixed-approximation
          (putnam-2007-a4-polynomial-approximation-term
           polynomial
           input-value
           fixed-precision))
         (candidate
          (list
           'floor
           (putnam-2007-a4-add-term
            fixed-approximation
            (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 1/2))
           (putnam-2007-a4-quoted 1)))
         (precision
          (putnam-2007-a4-evaluation-precision-term
           polynomial input-value epsilon))
         (approximation
          (putnam-2007-a4-polynomial-approximation-term
           polynomial input-value precision))
         (distance
          (putnam-2007-a4-absolute-term
           (putnam-2007-a4-subtract-term
            approximation candidate)))
         (qualification
          (putnam-2007-a4-and-terms
           (list
            (list 'natp input-index)
            (putnam-2007-a4-positive-rational-term
             epsilon))))
         (conclusion
          (putnam-2007-a4-and-terms
           (list
            (list 'rationalp fixed-approximation)
            (putnam-2007-a4-decimal-repunit-term
             candidate)
            (list 'rationalp approximation)
            (putnam-2007-a4-less-equal-term
             distance epsilon)))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(input-index epsilon)
     (putnam-2007-a4-implies-term
      qualification conclusion))))

(defun putnam-2007-a4-preserves-repunits-p
    (polynomial)
  (let ((matrix
         (putnam-2007-a4-preservation-function
          polynomial))
        (always-true
         (putnam-2007-a4-true-function
          '(input-index epsilon))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp matrix)
     (tamep-functionp always-true)
     (fn-equal matrix always-true))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2007-a4-statement
    (polynomial)
  (implies
   (putnam-2007-a4-real-polynomial-p polynomial)
   (iff
    (putnam-2007-a4-preserves-repunits-p polynomial)
    (putnam-2007-a4-solution-p polynomial))))

;; These evaluations ensure that every function object used by FN-EQUAL is
;; actually tame; they assert no theorem and admit no proof or axiom.
(value-triple
 (list
  :itpeval-tame-functions
  (tamep-functionp
   (putnam-2007-a4-real-name-cauchy-function
    '(lambda (epsilon) '0)))
  (tamep-functionp
   (putnam-2007-a4-real-equal-rational-function
    '(lambda (epsilon) '0)
    0))
  (tamep-functionp
   (putnam-2007-a4-digit-function))
  (tamep-functionp
   (putnam-2007-a4-preservation-function
    '((lambda (epsilon) '0))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2007_a4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2007_a4): classification of real polynomials
-- that map every base-10 repunit to a repunit. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<=Z_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_
infix 1 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data _<=Z_ : Int -> Int -> Set where
  pos<=posZ :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    m <=N n ->
    pos m <=Z pos n
  neg<=posZ :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    negsuc m <=Z pos n
  neg<=negZ :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    n <=N m ->
    negsuc m <=Z negsuc n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

nineN : Nat
nineN =
  suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc zero))))))))

tenN : Nat
tenN =
  suc nineN

oneMinusNat : Nat -> Int
oneMinusNat zero =
  pos oneN
oneMinusNat (suc zero) =
  pos zero
oneMinusNat (suc (suc n)) =
  negsuc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals (naturalPower reals x n) x

integerPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Int ->
  R
integerPower reals x (pos n) =
  naturalPower reals x n
integerPower reals x (negsuc n) =
  inverse reals (naturalPower reals x (suc n))

Polynomial : Set -> Set
Polynomial R =
  List R

evaluate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  R ->
  R
evaluate reals [] x =
  zeroR reals
evaluate reals (coefficient ∷ coefficients) x =
  add reals coefficient
    (multiply reals x (evaluate reals coefficients x))

repunitValue : Nat -> Nat
repunitValue zero =
  oneN
repunitValue (suc n) =
  tenN * repunitValue n + oneN

module Putnam2007A4Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  Repunit : R -> Set
  Repunit x =
    Exists Nat
      (\ digitsMinusOne ->
        x ==
        fromNat reals
          (repunitValue digitsMinusOne))

  PreservesRepunits :
    Polynomial R ->
    Set
  PreservesRepunits polynomial =
    (x : R) ->
    Repunit x ->
    Repunit (evaluate reals polynomial x)

  solutionValue :
    Nat ->
    Int ->
    R ->
    R
  solutionValue d c x =
    divide reals
      (subtract reals
        (multiply reals
          (integerPower reals (fromNat reals tenN) c)
          (naturalPower reals
            (add reals
              (multiply reals
                (fromNat reals nineN)
                x)
              (oneR reals))
            d))
        (oneR reals))
      (fromNat reals nineN)

  IsSolution :
    Polynomial R ->
    Set
  IsSolution polynomial =
    Exists Nat
      (\ d ->
        Exists Int
          (\ c ->
            oneMinusNat d <=Z c
            and
            ((x : R) ->
              evaluate reals polynomial x ==
              solutionValue d c x)))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (polynomial : Polynomial R) ->
    PreservesRepunits polynomial
    iff
    IsSolution polynomial

putnam-2007-a4 : Set1
putnam-2007-a4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2007A4Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a4:
  the classification of real polynomials that map every decimal repunit to a
  decimal repunit. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory realTheory intrealTheory
     real_sigmaTheory polyTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2007_a4 =
  ``let repunit =
      \x : real.
        ?m : num.
          x =
            &SIGMA
              (\i : num. 10 EXP i)
              (count (SUC m))
    in
      !p : real list.
        ((!x : real. repunit x ==> repunit (poly p x)) <=>
         ?d : num. ?c : int.
           c >= 1 - int_of_num d /\
           !x : real.
             poly p x =
               (((10 : real) powr real_of_int c) *
                  (9 * x + 1) pow d -
                1) /
               9)``;

title: putnam_2007_a4
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2007_a4: classification of the real polynomials that map every
  base-ten repunit to a base-ten repunit. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P07A4Repunit is the set of positive integers whose base-ten digits are all
  one: every such number, and only such a number, is a finite sum
  1 + 10 + ... + 10^m for a nonnegative integer m.

  Poly ` RR is set.mm's class of polynomial functions with real
  coefficients. The biconditional states the full classification from the
  ground truth: p preserves repunits exactly when there are d in NN0 and c
  in ZZ with c >= 1 - d such that, on every real x,

                 p(x) = (10^c (9x + 1)^d - 1) / 9.

  Thus the polynomial, real domain, universal repunit condition, and both
  internal classification witnesses are preserved. The declarations are
  unproved $a statement encodings; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

$c P07A4Repunit $.

p07a4-repunit-syntax $a class P07A4Repunit $.

${
  $d i m n $.

  p07a4-repunit-definition $a |- P07A4Repunit =
    {
      n e. NN |
        E. m e. NN0
          n =
          sum_ i e. ( 0 ... m )
            ( ; 1 0 ^ i )
    }
  $.
$}

${
  $d c d n p x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2007-a4 $a |-
    A. p e. ( Poly ` RR )
      (
        A. n e. P07A4Repunit
          ( p ` n ) e. P07A4Repunit
        <->
        E. d e. NN0 E. c e. ZZ
          (
            ( 1 - d ) <_ c
            /\
            A. x e. RR
              ( p ` x )
              =
              (
                (
                  (
                    ( ; 1 0 ^ c )
                    x.
                    ( ( ( 9 x. x ) + 1 ) ^ d )
                  )
                  -
                  1
                )
                /
                9
              )
          )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2007_a4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a4:
% classification of real polynomials that map every base-10 repunit to a
% base-10 repunit. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2007_a4: THEORY
BEGIN
  polynomial: TYPE = list[real]

  polynomial_value(p: polynomial, x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    CASES p OF
      null: 0,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        coefficient + x * polynomial_value(tail, x)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE p BY <<

  decimal_repunit(last_index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF last_index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      10 * decimal_repunit(last_index - 1) + 1
    ENDIF
  MEASURE last_index

  repunit(x: real): bool =
    EXISTS (last_index: nat):
      x = (decimal_repunit(last_index) :: real)

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN 0 ELSE numerator / denominator ENDIF

  preserves_repunits(f: polynomial): bool =
    FORALL (n: real):
      repunit(n) IMPLIES repunit(polynomial_value(f, n))

  classified_polynomial(f: polynomial): bool =
    EXISTS (d, p, q: nat):
      (p :: int) - (q :: int) >= 1 - (d :: int)
        AND
      (FORALL (x: real):
        polynomial_value(f, x)
          = safe_div(
              safe_div(
                (10 :: real) ^ p,
                (10 :: real) ^ q)
                * (9 * x + 1) ^ d
                - 1,
              9))

  putnam_2007_a4: bool =
    FORALL (f: polynomial):
      preserves_repunits(f) IFF classified_polynomial(f)
END putnam_2007_a4

Suppose that a finite group has exactly $n$ elements of order $p$, where $p$ is a prime. Prove that either $n = 0$ or $p$ divides $n+1$.
-/
theorem putnam_2007_a5
(G : Type*) [Group G] [Fintype G]
(p n : ℕ)
(hp : Nat.Prime p)
(hn : n = {g : G | orderOf g = p}.encard)
: n = 0 ∨ p ∣ (n + 1) :=

title: putnam_2007_a5
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_2007_a5:
   in a finite group, the number of elements of a given prime order is zero
   or one less than a multiple of that prime. This file contains no proof. *)

From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect.

Record putnam_2007_a5_group (G : finType) : Type := {
  group_mul : G -> G -> G;
  group_one : G;
  group_inv : G -> G;
  group_assoc :
    forall x y z : G,
      group_mul x (group_mul y z) = group_mul (group_mul x y) z;
  group_left_identity :
    forall x : G, group_mul group_one x = x;
  group_right_identity :
    forall x : G, group_mul x group_one = x;
  group_left_inverse :
    forall x : G, group_mul (group_inv x) x = group_one;
  group_right_inverse :
    forall x : G, group_mul x (group_inv x) = group_one
}.

Arguments group_mul {G} _ _ _.
Arguments group_one {G} _.

Fixpoint group_pow
    {G : finType}
    (grp : putnam_2007_a5_group G)
    (x : G)
    (k : nat) : G :=
  match k with
  | 0 => group_one grp
  | k'.+1 => group_mul grp x (group_pow grp x k')
  end.

Definition has_order
    {G : finType}
    (grp : putnam_2007_a5_group G)
    (x : G)
    (p : nat) : bool :=
  (group_pow grp x p == group_one grp) &&
  all
    (fun k : nat => group_pow grp x k != group_one grp)
    (iota 1 p.-1).

Theorem putnam_2007_a5
    (G : finType)
    (grp : putnam_2007_a5_group G)
    (p n : nat)
    (hp : prime p)
    (hn : n = #|[set g : G | has_order grp g p]|) :
  n = 0 \/ p %| n.+1.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a5:
  for a finite group, the number of elements of prime order p is either zero
  or one less than a multiple of p. This file contains no proof.
*)

needs "Library/iter.ml";;

let statement =
  `!mul:A->A->A. !e:A. !ginv:A->A. !p n:num.
     FINITE (UNIV:A->bool) /\
     (!a b c:A. mul a (mul b c) = mul (mul a b) c) /\
     (!a:A. mul e a = a /\ mul a e = a) /\
     (!a:A. mul (ginv a) a = e /\ mul a (ginv a) = e) /\
     prime p /\
     n = CARD {g:A |
                 ITER p (mul g) e = e /\
                 (!k:num.
                    0 < k /\ k < p ==> ~(ITER k (mul g) e = e))}
     ==> n = 0 \/ p divides (n + 1)`;;

title: putnam_2007_a5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a5:
;; in a finite group, the number of elements of prime order p is either zero
;; or congruent to -1 modulo p. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A duplicate-free carrier and a complete multiplication table represent an
;; arbitrary finite group up to relabeling. The group predicate checks the
;; axioms on every carrier element and keeps inverse witnesses internal.

(defun putnam-2007-a5-set-list-p (xs)
  (if (consp xs)
      (and
       (not (member-equal (car xs) (cdr xs)))
       (putnam-2007-a5-set-list-p (cdr xs)))
    (equal xs nil)))

(defun putnam-2007-a5-binary-table-p (table carrier)
  (if (consp table)
      (let* ((entry (car table))
             (arguments (car entry))
             (value (cdr entry)))
        (and
         (consp entry)
         (true-listp arguments)
         (equal (len arguments) 2)
         (member-equal (car arguments) carrier)
         (member-equal (cadr arguments) carrier)
         (member-equal value carrier)
         (not (assoc-equal arguments (cdr table)))
         (putnam-2007-a5-binary-table-p
          (cdr table) carrier)))
    (equal table nil)))

(defun putnam-2007-a5-multiply (left right table)
  (cdr (assoc-equal (list left right) table)))

(defun putnam-2007-a5-associative-z-p
    (zs x y table)
  (if (endp zs)
      t
    (let* ((z (car zs))
           (xy (putnam-2007-a5-multiply x y table))
           (yz (putnam-2007-a5-multiply y z table)))
      (and
       (equal
        (putnam-2007-a5-multiply xy z table)
        (putnam-2007-a5-multiply x yz table))
       (putnam-2007-a5-associative-z-p
        (cdr zs) x y table)))))

(defun putnam-2007-a5-group-y-axioms-p
    (ys carrier x table)
  (if (endp ys)
      t
    (let ((y (car ys)))
      (and
       (assoc-equal (list x y) table)
       (putnam-2007-a5-associative-z-p
        carrier x y table)
       (putnam-2007-a5-group-y-axioms-p
        (cdr ys) carrier x table)))))

(defun putnam-2007-a5-inverse-exists-p
    (x candidates one table)
  (if (endp candidates)
      nil
    (or
     (and
      (equal
       (putnam-2007-a5-multiply x (car candidates) table)
       one)
      (equal
       (putnam-2007-a5-multiply (car candidates) x table)
       one))
     (putnam-2007-a5-inverse-exists-p
      x (cdr candidates) one table))))

(defun putnam-2007-a5-group-x-axioms-p
    (xs carrier one table)
  (if (endp xs)
      t
    (let ((x (car xs)))
      (and
       (equal
        (putnam-2007-a5-multiply one x table)
        x)
       (equal
        (putnam-2007-a5-multiply x one table)
        x)
       (putnam-2007-a5-inverse-exists-p
        x carrier one table)
       (putnam-2007-a5-group-y-axioms-p
        carrier carrier x table)
       (putnam-2007-a5-group-x-axioms-p
        (cdr xs) carrier one table)))))

(defun putnam-2007-a5-finite-group-p
    (carrier one table)
  (and
   (putnam-2007-a5-set-list-p carrier)
   (consp carrier)
   (member-equal one carrier)
   (putnam-2007-a5-binary-table-p table carrier)
   (putnam-2007-a5-group-x-axioms-p
    carrier carrier one table)))

(defun putnam-2007-a5-power
    (element exponent one table)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      one
    (putnam-2007-a5-multiply
     element
     (putnam-2007-a5-power
      element (- exponent 1) one table)
     table)))

;; In a finite group, every element order is at most the carrier cardinality.
;; Searching exponents 1 through |G| therefore returns the exact order rather
;; than a bounded approximation.

(defun putnam-2007-a5-order-search
    (element exponent remaining one table)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (if (equal
         (putnam-2007-a5-power
          element exponent one table)
         one)
        exponent
      (putnam-2007-a5-order-search
       element
       (+ exponent 1)
       (- remaining 1)
       one
       table))))

(defun putnam-2007-a5-element-order
    (element carrier one table)
  (putnam-2007-a5-order-search
   element 1 (len carrier) one table))

(defun putnam-2007-a5-count-order
    (elements carrier one table p)
  (if (endp elements)
      0
    (+
     (if (equal
          (putnam-2007-a5-element-order
           (car elements) carrier one table)
          p)
         1
       0)
     (putnam-2007-a5-count-order
      (cdr elements) carrier one table p))))

(defun putnam-2007-a5-no-divisor-from-p (number divisor)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix (- number divisor))))
  (if (and (natp number)

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2007_a5): divisibility of one more than the
-- number of elements of prime order in a finite group. This file contains no
-- proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)
open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc; _⊔_)

infix 4 _<N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

record Top : Set where
  constructor truth

Not :
  {a : Level} ->
  Set a ->
  Set a
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

record _and_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists
  {a p : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (P : A -> Set p) :
  Set (a ⊔ p) where

  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<suc : {n : Nat} -> zero <N suc n
  suc<suc  : {m n : Nat} -> m <N n -> suc m <N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record HasCardinality
  {a p : Level}
  {A : Set a}
  (P : A -> Set p)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set (a ⊔ p) where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      P (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (x : A) ->
      P x ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> x == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

record FiniteCarrier
  {a : Level}
  (A : Set a) :
  Set a where

  field
    cardinality :
      Nat
    has-cardinality :
      HasCardinality {A = A} (\ _ -> Top) cardinality

record Group
  {a : Level}
  (G : Set a) :
  Set a where

  field
    identity :
      G
    multiply :
      G ->
      G ->
      G
    inverse :
      G ->
      G
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : G) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    identity-left :
      (x : G) ->
      multiply identity x == x
    identity-right :
      (x : G) ->
      multiply x identity == x
    inverse-left :
      (x : G) ->
      multiply (inverse x) x == identity
    inverse-right :
      (x : G) ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == identity

open Group

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

Divides :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Set
Divides divisor number =
  Exists Nat
    (\ quotient ->
      number == divisor * quotient)

Prime :
  Nat ->
  Set
Prime p =
  one <N p
  and
  ((divisor : Nat) ->
    Divides divisor p ->
    divisor == one or divisor == p)

naturalPower :
  {a : Level} ->
  {G : Set a} ->
  Group G ->
  G ->
  Nat ->
  G
naturalPower group x zero =
  identity group
naturalPower group x (suc exponent) =
  multiply group
    (naturalPower group x exponent)
    x

HasOrder :
  {a : Level} ->
  {G : Set a} ->
  Group G ->
  G ->
  Nat ->
  Set a
HasOrder group x order =
  zero <N order
  and
  naturalPower group x order == identity group
  and
  ((exponent : Nat) ->
    zero <N exponent ->
    exponent <N order ->
    Not (naturalPower group x exponent == identity group))

putnam-2007-a5 :
  (a : Level) ->
  Set (lsuc a)
putnam-2007-a5 a =
  (G : Set a) ->
  (group : Group G) ->
  FiniteCarrier G ->
  (p n : Nat) ->
  Prime p ->
  HasCardinality
    (\ g -> HasOrder group g p)
    n ->
  n == zero or Divides p (n + one)

  putnam_2007_a5: divisibility of one more than the number of elements of
  prime order in a finite group. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  In SetMM, G e. Grp supplies an arbitrary group, Base ` G is its carrier,
  ( od ` G ) is its group-element order function, Fin is the class of finite
  sets, # is finite cardinality, Prime is the class of natural primes, and ||
  is integer divisibility.

  The restricted class contains exactly the carrier elements whose order is
  p, so its cardinality is the source number n. The conclusion preserves the
  source disjunction n = 0 or p divides n + 1. The final declaration is the
  single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

${
  $d G g n p $.

  putnambench-putnam-2007-a5 $a |-
    A. G A. p e. Prime A. n e. NN0
      (
        (
          (
            G e. Grp
            /\
            ( Base ` G ) e. Fin
          )
          /\
          n
          =
          (
            #
            `
            { g e. ( Base ` G ) |
              ( ( od ` G ) ` g ) = p
            }
          )
        )
        ->
        (
          n = 0
          \/
          p || ( n + 1 )
        )
      )
  $.
$}

putnam_2007_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_a5:
% in a finite group, the number of elements of a given prime order is either
% zero or is congruent to minus one modulo that prime. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2007_a5[
  Element: TYPE+,
  multiply: [Element, Element -> Element],
  inverse: [Element -> Element],
  one: Element
]: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[Element]

  group_laws(G: finite_set[Element]): bool =
    G(one)
      AND (FORALL (x, y: Element):
        G(x) AND G(y) IMPLIES G(multiply(x, y)))
      AND (FORALL (x, y, z: Element):
        G(x) AND G(y) AND G(z) IMPLIES
          multiply(multiply(x, y), z)
            = multiply(x, multiply(y, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x: Element):
        G(x) IMPLIES
          multiply(one, x) = x
            AND multiply(x, one) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x: Element):
        G(x) IMPLIES
          G(inverse(x))
            AND multiply(inverse(x), x) = one
            AND multiply(x, inverse(x)) = one)

  group_power(base: Element, exponent: nat): RECURSIVE Element =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      one
    ELSE
      multiply(
        group_power(base, exponent - 1),
        base)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  has_exact_order(
      G: finite_set[Element],
      element: Element,
      order: nat): bool =
    G(element)
      AND order > 0
      AND group_power(element, order) = one
      AND (FORALL (exponent: nat):
        exponent > 0 AND exponent < order IMPLIES
          group_power(element, exponent) /= one)

  elements_of_order(
      G: finite_set[Element],
      order: nat): finite_set[Element] =
    intersection(
      G,
      {element: Element | has_exact_order(G, element, order)})

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND (FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value)

  putnam_2007_a5: bool =
    FORALL (G: finite_set[Element]), (p, n: nat):
      (group_laws(G)
        AND prime_nat(p)
        AND n = card(elements_of_order(G, p)))
      IMPLIES
        n = 0 OR nat_divides(p, n + 1)
END putnam_2007_a5

    (k x : nat) : nat :=

title: putnam_2007_b1

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_b1:
;; a nonconstant integer polynomial with nonnegative coefficients satisfies
;; f(n) divides f(f(n)+1) exactly when the positive integer n is 1.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Coefficients are listed in ascending degree order. Every integer polynomial
;; has such a finite list, and allowing trailing zeroes does not change either
;; its evaluation or the proposition, so this represents the full source
;; polynomial domain rather than a bounded family.

(defun putnam-2007-b1-nonnegative-integer-coefficients-p
    (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and
       (integerp (car coefficients))
       (<= 0 (car coefficients))
       (putnam-2007-b1-nonnegative-integer-coefficients-p
        (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

;; Applied to the positive-degree tail, this is the source's internal
;; existential assertion that some coefficient of degree greater than zero
;; is positive.
(defun putnam-2007-b1-positive-coefficient-exists-p
    (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (or
       (< 0 (car coefficients))
       (putnam-2007-b1-positive-coefficient-exists-p
        (cdr coefficients)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2007-b1-evaluate (coefficients x)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (+ (car coefficients)
         (* x
            (putnam-2007-b1-evaluate
             (cdr coefficients) x)))
    0))

(defun putnam-2007-b1-integer-divides-p (divisor multiple)
  (and
   (integerp divisor)
   (integerp multiple)
   (if (equal divisor 0)
       (equal multiple 0)
     (equal (mod multiple divisor) 0))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2007-b1-statement (coefficients n)
  (implies
   (and
    (true-listp coefficients)
    (putnam-2007-b1-nonnegative-integer-coefficients-p
     coefficients)
    (putnam-2007-b1-positive-coefficient-exists-p
     (cdr coefficients))
    (integerp n)
    (< 0 n))
   (let* ((f-of-n
           (putnam-2007-b1-evaluate coefficients n))
          (f-of-f-of-n-plus-one
           (putnam-2007-b1-evaluate
            coefficients (+ f-of-n 1))))
     (equal
      (putnam-2007-b1-integer-divides-p
       f-of-n f-of-f-of-n-plus-one)
      (equal n 1)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2007_b1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_b1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2007_b1): for an integer polynomial with
-- nonnegative coefficients and a positive nonconstant coefficient, f(n)
-- divides f(f(n) + 1) exactly when the positive integer n is 1.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixr 3 _and_
infix 1 _iff_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data PositiveNatural : Nat -> Set where
  positive-natural :
    {n : Nat} ->
    PositiveNatural (suc n)

data NonnegativeInteger : Int -> Set where
  nonnegative-integer :
    {n : Nat} ->
    NonnegativeInteger (pos n)

data PositiveInteger : Int -> Set where
  positive-integer :
    {n : Nat} ->
    PositiveInteger (pos (suc n))

negativeNat : Nat -> Int
negativeNat zero =
  pos zero
negativeNat (suc n) =
  negsuc n

differenceNat : Nat -> Nat -> Int
differenceNat zero zero =
  pos zero
differenceNat (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
differenceNat zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
differenceNat (suc m) (suc n) =
  differenceNat m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  differenceNat m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  differenceNat n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negativeNat (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negativeNat (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

zeroZ : Int
zeroZ =
  pos zero

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos (suc zero)

Polynomial : Set
Polynomial =
  List Int

coefficientAt : Polynomial -> Nat -> Int
coefficientAt [] index =
  zeroZ
coefficientAt (coefficient ∷ coefficients) zero =
  coefficient
coefficientAt (coefficient ∷ coefficients) (suc index) =
  coefficientAt coefficients index

evaluate : Polynomial -> Int -> Int
evaluate [] x =
  zeroZ
evaluate (coefficient ∷ coefficients) x =
  addInt
    coefficient
    (multiplyInt x (evaluate coefficients x))

AllCoefficientsNonnegative : Polynomial -> Set
AllCoefficientsNonnegative polynomial =
  (index : Nat) ->
  NonnegativeInteger (coefficientAt polynomial index)

HasPositiveNonconstantCoefficient : Polynomial -> Set
HasPositiveNonconstantCoefficient polynomial =
  Exists Nat
    (\ index ->
      PositiveNatural index
      and
      PositiveInteger (coefficientAt polynomial index))

record Divides (divisor dividend : Int) : Set where
  constructor division
  field
    quotient : Int
    division-equation :
      multiplyInt divisor quotient == dividend

putnam-2007-b1 : Set
putnam-2007-b1 =
  (polynomial : Polynomial) ->
  AllCoefficientsNonnegative polynomial ->
  HasPositiveNonconstantCoefficient polynomial ->
  (n : Int) ->
  PositiveInteger n ->
  Divides
    (evaluate polynomial n)
    (evaluate polynomial
      (addInt (evaluate polynomial n) oneZ))
  iff
  n == oneZ

  the divisibility criterion for a nonconstant integer polynomial with
  nonnegative coefficients evaluated at a positive integer. This file

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory;

val putnam_2007_b1 =
  ``let eval_int_poly =
      \coeffs : int list.
      \x : int.
        FOLDR (\c acc. c + x * acc) 0 coeffs
    in
      !f : int list. !n : int.
        (!i : num. i < LENGTH f ==> 0 <= EL i f) /\
        (?i : num. 0 < i /\ i < LENGTH f /\ 0 < EL i f) /\
        0 < n

        ((eval_int_poly f n) int_divides
           (eval_int_poly f (eval_int_poly f n + 1)) <=>
         n = 1)``;

  univariate polynomials over the integers. The function coe1 extracts the
  complete NN0-indexed coefficient function, and eval1 evaluates a polynomial
  at an integer.

  coefficient at an index in NN express exactly the source assumptions that
  every coefficient is nonnegative and that the polynomial is nonconstant.

  and both polynomial evaluations are preserved directly.

    A. f e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) )

                0 <_ ( ( coe1 ` f ) ` k )
              /\
              E. k e. NN

            )
            /\
            0 < n
          )
          ->
          (
            ( ( ( eval1 ` ZZring ) ` f ) ` n )
            ||
            (
              ( ( eval1 ` ZZring ) ` f )
              `
              (
                ( ( ( eval1 ` ZZring ) ` f ) ` n )
                +
                1
              )
            )
            <->
            n = 1
          )
        )
  $.
$}

  for f being Polynomial of INT.Ring,
      n being Element of INT.Ring st
    (for i being Nat holds 0 <= f.i) &
    (ex i being Nat st 0 < i & 0 < f.i) &
    0 < n
  holds
    (eval(f,n) divides eval(f,eval(f,n) + 1.INT.Ring)
      iff n = 1.INT.Ring)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2007_b1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2007_b1:
% divisibility of values of a nonconstant integer polynomial with nonnegative
% coefficients at a positive integer. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2007_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  polynomial: TYPE = list[int]

  coefficient(p: polynomial, degree: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES p OF
      null: 0,
      cons(head_coefficient, tail):
        IF degree = 0 THEN
          head_coefficient
        ELSE
          coefficient(tail, degree - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE p BY <<

  polynomial_value(p: polynomial, x: int): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES p OF
      null: 0,
      cons(head_coefficient, tail):
        head_coefficient + x * polynomial_value(tail, x)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE p BY <<

  int_divides(divisor, value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: int):
      value = divisor * quotient

  nonnegative_coefficients(p: polynomial): bool =
    FORALL (degree: nat):
      coefficient(p, degree) >= 0

  nonconstant_with_positive_coefficient(p: polynomial): bool =
    EXISTS (degree: nat):
      degree > 0 AND coefficient(p, degree) > 0

  putnam_2007_b1: bool =
    FORALL (f: polynomial), (n: int):
      (nonnegative_coefficients(f)
        AND nonconstant_with_positive_coefficient(f)
        AND n > 0)
      IMPLIES
        (int_divides(
          polynomial_value(f, n),
          polynomial_value(
            f,
            polynomial_value(f, n) + 1))
          IFF n = 1)
END putnam_2007_b1

import Mathlib

open Set Nat Function

/--
Suppose that $f: [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ has a continuous derivative and that $\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx = 0$. Prove that for every $\alpha \in (0,1)$,
\[
\left| \int_0^\alpha f(x)\,dx \right| \leq \frac{1}{8} \max_{0 \leq x
\leq 1} |f'(x)|.
\]
-/
theorem putnam_2007_b2
(f : ℝ → ℝ)
(hf : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (Icc 0 1))
(hfint : ∫ x in (0)..1, f x = 0)
(max : ℝ)
(heqmax : ∃ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, |deriv f x| = max)
(hmaxub : ∀ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, |deriv f x| ≤ max)
: (∀ α ∈ (Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1), |∫ x in (0)..α, f x| ≤ (1 / 8) * max) :=
sorry

Require Import Reals Coquelicot.Coquelicot.
Theorem putnam_2007_b2
    (f: R -> R)
    (hf : (forall (x: R), 0 <= x <= 1 -> ex_derive f x /\ continuity_pt (Derive f) x) /\ RInt f 0 1 = 0)
    (max_f_prime_abs: R)
    (heqmax: exists (x: R), 0 <= x <= 1 -> max_f_prime_abs = Rabs (Derive f x))
    (hmaxub: forall (x: R), 0 <= x <= 1 -> max_f_prime_abs >= Rabs (Derive f x))
    : forall (a: R), 0 < a < 1 -> Rabs (RInt f 0 a) <= max_f_prime_abs / 8.
Proof. Admitted.
