/--
Let $d_n$ be the determinant of the $n \times n$ matrix whose entries, from left to right and then from top to bottom, are $\cos 1, \cos 2, \dots, \cos n^2$. (For example,\[ d_3 = \left|\begin{matrix} \cos 1 & \cos 2 & \cos 3 \\ \cos 4 & \cos 5 & \cos 6 \\  \cos 7 & \cos 8 & \cos 9 \end{matrix} \right|. \]The argument of $\cos$ is always in radians, not degrees.) Evaluate $\lim_{n\to\infty} d_n$.

theorem putnam_2009_a3
(cos_matrix : (n : ℕ) → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
(hM : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ i j : Fin n, (cos_matrix n) i j = Real.cos (1 + n * i + j))
: Tendsto (fun n => (cos_matrix n).det) atTop (𝓝 putnam_2009_a3_solution) :=

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_a3:
   the determinants of the n by n real matrices with consecutive cosine
   entries converge to zero; this file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals List Arith.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope R_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_2009_a3_sum (xs : list R) : R :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0
  | x :: rest => x + putnam_2009_a3_sum rest
  end.

Definition putnam_2009_a3_delete_nth
    {T : Type} (j : nat) (xs : list T) : list T :=
  firstn j xs ++ skipn (S j) xs.

Definition putnam_2009_a3_cofactor_sign (j : nat) : R :=
  if Nat.even j then 1 else -1.

Fixpoint putnam_2009_a3_det
    (n : nat) (M : list (list R)) {struct n} : R :=
  match n with
  | O => 1
  | S k =>
      match M with
      | [] => 0
      | row :: rows =>
          putnam_2009_a3_sum
            (map
              (fun j : nat =>
                putnam_2009_a3_cofactor_sign j *
                nth j row 0 *
                putnam_2009_a3_det k
                  (map (putnam_2009_a3_delete_nth j) rows))
              (seq 0 (S k)))
      end
  end.

Definition putnam_2009_a3_matrix
    (n : nat) (A : nat -> nat -> R) : list (list R) :=
  map
    (fun i : nat =>
      map (fun j : nat => A i j) (seq 0 n))
    (seq 0 n).

Definition putnam_2009_a3_tends_to
    (u : nat -> R) (limit : R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    0 < epsilon ->
    exists N : nat,
      forall n : nat,
        (N <= n)%nat ->
        Rabs (u n - limit) < epsilon.

Theorem putnam_2009_a3
    (cos_matrix : nat -> nat -> nat -> R)
    (hM :
      forall n i j : nat,
        (i < n)%nat ->
        (j < n)%nat ->
        cos_matrix n i j =
          cos (INR ((1 + n * i + j)%nat))) :
  putnam_2009_a3_tends_to
    (fun n : nat =>
      putnam_2009_a3_det n
        (putnam_2009_a3_matrix n (cos_matrix n)))
    0.
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_a3:
;; the determinants of the n-by-n real cosine matrices with entry
;; cos(1+n*i+j), in radians, converge to 0. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Standard ACL2 has exact rational arithmetic rather than primitive real
;; cosine.  The rational pairs below form an unbounded Cauchy approximation
;; to (cos(1),sin(1)).  Exact complex powering then approximates cos(k) for
;; every natural k, so no real value is replaced by a fixed rational sample.

(defun putnam-2009-a3-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n
       (putnam-2009-a3-factorial (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-cosine-one-prefix (terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (degree (* 2 index))
           (sign (if (equal (mod index 2) 0) 1 -1)))
      (+ (putnam-2009-a3-cosine-one-prefix index)
         (/ sign
            (putnam-2009-a3-factorial degree))))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-sine-one-prefix (terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (degree (+ (* 2 index) 1))
           (sign (if (equal (mod index 2) 0) 1 -1)))
      (+ (putnam-2009-a3-sine-one-prefix index)
         (/ sign
            (putnam-2009-a3-factorial degree))))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-complex-multiply (left right)
  (let ((a (car left))
        (b (cdr left))
        (c (car right))
        (d (cdr right)))
    (cons (- (* a c) (* b d))
          (+ (* a d) (* b c)))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-complex-power (base exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      (cons 1 0)
    (putnam-2009-a3-complex-multiply
     base
     (putnam-2009-a3-complex-power
      base (- exponent 1)))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-cosine-integer-prefix
    (integer terms)
  (car
   (putnam-2009-a3-complex-power
    (cons
     (putnam-2009-a3-cosine-one-prefix terms)
     (putnam-2009-a3-sine-one-prefix terms))
    integer)))

;; This precision grows without bound as the rational tolerance tends to zero
;; and also dominates the largest angle, n^2, in the matrix.  The alternating
;; Taylor remainder and continuity of finite products therefore make the
;; rational matrix below a Cauchy name for the source real cosine matrix.
(defun putnam-2009-a3-approximation-terms
    (epsilon n)
  (if (and (rationalp epsilon)
           (< 0 epsilon))
      (+ 1
         (* 2
            (+ (denominator epsilon)
               (* (+ 1 (nfix n))
                  (+ 1 (nfix n))))))
    1))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-range-from (start count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons start
          (putnam-2009-a3-range-from
           (+ 1 start) (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-matrix-row
    (n row columns terms)
  (if (endp columns)
      nil
    (cons
     (putnam-2009-a3-cosine-integer-prefix
      (+ 1 (* n row) (car columns))
      terms)
     (putnam-2009-a3-matrix-row
      n row (cdr columns) terms))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-matrix-rows
    (n rows columns terms)
  (if (endp rows)
      nil
    (cons
     (putnam-2009-a3-matrix-row
      n (car rows) columns terms)
     (putnam-2009-a3-matrix-rows
      n (cdr rows) columns terms))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-matrix (n terms)
  (let ((indices
         (putnam-2009-a3-range-from 0 n)))
    (putnam-2009-a3-matrix-rows
     n indices indices terms)))

;; The determinant is the full Leibniz signed sum over all permutations.

(defun putnam-2009-a3-prefix-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (cons (cons item (car lists))
          (putnam-2009-a3-prefix-each
           item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-insert-everywhere (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list (list item))
    (cons
     (cons item list)
     (putnam-2009-a3-prefix-each
      (car list)
      (putnam-2009-a3-insert-everywhere
       item (cdr list))))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-insert-into-each
    (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-2009-a3-insert-everywhere
      item (car lists))
     (putnam-2009-a3-insert-into-each
      item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-permutations (list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list nil)
    (putnam-2009-a3-insert-into-each
     (car list)
     (putnam-2009-a3-permutations
      (cdr list)))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-count-greater (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      0
    (+ (if (> item (car list)) 1 0)
       (putnam-2009-a3-count-greater
        item (cdr list)))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-inversion-count (permutation)
  (if (endp permutation)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2009-a3-count-greater
        (car permutation) (cdr permutation))
       (putnam-2009-a3-inversion-count
        (cdr permutation)))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-diagonal-product
    (matrix permutation row)
  (if (endp permutation)
      1
    (* (nth (car permutation) (nth row matrix))
       (putnam-2009-a3-diagonal-product
        matrix (cdr permutation) (+ 1 row)))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-determinant-sum
    (matrix permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      0
    (let* ((permutation (car permutations))
           (product
            (putnam-2009-a3-diagonal-product
             matrix permutation 0))
           (signed-product
            (if (equal
                 (mod
                  (putnam-2009-a3-inversion-count
                   permutation)
                  2)
                 0)
                product
              (- product))))
      (+ signed-product
         (putnam-2009-a3-determinant-sum
          matrix (cdr permutations))))))

(defun putnam-2009-a3-determinant-prefix
    (n terms)
  (putnam-2009-a3-determinant-sum
   (putnam-2009-a3-matrix n terms)
   (putnam-2009-a3-permutations
    (putnam-2009-a3-range-from 0 n))))

;; The determinant prefixes form a regular-Cauchy name for each source real
;; determinant. The tail predicate separates the requested limit tolerance
;; EPSILON from the independent approximation tolerance ETA. Requiring
;;
;;   |approximation| <= epsilon/2 + eta
;;
;; for every positive ETA implies that the exact determinant has absolute
;; value at most epsilon/2, hence strictly below epsilon. Conversely, ordinary
;; convergence to zero supplies such a tail after shrinking the tolerance.
;; Positive rational tolerances are cofinal among positive real tolerances.

(defun-sk putnam-2009-a3-tail-p (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall
   (n eta)
   (implies
    (and
     (natp n)
     (natp cutoff)
     (<= cutoff n)
     (rationalp eta)
     (< 0 eta))
    (<=
     (abs
      (putnam-2009-a3-determinant-prefix
       n
       (putnam-2009-a3-approximation-terms
        eta n)))
     (+ (/ epsilon 2) eta)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-a3-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists
   (cutoff)
   (and
    (natp cutoff)
    (putnam-2009-a3-tail-p epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-2009-a3-statement ()
  (forall
   (epsilon)
   (implies
    (and
     (rationalp epsilon)
     (< 0 epsilon))
    (putnam-2009-a3-cutoff-exists-p epsilon))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2009_a3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_a3:
-- the determinants of the n by n matrices with row-major entries
-- cos(1), cos(2), ..., cos(n squared), in radians, converge to zero.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2009A3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finToNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (finToNat i)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

alternatingPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingPower reals n =
  naturalPower reals
    (negate reals (oneR reals))
    n

cosineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
cosineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingPower reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (twoN * n)))
    (fromNat reals (factorial (twoN * n)))

record StandardCosine
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) : Set1 where
  field
    cosine : R -> R
    cosine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (cosineTerm reals x)
        (cosine x)

open StandardCosine

Matrix : Set -> Nat -> Set
Matrix R n =
  Fin n -> Fin n -> R

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

skip :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin (suc n)
skip {zero} column ()
skip {suc n} fzero k =
  fsuc k
skip {suc n} (fsuc column) fzero =
  fzero
skip {suc n} (fsuc column) (fsuc k) =
  fsuc (skip column k)

firstRowMinor :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R (suc n) ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Matrix R n
firstRowMinor A column i j =
  A (fsuc i) (skip column j)

alternatingSign :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  R
alternatingSign reals fzero =
  oneR reals
alternatingSign reals (fsuc i) =
  negate reals (alternatingSign reals i)

determinant :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  R
determinant reals {zero} A =
  oneR reals
determinant reals {suc n} A =
  sumFin reals
    (\ column ->
      multiply reals
        (alternatingSign reals column)
        (multiply reals
          (A fzero column)
          (determinant reals (firstRowMinor A column))))

matrixEntryArgument :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n ->
  Nat
matrixEntryArgument {n} i j =
  suc ((n * finToNat i) + finToNat j)

putnam-2009-a3 : Set1
putnam-2009-a3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (trigonometry : StandardCosine reals) ->
  (cosMatrix : (n : Nat) -> Matrix R n) ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    (i j : Fin n) ->
    cosMatrix n i j ==
    cosine trigonometry
      (fromNat reals (matrixEntryArgument i j))) ->
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> determinant reals (cosMatrix n))
    (zeroR reals)

title: putnam_2009_a3
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_a3:
  the determinants of the row-major n by n cosine matrices converge to zero
  as n tends to infinity. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory permutesTheory realTheory;
open real_topologyTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2009_a3 =
  ``let determinant =
      \n : num. \A : num -> num -> real.
        ITSET
          (\p : num -> num. \sum : real.
             (if evenperm p then
                ITSET
                  (\i : num. \acc : real. A i (p i) * acc)
                  (count n)
                  1
              else
                -(ITSET
                    (\i : num. \acc : real. A i (p i) * acc)
                    (count n)
                    1)) +
             sum)
          {p : num -> num | p permutes count n}
          0
    in
      !cos_matrix : num -> num -> num -> real.
        (!n i j : num.
           i < n /\ j < n
           ==>
           cos_matrix n i j = cos (&(1 + n * i + j)))
        ==>
        ((\n : num. determinant n (cos_matrix n)) --> (0 : real))
          sequentially``;

title: putnam_2009_a3
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2009_a3: the determinants of the n-by-n real matrices whose
  entries are cos(1 + n i + j) converge to zero. This file contains no
  proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For each n in NN0, the carrier 0 ..^ n is the canonical zero-based
  n-element index set. Thus the row-i, column-j entry below is
  cos(1 + n*i + j), so reading rows from left to right gives precisely
  cos(1), cos(2), ..., cos(n^2). SetMM's maDet over RRfld is the real
  determinant, and ~~> is real-sequence convergence.

  Inlining the uniquely specified source matrix is definitionally
  equivalent to universally quantifying that matrix under its entrywise
  defining hypothesis. The determinant at n = 0 does not affect the
  limit. The target zero is the solution annotated in both ground-truth
  sources. The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus
  statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d i j n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2009-a3 $a |-
    (
      n e. NN0 |->
        (
          ( ( 0 ..^ n ) maDet RRfld )
          `
          (
            i e. ( 0 ..^ n ) , j e. ( 0 ..^ n ) |->
              (
                cos
                `
                (
                  1
                  +
                  ( ( n x. i ) + j )
                )
              )
          )
        )
    )
    ~~>
    0
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2009_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_a3:
% the determinants of the n by n real matrices filled row by row with
% cos(1), cos(2), ..., cos(n^2), in radians, converge to zero. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_2009_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  square_matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  cosine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index),
              nat_factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  cosine_value(argument, value: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat): cosine_partial(argument, count),
      value)

  cosine(argument: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        cosine_value(argument, value))

  quotient_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      0
    ELSE
      1
        + quotient_aux(
            numerator - denominator,
            denominator,
            fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  remainder_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      numerator
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator - denominator,
        denominator,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  safe_ndiv(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    quotient_aux(
      numerator,
      denominator,
      numerator + 1)

  safe_mod(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator,
        denominator,
        numerator + 1)
    ENDIF

  function_code_count(size: nat): nat =
    IF size = 0 THEN 1 ELSE size ^ size ENDIF

  permutation_entry(code, row, size: nat): nat =
    IF size = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      safe_mod(safe_ndiv(code, size ^ row), size)
    ENDIF

  permutation_code(code, size: nat): bool =
    code < function_code_count(size)
      AND (FORALL (row_1, row_2: nat):
        (row_1 < size
          AND row_2 < size
          AND permutation_entry(code, row_1, size)
            = permutation_entry(code, row_2, size))
        IMPLIES row_1 = row_2)

  pair_row(pair, size: nat): nat =
    safe_ndiv(pair, size)

  pair_column(pair, size: nat): nat =
    safe_mod(pair, size)

  inversion_at(code, pair, size: nat): bool =
    pair_row(pair, size) < size
      AND pair_column(pair, size) < size
      AND pair_row(pair, size) < pair_column(pair, size)
      AND permutation_entry(code, pair_row(pair, size), size)
        > permutation_entry(code, pair_column(pair, size), size)

  count_true(
      property: [nat -> bool],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_true(property, count - 1)
        + IF property(count - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  inversion_count(code, size: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      (LAMBDA (pair: nat): inversion_at(code, pair, size)),
      size * size)

  permutation_sign(code, size: nat): real =
    IF mod(inversion_count(code, size), 2) = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -1
    ENDIF

  permutation_product(
      A: square_matrix,
      code, size, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      permutation_product(A, code, size, count - 1)
        * A(
            count - 1,
            permutation_entry(code, count - 1, size))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  determinant_sum(
      A: square_matrix,
      size, limit: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET code: nat = limit - 1 IN
        determinant_sum(A, size, limit - 1)
          + IF permutation_code(code, size) THEN
              permutation_sign(code, size)
                * permutation_product(A, code, size, size)
            ELSE
              0
            ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  determinant(A: square_matrix, size: nat): real =
    determinant_sum(A, size, function_code_count(size))

  cosine_matrix(n: nat): square_matrix =
    LAMBDA (row, column: nat):
      cosine((1 + n * row + column) :: real)

  determinant_sequence(n: nat): real =
    determinant(cosine_matrix(n), n)

  putnam_2009_a3: bool =
    converges_to(determinant_sequence, 0)
END putnam_2009_a3

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_a4:
;; a proper set of rational numbers containing zero and closed under integer
;; shifts and the map x |-> 1/(x(x-1)). This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The source answer is False, so its biconditional is equivalent to the
;; existence of a proper set satisfying the three hypotheses. A tame unary
;; function object represents the characteristic function of that set.

(defun putnam-2009-a4-member-p (set x)
  (if (apply$ set (list x)) t nil))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-a4-closed-p (set)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (putnam-2009-a4-member-p set x))
     (and
      (putnam-2009-a4-member-p set (+ x 1))
      (putnam-2009-a4-member-p set (- x 1))
      (implies
       (and
        (not (equal x 0))
        (not (equal x 1)))
       (putnam-2009-a4-member-p
        set
        (/ 1 (* x (- x 1)))))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-a4-proper-p (set)
  (exists (omitted)
    (and
     (rationalp omitted)
     (not (putnam-2009-a4-member-p set omitted)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-a4-counterexample-exists-p ()
  (exists (set)
    (and
     (tamep-functionp set)
     (putnam-2009-a4-member-p set 0)
     (putnam-2009-a4-closed-p set)
     (putnam-2009-a4-proper-p set))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2009-a4-statement ()
  (putnam-2009-a4-counterexample-exists-p))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2009_a4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_a4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2009_a4): whether every set of rational numbers
-- containing zero and closed under shifts by one and the stated reciprocal
-- operation contains all rationals; the requested answer is False. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2009A4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)
open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; _⊔_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not :
  {ell : Level} ->
  Set ell ->
  Set ell
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ :
  {ell : Level} ->
  {A : Set ell} ->
  A ->
  A ->
  Set ell
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_
  {left-level right-level : Level}
  (A : Set left-level)
  (B : Set right-level) :
  Set (left-level ⊔ right-level) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Iff
  {left-level right-level : Level}
  (A : Set left-level)
  (B : Set right-level) :
  Set (left-level ⊔ right-level) where

  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists
  {element-level property-level : Level}
  (A : Set element-level)
  (P : A -> Set property-level) :
  Set (element-level ⊔ property-level) where

  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record RationalField (Q : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroQ oneQ : Q
    add multiply : Q -> Q -> Q
    negate inverse : Q -> Q
    fromNat : Nat -> Q
    fromInt : Int -> Q

    one-not-zero :
      oneQ != zeroQ

    add-commutative :
      (x y : Q) ->
      add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : Q) ->
      add x zeroQ == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : Q) ->
      add x (negate x) == zeroQ

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : Q) ->
      multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : Q) ->
      multiply x oneQ == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : Q) ->
      multiply x zeroQ == zeroQ
    distribute :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroQ == zeroQ
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : Q) ->
      x != zeroQ ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneQ

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroQ
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneQ
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    fromInt-nonnegative :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromInt (pos n) == fromNat n
    fromInt-negative :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromInt (negsuc n) == negate (fromNat (suc n))

    every-element-is-ratio :
      (x : Q) ->
      Exists Int
        (\ numerator ->
          Exists Nat
            (\ denominator-minus-one ->
              x ==
              multiply
                (fromInt numerator)
                (inverse
                  (fromNat (suc denominator-minus-one)))))

open RationalField

subtract :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q ->
  Q ->
  Q
subtract rationals x y =
  add rationals x (negate rationals y)

divide :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  Q ->
  Q ->
  Q
divide rationals x y =
  multiply rationals x (inverse rationals y)

module Putnam2009A4Statement
  {Q : Set}
  (rationals : RationalField Q) where

  ShiftClosed : (Q -> Set) -> Set
  ShiftClosed S =
    (x : Q) ->
    S x ->
    S (add rationals x (oneQ rationals))
    and
    S (subtract rationals x (oneQ rationals))

  ReciprocalClosed : (Q -> Set) -> Set
  ReciprocalClosed S =
    (x : Q) ->
    S x ->
    x != zeroQ rationals ->
    x != oneQ rationals ->
    S
      (divide rationals
        (oneQ rationals)
        (multiply rationals
          x
          (subtract rationals x (oneQ rationals))))

  ContainsAllRationals : (Q -> Set) -> Set
  ContainsAllRationals S =
    (r : Q) ->
    S r

  universal-claim : Set1
  universal-claim =
    (S : Q -> Set) ->
    S (zeroQ rationals) ->
    ShiftClosed S ->
    ReciprocalClosed S ->
    ContainsAllRationals S

putnam-2009-a4 : Set1
putnam-2009-a4 =
  (Q : Set) ->
  (rationals : RationalField Q) ->
  Iff
    (Putnam2009A4Statement.universal-claim rationals)
    Bottom

content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_a5:
   nonexistence of a finite abelian group whose element orders have product
   2^2009; this file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Arith.PeanoNat.

Record putnam_2009_a5_comm_group (G : Type) : Type := {
  putnam_2009_a5_mul : G -> G -> G;
  putnam_2009_a5_one : G;
  putnam_2009_a5_inv : G -> G;
  putnam_2009_a5_assoc :
    forall x y z : G,
      putnam_2009_a5_mul x (putnam_2009_a5_mul y z) =
      putnam_2009_a5_mul (putnam_2009_a5_mul x y) z;
  putnam_2009_a5_left_identity :
    forall x : G, putnam_2009_a5_mul putnam_2009_a5_one x = x;
  putnam_2009_a5_right_identity :
    forall x : G, putnam_2009_a5_mul x putnam_2009_a5_one = x;
  putnam_2009_a5_left_inverse :
    forall x : G,
      putnam_2009_a5_mul (putnam_2009_a5_inv x) x =
      putnam_2009_a5_one;
  putnam_2009_a5_right_inverse :
    forall x : G,
      putnam_2009_a5_mul x (putnam_2009_a5_inv x) =
      putnam_2009_a5_one;
  putnam_2009_a5_commutative :
    forall x y : G,
      putnam_2009_a5_mul x y = putnam_2009_a5_mul y x
}.

Arguments putnam_2009_a5_mul {G} _ _ _.
Arguments putnam_2009_a5_one {G} _.

Fixpoint putnam_2009_a5_pow
    {G : Type}
    (grp : putnam_2009_a5_comm_group G)
    (x : G)
    (n : nat) : G :=
  match n with
  | O => putnam_2009_a5_one grp
  | S k =>
      putnam_2009_a5_mul grp x
        (putnam_2009_a5_pow grp x k)
  end.

Definition putnam_2009_a5_has_order
    {G : Type}
    (grp : putnam_2009_a5_comm_group G)
    (x : G)
    (n : nat) : Prop :=
  (0 < n)%nat /\
  putnam_2009_a5_pow grp x n = putnam_2009_a5_one grp /\
  forall k : nat,
    (0 < k < n)%nat ->
    putnam_2009_a5_pow grp x k <> putnam_2009_a5_one grp.

Definition putnam_2009_a5_order_product
    {G : Type}
    (enumeration : list G)
    (ord : G -> nat) : nat :=
  fold_right Nat.mul 1 (map ord enumeration).

Definition putnam_2009_a5_solution : Prop := False.

Theorem putnam_2009_a5 :

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_a5:
-- no finite abelian group has the product of the orders of all its elements
-- equal to 2 raised to the 2009th power. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2009A5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_

data Bottom : Set where

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record Finite (A : Set) : Set where
  field
    size :
      Nat
    toFin :
      A ->
      Fin size
    fromFin :
      Fin size ->
      A
    from-to :
      (x : A) ->
      fromFin (toFin x) == x
    to-from :
      (i : Fin size) ->
      toFin (fromFin i) == i

record CommutativeGroup (A : Set) : Set where
  field
    identity :
      A
    multiply :
      A ->
      A ->
      A
    inverse :
      A ->
      A
    associative :
      (x y z : A) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    identity-left :
      (x : A) ->
      multiply identity x == x
    identity-right :
      (x : A) ->
      multiply x identity == x
    inverse-left :
      (x : A) ->
      multiply (inverse x) x == identity
    inverse-right :
      (x : A) ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == identity
    commutative :
      (x y : A) ->
      multiply x y == multiply y x

record FiniteAbelianGroup : Set1 where
  field
    Carrier :
      Set
    group :
      CommutativeGroup Carrier
    finite :
      Finite Carrier

open CommutativeGroup
open Finite
open FiniteAbelianGroup

powerElement :
  (G : FiniteAbelianGroup) ->
  Carrier G ->
  Nat ->
  Carrier G
powerElement G x zero =
  identity (group G)
powerElement G x (suc n) =
  multiply (group G) x (powerElement G x n)

record IsElementOrder
  (G : FiniteAbelianGroup)
  (x : Carrier G)
  (n : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    order-positive :
      Positive n
    power-is-identity :
      powerElement G x n == identity (group G)
    least-positive-power :
      (k : Nat) ->
      Positive k ->
      powerElement G x k == identity (group G) ->
      n <=N k

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

powerNat : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
powerNat base zero =
  one
powerNat base (suc exponent) =
  base * powerNat base exponent

productFin :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Nat) ->
  Nat
productFin {zero} term =
  one
productFin {suc n} term =
  term fzero *
  productFin (\ i -> term (fsuc i))

productOfElementOrders :
  (G : FiniteAbelianGroup) ->
  (Carrier G -> Nat) ->
  Nat
productOfElementOrders G order =
  productFin
    (\ i ->
      order (fromFin (finite G) i))

record Counterexample : Set1 where
  field
    finite-abelian-group :
      FiniteAbelianGroup
    element-order :
      Carrier finite-abelian-group ->
      Nat
    element-order-is-exact :
      (x : Carrier finite-abelian-group) ->
      IsElementOrder
        finite-abelian-group
        x
        (element-order x)
    product-equation :
      productOfElementOrders
        finite-abelian-group
        element-order
      ==
      powerNat two 2009

putnam-2009-a5 : Set1
putnam-2009-a5 =
  Counterexample ->
  Bottom

title: putnam_2009_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_a5:
% no finite abelian group has product of all element orders equal to 2^2009.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2009_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  group_power(
      n: posnat,
      multiply: [below(n), below(n) -> below(n)],
      one, element: below(n),
      exponent: nat): RECURSIVE below(n) =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      one
    ELSE
      multiply(
        group_power(n, multiply, one, element, exponent - 1),
        element)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  commutative_group_laws(
      n: posnat,
      multiply: [below(n), below(n) -> below(n)],
      inverse: [below(n) -> below(n)],
      one: below(n)): bool =
    (FORALL (x, y, z: below(n)):
      multiply(multiply(x, y), z)
        = multiply(x, multiply(y, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x: below(n)):
        multiply(one, x) = x
          AND multiply(x, one) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x: below(n)):
        multiply(inverse(x), x) = one
          AND multiply(x, inverse(x)) = one)
      AND (FORALL (x, y: below(n)):
        multiply(x, y) = multiply(y, x))

  is_element_order(
      n: posnat,
      multiply: [below(n), below(n) -> below(n)],
      one, element: below(n),
      order: nat): bool =
    order > 0
      AND group_power(n, multiply, one, element, order) = one
      AND (FORALL (smaller: nat):
        smaller > 0 AND smaller < order IMPLIES
          group_power(n, multiply, one, element, smaller) /= one)

  orders_product(
      n: posnat,
      orders: [below(n) -> nat],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      orders_product(n, orders, count - 1)
        * IF count <= n THEN orders(count - 1) ELSE 1 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_required_group: bool =
    EXISTS (n: posnat):
      EXISTS
          (multiply: [below(n), below(n) -> below(n)]),
          (inverse: [below(n) -> below(n)]),
          (one: below(n)),
          (orders: [below(n) -> nat]):
        commutative_group_laws(n, multiply, inverse, one)
          AND (FORALL (element: below(n)):
            is_element_order(
              n, multiply, one, element, orders(element)))
          AND orders_product(n, orders, n) = 2 ^ 2009

  putnam_2009_a5: bool =
    NOT has_required_group
END putnam_2009_a5

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A source family Fin k -> nat is represented by a proper ACL2 list of length
;; k. This is a bijective finite-sequence encoding; NIL represents k = 0 and
;; repeated list entries represent repeated primes. ACL2's rational arithmetic
;; gives the source's exact quotient, while DEFUN-SK keeps both finite families
;; existentially quantified inside the statement.

(defun putnam-2009-b1-no-proper-divisor-p (p d)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix d)))
  (if (zp d)
      t
    (and
     (or
      (equal d 1)
      (not (equal (mod p d) 0)))
     (putnam-2009-b1-no-proper-divisor-p p (1- d)))))

(defun putnam-2009-b1-prime-p (p)

   (natp p)
   (< 1 p)
   (putnam-2009-b1-no-proper-divisor-p p (1- p))))

  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (putnam-2009-b1-prime-p (car values))
       (putnam-2009-b1-prime-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n (putnam-2009-b1-factorial (1- n)))))

      (*

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2009_b1): every positive rational is a quotient
-- of finite products of factorials of primes. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2009B1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

Divides : Nat -> Nat -> Set
Divides divisor number =
  Exists Nat
    (\ factor -> divisor * factor == number)

Prime : Nat -> Set
Prime number =
  two <=N number
  and
  ((divisor : Nat) ->
    Divides divisor number ->
    divisor == one or divisor == number)

data All {A : Set} (P : A -> Set) : List A -> Set where
  all[]  : All P []
  all∷   : {x : A} {xs : List A} -> P x -> All P xs -> All P (x ∷ xs)

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  one
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

factorialProduct : List Nat -> Nat
factorialProduct [] =
  one
factorialProduct (n ∷ ns) =
  factorial n * factorialProduct ns

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

scaleInt : Int -> Nat -> Int
scaleInt (pos magnitude) factor =
  pos (magnitude * factor)
scaleInt (negsuc magnitude) factor =
  negative (suc magnitude * factor)

record Rational : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator             : Int
    denominator-minus-one : Nat

open Rational

denominator : Rational -> Nat
denominator q =
  suc (denominator-minus-one q)

data PositiveInt : Int -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> PositiveInt (pos (suc n))

PositiveRational : Rational -> Set
PositiveRational q =
  PositiveInt (numerator q)

RepresentsFactorialQuotient :
  List Nat ->
  List Nat ->
  Rational ->
  Set
RepresentsFactorialQuotient numerator-primes denominator-primes q =
  pos
    (factorialProduct numerator-primes * denominator q)
  ==
  scaleInt
    (numerator q)
    (factorialProduct denominator-primes)

putnam-2009-b1 : Set
putnam-2009-b1 =
  (q : Rational) ->
  PositiveRational q ->
  Exists (List Nat)
    (\ numerator-primes ->
      Exists (List Nat)
        (\ denominator-primes ->
          All Prime numerator-primes
          and
          All Prime denominator-primes
          and
          RepresentsFactorialQuotient
            numerator-primes
            denominator-primes
            q))

title: putnam_2009_b1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b1:
% every positive rational number is a quotient of finite products of
% factorials of not necessarily distinct primes. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2009_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  nat_factorial(n: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      n * nat_factorial(n - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value

  all_prime(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES values OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(value, tail):
        prime_nat(value) AND all_prime(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  factorial_product(values: list[nat]): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null: 1,
      cons(value, tail):
        nat_factorial(value) * factorial_product(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  is_quotient_of_prime_factorials(q: rat): bool =
    EXISTS (numerator_primes, denominator_primes: list[nat]):
      all_prime(numerator_primes)
        AND all_prime(denominator_primes)
        AND q * (factorial_product(denominator_primes) :: rat)
          = (factorial_product(numerator_primes) :: rat)

  putnam_2009_b1: bool =
    FORALL (q: rat):
      q > 0 IMPLIES is_quotient_of_prime_factorials(q)
END putnam_2009_b1

import Mathlib

open Topology MvPolynomial Filter Set

abbrev putnam_2009_b2_solution : Set ℝ := sorry
-- Ioc (1 / 3) 1
/--
A game involves jumping to the right on the real number line. If $a$ and $b$ are real numbers and $b > a$, the cost of jumping from $a$ to $b$ is $b^3-ab^2$. For what real numbers $c$ can one travel from $0$ to $1$ in a finite number of jumps with total cost exactly $c$?
-/
theorem putnam_2009_b2
: ({c : ℝ | ∃ s : ℕ → ℝ, s 0 = 0 ∧ StrictMono s ∧ (∃ n : ℕ, s n = 1 ∧ ((∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, ((s (i + 1)) ^ 3 - (s i) * (s (i + 1)) ^ 2)) = c))} = putnam_2009_b2_solution) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2009_b2
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b2:
   the attainable total costs of finite strictly rightward jumps from zero to
   one with cost b^3 - a*b^2 are exactly the reals in (1/3, 1]; this file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals Arith.PeanoNat.

Open Scope R_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_2009_b2_total_cost
    (s : nat -> R) (n : nat) : R :=
  match n with
  | O => 0
  | S k =>
      putnam_2009_b2_total_cost s k +
      ((s (S k)) ^ 3 - s k * (s (S k)) ^ 2)
  end.

Definition putnam_2009_b2_strict_mono
    (s : nat -> R) : Prop :=
  forall i j : nat, (i < j)%nat -> s i < s j.

Definition putnam_2009_b2_attainable
    (c : R) : Prop :=
  exists s : nat -> R,
    s O = 0 /\
    putnam_2009_b2_strict_mono s /\
    exists n : nat,
      s n = 1 /\
      putnam_2009_b2_total_cost s n = c.

Theorem putnam_2009_b2 :
  forall c : R,
    putnam_2009_b2_attainable c <->
    1 / 3 < c <= 1.
Admitted.

  the attainable total costs of finite rightward jumps from zero to one are
  exactly the real interval (1/3, 1]. This file contains no proof.

let statement =
  `{c:real |
      ?s:num->real.
        s 0 = &0 /\
        (!i j:num. i < j ==> s i < s j) /\
        ?n:num.
          s n = &1 /\
          sum (0..n - 1)

title: putnam_2009_b2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b2:
;; the costs attainable by finitely many strictly rightward real jumps from
;; 0 to 1 are exactly the real numbers c with 1/3 < c <= 1. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Conservative DEFSTUB symbols present an arbitrary scalar carrier and its
;; operations without restricting them to APPLY$-tame function objects. Every
;; field, order, closure, real-closedness, and Archimedean law used below is an
;; explicit hypothesis of the statement.
;;
;; This is an exact field-independent presentation of the source real-number
;; statement. Every Archimedean real-closed ordered field embeds as a
;; real-closed ordered subfield of the reals, and model completeness transfers
;; each fixed finite-path formula in both directions.
;;
;; A path is internally existentially quantified as the finite prefix
;; s(0),...,s(n). Adjacent strict increase is equivalent to strict increase on
;; that prefix, and every such prefix ending at 1 extends to a strictly
;; increasing sequence on all naturals by continuing with 2,3,4,... .

(defstub putnam-2009-b2-carrier (x) t)
(defstub putnam-2009-b2-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub putnam-2009-b2-multiply-op (x y) t)
(defstub putnam-2009-b2-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub putnam-2009-b2-inverse-op (x) t)
(defstub putnam-2009-b2-less-op (x y) t)

(defun putnam-2009-b2-member-p (value)
  (if (putnam-2009-b2-carrier value) t nil))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-add (left right)
  (putnam-2009-b2-add-op left right))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-multiply (left right)
  (putnam-2009-b2-multiply-op left right))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-negate (value)
  (putnam-2009-b2-negate-op value))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-inverse (value)
  (putnam-2009-b2-inverse-op value))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-less-p (left right)
  (if (putnam-2009-b2-less-op left right) t nil))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-less-equal-p (left right)
  (not (putnam-2009-b2-less-p right left)))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-subtract (left right)
  (putnam-2009-b2-add
   left (putnam-2009-b2-negate right)))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-divide (numerator denominator)
  (putnam-2009-b2-multiply
   numerator (putnam-2009-b2-inverse denominator)))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-natural-value (n zero one)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      zero
    (putnam-2009-b2-add
     one
     (putnam-2009-b2-natural-value (1- n) zero one))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b2-field-laws-p (zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2009-b2-member-p x)
      (putnam-2009-b2-member-p y)
      (putnam-2009-b2-member-p z))
     (let* ((xy-add
             (putnam-2009-b2-add x y))
            (yz-add
             (putnam-2009-b2-add y z))
            (xy-multiply
             (putnam-2009-b2-multiply x y))
            (yz-multiply
             (putnam-2009-b2-multiply y z))
            (negative-x
             (putnam-2009-b2-negate x))
            (inverse-x
             (putnam-2009-b2-inverse x)))
       (and
        (putnam-2009-b2-member-p xy-add)
        (putnam-2009-b2-member-p xy-multiply)
        (putnam-2009-b2-member-p negative-x)
        (putnam-2009-b2-member-p inverse-x)
        (equal
         (putnam-2009-b2-add xy-add z)
         (putnam-2009-b2-add x yz-add))
        (equal xy-add
               (putnam-2009-b2-add y x))
        (equal
         (putnam-2009-b2-add x zero)
         x)
        (equal
         (putnam-2009-b2-add x negative-x)
         zero)
        (equal
         (putnam-2009-b2-multiply xy-multiply z)
         (putnam-2009-b2-multiply x yz-multiply))
        (equal
         xy-multiply
         (putnam-2009-b2-multiply y x))
        (equal
         (putnam-2009-b2-multiply x one)
         x)
        (implies
         (equal x zero)
         (equal inverse-x zero))
        (implies
         (not (equal x zero))
         (equal
          (putnam-2009-b2-multiply x inverse-x)
          one))
        (equal
         (putnam-2009-b2-multiply x yz-add)
         (putnam-2009-b2-add
          (putnam-2009-b2-multiply x y)
          (putnam-2009-b2-multiply x z))))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b2-order-laws-p (zero)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2009-b2-member-p x)
      (putnam-2009-b2-member-p y)
      (putnam-2009-b2-member-p z))
     (and
      (not (putnam-2009-b2-less-p x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (putnam-2009-b2-less-p x y)
       (putnam-2009-b2-less-p y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (putnam-2009-b2-less-p x y)
        (putnam-2009-b2-less-p y z))
       (putnam-2009-b2-less-p x z))
      (implies
       (putnam-2009-b2-less-p x y)
       (putnam-2009-b2-less-p
        (putnam-2009-b2-add x z)
        (putnam-2009-b2-add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (putnam-2009-b2-less-p zero x)
        (putnam-2009-b2-less-p zero y))
       (putnam-2009-b2-less-p
        zero (putnam-2009-b2-multiply x y)))))))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-coefficient-list-p (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and
       (putnam-2009-b2-member-p (car coefficients))
       (putnam-2009-b2-coefficient-list-p
        (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-polynomial-value
    (coefficients x zero)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (putnam-2009-b2-add
       (car coefficients)
       (putnam-2009-b2-multiply
        x
        (putnam-2009-b2-polynomial-value
         (cdr coefficients) x zero)))
    zero))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-odd-degree-polynomial-p
    (coefficients zero)
  (and
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (consp coefficients)
   (evenp (len coefficients))
   (putnam-2009-b2-coefficient-list-p coefficients)
   (not (equal (car (last coefficients)) zero))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b2-square-root-exists-p (x)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (putnam-2009-b2-member-p root)
     (equal
      (putnam-2009-b2-multiply root root)
      x))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b2-square-root-law-p (zero)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2009-b2-member-p x)
      (putnam-2009-b2-less-equal-p zero x))
     (putnam-2009-b2-square-root-exists-p x))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b2-odd-root-exists-p
    (zero coefficients)
  (exists (root)
    (and
     (putnam-2009-b2-member-p root)
     (equal
      (putnam-2009-b2-polynomial-value
       coefficients root zero)
      zero))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b2-odd-root-law-p (zero)
  (forall (coefficients)
    (implies
     (putnam-2009-b2-odd-degree-polynomial-p
      coefficients zero)
     (putnam-2009-b2-odd-root-exists-p
      zero coefficients))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b2-archimedean-bound-exists-p
    (zero one x)
  (exists (n)
    (and
     (natp n)
     (putnam-2009-b2-less-p
      x
      (putnam-2009-b2-natural-value n zero one)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b2-archimedean-law-p
    (zero one)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (putnam-2009-b2-member-p x)
     (putnam-2009-b2-archimedean-bound-exists-p
      zero one x))))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-real-context-p (zero one)
  (and
   (putnam-2009-b2-member-p zero)
   (putnam-2009-b2-member-p one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (putnam-2009-b2-field-laws-p zero one)
   (putnam-2009-b2-order-laws-p zero)
   (putnam-2009-b2-less-p zero one)
   (putnam-2009-b2-square-root-law-p zero)
   (putnam-2009-b2-odd-root-law-p zero)
   (putnam-2009-b2-archimedean-law-p zero one)))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-carrier-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (putnam-2009-b2-member-p (car values))
       (putnam-2009-b2-carrier-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-adjacent-increasing-p (values)
  (if (and (consp values)
           (consp (cdr values)))
      (and
       (putnam-2009-b2-less-p
        (car values) (cadr values))
       (putnam-2009-b2-adjacent-increasing-p
        (cdr values)))
    t))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-jump-cost (left right)
  (let* ((right-squared
          (putnam-2009-b2-multiply right right))
         (right-cubed
          (putnam-2009-b2-multiply right right-squared))
         (left-times-right-squared
          (putnam-2009-b2-multiply left right-squared)))
    (putnam-2009-b2-subtract
     right-cubed left-times-right-squared)))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-total-cost (values zero)
  (if (and (consp values)
           (consp (cdr values)))
      (putnam-2009-b2-add
       (putnam-2009-b2-jump-cost
        (car values) (cadr values))
       (putnam-2009-b2-total-cost
        (cdr values) zero))
    zero))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-path-witness-p
    (path c zero one)
  (and
   (true-listp path)
   (consp path)
   (consp (cdr path))
   (putnam-2009-b2-carrier-list-p path)
   (equal (car path) zero)
   (equal (car (last path)) one)
   (putnam-2009-b2-adjacent-increasing-p path)
   (equal
    (putnam-2009-b2-total-cost path zero)
    c)))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b2-attainable-p
    (c zero one)
  (exists (path)
    (putnam-2009-b2-path-witness-p
     path c zero one)))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-one-third (one)
  (let ((three
         (putnam-2009-b2-add
          one (putnam-2009-b2-add one one))))
    (putnam-2009-b2-divide one three)))

(defun putnam-2009-b2-in-solution-interval-p
    (c one)
  (and
   (putnam-2009-b2-less-p
    (putnam-2009-b2-one-third one)
    c)
   (putnam-2009-b2-less-equal-p c one)))

(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-2009-b2-statement
    (zero one)
  (forall (c)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2009-b2-real-context-p zero one)
      (putnam-2009-b2-member-p c))
     (iff
      (putnam-2009-b2-attainable-p c zero one)
      (putnam-2009-b2-in-solution-interval-p
       c one)))))

title: putnam_2009_b2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b2:
-- the attainable total costs of finite strictly rightward journeys from 0 to
-- 1 are exactly the real numbers c with 1/3 < c <= 1. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2009B2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record Equivalent (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalent
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

NatStrictLess : Nat -> Nat -> Set
NatStrictLess m n =
  suc m <=N n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

StrictlyIncreasing :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Set
StrictlyIncreasing reals sequence =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  NatStrictLess i j ->
  StrictLess reals (sequence i) (sequence j)

three : Nat
three =
  suc (suc (suc zero))

oneThird :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
oneThird reals =
  divide reals
    (oneR reals)
    (fromNat reals three)

jumpCost :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
jumpCost reals a b =
  subtract reals
    (naturalPower reals b three)
    (multiply reals
      a
      (naturalPower reals b (suc (suc zero))))

journeyCost :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
journeyCost reals sequence n =
  sumFirst reals n
    (\ i ->
      jumpCost reals
        (sequence i)
        (sequence (suc i)))

AttainableCost :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
AttainableCost {R} reals c =
  Exists (Nat -> R)
    (\ sequence ->
      sequence zero == zeroR reals
      and
      StrictlyIncreasing reals sequence
      and
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          sequence n == oneR reals
          and
          journeyCost reals sequence n == c))

InSolutionInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
InSolutionInterval reals c =
  StrictLess reals (oneThird reals) c
  and
  lessOrEqual reals c (oneR reals)

putnam-2009-b2 : Set1
putnam-2009-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (c : R) ->
  Equivalent
    (AttainableCost reals c)
    (InSolutionInterval reals c)

title: putnam_2009_b2
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b2:
  the attainable total costs of finite strictly rightward jump sequences from
  zero to one form the real interval (1/3, 1]. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;

val putnam_2009_b2 =
  ``{c : real |
       ?s : num -> real.
         s 0 = 0 /\
         (!i j : num. i < j ==> s i < s j) /\
         ?n : num.
           s n = 1 /\
           SIGMA
             (\i : num.
                s (i + 1) pow 3 -
                s i * s (i + 1) pow 2)
             (count n) =
           c} =
    {c : real | 1 / 3 < c /\ c <= 1}``;

title: putnam_2009_b2
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2009_b2: the attainable total costs of finite increasing jump
  sequences from zero to one are exactly the reals greater than one third
  and at most one. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  RR ^m NN0 is the class of all real-valued sequences indexed by the
  nonnegative integers. The first two conjuncts require that s starts at zero
  and is strictly increasing on all natural indices, exactly as in the source
  formalizations. The endpoint index n remains internally existential.

  The half-open integer interval 0 ..^ n consists of the indices from zero
  through n - 1, so the finite sum is the total of the source jump costs

    s(i+1)^3 - s(i) * s(i+1)^2.

  The right side is the annotated solution Ioc (1 / 3) 1. The final
  declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d c i j n s $.

  putnambench-putnam-2009-b2 $a |-
    {
      c e. RR |
      E. s e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
        (
          ( s ` 0 ) = 0
          /\
          (
            A. i e. NN0 A. j e. NN0
              (
                i < j
                ->
                ( s ` i ) < ( s ` j )
              )
            /\
            E. n e. NN0
              (
                ( s ` n ) = 1
                /\
                (
                  sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                    (
                      ( ( s ` ( i + 1 ) ) ^ 3 )
                      -
                      (
                        ( s ` i )
                        x.
                        ( ( s ` ( i + 1 ) ) ^ 2 )
                      )
                    )
                )
                =
                c
              )
          )
        )
    }
    =
    {
      c e. RR |
      (
        ( 1 / 3 ) < c
        /\
        c <_ 1
      )
    }
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2009_b2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b2:
% the real costs attainable by finitely many rightward jumps from 0 to 1 are
% exactly those greater than 1/3 and at most 1. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2009_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  strictly_increasing(sequence: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      i < j IMPLIES sequence(i) < sequence(j)

  jump_cost_sum(
      sequence: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      jump_cost_sum(sequence, count - 1)
        + (sequence(count) ^ 3
            - sequence(count - 1) * sequence(count) ^ 2)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  reachable_cost(cost: real): bool =
    EXISTS (sequence: real_sequence), (jump_count: nat):
      sequence(0) = 0
        AND strictly_increasing(sequence)
        AND sequence(jump_count) = 1
        AND jump_cost_sum(sequence, jump_count) = cost

  putnam_2009_b2: bool =
    FORALL (cost: real):
      reachable_cost(cost)
        IFF (1 / 3 < cost AND cost <= 1)
END putnam_2009_b2

import Mathlib

open Topology MvPolynomial Filter Set

abbrev putnam_2009_b3_solution : Set ℤ := sorry
-- {n : ℤ | ∃ k ≥ 1, n = 2 ^ k - 1}
/--
Call a subset $S$ of $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ \emph{mediocre} if it has the following property: Whenever $a$ and $b$ are elements of $S$ whose average is an integer, that average is also an element of $S$. Let $A(n)$ be the number of mediocre subsets of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. [For instance, every subset of $\{1,2,3\}$ except $\{1,3\}$ is mediocre, so $A(3) = 7$.] Find all positive integers $n$ such that $A(n+2) - 2A(n+1) + A(n) = 1$.
-/
theorem putnam_2009_b3
(mediocre : ℤ → Set ℤ → Prop)
(hmediocre : ∀ n S, mediocre n S ↔ (S ⊆ Icc 1 n) ∧ ∀ a ∈ S, ∀ b ∈ S, 2 ∣ a + b → (a + b) / 2 ∈ S)
(A : ℤ → ℤ)
(hA : A = fun n ↦ ({S : Set ℤ | mediocre n S}.ncard : ℤ))
: ({n : ℤ | n > 0 ∧ A (n + 2) - 2 * A (n + 1) + A n = 1} = putnam_2009_b3_solution) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2009_b3
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b3:
   characterization of the positive indices where the second difference of
   the number of average-closed subsets equals one. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith List Ensembles.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition putnam_2009_b3_mediocre
    (n : Z) (S : Ensemble Z) : Prop :=
  (forall x : Z, In Z S x -> 1 <= x <= n) /\
  forall a b q : Z,
    In Z S a ->
    In Z S b ->
    a + b = 2 * q ->
    In Z S q.

Definition putnam_2009_b3_has_integer_cardinality
    (P : Ensemble Z -> Prop) (cardinality : Z) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list (Ensemble Z),
    List.NoDup enumeration /\
    (forall S T : Ensemble Z,
      List.In S enumeration ->
      List.In T enumeration ->
      Same_set Z S T ->
      S = T) /\
    (forall S : Ensemble Z,
      P S <->
      exists T : Ensemble Z,
        List.In T enumeration /\ Same_set Z S T) /\
    cardinality = Z.of_nat (List.length enumeration).

Theorem putnam_2009_b3
    (A : Z -> Z)
    (hA :
      forall n : Z,
        putnam_2009_b3_has_integer_cardinality
          (putnam_2009_b3_mediocre n)
          (A n)) :
  forall n : Z,
    (0 < n /\
      A (n + 2) - 2 * A (n + 1) + A n = 1) <->
    exists k : nat,
      (1 <= k)%nat /\
      n = Z.of_nat (Nat.pow 2 k) - 1.
Admitted.

theory putnam_2009_b3 imports Complex_Main
begin

definition putnam_2009_b3_solution :: "nat set" where "putnam_2009_b3_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* {n::nat. (\<exists>k::nat\<ge>1. n = 2^k - 1)} *)
theorem putnam_2009_b3:
  fixes mediocre :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat set \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and A :: "nat \<Rightarrow> int"
  defines "mediocre \<equiv> (\<lambda>(n::nat)(S::nat set). S \<subseteq> {1..n} \<and> (\<forall>a\<in>S. \<forall>b\<in>S. 2 dvd (a + b) \<longrightarrow> (nat (round ((a + b)/2))) \<in> S))"
  and "A \<equiv> (\<lambda>n::nat. card {S::nat set. mediocre n S})"
  shows "{n::nat. n > 0 \<and> A (n+2) - 2*A (n+1) + A n = 1} = putnam_2009_b3_solution"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b3:
  the positive integers where the second difference of the number of
  average-closed subsets of an integer interval equals one. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let mediocre =
     \(n:int) (S:int->bool).
       S SUBSET {x:int | &1 <= x /\ x <= n} /\
       (!a b c:int.
          a IN S /\ b IN S /\ a + b = &2 * c
          ==> c IN S) in
   let A =
     \n:int. (&(CARD {S:int->bool | mediocre n S}):int) in
   {n:int |
      &0 < n /\
      A (n + &2) - &2 * A (n + &1) + A n = &1} =
   {n:int |
      ?k:num. 1 <= k /\ n = (&2:int) pow k - &1}`;;

title: putnam_2009_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b3:
;; the positive integers where the second difference of the number of
;; mediocre subsets of {1,...,n} is one are exactly 2^k-1 for k at least one.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The list (1 ... n) is a duplicate-free enumeration of the source interval.
;; Its powerset therefore contains every extensional subset exactly once.

(defun putnam-2009-b3-one-through (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (or (not (natp n))
          (zp n))
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-2009-b3-one-through (- n 1))
     (list n))))

(defun putnam-2009-b3-adjoin-to-each (element sets)
  (if (endp sets)
      nil
    (cons
     (cons element (car sets))
     (putnam-2009-b3-adjoin-to-each
      element (cdr sets)))))

(defun putnam-2009-b3-powerset (carrier)
  (if (endp carrier)
      (list nil)
    (let ((tail-powerset
           (putnam-2009-b3-powerset (cdr carrier))))
      (append
       tail-powerset
       (putnam-2009-b3-adjoin-to-each
        (car carrier) tail-powerset)))))

;; FIRST and every element of REMAINING belong to SUBSET. When their sum is
;; even, ACL2's exact rational division by two is the integer average from the
;; source statement.
(defun putnam-2009-b3-closed-with-first-p
    (first remaining subset)
  (if (endp remaining)
      t
    (and
     (implies
      (equal (mod (+ first (car remaining)) 2) 0)
      (member-equal
       (/ (+ first (car remaining)) 2)
       subset))
     (putnam-2009-b3-closed-with-first-p
      first (cdr remaining) subset))))

(defun putnam-2009-b3-mediocre-elements-p
    (remaining subset)
  (if (endp remaining)
      t
    (and
     (putnam-2009-b3-closed-with-first-p
      (car remaining) subset subset)
     (putnam-2009-b3-mediocre-elements-p
      (cdr remaining) subset))))

(defun putnam-2009-b3-mediocre-p (subset)
  (putnam-2009-b3-mediocre-elements-p subset subset))

(defun putnam-2009-b3-count-mediocre-subsets (subsets)
  (if (endp subsets)
      0
    (+
     (if (putnam-2009-b3-mediocre-p (car subsets))
         1
       0)
     (putnam-2009-b3-count-mediocre-subsets
      (cdr subsets)))))

(defun putnam-2009-b3-a (n)
  (if (natp n)
      (putnam-2009-b3-count-mediocre-subsets
       (putnam-2009-b3-powerset
        (putnam-2009-b3-one-through n)))
    0))

;; For positive n, any k>=1 satisfying n=2^k-1 also satisfies k<=n.
;; This finite search is therefore exactly the source existential quantifier.
(defun putnam-2009-b3-solution-through-k-p (n k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix k)))
  (if (or (not (integerp n))
          (not (natp k))
          (zp k))
      nil
    (or
     (equal n (- (expt 2 k) 1))
     (putnam-2009-b3-solution-through-k-p
      n (- k 1)))))

(defun putnam-2009-b3-solution-member-p (n)
  (and
   (integerp n)
   (< 0 n)
   (putnam-2009-b3-solution-through-k-p n n)))

;; The ACL2 argument N supplies the universal integer quantifier needed for
;; extensional equality of the two sets in the source theorem.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2009-b3-statement (n)
  (implies
   (integerp n)
   (iff
    (and
     (< 0 n)
     (equal
      (+
       (-
        (putnam-2009-b3-a (+ n 2))
        (* 2 (putnam-2009-b3-a (+ n 1))))
       (putnam-2009-b3-a n))
      1))
    (putnam-2009-b3-solution-member-p n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2009_b3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2009_b3): the positive indices where the
-- second difference of the number of subsets closed under integral averages
-- equals one are exactly the Mersenne numbers. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2009B3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<=Z_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data _<=Z_ : Int -> Int -> Set where
  negative<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    negsuc m <=Z pos n
  positive<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    m <=N n ->
    pos m <=Z pos n
  negative<=negative :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    n <=N m ->
    negsuc m <=Z negsuc n

data PositiveNat : Nat -> Set where
  positiveNat : {n : Nat} -> PositiveNat (suc n)

data PositiveInt : Int -> Set where
  positiveInt : {n : Nat} -> PositiveInt (pos (suc n))

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos oneN

twoZ : Int
twoZ =
  pos twoN

powerOfTwo : Nat -> Nat
powerOfTwo zero =
  oneN
powerOfTwo (suc n) =
  twoN * powerOfTwo n

predecessor : Nat -> Nat
predecessor zero =
  zero
predecessor (suc n) =
  n

Subset : Set1
Subset =
  Int -> Set

SameSubset : Subset -> Subset -> Set
SameSubset left right =
  (x : Int) ->
  Iff (left x) (right x)

InInterval : Int -> Int -> Set
InInterval upper x =
  oneZ <=Z x
  and
  x <=Z upper

SubsetOfInterval : Int -> Subset -> Set
SubsetOfInterval upper S =
  (x : Int) ->
  S x ->
  InInterval upper x

ClosedUnderIntegralAverages : Subset -> Set
ClosedUnderIntegralAverages S =
  (a b : Int) ->
  S a ->
  S b ->
  (average : Int) ->
  addInt a b == addInt average average ->
  S average

Mediocre : Int -> Subset -> Set
Mediocre n S =
  SubsetOfInterval n S
  and
  ClosedUnderIntegralAverages S

record FamilyHasCardinality
  (member : Subset -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set1 where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      Subset
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (S : Subset) ->
      member S ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index ->
          SameSubset S (enumerate index))
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      SameSubset
        (enumerate left-index)
        (enumerate right-index) ->
      left-index == right-index

record CountedBy
  (member : Subset -> Set)
  (count : Int) :
  Set1 where

  field
    magnitude :
      Nat
    count-is-magnitude :
      count == pos magnitude
    has-cardinality :
      FamilyHasCardinality member magnitude

CountsMediocreSubsets : (Int -> Int) -> Set1
CountsMediocreSubsets A =
  (n : Int) ->
  CountedBy (Mediocre n) (A n)

secondDifference : (Int -> Int) -> Int -> Int
secondDifference A n =
  addInt
    (addInt
      (A (addInt n twoZ))
      (negateInt
        (multiplyInt
          twoZ
          (A (addInt n oneZ)))))
    (A n)

QualifyingIndex : (Int -> Int) -> Int -> Set
QualifyingIndex A n =
  PositiveInt n
  and
  secondDifference A n == oneZ

MersenneNumber : Int -> Set
MersenneNumber n =
  Exists Nat
    (\ exponent ->
      PositiveNat exponent
      and
      n == pos (predecessor (powerOfTwo exponent)))

SameIntegerSet :
  (Int -> Set) ->
  (Int -> Set) ->
  Set
SameIntegerSet left right =
  (n : Int) ->
  Iff (left n) (right n)

putnam-2009-b3 : Set1
putnam-2009-b3 =
  (A : Int -> Int) ->
  CountsMediocreSubsets A ->
  SameIntegerSet
    (QualifyingIndex A)
    MersenneNumber

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b3:
  the positive indices where the count of average-closed subsets has second
  finite difference one are exactly one less than positive powers of two.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2009_b3 =
  ``let mediocre =
      \n : num.
      \S : num set.
        S SUBSET {m : num | 1 <= m /\ m <= n} /\
        !a b : num.
          a IN S /\ b IN S /\ EVEN (a + b)
          ==>
          (a + b) DIV 2 IN S

    let A =

          (CARD {s : num set | mediocre n s})

      {n : num |
         0 < n /\
         A (n + 2) - 2 * A (n + 1) + A n = 1} =
      {n : num |
         ?k : num.
           1 <= k /\ n = 2 EXP k - 1}``;

            |

${
