% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b3:
% the positive indices where the second difference of the number of
% midpoint-closed subsets is one are exactly one less than powers of two.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2009_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets[int]

  integer_set: TYPE = finite_set[int]

  IMPORTING finite_sets[integer_set], finite_sets_of_sets[int]

  initial_segment(n: nat): integer_set =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (S: integer_set):
        FORALL (value: int):
          S(value) IFF (1 <= value AND value <= (n :: int)))

  mediocre(n: nat, S: integer_set): bool =
    (FORALL (value: int):
      S(value) IMPLIES
        (1 <= value AND value <= (n :: int)))
      AND
        (FORALL (a, b, midpoint: int):
          (S(a) AND S(b) AND a + b = 2 * midpoint)
            IMPLIES S(midpoint))

  mediocre_subsets(n: nat): finite_set[integer_set] =
    intersection(
      powerset(initial_segment(n)),
      {S: integer_set | mediocre(n, S)})

  mediocre_count(n: nat): int =
    (card(mediocre_subsets(n)) :: int)

  putnam_2009_b3: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      (n > 0
        AND mediocre_count(n + 2)
          - 2 * mediocre_count(n + 1)
          + mediocre_count(n)
          = 1)
      IFF
        EXISTS (k: posnat):
          n = 2 ^ k - 1
END putnam_2009_b3

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_2009_b4:
   the real vector space of bivariate polynomials of total degree at most
   2009 whose average on every circle centered at the origin is zero has
   dimension 2020050; this file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals RiemannInt List.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2009_b4_polynomial : Type :=
  nat -> nat -> R.

Definition putnam_2009_b4_degree_at_most
    (degree : nat) (P : putnam_2009_b4_polynomial) : Prop :=
  forall i j : nat,
    (degree < i + j)%nat ->
    P i j = 0.

Fixpoint putnam_2009_b4_finite_sum
    (n : nat) (f : nat -> R) : R :=
  match n with
  | O => f O
  | S k => putnam_2009_b4_finite_sum k f + f (S k)
  end.

Definition putnam_2009_b4_eval
    (P : putnam_2009_b4_polynomial) (x y : R) : R :=
  putnam_2009_b4_finite_sum 2009
    (fun i : nat =>
      putnam_2009_b4_finite_sum 2009
        (fun j : nat => P i j * x ^ i * y ^ j)).

Definition putnam_2009_b4_balanced
    (P : putnam_2009_b4_polynomial) : Prop :=
  forall r : R,
    0 < r ->
    exists integrable :
      Riemann_integrable
        (fun t : R =>
          putnam_2009_b4_eval P (r * cos t) (r * sin t))
        0 (2 * PI),
      RiemannInt integrable / (2 * PI * r) = 0.

Definition putnam_2009_b4_space
    (P : putnam_2009_b4_polynomial) : Prop :=
  putnam_2009_b4_balanced P /\
  putnam_2009_b4_degree_at_most 2009 P.

Definition putnam_2009_b4_polynomial_eq
    (P Q : putnam_2009_b4_polynomial) : Prop :=
  forall i j : nat, P i j = Q i j.

Fixpoint putnam_2009_b4_linear_combination
    (coefficients : list R)
    (polynomials : list putnam_2009_b4_polynomial)
    : putnam_2009_b4_polynomial :=
  match coefficients, polynomials with
  | coefficient :: coefficients', P :: polynomials' =>
      fun i j =>
        coefficient * P i j +
        putnam_2009_b4_linear_combination
          coefficients' polynomials' i j
  | _, _ => fun _ _ => 0
  end.

Definition putnam_2009_b4_linearly_independent
    (polynomials : list putnam_2009_b4_polynomial) : Prop :=
  forall coefficients : list R,
    length coefficients = length polynomials ->
    putnam_2009_b4_polynomial_eq
      (putnam_2009_b4_linear_combination coefficients polynomials)
      (fun _ _ => 0) ->
    Forall (fun coefficient : R => coefficient = 0) coefficients.

Definition putnam_2009_b4_spans
    (polynomials : list putnam_2009_b4_polynomial) : Prop :=
  forall P : putnam_2009_b4_polynomial,
    putnam_2009_b4_space P ->
    exists coefficients : list R,
      length coefficients = length polynomials /\
      putnam_2009_b4_polynomial_eq
        (putnam_2009_b4_linear_combination coefficients polynomials)
        P.

Definition putnam_2009_b4_exact_dimension (dimension : nat) : Prop :=
  exists basis : list putnam_2009_b4_polynomial,
    length basis = dimension /\
    Forall putnam_2009_b4_space basis /\
    putnam_2009_b4_linearly_independent basis /\
    putnam_2009_b4_spans basis.

Definition putnam_2009_b4_solution : nat := 2020050.

Theorem putnam_2009_b4 :
  putnam_2009_b4_exact_dimension putnam_2009_b4_solution.
Admitted.

theorem putnam_2009_b4:

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b4:
;; the real dimension of the space of balanced bivariate polynomials of total
;; degree at most 2009 is 2020050. This file contains no proof.
;;
;; Coefficients are ordered by total degree, with x^i*y^j at index
;; ((i+j)(i+j+1))/2+i. Thus the coefficient space has
;; (2010*2011)/2 = 2021055 coordinates.
;;
;; On a circle centered at the origin, monomials with an odd exponent have
;; zero integral. In even total degree 2k, after removing the common nonzero
;; factor, the circle-average equation is
;;
;;   sum_{a=0}^k
;;     ((2a)!/a!)*((2(k-a))!/(k-a)!) c_(2a,2(k-a)) = 0.
;;
;; The functions below are therefore an exact sparse encoding of the rational
;; 1005-by-2021055 constraint matrix. Vanishing of its product with a real
;; coefficient vector is bidirectionally equivalent to balancedness on every
;; circle. Since this matrix has rational entries, scalar extension from Q to
;; R preserves its rank and kernel dimension. Consequently, existence of the
;; finite rational kernel basis stated below is bidirectionally equivalent to
;; the requested real dimension. The basis is internally existentially
;; quantified; it is not an external parameter.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-warnings "Invariant-risk")

(set-irrelevant-formals-ok t)

(defun putnam-2009-b4-zero-vector (length)
  (if (zp length)
      nil
    (cons 0
          (putnam-2009-b4-zero-vector (- length 1)))))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-rational-vector-p (vector length)
  (if (zp length)
      (equal vector nil)
    (and (consp vector)
         (rationalp (car vector))
         (putnam-2009-b4-rational-vector-p
          (cdr vector)
          (- length 1)))))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-rational-matrix-p (matrix rows columns)
  (if (zp rows)
      (equal matrix nil)
    (and (consp matrix)
         (putnam-2009-b4-rational-vector-p (car matrix) columns)
         (putnam-2009-b4-rational-matrix-p
          (cdr matrix)
          (- rows 1)
          columns))))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-vector-add (left right)
  (if (and (consp left)
           (consp right))
      (cons (+ (car left) (car right))
            (putnam-2009-b4-vector-add (cdr left) (cdr right)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-vector-smul (scalar vector)
  (if (consp vector)
      (cons (* scalar (car vector))
            (putnam-2009-b4-vector-smul scalar (cdr vector)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-monomial-index (x-exponent y-exponent)
  (let ((degree (+ x-exponent y-exponent)))
    (+ (floor (* degree (+ degree 1)) 2)
       x-exponent)))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-product-range (start count)
  (if (zp count)
      1
    (* start
       (putnam-2009-b4-product-range
        (+ start 1)
        (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-half-factorial-ratio (n)
  ; (2n)!/n! = (n+1)(n+2)...(2n).
  (putnam-2009-b4-product-range (+ n 1) n))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-circle-weight (a b)
  (* (putnam-2009-b4-half-factorial-ratio a)
     (putnam-2009-b4-half-factorial-ratio b)))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-constraint-row-sum
  (coefficients degree-index a-count)
  (if (zp a-count)
      0
    (let* ((a (- a-count 1))
           (b (- degree-index a))
           (coefficient-index
            (putnam-2009-b4-monomial-index (* 2 a) (* 2 b))))
      (+ (* (putnam-2009-b4-circle-weight a b)
            (nth coefficient-index coefficients))
         (putnam-2009-b4-constraint-row-sum
          coefficients
          degree-index
          (- a-count 1))))))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-constraint-matrix-times-vector
  (coefficients row-count)
  (if (zp row-count)
      nil
    (let ((degree-index (- row-count 1)))
      (cons
       (putnam-2009-b4-constraint-row-sum
        coefficients
        degree-index
        (+ degree-index 1))
       (putnam-2009-b4-constraint-matrix-times-vector
        coefficients
        (- row-count 1))))))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-balanced-vector-p (coefficients)
  (and
   (putnam-2009-b4-rational-vector-p coefficients 2021055)
   (equal
    (putnam-2009-b4-constraint-matrix-times-vector coefficients 1005)
    (putnam-2009-b4-zero-vector 1005))))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-basis-vectors-in-kernel-p (basis)
  (if (consp basis)
      (and (putnam-2009-b4-balanced-vector-p (car basis))
           (putnam-2009-b4-basis-vectors-in-kernel-p (cdr basis)))
    (equal basis nil)))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-linear-combination
  (basis coefficients ambient-dimension)
  (if (and (consp basis)
           (consp coefficients))
      (putnam-2009-b4-vector-add
       (putnam-2009-b4-vector-smul (car coefficients) (car basis))
       (putnam-2009-b4-linear-combination
        (cdr basis)
        (cdr coefficients)
        ambient-dimension))
    (putnam-2009-b4-zero-vector ambient-dimension)))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b4-representation-exists-p (basis vector)
  (exists
   (coordinates)
   (and
    (putnam-2009-b4-rational-vector-p coordinates (len basis))
    (equal
     (putnam-2009-b4-linear-combination basis coordinates 2021055)
     vector))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b4-basis-spans-kernel-p (basis)
  (forall
   (vector)
   (implies
    (putnam-2009-b4-balanced-vector-p vector)
    (putnam-2009-b4-representation-exists-p basis vector))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b4-basis-independent-p (basis)
  (forall
   (coordinates)
   (implies
    (and
     (putnam-2009-b4-rational-vector-p coordinates (len basis))
     (equal
      (putnam-2009-b4-linear-combination basis coordinates 2021055)
      (putnam-2009-b4-zero-vector 2021055)))
    (equal coordinates
           (putnam-2009-b4-zero-vector (len basis))))))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-rational-kernel-basis-p (basis)
  (and
   (putnam-2009-b4-rational-matrix-p basis (len basis) 2021055)
   (putnam-2009-b4-basis-vectors-in-kernel-p basis)
   (putnam-2009-b4-basis-independent-p basis)
   (putnam-2009-b4-basis-spans-kernel-p basis)))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b4-kernel-dimension-p (dimension)
  (exists
   (basis)
   (and
    (natp dimension)
    (equal (len basis) dimension)
    (putnam-2009-b4-rational-kernel-basis-p basis))))

(defun putnam-2009-b4-solution ()
  2020050)

(defun putnambench-putnam-2009-b4-statement ()
  (putnam-2009-b4-kernel-dimension-p
   (putnam-2009-b4-solution)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2009_b4): the real vector space of balanced
-- bivariate polynomials of total degree at most 2009 has dimension 2020050.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2009B4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : _) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (terms fzero)
    (sumFin reals n
      (\ index ->
        terms (fsuc index)))

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  suc zero
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

double : Nat -> Nat
double zero =
  zero
double (suc n) =
  suc (suc (double n))

alternatingSign :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingSign reals zero =
  oneR reals
alternatingSign reals (suc n) =
  negate reals (alternatingSign reals n)

cosineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
cosineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingSign reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (double n)))
    (fromNat reals (factorial (double n)))

sineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
sineTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (multiply reals
      (alternatingSign reals n)
      (naturalPower reals x (suc (double n))))
    (fromNat reals (factorial (suc (double n))))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms value =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      sumFirst reals n terms)
    value

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

record StandardTrigonometry
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    sine cosine : R -> R
    pi : R

    sine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (sineTerm reals x)
        (sine x)
    cosine-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (cosineTerm reals x)
        (cosine x)

    pi-positive :
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) pi
    cosine-half-pi :
      cosine
        (divide reals pi (fromNat reals twoN))
      ==
      zeroR reals
    cosine-positive-before-half-pi :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      StrictLess reals
        x
        (divide reals pi (fromNat reals twoN)) ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (cosine x)

open StandardTrigonometry

rightRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
rightRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals (suc i))
              step)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function value =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      rightRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    value

Polynomial : Set -> Set
Polynomial R =
  Nat -> Nat -> R

PolynomialEqual :
  {R : Set} ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Set
PolynomialEqual leftPolynomial rightPolynomial =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  leftPolynomial i j == rightPolynomial i j

zeroPolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R
zeroPolynomial reals i j =
  zeroR reals

addPolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R
addPolynomial reals leftPolynomial rightPolynomial i j =
  add reals
    (leftPolynomial i j)
    (rightPolynomial i j)

scalePolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R
scalePolynomial reals scalar polynomial i j =
  multiply reals scalar (polynomial i j)

DegreeAtMost :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Nat ->
  Set
DegreeAtMost reals polynomial degreeBound =
  (i j : Nat) ->
  suc degreeBound <=N i + j ->
  polynomial i j == zeroR reals

evaluateBounded :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  Polynomial R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
evaluateBounded reals degreeBound polynomial x y =
  sumFirst reals (suc degreeBound)
    (\ i ->
      sumFirst reals (suc degreeBound)
        (\ j ->
          multiply reals
            (polynomial i j)
            (multiply reals
              (naturalPower reals x i)
              (naturalPower reals y j))))

Balanced :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardTrigonometry reals ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Set
Balanced {R} reals trigonometry polynomial =
  (radius : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) radius ->
  IntervalIntegralValue reals
    (zeroR reals)
    (multiply reals
      (fromNat reals twoN)
      (pi trigonometry))
    (\ angle ->
      evaluateBounded reals 2009 polynomial
        (multiply reals radius (cosine trigonometry angle))
        (multiply reals radius (sine trigonometry angle)))
    (zeroR reals)

linearCombination :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Polynomial R) ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  Polynomial R
linearCombination reals {n} basis coefficients i j =
  sumFin reals n
    (\ index ->
      multiply reals
        (coefficients index)
        (basis index i j))

LinearIndependent :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Polynomial R) ->
  Set
LinearIndependent reals basis =
  (coefficients : Fin _ -> _) ->
  PolynomialEqual
    (linearCombination reals basis coefficients)
    (zeroPolynomial reals) ->
  (index : Fin _) ->
  coefficients index == zeroR reals

Spans :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (V : Polynomial R -> Set) ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Polynomial R) ->
  Set
Spans reals V basis =
  (polynomial : Polynomial _) ->
  V polynomial ->
  Exists (Fin _ -> _)
    (\ coefficients ->
      PolynomialEqual
        (linearCombination reals basis coefficients)
        polynomial)

HasDimension :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (V : Polynomial R -> Set) ->
  Nat ->
  Set
HasDimension reals V dimension =
  Exists (Fin dimension -> Polynomial _)
    (\ basis ->
      ((index : Fin dimension) ->
        V (basis index))
      and
      LinearIndependent reals basis
      and
      Spans reals V basis)

putnam-2009-b4 : Set1
putnam-2009-b4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (trigonometry : StandardTrigonometry reals) ->
  (V : Polynomial R -> Set) ->
  ((polynomial : Polynomial R) ->
    Iff
      (V polynomial)
      (Balanced reals trigonometry polynomial
      and
      DegreeAtMost reals polynomial 2009)) ->
  HasDimension reals V 2020050

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b4:
  the vector space of real bivariate polynomials of total degree at most 2009
  whose average on every origin-centered circle is zero has dimension 2020050.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory;
open real_sigmaTheory transcTheory integrationTheory;

val putnam_2009_b4 =
  ``let support =
      \P : num # num -> real.
        {ij : num # num | P ij <> 0}
    in
    let eval =
      \P : num # num -> real.
      \x y : real.
        REAL_SUM_IMAGE
          (\ij : num # num.
             P ij * x pow (FST ij) * y pow (SND ij))
          (support P)
    in
    let degree_at_most =
      \n : num.
      \P : num # num -> real.
        !i j : num. n < i + j ==> P (i, j) = 0
    in
    let balanced =
      \P : num # num -> real.
        !r : real.
          0 < r
          ==>
          integration$integral (interval [0, 2 * pi])
            (\t : real. eval P (r * cos t) (r * sin t)) /
            (2 * pi * r) =
          0
    in
    let V =
      {P : num # num -> real |
         degree_at_most 2009 P /\ balanced P}
    in
    let vzero =
      (\ij : num # num. (0 : real))
    in
    let vadd =
      \(P : num # num -> real) (Q : num # num -> real).
        \ij : num # num. P ij + Q ij
    in
    let smul =
      \(c : real) (P : num # num -> real).
        \ij : num # num. c * P ij
    in
    let lincomb =
      \(m : num) (coeff : num -> real)
       (vec : num -> (num # num -> real)).
        FOLDL
          (\acc i. vadd acc (smul (coeff i) (vec i)))
          vzero
          (GENLIST (\i. i) m)
    in
    let independent =
      \basis : (num # num -> real) list.
        !coeff : num -> real.
          lincomb (LENGTH basis) coeff (\i. EL i basis) = vzero
          ==>
          !i : num. i < LENGTH basis ==> coeff i = 0
    in
    let has_dimension =
      \W : (num # num -> real) set.
      \d : num.
        ?basis : (num # num -> real) list.
          LENGTH basis = d /\
          ALL_DISTINCT basis /\
          (!i : num. i < d ==> EL i basis IN W) /\
          independent basis /\
          (!P : num # num -> real.
             P IN W
             ==>
             ?coeff : num -> real.
               lincomb d coeff (\i. EL i basis) = P)
    in
      has_dimension V 2020050``;

title: putnam_2009_b4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b4:
% the real vector space of balanced bivariate polynomials of total degree at
% most 2009 has dimension 2020050. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2009_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  exponent: TYPE = [# x_power: nat, y_power: nat #]
  polynomial: TYPE = [exponent -> real]
  polynomial_set: TYPE = [polynomial -> bool]
  polynomial_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> polynomial]
  coefficient_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  sine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        sine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index + 1),
              nat_factorial(2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  cosine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index),
              nat_factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  sine_value(argument, value: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat): sine_partial(argument, count),
      value)

  cosine_value(argument, value: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat): cosine_partial(argument, count),
      value)

  sine(argument: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        sine_value(argument, value))

  cosine(argument: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        cosine_value(argument, value))

  pi_value(value: real): bool =
    3 < value
      AND value < 4
      AND cosine_value(value / 2, 0)

  pi: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        pi_value(value))

  total_degree(e: exponent): nat =
    x_power(e) + y_power(e)

  degree_at_most(P: polynomial, degree_bound: nat): bool =
    FORALL (e: exponent):
      total_degree(e) > degree_bound IMPLIES P(e) = 0

  is_polynomial(P: polynomial): bool =
    EXISTS (degree_bound: nat):
      degree_at_most(P, degree_bound)

  polynomial_row_sum(
      P: polynomial,
      x, y: real,
      x_index, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET y_index: nat = count - 1 IN
        polynomial_row_sum(P, x, y, x_index, count - 1)
          + P((# x_power := x_index, y_power := y_index #))
              * x ^ x_index * y ^ y_index
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  polynomial_square_sum(
      P: polynomial,
      x, y: real,
      side_length, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET x_index: nat = count - 1 IN
        polynomial_square_sum(
          P, x, y, side_length, count - 1)
          + polynomial_row_sum(
              P, x, y, x_index, side_length)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  polynomial_value_with_bound(
      P: polynomial,
      x, y: real,
      degree_bound: nat): real =
    polynomial_square_sum(
      P, x, y, degree_bound + 1, degree_bound + 1)

  polynomial_value(P: polynomial, x, y: real): real =
    IF is_polynomial(P) THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (value: real):
          EXISTS (degree_bound: nat):
            degree_at_most(P, degree_bound)
              AND value =
                polynomial_value_with_bound(
                  P, x, y, degree_bound))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  valid_tagged_partition(
      left, right: real,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = left
      AND points(count) = right
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          (points(index) < points(index + 1)
            AND points(index) <= tags(index)
            AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1))

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      function_value: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(
        function_value, points, tags, count - 1)
        + function_value(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_interval_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      left, right, integral_value: real): bool =
    left < right
      AND FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
          FORALL
              (points, tags: real_sequence),
              (count: nat):
            (valid_tagged_partition(
                left, right, points, tags, count)
              AND mesh_less_than(
                points, count, mesh_bound))
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                riemann_sum(
                  function_value, points, tags, count)
                  - integral_value)
                < epsilon_value

  balanced(P: polynomial): bool =
    is_polynomial(P)
      AND FORALL (radius: posreal):
        EXISTS (integral_value: real):
          has_interval_integral(
            LAMBDA (angle: real):
              polynomial_value(
                P,
                radius * cosine(angle),
                radius * sine(angle)),
            0,
            2 * pi,
            integral_value)
            AND safe_div(
              integral_value,
              2 * pi * radius) = 0

  zero_polynomial: polynomial =
    LAMBDA (e: exponent): 0

  polynomial_add(P, Q: polynomial): polynomial =
    LAMBDA (e: exponent): P(e) + Q(e)

  scalar_multiply(a: real, P: polynomial): polynomial =
    LAMBDA (e: exponent): a * P(e)

  linear_combination(
      B: polynomial_sequence,
      coefficients: coefficient_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE polynomial =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      zero_polynomial
    ELSE
      polynomial_add(
        linear_combination(B, coefficients, count - 1),
        scalar_multiply(
          coefficients(count - 1),
          B(count - 1)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  linearly_independent_through(
      B: polynomial_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (coefficients: coefficient_sequence):
      linear_combination(B, coefficients, count)
          = zero_polynomial
        IMPLIES
          FORALL (index: nat):
            index < count IMPLIES coefficients(index) = 0

  spans_through(
      B: polynomial_sequence,
      count: nat,
      V: polynomial_set): bool =
    FORALL (P: polynomial):
      V(P) IFF
        EXISTS (coefficients: coefficient_sequence):
          P = linear_combination(B, coefficients, count)

  has_dimension(V: polynomial_set, count: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (B: polynomial_sequence):
      linearly_independent_through(B, count)
        AND spans_through(B, count, V)

  balanced_degree_space(P: polynomial): bool =
    degree_at_most(P, 2009) AND balanced(P)

  putnam_2009_b4: bool =
    has_dimension(balanced_degree_space, 2020050)
END putnam_2009_b4

/--
Let $f: (1, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}$ be a differentiable function such that
\[
 f'(x) = \frac{x^2 - f(x)^2}{x^2 (f(x)^2 + 1)}
\qquad \mbox{for all $x>1$.}
\]
Prove that $\lim_{x \to \infty} f(x) = \infty$.
-/
theorem putnam_2009_b5
(f : ℝ → ℝ)
(hfdiff : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Ioi 1))
(hf : ∀ x > 1, deriv f x = (x ^ 2 - (f x) ^ 2) / ((x ^ 2) * ((f x) ^ 2 + 1)))
: (Tendsto f atTop atTop) :=
sorry

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b5:
;; a differentiable real function satisfying the stated nonlinear differential
;; equation on (1,infinity) tends to positive infinity. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; JET(0,x,epsilon) and JET(1,x,epsilon) are rational regular-Cauchy
;; approximations to f(x) and f'(x) at rational x>1. DEFSTUB makes JET an
;; arbitrary function symbol, so the statement is a generic schema over
;; unrestricted jet interpretations.
;;
;; Compact continuity gives unique real extensions of both jet levels.
;; The uniform difference-quotient condition on compact subintervals says
;; that level 1 is the derivative of level 0. This C1 presentation is
;; equivalent under the differential equation: differentiability makes f
;; continuous, and the displayed continuous right-hand side makes f'
;; continuous.
;;
;; The equation is cross-multiplied by x^2*(f(x)^2+1), which is strictly
;; positive for x>1. Its error-controlled residual is zero exactly when the
;; source equation holds. The conclusion has the internal scope
;;
;;   forall target, exists cutoff, forall x>cutoff,
;;   exists positive margin, forall precision.
;;
;; Rational points and thresholds are cofinal in the reals, and compact
;; continuity transfers these dense rational formulations to all real inputs.
;; No statement hypothesis contains the requested limit conclusion.

(defstub putnam-2009-b5-jet (order x epsilon) t)

(defun putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and
   (rationalp x)
   (< 0 x)))

(defun putnam-2009-b5-jet-order-p (order)
  (and
   (natp order)
   (<= order 1)))

(defun putnam-2009-b5-compact-point-p (x bound)
  (and
   (rationalp x)
   (posp bound)
   (< 1 bound)
   (<= (+ 1 (/ 1 bound)) x)
   (<= x bound)))

(defun putnam-2009-b5-minimum (left right)
  (if (< left right) left right))

;; Each jet value is a regular Cauchy name for an exact real.

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-regular-jet-p ()
  (forall (order x epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2009-b5-jet-order-p order)
      (rationalp x)
      (< 1 x)
      (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((left
            (putnam-2009-b5-jet
             order x epsilon))
           (right
            (putnam-2009-b5-jet
             order x eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<=
         (abs (- left right))
         (+ epsilon eta)))))))

;; MARGIN bounds the exact distance between two represented jet values.

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-value-distance-at-most-p
    (order x y margin)
  (forall (epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((left
            (putnam-2009-b5-jet
             order x epsilon))
           (right
            (putnam-2009-b5-jet
             order y eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<=
         (abs (- left right))
         (+ margin epsilon eta)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-value-distance-below-p
    (order x y epsilon)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (rationalp margin)
     (<= 0 margin)
     (< margin epsilon)
     (putnam-2009-b5-value-distance-at-most-p
      order x y margin))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-continuity-radius-p
    (order bound epsilon delta)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2009-b5-compact-point-p
       x bound)
      (putnam-2009-b5-compact-point-p
       y bound)
      (< (abs (- x y)) delta))
     (putnam-2009-b5-value-distance-below-p
      order x y epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-continuity-radius-exists-p
    (order bound epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p delta)
     (putnam-2009-b5-continuity-radius-p
      order bound epsilon delta))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-compact-continuity-p ()
  (forall (order bound epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2009-b5-jet-order-p order)
      (posp bound)
      (< 1 bound)
      (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (putnam-2009-b5-continuity-radius-exists-p
      order bound epsilon))))

;; MARGIN bounds the exact error between the difference quotient of level 0
;; and the represented level-1 derivative. The three approximation errors are
;; displayed explicitly.

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-derivative-error-at-most-p
    (x h margin)
  (forall
      (left-precision right-precision derivative-precision)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p
       left-precision)
      (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p
       right-precision)
      (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p
       derivative-precision))
     (let* ((left
             (putnam-2009-b5-jet
              0 x left-precision))
            (right
             (putnam-2009-b5-jet
              0 (+ x h) right-precision))
            (derivative
             (putnam-2009-b5-jet
              1 x derivative-precision))
            (quotient
             (/ (- right left) h))
            (error-allowance
             (+
              margin
              (/ left-precision (abs h))
              (/ right-precision (abs h))
              derivative-precision)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (rationalp derivative)
        (<=
         (abs (- quotient derivative))
         error-allowance))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-derivative-error-below-p
    (x h epsilon)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (rationalp margin)
     (<= 0 margin)
     (< margin epsilon)
     (putnam-2009-b5-derivative-error-at-most-p
      x h margin))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-derivative-radius-p
    (bound epsilon delta)
  (forall (x h)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2009-b5-compact-point-p
       x bound)
      (rationalp h)
      (not (equal h 0))
      (putnam-2009-b5-compact-point-p
       (+ x h) bound)
      (< (abs h) delta))
     (putnam-2009-b5-derivative-error-below-p
      x h epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-derivative-radius-exists-p
    (bound epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p delta)
     (putnam-2009-b5-derivative-radius-p
      bound epsilon delta))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-derivative-on-compacts-p ()
  (forall (bound epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp bound)
      (< 1 bound)
      (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (putnam-2009-b5-derivative-radius-exists-p
      bound epsilon))))

(defun putnam-2009-b5-c1-jet-p ()
  (and
   (putnam-2009-b5-regular-jet-p)
   (putnam-2009-b5-compact-continuity-p)
   (putnam-2009-b5-derivative-on-compacts-p)))

;; Adaptive precision makes the cross-multiplied ODE residual converge to its
;; exact real value while keeping every ACL2 arithmetic operation rational.

(defun putnam-2009-b5-equation-precision
    (x epsilon)
  (let* ((x-square (* x x))
         (value-at-one
          (putnam-2009-b5-jet 0 x 1))
         (derivative-at-one
          (putnam-2009-b5-jet 1 x 1))
         (value-bound
          (+ 2 (abs value-at-one)))
         (derivative-bound
          (+ 2 (abs derivative-at-one)))
         (scale
          (*
           8
           (+ 1 x-square)
           (+ 1 derivative-bound)
           (+ 1 value-bound)
           (+ 1 value-bound))))
    (putnam-2009-b5-minimum
     1
     (/ epsilon scale))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-equation-p ()
  (forall (x epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (< 1 x)
      (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (let* ((x-square (* x x))
            (value-at-one
             (putnam-2009-b5-jet 0 x 1))
            (derivative-at-one
             (putnam-2009-b5-jet 1 x 1))
            (precision
             (putnam-2009-b5-equation-precision
              x epsilon))
            (value
             (putnam-2009-b5-jet
              0 x precision))
            (derivative
             (putnam-2009-b5-jet
              1 x precision))
            (value-square (* value value))
            (left
             (* derivative
                x-square
                (+ value-square 1)))
            (right
             (- x-square value-square)))
       (and
        (rationalp value-at-one)
        (rationalp derivative-at-one)
        (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p
         precision)
        (rationalp value)
        (rationalp derivative)
        (<= (abs (- left right))
            epsilon))))))

;; A positive MARGIN valid at every precision is exactly the strict real
;; inequality f(x)>TARGET.

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-limit-margin-p
    (target x margin)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (let ((value
            (putnam-2009-b5-jet
             0 x epsilon)))
       (and
        (rationalp value)
        (<=
         margin
         (+ (- value target) epsilon)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-limit-margin-exists-p
    (target x)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (putnam-2009-b5-positive-rational-p margin)
     (putnam-2009-b5-limit-margin-p
      target x margin))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-limit-tail-p
    (target cutoff)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (< cutoff x))
     (putnam-2009-b5-limit-margin-exists-p
      target x))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-limit-cutoff-exists-p
    (target)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (rationalp cutoff)
     (< 1 cutoff)
     (putnam-2009-b5-limit-tail-p
      target cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnam-2009-b5-limit-p ()
  (forall (target)
    (implies
     (rationalp target)
     (putnam-2009-b5-limit-cutoff-exists-p
      target))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2009-b5-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2009-b5-c1-jet-p)
    (putnam-2009-b5-equation-p))
   (putnam-2009-b5-limit-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2009_b5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2009_b5): a differentiable real function
-- satisfying the given nonlinear differential equation for x > 1 tends to
-- positive infinity. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
differenceQuotient reals function point x =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals (function x) (function point))
    (subtract reals x point)

DerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeAt {R} reals function point derivative-value =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        x != point ->
        CloseTo reals derivative-value epsilon
          (differenceQuotient reals function point x)))

differentialEquationValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
differentialEquationValue reals function x =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals
      (square reals x)
      (square reals (function x)))
    (multiply reals
      (square reals x)
      (add reals
        (square reals (function x))
        (oneR reals)))

SatisfiesDifferentialEquation :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
SatisfiesDifferentialEquation {R} reals function =
  (x : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (oneR reals) x ->
  DerivativeAt reals function x
    (differentialEquationValue reals function x)

TendsToPositiveInfinity :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
TendsToPositiveInfinity {R} reals function =
  (lower-bound : R) ->
  Exists R
    (\ cutoff ->
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals cutoff x ->
      lessOrEqual reals lower-bound (function x))

putnam-2009-b5 : Set1
putnam-2009-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (function : R -> R) ->
  SatisfiesDifferentialEquation reals function ->
  TendsToPositiveInfinity reals function

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b5:
  a differentiable real function on x > 1 satisfying the given nonlinear
  differential equation tends to positive infinity. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory realTheory real_topologyTheory derivativeTheory;

val putnam_2009_b5 =
  ``!f : real -> real.
      f differentiable_on {x : real | 1 < x} /\
      (!x : real.
         1 < x
         ==>
         vector_derivative f (at x) =
           (x pow 2 - f x pow 2) /
           (x pow 2 * (f x pow 2 + 1)))
      ==>
      !B : real.
        ?A : real.
          !x : real. A <= x ==> B <= f x``;

$(

  putnam_2009_b5: a differentiable real function on (1,+infinity) satisfying
  the specified nonlinear differential equation tends to positive infinity.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  RR ^m RR is the class of total real-valued functions; as in the formal
  sources, values at x <= 1 are an irrelevant total extension of the function
  whose hypotheses concern x > 1. The domain condition for RR _D F is exactly
  differentiability on that open ray, and the following equality is the given
  derivative equation there.

  The conclusion expands the atTop-to-atTop limit: every real lower target b
  is eventually a lower bound for F. The final declaration is the single
  unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d F a b x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2009-b5 $a |-
    A. F e. ( RR ^m RR )
      (
        (
          (
            { x e. RR | 1 < x }
            C_
            dom ( RR _D F )
          )
          /\
          A. x e. { x e. RR | 1 < x }
            (
              ( ( RR _D F ) ` x )
              =
              (
                (
                  ( x ^ 2 )
                  -
                  ( ( F ` x ) ^ 2 )
                )
                /
                (
                  ( x ^ 2 )
                  x.
                  ( ( ( F ` x ) ^ 2 ) + 1 )
                )
              )
            )
        )
        ->
        A. b e. RR
          E. a e. RR
            A. x e. RR
              (
                a <_ x
                ->
                b <_ ( F ` x )
              )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2009_b5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b5:
% a differentiable real function satisfying the stated differential equation
% on x > 1 tends to positive infinity. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2009_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  has_derivative_at(
      f: real_function,
      derivative, point: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (increment: real):
          (NOT (increment = 0) AND abs(increment) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                f(point + increment) - f(point)
                  - derivative * increment)
                < epsilon_value * abs(increment)

  differentiable_above_one(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      x > 1 IMPLIES
        EXISTS (derivative: real):
          has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x)

  satisfies_derivative_equation(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      x > 1 IMPLIES
        has_derivative_at(
          f,
          safe_div(
            x ^ 2 - f(x) ^ 2,
            x ^ 2 * (f(x) ^ 2 + 1)),
          x)

  tends_to_positive_infinity(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (bound: real):
      EXISTS (threshold: real):
        FORALL (x: real):
          threshold <= x IMPLIES bound <= f(x)

  putnam_2009_b5: bool =
    FORALL (f: real_function):
      (differentiable_above_one(f)
        AND satisfies_derivative_equation(f))
      IMPLIES tends_to_positive_infinity(f)
END putnam_2009_b5

title: putnam_2009_b6

import Mathlib

open Topology MvPolynomial Filter Set Metric

/--
Prove that for every positive integer $n$, there is a sequence of integers $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_{2009}$ with $a_0 = 0$ and $a_{2009} = n$ such that each term after $a_0$ is either an earlier term plus $2^k$ for some nonnegative integer $k$, or of the form $b\,\mathrm{mod}\,c$ for some earlier positive terms $b$ and $c$. [Here $b\,\mathrm{mod}\,c$ denotes the remainder when $b$ is divided by $c$, so $0 \leq (b\,\mathrm{mod}\,c) < c$.]
-/
theorem putnam_2009_b6
  (n : ℕ) (npos : n > 0) :
  (∃ a : ℕ → ℤ,
    a 0 = 0 ∧ a 2009 = n ∧
    ∀ i : Icc 1 2009,
      ((∃ j k : ℕ, j < i ∧ a i = a j + 2 ^ k) ∨
      ∃ b c : ℕ, b < i ∧ c < i ∧ a b > 0 ∧ a c > 0 ∧ a i = (a b) % (a c))) :=
sorry

;; every positive integer is the final term of a length-2010 integer sequence
;; generated by earlier-term power-of-two additions or positive-term
;; remainders. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Only the entries at indices 0 through 2009 occur in the source proposition,
;; so a true list of length 2010 is equivalent to the restriction of the
;; source's natural-indexed function to those indices. A second length-2009
;; list carries one existential certificate for each later entry:
;;
;;   (0 j k) records a_i = a_j + 2^k with j < i and k natural;
;;   (1 b c) records a_i = a_b mod a_c with b,c < i and positive entries.
;;
;; Bundling these finitely many certificates with the sequence preserves all
;; inner existential quantifiers. The outer negated FN-EQUAL keeps the bundled
;; witness existentially quantified inside the statement. Every function
;; passed to APPLY$ is built solely from badged primitives and tame LOOP$
;; scions; no user-defined predicate is invoked through APPLY$.

(defun putnam-2009-b6-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2009-b6-list-term (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'cons
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2009-b6-list-term (cdr terms)))
    (putnam-2009-b6-quoted nil)))

(defun putnam-2009-b6-and-terms (terms)

    (putnam-2009-b6-quoted t)))

    (putnam-2009-b6-quoted nil)))

   'from-to-by

  '(lambda (globals entry)

(defun putnam-2009-b6-step-function ()

            (list 'natp second-witness)

            (list 'natp first-witness)
            (list 'natp second-witness)

    (putnam-2009-b6-step-function))

title: putnam_2009_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2009_b6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2009_b6): every positive integer is the endpoint
-- at index 2009 of an integer sequence built from earlier terms by adding a
-- nonnegative power of two or taking a remainder of earlier positive terms.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; mod-helper)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data PositiveNat : Nat -> Set where
  positiveNat : {n : Nat} -> PositiveNat (suc n)

data PositiveInt : Int -> Set where
  positiveInt : {n : Nat} -> PositiveInt (pos (suc n))

differenceNat : Nat -> Nat -> Int
differenceNat zero zero =
  pos zero
differenceNat (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
differenceNat zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
differenceNat (suc m) (suc n) =
  differenceNat m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  differenceNat m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  differenceNat n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

powerOfTwoNat : Nat -> Nat
powerOfTwoNat zero =
  oneN
powerOfTwoNat (suc exponent) =
  twoN * powerOfTwoNat exponent

powerOfTwo : Nat -> Int
powerOfTwo exponent =
  pos (powerOfTwoNat exponent)

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero =
  zero
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

integerRemainder : Int -> Int -> Int
integerRemainder (pos numerator) (pos (suc denominator)) =
  pos (naturalMod numerator (suc denominator))
integerRemainder (pos numerator) (pos zero) =
  pos numerator
integerRemainder _ _ =
  pos zero

IncrementStep :
  (Nat -> Int) ->
  Nat ->
  Set
IncrementStep sequence i =
  Exists Nat
    (\ j ->
      j <N i
      and
      Exists Nat
        (\ k ->
          sequence i ==
          addInt (sequence j) (powerOfTwo k)))

RemainderStep :
  (Nat -> Int) ->
  Nat ->
  Set
RemainderStep sequence i =
  Exists Nat
    (\ b ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ c ->
          b <N i
          and
          c <N i
          and
          PositiveInt (sequence b)
          and
          PositiveInt (sequence c)
          and
          sequence i ==
          integerRemainder (sequence b) (sequence c)))

AdmissibleStep :
  (Nat -> Int) ->
  Nat ->
  Set
AdmissibleStep sequence i =
  IncrementStep sequence i
  or
  RemainderStep sequence i

lastIndex : Nat
lastIndex =
  2009

putnam-2009-b6 : Set
putnam-2009-b6 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  PositiveNat n ->
  Exists (Nat -> Int)
    (\ sequence ->
      sequence zero == pos zero
      and
      sequence lastIndex == pos n
      and
      ((i : Nat) ->
        oneN <=N i ->
        i <=N lastIndex ->
        AdmissibleStep sequence i))

import Mathlib

noncomputable abbrev putnam_2010_a1_solution : ℕ → ℕ := sorry
-- (fun n : ℕ => Nat.ceil ((n : ℝ) / 2))
/--
Given a positive integer $n$, what is the largest $k$ such that the numbers $1,2,\dots,n$ can be put into $k$ boxes so that the sum of the numbers in each box is the same? [When $n=8$, the example $\{1,2,3,6\},\{4,8\},\{5,7\}$ shows that the largest $k$ is \emph{at least} $3$.]
-/
theorem putnam_2010_a1
    (n : ℕ)
    (kboxes : ℕ → Prop)
    (npos : n > 0)
    (hkboxes : ∀ k : ℕ, kboxes k =
      (∃ boxes : Finset.Icc 1 n → Fin k, ∀ i j : Fin k,
        ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (boxes · = i), (x : ℕ) =
        ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (boxes · = j), (x : ℕ))) :
    IsGreatest kboxes (putnam_2010_a1_solution n) :=
  sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_a1:
   the greatest number of boxes into which 1 through n can be partitioned
   with equal sums is the ceiling of n/2. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat.

Fixpoint putnam_2010_a1_box_sum
    (boxes : nat -> nat) (box n : nat) : nat :=
  match n with
  | O => O
  | S m =>
      putnam_2010_a1_box_sum boxes box m +
      if Nat.eqb (boxes (S m)) box then S m else O
  end.

Definition putnam_2010_a1_admissible (n k : nat) : Prop :=
  exists boxes : nat -> nat,
    (forall m : nat,
        1 <= m <= n ->
        1 <= boxes m <= k) /\
    (forall i j : nat,
        1 <= i <= k ->
        1 <= j <= k ->
        putnam_2010_a1_box_sum boxes i n =
        putnam_2010_a1_box_sum boxes j n).

Definition putnam_2010_a1_is_greatest
    (P : nat -> Prop) (greatest : nat) : Prop :=
  P greatest /\
  forall k : nat, P k -> k <= greatest.

Theorem putnam_2010_a1
    (n : nat)
    (kboxes : nat -> Prop)
    (npos : 0 < n)
    (hkboxes :
      forall k : nat,
        kboxes k <-> putnam_2010_a1_admissible n k) :
  putnam_2010_a1_is_greatest kboxes (Nat.div (n + 1) 2).
Admitted.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For positive K, each code below K^N has exactly N base-K digits (allowing
;; leading zeroes). Reading those digits as box labels gives a bijection with
;; all functions from {1,...,N} to the K boxes. Thus the exhaustive search
;; below is exactly the source's internal existential over BOXES.

(defun putnam-2010-a1-box-sum
    (code remaining k box)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+ (if (equal (mod code k) box)
           remaining
         0)
       (putnam-2010-a1-box-sum
        (floor code k)
        (- remaining 1)
        k
        box))))

(defun putnam-2010-a1-all-box-sums-equal-p
    (code n k remaining-boxes reference-sum)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining-boxes)))
  (if (zp remaining-boxes)
      t
    (let ((box (- remaining-boxes 1)))
      (and
       (equal
        (putnam-2010-a1-box-sum code n k box)
        reference-sum)
       (putnam-2010-a1-all-box-sums-equal-p
        code n k box reference-sum)))))

(defun putnam-2010-a1-valid-boxing-code-p (code n k)
  (and
   (natp code)
   (posp k)
   (< code (expt k n))
   (putnam-2010-a1-all-box-sums-equal-p
    code
    n
    k
    k
    (putnam-2010-a1-box-sum code n k 0))))

(defun putnam-2010-a1-boxing-code-exists-p
    (candidate-count n k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate-count)))
  (if (zp candidate-count)
      nil
    (let ((code (- candidate-count 1)))
      (or
       (putnam-2010-a1-valid-boxing-code-p code n k)
       (putnam-2010-a1-boxing-code-exists-p
        code n k)))))

(defun putnam-2010-a1-equal-sum-boxing-exists-p (n k)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (posp k)
   (putnam-2010-a1-boxing-code-exists-p
    (expt k n) n k)))

;; When N is positive, equal sums make every box nonempty: an empty box would
;; have sum zero, forcing every box sum and hence the total 1+...+N to be zero.
;; Therefore every valid K is at most N. Searching downward from N consequently
;; returns exactly the greatest K from the source predicate.
(defun putnam-2010-a1-greatest-box-count-through
    (n candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (zp candidate)
      0
    (if (putnam-2010-a1-equal-sum-boxing-exists-p
         n candidate)
        candidate
      (putnam-2010-a1-greatest-box-count-through
       n (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-2010-a1-solution (n)
  (floor (+ n 1) 2))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2010-a1-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (< 0 n))
   (equal
    (putnam-2010-a1-greatest-box-count-through n n)
    (putnam-2010-a1-solution n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2010_a1

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_a1:
-- for every positive n, ceil(n / 2) is the largest number of boxes into which
-- 1 through n can be partitioned with equal box sums. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2010A1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; true; false)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infix 4 _≤N_

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data _≤N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero≤N   : {n : Nat} -> zero ≤N n
  suc≤sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m ≤N n -> suc m ≤N suc n

finToNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (finToNat i)

finEqual : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin n -> Bool
finEqual fzero fzero =
  true
finEqual fzero (fsuc _) =
  false
finEqual (fsuc _) fzero =
  false
finEqual (fsuc i) (fsuc j) =
  finEqual i j

whenTrue : Bool -> Nat -> Nat
whenTrue true value =
  value
whenTrue false value =
  zero

sumFin : {n : Nat} -> (Fin n -> Nat) -> Nat
sumFin {zero} term =
  zero
sumFin {suc n} term =
  term fzero + sumFin (λ i -> term (fsuc i))

boxSum :
  {n k : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Fin k) ->
  Fin k ->
  Nat
boxSum boxes box =
  sumFin
    (λ index ->
      whenTrue
        (finEqual (boxes index) box)
        (suc (finToNat index)))

EqualBoxSums :
  {n k : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Fin k) ->
  Set
EqualBoxSums {k = k} boxes =
  (i j : Fin k) ->
  boxSum boxes i ≡ boxSum boxes j

HasEqualPartition : Nat -> Nat -> Set
HasEqualPartition n k =
  Σ (Fin n -> Fin k) EqualBoxSums

ceilingHalf : Nat -> Nat
ceilingHalf zero =
  zero
ceilingHalf (suc zero) =
  suc zero
ceilingHalf (suc (suc n)) =
  suc (ceilingHalf n)

record IsGreatestPartition (n greatest : Nat) : Set where
  field
    attainable :
      HasEqualPartition n greatest
    upper-bound :
      (k : Nat) ->
      HasEqualPartition n k ->
      k ≤N greatest

putnam-2010-a1 : Set
putnam-2010-a1 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  IsGreatestPartition n (ceilingHalf n)

title: putnam_2010_a1
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_a1:
  the largest number of equal-sum boxes into which the integers from 1 through
  a positive integer n can be partitioned. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory real_sigmaTheory;

val putnam_2010_a1 =
  ``!n : num. !kboxes : num -> bool.
      0 < n /\
      (!k : num.
         kboxes k <=>
         ?boxes : num -> num.
           (!m : num.
              m IN IMAGE SUC (count n)
              ==>
              boxes m < k) /\
           (!i j : num.
              i < k /\ j < k
              ==>
              SIGMA
                (\x : num. if boxes x = i then x else 0)
                (IMAGE SUC (count n)) =
              SIGMA
                (\x : num. if boxes x = j then x else 0)
                (IMAGE SUC (count n))))
      ==>
      kboxes ((n + 1) DIV 2) /\
      (!k : num. kboxes k ==> k <= (n + 1) DIV 2)``;

title: putnam_2010_a1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2010_a1: the largest number of boxes into which the integers from
  one through a positive n can be placed with equal box sums is the
  specified natural-valued solution. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P2010A1Solution is the resolved function floor((n+1)/2), equivalently
  ceil(n/2) on natural n. P2010A1Feasible n k says that there is a
  total assignment of the integers 1 through n to the k-element ordinal
  0 ..^ k such that every two fibers have the same sum.

  The source predicate kboxes is eliminated using its defining equivalence.
  The final conjunction expands IsGreatest: the specified solution value is
  feasible, and every feasible natural k is at most that value. Thus this is
  a bidirectionally equivalent rendering of the source theorem. All
  declarations are unproved $a statement encodings; there is no $p proof.
$)

$c P2010A1Solution P2010A1Feasible $.

p2010a1-solution-syntax $a class P2010A1Solution $.
p2010a1-feasible-syntax $a wff ( P2010A1Feasible A B ) $.

p2010a1-solution-definition $a |- P2010A1Solution =
  ( n e. NN0 |-> ( |_ ` ( ( n + 1 ) / 2 ) ) ) $.

${
  $d A B b i j x $.

  p2010a1-feasible-definition $a |- (
    ( P2010A1Feasible A B )
    <->
    E. b e. ( ( 0 ..^ B ) ^m ( 1 ... A ) )
      A. i e. ( 0 ..^ B )
        A. j e. ( 0 ..^ B )
          (
            sum_ x e. { x e. ( 1 ... A ) | ( b ` x ) = i } x
            =
            sum_ x e. { x e. ( 1 ... A ) | ( b ` x ) = j } x
          )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2010-a1 $a |- A. n e. NN
    (
      ( P2010A1Feasible n ( P2010A1Solution ` n ) )
      /\
      A. k e. NN0
        (
          ( P2010A1Feasible n k )
          ->
          k <_ ( P2010A1Solution ` n )
        )
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2010_a1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_2010_a1:
% for every positive n, the largest number of boxes into which 1 through n
% can be placed with equal sums is ceil(n/2). This file contains no proof.

putnam_2010_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  box_assignment: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  box_sum(
      boxes: box_assignment,
      box_number, count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      box_sum(boxes, box_number, count - 1)
        + IF boxes(count) = box_number THEN count ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  equal_sum_boxing(
      n, k: nat,
      boxes: box_assignment): bool =
    k > 0
      AND (FORALL (value: nat):
        1 <= value AND value <= n IMPLIES
          1 <= boxes(value) AND boxes(value) <= k)
      AND (FORALL (left_box, right_box: nat):
        1 <= left_box AND left_box <= k
          AND 1 <= right_box AND right_box <= k
        IMPLIES
          box_sum(boxes, left_box, n)
            = box_sum(boxes, right_box, n))

  admits_equal_sum_boxing(n, k: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (boxes: box_assignment):
      equal_sum_boxing(n, k, boxes)

  putnam_2010_a1_solution(n: nat): nat =
    ndiv(n + 1, 2)

  putnam_2010_a1: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n > 0 IMPLIES
        admits_equal_sum_boxing(
          n, putnam_2010_a1_solution(n))
          AND (FORALL (k: nat):
            admits_equal_sum_boxing(n, k)
              IMPLIES k <= putnam_2010_a1_solution(n))
END putnam_2010_a1

import Mathlib

abbrev putnam_2010_a2_solution : Set (ℝ → ℝ) := sorry
-- {f : ℝ → ℝ | ∃ c d : ℝ, ∀ x : ℝ, f x = c*x + d}
/--
Find all differentiable functions $f:\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that
\[
f'(x) = \frac{f(x+n)-f(x)}{n}
\]
for all real numbers $x$ and all positive integers $n$.
-/
theorem putnam_2010_a2
: {f : ℝ → ℝ | Differentiable ℝ f ∧
∀ x : ℝ, ∀ n : ℤ, n > 0 → deriv f x = (f (x + n) - f x)/n} = putnam_2010_a2_solution :=
sorry

Require Import Reals Coquelicot.Coquelicot.
Definition putnam_2010_a2_solution (f: R -> R) := exists (c d: R), f = (fun x => c * x + d).
Theorem putnam_2010_a2
    (f: R -> R)
    : (forall (x: R) (n: nat), gt n 0 -> ex_derive f x /\ Derive f x = (f (x + (INR n)) - f x) / (INR n)) <-> putnam_2010_a2_solution f.
Proof. Admitted.
