-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_a5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2010_a5): a group embedded in real three-space
-- whose cross products are group products or zero has all cross products zero.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2010A5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)
open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc; _⊔_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not :
  {a : Level} ->
  Set a ->
  Set a
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ :
  {a : Level} ->
  {A : Set a} ->
  A ->
  A ->
  Set a
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists
  {a p : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (property : A -> Set p) :
  Set (a ⊔ p) where

  constructor witness
  field
    value     : A
    satisfies : property value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

record Vector3 (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor vector3
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R
    z-coordinate : R

open Vector3

zeroVector :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Vector3 R
zeroVector reals =
  vector3
    (zeroR reals)
    (zeroR reals)
    (zeroR reals)

crossProduct :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Vector3 R
crossProduct reals u v =
  vector3
    (subtract reals
      (multiply reals (y-coordinate u) (z-coordinate v))
      (multiply reals (z-coordinate u) (y-coordinate v)))
    (subtract reals
      (multiply reals (z-coordinate u) (x-coordinate v))
      (multiply reals (x-coordinate u) (z-coordinate v)))
    (subtract reals
      (multiply reals (x-coordinate u) (y-coordinate v))
      (multiply reals (y-coordinate u) (x-coordinate v)))

record Group
  {ell : Level}
  (G : Set ell) :
  Set ell where

  field
    identity       : G
    inverseG       : G -> G
    multiplyG      : G -> G -> G
    associative    : (x y z : G) ->
                     multiplyG (multiplyG x y) z ==
                     multiplyG x (multiplyG y z)
    identity-left  : (x : G) -> multiplyG identity x == x
    identity-right : (x : G) -> multiplyG x identity == x
    inverse-left   : (x : G) ->
                     multiplyG (inverseG x) x == identity
    inverse-right  : (x : G) ->
                     multiplyG x (inverseG x) == identity

open Group

record Injection
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  field
    map : A -> B
    map-injective :
      (x y : A) ->
      map x == map y ->
      x == y

open Injection

putnam-2010-a5 :
  (ell : Level) ->
  Set (lsuc ell)
putnam-2010-a5 ell =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (G : Set ell) ->
  (group : Group G) ->
  (embedding : Injection G (Vector3 R)) ->
  ((a b : G) ->
    crossProduct reals (map embedding a) (map embedding b) ==
      map embedding (multiplyG group a b)
    or
    crossProduct reals (map embedding a) (map embedding b) ==
      zeroVector reals) ->
  (a b : G) ->
  crossProduct reals (map embedding a) (map embedding b) ==
    zeroVector reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_a5:
  a group contained in real three-space in which each pair's cross product
  equals either its group product or zero must have all pairwise cross products
  equal to zero. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory groupTheory;

val putnam_2010_a5 =
  ``let zero3 = ((0, 0), 0) : (real # real) # real
    in
    let cross3 =
      \a b : (real # real) # real.
        ((SND (FST a) * SND b - SND a * SND (FST b),
          SND a * FST (FST b) - FST (FST a) * SND b),
         FST (FST a) * SND (FST b) -
           SND (FST a) * FST (FST b))
    in
      !(g : ((real # real) # real) group).
        Group g /\
        (!a b : (real # real) # real.
           a IN g.carrier /\ b IN g.carrier
           ==>
           cross3 a b = g.op a b \/ cross3 a b = zero3)
        ==>
        !a b : (real # real) # real.
          a IN g.carrier /\ b IN g.carrier
          ==>
          cross3 a b = zero3``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2010_a5: a group embedded in real three-space whose pairwise cross
  products are always either the embedded group product or zero has all
  pairwise cross products zero. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P10A5R3 is the full space of real-valued functions on the three-element
  interval 0 ... 2, P10A5Zero is its zero vector, and P10A5Cross is the
  ordinary coordinate cross product. In SetMM, g e. Grp supplies an arbitrary
  group, Base ` g is its carrier, and +g ` g is its operation.

  The map i ranges over all injections of the group carrier into real
  three-space, exactly representing the source embedding. The hypothesis
  and conclusion quantify over every pair of carrier elements, and the
  group product is compared only after applying i. All declarations are
  unproved $a statement encodings; this database contains no $p proof.
$)

$c P10A5R3 P10A5Zero P10A5Cross $.

p10a5-space-syntax $a class P10A5R3 $.
p10a5-zero-syntax $a class P10A5Zero $.
p10a5-cross-syntax $a class ( P10A5Cross A B ) $.

p10a5-space-definition $a |- P10A5R3 = ( RR ^m ( 0 ... 2 ) ) $.

${
  p10a5-zero-definition $a |- P10A5Zero =
    ( k e. ( 0 ... 2 ) |-> 0 )
  $.
$}

${
  $d A B k $.

  p10a5-cross-definition $a |- (
    P10A5Cross A B
  ) = (
    k e. ( 0 ... 2 ) |->
      if (
        k = 0 ,
        (
          ( ( A ` 1 ) x. ( B ` 2 ) )
          -
          ( ( A ` 2 ) x. ( B ` 1 ) )
        ) ,
        if (
          k = 1 ,
          (
            ( ( A ` 2 ) x. ( B ` 0 ) )
            -
            ( ( A ` 0 ) x. ( B ` 2 ) )
          ) ,
          (
            ( ( A ` 0 ) x. ( B ` 1 ) )
            -
            ( ( A ` 1 ) x. ( B ` 0 ) )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d a b g i $.

  putnambench-putnam-2010-a5 $a |- A. g A. i
    (
      (
        g e. Grp
        /\
        i : ( Base ` g ) -1-1-> P10A5R3
      )
      ->
      (
        A. a e. ( Base ` g )
          A. b e. ( Base ` g )
            (
              ( P10A5Cross ( i ` a ) ( i ` b ) )
              =
              (
                i
                `
                ( a ( +g ` g ) b )
              )
              \/
              ( P10A5Cross ( i ` a ) ( i ` b ) ) = P10A5Zero
            )
        ->
        A. a e. ( Base ` g )
          A. b e. ( Base ` g )
            ( P10A5Cross ( i ` a ) ( i ` b ) ) = P10A5Zero
      )
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2010_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_a5:
% a group embedded in real three-space whose pairwise cross products are
% either group products or zero has all pairwise cross products zero.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2010_a5[Element: TYPE+]: THEORY
BEGIN
  vector3: TYPE =
    [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real, z_coord: real #]
  binary_operation: TYPE = [Element, Element -> Element]
  unary_operation: TYPE = [Element -> Element]
  embedding_function: TYPE = [Element -> vector3]

  zero_vector: vector3 =
    (# x_coord := 0, y_coord := 0, z_coord := 0 #)

  cross_product(a, b: vector3): vector3 =
    (# x_coord :=
         y_coord(a) * z_coord(b) - z_coord(a) * y_coord(b),
       y_coord :=
         z_coord(a) * x_coord(b) - x_coord(a) * z_coord(b),
       z_coord :=
         x_coord(a) * y_coord(b) - y_coord(a) * x_coord(b) #)

  group_laws(
      multiply: binary_operation,
      inverse: unary_operation,
      one: Element): bool =
    (FORALL (x, y, z: Element):
      multiply(multiply(x, y), z)
        = multiply(x, multiply(y, z)))
      AND (FORALL (x: Element):
        multiply(one, x) = x
          AND multiply(x, one) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x: Element):
        multiply(inverse(x), x) = one
          AND multiply(x, inverse(x)) = one)

  injective(embedding: embedding_function): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: Element):
      embedding(x) = embedding(y) IMPLIES x = y

  cross_product_condition(
      multiply: binary_operation,
      embedding: embedding_function): bool =
    FORALL (a, b: Element):
      cross_product(embedding(a), embedding(b))
          = embedding(multiply(a, b))
        OR cross_product(embedding(a), embedding(b)) = zero_vector

  putnam_2010_a5: bool =
    FORALL
        (multiply: binary_operation),
        (inverse: unary_operation),
        (one: Element),
        (embedding: embedding_function):
      (group_laws(multiply, inverse, one)
        AND injective(embedding)
        AND cross_product_condition(multiply, embedding))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (a, b: Element):
          cross_product(embedding(a), embedding(b)) = zero_vector
END putnam_2010_a5

(*

  divergence of an improper integral associated with a strictly decreasing
  continuous function on the nonnegative reals that tends to zero. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let analysis_output = open_out "/dev/null";;
let analysis_formatter = Format.formatter_of_out_channel analysis_output;;
let analysis_loaded =
  Toploop.use_file analysis_formatter "Library/transc.ml";;
Format.pp_print_flush analysis_formatter ();;
close_out analysis_output;;
if not analysis_loaded then failwith "failed to load Library/transc.ml";;

let statement =
  `let continuous_on_nonnegative =
     \(f:real->real).
       !x:real.
         &0 <= x
         ==> !e:real.
               &0 < e
               ==> ?d:real.
                     &0 < d /\
                     !y:real.
                       &0 <= y /\ abs (y - x) < d
                       ==> abs (f y - f x) < e in
   let tends_at_posinfinity =
     \(g:real->real) (l:real).
       !e:real.
         &0 < e
         ==> ?B:real.
               !x:real. B <= x ==> abs (g x - l) < e in
   !f:real->real.
     (!x y:real.
        &0 <= x /\ &0 <= y /\ x < y
        ==> f y < f x) /\
     continuous_on_nonnegative f /\
     tends_at_posinfinity f (&0)
     ==>
     ~(?l:real.
         tends_at_posinfinity
           (\z:real.
              integral(&0,z)
                (\x:real. (f x - f (x + &1)) / f x))
           l)`;;

title: putnam_2010_a6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_a6:
;; a strictly decreasing continuous real function tending to zero has a
;; divergent improper integral of (f(x)-f(x+1))/f(x). This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; For nonnegative rational X and positive rational EPSILON, F-APPROX is an
;; EPSILON-approximation to f(X). The regular-name and compact-continuity
;; predicates below present exactly the restriction to [0,infinity) of a
;; continuous real function. Since the source statement never uses f at a
;; negative argument, this loses no data relevant to the proposition.
(defstub putnam-2010-a6-f-approx (x epsilon) t)

(defun putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and (rationalp x) (< 0 x)))

(defun putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p (x)
  (and (rationalp x) (<= 0 x)))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-regular-name-p ()
  (forall (x epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p x)
      (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p eta))
     (and
      (rationalp (putnam-2010-a6-f-approx x epsilon))
      (rationalp (putnam-2010-a6-f-approx x eta))
      (<=
       (abs
        (-
         (putnam-2010-a6-f-approx x epsilon)
         (putnam-2010-a6-f-approx x eta)))
       (+ epsilon eta))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-continuity-tail-p
    (bound epsilon delta)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p x)
      (putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p y)
      (<= x bound)
      (<= y bound)
      (< (abs (- x y)) delta))
     (<=
      (abs
       (-
        (putnam-2010-a6-f-approx x (/ epsilon 8))
        (putnam-2010-a6-f-approx y (/ epsilon 8))))
      (/ epsilon 2)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-continuity-delta-exists-p
    (bound epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p delta)
     (putnam-2010-a6-continuity-tail-p
      bound epsilon delta))))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-continuous-on-nonnegative-reals-p ()
  (forall (bound epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp bound)
      (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (putnam-2010-a6-continuity-delta-exists-p
      bound epsilon))))

;; A positive rational gap between sufficiently accurate names is equivalent
;; to strict inequality between the represented real values.
(defun putnam-2010-a6-decrease-gap-p (x y gap)
  (and
   (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p gap)
   (<=
    gap
    (-
     (putnam-2010-a6-f-approx x (/ gap 8))
     (putnam-2010-a6-f-approx y (/ gap 8))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-decrease-gap-exists-p (x y)
  (exists (gap)
    (putnam-2010-a6-decrease-gap-p x y gap)))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-strictly-decreasing-p ()
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p x)
      (putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p y)
      (< x y))
     (putnam-2010-a6-decrease-gap-exists-p x y))))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-zero-limit-tail-p
    (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p x)
      (<= cutoff x))
     (<=
      (abs
       (putnam-2010-a6-f-approx x (/ epsilon 4)))
      (/ epsilon 2)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-zero-limit-cutoff-exists-p
    (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p cutoff)
     (putnam-2010-a6-zero-limit-tail-p
      epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-tends-to-zero-p ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (putnam-2010-a6-zero-limit-cutoff-exists-p
      epsilon))))

;; Right Riemann sums for the continuous integrand
;; (f(x)-f(x+1))/f(x) on [0,UPPER]. DELTA is the accuracy used for each
;; regular-Cauchy name. Strict decrease together with the zero limit makes
;; f positive on [0,infinity), so the represented denominator is nonzero in
;; the limit. These sums therefore converge to the source interval integral.
(defun putnam-2010-a6-riemann-sum-aux
    (upper n i delta)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix i)))
  (if (zp i)
      0
    (let* ((x (* upper (/ i n)))
           (fx
            (putnam-2010-a6-f-approx x delta))
           (fx1
            (putnam-2010-a6-f-approx (+ x 1) delta))
           (integrand (/ (- fx fx1) fx)))
      (+
       (putnam-2010-a6-riemann-sum-aux
        upper n (- i 1) delta)
       (* (/ upper n) integrand)))))

(defun putnam-2010-a6-riemann-sum
    (upper n delta)
  (if
   (and
    (putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p upper)
    (posp n)
    (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p delta))
   (putnam-2010-a6-riemann-sum-aux
    upper n n delta)
   0))

;; For fixed rational endpoints X and Y, this is the exact assertion that the
;; two represented integral values differ by less than EPSILON: all
;; sufficiently fine partitions and sufficiently accurate f-values satisfy
;; the displayed bound. The four approximation thresholds are existential
;; after X and Y, so no uniform convergence rate on an unbounded interval is
;; imposed.
(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-integral-comparison-tail-p
    (epsilon x y nx ny precision-x precision-y)
  (forall (n m delta eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp n)
      (posp m)
      (<= nx n)
      (<= ny m)
      (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p delta)
      (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p eta)
      (<= delta precision-x)
      (<= eta precision-y))
     (<
      (abs
       (-
        (putnam-2010-a6-riemann-sum x n delta)
        (putnam-2010-a6-riemann-sum y m eta)))
      epsilon))))

(defun putnam-2010-a6-integral-comparison-witness-p
    (epsilon x y witness)
  (let
      ((nx (nth 0 witness))
       (ny (nth 1 witness))
       (precision-x (nth 2 witness))
       (precision-y (nth 3 witness)))
    (and
     (true-listp witness)
     (equal (len witness) 4)
     (posp nx)
     (posp ny)
     (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p precision-x)
     (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p precision-y)
     (putnam-2010-a6-integral-comparison-tail-p
      epsilon x y nx ny precision-x precision-y))))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-integral-comparison-exists-p
    (epsilon x y)
  (exists (witness)
    (putnam-2010-a6-integral-comparison-witness-p
     epsilon x y witness)))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-integral-limit-tail-p
    (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p x)
      (putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p y)
      (<= cutoff x)
      (<= cutoff y))
     (putnam-2010-a6-integral-comparison-exists-p
      epsilon x y))))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-integral-limit-cutoff-exists-p
    (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (putnam-2010-a6-nonnegative-rational-p cutoff)
     (putnam-2010-a6-integral-limit-tail-p
      epsilon cutoff))))

;; Completeness of the real numbers makes this Cauchy-at-infinity condition
;; equivalent to the existence of the finite real limit quantified in the
;; Lean, Isabelle, and Rocq statements. Nonnegative rationals are cofinal in
;; the real atTop filter, and continuity of the finite integral makes checking
;; them equivalent to checking all real upper endpoints.
(defun-sk putnam-2010-a6-integral-has-finite-limit-p ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2010-a6-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (putnam-2010-a6-integral-limit-cutoff-exists-p
      epsilon))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2010-a6-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2010-a6-regular-name-p)
    (putnam-2010-a6-continuous-on-nonnegative-reals-p)

title: putnam_2010_a6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_a6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2010_a6): divergence of the improper integral
-- associated with a strictly decreasing continuous real function tending to
-- zero at positive infinity. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

Nonnegative :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
Nonnegative reals x =
  lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x

Between :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
Between reals lower upper x =
  lessOrEqual reals lower x
  and
  lessOrEqual reals x upper

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

LimitAtPositiveInfinity :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
LimitAtPositiveInfinity {R} reals function limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ threshold ->
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals threshold x ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (function x))

StrictlyDecreasingOnNonnegative :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
StrictlyDecreasingOnNonnegative {R} reals function =
  (x y : R) ->
  Nonnegative reals x ->
  Nonnegative reals y ->
  StrictLess reals x y ->
  StrictLess reals (function y) (function x)

ContinuousOnNonnegative :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
ContinuousOnNonnegative {R} reals function =
  (point : R) ->
  Nonnegative reals point ->
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        Nonnegative reals x ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function point)
          epsilon
          (function x)))

ContinuousOnInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
ContinuousOnInterval {R} reals lower upper function =
  (point : R) ->
  Between reals lower upper point ->
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        Between reals lower upper x ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function point)
          epsilon
          (function x)))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

midpointRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
midpointRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
    halfStep =
      divide reals
        step
        (fromNat reals twoN)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (add reals
              (multiply reals
                (fromNat reals i)
                step)
              halfStep)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function value =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      midpointRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    value

record StandardIntervalIntegration
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) : Set1 where
  field
    intervalIntegral :
      R ->
      R ->
      (R -> R) ->
      R

    integral-of-continuous :
      (lower upper : R) ->
      (function : R -> R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals lower upper ->
      ContinuousOnInterval reals lower upper function ->
      IntervalIntegralValue reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (intervalIntegral lower upper function)

open StandardIntervalIntegration

module Putnam2010A6Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (integration : StandardIntervalIntegration reals)
  (function : R -> R) where

  integrand : R -> R
  integrand x =
    divide reals
      (subtract reals
        (function x)
        (function (add reals x (oneR reals))))
      (function x)

  partialIntegral : R -> R
  partialIntegral upper =
    intervalIntegral integration
      (zeroR reals)
      upper
      integrand

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    Not
      (Exists R
        (\ finiteLimit ->
          LimitAtPositiveInfinity reals
            partialIntegral
            finiteLimit))

putnam-2010-a6 : Set1
putnam-2010-a6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (integration : StandardIntervalIntegration reals) ->
  (function : R -> R) ->
  StrictlyDecreasingOnNonnegative reals function ->
  ContinuousOnNonnegative reals function ->
  LimitAtPositiveInfinity reals function (zeroR reals) ->
  Putnam2010A6Statement.proposition reals integration function

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2010_a6: divergence of the improper integral formed from a strictly
  decreasing continuous real function on the nonnegative half-line that
  tends to zero at positive infinity. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The interval ( 0 [,) +oo ) is set.mm's full set of nonnegative real
  numbers. The first two hypotheses say exactly that the restriction of f to
  this interval is strictly decreasing and continuous, while f ~~>r 0 is its
  finite real limit at positive infinity.

  The S. binder is set.mm's real Lebesgue integral. Closed rather than
  half-open finite endpoints do not change its value, so the upper-endpoint
  function agrees with the source interval integral. The negated
  existential keeps the finite real limit witness internal and states
  divergence in exactly the source sense. The final declaration is the
  single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

${
  $d L f x y z $.

  putnambench-putnam-2010-a6 $a |- A. f e. ( RR ^m RR )
    (
      (
        (
          A. x e. ( 0 [,) +oo )
            A. y e. ( 0 [,) +oo )
              (
                x < y
                ->
                ( f ` y ) < ( f ` x )
              )
          /\
          ( f |` ( 0 [,) +oo ) )
            e. ( ( 0 [,) +oo ) -cn-> RR )
        )
        /\
        f ~~>r 0
      )
      ->
      -.
      E. L e. RR
        (
          z e. RR |->
            S. ( 0 [,] z )
              (
                (
                  ( f ` x )
                  -
                  ( f ` ( x + 1 ) )
                )
                /
                ( f ` x )
              )
              _d x
        )
        ~~>r
        L
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2010_a6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_a6:
% a strictly decreasing continuous real function on the nonnegative half-line
% tending to zero has a divergent improper integral of its relative unit
% decrement. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2010_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  strictly_decreasing_on_nonnegative(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: real):
      (0 <= x AND x < y) IMPLIES f(y) < f(x)

  continuous_on_nonnegative(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      0 <= x IMPLIES
        FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
          EXISTS (delta: posreal):
            FORALL (y: real):
              (0 <= y AND abs(y - x) < delta)
                IMPLIES
                  abs(f(y) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  tends_to_zero_at_real_top(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: real):
        FORALL (x: real):
          cutoff <= x IMPLIES
            abs(f(x)) < epsilon_value

  valid_tagged_partition(
      left, right: real,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = left
      AND points(count) = right
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          (points(index) < points(index + 1)
            AND points(index) <= tags(index)
            AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1))

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      f: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count - 1)
        + f(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_interval_integral(
      f: real_function,
      left, right, integral_value: real): bool =
    left < right
      AND FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
          FORALL
              (points, tags: real_sequence),
              (count: nat):
            (valid_tagged_partition(
                left, right, points, tags, count)
              AND mesh_less_than(points, count, mesh_bound))
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count)
                  - integral_value)
                < epsilon_value

  interval_integral(
      f: real_function,
      left, right: real): real =
    IF left = right THEN
      0
    ELSIF left < right THEN
      IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
          has_interval_integral(f, left, right, integral_value)
      THEN
        epsilon(
          LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
            has_interval_integral(
              f, left, right, integral_value))
      ELSE
        0
      ENDIF
    ELSE
      IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
          has_interval_integral(f, right, left, integral_value)
      THEN
        -epsilon(
          LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
            has_interval_integral(
              f, right, left, integral_value))
      ELSE
        0
      ENDIF
    ENDIF

  relative_unit_decrement(f: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      safe_div(f(x) - f(x + 1), f(x))

  truncated_integral(f: real_function, endpoint: real): real =
    interval_integral(relative_unit_decrement(f), 0, endpoint)

  converges_at_real_top(
      values: real_function,
      limit_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: real):
        FORALL (endpoint: real):
          cutoff <= endpoint IMPLIES
            abs(values(endpoint) - limit_value) < epsilon_value

  putnam_2010_a6: bool =
    FORALL (f: real_function):
      (strictly_decreasing_on_nonnegative(f)
        AND continuous_on_nonnegative(f)
        AND tends_to_zero_at_real_top(f))
      IMPLIES
        NOT EXISTS (limit_value: real):
          converges_at_real_top(
            LAMBDA (endpoint: real):
              truncated_integral(f, endpoint),
            limit_value)
END putnam_2010_a6

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b1:
;; no real sequence has m-th power series summing to m for every positive
;; integer m. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The conservative generic symbol supplies a rational regular Cauchy name
;; for a_i at every natural index i. It is arbitrary, not a rational-valued
;; sequence or a finite table. Every real sequence admits such names, and
;; every symbol satisfying PUTNAM-2010-B1-REGULAR-REAL-SEQUENCE-NAME-P
;; determines a unique real sequence.
;;
;; Since the requested answer is false, negating the source existential gives
;; the equivalent universal statement that every such sequence fails the
;; power-series condition. DEFSTUB represents that arbitrary sequence, while
;; all scalar quantifiers and convergence witnesses remain internal DEFUN-SK
;; quantifiers.

(defstub putnam-2010-b1-sequence-approx (index precision) t)

(defun putnam-2010-b1-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and
   (rationalp x)
   (< 0 x)))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-b1-regular-real-sequence-name-p ()
  (forall (index epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (putnam-2010-b1-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2010-b1-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((left
            (putnam-2010-b1-sequence-approx index epsilon))
           (right
            (putnam-2010-b1-sequence-approx index eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<= (abs (- left right))
            (+ epsilon eta)))))))

;; This is the rational approximation, at a common precision, to the first
;; TERMS entries of the real series sum_i (a_i)^EXPONENT.

(defun putnam-2010-b1-partial-power-sum
    (exponent terms precision)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let ((index (- (nfix terms) 1)))
      (+
       (putnam-2010-b1-partial-power-sum
        exponent index precision)
       (expt

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2010_b1): no sequence of real numbers has the
-- sum of its m-th powers equal to m for every positive integer m.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2010B1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms total =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    total

module Putnam2010B1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  PowerSumProperty : (Nat -> R) -> Set
  PowerSumProperty sequence =
    (m : Nat) ->
    m != zero ->
    SeriesHasSum reals
      (\ i -> naturalPower reals (sequence i) m)
      (fromNat reals m)

  DesiredSequenceExists : Set
  DesiredSequenceExists =
    Exists (Nat -> R) PowerSumProperty

  solution : Set
  solution =
    Bottom

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    Iff DesiredSequenceExists solution

putnam-2010-b1 : Set1
putnam-2010-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2010B1Statement.proposition reals

    E. a e. ( RR ^m NN0 )

        ( sum_ i e. NN0 ( ( a ` i ) ^ m ) ) = m

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b1:
% no infinite real sequence has its m-th power series sum equal to m for every
% positive integer m. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2010_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  power_partial_sum(
      sequence: real_sequence,
      exponent, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      power_partial_sum(sequence, exponent, count - 1)
        + sequence(count - 1) ^ exponent
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  power_series_sums_to(
      sequence: real_sequence,
      exponent: nat,
      total: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(
              power_partial_sum(sequence, exponent, count)
                - total) < epsilon_value

  has_requested_power_sums: bool =
    EXISTS (sequence: real_sequence):
      FORALL (m: nat):
        m > 0 IMPLIES
          power_series_sums_to(sequence, m, m :: real)

  putnam_2010_b1_solution: bool = FALSE

  putnam_2010_b1: bool =
    has_requested_power_sums IFF putnam_2010_b1_solution
END putnam_2010_b1

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b2:
  the least possible distance AB among noncollinear lattice-point triangles
  with all three side lengths integral is 3. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let lattice_point =
     \(p:real#real).
       ?m n:int.
         FST p = real_of_int m /\ SND p = real_of_int n in
   let edist =
     \(p:real#real) (q:real#real).
       sqrt ((FST p - FST q) pow 2 + (SND p - SND q) pow 2) in
   let integral_distance =
     \(p:real#real) (q:real#real).
       ?n:int. edist p q = real_of_int n in
   let noncollinear =
     \(a:real#real) (b:real#real) (c:real#real).
       ~((FST b - FST a) * (SND c - SND a) =
         (SND b - SND a) * (FST c - FST a)) in
   let admissible =
     \(a:real#real) (b:real#real) (c:real#real).
       lattice_point a /\
       lattice_point b /\
       lattice_point c /\
       integral_distance a b /\
       integral_distance a c /\
       integral_distance b c /\
       noncollinear a b c in
   (?a b c:real#real.
      admissible a b c /\ edist a b = &3) /\
   (!a b c:real#real.
      admissible a b c ==> &3 <= edist a b)`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b2:
;; noncollinear plane points with integer coordinates and integer pairwise
;; distances have minimum possible distance AB equal to 3. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-2010-b2-squared-distance (x1 y1 x2 y2)
  (+ (* (- x2 x1) (- x2 x1))
     (* (- y2 y1) (- y2 y1))))

(defun putnam-2010-b2-determinant (ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (- (* (- bx ax) (- cy ay))
     (* (- by ay) (- cx ax))))

;; For a natural number x, this finite search holds exactly when x is the
;; square of a natural number. Thus it expresses internally that the
;; corresponding nonnegative Euclidean distance is an integer.
(defun putnam-2010-b2-square-witness-down-p (x candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (zp candidate)
      (equal x 0)
    (or (equal (* candidate candidate) x)
        (putnam-2010-b2-square-witness-down-p
         x
         (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-2010-b2-perfect-square-p (x)
  (and (natp x)
       (putnam-2010-b2-square-witness-down-p x x)))

(defun putnam-2010-b2-configuration-p
    (ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (and (integerp ax)
       (integerp ay)
       (integerp bx)
       (integerp by)
       (integerp cx)
       (integerp cy)
       (putnam-2010-b2-perfect-square-p
        (putnam-2010-b2-squared-distance ax ay bx by))
       (putnam-2010-b2-perfect-square-p
        (putnam-2010-b2-squared-distance ax ay cx cy))
       (putnam-2010-b2-perfect-square-p
        (putnam-2010-b2-squared-distance bx by cx cy))
       (not (equal (putnam-2010-b2-determinant
                    ax ay bx by cx cy)
                   0))))

;; A=(0,0), B=(3,0), C=(0,4) attains the distance AB=3.
(defun putnam-2010-b2-attainment-certificate-p ()
  (and
   (putnam-2010-b2-configuration-p 0 0 3 0 0 4)
   (equal (putnam-2010-b2-squared-distance 0 0 3 0)
          9)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2010-b2-statement
    (ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (and
   (putnam-2010-b2-attainment-certificate-p)
   (implies
    (putnam-2010-b2-configuration-p ax ay bx by cx cy)
    (<= 9
        (putnam-2010-b2-squared-distance ax ay bx by)))))

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2010_b2): the least possible side length of a
-- noncollinear integer-coordinate triangle whose three side lengths are
-- integers is 3. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2010B2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

subtractInt : Int -> Int -> Int
subtractInt x y =
  addInt x (negateInt y)

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

squareInt : Int -> Int
squareInt x =
  multiplyInt x x

record Point : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : Int
    y-coordinate : Int

open Point

squaredDistance : Point -> Point -> Int
squaredDistance p q =
  addInt
    (squareInt
      (subtractInt (x-coordinate p) (x-coordinate q)))
    (squareInt
      (subtractInt (y-coordinate p) (y-coordinate q)))

HasDistance : Point -> Point -> Nat -> Set
HasDistance p q n =
  squaredDistance p q == pos (n * n)

Noncollinear : Point -> Point -> Point -> Set
Noncollinear a b c =
  multiplyInt
    (subtractInt (x-coordinate b) (x-coordinate a))
    (subtractInt (y-coordinate c) (y-coordinate a))
  !=
  multiplyInt
    (subtractInt (y-coordinate b) (y-coordinate a))
    (subtractInt (x-coordinate c) (x-coordinate a))

record ValidTriangleWithAB (ab : Nat) : Set where
  field
    A B C : Point
    ac bc : Nat
    noncollinear : Noncollinear A B C
    ab-distance : HasDistance A B ab
    ac-distance : HasDistance A C ac
    bc-distance : HasDistance B C bc

record IsLeast (P : Nat -> Set) (n : Nat) : Set where
  field
    member      : P n
    lower-bound : (m : Nat) -> P m -> n <=N m

three : Nat
three =
  suc (suc (suc zero))

putnam-2010-b2 : Set
putnam-2010-b2 =
  IsLeast ValidTriangleWithAB three

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b2:
  the least possible distance between two vertices of a noncollinear lattice
  triangle whose three side lengths are integers is 3. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open integerTheory pairTheory realTheory intrealTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2010_b2 =
  ``let dist =
      \P Q : int # int.
        sqrt
          ((real_of_int (FST P - FST Q)) pow 2 +
           (real_of_int (SND P - SND Q)) pow 2)
    in
    let noncollinear =
      \A B C : int # int.
        (FST B - FST A) * (SND C - SND A) <>
        (SND B - SND A) * (FST C - FST A)
    in
    let integral_distance =
      \P Q : int # int.
        ?n : num. dist P Q = (&n : real)
    in
    let admissible =
      \A B C : int # int.
        noncollinear A B C /\
        integral_distance A B /\
        integral_distance A C /\
        integral_distance B C
    in
      (!A B C : int # int.
         admissible A B C ==> (3 : real) <= dist A B) /\
      (?A B C : int # int.
         admissible A B C /\ dist A B = (3 : real))``;

$(

  putnam_2010_b2: the least possible distance AB among noncollinear
  integer-coordinate planar triples whose three pairwise distances are
  integers is 3. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P10B2I is the two-coordinate index set, P10B2R2 is the full real
  coordinate plane, P10B2Dist is ordinary Euclidean distance, and
  P10B2Noncol is determinant noncollinearity. P10B2Good A B C states that
  A, B, and C have integer coordinates, are noncollinear, and have all
  three pairwise distances in ZZ.

  The final conjunction is the explicit IsLeast characterization from the
  sources: an admissible triple attains AB = 3, and every admissible triple
  has AB at least 3. All witnesses remain internally quantified. Every
  declaration below is an unproved $a statement, not a proof.
$)

$c P10B2I P10B2R2 P10B2Dist P10B2Noncol P10B2Good $.

p10b2-index-syntax $a class P10B2I $.
p10b2-plane-syntax $a class P10B2R2 $.
p10b2-distance-syntax $a class ( P10B2Dist A B ) $.
p10b2-noncollinear-syntax $a wff ( P10B2Noncol A B C ) $.
p10b2-good-syntax $a wff ( P10B2Good A B C ) $.

p10b2-index-definition $a |- P10B2I = ( 1 ... 2 ) $.

p10b2-plane-definition $a |- P10B2R2 = ( RR ^m P10B2I ) $.

${
  $d A B j $.

  p10b2-distance-definition $a |- (
    P10B2Dist A B
  ) = (
    sqrt
    `
    (
      sum_ j e. P10B2I
        ( ( ( A ` j ) - ( B ` j ) ) ^ 2 )
    )
  ) $.
$}

p10b2-noncollinear-definition $a |- (
  ( P10B2Noncol A B C )
  <->
  (
    (
      ( ( B ` 1 ) - ( A ` 1 ) )
      x.
      ( ( C ` 2 ) - ( A ` 2 ) )
    )
    =/=
    (
      ( ( B ` 2 ) - ( A ` 2 ) )
      x.
      ( ( C ` 1 ) - ( A ` 1 ) )
    )
  )
) $.

p10b2-good-definition $a |- (
  ( P10B2Good A B C )
  <->
  (
    (
      A e. ( ZZ ^m P10B2I )
      /\
      (
        B e. ( ZZ ^m P10B2I )
        /\
        C e. ( ZZ ^m P10B2I )
      )
    )
    /\
    (
      ( P10B2Noncol A B C )
      /\
      (
        ( P10B2Dist A B ) e. ZZ
        /\
        (
          ( P10B2Dist A C ) e. ZZ
          /\
          ( P10B2Dist B C ) e. ZZ
        )
      )
    )
  )
) $.

${
  $d a b c $.

  putnambench-putnam-2010-b2 $a |- (
    E. a E. b E. c
      (
        ( P10B2Good a b c )
        /\
        ( P10B2Dist a b ) = 3
      )
    /\
    A. a A. b A. c
      (
        ( P10B2Good a b c )
        ->
        3 <_ ( P10B2Dist a b )
      )
  ) $.
$}

title: putnam_2010_b2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b2:
% among noncollinear integer-coordinate triples in the real plane whose three
% pairwise distances are integers, the least possible distance AB is 3. This
% file contains no proof.

putnam_2010_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]

  integer_point(P: point): bool =
    EXISTS (m, n: int):
      x_coord(P) = (m :: real)
        AND y_coord(P) = (n :: real)

  squared_distance(P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(Q) - x_coord(P)) ^ 2
      + (y_coord(Q) - y_coord(P)) ^ 2

  is_euclidean_distance(distance: real, P, Q: point): bool =
    distance >= 0
      AND distance * distance = squared_distance(P, Q)

  has_integer_distance(P, Q: point): bool =
    EXISTS (distance: real), (value: int):
      is_euclidean_distance(distance, P, Q)
        AND distance = (value :: real)

  cross_from(P, Q, R: point): real =
    (x_coord(Q) - x_coord(P)) * (y_coord(R) - y_coord(P))
      - (y_coord(Q) - y_coord(P)) * (x_coord(R) - x_coord(P))

  admissible_triangle(A, B, C: point): bool =
    integer_point(A)
      AND integer_point(B)
      AND integer_point(C)
      AND cross_from(A, B, C) /= 0
      AND has_integer_distance(A, B)
      AND has_integer_distance(A, C)
      AND has_integer_distance(B, C)

  is_minimum_ab_distance(value: real): bool =
    (EXISTS (A, B, C: point):
      admissible_triangle(A, B, C)
        AND is_euclidean_distance(value, A, B))
      AND
        (FORALL (A, B, C: point), (distance: real):
          (admissible_triangle(A, B, C)
            AND is_euclidean_distance(distance, A, B))
          IMPLIES value <= distance)

  putnam_2010_b2_solution: real = 3

  putnam_2010_b2: bool =
    is_minimum_ab_distance(putnam_2010_b2_solution)
END putnam_2010_b2

title: putnam_2010_b3

import Mathlib

open Filter Topology Set

abbrev putnam_2010_b3_solution : Set ℕ := sorry
-- Ici 1005
/--
There are $2010$ boxes labeled $B_1, B_2, \dots, B_{2010}$, and $2010n$ balls have been distributed among them, for some positive integer $n$. You may redistribute the balls by a sequence of moves, each of which consists of choosing an $i$ and moving \emph{exactly} $i$ balls from box $B_i$ into any one other box. For which values of $n$ is it possible to reach the distribution with exactly $n$ balls in each box, regardless of the initial distribution of balls?
-/
theorem putnam_2010_b3
      (n : ℕ) (hn : n > 0)
      (trans : (ℕ → Fin 2010 → ℕ) → ℕ → Prop)
      (htrans : ∀ P T, trans P T ↔ ∀ t : ℕ, t < T → ∃ i j,
            i ≠ j ∧
            P t i ≥ i.1 + 1 ∧ P (t + 1) i = P t i - (i.1 + 1) ∧ P (t + 1) j = P t j + (i.1 + 1) ∧
            ∀ k : Fin 2010, k ≠ i → k ≠ j → P (t + 1) k = P t k) :
      (∀ B, ∑ i, B i = 2010 * n → ∃ᵉ (P) (T), P 0 = B ∧ trans P T ∧ ∀ i, P T i = n)
      ↔ n ∈ putnam_2010_b3_solution :=
sorry

title: putnam_2010_b3
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b3:
   characterization of the positive integers for which every distribution of
   2010n balls among 2010 indexed boxes can be made uniform by the prescribed
   box-to-box moves; this file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Vectors.Fin.

Open Scope nat_scope.

Definition putnam_2010_b3_configuration : Type :=
  Fin.t 2010 -> nat.

Fixpoint putnam_2010_b3_fin_sum
    (m : nat) : (Fin.t m -> nat) -> nat :=
  match m as k return (Fin.t k -> nat) -> nat with
  | O => fun _ => 0
  | S k =>
      fun f =>
        f Fin.F1 +
        putnam_2010_b3_fin_sum k (fun i => f (Fin.FS i))
  end.

Definition putnam_2010_b3_index
    {m : nat} (i : Fin.t m) : nat :=
  proj1_sig (Fin.to_nat i).

Definition putnam_2010_b3_move_amount
    (i : Fin.t 2010) : nat :=
  putnam_2010_b3_index i + 1.

Definition putnam_2010_b3_transitions
    (P : nat -> putnam_2010_b3_configuration)
    (T : nat) : Prop :=
  forall t : nat,
    t < T ->
    exists i j : Fin.t 2010,
      i <> j /\
      P t i >= putnam_2010_b3_move_amount i /\
      P (t + 1) i =
        P t i - putnam_2010_b3_move_amount i /\
      P (t + 1) j =
        P t j + putnam_2010_b3_move_amount i /\
      forall k : Fin.t 2010,
        k <> i ->
        k <> j ->
        P (t + 1) k = P t k.

Definition putnam_2010_b3_solution (n : nat) : Prop :=
  1005 <= n.

Theorem putnam_2010_b3
    (n : nat)
    (hn : 0 < n) :
  (forall B : putnam_2010_b3_configuration,
      putnam_2010_b3_fin_sum 2010 B = 2010 * n ->
      exists
        (P : nat -> putnam_2010_b3_configuration)
        (T : nat),
        P 0 = B /\
        putnam_2010_b3_transitions P T /\
        forall i : Fin.t 2010, P T i = n) <->
  putnam_2010_b3_solution n.
Admitted.

theory putnam_2010_b3 imports Complex_Main
begin

(* Note: Boosts Fin 2010 to nat *)
definition putnam_2010_b3_solution :: "nat set" where
  "putnam_2010_b3_solution \<equiv> {1005..}"
(* {1005..} *)
theorem putnam_2010_b3:
  fixes n :: "nat"
    and trans :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool"
  defines "trans \<equiv> \<lambda> P :: nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat. \<lambda> T :: nat. \<forall> t :: nat < T. \<exists> i \<in> {0..2009}. \<exists> j \<in> {0..2009}. i \<noteq> j \<and> P t i \<ge> i + 1 \<and> P (t + 1) i = P t i - (i + 1) \<and> P (t + 1) j = P t j + (i + 1) \<and> (\<forall> k \<in> {0..2009}. (k \<noteq> i \<longrightarrow> k \<noteq> j \<longrightarrow> P (t + 1) k = P t k))"
  assumes npos : "n > 0"
  shows "(\<forall>B :: nat \<Rightarrow> nat.
    (\<Sum>i \<in> {0..2009}. B i) = 2010 * n \<longrightarrow>
    (\<exists>(P :: nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat) (T :: nat).
      P 0 = B \<and> trans P T \<and> (\<forall>i \<in> {0..2009}. P T i = n)))
    \<longleftrightarrow> n \<in> putnam_2010_b3_solution"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b3:
  classification of the positive integers for which every distribution of
  2010n balls among 2010 labeled boxes can be made uniform by legal box-index
  transfers. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let boxes = 1..2010 in
   let legal_run =
     \(P:num->num->num) (steps:num).
       !t:num.
         t < steps
         ==> ?i j:num.
               i IN boxes /\
               j IN boxes /\
               ~(i = j) /\
               i <= P t i /\
               P (t + 1) i = P t i - i /\
               P (t + 1) j = P t j + i /\
               (!k:num.
                  k IN boxes /\ ~(k = i) /\ ~(k = j)
                  ==> P (t + 1) k = P t k) in
   let solvable =
     \n:num.
       !B:num->num.
         nsum boxes B = 2010 * n
         ==> ?P:num->num->num. ?steps:num.
               (!i:num. i IN boxes ==> P 0 i = B i) /\
               legal_run P steps /\
               (!i:num. i IN boxes ==> P steps i = n) in
   let putnam_2010_b3_solution =
     {n:num | 1005 <= n} in
   !n:num.
     0 < n
     ==> (solvable n <=> n IN putnam_2010_b3_solution)`;;

title: putnam_2010_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b3:
;; every distribution of 2010n balls among 2010 labeled boxes can be made
;; uniform by the prescribed moves exactly when n is at least 1005. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A function Fin 2010 -> Nat is represented exactly by its ordered
;; 2010-tuple of values. The outer DEFUN-SK therefore ranges over every source
;; distribution, without restricting the unbounded natural-number entries.
;;
;; A witness trace is its finite prefix P(0),...,P(T). Conversely, every such
;; list defines the constrained prefix of a source trace and can be extended
;; arbitrarily after T. Thus the internal existential trace below is
;; bidirectionally equivalent to the source's existential P and T. Each call
;; of PUTNAM-2010-B3-STEP-P keeps the source and target boxes existential and
;; internal to that particular move.

(defun putnam-2010-b3-natural-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (natp (car values))
       (putnam-2010-b3-natural-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-2010-b3-sum (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (+ (car values)
         (putnam-2010-b3-sum (cdr values)))
    0))

(defun putnam-2010-b3-distribution-p (distribution)
  (and
   (true-listp distribution)
   (equal (len distribution) 2010)
   (putnam-2010-b3-natural-list-p distribution)))

(defun putnam-2010-b3-other-boxes-unchanged-p
    (remaining box source target before after)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (and
     (or
      (equal box source)
      (equal box target)
      (equal (nth box after)
             (nth box before)))
     (putnam-2010-b3-other-boxes-unchanged-p
      (- remaining 1)
      (+ box 1)
      source
      target
      before
      after))))

(defun putnam-2010-b3-step-witness-p
    (before after source target)
  (let ((amount (+ source 1)))
    (and
     (putnam-2010-b3-distribution-p before)
     (putnam-2010-b3-distribution-p after)
     (natp source)
     (< source 2010)
     (natp target)
     (< target 2010)
     (not (equal source target))
     (<= amount (nth source before))
     (equal (nth source after)
            (- (nth source before) amount))
     (equal (nth target after)
            (+ (nth target before) amount))
     (putnam-2010-b3-other-boxes-unchanged-p
      2010 0 source target before after))))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-b3-step-p (before after)
  (exists (source target)
    (putnam-2010-b3-step-witness-p
     before after source target)))

(defun putnam-2010-b3-trace-steps-p (trace)
  (declare (xargs :measure (acl2-count trace)))
  (if (and (consp trace)
           (consp (cdr trace)))
      (and
       (putnam-2010-b3-step-p
        (car trace)
        (car (cdr trace)))
       (putnam-2010-b3-trace-steps-p
        (cdr trace)))
    t))

(defun putnam-2010-b3-all-equal-p (values n)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (equal (car values) n)
       (putnam-2010-b3-all-equal-p (cdr values) n))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-2010-b3-uniform-distribution-p
    (distribution n)
  (and
   (putnam-2010-b3-distribution-p distribution)
   (putnam-2010-b3-all-equal-p distribution n)))

(defun putnam-2010-b3-trace-witness-p
    (n initial trace)
  (and
   (true-listp trace)
   (consp trace)
   (equal (car trace) initial)
   (putnam-2010-b3-trace-steps-p trace)
   (putnam-2010-b3-uniform-distribution-p
    (car (last trace))
    n)))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-b3-trace-exists-p (n initial)
  (exists (trace)
    (putnam-2010-b3-trace-witness-p
     n initial trace)))

(defun-sk putnam-2010-b3-all-distributions-reachable-p (n)
  (forall (initial)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2010-b3-distribution-p initial)
      (equal
       (putnam-2010-b3-sum initial)
       (* 2010 n)))
     (putnam-2010-b3-trace-exists-p
      n initial))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2010-b3-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp n)
    (< 0 n))
   (iff
    (putnam-2010-b3-all-distributions-reachable-p n)
    (<= 1005 n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2010_b3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2010_b3): redistribution among 2010 labeled
-- boxes by moving the source box's label number of balls, classified by
-- exactly the positive integers n at least 1005. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2010B3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finToNat :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc index) =
  suc (finToNat index)

sumFin :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Nat) ->
  Nat
sumFin {zero} values =
  zero
sumFin {suc n} values =
  values fzero + sumFin (\ index -> values (fsuc index))

Box : Set
Box =
  Fin 2010

Distribution : Set
Distribution =
  Box -> Nat

Process : Set
Process =
  Nat -> Distribution

SameDistribution :
  Distribution ->
  Distribution ->
  Set
SameDistribution left right =
  (box : Box) ->
  left box == right box

Move :
  Process ->
  Nat ->
  Set
Move process time =
  Exists Box
    (\ source ->
      Exists Box
        (\ destination ->
          source != destination
          and
          suc (finToNat source) <=N process time source
          and
          process (suc time) source
            == process time source - suc (finToNat source)
          and
          process (suc time) destination
            == process time destination + suc (finToNat source)
          and
          ((box : Box) ->
            box != source ->
            box != destination ->
            process (suc time) box == process time box)))

ValidThrough :
  Process ->
  Nat ->
  Set
ValidThrough process stoppingTime =
  (time : Nat) ->
  time <N stoppingTime ->
  Move process time

Uniform :
  Nat ->
  Distribution ->
  Set
Uniform n distribution =
  (box : Box) ->
  distribution box == n

CanReachUniform :
  Distribution ->
  Nat ->
  Set
CanReachUniform initial n =
  Exists Process
    (\ process ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ stoppingTime ->
          SameDistribution (process zero) initial
          and
          ValidThrough process stoppingTime
          and
          Uniform n (process stoppingTime)))

putnam-2010-b3 : Set
putnam-2010-b3 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  zero <N n ->
  Iff
    ((initial : Distribution) ->
      sumFin initial == 2010 * n ->
      CanReachUniform initial n)
    (1005 <=N n)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b3:
  redistribution among 2010 labeled boxes by moving the source box's label
  number of balls reaches the uniform distribution for every initial
  distribution exactly when the positive integer n is at least 1005.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2010_b3 =
  ``!n : num.
      0 < n
      ==>
      ((!B : num -> num.
          SIGMA B (count 2010) = 2010 * n
          ==>
          ?P : num -> num -> num.
          ?T : num.
            (!i : num. i < 2010 ==> P 0 i = B i) /\
            (!t : num.
               t < T
               ==>
               ?i j : num.
                 i < 2010 /\
                 j < 2010 /\
                 i <> j /\
                 i + 1 <= P t i /\
                 P (t + 1) i = P t i - (i + 1) /\
                 P (t + 1) j = P t j + (i + 1) /\
                 !k : num.
                   k < 2010 /\ k <> i /\ k <> j
                   ==>
                   P (t + 1) k = P t k) /\
            !i : num. i < 2010 ==> P T i = n)
       <=>
       1005 <= n)``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2010_b3: characterization of the positive integers for which every
  distribution of 2010n balls among 2010 labeled boxes can be equalized by
  the prescribed exact-size transfers. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P2010B3I is the 2010-element ordinal 0 ..^ 2010, representing Fin 2010.
  A distribution is an NN0-valued function on this carrier. A trajectory is
  an NN0-indexed family of distributions. P2010B3Trans P T says that at each
  time t < T, one chooses distinct indices i and j, removes exactly i+1 balls
  from box i, adds them to box j, and leaves every other box unchanged.

  The corpus assertion quantifies over every initial distribution with total
  2010n, keeps the trajectory and terminal time existential, and requires the
  terminal distribution to be constantly n. The right side gives the intended
  solution set {n in NN | 1005 <= n}. The auxiliary $a declarations are
  syntax and faithful definitions; the final $a is the single unproved corpus
  statement. This database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P2010B3I P2010B3Trans $.

p2010b3-index-syntax $a class P2010B3I $.
p2010b3-transition-syntax $a wff ( P2010B3Trans P T ) $.

p2010b3-index-definition $a |-
  P2010B3I = ( 0 ..^ ; ; ; 2 0 1 0 )
$.

${
  $d P T i j k t $.

  p2010b3-transition-definition $a |- (
    ( P2010B3Trans P T )
    <->
    A. t e. ( 0 ..^ T )
      E. i e. P2010B3I E. j e. P2010B3I
        (
          i =/= j
          /\
          (
            ( i + 1 ) <_ ( ( P ` t ) ` i )
            /\
            (
              ( ( P ` ( t + 1 ) ) ` i )
              =
              ( ( ( P ` t ) ` i ) - ( i + 1 ) )
              /\
              (
                ( ( P ` ( t + 1 ) ) ` j )
                =
                ( ( ( P ` t ) ` j ) + ( i + 1 ) )
                /\
                A. k e. P2010B3I
                  (
                    (
                      k =/= i
                      /\
                      k =/= j
                    )
                    ->
                    ( ( P ` ( t + 1 ) ) ` k )
                    =
                    ( ( P ` t ) ` k )
                  )
              )
            )
          )
        )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d b i n p s $.

  putnambench-putnam-2010-b3 $a |- A. n e. NN
    (
      (
        A. b e. ( NN0 ^m P2010B3I )
          (
            (
              sum_ i e. P2010B3I ( b ` i )
            )
            =
            ( ; ; ; 2 0 1 0 x. n )
            ->
            E. p e. ( ( NN0 ^m P2010B3I ) ^m NN0 )
              E. s e. NN0
                (
                  ( p ` 0 ) = b
                  /\
                  (
                    ( P2010B3Trans p s )
                    /\
                    A. i e. P2010B3I
                      ( ( p ` s ) ` i ) = n
                  )
                )
          )
      )
      <->
      ; ; ; 1 0 0 5 <_ n
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2010_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b3:
% redistribution among 2010 labeled boxes can always reach the uniform
% distribution exactly when the positive integer n is at least 1005.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2010_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  box_index: TYPE = below(2010)
  distribution: TYPE = [box_index -> nat]
  process: TYPE = [nat -> distribution]

  total_balls(
      boxes: distribution,
      count: upto(2010)): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      total_balls(boxes, count - 1) + boxes(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  valid_transition(P: process, time: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (source, destination: box_index):
      source /= destination
        AND P(time)(source) >= source + 1
        AND P(time + 1)(source)
          = P(time)(source) - (source + 1)
        AND P(time + 1)(destination)
          = P(time)(destination) + (source + 1)
        AND (FORALL (box: box_index):
          box /= source AND box /= destination IMPLIES
            P(time + 1)(box) = P(time)(box))

  reaches_uniform(
      initial: distribution,
      n: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (P: process), (final_time: nat):
      P(0) = initial
        AND (FORALL (time: nat):
          time < final_time IMPLIES valid_transition(P, time))
        AND (FORALL (box: box_index):
          P(final_time)(box) = n)

  uniform_reachable_from_every_distribution(n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (initial: distribution):
      total_balls(initial, 2010) = 2010 * n IMPLIES
        reaches_uniform(initial, n)

  putnam_2010_b3_solution(n: nat): bool =
    n >= 1005

  putnam_2010_b3: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n > 0 IMPLIES
        (uniform_reachable_from_every_distribution(n)
          IFF putnam_2010_b3_solution(n))
END putnam_2010_b3

import Mathlib

open Filter Topology Set

abbrev putnam_2010_b4_solution : Set (Polynomial ℝ × Polynomial ℝ) := sorry
-- {(p, q) : Polynomial ℝ × Polynomial ℝ | p.degree ≤ 1 ∧ q.degree ≤ 1 ∧ p.coeff 0 * q.coeff 1 - p.coeff 1 * q.coeff 0 = 1}
/--
Find all pairs of polynomials $p(x)$ and $q(x)$ with real coefficients for which $p(x)q(x+1)-p(x+1)q(x)=1$.
-/
theorem putnam_2010_b4
(p q : Polynomial ℝ)
: (∀ x : ℝ, p.eval x * q.eval (x + 1) - p.eval (x + 1) * q.eval x = 1) ↔ (p, q) ∈ putnam_2010_b4_solution :=
sorry

Require Import Reals Coquelicot.Coquelicot.
Definition P : (nat -> R) -> nat -> R -> R := fun c n x => sum_n (fun i => c i * x ^ i) n.
Definition putnam_2010_b4_solution (c1 c2: nat -> R) (n m: nat) := exists (a b c d: R), b * c - a * d = 1 /\ P c1 n = (fun x => a * x + b) /\ P c2 m = (fun x => c * x + d).
Theorem putnam_2010_b4
    (c1 c2: nat -> R)
    (n m: nat)
    : (forall (x: R), (P c1 n x) * (P c2 m (x + 1)) - (P c1 n (x + 1)) * (P c2 m x) = 1) <-> putnam_2010_b4_solution c1 c2 n m.
Proof. Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b4:
  classification of pairs of real polynomials satisfying a unit forward-shift
  determinant identity. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let eval =
     \p:real list. \x:real.
       ITLIST (\c acc. c + x * acc) p (&0) in
   !p q:real list.
     ((!x:real.
         eval p x * eval q (x + &1) -
         eval p (x + &1) * eval q x = &1)
      <=>
      (?a b c d:real.
