;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b4:
;; pairs of real polynomials whose shifted determinant is identically one are
;; exactly the affine pairs with coefficient determinant one. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The real coefficient domain is presented as a real closed ordered field.
;; The square-root and odd-degree-root laws are the standard algebraic
;; characterization of real closedness.  Polynomials are canonical nonempty
;; coefficient lists in ascending degree order.
;;
;; This is bidirectionally equivalent to the source statement: the reals form
;; such a field, while completeness of real closed fields transfers this
;; first-order polynomial assertion between any real closed field and the
;; reals. Canonical coefficient-list equality is polynomial equality because
;; every ordered field is infinite.
;;
;; ACL2 function objects supply the field operations and polynomial
;; evaluation. FN-EQUAL against a constant-T function expresses the source's
;; universal quantification over every real input without turning that input
;; into an external statement parameter. The solution predicate reads the
;; constant and linear coefficients of the canonical lists, so degree at most
;; one and the determinant equation are represented directly.

(defun putnam-2010-b4-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2010-b4-quoted function)
   (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2010-b4-quoted function)
   (list 'cons left (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-and-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2010-b4-quoted t)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2010-b4-and-term (cdr terms))
     (putnam-2010-b4-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-or-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2010-b4-quoted nil)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2010-b4-quoted t)
     (putnam-2010-b4-or-term (cdr terms)))))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-not-term (term)
  (list
   'if
   term
   (putnam-2010-b4-quoted nil)
   (putnam-2010-b4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-implies-term (antecedent consequent)
  (list
   'if
   antecedent
   consequent
   (putnam-2010-b4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-true-function (formals)
  (list
   'lambda
   formals
   (putnam-2010-b4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-2010-b4-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-operation-term (operation left right)
  (putnam-2010-b4-apply2-term operation left right))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-all-coefficients-function (carrier)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)
   (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term
    carrier 'loop$-ivars)))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-all-coefficients-term
    (carrier coefficients)
  (list
   'always$+
   (putnam-2010-b4-quoted
    (putnam-2010-b4-all-coefficients-function
     carrier))
   (putnam-2010-b4-quoted nil)
   coefficients))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-polynomial-term
    (carrier zero coefficients)
  (putnam-2010-b4-and-term
   (list
    (list 'true-listp coefficients)
    (list 'consp coefficients)
    (putnam-2010-b4-all-coefficients-term
     carrier coefficients)
    (putnam-2010-b4-or-term
     (list
      (list 'equal
            (list 'len coefficients)
            (putnam-2010-b4-quoted 1))
      (putnam-2010-b4-not-term
       (list 'equal
             (list 'car (list 'last coefficients))
             (putnam-2010-b4-quoted zero))))))))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-field-laws-function
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (y 'y)
         (z 'z)
         (qzero (putnam-2010-b4-quoted zero))
         (qone (putnam-2010-b4-quoted one))
         (add-xy
          (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term add x y))
         (add-yz
          (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term add y z))
         (mul-xy
          (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term mul x y))
         (mul-yz
          (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term mul y z))
         (neg-x
          (putnam-2010-b4-apply1-term neg x))
         (inv-x
          (putnam-2010-b4-apply1-term inv x))
         (domain
          (putnam-2010-b4-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier y)
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier z))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2010-b4-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier add-xy)
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier mul-xy)
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier neg-x)
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier inv-x)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term add add-xy z)
             (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term add x add-yz))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term mul mul-xy z)
             (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term mul x mul-yz))
            (list

             add-xy

              add
              (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term mul x y)
              (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term mul x z)))))))
    (list

     '(x y z)
     (putnam-2010-b4-implies-term domain laws))))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-order-laws-function
    (carrier zero add mul lt)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (y 'y)
         (z 'z)
         (qzero (putnam-2010-b4-quoted zero))
         (lt-xy
          (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term lt x y))
         (lt-yx
          (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term lt y x))
         (lt-yz
          (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term lt y z))
         (lt-xz
          (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term lt x z))
         (domain
          (putnam-2010-b4-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier y)
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier z))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2010-b4-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2010-b4-not-term
             (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term lt x x))
            (putnam-2010-b4-or-term
             (list
              lt-xy
              (list 'equal x y)
              lt-yx))
            (putnam-2010-b4-implies-term
             (putnam-2010-b4-and-term
              (list lt-xy lt-yz))

            (putnam-2010-b4-implies-term
             lt-xy
             (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term
              lt
              (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term add x z)
              (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term add y z)))

             (putnam-2010-b4-and-term
              (list

              qzero
              (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term mul x y)))))))
    (list
     'lambda

(defun putnam-2010-b4-square-root-laws-function
    (carrier zero mul lt square-root)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (qzero (putnam-2010-b4-quoted zero))
         (root
          (putnam-2010-b4-apply1-term square-root x))
         (domain
          (putnam-2010-b4-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2010-b4-not-term

         (laws
          (putnam-2010-b4-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier root)

             'equal
             (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term mul root root)
             x)))))

     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-2010-b4-implies-term domain laws))))

(defun putnam-2010-b4-evaluation-laws-function
    (carrier zero add mul evaluate)
  (let* ((coefficient 'coefficient)
         (rest 'rest)
         (x 'x)
         (qzero (putnam-2010-b4-quoted zero))
         (domain
          (putnam-2010-b4-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term
             carrier coefficient)
            (list 'true-listp rest)
            (putnam-2010-b4-all-coefficients-term
             carrier rest)
            (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier x))))
         (empty-law
          (putnam-2010-b4-implies-term
           (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term carrier x)
           (list
            'equal
            (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term
             evaluate
             (putnam-2010-b4-quoted nil)
             x)
            qzero)))
         (recursive-value
          (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term
           add
           coefficient
           (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term
            mul
            x
            (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term
             evaluate rest x))))
         (recursive-law
          (putnam-2010-b4-implies-term
           domain
           (putnam-2010-b4-and-term
            (list
             (putnam-2010-b4-carrier-term
              carrier
              (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term
               evaluate
               (list 'cons coefficient rest)
               x))
             (list
              'equal
              (putnam-2010-b4-operation-term
               evaluate
               (list 'cons coefficient rest)
               x)

    (list
     'lambda
     '(coefficient rest x)

(defun putnam-2010-b4-odd-root-laws-function
    (carrier zero evaluate odd-root)
  (let* ((coefficients 'coefficients)
         (root
          (putnam-2010-b4-apply1-term

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2010_b4): classification of pairs of real
-- polynomials satisfying p(x)q(x+1) - p(x+1)q(x) = 1. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infix 1 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

Polynomial : Set -> Set
Polynomial R =
  List R

evaluate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  R ->
  R
evaluate reals [] x =
  zeroR reals
evaluate reals (coefficient ∷ coefficients) x =
  add reals
    coefficient
    (multiply reals x (evaluate reals coefficients x))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

module Putnam2010B4Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (p q : Polynomial R) where

  affine : R -> R -> R -> R
  affine slope intercept x =
    add reals
      (multiply reals slope x)
      intercept

  FunctionalEquation : Set
  FunctionalEquation =
    (x : R) ->
    subtract reals
      (multiply reals
        (evaluate reals p x)
        (evaluate reals q (add reals x (oneR reals))))
      (multiply reals
        (evaluate reals p (add reals x (oneR reals)))
        (evaluate reals q x))
    ==
    oneR reals

  Solution : Set
  Solution =
    Exists R
      (\ a ->
        Exists R
          (\ b ->
            Exists R
              (\ c ->
                Exists R
                  (\ d ->
                    subtract reals
                      (multiply reals b c)
                      (multiply reals a d)
                    ==
                    oneR reals
                    and
                    ((x : R) ->
                      evaluate reals p x == affine a b x)
                    and
                    ((x : R) ->
                      evaluate reals q x == affine c d x)))))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    FunctionalEquation iff Solution

putnam-2010-b4 : Set1
putnam-2010-b4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (p q : Polynomial R) ->
  Putnam2010B4Statement.proposition reals p q

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b4:
  the affine real-polynomial pairs satisfying a unit finite-difference
  determinant identity are exactly those with coefficient determinant one.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open realTheory polyTheory;

val putnam_2010_b4 =
  ``!p q : real list.
      (!x : real.
         poly p x * poly q (x + 1) -
           poly p (x + 1) * poly q x =
         1)
      <=>
      ?a b c d : real.
        b * c - a * d = 1 /\
        (!x : real. poly p x = a * x + b) /\
        (!x : real. poly q x = c * x + d)``;

$(

  p(x)q(x+1) - p(x+1)q(x) = 1 for every real x. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  Poly1 ` RRfld is set.mm's ring of all finite-support univariate real
  polynomials, and eval1 is ordinary polynomial evaluation. The right side
  states internally that p(x) = ax + b and q(x) = cx + d for real
  coefficients with b*c - a*d = 1. This is exactly the coefficient
  characterization recorded by the ground-truth sources.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d a b c d p q x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2010-b4 $a |-
    A. p e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
    A. q e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
      (
        A. x e. RR
          (
            (
              (
                ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` p )
                `
                x
              )
              x.
              (
                ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` q )
                `
                ( x + 1 )
              )
            )
            -
            (
              (
                ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` p )
                `
                ( x + 1 )
              )
              x.
              (
                ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` q )
                `
                x
              )
            )
            =
            1
          )
        <->
        E. a e. RR E. b e. RR E. c e. RR E. d e. RR
          (
            (
              p
              =
              (
                (
                  ( ( algSc ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) ) ` a )
                  ( .r ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
                  ( var1 ` RRfld )
                )
                ( +g ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
                ( ( algSc ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) ) ` b )
              )
              /\
              q
              =
              (
                (
                  ( ( algSc ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) ) ` c )
                  ( .r ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
                  ( var1 ` RRfld )
                )
                ( +g ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
                ( ( algSc ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) ) ` d )
              )
            )
            /\
            (
              ( b x. c )
              -
              ( a x. d )
            )
            =
            1
          )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2010_b4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b4:
% pairs of real polynomials satisfying the unit shifted determinant identity
% are exactly the affine pairs with the stated coefficient determinant.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2010_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  polynomial: TYPE = list[real]

  polynomial_value(p: polynomial, x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    CASES p OF
      null: 0,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        coefficient + x * polynomial_value(tail, x)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE p BY <<

  polynomial_coefficient(
      p: polynomial,
      degree: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    CASES p OF
      null: 0,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        IF degree = 0 THEN
          coefficient
        ELSE
          polynomial_coefficient(tail, degree - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE p BY <<

  degree_at_most_one(p: polynomial): bool =
    FORALL (degree: nat):
      degree >= 2 IMPLIES polynomial_coefficient(p, degree) = 0

  satisfies_shifted_identity(p, q: polynomial): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      polynomial_value(p, x) * polynomial_value(q, x + 1)
        - polynomial_value(p, x + 1) * polynomial_value(q, x)
        = 1

  putnam_2010_b4_solution(p, q: polynomial): bool =
    degree_at_most_one(p)
      AND degree_at_most_one(q)
      AND polynomial_coefficient(p, 0)
            * polynomial_coefficient(q, 1)
          - polynomial_coefficient(q, 0)
            * polynomial_coefficient(p, 1)
        = 1

  putnam_2010_b4: bool =
    FORALL (p, q: polynomial):
      satisfies_shifted_identity(p, q)
        IFF putnam_2010_b4_solution(p, q)
END putnam_2010_b4

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2010_b5): nonexistence of a strictly increasing
-- differentiable real function satisfying f'(x) = f(f(x)) for every real x.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
differenceQuotient reals function point x =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals (function x) (function point))
    (subtract reals x point)

DerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeAt {R} reals function point derivative-value =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        x != point ->
        CloseTo reals derivative-value epsilon
          (differenceQuotient reals function point x)))

StrictlyIncreasing :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
StrictlyIncreasing {R} reals function =
  (x y : R) ->
  StrictLess reals x y ->
  StrictLess reals (function x) (function y)

SatisfiesDifferentialEquation :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
SatisfiesDifferentialEquation {R} reals function =
  (x : R) ->
  DerivativeAt reals
    function
    x
    (function (function x))

putnam-2010-b5 : Set1
putnam-2010-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Not
    (Exists (R -> R)
      (\ function ->
        StrictlyIncreasing reals function
        and
        SatisfiesDifferentialEquation reals function))

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b5:
% there is no strictly increasing differentiable function from the reals to
% the reals whose derivative at every x equals f(f(x)). This file contains no
% proof.

putnam_2010_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  has_derivative_at(
      f: real_function,
      derivative, x: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (h: real):
          (h /= 0 AND abs(h) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                f(x + h) - f(x)
                  - derivative * h)
                < epsilon_value * abs(h)

  differentiable_at(f: real_function, x: real): bool =
    EXISTS (derivative: real):
      has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x)

  differentiable(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      differentiable_at(f, x)

  derivative_value(f: real_function, x: real): real =
    IF differentiable_at(f, x) THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (derivative: real):
          has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  strictly_increasing(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: real):
      x < y IMPLIES f(x) < f(y)

  putnam_2010_b5_solution: bool = FALSE

  putnam_2010_b5: bool =
    (EXISTS (f: real_function):
      strictly_increasing(f)
        AND differentiable(f)
        AND (FORALL (x: real):
          derivative_value(f, x) = f(f(x))))
      IFF putnam_2010_b5_solution
END putnam_2010_b5

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b6:
   equality of ordinary and entrywise positive powers of a real square matrix
   follows for every exponent from the first n+1 cases. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Vectors.Fin Reals Arith.PeanoNat.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2010_b6_matrix (n : nat) : Type :=
  Fin.t n -> Fin.t n -> R.

Definition putnam_2010_b6_matrix_eq
    {n : nat}
    (A B : putnam_2010_b6_matrix n) : Prop :=
  forall i j : Fin.t n, A i j = B i j.

Fixpoint putnam_2010_b6_indices (n : nat) : list (Fin.t n) :=
  match n with
  | O => []
  | S k => Fin.F1 :: map Fin.FS (putnam_2010_b6_indices k)
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2010_b6_sum (xs : list R) : R :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0
  | x :: rest => x + putnam_2010_b6_sum rest
  end.

Definition putnam_2010_b6_mul
    {n : nat}
    (A B : putnam_2010_b6_matrix n) :
    putnam_2010_b6_matrix n :=
  fun i j =>
    putnam_2010_b6_sum
      (map
        (fun k => A i k * B k j)
        (putnam_2010_b6_indices n)).

Definition putnam_2010_b6_identity
    (n : nat) : putnam_2010_b6_matrix n :=
  fun i j =>
    if Fin.eq_dec i j then 1 else 0.

Fixpoint putnam_2010_b6_matrix_power
    {n : nat}
    (A : putnam_2010_b6_matrix n)
    (k : nat) : putnam_2010_b6_matrix n :=
  match k with
  | O => putnam_2010_b6_identity n
  | S l =>
      putnam_2010_b6_mul A
        (putnam_2010_b6_matrix_power A l)
  end.

Definition putnam_2010_b6_entrywise_power
    {n : nat}
    (A : putnam_2010_b6_matrix n)
    (k : nat) : putnam_2010_b6_matrix n :=
  fun i j => (A i j) ^ k.

Theorem putnam_2010_b6
    (n : nat)
    (npos : (1 <= n)%nat)
    (A : putnam_2010_b6_matrix n)
    (Apow : nat -> putnam_2010_b6_matrix n)
    (hApow :
      forall k : nat,
        (0 < k)%nat ->
        putnam_2010_b6_matrix_eq
          (Apow k)
          (putnam_2010_b6_entrywise_power A k)) :
  (forall k : nat,
    (1 <= k <= n + 1)%nat ->
    putnam_2010_b6_matrix_eq
      (putnam_2010_b6_matrix_power A k)
      (Apow k)) ->
  forall k : nat,
    (1 <= k)%nat ->
    putnam_2010_b6_matrix_eq
      (putnam_2010_b6_matrix_power A k)
      (Apow k).
Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b6:
;; an n-by-n real matrix whose first n+1 ordinary powers equal its entrywise
;; powers has that equality for every positive exponent. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A finite tuple of real algebraic numbers is represented in one field
;; Q(alpha).  ALPHA is the unique real root, in a rational isolating interval,
;; of PRIMITIVE.  Each matrix entry is a rational polynomial in ALPHA.
;;
;; For fixed n and a fixed counterexample exponent k, the hypothesis and the
;; failure of the conclusion are a finite system of polynomial equalities and
;; inequalities over Q.  Real-closed-field completeness says that such a
;; system has a real solution exactly when it has a real-algebraic solution.
;; Thus quantifying over these exact representations preserves arbitrary real
;; matrices; it does not restrict the theorem to rational matrices.  The ACL2
;; argument K is universally quantified, preserving "for every k >= 1".

;; Rational polynomials in alpha use descending coefficient order.

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-p (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (and (rationalp (car polynomial))
           (putnam-2010-b6-rp-p (cdr polynomial)))
    (equal polynomial nil)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (if (equal (car polynomial) 0)
          (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize (cdr polynomial))
        polynomial)
    nil))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-negate (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons (- (car polynomial))
            (putnam-2010-b6-rp-negate (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-add-raw (left right)
  (declare
   (xargs :measure (+ (acl2-count left) (acl2-count right))))
  (cond
   ((endp left) right)
   ((endp right) left)
   ((< (len left) (len right))
    (cons (car right)
          (putnam-2010-b6-rp-add-raw left (cdr right))))
   ((< (len right) (len left))
    (cons (car left)
          (putnam-2010-b6-rp-add-raw (cdr left) right)))
   (t
    (cons (+ (car left) (car right))
          (putnam-2010-b6-rp-add-raw
           (cdr left) (cdr right))))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-add (left right)
  (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize
   (putnam-2010-b6-rp-add-raw left right)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-subtract (left right)
  (putnam-2010-b6-rp-add
   left
   (putnam-2010-b6-rp-negate right)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-scale (coefficient polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons (* coefficient (car polynomial))
            (putnam-2010-b6-rp-scale
             coefficient (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-zeroes (count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons 0
          (putnam-2010-b6-zeroes (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-scale-shift
    (coefficient polynomial shift)
  (append
   (putnam-2010-b6-rp-scale coefficient polynomial)
   (putnam-2010-b6-zeroes shift)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-multiply-raw (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (putnam-2010-b6-rp-add
       (putnam-2010-b6-rp-scale-shift
        (car left) right (len (cdr left)))
       (putnam-2010-b6-rp-multiply-raw (cdr left) right))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-multiply (left right)
  (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize
   (putnam-2010-b6-rp-multiply-raw left right)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-eval-aux
    (polynomial value accumulator)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (putnam-2010-b6-rp-eval-aux
       (cdr polynomial)
       value
       (+ (* accumulator value) (car polynomial)))
    accumulator))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-eval (polynomial value)
  (putnam-2010-b6-rp-eval-aux polynomial value 0))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-derivative-aux
    (polynomial degree)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (if (zp degree)
          nil
        (cons
         (* degree (car polynomial))
         (putnam-2010-b6-rp-derivative-aux
          (cdr polynomial) (- degree 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-derivative (polynomial)
  (let ((normalized
         (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize polynomial)))
    (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize
     (putnam-2010-b6-rp-derivative-aux
      normalized
      (nfix (- (len normalized) 1))))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-remainder-fuel
    (left right fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((left (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize left))
        (right (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize right)))
    (if (or (zp fuel)
            (endp right)
            (< (len left) (len right)))
        left
      (putnam-2010-b6-rp-remainder-fuel
       (putnam-2010-b6-rp-subtract
        left
        (putnam-2010-b6-rp-scale-shift
         (/ (car left) (car right))
         right
         (- (len left) (len right))))
       right
       (- fuel 1)))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-remainder (left right)
  (putnam-2010-b6-rp-remainder-fuel
   left
   right
   (+ 1 (len (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize left)))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-sturm-tail
    (previous current fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((current
         (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize current)))
    (if (or (zp fuel) (endp current))
        nil
      (cons
       current
       (putnam-2010-b6-rp-sturm-tail
        current
        (putnam-2010-b6-rp-negate
         (putnam-2010-b6-rp-remainder
          previous current))
        (- fuel 1))))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-sturm-sequence
    (polynomial derivative)
  (let ((polynomial
         (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize polynomial))
        (derivative
         (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize derivative)))
    (if (endp polynomial)
        nil
      (cons
       polynomial
       (if (endp derivative)
           nil
         (cons
          derivative
          (putnam-2010-b6-rp-sturm-tail
           polynomial
           derivative
           (+ 1 (len polynomial) (len derivative)))))))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rational-sign (value)
  (cond ((< value 0) -1)
        ((< 0 value) 1)
        (t 0)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-variations-aux
    (polynomials value previous-sign)
  (if (consp polynomials)
      (let ((sign
             (putnam-2010-b6-rational-sign
              (putnam-2010-b6-rp-eval
               (car polynomials) value))))
        (if (equal sign 0)
            (putnam-2010-b6-rp-variations-aux
             (cdr polynomials) value previous-sign)
          (+ (if (and (not (equal previous-sign 0))
                      (not (equal sign previous-sign)))
                 1
               0)
             (putnam-2010-b6-rp-variations-aux
              (cdr polynomials) value sign))))
    0))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-variations
    (polynomials value)
  (putnam-2010-b6-rp-variations-aux
   polynomials value 0))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-cauchy-index
    (polynomial query lower upper)
  (let ((sequence
         (putnam-2010-b6-rp-sturm-sequence
          polynomial query)))
    (- (putnam-2010-b6-rp-variations sequence lower)
       (putnam-2010-b6-rp-variations sequence upper))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-root-count
    (polynomial lower upper)
  (putnam-2010-b6-rp-cauchy-index
   polynomial
   (putnam-2010-b6-rp-derivative polynomial)
   lower
   upper))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-primitive-p
    (primitive lower upper)
  (and
   (putnam-2010-b6-rp-p primitive)
   (consp (putnam-2010-b6-rp-normalize primitive))
   (rationalp lower)
   (rationalp upper)
   (< lower upper)
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-2010-b6-rp-eval primitive lower)
     0))
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-2010-b6-rp-eval primitive upper)
     0))
   (equal
    (putnam-2010-b6-rp-root-count
     primitive lower upper)
    1)))

;; This Sturm-Tarski query is the sign of VALUE(alpha).

(defun putnam-2010-b6-algebraic-sign
    (primitive lower upper value)
  (putnam-2010-b6-rp-cauchy-index
   primitive
   (putnam-2010-b6-rp-multiply
    (putnam-2010-b6-rp-derivative primitive)
    value)
   lower
   upper))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-algebraic-equal-p
    (primitive lower upper left right)
  (equal
   (putnam-2010-b6-algebraic-sign
    primitive
    lower
    upper
    (putnam-2010-b6-rp-subtract left right))
   0))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-algebraic-row-p
    (row dimension)
  (if (consp row)
      (and
       (natp dimension)
       (< 0 dimension)
       (putnam-2010-b6-rp-p (car row))
       (putnam-2010-b6-algebraic-row-p
        (cdr row) (- dimension 1)))
    (and
     (equal row nil)
     (equal dimension 0))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-row-p (row dimension)
  (and
   (true-listp row)
   (equal (len row) dimension)
   (putnam-2010-b6-algebraic-row-p row dimension)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-matrix-rows-p
    (matrix dimension)
  (if (consp matrix)
      (and
       (putnam-2010-b6-row-p (car matrix) dimension)
       (putnam-2010-b6-matrix-rows-p
        (cdr matrix) dimension))
    (equal matrix nil)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-matrix-p (matrix dimension)
  (and
   (true-listp matrix)
   (equal (len matrix) dimension)
   (putnam-2010-b6-matrix-rows-p
    matrix dimension)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rp-power (value exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      (list 1)
    (putnam-2010-b6-rp-multiply
     value
     (putnam-2010-b6-rp-power
      value (- exponent 1)))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-entrywise-row-power
    (row exponent)
  (if (consp row)
      (cons
       (putnam-2010-b6-rp-power
        (car row) exponent)
       (putnam-2010-b6-entrywise-row-power
        (cdr row) exponent))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-entrywise-power
    (matrix exponent)
  (if (consp matrix)
      (cons
       (putnam-2010-b6-entrywise-row-power
        (car matrix) exponent)
       (putnam-2010-b6-entrywise-power
        (cdr matrix) exponent))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-first-column (matrix)
  (if (consp matrix)
      (cons (caar matrix)
            (putnam-2010-b6-first-column
             (cdr matrix)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rest-columns (matrix)
  (if (consp matrix)
      (cons (cdar matrix)
            (putnam-2010-b6-rest-columns
             (cdr matrix)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-transpose (matrix)
  (if (or (endp matrix) (endp (car matrix)))
      nil
    (cons
     (putnam-2010-b6-first-column matrix)
     (putnam-2010-b6-transpose
      (putnam-2010-b6-rest-columns matrix)))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-dot-product (left right)
  (if (or (endp left) (endp right))
      nil
    (putnam-2010-b6-rp-add
     (putnam-2010-b6-rp-multiply
      (car left) (car right))
     (putnam-2010-b6-dot-product
      (cdr left) (cdr right)))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-row-times-columns
    (row columns)
  (if (consp columns)
      (cons
       (putnam-2010-b6-dot-product
        row (car columns))
       (putnam-2010-b6-row-times-columns
        row (cdr columns)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-matrix-times-columns
    (matrix columns)
  (if (consp matrix)
      (cons
       (putnam-2010-b6-row-times-columns
        (car matrix) columns)
       (putnam-2010-b6-matrix-times-columns
        (cdr matrix) columns))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-matrix-multiply (left right)
  (putnam-2010-b6-matrix-times-columns
   left
   (putnam-2010-b6-transpose right)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-identity-row
    (row column count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons
     (if (equal row column) (list 1) nil)
     (putnam-2010-b6-identity-row
      row (+ column 1) (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-identity-rows
    (row count dimension)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
      (cons
       (putnam-2010-b6-identity-row row 0 dimension)
       (putnam-2010-b6-identity-rows
        (+ row 1) (- count 1) dimension))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-identity-matrix (dimension)
  (putnam-2010-b6-identity-rows
   0 dimension dimension))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-matrix-power
    (matrix exponent dimension)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      (putnam-2010-b6-identity-matrix dimension)
    (putnam-2010-b6-matrix-multiply
     matrix
     (putnam-2010-b6-matrix-power
      matrix (- exponent 1) dimension))))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-rows-equal-p
    (primitive lower upper left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (and
       (consp right)
       (putnam-2010-b6-algebraic-equal-p
        primitive lower upper (car left) (car right))
       (putnam-2010-b6-rows-equal-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr left) (cdr right)))
    (equal right nil)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-matrices-equal-p
    (primitive lower upper left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (and
       (consp right)
       (putnam-2010-b6-rows-equal-p
        primitive lower upper (car left) (car right))
       (putnam-2010-b6-matrices-equal-p
        primitive lower upper (cdr left) (cdr right)))
    (equal right nil)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-power-equality-p
    (primitive lower upper matrix dimension exponent)
  (putnam-2010-b6-matrices-equal-p
   primitive
   lower
   upper
   (putnam-2010-b6-matrix-power
    matrix exponent dimension)
   (putnam-2010-b6-entrywise-power
    matrix exponent)))

(defun putnam-2010-b6-initial-equalities-p
    (primitive lower upper matrix dimension exponent count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      t
    (and
     (putnam-2010-b6-power-equality-p
      primitive lower upper matrix dimension exponent)
     (putnam-2010-b6-initial-equalities-p
      primitive
      lower
      upper
      matrix
      dimension
      (+ exponent 1)
      (- count 1)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2010-b6-statement
    (n primitive lower upper matrix k)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp n)
    (< 0 n)
    (putnam-2010-b6-primitive-p
     primitive lower upper)
    (putnam-2010-b6-matrix-p matrix n)
    (putnam-2010-b6-initial-equalities-p
     primitive lower upper matrix n 1 (+ n 1)))
   (implies
    (and (natp k) (< 0 k))
    (putnam-2010-b6-power-equality-p
     primitive lower upper matrix n k))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2010_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2010_b6): equality of ordinary and entrywise
-- positive powers of a real square matrix, propagated from exponents 1 through
-- n + 1 to every positive exponent. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2010B6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; true; false)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finEqual :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n ->
  Bool
finEqual fzero fzero =
  true
finEqual fzero (fsuc j) =
  false
finEqual (fsuc i) fzero =
  false
finEqual (fsuc i) (fsuc j) =
  finEqual i j

select :
  {A : Set} ->
  Bool ->
  A ->
  A ->
  A
select true yes no =
  yes
select false yes no =
  no

Matrix :
  Set ->
  Nat ->
  Set
Matrix R n =
  Fin n -> Fin n -> R

MatrixEqual :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Set
MatrixEqual {n = n} A B =
  (i j : Fin n) ->
  A i j == B i j

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

identityMatrix :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n
identityMatrix reals i j =
  select (finEqual i j)
    (oneR reals)
    (zeroR reals)

matrixMultiply :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n
matrixMultiply reals A B i j =
  sumFin reals
    (\ k ->
      multiply reals
        (A i k)
        (B k j))

matrixPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Nat ->
  Matrix R n
matrixPower reals A zero =
  identityMatrix reals
matrixPower reals A (suc k) =
  matrixMultiply reals A (matrixPower reals A k)

scalarPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
scalarPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
scalarPower reals x (suc k) =
  multiply reals x (scalarPower reals x k)

entrywisePower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Nat ->
  Matrix R n
entrywisePower reals A k i j =
  scalarPower reals (A i j) k

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

putnam-2010-b6 : Set1
putnam-2010-b6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  oneN <=N n ->
  (A : Matrix R n) ->
  (Apow : Nat -> Matrix R n) ->
  ((k : Nat) ->
    oneN <=N k ->
    MatrixEqual (Apow k) (entrywisePower reals A k)) ->
  ((k : Nat) ->
    oneN <=N k ->
    k <=N (n + oneN) ->
    MatrixEqual (matrixPower reals A k) (Apow k)) ->
  (k : Nat) ->
  oneN <=N k ->
  MatrixEqual (matrixPower reals A k) (Apow k)

title: putnam_2010_b6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b6:
  entrywise powers of a positive-dimensional real square matrix agree with
  its ordinary matrix powers for all positive exponents if they agree through
  exponent n + 1. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;

val putnam_2010_b6 =
  ``let matrix_eq =
      \n : num.
      \A B : num -> num -> real.
        !i j : num.
          i < n /\ j < n ==> A i j = B i j
    in
    let matrix_mul =
      \n : num.
      \A B : num -> num -> real.
      \i j : num.
        if i < n /\ j < n
        then SIGMA (\r : num. A i r * B r j) (count n)
        else 0
    in
    let matrix_one =
      \n : num.
      \i j : num.
        if i < n /\ j < n /\ i = j then 1 else 0
    in
    let matrix_pow =
      \n : num.
      \A : num -> num -> real.
      \k : num.
        FUNPOW
          (\B : num -> num -> real. matrix_mul n B A)
          k (matrix_one n)
    in
    let entrywise_pow =
      \A : num -> num -> real.
      \k : num.
      \i j : num.
        A i j pow k
    in
      !n : num.
      !A : num -> num -> real.
        1 <= n
        ==>
        ((!k : num.
            1 <= k /\ k <= n + 1
            ==>
            matrix_eq n (matrix_pow n A k) (entrywise_pow A k))
         ==>
         !k : num.
           1 <= k
           ==>
           matrix_eq n (matrix_pow n A k) (entrywise_pow A k))``;

title: putnam_2010_b6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2010_b6: equality of ordinary and entrywise powers of a real square
  matrix through exponent n+1 implies equality for every positive exponent.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For positive n, the carrier 0 ..^ n is the canonical n-element index set,
  and Base ` ((0 ..^ n) Mat RRfld) is the full set of real n-by-n matrices.
  The operation .g of the matrix ring's multiplicative group gives ordinary
  matrix powers, while the maps-to expression raises each real entry of A to
  the same natural exponent.

  The source function Apow is uniquely fixed at every positive exponent by
  its defining hypothesis. Substituting that entrywise definition in both

title: putnam_2010_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2010_b6:
% agreement of ordinary and entrywise powers of a positive-dimensional real
% square matrix through exponent n+1 forces agreement at every positive
% exponent. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2010_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  matrix(n: posnat): TYPE = [below(n), below(n) -> real]
  matrix_sequence(n: posnat): TYPE = [nat -> matrix(n)]

  bounded_real_sum(
      n: posnat,
      values: [below(n) -> real],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      bounded_real_sum(n, values, count - 1)
        + IF count <= n THEN
            values(count - 1)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  identity_matrix(n: posnat): matrix(n) =
    LAMBDA (row, column: below(n)):
      IF row = column THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF

  matrix_multiply(n: posnat)(A, B: matrix(n)): matrix(n) =
    LAMBDA (row, column: below(n)):
      bounded_real_sum(
        n,
        LAMBDA (inner: below(n)):
          A(row, inner) * B(inner, column),
        n)

  matrix_power(
      n: posnat)(
      A: matrix(n),
      exponent: nat): RECURSIVE matrix(n) =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      identity_matrix(n)
    ELSE
      matrix_multiply(
        n)(
        A,
        matrix_power(n)(A, exponent - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  entrywise_power(
      n: posnat)(
      A: matrix(n),
      exponent: nat): matrix(n) =
    LAMBDA (row, column: below(n)):
      A(row, column) ^ exponent

  putnam_2010_b6: bool =
    FORALL
        (n: posnat),
        (A: matrix(n)),
        (Apow: matrix_sequence(n)):
      (FORALL (k: nat):
        k > 0 IMPLIES
          Apow(k) = entrywise_power(n)(A, k))
      IMPLIES
        ((FORALL (k: nat):
            1 <= k AND k <= n + 1 IMPLIES
              matrix_power(n)(A, k) = Apow(k))
          IMPLIES
            (FORALL (k: nat):
              k >= 1 IMPLIES
                matrix_power(n)(A, k) = Apow(k)))
END putnam_2010_b6

import Mathlib

abbrev putnam_2011_a1_solution : ℕ := sorry
-- 10053
/--
Define a \emph{growing spiral} in the plane to be a sequence of points with integer coordinates $P_0=(0,0),P_1,\dots,P_n$ such that $n \geq 2$ and:
\begin{itemize}
\item the directed line segments $P_0P_1,P_1P_2,\dots,P_{n-1}P_n$ are in the successive coordinate directions east (for $P_0P_1$), north, west, south, east, etc.;
\item the lengths of these line segments are positive and strictly increasing.
\end{itemize}
How many of the points $(x,y)$ with integer coordinates $0 \leq x \leq 2011,0 \leq y \leq 2011$ \emph{cannot} be the last point, $P_n$ of any growing spiral?
-/
theorem putnam_2011_a1
  (IsSpiral : List (Fin 2 → ℤ) → Prop)
  (IsSpiral_def : ∀ P, IsSpiral P ↔ P.length ≥ 3 ∧ P[0]! = 0 ∧
  (∃ l : Fin (P.length - 1) → ℕ, (∀ i, 0 < l i) ∧ StrictMono l ∧ (∀ i : Fin (P.length - 1),
    (i.1 % 4 = 0 → (P[i] 0 + l i = P[i.1 + 1]! 0 ∧ P[i] 1 = P[i.1 + 1]! 1)) ∧
    (i.1 % 4 = 1 → (P[i] 0 = P[i.1 + 1]! 0 ∧ P[i] 1 + l i = P[i.1 + 1]! 1)) ∧
    (i.1 % 4 = 2 → (P[i] 0 - l i = P[i.1 + 1]! 0 ∧ P[i] 1 = P[i.1 + 1]! 1)) ∧
    (i.1 % 4 = 3 → (P[i] 0 = P[i.1 + 1]! 0 ∧ P[i] 1 - l i = P[i.1 + 1]! 1))))) :
  {p | 0 ≤ p 0 ∧ p 0 ≤ 2011 ∧ 0 ≤ p 1 ∧ p 1 ≤ 2011 ∧ ¬∃ spiral, IsSpiral spiral ∧ spiral.getLast! = p}.encard = putnam_2011_a1_solution :=
sorry

title: putnam_2011_a1
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a1:
   counting points with integer coordinates from 0 through 2011 that cannot
   be endpoints of a growing axis-aligned spiral. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import List ZArith.
Import ListNotations.
Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition putnam_2011_a1_point : Type := (Z * Z)%type.

Inductive putnam_2011_a1_direction : Type :=
  | East
  | North
  | West
  | South.

Definition putnam_2011_a1_next_direction
    (direction : putnam_2011_a1_direction)
    : putnam_2011_a1_direction :=
  match direction with
  | East => North
  | North => West
  | West => South
  | South => East
  end.

Definition putnam_2011_a1_step
    (direction : putnam_2011_a1_direction)
    (p q : putnam_2011_a1_point)
    (distance : nat) : Prop :=
  let d := Z.of_nat distance in
  match direction with
  | East =>
      fst q = fst p + d /\ snd q = snd p
  | North =>
      fst q = fst p /\ snd q = snd p + d
  | West =>
      fst q = fst p - d /\ snd q = snd p
  | South =>
      fst q = fst p /\ snd q = snd p - d
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2011_a1_strictly_increasing
    (distances : list nat) : Prop :=
  match distances with
  | [] => True
  | distance :: remaining =>
      Forall (fun later => (distance < later)%nat) remaining /\
      putnam_2011_a1_strictly_increasing remaining
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2011_a1_follows_directions
    (direction : putnam_2011_a1_direction)
    (points : list putnam_2011_a1_point)
    (distances : list nat) : Prop :=
  match points with
  | [] => False
  | p :: remaining_points =>
      match remaining_points, distances with
      | [], [] => True
      | q :: later_points, distance :: later_distances =>
          putnam_2011_a1_step direction p q distance /\
          putnam_2011_a1_follows_directions
            (putnam_2011_a1_next_direction direction)
            (q :: later_points)
            later_distances
      | _, _ => False
      end
  end.

Definition putnam_2011_a1_is_spiral
    (points : list putnam_2011_a1_point) : Prop :=
  (3 <= length points)%nat /\
  hd_error points = Some (0%Z, 0%Z) /\
  exists distances : list nat,
    Forall (fun distance => (0 < distance)%nat) distances /\
    putnam_2011_a1_strictly_increasing distances /\
    putnam_2011_a1_follows_directions East points distances.

Definition putnam_2011_a1_ends_at
    (points : list putnam_2011_a1_point)
    (p : putnam_2011_a1_point) : Prop :=
  exists prefix, points = prefix ++ [p].

Definition putnam_2011_a1_unreachable
    (p : putnam_2011_a1_point) : Prop :=
  0 <= fst p /\ fst p <= 2011 /\
  0 <= snd p /\ snd p <= 2011 /\
  ~ exists spiral,
      putnam_2011_a1_is_spiral spiral /\
      putnam_2011_a1_ends_at spiral p.

Definition putnam_2011_a1_has_cardinality
    {A : Type} (members : A -> Prop) (n : nat) : Prop :=
  exists elements : list A,
    NoDup elements /\
    length elements = n /\
    forall x : A, In x elements <-> members x.

Theorem putnam_2011_a1 :
  putnam_2011_a1_has_cardinality putnam_2011_a1_unreachable 10053.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a1:
  exactly 10053 integer points in the 2011 by 2011 coordinate box cannot be
  endpoints of growing lattice spirals with positive strictly increasing
  segment lengths. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let is_spiral =
     \P:(int#int)list.
       3 <= LENGTH P /\
       EL 0 P = ((&0:int),(&0:int)) /\
       ?l:num->num.
         (!i:num. i + 1 < LENGTH P ==> 0 < l i) /\
         (!i j:num.
            i < j /\ j + 1 < LENGTH P
            ==> l i < l j) /\
         (!i:num.
            i + 1 < LENGTH P
            ==>
            (i MOD 4 = 0
             ==> FST (EL i P) + (&(l i):int) = FST (EL (i + 1) P) /\
                 SND (EL i P) = SND (EL (i + 1) P)) /\
            (i MOD 4 = 1
             ==> FST (EL i P) = FST (EL (i + 1) P) /\
                 SND (EL i P) + (&(l i):int) = SND (EL (i + 1) P)) /\
            (i MOD 4 = 2
             ==> FST (EL i P) - (&(l i):int) = FST (EL (i + 1) P) /\
                 SND (EL i P) = SND (EL (i + 1) P)) /\
            (i MOD 4 = 3
             ==> FST (EL i P) = FST (EL (i + 1) P) /\
                 SND (EL i P) - (&(l i):int) = SND (EL (i + 1) P))) in
   CARD
     {p:int#int |
        (&0:int) <= FST p /\ FST p <= &2011 /\
        (&0:int) <= SND p /\ SND p <= &2011 /\
        ~(?P:(int#int)list. is_spiral P /\ LAST P = p)} =
   10053`;;

;; exactly 10053 integer points in the square from (0,0) through (2011,2011)
;; cannot be endpoints of growing axis-aligned spirals. This file contains no
;; proof.

;; A point is represented by the two-element list (x y), and a spiral by a
;; true list of such points. This is a bijective encoding of the source lists
;; of integer-coordinate pairs. The three lambdas traversing a witness use
;; only tame ACL2 primitives and standard APPLY$ scions.

;; The source existential quantifier remains internal. Every source spiral and
;; its positive strictly increasing length sequence form one two-element ACL2
;; witness, and every accepted witness decodes to such a source spiral.

title: putnam_2011_a1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2011_a1): exactly 10053 integer points in the
-- 2011 by 2011 coordinate square cannot end a growing axis-aligned spiral.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2011A1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_ _<=Z_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

record Top : Set where
  constructor truth

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data _<=Z_ : Int -> Int -> Set where
  negative<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    negsuc m <=Z pos n
  positive<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    m <=N n ->
    pos m <=Z pos n
  negative<=negative :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    n <=N m ->
    negsuc m <=Z negsuc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

Predicate : Set -> Set1
Predicate A =
  A -> Set

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : Predicate A)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A

    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)

    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> item == enumerate index)

    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

length : {A : Set} -> List A -> Nat
length [] =
  zero
length (_ ∷ xs) =
  suc (length xs)

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

subtractInt : Int -> Int -> Int
subtractInt x y =
  addInt x (negateInt y)

record Point : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : Int
    y-coordinate : Int

open Point

origin : Point
origin =
  point (pos zero) (pos zero)

data Direction : Set where
  east north west south : Direction

nextDirection : Direction -> Direction
nextDirection east =
  north
nextDirection north =
  west
nextDirection west =
  south
nextDirection south =
  east

Step : Direction -> Nat -> Point -> Point -> Set
Step east segmentLength p q =
  (x-coordinate q == addInt (x-coordinate p) (pos segmentLength))
  and
  (y-coordinate q == y-coordinate p)
Step north segmentLength p q =
  (x-coordinate q == x-coordinate p)
  and
  (y-coordinate q == addInt (y-coordinate p) (pos segmentLength))
Step west segmentLength p q =
  (x-coordinate q == subtractInt (x-coordinate p) (pos segmentLength))
  and
  (y-coordinate q == y-coordinate p)
Step south segmentLength p q =
  (x-coordinate q == x-coordinate p)
  and
  (y-coordinate q == subtractInt (y-coordinate p) (pos segmentLength))

AllPositive : List Nat -> Set
AllPositive [] =
  Top
AllPositive (n ∷ ns) =
  (zero <N n) and AllPositive ns

StrictlyIncreasing : List Nat -> Set
StrictlyIncreasing [] =
  Top
StrictlyIncreasing (_ ∷ []) =
  Top
StrictlyIncreasing (m ∷ n ∷ ns) =
  (m <N n) and StrictlyIncreasing (n ∷ ns)

Follows :
  Direction ->
  List Nat ->
  List Point ->
  Set
Follows direction [] [] =
  Bottom
Follows direction [] (_ ∷ []) =
  Top
Follows direction [] (_ ∷ _ ∷ _) =
  Bottom
Follows direction (_ ∷ _) [] =
  Bottom
Follows direction (_ ∷ _) (_ ∷ []) =
  Bottom
Follows direction (segmentLength ∷ lengths) (p ∷ q ∷ points) =
  Step direction segmentLength p q
  and
  Follows (nextDirection direction) lengths (q ∷ points)

HeadIsOrigin : List Point -> Set
HeadIsOrigin [] =
  Bottom
HeadIsOrigin (p ∷ _) =
  p == origin

LastIs : List Point -> Point -> Set
LastIs [] endpoint =
  Bottom
LastIs (p ∷ []) endpoint =
  p == endpoint
LastIs (_ ∷ q ∷ points) endpoint =
  LastIs (q ∷ points) endpoint

GrowingSpiral : List Point -> Set
GrowingSpiral points =
  HeadIsOrigin points
  and
  Exists (List Nat)
    (\ lengths ->
      (suc (length lengths) == length points)
      and
      ((suc (suc zero) <=N length lengths)
      and
      (AllPositive lengths
      and
      (StrictlyIncreasing lengths
      and
      Follows east lengths points))))

InCoordinateSquare : Point -> Set
InCoordinateSquare p =
  ((pos zero <=Z x-coordinate p)
  and
  (x-coordinate p <=Z pos 2011))
  and
  ((pos zero <=Z y-coordinate p)
  and
  (y-coordinate p <=Z pos 2011))

CanEndGrowingSpiral : Point -> Set
CanEndGrowingSpiral endpoint =
  Exists (List Point)
    (\ points ->
      GrowingSpiral points
      and
      LastIs points endpoint)

UnreachablePoint : Point -> Set
UnreachablePoint p =
  InCoordinateSquare p
  and
  Not (CanEndGrowingSpiral p)

putnam-2011-a1 : Set
putnam-2011-a1 =
  HasCardinality UnreachablePoint 10053

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a1:
  the number of integer points in the coordinate square [0,2011] x [0,2011]
  that
  cannot be endpoints of growing axis-aligned spirals is 10053. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2011_a1 =
  ``let is_spiral =
      \P : (int # int) list.
        3 <= LENGTH P /\
        EL 0 P = (0, 0) /\
        ?l : num -> num.
          (!i : num.
             i < LENGTH P - 1
             ==>
             0 < l i) /\
          (!i j : num.
             i < j /\ j < LENGTH P - 1
             ==>
             l i < l j) /\
          (!i : num.
             i < LENGTH P - 1
             ==>
             (i MOD 4 = 0
              ==>
              FST (EL (i + 1) P) =
                FST (EL i P) + int_of_num (l i) /\
              SND (EL (i + 1) P) = SND (EL i P)) /\
             (i MOD 4 = 1
              ==>
              FST (EL (i + 1) P) = FST (EL i P) /\
              SND (EL (i + 1) P) =
                SND (EL i P) + int_of_num (l i)) /\
             (i MOD 4 = 2
              ==>
              FST (EL (i + 1) P) =
                FST (EL i P) - int_of_num (l i) /\
              SND (EL (i + 1) P) = SND (EL i P)) /\
             (i MOD 4 = 3
              ==>
              FST (EL (i + 1) P) = FST (EL i P) /\
              SND (EL (i + 1) P) =
                SND (EL i P) - int_of_num (l i)))
    in
      CARD
        {p : int # int |
           0 <= FST p /\ FST p <= 2011 /\
           0 <= SND p /\ SND p <= 2011 /\
           ~?spiral : (int # int) list.
             is_spiral spiral /\ LAST spiral = p} =
      10053``;

  putnam_2011_a1: the number of integer points in the 2011 by 2011
  nonnegative coordinate square that cannot be endpoints of growing spirals.
  This file contains no proof.

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  A path with N steps is represented by a function P on 0 ... N, so it has
  exactly N + 1 integer-coordinate points. Its length function L is defined
  on 0 ..^ N, the step indices. Requiring N >= 2 matches the source's
  requirement of at least three points.

  P11A1Spiral requires P(0) = (0,0), positive integer step lengths, strict
  increase of those lengths, and the successive directions east, north,
  west, and south according to the step index modulo four. P11A1Endpoints
  is the set of endpoints of all such finite paths. Finite function
  sequences and ordered integer pairs are bijectively equivalent to the
  source lists of two-coordinate integer vectors.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P11A1Spiral P11A1Endpoints $.

p11a1-spiral-syntax $a wff ( P11A1Spiral P N L ) $.
p11a1-endpoints-syntax $a class P11A1Endpoints $.

${
  $d L N P i j $.

  p11a1-spiral-definition $a |- (
    ( P11A1Spiral P N L )
    <->
    (
      (
        N e. NN
        /\
        2 <_ N
      )
      /\
      (
        P : ( 0 ... N ) --> ( ZZ X. ZZ )
        /\
        (
          L : ( 0 ..^ N ) --> NN
          /\
          (
            ( P ` 0 ) = <. 0 , 0 >.
            /\
            (
              A. i e. ( 0 ..^ N ) A. j e. ( 0 ..^ N )
                (
                  i < j
                  ->
                  ( L ` i ) < ( L ` j )
                )
              /\
              A. i e. ( 0 ..^ N )
                (
                  (
                    ( i mod 4 ) = 0
                    ->
                    (
                      ( 1st ` ( P ` ( i + 1 ) ) )
                      =
                      ( ( 1st ` ( P ` i ) ) + ( L ` i ) )
                      /\
                      ( 2nd ` ( P ` ( i + 1 ) ) )
                      =
                      ( 2nd ` ( P ` i ) )
                    )
                  )
                  /\
                  (
                    (
                      ( i mod 4 ) = 1
                      ->
                      (
                        ( 1st ` ( P ` ( i + 1 ) ) )
                        =
                        ( 1st ` ( P ` i ) )
                        /\
                        ( 2nd ` ( P ` ( i + 1 ) ) )
                        =
                        ( ( 2nd ` ( P ` i ) ) + ( L ` i ) )
                      )
                    )
                    /\
                    (
                      (
                        ( i mod 4 ) = 2
                        ->
                        (
                          ( 1st ` ( P ` ( i + 1 ) ) )
                          =
                          ( ( 1st ` ( P ` i ) ) - ( L ` i ) )
                          /\
                          ( 2nd ` ( P ` ( i + 1 ) ) )
                          =
                          ( 2nd ` ( P ` i ) )
                        )
                      )
                      /\
                      (
                        ( i mod 4 ) = 3
                        ->
                        (
                          ( 1st ` ( P ` ( i + 1 ) ) )
                          =
                          ( 1st ` ( P ` i ) )
                          /\
                          ( 2nd ` ( P ` ( i + 1 ) ) )
                          =
                          ( ( 2nd ` ( P ` i ) ) - ( L ` i ) )
                        )
                      )
                    )
                  )
                )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d f l n p $.

  p11a1-endpoints-definition $a |- P11A1Endpoints = {
    p e. ( ZZ X. ZZ ) |
    E. n E. f E. l
      (
        ( P11A1Spiral f n l )
        /\
        ( f ` n ) = p
      )
  } $.
$}

putnambench-putnam-2011-a1 $a |- (
  #
  `
  {
    p e. ( ZZ X. ZZ ) |
    (
      (
        0 <_ ( 1st ` p )
        /\
        ( 1st ` p ) <_ ; ; ; 2 0 1 1
      )

          /\
          ( 2nd ` p ) <_ ; ; ; 2 0 1 1
        )
        /\
        -. p e. P11A1Endpoints
      )
    )

) = ; ; ; ; 1 0 0 5 3 $.

content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a1:
% exactly 10053 integer points with coordinates between 0 and 2011 cannot be
% endpoints of growing spirals with positive strictly increasing lengths.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2011_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: int, y_coord: int #]
  point_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> point]
  length_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  IMPORTING finite_sets[point]

  origin: point = (# x_coord := 0, y_coord := 0 #)

  positive_below(lengths: length_sequence, segment_count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < segment_count IMPLIES lengths(index) > 0

  strictly_increasing_below(
      lengths: length_sequence,
      segment_count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (left, right: nat):
      left < right AND right < segment_count
        IMPLIES lengths(left) < lengths(right)

  directed_segment(
      points: point_sequence,
      lengths: length_sequence,
      index: nat): bool =
    (mod(index, 4) = 0 IMPLIES
      x_coord(points(index + 1))
        = x_coord(points(index)) + (lengths(index) :: int)
        AND y_coord(points(index + 1)) = y_coord(points(index)))
      AND
    (mod(index, 4) = 1 IMPLIES
      x_coord(points(index + 1)) = x_coord(points(index))
        AND y_coord(points(index + 1))
          = y_coord(points(index)) + (lengths(index) :: int))
      AND
    (mod(index, 4) = 2 IMPLIES
      x_coord(points(index + 1))
        = x_coord(points(index)) - (lengths(index) :: int)
        AND y_coord(points(index + 1)) = y_coord(points(index)))
      AND
    (mod(index, 4) = 3 IMPLIES
      x_coord(points(index + 1)) = x_coord(points(index))
        AND y_coord(points(index + 1))
          = y_coord(points(index)) - (lengths(index) :: int))

  growing_spiral(
      points: point_sequence,
      segment_count: nat): bool =
    segment_count >= 2
      AND points(0) = origin
      AND EXISTS (lengths: length_sequence):
        positive_below(lengths, segment_count)
          AND strictly_increasing_below(lengths, segment_count)
          AND (FORALL (index: nat):
            index < segment_count IMPLIES
              directed_segment(points, lengths, index))

  reachable_endpoint(P: point): bool =
    EXISTS (points: point_sequence), (segment_count: nat):
      growing_spiral(points, segment_count)
        AND points(segment_count) = P

  grid_point(P: point): bool =
    0 <= x_coord(P)
      AND x_coord(P) <= 2011
      AND 0 <= y_coord(P)
      AND y_coord(P) <= 2011

  putnam_2011_a1_solution: nat = 10053

  putnam_2011_a1: bool =
    EXISTS (unreachable_points: finite_set[point]):
      card(unreachable_points) = putnam_2011_a1_solution
        AND (FORALL (P: point):
          unreachable_points(P)
            IFF grid_point(P) AND NOT reachable_endpoint(P))
END putnam_2011_a1

-- 3/2
/--
Let $a_1,a_2,\dots$ and $b_1,b_2,\dots$ be sequences of positive real numbers such that $a_1 = b_1 = 1$ and $b_n = b_{n-1} a_n - 2$ for$n=2,3,\dots$. Assume that the sequence $(b_j)$ is bounded. Prove tha \[ S = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{a_1...a_n} \] converges, and evaluate $S$.
-/
theorem putnam_2011_a2
(a b : ℕ → ℝ)
(habn : ∀ n : ℕ, a n > 0 ∧ b n > 0)
(hab1 : a 0 = 1 ∧ b 0 = 1)
(hb : ∀ n ≥ 1, b n = b (n-1) * a n - 2)
(hbnd : ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, |b n| ≤ B)
: Tendsto (fun n => ∑ i : Fin n, 1/(∏ j : Fin (i + 1), (a j))) atTop (𝓝 putnam_2011_a2_solution) :=
sorry

From mathcomp Require Import all_algebra all_ssreflect.
From mathcomp Require Import reals sequences topology normedtype.
From mathcomp Require Import classical_sets.
Import numFieldNormedType.Exports.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.
Local Open Scope classical_set_scope.

Variable R : realType.
Definition putnam_2011_a2_solution : R := 3/2.
Theorem putnam_2011_a2
    (a b : R ^nat)
    (habn : forall n : nat, a n > 0 /\ b n > 0)
    (hab1 : a 0%nat = 1 /\ b 0%nat = 1)
    (hb : forall n : nat, ge n 1 -> b n = b (n.-1) * a n - 2)
    (hbnd : exists B : R, forall n : nat, `|b n| <= B)
    : (fun n : nat =>
        \sum_(i < n) 1 / (\prod_(j < i.+1) (a j))) @ \oo -->
      putnam_2011_a2_solution.
Proof. Admitted.

definition putnam_2011_a2_solution :: real where "putnam_2011_a2_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* 3/2 *)
theorem putnam_2011_a2:
  fixes a b :: "nat \<Rightarrow> real"
  assumes habn: "\<forall>n::nat. a n > 0 \<and> b n > 0"
  and hab1: "a 0 = 1 \<and> b 0 = 1"
  and hb: "\<forall>n::nat\<ge>1. b n = b (n-1) * a n - 2"
  and hbnd: "\<exists>B::real. \<forall>n::nat. \<bar>b n\<bar> \<le> B"
  shows "filterlim (\<lambda>n::nat. \<Sum>i::nat=0..(n-1). 1 / (\<Prod>j::nat=0..i. a j)) (nhds putnam_2011_a2_solution) at_top"
  sorry

end
