(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2011_a3: the positive limiting value of a ratio of sine- and
  cosine-weighted real-power integrals on (0, pi/2), after normalization by
  a real power of the parameter. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory realTheory transcTheory netsTheory real_topologyTheory;
open extrealTheory measureTheory borelTheory lebesgueTheory;

val putnam_2011_a3 =
  ``let c = (-1 : real) in
    let L = 2 / pi in
    let domain = {x : real | 0 < x /\ x < pi / 2} in
      L > 0 /\
      ((\r : real.
          (r powr c *
             real
               (integral lborel
                 (\x.
                    Normal (x powr r * sin x) *
                    indicator_fn domain x))) /
          real
            (integral lborel
              (\x.
                 Normal (x powr r * cos x) *
                 indicator_fn domain x))) -->
       L) at_posinfinity``;

title: putnam_2011_a3
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2011_a3: the choice c = -1 and L = 2 / pi gives a positive
  real limit for the specified ratio of two trigonometric power integrals.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  Set.mm's S. binder is the real Lebesgue integral. The open interval
  ( 0 , pi / 2 ) exactly matches the primary Lean and Isabelle sources.
  On this interval x is positive, so x ^c r is real-valued and agrees with
  their real-power operation for every real exponent r.

  The maps-to expression retains the source's arbitrary real parameter r,
  and ~~>r is set.mm's finite real limit at positive infinity. The factor
  r ^c ( -1 ) is the source factor r^c for the explicit solution c = -1;
  its values away from the eventually positive part of the real line do not
  affect the limit. The target 2 / _pi is the explicit positive value given
  by the Rocq source and by the solution annotations in the Lean and
  Isabelle sources.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d r x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2011-a3 $a |- (
    0 < ( 2 / _pi )
    /\
    (
      (
        r e. RR |->
          (
            (
              ( r ^c ( -u 1 ) )
              x.
              S. ( 0 (,) ( _pi / 2 ) )
                (
                  ( x ^c r )
                  x.
                  ( sin ` x )
                )
                _d x
            )
            /
            S. ( 0 (,) ( _pi / 2 ) )
              (
                ( x ^c r )
                x.
                ( cos ` x )
              )
              _d x
          )
      )
      ~~>r
      ( 2 / _pi )
    )
  ) $.
$}

title: putnam_2011_a3
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a3
:: (putnambench__mizar__putnam_2011_a3): the scaled ratio of the sine- and
:: cosine-weighted power integrals on (0, pi/2) has the specified positive
:: limit as the real exponent tends to positive infinity. This file contains
:: no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    PARTFUN1, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, COMPLEX1, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1,
    ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, REAL_1, NAT_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, ORDINAL1,
    NEWTON, PREPOWER, POWER, SUPINF_2, MEASURE1, MESFUNC1, MESFUNC5,
    MEASUR12, INTEGRA5, SIN_COS, LIMFUNC1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    PARTFUN1, FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    REAL_1, COMPLEX1, XXREAL_0, XXREAL_1, XXREAL_3, NEWTON, PREPOWER,
    POWER, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, SIN_COS, SUPINF_2, MEASURE1, MESFUNC1,
    MESFUNC5, MESFUNC6, MEASUR12, INTEGRA5, EXTREAL1, LIMFUNC1;
  constructors FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1, REAL_1, COMPLEX1,
    NAT_1, NEWTON, PREPOWER, POWER, SIN_COS, MESFUNC1, MESFUNC5,
    MESFUNC6, MEASUR12, INTEGRA5, EXTREAL1, LIMFUNC1, BINOP_2;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, CARD_1, XXREAL_0, MEMBERED, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, NAT_1, NEWTON, PREPOWER,
    XXREAL_3, MEASURE1, MEASUR12, SIN_COS;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;
  definitions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0;
  expansions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  ex c,L being Real,
     I being Subset of REAL,
     F being Function of REAL,REAL st
    c = -1 &
    L = 2 / PI &
    0 < L &
    I = {x where x is Real : 0 < x & x < PI / 2} &
    (for r being Real holds
      ex f,g being Function of REAL,REAL st
        (for x being Real st x in I holds
          f.x = (x to_power r) * sin.x &
          g.x = (x to_power r) * cos.x) &
        F.r =
          ((r to_power c) * Integral(L-Meas,f|I)) /
            Integral(L-Meas,g|I)) &
    F is convergent_in+infty &
    lim_in+infty F = L
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2011_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a3:
% the real-power scaling and positive finite limit of a ratio of sine- and
% cosine-weighted power integrals on (0, pi/2). This file contains no proof.

putnam_2011_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  sine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        sine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index + 1),
              nat_factorial(2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  cosine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        cosine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index),
              nat_factorial(2 * index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  natural_log(x: real): real =
    IF x > 0 THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (value: real):
          real_exponential(value) = x)
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  real_power(base, exponent: real): real =
    IF base > 0 THEN
      real_exponential(exponent * natural_log(base))
    ELSIF base = 0 AND exponent = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  sine(argument: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            sine_partial(argument, count),
          value))

  cosine(argument: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            cosine_partial(argument, count),
          value))

  pi_value(value: real): bool =
    3 < value
      AND value < 4
      AND cosine(value / 2) = 0

  pi: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        pi_value(value))

  valid_tagged_partition(
      left, right: real,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = left
      AND points(count) = right
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          (points(index) < points(index + 1)
            AND points(index) <= tags(index)
            AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1))

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      function_value: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(
        function_value, points, tags, count - 1)
        + function_value(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_interval_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      left, right, integral_value: real): bool =
    left < right
      AND FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
          FORALL
              (points, tags: real_sequence),
              (count: nat):
            (valid_tagged_partition(
                left, right, points, tags, count)
              AND mesh_less_than(
                points, count, mesh_bound))
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                riemann_sum(
                  function_value, points, tags, count)
                  - integral_value)
                < epsilon_value

  interval_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      left, right: real): real =
    IF left = right THEN
      0
    ELSIF left < right THEN
      IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
          has_interval_integral(
            function_value, left, right, integral_value)
      THEN
        epsilon(
          LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
            has_interval_integral(
              function_value, left, right, integral_value))
      ELSE
        0
      ENDIF
    ELSE
      IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
          has_interval_integral(
            function_value, right, left, integral_value)
      THEN
        -epsilon(
          LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
            has_interval_integral(
              function_value, right, left, integral_value))
      ELSE
        0
      ENDIF
    ENDIF

  sine_integral(r: real): real =
    interval_integral(
      LAMBDA (x: real):
        real_power(x, r) * sine(x),
      0,
      pi / 2)

  cosine_integral(r: real): real =
    interval_integral(
      LAMBDA (x: real):
        real_power(x, r) * cosine(x),
      0,
      pi / 2)

  scaled_integral_ratio(r, c: real): real =
    safe_div(
      real_power(r, c) * sine_integral(r),
      cosine_integral(r))

  converges_at_real_top(
      function_value: real_function,
      limit_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: real):
        FORALL (r: real):
          cutoff <= r IMPLIES
            abs(function_value(r) - limit_value)
              < epsilon_value

  putnam_2011_a3: bool =
    EXISTS (c, limit_value: real):
      c = -1
        AND limit_value = safe_div(2, pi)
        AND limit_value > 0
        AND converges_at_real_top(
          LAMBDA (r: real):
            scaled_integral_ratio(r, c),
          limit_value)
END putnam_2011_a3

import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Matrix

abbrev putnam_2011_a4_solution : Set ℕ := sorry
-- {n : ℕ | Odd n}
/--
For which positive integers $n$ is there an $n \times n$ matrix with integer entries such that every dot product of a row with itself is even, while every dot product of two different rows is odd?
-/
theorem putnam_2011_a4
    (nmat : ℕ → Prop)
    (hnmat : ∀ n, nmat n ↔
      ∃ A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℤ,
        (∀ r, Even ((A r) ⬝ᵥ (A r))) ∧
        Pairwise fun r1 r2 ↦ Odd ((A r1) ⬝ᵥ (A r2)))
    (n : ℕ) (npos : 0 < n) :
    nmat n ↔ n ∈ putnam_2011_a4_solution :=
  sorry

title: putnam_2011_a4
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a4:
   positive dimensions admitting an integer matrix with even row norms and
   odd dot products between distinct rows. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Vectors.Fin ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition putnam_2011_a4_matrix (n : nat) : Type :=
  Fin.t n -> Fin.t n -> Z.

Fixpoint putnam_2011_a4_fin_sum
    (n : nat) : (Fin.t n -> Z) -> Z :=
  match n as m return (Fin.t m -> Z) -> Z with
  | O => fun _ => 0
  | S k =>
      fun f =>
        f Fin.F1 +
        putnam_2011_a4_fin_sum k (fun i => f (Fin.FS i))
  end.

Definition putnam_2011_a4_row_dot
    {n : nat}
    (A : putnam_2011_a4_matrix n)
    (r1 r2 : Fin.t n) : Z :=
  putnam_2011_a4_fin_sum n (fun c => A r1 c * A r2 c).

Definition putnam_2011_a4_solution (n : nat) : Prop :=
  Nat.Odd n.

Theorem putnam_2011_a4
    (nmat : nat -> Prop)
    (hnmat :
      forall n : nat,
        nmat n <->
        exists A : putnam_2011_a4_matrix n,
          (forall r : Fin.t n,
            Z.even (putnam_2011_a4_row_dot A r r) = true) /\
          (forall r1 r2 : Fin.t n,
            r1 <> r2 ->
            Z.odd (putnam_2011_a4_row_dot A r1 r2) = true))
    (n : nat)
    (npos : (0 < n)%nat) :
  nmat n <-> putnam_2011_a4_solution n.
Admitted.

  positive matrix orders admitting an integer matrix whose row self-dot
  products are even and whose distinct-row dot products are odd are exactly

let statement =

     \x:int. ?k:int. x = &2 * k in
   let odd_integer =
     \x:int. ?k:int. x = &2 * k + &1 in
   let row_dot =
     \n:num. \A:num->num->int. \r s:num.
       isum (0..n - 1) (\j:num. A r j * A s j) in

         (!r:num.

title: putnam_2011_a4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a4:
;; a positive integer n admits an n by n integer matrix with even row
;; self-dot-products and odd dot products between distinct rows exactly when
;; n is odd. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A matrix is represented by its row-major list of exactly n^2 integer
;; entries. This is a bijective encoding of Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Z.
;; Negated FN-EQUAL retains the matrix as an internal existential witness.
;; The tame row-pair predicate ranges over every ordered pair of row indices;
;; SUM$+ computes the corresponding finite integer dot product exactly.

(defun putnam-2011-a4-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-list-term (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'cons
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2011-a4-list-term (cdr terms)))
    (putnam-2011-a4-quoted nil)))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'if
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2011-a4-and-terms (cdr terms))
       (putnam-2011-a4-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2011-a4-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-multiply-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-* left right))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-range-term (upper)
  (list
   'from-to-by
   (putnam-2011-a4-quoted 0)
   upper
   (putnam-2011-a4-quoted 1)))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-iteration-term (values)
  (list
   'loop$-as
   (putnam-2011-a4-list-term
    (list values))))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-integer-entry-function ()
  '(lambda (globals entry)
     (integerp (car entry))))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-dot-summand-function ()
  (let* ((matrix (list 'car 'globals))
         (n (list 'nth
                  (putnam-2011-a4-quoted 1)
                  'globals))
         (left-row (list 'nth
                         (putnam-2011-a4-quoted 2)
                         'globals))
         (right-row (list 'nth
                          (putnam-2011-a4-quoted 3)
                          'globals))
         (column (list 'car 'entry))
         (left-index
          (putnam-2011-a4-add-term
           (putnam-2011-a4-multiply-term left-row n)
           column))
         (right-index
          (putnam-2011-a4-add-term
           (putnam-2011-a4-multiply-term right-row n)
           column)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(globals entry)
     (putnam-2011-a4-multiply-term
      (list 'nth left-index matrix)
      (list 'nth right-index matrix)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-dot-product-term
    (matrix n left-row right-row)
  (let ((summand-function
         (putnam-2011-a4-dot-summand-function)))
    (list
     'sum$+
     (putnam-2011-a4-quoted summand-function)
     (putnam-2011-a4-list-term
      (list matrix n left-row right-row))
     (putnam-2011-a4-iteration-term
      (putnam-2011-a4-range-term
       (putnam-2011-a4-add-term
        n
        (putnam-2011-a4-quoted -1)))))))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-row-pair-function ()
  (let* ((matrix (list 'car 'globals))
         (n (list 'nth
                  (putnam-2011-a4-quoted 1)
                  'globals))
         (pair-index (list 'car 'entry))
         (left-row (list 'floor pair-index n))
         (right-row (list 'mod pair-index n))
         (dot-product
          (putnam-2011-a4-dot-product-term
           matrix n left-row right-row)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(globals entry)
     (list
      'if
      (list 'equal left-row right-row)
      (list 'evenp dot-product)
      (list 'oddp dot-product)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-witness-failure-function (n)
  (let* ((integer-entry-function
          (putnam-2011-a4-integer-entry-function))
         (row-pair-function
          (putnam-2011-a4-row-pair-function))
         (quoted-n (putnam-2011-a4-quoted n))
         (entry-count
          (putnam-2011-a4-multiply-term quoted-n quoted-n))
         (last-index
          (putnam-2011-a4-add-term
           entry-count
           (putnam-2011-a4-quoted -1)))
         (qualification
          (putnam-2011-a4-and-terms
           (list
            (list 'true-listp 'matrix)
            (list 'equal
                  (list 'len 'matrix)
                  entry-count)
            (list
             'always$+
             (putnam-2011-a4-quoted integer-entry-function)
             (putnam-2011-a4-quoted nil)
             (putnam-2011-a4-iteration-term 'matrix))
            (list
             'always$+
             (putnam-2011-a4-quoted row-pair-function)
             (putnam-2011-a4-list-term
              (list 'matrix quoted-n))
             (putnam-2011-a4-iteration-term
              (putnam-2011-a4-range-term last-index)))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(matrix)
     (list
      'if
      qualification
      (putnam-2011-a4-quoted nil)
      (putnam-2011-a4-quoted t)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-true-function ()
  '(lambda (matrix) 't))

(defun putnam-2011-a4-matrix-exists-p (n)
  (let* ((integer-entry-function
          (putnam-2011-a4-integer-entry-function))
         (dot-summand-function
          (putnam-2011-a4-dot-summand-function))
         (row-pair-function
          (putnam-2011-a4-row-pair-function))
         (failure-function
          (putnam-2011-a4-witness-failure-function n))
         (true-function
          (putnam-2011-a4-true-function)))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp integer-entry-function)
     (tamep-functionp dot-summand-function)
     (tamep-functionp row-pair-function)
     (tamep-functionp failure-function)
     (tamep-functionp true-function)
     (not
      (fn-equal failure-function true-function)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2011-a4-statement (n)
  (implies
   (posp n)
   (iff
    (putnam-2011-a4-matrix-exists-p n)
    (oddp n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2011_a4): positive sizes admitting a square
-- integer matrix with even row self-dot-products and odd dot-products between
-- distinct rows are exactly the odd sizes. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2011A4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixl 6 _+Z_
infixl 7 _*Z_
infixr 3 _and_
infix 2 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data OddNat : Nat -> Set where
  odd-one  : OddNat (suc zero)
  odd-step : {n : Nat} -> OddNat n -> OddNat (suc (suc n))

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

_+Z_ : Int -> Int -> Int
pos m +Z pos n =
  pos (m + n)
pos m +Z negsuc n =
  difference m (suc n)
negsuc m +Z pos n =
  difference n (suc m)
negsuc m +Z negsuc n =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

_*Z_ : Int -> Int -> Int
pos m *Z pos n =
  pos (m * n)
pos m *Z negsuc n =
  negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *Z pos n =
  negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *Z negsuc n =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos (suc zero)

twoZ : Int
twoZ =
  pos (suc (suc zero))

EvenInt : Int -> Set
EvenInt value =
  Exists Int
    (\ half -> value == twoZ *Z half)

OddInt : Int -> Set
OddInt value =
  Exists Int
    (\ half -> value == (twoZ *Z half) +Z oneZ)

Matrix : Nat -> Set
Matrix n =
  Fin n -> Fin n -> Int

sumFinInt :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Int) ->
  Int
sumFinInt {zero} terms =
  pos zero
sumFinInt {suc n} terms =
  terms fzero +Z
  sumFinInt (\ i -> terms (fsuc i))

rowDot :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix n ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n ->
  Int
rowDot {n} A leftRow rightRow =
  sumFinInt
    (\ column ->
      A leftRow column *Z A rightRow column)

RequiredRowParities :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix n ->
  Set
RequiredRowParities {n} A =
  ((row : Fin n) ->
    EvenInt (rowDot A row row))
  and
  ((leftRow rightRow : Fin n) ->
    leftRow != rightRow ->
    OddInt (rowDot A leftRow rightRow))

AdmitsRequiredMatrix : Nat -> Set
AdmitsRequiredMatrix n =
  Exists (Matrix n) RequiredRowParities

putnam-2011-a4 : Set
putnam-2011-a4 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  AdmitsRequiredMatrix n iff OddNat n

  positive sizes admitting an integer square matrix whose row self-dot-products
  are even and whose distinct-row dot-products are odd are exactly the odd
  sizes. This file contains no proof.

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2011_a4 =
  ``!n : num.

             r < n

title: putnam_2011_a4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a4:
% positive dimensions admitting an integer square matrix with even row
% self-dot-products and odd dot-products between distinct rows are exactly
% the odd dimensions. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2011_a4: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_matrix(n: posnat): TYPE =
    [below(n), below(n) -> int]

  bounded_integer_sum(
      n: posnat,
      values: [below(n) -> int],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      bounded_integer_sum(n, values, count - 1)
        + IF count <= n THEN
            values(count - 1)
          ELSE
            0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  row_dot_product(
      n: posnat,
      A: integer_matrix(n),
      first_row, second_row: below(n)): int =
    bounded_integer_sum(
      n,
      LAMBDA (column: below(n)):
        A(first_row, column) * A(second_row, column),
      n)

  even_integer(value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (half: int):
      value = 2 * half

  odd_integer(value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (half: int):
      value = 2 * half + 1

  has_required_matrix(n: posnat): bool =
    EXISTS (A: integer_matrix(n)):
      (FORALL (row: below(n)):
        even_integer(row_dot_product(n, A, row, row)))
        AND
      (FORALL (first_row, second_row: below(n)):
        first_row /= second_row IMPLIES
          odd_integer(
            row_dot_product(
              n, A, first_row, second_row)))

  putnam_2011_a4_solution(n: posnat): bool =
    EXISTS (half: nat):
      n = 2 * half + 1

  putnam_2011_a4: bool =
    FORALL (n: posnat):
      has_required_matrix(n)
        IFF putnam_2011_a4_solution(n)
END putnam_2011_a4

import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Matrix

/--
Let $F:\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ and $g:\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be twice continuously differentiable functions with the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item $F(u,u)=0$ for every $u \in \mathbb{R}$;
\item for every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, $g(x)>0$ and $x^2g(x) \leq 1$;
\item for every $(u,v) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, the vector $\nabla F(u,v)$ is either $\mathbf{0}$ or parallel to the vector $\langle g(u),-g(v) \rangle$.
\end{itemize}
Prove that there exists a constant $C$ such that for every $n \geq 2$ and any $x_1,\dots,x_{n+1} \in \mathbb{R}$, we have $\min_{i \neq j} |F(x_i,x_j)| \leq \frac{C}{n}$.
-/
theorem putnam_2011_a5
(F : (Fin 2 → ℝ) → ℝ)
(g : ℝ → ℝ)
(vec : ℝ → ℝ → (Fin 2 → ℝ))
(Fgrad : (Fin 2 → ℝ) → (Fin 2 → ℝ))
(parallel : (Fin 2 → ℝ) → (Fin 2 → ℝ) → Prop)
(hparallel : parallel = (fun u v : Fin 2 → ℝ => ∃ c : ℝ, u = c • v))
(Fgdiff : ContDiff ℝ 2 F ∧ ContDiff ℝ 2 g)
(prop1 : ∀ uu : Fin 2 → ℝ, uu 0 = uu 1 → F uu = 0)
(prop2 : ∀ x : ℝ, g x > 0 ∧ x ^ 2 * g x ≤ 1)
(hvec : ∀ x y : ℝ, (vec x y) 0 = x ∧ (vec x y) 1 = y)
(hFgrad : ∀ uv : Fin 2 → ℝ, Fgrad uv 0 = deriv (fun x : ℝ => F (vec x (uv 1))) (uv 0) ∧ Fgrad uv 1 = deriv (fun y : ℝ => F (vec (uv 0) y)) (uv 1))
(prop3 : ∀ uv : Fin 2 → ℝ, Fgrad uv = 0 ∨ parallel (Fgrad uv) (vec (g (uv 0)) (-g (uv 1))))
: ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ x : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ, sInf {Fxx : ℝ | ∃ i j : Fin (n + 1), i ≠ j ∧ Fxx = |F (vec (x i) (x j))|} ≤ C / n :=

title: putnam_2011_a5
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a5:
   a bound for pairwise values of a twice continuously differentiable
   real function whose gradient is governed by a positive function satisfying
   x^2 * g(x) <= 1; this file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Vectors.Fin Reals ClassicalEpsilon.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2011_a5_continuous1 (h : R -> R) : Prop :=
  forall x epsilon : R,
    epsilon > 0 ->
    exists delta : R,
      delta > 0 /\
      forall y : R,
        Rabs (y - x) < delta ->
        Rabs (h y - h x) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_2011_a5_distance2
    (x1 x2 y1 y2 : R) : R :=
  sqrt ((x1 - y1) ^ 2 + (x2 - y2) ^ 2).

Definition putnam_2011_a5_continuous2
    (h : R -> R -> R) : Prop :=
  forall x y epsilon : R,
    epsilon > 0 ->
    exists delta : R,
      delta > 0 /\
      forall x' y' : R,
        putnam_2011_a5_distance2 x' y' x y < delta ->
        Rabs (h x' y' - h x y) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_2011_a5_derivable_at
    (h : R -> R) (x d : R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    epsilon > 0 ->
    exists delta : R,
      delta > 0 /\
      forall y : R,
        y <> x ->
        Rabs (y - x) < delta ->
        Rabs ((h y - h x) / (y - x) - d) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_2011_a5_derivative
    (h : R -> R) (x : R) : R :=
  epsilon (inhabits (0 : R))
    (fun d : R => putnam_2011_a5_derivable_at h x d).

Definition putnam_2011_a5_dx
    (F : R -> R -> R) (u v : R) : R :=
  putnam_2011_a5_derivative (fun x : R => F x v) u.

Definition putnam_2011_a5_dy
    (F : R -> R -> R) (u v : R) : R :=
  putnam_2011_a5_derivative (fun y : R => F u y) v.

Definition putnam_2011_a5_dxx
    (F : R -> R -> R) (u v : R) : R :=
  putnam_2011_a5_derivative
    (fun x : R => putnam_2011_a5_dx F x v) u.

Definition putnam_2011_a5_dxy
    (F : R -> R -> R) (u v : R) : R :=
  putnam_2011_a5_derivative
    (fun y : R => putnam_2011_a5_dx F u y) v.

Definition putnam_2011_a5_dyx
    (F : R -> R -> R) (u v : R) : R :=
  putnam_2011_a5_derivative
    (fun x : R => putnam_2011_a5_dy F x v) u.

Definition putnam_2011_a5_dyy
    (F : R -> R -> R) (u v : R) : R :=
  putnam_2011_a5_derivative
    (fun y : R => putnam_2011_a5_dy F u y) v.

Definition putnam_2011_a5_c2_univariate (h : R -> R) : Prop :=
  (forall x : R,
      putnam_2011_a5_derivable_at
        h x (putnam_2011_a5_derivative h x)) /\
  (forall x : R,
      putnam_2011_a5_derivable_at
        (putnam_2011_a5_derivative h) x
        (putnam_2011_a5_derivative
          (putnam_2011_a5_derivative h) x)) /\
  putnam_2011_a5_continuous1 h /\
  putnam_2011_a5_continuous1
    (putnam_2011_a5_derivative h) /\
  putnam_2011_a5_continuous1
    (putnam_2011_a5_derivative
      (putnam_2011_a5_derivative h)).

Definition putnam_2011_a5_c2_bivariate
    (F : R -> R -> R) : Prop :=
  putnam_2011_a5_continuous2 F /\
  (forall u v : R,
      putnam_2011_a5_derivable_at
        (fun x : R => F x v) u (putnam_2011_a5_dx F u v) /\
      putnam_2011_a5_derivable_at
        (fun y : R => F u y) v (putnam_2011_a5_dy F u v)) /\
  putnam_2011_a5_continuous2 (putnam_2011_a5_dx F) /\
  putnam_2011_a5_continuous2 (putnam_2011_a5_dy F) /\
  (forall u v : R,
      putnam_2011_a5_derivable_at
        (fun x : R => putnam_2011_a5_dx F x v)
        u (putnam_2011_a5_dxx F u v) /\
      putnam_2011_a5_derivable_at
        (fun y : R => putnam_2011_a5_dx F u y)
        v (putnam_2011_a5_dxy F u v) /\
      putnam_2011_a5_derivable_at
        (fun x : R => putnam_2011_a5_dy F x v)
        u (putnam_2011_a5_dyx F u v) /\
      putnam_2011_a5_derivable_at
        (fun y : R => putnam_2011_a5_dy F u y)
        v (putnam_2011_a5_dyy F u v)) /\
  putnam_2011_a5_continuous2 (putnam_2011_a5_dxx F) /\
  putnam_2011_a5_continuous2 (putnam_2011_a5_dxy F) /\
  putnam_2011_a5_continuous2 (putnam_2011_a5_dyx F) /\
  putnam_2011_a5_continuous2 (putnam_2011_a5_dyy F).

Definition putnam_2011_a5_gradient_condition
    (F : R -> R -> R) (g : R -> R) : Prop :=
  forall u v : R,
    (putnam_2011_a5_dx F u v = 0 /\
     putnam_2011_a5_dy F u v = 0) \/
    exists c : R,
      putnam_2011_a5_dx F u v = c * g u /\
      putnam_2011_a5_dy F u v = c * (- g v).

Theorem putnam_2011_a5
    (F : R -> R -> R)
    (g : R -> R)
    (Fgdiff :
      putnam_2011_a5_c2_bivariate F /\
      putnam_2011_a5_c2_univariate g)
    (prop1 : forall u : R, F u u = 0)
    (prop2 :
      forall x : R,
        g x > 0 /\ x ^ 2 * g x <= 1)
    (prop3 : putnam_2011_a5_gradient_condition F g) :
  exists C : R,
    forall n : nat,
      (2 <= n)%nat ->
      forall x : Fin.t (S n) -> R,
        exists i j : Fin.t (S n),
          i <> j /\
          Rabs (F (x i) (x j)) <= C / INR n.
Admitted.

title: putnam_2011_a5
content:
theory putnam_2011_a5 imports
Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Derivative"
begin

theorem putnam_2011_a5:
  fixes f :: "real \<Rightarrow> real \<Rightarrow> real"
  and g :: "real \<Rightarrow> real"
  and C1diff :: "(real \<Rightarrow> real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  defines "C1diff \<equiv> \<lambda> h. (\<forall> u. (h u) C1_differentiable_on UNIV) \<and> (\<forall> v. (\<lambda> x. h x v) C1_differentiable_on UNIV)"
  assumes Fgdiff: "g C1_differentiable_on UNIV \<and> (deriv g) C1_differentiable_on UNIV \<and> 
                    C1diff f \<and> (C1diff (\<lambda> u. deriv (f u))) \<and> C1diff (\<lambda> u v. deriv (\<lambda> x. f x v) u)"
  and prop1: "\<forall> u :: real. f u u = 0"
  and prop2: "\<forall> x :: real. g x > 0 \<and> x ^ 2 * g x \<le> 1"
  and prop3: "\<forall> u v :: real. \<exists> c :: real. deriv (\<lambda> x. f x v) u = c * g u \<and> deriv (f u) v = c * (-g v)"
  shows "\<exists>C :: real. \<forall>n \<ge> 2. \<forall>x :: nat \<Rightarrow> real.
    (LEAST Fxx :: real. \<exists>i j :: nat.
      i \<le> n \<and> j \<le> n \<and> i \<noteq> j \<and> Fxx = \<bar>f (x i) (x j)\<bar>) \<le> C / n"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_2011_a5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a5:
  a uniform inverse-linear bound for pairwise values of a twice continuously
  differentiable function whose gradient is parallel to a prescribed positive
  vector field. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let pair =
     \(u:real) (v:real).
       (lambda i. if i = 1 then u else v):real^2 in
   let xrepl =
     \(x:real^2) (i:num) (t:real).
       (lambda k. if k = i then t else x$k):real^2 in
   let has_derivative_at =
     \(f:real->real) (d:real) (x:real).
       !e:real.
         &0 < e
         ==> ?delta:real.
               &0 < delta /\
               !y:real.
                 &0 < abs (y - x) /\ abs (y - x) < delta
                 ==> abs ((f y - f x) / (y - x) - d) < e in
   let continuous1 =
     \(f:real->real).
       !x e:real.
         &0 < e
         ==> ?delta:real.
               &0 < delta /\
               !y:real.
                 abs (y - x) < delta
                 ==> abs (f y - f x) < e in
   let continuous2 =
     \(f:real^2->real).
       !x:real^2. !e:real.
         &0 < e
         ==> ?delta:real.
               &0 < delta /\
               !y:real^2.
                 (!i:num.
                    1 <= i /\ i <= 2
                    ==> abs (y$i - x$i) < delta)
                 ==> abs (f y - f x) < e in
   let deriv1 =
     \(f:real->real) (x:real).
       @d:real. has_derivative_at f d x in
   let partial =
     \(f:real^2->real) (i:num) (x:real^2).
       @d:real.
         has_derivative_at
           (\t:real. f (xrepl x i t)) d (x$i) in
   let second_partial =
     \(f:real^2->real) (i:num) (j:num) (x:real^2).
       @d:real.
         has_derivative_at
           (\t:real. partial f i (xrepl x j t)) d (x$j) in
   let twice_continuously_differentiable1 =
     \(f:real->real).
       (!x:real. has_derivative_at f (deriv1 f x) x) /\
       continuous1 (deriv1 f) /\
       (!x:real.
          has_derivative_at
            (deriv1 f) (deriv1 (deriv1 f) x) x) /\
       continuous1 (deriv1 (deriv1 f)) in
   let twice_continuously_differentiable2 =
     \(f:real^2->real).
       (!i:num.
          1 <= i /\ i <= 2
          ==>
          (!x:real^2.
             has_derivative_at
               (\t:real. f (xrepl x i t))
               (partial f i x) (x$i)) /\
          continuous2 (partial f i)) /\
       (!i j:num.
          1 <= i /\ i <= 2 /\ 1 <= j /\ j <= 2
          ==>
          (!x:real^2.
             has_derivative_at
               (\t:real. partial f i (xrepl x j t))
               (second_partial f i j x) (x$j)) /\
          continuous2 (second_partial f i j)) in
   !f:real^2->real. !g:real->real.
     twice_continuously_differentiable2 f /\
     twice_continuously_differentiable1 g /\
     (!u:real. f (pair u u) = &0) /\
     (!x:real. &0 < g x /\ x pow 2 * g x <= &1) /\
     (!uv:real^2.
        ?c:real.
          partial f 1 uv = c * g (uv$1) /\
          partial f 2 uv = c * --(g (uv$2)))
     ==>
     ?C:real.
       !n:num. !x:num->real.
         2 <= n
         ==>
         ?i j:num.
           i <= n /\ j <= n /\ ~(i = j) /\
           abs (f (pair (x i) (x j))) <= C / &n`;;

title: putnam_2011_a5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a5:
;; twice continuously differentiable real functions with diagonal zeroes,
;; controlled positive g, and gradient parallel to (g(u),-g(v)) satisfy the
;; stated O(1/n) pair-value bound. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Reals are rational regular Cauchy names, and real functions are extensional
;; ACL2 function objects on those names. Positive rational tolerances and
;; radii are cofinal in the positive reals. Derivative functions, pointwise
;; parallelism scalars, and the concluding constant are all internally
;; quantified by negated FN-EQUAL tests; none is an external parameter.
;;
;; Differentiability is expressed using every real base point and every
;; nonzero rational increment. Joint continuity of F and all partial
;; derivatives, and continuity of g and its first two derivatives, make these
;; dense-increment limits equivalent to the source C^2 assumptions. A list of
;; exactly n+1 real names is a bijective encoding of Fin (n+1) -> R, and the
;; recursive pair search is exactly the finite minimum conclusion.

(defun putnam-2011-a5-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'cons
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2011-a5-term-list (cdr terms)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-apply-term (function arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2011-a5-quoted function)
        (putnam-2011-a5-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-apply-object-term
    (function-term arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        function-term
        (putnam-2011-a5-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'if
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2011-a5-and-terms (cdr terms))
            (putnam-2011-a5-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2011-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list 'if
        hypothesis
        conclusion
        (putnam-2011-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-not-term (term)
  (list 'if
        term
        (putnam-2011-a5-quoted nil)
        (putnam-2011-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-negate-term (value)
  (list 'unary-- value))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-subtract-term (left right)
  (putnam-2011-a5-add-term
   left
   (putnam-2011-a5-negate-term right)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-multiply-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-* left right))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-divide-term (numerator denominator)
  (putnam-2011-a5-multiply-term
   numerator
   (list 'unary-/ denominator)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-absolute-term (value)
  (list 'if
        (list '< value (putnam-2011-a5-quoted 0))
        (putnam-2011-a5-negate-term value)
        value))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-less-equal-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        (list '< right left)
        (putnam-2011-a5-quoted nil)
        (putnam-2011-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-minimum-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        (list '< left right)
        left
        right))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-positive-rational-term (value)
  (putnam-2011-a5-and-terms
   (list
    (list 'rationalp value)
    (list '< (putnam-2011-a5-quoted 0) value))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda
        formals
        (putnam-2011-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-real-value-term (name precision)
  (putnam-2011-a5-apply-term name (list precision)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-object-real-value-term
    (name-term precision)
  (putnam-2011-a5-apply-object-term
   name-term
   (list precision)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-real-cauchy-function (name)
  (let* ((left
          (putnam-2011-a5-real-value-term name 'epsilon))
         (right
          (putnam-2011-a5-real-value-term name 'eta))
         (distance
          (putnam-2011-a5-absolute-term
           (putnam-2011-a5-subtract-term left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon eta)
     (putnam-2011-a5-implies-term
      (putnam-2011-a5-and-terms
       (list
        (putnam-2011-a5-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
        (putnam-2011-a5-positive-rational-term 'eta)))
      (putnam-2011-a5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2011-a5-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2011-a5-add-term
          'epsilon 'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-real-name-p (name)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2011-a5-real-cauchy-function name)
    (putnam-2011-a5-true-function
     '(epsilon eta)))))

;; Sampling both names at eta/4 makes the universal inequality equivalent to
;; the represented real distance being at most BOUND.
(defun putnam-2011-a5-real-distance-function
    (left-name right-name bound)
  (let* ((precision
          (putnam-2011-a5-multiply-term
           (putnam-2011-a5-quoted 1/4)
           'eta))
         (left
          (putnam-2011-a5-real-value-term
           left-name precision))
         (right
          (putnam-2011-a5-real-value-term
           right-name precision))
         (distance
          (putnam-2011-a5-absolute-term
           (putnam-2011-a5-subtract-term left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(eta)
     (putnam-2011-a5-implies-term
      (putnam-2011-a5-positive-rational-term 'eta)
      (putnam-2011-a5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2011-a5-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2011-a5-add-term
          (putnam-2011-a5-quoted bound)
          'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-real-distance-at-most-p
    (left-name right-name bound)
  (and
   (rationalp bound)
   (putnam-2011-a5-real-name-p left-name)
   (putnam-2011-a5-real-name-p right-name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2011-a5-real-distance-function
     left-name right-name bound)
    (putnam-2011-a5-true-function '(eta)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-real-equal-p
    (left-name right-name)
  (putnam-2011-a5-real-distance-at-most-p
   left-name right-name 0))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-unary-output-function
    (function)
  (let ((output
         (putnam-2011-a5-apply-term function (list 'x))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-2011-a5-implies-term
      (list 'putnam-2011-a5-real-name-p 'x)
      (list 'putnam-2011-a5-real-name-p output)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-unary-extensional-function
    (function)
  (let ((left-output
         (putnam-2011-a5-apply-term
          function (list 'x-left)))
        (right-output
         (putnam-2011-a5-apply-term
          function (list 'x-right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x-left x-right)
     (putnam-2011-a5-implies-term
      (list 'putnam-2011-a5-real-equal-p
            'x-left 'x-right)
      (list 'putnam-2011-a5-real-equal-p
            left-output right-output)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-real-function-p (function)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp function)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2011-a5-unary-output-function function)
    (putnam-2011-a5-true-function '(x)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2011-a5-unary-extensional-function function)
    (putnam-2011-a5-true-function
     '(x-left x-right)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-rational-shift-name (name shift)
  (let ((value
         (putnam-2011-a5-object-real-value-term
          (putnam-2011-a5-quoted name)
          (putnam-2011-a5-multiply-term
           (putnam-2011-a5-quoted 1/2)
           'precision))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(precision)
     (putnam-2011-a5-add-term
      value
      (putnam-2011-a5-quoted shift)))))

;; Continuity is stated using closed rational radii. Rescaling epsilon and
;; delta gives the usual open-ball definition in both directions.
(defun putnam-2011-a5-continuous-at-delta-function
    (function x epsilon delta)
  (let ((at-x
         (putnam-2011-a5-apply-term
          function
          (list (putnam-2011-a5-quoted x))))
        (at-y
         (putnam-2011-a5-apply-term
          function
          (list 'y))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(y)
     (putnam-2011-a5-implies-term
      (putnam-2011-a5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2011-a5-real-name-p 'y)
        (list 'putnam-2011-a5-real-distance-at-most-p
              (putnam-2011-a5-quoted x)
              'y
              (putnam-2011-a5-quoted delta))))
      (list 'putnam-2011-a5-real-distance-at-most-p
            at-x
            at-y
            (putnam-2011-a5-quoted epsilon))))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-continuous-at-delta-p
    (function x epsilon delta)
  (and
   (rationalp delta)
   (< 0 delta)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2011-a5-continuous-at-delta-function
     function x epsilon delta)
    (putnam-2011-a5-true-function '(y)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-continuity-delta-failure-function
    (function x epsilon)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(delta)
   (list
    'if
    (list 'putnam-2011-a5-continuous-at-delta-p
          (putnam-2011-a5-quoted function)
          (putnam-2011-a5-quoted x)
          (putnam-2011-a5-quoted epsilon)
          'delta)
    (putnam-2011-a5-quoted nil)
    (putnam-2011-a5-quoted t))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-continuity-delta-exists-p
    (function x epsilon)
  (not
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2011-a5-continuity-delta-failure-function
     function x epsilon)
    (putnam-2011-a5-true-function '(delta)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-continuity-function (function)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(x epsilon)
   (putnam-2011-a5-implies-term
    (putnam-2011-a5-and-terms
     (list
      (list 'putnam-2011-a5-real-name-p 'x)
      (putnam-2011-a5-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)))
    (list 'putnam-2011-a5-continuity-delta-exists-p
          (putnam-2011-a5-quoted function)
          'x
          'epsilon))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-continuous-p (function)
  (and
   (putnam-2011-a5-real-function-p function)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2011-a5-continuity-function function)
    (putnam-2011-a5-true-function
     '(x epsilon)))))

;; At precision eta, each numerator value is sampled at |h|*eta/4, so this is

    (values expected-length)
  (if (zp expected-length)
      (equal values nil)
    (and
     (consp values)
     (putnam-2011-a5-real-name-p (car values))
     (putnam-2011-a5-real-vector-p
      (cdr values)
      (- expected-length 1)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-pair-bound-inner-p
    (f bound left-value right-values i j)
  (if (endp right-values)
      nil
    (or
     (and
      (not (equal i j))
      (putnam-2011-a5-real-less-equal-p
       (putnam-2011-a5-real-absolute-name
        (apply$ f (list left-value (car right-values))))
       bound))
     (putnam-2011-a5-pair-bound-inner-p
      f bound left-value (cdr right-values) i (+ j 1)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-pair-bound-outer-p
    (f bound left-values all-values i)
  (if (endp left-values)
      nil
    (or
     (putnam-2011-a5-pair-bound-inner-p
      f bound (car left-values) all-values i 0)
     (putnam-2011-a5-pair-bound-outer-p
      f bound (cdr left-values) all-values (+ i 1)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-pair-bound-p
    (f c n values)
  (let ((bound
         (putnam-2011-a5-real-scale-name c (/ 1 n))))
    (putnam-2011-a5-pair-bound-outer-p
     f bound values values 0)))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-conclusion-for-c-function
    (f c)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(n values)
   (putnam-2011-a5-implies-term
    (putnam-2011-a5-and-terms
     (list
      (list 'natp 'n)
      (list '<= (putnam-2011-a5-quoted 2) 'n)
      (list 'putnam-2011-a5-real-vector-p
            'values
            (list 'binary-+ 'n
                  (putnam-2011-a5-quoted 1)))))
    (list 'putnam-2011-a5-pair-bound-p
          (putnam-2011-a5-quoted f)
          (putnam-2011-a5-quoted c)
          'n
          'values))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-conclusion-for-c-p (f c)
  (and
   (putnam-2011-a5-real-name-p c)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2011-a5-conclusion-for-c-function f c)
    (putnam-2011-a5-true-function '(n values)))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-conclusion-witness-failure-function
    (f)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(c)
   (list
    'if
    (list 'putnam-2011-a5-conclusion-for-c-p
          (putnam-2011-a5-quoted f)
          'c)
    (putnam-2011-a5-quoted nil)
    (putnam-2011-a5-quoted t))))

(defun putnam-2011-a5-conclusion-p (f)
  (let ((failure
         (putnam-2011-a5-conclusion-witness-failure-function
          f))
        (always-true
         (putnam-2011-a5-true-function '(c))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp failure)
     (tamep-functionp always-true)
     (not (fn-equal failure always-true)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2011-a5-statement (f g)
  (implies
   (putnam-2011-a5-hypothesis-p f g)
   (putnam-2011-a5-conclusion-p f)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2011_a5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2011_a5): twice continuously differentiable real
-- functions F and g, with F vanishing on the diagonal, g positive,
-- x^2*g(x) <= 1, and grad F(u,v) parallel to (g(u), -g(v)), have an O(1/n)
-- small value among any n+1 real inputs. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2011A5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

maximum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
maximum reals x y with order-total reals x y
... | left _ =
  y
... | right _ =
  x

absoluteValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
absoluteValue reals x =
  maximum reals x (negate reals x)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ContinuousAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ContinuousAt {R} reals function point =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function point)
          epsilon
          (function x)))

Continuous :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
Continuous {R} reals function =
  (point : R) ->
  ContinuousAt reals function point

ContinuousAt2 :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
ContinuousAt2 {R} reals function pointU pointV =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((u v : R) ->
        CloseTo reals pointU delta u ->
        CloseTo reals pointV delta v ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function pointU pointV)
          epsilon
          (function u v)))

Continuous2 :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R -> R) ->
  Set
Continuous2 {R} reals function =
  (u v : R) ->
  ContinuousAt2 reals function u v

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
differenceQuotient reals function point x =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals (function x) (function point))
    (subtract reals x point)

DerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeAt {R} reals function point derivativeValue =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        x != point ->
        CloseTo reals derivativeValue epsilon
          (differenceQuotient reals function point x)))

record TwiceContinuouslyDifferentiable1
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (function : R -> R) :
  Set where

  field
    firstDerivative secondDerivative : R -> R

    function-continuous :
      Continuous reals function
    first-derivative-correct :
      (x : R) ->
      DerivativeAt reals
        function
        x
        (firstDerivative x)
    first-derivative-continuous :
      Continuous reals firstDerivative
    second-derivative-correct :
      (x : R) ->
      DerivativeAt reals
        firstDerivative
        x
        (secondDerivative x)
    second-derivative-continuous :
      Continuous reals secondDerivative

record TwiceContinuouslyDifferentiable2
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (function : R -> R -> R) :
  Set where

  field
    firstPartialU firstPartialV : R -> R -> R
    secondPartialUU secondPartialUV : R -> R -> R
    secondPartialVU secondPartialVV : R -> R -> R

    function-continuous :
      Continuous2 reals function

    first-partial-u-correct :
      (u v : R) ->
      DerivativeAt reals
        (\ x -> function x v)
        u
        (firstPartialU u v)
    first-partial-v-correct :
      (u v : R) ->
      DerivativeAt reals
        (function u)
        v
        (firstPartialV u v)
    first-partial-u-continuous :
      Continuous2 reals firstPartialU
    first-partial-v-continuous :
      Continuous2 reals firstPartialV

    second-partial-uu-correct :
      (u v : R) ->
      DerivativeAt reals
        (\ x -> firstPartialU x v)
        u
        (secondPartialUU u v)
    second-partial-uv-correct :
      (u v : R) ->
      DerivativeAt reals
        (firstPartialU u)
        v
        (secondPartialUV u v)
    second-partial-vu-correct :
      (u v : R) ->
      DerivativeAt reals
        (\ x -> firstPartialV x v)
        u
        (secondPartialVU u v)
    second-partial-vv-correct :
      (u v : R) ->
      DerivativeAt reals
        (firstPartialV u)
        v
        (secondPartialVV u v)

    second-partial-uu-continuous :
      Continuous2 reals secondPartialUU
    second-partial-uv-continuous :
      Continuous2 reals secondPartialUV
    second-partial-vu-continuous :
      Continuous2 reals secondPartialVU
    second-partial-vv-continuous :
      Continuous2 reals secondPartialVV

open TwiceContinuouslyDifferentiable2

putnam-2011-a5 : Set1
putnam-2011-a5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (F : R -> R -> R) ->
  (g : R -> R) ->
  (smoothF : TwiceContinuouslyDifferentiable2 reals F) ->
  TwiceContinuouslyDifferentiable1 reals g ->
  ((u : R) ->
    F u u == zeroR reals) ->
  ((x : R) ->
    StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (g x)
    and
    lessOrEqual reals
      (multiply reals
        (square reals x)
        (g x))
      (oneR reals)) ->
  ((u v : R) ->
    Exists R
      (\ c ->
        (firstPartialU smoothF u v ==
          multiply reals c (g u))
        and
        (firstPartialV smoothF u v ==
          multiply reals c (negate reals (g v))))) ->
  Exists R
    (\ C ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      twoN <=N n ->
      (x : Fin (suc n) -> R) ->
      Exists (Fin (suc n))
        (\ i ->
          Exists (Fin (suc n))
            (\ j ->
              i != j
              and
              lessOrEqual reals
                (absoluteValue reals
                  (F (x i) (x j)))
                (divide reals
                  C
                  (fromNat reals n)))))

title: putnam_2011_a5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a5:
  a bound for pairwise values of a twice continuously differentiable real
  function whose gradient is governed by a positive decaying function. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory;
open real_topologyTheory limTheory;

val putnam_2011_a5 =
  ``let continuous2 =
      \h : real -> real -> real.
        !u v e : real.
          0 < e
          ==>
          ?d : real.
            0 < d /\
            !x y : real.
              (x - u) pow 2 + (y - v) pow 2 < d
              ==>
              abs (h x y - h u v) < e
    in
    let du =
      \F : real -> real -> real.
      \u v : real.
        diffn 1 (\x : real. F x v) u
    in
    let dv =
      \F : real -> real -> real.
      \u v : real.
        diffn 1 (F u) v
    in
    let duu =
      \F : real -> real -> real.
      \u v : real.
        diffn 2 (\x : real. F x v) u
    in
    let duv =
      \F : real -> real -> real.
      \u v : real.
        diffn 1 (\y : real. du F u y) v
    in
    let dvu =
      \F : real -> real -> real.
      \u v : real.
        diffn 1 (\x : real. dv F x v) u
    in
    let dvv =
      \F : real -> real -> real.
      \u v : real.
        diffn 2 (F u) v
    in
    let twice_continuously_differentiable =
      \h : real -> real.
        (!x : real. higher_differentiable 2 h x) /\
        (diffn 1 h) continuous_on UNIV /\
        (diffn 2 h) continuous_on UNIV
    in
    let twice_continuously_differentiable2 =
      \F : real -> real -> real.
        (!u v : real.
           higher_differentiable 2 (\x : real. F x v) u /\
           higher_differentiable 2 (F u) v /\
           higher_differentiable 1 (\y : real. du F u y) v /\
           higher_differentiable 1 (\x : real. dv F x v) u) /\
        continuous2 (du F) /\
        continuous2 (dv F) /\
        continuous2 (duu F) /\
        continuous2 (duv F) /\
        continuous2 (dvu F) /\
        continuous2 (dvv F)
    in
      !F : real -> real -> real.
      !g : real -> real.
        twice_continuously_differentiable2 F /\
        twice_continuously_differentiable g /\
        (!u : real. F u u = 0) /\
        (!x : real. 0 < g x /\ x pow 2 * g x <= 1) /\
        (!u v : real.
           ?c : real.
             du F u v = c * g u /\
             dv F u v = c * -g v)
        ==>
        ?C : real.
          !n : num.
            2 <= n
            ==>
            !x : num -> real.
              ?i j : num.
                i <= n /\ j <= n /\ i <> j /\
                abs (F (x i) (x j)) <= C / &n``;

title: putnam_2011_a5
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2011_a5: a bound on the minimum absolute value of a twice
  continuously differentiable real function at pairs from any finite
  real sequence, under diagonal, decay, and gradient-parallelism
  hypotheses. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P11A5Dx and P11A5Dy are the derivatives of the two coordinate slices of
  F. P11A5Dxx, P11A5Dxy, P11A5Dyx, and P11A5Dyy are the corresponding
  second coordinate partials. Their zero fallbacks make the operators total;
  all fallbacks are inactive under P11A5C2.

  P11A5Cont expands joint continuity on RR X. RR in epsilon-delta form.
  P11A5C2 requires existence and joint continuity of all coordinate partials
  through order two. For real-valued functions on the real plane this is
  equivalent to twice continuous differentiability. The one-variable
  function g uses set.mm's native global order-two C^n class.

  For n >= 2, the finite set of values indexed by distinct members of
  0 ... n is nonempty. Thus saying that one such value is at most C / n is
  equivalent to the source inequality for the minimum over the n + 1 input
  points. The indices remain internally existentially quantified. Every
  declaration is an unproved $a statement encoding.
$)

$c
  P11A5Dx P11A5Dy P11A5Dxx P11A5Dxy P11A5Dyx P11A5Dyy
  P11A5DX P11A5DY P11A5DXX P11A5DXY P11A5DYX P11A5DYY
  P11A5Cont P11A5C2
$.

p11a5-dx-syntax $a class ( P11A5Dx F x y ) $.
p11a5-dy-syntax $a class ( P11A5Dy F x y ) $.
p11a5-dxx-syntax $a class ( P11A5Dxx F x y ) $.
p11a5-dxy-syntax $a class ( P11A5Dxy F x y ) $.
p11a5-dyx-syntax $a class ( P11A5Dyx F x y ) $.
p11a5-dyy-syntax $a class ( P11A5Dyy F x y ) $.
p11a5-dx-function-syntax $a class ( P11A5DX F ) $.
p11a5-dy-function-syntax $a class ( P11A5DY F ) $.
p11a5-dxx-function-syntax $a class ( P11A5DXX F ) $.
p11a5-dxy-function-syntax $a class ( P11A5DXY F ) $.
p11a5-dyx-function-syntax $a class ( P11A5DYX F ) $.
p11a5-dyy-function-syntax $a class ( P11A5DYY F ) $.
p11a5-cont-syntax $a wff ( P11A5Cont F ) $.
p11a5-c2-syntax $a wff ( P11A5C2 F ) $.

${
  $d F t x y $.

  p11a5-dx-definition $a |- ( P11A5Dx F x y ) = if (
    x e. dom ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( F ` <. t , y >. ) ) ) ,
    ( ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( F ` <. t , y >. ) ) ) ` x ) ,
    0
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d F t x y $.

  p11a5-dy-definition $a |- ( P11A5Dy F x y ) = if (
    y e. dom ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( F ` <. x , t >. ) ) ) ,
    ( ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( F ` <. x , t >. ) ) ) ` y ) ,
    0
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d F t x y $.

  p11a5-dxx-definition $a |- ( P11A5Dxx F x y ) = if (
    x e. dom ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( P11A5Dx F t y ) ) ) ,
    ( ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( P11A5Dx F t y ) ) ) ` x ) ,
    0
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d F t x y $.

  p11a5-dxy-definition $a |- ( P11A5Dxy F x y ) = if (
    y e. dom ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( P11A5Dx F x t ) ) ) ,
    ( ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( P11A5Dx F x t ) ) ) ` y ) ,
    0
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d F t x y $.

  p11a5-dyx-definition $a |- ( P11A5Dyx F x y ) = if (
    x e. dom ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( P11A5Dy F t y ) ) ) ,
    ( ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( P11A5Dy F t y ) ) ) ` x ) ,
    0
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d F t x y $.

  p11a5-dyy-definition $a |- ( P11A5Dyy F x y ) = if (
    y e. dom ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( P11A5Dy F x t ) ) ) ,
    ( ( RR _D ( t e. RR |-> ( P11A5Dy F x t ) ) ) ` y ) ,
    0
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d F p $.

  p11a5-dx-function-definition $a |- ( P11A5DX F ) =
    ( p e. ( RR X. RR ) |->
      ( P11A5Dx F ( 1st ` p ) ( 2nd ` p ) ) ) $.
$}

${
  $d F p $.

  p11a5-dy-function-definition $a |- ( P11A5DY F ) =
    ( p e. ( RR X. RR ) |->
      ( P11A5Dy F ( 1st ` p ) ( 2nd ` p ) ) ) $.
$}

${
  $d F p $.

  p11a5-dxx-function-definition $a |- ( P11A5DXX F ) =
    ( p e. ( RR X. RR ) |->
      ( P11A5Dxx F ( 1st ` p ) ( 2nd ` p ) ) ) $.
$}

${
  $d F p $.

  p11a5-dxy-function-definition $a |- ( P11A5DXY F ) =
    ( p e. ( RR X. RR ) |->
      ( P11A5Dxy F ( 1st ` p ) ( 2nd ` p ) ) ) $.
$}

${
  $d F p $.

  p11a5-dyx-function-definition $a |- ( P11A5DYX F ) =
    ( p e. ( RR X. RR ) |->
      ( P11A5Dyx F ( 1st ` p ) ( 2nd ` p ) ) ) $.
$}

${
  $d F p $.

  p11a5-dyy-function-definition $a |- ( P11A5DYY F ) =

title: putnam_2011_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a5:
% a bound for pairwise values of a twice continuously differentiable real
% bivariate function whose gradient is constrained by a positive weight.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2011_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  bivariate_function: TYPE = [real, real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  continuous_real(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real), (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (y: real):
          abs(y - x) < delta IMPLIES
            abs(f(y) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  continuous_bivariate(f: bivariate_function): bool =
    FORALL (u, v: real), (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (x, y: real):
          (abs(x - u) < delta AND abs(y - v) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(f(x, y) - f(u, v)) < epsilon_value

  has_derivative_at(
      f: real_function,
      derivative, point: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (increment: real):
          (increment /= 0 AND abs(increment) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                f(point + increment) - f(point)
                  - derivative * increment)
                < epsilon_value * abs(increment)

  univariate_c2_data(
      g, g_first, g_second: real_function): bool =
    continuous_real(g)
      AND continuous_real(g_first)
      AND continuous_real(g_second)
      AND (FORALL (x: real):
        has_derivative_at(g, g_first(x), x)
          AND has_derivative_at(g_first, g_second(x), x))

  bivariate_c2_data(
      f, f_u, f_v,
      f_uu, f_uv, f_vu, f_vv: bivariate_function): bool =
    continuous_bivariate(f)
      AND continuous_bivariate(f_u)
      AND continuous_bivariate(f_v)
      AND continuous_bivariate(f_uu)
      AND continuous_bivariate(f_uv)
      AND continuous_bivariate(f_vu)
      AND continuous_bivariate(f_vv)
      AND (FORALL (u, v: real):
        has_derivative_at(
          LAMBDA (x: real): f(x, v),
          f_u(u, v),
          u)
        AND has_derivative_at(
          LAMBDA (y: real): f(u, y),
          f_v(u, v),
          v)
        AND has_derivative_at(
          LAMBDA (x: real): f_u(x, v),
          f_uu(u, v),
          u)
        AND has_derivative_at(
          LAMBDA (y: real): f_u(u, y),
          f_uv(u, v),
          v)
        AND has_derivative_at(
          LAMBDA (x: real): f_v(x, v),
          f_vu(u, v),
          u)
        AND has_derivative_at(
          LAMBDA (y: real): f_v(u, y),
          f_vv(u, v),
          v))

  admissible(f: bivariate_function, g: real_function): bool =
    EXISTS
        (g_first, g_second: real_function),
        (f_u, f_v,
         f_uu, f_uv, f_vu, f_vv: bivariate_function):
      univariate_c2_data(g, g_first, g_second)
        AND bivariate_c2_data(
          f, f_u, f_v, f_uu, f_uv, f_vu, f_vv)
        AND (FORALL (u: real): f(u, u) = 0)
        AND (FORALL (x: real):
          g(x) > 0 AND x ^ 2 * g(x) <= 1)
        AND (FORALL (u, v: real):
          EXISTS (scale: real):
            f_u(u, v) = scale * g(u)
              AND f_v(u, v) = scale * (-g(v)))

  putnam_2011_a5: bool =
    FORALL (f: bivariate_function), (g: real_function):
      admissible(f, g) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (C: real):
          FORALL (n: nat), (x: real_sequence):
            n >= 2 IMPLIES
              EXISTS (i, j: nat):
                i <= n
                  AND j <= n
                  AND i /= j
                  AND abs(f(x(i), x(j))) <= C / (n :: real)
END putnam_2011_a5

title: putnam_2011_a6
content:
import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Matrix

/--
Let $G$ be an abelian group with $n$ elements, and let $\{g_1=e,g_2,\dots,g_k\} \subsetneq G$ be a (not necessarily minimal) set of distinct generators of $G$. A special die, which randomly selects one of the elements $g_1,g_2,\dots,g_k$ with equal probability, is rolled $m$ times and the selected elements are multiplied to produce an element $g \in G$. Prove that there exists a real number $b \in (0,1)$ such that $\lim_{m \to \infty} \frac{1}{b^{2m}} \sum_{x \in G} (\text{Prob}(g=x)-\frac{1}{n})^2$ is positive and finite.
-/
theorem putnam_2011_a6
(G : Type*) [CommGroup G] [Fintype G]
(n : ℕ)
(gset : Set G)
(k : ℕ)
(mgprob : ℕ → G → ℝ)
(hmgprob : mgprob = (fun (m : ℕ) (x : G) => ({f : Fin m → gset | (∏ i : Fin m, (f i).1) = x}.ncard : ℝ) / k ^ m))
(hn : n = (Fintype.elems : Finset G).card)
(hk : gset.encard = k)
(hgsetprop : k < n)
(hgset1 : 1 ∈ gset)
(hgsetgen : Subgroup.closure gset = ⊤)
: ∃ b ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1, ∃ C > 0, Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => (1 / b ^ (2 * m)) * (∑ x : G, (mgprob m x - 1 / n) ^ 2)) atTop (𝓝 C) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2011_a6
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a6:
   exponential convergence of a random walk on a finite abelian group,
   generated by a proper set containing the identity. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Arith.PeanoNat Reals.

Import ListNotations.
Local Open Scope R_scope.

Record putnam_2011_a6_comm_group (G : Type) : Type := {
  putnam_2011_a6_mul : G -> G -> G;
  putnam_2011_a6_one : G;
  putnam_2011_a6_inv : G -> G;
  putnam_2011_a6_assoc :
    forall x y z : G,
      putnam_2011_a6_mul x (putnam_2011_a6_mul y z) =
      putnam_2011_a6_mul (putnam_2011_a6_mul x y) z;
  putnam_2011_a6_left_identity :
    forall x : G, putnam_2011_a6_mul putnam_2011_a6_one x = x;
  putnam_2011_a6_right_identity :
    forall x : G, putnam_2011_a6_mul x putnam_2011_a6_one = x;
  putnam_2011_a6_left_inverse :
    forall x : G,
      putnam_2011_a6_mul (putnam_2011_a6_inv x) x =
      putnam_2011_a6_one;
  putnam_2011_a6_right_inverse :
    forall x : G,
      putnam_2011_a6_mul x (putnam_2011_a6_inv x) =
      putnam_2011_a6_one;
  putnam_2011_a6_commutative :
    forall x y : G,
      putnam_2011_a6_mul x y = putnam_2011_a6_mul y x
}.

Arguments putnam_2011_a6_mul {G} _ _ _.
Arguments putnam_2011_a6_one {G} _.
Arguments putnam_2011_a6_inv {G} _ _.

Inductive putnam_2011_a6_generated
    {G : Type}
    (grp : putnam_2011_a6_comm_group G)
    (generators : list G) : G -> Prop :=
  | putnam_2011_a6_generated_one :
      putnam_2011_a6_generated grp generators
        (putnam_2011_a6_one grp)
  | putnam_2011_a6_generated_member :
      forall x : G,
        In x generators ->
        putnam_2011_a6_generated grp generators x
  | putnam_2011_a6_generated_mul :
      forall x y : G,
        putnam_2011_a6_generated grp generators x ->
        putnam_2011_a6_generated grp generators y ->
        putnam_2011_a6_generated grp generators
          (putnam_2011_a6_mul grp x y)
  | putnam_2011_a6_generated_inv :
      forall x : G,
        putnam_2011_a6_generated grp generators x ->
        putnam_2011_a6_generated grp generators
          (putnam_2011_a6_inv grp x).

Fixpoint putnam_2011_a6_words
    {G : Type}
    (generators : list G)
    (m : nat) : list (list G) :=
  match m with
  | O => [[]]
  | S m' =>
      flat_map
        (fun g =>
          map (fun word => g :: word)
            (putnam_2011_a6_words generators m'))
        generators
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2011_a6_product
    {G : Type}
    (grp : putnam_2011_a6_comm_group G)
    (word : list G) : G :=
  match word with
  | [] => putnam_2011_a6_one grp
  | x :: rest =>
      putnam_2011_a6_mul grp x
        (putnam_2011_a6_product grp rest)
  end.

Definition putnam_2011_a6_outcome_count
    {G : Type}
    (eq_dec : forall x y : G, {x = y} + {x <> y})
    (grp : putnam_2011_a6_comm_group G)
    (generators : list G)
    (m : nat)
    (x : G) : nat :=
  length
    (filter
      (fun word =>
        if eq_dec (putnam_2011_a6_product grp word) x
        then true
        else false)
      (putnam_2011_a6_words generators m)).

Fixpoint putnam_2011_a6_squared_distance
    {G : Type}
    (elements : list G)
    (mgprob : nat -> G -> R)
    (n m : nat) : R :=
  match elements with
  | [] => 0
  | x :: rest =>
      (mgprob m x - 1 / INR n) ^ 2 +
      putnam_2011_a6_squared_distance rest mgprob n m
  end.

Definition putnam_2011_a6_sequence_converges
    (sequence : nat -> R)
    (limit : R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    0 < epsilon ->
    exists N : nat,
      forall m : nat,
        (N <= m)%nat ->
        Rabs (sequence m - limit) < epsilon.

Theorem putnam_2011_a6 :
  forall
      (G : Type)
      (grp : putnam_2011_a6_comm_group G)
      (eq_dec : forall x y : G, {x = y} + {x <> y})
      (elements generators : list G)
      (n k : nat)
      (mgprob : nat -> G -> R),
    NoDup elements ->
    (forall x : G, In x elements) ->
    length elements = n ->
    NoDup generators ->
    length generators = k ->
    (k < n)%nat ->
    In (putnam_2011_a6_one grp) generators ->
    (forall x : G,
      putnam_2011_a6_generated grp generators x) ->
    (forall (m : nat) (x : G),
      mgprob m x =
      INR
        (putnam_2011_a6_outcome_count
          eq_dec grp generators m x) /
      (INR k) ^ m) ->
    exists b : R,
      0 < b < 1 /\
      exists C : R,
        0 < C /\
        putnam_2011_a6_sequence_converges
          (fun m : nat =>
            (1 / b ^ (Nat.mul 2 m)) *
            putnam_2011_a6_squared_distance
              elements mgprob n m)
          C.
Admitted.

theory putnam_2011_a6 imports
Complex_Main
"HOL-Library.Cardinality"
begin

theorem putnam_2011_a6:
  fixes n :: nat
  and gset :: "('g::ab_group_add) set"
  and k :: nat
  and mgprob :: "nat \<Rightarrow> 'g \<Rightarrow> real"
  defines "mgprob \<equiv> \<lambda> (m :: nat) (x :: 'g). card {l :: 'g list. length l = m \<and> set l \<subseteq> gset \<and> foldr plus l 0 = x} / k ^ m"
  assumes hn: "n = CARD('g) \<and> finite (UNIV :: 'g set)"
  and hk: "card gset = k"
  and hgsetprop: "k < n"
  and hgset0: "0 \<in> gset"
  and hgsetgen: "\<forall> x :: 'g. \<exists> l :: 'g list. set l \<subseteq> gset \<and> foldr plus l 0 = x"
  shows "\<exists>b \<in> {(0::real)<..<1}. \<exists>C > 0.
    (\<lambda>m :: nat. (1 / b powr (2 * real m)) *
      (\<Sum>x \<in> UNIV. (mgprob m x - 1 / n)^2)) \<longlonglongrightarrow> C"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_a6:
  exponential convergence of the product distribution of a uniform die on a
  proper generating subset of a finite abelian group to the uniform
  distribution. This file contains no proof.
*)

let analysis_output = open_out "/dev/null";;
let analysis_formatter = Format.formatter_of_out_channel analysis_output;;
let analysis_loaded =
  Toploop.use_file analysis_formatter "Library/analysis.ml";;
Format.pp_print_flush analysis_formatter ();;
close_out analysis_output;;
