title: putnam_2011_b3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b3:
-- nonzero continuity of a real function at zero and differentiability there
-- of both its product and quotient with another function force that function
-- to be differentiable at zero. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2011B3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data Either (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> Either A B
  right : B -> Either A B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record Truth : Set where
  constructor truth

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor iff
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      Either (lessOrEqual x y) (lessOrEqual y x)
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))

    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ContinuousAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ContinuousAt {R} reals function point =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function point)
          epsilon
          (function x)))

differenceQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
differenceQuotient reals function point x =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals (function x) (function point))
    (subtract reals x point)

HasDerivativeAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
HasDerivativeAt {R} reals function point derivative =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        x != point ->
        CloseTo reals
          derivative
          epsilon
          (differenceQuotient reals function point x)))

DifferentiableAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
DifferentiableAt {R} reals function point =
  Exists R
    (\ derivative ->
      HasDerivativeAt reals function point derivative)

pointwiseProduct :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
pointwiseProduct reals f g x =
  multiply reals (f x) (g x)

pointwiseQuotient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
pointwiseQuotient reals f g x =
  divide reals (f x) (g x)

putnam-2011-b3-claim :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Set
putnam-2011-b3-claim {R} reals =
  (f g : R -> R) ->
  g (zeroR reals) != zeroR reals ->
  ContinuousAt reals g (zeroR reals) ->
  DifferentiableAt reals
    (pointwiseProduct reals f g)
    (zeroR reals) ->
  DifferentiableAt reals
    (pointwiseQuotient reals f g)
    (zeroR reals) ->
  DifferentiableAt reals f (zeroR reals)

putnam-2011-b3-solution : Set
putnam-2011-b3-solution =
  Truth

putnam-2011-b3 : Set1
putnam-2011-b3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Iff
    (putnam-2011-b3-claim reals)
    putnam-2011-b3-solution

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b3:
  continuity and nonvanishing of a real function at zero, together with
  differentiability there of a product and quotient, imply differentiability
  of the other factor. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open realTheory limTheory;

val putnam_2011_b3 =
  ``let putnam_2011_b3_solution = T
    in
      ((!f g : real -> real.
          g 0 <> 0 /\
          g contl 0 /\
          (\x : real. f x * g x) differentiable 0 /\
          (\x : real. f x / g x) differentiable 0
          ==>
          f differentiable 0)
       <=>
       putnam_2011_b3_solution)``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2011_b3: nonvanishing and continuity of a real function g at zero,
  together with differentiability there of f*g and f/g, imply
  differentiability of f at zero. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The functions f and g range over all total real-valued functions.
  Continuity of g at zero is expanded in the standard epsilon-delta form.
  Membership of zero in dom ( RR _D F ) is set.mm's native assertion that
  the real function F is differentiable at zero. The product and quotient
  functions are displayed explicitly.

  The source solution proposition is True, represented by set.mm's T., so
  the final biconditional preserves the source statement literally. The
  final declaration is a single unproved $a statement; this database
  contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d d e f g x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2011-b3 $a |- (
    (
      A. f e. ( RR ^m RR )
      A. g e. ( RR ^m RR )
        (
          (
            ( g ` 0 ) =/= 0
            /\
            (
              A. e e. RR
                (
                  0 < e
                  ->
                  E. d e. RR
                    (
                      0 < d
                      /\
                      A. x e. RR
                        (
                          ( abs ` x ) < d
                          ->
                          (
                            abs
                            `
                            (
                              ( g ` x )
                              -
                              ( g ` 0 )
                            )
                          )
                          < e
                        )
                    )
                )
              /\
              (
                0 e. dom
                  (
                    RR _D
                      (
                        x e. RR |->
                          (
                            ( f ` x )
                            x.
                            ( g ` x )
                          )
                      )
                  )
                /\
                0 e. dom
                  (
                    RR _D
                      (
                        x e. RR |->
                          (
                            ( f ` x )
                            /
                            ( g ` x )
                          )
                      )
                  )
              )
            )
          )
          ->
          0 e. dom ( RR _D f )
        )
    )
    <-> T.
  ) $.
$}

:: (putnambench__mizar__putnam_2011_b3): if a real function g has a nonzero

environ

::$P-

    g.0 <> 0 &

title: putnam_2011_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b3:
% a nonzero continuous factor at zero makes differentiability at zero of both
% the product and quotient imply differentiability of the other factor.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2011_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  continuous_at(f: real_function, point: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (x: real):
          abs(x - point) < delta IMPLIES
            abs(f(x) - f(point)) < epsilon_value

  has_derivative_at(
      f: real_function,
      derivative, point: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (increment: real):
          (increment /= 0 AND abs(increment) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                f(point + increment) - f(point)
                  - derivative * increment)
                < epsilon_value * abs(increment)

  differentiable_at(f: real_function, point: real): bool =
    EXISTS (derivative: real):
      has_derivative_at(f, derivative, point)

  product(f, g: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real): f(x) * g(x)

  quotient(f, g: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real): safe_div(f(x), g(x))

  putnam_2011_b3_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_2011_b3: bool =
    (FORALL (f, g: real_function):
      (g(0) /= 0
        AND continuous_at(g, 0)
        AND differentiable_at(product(f, g), 0)
        AND differentiable_at(quotient(f, g), 0))
      IMPLIES differentiable_at(f, 0))
    IFF putnam_2011_b3_solution
END putnam_2011_b3

title: putnam_2011_b4
content:
import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Matrix

/--
In a tournament, $2011$ players meet $2011$ times to play a multiplayer game. Every game is played by all $2011$ players together and ends with each of the players either winning or losing. The standings are kept in two $2011 \times 2011$ matrices, $T=(T_{hk})$ and $W=(W_{hk})$. Initially, $T=W=0$. After every game, for every $(h,k)$ (including for $h=k$), if players $h$ and $k$ tied (that is, both won or both lost), the entry $T_{hk}$ is increased by $1$, while if player $h$ won and player $k$ lost, the entry $W_{hk}$ is increased by $1$ and $W_{kh}$ is decreased by $1$. Prove that at the end of the tournament, $\det(T+iW)$ is a non-negative integer divisible by $2^{2010}$.
-/
theorem putnam_2011_b4
(games : Fin 2011 → Fin 2011 → Bool)
(T W : Matrix (Fin 2011) (Fin 2011) ℂ)
(hT : T = (fun p1 p2 => ({g | games g p1 = games g p2}.ncard : ℂ)))
(hW : W = (fun p1 p2 => ({g | games g p1 ∧ !games g p2}.ncard - {g | !games g p1 ∧ games g p2}.ncard : ℂ)))
: ∃ n : ℕ, (T + Complex.I • W).det = n ∧ (2 ^ 2010) ∣ n :=
sorry

title: putnam_2011_b4
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b4:
   the determinant of the complex tournament standings matrix is a
   nonnegative integer divisible by 2^2010. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List Vectors.Fin Reals.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2011_b4_complex : Type := (R * R)%type.

Definition putnam_2011_b4_czero : putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  (0, 0).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_cone : putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  (1, 0).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_ci : putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  (0, 1).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_cadd
    (z w : putnam_2011_b4_complex) : putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  (fst z + fst w, snd z + snd w).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_copp
    (z : putnam_2011_b4_complex) : putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  (- fst z, - snd z).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_csub
    (z w : putnam_2011_b4_complex) : putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  putnam_2011_b4_cadd z (putnam_2011_b4_copp w).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_cmul
    (z w : putnam_2011_b4_complex) : putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  (fst z * fst w - snd z * snd w,
   fst z * snd w + snd z * fst w).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_of_nat
    (n : nat) : putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  (INR n, 0).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_matrix (n : nat) : Type :=
  Fin.t n -> Fin.t n -> putnam_2011_b4_complex.

Definition putnam_2011_b4_matrix_add
    {n : nat}
    (A B : putnam_2011_b4_matrix n) :
    putnam_2011_b4_matrix n :=
  fun i j => putnam_2011_b4_cadd (A i j) (B i j).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_matrix_smul
    {n : nat}
    (z : putnam_2011_b4_complex)
    (A : putnam_2011_b4_matrix n) :
    putnam_2011_b4_matrix n :=
  fun i j => putnam_2011_b4_cmul z (A i j).

Fixpoint putnam_2011_b4_indices
    (n : nat) : list (Fin.t n) :=
  match n with
  | O => []
  | S k => Fin.F1 :: map Fin.FS (putnam_2011_b4_indices k)
  end.

Definition putnam_2011_b4_matrix_rows
    {n : nat}
    (A : putnam_2011_b4_matrix n) :
    list (list putnam_2011_b4_complex) :=
  map
    (fun i =>
      map (fun j => A i j) (putnam_2011_b4_indices n))
    (putnam_2011_b4_indices n).

Fixpoint putnam_2011_b4_csum
    (zs : list putnam_2011_b4_complex) :
    putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  match zs with
  | [] => putnam_2011_b4_czero
  | z :: rest =>
      putnam_2011_b4_cadd z (putnam_2011_b4_csum rest)
  end.

Definition putnam_2011_b4_delete_nth
    {T : Type} (j : nat) (xs : list T) : list T :=
  firstn j xs ++ skipn (S j) xs.

Definition putnam_2011_b4_cofactor_sign
    (j : nat) : putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  if Nat.even j
  then putnam_2011_b4_cone
  else ((-1)%R, 0%R).

Fixpoint putnam_2011_b4_det
    (n : nat)
    (M : list (list putnam_2011_b4_complex))
    {struct n} : putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  match n with
  | O => putnam_2011_b4_cone
  | S k =>
      match M with
      | [] => putnam_2011_b4_czero
      | row :: rows =>
          putnam_2011_b4_csum
            (map
              (fun j =>
                putnam_2011_b4_cmul
                  (putnam_2011_b4_cmul
                    (putnam_2011_b4_cofactor_sign j)
                    (nth j row putnam_2011_b4_czero))
                  (putnam_2011_b4_det k
                    (map
                      (putnam_2011_b4_delete_nth j)
                      rows)))
              (seq 0 (S k)))
      end
  end.

Definition putnam_2011_b4_determinant
    {n : nat}
    (A : putnam_2011_b4_matrix n) :
    putnam_2011_b4_complex :=
  putnam_2011_b4_det n (putnam_2011_b4_matrix_rows A).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_count
    {n : nat}
    (p : Fin.t n -> bool) : nat :=
  fold_right
    (fun i total => if p i then S total else total)
    O
    (putnam_2011_b4_indices n).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_tie_matrix
    (games : Fin.t 2011 -> Fin.t 2011 -> bool) :
    putnam_2011_b4_matrix 2011 :=
  fun h k =>
    putnam_2011_b4_of_nat
      (putnam_2011_b4_count
        (fun g => Bool.eqb (games g h) (games g k))).

Definition putnam_2011_b4_win_loss_matrix
    (games : Fin.t 2011 -> Fin.t 2011 -> bool) :
    putnam_2011_b4_matrix 2011 :=
  fun h k =>
    putnam_2011_b4_csub
      (putnam_2011_b4_of_nat
        (putnam_2011_b4_count
          (fun g =>
            andb (games g h) (negb (games g k)))))
      (putnam_2011_b4_of_nat
        (putnam_2011_b4_count
          (fun g =>
            andb (negb (games g h)) (games g k)))).

Theorem putnam_2011_b4
    (games : Fin.t 2011 -> Fin.t 2011 -> bool)
    (T W : putnam_2011_b4_matrix 2011)
    (hT : T = putnam_2011_b4_tie_matrix games)
    (hW : W = putnam_2011_b4_win_loss_matrix games) :
  exists n : nat,
    putnam_2011_b4_determinant
      (putnam_2011_b4_matrix_add
        T
        (putnam_2011_b4_matrix_smul putnam_2011_b4_ci W)) =
      putnam_2011_b4_of_nat n /\
    Nat.divide (Nat.pow 2 2010) n.
Admitted.

putnam_2011_b4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b4:
;; for every 2011-player, 2011-game Boolean outcome table, the determinant of
;; the standings matrix T+iW is a nonnegative integer divisible by 2^2010.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Since both source index types are Fin 2011, an exact 2011-by-2011 Boolean
;; table is the extensional representation of the source function games.

(defun putnam-2011-b4-boolean-p (value)
  (or (equal value t)
      (equal value nil)))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-boolean-row-p (row columns)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix columns)))
  (if (zp columns)
      (equal row nil)
    (and (consp row)
         (putnam-2011-b4-boolean-p (car row))
         (putnam-2011-b4-boolean-row-p
          (cdr row) (- columns 1)))))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-games-p (games rows columns)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix rows)))
  (if (zp rows)
      (equal games nil)
    (and (consp games)
         (putnam-2011-b4-boolean-row-p
          (car games) columns)
         (putnam-2011-b4-games-p
          (cdr games) (- rows 1) columns))))

;; Gaussian integers are represented extensionally as (real-part . imag-part).

(defun putnam-2011-b4-gaussian-add (left right)
  (cons (+ (car left) (car right))
        (+ (cdr left) (cdr right))))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-gaussian-neg (value)
  (cons (- (car value))
        (- (cdr value))))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-gaussian-mul (left right)
  (cons (- (* (car left) (car right))
           (* (cdr left) (cdr right)))
        (+ (* (car left) (cdr right))
           (* (cdr left) (car right)))))

;; Each matrix entry is (T_hk . W_hk), hence represents T_hk+iW_hk.

(defun putnam-2011-b4-entry (games player-h player-k)
  (if (consp games)
      (let ((h-won (nth player-h (car games)))
            (k-won (nth player-k (car games))))
        (putnam-2011-b4-gaussian-add
         (putnam-2011-b4-entry
          (cdr games) player-h player-k)
         (cons
          (if (equal h-won k-won) 1 0)
          (cond ((and h-won (not k-won)) 1)
                ((and (not h-won) k-won) -1)
                (t 0)))))
    (cons 0 0)))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-matrix-row
    (games player-h player-k columns)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix columns)))
  (if (zp columns)
      nil
    (cons
     (putnam-2011-b4-entry games player-h player-k)
     (putnam-2011-b4-matrix-row
      games player-h (+ player-k 1) (- columns 1)))))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-matrix
    (games player-h rows columns)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix rows)))
  (if (zp rows)
      nil
    (cons
     (putnam-2011-b4-matrix-row games player-h 0 columns)
     (putnam-2011-b4-matrix
      games (+ player-h 1) (- rows 1) columns))))

;; The determinant is the usual signed sum over all permutations.

(defun putnam-2011-b4-range-from (start count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons start
          (putnam-2011-b4-range-from
           (+ start 1) (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-prefix-each (item lists)
  (if (consp lists)
      (cons
       (cons item (car lists))
       (putnam-2011-b4-prefix-each item (cdr lists)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-insert-everywhere (item list)
  (if (consp list)
      (cons
       (cons item list)
       (putnam-2011-b4-prefix-each
        (car list)
        (putnam-2011-b4-insert-everywhere
         item (cdr list))))
    (list (list item))))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-insert-into-each (item lists)
  (if (consp lists)
      (append
       (putnam-2011-b4-insert-everywhere item (car lists))
       (putnam-2011-b4-insert-into-each item (cdr lists)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-permutations (list)
  (if (consp list)
      (putnam-2011-b4-insert-into-each
       (car list)
       (putnam-2011-b4-permutations (cdr list)))
    (list nil)))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-count-greater (item list)
  (if (consp list)
      (+ (if (> item (car list)) 1 0)
         (putnam-2011-b4-count-greater item (cdr list)))
    0))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-inversion-count (permutation)
  (if (consp permutation)
      (+ (putnam-2011-b4-count-greater
          (car permutation) (cdr permutation))
         (putnam-2011-b4-inversion-count
          (cdr permutation)))
    0))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-diagonal-product
    (matrix permutation row)
  (if (consp permutation)
      (putnam-2011-b4-gaussian-mul
       (nth (car permutation) (nth row matrix))
       (putnam-2011-b4-diagonal-product
        matrix (cdr permutation) (+ row 1)))
    (cons 1 0)))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-determinant-sum
    (matrix permutations)
  (if (consp permutations)
      (let* ((permutation (car permutations))
             (product
              (putnam-2011-b4-diagonal-product
               matrix permutation 0))
             (signed-product
              (if (evenp
                   (putnam-2011-b4-inversion-count permutation))
                  product
                (putnam-2011-b4-gaussian-neg product))))
        (putnam-2011-b4-gaussian-add
         signed-product
         (putnam-2011-b4-determinant-sum
          matrix (cdr permutations))))
    (cons 0 0)))

(defun putnam-2011-b4-determinant (matrix dimension)
  (putnam-2011-b4-determinant-sum
   matrix
   (putnam-2011-b4-permutations
    (putnam-2011-b4-range-from 0 dimension))))

;; A complex Gaussian integer equals some natural n exactly when its imaginary
;; part is zero and its real part is a natural. The source existential witness
;; can therefore be eliminated without changing its quantifier scope.

(defun putnambench-putnam-2011-b4-statement (games)
  (implies
   (putnam-2011-b4-games-p games 2011 2011)
   (let ((determinant
          (putnam-2011-b4-determinant
           (putnam-2011-b4-matrix games 0 2011 2011)
           2011)))
     (and
      (equal (cdr determinant) 0)
      (natp (car determinant))
      (equal
       (mod (car determinant) (expt 2 2010))
       0)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2011_b4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2011_b4): the determinant of the complex
-- tournament standings matrix is a nonnegative integer divisible by 2^2010.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2011B4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

ifNat : Bool -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat
ifNat true whenTrue whenFalse =
  whenTrue
ifNat false whenTrue whenFalse =
  whenFalse

sameOutcome : Bool -> Bool -> Bool
sameOutcome true true =
  true
sameOutcome true false =
  false
sameOutcome false true =
  false
sameOutcome false false =
  true

wonAndLost : Bool -> Bool -> Bool
wonAndLost true false =
  true
wonAndLost true true =
  false
wonAndLost false true =
  false
wonAndLost false false =
  false

countTrue :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Bool) ->
  Nat
countTrue {zero} predicate =
  zero
countTrue {suc n} predicate =
  ifNat
    (predicate fzero)
    (suc (countTrue (\ i -> predicate (fsuc i))))
    (countTrue (\ i -> predicate (fsuc i)))

record Complex (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor complex
  field
    realPart      : R
    imaginaryPart : R

open Complex

complexZero :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R
complexZero reals =
  complex (zeroR reals) (zeroR reals)

complexOne :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R
complexOne reals =
  complex (oneR reals) (zeroR reals)

imaginaryUnit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R
imaginaryUnit reals =
  complex (zeroR reals) (oneR reals)

complexFromNat :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  Complex R
complexFromNat reals n =
  complex (fromNat reals n) (zeroR reals)

complexAdd :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexAdd reals z w =
  complex
    (add reals (realPart z) (realPart w))
    (add reals (imaginaryPart z) (imaginaryPart w))

complexNegate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexNegate reals z =
  complex
    (negate reals (realPart z))
    (negate reals (imaginaryPart z))

complexSubtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexSubtract reals z w =
  complexAdd reals z (complexNegate reals w)

complexMultiply :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexMultiply reals z w =
  complex
    (add reals
      (multiply reals (realPart z) (realPart w))
      (negate reals
        (multiply reals (imaginaryPart z) (imaginaryPart w))))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals (realPart z) (imaginaryPart w))
      (multiply reals (imaginaryPart z) (realPart w)))

Matrix : Set -> Nat -> Set
Matrix A n =
  Fin n -> Fin n -> A

sumFinComplex :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Complex R) ->
  Complex R
sumFinComplex reals {zero} term =
  complexZero reals
sumFinComplex reals {suc n} term =
  complexAdd reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFinComplex reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

skip :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin (suc n)
skip {zero} removed ()
skip {suc n} fzero i =
  fsuc i
skip {suc n} (fsuc removed) fzero =
  fzero
skip {suc n} (fsuc removed) (fsuc i) =
  fsuc (skip removed i)

firstRowMinor :
  {A : Set} {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix A (suc n) ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Matrix A n
firstRowMinor matrix removedColumn i j =
  matrix (fsuc i) (skip removedColumn j)

alternatingSign :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Complex R
alternatingSign reals fzero =
  complexOne reals
alternatingSign reals (fsuc i) =
  complexNegate reals (alternatingSign reals i)

determinant :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix (Complex R) n ->
  Complex R
determinant reals {zero} matrix =
  complexOne reals
determinant reals {suc n} matrix =
  sumFinComplex reals
    (\ column ->
      complexMultiply reals
        (alternatingSign reals column)
        (complexMultiply reals
          (matrix fzero column)
          (determinant reals (firstRowMinor matrix column))))

naturalPower : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalPower base zero =
  suc zero
naturalPower base (suc exponent) =
  base * naturalPower base exponent

Divides : Nat -> Nat -> Set
Divides divisor dividend =
  Exists Nat
    (\ quotient -> divisor * quotient == dividend)

playerCount : Nat
playerCount =
  2011

gameCount : Nat
gameCount =
  2011

Games : Set
Games =
  Fin gameCount -> Fin playerCount -> Bool

expectedT :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Games ->
  Matrix (Complex R) playerCount
expectedT reals games player1 player2 =
  complexFromNat reals
    (countTrue
      (\ game ->
        sameOutcome
          (games game player1)
          (games game player2)))

expectedW :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Games ->
  Matrix (Complex R) playerCount
expectedW reals games player1 player2 =
  complexSubtract reals
    (complexFromNat reals
      (countTrue
        (\ game ->
          wonAndLost
            (games game player1)
            (games game player2))))
    (complexFromNat reals
      (countTrue
        (\ game ->
          wonAndLost
            (games game player2)
            (games game player1))))

tournamentMatrix :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Matrix (Complex R) playerCount ->
  Matrix (Complex R) playerCount ->
  Matrix (Complex R) playerCount
tournamentMatrix reals T W player1 player2 =
  complexAdd reals
    (T player1 player2)
    (complexMultiply reals
      (imaginaryUnit reals)
      (W player1 player2))

putnam-2011-b4 : Set1
putnam-2011-b4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (games : Games) ->
  (T W : Matrix (Complex R) playerCount) ->
  T == expectedT reals games ->
  W == expectedW reals games ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ n ->
      determinant reals (tournamentMatrix reals T W) ==
      complexFromNat reals n
      and
      Divides (naturalPower 2 2010) n)

title: putnam_2011_b4
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b4:
  the determinant of the complex tournament matrix T + iW is a nonnegative
  integer divisible by 2^2010. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory dividesTheory pred_setTheory permutesTheory realTheory
     complexTheory;

val putnam_2011_b4 =
  ``let determinant =
      \size : num. \M : num -> num -> complex.
        ITSET
          (\p : num -> num. \sum : complex.
             (if evenperm p then
                ITSET
                  (\row : num. \acc : complex. M row (p row) * acc)
                  (count size)
                  (1 : complex)
              else
                -(ITSET
                    (\row : num. \acc : complex. M row (p row) * acc)
                    (count size)
                    (1 : complex))) +
             sum)
          {p : num -> num | p permutes count size}
          (0 : complex)
    in
      !games : num -> num -> bool.
        let T =
          \row col : num.
            complex_of_real
              (&(CARD
                   {game : num |
                      game < 2011 /\
                      games game row = games game col}))
        in
        let W =
          \row col : num.
            complex_of_real
              (&(CARD
                   {game : num |
                      game < 2011 /\
                      games game row /\
                      ~games game col}) -
               &(CARD
                   {game : num |
                      game < 2011 /\
                      ~games game row /\
                      games game col}))
        in
          ?n : num.
            determinant 2011
              (\row col. T row col + i * W row col) =
              complex_of_real (&n) /\
            divides (2 EXP 2010) n``;

title: putnam_2011_b4
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2011_b4: the complex determinant of the tie and signed win-loss
  matrices of a 2011-game, 2011-player tournament is a nonnegative integer
  divisible by 2^2010. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The carrier 0 ..^ 2011 represents both the games and the players. An
  arbitrary subset G of its Cartesian square is equivalent to the source
  Boolean-valued outcome function: <. g , i >. e. G means that player i
  wins game g.

  For each pair i,j, the displayed matrix entry is the number of games in
  which i and j have the same outcome, plus the imaginary unit times the
  number in which i wins and j loses minus the number in which i loses and
  j wins. Thus this matrix is definitionally T + iW from the source after
  eliminating the uniquely defined T and W parameters. SetMM's maDet over
  CCfld is the complex determinant.

  The witnesses n and k remain existentially quantified natural numbers.
  The equation n = 2^2010 k is exactly natural-number divisibility, while
  n's membership in NN0 states nonnegativity. The final declaration is the
  single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  statement.
$)

${
  $d g i j k n s $.

  putnambench-putnam-2011-b4 $a |-
    A. s e.
      ~P
      (
        ( 0 ..^ ; ; ; 2 0 1 1 )
        X.
        ( 0 ..^ ; ; ; 2 0 1 1 )
      )
      E. n e. NN0
        (
          (
            (
              ( ( 0 ..^ ; ; ; 2 0 1 1 ) maDet CCfld )
              `
              (
                i e. ( 0 ..^ ; ; ; 2 0 1 1 ) ,
                j e. ( 0 ..^ ; ; ; 2 0 1 1 ) |->
                  (
                    (
                      #
                      `
                      {
                        g e. ( 0 ..^ ; ; ; 2 0 1 1 ) |
                        (
                          <. g , i >. e. s
                          <->
                          <. g , j >. e. s
                        )
                      }
                    )
                    +
                    (
                      _i
                      x.
                      (
                        (
                          #
                          `
                          {
                            g e. ( 0 ..^ ; ; ; 2 0 1 1 ) |
                            (
                              <. g , i >. e. s
                              /\
                              -. <. g , j >. e. s
                            )
                          }
                        )
                        -
                        (
                          #
                          `
                          {
                            g e. ( 0 ..^ ; ; ; 2 0 1 1 ) |
                            (
                              -. <. g , i >. e. s
                              /\
                              <. g , j >. e. s
                            )
                          }
                        )
                      )
                    )
                  )
              )
            )
            =
            n
          )
          /\
          E. k e. NN0
            n =
              (
                ( 2 ^ ; ; ; 2 0 1 0 )
                x.
                k
              )
        )
  $.
$}

:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b4:

title: putnam_2011_b4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b4:
% the determinant of the complex standings matrix from 2011 multiplayer
% win-loss games is a natural number divisible by 2^2010. This file contains
% no proof.

putnam_2011_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  player_count: posnat = 2011

  complex: TYPE = [# real_part: real, imag_part: real #]
  game_results: TYPE = [nat, nat -> bool]
  matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> complex]

  complex_zero: complex =
    (# real_part := 0, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_one: complex =
    (# real_part := 1, imag_part := 0 #)

  imaginary_unit: complex =
    (# real_part := 0, imag_part := 1 #)

  complex_of_real(value: real): complex =
    (# real_part := value, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_of_nat(value: nat): complex =
    complex_of_real(value :: real)

  complex_neg(value: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := -real_part(value),
       imag_part := -imag_part(value) #)

  complex_add(left, right: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := real_part(left) + real_part(right),
       imag_part := imag_part(left) + imag_part(right) #)

  complex_sub(left, right: complex): complex =
    complex_add(left, complex_neg(right))

  complex_mul(left, right: complex): complex =
    (# real_part :=
         real_part(left) * real_part(right)
           - imag_part(left) * imag_part(right),
       imag_part :=
         real_part(left) * imag_part(right)
           + imag_part(left) * real_part(right) #)

  count_true(
      property: [nat -> bool],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_true(property, count - 1)
        + IF property(count - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  tied_count(
      games: game_results,
      first_player, second_player: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      (LAMBDA (game: nat):
        games(game, first_player)
          = games(game, second_player)),
      player_count)

  first_wins_second_loses_count(
      games: game_results,
      first_player, second_player: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      (LAMBDA (game: nat):
        games(game, first_player)
          AND NOT games(game, second_player)),
      player_count)

  standings_t_entry(
      games: game_results,
      first_player, second_player: nat): complex =
    complex_of_nat(
      tied_count(games, first_player, second_player))

  standings_w_entry(
      games: game_results,
      first_player, second_player: nat): complex =
    complex_sub(
      complex_of_nat(
        first_wins_second_loses_count(
          games, first_player, second_player)),
      complex_of_nat(
        first_wins_second_loses_count(
          games, second_player, first_player)))

  is_standings_t(games: game_results, T: matrix): bool =
    FORALL (first_player, second_player: nat):
      (first_player < player_count
        AND second_player < player_count)
      IMPLIES
        T(first_player, second_player)
          = standings_t_entry(
              games, first_player, second_player)

  is_standings_w(games: game_results, W: matrix): bool =
    FORALL (first_player, second_player: nat):
      (first_player < player_count
        AND second_player < player_count)
      IMPLIES
        W(first_player, second_player)
          = standings_w_entry(
              games, first_player, second_player)

  quotient_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      0
    ELSE
      1
        + quotient_aux(
            numerator - denominator,
            denominator,
            fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  remainder_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      numerator
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator - denominator,
        denominator,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  safe_ndiv(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    quotient_aux(
      numerator,
      denominator,
      numerator + 1)

  safe_mod(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator,
        denominator,
        numerator + 1)
    ENDIF

  function_code_count: nat =
    player_count ^ player_count

  permutation_entry(code, row: nat): nat =
    safe_mod(
      safe_ndiv(code, player_count ^ row),
      player_count)

  permutation_code(code: nat): bool =
    code < function_code_count
      AND (FORALL (row_1, row_2: nat):
        (row_1 < player_count
          AND row_2 < player_count
          AND permutation_entry(code, row_1)
            = permutation_entry(code, row_2))
        IMPLIES row_1 = row_2)

  pair_row(pair: nat): nat =
    safe_ndiv(pair, player_count)

  pair_column(pair: nat): nat =
    safe_mod(pair, player_count)

  inversion_at(code, pair: nat): bool =
    pair_row(pair) < player_count
      AND pair_column(pair) < player_count
      AND pair_row(pair) < pair_column(pair)
      AND permutation_entry(code, pair_row(pair))
        > permutation_entry(code, pair_column(pair))

  inversion_count(code: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      (LAMBDA (pair: nat):
        inversion_at(code, pair)),
      player_count * player_count)

  permutation_sign(code: nat): complex =
    IF mod(inversion_count(code), 2) = 0 THEN
      complex_one
    ELSE
      complex_of_real(-1)
    ENDIF

  permutation_product(
      A: matrix,
      code, count: nat): RECURSIVE complex =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      complex_one
    ELSE
      complex_mul(
        permutation_product(A, code, count - 1),
        A(
          count - 1,
          permutation_entry(code, count - 1)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  determinant_sum(
      A: matrix,
      limit: nat): RECURSIVE complex =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      complex_zero
    ELSE
      LET code: nat = limit - 1 IN
        complex_add(
          determinant_sum(A, limit - 1),
          IF permutation_code(code) THEN
            complex_mul(
              permutation_sign(code),
              permutation_product(
                A, code, player_count))
          ELSE
            complex_zero
          ENDIF)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  determinant(A: matrix): complex =
    determinant_sum(A, function_code_count)

  complex_standings_matrix(T, W: matrix): matrix =
    LAMBDA (row, column: nat):
      complex_add(
        T(row, column),
        complex_mul(
          imaginary_unit,
          W(row, column)))

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  putnam_2011_b4: bool =
    FORALL
        (games: game_results),
        (T, W: matrix):
      (is_standings_t(games, T)
        AND is_standings_w(games, W))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (n: nat):
          determinant(complex_standings_matrix(T, W))
            = complex_of_nat(n)
            AND nat_divides(2 ^ 2010, n)
END putnam_2011_b4

import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Matrix

/--
Let $a_1, a_2, \dots$ be real numbers. Suppose that there is a constant $A$ such that for all $n$,
\[
\int_{-\infty}^\infty \left( \sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{1 + (x-a_i)^2} \right)^2\,dx \leq An.
\]
Prove there is a constant $B>0$ such that for all $n$,
\[
\sum_{i,j=1}^n (1 + (a_i - a_j)^2) \geq Bn^3.
\]
-/
theorem putnam_2011_b5
  (a : ℕ → ℝ)
  (h : ∃ A : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, ∫ x : ℝ, ((∑ i : Finset.range n, 1 / (1 + (x - a i) ^ 2)) ^ 2) ≤ A * n) :
  ∃ B : ℝ, B > 0 ∧
    ∀ n : ℕ, ∑' i : Finset.range n, ∑' j : Finset.range n, (1 + (a i - a j) ^ 2) ≥ B * n ^ 3 :=
sorry

Theorem putnam_2011_b5
    (a: nat -> R)
    (ha : exists (A: R), forall (n: nat), exists (L : R), is_lim_seq (fun nInc => (RInt (fun x => (sum_n_m (fun i => 1 / (1 + (x - a i) ^ 2)) 1 n) ^ 2) (-1 * INR nInc) (INR nInc))) L /\ L <= A * INR n)

putnam_2011_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b5:
;; a whole-line integral bound for finite sums of Cauchy kernels implies a
;; positive cubic lower bound for the pairwise squared-distance sum. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; This conservative generic symbol supplies a regular rational Cauchy name
;; for a_n at every natural n. It is an arbitrary function symbol, not a
;; rational-valued sequence or a finite table. Every real sequence admits such
;; a name, and every name satisfying PUTNAM-2011-B5-REGULAR-NAME-P determines
;; a unique real sequence.
(defstub putnam-2011-b5-a-approx (n epsilon) t)

(defun putnam-2011-b5-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and
   (rationalp x)
   (< 0 x)))

(defun-sk putnam-2011-b5-regular-name-p ()
  (forall (n epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (putnam-2011-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2011-b5-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((at-epsilon
            (putnam-2011-b5-a-approx n epsilon))
           (at-eta
            (putnam-2011-b5-a-approx n eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp at-epsilon)
        (rationalp at-eta)
        (<=
         (abs (- at-epsilon at-eta))
         (+ epsilon eta)))))))

;; Expanding the square in the source integral and integrating termwise uses
;; the exact identity
;;
;;   integral_R 1/((1+(x-u)^2)(1+(x-v)^2)) dx
;;     = 2*pi/(4+(u-v)^2).
;;
;; Thus the source hypothesis is equivalent to a linear bound on the finite
;; double sum of 1/(4+(a_i-a_j)^2). The positive factor 2*pi is absorbed into
;; the existential constant. A real bound exists exactly when a rational
;; bound exists, since a larger rational may be chosen.

(defun putnam-2011-b5-reciprocal-row
    (left-value remaining precision)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (let* ((index (- (nfix remaining) 1))
           (right-value
            (putnam-2011-b5-a-approx index precision))
           (difference (- left-value right-value)))
      (+ (/ 1 (+ 4 (* difference difference)))
         (putnam-2011-b5-reciprocal-row
          left-value index precision)))))

(defun putnam-2011-b5-reciprocal-sum-aux
    (remaining total precision)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (let* ((index (- (nfix remaining) 1))
           (left-value
            (putnam-2011-b5-a-approx index precision)))
      (+ (putnam-2011-b5-reciprocal-row
          left-value total precision)
         (putnam-2011-b5-reciprocal-sum-aux
          index total precision)))))

;; The reciprocal kernel is globally Lipschitz. With this precision, the
;; approximation error in the terms-by-terms double sum is strictly less than
;; the requested epsilon.
(defun putnam-2011-b5-reciprocal-precision
    (epsilon terms)
  (/ epsilon
     (* 4
        (expt (+ (nfix terms) 1) 2))))

(defun putnam-2011-b5-reciprocal-sum
    (terms epsilon)
  (let ((precision
         (putnam-2011-b5-reciprocal-precision
          epsilon terms)))
    (putnam-2011-b5-reciprocal-sum-aux
     terms terms precision)))

(defun-sk putnam-2011-b5-upper-bound-p (constant)
  (forall (terms epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp terms)
      (putnam-2011-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (<=
      (putnam-2011-b5-reciprocal-sum
       terms epsilon)
      (+ (* constant terms)
         epsilon)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2011-b5-upper-bound-exists-p ()
  (exists (constant)
    (and
     (rationalp constant)
     (putnam-2011-b5-upper-bound-p constant))))

;; A precision-one approximation gives a finite magnitude bound for every
;; entry in the prefix. This makes the chosen precision below control the
;; error introduced by squaring unbounded real differences.

(defun putnam-2011-b5-prefix-bound (remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      1
    (let ((index (- (nfix remaining) 1)))
      (+ 2
         (abs
          (putnam-2011-b5-a-approx index 1))
         (putnam-2011-b5-prefix-bound index)))))

(defun putnam-2011-b5-square-row
    (left-value remaining precision)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (let* ((index (- (nfix remaining) 1))
           (right-value
            (putnam-2011-b5-a-approx index precision))
           (difference (- left-value right-value)))
      (+ 1
         (* difference difference)
         (putnam-2011-b5-square-row
          left-value index precision)))))

(defun putnam-2011-b5-square-sum-aux
    (remaining total precision)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (let* ((index (- (nfix remaining) 1))
           (left-value
            (putnam-2011-b5-a-approx index precision)))
      (+ (putnam-2011-b5-square-row
          left-value total precision)
         (putnam-2011-b5-square-sum-aux
          index total precision)))))

(defun putnam-2011-b5-square-precision
    (terms epsilon)
  (let ((candidate
         (/ epsilon
            (* 16
               (putnam-2011-b5-prefix-bound terms)
               (expt (+ (nfix terms) 1) 2)))))
    (if (< candidate 1)
        candidate
      1)))

(defun putnam-2011-b5-square-sum
    (terms epsilon)
  (let ((precision
         (putnam-2011-b5-square-precision
          terms epsilon)))
    (putnam-2011-b5-square-sum-aux
     terms terms precision)))

;; Requiring the epsilon-relaxed comparison at every positive rational
;; epsilon is exactly the comparison between the represented real sum and
;; B*n^3. Restricting B to positive rationals is equivalent to the source's
;; positive real witness, since a smaller positive rational may be chosen.

(defun-sk putnam-2011-b5-lower-bound-p (constant)
  (forall (terms epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp terms)
      (putnam-2011-b5-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (<=
      (* constant (expt terms 3))
      (+ (putnam-2011-b5-square-sum
          terms epsilon)
         epsilon)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2011-b5-lower-bound-exists-p ()
  (exists (constant)
    (and
     (putnam-2011-b5-positive-rational-p constant)
     (putnam-2011-b5-lower-bound-p constant))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2011-b5-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2011-b5-regular-name-p)
    (putnam-2011-b5-upper-bound-exists-p))
   (putnam-2011-b5-lower-bound-exists-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2011_b5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2011_b5): a linear whole-line integral bound
-- for squared sums of Cauchy kernels implies a uniform positive cubic lower
-- bound for the associated double sums. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2011B5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

rightRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
rightRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals (suc i))
              step)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function integralValue =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ mesh ->
      rightRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc mesh))
    integralValue

WholeLineIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
WholeLineIntegralValue {R} reals function integralValue =
  Exists (Nat -> R)
    (\ truncatedIntegrals ->
      ((radius : Nat) ->
        IntervalIntegralValue reals
          (negate reals (fromNat reals radius))
          (fromNat reals radius)
          function
          (truncatedIntegrals radius))
      and
      ConvergesTo reals truncatedIntegrals integralValue)

kernelSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  R
kernelSum reals a n x =
  sumFirst reals n
    (\ i ->
      divide reals
        (oneR reals)
        (add reals
          (oneR reals)
          (square reals (subtract reals x (a i)))))

integrand :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  R
integrand reals a n x =
  square reals (kernelSum reals a n x)

doubleSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
doubleSum reals a n =
  sumFirst reals n
    (\ i ->
      sumFirst reals n
        (\ j ->
          add reals
            (oneR reals)
            (square reals
              (subtract reals (a i) (a j)))))

three : Nat
three =
  suc (suc (suc zero))

putnam-2011-b5 : Set1
putnam-2011-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (a : Nat -> R) ->
  Exists R
    (\ A ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      Exists R
        (\ integralValue ->
          WholeLineIntegralValue reals
            (integrand reals a n)
            integralValue
          and
          lessOrEqual reals
            integralValue
            (multiply reals A (fromNat reals n)))) ->
  Exists R
    (\ B ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) B
      and
      ((n : Nat) ->
        lessOrEqual reals
          (multiply reals
            B
            (naturalPower reals (fromNat reals n) three))
          (doubleSum reals a n)))

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b5:
  a uniform linear bound on whole-real-line integrals of squared finite sums
  of Cauchy kernels implies a positive cubic lower bound for the associated
  double sums. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory integrationTheory;

val putnam_2011_b5 =
  ``!a : num -> real.
      (?A : real.
         !n : num.
           integration$integral UNIV
             (\x : real.
                (SIGMA
                   (\i : num. 1 / (1 + (x - a i) pow 2))
                   (count n)) pow 2) <=
           A * &n)
      ==>
      ?B : real.
        0 < B /\
        !n : num.
          B * (&n) pow 3 <=
          SIGMA
            (\i : num.
               SIGMA
                 (\j : num. 1 + (a i - a j) pow 2)
                 (count n))
            (count n)``;

  double sums for an arbitrary real sequence. This file contains no proof.

$(

  database contains no $p proof statement.

${

  putnambench-putnam-2011-b5 $a |-
    A. a e. ( RR ^m NN0 )

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b5:
% a linear bound on full-line integrals of squared finite Cauchy-kernel sums
% implies a positive cubic lower bound for the pairwise-distance sum.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2011_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  finite_sum(
      values: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      finite_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  valid_tagged_partition(
      left, right: real,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = left
      AND points(count) = right
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          (points(index) < points(index + 1)
            AND points(index) <= tags(index)
            AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1))

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      function_value: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(
        function_value, points, tags, count - 1)
        + function_value(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_interval_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      left, right, integral_value: real): bool =
    left < right
      AND FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
          FORALL
              (points, tags: real_sequence),
              (count: nat):
            (valid_tagged_partition(
                left, right, points, tags, count)
              AND mesh_less_than(
                points, count, mesh_bound))
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                riemann_sum(
                  function_value, points, tags, count)
                  - integral_value)
                < epsilon_value

  has_full_line_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: posreal):
        FORALL (radius: posreal):
          cutoff <= radius IMPLIES
            EXISTS (truncated_value: real):
              has_interval_integral(
                function_value,
                -radius,
                radius,
                truncated_value)
                AND abs(truncated_value - integral_value)
                  < epsilon_value

  cauchy_kernel_sum(
      a: real_sequence,
      n: nat,
      x: real): real =
    finite_sum(
      LAMBDA (index: nat):
        safe_div(1, 1 + (x - a(index)) ^ 2),
      n)

  squared_kernel_sum(
      a: real_sequence,
      n: nat): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      cauchy_kernel_sum(a, n, x) ^ 2

  pairwise_distance_sum(
      a: real_sequence,
      n: nat): real =
    finite_sum(
      LAMBDA (i: nat):
        finite_sum(
          LAMBDA (j: nat):
            1 + (a(i) - a(j)) ^ 2,
          n),
      n)

  putnam_2011_b5: bool =
    FORALL (a: real_sequence):
      (EXISTS (A: real):
        FORALL (n: nat):
          EXISTS (integral_value: real):
            has_full_line_integral(
              squared_kernel_sum(a, n),
              integral_value)
              AND integral_value <= A * (n :: real))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (B: real):
          B > 0
            AND FORALL (n: nat):
              pairwise_distance_sum(a, n)
                >= B * (n :: real) ^ 3
END putnam_2011_b5

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b6:
;; for every odd prime p, at least (p+1)/2 residues n from 0 through p-1
;; make the factorial polynomial sum from k=0 through p-1 nonzero modulo p.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Testing every possible divisor from 2 through NUMBER-1 is exactly the
;; usual primality condition for a natural number greater than one.
(defun putnam-2011-b6-no-divisor-through-p (number divisor)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix divisor)))
  (if (or (not (natp divisor))
          (<= divisor 1))
      t
    (and
     (not (equal (mod number divisor) 0))
     (putnam-2011-b6-no-divisor-through-p
      number (- divisor 1)))))

(defun putnam-2011-b6-prime-p (number)
  (and
   (natp number)
   (< 1 number)
   (putnam-2011-b6-no-divisor-through-p
    number (- number 1))))

(defun putnam-2011-b6-factorial (k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix k)))
  (if (zp k)
      1
    (* k
       (putnam-2011-b6-factorial (- k 1)))))

;; COUNT represents the source index range 0,...,COUNT-1.
(defun putnam-2011-b6-factorial-polynomial-sum (n count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (or (not (natp n))
          (not (natp count))
          (zp count))
      0
    (let ((k (- count 1)))
      (+ (* (putnam-2011-b6-factorial k)
            (expt n k))
         (putnam-2011-b6-factorial-polynomial-sum
          n k)))))

(defun putnam-2011-b6-nondivisible-p (p n)
  (and
   (natp p)
   (< 0 p)
   (natp n)
   (not
    (equal
     (mod
      (putnam-2011-b6-factorial-polynomial-sum n p)
      p)
     0))))

;; COUNT represents the source residue range 0,...,COUNT-1, so calling this
;; with COUNT=P computes exactly the cardinality appearing in the statement.
(defun putnam-2011-b6-nondivisible-count (p count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (or (not (natp p))
          (not (natp count))
          (zp count))
      0
    (let ((n (- count 1)))
      (+ (if (putnam-2011-b6-nondivisible-p p n)
             1
           0)
         (putnam-2011-b6-nondivisible-count
          p n)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2011-b6-statement (p)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2011-b6-prime-p p)
    (equal (mod p 2) 1))
   (<= (floor (+ p 1) 2)
       (putnam-2011-b6-nondivisible-count p p))))

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2011_b6): for an odd prime p, the factorial
-- polynomial sum is nonzero modulo p at at least (p + 1) / 2 residues below p.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2011B6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record AtLeastCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A

    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)

    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

record Divides (divisor number : Nat) : Set where
  constructor divides
  field
    quotient : Nat
    equation : divisor * quotient == number

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

Odd : Nat -> Set
Odd number =
  Exists Nat
    (\ half ->
      number == twoN * half + oneN)

Prime : Nat -> Set
Prime number =
  twoN <=N number
  and
  ((divisor : Nat) ->
    Divides divisor number ->
    divisor == oneN or divisor == number)

naturalPower : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalPower base zero =
  oneN
naturalPower base (suc exponent) =
  naturalPower base exponent * base

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =

factorial (suc n) =

sumFirst : Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat
sumFirst zero term =
  zero
sumFirst (suc length) term =
  sumFirst length term + term length

factorialPolynomial : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
factorialPolynomial p n =
  sumFirst p
    (\ k ->
      factorial k * naturalPower n k)

GoodResidue : Nat -> Nat -> Set
GoodResidue p n =
  n <N p
  and
  Not (Divides p (factorialPolynomial p n))

halfFloor : Nat -> Nat
halfFloor zero =
  zero
halfFloor (suc zero) =
  zero
halfFloor (suc (suc n)) =
  suc (halfFloor n)

title: putnam_2011_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2011_b6:
% for every odd prime p, at least (p + 1) / 2 residues n below p make the
% factorial polynomial sum from k = 0 through p - 1 nondivisible by p.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2011_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  factorial_polynomial_sum(
      n, count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      factorial_polynomial_sum(n, count - 1)
        + nat_factorial(count - 1) * n ^ (count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value

  count_below(
      limit: nat,
      property: [nat -> bool]): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_below(limit - 1, property)
        + IF property(limit - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  putnam_2011_b6: bool =
    FORALL (p: nat):
      (mod(p, 2) = 1 AND prime_nat(p))
      IMPLIES
        count_below(
          p,
          LAMBDA (n: nat):
            NOT nat_divides(
              p,
              factorial_polynomial_sum(n, p)))
          >= ndiv(p + 1, 2)
END putnam_2011_b6

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_a1:
;; among twelve real numbers in the open interval (1,12), three distinct
;; entries are the side lengths of an acute triangle. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Standard ACL2 represents exact rationals rather than arbitrary reals. For
;; this closed statement, the rational formulation below is bidirectionally
;; equivalent to the source real formulation. If a real counterexample is
;; sorted as x_1 <= ... <= x_12, then it satisfies
;; x_(k-2)^2 + x_(k-1)^2 <= x_k^2 for k = 3,...,12. Multiplying x_k by
;; t^k for a sufficiently small rational t > 1 makes all these inequalities
;; strict while keeping every entry in (1,12). A sufficiently close rational
;; perturbation then preserves the strict ordering, recurrence inequalities,
;; and interval bounds, yielding a rational counterexample. Conversely, every
;; rational counterexample is already a real counterexample.

(defun putnam-2012-a1-entry-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (rationalp (car values))
       (< 1 (car values))
       (< (car values) 12)
       (putnam-2012-a1-entry-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-2012-a1-square (value)
  (* value value))

(defun putnam-2012-a1-acute-witness-p (values i j k)
  (and
   (natp i)
   (natp j)
   (natp k)
   (< i 12)
   (< j 12)
   (< k 12)
   (not (equal i j))
   (not (equal i k))
   (not (equal j k))
   (<= (nth i values) (nth k values))
   (<= (nth j values) (nth k values))
   (<
    (putnam-2012-a1-square (nth k values))
    (+
     (putnam-2012-a1-square (nth i values))
     (putnam-2012-a1-square (nth j values))))))

(defun putnam-2012-a1-search-k (values i j k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix k)))
  (if (natp k)
      (or
       (putnam-2012-a1-acute-witness-p values i j k)
       (and
        (not (zp k))
        (putnam-2012-a1-search-k values i j (- k 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2012-a1-search-j (values i j)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix j)))
  (if (natp j)
      (or
       (putnam-2012-a1-search-k values i j 11)
       (and
        (not (zp j))
        (putnam-2012-a1-search-j values i (- j 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2012-a1-search-i (values i)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix i)))
  (if (natp i)
      (or
       (putnam-2012-a1-search-j values i 11)
       (and
        (not (zp i))
        (putnam-2012-a1-search-i values (- i 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2012-a1-statement (values)
  (implies
   (and
    (true-listp values)
    (equal (len values) 12)
    (putnam-2012-a1-entry-list-p values))
   (putnam-2012-a1-search-i values 11)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

module Putnam2012A1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B
