(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b3:
  in every round-robin tournament on 2n teams, one can choose a winning team
  from each of the 2n - 1 days without choosing any team twice. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2012_b3 =
  ``let matchup_games =
      \n (matchups : num -> num -> num).
        !d t : num.
          d < 2 * n - 1 /\ t < 2 * n
          ==>
          matchups d t < 2 * n /\
          matchups d t <> t /\
          matchups d (matchups d t) = t
    in
    let matchup_all =
      \n (matchups : num -> num -> num).
        !t1 t2 : num.
          t1 < 2 * n /\ t2 < 2 * n /\ t1 <> t2
          ==>
          ?d : num. d < 2 * n - 1 /\ matchups d t1 = t2
    in
    let matchup_wins =
      \n (matchups : num -> num -> num) (wins : num -> num -> bool).
        !d t : num.
          d < 2 * n - 1 /\ t < 2 * n
          ==>
          (wins d t <=> ~wins d (matchups d t))
    in
    let winning_choices =
      \n (wins : num -> num -> bool).
        ?choices : num -> num.
          (!d : num.
             d < 2 * n - 1
             ==>
             choices d < 2 * n /\ wins d (choices d)) /\
          INJ choices (count (2 * n - 1)) (count (2 * n))
    in
      ((!n : num.
          1 <= n
          ==>
          !matchups : num -> num -> num.
          !wins : num -> num -> bool.
            matchup_games n matchups /\
            matchup_all n matchups /\
            matchup_wins n matchups wins
            ==>
            winning_choices n wins)
       <=>
       T)``;

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For positive n, 0 ..^ (2n - 1) and 0 ..^ 2n are respectively the finite

  day-indexed family of team maps. The fixed-point-free involution conditions
  say that every team plays exactly one opponent each day, and the following
  existential condition says every distinct pair meets during the tournament.

  W is a day-indexed family of functions from teams to the two-element ordinal
  2o = {0,1}, a definitional encoding of the source Bool-valued win function.
  Inequality of the two values is equivalent to Boolean complementation. The
  witness C remains internally existential and is required to be a one-to-one
  function from all days to teams, with every chosen team assigned win value
  one. The source solution proposition is True, represented by T. in the final
  biconditional. The sole declaration is an unproved $a statement encoding;
  this database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d C M W d n t u $.

  putnambench-putnam-2012-b3 $a |- (
    (
      A. n e. NN
        A. M e.
          (
            (
              ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
              ^m
              ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
            )
            ^m
            ( 0 ..^ ( ( 2 x. n ) - 1 ) )
          )
          A. W e.
            (
              (
                2o
                ^m
                ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
              )
              ^m
              ( 0 ..^ ( ( 2 x. n ) - 1 ) )
            )
            (
              (
                (
                  A. d e. ( 0 ..^ ( ( 2 x. n ) - 1 ) )
                    A. t e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
                      (
                        (
                          ( ( M ` d ) ` t )
                          =/=
                          t
                        )
                        /\
                        (
                          ( ( M ` d ) ` ( ( M ` d ) ` t ) )
                          =
                          t
                        )
                      )
                  /\
                  A. t e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
                    A. u e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
                      (
                        t =/= u
                        ->
                        E. d e. ( 0 ..^ ( ( 2 x. n ) - 1 ) )
                          ( ( M ` d ) ` t ) = u
                      )
                )
                /\
                A. d e. ( 0 ..^ ( ( 2 x. n ) - 1 ) )
                  A. t e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
                    (
                      ( ( W ` d ) ` t )
                      =/=
                      ( ( W ` d ) ` ( ( M ` d ) ` t ) )
                    )
              )
              ->
              E. C
                (
                  C
                  :
                  ( 0 ..^ ( ( 2 x. n ) - 1 ) )
                  -1-1->
                  ( 0 ..^ ( 2 x. n ) )
                  /\
                  A. d e. ( 0 ..^ ( ( 2 x. n ) - 1 ) )
                    ( ( W ` d ) ` ( C ` d ) ) = 1
                )
            )
    )
    <-> T.
  ) $.
$}

title: putnam_2012_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b3:
% every round-robin tournament on 2n teams admits a choice of one winning team
% from each day with no team chosen twice. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2012_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  matchup_table: TYPE = [nat, nat -> nat]
  win_table: TYPE = [nat, nat -> bool]
  choice_function: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  team_count(n: posnat): nat = 2 * n

  day_count(n: posnat): nat = 2 * n - 1

  valid_daily_matchups(
      n: posnat,
      matchups: matchup_table): bool =
    FORALL (day, team: nat):
      day < day_count(n) AND team < team_count(n)
        IMPLIES
          matchups(day, team) < team_count(n)
            AND matchups(day, team) /= team
            AND matchups(day, matchups(day, team)) = team

  complete_round_robin(
      n: posnat,
      matchups: matchup_table): bool =
    FORALL (first_team, second_team: nat):
      first_team < team_count(n)
        AND second_team < team_count(n)
        AND first_team /= second_team
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (day: nat):
          day < day_count(n)
            AND matchups(day, first_team) = second_team

  consistent_results(
      n: posnat,
      matchups: matchup_table,
      wins: win_table): bool =
    FORALL (day, team: nat):
      day < day_count(n) AND team < team_count(n)
        IMPLIES
          wins(day, team)
            = NOT wins(day, matchups(day, team))

  injective_on_days(
      n: posnat,
      choices: choice_function): bool =
    FORALL (first_day, second_day: nat):
      first_day < day_count(n)
        AND second_day < day_count(n)
        AND choices(first_day) = choices(second_day)
      IMPLIES first_day = second_day

  winning_representatives_exist(
      n: posnat,
      wins: win_table): bool =
    EXISTS (choices: choice_function):
      (FORALL (day: nat):
        day < day_count(n)
          IMPLIES
            choices(day) < team_count(n)
              AND wins(day, choices(day)))
        AND injective_on_days(n, choices)

  putnam_2012_b3: bool =
    FORALL
        (n: posnat),
        (matchups: matchup_table),
        (wins: win_table):
      (valid_daily_matchups(n, matchups)
        AND complete_round_robin(n, matchups)
        AND consistent_results(n, matchups, wins))
      IMPLIES winning_representatives_exist(n, wins)
END putnam_2012_b3

import Mathlib

open Matrix Function Real Topology Filter

noncomputable abbrev putnam_2012_b4_solution : Prop := True
/--
Suppose that $a_0 = 1$ and that $a_{n+1} = a_n + e^{-a_n}$ for $n=0,1,2,\dots$. Does $a_n - \log n$
have a finite limit as $n \to \infty$? (Here $\log n = \log_e n = \ln n$.)
-/
theorem putnam_2012_b4
(a : ℕ → ℝ)
(ha0 : a 0 = 1)
(han : ∀ n : ℕ, a (n + 1) = a n + exp (-a n))
: ((∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n ↦ a n - Real.log n) atTop (𝓝 L)) ↔ putnam_2012_b4_solution) :=
sorry

    end)

putnam_2012_b4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b4:
;; whether the real sequence a_n - ln(n), where a_0 = 1 and
;; a_(n+1) = a_n + exp(-a_n), has a finite limit. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The recurrence uniquely determines the source sequence.  The definitions
;; below give each of its terms concrete exact rational interval names.
;; Exponential bounds come from the positive Taylor series with a geometric
;; remainder bound, and logarithm bounds come from the atanh series
;;
;;   ln(n) = 2 * sum_{j>=0} z^(2*j+1)/(2*j+1),
;;   z = (n-1)/(n+1).
;;
;; Refinement is unbounded.  Thus no real is replaced by a fixed-precision
;; rational, finite table, opaque carrier, or external witness.

(defun p12b4-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n (p12b4-factorial (1- n)))))

(defun p12b4-power (base exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      1
    (* base
       (p12b4-power base (1- exponent)))))

;; Sum x^j/j! for 0 <= j < TERMS.

(defun p12b4-exp-prefix (x terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let ((j (1- terms)))
      (+ (p12b4-exp-prefix x j)
         (/ (p12b4-power x j)
            (p12b4-factorial j))))))

;; For nonnegative rational X, this count is strictly larger than X and
;; tends to infinity with PRECISION.

(defun p12b4-exp-term-count (x precision)
  (+ 2
     (nfix precision)
     (if (rationalp x)
         (abs (numerator x))
       0)))

;; If TERMS > X >= 0, the omitted Taylor tail is at most
;;
;;   (x^terms/terms!) / (1 - x/(terms+1)).

(defun p12b4-exp-tail-bound (x terms)
  (let* ((first-omitted
          (/ (p12b4-power x terms)
             (p12b4-factorial terms)))
         (ratio (/ x (+ terms 1))))
    (/ first-omitted (- 1 ratio))))

(defun p12b4-exp-positive-lower (x precision)
  (let ((terms
         (p12b4-exp-term-count x precision)))
    (p12b4-exp-prefix x terms)))

(defun p12b4-exp-positive-upper (x precision)
  (let ((terms
         (p12b4-exp-term-count x precision)))
    (+ (p12b4-exp-prefix x terms)
       (p12b4-exp-tail-bound x terms))))

;; Reciprocal interval bounds for exp(-X), with X nonnegative.

(defun p12b4-exp-negative-lower (x precision)
  (/ 1 (p12b4-exp-positive-upper x precision)))

(defun p12b4-exp-negative-upper (x precision)
  (/ 1 (p12b4-exp-positive-lower x precision)))

;; Concrete rational enclosures of the uniquely determined a_n.  Monotonicity
;; of x |-> exp(-x) reverses the endpoints in the exponential summand.

(mutual-recursion
 (defun p12b4-a-lower (n precision)
   (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
   (if (zp n)
       1
     (let* ((previous (1- n))
            (inner-precision
             (+ (nfix precision) (nfix n)))
            (lower
             (p12b4-a-lower
              previous inner-precision))
            (upper
             (p12b4-a-upper
              previous inner-precision)))
       (+ lower
          (p12b4-exp-negative-lower
           upper inner-precision)))))
 (defun p12b4-a-upper (n precision)
   (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
   (if (zp n)
       1
     (let* ((previous (1- n))
            (inner-precision
             (+ (nfix precision) (nfix n)))
            (lower
             (p12b4-a-lower
              previous inner-precision))
            (upper
             (p12b4-a-upper
              previous inner-precision)))
       (+ upper
          (p12b4-exp-negative-upper
           lower inner-precision))))))

;; Sum the first TERMS terms of the exact atanh series for ln(N).

(defun p12b4-log-z (n)
  (if (posp n)
      (/ (- n 1) (+ n 1))
    0))

(defun p12b4-log-prefix-aux (z terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((j (1- terms))
           (degree (+ (* 2 j) 1)))
      (+ (p12b4-log-prefix-aux z j)
         (/ (* 2
               (p12b4-power z degree))
            degree)))))

(defun p12b4-log-prefix (n terms)
  (if (posp n)
      (p12b4-log-prefix-aux
       (p12b4-log-z n) terms)
    0))

;; Dropping the denominators 2*j+1 bounds the remaining positive series by
;; a geometric tail.  This is zero at N=1 and tends to zero for every fixed
;; positive N.

(defun p12b4-log-tail-bound (n terms)
  (if (posp n)
      (let* ((z (p12b4-log-z n))
             (degree (+ (* 2 (nfix terms)) 1)))
        (/ (* 2 (p12b4-power z degree))
           (- 1 (p12b4-power z 2))))
    0))

(defun p12b4-log-lower (n precision)
  (p12b4-log-prefix
   n (+ 1 (nfix precision))))

(defun p12b4-log-upper (n precision)
  (let ((terms (+ 1 (nfix precision))))
    (+ (p12b4-log-prefix n terms)
       (p12b4-log-tail-bound n terms))))

;; Rational interval names for a_n - ln(n).  At n=0, LOG-LOWER and
;; LOG-UPPER are both zero, matching the totalized logarithm in the formal
;; ground-truth statements.

(defun p12b4-difference-lower (n precision)
  (- (p12b4-a-lower n precision)
     (p12b4-log-upper n precision)))

(defun p12b4-difference-upper (n precision)
  (- (p12b4-a-upper n precision)
     (p12b4-log-lower n precision)))

;; A strict distance bound between two exact interval-named reals holds when
;; some finite refinement certifies both directed endpoint inequalities.
;; Because all bounds shrink to their exact denotations, this is equivalent
;; to |(a_m-ln m) - (a_n-ln n)| < EPSILON over the real numbers.

(defun p12b4-close-at-refinement-p
    (m n epsilon refinement)
  (let ((m-lower
         (p12b4-difference-lower
          m refinement))
        (m-upper
         (p12b4-difference-upper
          m refinement))
        (n-lower
         (p12b4-difference-lower
          n refinement))
        (n-upper
         (p12b4-difference-upper
          n refinement)))
    (and
     (< (- m-upper n-lower) epsilon)
     (< (- n-upper m-lower) epsilon))))

(defun-sk p12b4-exact-close-p (m n epsilon)
  (exists (refinement)
    (and
     (natp refinement)
     (p12b4-close-at-refinement-p
      m n epsilon refinement))))

(defun-sk p12b4-cauchy-tail-p (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (m n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp m)
      (natp n)
      (natp cutoff)
      (<= cutoff m)
      (<= cutoff n))
     (p12b4-exact-close-p m n epsilon))))

(defun-sk p12b4-cauchy-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (p12b4-cauchy-tail-p
      epsilon cutoff))))

;; A real sequence has a finite real limit exactly when it is Cauchy.
;; Quantifying over every positive rational epsilon is equivalent to
;; quantifying over every positive real epsilon, by density of the rationals.
;; This keeps the limit and cutoff content internal without restricting the
;; putative limit to an ACL2 rational.

(defun-sk p12b4-finite-limit-exists-p ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (p12b4-cauchy-cutoff-exists-p
      epsilon))))

(defun putnambench-acl2-putnam-2012-b4-statement ()
  ;; The published answer to the source's yes/no question is True.
  (p12b4-finite-limit-exists-p))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2012_b4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2012_b4): the recursively defined real sequence
-- a[0] = 1, a[n+1] = a[n] + exp(-a[n]) has a finite limit after subtracting
-- log n. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  suc zero
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

exponentialTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

ExponentialValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
ExponentialValue reals x value =
  SeriesHasSum reals
    (exponentialTerm reals x)
    value

record StandardExponentialLogarithm
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    exponential logarithm : R -> R

    exponential-series :
      (x : R) ->
      ExponentialValue reals x (exponential x)

    exponential-positive :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals
        (zeroR reals)
        (exponential x)

    exponential-injective :
      (x y : R) ->
      exponential x == exponential y ->
      x == y

    exponential-logarithm :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      exponential (logarithm x) == x

    logarithm-zero :
      logarithm (zeroR reals) == zeroR reals

open StandardExponentialLogarithm

module Putnam2012B4Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (analysis : StandardExponentialLogarithm reals) where

  normalizedSequence :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    R
  normalizedSequence a n =
    subtract reals
      (a n)
      (logarithm analysis (fromNat reals n))

  Recurrence :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  Recurrence a =
    (n : Nat) ->
    a (suc n) ==
    add reals
      (a n)
      (exponential analysis (negate reals (a n)))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (a : Nat -> R) ->
    a zero == oneR reals ->
    Recurrence a ->
    Exists R
      (\ limit ->
        ConvergesTo reals
          (normalizedSequence a)
          limit)

putnam-2012-b4 : Set1
putnam-2012-b4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (analysis : StandardExponentialLogarithm reals) ->
  Putnam2012B4Statement.proposition reals analysis

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2012_b4: finite-limit convergence of a logarithmically adjusted
  real sequence defined by an exponential recurrence. This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  A ranges over arbitrary real-valued sequences indexed by the nonnegative
  integers. The antecedent preserves the initial value A(0) = 1 and the
  recurrence A(n+1) = A(n) + exp(-A(n)) at every nonnegative index.

  The conclusion keeps the finite real limit internally existential. It uses
  the positive-index tail n |-> A(n) - log(n), where the natural logarithm is
  defined; deleting the single index zero does not change convergence at
  infinity. The Rocq source defines the solution proposition as True, in
  agreement with the Lean and Isabelle annotations, so the source
  biconditional is logically equivalent to the convergence assertion below.
  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d A L n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2012-b4 $a |-
    A. A e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
      (
        (
          ( A ` 0 ) = 1
          /\
          A. n e. NN0
            ( A ` ( n + 1 ) )
            =
            (
              ( A ` n )
              +
              ( exp ` ( -u ( A ` n ) ) )
            )
        )
        ->
        E. L e. RR
          (
            n e. NN |->
              (
                ( A ` n )
                -
                ( log ` n )
              )
          )
          ~~>
          L
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2012_b4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b4:
% the recursively defined real sequence a(0) = 1,
% a(n + 1) = a(n) + exp(-a(n)) has a(n) - ln(n) converge to a finite real
% limit. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2012_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  natural_log(x: real): real =
    IF x > 0 THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (value: real):
          real_exponential(value) = x)
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  has_finite_log_adjusted_limit(a: real_sequence): bool =
    EXISTS (limit_value: real):
      converges_to(
        LAMBDA (n: nat):
          a(n) - natural_log(n :: real),
        limit_value)

  putnam_2012_b4_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_2012_b4: bool =
    FORALL (a: real_sequence):
      (a(0) = 1
        AND (FORALL (n: nat):
          a(n + 1) = a(n) + real_exponential(-a(n))))
      IMPLIES
        (has_finite_log_adjusted_limit(a)
          IFF putnam_2012_b4_solution)
END putnam_2012_b4

/--
Prove that, for any two bounded functions $g_1, g_2: \RR \to [1, \infty)$, there exist functions $h_1, h_2: \RR \to \RR$ such that, for every $x \in \RR$, \[ \sup_{s \in \RR} (g_1(s)^x g_2(s))  = \max_{t \in \RR} (x h_1(t) + h_2(t)).\]

theorem putnam_2012_b5
(g1 g2 : ℝ → ℝ)
(hgim : ∀ x : ℝ, g1 x ≥ 1 ∧ g2 x ≥ 1)
(hgbd : ∃ B1 B2 : ℝ, ∀ x : ℝ, g1 x ≤ B1 ∧ g2 x ≤ B2)
: ∃ h1 h2 : ℝ → ℝ, ∀ x : ℝ, sSup {((g1 s)^x * (g2 s)) | s : ℝ} = sSup {(x * (h1 t) + h2 t) | t : ℝ} :=

title: putnam_2012_b5

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b5:
   the supremum of a power-product family from two bounded real functions
   represented as a maximum of affine functions. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2012_b5_is_supremum
    (values : R -> Prop) (bound : R) : Prop :=
  (forall value : R, values value -> value <= bound) /\
  (forall upper : R,
      (forall value : R, values value -> value <= upper) ->
      bound <= upper).

Definition putnam_2012_b5_power_values
    (g1 g2 : R -> R) (x : R) : R -> Prop :=
  fun value : R =>
    exists s : R, value = Rpower (g1 s) x * g2 s.

Definition putnam_2012_b5_affine_values
    (h1 h2 : R -> R) (x : R) : R -> Prop :=
  fun value : R =>
    exists t : R, value = x * h1 t + h2 t.

Definition putnam_2012_b5_is_maximum
    (values : R -> Prop) (maximum : R) : Prop :=
  values maximum /\
  forall value : R, values value -> value <= maximum.

Theorem putnam_2012_b5
    (g1 g2 : R -> R)
    (hgim : forall x : R, 1 <= g1 x /\ 1 <= g2 x)
    (hgbd :
      exists B1 B2 : R,
        forall x : R, g1 x <= B1 /\ g2 x <= B2) :
  exists h1 h2 : R -> R,
    forall x : R,
      exists bound : R,
        putnam_2012_b5_is_supremum
          (putnam_2012_b5_power_values g1 g2 x) bound /\
        putnam_2012_b5_is_maximum
          (putnam_2012_b5_affine_values h1 h2 x) bound.
Admitted.

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b5:
;; bounded real functions with values at least one admit two real functions
;; whose affine suprema equal the suprema of g1(s)^x*g2(s). This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Reals are rational regular Cauchy names, and real functions are extensional
;; ACL2 function objects on those names. FN-EQUAL supplies unbounded universal
;; quantification over names and function objects; NOT/FN-EQUAL supplies the
;; source's internal existential quantifiers, so no finite carrier or external
;; witness replaces a source quantifier.
;;
;; A power oracle P(s,x) is bundled into the conclusion witness. Positivity,
;; P(s,0)=1, P(s,1)=g1(s), multiplicativity in x, and monotonicity in x
;; uniquely characterize g1(s)^x because g1(s)>=1. Every such base has this
;; oracle, so adding it as a definitional witness is bidirectionally
;; equivalent to using real powr.
;;
;; A common value is the supremum of each displayed family exactly when it is
;; an upper bound and is below every upper bound. The source hypotheses make
;; the left family nonempty and bounded for every real x. Thus the internal
;; common-supremum function is exactly equivalent to equality of the two sSup
;; values, including boundedness of the affine family.

(defun putnam-2012-b5-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'cons
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2012-b5-term-list (cdr terms)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-apply-term (function arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2012-b5-quoted function)
        (putnam-2012-b5-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-apply-object-term
    (function-term arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        function-term
        (putnam-2012-b5-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'if
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms (cdr terms))
            (putnam-2012-b5-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2012-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list 'if
        hypothesis
        conclusion
        (putnam-2012-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-negate-term (value)
  (list 'unary-- value))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-subtract-term (left right)
  (putnam-2012-b5-add-term
   left
   (putnam-2012-b5-negate-term right)))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-multiply-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-* left right))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-divide-term (numerator denominator)
  (putnam-2012-b5-multiply-term
   numerator
   (list 'unary-/ denominator)))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-absolute-term (value)
  (list 'if
        (list '< value (putnam-2012-b5-quoted 0))
        (putnam-2012-b5-negate-term value)
        value))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-less-equal-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        (list '< right left)
        (putnam-2012-b5-quoted nil)
        (putnam-2012-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-positive-rational-term (value)
  (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
   (list
    (list 'rationalp value)
    (list '< (putnam-2012-b5-quoted 0) value))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda
        formals
        (putnam-2012-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-real-value-term (name precision)
  (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term name (list precision)))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-object-real-value-term
    (name-term precision)
  (putnam-2012-b5-apply-object-term
   name-term
   (list precision)))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-real-cauchy-function (name)
  (let* ((left
          (putnam-2012-b5-real-value-term name 'epsilon))
         (right
          (putnam-2012-b5-real-value-term name 'eta))
         (distance
          (putnam-2012-b5-absolute-term
           (putnam-2012-b5-subtract-term left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon eta)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (putnam-2012-b5-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
        (putnam-2012-b5-positive-rational-term 'eta)))
      (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2012-b5-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2012-b5-add-term
          'epsilon 'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p (name)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-real-cauchy-function name)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function
     '(epsilon eta)))))

;; Sampling at eta/4 makes these universal rational inequalities exact
;; predicates on the represented real limits.

(defun putnam-2012-b5-real-distance-function
    (left-name right-name bound)
  (let* ((precision
          (putnam-2012-b5-multiply-term 1/4 'eta))
         (left
          (putnam-2012-b5-real-value-term
           left-name precision))
         (right
          (putnam-2012-b5-real-value-term
           right-name precision))
         (distance
          (putnam-2012-b5-absolute-term
           (putnam-2012-b5-subtract-term left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(eta)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2012-b5-positive-rational-term 'eta)
      (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2012-b5-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2012-b5-add-term
          (putnam-2012-b5-quoted bound)
          'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-real-distance-at-most-p
    (left-name right-name bound)
  (and
   (rationalp bound)
   (putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p left-name)
   (putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p right-name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-real-distance-function
     left-name right-name bound)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(eta)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-real-equal-p
    (left-name right-name)
  (putnam-2012-b5-real-distance-at-most-p
   left-name right-name 0))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-real-order-function
    (left-name right-name)
  (let* ((precision
          (putnam-2012-b5-multiply-term 1/4 'eta))
         (left
          (putnam-2012-b5-real-value-term
           left-name precision))
         (right
          (putnam-2012-b5-real-value-term
           right-name precision)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(eta)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2012-b5-positive-rational-term 'eta)
      (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2012-b5-less-equal-term
         left
         (putnam-2012-b5-add-term
          right 'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-real-le-p
    (left-name right-name)
  (and
   (putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p left-name)
   (putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p right-name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-real-order-function
     left-name right-name)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(eta)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-real-lt-p
    (left-name right-name)
  (and
   (putnam-2012-b5-real-le-p left-name right-name)
   (not
    (putnam-2012-b5-real-equal-p
     left-name right-name))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-rational-name (value)
  (list 'lambda
        '(precision)
        (putnam-2012-b5-quoted value)))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-add-name (left-name right-name)
  (let* ((precision
          (putnam-2012-b5-multiply-term 1/2 'epsilon))
         (left
          (putnam-2012-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2012-b5-quoted left-name)
           precision))
         (right
          (putnam-2012-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2012-b5-quoted right-name)
           precision)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2012-b5-add-term left right))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-multiply-name
    (left-name right-name)
  (let* ((left-at-one
          (putnam-2012-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2012-b5-quoted left-name)
           1))
         (right-at-one
          (putnam-2012-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2012-b5-quoted right-name)
           1))
         (scale
          (putnam-2012-b5-multiply-term
           8
           (putnam-2012-b5-add-term
            3
            (putnam-2012-b5-add-term
             (putnam-2012-b5-absolute-term left-at-one)
             (putnam-2012-b5-absolute-term right-at-one)))))
         (candidate
          (putnam-2012-b5-divide-term
           'epsilon scale))
         (precision
          (list 'if
                (list '< 1 candidate)
                1
                candidate))
         (left
          (putnam-2012-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2012-b5-quoted left-name)
           precision))
         (right
          (putnam-2012-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2012-b5-quoted right-name)
           precision)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2012-b5-multiply-term left right))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-unary-output-function
    (function)
  (let ((output
         (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term function '(x))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 'x)
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p output)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-unary-extensional-function
    (function)
  (let ((left-output
         (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term
          function '(left)))
        (right-output
         (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term
          function '(right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(left right)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-equal-p
            'left 'right)
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-equal-p
            left-output right-output)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-real-function-p (function)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp function)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-unary-output-function function)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(x)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-unary-extensional-function function)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function
     '(left right)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-lower-one-function (function)
  (let ((value
         (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term function '(x))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 'x)
      (list
       'putnam-2012-b5-real-le-p
       (putnam-2012-b5-quoted
        (putnam-2012-b5-rational-name 1))
       value)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-lower-one-p (function)
  (fn-equal
   (putnam-2012-b5-lower-one-function function)
   (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(x))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-bound-function
    (g1 g2 bound1 bound2)
  (let ((value1
         (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term g1 '(x)))
        (value2
         (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term g2 '(x))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 'x)
      (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-le-p
              value1
              (putnam-2012-b5-quoted bound1))
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-le-p
              value2
              (putnam-2012-b5-quoted bound2))))))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-bound-witness-p
    (witness g1 g2)
  (and
   (true-listp witness)
   (equal (len witness) 2)
   (let ((bound1 (nth 0 witness))
         (bound2 (nth 1 witness)))
     (and
      (putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p bound1)
      (putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p bound2)
      (fn-equal
       (putnam-2012-b5-bound-function
        g1 g2 bound1 bound2)
       (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(x)))))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-bound-failure-function (g1 g2)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(witness)
   (list
    'if
    (list 'putnam-2012-b5-bound-witness-p
          'witness
          (putnam-2012-b5-quoted g1)
          (putnam-2012-b5-quoted g2))
    (putnam-2012-b5-quoted nil)
    (putnam-2012-b5-quoted t))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-bounds-exist-p (g1 g2)
  (not
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-bound-failure-function g1 g2)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(witness)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-power-output-function (power)
  (let ((output
         (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term power '(s x))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(s x)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 's)
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 'x)))
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p output)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-power-extensional-function (power)
  (let ((left-output
         (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term
          power '(s-left x-left)))
        (right-output
         (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term
          power '(s-right x-right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(s-left s-right x-left x-right)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-equal-p
              's-left 's-right)
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-equal-p
              'x-left 'x-right)))
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-equal-p
            left-output right-output)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-power-law-function (g1 power)
  (let* ((zero-name
          (putnam-2012-b5-rational-name 0))
         (one-name
          (putnam-2012-b5-rational-name 1))
         (at-x
          (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term power '(s x)))
         (at-y
          (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term power '(s y)))
         (at-zero
          (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term
           power
           (list 's
                 (putnam-2012-b5-quoted zero-name))))
         (at-one
          (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term
           power
           (list 's
                 (putnam-2012-b5-quoted one-name))))
         (base
          (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term g1 '(s)))
         (sum-name
          (list 'putnam-2012-b5-add-name 'x 'y))
         (at-sum
          (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term
           power
           (list 's sum-name)))
         (product-name
          (list 'putnam-2012-b5-multiply-name
                at-x at-y)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(s x y)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 's)
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 'x)
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 'y)))
      (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2012-b5-quoted zero-name)
              at-x)
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-equal-p
              at-zero
              (putnam-2012-b5-quoted one-name))
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-equal-p
              at-one base)
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-equal-p
              at-sum product-name)
        (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
         (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-le-p 'x 'y)
         (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-le-p
               at-x at-y))))))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-power-oracle-p (g1 power)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp power)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-power-output-function power)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(s x)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-power-extensional-function power)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function
     '(s-left s-right x-left x-right)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-power-law-function g1 power)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(s x y)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-left-upper-bound-function
    (g2 power x bound)
  (let* ((power-value
          (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term
           power
           (list 's
                 (putnam-2012-b5-quoted x))))
         (g2-value
          (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term g2 '(s)))
         (family-value
          (list 'putnam-2012-b5-multiply-name
                power-value g2-value)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(s)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 's)
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-le-p
            family-value
            (putnam-2012-b5-quoted bound))))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-left-upper-bound-p
    (g2 power x bound)
  (and
   (putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p x)
   (putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p bound)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-left-upper-bound-function
     g2 power x bound)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(s)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-left-least-function
    (g2 power x supremum)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(bound)
   (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
    (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
     (list
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 'bound)
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-left-upper-bound-p
            (putnam-2012-b5-quoted g2)
            (putnam-2012-b5-quoted power)
            (putnam-2012-b5-quoted x)
            'bound)))
    (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-le-p
          (putnam-2012-b5-quoted supremum)
          'bound))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-left-supremum-p
    (g2 power x supremum)
  (and
   (putnam-2012-b5-left-upper-bound-p
    g2 power x supremum)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-left-least-function
     g2 power x supremum)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(bound)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-right-upper-bound-function
    (h1 h2 x bound)
  (let* ((h1-value
          (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term h1 '(t-index)))
         (h2-value
          (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term h2 '(t-index)))
         (product
          (list 'putnam-2012-b5-multiply-name
                (putnam-2012-b5-quoted x)
                h1-value))
         (family-value
          (list 'putnam-2012-b5-add-name
                product h2-value)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(t-index)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 't-index)
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-le-p
            family-value
            (putnam-2012-b5-quoted bound))))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-right-upper-bound-p
    (h1 h2 x bound)
  (and
   (putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p x)
   (putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p bound)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-right-upper-bound-function
     h1 h2 x bound)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(t-index)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-right-least-function
    (h1 h2 x supremum)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(bound)
   (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
    (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
     (list
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 'bound)
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-right-upper-bound-p
            (putnam-2012-b5-quoted h1)
            (putnam-2012-b5-quoted h2)
            (putnam-2012-b5-quoted x)
            'bound)))
    (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-le-p
          (putnam-2012-b5-quoted supremum)
          'bound))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-right-supremum-p
    (h1 h2 x supremum)
  (and
   (putnam-2012-b5-right-upper-bound-p
    h1 h2 x supremum)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-right-least-function
     h1 h2 x supremum)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(bound)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-common-supremum-function
    (g2 power h1 h2 supremum-function)
  (let ((supremum
         (putnam-2012-b5-apply-term
          supremum-function '(x))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-2012-b5-implies-term
      (list 'putnam-2012-b5-real-name-p 'x)
      (putnam-2012-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-left-supremum-p
              (putnam-2012-b5-quoted g2)
              (putnam-2012-b5-quoted power)
              'x
              supremum)
        (list 'putnam-2012-b5-right-supremum-p
              (putnam-2012-b5-quoted h1)
              (putnam-2012-b5-quoted h2)
              'x
              supremum)))))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-conclusion-witness-p
    (witness g1 g2)
  (and
   (true-listp witness)
   (equal (len witness) 4)
   (let ((power (nth 0 witness))
         (h1 (nth 1 witness))
         (h2 (nth 2 witness))
         (supremum-function (nth 3 witness)))
     (and
      (putnam-2012-b5-power-oracle-p g1 power)
      (putnam-2012-b5-real-function-p h1)
      (putnam-2012-b5-real-function-p h2)
      (putnam-2012-b5-real-function-p
       supremum-function)
      (fn-equal
       (putnam-2012-b5-common-supremum-function
        g2 power h1 h2 supremum-function)
       (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(x)))))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-conclusion-failure-function
    (g1 g2)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(witness)
   (list
    'if
    (list 'putnam-2012-b5-conclusion-witness-p
          'witness
          (putnam-2012-b5-quoted g1)
          (putnam-2012-b5-quoted g2))
    (putnam-2012-b5-quoted nil)
    (putnam-2012-b5-quoted t))))

(defun putnam-2012-b5-conclusion-exists-p (g1 g2)
  (not
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2012-b5-conclusion-failure-function
     g1 g2)
    (putnam-2012-b5-true-function '(witness)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2012-b5-statement (g1 g2)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2012-b5-real-function-p g1)
    (putnam-2012-b5-real-function-p g2)
    (putnam-2012-b5-lower-one-p g1)
    (putnam-2012-b5-lower-one-p g2)
    (putnam-2012-b5-bounds-exist-p g1 g2))
   (putnam-2012-b5-conclusion-exists-p g1 g2)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2012_b5): bounded real functions with values at
-- least one admit affine functions whose attained maximum equals the supremum
-- of the corresponding real-power products. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

exponentialTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

ExponentialValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
ExponentialValue reals x value =
  SeriesHasSum reals
    (exponentialTerm reals x)
    value

record StandardRealPowers
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    exponential logarithm : R -> R

    exponential-series :
      (x : R) ->
      ExponentialValue reals x (exponential x)

    exponential-positive :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals
        (zeroR reals)
        (exponential x)

    exponential-injective :
      (x y : R) ->
      exponential x == exponential y ->
      x == y

    exponential-logarithm :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      exponential (logarithm x) == x

open StandardRealPowers

realPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardRealPowers reals ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
realPower reals powers base exponent =
  exponential powers
    (multiply reals exponent (logarithm powers base))

IsSupremumOfRange :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IsSupremumOfRange {R} reals values supremum =
  ((index : R) ->
    lessOrEqual reals (values index) supremum)
  and
  ((upper : R) ->
    ((index : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (values index) upper) ->
    lessOrEqual reals supremum upper)

IsMaximumOfRange :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IsMaximumOfRange {R} reals values maximum =
  Exists R (\ index -> values index == maximum)
  and
  ((index : R) ->
    lessOrEqual reals (values index) maximum)

module Putnam2012B5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (powers : StandardRealPowers reals) where

  PowerProduct :
    (R -> R) ->
    (R -> R) ->
    R ->
    R ->
    R
  PowerProduct g1 g2 exponent index =
    multiply reals
      (realPower reals powers (g1 index) exponent)
      (g2 index)

  AffineValue :
    (R -> R) ->
    (R -> R) ->
    R ->
    R ->
    R
  AffineValue h1 h2 x index =
    add reals
      (multiply reals x (h1 index))
      (h2 index)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (g1 g2 : R -> R) ->
    ((x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (oneR reals) (g1 x)
      and
      lessOrEqual reals (oneR reals) (g2 x)) ->
    Exists R
      (\ bound1 ->
        Exists R
          (\ bound2 ->
            (x : R) ->
            lessOrEqual reals (g1 x) bound1
            and
            lessOrEqual reals (g2 x) bound2)) ->
    Exists (R -> R)
      (\ h1 ->
        Exists (R -> R)
          (\ h2 ->
            (x : R) ->
            Exists R
              (\ commonValue ->
                IsSupremumOfRange reals
                  (PowerProduct g1 g2 x)
                  commonValue
                and
                IsMaximumOfRange reals
                  (AffineValue h1 h2 x)
                  commonValue)))

putnam-2012-b5 : Set1
putnam-2012-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (powers : StandardRealPowers reals) ->
  Putnam2012B5Statement.proposition reals powers

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b5:
  bounded real functions with values at least one admit a representation of
  their real-power supremum by an attained affine maximum. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory realTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2012_b5 =
  ``!(g1 g2 : real -> real).
      (!x : real. 1 <= g1 x /\ 1 <= g2 x) /\
      (?B1 B2 : real.
         !x : real. g1 x <= B1 /\ g2 x <= B2)
      ==>
      ?h1 h2 : real -> real.
        !x : real.
          ?t0 : real.
            sup (IMAGE (\s : real. g1 s powr x * g2 s) UNIV) =
              x * h1 t0 + h2 t0 /\
            !t : real.
              x * h1 t + h2 t <= x * h1 t0 + h2 t0``;

title: putnam_2012_b5
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2012_b5: bounded real functions with values at least one admit a
  representation equating the suprema of an exponential family and an
  affine family at every real parameter. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  G and H range over arbitrary real-valued functions on RR. Their common
  antecedent preserves the pointwise lower bounds and the internally
  existential joint upper bounds from the sources.

  For bases at least one, set.mm's complex-power operation ^c is real-valued
  and agrees with the source real power exp(x log(G(s))). Each set in a sup
  expression is the unrestricted real image of the corresponding family.
  Set.mm's sup(A, RR, <) is the real-order supremum, matching sSup/Sup in the
  Lean and Isabelle ground truth.

  U and V remain internally existential arbitrary functions RR -> RR. The
  final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d B C G H U V s t x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-2012-b5 $a |-
    A. G e. ( RR ^m RR )
      A. H e. ( RR ^m RR )
        (
          (
            A. x e. RR
              (
                1 <_ ( G ` x )
                /\
                1 <_ ( H ` x )
              )
            /\
            E. B e. RR
              E. C e. RR
                A. x e. RR
                  (
                    ( G ` x ) <_ B
                    /\
                    ( H ` x ) <_ C
                  )
          )
          ->
          E. U e. ( RR ^m RR )
            E. V e. ( RR ^m RR )
              A. x e. RR
                sup
                  (
                    {
                      y e. RR |
                        E. s e. RR
                          y =
                          (
                            ( ( G ` s ) ^c x )
                            x.
                            ( H ` s )
                          )
                    } ,
                    RR ,
                    <
                  )
                =
                sup
                  (
                    {
                      y e. RR |
                        E. t e. RR
                          y =
                          (
                            ( x x. ( U ` t ) )
                            +
                            ( V ` t )
                          )
                    } ,
                    RR ,
                    <
                  )
        )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2012_b5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b5:
% bounded real functions with values at least one admit a representation of
% their real-power supremum by an attained affine maximum. This file contains
% no proof.

putnam_2012_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  natural_log(x: real): real =
    IF x > 0 THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (value: real):
          real_exponential(value) = x)
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  real_power(base, exponent: real): real =
    IF base > 0 THEN
      real_exponential(exponent * natural_log(base))
    ELSIF base = 0 AND exponent = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  is_supremum_of_range(
      values: real_function,
      supremum_value: real): bool =
    (FORALL (index: real):
      values(index) <= supremum_value)
      AND (FORALL (bound: real):
        (FORALL (index: real):
          values(index) <= bound)
        IMPLIES supremum_value <= bound)

  is_maximum_of_range(
      values: real_function,
      maximum_value: real): bool =
    (EXISTS (index: real):
      values(index) = maximum_value)
      AND (FORALL (index: real):
        values(index) <= maximum_value)

  power_product(
      g1, g2: real_function,
      exponent: real): real_function =
    LAMBDA (index: real):
      real_power(g1(index), exponent) * g2(index)

  affine_values(
      h1, h2: real_function,
      x: real): real_function =
    LAMBDA (index: real):
      x * h1(index) + h2(index)

  putnam_2012_b5: bool =
    FORALL (g1, g2: real_function):
      ((FORALL (x: real):
        g1(x) >= 1 AND g2(x) >= 1)
        AND (EXISTS (bound1, bound2: real):
          FORALL (x: real):
            g1(x) <= bound1 AND g2(x) <= bound2))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (h1, h2: real_function):
          FORALL (x: real):
            EXISTS (common_value: real):
              is_supremum_of_range(
                power_product(g1, g2, x),
                common_value)
                AND is_maximum_of_range(
                  affine_values(h1, h2, x),
                  common_value)
END putnam_2012_b5

import Mathlib

open Matrix Function Real Topology Filter

/--
Let $p$ be an odd prime number such that $p \equiv 2 \pmod{3}$. Define a permutation $\pi$ of the residue classes modulo $p$ by $\pi(x) \equiv x^3 \pmod{p}$. Show that $\pi$ is an even permutation if and only if $p \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$.
-/
theorem putnam_2012_b6
(p : ℕ)
(hpodd : Odd p)
(hpprime : Nat.Prime p)
(hpmod3 : p ≡ 2 [MOD 3])
(P : Equiv.Perm (Fin p))
(hP : ∀ i : Fin p, P i = (i * i * i))
: Equiv.Perm.signAux P = 1 ↔ (p ≡ 3 [MOD 4]) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2012_b6
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b6:
   the parity of the cubing permutation on residue classes modulo an odd prime
   p congruent to 2 modulo 3. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List Vectors.Fin.

Import ListNotations.

Definition putnam_2012_b6_prime (p : nat) : Prop :=
  2 <= p /\
  forall d : nat, Nat.divide d p -> d = 1 \/ d = p.

Record putnam_2012_b6_permutation (p : nat) : Type := {
  putnam_2012_b6_perm_fun : Fin.t p -> Fin.t p;
  putnam_2012_b6_perm_inv : Fin.t p -> Fin.t p;
  putnam_2012_b6_perm_inv_l :
    forall x : Fin.t p,
      putnam_2012_b6_perm_inv (putnam_2012_b6_perm_fun x) = x;
  putnam_2012_b6_perm_inv_r :
    forall x : Fin.t p,
      putnam_2012_b6_perm_fun (putnam_2012_b6_perm_inv x) = x
}.

Definition putnam_2012_b6_swap {p : nat}
    (a b x : Fin.t p) : Fin.t p :=
  if Fin.eq_dec x a then b
  else if Fin.eq_dec x b then a
  else x.

Fixpoint putnam_2012_b6_apply_transpositions {p : nat}
    (swaps : list (Fin.t p * Fin.t p)) (x : Fin.t p) : Fin.t p :=
  match swaps with
  | [] => x
  | (a, b) :: rest =>
      putnam_2012_b6_swap a b
        (putnam_2012_b6_apply_transpositions rest x)
  end.

Definition putnam_2012_b6_even {p : nat}
    (P : putnam_2012_b6_permutation p) : Prop :=
  exists (swaps : list (Fin.t p * Fin.t p)) (k : nat),
    Forall (fun swap => fst swap <> snd swap) swaps /\
    length swaps = 2 * k /\
    forall x : Fin.t p,
      putnam_2012_b6_apply_transpositions swaps x =
      putnam_2012_b6_perm_fun p P x.

Definition putnam_2012_b6_residue {p : nat} (x : Fin.t p) : nat :=
  proj1_sig (Fin.to_nat x).

Theorem putnam_2012_b6
    (p : nat)
    (hpodd : Nat.Odd p)
    (hpprime : putnam_2012_b6_prime p)
    (hpmod3 : Nat.modulo p 3 = 2)
    (P : putnam_2012_b6_permutation p)
    (hP : forall x : Fin.t p,
      putnam_2012_b6_residue (putnam_2012_b6_perm_fun p P x) =
      Nat.modulo
        (putnam_2012_b6_residue x *
         putnam_2012_b6_residue x *
         putnam_2012_b6_residue x) p) :
  putnam_2012_b6_even P <->
  Nat.modulo p 4 = 3.
Admitted.

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b6:
;; the cubic permutation of residue classes modulo an odd prime p congruent
;; to 2 modulo 3 is even exactly when p is 3 modulo 4. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-2012-b6-no-divisor-through-p (p candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (or (not (natp candidate))
          (<= candidate 1))
      t
    (and
     (not (equal (mod p candidate) 0))
     (putnam-2012-b6-no-divisor-through-p
      p (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-2012-b6-prime-p (p)
  (and
   (natp p)
   (< 1 p)
   (putnam-2012-b6-no-divisor-through-p
    p (- p 1))))

;; Fin p is represented by its canonical natural representatives
;; 0,...,p-1. Multiplication in Fin p is multiplication modulo p.
(defun putnam-2012-b6-cube-residue (x p)
  (if (and (natp x)
           (posp p))
      (mod (* x x x) p)
    0))

;; Count inversions formed by the entry at index I and all earlier indices.
(defun putnam-2012-b6-inversions-with-lower-indices
    (p i count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (and (natp p)
           (natp i)
           (natp count))
      (if (zp count)
          0
        (let ((j (- count 1)))
          (+
           (if
            (>
             (putnam-2012-b6-cube-residue j p)
             (putnam-2012-b6-cube-residue i p))
            1
            0)
           (putnam-2012-b6-inversions-with-lower-indices
            p i j))))
    0))

;; This is the full inversion count of the list
;; [0^3 mod p, 1^3 mod p, ..., (p-1)^3 mod p]. Under the hypotheses below
;; that list is exactly the source cube permutation, and even inversion
;; parity is equivalent to permutation sign +1.
(defun putnam-2012-b6-cube-inversion-count-through
    (p count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (and (natp p)
           (natp count))
      (if (zp count)
          0
        (let ((i (- count 1)))
          (+
           (putnam-2012-b6-inversions-with-lower-indices
            p i i)
           (putnam-2012-b6-cube-inversion-count-through
            p i))))
    0))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2012-b6-statement (p)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2012-b6-prime-p p)
    (equal (mod p 2) 1)
    (equal (mod p 3) 2))
   (iff
    (equal
     (mod
      (putnam-2012-b6-cube-inversion-count-through p p)
      2)
     0)
    (equal (mod p 4) 3))))

:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b6:
-- the cubic permutation of residue classes modulo an odd prime p congruent to
-- 2 modulo 3 is even exactly when p is congruent to 3 modulo 4. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2012B6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_; mod-helper)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _divides_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_
infix 1 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record Pair (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    first-coordinate  : A
    second-coordinate : B

open Pair

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record _divides_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    division-equation : dividend == divisor * quotient

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

toNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
toNat fzero =
  zero
toNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (toNat i)

finEqual : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin n -> Bool
finEqual fzero fzero =
  true
finEqual fzero (fsuc j) =
  false
finEqual (fsuc i) fzero =
  false
finEqual (fsuc i) (fsuc j) =
  finEqual i j

swap :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n
swap left-index right-index index with finEqual index left-index
... | true =
  right-index
... | false with finEqual index right-index
...   | true =
  left-index
...   | false =
  index

applyTranspositions :
  {n count : Nat} ->
  (Fin count -> Pair (Fin n) (Fin n)) ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n
applyTranspositions {count = zero} transpositions index =
  index
applyTranspositions {count = suc count} transpositions index =
  applyTranspositions
    (\ i -> transpositions (fsuc i))
    (swap
      (first-coordinate (transpositions fzero))
      (second-coordinate (transpositions fzero))
      index)

PointwiseEqual :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Fin n) ->
  (Fin n -> Fin n) ->
  Set
PointwiseEqual left-function right-function =
  (index : _) ->
  left-function index == right-function index

Injective :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set
Injective function =
  (x y : _) ->
  function x == function y ->
  x == y

Surjective :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set
Surjective {A} {B} function =
  (y : B) ->
  Exists A
    (\ x -> function x == y)

IsPermutation :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Fin n) ->
  Set
IsPermutation permutation =
  Injective permutation
  and
  Surjective permutation

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

three : Nat
three =
  suc two

four : Nat
four =
  suc three

record Odd (n : Nat) : Set where
  field
    half : Nat
    odd-equation : n == two * half + one

record Prime (p : Nat) : Set where
  field
    at-least-two : two <=N p
    only-trivial-divisors :
      (d : Nat) ->
      d divides p ->
      (d == one) or (d == p)

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero =
  numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

ModEq : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Set
ModEq modulus left-value right-value =
  naturalMod left-value modulus == naturalMod right-value modulus

CubicPermutation :
  {p : Nat} ->
  (Fin p -> Fin p) ->
  Set
CubicPermutation {p} permutation =
  IsPermutation permutation
  and
  ((index : Fin p) ->
    toNat (permutation index)
    ==
    naturalMod
      (toNat index * toNat index * toNat index)
      p)

EvenPermutation :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Fin n) ->
  Set
EvenPermutation {n} permutation =
  Exists Nat
    (\ half-length ->
      Exists (Fin (two * half-length) -> Pair (Fin n) (Fin n))
        (\ transpositions ->
          ((index : Fin (two * half-length)) ->
            first-coordinate (transpositions index)
            !=
            second-coordinate (transpositions index))
          and
          PointwiseEqual
            permutation
            (applyTranspositions transpositions)))

putnam-2012-b6 : Set
putnam-2012-b6 =
  (p : Nat) ->
  Odd p ->
  Prime p ->
  ModEq three p two ->
  (permutation : Fin p -> Fin p) ->
  CubicPermutation permutation ->
  EvenPermutation permutation
  iff
  ModEq four p three

(*

  the cubing permutation of residue classes modulo an odd prime congruent to
  two modulo three is even exactly when the prime is three modulo four. This
  file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory permutesTheory;

val putnam_2012_b6 =
  ``!p : num. !P : num -> num.
      ODD p /\
      prime p /\
      p MOD 3 = 2 /\
      P permutes count p /\
      (!i : num. i < p ==> P i = (i EXP 3) MOD p)
      ==>
      (evenperm P <=> p MOD 4 = 3)``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2012_b6: parity of the cube permutation on residue classes modulo
  an odd prime congruent to two modulo three. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For p in NN, 0 ..^ p is the full set of residue representatives modulo p.
  Base ` ( SymGrp ` ( 0 ..^ p ) ) is exactly the set of permutations of that
  carrier. The pointwise hypothesis identifies P with the source permutation
  x |-> x^3 modulo p, preserving the Fin p multiplication used by the Lean
  statement.

  Prime and Odd are SetMM's classes of natural primes and odd integers.
  Equality of remainders expresses the two source congruences. SetMM's pmSgn
  is 1 exactly on even permutations, so the final biconditional is the source
  parity characterization. The final declaration is the single unproved $a
  corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d P i p $.

  putnambench-putnam-2012-b6 $a |- A. p e. NN
    A. P e. ( Base ` ( SymGrp ` ( 0 ..^ p ) ) )
      (
        (
          (
            (
              p e. Prime
              /\
              p e. Odd
            )
            /\
            ( p mod 3 ) = 2
          )
          /\
          A. i e. ( 0 ..^ p )
            ( P ` i ) = ( ( i ^ 3 ) mod p )
        )
        ->
        (
          (
            ( pmSgn ` ( 0 ..^ p ) )
            `
            P
          )
          =
          1
          <->
          ( p mod 4 ) = 3
        )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2012_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2012_b6:
% the cubic permutation of residue classes modulo an odd prime p congruent to
% 2 modulo 3 is even exactly when p is congruent to 3 modulo 4. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_2012_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  residue_function: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  nat_divides(divisor: posnat, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value

  residue_permutation(
      p: nat,
      P: residue_function): bool =
    (FORALL (i: nat):
      i < p IMPLIES P(i) < p)
      AND
        (FORALL (i, j: nat):
          (i < p AND j < p AND P(i) = P(j))
            IMPLIES i = j)
      AND
        (FORALL (j: nat):
          j < p IMPLIES
            EXISTS (i: nat):
              i < p AND P(i) = j)

  cubic_residue_permutation(
      p: nat,
      P: residue_function): bool =
    residue_permutation(p, P)
      AND
        (FORALL (i: nat):
          i < p IMPLIES
            P(i) = mod(i * i * i, p))

  inversions_before(
      P: residue_function,
      j, limit: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      inversions_before(P, j, limit - 1)
        + IF P(limit - 1) > P(j) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  inversion_count(
      P: residue_function,
      limit: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      inversion_count(P, limit - 1)
        + inversions_before(P, limit - 1, limit - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  even_residue_permutation(
      p: nat,
      P: residue_function): bool =
    mod(inversion_count(P, p), 2) = 0

  putnam_2012_b6: bool =
    FORALL (p: nat), (P: residue_function):
      (mod(p, 2) = 1
        AND prime_nat(p)
        AND mod(p, 3) = 2
        AND cubic_residue_permutation(p, P))
      IMPLIES
        (even_residue_permutation(p, P)
          IFF mod(p, 4) = 3)
END putnam_2012_b6

import Mathlib

open Function Set

/--
Let $S$ be the set of all positive integers that are \emph{not} perfect squares. For $n$ in $S$, consider choices of integers
$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_r$ such that $n < a_1<  a_2 < \cdots < a_r$
and $n \cdot a_1 \cdot a_2 \cdots a_r$ is a perfect square, and
let $f(n)$ be the minumum of $a_r$ over all such choices. For example,
$2 \cdot 3 \cdot 6$ is a perfect square, while $2 \cdot 3$, $2 \cdot 4$,
$2 \cdot 5$, $2 \cdot 3 \cdot 4$, $2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$, $2 \cdot 4 \cdot 5$, and $2 \cdot 3 \cdot 4 \cdot 5$ are not, and so $f(2) = 6$.
Show that the function $f$ from $S$ to the integers is one-to-one.
-/
theorem putnam_2013_a2
  (S : Set ℤ)
  (hS : S = {n : ℤ | n > 0 ∧ ¬∃ m : ℤ, m ^ 2 = n})
  (P : ℤ → List ℤ → Prop)
  (hP : ∀ n a, P n a ↔
    a.length > 0 ∧ n < a[0]! ∧
    (∃ m : ℤ, m ^ 2 = n * a.prod) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin (a.length - 1), a[i] < a[i+(1:ℕ)]))
  (T : ℤ → Set ℤ)
  (hT : T = fun n : ℤ => {m : ℤ | ∃ a : List ℤ, P n a ∧ a[a.length - 1]! = m})
  (f : ℤ → ℤ)
  (hf : ∀ n ∈ S, ((∃ r ∈ T n, f n = r) ∧ ∀ r ∈ T n, f n ≤ r)) :
  InjOn f S :=
sorry
