(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a2:
   injectivity of the least attainable final term in an increasing integer
   sequence whose product with a positive nonsquare is a square. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import ZArith Lists.List.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_2013_a2_product (values : list Z) : Z :=
  match values with
  | nil => 1
  | value :: rest => value * putnam_2013_a2_product rest
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2013_a2_strictly_increasing
    (values : list Z) : Prop :=
  match values with
  | nil => True
  | value :: rest =>
      match rest with
      | nil => True
      | next :: _ =>
          value < next /\
          putnam_2013_a2_strictly_increasing rest
      end
  end.

Definition putnam_2013_a2_nonsquare (n : Z) : Prop :=
  0 < n /\ ~ exists root : Z, root ^ 2 = n.

Definition putnam_2013_a2_qualifying_sequence
    (n : Z) (values : list Z) : Prop :=
  match values with
  | nil => False
  | first :: _ =>
      n < first /\
      (exists root : Z,
        root ^ 2 = n * putnam_2013_a2_product values) /\
      putnam_2013_a2_strictly_increasing values
  end.

Definition putnam_2013_a2_attainable_last
    (n last_value : Z) : Prop :=
  exists values : list Z,
    putnam_2013_a2_qualifying_sequence n values /\
    List.last values 0 = last_value.

Theorem putnam_2013_a2 :
  forall f : Z -> Z,
    (forall n : Z,
      putnam_2013_a2_nonsquare n ->
      putnam_2013_a2_attainable_last n (f n) /\
      forall last_value : Z,
        putnam_2013_a2_attainable_last n last_value ->
        f n <= last_value) ->
    forall x y : Z,
      putnam_2013_a2_nonsquare x ->
      putnam_2013_a2_nonsquare y ->
      f x = f y ->
      x = y.
Admitted.

  injectivity on the positive nonsquare integers of the minimum possible last
  entry in a strictly increasing integer list whose product with the initial
  integer is a perfect square. This file contains no proof.

let statement =
  `let S =
     {n:int | (&0:int) < n /\ ~(?m:int. m pow 2 = n)} in
   let P =
     \(n:int) (a:int list).
       0 < LENGTH a /\
       n < EL 0 a /\
       (?m:int.
          m pow 2 =
          n * ITLIST (\x acc. x * acc) a (&1:int)) /\
       (!i:num.
          i + 1 < LENGTH a
          ==> EL i a < EL (i + 1) a) in
   let T =
     \(n:int).
       {r:int |
          ?a:int list.
            P n a /\ LAST a = r} in
   !f:int->int.
     (!n:int.
        n IN S
        ==>
        f n IN T n /\
        (!r:int. r IN T n ==> f n <= r))

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a2:
;; the least possible final terms of increasing integer lists that make
;; n times the list product a square distinguish positive nonsquare integers.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; S, P, T, and f are eliminated using their source definitions. For fixed
;; positive N and endpoint R, every admissible increasing list ending in R is
;; uniquely R preceded by a subset of the finite interval N+1,...,R-1.
;; PUTNAM-2013-A2-ENDPOINT-P exhausts exactly those subsets; R itself remains
;; unbounded. The final predicate is therefore the relational form of
;; injectivity of the unique least endpoint.

(defun putnam-2013-a2-floor-sqrt-down (x candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (zp candidate)
      0
    (if (<= (* candidate candidate) x)
        candidate
      (putnam-2013-a2-floor-sqrt-down
       x (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a2-perfect-square-p (x)
  (if (and (integerp x)
           (<= 0 x))
      (let ((root
             (putnam-2013-a2-floor-sqrt-down x x)))
        (equal (* root root) x))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2013-a2-positive-nonsquare-p (n)
  (and (integerp n)
       (< 0 n)
       (not (putnam-2013-a2-perfect-square-p n))))

(defun putnam-2013-a2-subset-square-exists-p
    (n current endpoint partial-product steps)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix steps)))
  (if (zp steps)
      (putnam-2013-a2-perfect-square-p
       (* n endpoint partial-product))
    (or
     (putnam-2013-a2-subset-square-exists-p
      n
      (+ current 1)
      endpoint
      (* partial-product current)
      (- steps 1))
     (putnam-2013-a2-subset-square-exists-p
      n
      (+ current 1)
      endpoint
      partial-product
      (- steps 1)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a2-endpoint-p (n endpoint)
  (and
   (integerp n)
   (integerp endpoint)
   (< n endpoint)
   (putnam-2013-a2-subset-square-exists-p
    n
    (+ n 1)
    endpoint
    1
    (- (- endpoint n) 1))))

(defun putnam-2013-a2-no-smaller-endpoint-p
    (n candidate steps)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix steps)))
  (if (zp steps)
      t
    (and
     (not (putnam-2013-a2-endpoint-p n candidate))
     (putnam-2013-a2-no-smaller-endpoint-p
      n
      (+ candidate 1)
      (- steps 1)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a2-minimum-endpoint-p (n endpoint)
  (and
   (putnam-2013-a2-endpoint-p n endpoint)
   (putnam-2013-a2-no-smaller-endpoint-p
    n
    (+ n 1)
    (- (- endpoint n) 1))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2013-a2-statement
    (left right common-endpoint)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2013-a2-positive-nonsquare-p left)
    (putnam-2013-a2-positive-nonsquare-p right)
    (putnam-2013-a2-minimum-endpoint-p
     left common-endpoint)
    (putnam-2013-a2-minimum-endpoint-p

    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data _<=Z_ : Int -> Int -> Set where
  negative<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    negsuc m <=Z pos n
  positive<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    m <=N n ->
    pos m <=Z pos n
  negative<=negative :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    n <=N m ->
    negsuc m <=Z negsuc n

_<Z_ : Int -> Int -> Set
x <Z y =
  (x <=Z y) and (x != y)

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos (suc zero)

product : List Int -> Int
product [] =
  oneZ
product (x ∷ xs) =
  multiplyInt x (product xs)

StrictlyIncreasing : List Int -> Set
StrictlyIncreasing [] =
  Top
StrictlyIncreasing (_ ∷ []) =
  Top
StrictlyIncreasing (x ∷ y ∷ xs) =
  (x <Z y) and StrictlyIncreasing (y ∷ xs)

LastIs : List Int -> Int -> Set
LastIs [] last =
  Bottom
LastIs (x ∷ []) last =
  x == last
LastIs (_ ∷ y ∷ xs) last =
  LastIs (y ∷ xs) last

PositiveNonSquare : Int -> Set
PositiveNonSquare n =
  ((pos zero) <Z n)
  and
  Not
    (Exists Int
      (\ m ->
        multiplyInt m m == n))

Admissible : Int -> List Int -> Set
Admissible n [] =
  Bottom
Admissible n (a ∷ as) =
  (n <Z a)
  and
  (Exists Int
    (\ m ->
      multiplyInt m m ==
        multiplyInt n (product (a ∷ as))))
  and
  StrictlyIncreasing (a ∷ as)

TerminalValue : Int -> Int -> Set
TerminalValue n last =
  Exists (List Int)
    (\ choices ->
      Admissible n choices
      and
      LastIs choices last)

IsMinimumTerminal : (Int -> Int) -> Int -> Set
IsMinimumTerminal f n =
  TerminalValue n (f n)
  and
  ((last : Int) ->
    TerminalValue n last ->
    f n <=Z last)

InjectiveOnPositiveNonSquares : (Int -> Int) -> Set
InjectiveOnPositiveNonSquares f =
  (x y : Int) ->
  PositiveNonSquare x ->
  PositiveNonSquare y ->
  f x == f y ->
  x == y

putnam-2013-a2 : Set
putnam-2013-a2 =
  (f : Int -> Int) ->
  ((n : Int) ->
    PositiveNonSquare n ->
    IsMinimumTerminal f n) ->
  InjectiveOnPositiveNonSquares f

title: putnam_2013_a2
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a2:
  the minimum final term in an increasing integer list that makes a positive
  nonsquare integer times the list product a square defines an injective
  function. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2013_a2 =
  ``let S =
      {n : int | 0 < n /\ ~(?m : int. m ** 2 = n)}
    in
    let admissible =
      \n : int. \a : int list.
        a <> [] /\
        n < HD a /\
        (?m : int.
           m ** 2 =
             n * FOLDR (\x acc : int. x * acc) 1 a) /\
        (!i : num.
           SUC i < LENGTH a
           ==>
           EL i a < EL (SUC i) a)
    in
    let T =
      \n : int.
        {r : int |
           ?a : int list.
             admissible n a /\ LAST a = r}
    in
      !f : int -> int.
        (!n : int.
           n IN S
           ==>
           f n IN T n /\
           !r : int. r IN T n ==> f n <= r)
        ==>
        !x y : int.
          x IN S /\ y IN S /\ f x = f y
          ==>
          x = y``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2013_a2: injectivity of the least possible final entry of a strictly
  increasing integer sequence whose product with a positive nonsquare integer
  is a perfect square. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The variables n, x, and y range over all integers. The repeated conditions
  0 < n and nonexistence of an integer square root define exactly the source
  set S of positive nonsquares.

  For r in NN, a in ( ZZ ^m ( 1 ... r ) ) is a nonempty finite integer
  sequence. The first-entry bound, strict inequalities on 1 ..^ r, and the
  internally existential square witness are exactly the source predicate P.
  The first minimum clause says that f(n) is attained as a(r); the second says
  it is no larger than the final entry of every admissible sequence. Together
  they expand membership in T(n) and the source least-element condition
  without externalizing a sequence or square witness.

  The conclusion is the pointwise expansion of injectivity of f on S. The
  final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d a f i m n r x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-2013-a2 $a |-
    A. f e. ( ZZ ^m ZZ )
      (
        A. n e. ZZ
          (
            (
              0 < n
              /\
              -. E. m e. ZZ ( m ^ 2 ) = n
            )
            ->
            (
              E. r e. NN
                E. a e. ( ZZ ^m ( 1 ... r ) )
                  (
                    (
                      (
                        n < ( a ` 1 )
                        /\
                        A. i e. ( 1 ..^ r )
                          ( a ` i ) < ( a ` ( i + 1 ) )
                      )
                      /\
                      E. m e. ZZ
                        ( m ^ 2 )
                        =
                        (
                          n
                          x.
                          prod_ i e. ( 1 ... r ) ( a ` i )
                        )
                    )
                    /\
                    ( f ` n ) = ( a ` r )
                  )
              /\
              A. r e. NN
                A. a e. ( ZZ ^m ( 1 ... r ) )
                  (
                    (
                      (
                        n < ( a ` 1 )
                        /\
                        A. i e. ( 1 ..^ r )
                          ( a ` i ) < ( a ` ( i + 1 ) )
                      )
                      /\
                      E. m e. ZZ
                        ( m ^ 2 )
                        =
                        (
                          n
                          x.
                          prod_ i e. ( 1 ... r ) ( a ` i )
                        )
                    )
                    ->
                    ( f ` n ) <_ ( a ` r )
                  )
            )
          )
        ->
        A. x e. ZZ
          A. y e. ZZ
            (
              (
                (
                  (
                    0 < x
                    /\
                    -. E. m e. ZZ ( m ^ 2 ) = x
                  )
                  /\
                  (
                    0 < y
                    /\
                    -. E. m e. ZZ ( m ^ 2 ) = y
                  )
                )
                /\
                ( f ` x ) = ( f ` y )
              )
              ->
              x = y
            )
      )
  $.
$}

  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,
    FUNCT_2, PARTFUN1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,

    VALUED_1, RVSUM_1, MEMBERED;
  requirements BOOLE, SUBSET, NUMERALS, ARITHM, REAL;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for f being Function of INT,INT st
    (for n being Integer st
      0 < n & not ex s being Integer st s*s = n
    holds
      (ex a being FinSequence of INT st
        0 < len a &
        n < a.1 &
        (for i being Nat st i in Seg (len a -' 1) holds
          a.i < a.(i+1)) &
        (ex s being Integer st s*s = n * Product a) &
        f.n = a.(len a)) &

        0 < len a &
        n < a.1 &
        (for i being Nat st i in Seg (len a -' 1) holds
          a.i < a.(i+1)) &
        (ex s being Integer st s*s = n * Product a)

  holds

      0 < n2 & not ex s2 being Integer st s2*s2 = n2 &

title: putnam_2013_a2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a2:
% the least terminal elements of increasing integer sequences whose products
% with positive nonsquares are squares define an injective function. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2013_a2: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> int]

  positive_nonsquare(n: int): bool =
    n > 0
      AND NOT EXISTS (m: int): m * m = n

  prefix_product(
      values: integer_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      prefix_product(values, count - 1) * values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  strictly_increasing_prefix(
      values: integer_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i: nat):
      i + 1 < count IMPLIES values(i) < values(i + 1)

  terminal_candidate(n, terminal: int): bool =
    EXISTS (count: nat), (values: integer_sequence):
      count > 0
        AND n < values(0)
        AND (EXISTS (square_root: int):
          square_root * square_root
            = n * prefix_product(values, count))
        AND strictly_increasing_prefix(values, count)
        AND terminal = values(count - 1)

  is_minimum_terminal(
      n, terminal: int): bool =
    terminal_candidate(n, terminal)
      AND (FORALL (other: int):
        terminal_candidate(n, other) IMPLIES terminal <= other)

  injective_on_positive_nonsquares(f: [int -> int]): bool =
    FORALL (left, right: int):
      (positive_nonsquare(left)
        AND positive_nonsquare(right)
        AND f(left) = f(right))
      IMPLIES left = right

  putnam_2013_a2: bool =
    FORALL (f: [int -> int]):
      (FORALL (n: int):
        positive_nonsquare(n) IMPLIES is_minimum_terminal(n, f(n)))
      IMPLIES injective_on_positive_nonsquares(f)
END putnam_2013_a2

title: putnam_2013_a3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a3:
;; a vanishing weighted sum of real coefficients at a point in the open unit
;; interval guarantees a root there for the corresponding polynomial. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The parameters below present an arbitrary real closed ordered field rather
;; than replacing the source real numbers by ACL2 rationals. Completeness of
;; real closed fields transfers this first-order assertion bidirectionally
;; between that presentation and the real numbers. FN-EQUAL supplies the
;; unbounded universal quantification used by the field laws.
;;
;; The coefficient list is exactly the restriction of the source family to
;; indices 0 through n; restriction and arbitrary extension outside this
;; range give the two directions of equivalence. Negated FN-EQUAL keeps the
;; required root y existentially quantified inside the statement predicate.

(defun putnam-2013-a3-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2013-a3-quoted function)
   (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2013-a3-quoted function)
   (list 'cons left (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-and-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2013-a3-quoted t)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2013-a3-and-term (cdr terms))
     (putnam-2013-a3-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-or-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2013-a3-quoted nil)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2013-a3-quoted t)
     (putnam-2013-a3-or-term (cdr terms)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-not-term (term)
  (list
   'if
   term
   (putnam-2013-a3-quoted nil)
   (putnam-2013-a3-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-implies-term (antecedent consequent)
  (list
   'if
   antecedent
   consequent
   (putnam-2013-a3-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-true-function (formals)
  (list
   'lambda
   formals
   (putnam-2013-a3-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-2013-a3-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-operation-term (operation left right)
  (putnam-2013-a3-apply2-term operation left right))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-all-coefficients-function (carrier)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)
   (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term
    carrier 'loop$-ivars)))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-all-coefficients-term
    (carrier coefficients)
  (list
   'always$+
   (putnam-2013-a3-quoted
    (putnam-2013-a3-all-coefficients-function
     carrier))
   (putnam-2013-a3-quoted nil)
   coefficients))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-polynomial-term
    (carrier zero coefficients)
  (putnam-2013-a3-and-term
   (list
    (list 'true-listp coefficients)
    (list 'consp coefficients)
    (putnam-2013-a3-all-coefficients-term
     carrier coefficients)
    (putnam-2013-a3-or-term
     (list
      (list 'equal
            (list 'len coefficients)
            (putnam-2013-a3-quoted 1))
      (putnam-2013-a3-not-term
       (list 'equal
             (list 'car (list 'last coefficients))
             (putnam-2013-a3-quoted zero))))))))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-field-laws-function
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (y 'y)
         (z 'z)
         (qzero (putnam-2013-a3-quoted zero))
         (qone (putnam-2013-a3-quoted one))
         (add-xy
          (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term add x y))
         (add-yz
          (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term add y z))
         (mul-xy
          (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul x y))
         (mul-yz
          (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul y z))
         (neg-x
          (putnam-2013-a3-apply1-term neg x))
         (inv-x
          (putnam-2013-a3-apply1-term inv x))
         (domain
          (putnam-2013-a3-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier y)
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier z))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2013-a3-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier add-xy)
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier mul-xy)
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier neg-x)
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier inv-x)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term add add-xy z)
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term add x add-yz))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul mul-xy z)
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul x mul-yz))
            (list
             'equal
             add-xy
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term add y x))
            (list
             'equal
             mul-xy
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul y x))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term add x qzero)
             x)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term add x neg-x)
             qzero)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul x qone)
             x)
            (putnam-2013-a3-implies-term
             (list 'equal x qzero)
             (list 'equal inv-x qzero))
            (putnam-2013-a3-implies-term
             (putnam-2013-a3-not-term
              (list 'equal x qzero))
             (list
              'equal
              (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul x inv-x)
              qone))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul x add-yz)
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term
              add
              (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul x y)
              (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul x z)))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y z)
     (putnam-2013-a3-implies-term domain laws))))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-order-laws-function
    (carrier zero add mul lt)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (y 'y)
         (z 'z)
         (qzero (putnam-2013-a3-quoted zero))
         (lt-xy
          (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term lt x y))
         (lt-yx
          (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term lt y x))
         (lt-yz
          (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term lt y z))
         (lt-xz
          (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term lt x z))
         (domain
          (putnam-2013-a3-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier y)
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier z))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2013-a3-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2013-a3-not-term
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term lt x x))
            (putnam-2013-a3-or-term
             (list
              lt-xy
              (list 'equal x y)
              lt-yx))
            (putnam-2013-a3-implies-term
             (putnam-2013-a3-and-term
              (list lt-xy lt-yz))
             lt-xz)
            (putnam-2013-a3-implies-term
             lt-xy
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term
              lt
              (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term add x z)
              (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term add y z)))
            (putnam-2013-a3-implies-term
             (putnam-2013-a3-and-term
              (list
               (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term lt qzero x)
               (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term lt qzero y)))
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term
              lt
              qzero
              (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul x y)))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y z)
     (putnam-2013-a3-implies-term domain laws))))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-square-root-laws-function
    (carrier zero mul lt square-root)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (qzero (putnam-2013-a3-quoted zero))
         (root
          (putnam-2013-a3-apply1-term square-root x))
         (domain
          (putnam-2013-a3-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2013-a3-not-term
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term lt x qzero)))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2013-a3-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier root)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term mul root root)
             x)))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-2013-a3-implies-term domain laws))))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-evaluation-laws-function
    (carrier zero add mul evaluate)
  (let* ((coefficient 'coefficient)
         (rest 'rest)
         (x 'x)
         (qzero (putnam-2013-a3-quoted zero))
         (domain
          (putnam-2013-a3-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term
             carrier coefficient)
            (list 'true-listp rest)
            (putnam-2013-a3-all-coefficients-term
             carrier rest)
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier x))))
         (empty-law
          (putnam-2013-a3-implies-term

(defun putnam-2013-a3-odd-root-laws-function

(defun putnam-2013-a3-real-closed-field-p
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv lt square-root odd-root evaluate)
  (let* ((field-laws
          (putnam-2013-a3-field-laws-function
           carrier zero one add mul neg inv))
         (field-laws-true
          (putnam-2013-a3-true-function '(x y z)))
         (order-laws

     (tamep-functionp add)
     (tamep-functionp mul)
     (tamep-functionp neg)
     (tamep-functionp inv)
     (tamep-functionp lt)

     (tamep-functionp evaluate)

     (tamep-functionp field-laws-true)
     (tamep-functionp order-laws)
     (tamep-functionp order-laws-true)
     (tamep-functionp square-root-laws)
     (tamep-functionp square-root-laws-true)
     (tamep-functionp evaluation-laws)
     (tamep-functionp evaluation-laws-true)
     (tamep-functionp odd-root-laws)
     (tamep-functionp odd-root-laws-true)
     (apply$ carrier (list zero))
     (apply$ carrier (list one))
     (not (equal zero one))
     (fn-equal field-laws field-laws-true)
     (fn-equal order-laws order-laws-true)
     (fn-equal square-root-laws square-root-laws-true)
     (fn-equal evaluation-laws evaluation-laws-true)
     (fn-equal odd-root-laws odd-root-laws-true))))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-add (add left right)

(defun putnam-2013-a3-power (mul one value exponent)

    (putnam-2013-a3-mul
     mul

(defun putnam-2013-a3-less-p (lt left right)

(defun putnam-2013-a3-coefficient-list-p
    (coefficients carrier)

      (equal coefficients nil)
    (and
     (apply$ carrier (list (car coefficients)))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-weighted-sum
    (coefficients index zero one add mul neg inv x)

           (denominator

       add
       term
       (putnam-2013-a3-weighted-sum
        (cdr coefficients)
        (+ index 1)
        zero one add mul neg inv x)))))

;; Build a tame term for a_0 + y*(a_1 + y*(... + y*a_n)).
(defun putnam-2013-a3-polynomial-value-term
    (coefficients zero add mul y)
  (if (endp coefficients)
      (putnam-2013-a3-quoted zero)
    (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term
     add
     (putnam-2013-a3-quoted (car coefficients))
     (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term
      mul
      y
      (putnam-2013-a3-polynomial-value-term

(defun putnam-2013-a3-root-failure-function
    (carrier zero one add mul lt coefficients)
  (let* ((y 'y)
         (qzero (putnam-2013-a3-quoted zero))
         (qone (putnam-2013-a3-quoted one))
         (value
          (putnam-2013-a3-polynomial-value-term
           coefficients zero add mul y))
         (qualification
          (putnam-2013-a3-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2013-a3-carrier-term carrier y)
            (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term lt qzero y)
            (putnam-2013-a3-operation-term lt y qone)
            (list 'equal value qzero)))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(y)
     (list
      'if
      qualification
      (putnam-2013-a3-quoted nil)
      (putnam-2013-a3-quoted t)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a3-root-exists-p
    (carrier zero one add mul lt coefficients)
  (let ((failure
         (putnam-2013-a3-root-failure-function
          carrier zero one add mul lt coefficients))
        (always-true
         (putnam-2013-a3-true-function '(y))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp failure)
     (tamep-functionp always-true)
     (not (fn-equal failure always-true)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2013-a3-statement
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv lt square-root odd-root
             evaluate n coefficients x)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2013-a3-real-closed-field-p
     carrier zero one add mul neg inv lt square-root odd-root evaluate)
    (natp n)
    (true-listp coefficients)
    (equal (len coefficients) (+ n 1))
    (putnam-2013-a3-coefficient-list-p
     coefficients carrier)
    (apply$ carrier (list x))
    (putnam-2013-a3-less-p lt zero x)
    (putnam-2013-a3-less-p lt x one)
    (equal
     (putnam-2013-a3-weighted-sum
      coefficients 0 zero one add mul neg inv x)
     zero))
   (putnam-2013-a3-root-exists-p
    carrier zero one add mul lt coefficients)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2013_a3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2013_a3): a vanishing finite weighted sum with
-- denominators 1 - x^(i+1), for 0 < x < 1, forces the associated real
-- polynomial to have a root in (0,1). This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2013A3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

toNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
toNat fzero =
  zero
toNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (toNat i)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals numerator denominator =
  multiply reals numerator (inverse reals denominator)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc exponent) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x exponent)
    x

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} terms =
  add reals
    (terms fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> terms (fsuc i)))

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

weightedSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
weightedSum reals coefficients x =
  sumFin reals
    (\ i ->
      divide reals
        (coefficients i)
        (subtract reals
          (oneR reals)
          (naturalPower reals x (suc (toNat i)))))

polynomialValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
polynomialValue reals coefficients y =
  sumFin reals
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (coefficients i)
        (naturalPower reals y (toNat i)))

Putnam2013A3 :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Set
Putnam2013A3 {R} reals =
  (n : Nat) ->
  (coefficients : Fin (suc n) -> R) ->
  (x : R) ->
  (StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) x
    and
    StrictLess reals x (oneR reals)) ->
  weightedSum reals coefficients x == zeroR reals ->
  Exists R
    (\ y ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) y
      and
      (StrictLess reals y (oneR reals)
      and
      polynomialValue reals coefficients y == zeroR reals))

putnam-2013-a3 : Set1
putnam-2013-a3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2013A3 reals

title: putnam_2013_a3

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a3:
  a vanishing real sum weighted by reciprocals of 1 - x^(i+1) yields a root
  in the open unit interval of the corresponding finite polynomial. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;

val putnam_2013_a3 =
  ``!n : num. !a : num -> real. !x : real.
      0 < x /\ x < 1 /\
      SIGMA
        (\i : num. a i / (1 - x pow (i + 1)))
        (count (SUC n)) = 0
      ==>
      ?y : real.
        0 < y /\ y < 1 /\
        SIGMA
          (\i : num. a i * y pow i)
          (count (SUC n)) = 0``;

title: putnam_2013_a3
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2013_a3: a vanishing finite sum of real coefficients divided by
  one minus successive powers of a point in the open unit interval implies
  that the associated real polynomial has a root in that interval. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For n in NN0, the interval 0 ... n is exactly the source index set from
  zero through n, and RR ^m ( 0 ... n ) is the class of all real coefficient
  families on that finite carrier. Thus both finite sums use precisely the
  coefficients a_0 through a_n.

  The antecedent preserves 0 < x < 1 and the vanishing sum with denominator
  1 - x^(i+1). The witness y remains existentially quantified inside the
  conclusion, with 0 < y < 1 and the associated polynomial sum equal to zero.
  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d a i n x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-2013-a3 $a |-
    A. n e. NN0
      A. a e. ( RR ^m ( 0 ... n ) )
        A. x e. RR
          (
            (
              (
                0 < x
                /\
                x < 1
              )
              /\
              (
                sum_ i e. ( 0 ... n )
                  (
                    ( a ` i )
                    /
                    (
                      1
                      -
                      ( x ^ ( i + 1 ) )
                    )
                  )
              )
              =
              0
            )
            ->
            E. y e. RR
              (
                (
                  0 < y
                  /\
                  y < 1
                )
                /\
                (
                  sum_ i e. ( 0 ... n )
                    (
                      ( a ` i )
                      x.
                      ( y ^ i )
                    )
                )
                =
                0
              )
          )
  $.
$}

content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a3
:: (putnambench__mizar__putnam_2013_a3): a vanishing finite weighted
:: reciprocal sum yields a zero of the associated real polynomial in (0,1).

environ

    FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, XREAL_0, XCMPLX_0, COMPLEX1, CARD_1, XXREAL_0,

  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,

    PREPOWER;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat,
      a being FinSequence of REAL,
      x being Real st
    len a = n + 1 &
    0 < x & x < 1 &
    (ex weightedTerms being FinSequence of REAL st
      len weightedTerms = n + 1 &

      0 < y & y < 1 &

      (for k being Nat st k in Seg (n + 1) holds

      Sum polynomialTerms = 0
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2013_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a3:
% a vanishing finite sum of a_i / (1 - x^(i+1)) for 0 < x < 1 implies that
% the corresponding real polynomial has a root in (0, 1). This file contains no proof.

putnam_2013_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  reciprocal_sum(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      safe_div(coefficients(0), 1 - x)
    ELSE
      reciprocal_sum(coefficients, x, count - 1)
        + safe_div(coefficients(count), 1 - x ^ (count + 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  polynomial_sum(
      coefficients: real_sequence,
      y: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      coefficients(0)
    ELSE
      polynomial_sum(coefficients, y, count - 1)
        + coefficients(count) * y ^ count
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  putnam_2013_a3: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (a: real_sequence), (x: real):
      (0 < x AND x < 1 AND reciprocal_sum(a, x, n) = 0)
        IMPLIES
          EXISTS (y: real):
            0 < y AND y < 1 AND polynomial_sum(a, y, n) = 0
END putnam_2013_a3

title: putnam_2013_a4
content:
import Mathlib

open Function Set

/--
A finite collection of digits $0$ and $1$ is written around a circle. An \emph{arc} of length $L \geq 0$ consists of $L$ consecutive digits around the circle. For each arc $w$, let $Z(w)$ and $N(w)$ denote the number of $0$'s in $w$ and the number of $1$'s in $w$, respectively. Assume that $|Z(w)-Z(w')| \leq 1$ for any two arcs $w,w'$ of the same length. Suppose that some arcs $w_1,\dots,w_k$ have the property that $Z=\frac{1}{k}\sum_{j=1}^k Z(w_j)$ and $N=\frac{1}{k}\sum_{j=1}^k N(w_j)$ are both integers. Prove that there exists an arc $w$ with $Z(w)=Z$ and $N(w)=N$.
-/
theorem putnam_2013_a4
(n k : ℕ)
(circle : Fin n → Fin 2)
(Z N : Fin n × Fin (n + 1) → ℤ)
(ws : Fin k → Fin n × Fin (n + 1))
(Zsum Nsum : ℤ)
(npos : n ≥ 1) (kpos : k ≥ 1)
(hZ : ∀ w, Z w = ∑ l ∈ {x : Fin n | x.1 < w.2.1}, if (circle (w.1 + l) = 0) then 1 else 0)
(hN : ∀ w, N w = ∑ l ∈ {x : Fin n | x.1 < w.2.1}, if (circle (w.1 + l) = 1) then 1 else 0)
(Zle1 : ∀ w w', w.2 = w'.2 → |(Z w : ℤ) - Z w'| ≤ 1)

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a4:
   balanced zero counts on equal-length arcs of a finite binary circle force
   an arc realizing integral average zero and one counts. This file contains
   no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat ZArith.

Inductive putnam_2013_a4_digit : Type :=
  | putnam_2013_a4_zero
  | putnam_2013_a4_one.

Definition putnam_2013_a4_digit_eqb
    (a b : putnam_2013_a4_digit) : bool :=
  match a, b with
  | putnam_2013_a4_zero, putnam_2013_a4_zero => true
  | putnam_2013_a4_one, putnam_2013_a4_one => true
  | _, _ => false
  end.

Definition putnam_2013_a4_index (n : nat) : Type :=
  {i : nat | (i < n)%nat}.

Definition putnam_2013_a4_length (n : nat) : Type :=
  {l : nat | (l <= n)%nat}.

Definition putnam_2013_a4_arc (n : nat) : Type :=
  (putnam_2013_a4_index n * putnam_2013_a4_length n)%type.

Definition putnam_2013_a4_cyclic_index
    (n : nat)
    (npos : (0 < n)%nat)
    (start : putnam_2013_a4_index n)
    (offset : nat) : putnam_2013_a4_index n :=
  exist
    (fun i : nat => (i < n)%nat)
    ((proj1_sig start + offset) mod n)
    (Nat.mod_upper_bound
      (proj1_sig start + offset)
      n
      (proj2 (Nat.neq_0_lt_0 n) npos)).

Fixpoint putnam_2013_a4_count_digit
    (n : nat)
    (npos : (0 < n)%nat)
    (circle : putnam_2013_a4_index n -> putnam_2013_a4_digit)
    (start : putnam_2013_a4_index n)
    (target : putnam_2013_a4_digit)
    (length : nat) : Z :=
  match length with
  | O => 0%Z
  | S l =>
      (putnam_2013_a4_count_digit n npos circle start target l +
       if putnam_2013_a4_digit_eqb
            (circle (putnam_2013_a4_cyclic_index n npos start l))
            target
       then 1
       else 0)%Z
  end.

Definition putnam_2013_a4_zero_count
    (n : nat)
    (npos : (0 < n)%nat)
    (circle : putnam_2013_a4_index n -> putnam_2013_a4_digit)
    (w : putnam_2013_a4_arc n) : Z :=
  putnam_2013_a4_count_digit
    n npos circle (fst w) putnam_2013_a4_zero (proj1_sig (snd w)).

Definition putnam_2013_a4_one_count
    (n : nat)
    (npos : (0 < n)%nat)
    (circle : putnam_2013_a4_index n -> putnam_2013_a4_digit)
    (w : putnam_2013_a4_arc n) : Z :=
  putnam_2013_a4_count_digit
    n npos circle (fst w) putnam_2013_a4_one (proj1_sig (snd w)).

Fixpoint putnam_2013_a4_fin_sum
    (n : nat) : (putnam_2013_a4_index n -> Z) -> Z :=
  match n as m return (putnam_2013_a4_index m -> Z) -> Z with
  | O => fun _ => 0%Z
  | S m =>
      fun f =>
        (f (exist
              (fun i : nat => (i < S m)%nat)
              O
              (Nat.lt_0_succ m)) +
         putnam_2013_a4_fin_sum m
           (fun i =>
              f (exist
                   (fun j : nat => (j < S m)%nat)
                   (S (proj1_sig i))
                   (proj1
                     (Nat.succ_lt_mono (proj1_sig i) m)
                     (proj2_sig i)))))%Z
  end.

Theorem putnam_2013_a4
    (n k : nat)
    (circle : putnam_2013_a4_index n -> putnam_2013_a4_digit)
    (ws : putnam_2013_a4_index k -> putnam_2013_a4_arc n)
    (Zsum Nsum : Z)
    (npos : (0 < n)%nat)
    (kpos : (0 < k)%nat)
    (Zle1 :
      forall w w' : putnam_2013_a4_arc n,
        proj1_sig (snd w) = proj1_sig (snd w') ->
        (Z.abs
          (putnam_2013_a4_zero_count n npos circle w -
           putnam_2013_a4_zero_count n npos circle w') <= 1)%Z)
    (hZsum :
      (Z.of_nat k * Zsum =
       putnam_2013_a4_fin_sum k
         (fun j => putnam_2013_a4_zero_count n npos circle (ws j)))%Z)
    (hNsum :
      (Z.of_nat k * Nsum =
       putnam_2013_a4_fin_sum k
         (fun j => putnam_2013_a4_one_count n npos circle (ws j)))%Z) :
  exists w : putnam_2013_a4_arc n,
    putnam_2013_a4_zero_count n npos circle w = Zsum /\
    putnam_2013_a4_one_count n npos circle w = Nsum.
Admitted.

theory putnam_2013_a4 imports Complex_Main

begin

theorem putnam_2013_a4:
  fixes n k :: "nat"
    and Zsum Nsum :: "real"
    and circle :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
    and Z N :: "(nat \<times> nat) \<Rightarrow> nat"
    and ws :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<times> nat)"
  defines "Zsum \<equiv> (1 / real_of_nat k) * (\<Sum>j\<in>{0..<k}. Z (ws j))"
    and "Nsum \<equiv> (1 / real_of_nat k) * (\<Sum>j\<in>{0..<k}. N (ws j))"
  assumes npos : "n \<ge> 1"
    and kpos : "k \<ge> 1"
    and hcircle : "\<forall> i :: nat. circle i \<in> {0 :: nat..1}"
    and hZ : "\<forall>w \<in> {0..n-1} \<times> {0..n}.
      Z w = (\<Sum>l :: nat \<in> {0..<snd w}. if circle ((fst w + l) mod n) = 0 then 1 else 0)"
    and hN : "\<forall>w \<in> {0..n-1} \<times> {0..n}.
      N w = (\<Sum>l :: nat \<in> {0..<snd w}. if circle ((fst w + l) mod n) = 1 then 1 else 0)"
    and hws : "\<forall>j \<in> {0..<k}. ws j \<in> {0..n-1} \<times> {0..n}"
    and Zle1 : "\<forall> w \<in> {0..n-1} \<times> {0..n}. \<forall> w' \<in> {0..n-1} \<times> {0..n}. (snd w) = (snd w') \<longrightarrow> \<bar>int (Z w) - int (Z w')\<bar> \<le> 1"
    and hNZsum : "round Nsum = Nsum \<and> round Zsum = Zsum"
  shows "\<exists>w \<in> {0..n-1} \<times> {0..n}.
    real (Z w) = Zsum \<and> real (N w) = Nsum"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a4:
  balanced zero counts on equal-length arcs of a finite binary circle force
  integral average zero and one counts to occur on one arc. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `!n k:num.
   !circle:num->num.
   !Z N:(num#num)->int.
   !ws:num->(num#num).
   !Zsum Nsum:int.
     let arc =
       \w:num#num. FST w < n /\ SND w <= n in
     1 <= n /\
     1 <= k /\
     (!i:num.
        i < n ==> circle i = 0 \/ circle i = 1) /\
     (!w:num#num.
        arc w
        ==>
        Z w =
        isum {l:num | l < SND w}
          (\l. if circle ((FST w + l) MOD n) = 0 then &1 else &0)) /\
     (!w:num#num.
        arc w
        ==>
        N w =
        isum {l:num | l < SND w}
          (\l. if circle ((FST w + l) MOD n) = 1 then &1 else &0)) /\
     (!w w':num#num.
        arc w /\ arc w' /\ SND w = SND w'
        ==> abs (Z w - Z w') <= &1) /\
     (!j:num. j < k ==> arc (ws j)) /\
     real_of_int Zsum =
       sum {j:num | j < k} (\j. real_of_int (Z (ws j))) / &k /\
     real_of_int Nsum =
       sum {j:num | j < k} (\j. real_of_int (N (ws j))) / &k
     ==>
     ?w:num#num.
       arc w /\ Z w = Zsum /\ N w = Nsum`;;

title: putnam_2013_a4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a4:
;; balanced zero counts on equal-length arcs of a finite binary circle force
;; an arc realizing both integral average digit counts. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A natural below 2^N is the unique N-bit table for a function
;; Fin N -> Fin 2.  An arc is the two-element list (start length), with
;; start in Fin N and length in Fin (N+1).

(defun putnam-2013-a4-bit (circle-code position)
  (mod (floor circle-code (expt 2 position)) 2))

(defun putnam-2013-a4-arc-p (arc n)
  (and
   (true-listp arc)
   (equal (len arc) 2)
   (natp (nth 0 arc))
   (< (nth 0 arc) n)
   (natp (nth 1 arc))
   (<= (nth 1 arc) n)))

(defun putnam-2013-a4-all-arcs-p (arcs n)
  (if (endp arcs)
      t
    (and
     (putnam-2013-a4-arc-p (car arcs) n)
     (putnam-2013-a4-all-arcs-p (cdr arcs) n))))

(defun putnam-2013-a4-digit-count
    (circle-code n start length digit)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix length)))
  (if (zp length)
      0
    (let* ((offset (- length 1))
           (position (mod (+ start offset) n)))
      (+
       (if (equal
            (putnam-2013-a4-bit circle-code position)
            digit)
           1
         0)
       (putnam-2013-a4-digit-count
        circle-code n start offset digit)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a4-zero-count
    (circle-code n arc)
  (putnam-2013-a4-digit-count
   circle-code n (nth 0 arc) (nth 1 arc) 0))

(defun putnam-2013-a4-one-count
    (circle-code n arc)
  (putnam-2013-a4-digit-count
   circle-code n (nth 0 arc) (nth 1 arc) 1))

;; These nested recursions exhaust all pairs of starts for one fixed length.

(defun putnam-2013-a4-balanced-against-p
    (circle-code n length start other-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix other-count)))
  (if (zp other-count)
      t
    (let ((other (- other-count 1)))
      (and
       (<=
        (abs
         (-
          (putnam-2013-a4-digit-count
           circle-code n start length 0)
          (putnam-2013-a4-digit-count
           circle-code n other length 0)))
        1)
       (putnam-2013-a4-balanced-against-p
        circle-code n length start other)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a4-balanced-starts-p
    (circle-code n length start-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix start-count)))
  (if (zp start-count)
      t
    (let ((start (- start-count 1)))
      (and
       (putnam-2013-a4-balanced-against-p
        circle-code n length start n)
       (putnam-2013-a4-balanced-starts-p
        circle-code n length start)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a4-balanced-lengths-p
    (circle-code n length-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix length-count)))
  (if (zp length-count)
      t
    (let ((length (- length-count 1)))
      (and
       (putnam-2013-a4-balanced-starts-p
        circle-code n length n)
       (putnam-2013-a4-balanced-lengths-p
        circle-code n length)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a4-zero-sum
    (circle-code n arcs)
  (if (endp arcs)
      0
    (+
     (putnam-2013-a4-zero-count
      circle-code n (car arcs))
     (putnam-2013-a4-zero-sum
      circle-code n (cdr arcs)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a4-one-sum
    (circle-code n arcs)
  (if (endp arcs)
      0
    (+
     (putnam-2013-a4-one-count
      circle-code n (car arcs))
     (putnam-2013-a4-one-sum
      circle-code n (cdr arcs)))))

;; The source conclusion is existential.  The two searches below keep its
;; witness internal while ranging over every start and every permitted length.

(defun putnam-2013-a4-target-at-start-p
    (circle-code n k zero-total one-total length start-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix start-count)))
  (if (zp start-count)
      nil
    (let* ((start (- start-count 1))
           (arc (list start length)))
      (or
       (and
        (equal
         (* k
            (putnam-2013-a4-zero-count
             circle-code n arc))
         zero-total)
        (equal
         (* k
            (putnam-2013-a4-one-count
             circle-code n arc))
         one-total))
       (putnam-2013-a4-target-at-start-p
        circle-code n k zero-total one-total length start)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a4-target-arc-exists-p
    (circle-code n k zero-total one-total length-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix length-count)))
  (if (zp length-count)
      nil
    (let ((length (- length-count 1)))
      (or
       (putnam-2013-a4-target-at-start-p
        circle-code n k zero-total one-total length n)
       (putnam-2013-a4-target-arc-exists-p
        circle-code n k zero-total one-total length)))))

;; The source functions Z and N are uniquely fixed by their digit-count
;; equations, so they are unfolded above.  Likewise, the integer-valued
;; average parameters are eliminated definitionally: for positive K their
;; existence is exactly divisibility of the corresponding sums by K.

(defun putnambench-putnam-2013-a4-statement
    (n k circle-code selected-arcs)
  (let ((zero-total
         (putnam-2013-a4-zero-sum
          circle-code n selected-arcs))
        (one-total
         (putnam-2013-a4-one-sum
          circle-code n selected-arcs)))
    (implies
     (and
      (posp n)
      (posp k)
      (natp circle-code)
      (< circle-code (expt 2 n))
      (true-listp selected-arcs)
      (equal (len selected-arcs) k)
      (putnam-2013-a4-all-arcs-p selected-arcs n)
      (putnam-2013-a4-balanced-lengths-p
       circle-code n (+ n 1))
      (equal (mod zero-total k) 0)
      (equal (mod one-total k) 0))
     (putnam-2013-a4-target-arc-exists-p
      circle-code n k zero-total one-total (+ n 1)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2013_a4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2013_a4): balanced zero counts on equal-length
-- arcs of a finite binary circle force an arc realizing both integral average
-- digit counts. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2013A4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

toNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
toNat fzero =
  zero
toNat (fsuc index) =
  suc (toNat index)

record Arc (n : Nat) : Set where
  constructor arc
  field
    start  : Fin n
    length : Fin (suc n)

open Arc

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

subtractInt : Int -> Int -> Int
subtractInt x y =
  addInt x (negateInt y)

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

absoluteValue : Int -> Nat
absoluteValue (pos n) =
  n
absoluteValue (negsuc n) =
  suc n

sumFinInt :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Int) ->
  Int
sumFinInt {zero} term =
  pos zero
sumFinInt {suc n} term =
  addInt
    (term fzero)
    (sumFinInt (\ index -> term (fsuc index)))

sameBool : Bool -> Bool -> Bool
sameBool false false =
  true
sameBool false true =
  false
sameBool true false =
  false
sameBool true true =
  true

indicator : Bool -> Bool -> Int
indicator actual expected with sameBool actual expected
... | false =
  pos zero
... | true =
  pos (suc zero)

countDigit :
  (Nat -> Bool) ->
  Bool ->
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Int
countDigit circle digit start-index zero =
  pos zero
countDigit circle digit start-index (suc remaining) =
  addInt
    (indicator (circle start-index) digit)
    (countDigit circle digit (suc start-index) remaining)

ArcCount :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Nat -> Bool) ->
  Bool ->
  Arc n ->
  Int
ArcCount circle digit w =
  countDigit
    circle
    digit
    (toNat (start w))
    (toNat (length w))

Periodic : (Nat -> Bool) -> Nat -> Set
Periodic circle period =
  (index : Nat) ->
  circle (index + period) == circle index

CorrectCounts :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Nat -> Bool) ->
  (Arc n -> Int) ->
  (Arc n -> Int) ->
  Set
CorrectCounts circle Z N =
  ((w : Arc _) -> Z w == ArcCount circle false w)
  and
  ((w : Arc _) -> N w == ArcCount circle true w)

BalancedZeroCounts :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Arc n -> Int) ->
  Set
BalancedZeroCounts Z =
  (w w' : Arc _) ->
  length w == length w' ->
  absoluteValue (subtractInt (Z w) (Z w')) <=N suc zero

IntegralAverages :
  {n k : Nat} ->
  (Arc n -> Int) ->
  (Arc n -> Int) ->
  (Fin k -> Arc n) ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  Set
IntegralAverages {k = k} Z N ws Zsum Nsum =
  (multiplyInt (pos k) Zsum ==
    sumFinInt (\ index -> Z (ws index)))
  and
  (multiplyInt (pos k) Nsum ==
    sumFinInt (\ index -> N (ws index)))

RealizesAverages :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Arc n -> Int) ->
  (Arc n -> Int) ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  Set
RealizesAverages {n} Z N Zsum Nsum =
  Exists (Arc n)
    (\ w ->
      (Z w == Zsum)
      and
      (N w == Nsum))

putnam-2013-a4 : Set
putnam-2013-a4 =
  (n k : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  Positive k ->
  (circle : Nat -> Bool) ->
  Periodic circle n ->
  (Z N : Arc n -> Int) ->
  (ws : Fin k -> Arc n) ->
  (Zsum Nsum : Int) ->
  CorrectCounts circle Z N ->
  BalancedZeroCounts Z ->
  IntegralAverages Z N ws Zsum Nsum ->
  RealizesAverages Z N Zsum Nsum

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a4:
  balanced zero counts on equal-length arcs of a finite binary circle force
  an arc realizing integral average zero and one counts. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2013_a4 =
  ``!n k : num.
      !circle : num -> num.
      !ws : num -> num # num.
      !Zsum Nsum : int.
      0 < n /\
      0 < k /\
      (!i : num. i < n ==> circle i < 2) /\
      (!j : num.
         j < k ==> FST (ws j) < n /\ SND (ws j) <= n)
      ==>
      let Z =
        \w : num # num.
          SIGMA
            (\l : num.
               if circle ((FST w + l) MOD n) = 0
               then (1 : int)
               else 0)
            (count (SND w))
      in
      let N =
        \w : num # num.
          SIGMA
            (\l : num.
               if circle ((FST w + l) MOD n) = 1
               then (1 : int)
               else 0)
            (count (SND w))
      in
        (!w w' : num # num.
           FST w < n /\ SND w <= n /\
           FST w' < n /\ SND w' <= n /\
           SND w = SND w'
           ==>
           ABS (Z w - Z w') <= 1) /\
        int_of_num k * Zsum =
          SIGMA (\j : num. Z (ws j)) (count k) /\
        int_of_num k * Nsum =
          SIGMA (\j : num. N (ws j)) (count k)
        ==>
        ?w : num # num.
          FST w < n /\ SND w <= n /\
          Z w = Zsum /\ N w = Nsum``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2013_a4: binary digits arranged on a finite circle, with zero counts
  on equal-length arcs differing by at most one, admit an arc realizing the
  integral average zero and one counts of any finite family of arcs. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The ordinal 0 ..^ n represents Fin n, and 0 ... n represents Fin (n + 1).
  Thus their Cartesian product is the full carrier of circular arcs, encoded
  by a starting position and a length from zero through n. Addition modulo n
  renders Fin n addition and hence circular wraparound exactly.

  C ranges over every binary-valued function on the n positions. Z and N are
  integer-valued functions on all arcs and are constrained to be precisely the
  zero and one counts. W is an arbitrary k-indexed family of arcs. The integer
  variables z and q satisfy the same real average equalities as Zsum and Nsum
  in the primary Lean source. The final existential remains internal to the
  conclusion. The sole declaration below is an unproved $a corpus statement;
  this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d C N W Z j k l n q v w z $.

  putnambench-putnam-2013-a4 $a |- A. n e. NN A. k e. NN
    A. C e. ( ( 0 ..^ 2 ) ^m ( 0 ..^ n ) )
      A. Z e. ( ZZ ^m ( ( 0 ..^ n ) X. ( 0 ... n ) ) )
        A. N e. ( ZZ ^m ( ( 0 ..^ n ) X. ( 0 ... n ) ) )
          A. W e.
            ( ( ( 0 ..^ n ) X. ( 0 ... n ) ) ^m ( 0 ..^ k ) )
            A. z e. ZZ A. q e. ZZ
              (
                (
                  A. w e. ( ( 0 ..^ n ) X. ( 0 ... n ) )
                    ( Z ` w )
                    =
                    (
                      sum_ l e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2nd ` w ) )
                        if (
                          (

                            (

                              )
                              mod

                            )
                          )
                          =
                          0 ,
                          1 ,
                          0
                        )
                    )
                  /\
                  (
                    A. w e. ( ( 0 ..^ n ) X. ( 0 ... n ) )
                      ( N ` w )

                      (
                        sum_ l e. ( 0 ..^ ( 2nd ` w ) )
                          if (
                            (

                                  +
                                  l
                                )

                              )
                            )
                            =

                          )
                      )
                    /\
                    (
                      A. w e. ( ( 0 ..^ n ) X. ( 0 ... n ) )
                        A. v e. ( ( 0 ..^ n ) X. ( 0 ... n ) )
                          (

                            ->

title: putnam_2013_a4
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a4:
:: balanced zero counts on equal-length arcs of a finite binary circle force
:: an arc realizing both integral average digit counts. This file contains no
:: proof.

environ
  vocabularies NUMBERS, NAT_1, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, TARSKI, CARD_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0,
    XXREAL_0, ORDINAL1, INT_1, ARYTM_1, ARYTM_3, CARD_3, VALUED_0,
    VALUED_1, ZFMISC_1, MCART_1, COMPLEX1, BINOP_1;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, XTUPLE_0, SUBSET_1, ORDINAL1,
    CARD_1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, INT_1, RELAT_1,
    FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, FINSEQ_1, RVSUM_1, FINSEQ_2, NAT_1,
    NAT_D, COMPLEX1, MCART_1, BINOP_1;
  constructors REAL_1, NAT_D, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, NUMBERS, INT_1, RVSUM_1,
    FINSEQOP, ZFMISC_1, MCART_1, BINOP_1;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,
    ORDINAL1, NUMBERS, XCMPLX_0, XXREAL_0, XREAL_0, NAT_1, INT_1,
    FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, RVSUM_1, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, CARD_1,
    MEMBERED, ZFMISC_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n,k being Nat,
      circle being Function of NAT,NAT,
      Z,N being Function of [:NAT,NAT:],INT,
      starts,lengths being FinSequence of NAT,
      Zsum,Nsum being Integer st
    0 < n &
    0 < k &
    len starts = k &
    len lengths = k &
    (for i being Nat st i < n holds
      circle.i = 0 or circle.i = 1) &
    (for j being Nat st j in Seg k holds
      starts.j < n & lengths.j <= n) &
    (for s,L being Nat st
      s < n & L <= n
    holds
      ex zeroTerms being FinSequence of INT st
        len zeroTerms = L &
        (for i being Nat st i in Seg L holds
          (circle.((s + (i -' 1)) mod n) = 0 &
             zeroTerms.i = 1) or
          (circle.((s + (i -' 1)) mod n) <> 0 &
             zeroTerms.i = 0)) &
        Z.([s,L]) = Sum zeroTerms) &
    (for s,L being Nat st
      s < n & L <= n
    holds
      ex oneTerms being FinSequence of INT st
        len oneTerms = L &
        (for i being Nat st i in Seg L holds
          (circle.((s + (i -' 1)) mod n) = 1 &
             oneTerms.i = 1) or
          (circle.((s + (i -' 1)) mod n) <> 1 &
             oneTerms.i = 0)) &
        N.([s,L]) = Sum oneTerms) &
    (for s,t,L being Nat st
      s < n & t < n & L <= n
    holds
      Z.([s,L]) - Z.([t,L]) <= 1 &
      Z.([t,L]) - Z.([s,L]) <= 1) &
    (ex zeroTotals,oneTotals being FinSequence of INT st
      len zeroTotals = k &
      len oneTotals = k &
      (for j being Nat st j in Seg k holds
        zeroTotals.j = Z.([starts.j,lengths.j]) &
        oneTotals.j = N.([starts.j,lengths.j])) &
      Sum zeroTotals = (k qua Integer) * Zsum &
      Sum oneTotals = (k qua Integer) * Nsum)
  holds
    ex s,L being Nat st
      s < n & L <= n &
      Z.([s,L]) = Zsum & N.([s,L]) = Nsum
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2013_a4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a4:
% balanced zero counts on equal-length arcs of a finite binary circle force
% integer average zero and one counts to occur on one arc. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2013_a4[n, k: posnat]: THEORY
BEGIN
  position: TYPE = below(n)
  arc_length: TYPE = upto(n)
  digit: TYPE = below(2)
  arc: TYPE = [# start: position, length: arc_length #]
  circle_type: TYPE = [position -> digit]
  arc_integer_value: TYPE = [arc -> int]
  arc_sequence: TYPE = [below(k) -> arc]

  zero_count(
      circle: circle_type,
      first: position,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      zero_count(circle, first, count - 1)
        + IF circle(mod(first + count - 1, n)) = 0
            THEN 1
            ELSE 0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  one_count(
      circle: circle_type,
      first: position,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      one_count(circle, first, count - 1)
        + IF circle(mod(first + count - 1, n)) = 1
            THEN 1
            ELSE 0
          ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  integer_prefix_sum(
      values: [below(k) -> int],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      integer_prefix_sum(values, count - 1)
        + IF count <= k THEN values(count - 1) ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  putnam_2013_a4: bool =
    FORALL
        (circle: circle_type),
        (Z, N: arc_integer_value),
        (ws: arc_sequence),
        (Zsum, Nsum: int):
      ((FORALL (w: arc):
          Z(w) = (zero_count(circle, start(w), length(w)) :: int))
        AND
          (FORALL (w: arc):
            N(w) = (one_count(circle, start(w), length(w)) :: int))
        AND
          (FORALL (w, w_prime: arc):
            length(w) = length(w_prime)
              IMPLIES abs(Z(w) - Z(w_prime)) <= 1)
        AND
          (Zsum :: real)
            = (1 / (k :: real))
                * (integer_prefix_sum(
                    (LAMBDA (j: below(k)): Z(ws(j))),
                    k) :: real)
        AND
          (Nsum :: real)
            = (1 / (k :: real))
                * (integer_prefix_sum(
                    (LAMBDA (j: below(k)): N(ws(j))),
                    k) :: real))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (w: arc):
          Z(w) = Zsum
            AND N(w) = Nsum
END putnam_2013_a4

title: putnam_2013_a5
content:
import Mathlib

open Function Set MeasureTheory

-- Note: uses (Fin m → Fin m → Fin m → ℝ) instead of ensuring inputs are strictly increasing
/--
For $m \geq 3$, a list of $\binom{m}{3}$ real numbers $a_{ijk}$ ($1 \leq i< j< k \leq m$) is said to be \emph{area definite} for $\mathbb{R}^n$ if the inequality $\sum_{1 \leq i< j< k \leq m} a_{ijk} \cdot \text{Area}(\Delta A_iA_jA_k) \geq 0$ holds for every choice of $m$ points $A_1,\dots,A_m$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$. For example, the list of four numbers $a_{123}=a_{124}=a_{134}=1$, $a_{234}=-1$ is area definite for $\mathbb{R}^2$. Prove that if a list of $\binom{m}{3}$ numbers is area definite for $\mathbb{R}^2$, then it is area definite for $\mathbb{R}^3$.
-/
theorem putnam_2013_a5
(m : ℕ)
(area2 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) →
  EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ)
(area3 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) →
  EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → ℝ)
(areadef2 : (Fin m → Fin m → Fin m → ℝ) → Prop)
(areadef3 : (Fin m → Fin m → Fin m → ℝ) → Prop)
(mge3 : m ≥ 3)
(harea2 : ∀ a b c, area2 a b c = (volume (convexHull ℝ {a, b, c})).toReal)
(harea3 : ∀ a b c, area3 a b c = (μH[2] (convexHull ℝ {a, b, c})).toReal)
(hareadef2 : ∀ a, areadef2 a ↔
  ∀ A : Fin m → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2),
    (∑ i : Fin m, ∑ j : Fin m, ∑ k : Fin m,
      if i < j ∧ j < k then a i j k * area2 (A i) (A j) (A k) else 0) ≥ 0)
(hareadef3 : ∀ a, areadef3 a ↔
  ∀ A : Fin m → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3),
    (∑ i : Fin m, ∑ j : Fin m, ∑ k : Fin m,
      if i < j ∧ j < k then a i j k * area3 (A i) (A j) (A k) else 0) ≥ 0)
: ∀ a, areadef2 a → areadef3 a :=
sorry

title: putnam_2013_a5
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a5:
   area-definite real coefficients for triangles in the Euclidean plane remain
   area definite for triangles in Euclidean three-space. This file contains no
   proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals Arith.PeanoNat.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2013_a5_point2 : Type := (R * R)%type.
Definition putnam_2013_a5_point3 : Type := (R * (R * R))%type.

Definition putnam_2013_a5_area2
    (a b c : putnam_2013_a5_point2) : R :=
  Rabs
    ((fst b - fst a) * (snd c - snd a) -
     (snd b - snd a) * (fst c - fst a)) / 2.

Definition putnam_2013_a5_cross_x
    (a b c : putnam_2013_a5_point3) : R :=
  (fst (snd b) - fst (snd a)) * (snd (snd c) - snd (snd a)) -
  (snd (snd b) - snd (snd a)) * (fst (snd c) - fst (snd a)).

Definition putnam_2013_a5_cross_y
    (a b c : putnam_2013_a5_point3) : R :=
  (snd (snd b) - snd (snd a)) * (fst c - fst a) -
  (fst b - fst a) * (snd (snd c) - snd (snd a)).

Definition putnam_2013_a5_cross_z
    (a b c : putnam_2013_a5_point3) : R :=
  (fst b - fst a) * (fst (snd c) - fst (snd a)) -
  (fst (snd b) - fst (snd a)) * (fst c - fst a).

Definition putnam_2013_a5_area3
    (a b c : putnam_2013_a5_point3) : R :=
  sqrt
    (putnam_2013_a5_cross_x a b c ^ 2 +
     putnam_2013_a5_cross_y a b c ^ 2 +
     putnam_2013_a5_cross_z a b c ^ 2) / 2.

Fixpoint putnam_2013_a5_sum_first
    (n : nat) (f : nat -> R) : R :=
  match n with
  | O => 0
  | S k => putnam_2013_a5_sum_first k f + f k
  end.

Definition putnam_2013_a5_weighted_sum2
    (m : nat)
    (coefficients : nat -> nat -> nat -> R)
    (points : nat -> putnam_2013_a5_point2) : R :=
  putnam_2013_a5_sum_first m
    (fun i =>
      putnam_2013_a5_sum_first m
        (fun j =>
          putnam_2013_a5_sum_first m
            (fun k =>
              if andb (Nat.ltb i j) (Nat.ltb j k)
              then coefficients i j k *
                putnam_2013_a5_area2 (points i) (points j) (points k)
              else 0))).

Definition putnam_2013_a5_weighted_sum3
    (m : nat)
    (coefficients : nat -> nat -> nat -> R)
    (points : nat -> putnam_2013_a5_point3) : R :=
  putnam_2013_a5_sum_first m
    (fun i =>
      putnam_2013_a5_sum_first m
        (fun j =>
          putnam_2013_a5_sum_first m
            (fun k =>
              if andb (Nat.ltb i j) (Nat.ltb j k)
              then coefficients i j k *
                putnam_2013_a5_area3 (points i) (points j) (points k)
              else 0))).

Definition putnam_2013_a5_area_definite2
    (m : nat) (coefficients : nat -> nat -> nat -> R) : Prop :=
  forall points : nat -> putnam_2013_a5_point2,
    0 <= putnam_2013_a5_weighted_sum2 m coefficients points.

Definition putnam_2013_a5_area_definite3
    (m : nat) (coefficients : nat -> nat -> nat -> R) : Prop :=
  forall points : nat -> putnam_2013_a5_point3,
    0 <= putnam_2013_a5_weighted_sum3 m coefficients points.

Theorem putnam_2013_a5 :
  forall (m : nat) (coefficients : nat -> nat -> nat -> R),
    (3 <= m)%nat ->
    putnam_2013_a5_area_definite2 m coefficients ->
    putnam_2013_a5_area_definite3 m coefficients.
Admitted.

content:
theory putnam_2013_a5 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Finite_Cartesian_Product"
"HOL-Analysis.Lebesgue_Measure"
"HOL-Analysis.Cross3"
begin

(* uses (nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> real), (nat \<Rightarrow> (real^2)), and (nat \<Rightarrow> (real^3)) instead of limiting inputs to (Fin m) and ensuring inputs are strictly increasing *)
theorem putnam_2013_a5:
  fixes m :: nat
    and area2 :: "(real^2) \<Rightarrow> (real^2) \<Rightarrow> (real^2) \<Rightarrow> real"
    and area3 :: "(real^3) \<Rightarrow> (real^3) \<Rightarrow> (real^3) \<Rightarrow> real"
    and areadef2 :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
    and areadef3 :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  assumes mge3: "m \<ge> 3"
    and harea2: "\<forall>a b c::real^2. area2 a b c =
      \<bar>((b-a)$0) * ((c-a)$1) - ((b-a)$1) * ((c-a)$0)\<bar> / 2"
    and harea3: "\<forall>a b c::real^3. area3 a b c =
      norm (cross3 (b-a) (c-a)) / 2"
    and hareadef2: "\<forall>a::nat\<Rightarrow>nat\<Rightarrow>nat\<Rightarrow>real. areadef2 a = (\<forall>A::nat\<Rightarrow>(real^2). (\<Sum>i::nat\<in>{0..(m-1)}. \<Sum>j::nat\<in>{i<..(m-1)}. \<Sum>k::nat\<in>{j<..(m-1)}. (a i j k * area2 (A i) (A j) (A k))) \<ge> 0)"
    and hareadef3: "\<forall>a::nat\<Rightarrow>nat\<Rightarrow>nat\<Rightarrow>real. areadef3 a = (\<forall>A::nat\<Rightarrow>(real^3). (\<Sum>i::nat\<in>{0..(m-1)}. \<Sum>j::nat\<in>{i<..(m-1)}. \<Sum>k::nat\<in>{j<..(m-1)}. (a i j k * area3 (A i) (A j) (A k))) \<ge> 0)"
  shows "\<forall>a::nat\<Rightarrow>nat\<Rightarrow>nat\<Rightarrow>real. (areadef2 a \<longrightarrow> areadef3 a)"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a5:
  area-definiteness of coefficients for triangles in the Euclidean plane
  implies area-definiteness for triangles in three-dimensional Euclidean
  space. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let area2 =
     \(P:real^2) (Q:real^2) (R:real^2).
       abs ((Q$1 - P$1) * (R$2 - P$2) -
            (Q$2 - P$2) * (R$1 - P$1)) / &2 in
   let area3 =
     \(P:real^3) (Q:real^3) (R:real^3).
       sqrt
         (((Q$2 - P$2) * (R$3 - P$3) -
           (Q$3 - P$3) * (R$2 - P$2)) pow 2 +
          ((Q$3 - P$3) * (R$1 - P$1) -
           (Q$1 - P$1) * (R$3 - P$3)) pow 2 +
          ((Q$1 - P$1) * (R$2 - P$2) -
           (Q$2 - P$2) * (R$1 - P$1)) pow 2) / &2 in
   !m:num. !a:num->num->num->real.
     3 <= m /\
     (!A:num->real^2.
        &0 <=
        sum (0..m - 1)
          (\i:num.
             sum (i + 1..m - 1)
               (\j:num.
                  sum (j + 1..m - 1)
                    (\k:num. a i j k * area2 (A i) (A j) (A k)))))
     ==>
     !A:num->real^3.
       &0 <=
       sum (0..m - 1)
         (\i:num.
            sum (i + 1..m - 1)
              (\j:num.
                 sum (j + 1..m - 1)
                   (\k:num. a i j k * area3 (A i) (A j) (A k))))`;;

title: putnam_2013_a5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2013_a5:
;; area-definiteness of real coefficients for every planar point configuration
;; implies area-definiteness for every spatial configuration. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The real scalar domain is presented as an arbitrary real closed ordered
;; field.  Real closed fields have the same first-order theory as the reals,
;; and all formulas below use only ordered-field operations and the unique
;; nonnegative square root.  Thus this presentation is bidirectionally
;; equivalent to the source statement over R.
;;
;; A function Fin m x Fin m x Fin m -> R is represented exactly by a list of
;; length m^3, and a configuration Fin m -> R^d by a list of m d-tuples.
;; DEFUN-SK directly quantifies over every such configuration.  The
;; triangle-area terms are sqrt(det^2)/2 in dimension two and
;; sqrt(||u cross v||^2)/2 in dimension three, the standard algebraic
;; formulas for the source Euclidean areas.

(defun putnam-2013-a5-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2013-a5-quoted function)
   (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2013-a5-quoted function)
   (list 'cons left (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-and-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2013-a5-quoted t)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2013-a5-and-term (cdr terms))
     (putnam-2013-a5-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-or-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2013-a5-quoted nil)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2013-a5-quoted t)
     (putnam-2013-a5-or-term (cdr terms)))))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-not-term (term)
  (list
   'if
   term
   (putnam-2013-a5-quoted nil)
   (putnam-2013-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-implies-term (antecedent consequent)
  (list
   'if
   antecedent
   consequent
   (putnam-2013-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-true-function (formals)
  (list
   'lambda
   formals
   (putnam-2013-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-2013-a5-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-operation-term (operation left right)
  (putnam-2013-a5-apply2-term operation left right))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-all-coefficients-function ()
  '(lambda (loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)
     (apply$ (car loop$-gvars)
             (cons loop$-ivars 'nil))))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-all-coefficients-term
    (carrier coefficients)
  (list
   'always$+
   (putnam-2013-a5-quoted
    (putnam-2013-a5-all-coefficients-function))
   (list 'cons
         (putnam-2013-a5-quoted carrier)
         nil)
   coefficients))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-polynomial-term
    (carrier zero coefficients)
  (putnam-2013-a5-and-term
   (list
    (list 'true-listp coefficients)
    (list 'consp coefficients)
    (putnam-2013-a5-all-coefficients-term
     carrier coefficients)
    (putnam-2013-a5-or-term
     (list
      (list 'equal
            (list 'len coefficients)
            (putnam-2013-a5-quoted 1))
      (putnam-2013-a5-not-term
       (list 'equal
             (list 'car (list 'last coefficients))
             (putnam-2013-a5-quoted zero))))))))

(defun putnam-2013-a5-field-laws-function
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (y 'y)
         (z 'z)
         (qzero (putnam-2013-a5-quoted zero))
         (qone (putnam-2013-a5-quoted one))
         (add-xy
          (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term add x y))
         (add-yz
          (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term add y z))
         (mul-xy
          (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term mul x y))
         (mul-yz
          (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term mul y z))
         (neg-x
          (putnam-2013-a5-apply1-term neg x))
         (inv-x
          (putnam-2013-a5-apply1-term inv x))
         (domain
          (putnam-2013-a5-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2013-a5-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2013-a5-carrier-term carrier y)
            (putnam-2013-a5-carrier-term carrier z))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2013-a5-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2013-a5-carrier-term carrier add-xy)
            (putnam-2013-a5-carrier-term carrier mul-xy)
            (putnam-2013-a5-carrier-term carrier neg-x)
            (putnam-2013-a5-carrier-term carrier inv-x)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term add add-xy z)
             (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term add x add-yz))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term mul mul-xy z)
             (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term mul x mul-yz))
            (list
             'equal
             add-xy
             (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term add y x))
            (list
             'equal
             mul-xy
             (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term mul y x))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term add x qzero)
             x)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2013-a5-operation-term add x neg-x)
             qzero)
