title: putnam_2014_a1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2014_a1: every nonzero Taylor coefficient at zero of
  (1 - x + x^2) exp(x) is rational with reduced numerator equal to one
  or a prime. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  RR ^m RR and RR ^m NN0 retain the source's total real function and
  real-valued coefficient sequence. The all-orders C^n condition is the
  global smoothness assumption from Lean and the derivative-existence
  assumption from Rocq.

  P14A1Deriv totalizes set.mm's partial real derivative by assigning zero
  outside its domain. Under the smoothness premise this agrees everywhere
  with the ordinary derivative, and IterComp includes derivative order zero.
  Thus the displayed quotient by n factorial is the source Taylor
  coefficient at zero.

  The internally existential rational q is identified with the coefficient.
  Set.mm's numer is the integer numerator of q in its unique reduced
  representation with positive denominator, and Prime is its class of
  positive natural primes. The final declaration is the single unproved $a
  corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c P14A1Deriv P14A1IterDeriv $.

p14a1-deriv-syntax $a class P14A1Deriv $.
p14a1-iter-deriv-syntax $a class ( P14A1IterDeriv n A ) $.

${
  $d A x $.

  p14a1-deriv-definition $a |- P14A1Deriv =
    (
      A e. ( RR ^m RR ) |->
        (
          x e. RR |->
            if (
              x e. dom ( RR _D A ) ,
              ( ( RR _D A ) ` x ) ,
              0
            )
        )
    ) $.
$}

p14a1-iter-deriv-definition $a |- ( P14A1IterDeriv n A ) =
  (
    ( ( IterComp ` P14A1Deriv ) ` n )
    `
    A
  ) $.

${
  $d c f k n q x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2014-a1 $a |-
    A. f e. ( RR ^m RR )
    A. c e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
      (
        (
          (
            A. x e. RR
              ( f ` x )
              =
              (
                (
                  ( 1 - x )
                  +
                  ( x ^ 2 )
                )
                x.
                ( exp ` x )
              )
            /\
            A. n e. NN0
              f e. ( ( C^n ` RR ) ` n )
          )
          /\
          A. n e. NN0
            ( c ` n )
            =
            (
              (
                ( P14A1IterDeriv n f )
                `
                0
              )
              /
              ( ! ` n )
            )
        )
        ->
        A. k e. NN0
          (
            ( c ` k ) =/= 0
            ->
            E. q e. QQ
              (
                ( c ` k ) = q
                /\
                (
                  ( numer ` q ) = 1
                  \/
                  ( numer ` q ) e. Prime
                )
              )
          )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2014_a1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a1:
% every nonzero Taylor coefficient at zero of (1 - x + x^2) * exp(x) is
% rational with reduced numerator equal to 1 or a prime. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2014_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  has_derivative_at(
      f: real_function,
      derivative, x: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (h: real):
          (h /= 0 AND abs(h) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                f(x + h) - f(x)
                  - derivative * h)
                < epsilon_value * abs(h)

  differentiable_at(f: real_function, x: real): bool =
    EXISTS (derivative: real):
      has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x)

  derivative_value(f: real_function, x: real): real =
    IF differentiable_at(f, x) THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (derivative: real):
          has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  derivative_function(f: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real): derivative_value(f, x)

  iterated_derivative(
      f: real_function,
      order: nat): RECURSIVE real_function =
    IF order = 0 THEN
      f
    ELSE
      derivative_function(
        iterated_derivative(f, order - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE order

  continuous(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real), (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (y: real):
          abs(y - x) < delta IMPLIES
            abs(f(y) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  infinitely_continuously_differentiable(
      f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (order: nat):
      continuous(iterated_derivative(f, order))
        AND FORALL (x: real):
          differentiable_at(
            iterated_derivative(f, order), x)

  taylor_coefficient(
      f: real_function,
      order: nat): real =
    safe_div(
      iterated_derivative(f, order)(0),
      nat_factorial(order) :: real)

  nat_divides(divisor: posnat, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  coprime_nat(left, right: nat): bool =
    FORALL (divisor: posnat):
      nat_divides(divisor, left)
        AND nat_divides(divisor, right)
        IMPLIES divisor = 1

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value

  has_prime_or_one_reduced_numerator(q: rat): bool =
    EXISTS (numerator: nat), (denominator: posnat):
      q = (numerator :: rat) / (denominator :: rat)
        AND coprime_nat(numerator, denominator)
        AND (numerator = 1 OR prime_nat(numerator))

  putnam_2014_a1: bool =
    FORALL (f: real_function), (coefficients: real_sequence):
      ((FORALL (x: real):
          f(x) =
            (1 - x + x ^ 2) * real_exponential(x))
        AND infinitely_continuously_differentiable(f)
        AND (FORALL (order: nat):
          coefficients(order) =
            taylor_coefficient(f, order)))
      IMPLIES
        FORALL (order: nat):
          coefficients(order) /= 0 IMPLIES
            EXISTS (q: rat):
              coefficients(order) = q
                AND has_prime_or_one_reduced_numerator(q)
END putnam_2014_a1

import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Nat

abbrev putnam_2014_a2_solution : ℕ → ℝ := sorry
-- (fun n : ℕ => (-1) ^ (n - 1) / ((n - 1)! * (n)!))
/--
Let $A$ be the $n \times n$ matrix whose entry in the $i$-th row and $j$-th column is $\frac{1}{\min(i,j)}$ for $1 \leq i,j \leq n$. Compute $\det(A)$.
-/
theorem putnam_2014_a2
(n : ℕ)
(A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
(npos : n > 0)
(hA : ∀ i j : Fin n, A i j = 1 / min (i.1 + 1 : ℚ) (j.1 + 1))
: A.det = putnam_2014_a2_solution n :=
sorry

title: putnam_2014_a2
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a2:
   the determinant of the positive-dimensional real matrix with entries
   reciprocal to the minimum of their one-based indices. This file contains
   no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Arith.PeanoNat Arith.Factorial
  Vectors.Fin Reals.

Import ListNotations.
Open Scope R_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_2014_a2_fin_list
    (n : nat) : list (Fin.t n) :=
  match n as m return list (Fin.t m) with
  | O => []
  | S k =>
      Fin.F1 :: map Fin.FS (putnam_2014_a2_fin_list k)
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2014_a2_sum (xs : list R) : R :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0
  | x :: rest => x + putnam_2014_a2_sum rest
  end.

Definition putnam_2014_a2_delete_nth
    {T : Type} (j : nat) (xs : list T) : list T :=
  firstn j xs ++ skipn (S j) xs.

Definition putnam_2014_a2_cofactor_sign (j : nat) : R :=
  if Nat.even j then 1 else -1.

Fixpoint putnam_2014_a2_list_det
    (n : nat) (M : list (list R)) {struct n} : R :=
  match n with
  | O => 1
  | S k =>
      match M with
      | [] => 0
      | row :: rows =>
          putnam_2014_a2_sum
            (map
              (fun j : nat =>
                putnam_2014_a2_cofactor_sign j *
                nth j row 0 *
                putnam_2014_a2_list_det k
                  (map (putnam_2014_a2_delete_nth j) rows))
              (seq 0 (S k)))
      end
  end.

Definition putnam_2014_a2_matrix (n : nat) : Type :=
  Fin.t n -> Fin.t n -> R.

Definition putnam_2014_a2_rows
    (n : nat) (A : putnam_2014_a2_matrix n) :
    list (list R) :=
  map
    (fun i =>
      map (fun j => A i j) (putnam_2014_a2_fin_list n))
    (putnam_2014_a2_fin_list n).

Definition putnam_2014_a2_determinant
    (n : nat) (A : putnam_2014_a2_matrix n) : R :=
  putnam_2014_a2_list_det n (putnam_2014_a2_rows n A).

Definition putnam_2014_a2_index
    {n : nat} (i : Fin.t n) : nat :=
  proj1_sig (Fin.to_nat i).

Definition putnam_2014_a2_solution (n : nat) : R :=
  (-1) ^ (n - 1) /
  (INR (fact (n - 1)) * INR (fact n)).

Theorem putnam_2014_a2
    (n : nat)
    (A : putnam_2014_a2_matrix n)
    (npos : (0 < n)%nat)
    (hA :
      forall i j : Fin.t n,
        A i j =
        1 / INR
          (Nat.min
            (S (putnam_2014_a2_index i))
            (S (putnam_2014_a2_index j)))) :
  putnam_2014_a2_determinant n A =
  putnam_2014_a2_solution n.
Admitted.

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a2:
;; for every positive n, the determinant of the n by n real matrix whose
;; (i,j)-entry is 1/min(i,j), with indices starting at 1, is
;; (-1)^(n-1)/((n-1)! n!). This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The source entry hypothesis determines A extensionally, so quantifying over
;; A under that hypothesis is equivalent to taking the canonical matrix below.
;; Every entry is rational, and the Leibniz formula uses only field operations,
;; so its real determinant is the canonical real embedding of this exact ACL2
;; rational. Equality of these rationals is therefore bidirectionally
;; equivalent to the source real equality; no arbitrary real value is narrowed.

(defun putnam-2014-a2-range-from (start count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons start
          (putnam-2014-a2-range-from
           (+ 1 start) (- count 1)))))

;; Generate all permutations of the zero-based column indices.

(defun putnam-2014-a2-prefix-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (cons (cons item (car lists))
          (putnam-2014-a2-prefix-each item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a2-insert-everywhere (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list (list item))
    (cons (cons item list)
          (putnam-2014-a2-prefix-each
           (car list)
           (putnam-2014-a2-insert-everywhere
            item (cdr list))))))

(defun putnam-2014-a2-insert-into-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-2014-a2-insert-everywhere item (car lists))
     (putnam-2014-a2-insert-into-each
      item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a2-permutations (list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list nil)
    (putnam-2014-a2-insert-into-each
     (car list)
     (putnam-2014-a2-permutations (cdr list)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a2-count-greater (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      0
    (+ (if (> item (car list)) 1 0)
       (putnam-2014-a2-count-greater item (cdr list)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a2-inversion-count (permutation)
  (if (endp permutation)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2014-a2-count-greater
        (car permutation) (cdr permutation))
       (putnam-2014-a2-inversion-count
        (cdr permutation)))))

;; Zero-based row and column indices represent the source indices i=row+1 and
;; j=column+1.

(defun putnam-2014-a2-entry (row column)
  (/ 1
     (if (< row column)
         (+ row 1)
       (+ column 1))))

(defun putnam-2014-a2-diagonal-product (permutation row)
  (if (endp permutation)
      1
    (* (putnam-2014-a2-entry row (car permutation))
       (putnam-2014-a2-diagonal-product
        (cdr permutation) (+ row 1)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a2-determinant-sum (permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      0
    (let* ((permutation (car permutations))
           (product
            (putnam-2014-a2-diagonal-product permutation 0))
           (signed-product
            (if (evenp
                 (putnam-2014-a2-inversion-count permutation))
                product
              (- product))))
      (+ signed-product
         (putnam-2014-a2-determinant-sum
          (cdr permutations))))))

(defun putnam-2014-a2-determinant (n)
  (putnam-2014-a2-determinant-sum
   (putnam-2014-a2-permutations
    (putnam-2014-a2-range-from 0 n))))

(defun putnam-2014-a2-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n
       (putnam-2014-a2-factorial (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a2-solution (n)
  (/ (if (evenp (- n 1)) 1 -1)
     (* (putnam-2014-a2-factorial (- n 1))
        (putnam-2014-a2-factorial n))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2014-a2-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and (natp n)
        (< 0 n))
   (equal
    (putnam-2014-a2-determinant n)
    (putnam-2014-a2-solution n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2014_a2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2014_a2): the determinant of the real matrix
-- with entry 1 / min(i,j) for indices 1 through n. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  suc zero <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

toNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
toNat fzero =
  zero
toNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (toNat i)

minimum : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
minimum zero n =
  zero
minimum (suc m) zero =
  zero
minimum (suc m) (suc n) =
  suc (minimum m n)

predecessor : Nat -> Nat
predecessor zero =
  zero
predecessor (suc n) =
  n

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  suc zero
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals numerator denominator =
  multiply reals numerator (inverse reals denominator)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc exponent) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x exponent)
    x

Matrix : Set -> Nat -> Set
Matrix R n =
  Fin n -> Fin n -> R

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

skip :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin (suc n)
skip {zero} removed ()
skip {suc n} fzero i =
  fsuc i
skip {suc n} (fsuc removed) fzero =
  fzero
skip {suc n} (fsuc removed) (fsuc i) =
  fsuc (skip removed i)

firstRowMinor :
  {R : Set} {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R (suc n) ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Matrix R n
firstRowMinor A removedColumn i j =
  A (fsuc i) (skip removedColumn j)

alternatingSign :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  R
alternatingSign reals fzero =
  oneR reals
alternatingSign reals (fsuc i) =
  negate reals (alternatingSign reals i)

determinant :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  R
determinant reals {zero} A =
  oneR reals
determinant reals {suc n} A =
  sumFin reals
    (\ column ->
      multiply reals
        (alternatingSign reals column)
        (multiply reals
          (A fzero column)
          (determinant reals (firstRowMinor A column))))

HasPrescribedEntries :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Set
HasPrescribedEntries reals A =
  (i j : _) ->
  A i j ==
  divide reals
    (oneR reals)
    (fromNat reals
      (minimum
        (suc (toNat i))
        (suc (toNat j))))

solution :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
solution reals n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals
      (negate reals (oneR reals))
      (predecessor n))
    (fromNat reals
      (factorial (predecessor n) * factorial n))

putnam-2014-a2 : Set1
putnam-2014-a2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  (A : Matrix R n) ->
  HasPrescribedEntries reals A ->
  determinant reals A == solution reals n

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a2:
  the determinant of the n by n real matrix whose (i,j)-entry is the
  reciprocal of min(i,j), with one-based indices, is the stated signed
  reciprocal product of consecutive factorials. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory permutesTheory realTheory;

val putnam_2014_a2 =
  ``let determinant =
      \n : num. \A : num -> num -> real.
        ITSET
          (\p : num -> num. \sum : real.
             (if evenperm p then
                ITSET
                  (\i : num. \acc : real. A i (p i) * acc)
                  (count n)
                  1
              else
                -(ITSET
                    (\i : num. \acc : real. A i (p i) * acc)
                    (count n)
                    1)) +
             sum)
          {p : num -> num | p permutes count n}
          0
    in
      !n : num. !A : num -> num -> real.
        0 < n /\
        (!i j : num.
           i < n /\ j < n
           ==>
           A i j = 1 / &(MIN (SUC i) (SUC j)))
        ==>
        determinant n A =
          (-1 : real) pow (n - 1) /
          (&(FACT (n - 1)) * &(FACT n))``;

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For positive n, 0 ..^ n is the canonical zero-based carrier for Fin n.
  Hence the entry below is 1/min(i+1,j+1): the conditional selects i+1
  exactly when i <= j, and otherwise selects j+1. SetMM's maDet over RRfld
  is the real determinant.

  Inlining this uniquely specified matrix is definitionally equivalent to
  universally quantifying a matrix under the source's entrywise defining
  hypothesis. The right side is the solution annotated in both ground-truth
  sources, (-1)^(n-1) / ((n-1)! n!). The final declaration is the single
  unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d i j n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2014-a2 $a |- A. n e. NN
    (
      (
        ( ( 0 ..^ n ) maDet RRfld )
        `
        (
          i e. ( 0 ..^ n ) , j e. ( 0 ..^ n ) |->
            (
              1
              /
              if (
                i <_ j ,
                ( i + 1 ) ,
                ( j + 1 )
              )
            )
        )
      )
      =
      (
        ( ( -u 1 ) ^ ( n - 1 ) )
        /
        (
          ( ! ` ( n - 1 ) )
          x.
          ( ! ` n )
        )
      )
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2014_a2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a2:
% the determinant of the n-by-n real matrix with (i,j)-entry 1/min(i,j),
% indexed from 1, equals (-1)^(n-1)/((n-1)! n!). This file contains no proof.

putnam_2014_a2: THEORY
BEGIN
  square_matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_min(left, right: nat): nat =
    IF left <= right THEN left ELSE right ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  nat_predecessor(index: nat): nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN 0 ELSE index - 1 ENDIF

  quotient_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      0
    ELSE
      1
        + quotient_aux(
            numerator - denominator,
            denominator,
            fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  remainder_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      numerator
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator - denominator,
        denominator,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  safe_ndiv(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    quotient_aux(
      numerator,
      denominator,
      numerator + 1)

  safe_mod(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator,
        denominator,
        numerator + 1)
    ENDIF

  function_code_count(size: nat): nat =
    IF size = 0 THEN 1 ELSE size ^ size ENDIF

  permutation_entry(code, row, size: nat): nat =
    IF size = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      safe_mod(safe_ndiv(code, size ^ row), size)
    ENDIF

  permutation_code(code, size: nat): bool =
    code < function_code_count(size)
      AND (FORALL (row_1, row_2: nat):
        (row_1 < size
          AND row_2 < size
          AND permutation_entry(code, row_1, size)
            = permutation_entry(code, row_2, size))
        IMPLIES row_1 = row_2)

  pair_row(pair, size: nat): nat =
    safe_ndiv(pair, size)

  pair_column(pair, size: nat): nat =
    safe_mod(pair, size)

  inversion_at(code, pair, size: nat): bool =
    pair_row(pair, size) < size
      AND pair_column(pair, size) < size
      AND pair_row(pair, size) < pair_column(pair, size)
      AND permutation_entry(code, pair_row(pair, size), size)
        > permutation_entry(code, pair_column(pair, size), size)

  count_true(
      property: [nat -> bool],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_true(property, count - 1)
        + IF property(count - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  inversion_count(code, size: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      (LAMBDA (pair: nat): inversion_at(code, pair, size)),
      size * size)

  permutation_sign(code, size: nat): real =
    IF mod(inversion_count(code, size), 2) = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -1
    ENDIF

  permutation_product(
      A: square_matrix,
      code, size, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      permutation_product(A, code, size, count - 1)
        * A(
            count - 1,
            permutation_entry(code, count - 1, size))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  determinant_sum(
      A: square_matrix,
      size, limit: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET code: nat = limit - 1 IN
        determinant_sum(A, size, limit - 1)
          + IF permutation_code(code, size) THEN
              permutation_sign(code, size)
                * permutation_product(A, code, size, size)
            ELSE
              0
            ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  determinant(A: square_matrix, size: nat): real =
    determinant_sum(A, size, function_code_count(size))

  has_putnam_entries(A: square_matrix, n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      (i < n AND j < n)
        IMPLIES
          A(i, j)
            = safe_div(
                1,
                nat_min(i + 1, j + 1) :: real)

  putnam_2014_a2_solution(n: nat): real =
    safe_div(
      (-1 :: real) ^ nat_predecessor(n),
      (nat_factorial(nat_predecessor(n))
        * nat_factorial(n)) :: real)

  putnam_2014_a2: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (A: square_matrix):
      (n > 0 AND has_putnam_entries(A, n))
        IMPLIES
          determinant(A, n) = putnam_2014_a2_solution(n)
END putnam_2014_a2

-- 3 / 7
/--
Let \( a_0 = \frac{5}{2} \) and \( a_k = a_{k-1}^2 - 2 \) for \( k \geq 1 \). Compute \( \prod_{k=0}^{\infty} \left(1 - \frac{1}{a_k}\right) \) in closed form.
-/
theorem putnam_2014_a3
(a : ℕ → ℝ)
(a0 : a 0 = 5 / 2)
(ak : ∀ k ≥ 1, a k = (a (k - 1)) ^ 2 - 2)
: Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ∏ k ∈ Finset.range n, (1 - 1 / a k)) atTop (𝓝 putnam_2014_a3_solution) :=
sorry

Definition putnam_2014_a3_solution := 3 / 7.
Theorem putnam_2014_a3
    (prodn := fix prod_n (m: nat -> R) (n : nat) : R :=
        match n with
        | O => 1
        | S n' => prod_n m n' * m n'
    end)
    (A := fix a (n: nat) :=
        match n with
        | O => 5 / 2
        | S n' => (a n') ^ 2 - 2
    end)
    : is_lim_seq
        (fun n : nat => prodn (fun k => 1 - 1 / A k) n)
        putnam_2014_a3_solution.
Proof. Admitted.

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a3:
;; the finite products associated with a_0 = 5/2 and
;; a_k = a_(k-1)^2 - 2 converge to 3/7. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The recurrence uniquely determines the source real sequence, and every
;; value is rational. Thus this exact recursive definition eliminates the
;; arbitrary sequence parameter without restricting the source statement.
(defun putnam-2014-a3-sequence-value (index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (zp index)
      5/2
    (let ((previous
           (putnam-2014-a3-sequence-value (- index 1))))
      (- (* previous previous) 2))))

;; Product over 0 <= k < terms, including the empty product at terms = 0.
(defun putnam-2014-a3-partial-product (terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      1
    (* (putnam-2014-a3-partial-product (- terms 1))
       (- 1
          (/ 1
             (putnam-2014-a3-sequence-value
              (- terms 1)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a3-tail-p (epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (terms)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp terms)
      (<= cutoff terms))
     (<
      (abs
       (- (putnam-2014-a3-partial-product terms)
          3/7))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a3-cutoff-exists-p (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (putnam-2014-a3-tail-p epsilon cutoff))))

;; Because all partial products and the proposed limit are rational,
;; quantifying over positive rational epsilons is equivalent to the usual
;; real epsilon definition of convergence.
(defun-sk putnam-2014-a3-converges-p ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-2014-a3-cutoff-exists-p epsilon))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2014-a3-statement ()
  (putnam-2014-a3-converges-p))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2014_a3): the finite products associated with
-- a_0 = 5/2 and a_k = a_(k-1)^2 - 2 converge to 3/7.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2014A3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc (suc zero)

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc (suc (suc (suc (suc zero))))

sevenN : Nat
sevenN =
  suc (suc fiveN)

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

productFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
productFirst reals zero factor =
  oneR reals
productFirst reals (suc n) factor =
  multiply reals
    (productFirst reals n factor)
    (factor n)

fiveHalves :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
fiveHalves reals =
  divide reals
    (fromNat reals fiveN)
    (fromNat reals twoN)

threeSevenths :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
threeSevenths reals =
  divide reals
    (fromNat reals threeN)
    (fromNat reals sevenN)

putnamFactor :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
putnamFactor reals a k =
  subtract reals
    (oneR reals)
    (divide reals (oneR reals) (a k))

putnam-2014-a3 : Set1
putnam-2014-a3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (a : Nat -> R) ->
  a zero == fiveHalves reals ->
  ((n : Nat) ->
    a (suc n) ==
    subtract reals
      (naturalPower reals (a n) twoN)
      (fromNat reals twoN)) ->
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      productFirst reals n
        (putnamFactor reals a))
    (threeSevenths reals)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a3:
  the real sequence beginning at 5/2 and satisfying a_k = a_(k-1)^2 - 2 has
  its prefix products of (1 - 1/a_k) converging to 3/7. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;
open real_topologyTheory;

val putnam_2014_a3 =
  ``!a : num -> real.
      a 0 = 5 / 2 /\
      (!k : num.
         1 <= k
         ==>
         a k = (a (k - 1)) pow 2 - 2)
      ==>
      ((\n : num.
          REAL_PROD_IMAGE
            (\k : num. 1 - 1 / a k)
            (count n)) -->
        (3 / 7))
      sequentially``;

title: putnam_2014_a3
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2014_a3: evaluation as 3/7 of the infinite product associated with
  the real recurrence a_0 = 5/2 and a_k = a_(k-1)^2 - 2. This file contains
  no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  RR ^m NN0 is set.mm's class of all real-valued sequences indexed by the
  nonnegative integers. Quantification over NN states the recurrence at
  exactly the positive indices, where k - 1 remains in NN0.

  For n in NN0, 0 ..^ n is the half-open interval from 0 through n - 1.
  Therefore the maps-to expression is precisely the sequence of finite
  products used by the Lean source, including the empty product at n = 0.
  Set.mm's ~~> relation states convergence of this real sequence to the
  explicit value 3/7 given by the published problem and the Rocq source.
  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d a k n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2014-a3 $a |-
    A. a e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
      (
        (
          ( a ` 0 ) = ( 5 / 2 )
          /\
          A. k e. NN
            ( a ` k )
            =
            ( ( ( a ` ( k - 1 ) ) ^ 2 ) - 2 )
        )
        ->
        (
          n e. NN0 |->
            prod_ k e. ( 0 ..^ n )
              ( 1 - ( 1 / ( a ` k ) ) )
        )
        ~~>
        ( 3 / 7 )
      )
  $.
$}

:: Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a3:
:: the infinite product associated with the real recurrence a(0) = 5/2 and
:: a(k) = a(k-1)^2 - 2 for k >= 1 converges to 3/7.
:: This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, FUNCT_2,

  constructors FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1, REAL_1, COMPLEX1,
    INT_1, XXREAL_0, NEWTON, NAT_1, NAT_D, SEQ_2, SEQM_3, SEQ_4,
    PREPOWER, BINOP_1, BINOP_2, COMSEQ_2, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_4,
    VALUED_1, FINSEQOP, FINSOP_1, SETWOP_2, RVSUM_1, SETWISEO;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1,

    VALUED_1, XCMPLX_0, XREAL_0, ORDINAL1, NAT_1, INT_1, NEWTON,
    PREPOWER, SEQ_4, FINSEQ_1, FINSEQ_2, FINSEQ_4, RVSUM_1;
  requirements REAL, NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE, ARITHM;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for a being Real_Sequence st
    a.0 = (5 qua Real) / 2 &
    (for k being Nat st 1 <= k holds
      a.k = (a.(k -' 1) |^ 2) - 2)
  holds
    ex p being Real_Sequence st
      (for n being Nat holds

          len factors = n &

            factors.j = 1 - 1 / a.(j -' 1)) &

      lim p = (3 qua Real) / 7
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2014_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a3:
% the infinite product associated with the real recurrence a(0) = 5/2 and
% a(k) = a(k-1)^2 - 2 converges to 3/7. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2014_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  finite_product(
      values: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      finite_product(values, count - 1) * values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(count) - value) < epsilon_value

  satisfies_recurrence(a: real_sequence): bool =
    a(0) = 5 / 2
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index >= 1 IMPLIES
          a(index) = a(index - 1) ^ 2 - 2

  partial_products(a: real_sequence): real_sequence =
    LAMBDA (count: nat):
      finite_product(
        LAMBDA (index: nat):
          1 - safe_div(1, a(index)),
        count)

  putnam_2014_a3: bool =
    FORALL (a: real_sequence):
      satisfies_recurrence(a) IMPLIES
        converges_to(partial_products(a), 3 / 7)
END putnam_2014_a3

import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Nat

noncomputable abbrev putnam_2014_a4_solution : ℝ := sorry
-- 1 / 3
/--
Suppose $X$ is a random variable that takes on only nonnegative integer values, with $E\left[X\right]=1$, $E\left[X^2\right]=2$, and $E\left[X^3\right]=5$. (Here $E\left[Y\right]$ denotes the expectation of the random variable $Y$.) Determine the smallest possible value of the probability of the event $X=0$.
-/
theorem putnam_2014_a4
(Xrandvar : (ℕ → ℝ) → Prop)
(hXrandvar : Xrandvar = (fun X : ℕ → ℝ => (∀ n : ℕ, X n ∈ Set.Icc 0 1) ∧ ∑' n : ℕ, X n = 1))
(E : (ℕ → ℝ) → (ℕ → ℝ) → ℝ)
(hE : E = (fun (X : ℕ → ℝ) (f : ℕ → ℝ) => ∑' n : ℕ, f n * X n))
: sInf {X0 : ℝ | ∃ X : ℕ → ℝ, Xrandvar X ∧ E X (fun x : ℕ => x) = 1 ∧ E X (fun x : ℕ => x ^ 2) = 2 ∧ E X (fun x : ℕ => x ^ 3) = 5 ∧ X0 = X 0} = putnam_2014_a4_solution :=
sorry

title: putnam_2014_a4
content:
Require Import Reals Coquelicot.Coquelicot.

Definition putnam_2014_a4_solution : R := 1 / 3.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2014_a4_admissible (mass : nat -> R) : Prop :=
  (forall n : nat, 0 <= mass n) /\
  is_series mass 1 /\
  is_series (fun n => INR n * mass n) 1 /\
  is_series (fun n => (INR n) ^ 2 * mass n) 2 /\
  is_series (fun n => (INR n) ^ 3 * mass n) 5.

Theorem putnam_2014_a4
    : (forall mass : nat -> R,
        putnam_2014_a4_admissible mass ->
        putnam_2014_a4_solution <= mass 0%nat) /\
      (exists mass : nat -> R,
        putnam_2014_a4_admissible mass /\
        mass 0%nat = putnam_2014_a4_solution).
Proof. Admitted.

definition putnam_2014_a4_solution :: real where

(* 1 / 3 *)
theorem putnam_2014_a4:
  fixes Xrandvar :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and E :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> real"
  defines "Xrandvar \<equiv> \<lambda>X :: nat \<Rightarrow> real.
    (\<forall>n. X n \<in> {0 .. 1}) \<and> summable X \<and> suminf X = 1"
  and "E \<equiv> \<lambda>(X :: nat \<Rightarrow> real) (f :: nat \<Rightarrow> real).
    suminf (\<lambda>n. f n * X n)"
  shows "Inf {X0 :: real. \<exists>X :: nat \<Rightarrow> real.
    Xrandvar X \<and>

    summable (\<lambda>n. (real n)^2 * X n) \<and>
    summable (\<lambda>n. (real n)^3 * X n) \<and>
    E X (\<lambda>n. real n) = 1 \<and>
    E X (\<lambda>n. (real n)^2) = 2 \<and>
    E X (\<lambda>n. (real n)^3) = 5 \<and>
    X0 = X 0} = putnam_2014_a4_solution"
  sorry

title: putnam_2014_a4
putnam_2014_a4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a4:
;; the smallest possible probability that a nonnegative integer-valued random
;; variable with first three moments 1, 2, and 5 equals zero is 1/3.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A value MASS-APPROX(INDEX, PRECISION) is a rational approximation, within
;; PRECISION, to the real probability mass at INDEX.  The regularity predicate
;; below is the standard regular-Cauchy-name presentation of a real number.
;; Thus rational approximants represent arbitrary real masses, not a
;; rational-valued or finite-support restriction.

(defstub putnam-2014-a4-arbitrary-mass-approx
  (index precision)
  t)

;; The explicit optimizer has masses 1/3, 1/2, and 1/6 at 0, 1, and 3.

(defun putnam-2014-a4-witness-mass-approx (index precision)
  (declare (ignore precision))
  (cond
   ((equal index 0) 1/3)
   ((equal index 1) 1/2)
   ((equal index 3) 1/6)
   (t 0)))

(defun putnam-2014-a4-mass-approx (distribution index precision)
  (if (equal distribution :arbitrary)
      (putnam-2014-a4-arbitrary-mass-approx index precision)
    (putnam-2014-a4-witness-mass-approx index precision)))

(defun putnam-2014-a4-positive-rational-p (value)
  (and
   (rationalp value)
   (< 0 value)))

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a4-regular-real-sequence-name-p
    (distribution)
  (forall (index epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp index)
      (putnam-2014-a4-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2014-a4-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((left
            (putnam-2014-a4-mass-approx
             distribution index epsilon))
           (right
            (putnam-2014-a4-mass-approx
             distribution index eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<= (abs (- left right))
            (+ epsilon eta)))))))

;; For a regular Cauchy name, these approximation inequalities are
;; bidirectionally equivalent to the represented real lying in [0,1].

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a4-mass-in-unit-interval-p
    (distribution index)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2014-a4-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (let ((approximation
            (putnam-2014-a4-mass-approx
             distribution index epsilon)))
       (and
        (rationalp approximation)
        (<= (- epsilon) approximation)
        (<= approximation (+ 1 epsilon)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a4-all-masses-in-unit-interval-p
    (distribution)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (natp index)
     (putnam-2014-a4-mass-in-unit-interval-p
      distribution index))))

;; This is a rational approximation to
;;   sum_{INDEX < TERMS} INDEX^EXPONENT * probability(INDEX).
;; Taking EXPONENT = 0 gives total probability.

(defun putnam-2014-a4-partial-moment-sum
    (distribution exponent terms precision)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let ((index (- (nfix terms) 1)))
      (+
       (putnam-2014-a4-partial-moment-sum
        distribution exponent index precision)
       (*
        (expt index exponent)
        (putnam-2014-a4-mass-approx
         distribution index precision))))))

;; For fixed TERMS, sufficiently precise rational approximations determine
;; the exact real finite partial sum.  Positive rational tolerances are
;; cofinal in the positive reals, so the following tail definition is
;; equivalent to convergence of the infinite moment series to TARGET.

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a4-partial-moment-close-below-p
    (distribution exponent terms target epsilon precision-bound)
  (forall (precision)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2014-a4-positive-rational-p precision)
      (<= precision precision-bound))
     (let ((partial-sum
            (putnam-2014-a4-partial-moment-sum
             distribution exponent terms precision)))
       (and
        (rationalp partial-sum)
        (< (abs (- partial-sum target))
           epsilon))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a4-partial-moment-close-p
    (distribution exponent terms target epsilon)
  (exists (precision-bound)
    (and
     (putnam-2014-a4-positive-rational-p precision-bound)
     (<= precision-bound epsilon)
     (putnam-2014-a4-partial-moment-close-below-p
      distribution exponent terms target epsilon
      precision-bound))))

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a4-moment-tail-p
    (distribution exponent target epsilon cutoff)
  (forall (terms)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp terms)
      (natp cutoff)
      (<= cutoff terms))
     (putnam-2014-a4-partial-moment-close-p
      distribution exponent terms target epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a4-moment-cutoff-exists-p
    (distribution exponent target epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (putnam-2014-a4-moment-tail-p
      distribution exponent target epsilon cutoff))))

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a4-moment-sums-to-p
    (distribution exponent target)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2014-a4-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (putnam-2014-a4-moment-cutoff-exists-p
      distribution exponent target epsilon))))

(defun putnam-2014-a4-distribution-p (distribution)
  (and
   (putnam-2014-a4-regular-real-sequence-name-p distribution)
   (putnam-2014-a4-all-masses-in-unit-interval-p distribution)
   (putnam-2014-a4-moment-sums-to-p distribution 0 1)
   (putnam-2014-a4-moment-sums-to-p distribution 1 1)
   (putnam-2014-a4-moment-sums-to-p distribution 2 2)
   (putnam-2014-a4-moment-sums-to-p distribution 3 5)))

;; These predicates are the exact real comparisons encoded through a regular
;; Cauchy name.

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a4-mass-at-least-rational-p
    (distribution index lower-bound)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2014-a4-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (<= (- lower-bound epsilon)
         (putnam-2014-a4-mass-approx
          distribution index epsilon)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2014-a4-mass-equals-rational-p
    (distribution index target)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2014-a4-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (<=
      (abs
       (-
        (putnam-2014-a4-mass-approx
         distribution index epsilon)
        target))
      epsilon))))

;; The DEFSTUB sequence is arbitrary, so the implication is the universal
;; lower bound over every admissible probability mass function.  The second
;; conjunct supplies attainability by the explicit distribution above.

(defun putnambench-putnam-2014-a4-statement ()
  (and
   (implies
    (putnam-2014-a4-distribution-p :arbitrary)
    (putnam-2014-a4-mass-at-least-rational-p
     :arbitrary 0 1/3))
   (putnam-2014-a4-distribution-p :witness)
   (putnam-2014-a4-mass-equals-rational-p
    :witness 0 1/3)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2014_a4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2014_a4): the smallest possible probability
-- at zero for a nonnegative-integer-valued random variable whose first three
-- moments are 1, 2, and 5 is 1 / 3. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2014A4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  twoN + threeN

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SequentialLimit {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms total =
  SequentialLimit reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    total

module Putnam2014A4Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  ProbabilityMassFunction :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  ProbabilityMassFunction p =
    ((n : Nat) ->
      lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (p n)
      and
      lessOrEqual reals (p n) (oneR reals))
    and
    SeriesHasSum reals p (oneR reals)

  MomentHasValue :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    R ->
    Set
  MomentHasValue p exponent value =
    SeriesHasSum reals
      (\ n ->
        multiply reals
          (naturalPower reals (fromNat reals n) exponent)
          (p n))
      value

  HasPrescribedMoments :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  HasPrescribedMoments p =
    MomentHasValue p oneN (oneR reals)
    and
    MomentHasValue p twoN (fromNat reals twoN)
    and
    MomentHasValue p threeN (fromNat reals fiveN)

  oneThird : R
  oneThird =
    divide reals
      (oneR reals)
      (fromNat reals threeN)

  IsSmallestPossibleMassAtZero :
    R ->
    Set
  IsSmallestPossibleMassAtZero candidate =
    ((p : Nat -> R) ->
      ProbabilityMassFunction p ->
      HasPrescribedMoments p ->
      lessOrEqual reals candidate (p zero))
    and
    Exists (Nat -> R)
      (\ p ->
        ProbabilityMassFunction p
        and
        HasPrescribedMoments p
        and
        p zero == candidate)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    IsSmallestPossibleMassAtZero oneThird

putnam-2014-a4 : Set1
putnam-2014-a4 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2014A4Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a4:
  the smallest possible probability of zero for a nonnegative integer-valued
  random variable with first three moments 1, 2, and 5 is 1/3. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory realTheory seqTheory;

val putnam_2014_a4 =
  ``let admissible =
      \p : num -> real.
        (!n : num. 0 <= p n /\ p n <= 1) /\
        summable p /\
        suminf p = 1 /\
        summable (\n : num. (&n : real) * p n) /\
        suminf (\n : num. (&n : real) * p n) = 1 /\
        summable (\n : num. (&n : real) pow 2 * p n) /\
        suminf (\n : num. (&n : real) pow 2 * p n) = 2 /\
        summable (\n : num. (&n : real) pow 3 * p n) /\
        suminf (\n : num. (&n : real) pow 3 * p n) = 5
    in
    let solution = (1 / 3 : real)
    in
      (!p : num -> real.
         admissible p
         ==>
         solution <= p 0) /\
      (?p : num -> real.
         admissible p /\
         p 0 = solution)``;

title: putnam_2014_a4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a4:
% the smallest possible mass at zero for a probability distribution on the
% nonnegative integers with first three moments 1, 2, and 5 is 1/3.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2014_a4: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  partial_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  series_sums_to(
      values: real_sequence,
      total: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(partial_sum(values, count) - total)
              < epsilon_value

  probability_distribution(p: real_sequence): bool =
    (FORALL (n: nat): 0 <= p(n) AND p(n) <= 1)
      AND series_sums_to(p, 1)

  prescribed_moments(p: real_sequence): bool =
    series_sums_to(
      LAMBDA (n: nat): (n :: real) * p(n),
      1)
      AND series_sums_to(
        LAMBDA (n: nat): (n :: real) ^ 2 * p(n),
        2)
      AND series_sums_to(
        LAMBDA (n: nat): (n :: real) ^ 3 * p(n),
        5)

  putnam_2014_a4_solution: real = 1 / 3

  putnam_2014_a4: bool =
    (FORALL (p: real_sequence):
      (probability_distribution(p)
        AND prescribed_moments(p))
      IMPLIES putnam_2014_a4_solution <= p(0))
      AND
        (EXISTS (p: real_sequence):
          probability_distribution(p)
            AND prescribed_moments(p)
            AND p(0) = putnam_2014_a4_solution)
END putnam_2014_a4

title: putnam_2014_a5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a5:
;; the polynomials P_n(x) = 1 + 2*x + ... + n*x^(n-1) are relatively prime
;; for all distinct positive indices. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The source hypotheses determine P_n extensionally, so the canonical
;; ascending coefficient list (1,2,...,n) below preserves that quantification.
;; Its coefficients are rational. For rational polynomials, coprimality over
;; Q, R, any real closed field, and C is equivalent: a rational Bezout
;; identity remains one after scalar extension, while a nonconstant common
;; divisor over Q remains common in every extension. Thus equality of the
;; exact monic rational gcd with 1 is bidirectionally equivalent to each
;; source formulation, including the existential real-polynomial identity.

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (let ((tail
             (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize
              (cdr polynomial))))
        (if (and (equal (car polynomial) 0)
                 (not (consp tail)))
            nil
          (cons (car polynomial) tail)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-add (left right)
  (cond
   ((consp left)
    (if (consp right)
        (cons (+ (car left) (car right))
              (putnam-2014-a5-poly-add
               (cdr left) (cdr right)))
      left))
   (t right)))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-scale (scalar polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons (* scalar (car polynomial))
            (putnam-2014-a5-poly-scale
             scalar (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-negate (polynomial)
  (putnam-2014-a5-poly-scale -1 polynomial))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-subtract (left right)
  (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize
   (putnam-2014-a5-poly-add
    left
    (putnam-2014-a5-poly-negate right))))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-zero-list (count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons 0
          (putnam-2014-a5-zero-list (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-monomial (coefficient degree)
  (if (equal coefficient 0)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-2014-a5-zero-list degree)
     (list coefficient))))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-degree (polynomial)
  (let ((normalized
         (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize polynomial)))
    (if (consp normalized)
        (- (len normalized) 1)
      0)))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-leading-coefficient (polynomial)
  (let ((normalized
         (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize polynomial)))
    (if (consp normalized)
        (nth (putnam-2014-a5-poly-degree normalized)
             normalized)
      0)))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-divmod-steps
    (remainder divisor quotient steps)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix steps)))
  (if (zp steps)
      (cons
       (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize quotient)
       (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize remainder))
    (let* ((normalized-remainder
            (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize remainder))
           (normalized-divisor
            (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize divisor)))
      (if (or (not (consp normalized-remainder))
              (not (consp normalized-divisor))
              (< (putnam-2014-a5-poly-degree
                  normalized-remainder)
                 (putnam-2014-a5-poly-degree
                  normalized-divisor)))
          (cons
           (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize quotient)
           normalized-remainder)
        (let* ((degree-difference
                (- (putnam-2014-a5-poly-degree
                    normalized-remainder)
                   (putnam-2014-a5-poly-degree
                    normalized-divisor)))
               (coefficient
                (/ (putnam-2014-a5-poly-leading-coefficient
                    normalized-remainder)
                   (putnam-2014-a5-poly-leading-coefficient
                    normalized-divisor)))
               (term
                (putnam-2014-a5-poly-monomial
                 coefficient degree-difference)))
          (putnam-2014-a5-poly-divmod-steps
           (putnam-2014-a5-poly-subtract
            normalized-remainder
            (putnam-2014-a5-poly-scale
             coefficient
             (append
              (putnam-2014-a5-zero-list degree-difference)
              normalized-divisor)))
           normalized-divisor
           (putnam-2014-a5-poly-add quotient term)
           (- steps 1)))))))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-divmod (dividend divisor)
  (putnam-2014-a5-poly-divmod-steps
   dividend
   divisor
   nil
   (+ 1
      (len (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize dividend)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-remainder (dividend divisor)
  (cdr (putnam-2014-a5-poly-divmod dividend divisor)))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-gcd-steps (left right steps)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix steps)))
  (let ((normalized-left
         (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize left))
        (normalized-right
         (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize right)))
    (if (or (zp steps)
            (not (consp normalized-right)))
        normalized-left
      (putnam-2014-a5-poly-gcd-steps
       normalized-right
       (putnam-2014-a5-poly-remainder
        normalized-left normalized-right)
       (- steps 1)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-gcd (left right)
  (putnam-2014-a5-poly-gcd-steps
   left
   right
   (+ 2
      (len (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize left))
      (len (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize right)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-poly-monic (polynomial)
  (let* ((normalized
          (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize polynomial))
         (leading-coefficient
          (putnam-2014-a5-poly-leading-coefficient normalized)))
    (if (consp normalized)
        (putnam-2014-a5-poly-normalize
         (putnam-2014-a5-poly-scale
          (/ 1 leading-coefficient)
          normalized))
      nil)))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-polynomial-from (coefficient count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons coefficient
          (putnam-2014-a5-polynomial-from
           (+ coefficient 1)
           (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a5-polynomial (n)
  (putnam-2014-a5-polynomial-from 1 n))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2014-a5-statement (j k)
  (implies
   (and (natp j)
        (natp k)
        (< 0 j)
        (< 0 k)
        (not (equal j k)))
   (equal
    (putnam-2014-a5-poly-monic
     (putnam-2014-a5-poly-gcd
      (putnam-2014-a5-polynomial j)
      (putnam-2014-a5-polynomial k)))
    (list 1))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a5:
-- the polynomials P_n(x) = 1 + 2x + ... + n*x^(n-1) are relatively prime
-- for distinct positive indices. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2014A5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

Polynomial : Set -> Set
Polynomial R =
  List R

coefficient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Nat ->
  R
coefficient reals [] n =
  zeroR reals
coefficient reals (c ∷ coefficients) zero =
  c
coefficient reals (c ∷ coefficients) (suc n) =
  coefficient reals coefficients n

PolynomialEqual :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Set
PolynomialEqual reals p q =
  (n : Nat) ->
  coefficient reals p n == coefficient reals q n

addPolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R
addPolynomial reals [] q =
  q
addPolynomial reals p [] =
  p
addPolynomial reals (a ∷ p) (b ∷ q) =
  add reals a b ∷ addPolynomial reals p q

scalePolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R
scalePolynomial reals scalar [] =
  []
scalePolynomial reals scalar (c ∷ coefficients) =
  multiply reals scalar c ∷
  scalePolynomial reals scalar coefficients

shiftPolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R
shiftPolynomial reals p =
  zeroR reals ∷ p

multiplyPolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R
multiplyPolynomial reals [] q =
  []
multiplyPolynomial reals (a ∷ p) q =
  addPolynomial reals
    (scalePolynomial reals a q)
    (shiftPolynomial reals
      (multiplyPolynomial reals p q))

snoc :
  {A : Set} ->
  List A ->
  A ->
  List A
snoc [] x =
  x ∷ []
snoc (x ∷ xs) y =
  x ∷ snoc xs y

putnamPolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  Polynomial R
putnamPolynomial reals zero =
  []
putnamPolynomial reals (suc n) =
  snoc
    (putnamPolynomial reals n)
    (fromNat reals (suc n))

onePolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R
onePolynomial reals =
  oneR reals ∷ []

RelativelyPrime :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Set
RelativelyPrime {R} reals p q =
  Exists (Polynomial R)
    (\ a ->
      Exists (Polynomial R)
        (\ b ->
          PolynomialEqual reals
            (addPolynomial reals
              (multiplyPolynomial reals a p)
              (multiplyPolynomial reals b q))
            (onePolynomial reals)))

putnam-2014-a5 : Set1
putnam-2014-a5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (j k : Nat) ->
  Positive j ->
  Positive k ->
  j != k ->
  RelativelyPrime reals
    (putnamPolynomial reals j)
    (putnamPolynomial reals k)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a5:
  the polynomials with coefficients 1 through n are relatively prime for
  distinct positive indices. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory realTheory polyTheory;

val putnam_2014_a5 =
  ``let P =
      \n : num.
        GENLIST (\i : num. &(i + 1) : real) n
    in
      !j k : num.
        0 < j /\ 0 < k /\ j <> k
        ==>
        ?a b : real list.
          !x : real.
            poly a x * poly (P j) x +
            poly b x * poly (P k) x =
            1``;

title: putnam_2014_a5
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2014_a5: the polynomials
  P_n(X) = 1 + 2 X + ... + n X^(n-1) are relatively prime for all
  distinct positive integers j and k. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P14A5Poly is set.mm's ring carrier of arbitrary finite-support
  complex-coefficient univariate polynomials. P14A5P maps each n in NN0 to
  the finite polynomial-ring sum from i = 1 through n of i times X^(i-1),
  exactly the polynomial family in the source.

  Coprimality is expressed by the equivalent Bezout identity in CC[X]:
  there are polynomials a and b such that a P_j + b P_k = 1. Both witnesses
  remain existentially quantified inside the conclusion. The final
  declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c P14A5Poly P14A5P $.

p14a5-poly-syntax $a class P14A5Poly $.
p14a5-p-syntax $a class P14A5P $.

p14a5-poly-definition $a |- P14A5Poly =
  ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` CCfld ) ) $.

${
  $d i n $.

  p14a5-p-definition $a |- P14A5P =
    (
      n e. NN0 |->
        (
          ( Poly1 ` CCfld )
          gsum
          (
            i e. ( 1 ... n ) |->
              (
                ( ( algSc ` ( Poly1 ` CCfld ) ) ` i )
                ( .r ` ( Poly1 ` CCfld ) )
                (
                  ( i - 1 )
                  ( .g ` ( mulGrp ` ( Poly1 ` CCfld ) ) )
                  ( var1 ` CCfld )
                )
              )
          )
        )
    ) $.
$}

${
  $d a b j k $.

  putnambench-putnam-2014-a5 $a |-
    A. j e. NN
      A. k e. NN
        (
          j =/= k
          ->
          E. a e. P14A5Poly
            E. b e. P14A5Poly
              (
                (
                  a
                  ( .r ` ( Poly1 ` CCfld ) )
                  ( P14A5P ` j )
                )
                ( +g ` ( Poly1 ` CCfld ) )
                (
                  b
                  ( .r ` ( Poly1 ` CCfld ) )
                  ( P14A5P ` k )
                )
              )
              =
              ( 1r ` ( Poly1 ` CCfld ) )
        )
  $.
$}
