title: putnam_2014_a5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a5:
% the polynomials P_n(x) = 1 + 2*x + ... + n*x^(n-1) are relatively prime
% for every pair of distinct positive indices. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2014_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  complex: TYPE = [# real_part: real, imag_part: real #]
  polynomial: TYPE = list[complex]

  complex_zero: complex =
    (# real_part := 0, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_one: complex =
    (# real_part := 1, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_of_nat(value: nat): complex =
    (# real_part := value :: real, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_add(left, right: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := real_part(left) + real_part(right),
       imag_part := imag_part(left) + imag_part(right) #)

  complex_mul(left, right: complex): complex =
    (# real_part :=
         real_part(left) * real_part(right)
           - imag_part(left) * imag_part(right),
       imag_part :=
         real_part(left) * imag_part(right)
           + imag_part(left) * real_part(right) #)

  polynomial_coefficient(
      p: polynomial,
      degree: nat): RECURSIVE complex =
    CASES p OF
      null: complex_zero,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        IF degree = 0 THEN
          coefficient
        ELSE
          polynomial_coefficient(tail, degree - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE p BY <<

  polynomial_equal(left, right: polynomial): bool =
    FORALL (degree: nat):
      polynomial_coefficient(left, degree)
        = polynomial_coefficient(right, degree)

  polynomial_add(
      left, right: polynomial): RECURSIVE polynomial =
    CASES left OF
      null: right,
      cons(left_coefficient, left_tail):
        CASES right OF
          null: left,
          cons(right_coefficient, right_tail):
            cons(
              complex_add(left_coefficient, right_coefficient),
              polynomial_add(left_tail, right_tail))
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE left BY <<

  polynomial_scale(
      scalar: complex,
      p: polynomial): RECURSIVE polynomial =
    CASES p OF
      null: null,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        cons(
          complex_mul(scalar, coefficient),
          polynomial_scale(scalar, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE p BY <<

  polynomial_multiply(
      left, right: polynomial): RECURSIVE polynomial =
    CASES left OF
      null: null,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        polynomial_add(
          polynomial_scale(coefficient, right),
          cons(
            complex_zero,
            polynomial_multiply(tail, right)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE left BY <<

  coefficient_segment(
      first, count: nat): RECURSIVE polynomial =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      cons(
        complex_of_nat(first),
        coefficient_segment(first + 1, count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  P(n: nat): polynomial =
    coefficient_segment(1, n)

  polynomial_one: polynomial =
    cons(complex_one, null)

  relatively_prime(left, right: polynomial): bool =
    EXISTS (a, b: polynomial):
      polynomial_equal(
        polynomial_add(
          polynomial_multiply(a, left),
          polynomial_multiply(b, right)),
        polynomial_one)

  putnam_2014_a5: bool =
    FORALL (j, k: nat):
      (j > 0 AND k > 0 AND j /= k)
        IMPLIES relatively_prime(P(j), P(k))
END putnam_2014_a5

title: putnam_2014_a6
content:
import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Nat

abbrev putnam_2014_a6_solution : ℕ → ℕ := sorry
-- (fun n : ℕ => n ^ n)
/--
Let \( n \) be a positive integer. What is the largest \( k \) for which there exist \( n \times n \) matrices \( M_1, \ldots, M_k \) and \( N_1, \ldots, N_k \) with real entries such that for all \( i \) and \( j \), the matrix product \( M_i N_j \) has a zero entry somewhere on its diagonal if and only if \( i \neq j \)?
-/
theorem putnam_2014_a6
(n : ℕ)
(kex : ℕ → Prop)
(npos : n > 0)
(hkex : ∀ k ≥ 1, kex k = ∃ M N : Fin k → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ, ∀ i j : Fin k, ((∃ p : Fin n, (M i * N j) p p = 0) ↔ i ≠ j))
: (putnam_2014_a6_solution n ≥ 1 ∧ kex (putnam_2014_a6_solution n)) ∧ (∀ k ≥ 1, kex k → k ≤ putnam_2014_a6_solution n) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2014_a6
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a6:
   the largest size of two indexed families of real square matrices whose
   cross-products have a zero diagonal entry exactly off the matching index
   is n^n. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Vectors.Fin Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2014_a6_matrix (n : nat) : Type :=
  Fin.t n -> Fin.t n -> R.

Fixpoint putnam_2014_a6_fin_sum
    (n : nat) : (Fin.t n -> R) -> R :=
  match n as m return (Fin.t m -> R) -> R with
  | O => fun _ => 0
  | S m =>
      fun f =>
        f Fin.F1 +
        putnam_2014_a6_fin_sum m (fun i => f (Fin.FS i))
  end.

Definition putnam_2014_a6_matrix_mul
    {n : nat}
    (A B : putnam_2014_a6_matrix n) :
    putnam_2014_a6_matrix n :=
  fun i j =>
    putnam_2014_a6_fin_sum n (fun p => A i p * B p j).

Definition putnam_2014_a6_solution (n : nat) : nat :=
  Nat.pow n n.

Theorem putnam_2014_a6
    (n : nat)
    (kex : nat -> Prop)
    (npos : (0 < n)%nat)
    (hkex :
      forall k : nat,
        (1 <= k)%nat ->
        (kex k <->
          exists M N : Fin.t k -> putnam_2014_a6_matrix n,
            forall i j : Fin.t k,
              ((exists p : Fin.t n,
                  putnam_2014_a6_matrix_mul (M i) (N j) p p = 0)
               <-> i <> j))) :
  ((1 <= putnam_2014_a6_solution n)%nat /\
    kex (putnam_2014_a6_solution n)) /\
  (forall k : nat,
    (1 <= k)%nat ->
    kex k ->
    (k <= putnam_2014_a6_solution n)%nat).
Admitted.

theory putnam_2014_a6 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Finite_Cartesian_Product"
begin

(* uses (nat \<Rightarrow> real^'n^'n) instead of (Fin k \<Rightarrow> real^'n^'n) *)
definition putnam_2014_a6_solution :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where "putnam_2014_a6_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* (\<lambda>n::nat. n^n) *)
theorem putnam_2014_a6:
  fixes n :: nat
  and kex :: "nat \<Rightarrow> bool"
  assumes npos: "n > 0"
  and pncard: "CARD('n) = n"
  and hkex: "\<forall>k::nat\<ge>1. kex k = (\<exists>M N::nat\<Rightarrow>real^'n^'n. \<forall>i::nat\<in>{0..(k-1)}. \<forall>j::nat\<in>{0..(k-1)}. ((\<exists>p::'n. (M i ** N j)$p$p = 0) \<longleftrightarrow> i \<noteq> j))"
  shows "(GREATEST k::nat. k \<ge> 1 \<and> kex k) = putnam_2014_a6_solution n"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_2014_a6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a6:
  the largest size of two families of real square matrices whose cross-products
  have a zero diagonal entry exactly for unequal family indices. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let matrix_mul =
     \(A:real^N^N) (B:real^N^N).
       (lambda i j.
          sum (1..dimindex(:N)) (\p. A$i$p * B$p$j)):real^N^N in
   let admissible =
     \k:num.
       ?M:num->real^N^N.
         ?N:num->real^N^N.
         !i:num. !j:num.
           i < k /\ j < k
           ==>
           ((?p:num.
               1 <= p /\ p <= dimindex(:N) /\
               (matrix_mul (M i) (N j))$p$p = &0) <=>
            ~(i = j)) in
   !n:num.
     0 < n /\ dimindex(:N) = n
     ==>
     1 <= n EXP n /\
     admissible (n EXP n) /\
     (!k:num. 1 <= k /\ admissible k ==> k <= n EXP n)`;;

title: putnam_2014_a6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a6:
;; the largest size of two real n-by-n matrix families whose cross-products
;; have a zero diagonal entry exactly off the matching pairs is n^n. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The entries are interpreted in an arbitrary real closed ordered field.
;; Real closed fields are elementarily equivalent, so each fixed finite
;; matrix-existence assertion below holds in this presentation exactly when
;; it holds over the real numbers. Matrix families are flat finite lists only
;; as a representation of their finite index types, not as a restriction on
;; their entries. Negated FN-EQUAL supplies the internal existential
;; quantifier over the complete pair of matrix families.

(defun putnam-2014-a6-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2014-a6-quoted function)
   (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2014-a6-quoted function)
   (list 'cons left (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-and-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2014-a6-quoted t)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2014-a6-and-term (cdr terms))
     (putnam-2014-a6-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-or-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2014-a6-quoted nil)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2014-a6-quoted t)
     (putnam-2014-a6-or-term (cdr terms)))))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-not-term (term)
  (list
   'if
   term
   (putnam-2014-a6-quoted nil)
   (putnam-2014-a6-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-implies-term (antecedent consequent)
  (list
   'if
   antecedent
   consequent
   (putnam-2014-a6-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-true-function (formals)
  (list
   'lambda
   formals
   (putnam-2014-a6-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-2014-a6-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-operation-term (operation left right)
  (putnam-2014-a6-apply2-term operation left right))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-all-coefficients-function (carrier)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)
   (putnam-2014-a6-carrier-term carrier 'loop$-ivars)))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-all-coefficients-term
    (carrier coefficients)
  (list
   'always$+
   (putnam-2014-a6-quoted
    (putnam-2014-a6-all-coefficients-function carrier))
   (putnam-2014-a6-quoted nil)
   coefficients))

(defun putnam-2014-a6-polynomial-term
    (carrier zero coefficients)
  (putnam-2014-a6-and-term

title: putnam_2014_a6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2014_a6): the largest number of pairs of real
-- square matrices whose cross-products have a zero diagonal entry exactly
-- off the matching indices is n raised to the nth power. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2014A6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_
infix 1 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  oneN <=N n

power : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
power base zero =
  oneN
power base (suc exponent) =
  base * power base exponent

Matrix : Set -> Nat -> Set
Matrix R n =
  Fin n -> Fin n -> R

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} term =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} term =
  add reals
    (term fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

matrixProduct :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Matrix R n
matrixProduct reals M N i j =
  sumFin reals
    (\ p ->
      multiply reals
        (M i p)
        (N p j))

HasZeroDiagonalEntry :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix R n ->
  Set
HasZeroDiagonalEntry {R} reals {n} A =
  Exists (Fin n)
    (\ p ->
      A p p == zeroR reals)

Admissible :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Set
Admissible {R} reals n k =
  Exists (Fin k -> Matrix R n)
    (\ M ->
      Exists (Fin k -> Matrix R n)
        (\ N ->
          (i j : Fin k) ->
          HasZeroDiagonalEntry reals
            (matrixProduct reals (M i) (N j))
          iff
          i != j))

IsLargestAdmissible :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Set
IsLargestAdmissible reals n maximum =
  Positive maximum
  and
  Admissible reals n maximum
  and
  ((k : Nat) ->
    Positive k ->
    Admissible reals n k ->
    k <=N maximum)

putnam-2014-a6 : Set1
putnam-2014-a6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  IsLargestAdmissible reals n (power n n)

title: putnam_2014_a6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a6:
  for positive n, the largest size of two indexed families of real n by n
  matrices whose products have a diagonal zero exactly for distinct family
  indices is n^n. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;

val putnam_2014_a6 =
  ``let admissible =
      \n k : num.
        ?M N : num -> num -> num -> real.
          !i j : num.
            i < k /\ j < k
            ==>
            ((?p : num.
                p < n /\
                SIGMA
                  (\r : num. M i p r * N j r p)
                  (count n) =
                0) <=>
             i <> j)
    in
      !n : num.
        0 < n
        ==>
        (1 <= n EXP n /\ admissible n (n EXP n)) /\
        (!k : num.
           1 <= k /\ admissible n k
           ==>
           k <= n EXP n)``;

  putnam_2014_a6: the largest size of two indexed families of real square
  matrices whose cross-products have a zero diagonal entry exactly for
  distinct indices is n^n. This file contains no proof.

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For positive n and k, P14A6Feasible n k says that there are two k-term
  families of real n-by-n matrices such that, for every pair of family
  indices i and j, the product M_i N_j has some zero diagonal entry if and
  only if i and j are distinct.

  The carriers 0 ..^ n and 0 ..^ k are the canonical n-element and k-element
  finite ordinals. Base ` ((0 ..^ n) Mat RRfld) is the full real n-by-n
  matrix carrier, and its ring multiplication is ordinary matrix
  multiplication. Thus the existential matrix families and the diagonal
  witness remain quantified exactly as in the source.

  source largest-value formulation after expanding kex and the stated

  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c P14A6Feasible $.

p14a6-feasible-syntax $a wff ( P14A6Feasible n k ) $.

${
  $d M N i j k n p $.

  p14a6-feasible-definition $a |- (
    ( P14A6Feasible n k )
    <->
    E. M e.
      (
        ( Base ` ( ( 0 ..^ n ) Mat RRfld ) )
        ^m
        ( 0 ..^ k )
      )
      E. N e.
        (
          ( Base ` ( ( 0 ..^ n ) Mat RRfld ) )
          ^m
          ( 0 ..^ k )
        )
        A. i e. ( 0 ..^ k )
          A. j e. ( 0 ..^ k )
            (
              E. p e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                (
                  (
                    (
                      ( M ` i )
                      ( .r ` ( ( 0 ..^ n ) Mat RRfld ) )
                      ( N ` j )
                    )
                    `
                    <. p , p >.
                  )
                  =
                  0
                )
              <->
              i =/= j
            )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d k n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2014-a6 $a |- A. n e. NN
    (
      ( P14A6Feasible n ( n ^ n ) )
      /\
      A. k e. NN
        (
          ( P14A6Feasible n k )
          ->
          k <_ ( n ^ n )
        )
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2014_a6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_a6:
% for positive n, the largest number of paired families of real n-by-n
% matrices with the specified diagonal-zero product pattern is n^n.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2014_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> real]
  matrix_family: TYPE = [nat -> matrix]

  matrix_product_entry(
      left, right: matrix,
      row, column, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      matrix_product_entry(
        left, right, row, column, count - 1)
        + left(row, count - 1) * right(count - 1, column)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_diagonal_zero_pattern(
      n, k: nat,
      M, N: matrix_family): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      (i < k AND j < k)
        IMPLIES
          ((EXISTS (p: nat):
              p < n
                AND matrix_product_entry(
                  M(i), N(j), p, p, n) = 0)
            IFF i /= j)

  admissible_size(n, k: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (M, N: matrix_family):
      has_diagonal_zero_pattern(n, k, M, N)

  putnam_2014_a6_solution(n: nat): nat =
    n ^ n

  putnam_2014_a6: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n > 0 IMPLIES
        (putnam_2014_a6_solution(n) >= 1
          AND admissible_size(
            n, putnam_2014_a6_solution(n)))
        AND (FORALL (k: nat):
          k >= 1 AND admissible_size(n, k)
            IMPLIES k <= putnam_2014_a6_solution(n))
END putnam_2014_a6

title: putnam_2014_b1
content:
import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Nat

abbrev putnam_2014_b1_solution : Set ℕ := sorry
-- {n : ℕ | n > 0 ∧ ¬∃ a ∈ digits 10 n, a = 0}
/--
A \emph{base $10$ over-expansion} of a positive integer $N$ is an expression of the form
\[
N = d_k 10^k + d_{k-1} 10^{k-1} + \cdots + d_0 10^0
\]
with $d_k \neq 0$ and $d_i \in \{0,1,2,\dots,10\}$ for all $i$. For instance, the integer $N = 10$ has two base $10$ over-expansions: $10 = 10 \cdot 10^0$ and the usual base $10$ expansion $10 = 1 \cdot 10^1 + 0 \cdot 10^0$. Which positive integers have a unique base $10$ over-expansion?
-/
theorem putnam_2014_b1
(overexpansion : ℕ → List ℕ → Prop)
(hoverexpansion : overexpansion = fun N d ↦ N = ∑ i : Fin d.length, (d.get i) * 10 ^ i.1 ∧ d.getLastI ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ a ∈ d, a ∈ Finset.range 11)
(S : Set ℕ)
(hS : ∀ N : ℕ, N ∈ S ↔ N > 0 ∧ ∃! d : List ℕ, overexpansion N d)
: (S = putnam_2014_b1_solution) :=
sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b1:
   positive integers with a unique base-10 over-expansion are exactly those
   whose ordinary decimal expansion contains no zero digit; this file contains
   no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List Ensembles.

Fixpoint putnam_2014_b1_value (digits : list nat) : nat :=
  match digits with
  | nil => 0
  | digit :: remaining =>
      digit + 10 * putnam_2014_b1_value remaining
  end.

Definition putnam_2014_b1_overexpansion
    (N : nat) (digits : list nat) : Prop :=
  putnam_2014_b1_value digits = N /\
  last digits 0 <> 0 /\
  Forall (fun digit : nat => (digit <= 10)%nat) digits.

Definition putnam_2014_b1_solution : Ensemble nat :=
  fun N : nat =>
    (0 < N)%nat /\
    forall k : nat,
      (0 < Nat.div N (Nat.pow 10 k))%nat ->
      Nat.modulo (Nat.div N (Nat.pow 10 k)) 10 <> 0.

Theorem putnam_2014_b1
    (S : Ensemble nat)
    (hS :
      forall N : nat,
        In nat S N <->
        (0 < N)%nat /\
        exists digits : list nat,
          putnam_2014_b1_overexpansion N digits /\
          forall other : list nat,
            putnam_2014_b1_overexpansion N other ->
            other = digits) :
  S = putnam_2014_b1_solution.
Admitted.

definition putnam_2014_b1_solution :: "nat set" where
  "putnam_2014_b1_solution \<equiv>
    {N. N > 0 \<and> (\<forall>i. N div 10^i > 0 \<longrightarrow> (N div 10^i) mod 10 \<noteq> 0)}"
(* {n::nat. n > 0 \<and> (\<forall>d::nat. (\<lfloor>n / 10^d\<rfloor> > 0) \<longrightarrow> (\<lfloor>n / 10^d\<rfloor> mod 10 \<noteq> 0))} *)
theorem putnam_2014_b1:

  and S :: "nat set"
  defines "overexpansion \<equiv> (\<lambda>(N :: nat) (d :: nat list).
    d \<noteq> [] \<and>
    N = (\<Sum>i<length d. (d ! i) * 10^i) \<and>
    last d \<noteq> 0 \<and>
    (\<forall>i<length d. d ! i \<le> 10))"
  assumes hS: "\<forall>N::nat. (N \<in> S \<longleftrightarrow> (N > 0 \<and> (\<exists>!d::nat list. overexpansion N d)))"
  shows "S = putnam_2014_b1_solution"

end

title: putnam_2014_b1
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b1:
;; the positive integers with a unique base-10 over-expansion using digits
;; from 0 through 10 are exactly those whose ordinary decimal expansion has
;; no zero digit. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Write an over-expansion least-significant digit first. A valid expansion of
;; positive N is either the one-term list (N), possible exactly for N<=10, or
;; D followed by a valid expansion of M>0, where N=D+10*M and 0<=D<=10.
;; If R=N mod 10 and Q=floor(N/10), the latter case has D=R and M=Q, plus
;; the disjoint alternative D=10 and M=Q-1 exactly when R=0 and Q>1.
;; Consequently this recursion counts every source digit list exactly once.
;; The fuel N+1 exceeds the depth of every recursive quotient branch, so it
;; only supplies an ACL2 termination measure and does not bound the domain.

(defun putnam-2014-b1-overexpansion-count-aux (fuel n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (or (zp fuel)
          (not (natp n))
          (zp n))
      0
    (let* ((quotient (floor n 10))
           (remainder (mod n 10))
           (one-term-count
            (if (<= n 10) 1 0))
           (ordinary-low-digit-count
            (if (< 0 quotient)
                (putnam-2014-b1-overexpansion-count-aux
                 (- fuel 1) quotient)
              0))
           (digit-ten-count
            (if (and (equal remainder 0)
                     (< 1 quotient))
                (putnam-2014-b1-overexpansion-count-aux
                 (- fuel 1) (- quotient 1))
              0)))
      (+ one-term-count
         ordinary-low-digit-count
         digit-ten-count))))

(defun putnam-2014-b1-overexpansion-count (n)
  (if (natp n)
      (putnam-2014-b1-overexpansion-count-aux
       (+ n 1) n)
    0))

(defun putnam-2014-b1-no-zero-decimal-digits-aux (fuel n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (if (or (zp fuel)
          (zp n))
      t
    (and
     (not (equal (mod n 10) 0))
     (putnam-2014-b1-no-zero-decimal-digits-aux
      (- fuel 1) (floor n 10)))))

(defun putnam-2014-b1-no-zero-decimal-digits-p (n)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (< 0 n)
   (putnam-2014-b1-no-zero-decimal-digits-aux
    (+ n 1) n)))

;; The source hypothesis defines S pointwise as the positive naturals having
;; exactly one over-expansion, while the annotated solution defines membership
;; as positivity with no zero decimal digit. Universal closure over N makes
;; this Boolean equivalence exactly their extensional set equality.

(defun putnambench-putnam-2014-b1-statement (n)
  (implies
   (natp n)
   (equal
    (and
     (< 0 n)
     (equal
      (putnam-2014-b1-overexpansion-count n)
      1))
    (putnam-2014-b1-no-zero-decimal-digits-p n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2014_b1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2014_b1): positive integers with a unique
-- base-10 over-expansion are exactly those whose ordinary decimal expansion
-- has no zero digit. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_
infix 2 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

record Top : Set where
  constructor truth

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record ExistsUnique (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  field
    unique-value    : A
    unique-property : P unique-value
    uniqueness      : (other : A) -> P other -> other == unique-value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  zero <N n

All : {A : Set} -> (A -> Set) -> List A -> Set
All P [] =
  Top
All P (x ∷ xs) =
  P x and All P xs

LeadingNonzero : List Nat -> Set
LeadingNonzero [] =
  Bottom
LeadingNonzero (digit ∷ []) =
  digit != zero
LeadingNonzero (digit ∷ next ∷ rest) =
  LeadingNonzero (next ∷ rest)

decimalValue : List Nat -> Nat
decimalValue [] =
  zero
decimalValue (digit ∷ rest) =
  digit + 10 * decimalValue rest

OverExpansionDigit : Nat -> Set
OverExpansionDigit digit =
  digit <=N 10

OrdinaryDecimalDigit : Nat -> Set
OrdinaryDecimalDigit digit =
  digit <N 10

NonzeroDigit : Nat -> Set
NonzeroDigit digit =
  digit != zero

OverExpansion : Nat -> List Nat -> Set
OverExpansion N digits =
  decimalValue digits == N
  and
  (LeadingNonzero digits
  and
  All OverExpansionDigit digits)

ZeroFreeOrdinaryExpansion : Nat -> List Nat -> Set
ZeroFreeOrdinaryExpansion N digits =
  decimalValue digits == N
  and
  (LeadingNonzero digits
  and
  (All OrdinaryDecimalDigit digits
  and
  All NonzeroDigit digits))

UniqueOverExpansion : Nat -> Set
UniqueOverExpansion N =
  ExistsUnique (List Nat) (OverExpansion N)

HasZeroFreeOrdinaryExpansion : Nat -> Set
HasZeroFreeOrdinaryExpansion N =
  Exists (List Nat) (ZeroFreeOrdinaryExpansion N)

putnam-2014-b1 : Set
putnam-2014-b1 =
  (N : Nat) ->
  (Positive N and UniqueOverExpansion N)
  iff
  (Positive N and HasZeroFreeOrdinaryExpansion N)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b1:
  positive integers have a unique base-10 over-expansion exactly when their
  ordinary decimal expansion contains no zero digit. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory numposrepTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2014_b1 =
  ``!(overexpansion : num -> num list -> bool) (S : num set).
      overexpansion =
        (\N d.
           d <> [] /\
           N =
             ITSET
               (\i acc. EL i d * 10 ** i + acc)
               (count (LENGTH d))
               0 /\
           LAST d <> 0 /\
           EVERY (\a : num. a <= 10) d) /\
      (!N : num.
         N IN S <=>
         0 < N /\ ?!d : num list. overexpansion N d)
      ==>

        {N : num |
           0 < N /\
           EVERY (\a : num. a <> 0) (n2l 10 N)}``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2014_b1: positive integers with a unique base-10 over-expansion
  using coefficients from 0 through 10 are exactly those whose ordinary
  decimal expansion has no zero digit. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  Word ( 0 ... 10 ) is set.mm's class of arbitrary finite sequences with
  entries from 0 through 10, and # gives their length. Excluding the empty
  word and requiring its last entry to be nonzero preserve the source's
  finite digit list and leading-coefficient condition. The positional sum
  is exactly the source over-expansion value, with index zero the units
  coefficient. Thus the restricted unique existential quantifies the entire
  finite list internally.

  For a positive natural N, the ordinary decimal position i is active
  exactly when 10^i <= N. Its digit is nonzero exactly when the residue of N
  modulo 10^(i+1) is at least 10^i. Hence the right side is bidirectionally
  equivalent to saying that the ordinary base-10 expansion of N contains no
  zero digit. The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus
  statement; this database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c P14B1Overexpansion $.

p14b1-overexpansion-syntax $a
  wff ( P14B1Overexpansion N d ) $.

${
  $d N d i $.

  p14b1-overexpansion-definition $a |- (
    ( P14B1Overexpansion N d )
    <->
    (
      (
        d e. ( Word ( 0 ... ; 1 0 ) \ { (/) } )
        /\
        ( d ` ( ( # ` d ) - 1 ) ) =/= 0
      )
      /\
      N
      =
      (
        sum_ i e. ( 0 ..^ ( # ` d ) )
          (
            ( d ` i )
            x.
            ( ; 1 0 ^ i )
          )
      )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d N d i $.

  putnambench-putnam-2014-b1 $a |- A. N e. NN
    (
      E! d e. Word ( 0 ... ; 1 0 )
        ( P14B1Overexpansion N d )
      <->
      A. i e. NN0
        (
          ( ; 1 0 ^ i ) <_ N
          ->
          ( ; 1 0 ^ i )
          <_
          (
            N
            mod
            ( ; 1 0 ^ ( i + 1 ) )
          )
        )
    )
  $.
$}

        N > 0 &
        ex d being FinSequence of NAT st
          0 < len d &
          d.(len d) <> 0 &
          (for i being Nat st i in Seg len d holds d.i <= 10) &
          (ex terms being FinSequence of NAT st
            len terms = len d &
            (for i being Nat st i in Seg len d holds
              terms.i = d.i * ((10 qua Nat) |^ (i -' 1))) &
            Sum terms = N) &
          (for e being FinSequence of NAT st
            0 < len e &
            e.(len e) <> 0 &
            (for i being Nat st i in Seg len e holds e.i <= 10) &
            (ex terms being FinSequence of NAT st
              len terms = len e &
              (for i being Nat st i in Seg len e holds
                terms.i = e.i * ((10 qua Nat) |^ (i -' 1))) &
              Sum terms = N)
          holds e = d)))
  holds
    S = {n where n is Element of NAT :
      n > 0 &
      (for k being Nat st
        n div ((10 qua Nat) |^ k) <> 0
      holds
        (n div ((10 qua Nat) |^ k)) mod 10 <> 0)}
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2014_b1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b1:
% positive integers have a unique base-10 over-expansion exactly when their
% ordinary decimal expansion contains no zero digit. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2014_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  digit_list: TYPE = list[nat]
  natural_set: TYPE = [nat -> bool]
  overexpansion_relation: TYPE = [nat, digit_list -> bool]

  decimal_value(digits: digit_list): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES digits OF
      null: 0,
      cons(digit, tail):
        digit + 10 * decimal_value(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE digits BY <<

  digits_at_most_ten(digits: digit_list): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES digits OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(digit, tail):
        digit <= 10 AND digits_at_most_ten(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE digits BY <<

  leading_digit_nonzero(digits: digit_list): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES digits OF
      null: FALSE,
      cons(digit, tail):
        IF tail = null THEN
          digit /= 0
        ELSE
          leading_digit_nonzero(tail)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE digits BY <<

  is_overexpansion(N: nat, digits: digit_list): bool =
    decimal_value(digits) = N
      AND leading_digit_nonzero(digits)
      AND digits_at_most_ten(digits)

  unique_overexpansion(
      overexpansion: overexpansion_relation,
      N: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (digits: digit_list):
      overexpansion(N, digits)
        AND (FORALL (other: digit_list):
          overexpansion(N, other) IMPLIES other = digits)

  putnam_2014_b1_solution(N: nat): bool =
    N > 0
      AND (FORALL (position: nat):
        ndiv(N, 10 ^ position) > 0 IMPLIES
          mod(ndiv(N, 10 ^ position), 10) /= 0)

  putnam_2014_b1: bool =
    FORALL
        (overexpansion: overexpansion_relation),
        (S: natural_set):
      ((FORALL (N: nat), (digits: digit_list):
          overexpansion(N, digits)
            IFF is_overexpansion(N, digits))
        AND (FORALL (N: nat):
          S(N)
            IFF
              (N > 0
                AND unique_overexpansion(overexpansion, N))))
      IMPLIES
        (FORALL (N: nat):
          S(N) IFF putnam_2014_b1_solution(N))
END putnam_2014_b1

title: putnam_2014_b2
content:
import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Nat

-- Note: uses (ℝ → ℝ) instead of (Set.Icc (1 : ℝ) 3 → ℝ)
noncomputable abbrev putnam_2014_b2_solution : ℝ := sorry
-- Real.log (4 / 3)
/--
Suppose that \( f \) is a function on the interval \([1,3]\) such that \(-1 \leq f(x) \leq 1\) for all \( x \) and \( \int_{1}^{3} f(x) \, dx = 0 \). How large can \(\int_{1}^{3} \frac{f(x)}{x} \, dx \) be?
-/
theorem putnam_2014_b2 :
  IsGreatest {t | ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ,
    (∀ x : Set.Icc (1 : ℝ) 3, -1 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ 1) ∧
    (∫ x in Set.Ioo 1 3, f x = 0) ∧
    (∫ x in Set.Ioo 1 3, (f x) / x) = t}
  putnam_2014_b2_solution :=
sorry

title: putnam_2014_b2
content:
Require Import Reals Coquelicot.Coquelicot.
Definition putnam_2014_b2_solution : R := ln (4 / 3).
Theorem putnam_2014_b2
    (fbound : (R -> R) -> Prop := fun f => forall x : R, 1 <= x <= 3 -> -1 <= f x <= 1)
    (finteq0 : (R -> R) -> Prop := fun f => RInt f 1 3 = 0)
    (fint : (R -> R) -> R := fun f => RInt (fun x => f x / x) 1 3)
    : (exists f : R -> R, fbound f /\ finteq0 f /\ fint f = putnam_2014_b2_solution) /\ (forall f : R -> R, fbound f /\ finteq0 f -> fint f <= putnam_2014_b2_solution).
Proof. Admitted.

title: putnam_2014_b2
content:
theory putnam_2014_b2 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Interval_Integral"
begin

(* uses (real \<Rightarrow> real) instead of ({1..3} \<Rightarrow> real) *)
definition putnam_2014_b2_solution :: real where "putnam_2014_b2_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* ln (4/3) *)
theorem putnam_2014_b2:
  fixes fbound :: "(real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and finteq0 :: "(real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and fint :: "(real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> real"
  defines "fbound \<equiv> (\<lambda>f::real\<Rightarrow>real. (\<forall>x::real\<in>{1..3}. -1 \<le> f x \<and> f x \<le> 1))"
  and "finteq0 \<equiv> (\<lambda>f::real\<Rightarrow>real. (interval_lebesgue_integral lebesgue 1 3 f) = 0)"
  and "fint \<equiv> (\<lambda>f::real\<Rightarrow>real. interval_lebesgue_integral lebesgue 1 3 (\<lambda>x::real. (f x)/x))"
  shows "(GREATEST ffint::real. (\<exists>f::real\<Rightarrow>real. fbound f \<and> finteq0 f \<and> ffint = fint f)) = putnam_2014_b2_solution"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_2014_b2
putnam_2014_b2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b2:
;; the maximum of the integral of f(x)/x on [1,3], for real integrable f
;; bounded between -1 and 1 with integral zero, is ln(4/3). This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A Dedekind-complete ordered field presents the real numbers up to the
;; unique ordered-field isomorphism. APPLY$ objects present arbitrary sets and
;; real-valued functions without replacing them by finite tables. Integrals
;; are defined below by the unbounded tagged-partition criterion for the
;; Riemann integral. This is the integral intended by the published problem;
;; changing open to closed interval endpoints does not change its value.

(defun p14b2-member-p (carrier x)
  (if (apply$ carrier (list x)) t nil))

(defun p14b2-unary-value (operation x)
  (apply$ operation (list x)))

(defun p14b2-binary-value (operation x y)
  (apply$ operation (list x y)))

(defun-sk p14b2-valid-scalar-set-p (carrier set)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (apply$ set (list x))
     (p14b2-member-p carrier x))))

(defun-sk p14b2-field-laws-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p14b2-member-p carrier x)
      (p14b2-member-p carrier y)
      (p14b2-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (p14b2-member-p
       carrier (p14b2-binary-value add x y))
      (p14b2-member-p
       carrier (p14b2-binary-value multiply x y))
      (p14b2-member-p
       carrier (p14b2-unary-value negate x))
      (p14b2-member-p
       carrier (p14b2-unary-value inverse x))
      (equal
       (p14b2-binary-value
        add (p14b2-binary-value add x y) z)
       (p14b2-binary-value
        add x (p14b2-binary-value add y z)))
      (equal
       (p14b2-binary-value add x y)
       (p14b2-binary-value add y x))
      (equal (p14b2-binary-value add x zero) x)
      (equal
       (p14b2-binary-value
        add x (p14b2-unary-value negate x))
       zero)
      (equal
       (p14b2-binary-value
        multiply (p14b2-binary-value multiply x y) z)
       (p14b2-binary-value
        multiply x (p14b2-binary-value multiply y z)))
      (equal
       (p14b2-binary-value multiply x y)
       (p14b2-binary-value multiply y x))
      (equal (p14b2-binary-value multiply x one) x)
      (equal (p14b2-unary-value inverse zero) zero)
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal
        (p14b2-binary-value
         multiply x (p14b2-unary-value inverse x))
        one))
      (equal
       (p14b2-binary-value
        multiply x (p14b2-binary-value add y z))
       (p14b2-binary-value
        add
        (p14b2-binary-value multiply x y)
        (p14b2-binary-value multiply x z)))))))

(defun-sk p14b2-order-laws-p
    (carrier add multiply zero less)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p14b2-member-p carrier x)
      (p14b2-member-p carrier y)
      (p14b2-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (not (p14b2-binary-value less x x))
      (or
       (equal x y)
       (p14b2-binary-value less x y)
       (p14b2-binary-value less y x))
      (implies
       (and
        (p14b2-binary-value less x y)
        (p14b2-binary-value less y z))
       (p14b2-binary-value less x z))
      (implies
       (p14b2-binary-value less x y)
       (p14b2-binary-value
        less
        (p14b2-binary-value add x z)
        (p14b2-binary-value add y z)))
      (implies
       (and
        (p14b2-binary-value less zero x)
        (p14b2-binary-value less zero y))
       (p14b2-binary-value
        less zero (p14b2-binary-value multiply x y)))))))

(defun-sk p14b2-scalar-set-nonempty-p (carrier set)
  (exists (x)
    (and
     (p14b2-member-p carrier x)
     (apply$ set (list x)))))

(defun-sk p14b2-upper-bound-p (carrier less set bound)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (p14b2-member-p carrier x)
      (apply$ set (list x)))
     (not (p14b2-binary-value less bound x)))))

(defun-sk p14b2-bounded-above-p (carrier less set)
  (exists (bound)
    (and
     (p14b2-member-p carrier bound)
     (p14b2-upper-bound-p carrier less set bound))))

(defun-sk p14b2-supremum-p (carrier less set supremum)
  (forall (bound)
    (and
     (p14b2-member-p carrier supremum)
     (p14b2-upper-bound-p carrier less set supremum)
     (implies
      (and
       (p14b2-member-p carrier bound)
       (p14b2-upper-bound-p carrier less set bound))
      (not (p14b2-binary-value less bound supremum))))))

(defun-sk p14b2-has-supremum-p (carrier less set)
  (exists (supremum)
    (p14b2-supremum-p carrier less set supremum)))

(defun-sk p14b2-dedekind-complete-p (carrier less)
  (forall (set)
    (implies
     (and
      (tamep-functionp set)
      (p14b2-valid-scalar-set-p carrier set)
      (p14b2-scalar-set-nonempty-p carrier set)
      (p14b2-bounded-above-p carrier less set))
     (p14b2-has-supremum-p carrier less set))))

(defun p14b2-real-field-p
    (carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one less)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp add)
   (tamep-functionp multiply)
   (tamep-functionp negate)
   (tamep-functionp inverse)
   (tamep-functionp less)
   (p14b2-member-p carrier zero)
   (p14b2-member-p carrier one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (p14b2-field-laws-p
    carrier add multiply negate inverse zero one)
   (p14b2-order-laws-p carrier add multiply zero less)
   (p14b2-binary-value less zero one)
   (p14b2-dedekind-complete-p carrier less)))

(defun p14b2-r-carrier (ctx) (nth 0 ctx))
(defun p14b2-r-zero (ctx) (nth 1 ctx))
(defun p14b2-r-one (ctx) (nth 2 ctx))
(defun p14b2-r-add (ctx) (nth 3 ctx))
(defun p14b2-r-mul (ctx) (nth 4 ctx))
(defun p14b2-r-neg (ctx) (nth 5 ctx))
(defun p14b2-r-inv (ctx) (nth 6 ctx))
(defun p14b2-r-lt (ctx) (nth 7 ctx))

(defun p14b2-context-p (ctx)
  (and
   (true-listp ctx)
   (equal (len ctx) 8)
   (p14b2-real-field-p
    (p14b2-r-carrier ctx)
    (p14b2-r-add ctx)
    (p14b2-r-mul ctx)
    (p14b2-r-neg ctx)
    (p14b2-r-inv ctx)
    (p14b2-r-zero ctx)
    (p14b2-r-one ctx)
    (p14b2-r-lt ctx))))

(defun p14b2-r-add-value (ctx x y)
  (p14b2-binary-value (p14b2-r-add ctx) x y))

(defun p14b2-r-mul-value (ctx x y)
  (p14b2-binary-value (p14b2-r-mul ctx) x y))

(defun p14b2-r-neg-value (ctx x)
  (p14b2-unary-value (p14b2-r-neg ctx) x))

(defun p14b2-r-inv-value (ctx x)
  (p14b2-unary-value (p14b2-r-inv ctx) x))

(defun p14b2-r-sub-value (ctx x y)
  (p14b2-r-add-value ctx x (p14b2-r-neg-value ctx y)))

(defun p14b2-r-div-value (ctx x y)
  (p14b2-r-mul-value ctx x (p14b2-r-inv-value ctx y)))

(defun p14b2-r-lt-p (ctx x y)
  (if (p14b2-binary-value (p14b2-r-lt ctx) x y) t nil))

(defun p14b2-r-le-p (ctx x y)
  (not (p14b2-r-lt-p ctx y x)))

(defun p14b2-r-abs-value (ctx x)
  (if (p14b2-r-lt-p ctx x (p14b2-r-zero ctx))
      (p14b2-r-neg-value ctx x)
    x))

(defun p14b2-positive-real-p (ctx x)
  (and
   (p14b2-member-p (p14b2-r-carrier ctx) x)
   (p14b2-r-lt-p ctx (p14b2-r-zero ctx) x)))

(defun p14b2-natural (ctx n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (p14b2-r-zero ctx)
    (p14b2-r-add-value
     ctx
     (p14b2-r-one ctx)
     (p14b2-natural ctx (- n 1)))))

(defun p14b2-three (ctx)
  (p14b2-natural ctx 3))

(defun p14b2-four-thirds (ctx)
  (p14b2-r-div-value
   ctx (p14b2-natural ctx 4) (p14b2-three ctx)))

(defun-sk p14b2-real-function-p (ctx function)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p14b2-member-p (p14b2-r-carrier ctx) x)
     (p14b2-member-p
      (p14b2-r-carrier ctx)
      (p14b2-unary-value function x)))))

(defun p14b2-real-list-p (ctx values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (p14b2-member-p (p14b2-r-carrier ctx) (car values))
       (p14b2-real-list-p ctx (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun p14b2-strictly-increasing-p (ctx values)
  (if (and (consp values) (consp (cdr values)))
      (and
       (p14b2-r-lt-p ctx (car values) (cadr values))
       (p14b2-strictly-increasing-p ctx (cdr values)))
    (and (consp values) (endp (cdr values)))))

(defun p14b2-tags-fit-p (ctx nodes tags)
  (if (consp tags)
      (and
       (consp nodes)
       (consp (cdr nodes))
       (p14b2-r-le-p ctx (car nodes) (car tags))
       (p14b2-r-le-p ctx (car tags) (cadr nodes))
       (p14b2-tags-fit-p ctx (cdr nodes) (cdr tags)))
    (and
     (consp nodes)
     (endp (cdr nodes))
     (equal tags nil))))

(defun p14b2-tagged-partition-p (ctx a b nodes tags)
  (and
   (true-listp nodes)
   (true-listp tags)
   (p14b2-real-list-p ctx nodes)
   (p14b2-real-list-p ctx tags)
   (p14b2-strictly-increasing-p ctx nodes)
   (p14b2-tags-fit-p ctx nodes tags)
   (equal (car nodes) a)
   (equal (car (last nodes)) b)))

(defun p14b2-mesh-less-p (ctx nodes delta)
  (if (and (consp nodes) (consp (cdr nodes)))
      (and
       (p14b2-r-lt-p
        ctx
        (p14b2-r-sub-value ctx (cadr nodes) (car nodes))
        delta)
       (p14b2-mesh-less-p ctx (cdr nodes) delta))
    (and (consp nodes) (endp (cdr nodes)))))

(defun p14b2-integrand-value (ctx function mode x)
  (cond
   ((equal mode 'reciprocal)
    (p14b2-r-inv-value ctx x))
   ((equal mode 'divide-by-x)
    (p14b2-r-mul-value
     ctx
     (p14b2-unary-value function x)
     (p14b2-r-inv-value ctx x)))
   (t
    (p14b2-unary-value function x))))

(defun p14b2-riemann-sum (ctx function mode nodes tags)
  (if (consp tags)
      (p14b2-r-add-value
       ctx
       (p14b2-r-mul-value
        ctx
        (p14b2-integrand-value ctx function mode (car tags))
        (p14b2-r-sub-value ctx (cadr nodes) (car nodes)))
       (p14b2-riemann-sum
        ctx function mode (cdr nodes) (cdr tags)))
    (p14b2-r-zero ctx)))

(defun-sk p14b2-integral-delta-p
    (ctx function mode a b value epsilon delta)
  (forall (nodes tags)
    (implies
     (and
      (p14b2-tagged-partition-p ctx a b nodes tags)
      (p14b2-mesh-less-p ctx nodes delta))
     (p14b2-r-lt-p
      ctx
      (p14b2-r-abs-value
       ctx
       (p14b2-r-sub-value
        ctx
        (p14b2-riemann-sum ctx function mode nodes tags)
        value))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p14b2-integral-delta-exists-p
    (ctx function mode a b value epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (p14b2-positive-real-p ctx delta)
     (p14b2-integral-delta-p
      ctx function mode a b value epsilon delta))))

(defun-sk p14b2-integral-converges-p
    (ctx function mode a b value)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p14b2-positive-real-p ctx epsilon)
     (p14b2-integral-delta-exists-p
      ctx function mode a b value epsilon))))

(defun p14b2-integral-value-p
    (ctx function mode a b value)
  (and
   (p14b2-member-p (p14b2-r-carrier ctx) a)
   (p14b2-member-p (p14b2-r-carrier ctx) b)
   (p14b2-member-p (p14b2-r-carrier ctx) value)
   (p14b2-r-le-p ctx a b)
   (or
    (equal mode 'reciprocal)
    (and
     (tamep-functionp function)
     (p14b2-real-function-p ctx function)))
   (p14b2-integral-converges-p
    ctx function mode a b value)))

(defun p14b2-in-main-interval-p (ctx x)
  (and
   (p14b2-member-p (p14b2-r-carrier ctx) x)
   (p14b2-r-le-p ctx (p14b2-r-one ctx) x)
   (p14b2-r-le-p ctx x (p14b2-three ctx))))

(defun-sk p14b2-bounded-function-p (ctx function)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (p14b2-in-main-interval-p ctx x)
     (and
      (p14b2-r-le-p
       ctx
       (p14b2-r-neg-value ctx (p14b2-r-one ctx))
       (p14b2-unary-value function x))
      (p14b2-r-le-p
       ctx
       (p14b2-unary-value function x)
       (p14b2-r-one ctx))))))

(defun p14b2-feasible-value-p (ctx function value)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp function)
   (p14b2-real-function-p ctx function)
   (p14b2-bounded-function-p ctx function)
   (p14b2-integral-value-p
    ctx
    function
    'plain
    (p14b2-r-one ctx)
    (p14b2-three ctx)
    (p14b2-r-zero ctx))
   (p14b2-integral-value-p
    ctx
    function
    'divide-by-x
    (p14b2-r-one ctx)
    (p14b2-three ctx)
    value)))

(defun-sk p14b2-maximum-attained-p (ctx maximum)
  (exists (function)
    (p14b2-feasible-value-p ctx function maximum)))

(defun-sk p14b2-maximum-upper-bound-p (ctx maximum)
  (forall (function value)
    (implies
     (p14b2-feasible-value-p ctx function value)
     (p14b2-r-le-p ctx value maximum))))

(defun p14b2-is-maximum-p (ctx maximum)
  (and
   (p14b2-member-p (p14b2-r-carrier ctx) maximum)
   (p14b2-maximum-attained-p ctx maximum)
   (p14b2-maximum-upper-bound-p ctx maximum)))

;; On positive reals, ln(4/3) is definitionally the integral of 1/x from
;; 1 to 4/3. The solution remains an internal existential witness.

(defun-sk p14b2-conclusion-p (ctx)
  (exists (solution)
    (and
     (p14b2-integral-value-p
      ctx
      nil
      'reciprocal
      (p14b2-r-one ctx)
      (p14b2-four-thirds ctx)
      solution)
     (p14b2-is-maximum-p ctx solution))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2014-b2-statement (ctx)
  (implies
   (p14b2-context-p ctx)
   (p14b2-conclusion-p ctx)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2014_b2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2014_b2): the greatest weighted integral for a
-- bounded real function on [1,3] with zero integral is log(4/3).
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

Between :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
Between reals lower upper x =
  lessOrEqual reals lower x
  and
  lessOrEqual reals x upper

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

mesh :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
mesh reals lower upper pieces =
  divide reals
    (subtract reals upper lower)
    (fromNat reals pieces)

UniformTags :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (Nat -> Nat -> R) ->
  Set
UniformTags reals lower upper tags =
  (n i : Nat) ->
  i <N suc n ->
  Between reals
    (add reals lower
      (multiply reals
        (fromNat reals i)
        (mesh reals lower upper (suc n))))
    (add reals lower
      (multiply reals
        (fromNat reals (suc i))
        (mesh reals lower upper (suc n))))
    (tags n i)

uniformRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
uniformRiemannSum reals lower upper function tags pieces =
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function (tags i))
        (mesh reals lower upper pieces))

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue {R} reals lower upper function integralValue =
  (tags : Nat -> Nat -> R) ->
  UniformTags reals lower upper tags ->
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      uniformRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (tags n)
        (suc n))
    integralValue

module Putnam2014B2Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  oneN : Nat
  oneN =
    suc zero

  twoN : Nat
  twoN =
    suc oneN

  threeN : Nat
  threeN =
    suc twoN

  fourN : Nat
  fourN =
    suc threeN

  one three fourThirds : R
  one =
    oneR reals
  three =
    fromNat reals threeN
  fourThirds =
    divide reals
      (fromNat reals fourN)
      three

  BoundedOnInterval : (R -> R) -> Set
  BoundedOnInterval function =
    (x : R) ->
    Between reals one three x ->
    lessOrEqual reals
      (negate reals one)
      (function x)
    and
    lessOrEqual reals
      (function x)
      one

  HasZeroIntegral : (R -> R) -> Set
  HasZeroIntegral function =
    IntervalIntegralValue reals
      one
      three
      function
      (zeroR reals)

  Admissible : (R -> R) -> Set
  Admissible function =
    BoundedOnInterval function
    and
    HasZeroIntegral function

  weightedFunction : (R -> R) -> R -> R
  weightedFunction function x =
    divide reals (function x) x

  HasWeightedIntegral :
    (R -> R) ->
    R ->
    Set
  HasWeightedIntegral function value =
    IntervalIntegralValue reals
      one
      three
      (weightedFunction function)
      value

  reciprocal : R -> R
  reciprocal x =
    divide reals one x

  IsLogFourThirds : R -> Set
  IsLogFourThirds value =
    IntervalIntegralValue reals
      one
      fourThirds
      reciprocal
      value

  record IsGreatestWeightedIntegral
    (maximum : R) :
    Set where

    field
      attained :
        Exists (R -> R)
          (\ function ->
            Admissible function
            and
            HasWeightedIntegral function maximum)

      upper-bound :
        (function : R -> R) ->
        (value : R) ->
        Admissible function ->
        HasWeightedIntegral function value ->
        lessOrEqual reals value maximum

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    Exists R
      (\ maximum ->
        IsLogFourThirds maximum
        and
        IsGreatestWeightedIntegral maximum)

putnam-2014-b2 : Set1
putnam-2014-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2014B2Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b2:
  the exact maximum ln(4/3) of the integral of f(x)/x on [1,3], where both
  integrands are integrable, f is bounded between -1 and 1, and its integral
  is zero. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory realTheory transcTheory integrationTheory;

val putnam_2014_b2 =
  ``let source_interval = interval [1, 3]
    in
    let admissible =
      \f : real -> real.
        f integrable_on source_interval /\
        (\x : real. f x / x) integrable_on source_interval /\
        (!x : real.
           x IN source_interval
           ==>
           ~1 <= f x /\ f x <= 1) /\
        integration$integral source_interval f = 0
    in
    let weighted_integral =
      \f : real -> real.
        integration$integral source_interval
          (\x : real. f x / x)
    in
    let solution = ln (4 / 3)
    in
      (?f : real -> real.
         admissible f /\
         weighted_integral f = solution) /\
      (!f : real -> real.
         admissible f
         ==>
         weighted_integral f <= solution)``;

title: putnam_2014_b2
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2014_b2: the maximum of the integral of f(x) / x on [1,3] for
  integrable real functions bounded between -1 and 1 with integral zero is
  the natural logarithm of 4 / 3. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  RR ^m RR is set.mm's class of total real-valued functions. Membership of
  the restricted mapping in L^1 states Lebesgue integrability on [1,3], and
  S. is the corresponding real Lebesgue integral. Closed rather than open
  interval endpoints do not change either integral.

  The first conjunct gives an admissible function attaining log(4/3), and
  the second says that every admissible function has weighted integral at
  most log(4/3). Thus the conjunction expands the source IsGreatest
  assertion. The declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement;
  this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d f x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2014-b2 $a |- (
    E. f e. ( RR ^m RR )
      (
        (
          (
            ( x e. ( 1 [,] 3 ) |-> ( f ` x ) ) e. L^1
            /\
            A. x e. ( 1 [,] 3 )
              (
                ( -u 1 ) <_ ( f ` x )
                /\
                ( f ` x ) <_ 1
              )
          )
          /\
          S. ( 1 [,] 3 ) ( f ` x ) _d x = 0
        )
        /\
        S. ( 1 [,] 3 ) ( ( f ` x ) / x ) _d x
          =
          ( log ` ( 4 / 3 ) )
      )
    /\
    A. f e. ( RR ^m RR )
      (
        (
          (
            ( x e. ( 1 [,] 3 ) |-> ( f ` x ) ) e. L^1
            /\
            A. x e. ( 1 [,] 3 )
              (
                ( -u 1 ) <_ ( f ` x )
                /\
                ( f ` x ) <_ 1
              )
          )
          /\
          S. ( 1 [,] 3 ) ( f ` x ) _d x = 0
        )
        ->
        S. ( 1 [,] 3 ) ( ( f ` x ) / x ) _d x
          <_
          ( log ` ( 4 / 3 ) )
      )
  ) $.
$}

title: putnam_2014_b2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b2:
% the greatest integral of f(x)/x on [1,3], for real-valued f bounded between
% -1 and 1 with zero integral, is ln(4/3). This file contains no proof.

putnam_2014_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  valid_tagged_partition(
      left, right: real,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = left
      AND points(count) = right
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          (points(index) < points(index + 1)
            AND points(index) <= tags(index)
            AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1))

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      function_value: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(
        function_value, points, tags, count - 1)
        + function_value(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_interval_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      left, right, integral_value: real): bool =
    left < right
      AND FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
          FORALL
              (points, tags: real_sequence),
              (count: nat):
            (valid_tagged_partition(
                left, right, points, tags, count)
              AND mesh_less_than(
                points, count, mesh_bound))
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                riemann_sum(
                  function_value, points, tags, count)
                  - integral_value)
                < epsilon_value

  bounded_on_source_interval(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      (1 <= x AND x <= 3) IMPLIES
        (-1 <= f(x) AND f(x) <= 1)

  weighted_integrand(f: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real): safe_div(f(x), x)

  reciprocal: real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real): safe_div(1, x)

  admissible(f: real_function): bool =
    bounded_on_source_interval(f)
      AND has_interval_integral(f, 1, 3, 0)

  putnam_2014_b2: bool =
    EXISTS (solution_value: real):
      has_interval_integral(
        reciprocal, 1, safe_div(4, 3), solution_value)
        AND
          (EXISTS (f: real_function):
            admissible(f)
              AND has_interval_integral(
                weighted_integrand(f),
                1,
                3,
                solution_value))
        AND
          (FORALL
              (f: real_function),
              (weighted_value: real):
            (admissible(f)
              AND has_interval_integral(
                weighted_integrand(f),
                1,
                3,
                weighted_value))
            IMPLIES weighted_value <= solution_value)
END putnam_2014_b2

/--
Let $A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix with rational entries. Suppose that there are at least $m+n$ distinct prime numbers among the absolute values of the entries of $A$. Show that the rank of $A$ is at least 2.
-/
theorem putnam_2014_b3
(m n : ℕ)
(A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℚ)
(mnpos : 0 < m ∧ 0 < n)
(Aprime : {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ∃ (i : Fin m) (j : Fin n), |A i j| = p}.encard ≥ m + n)
: A.rank ≥ 2 :=

title: putnam_2014_b3
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b3:
   a rational matrix with at least m+n distinct prime absolute entry values
   has rank at least two. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Vectors.Fin QArith Qabs ZArith.Znumtheory.

Open Scope Q_scope.

Definition putnam_2014_b3_matrix (m n : nat) : Type :=
  Fin.t m -> Fin.t n -> Q.

Definition putnam_2014_b3_many_entry_primes
    {m n : nat} (A : putnam_2014_b3_matrix m n) : Prop :=
  exists ps : Fin.t (m + n) -> nat,
    (forall u v : Fin.t (m + n), ps u = ps v -> u = v) /\
    forall k : Fin.t (m + n),
      prime (Z.of_nat (ps k)) /\
      exists (i : Fin.t m) (j : Fin.t n),
        Qeq (Qabs (A i j)) (inject_Z (Z.of_nat (ps k))).

Theorem putnam_2014_b3
    (m n : nat)
    (A : putnam_2014_b3_matrix m n)
    (mnpos : (0 < m)%nat /\ (0 < n)%nat)
    (Aprime : putnam_2014_b3_many_entry_primes A) :
  exists (i1 i2 : Fin.t m) (j1 j2 : Fin.t n),
    i1 <> i2 /\
    j1 <> j2 /\
    ~ Qeq
        (A i1 j1 * A i2 j2 - A i1 j2 * A i2 j1)
        0.
Admitted.

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b3:
;; a positive-dimensional rational matrix with at least m+n distinct prime
;; absolute entry values has rank at least two. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A list of rows is an exact representation of the source finite matrix.

(defun putnam-2014-b3-rational-row-p (row n)
  (and
   (true-listp row)
   (equal (len row) n)
   (if (endp row)
       t
     (and
      (rationalp (car row))
      (putnam-2014-b3-rational-row-p (cdr row) (- n 1))))))

(defun putnam-2014-b3-rational-matrix-p (matrix m n)
  (and
   (true-listp matrix)
   (equal (len matrix) m)
   (if (endp matrix)
       t
     (and
      (putnam-2014-b3-rational-row-p (car matrix) n)
      (putnam-2014-b3-rational-matrix-p
       (cdr matrix) (- m 1) n)))))

(defun putnam-2014-b3-no-proper-divisor-from-p
    (number divisor)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix (- number divisor))))
  (if (and
       (natp number)
       (natp divisor)
       (<= 2 divisor)
       (< divisor number))
      (and
       (not (equal (mod number divisor) 0))
       (putnam-2014-b3-no-proper-divisor-from-p
        number (+ divisor 1)))
    t))

(defun putnam-2014-b3-prime-p (number)
  (and
   (natp number)
   (< 1 number)
   (putnam-2014-b3-no-proper-divisor-from-p number 2)))

(defun putnam-2014-b3-adjoin-prime-value (value primes)
  (let ((absolute-value (abs value)))
    (if (and
         (integerp value)
         (putnam-2014-b3-prime-p absolute-value)
         (not (member-equal absolute-value primes)))
        (cons absolute-value primes)
      primes)))

(defun putnam-2014-b3-collect-row-primes (row primes)
  (if (endp row)
      primes
    (putnam-2014-b3-collect-row-primes
     (cdr row)
     (putnam-2014-b3-adjoin-prime-value
      (car row) primes))))

(defun putnam-2014-b3-collect-matrix-primes (matrix primes)
  (if (endp matrix)
      primes
    (putnam-2014-b3-collect-matrix-primes
     (cdr matrix)
     (putnam-2014-b3-collect-row-primes
      (car matrix) primes))))

;; Over the rationals, rank is at least two exactly when some two rows and
;; two columns form a nonzero 2 by 2 minor.

(defun putnam-2014-b3-minor-with-first-column-p
    (first-row-tail second-row-tail first-a first-b)
  (if (or (endp first-row-tail)
          (endp second-row-tail))
      nil
    (or
     (not
      (equal
       (- (* first-a (car second-row-tail))
          (* (car first-row-tail) first-b))
       0))
     (putnam-2014-b3-minor-with-first-column-p
      (cdr first-row-tail)
      (cdr second-row-tail)
      first-a
      first-b))))

(defun putnam-2014-b3-two-rows-have-nonzero-minor-p
    (first-row second-row)
  (if (or (endp first-row)
          (endp second-row))
      nil
    (or
     (putnam-2014-b3-minor-with-first-column-p
      (cdr first-row)
      (cdr second-row)
      (car first-row)
      (car second-row))
     (putnam-2014-b3-two-rows-have-nonzero-minor-p
      (cdr first-row)
      (cdr second-row)))))

(defun putnam-2014-b3-row-has-nonzero-minor-p
    (row remaining-rows)
  (if (endp remaining-rows)
      nil
    (or
     (putnam-2014-b3-two-rows-have-nonzero-minor-p
      row (car remaining-rows))
     (putnam-2014-b3-row-has-nonzero-minor-p
      row (cdr remaining-rows)))))

(defun putnam-2014-b3-rank-at-least-two-p (matrix)
  (if (endp matrix)
      nil
    (or
     (putnam-2014-b3-row-has-nonzero-minor-p
      (car matrix) (cdr matrix))
     (putnam-2014-b3-rank-at-least-two-p
      (cdr matrix)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2014-b3-statement (m n matrix)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp m)
    (natp n)
    (< 0 m)
    (< 0 n)
    (putnam-2014-b3-rational-matrix-p matrix m n)
    (<=
     (+ m n)
     (len
      (putnam-2014-b3-collect-matrix-primes matrix nil))))
   (putnam-2014-b3-rank-at-least-two-p matrix)))

title: putnam_2014_b3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2014_b3): a rational matrix with at least m+n
-- distinct primes among its absolute entry values has rank at least two. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2014B3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixl 7 _*Z_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

Divides : Nat -> Nat -> Set
Divides divisor number =
  Exists Nat
    (\ factor -> divisor * factor == number)

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

infixr 2 _or_

Prime : Nat -> Set
Prime number =
  two <=N number
  and
  ((divisor : Nat) ->
    Divides divisor number ->
    divisor == one or divisor == number)

negativeNat : Nat -> Int
negativeNat zero =
  pos zero
negativeNat (suc n) =
  negsuc n

_*Z_ : Int -> Int -> Int
pos m *Z pos n =
  pos (m * n)
pos m *Z negsuc n =
  negativeNat (m * suc n)
negsuc m *Z pos n =
  negativeNat (suc m * n)
negsuc m *Z negsuc n =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

intMagnitude : Int -> Nat
intMagnitude (pos n) =
  n
intMagnitude (negsuc n) =
  suc n

record Rational : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator             : Int
    denominator-minus-one : Nat

open Rational

denominator : Rational -> Nat
denominator q =
  suc (denominator-minus-one q)

AbsoluteEqualsNat : Rational -> Nat -> Set
AbsoluteEqualsNat q n =
  intMagnitude (numerator q) == n * denominator q

Matrix : Nat -> Nat -> Set
Matrix m n =
  Fin m -> Fin n -> Rational

record AtLeastDistinctPrimeEntries
  {m n : Nat}
  (A : Matrix m n) :
  Set where

  field
    prime-values :
      Fin (m + n) ->
      Nat
    values-prime :
      (k : Fin (m + n)) ->
      Prime (prime-values k)
    values-occur :
      (k : Fin (m + n)) ->
      Exists (Fin m)
        (\ i ->
          Exists (Fin n)
            (\ j ->
              AbsoluteEqualsNat (A i j) (prime-values k)))
    values-injective :
      (k l : Fin (m + n)) ->
      prime-values k == prime-values l ->
      k == l

RationalProductsEqual :
  Rational ->
  Rational ->
  Rational ->
  Rational ->
  Set
RationalProductsEqual x y u v =
  (numerator x *Z numerator y)
    *Z pos (denominator u * denominator v)
  ==
  (numerator u *Z numerator v)
    *Z pos (denominator x * denominator y)

record RankAtLeastTwo
  {m n : Nat}
  (A : Matrix m n) :
  Set where

  field
    first-row second-row :
      Fin m
    first-column second-column :
      Fin n
    distinct-rows :
      first-row != second-row
    distinct-columns :
      first-column != second-column
    nonzero-minor :
      Not
        (RationalProductsEqual
          (A first-row first-column)
          (A second-row second-column)
          (A first-row second-column)
          (A second-row first-column))

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  one <=N n

putnam-2014-b3 : Set
putnam-2014-b3 =
  (m n : Nat) ->
  (A : Matrix m n) ->
  Positive m and Positive n ->
  AtLeastDistinctPrimeEntries A ->
  RankAtLeastTwo A

title: putnam_2014_b3

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b3:
  a positive-dimensional rational matrix with at least m+n distinct prime
  absolute entry values has rank at least two. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory primeTheory ratTheory;

val putnam_2014_b3 =
  ``!m n : num. !A : num -> num -> rat.
      0 < m /\
      0 < n /\
      m + n <=
        CARD
          {p : num |
             prime p /\
             ?i j : num.
               i < m /\
               j < n /\
               (A i j = rat_of_num p \/
                A i j = ~(rat_of_num p))}
      ==>
      ?i1 i2 j1 j2 : num.
        i1 < m /\
        i2 < m /\
        j1 < n /\
        j2 < n /\
        i1 <> i2 /\
        j1 <> j2 /\
        A i1 j1 * A i2 j2 - A i1 j2 * A i2 j1 <> 0q``;

title: putnam_2014_b3
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2014_b3: a rational matrix with at least m+n distinct primes among
  the absolute values of its entries has rank at least two. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For positive m and n, the carriers 0 ..^ m and 0 ..^ n represent Fin m
  and Fin n. Thus QQ ^m ((0 ..^ m) X. (0 ..^ n)) is the full class of
  m-by-n rational matrices, with no finiteness restriction on the entry
  values.

  The restricted class abstraction is exactly the set of natural primes
  occurring as absolute values of entries of A, and # gives its finite
  cardinality. The conclusion says that A has a nonzero two-by-two minor.
  Over the rationals this is equivalent to matrix rank at least two. The
  final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d A i j m n p r s $.

  putnambench-putnam-2014-b3 $a |-
    A. m e. NN
      A. n e. NN
        A. A e.
          (
            QQ
            ^m
            ( ( 0 ..^ m ) X. ( 0 ..^ n ) )
          )
          (
            (
              ( m + n )
              <_
              (
                #
                `
                {
                  p e. Prime |
                  E. i e. ( 0 ..^ m )
                    E. j e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                      ( abs ` ( A ` <. i , j >. ) ) = p
                }
              )
            )
            ->
            E. r e. ( 0 ..^ m )
              E. s e. ( 0 ..^ m )
                E. i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                  E. j e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                    (
                      ( r =/= s /\ i =/= j )
                      /\
                      (
                        (
                          ( A ` <. r , i >. )
                          x.
                          ( A ` <. s , j >. )
                        )
                        -
                        (
                          ( A ` <. r , j >. )
                          x.
                          ( A ` <. s , i >. )
                        )
                      )
                      =/=
                      0
                    )
          )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2014_b3:
% a positive-dimensional rational matrix with at least the sum of its
% dimensions in distinct prime absolute entry values has rank at least two.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2014_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  rational_matrix(m, n: posnat): TYPE =
    [below(m), below(n) -> rat]

  nat_divides(divisor: posnat, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND (FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value)

  injective_below(
      values: [nat -> nat],
      bound: nat): bool =
    FORALL (left, right: nat):
      left < bound
        AND right < bound
        AND values(left) = values(right)
      IMPLIES left = right

  has_enough_prime_entry_values(
      m, n: posnat,
      A: rational_matrix(m, n)): bool =
    EXISTS (values: [nat -> nat]):
      injective_below(values, m + n)
        AND (FORALL (index: nat):
          index < m + n IMPLIES
            prime_nat(values(index))
              AND (EXISTS
                  (row: below(m)),
                  (column: below(n)):
                abs(A(row, column)) = (values(index) :: rat)))

  rank_at_least_two(
      m, n: posnat,
      A: rational_matrix(m, n)): bool =
    EXISTS
        (first_row, second_row: below(m)),
        (first_column, second_column: below(n)):
      first_row /= second_row
        AND first_column /= second_column
        AND A(first_row, first_column) * A(second_row, second_column)
          - A(first_row, second_column) * A(second_row, first_column)
            /= 0

  putnam_2014_b3: bool =
    FORALL
        (m, n: posnat),
        (A: rational_matrix(m, n)):
      has_enough_prime_entry_values(m, n, A)
        IMPLIES rank_at_least_two(m, n, A)
END putnam_2014_b3
