theory putnam_2016_b5 imports Complex_Main
begin

(* uses ((real \<Rightarrow> real) set) instead of (({1<..} \<Rightarrow> {1<..}) set) *)
definition putnam_2016_b5_solution :: "(real \<Rightarrow> real) set" where
  "putnam_2016_b5_solution \<equiv>
    {f. \<exists>c::real. c > 0 \<and> (\<forall>x>1. f x = x powr c)}"
(* {f::real\<Rightarrow>real. (\<exists>c::real. c > 0 \<and> (\<forall>x::real>1. f x = x powr c))} *)
theorem putnam_2016_b5:
  fixes f :: "real \<Rightarrow> real"
  and fle :: bool
  defines hfle: "fle \<equiv>
    (\<forall>x::real>1. f x > 1) \<and>
    (\<forall>x::real>1. \<forall>y::real>1.
      (x^2 \<le> y \<and> y \<le> x^3) \<longrightarrow>
      ((f x)^2 \<le> f y \<and> f y \<le> (f x)^3))"
  shows "fle \<longleftrightarrow> f \<in> putnam_2016_b5_solution"
  sorry

end

title: putnam_2016_b5
putnam_2016_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2016_b5:
;; classification of functions from (1,infinity) to (1,infinity) preserving
;; the stated square-to-cube interval bounds as exactly the positive real
;; power functions. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Exact reals are represented by rational regular Cauchy names, and functions
;; on (1,infinity) are extensional ACL2 function objects on those names.
;; FN-EQUAL supplies unbounded universal quantification over names and function
;; objects. NOT/FN-EQUAL keeps the source's exponent witness internal.
;;
;; The internal power oracle P(s,x) is required, for every real s>1, to be
;; positive, normalized by P(s,0)=1 and P(s,1)=s, additive-to-multiplicative
;; in the exponent, and monotone in the exponent. These laws uniquely
;; characterize the standard real power s^x, and standard real power supplies
;; such an oracle. Thus the oracle is a bidirectionally equivalent definition,
;; not an uninterpreted operation or a restriction to rational exponents.

(defun putnam-2016-b5-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'cons
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2016-b5-term-list (cdr terms)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-apply-term (function arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2016-b5-quoted function)
        (putnam-2016-b5-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-apply-object-term
    (function-term arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        function-term
        (putnam-2016-b5-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'if
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms (cdr terms))
            (putnam-2016-b5-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2016-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list 'if
        hypothesis
        conclusion
        (putnam-2016-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-negate-term (value)
  (list 'unary-- value))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-subtract-term (left right)
  (putnam-2016-b5-add-term
   left
   (putnam-2016-b5-negate-term right)))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-multiply-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-* left right))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-divide-term (numerator denominator)
  (putnam-2016-b5-multiply-term
   numerator
   (list 'unary-/ denominator)))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-absolute-term (value)
  (list 'if
        (list '< value (putnam-2016-b5-quoted 0))
        (putnam-2016-b5-negate-term value)
        value))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-less-equal-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        (list '< right left)
        (putnam-2016-b5-quoted nil)
        (putnam-2016-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-positive-rational-term (value)
  (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
   (list
    (list 'rationalp value)
    (list '< (putnam-2016-b5-quoted 0) value))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda
        formals
        (putnam-2016-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-real-value-term (name precision)
  (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term name (list precision)))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-object-real-value-term
    (name-term precision)
  (putnam-2016-b5-apply-object-term
   name-term
   (list precision)))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-real-cauchy-function (name)
  (let* ((left
          (putnam-2016-b5-real-value-term name 'epsilon))
         (right
          (putnam-2016-b5-real-value-term name 'eta))
         (distance
          (putnam-2016-b5-absolute-term
           (putnam-2016-b5-subtract-term left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon eta)
     (putnam-2016-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (putnam-2016-b5-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
        (putnam-2016-b5-positive-rational-term 'eta)))
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2016-b5-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2016-b5-add-term
          'epsilon 'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p (name)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2016-b5-real-cauchy-function name)
    (putnam-2016-b5-true-function
     '(epsilon eta)))))

;; Sampling at eta/4 makes these exact predicates on the represented limits.

(defun putnam-2016-b5-real-distance-function
    (left-name right-name bound)
  (let* ((precision
          (putnam-2016-b5-multiply-term 1/4 'eta))
         (left
          (putnam-2016-b5-real-value-term
           left-name precision))
         (right
          (putnam-2016-b5-real-value-term
           right-name precision))
         (distance
          (putnam-2016-b5-absolute-term
           (putnam-2016-b5-subtract-term left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(eta)
     (putnam-2016-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2016-b5-positive-rational-term 'eta)
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2016-b5-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2016-b5-add-term
          (putnam-2016-b5-quoted bound)
          'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-real-distance-at-most-p
    (left-name right-name bound)
  (and
   (rationalp bound)
   (putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p left-name)
   (putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p right-name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2016-b5-real-distance-function
     left-name right-name bound)
    (putnam-2016-b5-true-function '(eta)))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-real-equal-p
    (left-name right-name)
  (putnam-2016-b5-real-distance-at-most-p
   left-name right-name 0))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-real-order-function
    (left-name right-name)
  (let* ((precision
          (putnam-2016-b5-multiply-term 1/4 'eta))
         (left
          (putnam-2016-b5-real-value-term
           left-name precision))
         (right
          (putnam-2016-b5-real-value-term
           right-name precision)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(eta)
     (putnam-2016-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2016-b5-positive-rational-term 'eta)
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2016-b5-less-equal-term
         left
         (putnam-2016-b5-add-term
          right 'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-real-le-p
    (left-name right-name)
  (and
   (putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p left-name)
   (putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p right-name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2016-b5-real-order-function
     left-name right-name)
    (putnam-2016-b5-true-function '(eta)))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
    (left-name right-name)
  (and
   (putnam-2016-b5-real-le-p left-name right-name)
   (not
    (putnam-2016-b5-real-equal-p
     left-name right-name))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-rational-name (value)
  (list 'lambda
        '(precision)
        (putnam-2016-b5-quoted value)))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-add-name (left-name right-name)
  (let* ((precision
          (putnam-2016-b5-multiply-term 1/2 'epsilon))
         (left
          (putnam-2016-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2016-b5-quoted left-name)
           precision))
         (right
          (putnam-2016-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2016-b5-quoted right-name)
           precision)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2016-b5-add-term left right))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-multiply-name
    (left-name right-name)
  (let* ((left-at-one
          (putnam-2016-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2016-b5-quoted left-name)
           1))
         (right-at-one
          (putnam-2016-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2016-b5-quoted right-name)
           1))
         (scale
          (putnam-2016-b5-multiply-term
           8
           (putnam-2016-b5-add-term
            3
            (putnam-2016-b5-add-term
             (putnam-2016-b5-absolute-term left-at-one)
             (putnam-2016-b5-absolute-term right-at-one)))))
         (candidate
          (putnam-2016-b5-divide-term
           'epsilon scale))
         (precision
          (list 'if
                (list '< 1 candidate)
                1
                candidate))
         (left
          (putnam-2016-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2016-b5-quoted left-name)
           precision))
         (right
          (putnam-2016-b5-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2016-b5-quoted right-name)
           precision)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2016-b5-multiply-term left right))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-interval-function-output-function
    (function)
  (let ((output
         (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term function '(x)))
        (one-name
         (putnam-2016-b5-rational-name 1)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-2016-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'x)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name)
              'x)))
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p output)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name)
              output)))))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-interval-function-extensional-function
    (function)
  (let ((left-output
         (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term
          function '(left)))
        (right-output
         (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term
          function '(right)))
        (one-name
         (putnam-2016-b5-rational-name 1)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(left right)
     (putnam-2016-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'left)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'right)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name)
              'left)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name)
              'right)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-equal-p
              'left 'right)))
      (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-equal-p
            left-output right-output)))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-interval-function-p (function)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp function)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2016-b5-interval-function-output-function
     function)
    (putnam-2016-b5-true-function '(x)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2016-b5-interval-function-extensional-function
     function)
    (putnam-2016-b5-true-function
     '(left right)))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-bound-condition-function (function)
  (let* ((one-name
          (putnam-2016-b5-rational-name 1))
         (x-square
          (list 'putnam-2016-b5-multiply-name
                'x 'x))
         (x-cube
          (list 'putnam-2016-b5-multiply-name
                x-square 'x))
         (fx
          (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term function '(x)))
         (fy
          (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term function '(y)))
         (fx-square
          (list 'putnam-2016-b5-multiply-name
                fx fx))
         (fx-cube
          (list 'putnam-2016-b5-multiply-name
                fx-square fx)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x y)
     (putnam-2016-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'x)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'y)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name)
              'x)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name)
              'y)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-le-p
              x-square 'y)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-le-p
              'y x-cube)))
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-le-p
              fx-square fy)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-le-p
              fy fx-cube)))))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-bound-condition-p (function)
  (fn-equal
   (putnam-2016-b5-bound-condition-function function)
   (putnam-2016-b5-true-function '(x y))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-power-output-function (power)
  (let ((output
         (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term power '(base exponent)))
        (one-name
         (putnam-2016-b5-rational-name 1)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(base exponent)
     (putnam-2016-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'base)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'exponent)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name)
              'base)))
      (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p output)))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-power-extensional-function (power)
  (let ((left-output
         (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term
          power '(base-left exponent-left)))
        (right-output
         (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term
          power '(base-right exponent-right)))
        (one-name
         (putnam-2016-b5-rational-name 1)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(base-left base-right exponent-left exponent-right)
     (putnam-2016-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'base-left)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'base-right)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'exponent-left)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'exponent-right)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name)
              'base-left)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name)
              'base-right)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-equal-p
              'base-left 'base-right)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-equal-p
              'exponent-left 'exponent-right)))
      (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-equal-p
            left-output right-output)))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-power-law-function (power)
  (let* ((zero-name
          (putnam-2016-b5-rational-name 0))
         (one-name
          (putnam-2016-b5-rational-name 1))
         (at-x
          (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term
           power '(base x)))
         (at-y
          (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term
           power '(base y)))
         (at-zero
          (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term
           power
           (list 'base
                 (putnam-2016-b5-quoted zero-name))))
         (at-one
          (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term
           power
           (list 'base
                 (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name))))
         (sum-name
          (list 'putnam-2016-b5-add-name 'x 'y))
         (at-sum
          (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term
           power
           (list 'base sum-name)))
         (product-name
          (list 'putnam-2016-b5-multiply-name
                at-x at-y)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(base x y)
     (putnam-2016-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'base)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'x)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'y)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name)
              'base)))
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted zero-name)
              at-x)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-equal-p
              at-zero
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name))
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-equal-p
              at-one 'base)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-equal-p
              at-sum product-name)
        (putnam-2016-b5-implies-term
         (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-le-p 'x 'y)
         (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-le-p
               at-x at-y))))))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-power-oracle-p (power)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp power)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2016-b5-power-output-function power)
    (putnam-2016-b5-true-function
     '(base exponent)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2016-b5-power-extensional-function power)
    (putnam-2016-b5-true-function
     '(base-left base-right exponent-left exponent-right)))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2016-b5-power-law-function power)
    (putnam-2016-b5-true-function
     '(base x y)))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-solution-equality-function
    (function exponent power)
  (let ((function-value
         (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term function '(x)))
        (power-value
         (putnam-2016-b5-apply-term
          power
          (list 'x
                (putnam-2016-b5-quoted exponent))))
        (one-name
         (putnam-2016-b5-rational-name 1)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (putnam-2016-b5-implies-term
      (putnam-2016-b5-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p 'x)
        (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p
              (putnam-2016-b5-quoted one-name)
              'x)))
      (list 'putnam-2016-b5-real-equal-p
            function-value power-value)))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-solution-witness-p
    (witness function)
  (and
   (true-listp witness)
   (equal (len witness) 2)
   (let ((exponent (nth 0 witness))
         (power (nth 1 witness))
         (zero-name
          (putnam-2016-b5-rational-name 0)))
     (and
      (putnam-2016-b5-real-name-p exponent)
      (putnam-2016-b5-real-lt-p zero-name exponent)
      (putnam-2016-b5-power-oracle-p power)
      (fn-equal
       (putnam-2016-b5-solution-equality-function
        function exponent power)
       (putnam-2016-b5-true-function '(x)))))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-solution-failure-function (function)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(witness)
   (list
    'if
    (list 'putnam-2016-b5-solution-witness-p
          'witness
          (putnam-2016-b5-quoted function))
    (putnam-2016-b5-quoted nil)
    (putnam-2016-b5-quoted t))))

(defun putnam-2016-b5-solution-exists-p (function)
  (not
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2016-b5-solution-failure-function function)
    (putnam-2016-b5-true-function '(witness)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2016-b5-statement (function)
  (implies
   (putnam-2016-b5-interval-function-p function)
   (iff
    (putnam-2016-b5-bound-condition-p function)
    (putnam-2016-b5-solution-exists-p function))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2016_b5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2016_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2016_b5): functions from (1,infinity) to
-- (1,infinity) satisfying the prescribed two-sided power inequalities are
-- exactly the functions x |-> x^c for a positive real c. This file contains
-- no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2016B5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    absoluteValueR : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    absolute-value-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (absoluteValueR x)
    absolute-value-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      absoluteValueR x == x
    absolute-value-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      absoluteValueR x == negate x

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

cube :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
cube reals x =
  multiply reals (multiply reals x x) x

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

Positive :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
Positive reals x =
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) x

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  Positive reals epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      StrictLess reals
        (absoluteValueR reals
          (subtract reals (sequence n) limit))
        epsilon)

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
sumFirst reals term zero =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals term (suc n) =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals term n)
    (term n)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

exponentialTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

ExponentialValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
ExponentialValue reals x result =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals (exponentialTerm reals x) n)
    result

record StandardRealPowers
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    exponential logarithm : R -> R

    exponential-series :
      (x : R) ->
      ExponentialValue reals x (exponential x)

    exponential-positive :
      (x : R) ->
      Positive reals (exponential x)

    exponential-injective :
      (x y : R) ->
      exponential x == exponential y ->
      x == y

    exponential-logarithm :
      (x : R) ->
      Positive reals x ->
      exponential (logarithm x) == x

open StandardRealPowers

realPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  {reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R} ->
  StandardRealPowers reals ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
realPower {reals = reals} powers base exponent =
  exponential powers
    (multiply reals exponent (logarithm powers base))

record AboveOne
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set where
  constructor aboveOne
  field
    number : R
    number-above-one :
      StrictLess reals (oneR reals) number

open AboveOne

module Putnam2016B5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (powers : StandardRealPowers reals) where

  FunctionOnAboveOne : Set
  FunctionOnAboveOne =
    AboveOne reals -> AboveOne reals

  Solution :
    FunctionOnAboveOne ->
    Set
  Solution f =
    Exists R
      (\ c ->
        Positive reals c
        and
        ((x : AboveOne reals) ->
          number (f x) ==
          realPower powers (number x) c))

  FunctionalInequality :
    FunctionOnAboveOne ->
    Set
  FunctionalInequality f =
    (x y : AboveOne reals) ->
    (lessOrEqual reals
      (square reals (number x))
      (number y)
    and
    lessOrEqual reals
      (number y)
      (cube reals (number x))) ->
    (lessOrEqual reals
      (square reals (number (f x)))
      (number (f y))
    and
    lessOrEqual reals
      (number (f y))
      (cube reals (number (f x))))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (f : FunctionOnAboveOne) ->
    Iff
      (Solution f)
      (FunctionalInequality f)

putnam-2016-b5 : Set1
putnam-2016-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (powers : StandardRealPowers reals) ->
  Putnam2016B5Statement.proposition reals powers

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2016_b5:
  the classification of functions from (1, infinity) to itself that preserve
  the interval between the square and cube of each input. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open realTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2016_b5 =
  ``!f : real -> real.
      ((!x : real. 1 < x ==> 1 < f x) /\
       (!x y : real.
          1 < x /\ 1 < y /\ x pow 2 <= y /\ y <= x pow 3
          ==>
          f x pow 2 <= f y /\ f y <= f x pow 3))
      <=>
      ?c : real.
        0 < c /\
        !x : real.
          1 < x ==> f x = x powr c``;

title: putnam_2016_b5

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2016_b5: classification of functions from (1, +infinity) to itself
  satisfying a two-sided power inequality as positive real power functions.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The class ( 1 (,) +oo ) is set.mm's open real interval (1, +infinity),
  and the function space quantifies arbitrary functions from that interval
  to itself. Thus the source codomain condition f(x) > 1 is retained in the
  type of f.

  Natural powers express the inequalities in the hypothesis. Since x > 1
  and c is real, set.mm's complex-power expression x ^c c is real-valued
  and agrees with the source real power. The exponent witness remains
  internally existentially quantified. The final declaration is the single
  unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof
  declaration.
$)

${
  $d c f x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-2016-b5 $a |-
    A. f e. ( ( 1 (,) +oo ) ^m ( 1 (,) +oo ) )
      (
        A. x e. ( 1 (,) +oo ) A. y e. ( 1 (,) +oo )
          (
            (
              ( x ^ 2 ) <_ y
              /\
              y <_ ( x ^ 3 )
            )
            ->
            (
              ( ( f ` x ) ^ 2 ) <_ ( f ` y )
              /\
              ( f ` y ) <_ ( ( f ` x ) ^ 3 )
            )
          )
        <->
        E. c e. RR
          (
            0 < c
            /\
            A. x e. ( 1 (,) +oo )
              ( f ` x ) = ( x ^c c )
          )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2016_b5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2016_b5:
% the functions from (1, infinity) to itself preserving the stated power
% bounds are exactly the positive real-power functions. This file contains
% no proof.

putnam_2016_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  above_one: TYPE = {x: real | x > 1}
  admissible_function: TYPE = [above_one -> above_one]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  natural_log(x: real): real =
    IF x > 0 THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (value: real):
          real_exponential(value) = x)
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  real_power(base, exponent: real): real =
    IF base > 0 THEN
      real_exponential(exponent * natural_log(base))
    ELSIF base = 0 AND exponent = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  satisfies_power_bounds(f: admissible_function): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: above_one):
      (x ^ 2 <= y AND y <= x ^ 3)
        IMPLIES
          (f(x) ^ 2 <= f(y) AND f(y) <= f(x) ^ 3)

  positive_real_power_function(f: admissible_function): bool =
    EXISTS (c: real):
      c > 0
        AND FORALL (x: above_one):
          f(x) = real_power(x, c)

  putnam_2016_b5: bool =
    FORALL (f: admissible_function):
      satisfies_power_bounds(f)
        IFF positive_real_power_function(f)
END putnam_2016_b5

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2016_b6:
;; the nested real series sum over k >= 1 and n >= 0 of
;; ((-1)^(k-1)/k)/(k*2^n+1) has value 1. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Every finite partial sum below is rational.  For fixed K, letting N tend
;; to infinity gives the first K terms of the source outer series.  Therefore
;; the source equality is equivalent to
;;
;;   for every epsilon > 0, eventually in K, eventually in N,
;;   |partial-sum(K,N) - 1| <= epsilon.
;;
;; MODULUS is internally existentially quantified below.  At (EPSILON, 0)
;; its car is the outer cutoff, and at (EPSILON, K) its cdr is the inner
;; cutoff.  The enclosing negated FN-EQUAL keeps this witness internal.

(defun putnam-2016-b6-inner-sum (k term-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix term-count)))
  (if (zp term-count)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2016-b6-inner-sum
        k (- term-count 1))
       (/ (+ (* k (expt 2 (- term-count 1)))
             1)))))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-partial-sum
    (outer-term-count inner-term-count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix outer-term-count)))
  (if (zp outer-term-count)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2016-b6-partial-sum
        (- outer-term-count 1)
        inner-term-count)
       (* (/ (expt -1 (- outer-term-count 1))
             outer-term-count)
          (putnam-2016-b6-inner-sum
           outer-term-count inner-term-count)))))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'cons
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2016-b6-term-list (cdr terms)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-apply-term (function arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2016-b6-quoted function)
        (putnam-2016-b6-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'if
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2016-b6-and-terms (cdr terms))
            (putnam-2016-b6-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2016-b6-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list 'if
        hypothesis
        conclusion
        (putnam-2016-b6-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-negate-term (value)
  (list 'unary-- value))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-subtract-term (left right)
  (putnam-2016-b6-add-term
   left
   (putnam-2016-b6-negate-term right)))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-absolute-term (value)
  (list 'if
        (list '< value 0)
        (putnam-2016-b6-negate-term value)
        value))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-less-equal-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        (list '< right left)
        (putnam-2016-b6-quoted nil)
        (putnam-2016-b6-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-positive-rational-term (value)
  (putnam-2016-b6-and-terms
   (list
    (list 'rationalp value)
    (list '< 0 value))))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda
        formals
        (putnam-2016-b6-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-limit-function (modulus)
  (let* ((outer-data
          (putnam-2016-b6-apply-term
           modulus '(epsilon 0)))
         (inner-data
          (putnam-2016-b6-apply-term
           modulus '(epsilon k)))
         (outer-cutoff
          (list 'car outer-data))
         (inner-cutoff
          (list 'cdr inner-data))
         (partial-sum
          (list 'putnam-2016-b6-partial-sum
                'k 'n))
         (error
          (putnam-2016-b6-absolute-term
           (putnam-2016-b6-subtract-term
            partial-sum 1))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon k n)
     (putnam-2016-b6-implies-term
      (putnam-2016-b6-positive-rational-term
       'epsilon)
      (putnam-2016-b6-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'consp outer-data)
        (list 'natp outer-cutoff)
        (putnam-2016-b6-implies-term
         (putnam-2016-b6-and-terms
          (list
           (list 'natp 'k)
           (putnam-2016-b6-less-equal-term
            outer-cutoff 'k)))
         (putnam-2016-b6-and-terms
          (list
           (list 'consp inner-data)
           (list 'natp inner-cutoff)
           (putnam-2016-b6-implies-term
            (putnam-2016-b6-and-terms
             (list
              (list 'natp 'n)
              (putnam-2016-b6-less-equal-term
               inner-cutoff 'n)))
            (putnam-2016-b6-and-terms
             (list
              (list 'rationalp partial-sum)
              (putnam-2016-b6-less-equal-term
               error 'epsilon)))))))))))))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-limit-witness-p (modulus)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp modulus)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2016-b6-limit-function modulus)
    (putnam-2016-b6-true-function
     '(epsilon k n)))))

(defun putnam-2016-b6-limit-failure-function ()
  (list
   'lambda
   '(modulus)
   (list
    'if
    (list 'putnam-2016-b6-limit-witness-p
          'modulus)
    (putnam-2016-b6-quoted nil)
    (putnam-2016-b6-quoted t))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2016-b6-statement ()
  (let ((failure
         (putnam-2016-b6-limit-failure-function))
        (always-true
         (putnam-2016-b6-true-function '(modulus))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp failure)
     (tamep-functionp always-true)
     (not (fn-equal failure always-true)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2016_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2016_b6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2016_b6): the nested real series with outer
-- terms (-1)^k/(k+1) and inner terms 1/((k+1)2^n+1) sums to one.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2016B6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms limit =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    limit

alternatingSign :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
alternatingSign reals k =
  naturalPower reals
    (negate reals (oneR reals))
    k

innerTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  R
innerTerm reals k n =
  divide reals
    (oneR reals)
    (add reals
      (multiply reals
        (fromNat reals (suc k))
        (naturalPower reals (fromNat reals twoN) n))
      (oneR reals))

outerWeight :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R
outerWeight reals k =
  divide reals
    (alternatingSign reals k)
    (fromNat reals (suc k))

PutnamSeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Set
PutnamSeriesHasSum {R} reals =
  Exists (Nat -> R)
    (\ innerSums ->
      ((k : Nat) ->
        SeriesHasSum reals
          (innerTerm reals k)
          (innerSums k))
      and
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (\ k ->
          multiply reals
            (outerWeight reals k)
            (innerSums k))
        (oneR reals))

putnam-2016-b6 : Set1
putnam-2016-b6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  PutnamSeriesHasSum reals

  the iterated real series over positive k and nonnegative n with terms
  ((-1)^(k-1) / k) / (k * 2^n + 1) converges to 1. This file contains no

open arithmeticTheory realTheory seqTheory;

val putnam_2016_b6 =

            1 / (&(k + 1) * (2 : real) pow n + 1))

title: putnam_2016_b6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2016_b6: evaluation of an alternating series whose terms contain
  reciprocal series over powers of two. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN is the class of positive integers and NN0 is the class of
  nonnegative integers. Thus the outer and inner sum_ binders preserve the
  source indices k >= 1 and n >= 0 exactly. Their nesting also preserves the
  source order: for each k, first form the reciprocal series over n, then form
  the alternating series over k.

  The right side is the published value 1, supplied explicitly by the Rocq
  source. The Rocq summand's inner denominator omits the successor on its
  zero-based outer index; the expression below follows the published problem
  and the mutually consistent Lean and Isabelle denominators instead.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d k n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2016-b6 $a |-
    (
      sum_ k e. NN
        (
          (
            ( ( -u 1 ) ^ ( k - 1 ) )
            /
            k
          )
          x.
          (
            sum_ n e. NN0
              (
                1
                /
                (
                  ( k x. ( 2 ^ n ) )
                  +
                  1
                )
              )
          )
        )
    )
    =
    1
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2016_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2016_b6:
% the iterated real series sum over k >= 1 of (-1)^(k-1)/k times the sum over
% n >= 0 of 1/(k*2^n + 1) converges to 1. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2016_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  inner_term(k_index, n: nat): real =
    safe_div(
      1,
      ((k_index + 1) :: real) * (2 :: real) ^ n + 1)

  inner_partial_sum(k_index, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      inner_partial_sum(k_index, count - 1)
        + inner_term(k_index, count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  outer_partial_sum(
      inner_sums: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET k_index: nat = count - 1 IN
        outer_partial_sum(inner_sums, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(k_index),
              (k_index + 1) :: real)
            * inner_sums(k_index)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (count: nat):
          cutoff <= count IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(count) - value) < epsilon_value

  putnam_2016_b6_solution: real = 1

  putnam_2016_b6: bool =
    EXISTS (inner_sums: real_sequence):
      (FORALL (k_index: nat):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            inner_partial_sum(k_index, count),
          inner_sums(k_index)))
      AND converges_to(
        LAMBDA (count: nat):
          outer_partial_sum(inner_sums, count),
        putnam_2016_b6_solution)
END putnam_2016_b6

title: putnam_2017_a1
content:
import Mathlib

abbrev putnam_2017_a1_solution : Set ℤ := sorry
-- {x : ℤ | x > 0 ∧ (x = 1 ∨ 5 ∣ x)}
/--
Let $S$ be the smallest set of positive integers such that (a) $2$ is in $S$, (b) $n$ is in $S$ whenever $n^2$ is in $S$, and (c) $(n+5)^2$ is in $S$ whenever $n$ is in $S$. Which positive integers are not in $S$?.
-/
theorem putnam_2017_a1
    (IsQualifying : Set ℤ → Prop)
    (IsQualifying_def : ∀ S, IsQualifying S ↔
      (∀ n ∈ S, 0 < n) ∧
      2 ∈ S ∧
      (∀ n > 0, n ^ 2 ∈ S → n ∈ S) ∧
      (∀ n ∈ S, (n + 5) ^ 2 ∈ S))
    (S : Set ℤ)
    (hS : IsLeast IsQualifying S) :
    Sᶜ ∩ {n | 0 < n} = putnam_2017_a1_solution :=
  sorry

title: putnam_2017_a1
content:
From mathcomp Require Import all_algebra all_ssreflect.
From mathcomp Require Import classical_sets.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.
Local Open Scope classical_set_scope.

Definition putnam_2017_a1_solution : set int := [set x : int | x > 0 /\ (x = 1 \/ (5 %| x)%Z)].
Theorem putnam_2017_a1
    (IsQualifying : (set int) -> Prop)
    (IsQualifying_def : forall S, IsQualifying S <-> 
        (forall n : int, n \in S -> n > 0) /\
        2 \in S /\
        (forall n : int, n > 0 /\ (n ^ 2) \in S -> n \in S) /\
        (forall n : int, n \in S -> (n + 5) ^ 2 \in S))
    (S : set int)
    (hS : IsQualifying S /\
      forall T : set int, IsQualifying T -> S `<=` T)
    : ~` S `&` [set n : int | n > 0] = putnam_2017_a1_solution.
Proof. Admitted.

begin

definition putnam_2017_a1_solution :: "int set" where
  "putnam_2017_a1_solution \<equiv>
    {x :: int. x > 0 \<and> (x = 1 \<or> 5 dvd x)}"
(* { x::int . x > 0 \<and> (x = 1 \<or> 5 dvd x) } *)
theorem putnam_2017_a1:
  fixes IsQualifying :: "(int set) \<Rightarrow> bool"
    and S :: "int set"

    (\<forall> n \<in> S. 0 < n) \<and>
    2 \<in> S \<and>
    (\<forall> n > 0. n^2 \<in> S \<longrightarrow> n \<in> S) \<and>
    (\<forall> n \<in> S. (n + 5)^2 \<in> S)"
    and hS : "IsQualifying S \<and> (\<forall>A. IsQualifying A \<longrightarrow> S \<subseteq> A)"
  shows "{x :: int. x > 0} - S = putnam_2017_a1_solution"

end

  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2017_a1): characterization of the positive
  integers omitted by the least set closed under the stated square and
  shifted-square conditions. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let is_qualifying =
     \S:int->bool.
       (!n:int. n IN S ==> &0 < n) /\
       (&2:int) IN S /\
       (!n:int. &0 < n /\ n pow 2 IN S ==> n IN S) /\
       (!n:int. n IN S ==> (n + &5) pow 2 IN S) in
   let putnam_2017_a1_solution =
     {x:int | &0 < x /\ (x = &1 \/ (&5:int) divides x)} in

     is_qualifying S /\

         putnam_2017_a1_solution`;;

title: putnam_2017_a1
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a1:
;; the positive integers outside the least set containing 2 and closed under
;; positive square roots and the map n |-> (n+5)^2 are exactly 1 and the
;; positive multiples of 5. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A finite trace lists derivation records (value rule parent-index). Each
;; value is either 2, (m+5)^2 for an earlier value m, or a positive square root
;; of an earlier value. The integers admitting such traces form exactly the
;; least qualifying set: appending one record proves closure under both source
;; rules, while induction along a trace puts every trace value in every
;; qualifying set.
;;
;; Negated FN-EQUAL keeps the finite trace existentially quantified inside the
;; statement predicate. It does not replace the resulting potentially infinite
;; least set by a finite carrier or expose the trace as an external parameter.

(defun putnam-2017-a1-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-list-term (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'cons
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2017-a1-list-term (cdr terms)))
    (putnam-2017-a1-quoted nil)))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'if
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2017-a1-and-terms (cdr terms))
       (putnam-2017-a1-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2017-a1-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-or-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'if
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2017-a1-quoted t)
       (putnam-2017-a1-or-terms (cdr terms)))
    (putnam-2017-a1-quoted nil)))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-multiply-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-* left right))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-nth-term (index values)
  (list 'nth index values))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-range-term (upper)
  (list
   'from-to-by
   (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 0)
   upper
   (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 1)))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-iteration-term (values)
  (list
   'loop$-as
   (putnam-2017-a1-list-term (list values))))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-true-function ()
  (list 'lambda '(trace) (putnam-2017-a1-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-entry-function ()
  (let* ((index (list 'car 'row))
         (trace (list 'car 'globals))
         (entry
          (putnam-2017-a1-nth-term index trace))
         (value
          (putnam-2017-a1-nth-term
           (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 0)
           entry))
         (rule
          (putnam-2017-a1-nth-term
           (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 1)
           entry))
         (parent-index
          (putnam-2017-a1-nth-term
           (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 2)
           entry))
         (parent-entry
          (putnam-2017-a1-nth-term parent-index trace))
         (parent-value
          (putnam-2017-a1-nth-term
           (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 0)
           parent-entry))
         (parent-before-p
          (putnam-2017-a1-and-terms
           (list
            (list 'natp parent-index)
            (list '< parent-index index))))
         (parent-plus-five
          (putnam-2017-a1-add-term
           parent-value
           (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 5)))
         (base-step
          (putnam-2017-a1-and-terms
           (list
            (list
             'equal rule
             (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 0))
            (list
             'equal value
             (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 2)))))
         (forward-step
          (putnam-2017-a1-and-terms
           (list
            (list
             'equal rule
             (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 1))
            parent-before-p
            (list
             'equal
             value
             (putnam-2017-a1-multiply-term
              parent-plus-five parent-plus-five)))))
         (square-root-step
          (putnam-2017-a1-and-terms
           (list
            (list
             'equal rule
             (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 2))
            parent-before-p
            (list
             'equal
             parent-value
             (putnam-2017-a1-multiply-term
              value value))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(globals row)
     (putnam-2017-a1-and-terms
      (list
       (list 'true-listp entry)
       (list
        'equal
        (list 'len entry)
        (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 3))
       (list 'integerp value)
       (list '< (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 0) value)
       (putnam-2017-a1-or-terms
        (list base-step forward-step square-root-step)))))))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-all-indices-term
    (entry-function globals upper)
  (list
   'always$+
   (putnam-2017-a1-quoted entry-function)
   globals
   (putnam-2017-a1-iteration-term
    (putnam-2017-a1-range-term upper))))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-trace-failure-function
    (target entry-function)
  (let* ((trace 'trace)
         (upper
          (putnam-2017-a1-add-term
           (list 'len trace)
           (putnam-2017-a1-quoted -1)))
         (globals
          (putnam-2017-a1-list-term (list trace)))
         (last-entry
          (putnam-2017-a1-nth-term upper trace))
         (last-value
          (putnam-2017-a1-nth-term
           (putnam-2017-a1-quoted 0)
           last-entry))
         (qualification
          (putnam-2017-a1-and-terms
           (list
            (list 'true-listp trace)
            (list 'consp trace)
            (putnam-2017-a1-all-indices-term
             entry-function globals upper)
            (list
             'equal
             last-value
             (putnam-2017-a1-quoted target))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(trace)
     (list
      'if
      qualification
      (putnam-2017-a1-quoted nil)
      (putnam-2017-a1-quoted t)))))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-in-least-set-p (n)
  (let* ((entry-function
          (putnam-2017-a1-entry-function))
         (failure-function
          (putnam-2017-a1-trace-failure-function
           n entry-function))
        (true-function
         (putnam-2017-a1-true-function)))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp entry-function)
     (tamep-functionp failure-function)
     (tamep-functionp true-function)
     (not (fn-equal failure-function true-function)))))

(defun putnam-2017-a1-solution-member-p (n)
  (and
   (integerp n)
   (< 0 n)
   (or (equal n 1)
       (equal (mod n 5) 0))))

;; ACL2 universally closes N. Restricting it to integers preserves the source
;; domain, and this IFF is the pointwise form of the source set equality.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2017-a1-statement (n)
  (implies
   (integerp n)
   (iff
    (and
     (< 0 n)
     (not (putnam-2017-a1-in-least-set-p n)))
    (putnam-2017-a1-solution-member-p n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2017_a1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a1:
-- the positive integers omitted by the least set closed under square roots
-- and the stated shifted-square operation. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2017A1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _divides_
infixl 6 _+Z_
infixl 7 _*Z_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

_+Z_ : Int -> Int -> Int
pos m +Z pos n =
  pos (m + n)
pos m +Z negsuc n =
  difference m (suc n)
negsuc m +Z pos n =
  difference n (suc m)
negsuc m +Z negsuc n =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

_*Z_ : Int -> Int -> Int
pos m *Z pos n =
  pos (m * n)
pos m *Z negsuc n =
  negative (m * suc n)
negsuc m *Z pos n =
  negative (suc m * n)
negsuc m *Z negsuc n =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos (suc zero)

twoZ : Int
twoZ =
  pos (suc (suc zero))

fiveZ : Int
fiveZ =
  pos (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc zero)))))

square : Int -> Int
square n =
  n *Z n

data PositiveInteger : Int -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> PositiveInteger (pos (suc n))

_divides_ : Int -> Int -> Set
divisor divides dividend =
  Exists Int
    (\ quotient ->
      dividend == divisor *Z quotient)

IntegerSet : Set1
IntegerSet =
  Int -> Set

Subset : IntegerSet -> IntegerSet -> Set
Subset A B =
  (x : Int) ->
  A x ->
  B x

SetEqual : IntegerSet -> IntegerSet -> Set
SetEqual A B =
  (x : Int) ->
  Iff (A x) (B x)

Qualifying : IntegerSet -> Set
Qualifying S =
  ((n : Int) -> S n -> PositiveInteger n)
  and
  (S twoZ
  and
  (((n : Int) ->
      PositiveInteger n ->
      S (square n) ->
      S n)
  and
  ((n : Int) ->
    S n ->
    S (square (n +Z fiveZ)))))

IsQualifyingDefinition : (IntegerSet -> Set) -> Set1
IsQualifyingDefinition IsQualifying =
  (S : IntegerSet) ->
  Iff (IsQualifying S) (Qualifying S)

record IsLeast
  (property : IntegerSet -> Set)
  (S : IntegerSet) :
  Set1 where

  field
    satisfies :
      property S
    contained-in-every-satisfying-set :
      (T : IntegerSet) ->
      property T ->
      Subset S T

putnam-2017-a1-solution : IntegerSet
putnam-2017-a1-solution x =
  PositiveInteger x
  and
  ((x == oneZ) or (fiveZ divides x))

putnam-2017-a1 : Set1
putnam-2017-a1 =
  (IsQualifying : IntegerSet -> Set) ->
  IsQualifyingDefinition IsQualifying ->
  (S : IntegerSet) ->
  IsLeast IsQualifying S ->
  SetEqual
    (\ x -> Not (S x) and PositiveInteger x)
    putnam-2017-a1-solution

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a1:
  the positive integers outside the least set containing 2 and closed under
  positive square roots and the stated shifted-square operation are exactly
  1 and the positive multiples of 5. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2017_a1 =
  ``let qualifying =
      \S : int set.
        (!n : int. n IN S ==> 0 < n) /\
        (2 : int) IN S /\
        (!n : int.
           0 < n /\ n ** 2 IN S
           ==>
           n IN S) /\
        (!n : int.
           n IN S
           ==>
           (n + 5) ** 2 IN S)
    in
      !S : int set.
        qualifying S /\
        (!T : int set. qualifying T ==> S SUBSET T)
        ==>
        {n : int | 0 < n /\ n NOTIN S} =
        {n : int |
           0 < n /\ (n = 1 \/ (5 : int) int_divides n)}``;

$(

  putnam_2017_a1: classification of the positive integers omitted by the
  smallest positive-integer set containing 2 and closed under the stated
  square-root and shifted-square rules. This file contains no proof.

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's ZZ is the set of integers. The antecedent expands the source
  predicate IsQualifying: S consists of positive integers, contains 2,
  contains a positive integer whenever it contains its square, and contains
  (n + 5)^2 whenever it contains n. Its second conjunct says that S is
  contained in every other qualifying integer set, which is exactly the
  source IsLeast condition after definitional substitution.

  The conclusion identifies the positive integers outside S with exactly 1
  and the positive multiples of 5. The final declaration is the single
  unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d S T n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2017-a1 $a |- A. S
    (
      (
        (
          (
            S C_ ZZ
            /\
            A. n e. S 0 < n
          )
          /\
          (
            2 e. S
            /\
            (
              A. n e. ZZ
                (
                  (
                    0 < n
                    /\
                    ( n ^ 2 ) e. S
                  )
                  ->
                  n e. S
                )
              /\
              A. n e. S ( ( n + 5 ) ^ 2 ) e. S
            )
          )
        )
        /\
        A. T
          (
            (
              (
                T C_ ZZ
                /\
                A. n e. T 0 < n
              )
              /\

                2 e. T

                (
                  A. n e. ZZ
                    (

                        /\
                        ( n ^ 2 ) e. T

                    )
                  /\
                  A. n e. T ( ( n + 5 ) ^ 2 ) e. T
                )
              )
            )

title: putnam_2017_a1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_2017_a1:
% the positive integers omitted from the least set containing 2 and closed
% under positive square roots and n -> (n + 5)^2 are exactly 1 and the
% positive multiples of 5. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2017_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_set: TYPE = [int -> bool]

  int_divides(divisor, value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: int):
      value = divisor * quotient

  qualifying(S: integer_set): bool =
    (FORALL (n: int):
      S(n) IMPLIES n > 0)
      AND S(2)
      AND (FORALL (n: int):
        n > 0 AND S(n ^ 2) IMPLIES S(n))
      AND (FORALL (n: int):
        S(n) IMPLIES S((n + 5) ^ 2))

  subset(S, T: integer_set): bool =
    FORALL (n: int):
      S(n) IMPLIES T(n)

  least_qualifying(S: integer_set): bool =
    qualifying(S)
      AND (FORALL (T: integer_set):
        qualifying(T) IMPLIES subset(S, T))

  putnam_2017_a1_solution(n: int): bool =
    n > 0
      AND (n = 1 OR int_divides(5, n))

  putnam_2017_a1: bool =
    FORALL (S: integer_set):
      least_qualifying(S) IMPLIES
        FORALL (n: int):
          (NOT S(n) AND n > 0)
            IFF putnam_2017_a1_solution(n)
END putnam_2017_a1

open Polynomial

/--
Let $Q_0(x)=1$, $Q_1(x)=x$, and $Q_n(x)=\frac{(Q_{n-1}(x))^2-1}{Q_{n-2}(x)}$ for all $n \geq 2$. Show that, whenever $n$ is a positive integer, $Q_n(x)$ is equal to a polynomial with integer coefficients.
-/
theorem putnam_2017_a2
    (Q : ℕ → RatFunc ℚ)
    (hQbase : Q 0 = 1 ∧ Q 1 = (X : ℚ[X]))
    (hQn : ∀ n, Q (n + 2) = (Q (n + 1) ^ 2 - 1) / Q n)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ∃ P : ℤ[X], Q n = P.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) :=

From mathcomp Require Import all_algebra all_ssreflect.
From mathcomp Require Import reals.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.

Definition putnam_2017_a2_ratfun := ({poly rat} * {poly rat})%type.

Definition putnam_2017_a2_valid (q : putnam_2017_a2_ratfun) : Prop :=
  q.2 != 0.

Definition putnam_2017_a2_eq
    (q r : putnam_2017_a2_ratfun) : Prop :=
  q.1 * r.2 = r.1 * q.2.

Definition putnam_2017_a2_mul
    (q r : putnam_2017_a2_ratfun) : putnam_2017_a2_ratfun :=
  (q.1 * r.1, q.2 * r.2).

Definition putnam_2017_a2_sub
    (q r : putnam_2017_a2_ratfun) : putnam_2017_a2_ratfun :=
  (q.1 * r.2 - r.1 * q.2, q.2 * r.2).

Definition putnam_2017_a2_one : putnam_2017_a2_ratfun :=
  ((1%Z%:Q)%:P, (1%Z%:Q)%:P).

Definition putnam_2017_a2_X : putnam_2017_a2_ratfun :=
  ('X, (1%Z%:Q)%:P).

Theorem putnam_2017_a2
    (Q : nat -> putnam_2017_a2_ratfun)
    (hQvalid : forall n, putnam_2017_a2_valid (Q n))
    (hQbase :
      putnam_2017_a2_eq (Q 0%nat) putnam_2017_a2_one /\
      putnam_2017_a2_eq (Q 1%nat) putnam_2017_a2_X)
    (hQn : forall n : nat,
      putnam_2017_a2_eq
        (putnam_2017_a2_mul (Q (n.+2)) (Q n))
        (putnam_2017_a2_sub
          (putnam_2017_a2_mul (Q (n.+1)) (Q (n.+1)))
          putnam_2017_a2_one))
    (n : nat)
    (hn : lt 0 n) :
    exists P : {poly int},
      putnam_2017_a2_eq
        (Q n)
        ((map_poly intr P : {poly rat}), (1%Z%:Q)%:P).
Proof. Admitted.

  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2017_a2): integer polynomiality of the
  positive-index terms in the stated rational-function recurrence.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let eval =
     \p:real list. \x:real.
       ITLIST (\c acc. c + x * acc) p (&0) in
   let eval_int =
     \p:int list. \x:real.
       ITLIST (\c acc. real_of_int c + x * acc) p (&0) in
   let is_rational =
     \x:real.
       ?a:int. ?b:num.
         ~(b = 0) /\ x = real_of_int a / &b in
   let rational_poly =
     \p:real list. !c:real. MEM c p ==> is_rational c in
   let valid =
     \q:(real list)#(real list).
       rational_poly (FST q) /\
       rational_poly (SND q) /\
       ~(!x:real. eval (SND q) x = &0) in
   let rat_eq =
     \q:(real list)#(real list).
     \r:(real list)#(real list).
       !x:real.
         eval (FST q) x * eval (SND r) x =
         eval (FST r) x * eval (SND q) x in
   let rat_zero =
     \q:(real list)#(real list).
       !x:real. eval (FST q) x = &0 in
   let recurrence =
     \qprev:(real list)#(real list).
     \qcur:(real list)#(real list).
     \qnext:(real list)#(real list).
       if rat_zero qprev
       then rat_eq qnext ([&0],[&1])
       else
         !x:real.
           eval (FST qnext) x *
           ((eval (SND qcur) x) pow 2 * eval (FST qprev) x) =
           (((eval (FST qcur) x) pow 2 -
             (eval (SND qcur) x) pow 2) *
            eval (SND qprev) x) *
           eval (SND qnext) x in
   !Q:num->(real list)#(real list).
     (!n:num. valid (Q n)) /\
     rat_eq (Q 0) ([&1],[&1]) /\
     rat_eq (Q 1) ([&0; &1],[&1]) /\
     (!n:num. recurrence (Q n) (Q (n + 1)) (Q (n + 2)))
     ==>
     !n:num.
       0 < n
       ==> ?p:int list.
             !x:real.
               eval (FST (Q n)) x =
               eval_int p x * eval (SND (Q n)) x`;;

title: putnam_2017_a2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a2:
;; the rational-function sequence starting with 1 and x and satisfying
;; Q_(n+2) = (Q_(n+1)^2 - 1) / Q_n has integer-polynomial terms at every
;; positive index. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Polynomials are finite coefficient lists in ascending degree order.
;; Trailing zeroes are allowed, and polynomial equality ignores them.
;; A rational function is a numerator/denominator pair with nonzero
;; denominator; equality is the usual cross-multiplication relation. This is
;; a presentation of Q(x), not a restriction to polynomial rational
;; functions or to finitely many evaluation points.
;;
;; The base values and recurrence uniquely determine Q in the field Q(x).
;; PUTNAM-2017-A2-SEQUENCE-VALUE therefore definitionally eliminates the
;; source function parameter while retaining the original nonlinear
;; recurrence. Exact polynomial division decides whether its value is the
;; image of an integer polynomial; by uniqueness of quotient and remainder,
;; this is equivalent to the source's internal existential polynomial.

(defun putnam-2017-a2-rational-list-p (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and
       (rationalp (car coefficients))
       (putnam-2017-a2-rational-list-p (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-integer-list-p (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and
       (integerp (car coefficients))
       (putnam-2017-a2-integer-list-p (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-poly-zero-p (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (and
       (equal (car polynomial) 0)
       (putnam-2017-a2-poly-zero-p (cdr polynomial)))
    t))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-poly-equal-p (left right)
  (declare
   (xargs :measure
          (+ (acl2-count left) (acl2-count right))))
  (cond
   ((consp left)
    (and
     (equal (car left)
            (if (consp right) (car right) 0))
     (putnam-2017-a2-poly-equal-p
      (cdr left)
      (if (consp right) (cdr right) nil))))
   ((consp right)
    (and
     (equal (car right) 0)
     (putnam-2017-a2-poly-equal-p nil (cdr right))))
   (t t)))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-poly-add (left right)
  (declare
   (xargs :measure
          (+ (acl2-count left) (acl2-count right))))
  (if (or (consp left) (consp right))
      (cons
       (+ (if (consp left) (car left) 0)
          (if (consp right) (car right) 0))
       (putnam-2017-a2-poly-add
        (if (consp left) (cdr left) nil)
        (if (consp right) (cdr right) nil)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-poly-neg (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons
       (- (car polynomial))
       (putnam-2017-a2-poly-neg (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-poly-sub (left right)
  (putnam-2017-a2-poly-add
   left
   (putnam-2017-a2-poly-neg right)))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-poly-scale (coefficient polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons
       (* coefficient (car polynomial))
       (putnam-2017-a2-poly-scale coefficient (cdr polynomial)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-poly-mul (left right)
  (if (consp left)
      (putnam-2017-a2-poly-add
       (putnam-2017-a2-poly-scale (car left) right)
       (cons
        0
        (putnam-2017-a2-poly-mul (cdr left) right)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-p (value)
  (and
   (true-listp value)
   (equal (len value) 2)
   (putnam-2017-a2-rational-list-p (car value))
   (putnam-2017-a2-rational-list-p (cadr value))
   (not (putnam-2017-a2-poly-zero-p (cadr value)))))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-zero ()
  (list nil (list 1)))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-one ()
  (list (list 1) (list 1)))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-x ()
  (list (list 0 1) (list 1)))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-zero-p (value)
  (putnam-2017-a2-poly-zero-p (car value)))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-equal-p (left right)
  (putnam-2017-a2-poly-equal-p
   (putnam-2017-a2-poly-mul (car left) (cadr right))
   (putnam-2017-a2-poly-mul (car right) (cadr left))))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-add (left right)
  (list
   (putnam-2017-a2-poly-add
    (putnam-2017-a2-poly-mul (car left) (cadr right))
    (putnam-2017-a2-poly-mul (car right) (cadr left)))
   (putnam-2017-a2-poly-mul (cadr left) (cadr right))))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-neg (value)
  (list
   (putnam-2017-a2-poly-neg (car value))
   (cadr value)))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-sub (left right)
  (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-add
   left
   (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-neg right)))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-mul (left right)
  (list
   (putnam-2017-a2-poly-mul (car left) (car right))
   (putnam-2017-a2-poly-mul (cadr left) (cadr right))))

;; Inversion sends zero to zero, as in the field structure used by the Lean
;; source. Otherwise it swaps numerator and denominator.
(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-inv (value)
  (if (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-zero-p value)
      (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-zero)
    (list (cadr value) (car value))))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-div (left right)
  (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-mul
   left
   (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-inv right)))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-poly-normalize (polynomial)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (let ((tail
             (putnam-2017-a2-poly-normalize (cdr polynomial))))
        (if (and (endp tail)
                 (equal (car polynomial) 0))
            nil
          (cons (car polynomial) tail)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-monomial (coefficient degree)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix degree)))
  (if (zp degree)
      (list coefficient)
    (cons
     0
     (putnam-2017-a2-monomial coefficient (- degree 1)))))

;; The fuel is the initial numerator length. Each long-division step cancels
;; its leading term, so this bound is sufficient for the exact quotient and
;; remainder while giving ACL2 an immediate structural termination measure.
(defun putnam-2017-a2-poly-divmod-aux
    (numerator denominator fuel)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix fuel)))
  (let ((num (putnam-2017-a2-poly-normalize numerator))
        (den (putnam-2017-a2-poly-normalize denominator)))
    (if (or
         (zp fuel)
         (endp num)
         (< (len num) (len den)))
        (list nil num)
      (let* ((degree-difference
              (- (len num) (len den)))
             (coefficient
              (/ (car (last num)) (car (last den))))
             (term
              (putnam-2017-a2-monomial
               coefficient degree-difference))
             (reduced
              (putnam-2017-a2-poly-normalize
               (putnam-2017-a2-poly-sub
                num
                (putnam-2017-a2-poly-mul term den))))
             (recursive-result
              (putnam-2017-a2-poly-divmod-aux
               reduced den (- fuel 1))))
        (list
         (putnam-2017-a2-poly-add
          term (car recursive-result))
         (cadr recursive-result))))))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-poly-divmod (numerator denominator)
  (let ((num (putnam-2017-a2-poly-normalize numerator))
        (den (putnam-2017-a2-poly-normalize denominator)))
    (if (endp den)
        (list nil num)
      (putnam-2017-a2-poly-divmod-aux
       num den (len num)))))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-integer-polynomial-p (value)
  (if (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-p value)
      (let ((division
             (putnam-2017-a2-poly-divmod
              (car value) (cadr value))))
        (and
         (putnam-2017-a2-poly-zero-p (cadr division))
         (putnam-2017-a2-integer-list-p
          (putnam-2017-a2-poly-normalize
           (car division)))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2017-a2-sequence-value (n)

  (cond
   ((zp n)
    (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-one))
   ((equal n 1)
    (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-x))
   (t
    (let ((previous
           (putnam-2017-a2-sequence-value (- n 1)))
          (previous-previous
           (putnam-2017-a2-sequence-value (- n 2))))
      (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-div
       (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-sub
        (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-mul previous previous)
        (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-one))
       previous-previous)))))

;; ACL2 universally closes N. The exact division predicate is true exactly
;; when there exists an integer-coefficient polynomial equal to Q_n.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2017-a2-statement (n)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp n)
    (< 0 n))
   (putnam-2017-a2-ratfunc-integer-polynomial-p
    (putnam-2017-a2-sequence-value n))))
