title: putnam_2017_a2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a2:
-- a rational-function sequence defined from 1 and X by a nonlinear recurrence
-- has an integer-coefficient polynomial at every positive index.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2017A2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

record Field (A : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroA oneA : A
    add multiply : A -> A -> A
    negate inverse : A -> A

    one-not-zero :
      oneA != zeroA

    add-commutative :
      (x y : A) ->
      add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : A) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : A) ->
      add x zeroA == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : A) ->
      add x (negate x) == zeroA

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : A) ->
      multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : A) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : A) ->
      multiply x oneA == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : A) ->
      multiply x zeroA == zeroA
    distribute :
      (x y z : A) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)

    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroA == zeroA
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : A) ->
      x != zeroA ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneA

open Field

subtract :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  A ->
  A ->
  A
subtract fieldA x y =
  add fieldA x (negate fieldA y)

divide :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  A ->
  A ->
  A
divide fieldA x y =
  multiply fieldA x (inverse fieldA y)

square :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  A ->
  A
square fieldA x =
  multiply fieldA x x

integerValue :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  (Nat -> A) ->
  Int ->
  A
integerValue fieldA fromNat (pos n) =
  fromNat n
integerValue fieldA fromNat (negsuc n) =
  negate fieldA (fromNat (suc n))

record RationalField (A : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    fieldStructure : Field A
    fromNat : Nat -> A

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroA fieldStructure
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) ==
      add fieldStructure (fromNat n) (oneA fieldStructure)
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) ==
      add fieldStructure (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) ==
      multiply fieldStructure (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    rational-generation :
      (x : A) ->
      Exists Int
        (\ numerator ->
          Exists Nat
            (\ denominator ->
              Positive denominator
              and
              (x ==
                divide fieldStructure
                  (integerValue fieldStructure fromNat numerator)
                  (fromNat denominator))))

open RationalField

Polynomial : Set -> Set
Polynomial A =
  List A

IntegerPolynomial : Set
IntegerPolynomial =
  List Int

coefficientAt :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  Polynomial A ->
  Nat ->
  A
coefficientAt fieldA [] n =
  zeroA fieldA
coefficientAt fieldA (coefficient ∷ coefficients) zero =
  coefficient
coefficientAt fieldA (coefficient ∷ coefficients) (suc n) =
  coefficientAt fieldA coefficients n

PolynomialEqual :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  Polynomial A ->
  Polynomial A ->
  Set
PolynomialEqual fieldA p q =
  (n : Nat) ->
  coefficientAt fieldA p n ==
  coefficientAt fieldA q n

zeroPolynomial :
  {A : Set} ->
  Polynomial A
zeroPolynomial =
  []

onePolynomial :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  Polynomial A
onePolynomial fieldA =
  oneA fieldA ∷ []

variablePolynomial :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  Polynomial A
variablePolynomial fieldA =
  zeroA fieldA ∷ oneA fieldA ∷ []

addPolynomial :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  Polynomial A ->
  Polynomial A ->
  Polynomial A
addPolynomial fieldA [] q =
  q
addPolynomial fieldA p [] =
  p
addPolynomial fieldA (a ∷ p) (b ∷ q) =
  add fieldA a b ∷ addPolynomial fieldA p q

negatePolynomial :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  Polynomial A ->
  Polynomial A
negatePolynomial fieldA [] =
  []
negatePolynomial fieldA (a ∷ p) =
  negate fieldA a ∷ negatePolynomial fieldA p

scalePolynomial :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  A ->
  Polynomial A ->
  Polynomial A
scalePolynomial fieldA scalar [] =
  []
scalePolynomial fieldA scalar (a ∷ p) =
  multiply fieldA scalar a ∷ scalePolynomial fieldA scalar p

multiplyPolynomial :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  Polynomial A ->
  Polynomial A ->
  Polynomial A
multiplyPolynomial fieldA [] q =
  []
multiplyPolynomial fieldA (a ∷ p) q =
  addPolynomial fieldA
    (scalePolynomial fieldA a q)
    (zeroA fieldA ∷ multiplyPolynomial fieldA p q)

mapIntegerPolynomial :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  (Nat -> A) ->
  IntegerPolynomial ->
  Polynomial A
mapIntegerPolynomial fieldA fromNat [] =
  []
mapIntegerPolynomial fieldA fromNat (coefficient ∷ coefficients) =
  integerValue fieldA fromNat coefficient
  ∷
  mapIntegerPolynomial fieldA fromNat coefficients

NonzeroPolynomial :
  {A : Set} ->
  Field A ->
  Polynomial A ->
  Set
NonzeroPolynomial fieldA p =
  Not (PolynomialEqual fieldA p zeroPolynomial)

record RationalFunctionField
  {A : Set}
  (rationals : RationalField A)
  (K : Set) :
  Set1 where

  private
    rationalField : Field A
    rationalField =
      fieldStructure rationals

  field
    functionField : Field K
    polynomialEmbedding : Polynomial A -> K

    embedding-zero :
      polynomialEmbedding zeroPolynomial ==
      zeroA functionField
    embedding-one :
      polynomialEmbedding (onePolynomial rationalField) ==
      oneA functionField
    embedding-addition :
      (p q : Polynomial A) ->
      polynomialEmbedding (addPolynomial rationalField p q) ==
      add functionField
        (polynomialEmbedding p)
        (polynomialEmbedding q)
    embedding-negation :
      (p : Polynomial A) ->
      polynomialEmbedding (negatePolynomial rationalField p) ==
      negate functionField (polynomialEmbedding p)
    embedding-multiplication :
      (p q : Polynomial A) ->
      polynomialEmbedding (multiplyPolynomial rationalField p q) ==
      multiply functionField
        (polynomialEmbedding p)
        (polynomialEmbedding q)

    embedding-respects-equality :
      (p q : Polynomial A) ->
      PolynomialEqual rationalField p q ->
      polynomialEmbedding p == polynomialEmbedding q
    embedding-reflects-equality :
      (p q : Polynomial A) ->
      polynomialEmbedding p == polynomialEmbedding q ->
      PolynomialEqual rationalField p q

    fraction-representation :
      (r : K) ->
      Exists (Polynomial A)
        (\ numerator ->
          Exists (Polynomial A)
            (\ denominator ->
              NonzeroPolynomial rationalField denominator
              and
              (r ==
                divide functionField
                  (polynomialEmbedding numerator)
                  (polynomialEmbedding denominator))))

open RationalFunctionField

integerPolynomialImage :
  {A K : Set} ->
  (rationals : RationalField A) ->
  RationalFunctionField rationals K ->
  IntegerPolynomial ->
  K
integerPolynomialImage rationals rationalFunctions p =
  polynomialEmbedding rationalFunctions
    (mapIntegerPolynomial
      (fieldStructure rationals)
      (fromNat rationals)
      p)

module Putnam2017A2Statement
  {A K : Set}
  (rationals : RationalField A)
  (rationalFunctions : RationalFunctionField rationals K) where

  rationalField : Field A
  rationalField =
    fieldStructure rationals

  functionFieldStructure : Field K
  functionFieldStructure =
    functionField rationalFunctions

  X : K
  X =
    polynomialEmbedding rationalFunctions
      (variablePolynomial rationalField)

  Recurrence : (Nat -> K) -> Set
  Recurrence Q =
    (k : Nat) ->
    Q (suc (suc k))
    ==
    divide functionFieldStructure
      (subtract functionFieldStructure
        (square functionFieldStructure (Q (suc k)))
        (oneA functionFieldStructure))
      (Q k)

  HasIntegerPolynomialCoefficients : K -> Set
  HasIntegerPolynomialCoefficients value =
    Exists IntegerPolynomial
      (\ p ->
        value ==
        integerPolynomialImage rationals rationalFunctions p)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (Q : Nat -> K) ->
    Q zero == oneA functionFieldStructure ->
    Q (suc zero) == X ->
    Recurrence Q ->
    (n : Nat) ->
    Positive n ->
    HasIntegerPolynomialCoefficients (Q n)

putnam-2017-a2 : Set1
putnam-2017-a2 =
  (A : Set) ->
  (rationals : RationalField A) ->
  (K : Set) ->
  (rationalFunctions : RationalFunctionField rationals K) ->
  Putnam2017A2Statement.proposition rationals rationalFunctions

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a2:
  recursively defined rational functions are integer-coefficient polynomials
  at every positive index. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory ratTheory;

val putnam_2017_a2 =
  ``let finite_poly =
      \p : num -> rat. FINITE {k : num | p k <> 0};
      int_poly =
        \p : num -> int. FINITE {k : num | p k <> 0};
      poly_zero =
        (\k : num. (0 : rat));
      poly_one =
        (\k : num. if k = 0 then (1 : rat) else 0);
      poly_X =
        (\k : num. if k = 1 then (1 : rat) else 0);
      poly_add =
        (\p q : num -> rat.
           \k : num. p k + q k);
      poly_neg =
        (\p : num -> rat.
           \k : num. -(p k));
      poly_mul =
        (\p q : num -> rat.
           \k : num.
             ITSET
               (\i : num. \acc : rat. p i * q (k - i) + acc)
               (count (k + 1))
               0q);
      poly_sub =
        (\p q : num -> rat.
           poly_add p (poly_neg q));
      ratfunc_valid =
        (\r : (num -> rat) # (num -> rat).
           finite_poly (FST r) /\
           finite_poly (SND r) /\
           SND r <> poly_zero);
      ratfunc_eq =
        (\r s : (num -> rat) # (num -> rat).
           ratfunc_valid r /\
           ratfunc_valid s /\
           poly_mul (FST r) (SND s) =
             poly_mul (FST s) (SND r));
      ratfunc_zero =
        (poly_zero, poly_one);
      ratfunc_one =
        (poly_one, poly_one);
      ratfunc_X =
        (poly_X, poly_one);
      ratfunc_mul =
        (\r s : (num -> rat) # (num -> rat).
           (poly_mul (FST r) (FST s),
            poly_mul (SND r) (SND s)));
      ratfunc_sub =
        (\r s : (num -> rat) # (num -> rat).
           (poly_sub
              (poly_mul (FST r) (SND s))
              (poly_mul (FST s) (SND r)),
            poly_mul (SND r) (SND s)));
      ratfunc_inv =
        (\r : (num -> rat) # (num -> rat).
           if FST r = poly_zero
           then ratfunc_zero
           else (SND r, FST r));
      ratfunc_div =
        (\r s : (num -> rat) # (num -> rat).
           ratfunc_mul r (ratfunc_inv s));
      lift_int_poly =
        (\p : num -> int.
           \k : num. rat_of_int (p k))
    in
      !Q : num -> ((num -> rat) # (num -> rat)).
        (!n : num. ratfunc_valid (Q n)) /\
        ratfunc_eq (Q 0) ratfunc_one /\
        ratfunc_eq (Q 1) ratfunc_X /\
        (!n : num.
           ratfunc_eq
             (Q (n + 2))
             (ratfunc_div
                (ratfunc_sub
                   (ratfunc_mul (Q (n + 1)) (Q (n + 1)))
                   ratfunc_one)
                (Q n)))
        ==>
        !n : num.
          0 < n
          ==>
          ?P : num -> int.
            int_poly P /\
            ratfunc_eq (Q n) (lift_int_poly P, poly_one)``;

title: putnam_2017_a2

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2017_a2: the rational-function sequence beginning with 1 and X and
  satisfying the stated nonlinear recurrence has integer-coefficient
  polynomial terms at every positive index. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P17A2QFld is Set.mm's rational subfield of the complex field. P17A2QPoly and
  P17A2ZPoly are its univariate polynomial ring and the univariate polynomial
  ring over the integers. P17A2RatFunc is the field of fractions of
  P17A2QPoly, hence the rational-function field over QQ. P17A2Embed is the
  canonical embedding p |-> p/1 into that field.

  The recurrence uses the native subtraction and total division operations of
  P17A2RatFunc, so it also agrees with the source field semantics when a
  divisor is zero. In the conclusion, P is an integer polynomial and p is its
  coefficientwise image under the canonical integer-to-rational homomorphism;
  Q(n) is then the embedded rational polynomial p. Thus the internal
  integer-polynomial witness and the arbitrary rational-function domain are
  both preserved.

  All declarations below are unproved $a statement encodings; this database
  contains no $p proof statement.
$)

$c P17A2QFld P17A2QPoly P17A2ZPoly P17A2RatFunc P17A2Embed $.

p17a2-qfld-syntax $a class P17A2QFld $.
p17a2-qpoly-syntax $a class P17A2QPoly $.
p17a2-zpoly-syntax $a class P17A2ZPoly $.
p17a2-ratfunc-syntax $a class P17A2RatFunc $.
p17a2-embed-syntax $a class P17A2Embed $.

p17a2-qfld-definition $a |-
  P17A2QFld = ( CCfld |`s QQ ) $.

p17a2-qpoly-definition $a |-
  P17A2QPoly = ( Poly1 ` P17A2QFld ) $.

p17a2-zpoly-definition $a |-
  P17A2ZPoly = ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) $.

p17a2-ratfunc-definition $a |-
  P17A2RatFunc = ( Frac ` P17A2QPoly ) $.

${
  p17a2-embed-definition $a |- P17A2Embed =
    (
      p e. ( Base ` P17A2QPoly ) |->
        [
          <. p , ( 1r ` P17A2QPoly ) >.
        ]
        ( P17A2QPoly ~RL ( RLReg ` P17A2QPoly ) )
    ) $.
$}

${
  $d P Q k n p $.

  putnambench-putnam-2017-a2 $a |-
    A. Q e. ( ( Base ` P17A2RatFunc ) ^m NN0 )
      (
        (
          (
            ( Q ` 0 )
            =
            ( P17A2Embed ` ( 1r ` P17A2QPoly ) )
            /\
            ( Q ` 1 )
            =
            ( P17A2Embed ` ( var1 ` P17A2QFld ) )
          )
          /\
          A. n e. NN0
            ( Q ` ( n + 2 ) )
            =
            (
              (
                (
                  ( Q ` ( n + 1 ) )
                  ( .r ` P17A2RatFunc )
                  ( Q ` ( n + 1 ) )
                )
                ( -g ` P17A2RatFunc )
                ( 1r ` P17A2RatFunc )
              )
              ( /r ` P17A2RatFunc )
              ( Q ` n )
            )
        )
        ->
        A. n e. NN
          E. P e. ( Base ` P17A2ZPoly )
            E. p e. ( Base ` P17A2QPoly )
              (
                A. k e. NN0
                  (
                    ( ( coe1 ` p ) ` k )
                    =
                    (
                      ( ZRHom ` P17A2QFld )
                      `
                      ( ( coe1 ` P ) ` k )
                    )
                  )
                /\
                ( Q ` n ) = ( P17A2Embed ` p )
              )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2017_a2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a2:
% a rational-function sequence with Q_0(x) = 1, Q_1(x) = x, and the stated
% recurrence has an integer-coefficient polynomial at every positive index.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2017_a2: THEORY
BEGIN
  rational_polynomial: TYPE = list[rat]
  integer_polynomial: TYPE = list[int]

  polynomial_coefficient(
      polynomial: rational_polynomial,
      degree: nat): RECURSIVE rat =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: 0,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        IF degree = 0 THEN
          coefficient
        ELSE
          polynomial_coefficient(tail, degree - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  polynomial_equal(
      left, right: rational_polynomial): bool =
    FORALL (degree: nat):
      polynomial_coefficient(left, degree)
        = polynomial_coefficient(right, degree)

  polynomial_add(
      left, right: rational_polynomial):
      RECURSIVE rational_polynomial =
    CASES left OF
      null: right,
      cons(left_coefficient, left_tail):
        CASES right OF
          null: left,
          cons(right_coefficient, right_tail):
            cons(
              left_coefficient + right_coefficient,
              polynomial_add(left_tail, right_tail))
        ENDCASES
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE left BY <<

  polynomial_negate(
      polynomial: rational_polynomial):
      RECURSIVE rational_polynomial =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: null,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        cons(-coefficient, polynomial_negate(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  polynomial_subtract(
      left, right: rational_polynomial):
      rational_polynomial =
    polynomial_add(left, polynomial_negate(right))

  polynomial_scale(
      scalar: rat,
      polynomial: rational_polynomial):
      RECURSIVE rational_polynomial =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: null,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        cons(
          scalar * coefficient,
          polynomial_scale(scalar, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  polynomial_multiply(
      left, right: rational_polynomial):
      RECURSIVE rational_polynomial =
    CASES left OF
      null: null,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        polynomial_add(
          polynomial_scale(coefficient, right),
          cons(0, polynomial_multiply(tail, right)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE left BY <<

  polynomial_zero: rational_polynomial = null

  polynomial_one: rational_polynomial =
    cons((1 :: rat), null)

  polynomial_X: rational_polynomial =
    cons((0 :: rat), cons((1 :: rat), null))

  rational_function_representation: TYPE =
    [# numerator: rational_polynomial,
       denominator: rational_polynomial #]

  valid_rational_function(
      value: rational_function_representation): bool =
    NOT polynomial_equal(denominator(value), polynomial_zero)

  rational_function_equal(
      left, right: rational_function_representation): bool =
    polynomial_equal(
      polynomial_multiply(
        numerator(left), denominator(right)),
      polynomial_multiply(
        numerator(right), denominator(left)))

  rational_zero: rational_function_representation =
    (# numerator := polynomial_zero,
       denominator := polynomial_one #)

  rational_one: rational_function_representation =
    (# numerator := polynomial_one,
       denominator := polynomial_one #)

  rational_X: rational_function_representation =
    (# numerator := polynomial_X,
       denominator := polynomial_one #)

  rational_add(
      left, right: rational_function_representation):
      rational_function_representation =
    (# numerator :=
         polynomial_add(
           polynomial_multiply(
             numerator(left), denominator(right)),
           polynomial_multiply(
             numerator(right), denominator(left))),
       denominator :=
         polynomial_multiply(
           denominator(left), denominator(right)) #)

  rational_negate(
      value: rational_function_representation):
      rational_function_representation =
    (# numerator := polynomial_negate(numerator(value)),
       denominator := denominator(value) #)

  rational_subtract(
      left, right: rational_function_representation):
      rational_function_representation =
    rational_add(left, rational_negate(right))

  rational_multiply(
      left, right: rational_function_representation):
      rational_function_representation =
    (# numerator :=
         polynomial_multiply(
           numerator(left), numerator(right)),
       denominator :=
         polynomial_multiply(
           denominator(left), denominator(right)) #)

  rational_inverse(
      value: rational_function_representation):
      rational_function_representation =
    IF polynomial_equal(numerator(value), polynomial_zero) THEN
      rational_zero
    ELSE
      (# numerator := denominator(value),
         denominator := numerator(value) #)
    ENDIF

  rational_divide(
      left, right: rational_function_representation):
      rational_function_representation =
    rational_multiply(left, rational_inverse(right))

  rational_square(
      value: rational_function_representation):
      rational_function_representation =
    rational_multiply(value, value)

  map_integer_polynomial(
      polynomial: integer_polynomial):
      RECURSIVE rational_polynomial =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: null,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        cons(
          (coefficient :: rat),
          map_integer_polynomial(tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  rational_of_integer_polynomial(
      polynomial: integer_polynomial):
      rational_function_representation =
    (# numerator := map_integer_polynomial(polynomial),
       denominator := polynomial_one #)

  rational_function_sequence: TYPE =
    [nat -> rational_function_representation]

  valid_sequence(Q: rational_function_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      valid_rational_function(Q(index))

  has_base_values(Q: rational_function_sequence): bool =
    rational_function_equal(Q(0), rational_one)
      AND rational_function_equal(Q(1), rational_X)

  has_recurrence(Q: rational_function_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      rational_function_equal(
        Q(index + 2),
        rational_divide(
          rational_subtract(
            rational_square(Q(index + 1)),
            rational_one),
          Q(index)))

  putnam_2017_a2: bool =
    FORALL (Q: rational_function_sequence), (n: nat):
      (valid_sequence(Q)
        AND has_base_values(Q)
        AND has_recurrence(Q)
        AND n > 0)
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (P: integer_polynomial):
          rational_function_equal(
            Q(n),
            rational_of_integer_polynomial(P))
END putnam_2017_a2

-- Note: uses (ℝ → ℝ) instead of (Set.Icc a b → Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ))
/--
Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers with $a< b$, and let $f$ and $g$ be continuous functions from $[a,b]$ to $(0,\infty)$ such that $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\int_a^b g(x)\,dx$ but $f \neq g$. For every positive integer $n$, define $I_n=\int_a^b \frac{(f(x))^{n+1}}{(g(x))^n}\,dx$. Show that $I_1,I_2,I_3,\dots$ is an increasing sequence with $\lim_{n \to \infty} I_n=\infty$.
-/
theorem putnam_2017_a3
(a b : ℝ)
(f g : ℝ → ℝ)
(I : ℕ → ℝ)
(altb : a < b)
(fgcont : ContinuousOn f (Set.Icc a b) ∧ ContinuousOn g (Set.Icc a b))
(fgimg : f '' (Set.Icc a b) ⊆ Set.Ioi 0 ∧ g '' (Set.Icc a b) ⊆ Set.Ioi 0)
(fgint : ∫ x in Set.Ioo a b, f x = ∫ x in Set.Ioo a b, g x)
(fneg : ∃ x : Set.Icc a b, f x ≠ g x)
(hI : ∀ n > 0, I n = ∫ x in Set.Ioo a b, ((f x) ^ (n + 1)) / ((g x) ^ n))
: (∀ n > 0, I (n + 1) > I n) ∧ Tendsto I atTop atTop :=
sorry

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a3
  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2017_a3): strict growth and divergence to
  positive infinity of an integral sequence formed from two distinct positive
  continuous functions with equal integrals. This file contains no proof.
*)

let analysis_output = open_out "/dev/null";;
let analysis_formatter = Format.formatter_of_out_channel analysis_output;;
let analysis_loaded =
  Toploop.use_file analysis_formatter "Library/transc.ml";;
Format.pp_print_flush analysis_formatter ();;
close_out analysis_output;;
if not analysis_loaded then failwith "failed to load Library/transc.ml";;

let statement =
  `let continuous_on_interval =
     \(a:real) (b:real) (h:real->real).
       !x:real.
         a <= x /\ x <= b
         ==> !e:real.
               &0 < e
               ==> ?d:real.
                     &0 < d /\
                     !y:real.
                       a <= y /\ y <= b /\ abs (y - x) < d
                       ==> abs (h y - h x) < e in
   let tends_to_posinfinity =
     \(u:num->real).
       !M:real.
         ?N:num.
           !n:num. N <= n ==> M <= u n in
   !a b:real. !f g:real->real. !seq:num->real.
     a < b /\
     continuous_on_interval a b f /\
     continuous_on_interval a b g /\
     (!x:real.
        a <= x /\ x <= b
        ==> &0 < f x /\ &0 < g x) /\
     integral(a,b) f = integral(a,b) g /\
     (?x:real. a <= x /\ x <= b /\ ~(f x = g x)) /\
     (!n:num.
        0 < n
        ==> seq n =
            integral(a,b)
              (\x:real. (f x) pow (n + 1) / (g x) pow n))
     ==>
     (!n:num. 0 < n ==> seq n < seq (n + 1)) /\
     tends_to_posinfinity seq`;;

title: putnam_2017_a3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a3:
;; strict growth and divergence of integral power ratios for distinct positive
;; continuous real functions with equal integrals. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The three DEFSTUB symbols are arbitrary regular Cauchy names, not
;; rational-valued functions or finite tables.  F-APPROX(x,e) and
;; G-APPROX(x,e), for rational x in [0,1], name the function values to error
;; at most e; I-APPROX(n,e) similarly names I_n.  Every real has such a name.
;; Conversely, the regularity inequalities below make each name converge to a
;; unique real.
;;
;; Uniformly continuous Cauchy data on the rational points of [0,1] extend
;; uniquely to continuous real functions on [0,1], and restriction gives the
;; inverse representation.  Thus the DEFSTUB symbols cover arbitrary source
;; functions.  Values outside the source interval are irrelevant, and every
;; continuous interval function has a continuous total extension.
;;
;; The positive affine substitution x=a+(b-a)t is bidirectional: from source
;; f and g define F(t)=(b-a)f(x) and G(t)=(b-a)g(x).  It preserves positivity,
;; distinctness, both base integrals, every displayed moment integral, and the
;; sequence I.  Conversely, [0,1] is a source interval.  Hence the normalized
;; statement below is equivalent in both directions to the source theorem.
;;
;; All integral predicates are unbounded double limits of right Riemann sums:
;; subdivisions tend to infinity and Cauchy-name precision tends to zero.
;; For continuous functions these limits are exactly the source integrals;
;; endpoint inclusion is immaterial.  The strict-order witnesses and rational
;; at-top bounds are also exact: regular-name error estimates give both
;; directions, and rational bounds are cofinal in the reals.
;;
;; The antecedent is non-vacuous.  Standard Cauchy names for F(t)=t+1/2,
;; G(t)=1, and I_n=integral_0^1 F(t)^(n+1) dt satisfy it: F and G are positive
;; continuous and distinct, and both base integrals equal 1.

(defstub p17a3-f-approx (x precision) t)
(defstub p17a3-g-approx (x precision) t)
(defstub p17a3-i-approx (n precision) t)

(defun p17a3-positive-rational-p (value)
  (and
   (rationalp value)
   (< 0 value)))

(defun p17a3-unit-rational-p (value)
  (and
   (rationalp value)
   (<= 0 value)
   (<= value 1)))

(defun p17a3-function-approx (which x precision)
  (if (equal which :f)
      (p17a3-f-approx x precision)
    (p17a3-g-approx x precision)))

;; Regular Cauchy names represent exact real values at every rational point.

(defun-sk p17a3-function-regular-p (which)
  (forall (x epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (p17a3-unit-rational-p x)
      (p17a3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (p17a3-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((left
            (p17a3-function-approx which x epsilon))
           (right
            (p17a3-function-approx which x eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<=
         (abs (- left right))
         (+ epsilon eta)))))))

(defun-sk p17a3-sequence-regular-p ()
  (forall (n epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (p17a3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (p17a3-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((left
            (p17a3-i-approx n epsilon))
           (right
            (p17a3-i-approx n eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<=
         (abs (- left right))
         (+ epsilon eta)))))))

;; This rational epsilon-delta condition is equivalent to uniform continuity
;; of the represented function.  Compactness makes it equivalent to the
;; source's ordinary continuity on the closed interval.

(defun-sk p17a3-uniform-continuity-scale-p
    (which epsilon delta)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (p17a3-unit-rational-p x)
      (p17a3-unit-rational-p y)
      (< (abs (- x y)) delta))
     (<
      (abs
       (-
        (p17a3-function-approx
         which x (* 1/8 epsilon))
        (p17a3-function-approx
         which y (* 1/8 epsilon))))
      (* 3/4 epsilon)))))

(defun-sk p17a3-uniform-continuity-radius-exists-p
    (which epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (p17a3-positive-rational-p delta)
     (p17a3-uniform-continuity-scale-p
      which epsilon delta))))

(defun-sk p17a3-continuous-on-unit-p (which)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p17a3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (p17a3-uniform-continuity-radius-exists-p
      which epsilon))))

;; A positive continuous function on a compact interval has a positive
;; minimum.  The following Cauchy-name lower margin is exactly that condition.

(defun-sk p17a3-positive-margin-p (which margin)
  (forall (x epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (p17a3-unit-rational-p x)
      (p17a3-positive-rational-p epsilon))
     (<=
      margin
      (+
       (p17a3-function-approx which x epsilon)
       epsilon)))))

(defun-sk p17a3-positive-on-unit-p (which)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (p17a3-positive-rational-p margin)
     (p17a3-positive-margin-p which margin))))

;; By density and continuity, two represented functions differ on [0,1] iff
;; they differ at a rational point.  A gap exceeding twice the name error is
;; equivalent to strict inequality of the corresponding exact real values.

(defun-sk p17a3-functions-distinct-on-unit-p ()
  (exists (x precision)
    (and
     (p17a3-unit-rational-p x)
     (p17a3-positive-rational-p precision)
     (<
      (* 2 precision)
      (abs
       (-
        (p17a3-f-approx x precision)
        (p17a3-g-approx x precision)))))))

;; Exact rational approximations to uniform right-endpoint Riemann sums.

(defun p17a3-function-grid-sum-aux
    (which subdivisions remaining precision)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (+
     (p17a3-function-approx
      which
      (/ remaining subdivisions)
      precision)
     (p17a3-function-grid-sum-aux
      which
      subdivisions
      (- remaining 1)
      precision))))

(defun p17a3-function-grid-sum
    (which subdivisions precision)
  (if (posp subdivisions)
      (/
       (p17a3-function-grid-sum-aux
        which subdivisions subdivisions precision)
       subdivisions)
    0))

(defun p17a3-moment-grid-sum-aux
    (n subdivisions remaining precision)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (let* ((x (/ remaining subdivisions))
           (left
            (p17a3-f-approx x precision))
           (right
            (p17a3-g-approx x precision))
           (term
            (/
             (expt left (+ n 1))
             (expt right n))))
      (+
       term
       (p17a3-moment-grid-sum-aux
        n
        subdivisions
        (- remaining 1)
        precision)))))

(defun p17a3-moment-grid-sum
    (n subdivisions precision)
  (if (and (natp n) (posp subdivisions))
      (/
       (p17a3-moment-grid-sum-aux
        n subdivisions subdivisions precision)
       subdivisions)
    0))

;; Equality of the two exact base integrals.  Both the mesh and value
;; precision quantifiers are unbounded; no finite approximation is substituted
;; for either integral.

(defun-sk p17a3-base-integral-tail-p
    (epsilon cutoff precision-bound)
  (forall (subdivisions precision)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp subdivisions)
      (<= cutoff subdivisions)
      (p17a3-positive-rational-p precision)
      (<= precision precision-bound))
     (<
      (abs
       (-
        (p17a3-function-grid-sum
         :f subdivisions precision)
        (p17a3-function-grid-sum
         :g subdivisions precision)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p17a3-base-integral-cutoffs-exist-p (epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff precision-bound)
    (and
     (posp cutoff)
     (p17a3-positive-rational-p precision-bound)
     (p17a3-base-integral-tail-p
      epsilon cutoff precision-bound))))

(defun-sk p17a3-equal-base-integrals-p ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p17a3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (p17a3-base-integral-cutoffs-exist-p epsilon))))

;; Exact equality I_n = integral F^(n+1)/G^n.  Positivity of G supplies a
;; uniform nonzero denominator below a sufficiently small precision bound.

(defun-sk p17a3-moment-value-tail-p
    (n epsilon cutoff precision-bound)
  (forall (subdivisions function-precision sequence-precision)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp subdivisions)
      (<= cutoff subdivisions)
      (p17a3-positive-rational-p function-precision)
      (<= function-precision precision-bound)
      (p17a3-positive-rational-p sequence-precision)
      (<= sequence-precision precision-bound))
     (<
      (abs
       (-
        (p17a3-moment-grid-sum
         n subdivisions function-precision)
        (p17a3-i-approx n sequence-precision)))
      epsilon))))

(defun-sk p17a3-moment-value-cutoffs-exist-p
    (n epsilon)
  (exists (cutoff precision-bound)
    (and
     (posp cutoff)
     (p17a3-positive-rational-p precision-bound)
     (p17a3-moment-value-tail-p
      n epsilon cutoff precision-bound))))

(defun-sk p17a3-moment-value-p (n)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (p17a3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (p17a3-moment-value-cutoffs-exist-p
      n epsilon))))

(defun-sk p17a3-moment-sequence-definition-p ()
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (posp n)
     (p17a3-moment-value-p n))))

;; Exact strict inequality for regular Cauchy names.

(defun-sk p17a3-strict-step-p (n)
  (exists (precision)
    (and
     (p17a3-positive-rational-p precision)
     (<
      (+
       (p17a3-i-approx n precision)
       (* 2 precision))
      (p17a3-i-approx (+ n 1) precision)))))

(defun-sk p17a3-strictly-increasing-positive-p ()
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (posp n)
     (p17a3-strict-step-p n))))

;; Exact at-top divergence.  P17A3-I-ABOVE-BOUND-P is equivalent to the exact
;; real value I_n exceeding BOUND.  Quantifying over rational BOUND is
;; equivalent to quantifying over all real bounds by rational cofinality.

(defun-sk p17a3-i-above-bound-p (n bound)
  (exists (precision)
    (and
     (p17a3-positive-rational-p precision)
     (<
      (+ bound precision)
      (p17a3-i-approx n precision)))))

(defun-sk p17a3-above-bound-tail-p (bound cutoff)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (<= cutoff n))
     (p17a3-i-above-bound-p n bound))))

(defun-sk p17a3-above-bound-cutoff-exists-p (bound)
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (p17a3-above-bound-tail-p
      bound cutoff))))

(defun-sk p17a3-tends-to-positive-infinity-p ()
  (forall (bound)
    (implies
     (rationalp bound)
     (p17a3-above-bound-cutoff-exists-p bound))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2017-a3-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (p17a3-function-regular-p :f)
    (p17a3-function-regular-p :g)
    (p17a3-sequence-regular-p)
    (p17a3-continuous-on-unit-p :f)
    (p17a3-continuous-on-unit-p :g)
    (p17a3-positive-on-unit-p :f)
    (p17a3-positive-on-unit-p :g)
    (p17a3-equal-base-integrals-p)
    (p17a3-functions-distinct-on-unit-p)
    (p17a3-moment-sequence-definition-p))
   (and
    (p17a3-strictly-increasing-positive-p)
    (p17a3-tends-to-positive-infinity-p))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2017_a3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2017_a3): distinct positive continuous real
-- functions with equal interval integrals define a strictly increasing integral
-- sequence tending to positive infinity. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2017A3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc exponent) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x exponent)
    x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

Between :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
Between reals lower upper x =
  lessOrEqual reals lower x
  and
  lessOrEqual reals x upper

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ContinuousOnInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
ContinuousOnInterval {R} reals lower upper function =
  (point : R) ->
  Between reals lower upper point ->
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        Between reals lower upper x ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals (function point) epsilon (function x)))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

SequentialLimit :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SequentialLimit reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : _) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

rightRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
rightRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals (suc i))
              step)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function value =
  SequentialLimit reals
    (\ n ->
      rightRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    value

PositiveNat : Nat -> Set
PositiveNat n =
  suc zero <=N n

TendsToPositiveInfinity :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  Set
TendsToPositiveInfinity {R} reals sequence =
  (lower-bound : R) ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      lessOrEqual reals lower-bound (sequence n))

module Putnam2017A3Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  integrand :
    (R -> R) ->
    (R -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    R ->
    R
  integrand f g n x =
    divide reals
      (naturalPower reals (f x) (suc n))
      (naturalPower reals (g x) n)

  EqualIntervalIntegrals :
    R ->
    R ->
    (R -> R) ->
    (R -> R) ->
    Set
  EqualIntervalIntegrals lower upper f g =
    Exists R
      (\ common-value ->
        IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper f common-value
        and
        IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper g common-value)

  DefinesIntegralSequence :
    R ->
    R ->
    (R -> R) ->
    (R -> R) ->
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  DefinesIntegralSequence lower upper f g I =
    (n : Nat) ->
    PositiveNat n ->
    IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper
      (integrand f g n)
      (I n)

  StrictlyIncreasingFromOne :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  StrictlyIncreasingFromOne I =
    (n : Nat) ->
    PositiveNat n ->
    StrictLess reals (I n) (I (suc n))

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (a b : R) ->
    (f g : R -> R) ->
    (I : Nat -> R) ->
    StrictLess reals a b ->
    ContinuousOnInterval reals a b f
    and
    ContinuousOnInterval reals a b g ->
    ((x : R) ->
      Between reals a b x ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (f x))
    and
    ((x : R) ->
      Between reals a b x ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (g x)) ->
    EqualIntervalIntegrals a b f g ->
    Exists R
      (\ x ->
        Between reals a b x
        and
        f x != g x) ->
    DefinesIntegralSequence a b f g I ->
    StrictlyIncreasingFromOne I
    and
    TendsToPositiveInfinity reals I

putnam-2017-a3 : Set1
putnam-2017-a3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2017A3Statement.proposition reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a3:
  strict growth and divergence to positive infinity of power-ratio integrals
  for distinct positive continuous functions with equal integrals. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_topologyTheory;
open extrealTheory sigma_algebraTheory measureTheory borelTheory;
open lebesgueTheory lebesgue_measureTheory;

val putnam_2017_a3 =
  ``!a b : real. !f g : real -> real. !I : num -> real.
      let interval_measure =
        restrict_space lebesgue (interval (a, b))
      in
      let integral_value =
        \h : real -> real.
          real
            (lebesgue$integral interval_measure
               (\x : real. Normal (h x)))
      in
        a < b /\
        f continuous_on interval [a, b] /\
        g continuous_on interval [a, b] /\
        (!x : real.
           x IN interval [a, b]
           ==>
           0 < f x /\ 0 < g x) /\
        integral_value f = integral_value g /\
        (?x : real.
           x IN interval [a, b] /\ f x <> g x) /\
        (!n : num.
           0 < n
           ==>
           I n =
             integral_value
               (\x : real.
                  f x pow (n + 1) / g x pow n))
        ==>
        (!n : num.
           0 < n ==> I n < I (n + 1)) /\
        (!B : real.
           ?N : num.
             !n : num.
               N <= n ==> B <= I n)``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2017_a3: strict increase and divergence to positive infinity of
  the integral sequence formed from two distinct positive continuous
  real functions with equal integrals. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  F and G range over all total real-valued functions, and I ranges over all
  real sequences indexed by NN0. Their restrictions to [a,b] are continuous,
  both functions are positive there, their integrals over (a,b) agree, and
  they differ at some point of [a,b].

  For every positive natural n, the displayed integral defines I(n). The
  second conclusion is the threshold definition of I tending to positive
  infinity: every real lower bound M is eventually exceeded by every term.
  This is equivalent to Tendsto I atTop atTop for a real sequence on NN0.
  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d F G I M N a b n x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2017-a3 $a |-
    A. a e. RR
      A. b e. RR
        A. F e. ( RR ^m RR )
          A. G e. ( RR ^m RR )
            A. I e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
              (
                (
                  (
                    (
                      (
                        (
                          a < b
                          /\
                          ( F |` ( a [,] b ) )
                            e. ( ( a [,] b ) -cn-> RR )
                        )
                        /\
                        ( G |` ( a [,] b ) )
                          e. ( ( a [,] b ) -cn-> RR )
                      )
                      /\
                      A. x e. ( a [,] b )
                        ( 0 < ( F ` x ) /\ 0 < ( G ` x ) )
                    )
                    /\
                    (
                      S. ( a (,) b ) ( F ` x ) _d x
                      =
                      S. ( a (,) b ) ( G ` x ) _d x
                    )
                  )
                  /\
                  E. x e. ( a [,] b ) ( F ` x ) =/= ( G ` x )
                )
                /\
                A. n e. NN
                  ( I ` n )
                  =
                  S. ( a (,) b )
                    (
                      ( ( F ` x ) ^ ( n + 1 ) )
                      /
                      ( ( G ` x ) ^ n )
                    )
                    _d x
              )
              ->
              (
                A. n e. NN
                  ( I ` n ) < ( I ` ( n + 1 ) )
                /\
                A. M e. RR
                  E. N e. NN0
                    A. n e. NN0
                      (
                        N <_ n
                        ->
                        M < ( I ` n )
                      )
              )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2017_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a3:
% positive continuous functions with equal integrals define a strictly
% increasing integral sequence that tends to positive infinity. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_2017_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  continuous_on_closed_interval(
      function_value: real_function,
      left, right: real): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      (left <= x AND x <= right) IMPLIES
        (FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
          EXISTS (delta: posreal):
            FORALL (y: real):
              (left <= y AND y <= right
                AND abs(y - x) < delta)
              IMPLIES
                abs(function_value(y) - function_value(x))
                  < epsilon_value)

  positive_on_closed_interval(
      function_value: real_function,
      left, right: real): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      (left <= x AND x <= right) IMPLIES
        function_value(x) > 0

  valid_tagged_partition(
      left, right: real,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = left
      AND points(count) = right
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          (points(index) < points(index + 1)
            AND points(index) <= tags(index)
            AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1))

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      function_value: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(
        function_value, points, tags, count - 1)
        + function_value(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_interval_integral(
      function_value: real_function,
      left, right, integral_value: real): bool =
    left < right
      AND FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
        EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
          FORALL
              (points, tags: real_sequence),
              (count: nat):
            (valid_tagged_partition(
                left, right, points, tags, count)
              AND mesh_less_than(
                points, count, mesh_bound))
            IMPLIES
              abs(
                riemann_sum(
                  function_value, points, tags, count)
                  - integral_value)
                < epsilon_value

  have_equal_interval_integrals(
      f, g: real_function,
      left, right: real): bool =
    EXISTS (integral_value: real):
      has_interval_integral(
        f, left, right, integral_value)
        AND has_interval_integral(
          g, left, right, integral_value)

  is_integral_sequence(
      f, g: real_function,
      sequence: real_sequence,
      left, right: real): bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n > 0 IMPLIES
        has_interval_integral(
          LAMBDA (x: real):
            safe_div(f(x) ^ (n + 1), g(x) ^ n),
          left,
          right,
          sequence(n))

  tends_to_positive_infinity(sequence: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (bound: real):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (n: nat):
          cutoff <= n IMPLIES bound <= sequence(n)

  putnam_2017_a3: bool =
    FORALL
        (a, b: real),
        (f, g: real_function),
        (I: real_sequence):
      (a < b
        AND continuous_on_closed_interval(f, a, b)
        AND continuous_on_closed_interval(g, a, b)
        AND positive_on_closed_interval(f, a, b)
        AND positive_on_closed_interval(g, a, b)
        AND have_equal_interval_integrals(f, g, a, b)
        AND (EXISTS (x: real):
          a <= x AND x <= b AND f(x) /= g(x))
        AND is_integral_sequence(f, g, I, a, b))
      IMPLIES
        ((FORALL (n: nat):
          n > 0 IMPLIES I(n + 1) > I(n))
          AND tends_to_positive_infinity(I))
END putnam_2017_a3

title: putnam_2017_a4
content:
import Mathlib

open Topology Filter

/--
A class with $2N$ students took a quiz, on which the possible scores were $0,1,\dots,10$. Each of these scores occurred at least once, and the average score was exactly $7.4$. Show that the class can be divided into two groups of $N$ students in such a way that the average score for each group was exactly $7.4$.
-/
theorem putnam_2017_a4
(N : ℕ)
(score : Fin (2 * N) → Fin 11)
(hsurj : ∀ k : Fin 11, ∃ i : Fin (2 * N), score i = k)
(havg : (∑ i : Fin (2 * N), (score i : ℝ)) / (2 * N) = 7.4)
: (∃ s : Finset (Fin (2 * N)), s.card = N ∧ (∑ i ∈ s, (score i : ℝ)) / N = 7.4 ∧ (∑ i ∈ sᶜ, (score i : ℝ)) / N = 7.4) :=
sorry

title: putnam_2017_a4
content:
From mathcomp Require Import all_algebra all_ssreflect.
From mathcomp Require Import reals derive normedtype sequences topology exp.
From mathcomp Require Import classical_sets cardinality.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.
Local Open Scope classical_set_scope.
Local Open Scope card_scope.

(* Note: A seq formalization seems most natural, however it seems messy to define the complement of s in score, so we omit that requirement which follows from the rest of the goal. *)
Variable R : realType.
Theorem putnam_2017_a4
    (N : nat)
    (score : seq 'I_11)
    (hscore : size score = N.*2)
    (hsurj : forall k : 'I_11, has (fun a => a == k) score)
    (avg_fun : seq 'I_11 -> R := fun s => (\sum_(i <- s) i%:R) / (size s)%:R)
    (havg : avg_fun score = 74/10)
    : exists s : seq 'I_11, subseq s score /\ size s = N /\ avg_fun s = 74/10.
Proof. Admitted.

  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2017_a4): partitioning 2N quiz scores from

let statement =

     (!i:num. i < 2 * N ==> score i < 11) /\
     (!k:num. k < 11 ==> ?i:num. i < 2 * N /\ score i = k) /\

title: putnam_2017_a4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a4:
;; a class of 2N students using every integer quiz score from 0 through 10
;; and averaging 7.4 admits two N-student groups each averaging 7.4. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The list order labels the students, so a length-2N list with entries in
;; 0,...,10 is bijective with the source function Fin(2N) -> Fin(11).
;; Selecting list positions below therefore represents an arbitrary subset of
;; students even when several students have equal scores.
(defun putnam-2017-a4-score-list-p (scores)
  (if (consp scores)
      (and
       (natp (car scores))
       (<= (car scores) 10)
       (putnam-2017-a4-score-list-p (cdr scores)))
    (equal scores nil)))

(defun putnam-2017-a4-score-sum (scores)
  (if (consp scores)
      (+ (car scores)
         (putnam-2017-a4-score-sum (cdr scores)))
    0))

(defun putnam-2017-a4-every-score-occurs-p (scores)
  (and
   (member-equal 0 scores)
   (member-equal 1 scores)
   (member-equal 2 scores)
   (member-equal 3 scores)
   (member-equal 4 scores)
   (member-equal 5 scores)
   (member-equal 6 scores)
   (member-equal 7 scores)
   (member-equal 8 scores)
   (member-equal 9 scores)
   (member-equal 10 scores)))

;; This exhaustive two-way recursion is the internal existential quantifier
;; over subsets of the labeled students. At the end, SELECTED-COUNT=N and the
;; two sum equalities say that both groups have average 37/5. Since every
;; position is placed in exactly one accumulator, the groups are complements.
(defun putnam-2017-a4-partition-search-p
    (scores n selected-count selected-sum unselected-sum)
  (if (consp scores)
      (or
       (putnam-2017-a4-partition-search-p
        (cdr scores)
        n
        (+ selected-count 1)
        (+ selected-sum (car scores))
        unselected-sum)
       (putnam-2017-a4-partition-search-p
        (cdr scores)
        n
        selected-count
        selected-sum
        (+ unselected-sum (car scores))))
    (and
     (equal selected-count n)
     (equal (* 5 selected-sum) (* 37 n))
     (equal (* 5 unselected-sum) (* 37 n)))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2017-a4-statement (n scores)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp n)
    (putnam-2017-a4-score-list-p scores)
    (equal (len scores) (* 2 n))
    (putnam-2017-a4-every-score-occurs-p scores)
    ;; sum/(2N)=37/5 is equivalent to 5*sum=74*N; the occurrence
    ;; hypothesis makes N positive, so no zero-denominator case is introduced.
    (equal
     (* 5 (putnam-2017-a4-score-sum scores))
     (* 74 n)))
   (putnam-2017-a4-partition-search-p
    scores n 0 0 0)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2017_a4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2017_a4): partitioning a class with quiz scores
-- 0 through 10 into two equal-size groups, each retaining average 7.4.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finToNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finToNat fzero = zero
finToNat (fsuc i) = suc (finToNat i)

sumFin : {n : Nat} -> (Fin n -> Nat) -> Nat
sumFin {zero} term = zero
sumFin {suc n} term =
  term fzero + sumFin (\ i -> term (fsuc i))

boolToNat : Bool -> Nat
boolToNat false = zero
boolToNat true = suc zero

notBool : Bool -> Bool
notBool false = true
notBool true = false

selectedCount :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Bool) ->
  Nat
selectedCount selected =
  sumFin (\ i -> boolToNat (selected i))

selectedScoreSum :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Fin 11) ->
  (Fin n -> Bool) ->
  Nat
selectedScoreSum score selected =
  sumFin
    (\ i ->
      boolToNat (selected i) * finToNat (score i))

totalScoreSum :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Fin 11) ->
  Nat
totalScoreSum score =
  sumFin (\ i -> finToNat (score i))

AverageIsSevenPointFour : Nat -> Nat -> Set
AverageIsSevenPointFour scoreSum studentCount =
  5 * scoreSum == 37 * studentCount

Surjective :
  {m n : Nat} ->
  (Fin m -> Fin n) ->
  Set
Surjective score =
  (k : _) ->
  Exists _ (\ i -> score i == k)

putnam-2017-a4 : Set
putnam-2017-a4 =
  (N : Nat) ->
  (score : Fin (2 * N) -> Fin 11) ->
  Surjective score ->
  AverageIsSevenPointFour
    (totalScoreSum score)
    (2 * N) ->
  Exists (Fin (2 * N) -> Bool)
    (\ selected ->
      selectedCount selected == N
      and
      (AverageIsSevenPointFour
        (selectedScoreSum score selected)
        N
      and
      AverageIsSevenPointFour
        (selectedScoreSum score (\ i -> notBool (selected i)))
        N))

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a4:
  quiz scores covering every integer from 0 through 10 with average 7.4 admit
  a partition into two equal-sized groups, each with average 7.4. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory real_sigmaTheory;

val putnam_2017_a4 =
  ``!N : num. !score : num -> num.
      (!i : num.
         i IN count (2 * N)
         ==>
         score i <= 10) /\
      (!k : num.
         k <= 10
         ==>
         ?i : num.
           i IN count (2 * N) /\
           score i = k) /\
      SIGMA
        (\i : num. &(score i))
        (count (2 * N)) /
        (&(2 * N) : real) =
        (74 : real) / 10
      ==>
      ?s : num set.
        s SUBSET count (2 * N) /\
        CARD s = N /\
        SIGMA
          (\i : num. &(score i))
          s /
          (&N : real) =
          (74 : real) / 10 /\
        SIGMA
          (\i : num. &(score i))
          (count (2 * N) DIFF s) /
          (&N : real) =
          (74 : real) / 10``;

${
  $d N f i k s $.

theorem

title: putnam_2017_a4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_a4:
% a quiz class of 2*N students attaining every score from 0 through 10 with
% average 74/10 can be split into two N-student groups with that average.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2017_a4: THEORY
BEGIN
  score_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]
  student_subset: TYPE = [nat -> bool]

  score_sum(
      score: score_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      score_sum(score, count - 1) + score(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  selected_count(
      selected: student_subset,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      selected_count(selected, count - 1)
        + IF selected(count - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  selected_score_sum(
      score: score_sequence,
      selected: student_subset,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      selected_score_sum(score, selected, count - 1)
        + IF selected(count - 1) THEN score(count - 1) ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  unselected_score_sum(
      score: score_sequence,
      selected: student_subset,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      unselected_score_sum(score, selected, count - 1)
        + IF selected(count - 1) THEN 0 ELSE score(count - 1) ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  valid_quiz_scores(N: nat, score: score_sequence): bool =
    (FORALL (i: nat):
      i < 2 * N IMPLIES score(i) <= 10)
      AND
        (FORALL (k: nat):
          k <= 10 IMPLIES
            EXISTS (i: nat):
              i < 2 * N AND score(i) = k)

  is_class_subset(N: nat, selected: student_subset): bool =
    FORALL (i: nat):
      selected(i) IMPLIES i < 2 * N

  putnam_2017_a4: bool =
    FORALL (N: nat), (score: score_sequence):
      (valid_quiz_scores(N, score)
        AND 10 * score_sum(score, 2 * N) = 74 * (2 * N))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (selected: student_subset):
          is_class_subset(N, selected)
            AND selected_count(selected, 2 * N) = N
            AND 10 * selected_score_sum(score, selected, 2 * N)
              = 74 * N
            AND 10 * unselected_score_sum(score, selected, 2 * N)
              = 74 * N
END putnam_2017_a4

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2017_b1:
   the intersection criterion for two distinct affine lines in the real plane
   via prescribed nonzero scalar multiples of displacement vectors. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2017_b1_point : Type := (R * R)%type.
Definition putnam_2017_b1_point_set : Type :=
  putnam_2017_b1_point -> Prop.

Definition putnam_2017_b1_point_zero : putnam_2017_b1_point :=
  (0, 0).

Definition putnam_2017_b1_point_add
    (p q : putnam_2017_b1_point) : putnam_2017_b1_point :=
  (fst p + fst q, snd p + snd q).

Definition putnam_2017_b1_point_sub
    (p q : putnam_2017_b1_point) : putnam_2017_b1_point :=
  (fst p - fst q, snd p - snd q).

Definition putnam_2017_b1_point_scale
    (a : R) (p : putnam_2017_b1_point) : putnam_2017_b1_point :=
  (a * fst p, a * snd p).

Definition putnam_2017_b1_affine_line
    (L : putnam_2017_b1_point_set) : Prop :=
  exists v w : putnam_2017_b1_point,
    w <> putnam_2017_b1_point_zero /\
    forall p : putnam_2017_b1_point,
      L p <->
      exists t : R,
        p =
          putnam_2017_b1_point_add
            v (putnam_2017_b1_point_scale t w).

Theorem putnam_2017_b1
    (lines : putnam_2017_b1_point_set -> Prop)
    (L1 L2 : putnam_2017_b1_point_set)
    (L1L2lines : lines L1 /\ lines L2)
    (L1L2distinct :
      ~ forall p : putnam_2017_b1_point, L1 p <-> L2 p)
    (hlines :
      forall L : putnam_2017_b1_point_set,
        lines L <-> putnam_2017_b1_affine_line L) :
  (exists p : putnam_2017_b1_point, L1 p /\ L2 p) <->
  forall lambda : R,
    lambda <> 0 ->
    forall P : putnam_2017_b1_point,
      (~ L1 P /\ ~ L2 P) ->
      exists A1 A2 : putnam_2017_b1_point,
        L1 A1 /\
        L2 A2 /\
        putnam_2017_b1_point_sub A2 P =
          putnam_2017_b1_point_scale
            lambda (putnam_2017_b1_point_sub A1 P).
Admitted.
