title: putnam_2019_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2019_b5:
;; the unique positive Fibonacci indices whose difference is the value at
;; 2019 of the degree-1008 polynomial interpolating the odd-index Fibonacci
;; values are 2019 and 1010. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; F is an arbitrary ACL2 function object. FN-EQUAL to a constant-true
;; function expresses the source's universal recurrence and integer codomain
;; over all natural indices. The recurrence and the two initial values uniquely
;; determine F at every positive index, while leaving F(0) irrelevant.

(defun putnam-2019-b5-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2019-b5-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2019-b5-quoted function)
   (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-2019-b5-true-function (formals)
  (list
   'lambda
   formals
   (putnam-2019-b5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2019-b5-integer-output-function (f)
  (let ((value (putnam-2019-b5-apply1-term f 'x)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (list
      'if
      (list 'natp 'x)
      (list 'integerp value)
      (putnam-2019-b5-quoted t)))))

(defun putnam-2019-b5-recurrence-function (f)
  (let ((fx (putnam-2019-b5-apply1-term f 'x))
        (fx1
         (putnam-2019-b5-apply1-term
          f
          (list 'binary-+ 'x (putnam-2019-b5-quoted 1))))
        (fx2
         (putnam-2019-b5-apply1-term
          f
          (list 'binary-+ 'x (putnam-2019-b5-quoted 2)))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(x)
     (list
      'if
      (list
       'if
       (list 'natp 'x)
       (list '< (putnam-2019-b5-quoted 0) 'x)
       (putnam-2019-b5-quoted nil))
      (list 'equal fx2 (list 'binary-+ fx1 fx))
      (putnam-2019-b5-quoted t)))))

(defun putnam-2019-b5-fibonacci-sequence-p (f)
  (let ((integer-output
         (putnam-2019-b5-integer-output-function f))
        (recurrence
         (putnam-2019-b5-recurrence-function f))
        (always-true
         (putnam-2019-b5-true-function '(x))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp f)
     (tamep-functionp integer-output)
     (tamep-functionp recurrence)
     (tamep-functionp always-true)
     (fn-equal integer-output always-true)
     (fn-equal recurrence always-true)
     (equal (apply$ f (list 1)) 1)
     (equal (apply$ f (list 2)) 1))))

;; Coefficients are in ascending monomial order. Although the source
;; polynomial has real coefficients, its values at the 1009 distinct rational
;; nodes 1,3,...,2017 are integers. Vandermonde uniqueness therefore forces
;; its coefficients to be rational, so this is an exact representation rather
;; than a restriction from reals to rationals.

(defun putnam-2019-b5-rational-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and
       (rationalp (car values))
       (putnam-2019-b5-rational-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-2019-b5-polynomial-eval (coefficients x)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (+ (car coefficients)
         (* x
            (putnam-2019-b5-polynomial-eval
             (cdr coefficients) x)))
    0))

(defun putnam-2019-b5-polynomial-p (coefficients)
  (and
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (equal (len coefficients) 1009)
   (putnam-2019-b5-rational-list-p coefficients)
   (not (equal (car (last coefficients)) 0))))

(defun putnam-2019-b5-interpolation-p
    (f coefficients remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (let* ((n (- 1009 remaining))
           (argument (+ (* 2 n) 1)))
      (and
       (equal
        (putnam-2019-b5-polynomial-eval
         coefficients argument)
        (apply$ f (list argument)))
       (putnam-2019-b5-interpolation-p
        f coefficients (- remaining 1))))))

;; ACL2 universally closes F, COEFFICIENTS, J, and K. Positivity of J and K
;; is explicit because the source recurrence fixes only positive-index
;; Fibonacci values; this is the guarded conclusion stated in the Lean source.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2019-b5-statement
    (f coefficients j k)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2019-b5-fibonacci-sequence-p f)
    (putnam-2019-b5-polynomial-p coefficients)
    (putnam-2019-b5-interpolation-p
     f coefficients 1009))
   (iff
    (and
     (posp j)
     (posp k)
     (equal
      (putnam-2019-b5-polynomial-eval
       coefficients 2019)
      (- (apply$ f (list j))
         (apply$ f (list k)))))
    (and
     (equal j 2019)
     (equal k 1010)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2019_b5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2019_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2019_b5): the degree-1008 real polynomial
-- interpolating odd-indexed Fibonacci numbers yields the unique positive
-- index pair (2019, 1010) in the stated difference equation. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_
infixl 6 _+Z_ _-Z_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left-choice  : A -> A or B
  right-choice : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record Pair (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor pair
  field
    left  : A
    right : B

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  oneN <=N n

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

_+Z_ : Int -> Int -> Int
pos m +Z pos n =
  pos (m + n)
pos m +Z negsuc n =
  difference m (suc n)
negsuc m +Z pos n =
  difference n (suc m)
negsuc m +Z negsuc n =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

_-Z_ : Int -> Int -> Int
x -Z y =
  x +Z negateInt y

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

record Polynomial
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set where

  field
    coefficient : Nat -> R
    degree      : Nat

    higher-coefficients-zero :
      (n : Nat) ->
      degree <N n ->
      coefficient n == zeroR reals

    leading-coefficient-nonzero :
      coefficient degree != zeroR reals

open Polynomial

evaluate :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Polynomial reals ->
  R ->
  R
evaluate reals polynomial x =
  sumFirst reals
    (suc (degree polynomial))
    (\ n ->
      multiply reals
        (coefficient polynomial n)
        (naturalPower reals x n))

FibonacciConditions :
  (Nat -> Int) ->
  Set
FibonacciConditions F =
  F oneN == pos oneN
  and
  F twoN == pos oneN
  and
  ((n : Nat) ->
    Positive n ->
    F (n + twoN) ==
    F (n + oneN) +Z F n)

InterpolationConditions :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (Nat -> Int) ->
  Polynomial reals ->
  Set
InterpolationConditions reals F polynomial =
  degree polynomial == 1008
  and
  ((n : Nat) ->
    n <=N 1008 ->
    evaluate reals polynomial
      (fromNat reals (twoN * n + oneN))
    ==
    fromInt reals (F (twoN * n + oneN)))

putnam-2019-b5-solution : Pair Nat Nat
putnam-2019-b5-solution =
  pair 2019 1010

SolutionEquation :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (Nat -> Int) ->
  Polynomial reals ->
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Set
SolutionEquation reals F polynomial j k =
  evaluate reals polynomial (fromNat reals 2019) ==
  fromInt reals (F j -Z F k)
  and
  Positive j
  and
  Positive k

putnam-2019-b5 : Set1
putnam-2019-b5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (F : Nat -> Int) ->
  (polynomial : Polynomial reals) ->
  FibonacciConditions F ->
  InterpolationConditions reals F polynomial ->
  (j k : Nat) ->
  Iff
    (SolutionEquation reals F polynomial j k)
    (pair j k == putnam-2019-b5-solution)

title: putnam_2019_b5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2019_b5:
% the degree-1008 real polynomial interpolating the odd-indexed Fibonacci
% numbers satisfies p(2019) = F_j - F_k at positive natural indices exactly
% for (j, k) = (2019, 1010). This file contains no proof.

putnam_2019_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> int]
  real_polynomial: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  solution_pair: TYPE = [# first: nat, second: nat #]

  putnam_2019_b5_solution: solution_pair =
    (# first := 2019, second := 1010 #)

  polynomial_value(
      coefficients: real_polynomial,
      degree: nat,
      x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    IF degree = 0 THEN
      coefficients(0)
    ELSE
      polynomial_value(coefficients, degree - 1, x)
        + coefficients(degree) * x ^ degree
    ENDIF
  MEASURE degree

  has_exact_degree(
      coefficients: real_polynomial,
      degree: nat): bool =
    coefficients(degree) /= 0
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        degree < index IMPLIES coefficients(index) = 0)

  is_fibonacci_sequence(F: integer_sequence): bool =
    F(1) = 1
      AND F(2) = 1
      AND (FORALL (index: nat):
        index >= 1 IMPLIES
          F(index + 2) = F(index + 1) + F(index))

  interpolates_odd_fibonacci_values(
      F: integer_sequence,
      P: real_polynomial): bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      n <= 1008 IMPLIES
        polynomial_value(P, 1008, (2 * n + 1) :: real)
          = (F(2 * n + 1) :: real)

  positive_index_equation(
      F: integer_sequence,
      P: real_polynomial,
      j, k: nat): bool =
    polynomial_value(P, 1008, 2019)
        = (F(j) :: real) - (F(k) :: real)
      AND 1 <= j
      AND 1 <= k

  putnam_2019_b5: bool =
    FORALL (F: integer_sequence), (P: real_polynomial):
      (is_fibonacci_sequence(F)
        AND has_exact_degree(P, 1008)
        AND interpolates_odd_fibonacci_values(F, P))
      IMPLIES
        (FORALL (j, k: nat):
          positive_index_equation(F, P, j, k)
            IFF
              (j = first(putnam_2019_b5_solution)
                AND k = second(putnam_2019_b5_solution)))
END putnam_2019_b5

import Mathlib

open Topology Filter Set Matrix

abbrev putnam_2019_b6_solution : Set ℕ := sorry
-- Set.Ici 1
/--
Let \( \mathbb{Z}^n \) be the integer lattice in \( \mathbb{R}^n \). Two points in \( \mathbb{Z}^n \) are called neighbors if they differ by exactly 1 in one coordinate and are equal in all other coordinates. For which integers \( n \geq 1 \) does there exist a set of points \( S \subset \mathbb{Z}^n \) satisfying the following two conditions? \begin{enumerate} \item If \( p \) is in \( S \), then none of the neighbors of \( p \) is in \( S \). \item If \( p \in \mathbb{Z}^n \) is not in \( S \), then exactly one of the neighbors of \( p \) is in \( S \). \end{enumerate}
-/
theorem putnam_2019_b6
  (n : ℕ)
  (neighbors : (Fin n → ℤ) → (Fin n → ℤ) → Prop)
  (neighbors_def : ∀ p q, neighbors p q ↔ (∃ i : Fin n, abs (p i - q i) = 1 ∧ ∀ j ≠ i, p j = q j)) :
  (1 ≤ n ∧ ∃ S : Set (Fin n → ℤ),
    (∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q, neighbors p q → q ∉ S) ∧ (∀ p ∉ S, {q ∈ S | neighbors p q}.encard = 1))
  ↔ n ∈ putnam_2019_b6_solution :=
sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2019_b6:
   existence of an independent perfect dominating set in the integer lattice
   Z^n exactly for positive dimensions. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Vectors.Fin ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Definition putnam_2019_b6_solution (n : nat) : Prop :=
  (1 <= n)%nat.

Theorem putnam_2019_b6
    (n : nat)
    (neighbors :
      (Fin.t n -> Z) -> (Fin.t n -> Z) -> Prop)
    (neighbors_def :
      forall p q : Fin.t n -> Z,
        neighbors p q <->
        exists i : Fin.t n,
          Z.abs (p i - q i) = 1 /\
          forall j : Fin.t n, j <> i -> p j = q j) :
  ((1 <= n)%nat /\
   exists S : (Fin.t n -> Z) -> Prop,
     (forall p : Fin.t n -> Z,
        S p ->
        forall q : Fin.t n -> Z,
          neighbors p q -> ~ S q) /\
     (forall p : Fin.t n -> Z,
        ~ S p ->
        exists! q : Fin.t n -> Z,
          S q /\ neighbors p q))
  <-> putnam_2019_b6_solution n.
Admitted.

(*

  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2019_b6): existence, in every positive
  dimension, of an independent perfect dominating set in the integer lattice.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let lattice_point =
     \n:num. \p:num->int.
       !i:num. n <= i ==> p i = &0 in
   let neighbors =
     \n:num. \p q:num->int.
       lattice_point n p /\
       lattice_point n q /\
       ?i:num.
         i < n /\
         abs (p i - q i) = &1 /\
         (!j:num. j < n /\ ~(j = i) ==> p j = q j) in
   let solution = {n:num | 1 <= n} in
   !n:num.
     (1 <= n /\
      ?S:(num->int)->bool.
        S SUBSET {p:num->int | lattice_point n p} /\
        (!p:num->int.
           p IN S
           ==> !q:num->int. neighbors n p q ==> ~(q IN S)) /\
        (!p:num->int.
           lattice_point n p /\ ~(p IN S)
           ==> ?!q:num->int. q IN S /\ neighbors n p q))
     <=> n IN solution`;;

title: putnam_2019_b6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2019_b6:
;; the existence of a perfect independent dominating set in the integer
;; lattice Z^n is classified by the positive dimensions. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A point of Z^n is an exact length-N list of integers. For a radius R, a
;; finite alist labels every point of the box [-R-1,R+1]^n by T or NIL, and
;; the source's two conditions are imposed on every point of [-R,R]^n.
;;
;; This finite-box formulation is bidirectionally equivalent to the source
;; existential quantifier over arbitrary subsets of Z^n. Restricting a global
;; set gives every finite labeling. Conversely, the constraints have Boolean
;; variables and finite neighborhoods, so satisfiability on every finite box
;; gives a global labeling by propositional compactness (equivalently,
;; Konig's lemma applied to the finitely branching tree of finite labelings).
;; The one-step-larger box contains every neighbor used by an inner constraint.

(defun putnam-2019-b6-point-p (point n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (equal point nil)
    (and
     (consp point)
     (integerp (car point))
     (putnam-2019-b6-point-p
      (cdr point) (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-2019-b6-coordinates-bounded-p
    (point radius)
  (if (consp point)
      (and
       (<= (abs (car point)) radius)
       (putnam-2019-b6-coordinates-bounded-p
        (cdr point) radius))
    (equal point nil)))

(defun putnam-2019-b6-in-box-p (point n radius)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (natp radius)
   (putnam-2019-b6-point-p point n)
   (putnam-2019-b6-coordinates-bounded-p
    point radius)))

(defun putnam-2019-b6-assignment-entry
    (point assignment)
  (assoc-equal point assignment))

(defun putnam-2019-b6-assignment-member-p
    (point assignment)
  (let ((entry
         (putnam-2019-b6-assignment-entry
          point assignment)))
    (and (consp entry)
         (cdr entry))))

(defun-sk putnam-2019-b6-assignment-covers-box-p
    (n radius assignment)
  (forall
   (point)
   (implies
    (putnam-2019-b6-in-box-p point n radius)
    (let ((entry
           (putnam-2019-b6-assignment-entry
            point assignment)))
      (and
       (consp entry)
       (booleanp (cdr entry)))))))

;; For a valid point these are exactly the 2N points obtained by changing one
;; coordinate by plus or minus one, with no duplicates.

(defun putnam-2019-b6-neighbor-count-aux
    (assignment point index remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      0
    (let* ((coordinate (nth index point))
           (plus-neighbor
            (update-nth index (+ coordinate 1) point))
           (minus-neighbor
            (update-nth index (- coordinate 1) point)))
      (+
       (if
           (putnam-2019-b6-assignment-member-p
            plus-neighbor assignment)
           1
         0)
       (if
           (putnam-2019-b6-assignment-member-p
            minus-neighbor assignment)
           1
         0)
       (putnam-2019-b6-neighbor-count-aux
        assignment point (+ index 1)
        (- remaining 1))))))

(defun putnam-2019-b6-neighbor-count
    (assignment point n)
  (putnam-2019-b6-neighbor-count-aux
   assignment point 0 n))

(defun putnam-2019-b6-point-condition-p
    (assignment point n)
  (let ((neighbor-count
         (putnam-2019-b6-neighbor-count
          assignment point n)))
    (if
        (putnam-2019-b6-assignment-member-p
         point assignment)
        (equal neighbor-count 0)
      (equal neighbor-count 1))))

(defun-sk putnam-2019-b6-inner-conditions-p
    (n radius assignment)
  (forall
   (point)
   (implies
    (putnam-2019-b6-in-box-p point n radius)
    (putnam-2019-b6-point-condition-p
     assignment point n))))

(defun putnam-2019-b6-valid-local-assignment-p
    (n radius assignment)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (natp radius)
   (true-listp assignment)
   (alistp assignment)
   (putnam-2019-b6-assignment-covers-box-p
    n (+ radius 1) assignment)
   (putnam-2019-b6-inner-conditions-p
    n radius assignment)))

(defun-sk putnam-2019-b6-local-assignment-exists-p
    (n radius)
  (exists
   (assignment)
   (putnam-2019-b6-valid-local-assignment-p
    n radius assignment)))

(defun-sk putnam-2019-b6-perfect-set-exists-p (n)
  (forall
   (radius)
   (implies
    (natp radius)
    (putnam-2019-b6-local-assignment-exists-p
     n radius))))

;; The published solution set is Set.Ici 1. ACL2 universally closes N, so
;; this pointwise equivalence is equality with the set of positive dimensions.

(defun putnambench-putnam-2019-b6-statement (n)
  (implies
   (natp n)
   (iff
    (and
     (<= 1 n)
     (putnam-2019-b6-perfect-set-exists-p n))
    (<= 1 n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2019_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2019_b6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2019_b6): every positive-dimensional integer
-- lattice has an independent set that uniquely dominates its complement.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infix 1 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record ExistsUniqueBy
  (A : Set)
  (equivalent : A -> A -> Set)
  (P : A -> Set) :
  Set where

  constructor uniqueWitness
  field
    value      : A
    property   : P value
    uniqueness :
      (other : A) ->
      P other ->
      equivalent other value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  oneN <=N n

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

differenceNat : Nat -> Nat -> Int
differenceNat zero zero =
  pos zero
differenceNat (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
differenceNat zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
differenceNat (suc m) (suc n) =
  differenceNat m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  differenceNat m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  differenceNat n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

subtractInt : Int -> Int -> Int
subtractInt x y =
  addInt x (negateInt y)

absoluteValue : Int -> Nat
absoluteValue (pos n) =
  n
absoluteValue (negsuc n) =
  suc n

Point : Nat -> Set
Point n =
  Fin n -> Int

PointEqual :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Point n ->
  Point n ->
  Set
PointEqual {n} p q =
  (i : Fin n) ->
  p i == q i

Neighbor :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Point n ->
  Point n ->
  Set
Neighbor {n} p q =
  Exists (Fin n)
    (\ i ->
      absoluteValue (subtractInt (p i) (q i)) == oneN
      and
      ((j : Fin n) ->
        j != i ->
        p j == q j))

record LatticeSubset (n : Nat) : Set1 where
  field
    contains :
      Point n ->
      Set
    respects-point-equality :
      (p q : Point n) ->
      PointEqual p q ->
      contains p iff contains q

open LatticeSubset

record PerfectIndependentDominatingSet (n : Nat) : Set1 where
  field
    subset :
      LatticeSubset n
    independent :
      (p : Point n) ->
      contains subset p ->
      (q : Point n) ->
      Neighbor p q ->
      Not (contains subset q)
    uniquely-dominates-complement :
      (p : Point n) ->
      Not (contains subset p) ->
      ExistsUniqueBy
        (Point n)
        PointEqual
        (\ q ->
          contains subset q
          and
          Neighbor p q)

putnam-2019-b6 : Set1
putnam-2019-b6 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  PerfectIndependentDominatingSet n

  independent perfect dominating sets in the integer lattice exist in every
  positive dimension. This file contains no proof.

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2019_b6 =
  ``let lattice_point =
      \n : num. \p : num -> int.
        !i : num. n <= i ==> p i = 0
    in
    let neighbors =
      \n : num. \p q : num -> int.
        lattice_point n p /\
        lattice_point n q /\
        ?i : num.
          i < n /\
          ABS (p i - q i) = 1 /\
          !j : num.
            j < n /\ j <> i
            ==>
            p j = q j
    in
    let solution = {n : num | 1 <= n}
    in
      !n : num.
        ((1 <= n /\
          ?S : (num -> int) set.
            (!p : num -> int.
               p IN S
               ==>
               lattice_point n p) /\
            (!p : num -> int.
               p IN S
               ==>
               !q : num -> int.
                 neighbors n p q
                 ==>
                 q NOTIN S) /\
            (!p : num -> int.
               lattice_point n p /\ p NOTIN S
               ==>
               {q : num -> int |
                  q IN S /\ neighbors n p q}
                 HAS_SIZE 1))
         <=>
         n IN solution)``;

title: putnam_2019_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2019_b6:
% the positive-dimensional integer lattices admitting an independent perfect
% dominating set are exactly those with dimension at least one. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_2019_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [nat -> int]
  point_set: TYPE = [point -> bool]

  is_lattice_point(n: nat, p: point): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index >= n IMPLIES p(index) = 0

  are_neighbors(n: nat, p, q: point): bool =
    is_lattice_point(n, p)
      AND is_lattice_point(n, q)
      AND EXISTS (coordinate: nat):
        coordinate < n
          AND abs(p(coordinate) - q(coordinate)) = 1
          AND FORALL (index: nat):
            index < n AND index /= coordinate
              IMPLIES p(index) = q(index)

  has_exactly_one_neighbor_in(
      n: nat,
      p: point,
      S: point_set): bool =
    EXISTS (q: point):
      S(q)
        AND are_neighbors(n, p, q)
        AND FORALL (r: point):
          S(r) AND are_neighbors(n, p, r)
            IMPLIES r = q

  is_independent_perfect_dominating_set(
      n: nat,
      S: point_set): bool =
    (FORALL (p: point):
      S(p) IMPLIES is_lattice_point(n, p))
      AND
    (FORALL (p, q: point):
      S(p) AND are_neighbors(n, p, q)
        IMPLIES NOT S(q))
      AND
    (FORALL (p: point):
      is_lattice_point(n, p) AND NOT S(p)
        IMPLIES has_exactly_one_neighbor_in(n, p, S))

  admits_independent_perfect_dominating_set(n: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (S: point_set):
      is_independent_perfect_dominating_set(n, S)

  putnam_2019_b6_solution(n: nat): bool =
    n >= 1

  putnam_2019_b6: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      (n >= 1
        AND admits_independent_perfect_dominating_set(n))
        IFF putnam_2019_b6_solution(n)
END putnam_2019_b6

;; the number of positive multiples of 2020 having at most 2020 decimal
;; digits and consisting of a nonempty block of ones followed by zeros is
;; 508536. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For ONES >= 1 and ZEROS >= 0, the represented number is the decimal
;; repunit with ONES digits, followed by ZEROS zero digits. Every positive
;; integer of the source form has exactly one such pair, and its number of
;; decimal digits is ONES + ZEROS. Thus counting the pairs with sum at most
;; 2020 is bijectively equivalent to taking the cardinality of the source set.

(defun putnam-2020-a1-repunit (ones)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix ones)))
  (if (zp ones)
      0
    (+ 1
       (* 10
          (putnam-2020-a1-repunit
           (- (nfix ones) 1))))))

  (* (putnam-2020-a1-repunit ones)
     (expt 10 (nfix zeros))))

(defun putnam-2020-a1-divisible-p (ones zeros)
  (equal
   (mod (putnam-2020-a1-number ones zeros) 2020)
   0))

;; Count all zero-block lengths from 0 through ZEROS for a fixed positive
;; one-block length. This is the source's existential digit description
;; internalized as an exact finite enumeration.
(defun putnam-2020-a1-count-zero-blocks (ones zeros)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix zeros)))
  (if (zp zeros)
      (if (putnam-2020-a1-divisible-p ones 0) 1 0)
    (+ (if (putnam-2020-a1-divisible-p
            ones (nfix zeros))
           1
         0)
       (putnam-2020-a1-count-zero-blocks
        ones (- (nfix zeros) 1)))))

;; Count the pairs (ONES,ZEROS) with 1 <= ONES <= MAX-DIGITS and
;; 0 <= ZEROS <= MAX-DIGITS-ONES.
(defun putnam-2020-a1-count-through-ones (ones max-digits)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix ones)))
  (if (zp ones)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2020-a1-count-zero-blocks
        (nfix ones)
        (- (nfix max-digits) (nfix ones)))
       (putnam-2020-a1-count-through-ones
        (- (nfix ones) 1)
        max-digits))))

  (equal
   (putnam-2020-a1-count-through-ones 2020 2020)
   508536))

-- the number of positive multiples of 2020 with at most 2020 decimal digits
-- whose digits are a nonempty block of ones followed by zeros is 508536.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2020A1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=_ _divides_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<= : {n : Nat} -> zero <= n
  suc<=suc : {m n : Nat} -> m <= n -> suc m <= suc n

record _divides_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  constructor quotient-witness
  field
    quotient : Nat
    equation : dividend == divisor * quotient

power : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
power base zero =
  suc zero
power base (suc exponent) =
  base * power base exponent

repunit : Nat -> Nat
repunit zero =
  zero
repunit (suc digits) =
  suc zero + 10 * repunit digits

decimalBlock : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
decimalBlock oneDigits zeroDigits =
  power 10 zeroDigits * repunit oneDigits

Qualifies : Nat -> Set
Qualifies n =
  (2020 divides n)
  and
  Exists Nat
    (\ oneDigitsTail ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ zeroDigits ->
          ((suc oneDigitsTail + zeroDigits) <= 2020)
          and
          (n == decimalBlock (suc oneDigitsTail) zeroDigits)))

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> item == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

putnam-2020-a1 : Set
putnam-2020-a1 =
  HasCardinality Qualifies 508536

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a1:
% exactly 508536 positive multiples of 2020 with at most 2020 decimal digits
% consist of consecutive ones followed by consecutive zeros. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_2020_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_set: TYPE = [nat -> bool]
  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  shifted_ones(zeros, count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      shifted_ones(zeros, count - 1)
        + 10 ^ (zeros + count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  consecutive_ones_then_zeros(value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (k, l: nat):
      l <= k
        AND value = shifted_ones(l, k - l + 1)

  qualifying_number(value: nat): bool =
    0 < value
      AND nat_divides(2020, value)
      AND value < 10 ^ 2020
      AND consecutive_ones_then_zeros(value)

  injective_below(
      enumeration: natural_sequence,
      bound: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      i < bound
        AND j < bound
        AND enumeration(i) = enumeration(j)
      IMPLIES i = j

  enumerates_exactly(
      enumeration: natural_sequence,
      set_value: natural_set,
      bound: nat): bool =
    FORALL (value: nat):
      set_value(value)
        IFF
          EXISTS (position: nat):
            position < bound
              AND enumeration(position) = value

  has_cardinality(
      set_value: natural_set,
      cardinality: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (enumeration: natural_sequence):
      injective_below(enumeration, cardinality)
        AND enumerates_exactly(
          enumeration, set_value, cardinality)

  putnam_2020_a1: bool =
    has_cardinality(qualifying_number, 508536)
END putnam_2020_a1

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a2:
-- for every nonnegative integer k, the finite sum from j = 0 through k of
-- 2^(k - j) times the binomial coefficient (k + j choose j) equals 4^k.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2020A2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

power : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
power base zero =
  one
power base (suc exponent) =
  base * power base exponent

choose : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
choose n zero =
  one
choose zero (suc j) =
  zero
choose (suc n) (suc j) =
  choose n (suc j) + choose n j

sumThrough : Nat -> (Nat -> Nat) -> Nat
sumThrough zero term =
  term zero
sumThrough (suc k) term =
  sumThrough k term + term (suc k)

putnam-2020-a2 : Set
putnam-2020-a2 =
  (k : Nat) ->
  sumThrough k
    (\ j ->
      power 2 (k - j) * choose (k + j) j)
  ==
  power 4 k

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a2:
% for every nonnegative integer k, the finite weighted binomial sum from
% j = 0 through k evaluates to 4^k. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2020_a2: THEORY
BEGIN
  binomial_coefficient(n, j: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF j = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSIF n = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      binomial_coefficient(n - 1, j - 1)
        + binomial_coefficient(n - 1, j)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  nat_subtract(n, j: nat): nat =
    IF j <= n THEN n - j ELSE 0 ENDIF

  weighted_binomial_sum(k, term_count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF term_count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET j: nat = term_count - 1 IN
        weighted_binomial_sum(k, term_count - 1)
          + 2 ^ nat_subtract(k, j)
              * binomial_coefficient(k + j, j)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE term_count

  putnam_2020_a2: bool =
    FORALL (k: nat):
      weighted_binomial_sum(k, k + 1) = 4 ^ k
END putnam_2020_a2

putnam_2020_a3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a3:
;; the series of squares of the sequence a_0 = pi/2 and
;; a_(n+1) = sin(a_n) diverges. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Every real quantity used below has a concrete rational Cauchy name.  There
;; is no external carrier or interpretation premise.  A name requested at a
;; positive rational tolerance EPSILON returns a rational within EPSILON of
;; the represented standard real.

(defun p20a3-positive-rational-p (x)
  (and (rationalp x)
       (< 0 x)))

(defun p20a3-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n
       (p20a3-factorial (- n 1)))))

;; Exact rational Taylor prefixes for arctan(z).
(defun p20a3-arctan-prefix (z terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (degree (+ (* 2 index) 1))
           (sign (if (evenp index) 1 -1)))
      (+ (p20a3-arctan-prefix z index)
         (/ (* sign (expt z degree))
            degree)))))

;; Machin's identity fixes the standard constant
;;   pi = 16 arctan(1/5) - 4 arctan(1/239).
(defun p20a3-pi-prefix (terms)
  (- (* 16 (p20a3-arctan-prefix 1/5 terms))
     (* 4 (p20a3-arctan-prefix 1/239 terms))))

;; The alternating-series error is less than 20/TERMS.  Taking strictly more
;; than 20/EPSILON terms therefore gives a rational EPSILON-approximation to
;; the standard real pi.  The term count is unbounded as EPSILON tends to zero.
(defun p20a3-pi-name-value (epsilon)
  (if (p20a3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (p20a3-pi-prefix
       (+ 1 (floor 20 epsilon)))
    0))

;; Exact rational Maclaurin prefixes for sine.
(defun p20a3-sine-prefix (x terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (degree (+ (* 2 index) 1))
           (sign (if (evenp index) 1 -1)))
      (+ (p20a3-sine-prefix x index)
         (/ (* sign (expt x degree))
            (p20a3-factorial degree))))))

;; Let A=floor(|x|)+1, D=floor(1/EPSILON)+1, and K=A^2*D.  Then A>|x|,
;; D>1/EPSILON, and the Taylor remainder after K sine terms is bounded by
;;
;;   |x|^(2K)/(2K)! < A^(2K)/K^K = (1/D)^K <= 1/D < EPSILON.
;;
;; Hence this is an exact unbounded rational Cauchy approximation to sin(x),
;; for every rational x and every requested positive rational tolerance.
(defun p20a3-sine-term-count (x epsilon)
  (if (and (rationalp x)
           (p20a3-positive-rational-p epsilon))
      (let* ((a (+ 1 (floor (abs x) 1)))
             (d (+ 1 (floor 1 epsilon))))
        (* a a d))
    1))

(defun p20a3-sine-rational-name-value (x epsilon)
  (if (and (rationalp x)
           (p20a3-positive-rational-p epsilon))
      (p20a3-sine-prefix
       x
       (p20a3-sine-term-count x epsilon))
    0))

;; This recursively names the unique source sequence.  At index zero, a
;; 2*EPSILON approximation to pi becomes an EPSILON approximation to pi/2.
;; At a successor, the previous name and the rational sine prefix each receive
;; half the error budget.  Since real sine is 1-Lipschitz, the result is within
;; EPSILON of sin(a_n).  Both the index and every precision remain unbounded.
(defun p20a3-sequence-name-value (n epsilon)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (not (p20a3-positive-rational-p epsilon))
      0
    (if (zp n)
        (/ (p20a3-pi-name-value (* 2 epsilon))
           2)
      (let* ((inner (/ epsilon 2))
             (previous
              (p20a3-sequence-name-value
               (- n 1)
               inner)))
        (p20a3-sine-rational-name-value
         previous
         inner)))))

;; The source partial sum at M is sum_{n=1}^M a_n^2.  Its exact rational name
;; uses one common approximation tolerance for its M sequence terms.
(defun p20a3-square-prefix-at-precision (m precision)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix m)))
  (if (zp m)
      0
    (let ((term
           (p20a3-sequence-name-value
            m
            precision)))
      (+ (p20a3-square-prefix-at-precision
          (- m 1)
          precision)
         (* term term)))))

;; The true iterates lie in [0,2].  With DELTA <= 1/2, their rational names
;; have absolute value below 5/2, so replacing one square changes it by less
;; than (9/2)*DELTA.  Choosing
;;
;;   DELTA <= EPSILON/(10*M)
;;
;; keeps the accumulated error in M squares below EPSILON.  Thus the function
;; below is a concrete rational Cauchy name for every finite partial sum, with
;; no finite cap on M or on the requested precision.
(defun p20a3-square-prefix-working-precision (m epsilon)
  (if (and (posp m)
           (p20a3-positive-rational-p epsilon))
      (let ((scaled (/ epsilon (* 10 m))))
        (if (< scaled 1/2)
            scaled
          1/2))
    1/2))

(defun p20a3-square-prefix-name-value (m epsilon)
  (if (and (natp m)
           (p20a3-positive-rational-p epsilon))
      (if (zp m)
          0
        (p20a3-square-prefix-at-precision
         m
         (p20a3-square-prefix-working-precision
          m
          epsilon)))
    0))

;; For an exact real partial sum S_m and its rational name q_m(epsilon),
;;
;;   q_m(epsilon) > bound + epsilon
;;
;; implies S_m > bound.  Conversely, whenever S_m > bound, some positive
;; rational epsilon smaller than half the gap makes the displayed inequality
;; true.  The precision and prefix witnesses are internal, so this predicate
;; is bidirectionally equivalent to an exact partial sum exceeding BOUND.
(defun-sk p20a3-partial-sum-above-bound-p (bound)
  (exists (m epsilon)
    (and (natp m)
         (p20a3-positive-rational-p epsilon)
         (< (+ bound epsilon)
            (p20a3-square-prefix-name-value
             m
             epsilon)))))

;; The nonnegative partial sums converge exactly when they are bounded above.
;; Rational bounds are cofinal in the reals.  Therefore universal failure of
;; rational upper bounds is equivalent, over the complete real numbers, to
;; divergence of the source series.  This is the published series statement;
;; the Rocq individual-term limit is a secondary transcription defect.
(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-2020-a3-statement ()
  (forall (bound)
    (implies (rationalp bound)
             (p20a3-partial-sum-above-bound-p
              bound))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)

:q

title: putnam_2020_a3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2020_a3): the sequence beginning at pi/2 and
-- iterated by sine has a divergent series of squared terms. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_
infix 1 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse absoluteValue : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    absolute-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (absoluteValue x)
    absolute-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      absoluteValue x == x
    absolute-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      absoluteValue x == negate x

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (absoluteValue reals (subtract reals x center))
    radius

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

alternate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  R
alternate reals zero x =
  x
alternate reals (suc n) x =
  negate reals (alternate reals n x)

evenExponent : Nat -> Nat
evenExponent n =
  n + n

oddExponent : Nat -> Nat
oddExponent n =
  suc (evenExponent n)

sineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
sineTerm reals x n =
  alternate reals n
    (divide reals
      (naturalPower reals x (oddExponent n))
      (fromNat reals (factorial (oddExponent n))))

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms value =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    value

record StandardSine
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    sine : R -> R
    pi : R

    sine-is-power-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (sineTerm reals x)
        (sine x)

    pi-positive :
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) pi
    sine-pi-zero :
      sine pi == zeroR reals
    pi-is-first-positive-sine-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      sine x == zeroR reals ->
      lessOrEqual reals pi x

open StandardSine

module Putnam2020A3Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (standardSine : StandardSine reals) where

  halfPi : R
  halfPi =
    divide reals
      (pi standardSine)
      (fromNat reals twoN)

  partialSquareSum :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Nat ->
    R
  partialSquareSum sequence zero =
    zeroR reals
  partialSquareSum sequence (suc n) =
    add reals
      (partialSquareSum sequence n)
      (square reals (sequence (suc n)))

  SquareSeriesConverges :
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  SquareSeriesConverges sequence =
    Exists R
      (\ limit ->
        ConvergesTo reals
          (partialSquareSum sequence)
          limit)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (sequence : Nat -> R) ->
    sequence zero == halfPi ->
    ((n : Nat) ->
      sequence (suc n) ==
      sine standardSine (sequence n)) ->
    SquareSeriesConverges sequence iff Bottom

putnam-2020-a3 : Set1
putnam-2020-a3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (standardSine : StandardSine reals) ->
  Putnam2020A3Statement.proposition reals standardSine

title: putnam_2020_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a3:
% the squared terms of the sine recurrence beginning at pi/2 form a divergent
% infinite series. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2020_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  alternating_sign(index: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -alternating_sign(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  leibniz_partial_sum(count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        leibniz_partial_sum(count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              alternating_sign(index),
              (2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  is_pi(value: real): bool =
    converges_to(
      LAMBDA (count: nat):
        4 * leibniz_partial_sum(count),
      value)

  pi: real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        is_pi(value))

  sine_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        sine_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              ((-1 :: real) ^ index) * x ^ (2 * index + 1),
              nat_factorial(2 * index + 1) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  sine(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            sine_partial(x, count),
          value))

  square_partial_sum(a: real_sequence, upper: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF upper = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      square_partial_sum(a, upper - 1) + a(upper) ^ 2
    ENDIF
  MEASURE upper

  square_series_converges(a: real_sequence): bool =
    EXISTS (limit_value: real):
      converges_to(
        LAMBDA (upper: nat):
          square_partial_sum(a, upper),
        limit_value)

  putnam_2020_a3_solution: bool = FALSE

  putnam_2020_a3: bool =
    FORALL (a: real_sequence):
      (a(0) = pi / 2
        AND (FORALL (n: nat):
          a(n + 1) = sine(a(n))))
      IMPLIES
        (square_series_converges(a)
          IFF putnam_2020_a3_solution)
END putnam_2020_a3

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a5:
   the greatest integer having exactly 2020 representations by sets of
   positive indices whose Fibonacci values sum to it. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List Sorting.Sorted ZArith.

Open Scope Z_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_2020_a5_fibonacci_pair (n : nat) : nat * nat :=
  match n with
  | O => (O, 1%nat)
  | S k =>
      let '(a, b) := putnam_2020_a5_fibonacci_pair k in
      (b, (a + b)%nat)
  end.

Definition putnam_2020_a5_fibonacci (n : nat) : nat :=
  fst (putnam_2020_a5_fibonacci_pair n).

Definition putnam_2020_a5_canonical_set (indices : list nat) : Prop :=
  StronglySorted Nat.lt indices /\
  Forall (fun k : nat => (0 < k)%nat) indices.

Definition putnam_2020_a5_sum (indices : list nat) : nat :=
  fold_right Nat.add 0%nat (map putnam_2020_a5_fibonacci indices).

Definition putnam_2020_a5_represents
    (n : Z) (indices : list nat) : Prop :=
  putnam_2020_a5_canonical_set indices /\
  Z.of_nat (putnam_2020_a5_sum indices) = n.

Definition putnam_2020_a5_has_cardinality
    {A : Type} (P : A -> Prop) (cardinality : nat) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list A,
    NoDup enumeration /\
    length enumeration = cardinality /\
    forall x : A, In x enumeration <-> P x.

Definition putnam_2020_a5_is_greatest
    (P : Z -> Prop) (greatest : Z) : Prop :=
  P greatest /\
  forall n : Z, P n -> n <= greatest.

Definition putnam_2020_a5_solution : Z :=
  Z.of_nat (putnam_2020_a5_fibonacci 4040%nat) - 1.

Theorem putnam_2020_a5 :
  putnam_2020_a5_is_greatest
    (fun n : Z =>
      putnam_2020_a5_has_cardinality
        (putnam_2020_a5_represents n)
        2020%nat)
    putnam_2020_a5_solution.
Admitted.

title: putnam_2020_a5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a5:
;; the greatest integer having exactly 2020 representations as a sum of
;; Fibonacci numbers at distinct positive indices is F_4040 - 1. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; This is the source Fibonacci sequence, including F_0 = 0, F_1 = 1.
(defun putnam-2020-a5-fibonacci (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      0
    (if (equal n 1)
        1
      (+ (putnam-2020-a5-fibonacci (- n 1))
         (putnam-2020-a5-fibonacci (- n 2))))))

;; Count subsets of {1,...,INDEX} whose Fibonacci values sum to REMAINING.
;; The two recursive branches omit or include INDEX, so each extensional
;; subset is counted exactly once; in particular the two indices with value
;; one remain distinct choices.
(defun putnam-2020-a5-subset-count-through (index remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (zp index)
      (if (equal remaining 0) 1 0)
    (let* ((current (nfix index))
           (weight (putnam-2020-a5-fibonacci current))
           (previous (- current 1)))
      (+ (putnam-2020-a5-subset-count-through
          previous remaining)
         (if (and (integerp remaining)
                  (<= weight remaining))
             (putnam-2020-a5-subset-count-through
              previous (- remaining weight))
           0)))))

;; For every positive k, F_k >= k-1. Hence a set with Fibonacci sum n cannot
;; contain an index above n+1. Enumerating subsets through n+1 is therefore
;; exactly the source cardinality over all finite sets, not a bounded-domain
;; approximation. For negative n the source set is empty and its cardinality
;; is zero.
(defun putnam-2020-a5-representation-count (n)
  (if (natp n)
      (putnam-2020-a5-subset-count-through (+ n 1) n)
    0))

(defun putnam-2020-a5-solution ()
  (- (putnam-2020-a5-fibonacci 4040) 1))

;; The source assumption uniquely defines a(n), so it is inlined above.
;; ACL2 universally closes N: the first conjunct places the designated
;; solution in {n | a(n)=2020}, and the implication says every member of that
;; set is at most the solution. Together these are exactly IsGreatest.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2020-a5-statement (n)
  (let ((solution (putnam-2020-a5-solution)))
    (and
     (equal
      (putnam-2020-a5-representation-count solution)
      2020)
     (implies
      (and
       (integerp n)
       (equal
        (putnam-2020-a5-representation-count n)
        2020))
      (<= n solution)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2020_a5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2020_a5): the largest integer for which exactly
-- 2020 finite sets of positive indices have their Fibonacci numbers sum to it
-- is the 4040th Fibonacci number minus one. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2020A5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<N_ _<=Z_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data _<=Z_ : Int -> Int -> Set where
  negative<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    negsuc m <=Z pos n
  positive<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    m <=N n ->
    pos m <=Z pos n
  negative<=negative :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    n <=N m ->
    negsuc m <=Z negsuc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> item == enumerate index)
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

record FiniteNatSet : Set where
  constructor finiteNatSet
  field
    membership      : Nat -> Bool
    size            : Nat
    has-cardinality :
      HasCardinality
        (\ n -> membership n == true)
        size

open FiniteNatSet
open HasCardinality

SameFiniteNatSet :
  FiniteNatSet ->
  FiniteNatSet ->
  Set
SameFiniteNatSet left right =
  (n : Nat) ->
  membership left n == membership right n

record HasExtensionalCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : A -> Set)
  (equivalent : A -> A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate-extensional :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member-extensional :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate-extensional index)
    enumeration-complete-extensional :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index ->
          equivalent item (enumerate-extensional index))
    enumeration-injective-extensional :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      equivalent
        (enumerate-extensional left-index)
        (enumerate-extensional right-index) ->
      left-index == right-index

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

fibonacci : Nat -> Nat
fibonacci zero =
  zero
fibonacci (suc zero) =
  oneN
fibonacci (suc (suc n)) =
  fibonacci n + fibonacci (suc n)

sumFin :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Nat) ->
  Nat
sumFin {zero} terms =
  zero
sumFin {suc n} terms =
  terms fzero
  + sumFin (\ index -> terms (fsuc index))

fibonacciSum : FiniteNatSet -> Nat
fibonacciSum finiteSet =
  sumFin
    (\ index ->
      fibonacci
        (enumerate (has-cardinality finiteSet) index))

AllIndicesPositive : FiniteNatSet -> Set
AllIndicesPositive finiteSet =
  (n : Nat) ->
  membership finiteSet n == true ->
  zero <N n

Represents :
  Int ->
  FiniteNatSet ->
  Set
Represents total finiteSet =
  AllIndicesPositive finiteSet
  and
  pos (fibonacciSum finiteSet) == total

RepresentationCount :
  Int ->
  Nat ->
  Set
RepresentationCount total count =
  HasExtensionalCardinality
    (Represents total)
    SameFiniteNatSet
    count

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

putnam-2020-a5-solution : Int
putnam-2020-a5-solution =
  difference (fibonacci 4040) oneN

IsGreatestInt :
  (Int -> Set) ->
  Int ->
  Set
IsGreatestInt property greatest =
  property greatest
  and
  ((n : Int) ->
    property n ->
    n <=Z greatest)

putnam-2020-a5 : Set
putnam-2020-a5 =
  IsGreatestInt
    (\ n -> RepresentationCount n 2020)
    putnam-2020-a5-solution

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a5:
% the largest integer having exactly 2020 representations as a sum of
% distinct positive-index Fibonacci numbers is F_4040 - 1. This file contains
% no proof.

putnam_2020_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  IMPORTING finite_sets@finite_sets_sum_real[nat]

  natural_set: TYPE = finite_set[nat]

  IMPORTING finite_sets[natural_set]

  fibonacci(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSIF index = 1 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      fibonacci(index - 1) + fibonacci(index - 2)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  qualifying_representation(S: natural_set, total: int): bool =
    (FORALL (index: nat): S(index) IMPLIES index > 0)
      AND sum(
        S,
        (LAMBDA (index: nat): fibonacci(index) :: real))
          = (total :: real)

  has_exactly_2020_representations(total: int): bool =
    EXISTS (representations: finite_set[natural_set]):
      card(representations) = 2020
        AND (FORALL (S: natural_set):
          representations(S)
            IFF qualifying_representation(S, total))

  putnam_2020_a5_solution: int =
    (fibonacci(4040) :: int) - 1

  putnam_2020_a5: bool =
    has_exactly_2020_representations(putnam_2020_a5_solution)
      AND (FORALL (total: int):
        has_exactly_2020_representations(total)
          IMPLIES total <= putnam_2020_a5_solution)
END putnam_2020_a5

import Mathlib

open Filter Topology Set

noncomputable abbrev putnam_2020_a6_solution : ℝ := sorry
-- Real.pi / 4
/--
For a positive integer $N$, let $f_N$ be the function defined by
\[
f_N(x) = \sum_{n=0}^N \frac{N+1/2-n}{(N+1)(2n+1)} \sin((2n+1)x).
\]
Determine the smallest constant $M$ such that $f_N(x) \leq M$ for all $N$ and all real $x$.
-/
theorem putnam_2020_a6
  (f : ℤ → (ℝ → ℝ))
  (hf : f = fun N : ℤ => fun x : ℝ =>
    ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 0 N, (N + 1/2 - n)/((N + 1)*(2*n + 1)) * Real.sin ((2*n + 1)*x))
  : putnam_2020_a6_solution = sSup {y | ∃ᵉ (N > 0) (x : ℝ), y = f N x} :=
sorry

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a6:
;; the least upper bound, over positive integers N and real x, of the given
;; weighted odd-sine sum is pi/4. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A pair (A . B) represents A+B*i. For rational A and B on the unit circle,
;; the imaginary part of (A+B*i)^m is sin(m*x) for some real x. Rational
;; points are dense in the unit circle, and each finite sum below is a
;; continuous polynomial in A and B. Consequently, bounding these rational
;; points is equivalent to bounding the source sum for every real x; this is
;; not a restriction of the real domain to rational x.
(defun putnam-2020-a6-pair-multiply (left right)
  (let ((a (car left))
        (b (cdr left))
        (c (car right))
        (d (cdr right)))
    (cons (- (* a c) (* b d))
          (+ (* a d) (* b c)))))

(defun putnam-2020-a6-pair-power (a b exponent)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix exponent)))
  (if (zp exponent)
      (cons 1 0)
    (putnam-2020-a6-pair-multiply
     (cons a b)
     (putnam-2020-a6-pair-power
      a b (- exponent 1)))))

(defun putnam-2020-a6-odd-sine-value (a b index)
  (cdr
   (putnam-2020-a6-pair-power
    a b (+ (* 2 index) 1))))

(defun putnam-2020-a6-weighted-term (n index a b)
  (* (/ (- (+ n (/ 1 2)) index)
        (* (+ n 1) (+ (* 2 index) 1)))
     (putnam-2020-a6-odd-sine-value
      a b index)))

(defun putnam-2020-a6-sum-through (n index a b)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (zp index)
      (putnam-2020-a6-weighted-term n 0 a b)
    (+ (putnam-2020-a6-weighted-term
        n index a b)
       (putnam-2020-a6-sum-through
        n (- index 1) a b))))

(defun putnam-2020-a6-weighted-sine-sum (n a b)
  (if (and (integerp n)
           (< 0 n))
      (putnam-2020-a6-sum-through n n a b)
    0))

;; The alternating reciprocal-odd prefixes with 2*K+2 terms increase to
;; pi/4.  Thus a rational q is strictly below pi/4 exactly when it is below
;; one of these prefixes.
(defun putnam-2020-a6-leibniz-prefix (terms)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (let* ((index (- terms 1))
           (sign (if (equal (mod index 2) 0)
                     1
                   -1)))
      (+ (putnam-2020-a6-leibniz-prefix index)
         (/ sign (+ (* 2 index) 1))))))

;; This is the strict rational lower cut of the supremum of the source
;; family.  Replacing arbitrary real x by rational points (A,B) on the unit
;; circle does not change this cut: those points are dense, and for each N
;; the displayed finite sum is a continuous polynomial in cos(x),sin(x).
(defun-sk putnam-2020-a6-source-supremum-lower-cut-p (q)
  (exists (n a b)
    (and
     (rationalp q)
     (integerp n)
     (< 0 n)
     (rationalp a)
     (rationalp b)
     (equal (+ (* a a) (* b b)) 1)
     (< q
        (putnam-2020-a6-weighted-sine-sum
         n a b)))))

;; This is the strict rational lower cut of pi/4.
(defun-sk putnam-2020-a6-pi-over-four-lower-cut-p (q)
  (exists (precision)
    (and
     (rationalp q)
     (natp precision)
     (< q
        (putnam-2020-a6-leibniz-prefix
         (+ (* 2 precision) 2))))))

;; Equality on all rational lower cuts is equality of the represented real
;; numbers.  Hence this closed predicate states exactly that the least
;; uniform upper bound of the original f_N(x) is pi/4.
(defun-sk putnambench-putnam-2020-a6-statement ()
  (forall (q)
    (implies
     (rationalp q)
     (iff
      (putnam-2020-a6-source-supremum-lower-cut-p q)
      (putnam-2020-a6-pi-over-four-lower-cut-p q)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2020_a6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2020_a6): the least uniform upper bound of the
-- specified finite trigonometric sums is pi divided by four. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  twoN + twoN

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

alternate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  R ->
  R
alternate reals zero x =
  x
alternate reals (suc n) x =
  negate reals (alternate reals n x)

evenExponent : Nat -> Nat
evenExponent n =
  n + n

oddExponent : Nat -> Nat
oddExponent n =
  suc (evenExponent n)

sineTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
sineTerm reals x n =
  alternate reals n
    (divide reals
      (naturalPower reals x (oddExponent n))
      (fromNat reals (factorial (oddExponent n))))

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms value =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    value

record StandardSine
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    sine : R -> R
    pi : R

    sine-is-power-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (sineTerm reals x)
        (sine x)

    pi-positive :
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) pi
    sine-pi-zero :
      sine pi == zeroR reals
    pi-is-first-positive-sine-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      sine x == zeroR reals ->
      lessOrEqual reals pi x

open StandardSine

IsLeastUpperBound :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> Set) ->
  R ->
  Set
IsLeastUpperBound {R} reals property bound =
  ((value : R) ->
    property value ->
    lessOrEqual reals value bound)
  and
  ((upper : R) ->
    ((value : R) ->
      property value ->
      lessOrEqual reals value upper) ->
    lessOrEqual reals bound upper)

module Putnam2020A6Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (trigonometry : StandardSine reals) where

  half : R
  half =
    divide reals
      (oneR reals)
      (fromNat reals twoN)

  oddNatural : Nat -> Nat
  oddNatural n =
    suc (n + n)

  summand : Nat -> R -> Nat -> R
  summand N x n =
    multiply reals
      (divide reals
        (subtract reals
          (add reals (fromNat reals N) half)
          (fromNat reals n))
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals (suc N))
          (fromNat reals (oddNatural n))))
      (sine trigonometry
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals (oddNatural n))
          x))

  finiteTrigonometricSum : Nat -> R -> R
  finiteTrigonometricSum N x =
    sumFirst reals
      (suc N)
      (summand N x)

  IsPositiveIndexValue : R -> Set
  IsPositiveIndexValue value =
    Exists Nat
      (\ positiveIndexTail ->
        Exists R
          (\ x ->
            value ==
            finiteTrigonometricSum
              (suc positiveIndexTail)
              x))

  solution : R
  solution =
    divide reals
      (pi trigonometry)
      (fromNat reals fourN)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    IsLeastUpperBound reals
      IsPositiveIndexValue
      solution

putnam-2020-a6 : Set1
putnam-2020-a6 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (trigonometry : StandardSine reals) ->
  Putnam2020A6Statement.proposition reals trigonometry

  putnam_2020_a6: the least uniform upper bound of a family of finite
  real sine sums indexed by positive integers is pi / 4. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  NN is set.mm's class of positive integers, so N has exactly the source
  domain. The interval 0 ... N is inclusive, and the displayed summand is
  the source definition of f_N(x), with all arithmetic embedded in the
  reals. The set in the ordered supremum contains exactly the attained
  values f_N(x) for positive N and real x.

  Set.mm's sin and _pi are the real sine and pi constants on these
  arguments, and sup(A, RR, <) is the real-order supremum. Thus the final
  declaration states directly that the smallest uniform upper bound is
  pi / 4. It is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d N n x y $.

  putnambench-putnam-2020-a6 $a |-
    sup
      (
        {
          y e. RR |
            E. N e. NN
              E. x e. RR
                y
                =
                (
                  sum_ n e. ( 0 ... N )
                    (
                      (
                        (
                          ( N + ( 1 / 2 ) )
                          -
                          n
                        )
                        /
                        (
                          ( N + 1 )
                          x.
                          ( ( 2 x. n ) + 1 )
                        )
                      )
                      x.
                      (
                        sin
                        `
                        (
                          ( ( 2 x. n ) + 1 )
                          x.
                          x
                        )
                      )
                    )
                )
        } ,
        RR ,
        <
      )
    =
    ( _pi / 4 )
  $.
$}
