content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b1:
;; every coefficient of the exponential power series of an integer polynomial
;; with zero constant term and odd linear coefficient is nonzero. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; POLYNOMIAL lists the integer coefficients a_0,...,a_d in ascending degree
;; order, with no trailing zero. This is a bijective presentation of the
;; source's integer polynomials under the hypotheses a_0 = 0 and odd a_1.

(defun putnam-2022-b1-integer-list-p (values)
  (if (consp values)
      (and (integerp (car values))
           (putnam-2022-b1-integer-list-p (cdr values)))
    (equal values nil)))

(defun putnam-2022-b1-polynomial-p (polynomial)
  (and
   (true-listp polynomial)
   (<= 2 (len polynomial))
   (putnam-2022-b1-integer-list-p polynomial)
   (not (equal (car (last polynomial)) 0))))

(defun putnam-2022-b1-polynomial-coefficient
    (polynomial degree)
  (if (and (natp degree)
           (< degree (len polynomial)))
      (nth degree polynomial)
    0))

;; If B(x) = sum_n b_n x^n = exp(P(x)), then B' = P' B. Coefficient
;; comparison gives
;;
;;   b_0 = 1,
;;   n b_n = sum_{j=1}^n j a_j b_{n-j}.
;;
;; PREVIOUS contains b_0,...,b_(n-1), and INDEX descends from n to 1.

(defun putnam-2022-b1-recurrence-sum
    (polynomial previous degree index)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix index)))
  (if (zp index)
      0
    (+ (* index
          (putnam-2022-b1-polynomial-coefficient
           polynomial index)
          (nth (- degree index) previous))
       (putnam-2022-b1-recurrence-sum
        polynomial previous degree (- index 1)))))

(defun putnam-2022-b1-coefficient-prefix-aux
    (polynomial remaining coefficients)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      coefficients
    (let* ((degree (len coefficients))
           (next
            (/ (putnam-2022-b1-recurrence-sum
                polynomial coefficients degree degree)
               degree)))
      (putnam-2022-b1-coefficient-prefix-aux
       polynomial
       (- remaining 1)
       (append coefficients (list next))))))

(defun putnam-2022-b1-exponential-coefficient
    (polynomial degree)
  (if (natp degree)
      (nth degree
           (putnam-2022-b1-coefficient-prefix-aux
            polynomial degree (list 1)))
    0))

;; The recurrence uniquely determines the formal series exp(P), and for every
;; real polynomial P this formal series is the Maclaurin series of the entire
;; function exp(P(x)). Conversely, the source HasSum/convergence hypothesis
;; uniquely forces b to have these coefficients. Since the a_j are integers,
;; the recurrence also proves that every forced real coefficient is rational;
;; ACL2's exact rationals therefore represent those same values rather than a
;; restriction of the source domain. Eliminating b and its defining analytic
;; hypothesis is thus bidirectionally equivalent to the source implication.
;; The free natural DEGREE is the source's universally quantified k.

(defun putnambench-putnam-2022-b1-statement
    (polynomial degree)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2022-b1-polynomial-p polynomial)
    (equal
     (putnam-2022-b1-polynomial-coefficient polynomial 0)
     0)
    (oddp
     (putnam-2022-b1-polynomial-coefficient polynomial 1))
    (natp degree))
   (not
    (equal
     (putnam-2022-b1-exponential-coefficient
      polynomial degree)
     0))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2022_b1): every coefficient in the real power
-- series of exp(P(x)) is nonzero when P has integer coefficients, zero
-- constant term, and odd linear coefficient. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2022B1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) ->
      multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) ->
      multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero term =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) term =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n term)
    (term n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms value =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    value

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

exponentialTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

record StandardExponential
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    exponential : R -> R
    exponential-is-power-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (exponentialTerm reals x)
        (exponential x)

open StandardExponential

Polynomial : Set
Polynomial =
  List Int

coefficient : Polynomial -> Nat -> Int
coefficient [] n =
  pos zero
coefficient (c ∷ coefficients) zero =
  c
coefficient (c ∷ coefficients) (suc n) =
  coefficient coefficients n

evaluatePolynomial :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial ->
  R ->
  R
evaluatePolynomial reals [] x =
  zeroR reals
evaluatePolynomial reals (c ∷ coefficients) x =
  add reals
    (fromInt reals c)
    (multiply reals
      x
      (evaluatePolynomial reals coefficients x))

data OddInteger : Int -> Set where
  positive-odd :
    (n : Nat) ->
    OddInteger (pos (suc (n + n)))
  negative-odd :
    (n : Nat) ->
    OddInteger (negsuc (n + n))

putnam-2022-b1 : Set1
putnam-2022-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (analysis : StandardExponential reals) ->
  (P : Polynomial) ->
  (b : Nat -> R) ->
  coefficient P zero == pos zero ->
  OddInteger (coefficient P oneN) ->
  ((x : R) ->
    SeriesHasSum reals
      (\ k ->
        multiply reals
          (b k)
          (naturalPower reals x k))
      (exponential analysis
        (evaluatePolynomial reals P x))) ->
  (k : Nat) ->
  b k != zeroR reals

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b1:
  every coefficient in the real power series of the exponential of an
  integer polynomial with zero constant term and odd linear coefficient is
  nonzero. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory realTheory intrealTheory
     polyTheory seqTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2022_b1 =
  ``!P : int list. !b : num -> real.
      1 < LENGTH P /\
      EL 0 P = 0 /\
      ODD (Num (ABS (EL 1 P))) /\
      (!x : real.
         (\k : num. b k * x pow k) sums
           exp (poly (MAP real_of_int P) x))
      ==>
      !k : num. b k <> 0``;

title: putnam_2022_b1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2022_b1: nonvanishing of every coefficient in the real power
  series of the exponential of an integer polynomial with zero constant
  coefficient and odd linear coefficient. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  Base ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) is Set.mm's ring of arbitrary finite-support
  integer-coefficient univariate polynomials, and coe1 gives the complete
  coefficient function. Thus the unbounded coefficient sum evaluating P at
  a real x is actually finite and is exactly the real evaluation of P.

  RR ^m NN0 is the class of all real coefficient sequences. For each real
  x, the maps-to expression is the sequence of inclusive partial sums of
  sum_k b(k) x^k. Its convergence to exp(P(x)) is equivalent to the source
  HasSum hypothesis. Membership of coefficient one in Odd is precisely the
  odd-integer assumption, and the conclusion retains every nonnegative
  coefficient index.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d P b k n x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2022-b1 $a |-
    A. P e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` ZZring ) )
      A. b e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
        (
          (
            (
              ( ( coe1 ` P ) ` 0 ) = 0
              /\
              ( ( coe1 ` P ) ` 1 ) e. Odd
            )
            /\
            A. x e. RR
              (
                n e. NN0 |->
                  sum_ k e. ( 0 ... n )
                    (
                      ( b ` k )
                      x.
                      ( x ^ k )
                    )
              )
              ~~>
              (
                exp
                `
                (
                  sum_ k e. NN0
                    (
                      ( ( coe1 ` P ) ` k )
                      x.
                      ( x ^ k )
                    )
                )
              )
          )
          ->
          A. k e. NN0
            ( b ` k ) =/= 0
        )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2022_b1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b1:
% an integer polynomial with zero constant term and odd linear coefficient
% has an exponential power series with no zero coefficient. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2022_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_polynomial: TYPE = list[int]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  coefficient(
      polynomial: integer_polynomial,
      degree: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: 0,
      cons(head_coefficient, tail):
        IF degree = 0 THEN
          head_coefficient
        ELSE
          coefficient(tail, degree - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  polynomial_value(
      polynomial: integer_polynomial,
      x: real): RECURSIVE real =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: 0,
      cons(head_coefficient, tail):
        (head_coefficient :: real)
          + x * polynomial_value(tail, x)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  odd_integer(value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (half: int):
      value = 2 * half + 1

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  power_series_partial(
      values: real_sequence,
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        power_series_partial(values, x, count - 1)
          + values(index) * x ^ index
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  putnam_2022_b1: bool =
    FORALL
        (P: integer_polynomial),
        (b: real_sequence):
      (coefficient(P, 0) = 0
        AND odd_integer(coefficient(P, 1))
        AND FORALL (x: real):
          converges_to(
            LAMBDA (count: nat):
              power_series_partial(b, x, count),
            real_exponential(polynomial_value(P, x))))
      IMPLIES
        (FORALL (k: nat):
          b(k) /= 0)
END putnam_2022_b1

import Mathlib

open Polynomial

abbrev putnam_2022_b2_solution : Set ℕ := sorry
-- {1, 7}
/--
Let $\times$ represent the cross product in $\mathbb{R}^3$. For what positive integers $n$ does there exist a set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ with exactly $n$ elements such that $S=\{v \times w:v,w \in S\}$?
-/
theorem putnam_2022_b2
  (n : ℕ)
  (P : Finset (Fin 3 → ℝ) → Prop)
  (P_def : ∀ S : Finset (Fin 3 → ℝ), P S ↔ (S = {u : Fin 3 → ℝ | ∃ v w : S, u = crossProduct v w})) :
  (0 < n ∧ ∃ S : Finset (Fin 3 → ℝ), S.card = n ∧ P S) ↔ n ∈ putnam_2022_b2_solution :=
sorry

title: putnam_2022_b2
content:
Require Import Ensembles Finite_sets Reals.
Open Scope R_scope.

Definition vect3 := (R * R * R)%type.

Definition cross_prod (v w : vect3) : vect3 :=
  let '(v1, v2, v3) := v in
  let '(w1, w2, w3) := w in
  (v2 * w3 - v3 * w2,
   v3 * w1 - v1 * w3,
   v1 * w2 - v2 * w1).

Definition putnam_2022_b2_solution : Ensemble nat :=
  fun n => n = 1%nat \/ n = 7%nat.
Theorem putnam_2022_b2
    (p : nat -> Prop := fun n =>
      exists A : Ensemble vect3,
        cardinal vect3 A n /\
        A = fun u =>
          exists v w : vect3,
            In _ A v /\
            In _ A w /\
            u = cross_prod v w)
    : forall (n: nat), ((n > 0)%nat /\ p n) <-> In _ putnam_2022_b2_solution n.
Proof. Admitted.

Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Cross3"
begin

definition putnam_2022_b2_solution :: "nat set" where
  "putnam_2022_b2_solution \<equiv> {1, 7}"
(* {1, 7} *)
theorem putnam_2022_b2:
  fixes n :: nat
  and Scross :: "(real^3) set \<Rightarrow> bool"
  assumes hScross: "\<forall>S::(real^3) set. Scross S = (S = {u::real^3. (\<exists>v\<in>S. \<exists>w\<in>S. u = cross3 v w)})"
  shows "(n > 0 \<and> (\<exists>S::(real^3) set. finite S \<and> card S = n \<and> Scross S)) \<longleftrightarrow> n \<in> putnam_2022_b2_solution"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b2:
  classification of the positive cardinalities of finite subsets of real
  three-space that are exactly closed under pairwise cross products. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let cross3 =
     \(v:real^3) (w:real^3).
       (lambda i.
          if i = 1 then v$2 * w$3 - v$3 * w$2
          else if i = 2 then v$3 * w$1 - v$1 * w$3
          else v$1 * w$2 - v$2 * w$1):real^3 in
   !n:num.
     (0 < n /\
      ?S:real^3->bool.
        FINITE S /\
        CARD S = n /\
        S =
          {u:real^3 |
             ?v w:real^3.
               v IN S /\ w IN S /\ u = cross3 v w})
     <=> n = 1 \/ n = 7`;;

title: putnam_2022_b2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b2:
;; the positive cardinalities of finite subsets of real three-space that are
;; exactly closed under taking all pairwise cross products are 1 and 7. This
;; file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The scalar domain is presented as a real closed ordered field. Completeness
;; of the first-order theory of real closed fields transfers this finite
;; algebraic assertion bidirectionally between the presentation and the real
;; numbers. A vector is a length-three field list.
;;
;; A duplicate-free list represents the finite set extensionally. The two
;; inclusions below say exactly that this set equals the set of all v cross w
;; with v and w in the set. NOT/FN-EQUAL keeps the finite-set witness internal
;; rather than adding it as a parameter of the root statement.

(defun putnam-2022-b2-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted function)
   (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted function)
   (list 'cons left (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-and-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2022-b2-quoted t)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2022-b2-and-term (cdr terms))
     (putnam-2022-b2-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-or-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2022-b2-quoted nil)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2022-b2-quoted t)
     (putnam-2022-b2-or-term (cdr terms)))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-not-term (term)
  (list
   'if
   term
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted nil)
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-implies-term (antecedent consequent)
  (list
   'if
   antecedent
   consequent
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-true-function (formals)
  (list
   'lambda
   formals
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-2022-b2-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-operation-term (operation left right)
  (putnam-2022-b2-apply2-term operation left right))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-all-coefficients-function (carrier)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)
   (putnam-2022-b2-carrier-term
    carrier 'loop$-ivars)))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-all-coefficients-term
    (carrier coefficients)
  (list
   'always$+
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted
    (putnam-2022-b2-all-coefficients-function
     carrier))
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted nil)
   coefficients))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-polynomial-term
    (carrier zero coefficients)
  (putnam-2022-b2-and-term
   (list
    (list 'true-listp coefficients)
    (list 'consp coefficients)
    (putnam-2022-b2-all-coefficients-term
     carrier coefficients)
    (putnam-2022-b2-or-term
     (list
      (list 'equal
            (list 'len coefficients)
            (putnam-2022-b2-quoted 1))
      (putnam-2022-b2-not-term
       (list 'equal
             (list 'car (list 'last coefficients))
             (putnam-2022-b2-quoted zero))))))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-field-laws-function
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (y 'y)
         (z 'z)
         (qzero (putnam-2022-b2-quoted zero))
         (qone (putnam-2022-b2-quoted one))
         (add-xy
          (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term add x y))
         (add-yz
          (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term add y z))
         (mul-xy
          (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term mul x y))
         (mul-yz
          (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term mul y z))
         (neg-x
          (putnam-2022-b2-apply1-term neg x))
         (inv-x
          (putnam-2022-b2-apply1-term inv x))
         (domain
          (putnam-2022-b2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2022-b2-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2022-b2-carrier-term carrier y)
            (putnam-2022-b2-carrier-term carrier z))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2022-b2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2022-b2-carrier-term carrier add-xy)
            (putnam-2022-b2-carrier-term carrier mul-xy)
            (putnam-2022-b2-carrier-term carrier neg-x)
            (putnam-2022-b2-carrier-term carrier inv-x)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term add add-xy z)
             (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term add x add-yz))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term mul mul-xy z)
             (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term mul x mul-yz))
            (list
             'equal
             add-xy
             (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term add y x))
            (list
             'equal
             mul-xy
             (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term mul y x))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term add x qzero)
             x)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term add x neg-x)
             qzero)
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term mul x qone)
             x)
            (putnam-2022-b2-implies-term
             (list 'equal x qzero)
             (list 'equal inv-x qzero))
            (putnam-2022-b2-implies-term
             (putnam-2022-b2-not-term
              (list 'equal x qzero))
             (list
              'equal
              (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term mul x inv-x)
              qone))
            (list

    (carrier zero add mul lt)

            (putnam-2022-b2-not-term

              (list lt-xy lt-yz))

            (putnam-2022-b2-implies-term
             lt-xy

              (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term add x z)

              (list
               (putnam-2022-b2-operation-term lt qzero x)

          (putnam-2022-b2-true-function
           '(coefficients)))
         (all-coefficients-loop
          (putnam-2022-b2-all-coefficients-function

    (and
     (tamep-functionp carrier)
     (tamep-functionp add)
     (tamep-functionp mul)
     (tamep-functionp neg)
     (tamep-functionp inv)
     (tamep-functionp lt)
     (tamep-functionp square-root)
     (tamep-functionp odd-root)
     (tamep-functionp evaluate)
     (tamep-functionp all-coefficients-loop)
     (tamep-functionp field-laws)
     (tamep-functionp field-laws-true)
     (tamep-functionp order-laws)
     (tamep-functionp order-laws-true)
     (tamep-functionp square-root-laws)
     (tamep-functionp square-root-laws-true)
     (tamep-functionp evaluation-laws)
     (tamep-functionp evaluation-laws-true)
     (tamep-functionp odd-root-laws)
     (tamep-functionp odd-root-laws-true)
     (apply$ carrier (list zero))
     (apply$ carrier (list one))
     (not (equal zero one))
     (fn-equal field-laws field-laws-true)
     (fn-equal order-laws order-laws-true)
     (fn-equal square-root-laws square-root-laws-true)
     (fn-equal evaluation-laws evaluation-laws-true)

(defun putnam-2022-b2-first-term (vector)

(defun putnam-2022-b2-second-term (vector)

(defun putnam-2022-b2-third-term (vector)

(defun putnam-2022-b2-vector-term (field-carrier vector)
  (putnam-2022-b2-and-term
   (list
    (list 'true-listp vector)
    (list
     'equal
     (list 'len vector)
     (putnam-2022-b2-quoted 3))
    (putnam-2022-b2-carrier-term
     field-carrier
     (putnam-2022-b2-first-term vector))
    (putnam-2022-b2-carrier-term

     (putnam-2022-b2-second-term vector))

        (left-1 (putnam-2022-b2-second-term left))

   (true-listp vector)
   (equal (len vector) 3)

   (apply$ field-carrier (list (nth 1 vector)))
   (apply$ field-carrier (list (nth 2 vector)))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-vector-list-p
    (vectors field-carrier)

      (equal vectors nil)

(defun putnam-2022-b2-scalar-difference
    (add mul neg left-a left-b right-a right-b)

   add
   (list
    (apply$ mul (list left-a left-b))

     neg
     (list
      (apply$ mul (list right-a right-b)))))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-cross
    (left right add mul neg)

   (putnam-2022-b2-scalar-difference
    add mul neg
    (nth 1 left) (nth 2 right)
    (nth 2 left) (nth 1 right))
   (putnam-2022-b2-scalar-difference
    add mul neg
    (nth 2 left) (nth 0 right)
    (nth 0 left) (nth 2 right))
   (putnam-2022-b2-scalar-difference
    add mul neg
    (nth 0 left) (nth 1 right)
    (nth 1 left) (nth 0 right))))

;; Every pairwise cross product belongs to the represented set.
(defun putnam-2022-b2-cross-with-all-in-set-p
    (left rights set add mul neg)
  (if (endp rights)
      (equal rights nil)
    (and
     (member-equal
      (putnam-2022-b2-cross
       left (car rights) add mul neg)
      set)
     (putnam-2022-b2-cross-with-all-in-set-p
      left (cdr rights) set add mul neg))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-all-crosses-in-set-p
    (lefts set add mul neg)

      (equal lefts nil)
    (and
     (putnam-2022-b2-cross-with-all-in-set-p
      (car lefts) set set add mul neg)
     (putnam-2022-b2-all-crosses-in-set-p
      (cdr lefts) set add mul neg))))

;; Every represented-set element is the cross product of two represented-set
;; elements, giving the reverse inclusion.
(defun putnam-2022-b2-cross-from-left-exists-p
    (target left rights add mul neg)
  (if (endp rights)
      nil
    (or
     (equal
      target
      (putnam-2022-b2-cross
       left (car rights) add mul neg))
     (putnam-2022-b2-cross-from-left-exists-p
      target left (cdr rights) add mul neg))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-cross-preimage-exists-p
    (target lefts set add mul neg)
  (if (endp lefts)
      nil
    (or
     (putnam-2022-b2-cross-from-left-exists-p
      target (car lefts) set add mul neg)
     (putnam-2022-b2-cross-preimage-exists-p
      target (cdr lefts) set add mul neg))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-all-elements-have-preimage-p
    (elements set add mul neg)
  (if (endp elements)
      (equal elements nil)
    (and
     (putnam-2022-b2-cross-preimage-exists-p
      (car elements) set set add mul neg)
     (putnam-2022-b2-all-elements-have-preimage-p
      (cdr elements) set add mul neg))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-set-witness-p
    (set n field-carrier add mul neg)
  (and
   (true-listp set)
   (no-duplicatesp-equal set)
   (equal (len set) n)
   (putnam-2022-b2-vector-list-p set field-carrier)
   (putnam-2022-b2-all-crosses-in-set-p
    set set add mul neg)
   (putnam-2022-b2-all-elements-have-preimage-p
    set set add mul neg)))

;; The FN-EQUAL witness is a three-part certificate:
;;
;;   (set ordered-pairs preimages).
;;
;; ORDERED-PAIRS is a duplicate-free list of |SET|^2 valid pairs, hence an
;; enumeration of every ordered pair from SET. PREIMAGES contains |SET|
;; records (target left right), with distinct targets, so it supplies exactly
;; one cross-product preimage for every element of SET. This finite
;; certificate is definitionally equivalent to the two recursive inclusions
;; above, while every lambda evaluated by FN-EQUAL contains primitives only.

(defun putnam-2022-b2-list-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2022-b2-quoted nil)
    (list
     'cons
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2022-b2-list-term (cdr terms)))))

    (field-carrier)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)

     'lambda

      (list
       (list 'true-listp pair)
       (list
        'equal
        (list 'len pair)
        (putnam-2022-b2-quoted 2))
       (list 'member-equal left set)
       (list 'member-equal right set)
       (list
        'member-equal
        (putnam-2022-b2-cross-term
         add mul neg left right)
        set))))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-preimage-loop-function
    (add mul neg)
  (let* ((record 'loop$-ivars)
         (set '(car loop$-gvars))
         (target (putnam-2022-b2-first-term record))
         (left (putnam-2022-b2-second-term record))
         (right (putnam-2022-b2-third-term record)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)
     (putnam-2022-b2-and-term
      (list
       (list 'true-listp record)
       (list
        'equal
        (list 'len record)
        (putnam-2022-b2-quoted 3))
       (list 'member-equal target set)
       (list 'member-equal left set)
       (list 'member-equal right set)
       (list
        'equal
        target
        (putnam-2022-b2-cross-term
         add mul neg left right)))))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-all-vectors-term
    (field-carrier set)
  (list
   'always$+
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted
    (putnam-2022-b2-vector-loop-function
     field-carrier))
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted nil)
   set))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-all-pairs-close-term
    (set ordered-pairs add mul neg)
  (list
   'always$+
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted
    (putnam-2022-b2-pair-closure-loop-function
     add mul neg))
   (putnam-2022-b2-list-term (list set))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-all-preimages-valid-term
    (set preimages add mul neg)

   'always$+
   (putnam-2022-b2-quoted
    (putnam-2022-b2-preimage-loop-function
     add mul neg))
   (putnam-2022-b2-list-term (list set))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-set-failure-function
    (n field-carrier add mul neg)
  (let* ((set '(car witness))
         (ordered-pairs '(car (cdr witness)))
         (preimages '(car (cdr (cdr witness))))
         (set-size (list 'len set))

          (putnam-2022-b2-and-term
           (list
            '(true-listp witness)
            '(equal (len witness) '3)
            (list 'true-listp set)

            (list
             'equal
             set-size

            (putnam-2022-b2-all-vectors-term

            (list 'true-listp preimages)

            (list
             'no-duplicatesp-equal
             (list 'strip-cars preimages))

             set preimages add mul neg)))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(witness)

      'if
      qualification
      (putnam-2022-b2-quoted nil)
      (putnam-2022-b2-quoted t)))))

(defun putnam-2022-b2-set-exists-p
    (n field-carrier add mul neg)
  (let ((failure-function
         (putnam-2022-b2-set-failure-function
          n field-carrier add mul neg))

         (putnam-2022-b2-true-function '(witness))))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp failure-function)

(defun putnambench-putnam-2022-b2-statement
    (n field-carrier zero one add mul neg field-inverse lt

  (implies

    (or
     (equal n 1)

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2022_b2): positive finite cardinalities of
-- subsets of real three-space equal to their pairwise cross-product image.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2022B2 where

open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; _⊔_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (P : A -> Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

record Vector3 (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor vector
  field
    first-coordinate  : R
    second-coordinate : R
    third-coordinate  : R

open Vector3

crossProduct :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Vector3 R
crossProduct reals v w =
  vector
    (add reals
      (multiply reals
        (second-coordinate v)
        (third-coordinate w))
      (negate reals
        (multiply reals
          (third-coordinate v)
          (second-coordinate w))))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals
        (third-coordinate v)
        (first-coordinate w))
      (negate reals
        (multiply reals
          (first-coordinate v)
          (third-coordinate w))))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals
        (first-coordinate v)
        (second-coordinate w))
      (negate reals
        (multiply reals
          (second-coordinate v)
          (first-coordinate w))))

record HasCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A

    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)

    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists
        (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index -> item == enumerate index)

    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      enumerate left-index == enumerate right-index ->
      left-index == right-index

record CrossProductFiniteSet
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set1 where

  field
    member :
      Vector3 R ->
      Set

    has-cardinality :
      HasCardinality member cardinality

    exactly-cross-products :
      (u : Vector3 R) ->
      Iff
        (member u)
        (Exists
          (Vector3 R)
          (\ v ->
            member v
            and
            Exists
              (Vector3 R)
              (\ w ->
                member w
                and
                u == crossProduct reals v w)))

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

seven : Nat
seven =
  suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc (suc zero))))))

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  one <=N n

putnam-2022-b2 : Set1
putnam-2022-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (n : Nat) ->
  Iff
    (Positive n and CrossProductFiniteSet reals n)
    (n == one or n == seven)

content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b2:
  the positive cardinalities of finite sets of vectors in real three-space
  that equal the set of all pairwise cross products are exactly 1 and 7.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory;

val putnam_2022_b2 =
  ``let cross3 =
      \v w : (real # real) # real.
        ((SND (FST v) * SND w - SND v * SND (FST w),
          SND v * FST (FST w) - FST (FST v) * SND w),
         FST (FST v) * SND (FST w) -
           SND (FST v) * FST (FST w))
    in
      !n : num.
        (0 < n /\
         ?S : ((real # real) # real) set.
           FINITE S /\
           CARD S = n /\
           S =
             {u |
                ?v w : (real # real) # real.
                  v IN S /\ w IN S /\ u = cross3 v w})
        <=>
        n = 1 \/ n = 7``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2022_b2: the positive cardinalities of finite subsets of real
  three-space equal to their set of pairwise cross products are exactly
  1 and 7. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P22B2I3 is the three-element coordinate interval {0,1,2}, P22B2R3 is the
  corresponding real coordinate space, and P22B2Cross is the ordinary
  coordinate cross product.
  The restricted class in the final assertion is therefore exactly
  { v cross w | v in S and w in S }.

  Quantification over n in NN0 together with the explicit positivity
  conjunct preserves the source statement for every natural number.
  The finite set S and both cross-product inputs remain internally
  existentially quantified. All declarations are unproved $a statement
  or definition encodings; this database contains no $p proof.
$)

$c P22B2I3 P22B2R3 P22B2Cross $.

p22b2-index-syntax $a class P22B2I3 $.
p22b2-space-syntax $a class P22B2R3 $.
p22b2-cross-syntax $a class ( P22B2Cross v w ) $.

p22b2-index-definition $a |- P22B2I3 = ( 0 ... 2 ) $.

p22b2-space-definition $a |- P22B2R3 = ( RR ^m P22B2I3 ) $.

${
  $d k v w $.

  p22b2-cross-definition $a |- (
    P22B2Cross v w
  ) = (
    k e. P22B2I3 |->
      if (
        k = 0 ,
        (
          ( ( v ` 1 ) x. ( w ` 2 ) )
          -
          ( ( v ` 2 ) x. ( w ` 1 ) )
        ) ,
        if (
          k = 1 ,
          (
            ( ( v ` 2 ) x. ( w ` 0 ) )
            -
            ( ( v ` 0 ) x. ( w ` 2 ) )
          ) ,
          (
            ( ( v ` 0 ) x. ( w ` 1 ) )
            -
            ( ( v ` 1 ) x. ( w ` 0 ) )
          )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d n s u v w $.

  putnambench-putnam-2022-b2 $a |- A. n e. NN0
    (
      (
        0 < n
        /\
        E. s e. Fin
          (
            s C_ P22B2R3
            /\
            (
              ( # ` s ) = n
              /\
              s =
                {
                  u e. P22B2R3 |
                    E. v e. s E. w e. s
                      u = ( P22B2Cross v w )
                }
            )
          )
      )
      <->
      (
        n = 1
        \/
        n = 7
      )
    )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b2:
% the positive cardinalities of finite subsets of real three-space that equal
% their set of pairwise cross products are exactly 1 and 7. This file contains
% no proof.

putnam_2022_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  vector3: TYPE =
    [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real, z_coord: real #]

  IMPORTING finite_sets[vector3]

  cross_product(v, w: vector3): vector3 =
    (# x_coord :=
         y_coord(v) * z_coord(w) - z_coord(v) * y_coord(w),
       y_coord :=
         z_coord(v) * x_coord(w) - x_coord(v) * z_coord(w),
       z_coord :=
         x_coord(v) * y_coord(w) - y_coord(v) * x_coord(w) #)

  closed_under_exact_cross_products(S: finite_set[vector3]): bool =
    FORALL (u: vector3):
      S(u)
        IFF
          EXISTS (v, w: vector3):
            S(v) AND S(w) AND u = cross_product(v, w)

  admissible_cardinality(n: nat): bool =
    n > 0
      AND EXISTS (S: finite_set[vector3]):
        card(S) = n AND closed_under_exact_cross_products(S)

  putnam_2022_b2_solution(n: nat): bool =
    n = 1 OR n = 7

  putnam_2022_b2: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      admissible_cardinality(n) IFF putnam_2022_b2_solution(n)
END putnam_2022_b2

import Mathlib

open Polynomial

-- Note: boosts domain of "isred" to all reals instead of just positive reals
abbrev putnam_2022_b3_solution : Prop := sorry
-- True
/--
Assign to each positive real number a color, either red or blue. Let $D$ be the set of all distances $d>0$ such that there are two points of the same color at distance $d$ apart. Recolor the positive reals so that the numbers in $D$ are red and the numbers not in $D$ are blue. If we iterate this recoloring process, will we always end up with all the numbers red after a finite number of steps?
-/
theorem putnam_2022_b3
  (recolor : (ℝ → Prop) → (ℝ → Prop))
  (hrecolor : ∀ isred d, recolor isred d ↔ ∃ p q : ℝ, p > 0 ∧ q > 0 ∧ p < q ∧ isred p = isred q ∧ q - p = d) :
  (∀ isred, (∃ k, ∀ p > 0, (recolor^[k] isred) p)) ↔ putnam_2022_b3_solution :=
sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b3:
   finite iteration of the same-color distance recoloring operation on the
   positive real numbers. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2022_b3_coloring : Type :=
  R -> Prop.

Definition putnam_2022_b3_recolor
    (isred : putnam_2022_b3_coloring) :
    putnam_2022_b3_coloring :=
  fun d : R =>
    exists p q : R,
      0 < p /\
      0 < q /\
      p < q /\
      (isred p <-> isred q) /\
      q - p = d.

Fixpoint putnam_2022_b3_iterate
    (k : nat)
    (isred : putnam_2022_b3_coloring) :
    putnam_2022_b3_coloring :=
  match k with
  | O => isred
  | S n =>
      putnam_2022_b3_recolor
        (putnam_2022_b3_iterate n isred)
  end.

Definition putnam_2022_b3_solution : Prop :=
  True.

Theorem putnam_2022_b3 :
  (forall isred : putnam_2022_b3_coloring,
      exists k : nat,
        forall p : R,
          0 < p ->
          putnam_2022_b3_iterate k isred p) <->
  putnam_2022_b3_solution.
Admitted.

title: putnam_2022_b3
putnam_2022_b3
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b3:
;; every red-blue coloring of the positive reals becomes all red after
;; finitely many iterations of the same-color distance recoloring. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Reals are represented by rational regular Cauchy names. Colorings are
;; extensional ACL2 predicate-valued function objects on those names, so they
;; are complete predicates on represented reals rather than finite tables.
;; Negated FN-EQUAL tests keep the witnesses p, q, the positive lower margins,
;; and the iteration count existentially quantified inside the statement.
;;
;; The source hypothesis uniquely defines RECOLOR, so RECOLOR-FUNCTION below
;; eliminates that parameter definitionally. Its k-fold recursive composition
;; is exactly the source function iterate, including k=0.

(defun putnam-2022-b3-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'cons
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2022-b3-term-list (cdr terms)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-apply-term (function arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        (putnam-2022-b3-quoted function)
        (putnam-2022-b3-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-apply-object-term
    (function-term arguments)
  (list 'apply$
        function-term
        (putnam-2022-b3-term-list arguments)))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'if
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2022-b3-and-terms (cdr terms))
            (putnam-2022-b3-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2022-b3-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list 'if
        hypothesis
        conclusion
        (putnam-2022-b3-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-iff-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        left
        (list 'if
              right
              (putnam-2022-b3-quoted t)
              (putnam-2022-b3-quoted nil))
        (list 'if
              right
              (putnam-2022-b3-quoted nil)
              (putnam-2022-b3-quoted t))))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-negate-term (value)
  (list 'unary-- value))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-subtract-term (left right)
  (putnam-2022-b3-add-term
   left
   (putnam-2022-b3-negate-term right)))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-multiply-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-* left right))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-absolute-term (value)
  (list 'if
        (list '< value (putnam-2022-b3-quoted 0))
        (putnam-2022-b3-negate-term value)
        value))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-less-equal-term (left right)
  (list 'if
        (list '< right left)
        (putnam-2022-b3-quoted nil)
        (putnam-2022-b3-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-positive-rational-term (value)
  (putnam-2022-b3-and-terms
   (list
    (list 'rationalp value)
    (list '< (putnam-2022-b3-quoted 0) value))))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda
        formals
        (putnam-2022-b3-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-real-value-term (name precision)
  (putnam-2022-b3-apply-term name (list precision)))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-object-real-value-term
    (name-term precision)
  (putnam-2022-b3-apply-object-term
   name-term
   (list precision)))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-real-cauchy-function (name)
  (let* ((left
          (putnam-2022-b3-real-value-term name 'epsilon))
         (right
          (putnam-2022-b3-real-value-term name 'eta))
         (distance
          (putnam-2022-b3-absolute-term
           (putnam-2022-b3-subtract-term left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon eta)
     (putnam-2022-b3-implies-term
      (putnam-2022-b3-and-terms
       (list
        (putnam-2022-b3-positive-rational-term 'epsilon)
        (putnam-2022-b3-positive-rational-term 'eta)))
      (putnam-2022-b3-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp left)
        (list 'rationalp right)
        (putnam-2022-b3-less-equal-term
         distance
         (putnam-2022-b3-add-term
          'epsilon 'eta))))))))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-real-name-p (name)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2022-b3-real-cauchy-function name)
    (putnam-2022-b3-true-function
     '(epsilon eta)))))

;; Two regular names denote the same real exactly when their values at every
;; positive rational precision differ by at most twice that precision.
(defun putnam-2022-b3-real-equality-function
    (left-name right-name)
  (let* ((left
          (putnam-2022-b3-real-value-term
           left-name 'epsilon))
         (right
          (putnam-2022-b3-real-value-term
           right-name 'epsilon))
         (distance
          (putnam-2022-b3-absolute-term
           (putnam-2022-b3-subtract-term
            left right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2022-b3-implies-term
      (putnam-2022-b3-positive-rational-term
       'epsilon)
      (putnam-2022-b3-less-equal-term
       distance
       (putnam-2022-b3-multiply-term
        (putnam-2022-b3-quoted 2)
        'epsilon))))))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-real-equal-p
    (left-name right-name)
  (and
   (putnam-2022-b3-real-name-p left-name)
   (putnam-2022-b3-real-name-p right-name)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2022-b3-real-equality-function
     left-name right-name)
    (putnam-2022-b3-true-function '(epsilon)))))

;; LOWER is an internal rational certificate that NAME denotes a real greater
;; than zero.
(defun putnam-2022-b3-positive-margin-function
    (name lower)
  (let ((value
         (putnam-2022-b3-real-value-term
          name 'epsilon)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(epsilon)
     (putnam-2022-b3-implies-term
      (putnam-2022-b3-positive-rational-term
       'epsilon)
      (putnam-2022-b3-and-terms
       (list
        (list 'rationalp value)
        (putnam-2022-b3-less-equal-term
         (putnam-2022-b3-quoted lower)
         (putnam-2022-b3-add-term
          value 'epsilon))))))))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-positive-margin-p
    (name lower)
  (and
   (rationalp lower)
   (< 0 lower)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2022-b3-positive-margin-function
     name lower)
    (putnam-2022-b3-true-function '(epsilon)))))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-positive-margin-failure-function
    (name)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(lower)
   (list
    'if
    (list
     'putnam-2022-b3-positive-margin-p
     (putnam-2022-b3-quoted name)
     'lower)
    (putnam-2022-b3-quoted nil)
    (putnam-2022-b3-quoted t))))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-positive-real-p (name)
  (let ((failure
         (putnam-2022-b3-positive-margin-failure-function
          name))
        (always-fails
         (putnam-2022-b3-true-function '(lower))))
    (and
     (putnam-2022-b3-real-name-p name)
     (tamep-functionp failure)
     (tamep-functionp always-fails)
     (not (fn-equal failure always-fails)))))

;; Sampling both inputs at half the requested precision produces a regular
;; Cauchy name for RIGHT-LEFT.
(defun putnam-2022-b3-difference-name
    (left-name right-name)
  (let* ((half-precision
          (putnam-2022-b3-multiply-term
           (putnam-2022-b3-quoted 1/2)
           'precision))
         (left
          (putnam-2022-b3-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2022-b3-quoted left-name)
           half-precision))
         (right
          (putnam-2022-b3-object-real-value-term
           (putnam-2022-b3-quoted right-name)
           half-precision)))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(precision)
     (putnam-2022-b3-subtract-term
      right left))))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-less-p
    (left-name right-name)
  (putnam-2022-b3-positive-real-p
   (putnam-2022-b3-difference-name
    left-name right-name)))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-coloring-extensional-function
    (coloring)
  (let ((left-color
         (putnam-2022-b3-apply-term
          coloring (list 'left)))
        (right-color
         (putnam-2022-b3-apply-term
          coloring (list 'right))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(left right)
     (putnam-2022-b3-implies-term
      (list 'putnam-2022-b3-real-equal-p
            'left 'right)
      (putnam-2022-b3-iff-term
       left-color right-color)))))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-coloring-p (coloring)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp coloring)
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2022-b3-coloring-extensional-function
     coloring)
    (putnam-2022-b3-true-function
     '(left right)))))

(defun putnam-2022-b3-same-color-p

title: putnam_2022_b3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2022_b3): finite iteration of the same-color
-- distance recoloring process on the positive real numbers. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2022B3 where

open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; _⊔_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

record Top : Set where
  constructor top

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (P : A -> Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

iterate :
  {a : Level} ->
  {A : Set a} ->
  (A -> A) ->
  Nat ->
  A ->
  A
iterate function zero x =
  x
iterate function (suc n) x =
  function (iterate function n x)

module Putnam2022B3Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  SameColor :
    (R -> Set) ->
    R ->
    R ->
    Set
  SameColor isred p q =
    Iff (isred p) (isred q)

  recolor :
    (R -> Set) ->
    R ->
    Set
  recolor isred d =
    Exists R
      (\ p ->
        Exists R
          (\ q ->
            StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) p
            and
            (StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) q
            and
            (StrictLess reals p q
            and
            (SameColor isred p q
            and
            subtract reals q p == d)))))

  EventuallyAllPositiveRed : Set1
  EventuallyAllPositiveRed =
    (isred : R -> Set) ->
    Exists Nat
      (\ k ->
        (p : R) ->
        StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) p ->
        iterate recolor k isred p)

  proposition : Set1
  proposition =
    Iff EventuallyAllPositiveRed Top

putnam-2022-b3 : Set1
putnam-2022-b3 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2022B3Statement.proposition reals

$(

  putnam_2022_b3: every red-blue coloring of the positive reals becomes
  entirely red after finitely many iterations of the same-color-distance
  recoloring operation. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  A coloring is represented by a subset X of RR, with membership meaning
  red. P22B3Recolor is a total function on the full power set of RR. Its
  value at X contains exactly those real d for which there are positive
  reals p < q of the same color with q - p = d. The biconditional of
  memberships is exactly equality of the two source truth values.

  IterComp is set.mm's native finite-iteration operator, including the
  identity iterate at k = 0. The final assertion quantifies over every
  coloring and retains the internally existential finite iterate. Since the
  ground-truth solution is True, this assertion is logically equivalent to
  the source proposition being biconditional with its solution proposition.
  Every declaration below is an unproved $a statement encoding; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c P22B3Recolor $.

p22b3-recolor-syntax $a class P22B3Recolor $.

${
  $d X d k p q $.

  p22b3-recolor-definition $a |- P22B3Recolor = (
    X e. ( ~P RR ) |->
      {
        d e. RR |
        E. p e. RR E. q e. RR
          (
            0 < p
            /\
            (
              0 < q
              /\
              (
                p < q
                /\
                (
                  ( p e. X <-> q e. X )
                  /\
                  ( q - p ) = d
                )
              )
            )
          )
      }
  ) $.

  putnambench-putnam-2022-b3 $a |- A. X e. ( ~P RR )
    E. k e. NN0 A. p e. RR
      (
        0 < p
        ->
        p
        e.
        (
          (
            ( IterComp ` P22B3Recolor )
            `
            k
          )
          `
          X
        )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2022_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2022_b3:
% iterating the recoloring of positive real distances determined by same-color
% pairs eventually makes every positive real red. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2022_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  coloring: TYPE = [real -> bool]

  recolor(isred: coloring): coloring =
    LAMBDA (d: real):
      EXISTS (p, q: real):
        p > 0
          AND q > 0
          AND p < q
          AND isred(p) = isred(q)
          AND q - p = d

  iterated_recolor(
      isred: coloring,
      iterations: nat): RECURSIVE coloring =
    IF iterations = 0 THEN
      isred
    ELSE
      recolor(iterated_recolor(isred, iterations - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE iterations

  putnam_2022_b3_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_2022_b3_statement: bool =
    ((FORALL (isred: coloring):
      EXISTS (iterations: nat):
        FORALL (p: real):
          p > 0 IMPLIES iterated_recolor(isred, iterations)(p))
      IFF putnam_2022_b3_solution)
END putnam_2022_b3

import Mathlib

open Polynomial

-- Note: uses (ℕ → ℝ) instead of (Fin n → ℝ)
abbrev putnam_2022_b4_solution : Set ℕ := sorry
-- {n : ℕ | 3 ∣ n ∧ n ≥ 9}
/--
Find all integers $n$ with $n \geq 4$ for which there exists a sequence of distinct real numbers $x_1,\dots,x_n$ such that each of the sets $\{x_1,x_2,x_3\},\{x_2,x_3,x_4\},\dots,\{x_{n-2},x_{n-1},x_n\},\{x_{n-1},x_n,x_1\}$, and $\{x_n,x_1,x_2\}$ forms a $3$-term arithmetic progression when arranged in increasing order.
-/
theorem putnam_2022_b4
  (n : ℕ)
  (hn : n ≥ 4)
  (ap3 : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ → Prop)
  (xprog : (ℕ → ℝ) → Prop)
  (hap3 : ∀ x0 x1 x2, ap3 x0 x1 x2 ↔ ∀ o0 o1 o2 : ℝ, (o0 < o1 ∧ o1 < o2 ∧ ({o0, o1, o2} : Set ℝ) = {x0, x1, x2}) → (o1 - o0 = o2 - o1))
  (hxprog : ∀ x, xprog x ↔
    ((∀ i j : Fin n, i.1 ≠ j.1 → x i.1 ≠ x j.1) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, ap3 (x i.1) (x ((i.1 + 1) % n)) (x ((i.1 + 2) % n))))) :
  (∃ x, xprog x) ↔ n ∈ putnam_2022_b4_solution :=
sorry

From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect ssrint ssralg ssrnum.
From mathcomp Require Import reals.
From mathcomp Require Import classical_sets.

Set Implicit Arguments.

Local Open Scope ring_scope.
Local Open Scope classical_set_scope.

Variable R : realType.
Definition putnam_2022_b4_solution : set nat := [set n | ge n 9 /\ 3%|n].
Theorem putnam_2022_b4
    (n : nat)
    (hn : ge n 4)
    (ap3 : R -> R -> R -> Prop)
    (xprog : (nat -> R) -> Prop)
    (hap3 : forall x0 x1 x2 : R, ap3 x0 x1 x2 <-> forall o0 o1 o2 : R, o0 < o1 < o2 -> [set x : R | x = o0 \/ x = o1 \/ x = o2] = [set x : R | x = x0 \/ x = x1 \/ x = x2] -> (o1 - o0 = o2 - o1))
    (hxprog : forall x, xprog x <->
        ((forall i j : nat, lt i n /\ lt j n /\ i <> j -> x i <> x j) /\ 
        forall i : nat, lt i n -> ap3 (x i) (x ((i.+1) %% n)) (x ((i.+2) %% n))))
    : (exists x, xprog x) <-> n \in putnam_2022_b4_solution.
Proof. Admitted.

  shows "(n \<ge> 4 \<and> (\<exists>x::nat\<Rightarrow>real. xprog x)) \<longleftrightarrow> n \<in> putnam_2022_b4_solution"
