let statement =
  `let phi = (&1 + sqrt (&5)) / &2 in
   let scale = sqrt (&1 + phi pow 2) in
   let vertex =
     \i:num.
       if i = 1 then
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then &1 else if j = 2 then phi else &0):real^3
       else if i = 2 then
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then -- &1 else if j = 2 then phi else &0):real^3
       else if i = 3 then
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then &1 else if j = 2 then --phi else &0):real^3
       else if i = 4 then
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then -- &1 else if j = 2 then --phi else &0):real^3
       else if i = 5 then
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then phi else if j = 2 then &0 else &1):real^3
       else if i = 6 then
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then phi else if j = 2 then &0 else -- &1):real^3
       else if i = 7 then
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then --phi else if j = 2 then &0 else &1):real^3
       else if i = 8 then
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then --phi else if j = 2 then &0 else -- &1):real^3
       else if i = 9 then
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then &0 else if j = 2 then &1 else phi):real^3
       else if i = 10 then
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then &0 else if j = 2 then -- &1 else phi):real^3
       else if i = 11 then
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then &0 else if j = 2 then &1 else --phi):real^3
       else
         (lambda j. if j = 1 then &0 else if j = 2 then -- &1 else --phi):real^3 in
   !(v:real^3^12).
     (?g:real^3->real^3.
        linear g /\
        (!x:real^3. norm (g x) = norm x) /\
        (!y:real^3. ?x:real^3. g x = y) /\
        (!i:num.
           i IN 1..12
           ==> g (v$i) = inv scale % vertex i))
     ==>
     !w:real^3. !e:real.
       &0 < e
       ==>
       ?a:int^12.
         norm
           (vsum (1..12)
              (\i:num. real_of_int (a$i) % v$i) -
            w) < e`;;

title: putnam_2023_a4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a4:
;; integer combinations of the twelve regular-icosahedron vertex vectors are
;; dense in three-dimensional Euclidean space. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; These unconstrained functions are arbitrary rational Cauchy presentations
;; of the three target coordinates and the positive tolerance. All properties
;; used below are explicit hypotheses of the statement predicate.
(defstub putnam-2023-a4-w-x-approx (precision) t)
(defstub putnam-2023-a4-w-y-approx (precision) t)
(defstub putnam-2023-a4-w-z-approx (precision) t)
(defstub putnam-2023-a4-epsilon-approx (precision) t)

(defun putnam-2023-a4-positive-rational-p (value)
  (and
   (rationalp value)
   (< 0 value)))

;; A regular name q satisfies |q(p)-q(r)| <= p+r. It therefore determines a
;; unique real x with |q(p)-x| <= p, and every real has such a rational name.
(defun-sk putnam-2023-a4-regular-cauchy-inputs-p ()
  (forall (precision eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2023-a4-positive-rational-p precision)
      (putnam-2023-a4-positive-rational-p eta))
     (and
      (rationalp
       (putnam-2023-a4-w-x-approx precision))
      (rationalp
       (putnam-2023-a4-w-x-approx eta))
      (rationalp
       (putnam-2023-a4-w-y-approx precision))
      (rationalp
       (putnam-2023-a4-w-y-approx eta))
      (rationalp
       (putnam-2023-a4-w-z-approx precision))
      (rationalp
       (putnam-2023-a4-w-z-approx eta))
      (rationalp
       (putnam-2023-a4-epsilon-approx precision))
      (rationalp
       (putnam-2023-a4-epsilon-approx eta))
      (<=
       (abs
        (-
         (putnam-2023-a4-w-x-approx precision)
         (putnam-2023-a4-w-x-approx eta)))
       (+ precision eta))
      (<=
       (abs
        (-
         (putnam-2023-a4-w-y-approx precision)
         (putnam-2023-a4-w-y-approx eta)))
       (+ precision eta))
      (<=
       (abs
        (-
         (putnam-2023-a4-w-z-approx precision)
         (putnam-2023-a4-w-z-approx eta)))
       (+ precision eta))
      (<=
       (abs
        (-
         (putnam-2023-a4-epsilon-approx precision)
         (putnam-2023-a4-epsilon-approx eta)))
       (+ precision eta))))))

;; The limit of the epsilon name is positive exactly when it has a positive
;; rational lower margin of this form.
(defun-sk putnam-2023-a4-epsilon-margin-p (lower)
  (forall (precision)
    (implies
     (putnam-2023-a4-positive-rational-p precision)
     (<=
      lower
      (+
       (putnam-2023-a4-epsilon-approx precision)
       precision)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2023-a4-positive-epsilon-p ()
  (exists (lower)
    (and
     (putnam-2023-a4-positive-rational-p lower)
     (putnam-2023-a4-epsilon-margin-p lower))))

;; A pair (r s) denotes the exact real number r+s*sqrt(5).
(defun putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-rational (value)
  (list value 0))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-add (left right)
  (list
   (+ (car left) (car right))
   (+ (cadr left) (cadr right))))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-negate (value)
  (list
   (- (car value))
   (- (cadr value))))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-subtract (left right)
  (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-add
   left
   (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-negate right)))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-multiply (left right)
  (list
   (+
    (* (car left) (car right))
    (* 5 (cadr left) (cadr right)))
   (+
    (* (car left) (cadr right))
    (* (cadr left) (car right)))))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-square (value)
  (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-multiply value value))

;; For rational r and positive rational s, decide the sign of r+s*sqrt(5)
;; by comparing r^2 with 5*s^2.
(defun putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-sign-positive-root
    (rational-part root-part)
  (cond
   ((<= 0 rational-part) 1)
   ((<
     (* rational-part rational-part)
     (* 5 root-part root-part))
    1)
   ((<
     (* 5 root-part root-part)
     (* rational-part rational-part))
    -1)
   (t 0)))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-sign (value)
  (let ((rational-part (car value))
        (root-part (cadr value)))
    (cond
     ((equal root-part 0)
      (cond
       ((< rational-part 0) -1)
       ((< 0 rational-part) 1)
       (t 0)))
     ((< 0 root-part)
      (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-sign-positive-root
       rational-part root-part))
     (t
      (-
       (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-sign-positive-root
        (- rational-part)
        (- root-part)))))))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-phi-affine
    (constant coefficient)
  ;; constant + coefficient*phi, where phi=(1+sqrt(5))/2.
  (list
   (+ constant (/ coefficient 2))
   (/ coefficient 2)))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-integer-prefix-p (values count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      t
    (and
     (consp values)
     (integerp (car values))
     (putnam-2023-a4-integer-prefix-p
      (cdr values)
      (- count 1)))))

;; For the displayed unnormalized vertices u_i, these six integer expressions
;; are the constant and phi coefficients of sum_i a_i*u_i.
(defun putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-x-constant (witness)
  (+
   (nth 0 witness)
   (- (nth 1 witness))
   (nth 2 witness)
   (- (nth 3 witness))))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-x-phi (witness)
  (+
   (nth 4 witness)
   (nth 5 witness)
   (- (nth 6 witness))
   (- (nth 7 witness))))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-y-constant (witness)
  (+
   (nth 8 witness)
   (- (nth 9 witness))
   (nth 10 witness)
   (- (nth 11 witness))))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-y-phi (witness)
  (+
   (nth 0 witness)
   (nth 1 witness)
   (- (nth 2 witness))
   (- (nth 3 witness))))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-z-constant (witness)
  (+
   (nth 4 witness)
   (- (nth 5 witness))
   (nth 6 witness)
   (- (nth 7 witness))))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-z-phi (witness)
  (+
   (nth 8 witness)
   (nth 9 witness)
   (- (nth 10 witness))
   (- (nth 11 witness))))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-coordinate-error
    (constant coefficient target-sample)
  (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-subtract
   (putnam-2023-a4-phi-affine
    constant coefficient)
   (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-rational
    target-sample)))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-squared-gap
    (epsilon-sample error-x error-y error-z)
  (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-subtract
   (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-rational
    (* epsilon-sample epsilon-sample))
   (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-add
    (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-square error-x)
    (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-add
     (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-square error-y)
     (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-square error-z)))))

;; The sampled squared gap converges to
;; epsilon^2-||sum_i a_i*u_i-w||^2. Requiring it to exceed one fixed positive
;; rational margin at every sufficiently fine precision is therefore exactly
;; the strict Euclidean norm inequality.
(defun-sk putnam-2023-a4-approximation-tail-p
    (witness cutoff margin)
  (forall (precision)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2023-a4-positive-rational-p precision)
      (< precision cutoff))
     (let* ((x-sample
             (putnam-2023-a4-w-x-approx precision))
            (y-sample
             (putnam-2023-a4-w-y-approx precision))
            (z-sample
             (putnam-2023-a4-w-z-approx precision))
            (epsilon-sample
             (putnam-2023-a4-epsilon-approx precision))
            (error-x
             (putnam-2023-a4-coordinate-error
              (putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-x-constant witness)
              (putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-x-phi witness)
              x-sample))
            (error-y
             (putnam-2023-a4-coordinate-error
              (putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-y-constant witness)
              (putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-y-phi witness)
              y-sample))
            (error-z
             (putnam-2023-a4-coordinate-error
              (putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-z-constant witness)
              (putnam-2023-a4-coefficient-z-phi witness)
              z-sample))
            (gap
             (putnam-2023-a4-squared-gap
              epsilon-sample error-x error-y error-z)))
       (and
        (rationalp x-sample)
        (rationalp y-sample)
        (rationalp z-sample)
        (rationalp epsilon-sample)
        (equal
         (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-sign
          (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-subtract
           gap
           (putnam-2023-a4-qroot5-rational margin)))
         1))))))

(defun putnam-2023-a4-approximation-witness-p
    (witness cutoff margin)
  (and
   (true-listp witness)
   (equal (len witness) 12)
   (putnam-2023-a4-integer-prefix-p witness 12)
   (putnam-2023-a4-positive-rational-p cutoff)
   (putnam-2023-a4-positive-rational-p margin)
   (putnam-2023-a4-approximation-tail-p
    witness cutoff margin)))

(defun-sk putnam-2023-a4-approximation-exists-p ()
  (exists (witness cutoff margin)
    (putnam-2023-a4-approximation-witness-p
     witness cutoff margin)))

;; If g(v_i)=u_i/s for the source isometry and positive normalization s, then
;; the source inequality is equivalent to
;; ||sum_i a_i*u_i-s*g(w)|| < s*epsilon. Conversely, choose v_i=u_i/s and the
;; identity isometry. Thus the canonical unnormalized density predicate below
;; is bidirectionally equivalent to the quantified source statement.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2023-a4-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2023-a4-regular-cauchy-inputs-p)
    (putnam-2023-a4-positive-epsilon-p))
   (putnam-2023-a4-approximation-exists-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2023_a4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2023_a4): density in real three-space of the
-- integer span of the normalized vertex vectors of a regular icosahedron.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2023A4 where

open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; _⊔_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : {l : Level} -> Set l -> Set l
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {l : Level} {A : Set l} -> A -> A -> Set l
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists
  {l1 l2 : Level}
  (A : Set l1)
  (P : A -> Set l2) :
  Set (l1 ⊔ l2) where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessThan : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR
    negate-involutive :
      (x : R) -> negate (negate x) == x

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-irreflexive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessThan x x ->
      Bottom
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessThan x y ->
      lessThan y z ->
      lessThan x z
    order-trichotomy :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessThan x y or
      (x == y or lessThan y x)
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessThan x y ->
      lessThan (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-positive :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessThan zeroR x ->
      lessThan zeroR y ->
      lessThan zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessThan zeroR oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) ==
      add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) ==
      multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessThan x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessThan x upper or x == upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessThan x supremum or x == supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessThan x upper or x == upper) ->
            lessThan supremum upper or supremum == upper))

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessThan zeroR (squareRoot x) or
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      (lessThan zeroR x or x == zeroR) ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      (lessThan x zeroR or x == zeroR) ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      (lessThan zeroR y or y == zeroR) ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

open CompleteOrderedRealField

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

threeN : Nat
threeN =
  suc twoN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  suc threeN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc fourN

sixN : Nat
sixN =
  suc fiveN

sevenN : Nat
sevenN =
  suc sixN

eightN : Nat
eightN =
  suc sevenN

nineN : Nat
nineN =
  suc eightN

tenN : Nat
tenN =
  suc nineN

elevenN : Nat
elevenN =
  suc tenN

twelveN : Nat
twelveN =
  suc elevenN

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

fromInt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Int ->
  R
fromInt reals (pos n) =
  fromNat reals n
fromInt reals (negsuc n) =
  negate reals (fromNat reals (suc n))

Vector3 : Set -> Set
Vector3 R =
  Fin threeN -> R

vec3 :
  {R : Set} ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Vector3 R
vec3 x y z fzero =
  x
vec3 x y z (fsuc fzero) =
  y
vec3 x y z (fsuc (fsuc fzero)) =
  z

SameVector :
  {R : Set} ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Set
SameVector leftVector rightVector =
  (coordinate : Fin threeN) ->
  leftVector coordinate == rightVector coordinate

zeroVector :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Vector3 R
zeroVector reals _ =
  zeroR reals

addVector :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Vector3 R
addVector reals x y coordinate =
  add reals (x coordinate) (y coordinate)

negateVector :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Vector3 R
negateVector reals x coordinate =
  negate reals (x coordinate)

subtractVector :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Vector3 R
subtractVector reals x y =
  addVector reals x (negateVector reals y)

scaleVector :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  Vector3 R
scaleVector reals scalar x coordinate =
  multiply reals scalar (x coordinate)

squaredNorm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  R
squaredNorm reals x =
  add reals
    (square reals (x fzero))
    (add reals
      (square reals (x (fsuc fzero)))
      (square reals (x (fsuc (fsuc fzero)))))

norm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Vector3 R ->
  R
norm reals x =
  squareRoot reals (squaredNorm reals x)

record LinearIsometryEquivalence
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where
  field
    toFunction inverseFunction :
      Vector3 R -> Vector3 R

    to-additive :
      (x y : Vector3 R) ->
      SameVector
        (toFunction (addVector reals x y))
        (addVector reals (toFunction x) (toFunction y))
    to-scaled :
      (scalar : R) ->
      (x : Vector3 R) ->
      SameVector
        (toFunction (scaleVector reals scalar x))
        (scaleVector reals scalar (toFunction x))

    left-inverse :
      (x : Vector3 R) ->
      SameVector
        (inverseFunction (toFunction x))
        x
    right-inverse :
      (x : Vector3 R) ->
      SameVector
        (toFunction (inverseFunction x))
        x

    norm-preserving :
      (x : Vector3 R) ->
      norm reals (toFunction x) == norm reals x

open LinearIsometryEquivalence

sumFin :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> R) ->
  R
sumFin reals {zero} terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFin reals {suc n} terms =
  add reals
    (terms fzero)
    (sumFin reals (\ i -> terms (fsuc i)))

module Putnam2023A4Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  phi : R
  phi =
    divide reals
      (add reals
        (oneR reals)
        (squareRoot reals (fromNat reals fiveN)))
      (fromNat reals twoN)

  normalization : R
  normalization =
    squareRoot reals
      (add reals
        (oneR reals)
        (square reals phi))

  canonicalVector :
    Fin twelveN ->
    Vector3 R
  canonicalVector fzero =
    vec3 (oneR reals) phi (zeroR reals)
  canonicalVector (fsuc fzero) =
    vec3 (negate reals (oneR reals)) phi (zeroR reals)
  canonicalVector (fsuc (fsuc fzero)) =
    vec3 (oneR reals) (negate reals phi) (zeroR reals)
  canonicalVector (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc fzero))) =
    vec3 (negate reals (oneR reals)) (negate reals phi) (zeroR reals)
  canonicalVector (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc fzero)))) =
    vec3 phi (zeroR reals) (oneR reals)
  canonicalVector (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc fzero))))) =
    vec3 phi (zeroR reals) (negate reals (oneR reals))
  canonicalVector (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc fzero)))))) =
    vec3 (negate reals phi) (zeroR reals) (oneR reals)
  canonicalVector (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc fzero))))))) =
    vec3 (negate reals phi) (zeroR reals) (negate reals (oneR reals))
  canonicalVector
    (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc fzero)))))))) =
    vec3 (zeroR reals) (oneR reals) phi
  canonicalVector
    (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc fzero))))))))) =
    vec3 (zeroR reals) (negate reals (oneR reals)) phi
  canonicalVector
    (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc fzero)))))))))) =
    vec3 (zeroR reals) (oneR reals) (negate reals phi)
  canonicalVector
    (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc (fsuc fzero))))))))))) =
    vec3
      (zeroR reals)
      (negate reals (oneR reals))
      (negate reals phi)

  normalizedCanonicalVector :
    Fin twelveN ->
    Vector3 R
  normalizedCanonicalVector i =
    scaleVector reals
      (inverse reals normalization)
      (canonicalVector i)

  IcosahedronModel :
    (Fin twelveN -> Vector3 R) ->
    Set1
  IcosahedronModel v =
    Exists (LinearIsometryEquivalence reals)
      (\ isometry ->
        (i : Fin twelveN) ->

          (toFunction isometry (v i))
          (normalizedCanonicalVector i))

  integerCombination :
    (Fin twelveN -> Vector3 R) ->
    (Fin twelveN -> Int) ->
    Vector3 R
  integerCombination v coefficients coordinate =
    sumFin reals
      (\ i ->
        multiply reals
          (fromInt reals (coefficients i))
          (v i coordinate))

  proposition : Set1
  proposition =
    (v : Fin twelveN -> Vector3 R) ->
    IcosahedronModel v ->
    (w : Vector3 R) ->
    (epsilon : R) ->
    lessThan reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
    Exists (Fin twelveN -> Int)
      (\ coefficients ->
        lessThan reals
          (norm reals
            (subtractVector reals
              (integerCombination v coefficients)
              w))
          epsilon)

putnam-2023-a4 =

(*

  integer linear combinations of the twelve unit vertex vectors of a regular
  icosahedron are dense in real three-space. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory;
open intrealTheory real_sigmaTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2023_a4 =
  ``let zero3 = (0, (0, 0)) : real # (real # real)
    in
    let add3 =
      \x y : real # (real # real).
        (FST x + FST y,
         (FST (SND x) + FST (SND y),
          SND (SND x) + SND (SND y)))
    in
    let sub3 =
      \x y : real # (real # real).
        (FST x - FST y,
         (FST (SND x) - FST (SND y),
          SND (SND x) - SND (SND y)))
    in
    let smul3 =
      \c : real.
      \x : real # (real # real).
        (c * FST x, (c * FST (SND x), c * SND (SND x)))
    in
    let norm3 =
      \x : real # (real # real).
        sqrt
          (FST x pow 2 +
           FST (SND x) pow 2 +
           SND (SND x) pow 2)
    in
    let linear_isometry =
      \g : (real # (real # real)) -> (real # (real # real)).
        BIJ g UNIV UNIV /\
        (!x y : real # (real # real).
           g (add3 x y) = add3 (g x) (g y)) /\
        (!c : real.
           !x : real # (real # real).
             g (smul3 c x) = smul3 c (g x)) /\
        (!x : real # (real # real). norm3 (g x) = norm3 x)
    in
    let phi = (1 + sqrt 5) / 2
    in
    let scale = sqrt (1 + phi pow 2)
    in
    let vertex =
      \i : num.
        if i = 0 then (1, (phi, 0))
        else if i = 1 then (~1, (phi, 0))
        else if i = 2 then (1, (~phi, 0))
        else if i = 3 then (~1, (~phi, 0))
        else if i = 4 then (phi, (0, 1))
        else if i = 5 then (phi, (0, ~1))
        else if i = 6 then (~phi, (0, 1))
        else if i = 7 then (~phi, (0, ~1))
        else if i = 8 then (0, (1, phi))
        else if i = 9 then (0, (~1, phi))
        else if i = 10 then (0, (1, ~phi))
        else if i = 11 then (0, (~1, ~phi))
        else zero3
    in
    let is_icosahedron =
      \v : num -> real # (real # real).
        ?g : (real # (real # real)) -> (real # (real # real)).
          linear_isometry g /\
          !i : num.
            i < 12
            ==>
            g (v i) = smul3 (1 / scale) (vertex i)
    in
    let integer_combination =
      \v : num -> real # (real # real).
      \a : num -> int.
        (SIGMA
           (\i : num. real_of_int (a i) * FST (v i))
           (count 12),
         (SIGMA
            (\i : num. real_of_int (a i) * FST (SND (v i)))
            (count 12),
          SIGMA
            (\i : num. real_of_int (a i) * SND (SND (v i)))
            (count 12)))
    in
      !v : num -> real # (real # real).
      !w : real # (real # real).
      !epsilon : real.
        is_icosahedron v /\
        0 < epsilon
        ==>
        ?a : num -> int.
          norm3 (sub3 (integer_combination v a) w) < epsilon``;

title: putnam_2023_a4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a4:
% the integer span of the twelve normalized regular-icosahedron vertex vectors
% is dense in real three-dimensional Euclidean space. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2023_a4: THEORY
BEGIN
  coordinate: TYPE = below(3)
  vertex_index: TYPE = below(12)
  vector: TYPE = [coordinate -> real]
  vertex_family: TYPE = [vertex_index -> vector]
  integer_coefficients: TYPE = [vertex_index -> int]
  matrix: TYPE = [coordinate, coordinate -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  dot_product(x, y: vector): real =
    x(0) * y(0) + x(1) * y(1) + x(2) * y(2)

  squared_distance(x, y: vector): real =
    (x(0) - y(0)) ^ 2
      + (x(1) - y(1)) ^ 2
      + (x(2) - y(2)) ^ 2

  scalar_multiply(scalar: real, x: vector): vector =
    LAMBDA (c: coordinate): scalar * x(c)

  matrix_vector_product(A: matrix, x: vector): vector =
    LAMBDA (row: coordinate):
      A(row, 0) * x(0)
        + A(row, 1) * x(1)
        + A(row, 2) * x(2)

  linear_isometric_equivalence(G, H: matrix): bool =
    (FORALL (x: vector):
      matrix_vector_product(G, matrix_vector_product(H, x)) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x: vector):
        matrix_vector_product(H, matrix_vector_product(G, x)) = x)
      AND (FORALL (x, y: vector):
        dot_product(
          matrix_vector_product(G, x),
          matrix_vector_product(G, y))
          = dot_product(x, y))

  sqrt_value(root, radicand: real): bool =
    0 <= root AND root ^ 2 = radicand

  icosahedron_vertex(index: vertex_index, phi: real): vector =
    LAMBDA (c: coordinate):
      IF index = 0 THEN
        IF c = 0 THEN 1 ELSIF c = 1 THEN phi ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ELSIF index = 1 THEN
        IF c = 0 THEN -1 ELSIF c = 1 THEN phi ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ELSIF index = 2 THEN
        IF c = 0 THEN 1 ELSIF c = 1 THEN -phi ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ELSIF index = 3 THEN
        IF c = 0 THEN -1 ELSIF c = 1 THEN -phi ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ELSIF index = 4 THEN
        IF c = 0 THEN phi ELSIF c = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ELSIF index = 5 THEN
        IF c = 0 THEN phi ELSIF c = 2 THEN -1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ELSIF index = 6 THEN
        IF c = 0 THEN -phi ELSIF c = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ELSIF index = 7 THEN
        IF c = 0 THEN -phi ELSIF c = 2 THEN -1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ELSIF index = 8 THEN
        IF c = 1 THEN 1 ELSIF c = 2 THEN phi ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ELSIF index = 9 THEN
        IF c = 1 THEN -1 ELSIF c = 2 THEN phi ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ELSIF index = 10 THEN
        IF c = 1 THEN 1 ELSIF c = 2 THEN -phi ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ELSE
        IF c = 1 THEN -1 ELSIF c = 2 THEN -phi ELSE 0 ENDIF
      ENDIF

  regular_icosahedron_vertices(vertices: vertex_family): bool =
    EXISTS (sqrt_five, phi, scale: real), (G, H: matrix):
      sqrt_value(sqrt_five, 5)
        AND phi = (1 + sqrt_five) / 2
        AND 0 < scale
        AND scale ^ 2 = 1 + phi ^ 2
        AND linear_isometric_equivalence(G, H)
        AND (FORALL (index: vertex_index):
          matrix_vector_product(G, vertices(index))
            = scalar_multiply(
                safe_div(1, scale),
                icosahedron_vertex(index, phi)))

  integer_combination(
      coefficients: integer_coefficients,
      vertices: vertex_family): vector =
    LAMBDA (c: coordinate):
      (coefficients(0) :: real) * vertices(0)(c)
        + (coefficients(1) :: real) * vertices(1)(c)
        + (coefficients(2) :: real) * vertices(2)(c)
        + (coefficients(3) :: real) * vertices(3)(c)
        + (coefficients(4) :: real) * vertices(4)(c)
        + (coefficients(5) :: real) * vertices(5)(c)
        + (coefficients(6) :: real) * vertices(6)(c)
        + (coefficients(7) :: real) * vertices(7)(c)
        + (coefficients(8) :: real) * vertices(8)(c)
        + (coefficients(9) :: real) * vertices(9)(c)
        + (coefficients(10) :: real) * vertices(10)(c)
        + (coefficients(11) :: real) * vertices(11)(c)

  putnam_2023_a4: bool =
    FORALL
        (vertices: vertex_family),
        (target: vector),
        (epsilon_value: posreal):
      regular_icosahedron_vertices(vertices)
        IMPLIES
          EXISTS (coefficients: integer_coefficients):
            squared_distance(
              integer_combination(coefficients, vertices),
              target)
              < epsilon_value ^ 2
END putnam_2023_a4

For a nonnegative integer $k$, let $f(k)$ be the number of ones in the base 3 representation of $k$. Find all complex numbers $z$ such that \[ \sum_{k=0}^{3^{1010}-1} (-2)^{f(k)} (z+k)^{2023} = 0. \]

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a5:
   the complex zeros of a weighted power sum determined by ternary digit counts;
   this file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Definition putnam_2023_a5_complex := (R * R)%type.

Definition putnam_2023_a5_cadd
    (z w : putnam_2023_a5_complex) : putnam_2023_a5_complex :=
  ((fst z + fst w)%R, (snd z + snd w)%R).

Definition putnam_2023_a5_cmul
    (z w : putnam_2023_a5_complex) : putnam_2023_a5_complex :=
  ((fst z * fst w - snd z * snd w)%R,
   (fst z * snd w + snd z * fst w)%R).

Fixpoint putnam_2023_a5_cpow
    (z : putnam_2023_a5_complex) (n : nat) : putnam_2023_a5_complex :=
  match n with
  | O => (1%R, 0%R)
  | S n' => putnam_2023_a5_cmul z (putnam_2023_a5_cpow z n')
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2023_a5_csum
    (f : nat -> putnam_2023_a5_complex) (n : nat)
    : putnam_2023_a5_complex :=
  match n with
  | O => f O
  | S n' => putnam_2023_a5_cadd (putnam_2023_a5_csum f n') (f (S n'))
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2023_a5_num_ones_aux (fuel k : nat) : nat :=
  match fuel with
  | O => O
  | S fuel' =>
      (if Nat.eqb (k mod 3) 1 then 1 else 0) +
      putnam_2023_a5_num_ones_aux fuel' (k / 3)
  end.

Definition putnam_2023_a5_num_ones (k : nat) : nat :=
  putnam_2023_a5_num_ones_aux (S k) k.

Definition putnam_2023_a5_center : R :=
  (- (INR (Nat.pow 3 1010) - 1) / 2)%R.

Definition putnam_2023_a5_offset : R :=
  (sqrt (INR (Nat.pow 9 1010) - 1) / 4)%R.

Definition putnam_2023_a5_polynomial
    (z : putnam_2023_a5_complex) : putnam_2023_a5_complex :=
  putnam_2023_a5_csum
    (fun k : nat =>
       putnam_2023_a5_cmul
         (putnam_2023_a5_cpow
            ((-2)%R, 0%R) (putnam_2023_a5_num_ones k))
         (putnam_2023_a5_cpow
            (putnam_2023_a5_cadd z (INR k, 0%R)) 2023))
    (Nat.pow 3 1010 - 1).

Theorem putnam_2023_a5 :
  forall z : putnam_2023_a5_complex,
    putnam_2023_a5_polynomial z = (0%R, 0%R) <->
    z = (putnam_2023_a5_center, 0%R) \/
    z = (putnam_2023_a5_center, putnam_2023_a5_offset) \/
    z = (putnam_2023_a5_center, (- putnam_2023_a5_offset)%R).
Proof.
Admitted.

;; the complex zeros of the weighted sum
;; sum_{k=0}^{3^1010-1} (-2)^(number of base-3 ones in k) (z+k)^2023
;; are exactly the three specified values. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Scalars are interpreted in an arbitrary real closed ordered field. Real
;; closed fields are elementarily equivalent, and the assertion below is
;; first-order in ordered-field operations. Complex numbers are pairs of field
;; elements, so this does not restrict their real or imaginary parts to ACL2's
;; rational numbers.
;; A tame external polynomial evaluator is constrained by universal Horner
;; laws, making it definitionally equivalent to polynomial evaluation while
;; keeping every FN-EQUAL operand within ACL2's APPLY$ language.
;;
;; The two nonreal roots have real part -(3^1010-1)/2 and imaginary part y
;; satisfying y^2 = (9^1010-1)/16. Over a real closed ordered field this is
;; bidirectionally equivalent to y = +/-sqrt(9^1010-1)/4, without turning the
;; square root into an external witness. The argument Z supplies the universal
;; quantifier implicit in the source set equality.

(defun putnam-2023-a5-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2023-a5-quoted function)
   (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2023-a5-quoted function)
   (list 'cons left (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-and-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2023-a5-quoted t)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2023-a5-and-term (cdr terms))
     (putnam-2023-a5-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-or-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2023-a5-quoted nil)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2023-a5-quoted t)
     (putnam-2023-a5-or-term (cdr terms)))))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-not-term (term)
  (list
   'if
   term
   (putnam-2023-a5-quoted nil)
   (putnam-2023-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-implies-term (antecedent consequent)
  (list
   'if
   antecedent
   consequent
   (putnam-2023-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-true-function (formals)
  (list
   'lambda
   formals
   (putnam-2023-a5-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-2023-a5-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-operation-term (operation left right)
  (putnam-2023-a5-apply2-term operation left right))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-all-coefficients-function (carrier)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)
   (putnam-2023-a5-carrier-term
    carrier 'loop$-ivars)))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-all-coefficients-term
    (carrier coefficients)
  (list
   'always$+
   (putnam-2023-a5-quoted
    (putnam-2023-a5-all-coefficients-function
     carrier))
   (putnam-2023-a5-quoted nil)
   coefficients))

(defun putnam-2023-a5-polynomial-term
    (carrier zero coefficients)
  (putnam-2023-a5-and-term
   (list

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2023_a5): the complex zeros of a finite
-- polynomial sum weighted by counts of ones in ternary expansions.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2023A5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_; div-helper; mod-helper)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_
infix 1 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse squareRoot : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) ==
      add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) ==
      multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

    square-root-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (squareRoot x)
    square-root-square :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      multiply (squareRoot x) (squareRoot x) == x
    square-root-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      squareRoot x == zeroR
    square-root-unique :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      multiply y y == x ->
      y == squareRoot x

open CompleteOrderedRealField

naturalPower : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalPower base zero =
  suc zero
naturalPower base (suc exponent) =
  naturalPower base exponent * base

naturalDiv : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalDiv numerator zero =
  zero
naturalDiv numerator (suc denominator) =
  div-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero =
  zero
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

oneIndicator : Nat -> Nat
oneIndicator zero =
  zero
oneIndicator (suc zero) =
  suc zero
oneIndicator (suc (suc n)) =
  zero

ternaryOneCountWithFuel : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
ternaryOneCountWithFuel zero n =
  zero
ternaryOneCountWithFuel (suc fuel) zero =
  zero
ternaryOneCountWithFuel (suc fuel) (suc n) =
  oneIndicator (naturalMod (suc n) 3) +
  ternaryOneCountWithFuel fuel (naturalDiv (suc n) 3)

ternaryOneCount : Nat -> Nat
ternaryOneCount zero =
  zero
ternaryOneCount (suc n) =
  ternaryOneCountWithFuel (suc n) (suc n)

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

record Complex (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor complex
  field
    realPart      : R
    imaginaryPart : R

open Complex

complexZero :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R
complexZero reals =
  complex (zeroR reals) (zeroR reals)

complexOne :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R
complexOne reals =
  complex (oneR reals) (zeroR reals)

complexFromNat :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  Complex R
complexFromNat reals n =
  complex (fromNat reals n) (zeroR reals)

complexAdd :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexAdd reals z w =
  complex
    (add reals (realPart z) (realPart w))
    (add reals (imaginaryPart z) (imaginaryPart w))

complexMultiply :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R ->
  Complex R
complexMultiply reals z w =
  complex
    (subtract reals
      (multiply reals (realPart z) (realPart w))
      (multiply reals (imaginaryPart z) (imaginaryPart w)))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals (realPart z) (imaginaryPart w))
      (multiply reals (imaginaryPart z) (realPart w)))

complexPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Complex R ->
  Nat ->
  Complex R
complexPower reals z zero =
  complexOne reals
complexPower reals z (suc n) =
  complexMultiply reals (complexPower reals z n) z

record FiniteComplexSummation
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set where
  field
    sumFirst :
      Nat ->
      (Nat -> Complex R) ->
      Complex R

    sum-zero :
      (term : Nat -> Complex R) ->
      sumFirst zero term == complexZero reals

    sum-successor :
      (count : Nat) ->
      (term : Nat -> Complex R) ->
      sumFirst (suc count) term ==
      complexAdd reals
        (sumFirst count term)
        (term count)

open FiniteComplexSummation

module Putnam2023A5Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R)
  (sums : FiniteComplexSummation reals) where

  threeTo1010 : Nat
  threeTo1010 =
    naturalPower 3 1010

  nineTo1010 : Nat
  nineTo1010 =
    naturalPower 9 1010

  minusTwo : Complex R
  minusTwo =
    complex
      (negate reals (fromNat reals 2))
      (zeroR reals)

  polynomialValue : Complex R -> Complex R
  polynomialValue z =
    sumFirst sums threeTo1010
      (\ k ->
        complexMultiply reals
          (complexPower reals minusTwo (ternaryOneCount k))
          (complexPower reals
            (complexAdd reals z (complexFromNat reals k))
            2023))

  center : R
  center =
    negate reals
      (divide reals
        (subtract reals
          (fromNat reals threeTo1010)
          (oneR reals))
        (fromNat reals 2))

  imaginaryOffset : R
  imaginaryOffset =
    divide reals
      (squareRoot reals
        (subtract reals
          (fromNat reals nineTo1010)
          (oneR reals)))
      (fromNat reals 4)

  ExplicitSolution : Complex R -> Set
  ExplicitSolution z =
    z == complex center (zeroR reals)
    or
    z == complex center imaginaryOffset
    or
    z == complex center (negate reals imaginaryOffset)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (z : Complex R) ->
    (polynomialValue z == complexZero reals)
    iff
    ExplicitSolution z

putnam-2023-a5 : Set1
putnam-2023-a5 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (sums : FiniteComplexSummation reals) ->
  Putnam2023A5Statement.proposition reals sums

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a5:
% the complex zeros of the weighted power sum whose coefficients count ones
% in ternary expansions are exactly the stated three values. This file contains
% no proof.

putnam_2023_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  complex: TYPE = [# real_part: real, imag_part: real #]

  complex_zero: complex =
    (# real_part := 0, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_one: complex =
    (# real_part := 1, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_of_real(value: real): complex =
    (# real_part := value, imag_part := 0 #)

  complex_of_nat(value: nat): complex =
    complex_of_real(value :: real)

  complex_add(left, right: complex): complex =
    (# real_part := real_part(left) + real_part(right),
       imag_part := imag_part(left) + imag_part(right) #)

  complex_mul(left, right: complex): complex =
    (# real_part :=
         real_part(left) * real_part(right)
           - imag_part(left) * imag_part(right),
       imag_part :=
         real_part(left) * imag_part(right)
           + imag_part(left) * real_part(right) #)

  complex_scale(scalar: real, value: complex): complex =
    complex_mul(complex_of_real(scalar), value)

  complex_power(value: complex, exponent: nat): RECURSIVE complex =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      complex_one
    ELSE
      complex_mul(complex_power(value, exponent - 1), value)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  ternary_one_count_below(
      value, count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        ternary_one_count_below(value, count - 1)
          + IF mod(ndiv(value, 3 ^ index), 3) = 1 THEN
              1
            ELSE
              0
            ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  base3_one_count(value: nat): nat =
    ternary_one_count_below(value, value + 1)

  weighted_power_sum(
      z: complex,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE complex =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      complex_zero
    ELSE
      LET k: nat = count - 1 IN
        complex_add(
          weighted_power_sum(z, count - 1),
          complex_scale(
            ((-2 :: real) ^ base3_one_count(k)),
            complex_power(
              complex_add(z, complex_of_nat(k)),
              2023)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  sqrt_value(root, radicand: real): bool =
    0 <= root AND root ^ 2 = radicand

  solution_center: real =
    -((3 ^ 1010 - 1) :: real) / 2

  putnam_2023_a5_solution(
      z: complex,
      sqrt_discriminant: real): bool =
    z = complex_of_real(solution_center)
      OR z =
        (# real_part := solution_center,
           imag_part := sqrt_discriminant / 4 #)
      OR z =
        (# real_part := solution_center,
           imag_part := -sqrt_discriminant / 4 #)

  putnam_2023_a5: bool =
    EXISTS (sqrt_discriminant: real):
      sqrt_value(
        sqrt_discriminant,
        (9 ^ 1010 - 1) :: real)
        AND FORALL (z: complex):
          (weighted_power_sum(z, 3 ^ 1010) = complex_zero)
            IFF
              putnam_2023_a5_solution(
                z, sqrt_discriminant)
END putnam_2023_a5

import Mathlib

open Finset

abbrev putnam_2023_a6_solution : Set ℕ := {n : ℕ | 0 < n}
/--
Alice and Bob play a game in which they take turns choosing integers from $1$ to $n$. Before any integers are chosen, Bob selects a goal of 'odd' or 'even'. On the first turn, Alice chooses one of the $n$ integers. On the second turn, Bob chooses one of the remaining integers. They continue alternately choosing one of the integers that has not yet been chosen, until the $n$th turn, which is forced and ends the game. Bob wins if the parity of $\{k : \mbox{the number $k$ was chosen on the $k$th turn}\}$ matches his goal. For which values of $n$ does Bob have a winning strategy?
-/
theorem putnam_2023_a6
    (IsValidGame : List ℕ → Prop)
    (IsValidGame_def : ∀ g, IsValidGame g ↔ g.Nodup ∧ (∀ i ∈ g, i ∈ Icc 1 g.length))
    (parityOf : List ℕ → ZMod 2)
    (parityOf_def : ∀ g, parityOf g = ((range g.length).filter fun i ↦ g[i]! = i + 1).card)
    (ConformsToStrategy : List ℕ → (List ℕ → ℕ) → Prop)
    (ConformsToStrategy_def : ∀ g s, ConformsToStrategy g s ↔
      ∀ (i) (h : i < g.length), Odd i → g[i] = s (g.take i))
    (IsValidStrategy : ℕ → (List ℕ → ℕ) → Prop)
    (IsValidStrategy_def : ∀ n s, IsValidStrategy n s ↔
      ∀ g : List ℕ, g.Nodup → (∀ k ∈ g, k ∈ Icc 1 n) →
        Odd g.length → g.length < n → s g ∈ Icc 1 n ∧ s g ∉ g)
    (IsWinningFor : ℕ → (List ℕ → ℕ) → Prop)
    (IsWinningFor_def : ∀ n s, IsWinningFor n s ↔
      IsValidStrategy n s ∧ ∃ p, ∀ g, g.length = n → IsValidGame g →
        ConformsToStrategy g s → parityOf g = p) :
    {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ ∃ s, IsWinningFor n s} = putnam_2023_a6_solution :=
  sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a6:
   Bob has a winning parity strategy in the alternating permutation game for
   every positive number of choices. This file contains no proof. *)

From Coq Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List.

Definition putnam_2023_a6_valid_game (n : nat) (g : list nat) : Prop :=
  length g = n /\
  NoDup g /\
  forall x : nat, In x g -> (1 <= x <= n)%nat.

Definition putnam_2023_a6_valid_partial_game
    (n : nat) (g : list nat) : Prop :=
  (length g <= n)%nat /\
  NoDup g /\
  forall x : nat, In x g -> (1 <= x <= n)%nat.

Definition putnam_2023_a6_fixed_at (g : list nat) (i : nat) : bool :=
  match nth_error g i with
  | Some x => Nat.eqb x (S i)
  | None => false
  end.

Definition putnam_2023_a6_parity (g : list nat) : nat :=
  (length
     (filter
        (putnam_2023_a6_fixed_at g)
        (seq 0 (length g)))) mod 2.

Definition putnam_2023_a6_conforms
    (g : list nat) (strategy : list nat -> nat) : Prop :=
  forall i : nat,
    (i < length g)%nat ->
    Nat.Odd i ->
    nth_error g i = Some (strategy (firstn i g)).

Definition putnam_2023_a6_valid_strategy
    (n : nat) (strategy : list nat -> nat) : Prop :=
  forall g : list nat,
    putnam_2023_a6_valid_partial_game n g ->
    (length g < n)%nat ->
    Nat.Odd (length g) ->
    (1 <= strategy g <= n)%nat /\
    ~ In (strategy g) g.

Definition putnam_2023_a6_winning_strategy
    (n : nat) (strategy : list nat -> nat) : Prop :=
  putnam_2023_a6_valid_strategy n strategy /\
  exists goal : nat,
    (goal < 2)%nat /\
    forall g : list nat,
      putnam_2023_a6_valid_game n g ->
      putnam_2023_a6_conforms g strategy ->
      putnam_2023_a6_parity g = goal.

Definition putnam_2023_a6_solution (n : nat) : Prop :=
  (0 < n)%nat.

Theorem putnam_2023_a6 :
  forall n : nat,
    ((0 < n)%nat /\
     exists strategy : list nat -> nat,
       putnam_2023_a6_winning_strategy n strategy) <->
    putnam_2023_a6_solution n.
Admitted.

"HOL-Number_Theory.Cong"
begin

definition putnam_2023_a6_solution :: "nat set" where
"putnam_2023_a6_solution \<equiv> {n :: nat. 0 < n}"
theorem putnam_2023_a6:
  fixes IsValidGame :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> bool"
    and parityOf :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat"
    and ConformsToStrategy :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> (nat list \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> bool"
    and IsValidStrategy :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat list \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> bool"
    and IsWinningFor :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat list \<Rightarrow> nat) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  assumes IsValidGame_def : "\<forall> g. (IsValidGame g \<longleftrightarrow>
	       distinct g \<and> (\<forall> i \<in> set g. i \<in> {1..length g}))"
    and parityOf_def : "\<forall> g. parityOf g =
      card {n :: nat. n \<in> {0..<length g} \<and> nth g n = n + 1} mod 2"
    and ConformsToStrategy_def : "\<forall> g s. (ConformsToStrategy g s \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall> i \<in> {1..<length g}. odd i \<longrightarrow> nth g i = s (take i g)))"
    and IsValidStrategy_def : "\<forall> n s. (IsValidStrategy n s \<longleftrightarrow>
      (\<forall> g. distinct g \<longrightarrow>
        (\<forall> k \<in> set g. k \<in> {1..n}) \<longrightarrow>
        odd (length g) \<longrightarrow> length g < n \<longrightarrow>
        s g \<in> {1..n} \<and> s g \<notin> set g))"
    and IsWinningFor_def : "\<forall> n s. (IsWinningFor n s \<longleftrightarrow>
          IsValidStrategy n s \<and>
          (\<exists> p. \<forall> g. length g = n \<longrightarrow> IsValidGame g
            \<longrightarrow> ConformsToStrategy g s \<longrightarrow> parityOf g = p))"
  shows "{n :: nat. 0 < n \<and> (\<exists> s. IsWinningFor n s)} = putnam_2023_a6_solution"

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a6
  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2023_a6): Bob has a winning parity strategy
  in the alternating permutation game for every positive n. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let legal_sequence =
     \(n:num) (g:num list).
       (!i:num.
          i < LENGTH g
          ==> 1 <= EL i g /\ EL i g <= n) /\
       (!i:num. !j:num.
          i < LENGTH g /\ j < LENGTH g /\ EL i g = EL j g
          ==> i = j) in
   let valid_game =
     \(n:num) (g:num list).
       LENGTH g = n /\ legal_sequence n g in
   let conforms_to_strategy =
     \(g:num list) (s:num list->num).
       !h:num list. !x:num. !t:num list.
         g = APPEND h (CONS x t) /\ ODD (LENGTH h)
         ==> x = s h in
   let valid_strategy =
     \(n:num) (s:num list->num).
       !g:num list.
         legal_sequence n g /\
         ODD (LENGTH g) /\
         LENGTH g < n
         ==> 1 <= s g /\ s g <= n /\ ~MEM (s g) g in
   let odd_match_parity =
     \(g:num list).
       ODD (CARD {i:num | i < LENGTH g /\ EL i g = i + 1}) in
   let winning_strategy =
     \(n:num) (s:num list->num).
       valid_strategy n s /\
       ?goal_is_odd:bool.
         !g:num list.
           valid_game n g /\ conforms_to_strategy g s
           ==> (odd_match_parity g <=> goal_is_odd) in
   {n:num | 0 < n /\ ?s:num list->num. winning_strategy n s} =
   {n:num | 0 < n}`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a6:
;; Bob has a winning parity strategy in the alternating permutation game for
;; every positive number of available integers. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The remaining integers are represented by their exact finite list. At an
;; Alice node every legal choice must preserve Bob's win; at a Bob node one
;; legal choice suffices. Thus backward induction is equivalent in both
;; directions to an existential Bob strategy followed by universal
;; quantification over all conforming valid games. The parity goal is selected
;; outside the game-tree search, so Bob chooses it before Alice's first move.

(defun putnam-2023-a6-range-from (start count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons
     start
     (putnam-2023-a6-range-from
      (+ start 1) (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2023-a6-remove-first (value values)
  (if (endp values)
      nil
    (if (equal value (car values))
        (cdr values)
      (cons
       (car values)
       (putnam-2023-a6-remove-first
        value (cdr values))))))

;; A :VALUE call starts a node, while a :SCAN call aggregates its legal
;; children. The lexicographic measure first counts moves left and then
;; distinguishes node entry from the number of unscanned choices.

(defun putnam-2023-a6-search-measure
    (moves-left phase choices-left)
  (make-ord
   1
   (+ 1 (nfix moves-left))
   (if (equal phase :value)
       (+ 1 (nfix moves-left))
     (nfix choices-left))))

(defun putnam-2023-a6-bob-wins-search
    (remaining moves-left turn fixed-points goal
               phase choices choices-left aggregate)
  (declare
   (xargs
    :measure
    (putnam-2023-a6-search-measure
     moves-left phase choices-left)
    :well-founded-relation o<))
  (cond
   ((equal phase :value)
    (if (or (zp moves-left)
            (endp remaining))
        (equal (mod fixed-points 2) goal)
      (putnam-2023-a6-bob-wins-search
       remaining
       moves-left
       turn
       fixed-points
       goal
       :scan
       remaining
       moves-left
       (if (evenp turn) t nil))))
   ((or (zp moves-left)
        (zp choices-left)
        (endp choices))
    aggregate)
   (t
    (let* ((choice (car choices))
           (next-fixed-points
            (+ fixed-points
               (if (equal choice (+ turn 1)) 1 0)))
           (child-win
            (putnam-2023-a6-bob-wins-search
             (putnam-2023-a6-remove-first
              choice remaining)
             (- moves-left 1)
             (+ turn 1)
             next-fixed-points
             goal
             :value
             nil
             0
             nil))
           (next-aggregate
            (if (evenp turn)
                (and aggregate child-win)
              (or aggregate child-win))))
      (putnam-2023-a6-bob-wins-search
       remaining
       moves-left
       turn
       fixed-points
       goal
       :scan
       (cdr choices)
       (- choices-left 1)
       next-aggregate)))))

(defun putnam-2023-a6-bob-has-winning-strategy-p (n)
  (let ((available
         (putnam-2023-a6-range-from 1 n)))
    (or
     (putnam-2023-a6-bob-wins-search
      available n 0 0 0 :value nil 0 nil)
     (putnam-2023-a6-bob-wins-search
      available n 0 0 1 :value nil 0 nil))))

;; Universal closure of N gives the pointwise form of the source set equality.

(defun putnambench-putnam-2023-a6-statement (n)
  (implies
   (natp n)
   (equal
    (and
     (< 0 n)
     (putnam-2023-a6-bob-has-winning-strategy-p n))
    (< 0 n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2023_a6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2023_a6): Bob has a winning parity strategy
-- in the alternating permutation game for every positive board size.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2023A6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<N_ _member_
infixr 3 _and_
infix 1 _iff_
infixr 5 _++_

data Bottom : Set where

data Top : Set where
  trivial : Top

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  oneN <=N n

InRange : Nat -> Nat -> Set
InRange n value =
  oneN <=N value and value <=N n

data _member_ {A : Set} (x : A) : List A -> Set where
  here :
    {xs : List A} ->
    x member (x ∷ xs)
  there :
    {y : A} ->
    {xs : List A} ->
    x member xs ->
    x member (y ∷ xs)

Distinct : {A : Set} -> List A -> Set
Distinct [] =
  Top
Distinct (x ∷ xs) =
  Not (x member xs) and Distinct xs

AllInRange : Nat -> List Nat -> Set
AllInRange n [] =
  Top
AllInRange n (x ∷ xs) =
  InRange n x and AllInRange n xs

length : {A : Set} -> List A -> Nat
length [] =
  zero
length (x ∷ xs) =
  suc (length xs)

_++_ : {A : Set} -> List A -> List A -> List A
[] ++ ys =
  ys
(x ∷ xs) ++ ys =
  x ∷ (xs ++ ys)

PartialGame : Nat -> List Nat -> Set
PartialGame n moves =
  Distinct moves and AllInRange n moves

ValidGame : Nat -> List Nat -> Set
ValidGame n moves =
  length moves == n and PartialGame n moves

data Parity : Set where
  even odd : Parity

toggle : Parity -> Parity
toggle even =
  odd
toggle odd =
  even

natEqual : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
natEqual zero zero =
  true
natEqual zero (suc n) =
  false
natEqual (suc m) zero =
  false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) =
  natEqual m n

fixedPointParityFrom : Nat -> List Nat -> Parity
fixedPointParityFrom index [] =
  even
fixedPointParityFrom index (value ∷ values)
  with natEqual value (suc index)
... | true =
  toggle (fixedPointParityFrom (suc index) values)
... | false =
  fixedPointParityFrom (suc index) values

fixedPointParity : List Nat -> Parity
fixedPointParity =
  fixedPointParityFrom zero

Strategy : Set
Strategy =
  List Nat -> Nat

data Turn : Set where
  alice bob : Turn

nextTurn : Turn -> Turn
nextTurn alice =
  bob
nextTurn bob =
  alice

MoveCondition :
  Turn ->
  Strategy ->
  List Nat ->
  Nat ->
  Set
MoveCondition alice strategy prefix value =
  Top
MoveCondition bob strategy prefix value =
  value == strategy prefix

ConformsFrom :
  Turn ->
  List Nat ->
  List Nat ->
  Strategy ->
  Set
ConformsFrom turn prefix [] strategy =
  Top
ConformsFrom turn prefix (value ∷ values) strategy =
  MoveCondition turn strategy prefix value
  and
  ConformsFrom
    (nextTurn turn)
    (prefix ++ (value ∷ []))
    values
    strategy

ConformsToStrategy : List Nat -> Strategy -> Set
ConformsToStrategy moves strategy =
  ConformsFrom alice [] moves strategy

BobTurnAfter : Nat -> Set
BobTurnAfter zero =
  Bottom
BobTurnAfter (suc zero) =
  Top
BobTurnAfter (suc (suc n)) =
  BobTurnAfter n

ValidStrategy : Nat -> Strategy -> Set
ValidStrategy n strategy =
  (prefix : List Nat) ->
  PartialGame n prefix ->
  length prefix <N n ->
  BobTurnAfter (length prefix) ->
  InRange n (strategy prefix)
  and
  Not (strategy prefix member prefix)

WinsWithGoal : Nat -> Parity -> Strategy -> Set
WinsWithGoal n goal strategy =
  ValidStrategy n strategy
  and
  ((moves : List Nat) ->
    ValidGame n moves ->
    ConformsToStrategy moves strategy ->
    fixedPointParity moves == goal)

BobHasWinningStrategy : Nat -> Set
BobHasWinningStrategy n =
  Exists Parity
    (\ goal ->
      Exists Strategy
        (\ strategy ->
          WinsWithGoal n goal strategy))

WinningSize : Nat -> Set
WinningSize n =
  Positive n and BobHasWinningStrategy n

SolutionSize : Nat -> Set
SolutionSize n =
  Positive n

putnam-2023-a6 : Set
putnam-2023-a6 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  WinningSize n iff SolutionSize n

title: putnam_2023_a6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a6:
  the positive game sizes are exactly those for which Bob has a strategy
  satisfying the specified validity and conformance conditions that forces a
  fixed parity for the fixed points of every valid play. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2023_a6 =
  ``let valid_game =
      \g : num list.
        ALL_DISTINCT g /\
        (!x : num.
           MEM x g
           ==>
           1 <= x /\ x <= LENGTH g)
    in
    let parity_of =
      \g : num list.
        CARD
          {i : num |
             i < LENGTH g /\
             EL i g = i + 1} MOD 2
    in
    let conforms_to_strategy =
      \g : num list.
      \s : num list -> num.
        !i : num.
          i < LENGTH g /\ ODD i
          ==>
          EL i g = s (TAKE i g)
    in
    let valid_history =
      \n : num.
      \g : num list.
        ODD (LENGTH g) /\
        LENGTH g < n /\
        ALL_DISTINCT g /\
        (!x : num.
           MEM x g
           ==>
           1 <= x /\ x <= n)
    in
    let valid_strategy =
      \n : num.
      \s : num list -> num.
        !g : num list.
          valid_history n g
          ==>
          1 <= s g /\ s g <= n /\ ~MEM (s g) g
    in
    let winning_for =
      \n : num.
      \s : num list -> num.
        valid_strategy n s /\
        ?p : num.
          p < 2 /\
          !g : num list.
            LENGTH g = n /\
            valid_game g /\
            conforms_to_strategy g s
            ==>
            parity_of g = p
    in
      {n : num | 0 < n /\ ?s : num list -> num. winning_for n s} =
      {n : num | 0 < n}``;

title: putnam_2023_a6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2023_a6: Bob has a strategy and a fixed parity goal that wins the
  alternating permutation game for every positive number of available
  integers. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  A complete n-turn game is represented by a bijection from the zero-based
  turn indices 0 ..^ n onto the chosen integers 1 ... n. A strategy is a
  total function on finite words over 1 ... n. At every odd-length injective
  prefix shorter than n, validity requires the strategy to choose an integer
  outside the prefix range. Conformance applies the strategy exactly at the
  odd zero-based indices, which are Bob's turns.

  P23A6Winning n keeps both the strategy and Bob's parity goal internally
  existential. The fixed-point set counts the turns i at which integer i+1
  is chosen, so its cardinality modulo two is the game's winning parity.
  The final assertion is the source solution-set equality. All declarations
  are unproved $a statement encodings; this database contains no $p proof
  declaration.
$)

$c P23A6Solution P23A6Game P23A6ValidStrategy P23A6Conforms
   P23A6Winning $.

p23a6-solution-syntax $a class P23A6Solution $.
p23a6-game-syntax $a wff ( P23A6Game n G ) $.
p23a6-valid-strategy-syntax $a wff ( P23A6ValidStrategy n S ) $.
p23a6-conforms-syntax $a wff ( P23A6Conforms n G S ) $.
p23a6-winning-syntax $a wff ( P23A6Winning n ) $.

p23a6-solution-definition $a |- P23A6Solution = NN $.

${
  $d G n $.

  p23a6-game-definition $a |- (
    ( P23A6Game n G )
    <->
    G : ( 0 ..^ n ) -1-1-onto-> ( 1 ... n )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d H S n $.

  p23a6-valid-strategy-definition $a |- (
    ( P23A6ValidStrategy n S )
    <->
    (
      S e. ( ( 1 ... n ) ^m ( Word ( 1 ... n ) ) )
      /\
      A. H e. ( Word ( 1 ... n ) )
        (
          (
            (
              H : ( 0 ..^ ( # ` H ) ) -1-1-> ( 1 ... n )
              /\
              ( # ` H ) < n
            )
            /\
            ( ( # ` H ) mod 2 ) = 1
          )
          ->
          ( S ` H ) e/ ran H
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d G S i n $.

  p23a6-conforms-definition $a |- (
    ( P23A6Conforms n G S )
    <->
    A. i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
      (
        ( i mod 2 ) = 1
        ->
        ( G ` i ) = ( S ` ( G |` ( 0 ..^ i ) ) )
      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d G S i n p $.

  p23a6-winning-definition $a |- (
    ( P23A6Winning n )
    <->
    E. S
      (
        ( P23A6ValidStrategy n S )
        /\
        E. p e. ( 0 ..^ 2 )
          A. G
            (
              (
                ( P23A6Game n G )
                /\
                ( P23A6Conforms n G S )
              )
              ->
              (
                (
                  #
                  `
                  {
                    i e. ( 0 ..^ n ) |
                    ( G ` i ) = ( i + 1 )
                  }
                )
                mod 2
              )
              =
              p
            )
      )
  ) $.
$}

putnambench-putnam-2023-a6 $a |- (
  {
    n e. NN0 |
    (
      0 < n
      /\
      ( P23A6Winning n )
    )
  }
  =
  P23A6Solution
) $.

environ

begin

::$P-
theorem
  {n where n is Nat :
    0 < n &
    ex s being Function of NAT*,NAT, p being Nat st
      p < 2 &
      (for h being FinSequence of NAT st
        h is one-to-one &
        rng h c= Seg n &
        len h < n &
        (len h) mod 2 = 1
      holds
        s.h in Seg n \ rng h) &
      (for g being FinSequence of NAT st
        len g = n &
        g is one-to-one &
        rng g c= Seg n &
        (for i being Nat st
          i < len g & i mod 2 = 1
        holds
          g.(i + 1) = s.(g|i))
      holds
        ex q being Nat st
          q = card {k where k is Nat :
            k in dom g & g.k = k} &
          q mod 2 = p)}
  =

proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2023_a6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_a6:
% Bob has a parity-goal winning strategy in the alternating permutation game
% on 1 through n for exactly every positive natural n. This file contains no
% proof.

putnam_2023_a6: THEORY
BEGIN
  game: TYPE = list[nat]
  strategy: TYPE = [game -> nat]

  game_length(g: game): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES g OF
      null: 0,
      cons(value, tail): 1 + game_length(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE g BY <<

  contains_value(g: game, value: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES g OF
      null: FALSE,
      cons(head_value, tail):
        head_value = value OR contains_value(tail, value)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE g BY <<

  has_no_duplicates(g: game): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES g OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(value, tail):
        NOT contains_value(tail, value)
          AND has_no_duplicates(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE g BY <<

  values_between_one_and(
      g: game,
      n: nat): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES g OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(value, tail):
        1 <= value
          AND value <= n
          AND values_between_one_and(tail, n)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE g BY <<

  take_prefix(
      g: game,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE game =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      null
    ELSE
      CASES g OF
        null: null,
        cons(value, tail):
          cons(value, take_prefix(tail, count - 1))
      ENDCASES
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  entry_at(
      g: game,
      index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES g OF
      null: 0,
      cons(value, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          value
        ELSE
          entry_at(tail, index - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE g BY <<

  fixed_point_count_from(
      g: game,
      index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES g OF
      null: 0,
      cons(value, tail):
        (IF value = index + 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
          + fixed_point_count_from(tail, index + 1)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE g BY <<

  fixed_point_parity(g: game): nat =
    mod(fixed_point_count_from(g, 0), 2)

  valid_partial_game(n: nat, g: game): bool =
    game_length(g) <= n
      AND has_no_duplicates(g)
      AND values_between_one_and(g, n)

  valid_game(n: nat, g: game): bool =
    game_length(g) = n
      AND has_no_duplicates(g)
      AND values_between_one_and(g, n)

  valid_bob_strategy(n: nat, s: strategy): bool =
    FORALL (history: game):
      (valid_partial_game(n, history)
        AND game_length(history) < n
        AND mod(game_length(history), 2) = 1)
      IMPLIES
        1 <= s(history)
          AND s(history) <= n
          AND NOT contains_value(history, s(history))

  conforms_to_strategy(g: game, s: strategy): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      (index < game_length(g) AND mod(index, 2) = 1)
      IMPLIES
        entry_at(g, index) = s(take_prefix(g, index))

  is_winning_for(n: nat, s: strategy): bool =
    valid_bob_strategy(n, s)
      AND EXISTS (goal: nat):
        goal < 2
          AND FORALL (g: game):
            (valid_game(n, g) AND conforms_to_strategy(g, s))
            IMPLIES fixed_point_parity(g) = goal

  putnam_2023_a6_solution(n: nat): bool =
    n > 0

  putnam_2023_a6: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      (n > 0 AND EXISTS (s: strategy): is_winning_for(n, s))
        IFF putnam_2023_a6_solution(n)
END putnam_2023_a6

title: putnam_2023_b1
content:
import Mathlib

open Nat

-- Note: uses (ℕ → ℕ → Bool) instead of (Fin m → Fin n → Bool)
abbrev putnam_2023_b1_solution : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ := sorry
-- (fun m n : ℕ => Nat.choose (m + n - 2) (m - 1))
/--
Consider an $m$-by-$n$ grid of unit squares, indexed by $(i,j)$ with $1 \leq i \leq m$ and $1 \leq j \leq n$. There are $(m-1)(n-1)$ coins, which are initially placed in the squares $(i,j)$ with $1 \leq i \leq m-1$ and $1 \leq j \leq n-1$. If a coin occupies the square $(i,j)$ with $i \leq m-1$ and $j \leq n-1$ and the squares $(i+1,j)$, $(i,j+1)$, and $(i+1,j+1)$ are unoccupied, then a legal move is to slide the coin from $(i,j)$ to $(i+1,j+1)$. How many distinct configurations of coins can be reached starting from the initial configuration by a (possibly empty) sequence of legal moves?
-/
theorem putnam_2023_b1
(m n : ℕ)
(initcoins : ℕ → ℕ → Bool)
(hinitcoins : initcoins = (fun i j : ℕ => (i ≤ m - 2 ∧ j ≤ n - 2 : Bool)))
(IsLegalMove : (ℕ → ℕ → Bool) → (ℕ → ℕ → Bool) → Prop)
(IsLegalMove_def : ∀ coins1 coins2,
  IsLegalMove coins1 coins2 ↔
    ∃ i j, i < m - 1 ∧ j < n - 1 ∧
      coins1 i j ∧ !coins1 (i + 1) j ∧ !coins1 i (j + 1) ∧ !coins1 (i + 1) (j + 1) ∧
      !coins2 i j ∧ !coins2 (i + 1) j ∧ !coins2 i (j + 1) ∧ coins2 (i + 1) (j + 1) ∧
      (∀ i' j', ((i', j') ≠ (i, j) ∧ (i', j') ≠ (i + 1, j) ∧ (i', j') ≠ (i, j + 1) ∧ (i', j') ≠ (i + 1, j + 1))
        → coins1 i' j' = coins2 i' j'))
(IsLegalSeq : List (ℕ → ℕ → Bool) → Prop)
(IsLegalSeq_def : ∀ seq, IsLegalSeq seq ↔ seq.length ≥ 1 ∧ seq[0]! = initcoins ∧ (∀ i < seq.length - 1, IsLegalMove seq[i]! seq[i + 1]!))
(mnpos : 1 < m ∧ 1 < n)
: {config : ℕ → ℕ → Bool | ∃ seq : List (ℕ → ℕ → Bool), IsLegalSeq seq ∧ config = seq.getLast!}.encard = putnam_2023_b1_solution m n :=
sorry

title: putnam_2023_b1
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b1:
   the number of coin configurations reachable by diagonal legal moves on an
   m-by-n grid is a binomial coefficient. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat Lists.List Bool.Bool.

Import ListNotations.

Definition putnam_2023_b1_configuration : Type :=
  nat -> nat -> bool.

Definition putnam_2023_b1_initial
    (m n : nat) : putnam_2023_b1_configuration :=
  fun i j =>
    andb (Nat.ltb i (m - 1)) (Nat.ltb j (n - 1)).

Definition putnam_2023_b1_same_configuration
    (coins1 coins2 : putnam_2023_b1_configuration) : Prop :=
  forall i j : nat, coins1 i j = coins2 i j.

Definition putnam_2023_b1_legal_move
    (m n : nat)
    (coins1 coins2 : putnam_2023_b1_configuration) : Prop :=
  exists i j : nat,
    (i < m - 1)%nat /\
    (j < n - 1)%nat /\
    coins1 i j = true /\
    coins1 (S i) j = false /\
    coins1 i (S j) = false /\
    coins1 (S i) (S j) = false /\
    coins2 i j = false /\
    coins2 (S i) j = false /\
    coins2 i (S j) = false /\
    coins2 (S i) (S j) = true /\
    forall i' j' : nat,
      (i', j') <> (i, j) ->
      (i', j') <> (S i, j) ->
      (i', j') <> (i, S j) ->
      (i', j') <> (S i, S j) ->
      coins1 i' j' = coins2 i' j'.

Fixpoint putnam_2023_b1_legal_transitions
    (m n : nat)
    (previous : putnam_2023_b1_configuration)
    (remaining : list putnam_2023_b1_configuration) : Prop :=
  match remaining with
  | [] => True
  | current :: rest =>
      putnam_2023_b1_legal_move m n previous current /\
      putnam_2023_b1_legal_transitions m n current rest
  end.

Definition putnam_2023_b1_legal_sequence
    (m n : nat)
    (sequence : list putnam_2023_b1_configuration) : Prop :=
  exists rest : list putnam_2023_b1_configuration,
    sequence = putnam_2023_b1_initial m n :: rest /\
    putnam_2023_b1_legal_transitions
      m n (putnam_2023_b1_initial m n) rest.

Definition putnam_2023_b1_reachable
    (m n : nat)
    (config : putnam_2023_b1_configuration) : Prop :=
  exists sequence : list putnam_2023_b1_configuration,
    putnam_2023_b1_legal_sequence m n sequence /\
    putnam_2023_b1_same_configuration
      config (last sequence (putnam_2023_b1_initial m n)).

Fixpoint putnam_2023_b1_no_duplicate_configurations
    (configurations : list putnam_2023_b1_configuration) : Prop :=
  match configurations with
  | [] => True
  | config :: rest =>
      (forall other : putnam_2023_b1_configuration,
        In other rest ->
        ~ putnam_2023_b1_same_configuration config other) /\
      putnam_2023_b1_no_duplicate_configurations rest
  end.

Definition putnam_2023_b1_has_cardinality
    (P : putnam_2023_b1_configuration -> Prop)
    (cardinality : nat) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list putnam_2023_b1_configuration,
    putnam_2023_b1_no_duplicate_configurations enumeration /\
    length enumeration = cardinality /\
    forall config : putnam_2023_b1_configuration,
      P config <->
      exists representative : putnam_2023_b1_configuration,
        In representative enumeration /\
        putnam_2023_b1_same_configuration config representative.

Fixpoint putnam_2023_b1_binomial (n k : nat) : nat :=
  match n, k with
  | _, O => 1
  | O, S _ => 0
  | S n', S k' =>
      putnam_2023_b1_binomial n' k' +
      putnam_2023_b1_binomial n' (S k')
  end.

Definition putnam_2023_b1_solution (m n : nat) : nat :=
  putnam_2023_b1_binomial (m + n - 2) (m - 1).

Theorem putnam_2023_b1 :
  forall m n : nat,
    (0 < m)%nat ->
    (0 < n)%nat ->
    putnam_2023_b1_has_cardinality
      (putnam_2023_b1_reachable m n)
      (putnam_2023_b1_solution m n).
Admitted.

theory putnam_2023_b1 imports
Complex_Main
begin

(* uses "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" instead of finite domains of cardinality m and n, respectively *)
definition putnam_2023_b1_solution :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "putnam_2023_b1_solution = (\<lambda>m n. (m + n - 2) choose (m - 1))"
theorem putnam_2023_b1:
  fixes m n :: nat
  and initcoins :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and legalmove :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool) \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and legalseq :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool) list \<Rightarrow> bool"
  defines "initcoins \<equiv> \<lambda> i j :: nat. i \<le> m - 2 \<and> j \<le> n - 2"
  and "legalmove \<equiv> \<lambda> (coins1 :: nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool) (coins2 :: nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool). \<exists> i j :: nat. i < m - 1 \<and> j < n - 1 \<and> 
        coins1 i j \<and> \<not>coins1 (i + 1) j \<and> \<not>coins1 i (j + 1) \<and> \<not>coins1 (i + 1) (j + 1) \<and> \<not>coins2 i j \<and> \<not>coins2 (i + 1) j \<and> \<not>coins2 i (j + 1) \<and> coins2 (i + 1) (j + 1) \<and>
        (\<forall> i' j' :: nat. ((i', j') \<noteq> (i, j) \<and> (i', j') \<noteq> (i + 1, j) \<and> (i', j') \<noteq> (i, j + 1) \<and> (i', j') \<noteq> (i + 1, j + 1)) \<longrightarrow> coins1 i' j' = coins2 i' j')"
  and "legalseq \<equiv> \<lambda> seq :: (nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool) list. length seq \<ge> 1 \<and> seq!0 = initcoins \<and> (\<forall> i < length seq - 1. legalmove (seq!i) (seq!(i + 1)))"
  assumes mnpos: "m > 1 \<and> n > 1"
  shows "card {config :: nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool.
      \<exists>seq :: (nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool) list.
        legalseq seq \<and> config = last seq}
    = putnam_2023_b1_solution m n"
  sorry

end
