begin

::$P-
theorem
  for n being Nat,
      Omega being non empty set,
      Sigma being SigmaField of Omega,
      P being Probability of Sigma,
      X being Function of NAT,Funcs(Omega,REAL),
      A being Function of Omega,REAL
  st
    2 <= n &
    X is Sigma-Random-Variable-Family &
    (for i being Nat st i < n holds
      ex Xi being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma,
         FXi being random_variable of Sigma,Borel_Sets,
         mu being Probability of Borel_Sets st
        Xi = X.i &
        FXi = Xi &
        probability(FXi,P) = mu &
        (for omega being Element of Omega holds
          0 <= Xi.omega & Xi.omega <= 1) &
        (for t being Real,
             B being Element of Borel_Sets
          st B = ].-infty,t.]
          holds
            (t < 0 implies (mu.B qua Real) = 0) &
            (0 <= t & t < 1 implies (mu.B qua Real) = t) &
            (1 <= t implies (mu.B qua Real) = 1))) &
    (for r being Nat,
         I being one-to-one FinSequence of NAT,
         B being FinSequence of Borel_Sets,
         E being FinSequence of Sigma,
         q being FinSequence of REAL
      st 0 < r &
         len I = r & len B = r & len E = r & len q = r &
         (for j being Nat st j in Seg r holds
           I.j < n &
           E.j = (X.(I.j))"(B.j) &
           q.j = (P.(E.j) qua Real))
      holds P.(meet rng E) = Product q) &
    (for omega being Element of Omega holds
      ex m being Nat st
        A.omega = (m qua Real) &
        (ex I being FinSequence of NAT st
          len I = m &
          (for j being Nat st j in Seg m holds
            I.j in Seg n) &
          (for j,k being Nat st
            j in Seg m & k in Seg m & j < k
          holds I.j < I.k) &
          (m = 1 or
            ((for j being Nat,
                  Xj,Xs being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma
                st j in Seg m & j+1 in Seg m &
                   Xj = X.(I.j-'1) &
                   Xs = X.(I.(j+1)-'1)
              holds Xs.omega <> Xj.omega) &
             (for j being Nat,
                  Xj,Xs,Xt being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma
                st j in Seg m & j+1 in Seg m & j+2 in Seg m &
                   Xj = X.(I.j-'1) &
                   Xs = X.(I.(j+1)-'1) &
                   Xt = X.(I.(j+2)-'1)
              holds
                (Xt.omega < Xs.omega iff Xj.omega < Xs.omega))))) &
        (for r being Nat,
             I being FinSequence of NAT
          st len I = r &
             (for j being Nat st j in Seg r holds
               I.j in Seg n) &
             (for j,k being Nat st
               j in Seg r & k in Seg r & j < k
             holds I.j < I.k) &
             (r = 1 or
               ((for j being Nat,
                     Xj,Xs being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma
                   st j in Seg r & j+1 in Seg r &
                      Xj = X.(I.j-'1) &
                      Xs = X.(I.(j+1)-'1)
                 holds Xs.omega <> Xj.omega) &
                (for j being Nat,
                     Xj,Xs,Xt being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma
                   st j in Seg r & j+1 in Seg r & j+2 in Seg r &
                      Xj = X.(I.j-'1) &
                      Xs = X.(I.(j+1)-'1) &
                      Xt = X.(I.(j+2)-'1)
                 holds
                   (Xt.omega < Xs.omega iff Xj.omega < Xs.omega))))
          holds r <= m))
  holds
    Integral(P2M(P),A) =
      (2 * (n qua Real) + 2) / 3
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2023_b3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b3:
% the expected length of the longest zigzag subsequence of independent
% uniform [0,1] random variables is (2n+2)/3. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2023_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  sample_space: TYPE+

  event: TYPE = [sample_space -> bool]
  event_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> event]
  sigma_algebra: TYPE = [event -> bool]
  probability_map: TYPE = [event -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  valid_size: TYPE = {n: nat | n >= 2}
  unit_interval: TYPE = {x: real | 0 <= x AND x <= 1}
  sample(n: valid_size): TYPE = [below(n) -> unit_interval]
  random_variable: TYPE = [sample_space -> unit_interval]
  random_vector(n: valid_size): TYPE = [below(n) -> random_variable]
  selection(n: valid_size): TYPE = [nat -> below(n)]

  full_event: event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space): TRUE

  empty_event: event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space): FALSE

  event_complement(A: event): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space): NOT A(omega)

  countable_union(events: event_sequence): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      EXISTS (index: nat): events(index)(omega)

  pairwise_disjoint(events: event_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (left_index, right_index: nat):
      left_index /= right_index IMPLIES
        FORALL (omega: sample_space):
          NOT (events(left_index)(omega)
            AND events(right_index)(omega))

  partial_real_sum(
      values: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      partial_real_sum(values, count - 1)
        + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(values: real_sequence, limit_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(values(index) - limit_value) < epsilon_value

  is_sigma_algebra(Sigma: sigma_algebra): bool =
    Sigma(full_event)
      AND (FORALL (A: event):
        Sigma(A) IMPLIES Sigma(event_complement(A)))
      AND (FORALL (events: event_sequence):
        (FORALL (index: nat): Sigma(events(index)))
          IMPLIES Sigma(countable_union(events)))

  partial_probability_sum(
      probability: probability_map,
      events: event_sequence,
      count: nat): real =
    partial_real_sum(
      LAMBDA (index: nat): probability(events(index)),
      count)

  is_probability_space(
      probability: probability_map,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra): bool =
    is_sigma_algebra(Sigma)
      AND probability(empty_event) = 0
      AND probability(full_event) = 1
      AND (FORALL (A: event):
        Sigma(A) IMPLIES probability(A) >= 0)
      AND (FORALL (events: event_sequence):
        ((FORALL (index: nat): Sigma(events(index)))
          AND pairwise_disjoint(events))
        IMPLIES
          converges_to(
            LAMBDA (count: nat):
              partial_probability_sum(
                probability, events, count),
            probability(countable_union(events))))

  measurable_unit(
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      value: random_variable): bool =
    FORALL (threshold: real):
      Sigma(
        LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
          value(omega) <= threshold)

  uniform_unit_cdf(threshold: real): real =
    IF threshold < 0 THEN
      0
    ELSIF threshold <= 1 THEN
      threshold
    ELSE
      1
    ENDIF

  finite_product(
      values: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      finite_product(values, count - 1)
        * values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  rectangle_event(
      n: valid_size,
      X: random_vector(n),
      thresholds: [below(n) -> real]): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      FORALL (index: below(n)):
        X(index)(omega) <= thresholds(index)

  rectangle_cdf_product(
      n: valid_size,
      thresholds: [below(n) -> real]): real =
    finite_product(
      LAMBDA (index: nat):
        IF index < n THEN
          uniform_unit_cdf(thresholds(index))
        ELSE
          1
        ENDIF,
      n)

  independent_uniform_vector(
      n: valid_size,
      probability: probability_map,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_vector(n)): bool =
    (FORALL (index: below(n)):
      measurable_unit(Sigma, X(index)))
      AND
    (FORALL (thresholds: [below(n) -> real]):
      probability(rectangle_event(n, X, thresholds))
        = rectangle_cdf_product(n, thresholds))

  strictly_increasing(
      n: valid_size,
      indices: selection(n),
      length: nat): bool =
    FORALL (position: nat):
      position + 1 < length IMPLIES
        indices(position) < indices(position + 1)

  is_zigzag_subsequence(
      n: valid_size,
      x: sample(n),
      indices: selection(n),
      length: nat): bool =
    length = 1
      OR
        ((FORALL (position: nat):
          position + 1 < length IMPLIES
            x(indices(position + 1))
              /= x(indices(position)))
        AND
        (FORALL (position: nat):
          position + 2 < length IMPLIES
            (x(indices(position + 2))
                < x(indices(position + 1))
              IFF
             x(indices(position))
                < x(indices(position + 1)))))

  admissible_length(
      n: valid_size,
      x: sample(n),
      length: nat): bool =
    1 <= length
      AND length <= n
      AND (EXISTS (indices: selection(n)):
        strictly_increasing(n, indices, length)
          AND is_zigzag_subsequence(
            n, x, indices, length))

  is_longest_length(
      n: valid_size,
      x: sample(n),
      length: nat): bool =
    admissible_length(n, x, length)
      AND (FORALL (other_length: nat):
        admissible_length(n, x, other_length)
          IMPLIES other_length <= length)

  longest_length_function(
      n: valid_size,
      a: [sample(n) -> nat]): bool =
    FORALL (x: sample(n)):
      is_longest_length(n, x, a(x))

  sampled_length(
      n: valid_size,
      X: random_vector(n),
      a: [sample(n) -> nat],
      omega: sample_space): nat =
    a(LAMBDA (index: below(n)): X(index)(omega))

  length_event(
      n: valid_size,
      X: random_vector(n),
      a: [sample(n) -> nat],
      length: nat): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      sampled_length(n, X, a, omega) = length

  expected_length_sum(
      n: valid_size,
      probability: probability_map,
      X: random_vector(n),
      a: [sample(n) -> nat],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      expected_length_sum(
        n, probability, X, a, count - 1)
        + ((count - 1) :: real)
            * probability(
                length_event(
                  n, X, a, count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  expected_longest_length(
      n: valid_size,
      probability: probability_map,
      X: random_vector(n),
      a: [sample(n) -> nat]): real =
    expected_length_sum(
      n, probability, X, a, n + 1)

  putnam_2023_b3_solution(n: valid_size): real =
    ((2 * n + 2) :: real) / 3

  putnam_2023_b3: bool =
    FORALL
        (n: valid_size),
        (Sigma: sigma_algebra),
        (probability: probability_map),
        (X: random_vector(n)),
        (a: [sample(n) -> nat]):
      (is_probability_space(probability, Sigma)
        AND independent_uniform_vector(
          n, probability, Sigma, X)
        AND longest_length_function(n, a))
      IMPLIES
        expected_longest_length(
          n, probability, X, a)
          = putnam_2023_b3_solution(n)
END putnam_2023_b3

title: putnam_2023_b4
content:
import Mathlib

open Nat Topology Filter

-- Note: uses (ℕ → ℝ) instead of (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) and (ℝ → ℝ) instead of (tall ts → ℝ)
abbrev putnam_2023_b4_solution : ℝ := sorry
-- 29
/--
For a nonnegative integer $n$ and a strictly increasing sequence of real numbers $t_0,t_1,\dots,t_n$, let $f(t)$ be the corresponding real-valued function defined for $t \geq t_0$ by the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $f(t)$ is continuous for $t \geq t_0$, and is twice differentiable for all $t>t_0$ other than $t_1,\dots,t_n$;
\item[(b)] $f(t_0)=1/2$;
\item[(c)] $\lim_{t \to t_k^+} f'(t)=0$ for $0 \leq k \leq n$;
\item[(d)] For $0 \leq k \leq n-1$, we have $f''(t)=k+1$ when $t_k< t< t_{k+1}$, and $f''(t)=n+1$ when $t>t_n$.
\end{enumerate}
Considering all choices of $n$ and $t_0,t_1,\dots,t_n$ such that $t_k \geq t_{k-1}+1$ for $1 \leq k \leq n$, what is the least possible value of $T$ for which $f(t_0+T)=2023$?
-/
theorem putnam_2023_b4
    (tne : ℕ → (ℕ → ℝ) → Set ℝ)
    (htne : ∀ n ts, tne n ts = {t | t > ts 0 ∧ ∀ i : Fin n, t ≠ ts (i.1 + 1)}) :
    IsLeast
    {(T : ℝ) | 0 ≤ T ∧ ∃ (n : ℕ) (ts : ℕ → ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ),
      (∀ k : Fin n, ts (k.1 + 1) ≥ ts k.1 + 1) ∧
      ContinuousOn f (Set.Ici (ts 0)) ∧
      ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f (tne n ts) ∧
      DifferentiableOn ℝ (derivWithin f (tne n ts)) (tne n ts) ∧
      f (ts 0) = 0.5 ∧
      (∀ k : Fin (n + 1),
        Tendsto (derivWithin f (tne n ts)) (𝓝[>] (ts k.1)) (𝓝 0)) ∧
      (∀ k : Fin n,
        ∀ t ∈ Set.Ioo (ts k.1) (ts (k.1 + 1)),
          iteratedDerivWithin 2 f (tne n ts) t = k.1 + 1) ∧
      (∀ t > ts n,
        iteratedDerivWithin 2 f (tne n ts) t = n + 1) ∧
      f (ts 0 + T) = 2023}
    putnam_2023_b4_solution :=
  sorry

title: putnam_2023_b4

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b4:
   the least time for a continuous piecewise twice differentiable real
   function with prescribed accelerations to reach 2023. This file contains
   no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2023_b4_solution : R := 29.

Definition putnam_2023_b4_regular_point
    (n : nat) (ts : nat -> R) (t : R) : Prop :=
  t > ts 0%nat /\
  forall i : nat, (1 <= i <= n)%nat -> t <> ts i.

Definition putnam_2023_b4_continuous_from
    (f : R -> R) (a : R) : Prop :=
  forall x : R,
    a <= x ->
    forall epsilon : R,
      epsilon > 0 ->
      exists delta : R,
        delta > 0 /\
        forall y : R,
          a <= y ->
          Rabs (y - x) < delta ->
          Rabs (f y - f x) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_2023_b4_has_derivative_at
    (f : R -> R) (x derivative : R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    epsilon > 0 ->
    exists delta : R,
      delta > 0 /\
      forall h : R,
        0 < Rabs h < delta ->
        Rabs ((f (x + h) - f x) / h - derivative) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_2023_b4_right_limit_zero
    (g : R -> R) (a : R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    epsilon > 0 ->
    exists delta : R,
      delta > 0 /\
      forall t : R,
        a < t < a + delta ->
        Rabs (g t) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_2023_b4_admissible
    (n : nat) (ts : nat -> R) (f : R -> R) : Prop :=
  (forall k : nat,
      (k < n)%nat ->
      ts (S k) >= ts k + 1) /\
  putnam_2023_b4_continuous_from f (ts 0%nat) /\
  exists first_derivative second_derivative : R -> R,
    (forall t : R,
        putnam_2023_b4_regular_point n ts t ->
        putnam_2023_b4_has_derivative_at f t (first_derivative t) /\
        putnam_2023_b4_has_derivative_at
          first_derivative t (second_derivative t)) /\
    f (ts 0%nat) = / 2 /\
    (forall k : nat,
        (k <= n)%nat ->
        putnam_2023_b4_right_limit_zero first_derivative (ts k)) /\
    (forall k : nat,
        (k < n)%nat ->
        forall t : R,
          ts k < t < ts (S k) ->
          second_derivative t = INR (S k)) /\
    (forall t : R,
        t > ts n ->
        second_derivative t = INR (S n)).

Definition putnam_2023_b4_feasible_time (T : R) : Prop :=
  0 <= T /\
  exists (n : nat) (ts : nat -> R) (f : R -> R),
    putnam_2023_b4_admissible n ts f /\
    f (ts 0%nat + T) = 2023.

Definition putnam_2023_b4_is_least_time (T : R) : Prop :=
  putnam_2023_b4_feasible_time T /\
  forall U : R,
    putnam_2023_b4_feasible_time U ->
    T <= U.

Theorem putnam_2023_b4 :
  putnam_2023_b4_is_least_time putnam_2023_b4_solution.
Admitted.

theory putnam_2023_b4 imports Complex_Main
"HOL-Analysis.Derivative"
begin

(* uses (nat \<Rightarrow> real) instead of (Fin (n+1) \<Rightarrow> real) and (real \<Rightarrow> real) instead of ({(ts 0)..} \<Rightarrow> real) *)
definition putnam_2023_b4_solution :: real where "putnam_2023_b4_solution \<equiv> undefined"
(* 29 *)
theorem putnam_2023_b4:
  fixes tne :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> real set"
  and fdiff :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> (real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and flim :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> (real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and fderiv1 :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> (real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and fderiv2 :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> (real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and fall :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> (real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and tinc :: "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool"
  and Tall :: "real \<Rightarrow> bool"
  assumes htne: "\<forall>(n::nat)(ts::nat\<Rightarrow>real). tne n ts = {t::real. t > ts 0 \<and> (\<forall>i::nat\<in>{1..n}. t \<noteq> ts i)}"
  and hfdiff: "\<forall>(n::nat)(ts::nat\<Rightarrow>real)(f::real\<Rightarrow>real). fdiff n ts f = (continuous_on {(ts 0)..} f \<and> f C1_differentiable_on (tne n ts) \<and> (deriv f) differentiable_on (tne n ts))"
  and hflim: "\<forall>(n::nat)(ts::nat\<Rightarrow>real)(f::real\<Rightarrow>real). flim n ts f = (\<forall>k::nat\<in>{0..n}. filterlim (deriv f) (nhds 0) (at_right (ts k)))"
  and hfderiv1: "\<forall>(n::nat)(ts::nat\<Rightarrow>real)(f::real\<Rightarrow>real). fderiv1 n ts f = (\<forall>k::nat\<in>{0..(n-1)}. \<forall>t::real\<in>{(ts k)<..<(ts (k+1))}. (deriv^^2) f t = k+1)"
  and hfderiv2: "\<forall>(n::nat)(ts::nat\<Rightarrow>real)(f::real\<Rightarrow>real). fderiv2 n ts f = (\<forall>t::real>(ts n). (deriv^^2) f t = n+1)"
  and hfall: "\<forall>(n::nat)(ts::nat\<Rightarrow>real)(f::real\<Rightarrow>real). fall n ts f = (fdiff n ts f \<and> f (ts 0) = 0.5 \<and> flim n ts f \<and> fderiv1 n ts f \<and> fderiv2 n ts f)"
  and htinc: "\<forall>(n::nat)(ts::nat\<Rightarrow>real). tinc n ts = (\<forall>k::nat\<in>{0..(n-1)}. ts (k+1) \<ge> ts k + 1)"
  and hTall: "\<forall>T::real. Tall T = (T \<ge> 0 \<and> (\<exists>(n::nat)(ts::nat\<Rightarrow>real)(f::real\<Rightarrow>real). tinc n ts \<and> fall n ts f \<and> f (ts 0 + T) = 2023))"
  shows "(LEAST T::real. Tall T) = putnam_2023_b4_solution"
  sorry

end

let statement =
  `let continuous_on_ray =
     \(f:real->real) (a:real).
       !x:real.
         a <= x
         ==> !e:real.
               &0 < e
               ==> ?d:real.
                     &0 < d /\
                     !y:real.
                       a <= y /\ abs (y - x) < d
                       ==> abs (f y - f x) < e in
   let right_limit =
     \(g:real->real) (a:real) (l:real).
       !e:real.

               &0 < d /\
               !x:real.
                 a < x /\ x - a < d
                 ==> abs (g x - l) < e in
   let attainable =
     \tau:real.
       &0 <= tau /\
       ?n:num. ?ts:num->real. ?f fp:real->real.
         (!k:num.

         continuous_on_ray f (ts 0) /\
         (!t:real.
            ts 0 < t /\

            k < n

                  ts k < t /\ t < ts (k + 1)
                  ==> (fp diffl &(k + 1)) t) /\
         (!t:real.
            ts n < t
            ==> (fp diffl &(n + 1)) t) /\
         f (ts 0 + tau) = &2023 in
   attainable (&29) /\
   (!tau:real. attainable tau ==> &29 <= tau)`;;

title: putnam_2023_b4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b4:
;; among continuous real functions with prescribed derivative resets and
;; piecewise constant second derivative, the least elapsed time to rise from
;; 1/2 to 2023 is 29. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The scalar parameters present a Dedekind-complete ordered field, hence a
;; copy of the real numbers. Function objects present the sequence of reset
;; times, the function, and its first and second derivatives. Continuity,
;; differentiability, one-sided limits, and the least-time conclusion are
;; stated directly by their quantified definitions; no closed-form motion
;; formula is assumed.

(defun p2023b4-member-p (carrier x)
  (if (apply$ carrier (list x)) t nil))

(defun p2023b4-call1 (function x)
  (apply$ function (list x)))

(defun p2023b4-call2 (operation x y)
  (apply$ operation (list x y)))

(defun p2023b4-add (add x y)
  (p2023b4-call2 add x y))

(defun p2023b4-mul (mul x y)
  (p2023b4-call2 mul x y))

(defun p2023b4-neg (neg x)
  (p2023b4-call1 neg x))

(defun p2023b4-sub (add neg x y)
  (p2023b4-add add x (p2023b4-neg neg y)))

(defun p2023b4-lt (lt x y)
  (if (p2023b4-call2 lt x y) t nil))

(defun p2023b4-le (lt x y)
  (not (p2023b4-lt lt y x)))

(defun p2023b4-positive-p (carrier zero lt x)
  (and
   (p2023b4-member-p carrier x)
   (p2023b4-lt lt zero x)))

(defun p2023b4-abs (zero neg lt x)
  (if (p2023b4-lt lt x zero)
      (p2023b4-neg neg x)
    x))

(defun p2023b4-nat-real (n zero one add)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      zero
    (p2023b4-add
     add one
     (p2023b4-nat-real (- n 1) zero one add))))

(defun p2023b4-one-half (one add mul inv)
  (p2023b4-mul
   mul one
   (p2023b4-call1 inv (p2023b4-add add one one))))

(defun-sk p2023b4-field-laws-p
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p2023b4-member-p carrier x)
      (p2023b4-member-p carrier y)
      (p2023b4-member-p carrier z))
     (and
      (p2023b4-member-p carrier (p2023b4-add add x y))
      (p2023b4-member-p carrier (p2023b4-mul mul x y))
      (p2023b4-member-p carrier (p2023b4-neg neg x))
      (p2023b4-member-p carrier (p2023b4-call1 inv x))
      (equal
       (p2023b4-add add (p2023b4-add add x y) z)
       (p2023b4-add add x (p2023b4-add add y z)))
      (equal (p2023b4-add add x y)
             (p2023b4-add add y x))
      (equal (p2023b4-add add x zero) x)
      (equal (p2023b4-add add x (p2023b4-neg neg x))
             zero)
      (equal
       (p2023b4-mul mul (p2023b4-mul mul x y) z)
       (p2023b4-mul mul x (p2023b4-mul mul y z)))
      (equal (p2023b4-mul mul x y)
             (p2023b4-mul mul y x))
      (equal (p2023b4-mul mul x one) x)
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2023_b4): the least nonnegative time for the
-- specified piecewise-accelerating real function to reach 2023 is 29.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finToNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc index) =
  suc (finToNat index)

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ContinuousWithinAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> Set) ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ContinuousWithinAt {R} reals domain function point =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        domain x ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function point)
          epsilon
          (function x)))

ContinuousOn :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> Set) ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
ContinuousOn {R} reals domain function =
  (point : R) ->
  domain point ->
  ContinuousWithinAt reals domain function point

DerivativeWithinAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> Set) ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
DerivativeWithinAt {R} reals domain function point derivativeValue =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        domain x ->
        CloseTo reals point delta x ->
        x != point ->
        CloseTo reals derivativeValue epsilon
          (divide reals
            (subtract reals (function x) (function point))
            (subtract reals x point))))

RightLimitAt :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
RightLimitAt {R} reals function point limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        StrictLess reals point x ->
        StrictLess reals x (add reals point delta) ->
        CloseTo reals limit epsilon (function x)))

module Putnam2023B4Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  PuncturedHalfLine :
    Nat ->
    (Nat -> R) ->
    R ->
    Set
  PuncturedHalfLine n times t =
    StrictLess reals (times zero) t
    and
    ((index : Fin n) ->
      t != times (suc (finToNat index)))

  ClosedHalfLine :
    R ->
    R ->
    Set
  ClosedHalfLine lower x =
    lessOrEqual reals lower x

  record TwiceDifferentiableData
    (n : Nat)
    (times : Nat -> R)
    (function : R -> R) :
    Set where

    field
      firstDerivative secondDerivative : R -> R

      first-derivative-correct :
        (x : R) ->
        PuncturedHalfLine n times x ->
        DerivativeWithinAt reals
          (PuncturedHalfLine n times)
          function
          x
          (firstDerivative x)

      first-derivative-continuous :
        ContinuousOn reals
          (PuncturedHalfLine n times)
          firstDerivative

      second-derivative-correct :
        (x : R) ->
        PuncturedHalfLine n times x ->
        DerivativeWithinAt reals
          (PuncturedHalfLine n times)
          firstDerivative
          x
          (secondDerivative x)

  open TwiceDifferentiableData

  SpacedTimes :
    Nat ->
    (Nat -> R) ->
    Set
  SpacedTimes n times =
    (index : Fin n) ->
    lessOrEqual reals
      (add reals
        (times (finToNat index))
        (oneR reals))
      (times (suc (finToNat index)))

  FunctionConditions :
    (n : Nat) ->
    (times : Nat -> R) ->
    (function : R -> R) ->
    TwiceDifferentiableData n times function ->
    Set
  FunctionConditions n times function derivatives =
    ContinuousOn reals
      (ClosedHalfLine (times zero))
      function
    and
    function (times zero) ==
      divide reals
        (oneR reals)
        (fromNat reals 2)
    and
    ((index : Fin (suc n)) ->
      RightLimitAt reals
        (firstDerivative derivatives)
        (times (finToNat index))
        (zeroR reals))
    and
    ((index : Fin n) ->
      (t : R) ->
      StrictLess reals
        (times (finToNat index))
        t ->
      StrictLess reals
        t
        (times (suc (finToNat index))) ->
      secondDerivative derivatives t ==
        fromNat reals (suc (finToNat index)))
    and
    ((t : R) ->
      StrictLess reals (times n) t ->
      secondDerivative derivatives t ==
        fromNat reals (suc n))

  AdmissibleTime : R -> Set
  AdmissibleTime T =
    lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) T
    and
    Exists Nat
      (\ n ->
        Exists (Nat -> R)
          (\ times ->
            Exists (R -> R)
              (\ function ->
                SpacedTimes n times
                and
                Exists
                  (TwiceDifferentiableData n times function)
                  (\ derivatives ->
                    FunctionConditions
                      n
                      times
                      function
                      derivatives
                    and
                    function
                      (add reals (times zero) T)
                    ==
                    fromNat reals 2023))))

  IsLeastAdmissibleTime : R -> Set
  IsLeastAdmissibleTime leastTime =
    AdmissibleTime leastTime
    and
    ((T : R) ->
      AdmissibleTime T ->
      lessOrEqual reals leastTime T)

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    IsLeastAdmissibleTime (fromNat reals 29)

putnam-2023-b4 : Set1
putnam-2023-b4 =

      \g : real -> real. \a l : real.
        !e : real.
          0 < e
          ==>
          ?d : real.
            0 < d /\
            !x : real.
              a < x /\ x - a < d
              ==>
              abs (g x - l) < e
    in
    let regular =
      \n : num. \ts : num -> real. \t : real.
        ts 0 < t /\
        (!i : num.
           1 <= i /\ i <= n
           ==>
           t <> ts i)
    in
    let attainable =
      \T : real.
        0 <= T /\
        ?n : num. ?ts : num -> real. ?f fp : real -> real.
          (!k : num.
             k < n
             ==>
             ts k + 1 <= ts (k + 1)) /\
          f continuous_on {t : real | ts 0 <= t} /\
          (!t : real.
             regular n ts t
             ==>
             (f diffl (fp t)) t /\
             (?d : real. (fp diffl d) t)) /\
          f (ts 0) = 1 / 2 /\
          (!k : num.
             k <= n
             ==>
             right_limit fp (ts k) 0) /\
          (!k : num.
             k < n
             ==>

               ts k < t /\ t < ts (k + 1)
               ==>

          (!t : real.
             ts n < t
             ==>

          f (ts 0 + T) = 2023
    in
      attainable 29 /\
      (!T : real.
         attainable T
         ==>
         29 <= T)``;

  with prescribed one-sided derivative limits and piecewise constant second

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  A in RR ^m NN0 is the arbitrary real sequence (t_k), and F in RR ^m RR
  is an arbitrary total real extension of the function defined on
  [t_0,+infinity). P23B4RightLimit(F,a) is the epsilon-delta expansion of
  the right-hand limit F'(x) -> 0 as x -> a, with membership in the
  derivative domain made explicit.

  P23B4Data(n,A,F) states the unit spacing of consecutive sequence entries,
  continuity on the closed half-line from t_0, twice differentiability at
  every point above t_0 except t_1 through t_n, the initial value 1/2, all
  right-hand derivative limits, and the specified piecewise values of the
  second derivative. The entries 1 and 2 of ( RR Dn F ) are set.mm's first
  and second real derivatives.

  P23B4Admissible(T) keeps n, A, and F internally existentially quantified
  and adds T >= 0 and F(t_0 + T) = 2023. The final conjunction expands
  IsLeast: 29 is admissible and is no greater than every admissible real T.
  All declarations are unproved $a statement encodings; this database
  contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c P23B4RightLimit P23B4Data P23B4Admissible $.

p23b4-right-limit-syntax $a wff ( P23B4RightLimit F a ) $.
p23b4-data-syntax $a wff ( P23B4Data n A F ) $.
p23b4-admissible-syntax $a wff ( P23B4Admissible T ) $.

${
  $d F a d e x $.

  p23b4-right-limit-definition $a |- (
    ( P23B4RightLimit F a )

      )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d A F a k n x $.

  p23b4-data-definition $a |- (
    ( P23B4Data n A F )
    <->
    (
      (
        n e. NN0
        /\
        A e. ( RR ^m NN0 )
        /\
        F e. ( RR ^m RR )

        (

        |`

      )

      /\
      A. k e. NN0
        (

      /\

            ( ( ( RR Dn F ) ` 2 ) ` x )

          )

$}

${
  $d A F T n $.

  p23b4-admissible-definition $a |- (

    <->

title: putnam_2023_b4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b4:
% 29 is the least nonnegative time at which a piecewise twice differentiable
% function with the prescribed accelerations and reset derivative limits can
% rise from 1/2 to 2023. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2023_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  has_derivative_at(
      f: real_function,
      derivative, x: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (h: real):
          (h /= 0 AND abs(h) < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(f(x + h) - f(x) - derivative * h)
                < epsilon_value * abs(h)

  differentiable_at(f: real_function, x: real): bool =
    EXISTS (derivative: real):
      has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x)

  derivative_value(f: real_function, x: real): real =
    IF differentiable_at(f, x) THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (derivative: real):
          has_derivative_at(f, derivative, x))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  derivative_function(f: real_function): real_function =
    LAMBDA (x: real):
      derivative_value(f, x)

  second_derivative_value(
      f: real_function,
      x: real): real =
    derivative_value(derivative_function(f), x)

  continuous_on_right_ray(
      f: real_function,
      start: real): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      x >= start IMPLIES
        FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
          EXISTS (delta: posreal):
            FORALL (z: real):
              (z >= start AND abs(z - x) < delta)
                IMPLIES
                  abs(f(z) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  away_from_breakpoints(
      n: nat,
      times: real_sequence,
      x: real): bool =
    x > times(0)
      AND
    FORALL (index: nat):
      (1 <= index AND index <= n)
        IMPLIES x /= times(index)

  twice_differentiable_away_from_breakpoints(
      n: nat,
      times: real_sequence,
      f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      away_from_breakpoints(n, times, x)
        IMPLIES
          (differentiable_at(f, x)
            AND differentiable_at(
              derivative_function(f), x))

  has_right_limit(
      f: real_function,
      x, limit_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (h: real):
          (0 < h AND h < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(f(x + h) - limit_value)
                < epsilon_value

  separated_times(
      n: nat,
      times: real_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < n IMPLIES
        times(index + 1) >= times(index) + 1

  prescribed_right_derivative_limits(
      n: nat,
      times: real_sequence,
      f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index <= n IMPLIES
        has_right_limit(
          derivative_function(f),
          times(index),
          0)

  prescribed_second_derivatives(
      n: nat,
      times: real_sequence,
      f: real_function): bool =
    (FORALL (index: nat):
      index < n IMPLIES
        FORALL (x: real):
          (times(index) < x
            AND x < times(index + 1))
          IMPLIES
            second_derivative_value(f, x)
              = ((index + 1) :: real))
      AND
    (FORALL (x: real):
      x > times(n) IMPLIES
        second_derivative_value(f, x)
          = ((n + 1) :: real))

  admissible_time(time: real): bool =
    time >= 0
      AND
    EXISTS
        (n: nat),
        (times: real_sequence),
        (f: real_function):
      separated_times(n, times)
        AND continuous_on_right_ray(f, times(0))
        AND twice_differentiable_away_from_breakpoints(
          n, times, f)
        AND f(times(0)) = 1 / 2
        AND prescribed_right_derivative_limits(
          n, times, f)
        AND prescribed_second_derivatives(
          n, times, f)
        AND f(times(0) + time) = 2023

  putnam_2023_b4_solution: real = 29

  putnam_2023_b4_statement: bool =
    admissible_time(putnam_2023_b4_solution)
      AND
    FORALL (time: real):
      admissible_time(time)
        IMPLIES putnam_2023_b4_solution <= time
END putnam_2023_b4

title: putnam_2023_b5
content:
import Mathlib

open Nat Topology Filter

abbrev putnam_2023_b5_solution : Set ℕ := sorry
-- {n : ℕ | n = 1 ∨ n ≡ 2 [MOD 4]}
/--
Determine which positive integers $n$ have the following property: For all integers $m$ that are relatively prime to $n$, there exists a permutation $\pi:\{1,2,\dots,n\} \to \{1,2,\dots,n\}$ such that $\pi(\pi(k)) \equiv mk \pmod{n}$ for all $k \in \{1,2,\dots,n\}$.
-/
theorem putnam_2023_b5
  (n : ℕ) :
  n ∈ putnam_2023_b5_solution ↔
    0 < n ∧
    (∀ m : ℤ, IsRelPrime m n → ∃ p : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
      ∀ k : Fin n, (p (p k)).1 + 1 ≡ m * (k.1 + 1) [ZMOD n]) :=
sorry

Require Import PeanoNat. From mathcomp Require Import div fintype perm ssrbool.
Definition putnam_2023_b5_solution (n : nat) := n = 1 \/ n mod 4 = 2.
Theorem putnam_2023_b5
    (p : nat -> Prop := fun n => forall m : nat, coprime m n -> exists (π: {perm 'I_n}), forall (k: 'I_n), nat_of_ord (π (π k)) = (m*(nat_of_ord k))%%n)
    : forall n : nat, (n > 0 /\ p n) <-> putnam_2023_b5_solution n.
Proof. Admitted.

"HOL-Number_Theory.Cong"

  "putnam_2023_b5_solution = {n::int. n > 0 \<and> (n = 1 \<or> [n = 2] (mod 4))}"
theorem putnam_2023_b5:

  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2023_b5): classification of the positive

title: putnam_2023_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b5:
;; positive integers whose every coprime multiplication permutation has a
;; permutation square root are exactly 1 and the integers congruent to 2
;; modulo 4. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; The residues 0,...,n-1 are the source carrier {1,...,n} modulo n, with n
;; represented by 0. A permutation is represented exactly by its image list
;; on these residues. For positive n, every integer m has one such residue,
;; and coprimality with n and the required congruences depend only on that
;; residue. Thus the finite searches below preserve both source quantifiers.

(defun putnam-2023-b5-residues (count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons (- count 1)
          (putnam-2023-b5-residues (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b5-prefix-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (cons (cons item (car lists))
          (putnam-2023-b5-prefix-each item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b5-insert-everywhere (item values)
  (if (endp values)
      (list (list item))
    (cons (cons item values)
          (putnam-2023-b5-prefix-each
           (car values)
           (putnam-2023-b5-insert-everywhere
            item (cdr values))))))

(defun putnam-2023-b5-insert-into-each (item permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-2023-b5-insert-everywhere
      item (car permutations))
     (putnam-2023-b5-insert-into-each
      item (cdr permutations)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b5-permutations (values)
  (if (endp values)
      (list nil)
    (putnam-2023-b5-insert-into-each
     (car values)
     (putnam-2023-b5-permutations (cdr values)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b5-coprime-through-p
    (m n divisor)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix divisor)))
  (if (and (natp divisor)
           (< 1 divisor))
      (and
       (not
        (and (equal (mod m divisor) 0)
             (equal (mod n divisor) 0)))
       (putnam-2023-b5-coprime-through-p
        m n (- divisor 1)))
    t))

(defun putnam-2023-b5-coprime-p (m n)
  (and
   (natp m)
   (posp n)
   (putnam-2023-b5-coprime-through-p m n n)))

(defun putnam-2023-b5-square-congruences-p
    (permutation m n remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (let* ((k (- n remaining))
           (first-image (nth k permutation))
           (second-image (nth first-image permutation)))
      (and
       (equal second-image (mod (* m k) n))
       (putnam-2023-b5-square-congruences-p
        permutation m n (- remaining 1))))))

(defun putnam-2023-b5-has-square-root-p
    (permutations m n)
  (if (endp permutations)
      nil
    (or
     (putnam-2023-b5-square-congruences-p
      (car permutations) m n n)
     (putnam-2023-b5-has-square-root-p
      (cdr permutations) m n))))

(defun putnam-2023-b5-all-multipliers-p
    (count n permutations)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      t
    (let ((m (- count 1)))
      (and
       (or
        (not (putnam-2023-b5-coprime-p m n))
        (putnam-2023-b5-has-square-root-p
         permutations m n))
       (putnam-2023-b5-all-multipliers-p
        (- count 1) n permutations)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b5-property-p (n)
  (and
   (posp n)
   (let ((permutations
          (putnam-2023-b5-permutations
           (putnam-2023-b5-residues n))))
     (putnam-2023-b5-all-multipliers-p
      n n permutations))))

(defun putnam-2023-b5-solution-p (n)
  (and
   (natp n)
   (or (equal n 1)
       (equal (mod n 4) 2))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2023-b5-statement (n)
  (implies
   (natp n)
   (equal
    (putnam-2023-b5-property-p n)
    (putnam-2023-b5-solution-p n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2023_b5): classification of positive integers
-- admitting permutation square roots of multiplication by every coprime
-- integer modulo n. This file contains no proof.

module Putnam2023B5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infixr 2 _or_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where

  right : B -> A or B

  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : (n : Nat) -> Positive (suc n)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

toNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
toNat fzero =
  zero
toNat (fsuc index) =
  suc (toNat index)

record Permutation (n : Nat) : Set where
  field
    apply         : Fin n -> Fin n
    inverse       : Fin n -> Fin n
    inverse-apply : (index : Fin n) -> inverse (apply index) == index
    apply-inverse : (index : Fin n) -> apply (inverse index) == index

open Permutation

negativeNat : Nat -> Int
negativeNat zero =
  pos zero
negativeNat (suc n) =
  negsuc n

differenceNat : Nat -> Nat -> Int
differenceNat zero zero =
  pos zero
differenceNat (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
differenceNat zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
differenceNat (suc m) (suc n) =
  differenceNat m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  differenceNat m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  differenceNat n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negativeNat (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negativeNat (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

fourN : Nat
fourN =
  twoN * twoN

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos oneN

record Coprime (m : Int) (n : Nat) : Set where
  constructor bezout
  field
    left-coefficient right-coefficient : Int
    combination :
      addInt
        (multiplyInt left-coefficient m)
        (multiplyInt right-coefficient (pos n))
      ==
      oneZ

record IntModEq
  (modulus : Nat)
  (left-value right-value : Int) :
  Set where

  constructor congruent
  field
    multiple : Int
    equation :
      left-value
      ==
      addInt
        right-value
        (multiplyInt (pos modulus) multiple)

finValue : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Int
finValue index =
  pos (suc (toNat index))

PermutationSquareProperty : Nat -> Set
PermutationSquareProperty n =
  (m : Int) ->
  Coprime m n ->
  Exists (Permutation n)
    (\ permutation ->
      (index : Fin n) ->
      IntModEq n
        (finValue (apply permutation (apply permutation index)))
        (multiplyInt m (finValue index)))

putnam-2023-b5-solution : Nat -> Set
putnam-2023-b5-solution n =
  (n == oneN)
  or
  Exists Nat
    (\ quotient ->
      n == fourN * quotient + twoN)

putnam-2023-b5 : Set
putnam-2023-b5 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Iff
    (putnam-2023-b5-solution n)
    (Positive n and PermutationSquareProperty n)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b5:
  the positive integers for which every coprime integer multiplier modulo n
  is the square of a permutation of the residues 1 through n are exactly 1
  and the integers congruent to 2 modulo 4. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory gcdTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2023_b5 =
  ``!n : num.
      (n = 1 \/ n MOD 4 = 2) <=>
      0 < n /\
      !m : int.
        gcd (Num (ABS m)) n = 1
        ==>
        ?p : num -> num.
          BIJ p (count n) (count n) /\
          !k : num.
            k < n
            ==>
            ?q : int.
              int_of_num (p (p k) + 1) =
                m * int_of_num (k + 1) + int_of_num n * q``;

  integer relatively prime to n has a permutation square acting as
  multiplication modulo n. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  NN0 is set.mm's class of nonnegative integers. For positive n, the
  inclusive interval 1 ... n is the problem's n-element carrier, and the
  base of its symmetric group is exactly the set of its permutations.
  Equality of the displayed residues is congruence modulo n.

  The integer multiplier m remains universally quantified, and the
  permutation p remains existentially quantified inside that scope. The
  right side is the documented classification n = 1 or n congruent to 2
  modulo 4. The final declaration is a single unproved $a corpus statement;
  this database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d k m n p $.

  putnambench-putnam-2023-b5 $a |- A. n e. NN0
    (
      (
        0 < n
        /\
        A. m e. ZZ
          (
            ( m gcd n ) = 1
            ->
            E. p e. ( Base ` ( SymGrp ` ( 1 ... n ) ) )
              A. k e. ( 1 ... n )
                (
                  ( ( p ` ( p ` k ) ) mod n )
                  =
                  ( ( m x. k ) mod n )
                )
          )
      )
      <->
      (
        n = 1
        \/
        ( n mod 4 ) = 2
      )
    )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2023_b5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b5:
% the positive integers admitting permutation square roots of multiplication
% by every relatively prime integer are exactly 1 and those congruent to 2
% modulo 4. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2023_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_function: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  int_divides(divisor, value: int): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: int):
      value = divisor * quotient

  relatively_prime(left, right: int): bool =
    FORALL (divisor: int):
      int_divides(divisor, left)
        AND int_divides(divisor, right)
      IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = -1

  in_initial_interval(value, n: nat): bool =
    1 <= value AND value <= n

  permutation_on_initial_interval(
      p: natural_function,
      n: nat): bool =
    (FORALL (index: nat):
      in_initial_interval(index, n)
        IMPLIES in_initial_interval(p(index), n))
      AND
        (FORALL (left, right: nat):
          in_initial_interval(left, n)
            AND in_initial_interval(right, n)
            AND p(left) = p(right)
          IMPLIES left = right)
      AND
        (FORALL (value: nat):
          in_initial_interval(value, n)
            IMPLIES
              EXISTS (index: nat):
                in_initial_interval(index, n)
                  AND p(index) = value)

  int_congruent_mod_nat(
      left, right: int,
      modulus: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (offset: int):
      left - right = (modulus :: int) * offset

  permutation_square_property(n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (m: int):
      relatively_prime(m, n :: int)
        IMPLIES
          EXISTS (p: natural_function):
            permutation_on_initial_interval(p, n)
              AND
                FORALL (k: nat):
                  in_initial_interval(k, n)
                    IMPLIES
                      int_congruent_mod_nat(
                        p(p(k)) :: int,
                        m * (k :: int),
                        n)

  putnam_2023_b5_solution(n: nat): bool =
    n = 1 OR mod(n, 4) = 2

  putnam_2023_b5: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      (n > 0 AND permutation_square_property(n))
        IFF putnam_2023_b5_solution(n)
END putnam_2023_b5

import Mathlib

open Nat Topology Filter

abbrev putnam_2023_b6_solution : ℕ → ℤ := sorry
-- (fun n : ℕ => (-1) ^ (⌈(n / 2 : ℚ)⌉₊ + 1) * 2 * ⌈(n / 2 : ℚ)⌉₊)
/--
Let $n$ be a positive integer. For $i$ and $j$ in $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, let $s(i,j)$ be the number of pairs $(a,b)$ of nonnegative integers satisfying $ai+bj=n$. Let $S$ be the $n$-by-$n$ matrix whose $(i,j)$ entry is $s(i,j)$. For example, when $n=5$, we have $S = \begin{bmatrix}
6 & 3 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\
3 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\
2 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\
2 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\
2 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 2
\end{bmatrix}$. Compute the determinant of $S$.
-/
theorem putnam_2023_b6
(n : ℕ)
(S : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℤ)
(npos : n > 0)
(hS : ∀ i j : Fin n, S i j = ∑' a : ℕ, ∑' b : ℕ, if a * (i.1 + 1) + b * (j.1 + 1) = (n : ℤ) then 1 else 0)
: S.det = putnam_2023_b6_solution n :=
sorry

title: putnam_2023_b6
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b6:
   the determinant of the integer matrix counting nonnegative solutions to
   a*i + b*j = n for 1 <= i,j <= n. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Vectors.Fin ZArith Arith.PeanoNat.

Import ListNotations.

Definition putnam_2023_b6_matrix (n : nat) : Type :=
  Fin.t n -> Fin.t n -> Z.

Definition putnam_2023_b6_fin_index
    {n : nat} (i : Fin.t n) : nat :=
  proj1_sig (Fin.to_nat i).

Fixpoint putnam_2023_b6_fin_list
    (n : nat) : list (Fin.t n) :=
  match n as k return list (Fin.t k) with
  | O => []
  | S k =>
      Fin.F1 :: map Fin.FS (putnam_2023_b6_fin_list k)
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2023_b6_zsum_upto
    (bound : nat) (f : nat -> Z) : Z :=
  match bound with
  | O => f O
  | S k => (putnam_2023_b6_zsum_upto k f + f (S k))%Z
  end.

Definition putnam_2023_b6_solution_count
    {n : nat} (i j : Fin.t n) : Z :=
  putnam_2023_b6_zsum_upto n
    (fun a =>
      putnam_2023_b6_zsum_upto n
        (fun b =>
          if Nat.eqb
               (a * (putnam_2023_b6_fin_index i + 1) +
                b * (putnam_2023_b6_fin_index j + 1))
               n
          then 1%Z
          else 0%Z)).

Definition putnam_2023_b6_rows
    {n : nat} (A : putnam_2023_b6_matrix n) :
    list (list Z) :=
  map
    (fun i =>
      map (fun j => A i j) (putnam_2023_b6_fin_list n))
    (putnam_2023_b6_fin_list n).

Definition putnam_2023_b6_delete_nth
    {T : Type} (j : nat) (xs : list T) : list T :=
  firstn j xs ++ skipn (S j) xs.

Definition putnam_2023_b6_cofactor_sign (j : nat) : Z :=
  if Nat.even j then 1%Z else (-1)%Z.

Fixpoint putnam_2023_b6_zsum (xs : list Z) : Z :=
  match xs with
  | [] => 0%Z
  | x :: rest => (x + putnam_2023_b6_zsum rest)%Z
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2023_b6_list_det
    (n : nat) (M : list (list Z)) {struct n} : Z :=
  match n with
  | O => 1%Z
  | S k =>
      match M with
      | [] => 0%Z
      | row :: rows =>
          putnam_2023_b6_zsum
            (map
              (fun j : nat =>
                (putnam_2023_b6_cofactor_sign j *
                 nth j row 0%Z *
                 putnam_2023_b6_list_det k
                   (map (putnam_2023_b6_delete_nth j) rows))%Z)
              (seq 0 (S k)))
      end
  end.

Definition putnam_2023_b6_determinant
    {n : nat} (A : putnam_2023_b6_matrix n) : Z :=
  putnam_2023_b6_list_det n (putnam_2023_b6_rows A).

Definition putnam_2023_b6_solution (n : nat) : Z :=
  let half := Nat.div (S n) 2 in
  (Z.pow (-1) (Z.of_nat (S half)) * 2 * Z.of_nat half)%Z.

Theorem putnam_2023_b6
    (n : nat)
    (S : putnam_2023_b6_matrix n)
    (npos : (0 < n)%nat)
    (hS :
      forall i j : Fin.t n,
        S i j = putnam_2023_b6_solution_count i j) :
  putnam_2023_b6_determinant S =
  putnam_2023_b6_solution n.
Admitted.

definition putnam_2023_b6_solution :: "int \<Rightarrow> int" where

theorem putnam_2023_b6:

  assumes npos: "n > 0"
  and pncard: "CARD('n) = (nat n)"

    (\<forall>i::int\<in>{0..(n-1)}. \<forall>j::int\<in>{0..(n-1)}.
      S$(pnind i)$(pnind j) =

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b6
  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2023_b6): the determinant of the matrix
  counting nonnegative solutions to a*i + b*j = n. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let integer_det =
     \(A:num->num->int) n.
       isum {p:num->num |
               BIJ p (1..n) (1..n) /\
               (!i:num. ~(i IN 1..n) ==> p i = i)}
            (\p.
               (if EVEN
                     (CARD
                       {(i,j) |
                          i IN 1..n /\
                          j IN 1..n /\
                          i < j /\
                          p j < p i})
                then (&1:int)
                else --(&1:int)) *
               iproduct (1..n) (\i. A i (p i))) in
   let putnam_2023_b6_solution =
     \n:num.
       let k = (n + 1) DIV 2 in
       (if EVEN (k + 1) then (&1:int) else --(&1:int)) *
       (&2:int) * &k in
   !n:num. !S:num->num->int.
     0 < n /\
     (!i j:num.
        i IN 1..n /\
        j IN 1..n
        ==> S i j =
            &(CARD {(a,b) | a * i + b * j = n}))
     ==> integer_det S n = putnam_2023_b6_solution n`;;

title: putnam_2023_b6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b6:
;; the determinant of the n by n integer matrix counting nonnegative solutions
;; of a(i+1)+b(j+1)=n equals the stated signed even integer. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; A finite matrix is represented extensionally by its rows in zero-based
;; index order. The source equation determines every entry. Since i+1 and j+1
;; are positive, every nonnegative solution has a,b <= n, so the bounded
;; recursive count below is exactly the source count over all naturals.

(defun putnam-2023-b6-count-b (a b n i j)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix b)))
  (if (zp b)
      (if (equal (* a (+ i 1)) n) 1 0)
    (+ (if (equal
            (+ (* a (+ i 1))
               (* b (+ j 1)))
            n)
           1
         0)
       (putnam-2023-b6-count-b
        a (- b 1) n i j))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-count-pairs (a n i j)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix a)))
  (if (zp a)
      (putnam-2023-b6-count-b 0 n n i j)
    (+ (putnam-2023-b6-count-b a n n i j)
       (putnam-2023-b6-count-pairs
        (- a 1) n i j))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-row-matches-p
    (row remaining n i j)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      (equal row nil)
    (and
     (consp row)
     (equal
      (car row)
      (putnam-2023-b6-count-pairs n n i j))
     (putnam-2023-b6-row-matches-p
      (cdr row) (- remaining 1) n i (+ j 1)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-matrix-matches-p
    (matrix remaining n i)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      (equal matrix nil)
    (and
     (consp matrix)
     (putnam-2023-b6-row-matches-p
      (car matrix) n n i 0)
     (putnam-2023-b6-matrix-matches-p
      (cdr matrix) (- remaining 1) n (+ i 1)))))

;; Generate all permutations of the zero-based column indices.

(defun putnam-2023-b6-indices (count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons (- count 1)
          (putnam-2023-b6-indices (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-prefix-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (cons (cons item (car lists))
          (putnam-2023-b6-prefix-each item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-insert-everywhere (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list (list item))
    (cons (cons item list)
          (putnam-2023-b6-prefix-each
           (car list)
           (putnam-2023-b6-insert-everywhere
            item (cdr list))))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-insert-into-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-2023-b6-insert-everywhere item (car lists))
     (putnam-2023-b6-insert-into-each
      item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-permutations (list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list nil)
    (putnam-2023-b6-insert-into-each
     (car list)
     (putnam-2023-b6-permutations (cdr list)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-count-smaller (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      0
    (+ (if (< (car list) item) 1 0)
       (putnam-2023-b6-count-smaller item (cdr list)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-inversion-count (permutation)
  (if (endp permutation)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2023-b6-count-smaller
        (car permutation) (cdr permutation))
       (putnam-2023-b6-inversion-count
        (cdr permutation)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-permutation-sign (permutation)
  (if (evenp
       (putnam-2023-b6-inversion-count permutation))
      1
    -1))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-diagonal-product
    (matrix row permutation)
  (if (endp permutation)
      1
    (* (nth (car permutation) (nth row matrix))
       (putnam-2023-b6-diagonal-product
        matrix (+ row 1) (cdr permutation)))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-determinant-sum
    (matrix permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      0
    (+ (* (putnam-2023-b6-permutation-sign
           (car permutations))
          (putnam-2023-b6-diagonal-product
           matrix 0 (car permutations)))
       (putnam-2023-b6-determinant-sum
        matrix (cdr permutations)))))

;; This is the exact Leibniz determinant of the represented integer matrix.

(defun putnam-2023-b6-determinant (matrix n)
  (putnam-2023-b6-determinant-sum
   matrix
   (putnam-2023-b6-permutations
    (putnam-2023-b6-indices n))))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-ceiling-half (n)
  (floor (+ n 1) 2))

(defun putnam-2023-b6-solution (n)
  (let ((half (putnam-2023-b6-ceiling-half n)))
    (* (if (evenp (+ half 1)) 1 -1)
       2
       half)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2023-b6-statement (n matrix)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp n)
    (< 0 n)
    (putnam-2023-b6-matrix-matches-p matrix n n 0))
   (equal
    (putnam-2023-b6-determinant matrix n)
    (putnam-2023-b6-solution n))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2023_b6): the determinant of the matrix counting
-- nonnegative integer solutions to a(i+1) + b(j+1) = n. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; true; false)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  suc zero <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finToNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finToNat fzero =
  zero
finToNat (fsuc i) =
  suc (finToNat i)

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

difference : Nat -> Nat -> Int
difference zero zero =
  pos zero
difference (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
difference zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
difference (suc m) (suc n) =
  difference m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  difference m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  difference n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

natEqual : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
natEqual zero zero =
  true
natEqual zero (suc n) =
  false
natEqual (suc m) zero =
  false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) =
  natEqual m n

indicator : Bool -> Nat
indicator true =
  suc zero
indicator false =
  zero

countFin :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Bool) ->
  Nat
countFin {zero} predicate =
  zero
countFin {suc n} predicate =
  indicator (predicate fzero) +
  countFin (\ i -> predicate (fsuc i))

sumFinNat :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Nat) ->
  Nat
sumFinNat {zero} term =
  zero
sumFinNat {suc n} term =
  term fzero +
  sumFinNat (\ i -> term (fsuc i))

Matrix : Set -> Nat -> Set
Matrix A n =
  Fin n -> Fin n -> A

solutionCount :
  (n : Nat) ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n ->
  Nat
solutionCount n i j =
  sumFinNat {suc n}
    (\ a ->
      countFin {suc n}
        (\ b ->
          natEqual
            (finToNat a * suc (finToNat i) +
             finToNat b * suc (finToNat j))
            n))

EntriesCountSolutions :
  (n : Nat) ->
  Matrix Int n ->
  Set
EntriesCountSolutions n S =
  (i j : Fin n) ->
  S i j == pos (solutionCount n i j)

sumFinInt :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Int) ->
  Int
sumFinInt {zero} term =
  pos zero
sumFinInt {suc n} term =
  addInt
    (term fzero)
    (sumFinInt (\ i -> term (fsuc i)))

skip :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin (suc n)
skip {zero} removed ()
skip {suc n} fzero i =
  fsuc i
skip {suc n} (fsuc removed) fzero =
  fzero
skip {suc n} (fsuc removed) (fsuc i) =
  fsuc (skip removed i)

firstRowMinor :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix Int (suc n) ->
  Fin (suc n) ->
  Matrix Int n
firstRowMinor S removedColumn i j =
  S (fsuc i) (skip removedColumn j)

alternatingSign :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Fin n ->
  Int
alternatingSign fzero =
  pos (suc zero)
alternatingSign (fsuc i) =
  negateInt (alternatingSign i)

determinant :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix Int n ->
  Int
determinant {zero} S =
  pos (suc zero)
determinant {suc n} S =
  sumFinInt
    (\ column ->
      multiplyInt
        (alternatingSign column)
        (multiplyInt
          (S fzero column)
          (determinant (firstRowMinor S column))))

ceilingHalf : Nat -> Nat
ceilingHalf zero =
  zero
ceilingHalf (suc zero) =
  suc zero
ceilingHalf (suc (suc n)) =
  suc (ceilingHalf n)

minusOnePower : Nat -> Int
minusOnePower zero =
  pos (suc zero)
minusOnePower (suc exponent) =
  negateInt (minusOnePower exponent)

putnam-2023-b6-solution : Nat -> Int
putnam-2023-b6-solution n =
  multiplyInt
    (minusOnePower (suc (ceilingHalf n)))
    (pos (suc (suc zero) * ceilingHalf n))

putnam-2023-b6 : Set
putnam-2023-b6 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  (S : Matrix Int n) ->
  EntriesCountSolutions n S ->
  determinant S == putnam-2023-b6-solution n

title: putnam_2023_b6
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b6
  (putnambench__hol4__putnam_2023_b6): the determinant of the matrix counting
  nonnegative integer solutions to a*i + b*j = n has the specified alternating
  closed form. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory permutesTheory;

val putnam_2023_b6 =
  ``let determinant =
      \n : num. \A : num -> num -> int.
        ITSET
          (\p : num -> num. \sum : int.
             (if evenperm p then 1 else ~1) *
             ITSET
               (\i : num. \acc : int. A i (p i) * acc)
               (count n)
               (1 : int) +
             sum)
          {p : num -> num | p permutes count n}
          (0 : int)
    in
      !n : num. !S : num -> num -> int.
        0 < n /\
        (!i j : num.
           i < n /\ j < n
           ==>
           S i j =
             int_of_num
               (CARD
                  {ab : num # num |
                     FST ab * (i + 1) + SND ab * (j + 1) = n}))
        ==>
        determinant n S =
          (~1 : int) ** ((n + 1) DIV 2 + 1) *
          int_of_num (2 * ((n + 1) DIV 2))``;

title: putnam_2023_b6
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2023_b6: the determinant of the integer matrix counting
  nonnegative solutions to a i + b j = n has the stated alternating
  ceiling-based closed form. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For positive n, 0 ..^ n is the canonical zero-based n-element index set.
  The row i, column j entry of the displayed binary map is the cardinality
  of the set of pairs (a,b) in NN0 X. NN0 satisfying
  a(i+1) + b(j+1) = n. It is therefore exactly the source matrix after
  shifting its one-based indices down by one. SetMM's maDet over ZZring is
  its integer determinant.

  The internally existential k is uniquely determined by n = 2k or
  n+1 = 2k, so k is exactly ceiling(n/2). Consequently the determinant
  equality is the annotated closed form
  (-1)^(ceiling(n/2)+1) * 2 * ceiling(n/2). Inlining the uniquely specified
  matrix and defining the ceiling through this parity characterization are
  bidirectionally equivalent to the source statement. The final declaration
  is a single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p
  proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d i j k n t $.

  putnambench-putnam-2023-b6 $a |- A. n e. NN
    E. k e. NN
      (
        (
          n = ( 2 x. k )
          \/
          ( n + 1 ) = ( 2 x. k )
        )
        /\
        (
          (
            ( ( 0 ..^ n ) maDet ZZring )
            `
            (
              i e. ( 0 ..^ n ) , j e. ( 0 ..^ n ) |->
                (
                  #
                  `
                  {
                    t e. ( NN0 X. NN0 )
                    |
                    (
                      (
                        ( ( 1st ` t ) x. ( i + 1 ) )
                        +
                        ( ( 2nd ` t ) x. ( j + 1 ) )
                      )
                      =
                      n
                    )
                  }
                )
            )
          )
          =
          (
            ( ( -u 1 ) ^ ( k + 1 ) )
            x.
            ( 2 x. k )
          )
        )
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2023_b6
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2023_b6:
% the determinant of the n-by-n integer matrix whose (i,j)-entry counts
% nonnegative solutions of ai + bj = n has the stated parity-dependent value.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2023_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  integer_matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> int]

  quotient_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      0
    ELSE
      1
        + quotient_aux(
            numerator - denominator,
            denominator,
            fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  remainder_aux(
      numerator, denominator, fuel: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF fuel = 0
        OR denominator = 0
        OR numerator < denominator THEN
      numerator
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator - denominator,
        denominator,
        fuel - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE fuel

  safe_ndiv(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    quotient_aux(
      numerator,
      denominator,
      numerator + 1)

  safe_mod(numerator, denominator: nat): nat =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      remainder_aux(
        numerator,
        denominator,
        numerator + 1)
    ENDIF

  count_true(
      property: [nat -> bool],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_true(property, count - 1)
        + IF property(count - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  pair_first(code, n: nat): nat =
    safe_ndiv(code, n + 1)

  pair_second(code, n: nat): nat =
    safe_mod(code, n + 1)

  is_solution_pair(code, n, i, j: nat): bool =
    code < (n + 1) ^ 2
      AND pair_first(code, n) * (i + 1)
        + pair_second(code, n) * (j + 1)
        = n

  solution_pair_count(n, i, j: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      (LAMBDA (code: nat):
        is_solution_pair(code, n, i, j)),
      (n + 1) ^ 2)

  has_putnam_entries(S: integer_matrix, n: nat): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      (i < n AND j < n)
        IMPLIES
          S(i, j) = (solution_pair_count(n, i, j) :: int)

  function_code_count(size: nat): nat =
    IF size = 0 THEN 1 ELSE size ^ size ENDIF

  permutation_entry(code, row, size: nat): nat =
    IF size = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      safe_mod(safe_ndiv(code, size ^ row), size)
    ENDIF

  permutation_code(code, size: nat): bool =
    code < function_code_count(size)
      AND (FORALL (row_1, row_2: nat):
        (row_1 < size
          AND row_2 < size
          AND permutation_entry(code, row_1, size)
            = permutation_entry(code, row_2, size))
        IMPLIES row_1 = row_2)

  pair_row(pair, size: nat): nat =
    safe_ndiv(pair, size)

  pair_column(pair, size: nat): nat =
    safe_mod(pair, size)

  inversion_at(code, pair, size: nat): bool =
    pair_row(pair, size) < size
      AND pair_column(pair, size) < size
      AND pair_row(pair, size) < pair_column(pair, size)
      AND permutation_entry(code, pair_row(pair, size), size)
        > permutation_entry(code, pair_column(pair, size), size)

  inversion_count(code, size: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      (LAMBDA (pair: nat): inversion_at(code, pair, size)),
      size * size)

  permutation_sign(code, size: nat): int =
    IF mod(inversion_count(code, size), 2) = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      -1
    ENDIF

  permutation_product(
      S: integer_matrix,
      code, size, count: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      permutation_product(S, code, size, count - 1)
        * S(
            count - 1,
            permutation_entry(code, count - 1, size))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  determinant_sum(
      S: integer_matrix,
      size, limit: nat): RECURSIVE int =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET code: nat = limit - 1 IN
        determinant_sum(S, size, limit - 1)
          + IF permutation_code(code, size) THEN
              permutation_sign(code, size)
                * permutation_product(S, code, size, size)
            ELSE
              0
            ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  determinant(S: integer_matrix, size: nat): int =
    determinant_sum(S, size, function_code_count(size))

  ceiling_half(n: nat): nat =
    safe_ndiv(n + 1, 2)

  putnam_2023_b6_solution(n: nat): int =
    (-1 :: int) ^ (ceiling_half(n) + 1)
      * 2
      * (ceiling_half(n) :: int)

  putnam_2023_b6: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (S: integer_matrix):
      (n > 0 AND has_putnam_entries(S, n))
        IMPLIES
          determinant(S, n) = putnam_2023_b6_solution(n)
END putnam_2023_b6

   (putnambench__rocq__putnam_2024_a1): the positive natural exponents
   admitting positive natural numbers a, b, and c satisfying
   2*a^n + 3*b^n = 4*c^n are exactly n = 1. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat.

Open Scope nat_scope.

Theorem putnam_2024_a1 :
  forall n : nat,
    (0 < n /\
     exists a b c : nat,
       0 < a /\
       0 < b /\
       0 < c /\
       2 * Nat.pow a n + 3 * Nat.pow b n = 4 * Nat.pow c n) <->
    n = 1.

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a1:
;; the positive integers n admitting positive integers a, b, and c with
;; 2*a^n + 3*b^n = 4*c^n are exactly {1}. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; FN-EQUAL supplies universal quantification over ACL2 objects. Its
;; inequality with the constant-true function below is therefore exactly the
;; source's internal existential quantifier over positive natural a, b, and c.

(defun putnam-2024-a1-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2024-a1-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list 'if
            (car terms)
            (putnam-2024-a1-and-terms (cdr terms))
            (putnam-2024-a1-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2024-a1-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2024-a1-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2024-a1-multiply-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-* left right))

(defun putnam-2024-a1-positive-natural-term (value)
  (putnam-2024-a1-and-terms
   (list
    (list 'natp value)
    (list '< (putnam-2024-a1-quoted 0) value))))

(defun putnam-2024-a1-true-function ()
  (list 'lambda
        '(a b c)
        (putnam-2024-a1-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2024-a1-witness-failure-function (n)
  (let* ((exponent (putnam-2024-a1-quoted n))
         (a-power (list 'expt 'a exponent))
         (b-power (list 'expt 'b exponent))
         (c-power (list 'expt 'c exponent))
         (left
          (putnam-2024-a1-add-term
           (putnam-2024-a1-multiply-term
            (putnam-2024-a1-quoted 2)
            a-power)
           (putnam-2024-a1-multiply-term
            (putnam-2024-a1-quoted 3)
            b-power)))
         (right
          (putnam-2024-a1-multiply-term
           (putnam-2024-a1-quoted 4)
           c-power))
         (qualification
          (putnam-2024-a1-and-terms
           (list
            (putnam-2024-a1-positive-natural-term 'a)
            (putnam-2024-a1-positive-natural-term 'b)
            (putnam-2024-a1-positive-natural-term 'c)
            (list 'equal left right)))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(a b c)
     (list
      'if
      qualification
      (putnam-2024-a1-quoted nil)
      (putnam-2024-a1-quoted t)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a1-witness-exists-p (n)
  (let ((failure-function
         (putnam-2024-a1-witness-failure-function n))
        (true-function
         (putnam-2024-a1-true-function)))
    (and
     (tamep-functionp failure-function)
     (tamep-functionp true-function)
     (not (fn-equal failure-function true-function)))))

;; ACL2 universally closes N. This pointwise IFF is the source set equality.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2024-a1-statement (n)
  (implies
   (natp n)
   (iff
    (and
     (< 0 n)
     (putnam-2024-a1-witness-exists-p n))
    (equal n 1))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2024_a1): the positive natural exponents for
-- which 2a^n + 3b^n = 4c^n has positive natural solutions are exactly n = 1.
-- This file contains no proof.

module Putnam2024A1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<N_
infixr 8 _^_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

_^_ : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
base ^ zero =
  suc zero
base ^ suc exponent =
  base * (base ^ exponent)

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

three : Nat
three =
  suc two

four : Nat
four =
  suc three

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  zero <N n

HasPositiveSolution : Nat -> Set
HasPositiveSolution n =
  Exists Nat
    (\ a ->
      Positive a
      and
      Exists Nat
        (\ b ->
          Positive b
          and
          Exists Nat
            (\ c ->
              Positive c
              and
              two * (a ^ n) + three * (b ^ n) ==
                four * (c ^ n))))

putnam-2024-a1 : Set
putnam-2024-a1 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Iff
    (Positive n and HasPositiveSolution n)
    (n == one)

title: putnam_2024_a1
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a1:
  the positive natural exponents admitting positive natural numbers a, b, and
  c with 2*a^n + 3*b^n = 4*c^n are exactly n = 1. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory;

val putnam_2024_a1 =
  ``!n : num.
      (0 < n /\
       ?a b c : num.
         0 < a /\
         0 < b /\
         0 < c /\
         2 * a EXP n + 3 * b EXP n = 4 * c EXP n)
      <=>
      n = 1``;
