$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2024_a1: the positive exponents for which positive integers a, b,
  and c satisfy 2 a^n + 3 b^n = 4 c^n are exactly the singleton { 1 }.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's NN0 and NN are respectively the nonnegative and positive integers.
  Thus the restricted class preserves the Lean natural-number domain for n,
  its explicit positivity condition, and the three internally existentially
  quantified positive-integer witnesses. The right-hand singleton is the
  source solution annotation {1}. The final declaration is the single
  unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d a b c n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2024-a1 $a |-
    {
      n e. NN0
      |
      (
        0 < n
        /\
        E. a e. NN E. b e. NN E. c e. NN
          (
            (
              ( 2 x. ( a ^ n ) )
              +
              ( 3 x. ( b ^ n ) )
            )
            =
            ( 4 x. ( c ^ n ) )
          )
      )
    }
    =
    { 1 }
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2024_a1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a1:
% the positive natural exponents admitting positive natural solutions to
% 2*a^n + 3*b^n = 4*c^n are exactly n = 1. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2024_a1: THEORY
BEGIN

  has_positive_solution(n: nat): bool =
    n > 0
      AND EXISTS (a, b, c: nat):
        a > 0
          AND b > 0
          AND c > 0
          AND 2 * a ^ n + 3 * b ^ n = 4 * c ^ n

  putnam_2024_a1_statement: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat):
      has_positive_solution(n) IFF n = 1

END putnam_2024_a1

title: putnam_2024_a2
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a2:
   the classification of real polynomials satisfying a composition and
   divisibility identity. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals List.

Open Scope R_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_2024_a2_polynomial_eval
    (coefficients : list R) (x : R) : R :=
  match coefficients with
  | nil => 0
  | coefficient :: remaining =>
      coefficient +
      x * putnam_2024_a2_polynomial_eval remaining x
  end.

Theorem putnam_2024_a2 :
  forall p : list R,
    (exists q : list R,
      forall x : R,
        putnam_2024_a2_polynomial_eval
          p (putnam_2024_a2_polynomial_eval p x) - x =
        (putnam_2024_a2_polynomial_eval p x - x) ^ 2 *
          putnam_2024_a2_polynomial_eval q x) <->
    exists a : R,
      (forall x : R,
        putnam_2024_a2_polynomial_eval p x = x + a) \/
      (forall x : R,
        putnam_2024_a2_polynomial_eval p x = - x + a).
Admitted.

title: putnam_2024_a2
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a2
  (putnambench__isabelle__putnam_2024_a2): the real polynomials p for which
  p(p(x)) - x is (p(x) - x)^2 times a real polynomial are exactly the affine
  polynomials with slope 1 or -1. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory putnam_2024_a2
  imports Complex_Main
begin

definition putnam_2024_a2_is_poly :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "putnam_2024_a2_is_poly p \<longleftrightarrow> finite {n. p n \<noteq> 0}"

definition putnam_2024_a2_eval :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> real \<Rightarrow> real" where
  "putnam_2024_a2_eval p x = (\<Sum>n\<in>{n. p n \<noteq> 0}. p n * x ^ n)"

definition putnam_2024_a2_solution :: "(nat \<Rightarrow> real) set" where
  "putnam_2024_a2_solution =
    {p. \<exists>a :: real.
      p = (\<lambda>n. if n = 0 then a else if n = 1 then 1 else 0) \<or>
      p = (\<lambda>n. if n = 0 then a else if n = 1 then -1 else 0)}"

theorem putnam_2024_a2:
  shows
    "{p :: nat \<Rightarrow> real.
      putnam_2024_a2_is_poly p \<and>
      (\<exists>q :: nat \<Rightarrow> real.
        putnam_2024_a2_is_poly q \<and>
        (\<forall>x :: real.
          putnam_2024_a2_eval p (putnam_2024_a2_eval p x) - x =
            (putnam_2024_a2_eval p x - x) ^ 2 *
              putnam_2024_a2_eval q x))}
      = putnam_2024_a2_solution"
  sorry

end

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a2
  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2024_a2): classification of the real
  polynomials p for which p(p(x)) - x is divisible by (p(x) - x)^2.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `!p:real->real.
     polynomial_function p
     ==>
     ((?q:real->real.
         polynomial_function q /\
         (!x:real.
            p (p x) - x = (p x - x) pow 2 * q x))
      <=>
      ?a:real.
        (!x:real. p x = x + a) \/
        (!x:real. p x = --x + a))`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a2:
;; the real polynomials p for which p(p(x))-x is divisible pointwise by
;; (p(x)-x)^2 are exactly p(x)=x+a and p(x)=-x+a. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The real coefficient domain is presented as a real closed ordered field.
;; The square-root and odd-degree-root laws are the standard algebraic
;; characterization of real closedness.  Polynomials are canonical nonempty
;; coefficient lists in ascending degree order.
;;
;; This is bidirectionally equivalent to the source statement: the reals form
;; such a field, while completeness of real closed fields transfers this
;; first-order polynomial assertion between any real closed field and the
;; reals. Canonical coefficient-list equality is polynomial equality because
;; every ordered field is infinite.
;;
;; ACL2 function objects supply the field operations and polynomial evaluation.
;; FN-EQUAL against a constant-T function expresses the field laws over the
;; whole represented carrier. The source's quantifiers are preserved directly:
;; DEFUN-SK existentially quantifies the polynomial q, and a second DEFUN-SK
;; universally quantifies x over the represented field in the pointwise
;; equation. No division algorithm, selected witness, or finite table replaces
;; either quantifier. The final IFF is the source set equality. The annotated
;; integer-unit slope is exactly one or negative one; canonical coefficient
;; lists therefore encode its solution polynomials as (a 1) and (a -1).

(defun putnam-2024-a2-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-apply1-term (function argument)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2024-a2-quoted function)
   (list 'cons argument nil)))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-apply2-term (function left right)
  (list
   'apply$
   (putnam-2024-a2-quoted function)
   (list 'cons left (list 'cons right nil))))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-and-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2024-a2-quoted t)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2024-a2-and-term (cdr terms))
     (putnam-2024-a2-quoted nil))))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-or-term (terms)
  (if (endp terms)
      (putnam-2024-a2-quoted nil)
    (list
     'if
     (car terms)
     (putnam-2024-a2-quoted t)
     (putnam-2024-a2-or-term (cdr terms)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-not-term (term)
  (list
   'if
   term
   (putnam-2024-a2-quoted nil)
   (putnam-2024-a2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-implies-term (antecedent consequent)
  (list
   'if
   antecedent
   consequent
   (putnam-2024-a2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-true-function (formals)
  (list
   'lambda
   formals
   (putnam-2024-a2-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-carrier-term (carrier element)
  (putnam-2024-a2-apply1-term carrier element))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-operation-term (operation left right)
  (putnam-2024-a2-apply2-term operation left right))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-all-coefficients-function (carrier)
  (list
   'lambda
   '(loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)
   (putnam-2024-a2-apply1-term carrier 'loop$-ivars)))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-all-coefficients-term
    (carrier coefficients)
  (list
   'always$+
   (putnam-2024-a2-quoted
    (putnam-2024-a2-all-coefficients-function carrier))
   (putnam-2024-a2-quoted nil)
   coefficients))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-polynomial-term
    (carrier zero coefficients)
  (putnam-2024-a2-and-term
   (list
    (list 'true-listp coefficients)
    (list 'consp coefficients)
    (putnam-2024-a2-all-coefficients-term
     carrier coefficients)
    (putnam-2024-a2-or-term
     (list
      (list 'equal
            (list 'len coefficients)
            (putnam-2024-a2-quoted 1))
      (putnam-2024-a2-not-term
       (list 'equal
             (list 'car (list 'last coefficients))
             (putnam-2024-a2-quoted zero))))))))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-field-laws-function
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (y 'y)

(defun putnam-2024-a2-order-laws-function
    (carrier zero add mul lt)
  (let* ((x 'x)
         (y 'y)
         (z 'z)
         (qzero (putnam-2024-a2-quoted zero))

            (putnam-2024-a2-carrier-term carrier x)
            (putnam-2024-a2-carrier-term carrier y)
            (putnam-2024-a2-carrier-term carrier z))))
         (laws
          (putnam-2024-a2-and-term
           (list
            (putnam-2024-a2-not-term

            (putnam-2024-a2-or-term

              lt-xy

            (putnam-2024-a2-implies-term

              (list lt-xy lt-yz))

            (putnam-2024-a2-implies-term

         (qzero (putnam-2024-a2-quoted zero))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-evaluation-laws-function

  (let* ((coefficient 'coefficient)
         (rest 'rest)
         (x 'x)
         (qzero (putnam-2024-a2-quoted zero))

          (putnam-2024-a2-and-term

            (putnam-2024-a2-all-coefficients-term

            'equal
            (putnam-2024-a2-operation-term

           coefficient
           (putnam-2024-a2-operation-term

            x
            (putnam-2024-a2-operation-term

(defun putnam-2024-a2-real-closed-field-p

             evaluate)

   (tamep-functionp add)
   (tamep-functionp mul)
   (tamep-functionp neg)
   (tamep-functionp inv)
   (tamep-functionp lt)
   (tamep-functionp square-root)
   (tamep-functionp odd-root)
   (tamep-functionp evaluate)
   (apply$ carrier (list zero))
   (apply$ carrier (list one))
   (not (equal zero one))
   (fn-equal
    (putnam-2024-a2-field-laws-function
     carrier zero one add mul neg inv)
    (putnam-2024-a2-true-function '(x y z)))

     '(coefficient rest x)))

    (putnam-2024-a2-odd-root-laws-function
     carrier zero evaluate odd-root)
    (putnam-2024-a2-true-function
     '(coefficients)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-coefficient-list-p

     (apply$ carrier (list (car coefficients)))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-polynomial-p
    (polynomial carrier zero)

   (true-listp polynomial)
   (consp polynomial)
   (putnam-2024-a2-coefficient-list-p
    polynomial carrier)
   (or
    (equal (len polynomial) 1)
    (not (equal (car (last polynomial)) zero)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-trim (coefficients zero)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (let ((tail
             (putnam-2024-a2-poly-trim
              (cdr coefficients) zero)))
        (if (and
             (equal (car coefficients) zero)
             (not (consp tail)))
            nil
          (cons (car coefficients) tail)))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-normalize (coefficients zero)
  (let ((trimmed
         (putnam-2024-a2-poly-trim coefficients zero)))
    (if (consp trimmed)
        trimmed
      (list zero))))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-zero-p (polynomial zero)
  (equal
   (putnam-2024-a2-poly-normalize polynomial zero)
   (list zero)))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-add-raw (left right add)
  (cond
   ((consp left)
    (if (consp right)
        (cons
         (apply$ add (list (car left) (car right)))
         (putnam-2024-a2-poly-add-raw
          (cdr left) (cdr right) add))
      left))
   (t right)))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-add (left right zero add)
  (putnam-2024-a2-poly-normalize
   (putnam-2024-a2-poly-add-raw left right add)
   zero))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-scale-raw
    (scalar polynomial mul)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons
       (apply$ mul (list scalar (car polynomial)))
       (putnam-2024-a2-poly-scale-raw
        scalar (cdr polynomial) mul))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-negate-raw (polynomial neg)
  (if (consp polynomial)
      (cons
       (apply$ neg (list (car polynomial)))
       (putnam-2024-a2-poly-negate-raw
        (cdr polynomial) neg))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-subtract
    (left right zero add neg)
  (putnam-2024-a2-poly-add
   left
   (putnam-2024-a2-poly-negate-raw right neg)
   zero
   add))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-multiply-raw
    (left right zero add mul)
  (if (consp left)
      (putnam-2024-a2-poly-add-raw
       (putnam-2024-a2-poly-scale-raw
        (car left) right mul)
       (cons
        zero
        (putnam-2024-a2-poly-multiply-raw
         (cdr left) right zero add mul))
       add)
    nil))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-multiply
    (left right zero add mul)
  (putnam-2024-a2-poly-normalize
   (putnam-2024-a2-poly-multiply-raw
    left right zero add mul)
   zero))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-compose-raw
    (outer inner zero add mul)
  (if (consp outer)
      (putnam-2024-a2-poly-add-raw
       (list (car outer))
       (putnam-2024-a2-poly-multiply-raw
        inner
        (putnam-2024-a2-poly-compose-raw
         (cdr outer) inner zero add mul)
        zero
        add
        mul)
       add)
    nil))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-compose
    (outer inner zero add mul)
  (putnam-2024-a2-poly-normalize
   (putnam-2024-a2-poly-compose-raw
    outer inner zero add mul)
   zero))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-zero-list (count zero)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons
     zero
     (putnam-2024-a2-zero-list (- count 1) zero))))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-monomial
    (coefficient degree zero)
  (putnam-2024-a2-poly-normalize
   (append
    (putnam-2024-a2-zero-list degree zero)
    (list coefficient))
   zero))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-leading-coefficient
    (polynomial zero)
  (car
   (last
    (putnam-2024-a2-poly-normalize polynomial zero))))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-divmod-steps
    (remainder divisor quotient zero add mul neg inv steps)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix steps)))
  (let* ((normalized-remainder
          (putnam-2024-a2-poly-normalize remainder zero))
         (normalized-divisor
          (putnam-2024-a2-poly-normalize divisor zero))
         (normalized-quotient
          (putnam-2024-a2-poly-normalize quotient zero)))
    (if (or
         (zp steps)
         (putnam-2024-a2-poly-zero-p
          normalized-remainder zero)
         (putnam-2024-a2-poly-zero-p
          normalized-divisor zero)
         (< (len normalized-remainder)
            (len normalized-divisor)))
        (cons normalized-quotient normalized-remainder)
      (let* ((degree-difference
              (- (len normalized-remainder)
                 (len normalized-divisor)))
             (coefficient
              (apply$
               mul
               (list
                (putnam-2024-a2-poly-leading-coefficient
                 normalized-remainder zero)
                (apply$
                 inv
                 (list
                  (putnam-2024-a2-poly-leading-coefficient
                   normalized-divisor zero))))))
             (term
              (putnam-2024-a2-poly-monomial
               coefficient degree-difference zero)))
        (putnam-2024-a2-poly-divmod-steps
         (putnam-2024-a2-poly-subtract
          normalized-remainder
          (putnam-2024-a2-poly-multiply
           term normalized-divisor zero add mul)
          zero
          add
          neg)
         normalized-divisor
         (putnam-2024-a2-poly-add
          normalized-quotient term zero add)
         zero
         add
         mul
         neg
         inv
         (- steps 1))))))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-poly-divmod
    (dividend divisor zero add mul neg inv)
  (putnam-2024-a2-poly-divmod-steps
   dividend
   divisor
   (list zero)
   zero
   add
   mul
   neg
   inv
   (+ 1
      (len
       (putnam-2024-a2-poly-normalize
        dividend zero)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-a2-pointwise-identity-p
    (carrier add mul neg evaluate polynomial quotient)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (apply$ carrier (list x))
     (let* ((p-of-x
             (apply$ evaluate (list polynomial x)))
            (p-of-p-of-x
             (apply$ evaluate (list polynomial p-of-x)))
            (q-of-x
             (apply$ evaluate (list quotient x)))
            (p-minus-x
             (apply$
              add
              (list p-of-x (apply$ neg (list x)))))
            (left
             (apply$
              add
              (list p-of-p-of-x (apply$ neg (list x)))))
            (right
             (apply$
              mul
              (list
               (apply$ mul (list p-minus-x p-minus-x))
               q-of-x))))
       (equal left right)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-a2-q-exists-p
    (carrier zero add mul neg evaluate polynomial)
  (exists (quotient)
    (and
     (putnam-2024-a2-polynomial-p quotient carrier zero)
     (putnam-2024-a2-pointwise-identity-p
      carrier add mul neg evaluate polynomial quotient))))

(defun putnam-2024-a2-solution-p
    (polynomial one neg)
  (and
   (equal (len polynomial) 2)
   (or
    (equal (cadr polynomial) one)
    (equal
     (cadr polynomial)
     (apply$ neg (list one))))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2024-a2-statement
    (carrier zero one add mul neg inv lt square-root odd-root
             evaluate polynomial)
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2024-a2-real-closed-field-p
     carrier zero one add mul neg inv lt square-root odd-root
     evaluate)
    (putnam-2024-a2-polynomial-p
     polynomial carrier zero))
   (iff
    (putnam-2024-a2-q-exists-p
     carrier zero add mul neg evaluate polynomial)
    (putnam-2024-a2-solution-p
     polynomial one neg))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2024_a2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2024_a2): the real polynomials satisfying the
-- given composition and divisibility identity are exactly the affine
-- polynomials with slope 1 or -1. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2024A2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

Polynomial : Set -> Set
Polynomial R =
  List R

coefficient :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Nat ->
  R
coefficient reals [] n =
  zeroR reals
coefficient reals (c ∷ coefficients) zero =
  c
coefficient reals (c ∷ coefficients) (suc n) =
  coefficient reals coefficients n

PolynomialEqual :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Set
PolynomialEqual reals p q =
  (n : Nat) ->
  coefficient reals p n == coefficient reals q n

evaluate :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  R ->
  R
evaluate reals [] x =
  zeroR reals
evaluate reals (c ∷ coefficients) x =
  add reals c
    (multiply reals x (evaluate reals coefficients x))

SatisfiesIdentity :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Set
SatisfiesIdentity {R} reals p =
  Exists (Polynomial R)
    (\ q ->
      (x : R) ->
      subtract reals
        (evaluate reals p (evaluate reals p x))
        x
      ==
      multiply reals
        (square reals
          (subtract reals (evaluate reals p x) x))
        (evaluate reals q x))

AffineWithUnitIntegerSlope :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Polynomial R ->
  Set
AffineWithUnitIntegerSlope {R} reals p =
  Exists R
    (\ constant ->
      PolynomialEqual reals p
        (constant ∷ oneR reals ∷ [])
      or
      PolynomialEqual reals p
        (constant ∷ negate reals (oneR reals) ∷ []))

putnam-2024-a2 : Set1
putnam-2024-a2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (p : Polynomial R) ->
  Iff
    (SatisfiesIdentity reals p)
    (AffineWithUnitIntegerSlope reals p)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a2:
  the real polynomials p for which p(p(x)) - x is a polynomial multiple of
  (p(x) - x)^2 are exactly the affine polynomials with slope 1 or -1.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open listTheory realTheory polyTheory;

val putnam_2024_a2 =
  ``!p : real list.
      ((?q : real list.
          !x : real.
            poly p (poly p x) - x =
            (poly p x - x) pow 2 * poly q x)
       <=>
       (?a : real.
          (!x : real. poly p x = x + a) \/
          (!x : real. poly p x = -x + a)))``;

$(

  putnam_2024_a2 (putnambench__metamath__putnam_2024_a2): the real
  polynomials p for which p(p(x)) - x is (p(x) - x)^2 times a real
  polynomial are exactly the affine polynomials with slope 1 or -1.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) is set.mm's ring of all finite-support
  univariate real polynomials, and eval1 is ordinary polynomial evaluation.
  The left restricted class preserves the internally existential polynomial
  Q and the universal real variable x from the source statement.

  On the right, algSc embeds a real number as a constant polynomial.
  Thus X + a and a - X are exactly the source solution family
  s X + a for integer units s, since the only integer units are 1 and -1.
  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this
  database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d P Q a x $.

  putnambench-putnam-2024-a2 $a |-
    {
      P e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
      |
      E. Q e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
        A. x e. RR
          (
            (
              (
                ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` P )
                `
                (
                  ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` P )
                  `
                  x
                )
              )
              -
              x
            )
            =
            (
              (
                (
                  ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` P )
                  `
                  x
                )
                -
                x
              )
              ^
              2
            )
            x.
            (
              ( ( eval1 ` RRfld ) ` Q )
              `
              x
            )
          )
    }
    =
    {
      P e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
      |
      E. a e. RR
        (
          P
          =
          (
            ( var1 ` RRfld )
            ( +g ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
            ( ( algSc ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) ) ` a )
          )
          \/
          P
          =
          (
            ( ( algSc ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) ) ` a )
            ( -g ` ( Poly1 ` RRfld ) )
            ( var1 ` RRfld )
          )
        )
    }
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2024_a2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a2:
% the real polynomials satisfying the stated composition factorization are
% exactly the affine polynomials with integer-unit slope. This file contains
% no proof.

putnam_2024_a2: THEORY
BEGIN
  coefficient_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  support_bounded(
      coefficients: coefficient_sequence,
      bound: nat): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      bound < index IMPLIES coefficients(index) = 0

  is_polynomial(coefficients: coefficient_sequence): bool =
    EXISTS (bound: nat):
      support_bounded(coefficients, bound)

  polynomial_bound(
      coefficients: coefficient_sequence): nat =
    IF is_polynomial(coefficients) THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (bound: nat):
          support_bounded(coefficients, bound))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  polynomial_partial_value(
      coefficients: coefficient_sequence,
      x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        polynomial_partial_value(
          coefficients, x, count - 1)
          + coefficients(index) * x ^ index
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  polynomial_value(
      coefficients: coefficient_sequence,
      x: real): real =
    polynomial_partial_value(
      coefficients,
      x,
      polynomial_bound(coefficients) + 1)

  has_composition_factorization(
      p: coefficient_sequence): bool =
    EXISTS (q: coefficient_sequence):
      is_polynomial(q)
        AND FORALL (x: real):
          polynomial_value(
            p,
            polynomial_value(p, x)) - x
          =
          (polynomial_value(p, x) - x) ^ 2
            * polynomial_value(q, x)

  integer_unit(s: int): bool =
    s = 1 OR s = -1

  affine_with_integer_unit_slope(
      p: coefficient_sequence): bool =
    EXISTS (a: real), (s: int):
      integer_unit(s)
        AND FORALL (index: nat):
          p(index)
            = IF index = 0 THEN
                a
              ELSIF index = 1 THEN
                (s :: real)
              ELSE
                0
              ENDIF

  putnam_2024_a2_statement: bool =
    FORALL (p: coefficient_sequence):
      is_polynomial(p)
        IMPLIES
          (has_composition_factorization(p)
            IFF affine_with_integer_unit_slope(p))
END putnam_2024_a2

import Mathlib

noncomputable abbrev putnam_2024_a3_solution : Prop := sorry
--True
/--
Let $S$ be the set of bijections $$T : \{1, 2, 3\} \times \{1, 2, ..., 2024\} \to \{1, 2, ..., 6072\}$$
such that $T(1, j) < T(2, j) < T(3, j)$ for all $j \in \{1, 2, ..., 2024\}$ and
$T(i, j) < T(i, j + 1)$ for all $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ and $j \in \{1, 2, ..., 2023\}$.
Do there exist $a, c$ in $\{1, 2, 3\}$ and $b$ and $d$ in $\{1, 2, ..., 2024\}$ such that
the fraction of elements $T$ in $S$ for which $T(a, b) < T(c, d)$ is at least $1/3$ and at most $2/3$?
-/
theorem putnam_2024_a3
    (S : Set (ℕ × ℕ → ℕ))
    (hS : S = {T | Set.BijOn T (Finset.Icc 1 3 ×ˢ Finset.Icc 1 2024) (Finset.Icc 1 6072) ∧
      (∀ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 2024, StrictMonoOn (fun i => T (i, j)) (Set.Icc 1 3)) ∧

  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2024_a3): existence of two grid positions
  for which between one third and two thirds of the admissible increasing
  bijections order their entries in the specified direction. This file
  contains no proof.

let statement =
  `let rows = 1..3 in
   let columns = 1..2024 in
   let grid = {(i,j) | i IN rows /\ j IN columns} in
   let values = 1..6072 in
   let admissible =
     \(t:num#num->num).
       BIJ t grid values /\
       (!j:num.
          j IN columns

                i IN rows /\ k IN rows /\ i < k
                ==> t (i,j) < t (k,j)) /\
       (!i:num.
          i IN rows
          ==> !j k:num.
                j IN columns /\ k IN columns /\ j < k
                ==> t (i,j) < t (i,k)) /\
       (!p:num#num. ~(p IN grid) ==> t p = 0) in
   let S = {t:num#num->num | admissible t} in
   ?a b c d:num.
     a IN rows /\
     b IN columns /\
     c IN rows /\
     d IN columns /\
     &1 / &3 <=
       &(CARD {t:num#num->num | t IN S /\ t (a,b) < t (c,d)}) /
       &(CARD S) /\
     &(CARD {t:num#num->num | t IN S /\ t (a,b) < t (c,d)}) /
       &(CARD S) <=

;; among the row- and column-strict bijective fillings of a 3 by 2024 grid
;; by 1 through 6072, two positions have comparison frequency in [1/3,2/3].
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; Reading a filling in row-major order identifies it with one permutation of
;; 1,...,6072. Conversely, zero-extending such a list outside the grid gives
;; exactly one total source function. Thus filtering all permutations by the
;; adjacent row and column inequalities gives a set in bijection with S.
;; Adjacent strict inequalities are equivalent to StrictMonoOn on each finite
;; interval, and the permutation generator has no duplicate outputs.

(defun putnam-2024-a3-values (count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons count
          (putnam-2024-a3-values (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-prefix-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (cons (cons item (car lists))
          (putnam-2024-a3-prefix-each item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-insert-everywhere (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list (list item))
    (cons (cons item list)
          (putnam-2024-a3-prefix-each
           (car list)
           (putnam-2024-a3-insert-everywhere
            item (cdr list))))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-insert-into-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-2024-a3-insert-everywhere item (car lists))
     (putnam-2024-a3-insert-into-each
      item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-permutations (list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list nil)
    (putnam-2024-a3-insert-into-each
     (car list)
     (putnam-2024-a3-permutations (cdr list)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-row-increasing-p
    (table offset remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (or (zp remaining)
          (equal remaining 1))
      t
    (and
     (< (nth offset table)
        (nth (+ offset 1) table))
     (putnam-2024-a3-row-increasing-p
      table (+ offset 1) (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-rows-increasing-p
    (table row remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (and
     (putnam-2024-a3-row-increasing-p
      table (* row 2024) 2024)
     (putnam-2024-a3-rows-increasing-p
      table (+ row 1) (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-column-increasing-p
    (table column row remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (or (zp remaining)
          (equal remaining 1))
      t
    (let ((offset (+ (* row 2024) column)))
      (and
       (< (nth offset table)
          (nth (+ offset 2024) table))
       (putnam-2024-a3-column-increasing-p
        table column (+ row 1) (- remaining 1))))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-columns-increasing-p
    (table column remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      t
    (and
     (putnam-2024-a3-column-increasing-p
      table column 0 3)
     (putnam-2024-a3-columns-increasing-p
      table (+ column 1) (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-table-p (table)
  (and
   (putnam-2024-a3-rows-increasing-p table 0 3)
   (putnam-2024-a3-columns-increasing-p table 0 2024)))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-filter-tables (permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      nil
    (if (putnam-2024-a3-table-p (car permutations))
        (cons (car permutations)
              (putnam-2024-a3-filter-tables
               (cdr permutations)))
      (putnam-2024-a3-filter-tables
       (cdr permutations)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-entry (table row column)
  (nth (+ (* (- row 1) 2024)
          (- column 1))
       table))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-qualifying-count
    (tables a b c d)
  (if (endp tables)
      0
    (+ (if (< (putnam-2024-a3-entry
               (car tables) a b)
              (putnam-2024-a3-entry
               (car tables) c d))
           1
         0)
       (putnam-2024-a3-qualifying-count
        (cdr tables) a b c d))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-balanced-p
    (tables total a b c d)
  (let ((fraction
         (/ (putnam-2024-a3-qualifying-count
             tables a b c d)
            total)))
    (and
     (<= (/ 1 3) fraction)
     (<= fraction (/ 2 3)))))

;; The following four finite searches are the source's internal existential
;; quantifiers over a,c in 1..3 and b,d in 1..2024.

(defun putnam-2024-a3-d-exists-p
    (tables total a b c d remaining)

  (if (zp remaining)
      nil
    (or
     (putnam-2024-a3-balanced-p
      tables total a b c d)
     (putnam-2024-a3-d-exists-p
      tables total a b c (+ d 1) (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-c-exists-p
    (tables total a b c remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      nil
    (or
     (putnam-2024-a3-d-exists-p
      tables total a b c 1 2024)
     (putnam-2024-a3-c-exists-p
      tables total a b (+ c 1) (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-b-exists-p
    (tables total a b remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      nil
    (or
     (putnam-2024-a3-c-exists-p
      tables total a b 1 3)
     (putnam-2024-a3-b-exists-p
      tables total a (+ b 1) (- remaining 1)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a3-a-exists-p
    (tables total a remaining)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix remaining)))
  (if (zp remaining)
      nil
    (or
     (putnam-2024-a3-b-exists-p
      tables total a 1 2024)
     (putnam-2024-a3-a-exists-p
      tables total (+ a 1) (- remaining 1)))))

;; The source answer is True, so its concluding IFF is definitionally the
;; proposition below after replacing S by the equal set specified by hS.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2024-a3-statement ()
  (let* ((tables
          (putnam-2024-a3-filter-tables
           (putnam-2024-a3-permutations
            (putnam-2024-a3-values 6072))))
         (total (len tables)))
    (putnam-2024-a3-a-exists-p tables total 1 3)))

title: putnam_2024_a3
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2024_a3): among increasing bijective 3 by 2024
-- tableaux, some pair of positions is ordered in between one third and two
-- thirds of all tableaux. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2024A3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _*_)

infix 4 _<F_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

data _<F_ : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin n -> Set where
  fzero<fsuc :
    {n : Nat} {j : Fin n} ->
    fzero <F fsuc j
  fsuc<fsuc :
    {n : Nat} {i j : Fin n} ->
    i <F j ->
    fsuc i <F fsuc j

Row : Set
Row =
  Fin 3

Column : Set
Column =
  Fin 2024

Value : Set
Value =
  Fin 6072

Grid : Set
Grid =
  Row -> Column -> Value

record Position : Set where
  constructor position
  field
    row    : Row
    column : Column

open Position

record IsBijection (tableau : Grid) : Set where
  field
    inverse : Value -> Position
    inverse-entry-row :
      (i : Row) ->
      (j : Column) ->
      row (inverse (tableau i j)) == i
    inverse-entry-column :
      (i : Row) ->
      (j : Column) ->
      column (inverse (tableau i j)) == j
    entry-inverse :
      (value : Value) ->
      tableau
        (row (inverse value))
        (column (inverse value)) == value

record Admissible (tableau : Grid) : Set where
  field
    bijective :
      IsBijection tableau
    columns-strictly-increasing :
      (j : Column) ->
      (i k : Row) ->
      i <F k ->
      tableau i j <F tableau k j
    rows-strictly-increasing :
      (i : Row) ->
      (j l : Column) ->
      j <F l ->
      tableau i j <F tableau i l

GridEqual : Grid -> Grid -> Set
GridEqual left right =
  (i : Row) ->
  (j : Column) ->
  left i j == right i j

record HasGridCardinality
  (member : Grid -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      Grid
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (tableau : Grid) ->
      member tableau ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index ->
          GridEqual tableau (enumerate index))
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      GridEqual
        (enumerate left-index)
        (enumerate right-index) ->
      left-index == right-index

Favorable :
  Row ->
  Column ->
  Row ->
  Column ->
  Grid ->
  Set
Favorable a b c d tableau =
  Admissible tableau
  and
  tableau a b <F tableau c d

putnam-2024-a3 : Set
putnam-2024-a3 =
  Exists Row
    (\ a ->
      Exists Column
        (\ b ->
          Exists Row
            (\ c ->
              Exists Column
                (\ d ->
                  Exists Nat
                    (\ total-predecessor ->
                      HasGridCardinality
                        Admissible
                        (suc total-predecessor)
                      and
                      Exists Nat
                        (\ favorable-count ->
                          HasGridCardinality
                            (Favorable a b c d)
                            favorable-count
                          and
                          ((suc total-predecessor <=N
                              3 * favorable-count)
                            and
                            (3 * favorable-count <=N
                              2 * suc total-predecessor))))))))

  existence of two positions in a 3 by 2024 increasing bijective array for
  which the comparison holds in between one third and two thirds of all such
  arrays. This file contains no proof.

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory realTheory;

val putnam_2024_a3 =
  ``let rows = {i : num | 1 <= i /\ i <= 3};
        cols = {j : num | 1 <= j /\ j <= 2024};
        values = {n : num | 1 <= n /\ n <= 6072};
        grid = rows CROSS cols;
        S =
          {T : (num # num) -> num |
             BIJ T grid values /\
             (!j : num.
                j IN cols
                ==>
                !i k : num.
                  i IN rows /\ k IN rows /\ i < k

                i IN rows
                ==>
                !j k : num.
                  j IN cols /\ k IN cols /\ j < k
                  ==>
                  T (i,j) < T (i,k)) /\
             (!x : num # num. x NOTIN grid ==> T x = 0)}
    in
      ?a b c d : num.

                     T IN S /\ T (a,b) < T (c,d)}) : real) /
          (&(CARD S) : real) /\
        (&(CARD {T : (num # num) -> num |

  thirds, inclusive. This file contains no proof.

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P24A3Rows, P24A3Cols, P24A3Cells, and P24A3Values are respectively
  1 ... 3, 1 ... 2024, their Cartesian product, and 1 ... 6072.
  P24A3Tableaux is the finite set of bijections from the cells to the
  values that are strictly increasing in each row and each column.

  The Lean source instead uses total maps on NN0 X. NN0 that vanish outside
  P24A3Cells. Restriction to P24A3Cells and extension by zero are inverse
  bijections between that set and P24A3Tableaux, and they preserve every
  displayed cell comparison. Thus the two finite cardinalities and their
  quotient are unchanged.

  Pairwise strict increase is exactly StrictMonoOn on each finite interval.
  The four cell coordinates remain internally existentially quantified, and
  the closed interval retains both source probability bounds. The annotated
  solution is True, so the source biconditional is equivalent to the final
  existence assertion. Every declaration is an unproved $a statement
  encoding; this database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c P24A3Rows P24A3Cols P24A3Cells P24A3Values P24A3Tableaux $.

p24a3-rows-syntax $a class P24A3Rows $.
p24a3-cols-syntax $a class P24A3Cols $.
p24a3-cells-syntax $a class P24A3Cells $.
p24a3-values-syntax $a class P24A3Values $.
p24a3-tableaux-syntax $a class P24A3Tableaux $.

p24a3-cols-definition $a |-
  P24A3Cols = ( 1 ... ( ; ; ; 2 0 2 4 ) ) $.

p24a3-cells-definition $a |-
  P24A3Cells = ( P24A3Rows X. P24A3Cols ) $.

p24a3-values-definition $a |-
  P24A3Values = ( 1 ... ( ; ; ; 6 0 7 2 ) ) $.

${
  $d T i j k l $.

  p24a3-tableaux-definition $a |- P24A3Tableaux =
    {
      T e. ( P24A3Values ^m P24A3Cells ) |
      (
        T : P24A3Cells -1-1-onto-> P24A3Values
        /\
        (
          A. j e. P24A3Cols
            A. i e. P24A3Rows
              A. k e. P24A3Rows
                (
                  i < k
                  ->
                  ( T ` <. i , j >. ) < ( T ` <. k , j >. )
                )
          /\
          A. i e. P24A3Rows
            A. j e. P24A3Cols
              A. l e. P24A3Cols
                (
                  j < l
                  ->
                  ( T ` <. i , j >. ) < ( T ` <. i , l >. )
                )
        )
      )
    } $.
$}

${
  $d T a b c d $.

  putnambench-putnam-2024-a3 $a |-
    E. a e. P24A3Rows
      E. b e. P24A3Cols
        E. c e. P24A3Rows
          E. d e. P24A3Cols
            (

                  `

                    T e. P24A3Tableaux |
                    ( T ` <. a , b >. ) < ( T ` <. c , d >. )
                  }
                )
                /
                ( # ` P24A3Tableaux )
              )
              e.
              ( ( 1 / 3 ) [,] ( 2 / 3 ) )

  $.
$}

title: putnam_2024_a3
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a3:
% among the increasing bijective 3-by-2024 tableaux with entries 1 through
% 6072, some pair of cells is ordered in between one third and two thirds of
% the tableaux. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2024_a3: THEORY
BEGIN
  row: TYPE = below(3)
  column: TYPE = below(2024)
  entry: TYPE = {value: nat | 1 <= value AND value <= 6072}
  tableau: TYPE = [row, column -> entry]

  IMPORTING finite_sets[tableau]

  injective_tableau(T: tableau): bool =
    FORALL (r_1, r_2: row), (c_1, c_2: column):
      T(r_1, c_1) = T(r_2, c_2)
        IMPLIES r_1 = r_2 AND c_1 = c_2

  surjective_tableau(T: tableau): bool =
    FORALL (value: entry):
      EXISTS (r: row), (c: column):
        T(r, c) = value

  increasing_in_rows(T: tableau): bool =
    FORALL (r_1, r_2: row), (c: column):
      r_1 < r_2 IMPLIES T(r_1, c) < T(r_2, c)

  increasing_in_columns(T: tableau): bool =
    FORALL (r: row), (c_1, c_2: column):
      c_1 < c_2 IMPLIES T(r, c_1) < T(r, c_2)

  admissible(T: tableau): bool =
    injective_tableau(T)
      AND surjective_tableau(T)
      AND increasing_in_rows(T)
      AND increasing_in_columns(T)

  is_admissible_family(S: finite_set[tableau]): bool =
    FORALL (T: tableau):
      S(T) IFF admissible(T)

  is_favorable_family(
      favorable, S: finite_set[tableau],
      a, c: row,
      b, d: column): bool =
    FORALL (T: tableau):
      favorable(T) IFF
        S(T) AND T(a, b) < T(c, d)

  fraction_between_one_third_and_two_thirds(
      favorable, S: finite_set[tableau]): bool =
    card(S) > 0
      AND card(S) <= 3 * card(favorable)
      AND 3 * card(favorable) <= 2 * card(S)

  putnam_2024_a3_statement: bool =
    EXISTS (S: finite_set[tableau]):
      is_admissible_family(S)
        AND EXISTS (a, c: row), (b, d: column),
                   (favorable: finite_set[tableau]):
          is_favorable_family(favorable, S, a, c, b, d)
            AND fraction_between_one_third_and_two_thirds(
              favorable, S)

END putnam_2024_a3

title: putnam_2024_a4
content:
import Mathlib

noncomputable abbrev putnam_2024_a4_solution : Set ℕ := sorry
--{7}
/--
Find all primes $p > 5$ for which there exists an integer $a$ and an integer $r$ satisfying $1 \le r \le p - 1$ with the following property:
the sequence $1, a, a^2, ..., a^{p-5}$ can be rearranged to form a sequence $b_0, ..., b_{p-5}$ such that $b_n - b_{n-1} - r$ is divisible by $p$ for $1 \le n \le p - 5$.
-/
theorem putnam_2024_a4 :
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ 5 < p ∧ ∃ a r : ℤ, 1 ≤ r ∧ r ≤ p - 1 ∧
      ∃ e : ℕ → ℕ, Set.BijOn e (Set.Icc 0 (p - 5 : ℕ)) (Set.Icc 0 (p - 5 : ℕ)) ∧
        ∀ n, 1 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ (p - 5 : ℕ) →
          (p : ℤ) ∣ a ^ (e n : ℕ) - a ^ (e (n - 1) : ℕ) - r} =
    putnam_2024_a4_solution :=
  sorry

title: putnam_2024_a4
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a4
   (putnambench__rocq__putnam_2024_a4): classification of the primes for which
   powers of an integer can be rearranged with a fixed nonzero modular
   difference. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat ZArith ZArith.Znumtheory.

Definition putnam_2024_a4_in_interval
    (upper n : nat) : Prop :=
  (n <= upper)%nat.

Definition putnam_2024_a4_bij_on_interval
    (e : nat -> nat) (upper : nat) : Prop :=
  (forall n : nat,
      putnam_2024_a4_in_interval upper n ->
      putnam_2024_a4_in_interval upper (e n)) /\
  (forall x y : nat,
      putnam_2024_a4_in_interval upper x ->
      putnam_2024_a4_in_interval upper y ->
      e x = e y ->
      x = y) /\
  (forall y : nat,
      putnam_2024_a4_in_interval upper y ->
      exists x : nat,
        putnam_2024_a4_in_interval upper x /\
        e x = y).

Definition putnam_2024_a4_qualifies (p : nat) : Prop :=
  Znumtheory.prime (Z.of_nat p) /\
  (5 < p)%nat /\
  exists a r : Z,
    (1 <= r)%Z /\
    (r <= Z.of_nat (p - 1))%Z /\
    exists e : nat -> nat,
      putnam_2024_a4_bij_on_interval e (p - 5) /\
      forall n : nat,
        (1 <= n)%nat /\ (n <= p - 5)%nat ->
        Z.divide
          (Z.of_nat p)
          (Z.pow a (Z.of_nat (e n)) -
           Z.pow a (Z.of_nat (e ((n - 1)%nat))) - r).

Definition putnam_2024_a4_solution (p : nat) : Prop :=
  p = 7%nat.

Theorem putnam_2024_a4 :
  forall p : nat,
    putnam_2024_a4_qualifies p <->
    putnam_2024_a4_solution p.
Admitted.

  (putnambench__isabelle__putnam_2024_a4): the primes greater than 5 admitting
  an integer geometric-power sequence whose terms can be reordered so that
  consecutive differences are constant modulo the prime. The solution set is
  {7}. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory putnam_2024_a4
  imports Complex_Main
begin

definition putnam_2024_a4_solution :: "nat set" where
  "putnam_2024_a4_solution = {7}"

theorem putnam_2024_a4:

      prime p \<and>
      5 < p \<and>
      (\<exists>a r :: int.
        1 \<le> r \<and>
        r \<le> int (p - 1) \<and>
        (\<exists>e :: nat \<Rightarrow> nat.

          (\<forall>n :: nat.

title: putnam_2024_a4
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a4:
;; the primes p > 5 admitting a rearrangement of 1,a,...,a^(p-5) whose
;; consecutive differences are all congruent to one nonzero residue modulo p
;; are exactly p = 7. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-2024-a4-no-divisor-from-p (n d)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix (- n d))))
  (if (and (natp n)
           (natp d)
           (<= 2 d)
           (< d n))
      (and (not (equal (mod n d) 0))
           (putnam-2024-a4-no-divisor-from-p n (+ d 1)))
    t))

(defun putnam-2024-a4-primep (p)
  (and (natp p)
       (< 1 p)
       (putnam-2024-a4-no-divisor-from-p p 2)))

;; For BASE > 0, the first COUNT base-BASE digits of CODE form a list.
;; When COUNT = BASE and CODE ranges below BASE^BASE, these lists enumerate
;; every function from {0,...,BASE-1} to itself.
(defun putnam-2024-a4-decode-exponents (code base count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons (mod code base)
          (putnam-2024-a4-decode-exponents
           (floor code base)
           base
           (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2024-a4-permutation-p (exponents maximum)
  (if (endp exponents)
      (equal exponents nil)
    (and (natp (car exponents))
         (<= (car exponents) maximum)
         (not (member-equal (car exponents) (cdr exponents)))
         (putnam-2024-a4-permutation-p
          (cdr exponents)
          maximum))))

(defun putnam-2024-a4-progression-p (p a r exponents)
  (if (and (consp exponents)
           (consp (cdr exponents)))
      (and
       (equal
        (mod
         (- (- (expt a (cadr exponents))
               (expt a (car exponents)))
            r)
         p)
        0)
       (putnam-2024-a4-progression-p
        p a r (cdr exponents)))
    t))

(defun putnam-2024-a4-rearrangement-code-p (p a r code)
  (let* ((maximum (- p 5))
         (base (+ maximum 1))
         (exponents
          (putnam-2024-a4-decode-exponents
           code base base)))
    (and
     (putnam-2024-a4-permutation-p exponents maximum)
     (putnam-2024-a4-progression-p p a r exponents))))

;; This finite search keeps the existentially quantified bijection internal.
;; A length-(p-4) duplicate-free list in 0..p-5 is exactly the restriction of
;; a source bijection e to that interval.
(defun putnam-2024-a4-rearrangement-through-p (p a r code)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix code)))
  (if (natp code)
      (or
       (putnam-2024-a4-rearrangement-code-p p a r code)
       (and
        (not (zp code))
        (putnam-2024-a4-rearrangement-through-p
         p a r (- code 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2024-a4-a-r-code-p (p code)
  (let* ((r-count (- p 1))
         (a (floor code r-count))
         (r (+ 1 (mod code r-count)))
         (base (- p 4)))
    (putnam-2024-a4-rearrangement-through-p
     p a r (- (expt base base) 1))))

;; Divisibility of differences of powers modulo positive p depends only on
;; a modulo p. Thus searching a = 0,...,p-1 is equivalent to the source
;; existential over all integers a; r already lies in 1,...,p-1.
(defun putnam-2024-a4-a-r-through-p (p code)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix code)))
  (if (natp code)
      (or
       (putnam-2024-a4-a-r-code-p p code)
       (and
        (not (zp code))
        (putnam-2024-a4-a-r-through-p p (- code 1))))
    nil))

(defun putnam-2024-a4-qualifying-prime-p (p)
  (and
   (putnam-2024-a4-primep p)
   (< 5 p)
   (putnam-2024-a4-a-r-through-p
    p (- (* p (- p 1)) 1))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2024-a4-statement (p)
  (implies
   (natp p)
   (equal
    (putnam-2024-a4-qualifying-prime-p p)
    (equal p 7))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2024_a4
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_a4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2024_a4): classification of primes greater than
-- 5 whose powers can be rearranged so every consecutive difference is a fixed
-- positive residue modulo the prime; the unique prime is 7. This file contains
-- no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_ _<N_ _<=Z_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_
infix 1 _iff_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record _iff_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

data _<=Z_ : Int -> Int -> Set where
  negative<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    negsuc m <=Z pos n
  positive<=positive :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    m <=N n ->
    pos m <=Z pos n
  negative<=negative :
    {m n : Nat} ->
    n <=N m ->
    negsuc m <=Z negsuc n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

fiveN : Nat
fiveN =
  suc (suc (suc (suc (suc zero))))

sevenN : Nat
sevenN =
  suc (suc fiveN)

oneZ : Int
oneZ =
  pos oneN

record DividesNat (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  constructor divides-nat-with
  field
    quotient : Nat
    equation : divisor * quotient == dividend

Prime : Nat -> Set
Prime p =
  twoN <=N p
  and
  ((divisor : Nat) ->
    DividesNat divisor p ->
    divisor == oneN or divisor == p)

negativeNat : Nat -> Int
negativeNat zero =
  pos zero
negativeNat (suc n) =
  negsuc n

differenceNat : Nat -> Nat -> Int
differenceNat zero zero =
  pos zero
differenceNat (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
differenceNat zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
differenceNat (suc m) (suc n) =
  differenceNat m n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos zero) =
  pos zero
negateInt (pos (suc n)) =
  negsuc n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  differenceNat m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  differenceNat n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negativeNat (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negativeNat (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

subtractInt : Int -> Int -> Int
subtractInt x y =
  addInt x (negateInt y)

powerInt : Int -> Nat -> Int
powerInt x zero =
  oneZ
powerInt x (suc exponent) =
  multiplyInt x (powerInt x exponent)

record DividesInt (divisor dividend : Int) : Set where
  constructor divides-int-with
  field
    quotient : Int
    equation : multiplyInt divisor quotient == dividend

Predicate : Set -> Set1
Predicate A =
  A -> Set

ClosedInterval : Nat -> Nat -> Predicate Nat
ClosedInterval lower upper n =
  lower <=N n and n <=N upper

record BijOn
  {A B : Set}
  (function : A -> B)
  (domain : Predicate A)
  (codomain : Predicate B) :
  Set where

  field
    maps-into :
      (x : A) ->
      domain x ->
      codomain (function x)

    injective-on :
      (x y : A) ->
      domain x ->
      domain y ->
      function x == function y ->
      x == y

    surjective-on :
      (y : B) ->
      codomain y ->
      Exists A
        (\ x ->
          domain x
          and
          function x == y)

ExponentUpperBound : Nat -> Nat
ExponentUpperBound p =
  p - fiveN

RearrangesExponentInterval :
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Set
RearrangesExponentInterval p rearrangement =
  BijOn
    rearrangement
    (ClosedInterval zero (ExponentUpperBound p))
    (ClosedInterval zero (ExponentUpperBound p))

ConsecutiveDifferenceCondition :
  Nat ->
  Int ->
  Int ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Set
ConsecutiveDifferenceCondition p a r rearrangement =
  (n : Nat) ->
  (oneN <=N n and n <=N ExponentUpperBound p) ->
  DividesInt
    (pos p)
    (subtractInt
      (subtractInt
        (powerInt a (rearrangement n))
        (powerInt a (rearrangement (n - oneN))))
      r)

Qualifies : Nat -> Set
Qualifies p =
  Prime p
  and
  fiveN <N p
  and
  Exists Int
    (\ a ->
      Exists Int
        (\ r ->
          oneZ <=Z r
          and
          r <=Z pos (p - oneN)
          and
          Exists (Nat -> Nat)
            (\ rearrangement ->
              RearrangesExponentInterval p rearrangement
              and
              ConsecutiveDifferenceCondition
                p
                a
                r
                rearrangement)))

putnam-2024-a4-solution : Nat -> Set
putnam-2024-a4-solution p =
  p == sevenN

putnam-2024-a4 : Set
putnam-2024-a4 =
  (p : Nat) ->
  Qualifies p iff putnam-2024-a4-solution p

  the primes greater than 5 whose powers admit a rearrangement with a fixed
  positive consecutive difference modulo the prime are exactly the prime 7.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory pred_setTheory primeTheory;

val putnam_2024_a4 =
  ``{p : num |
       prime p /\
       5 < p /\
       ?a r : int.
         1 <= r /\

title: putnam_2024_a4
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2024_a4: the primes greater than five admitting an integer
  geometric-power sequence whose rearrangement has a fixed nonzero
  consecutive difference modulo the prime form exactly the singleton
  set containing seven. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  Prime is set.mm's class of positive natural primes, ZZ is the class of
  integers, and || is integer divisibility. For p greater than five, the
  inclusive interval 0 ... (p - 5) indexes exactly the powers
  1, a, ..., a^(p-5).

  The internally existential e is a bijection of this interval, so its
  values give precisely a rearrangement of those powers. This is equivalent
  to the Lean total function with BijOn on the interval: restriction gives
  the displayed bijection, while any displayed finite bijection can be
  extended arbitrarily to a total function on the natural numbers. Every
  argument of e used below lies in the interval.

  The bounds on r and the divisibility condition retain the integer
  witnesses and every consecutive index from 1 through p - 5. The final
  biconditional is the pointwise form of equality with the annotated
  solution set {7}. The final declaration is a single unproved $a corpus
  statement; this database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d a e n p r $.

  putnambench-putnam-2024-a4 $a |- A. p e. NN
    (
      (
        (
          p e. Prime
          /\
          5 < p
        )
        /\
        E. a e. ZZ
          E. r e. ZZ
            (
              (
                1 <_ r
                /\
                r <_ ( p - 1 )
              )
              /\
              E. e
                (
                  e
                  :
                  ( 0 ... ( p - 5 ) )
                  -1-1-onto->
                  ( 0 ... ( p - 5 ) )
                  /\
                  A. n e. ( 1 ... ( p - 5 ) )
                    p
                    ||
                    (
                      (
                        ( a ^ ( e ` n ) )
                        -
                        ( a ^ ( e ` ( n - 1 ) ) )
                      )
                      -
                      r
                    )
                )
            )
      )
      <->
      p = 7
    )
  $.
$}

    XREAL_0, XXREAL_0, NAT_1, INT_1, INT_2, NEWTON, ABIAN, WSIERP_1,
    ABSVALUE, VALUED_0, VALUED_1, MEMBERED, FRAENKEL;
  requirements BOOLE, SUBSET, NUMERALS, ARITHM, REAL;
  definitions TARSKI;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for p being Nat holds
    ((p is prime & 5 < p &
      ex a,r being Integer,
         e being Function of NAT,NAT,
         D being Subset of NAT st
        1 <= r & r <= (p qua Integer) - 1 &
        D = {k where k is Element of NAT : k <= p -' 5} &
        (e | D) is one-to-one &
        rng (e | D) = D &
        (for n being Nat st 1 <= n & n <= p -' 5 holds
          ex i,j being Nat st
            i = e.n & j = e.(n -' 1) &
