 definitions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, FINSET_1;
 equalities PROB_1, RANDOM_2, PROB_4, RELAT_1, FINSEQ_1;
 expansions TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, RELAT_1, FINSEQ_1;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for Omega being non empty set,
      Sigma being SigmaField of Omega,
      P being Probability of Sigma,
      m,a being Function of [:NAT,NAT:],Funcs(Omega,REAL)
  st
    (for n,k being Nat holds
      ex mn,an being Function of Omega,REAL st
        mn = m.(n,k) & an = a.(n,k) &
        rng mn c= INT & rng an c= INT) &
    (for n,k being Nat st 0 < n holds
      ex mn being Function of Omega,REAL,
         mn0 being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma st
        mn = m.(n,k) &
        (C_Meas (P2M(P))).
          {omega where omega is Element of Omega :
            mn.omega <> mn0.omega}
          = 0 &
        (C_Meas (P2M(P))).
          {omega where omega is Element of Omega :
            not ex j being Nat st
              j in Seg n & mn.omega = (j qua Real)}
          = 0 &
        (for j being Nat st j in Seg n holds
          (C_Meas (P2M(P))).
            {omega where omega is Element of Omega :
              mn.omega = (j qua Real)}
            = 1 / (n qua Real))) &
    (for r being Nat,
         I being one-to-one FinSequence of [:NAT,NAT:],
         B being FinSequence of Borel_Sets,
         D being FinSequence of bool Omega,
         q being FinSequence of ExtREAL
      st 0 < r &
         len I = r & len B = r & len D = r & len q = r &
         (for j being Nat st j in Seg r holds
           D.j = (m.(I.j))"(B.j) &
           q.j = (C_Meas (P2M(P))).(D.j))
      holds
        (C_Meas (P2M(P))).(meet rng D) = Product q) &
    (for n being Nat st 0 < n holds
      for omega being Element of Omega holds
        (a.(n,0)).omega = 1) &
    (for n,k being Nat st 0 < n holds
      ex mn,ak,ak1 being Function of Omega,REAL st
        mn = m.(n,k) & ak = a.(n,k) & ak1 = a.(n,k+1) &
        (for omega being Element of Omega holds
          (mn.omega > ak.omega implies
            ak1.omega = ak.omega + 1) &
          (mn.omega = ak.omega implies
            ak1.omega = ak.omega) &
          (mn.omega < ak.omega implies
            ak1.omega = ak.omega - 1)))
  holds
    ex E being Real_Sequence st
      E.0 = 0 &
      (for n being Nat st 0 < n holds
        ex ann being Function of Omega,REAL st
          ex ann0 being Real-Valued-Random-Variable of Sigma st
            ann = a.(n,n) &
            (C_Meas (P2M(P))).
              {omega where omega is Element of Omega :
                ann.omega <> ann0.omega}
              = 0 &
            E.n = Integral(P2M(P),ann0) / (n qua Real)) &
      E is convergent &
      lim E = (1 - exp_R.(-2)) / 2
proof
end;
::$P+

title: putnam_2024_b4
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b4
% (putnambench__pvs__putnam_2024_b4): the normalized expected position of the
% independent uniform integer-driven walk converges to (1 - exp(-2))/2.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2024_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  sample_space: TYPE+

  event: TYPE = [sample_space -> bool]
  event_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> event]
  sigma_algebra: TYPE = [event -> bool]
  probability_measure: TYPE = [event -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]
  integer_set: TYPE = [int -> bool]
  integer_set_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> integer_set]
  integer_random_variable: TYPE = [sample_space -> int]
  random_array: TYPE = [nat, nat -> integer_random_variable]
  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  full_event: event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space): TRUE

  empty_event: event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space): FALSE

  event_complement(A: event): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      NOT A(omega)

  event_intersection(A, B: event): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      A(omega) AND B(omega)

  countable_union(events: event_sequence): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      EXISTS (index: nat): events(index)(omega)

  pairwise_disjoint(events: event_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (left_index, right_index: nat):
      left_index /= right_index IMPLIES
        FORALL (omega: sample_space):
          NOT (events(left_index)(omega)
            AND events(right_index)(omega))

  finite_sum(values: real_sequence, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      finite_sum(values, count - 1) + values(count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  converges_to(values: real_sequence, limit_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(values(index) - limit_value) < epsilon_value

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  is_sigma_algebra(Sigma: sigma_algebra): bool =
    Sigma(full_event)
      AND (FORALL (A: event):
        Sigma(A) IMPLIES Sigma(event_complement(A)))
      AND (FORALL (events: event_sequence):
        (FORALL (index: nat): Sigma(events(index)))
          IMPLIES Sigma(countable_union(events)))

  is_probability_measure(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra): bool =
    is_sigma_algebra(Sigma)
      AND M(empty_event) = 0
      AND M(full_event) = 1
      AND (FORALL (A: event):
        Sigma(A) IMPLIES 0 <= M(A))
      AND (FORALL (events: event_sequence):
        ((FORALL (index: nat): Sigma(events(index)))
          AND pairwise_disjoint(events))
        IMPLIES
          converges_to(
            LAMBDA (count: nat):
              finite_sum(
                LAMBDA (index: nat): M(events(index)),
                count),
            M(countable_union(events))))

  preimage_event(
      X: integer_random_variable,
      values: integer_set): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      values(X(omega))

  value_event(
      X: integer_random_variable,
      value: int): event =
    LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
      X(omega) = value

  measurable_integer_variable(
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: integer_random_variable): bool =
    FORALL (values: integer_set):
      Sigma(preimage_event(X, values))

  integer_interval_contains(n: nat, value: int): bool =
    1 <= value AND value <= (n :: int)

  uniform_integer_choice(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      n: nat,
      X: integer_random_variable): bool =
    measurable_integer_variable(Sigma, X)
      AND M(
        LAMBDA (omega: sample_space):
          integer_interval_contains(n, X(omega))) = 1
      AND (FORALL (value: int):
        M(value_event(X, value))
          = IF integer_interval_contains(n, value) THEN
              safe_div(1, n :: real)
            ELSE
              0
            ENDIF)

  distinct_index_pairs(
      rows, steps: natural_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (left_position, right_position: nat):
      (left_position < count
        AND right_position < count
        AND rows(left_position) = rows(right_position)
        AND steps(left_position) = steps(right_position))
      IMPLIES left_position = right_position

  finite_preimage_intersection(
      X: random_array,
      rows, steps: natural_sequence,
      values: integer_set_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE event =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      full_event
    ELSE
      event_intersection(
        finite_preimage_intersection(
          X, rows, steps, values, count - 1),
        preimage_event(
          X(rows(count - 1), steps(count - 1)),
          values(count - 1)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  finite_probability_product(
      M: probability_measure,
      X: random_array,
      rows, steps: natural_sequence,
      values: integer_set_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      finite_probability_product(
        M, X, rows, steps, values, count - 1)
        * M(preimage_event(
            X(rows(count - 1), steps(count - 1)),
            values(count - 1)))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  mutually_independent(
      M: probability_measure,
      Sigma: sigma_algebra,
      X: random_array): bool =
    (FORALL (row, step: nat):
      measurable_integer_variable(Sigma, X(row, step)))
      AND
    (FORALL
        (rows, steps: natural_sequence),
        (values: integer_set_sequence),
        (count: nat):
      distinct_index_pairs(rows, steps, count)
        IMPLIES
          M(finite_preimage_intersection(
            X, rows, steps, values, count))
            = finite_probability_product(
                M, X, rows, steps, values, count))

  integer_expectation_sum(
      M: probability_measure,
      X: integer_random_variable,
      bound, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1,
          value: int = (index :: int) - (bound :: int)
      IN
        integer_expectation_sum(M, X, bound, count - 1)
          + (value :: real) * M(value_event(X, value))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  bounded_integer_expectation(
      M: probability_measure,
      X: integer_random_variable,
      bound: nat): real =
    integer_expectation_sum(M, X, bound, 2 * bound + 1)

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  putnam_2024_b4_solution: real =
    safe_div(1 - real_exponential(-2), 2)

  normalized_expected_position(
      M: probability_measure,
      a: random_array,
      n: nat): real =
    safe_div(
      bounded_integer_expectation(M, a(n, n), n + 1),
      n :: real)

  putnam_2024_b4_statement: bool =
    FORALL
        (M: probability_measure),
        (Sigma: sigma_algebra),
        (m, a: random_array):
      (is_probability_measure(M, Sigma)
        AND (FORALL (n: nat):
          n > 0 IMPLIES
            FORALL (omega: sample_space):
              a(n, 0)(omega) = 1)
        AND (FORALL (n, k: nat):
          n > 0 IMPLIES
            uniform_integer_choice(M, Sigma, n, m(n, k)))
        AND (FORALL
            (n, k: nat),
            (omega: sample_space):
          n > 0 IMPLIES
            a(n, k + 1)(omega)
              = IF m(n, k)(omega) > a(n, k)(omega) THEN
                  a(n, k)(omega) + 1
                ELSIF m(n, k)(omega) = a(n, k)(omega) THEN
                  a(n, k)(omega)
                ELSE
                  a(n, k)(omega) - 1
                ENDIF)
        AND mutually_independent(M, Sigma, m))
      IMPLIES
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (n: nat):
            normalized_expected_position(M, a, n),
          putnam_2024_b4_solution)
END putnam_2024_b4

import Mathlib

open Polynomial

/--
Let $k$ and $m$ be positive integers. For a positive integer $n$, let $f(n)$ be the number of integer sequences $x_1, ..., x_k, y_1, ..., y_m, z$ satisfying $1 \leq x_1 \leq ... \leq x_k \leq z \leq n$
and $1 \leq y_1 \leq ... \leq y_m \leq z \leq n$. Show that $f(n)$ can be expressed as a polynomial in $n$ with nonnegative coefficients.
-/
theorem putnam_2024_b5
    (IsQualifyingSeq : {q : ℕ} → (Fin q → ℕ) → ℕ → Prop)
    (IsQualifyingSeq_def : ∀ q w z, ∀ [NeZero q],
      IsQualifyingSeq w z ↔ Monotone w ∧ 1 ≤ w 0 ∧ w (-1 : Fin q) ≤ z)
    (k m : ℕ) [NeZero k] [NeZero m]
    (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (f_def : ∀ n,
      f n = {(x, y, z) : (Fin k → ℕ) × (Fin m → ℕ) × ℕ |
        IsQualifyingSeq x z ∧ IsQualifyingSeq y z ∧ z ≤ n}.ncard) :
    ∃ P : ℚ[X],
      (∀ n > 0, f n = P.eval (n : ℚ)) ∧
      (∀ i, 0 ≤ P.coeff i) :=
  sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b5:
   polynomial enumeration of two nondecreasing positive integer sequences
   sharing an upper bound, with nonnegative rational coefficients. This file
   contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Sorting.Sorted Arith.PeanoNat QArith ZArith.

Open Scope Q_scope.

Definition putnam_2024_b5_has_cardinality
    {A : Type} (P : A -> Prop) (cardinality : nat) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list A,
    NoDup enumeration /\
    length enumeration = cardinality /\
    forall value : A, In value enumeration <-> P value.

Definition putnam_2024_b5_qualifying_sequence
    (q : nat) (values : list nat) (z : nat) : Prop :=
  length values = q /\
  StronglySorted Nat.le values /\
  (1 <= hd 0 values)%nat /\
  (last values 0 <= z)%nat.

Record putnam_2024_b5_triple : Type := {
  putnam_2024_b5_x : list nat;
  putnam_2024_b5_y : list nat;
  putnam_2024_b5_z : nat
}.

Definition putnam_2024_b5_polynomial : Type := list Q.

Fixpoint putnam_2024_b5_polynomial_eval
    (coefficients : putnam_2024_b5_polynomial) (x : Q) : Q :=
  match coefficients with
  | nil => 0
  | coefficient :: remaining =>
      coefficient +
      x * putnam_2024_b5_polynomial_eval remaining x
  end.

Definition putnam_2024_b5_polynomial_coeff
    (coefficients : putnam_2024_b5_polynomial) (i : nat) : Q :=
  nth i coefficients 0.

Definition putnam_2024_b5_nat_to_Q (n : nat) : Q :=
  inject_Z (Z.of_nat n).

Theorem putnam_2024_b5 :
  forall
    (IsQualifyingSeq : nat -> list nat -> nat -> Prop)
    (k m : nat)
    (f : nat -> nat),
    (forall (q : nat) (values : list nat) (z : nat),
      (0 < q)%nat ->
      (IsQualifyingSeq q values z <->
       putnam_2024_b5_qualifying_sequence q values z)) ->
    (0 < k)%nat ->
    (0 < m)%nat ->
    (forall n : nat,
      putnam_2024_b5_has_cardinality
        (fun triple : putnam_2024_b5_triple =>
          IsQualifyingSeq
            k (putnam_2024_b5_x triple) (putnam_2024_b5_z triple) /\
          IsQualifyingSeq
            m (putnam_2024_b5_y triple) (putnam_2024_b5_z triple) /\
          (putnam_2024_b5_z triple <= n)%nat)
        (f n)) ->
    exists P : putnam_2024_b5_polynomial,
      (forall n : nat,
        (0 < n)%nat ->
        putnam_2024_b5_nat_to_Q (f n) ==
        putnam_2024_b5_polynomial_eval
          P (putnam_2024_b5_nat_to_Q n)) /\
      forall i : nat,
        (0 <= putnam_2024_b5_polynomial_coeff P i)%Q.
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b5
  (putnambench__isabelle__putnam_2024_b5): counting pairs of nondecreasing
  positive integer sequences with a common bounded upper endpoint, and
  expressing that count by a rational polynomial with nonnegative
  coefficients. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory putnam_2024_b5
  imports Complex_Main
begin

definition putnam_2024_b5_qualifying :: "nat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "putnam_2024_b5_qualifying w z \<longleftrightarrow>
    w \<noteq> [] \<and>
    sorted w \<and>
    1 \<le> hd w \<and>
    last w \<le> z"

definition putnam_2024_b5_coeff :: "rat list \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> rat" where
  "putnam_2024_b5_coeff a i =
    (if i < length a then a ! i else 0)"

definition putnam_2024_b5_poly_eval :: "rat list \<Rightarrow> rat \<Rightarrow> rat" where
  "putnam_2024_b5_poly_eval a t =
    (\<Sum>i < length a. putnam_2024_b5_coeff a i * t ^ i)"

theorem putnam_2024_b5:
  fixes k m :: nat
    and f :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat"
  assumes hk: "0 < k"
    and hm: "0 < m"
    and f_def:
      "\<forall>n :: nat.
        f n =
          card
            {(x :: nat list, y :: nat list, z :: nat).
              length x = k \<and>
              putnam_2024_b5_qualifying x z \<and>
              length y = m \<and>
              putnam_2024_b5_qualifying y z \<and>
              z \<le> n}"
  shows
    "\<exists>a :: rat list.
      (\<forall>n :: nat.
        n > 0 \<longrightarrow>
          rat_of_nat (f n) =
            putnam_2024_b5_poly_eval a (rat_of_nat n)) \<and>
      (\<forall>i :: nat. 0 \<le> putnam_2024_b5_coeff a i)"
  sorry

end

  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2024_b5): the number of pairs of
  nondecreasing positive-integer sequences of prescribed positive lengths
  with a shared upper bound z at most n is a polynomial in positive n with
  nonnegative rational coefficients. This file contains no proof.

needs "Library/floor.ml";;

let statement =
  `let qualifying =
     \(q:num) (w:num list) (z:num).
       LENGTH w = q /\
       (!i j:num.
          i < j /\ j < q
          ==> EL i w <= EL j w) /\
       1 <= EL 0 w /\
       EL (q - 1) w <= z in
   !k m:num. !f:num->num.
     0 < k /\
     0 < m /\
     (!n:num.
        f n =
        CARD
          {(x,y,z):num list#num list#num |
             qualifying k x z /\
             qualifying m y z /\
             z <= n})
     ==>
     ?d:num. ?a:num->real.
       (!i:num. rational (a i) /\ &0 <= a i) /\
       (!i:num. d < i ==> a i = &0) /\

title: putnam_2024_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b5:
;; the number of two weakly increasing positive integer sequences with a
;; common upper bound agrees on positive integers with a rational polynomial
;; having nonnegative coefficients. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For positive Q, PUTNAM-2024-B5-QUALIFYING-SEQUENCE-COUNT(Q,Z) counts the
;; functions Fin Q -> Nat that are monotone, start at least at 1, and end at
;; most at Z. Such functions are in bijection with weakly increasing lists of
;; length Q over {1,...,Z}. Partitioning these lists according to whether the
;; last entry is Z gives the recurrence below, so no finite-table restriction
;; is placed on either the source function space or its natural-number range.
;;
;; The source hypotheses uniquely determine ISQUALIFYINGSEQ and F. Eliminating
;; them definitionally yields PUTNAM-2024-B5-COUNT(K,M,N): partition the finite
;; set of triples by Z and multiply the independent X- and Y-sequence counts.
;; Conversely, the predicates and function defined by these same conditions
;; instantiate the source hypotheses, making this direct counting statement
;; bidirectionally equivalent to the Lean statement.
;;
;; A rational polynomial is represented by its finite coefficient list in
;; ascending degree order; omitted coefficients are zero. DEFUN-SK keeps both
;; the universal quantifier over every positive natural N and the existential
;; polynomial witness internal to the statement.

(defun putnam-2024-b5-qualifying-sequence-count (q z)
  (declare (xargs :measure (+ (nfix q) (nfix z))))
  (if (zp q)
      1
    (if (zp z)
        0
      (+
       (putnam-2024-b5-qualifying-sequence-count
        q (- z 1))
       (putnam-2024-b5-qualifying-sequence-count
        (- q 1) z)))))

(defun putnam-2024-b5-count (k m n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      0
    (+
     (putnam-2024-b5-count k m (- n 1))
     (*
      (putnam-2024-b5-qualifying-sequence-count k n)
      (putnam-2024-b5-qualifying-sequence-count m n)))))

(defun putnam-2024-b5-nonnegative-rational-coefficients-p
    (coefficients)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (and
       (rationalp (car coefficients))
       (<= 0 (car coefficients))
       (putnam-2024-b5-nonnegative-rational-coefficients-p
        (cdr coefficients)))
    (equal coefficients nil)))

(defun putnam-2024-b5-polynomial-eval (coefficients x)
  (if (consp coefficients)
      (+
       (car coefficients)
       (* x
          (putnam-2024-b5-polynomial-eval
           (cdr coefficients) x)))
    0))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b5-polynomial-agrees-p
    (k m coefficients)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp n)
      (< 0 n))
     (equal
      (putnam-2024-b5-count k m n)
      (putnam-2024-b5-polynomial-eval
       coefficients n)))))

(defun putnam-2024-b5-polynomial-witness-p
    (k m coefficients)
  (and
   (true-listp coefficients)
   (putnam-2024-b5-nonnegative-rational-coefficients-p
    coefficients)
   (putnam-2024-b5-polynomial-agrees-p
    k m coefficients)))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b5-polynomial-exists-p (k m)
  (exists (coefficients)
    (putnam-2024-b5-polynomial-witness-p
     k m coefficients)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2024-b5-statement (k m)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp k)
    (< 0 k)
    (natp m)
    (< 0 m))
   (putnam-2024-b5-polynomial-exists-p k m)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2024_b5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2024_b5): the number of pairs of nondecreasing
-- positive integer sequences with a common bounded upper endpoint is a
-- polynomial in the bound with nonnegative rational coefficients. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2024B5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

Positive : Nat -> Set
Positive n =
  suc zero <=N n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

toNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
toNat fzero =
  zero
toNat (fsuc index) =
  suc (toNat index)

last : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
last {zero} =
  fzero
last {suc n} =
  fsuc last

MonotoneNatSequence :
  {q : Nat} ->
  (Fin q -> Nat) ->
  Set
MonotoneNatSequence {q} sequence =
  (i j : Fin q) ->
  toNat i <=N toNat j ->
  sequence i <=N sequence j

QualifyingSequence :
  {q : Nat} ->
  (Fin (suc q) -> Nat) ->
  Nat ->
  Set
QualifyingSequence sequence upper =
  MonotoneNatSequence sequence
  and
  (suc zero <=N sequence fzero
  and
  sequence last <=N upper)

record SequenceTriple (k m : Nat) : Set where
  constructor triple
  field
    x-sequence : Fin k -> Nat
    y-sequence : Fin m -> Nat
    endpoint   : Nat

open SequenceTriple

SameSequenceTriple :
  {k m : Nat} ->
  SequenceTriple k m ->
  SequenceTriple k m ->
  Set
SameSequenceTriple {k} {m} left-triple right-triple =
  ((i : Fin k) ->
    x-sequence left-triple i ==
    x-sequence right-triple i)
  and
  (((j : Fin m) ->
    y-sequence left-triple j ==
    y-sequence right-triple j)
  and
  endpoint left-triple == endpoint right-triple)

QualifyingTriple :
  (k-minus-one m-minus-one n : Nat) ->
  SequenceTriple (suc k-minus-one) (suc m-minus-one) ->
  Set
QualifyingTriple k-minus-one m-minus-one n sequences =
  QualifyingSequence
    (x-sequence sequences)
    (endpoint sequences)
  and
  (QualifyingSequence
    (y-sequence sequences)
    (endpoint sequences)
  and
  endpoint sequences <=N n)

record HasExtensionalCardinality
  {A : Set}
  (member : A -> Set)
  (equivalent : A -> A -> Set)
  (cardinality : Nat) :
  Set where

  field
    enumerate :
      Fin cardinality ->
      A
    enumerated-member :
      (index : Fin cardinality) ->
      member (enumerate index)
    enumeration-complete :
      (item : A) ->
      member item ->
      Exists (Fin cardinality)
        (\ index ->
          equivalent item (enumerate index))
    enumeration-injective :
      (left-index right-index : Fin cardinality) ->
      equivalent
        (enumerate left-index)
        (enumerate right-index) ->
      left-index == right-index

CountsQualifyingTriples :
  Nat ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Set
CountsQualifyingTriples k-minus-one m-minus-one f =
  (n : Nat) ->
  HasExtensionalCardinality
    (QualifyingTriple k-minus-one m-minus-one n)
    SameSequenceTriple
    (f n)

record RationalField (Q : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroQ oneQ : Q
    add multiply : Q -> Q -> Q
    negate inverse : Q -> Q
    lessOrEqual : Q -> Q -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> Q
    fromInt : Int -> Q

    one-not-zero :
      oneQ != zeroQ

    add-commutative :
      (x y : Q) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : Q) -> add x zeroQ == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : Q) -> add x (negate x) == zeroQ

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : Q) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : Q) -> multiply x oneQ == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : Q) -> multiply x zeroQ == zeroQ
    distribute :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroQ == zeroQ
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : Q) ->
      x != zeroQ ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneQ

    order-reflexive :
      (x : Q) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : Q) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroQ x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroQ y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroQ (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroQ oneQ and zeroQ != oneQ

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroQ
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneQ
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    fromInt-nonnegative :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromInt (pos n) == fromNat n
    fromInt-negative :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromInt (negsuc n) == negate (fromNat (suc n))

    every-element-is-ratio :
      (x : Q) ->
      Exists Int
        (\ numerator ->
          Exists Nat
            (\ denominator-minus-one ->
              x ==
              multiply
                (fromInt numerator)
                (inverse
                  (fromNat (suc denominator-minus-one)))))

open RationalField

coefficient :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  List Q ->
  Nat ->
  Q
coefficient rationals [] index =
  zeroQ rationals
coefficient rationals (value ∷ values) zero =
  value
coefficient rationals (value ∷ values) (suc index) =
  coefficient rationals values index

evaluatePolynomial :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  List Q ->
  Q ->
  Q
evaluatePolynomial rationals [] x =
  zeroQ rationals
evaluatePolynomial rationals (value ∷ values) x =
  add rationals
    value
    (multiply rationals
      x
      (evaluatePolynomial rationals values x))

AllCoefficientsNonnegative :
  {Q : Set} ->
  RationalField Q ->
  List Q ->
  Set
AllCoefficientsNonnegative rationals values =
  (index : Nat) ->
  lessOrEqual rationals
    (zeroQ rationals)
    (coefficient rationals values index)

putnam-2024-b5 : Set1
putnam-2024-b5 =
  (Q : Set) ->
  (rationals : RationalField Q) ->
  (k-minus-one m-minus-one : Nat) ->
  (f : Nat -> Nat) ->
  CountsQualifyingTriples k-minus-one m-minus-one f ->
  Exists (List Q)
    (\ coefficients ->
      ((n : Nat) ->
        Positive n ->
        fromNat rationals (f n) ==
        evaluatePolynomial rationals
          coefficients
          (fromNat rationals n))
      and
      AllCoefficientsNonnegative rationals coefficients)

title: putnam_2024_b5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b5
  (putnambench__hol4__putnam_2024_b5): f(n) counts triples (x,y,z), where x
  and y are nondecreasing positive-integer sequences of prescribed positive
  lengths and z is a chosen common upper bound with z <= n; this count is a
  polynomial in n with nonnegative rational coefficients. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory pred_setTheory ratTheory;

val putnam_2024_b5 =
  ``let qualifying =
      \q : num. \w : num list. \z : num.
        LENGTH w = q /\
        (!i j : num.
           i < j /\ j < q
           ==>
           EL i w <= EL j w) /\
        1 <= EL 0 w /\
        EL (q - 1) w <= z
    in
      !k m : num. !f : num -> num.
        0 < k /\
        0 < m /\
        (!n : num.
           f n =
           CARD
             {t : num list # num list # num |
                qualifying k (FST t) (SND (SND t)) /\
                qualifying m (FST (SND t)) (SND (SND t)) /\
                SND (SND t) <= n})
        ==>
        ?d : num. ?P : num -> rat.
          (!i : num. d < i ==> P i = 0q) /\
          (!i : num. 0q <= P i) /\
          (!n : num.
             0 < n
             ==>
             rat_of_num (f n) =
             ITSET
               (\i : num. \acc : rat.
                  P i * rat_expn (rat_of_num n) i + acc)
               (count (d + 1))
               0q)``;

title: putnam_2024_b5
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2024_b5: for positive sequence lengths k and m, the number of pairs
  of nondecreasing positive-integer sequences whose final terms are at most a
  common z at most n agrees on positive n with a rational polynomial having
  nonnegative coefficients. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The half-open interval 0 ..^ q is set.mm's q-element representation of
  Fin q. A qualifying sequence is represented as a function from this
  interval to NN. This is equivalent to a natural-valued monotone function
  whose first value is at least one; for positive q, monotonicity then makes
  every value positive. Its last value is the value at q - 1.

  P24B5Count uses the nested ordered-pair representation
  <. <. x , y >. , z >. of the source triples. The bounded final values and
  monotonicity make the displayed set finite, so # is exactly Set.ncard here.
  P24B5QFld is set.mm's rational subfield of the complex field, and Poly1,
  eval1, and coe1 provide rational polynomials, evaluation, and coefficients.

  The final declaration retains the arbitrary natural-valued function f and
  its defining equality at every natural n. It is the single unproved $a
  corpus statement; this database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c P24B5Count P24B5QFld $.

p24b5-count-syntax $a class ( P24B5Count A B C ) $.
p24b5-qfld-syntax $a class P24B5QFld $.

p24b5-qfld-definition $a |-
  P24B5QFld = ( CCfld |`s QQ ) $.

${
  $d i j t K $.
  $d i j t M $.
  $d i j t N $.

  p24b5-count-definition $a |- ( P24B5Count K M N ) =
    (
      # `
      {
        t e.
          (
            (
              ( NN ^m ( 0 ..^ K ) )
              X.
              ( NN ^m ( 0 ..^ M ) )
            )
            X.
            NN0
          )
        |
        (
          (
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ K )
              A. j e. ( 0 ..^ K )
                (
                  i <_ j
                  ->
                  (
                    ( ( 1st ` ( 1st ` t ) ) ` i )
                    <_
                    ( ( 1st ` ( 1st ` t ) ) ` j )
                  )
                )
            /\
            (
              ( ( 1st ` ( 1st ` t ) ) ` ( K - 1 ) )
              <_
              ( 2nd ` t )
            )
          )
          /\
          (
            (
              A. i e. ( 0 ..^ M )
                A. j e. ( 0 ..^ M )
                  (
                    i <_ j
                    ->
                    (
                      ( ( 2nd ` ( 1st ` t ) ) ` i )
                      <_
                      ( ( 2nd ` ( 1st ` t ) ) ` j )
                    )
                  )
              /\
              (
                ( ( 2nd ` ( 1st ` t ) ) ` ( M - 1 ) )
                <_
                ( 2nd ` t )
              )
            )
            /\
            ( ( 2nd ` t ) <_ N )
          )
        )
      }
    ) $.
$}

${
  $d P f i k m n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2024-b5 $a |-
    A. k e. NN
      A. m e. NN
        A. f e. ( NN0 ^m NN0 )
          (
            A. n e. NN0
              ( f ` n ) = ( P24B5Count k m n )
            ->
            E. P e. ( Base ` ( Poly1 ` P24B5QFld ) )
              (
                A. n e. NN
                  (
                    ( f ` n )
                    =
                    ( ( ( eval1 ` P24B5QFld ) ` P ) ` n )
                  )
                /\
                A. i e. NN0
                  0 <_ ( ( coe1 ` P ) ` i )
              )
          )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2024_b5
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b5:
% the count of pairs of nondecreasing positive integer sequences with a common
% upper bound is a rational polynomial with nonnegative coefficients. This file
% contains no proof.

putnam_2024_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_list_set: TYPE = finite_set[list[nat]]
  counted_object: TYPE = [list[nat], nat]
  counted_object_set: TYPE = finite_set[counted_object]

  prepend_value(value: nat, tails: natural_list_set): natural_list_set =
    image(
      (LAMBDA (tail: list[nat]): cons(value, tail)),
      tails)

  prepend_through(
      bound: nat,
      tails: natural_list_set): RECURSIVE natural_list_set =
    IF bound = 0 THEN
      prepend_value(0, tails)
    ELSE
      union(
        prepend_value(bound, tails),
        prepend_through(bound - 1, tails))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE bound

  bounded_lists(
      length, bound: nat): RECURSIVE natural_list_set =
    IF length = 0 THEN
      singleton(null)
    ELSE
      prepend_through(
        bound,
        bounded_lists(length - 1, bound))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE length

  attach_upper_bound(
      z: nat,
      values: natural_list_set): counted_object_set =
    image(
      (LAMBDA (value_list: list[nat]): (value_list, z)),
      values)

  counted_universe(
      length, n: nat): RECURSIVE counted_object_set =
    IF n = 0 THEN
      attach_upper_bound(0, bounded_lists(length, 0))
    ELSE
      union(
        attach_upper_bound(n, bounded_lists(length, n)),
        counted_universe(length, n - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE n

  list_value(
      values: list[nat],
      index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    CASES values OF
      null: 0,
      cons(head, tail):
        IF index = 0 THEN
          head
        ELSE
          list_value(tail, index - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE values BY <<

  nondecreasing_segment(
      values: list[nat],
      start: nat,
      length: posnat): bool =
    FORALL (left, right: below(length)):
      left <= right IMPLIES
        list_value(values, start + left)
          <= list_value(values, start + right)

  qualifying_sequence(
      values: list[nat],
      start: nat,
      length: posnat,
      z: nat): bool =
    nondecreasing_segment(values, start, length)
      AND
      (FORALL (index: below(length)):
        1 <= list_value(values, start + index)
          AND list_value(values, start + index) <= z)

  qualifying_triples(k, m: posnat, n: nat):
      counted_object_set =
    intersection(
      counted_universe(k + m, n),
      {object: counted_object |
        qualifying_sequence(object`1, 0, k, object`2)
          AND qualifying_sequence(object`1, k, m, object`2)})

  rational_polynomial: TYPE = list[rat]

  polynomial_value(
      polynomial: rational_polynomial,
      x: rat): RECURSIVE rat =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: 0,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        coefficient + x * polynomial_value(tail, x)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  polynomial_coefficient(
      polynomial: rational_polynomial,
      degree: nat): RECURSIVE rat =
    CASES polynomial OF
      null: 0,
      cons(coefficient, tail):
        IF degree = 0 THEN
          coefficient
        ELSE
          polynomial_coefficient(tail, degree - 1)
        ENDIF
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE polynomial BY <<

  putnam_2024_b5: bool =
    FORALL (k, m: posnat), (f: [nat -> nat]):
      (FORALL (n: nat):
        f(n) = card(qualifying_triples(k, m, n)))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (polynomial: rational_polynomial):
          (FORALL (n: posnat):
            (f(n) :: rat) = polynomial_value(polynomial, n))
          AND
          (FORALL (degree: nat):
            polynomial_coefficient(polynomial, degree) >= 0)
END putnam_2024_b5

title: putnam_2024_b6
content:
import Mathlib

open scoped Real
open scoped Topology

noncomputable abbrev putnam_2024_b6_solution : ℝ := sorry
-- -1/2
/--
For a real number $a$, let $F_a(x) = \sum_{n\geq 1} n^a e^{2n}x^{n^2}$ for $0 \leq x < 1$.
Find a real number $c$ such that $\lim_{x \to 1^-} F_a(x)e^{-1/(1-x)} = 0$ for all $a < c$, and $\lim_{x \to 1^-} F_a(x)e^{-1/(1-x)} = \infty$ for all $a > c$.
-/
theorem putnam_2024_b6
    (F : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ) (c : ℝ)
    (hF : ∀ a, ∀ x ∈ Set.Ico 0 1,
      HasSum (fun (n : ℕ) => (n+1)^a * rexp (2*(n+1)) * x^(n+1)^2) (F a x)) :
    ((∀ a < c, Filter.Tendsto (fun x => F a x * rexp (- 1 / (1-x))) (𝓝[<] 1) (𝓝 0)) ∧
    (∀ a > c, Filter.Tendsto (fun x => F a x * rexp (- 1 / (1-x))) (𝓝[<] 1) Filter.atTop))
    ↔ c = putnam_2024_b6_solution :=
  sorry

title: putnam_2024_b6
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b6
   (putnambench__rocq__putnam_2024_b6): the critical exponent for the
   left-limit asymptotics of a real power series near 1. This file contains
   no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals Rpower Arith.PeanoNat.

Open Scope R_scope.

Fixpoint putnam_2024_b6_partial_sum
    (u : nat -> R) (count : nat) : R :=
  match count with
  | O => 0
  | S k => putnam_2024_b6_partial_sum u k + u k
  end.

Definition putnam_2024_b6_series_sum
    (u : nat -> R) (sum : R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    0 < epsilon ->
    exists cutoff : nat,
      forall count : nat,
        (cutoff <= count)%nat ->
        Rabs (putnam_2024_b6_partial_sum u count - sum) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_2024_b6_term
    (a x : R) (n : nat) : R :=
  Rpower (INR (S n)) a *
  exp (2 * INR (S n)) *
  x ^ Nat.pow (S n) 2.

Definition putnam_2024_b6_left_limit
    (g : R -> R) (limit : R) : Prop :=
  forall epsilon : R,
    0 < epsilon ->
    exists delta : R,
      0 < delta /\
      forall x : R,
        0 < 1 - x < delta ->
        Rabs (g x - limit) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_2024_b6_left_limit_at_top
    (g : R -> R) : Prop :=
  forall bound : R,
    exists delta : R,
      0 < delta /\
      forall x : R,
        0 < 1 - x < delta ->
        bound <= g x.

Definition putnam_2024_b6_solution : R :=
  -1 / 2.

Theorem putnam_2024_b6 :
  forall (F : R -> R -> R) (c : R),
    (forall (a x : R),
      0 <= x < 1 ->
      putnam_2024_b6_series_sum
        (putnam_2024_b6_term a x) (F a x)) ->
    ((forall a : R,
        a < c ->
        putnam_2024_b6_left_limit
          (fun x : R =>
            F a x * exp (-1 / (1 - x)))
          0) /\
     (forall a : R,
        a > c ->
        putnam_2024_b6_left_limit_at_top
          (fun x : R =>
            F a x * exp (-1 / (1 - x)))))
    <->
    c = putnam_2024_b6_solution.
Admitted.

title: putnam_2024_b6

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b6
  (putnambench__isabelle__putnam_2024_b6): the threshold real exponent for
  the left-limit asymptotics of a power series with terms
  n^a * exp (2*n) * x^(n^2) is -1/2. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory putnam_2024_b6
  imports Complex_Main
begin

definition putnam_2024_b6_solution :: real where
  "putnam_2024_b6_solution = -1 / 2"

theorem putnam_2024_b6:
  fixes F :: "real \<Rightarrow> real \<Rightarrow> real"
    and c :: real
  assumes hF:
    "\<And>a x. x \<in> {0..<1} \<Longrightarrow>
      (\<lambda>n :: nat.
        real (Suc n) powr a *
        exp (2 * real (Suc n)) *
        x ^ ((Suc n) ^ 2))
      sums F a x"
  shows
    "((\<forall>a :: real. a < c \<longrightarrow>
        filterlim
          (\<lambda>x. F a x * exp (-1 / (1 - x)))
          (nhds 0) (at_left 1)) \<and>
      (\<forall>a :: real. c < a \<longrightarrow>
        filterlim
          (\<lambda>x. F a x * exp (-1 / (1 - x)))
          at_top (at_left 1)))
      \<longleftrightarrow> c = putnam_2024_b6_solution"
  sorry

end

  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2024_b6): the threshold real exponent for
  the left-hand asymptotics at 1 of an exponentially weighted power series.

let statement =
  `let rpow =
     \u a:real. exp (a * ln u) in
   let tends_at_left =
     \(f:real->real) (b:real) (l:real).
       !e:real.
         &0 < e
         ==> ?d:real.
               &0 < d /\
               !x:real.
                 x < b /\ abs (x - b) < d
                 ==> abs (f x - l) < e in
   let tends_at_left_posinfinity =
     \(f:real->real) (b:real).
       !M:real.
         ?d:real.
           &0 < d /\
           !x:real.
             x < b /\ abs (x - b) < d
             ==> M <= f x in
   let putnam_2024_b6_solution = --(&1 / &2) in
   !series_value:real->real->real. !c:real.

title: putnam_2024_b6
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b6:
;; the sharp real threshold for the normalized exponential power series is
;; c = -1/2, with decay below c and divergence above c. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; The source hypothesis determines F uniquely on 0 <= x < 1, so F is
;; eliminated definitionally.  After multiplication by exp(-1/(1-x)), its
;; n-th positive term is
;;
;;   exp(a*log(n) + 2*n + n^2*log(x) - 1/(1-x)).
;;
;; For positive rational x, the functions below give shrinking rational
;; intervals for log(x) and exp(x), hence for every finite partial sum.
;; Positivity makes "all finite partial sums are below epsilon" equivalent,
;; after the usual epsilon rescaling, to the normalized series tending to
;; zero.  Likewise, a finite partial sum above every rational target is
;; equivalent to divergence to positive infinity.
;;
;; The DEFSTUB below is an arbitrary rational approximation function for the
;; threshold c. Its regular-Cauchy law is explicit in the root predicate, so
;; no computability or first-class-function restriction is imposed. Rational
;; a values suffice without narrowing the theorem: they are dense, and the
;; positive summands are monotone in a. Rational x values suffice because the
;; normalized series is continuous at every x in (0,1). DEFUN-SK keeps every
;; universal quantifier and every limit witness inside the statement.

;; Exact real names and comparisons with rationals.

(defstub putnam-2024-b6-c-approx (precision) t)

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-real-cauchy-p ()
  (forall (epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and (rationalp epsilon)
          (< 0 epsilon)
          (rationalp eta)
          (< 0 eta))
     (let ((left
            (putnam-2024-b6-c-approx epsilon))
           (right
            (putnam-2024-b6-c-approx eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<= (abs (- left right))
            (+ epsilon eta)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-rational-lower-bound-p (lower)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and (rationalp epsilon)
          (< 0 epsilon))
     (let ((value
            (putnam-2024-b6-c-approx epsilon)))
       (and
        (rationalp value)
        (<= lower (+ value epsilon)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-rational-less-real-p
    (rational-value)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (rationalp rational-value)
     (rationalp margin)
     (< 0 margin)
     (putnam-2024-b6-rational-lower-bound-p
      (+ rational-value margin)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-rational-upper-bound-p (upper)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and (rationalp epsilon)
          (< 0 epsilon))
     (let ((value
            (putnam-2024-b6-c-approx epsilon)))
       (and
        (rationalp value)
        (<= (- value epsilon) upper))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-real-less-rational-p
    (rational-value)
  (exists (margin)
    (and
     (rationalp rational-value)
     (rationalp margin)
     (< 0 margin)
     (putnam-2024-b6-rational-upper-bound-p
      (- rational-value margin)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-real-equal-rational-p
    (rational-value)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and (rationalp rational-value)
          (rationalp epsilon)
          (< 0 epsilon))
     (let ((value
            (putnam-2024-b6-c-approx epsilon)))
       (and
        (rationalp value)
        (<= (abs (- value rational-value))
            epsilon))))))

;; Rational interval enclosures for log and exp.

(defun putnam-2024-b6-factorial (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      1
    (* n
       (putnam-2024-b6-factorial (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-exp-series (x degree)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix degree)))
  (if (zp degree)
      1
    (+ (putnam-2024-b6-exp-series
        x (- degree 1))
       (/ (expt x degree)
          (putnam-2024-b6-factorial degree)))))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-nonnegative-part (x)
  (if (< x 0) 0 x))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-exp-scale (x)
  (+ 1 (floor (abs x) 1)))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-exp-reduced-argument (x)
  (/ x (putnam-2024-b6-exp-scale x)))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-exp-tail (x degree)
  (let* ((y
          (putnam-2024-b6-exp-reduced-argument x))
         (next (+ 1 (nfix degree))))
    (/ (expt (abs y) next)
       (* (putnam-2024-b6-factorial next)
          (- 1 (abs y))))))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-exp-lower (x degree)
  (let* ((scale
          (putnam-2024-b6-exp-scale x))
         (reduced
          (putnam-2024-b6-exp-reduced-argument x))
         (center
          (putnam-2024-b6-exp-series reduced degree))
         (radius
          (putnam-2024-b6-exp-tail x degree)))
    (expt
     (putnam-2024-b6-nonnegative-part
      (- center radius))
     scale)))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-exp-upper (x degree)
  (let* ((scale
          (putnam-2024-b6-exp-scale x))
         (reduced
          (putnam-2024-b6-exp-reduced-argument x))
         (center
          (putnam-2024-b6-exp-series reduced degree))
         (radius
          (putnam-2024-b6-exp-tail x degree)))
    (expt (+ center radius) scale)))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-log-series (z degree)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix degree)))
  (if (zp degree)
      (* 2 z)
    (+ (putnam-2024-b6-log-series
        z (- degree 1))
       (/ (* 2
             (expt z (+ (* 2 degree) 1)))
          (+ (* 2 degree) 1)))))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-log-tail (z degree)
  (let ((next-odd (+ (* 2 (nfix degree)) 3)))
    (/ (* 2 (expt (abs z) next-odd))
       (* next-odd
          (- 1 (* z z))))))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-log-lower (x degree)
  (let* ((z (/ (- x 1) (+ x 1)))
         (center
          (putnam-2024-b6-log-series z degree))
         (radius
          (putnam-2024-b6-log-tail z degree)))
    (- center radius)))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-log-upper (x degree)
  (let* ((z (/ (- x 1) (+ x 1)))
         (center
          (putnam-2024-b6-log-series z degree))
         (radius
          (putnam-2024-b6-log-tail z degree)))
    (+ center radius)))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-scale-interval-lower
    (scalar lower upper)
  (if (< scalar 0)
      (* scalar upper)
    (* scalar lower)))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-scale-interval-upper
    (scalar lower upper)
  (if (< scalar 0)
      (* scalar lower)
    (* scalar upper)))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-exponent-lower
    (a x n degree)
  (let* ((log-n-lower
          (putnam-2024-b6-log-lower n degree))
         (log-n-upper
          (putnam-2024-b6-log-upper n degree))
         (log-x-lower
          (putnam-2024-b6-log-lower x degree)))
    (+ (putnam-2024-b6-scale-interval-lower
        a log-n-lower log-n-upper)
       (* n n log-x-lower)
       (* 2 n)
       (- (/ 1 (- 1 x))))))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-exponent-upper
    (a x n degree)
  (let* ((log-n-lower
          (putnam-2024-b6-log-lower n degree))
         (log-n-upper
          (putnam-2024-b6-log-upper n degree))
         (log-x-upper
          (putnam-2024-b6-log-upper x degree)))
    (+ (putnam-2024-b6-scale-interval-upper
        a log-n-lower log-n-upper)
       (* n n log-x-upper)
       (* 2 n)
       (- (/ 1 (- 1 x))))))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-term-lower
    (a x n degree)
  (putnam-2024-b6-exp-lower
   (putnam-2024-b6-exponent-lower
    a x n degree)
   degree))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-term-upper
    (a x n degree)
  (putnam-2024-b6-exp-upper
   (putnam-2024-b6-exponent-upper
    a x n degree)
   degree))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-partial-sum-lower
    (a x terms degree)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2024-b6-partial-sum-lower
        a x (- terms 1) degree)
       (putnam-2024-b6-term-lower
        a x terms degree))))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-partial-sum-upper
    (a x terms degree)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix terms)))
  (if (zp terms)
      0
    (+ (putnam-2024-b6-partial-sum-upper
        a x (- terms 1) degree)
       (putnam-2024-b6-term-upper
        a x terms degree))))

;; The zero-limit half of the threshold property.

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-upper-certificate-exists-p
    (a x terms epsilon)
  (exists (degree)
    (and
     (natp degree)
     (< (putnam-2024-b6-partial-sum-upper
         a x terms degree)
        epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-zero-tail-p
    (delta a epsilon)
  (forall (x terms)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (< 0 x)
      (< x 1)
      (< (- 1 x) delta)
      (natp terms))
     (putnam-2024-b6-upper-certificate-exists-p
      a x terms epsilon))))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-zero-delta-p
    (delta a epsilon)
  (and
   (rationalp delta)
   (< 0 delta)
   (putnam-2024-b6-zero-tail-p
    delta a epsilon)))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-zero-delta-exists-p
    (a epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (putnam-2024-b6-zero-delta-p
     delta a epsilon)))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-zero-limit-p (a)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp epsilon)
      (< 0 epsilon))
     (putnam-2024-b6-zero-delta-exists-p
      a epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-zero-side-p ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp a)
      (putnam-2024-b6-rational-less-real-p
       a))
     (putnam-2024-b6-zero-limit-p a))))

;; The divergence-to-positive-infinity half.

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-lower-witness-exists-p
    (a x target)
  (exists (terms degree)
    (and
     (natp terms)
     (natp degree)
     (< target
        (putnam-2024-b6-partial-sum-lower
         a x terms degree)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-infinity-tail-p
    (delta a target)
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp x)
      (< 0 x)
      (< x 1)
      (< (- 1 x) delta))
     (putnam-2024-b6-lower-witness-exists-p
      a x target))))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-infinity-delta-p
    (delta a target)
  (and
   (rationalp delta)
   (< 0 delta)
   (putnam-2024-b6-infinity-tail-p
    delta a target)))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-infinity-delta-exists-p
    (a target)
  (exists (delta)
    (putnam-2024-b6-infinity-delta-p
     delta a target)))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-infinity-limit-p (a)
  (forall (target)
    (implies
     (rationalp target)
     (putnam-2024-b6-infinity-delta-exists-p
      a target))))

(defun-sk putnam-2024-b6-infinity-side-p ()
  (forall (a)
    (implies
     (and
      (rationalp a)
      (putnam-2024-b6-real-less-rational-p
       a))
     (putnam-2024-b6-infinity-limit-p a))))

(defun putnam-2024-b6-threshold-property-p ()
  (and
   (putnam-2024-b6-zero-side-p)
   (putnam-2024-b6-infinity-side-p)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2024-b6-statement ()
  (implies
   (putnam-2024-b6-real-cauchy-p)
   (equal
    (if (putnam-2024-b6-threshold-property-p)
        t nil)
    (if (putnam-2024-b6-real-equal-rational-p
         -1/2)
        t nil))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2024_b6
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2024_b6): the threshold for the left-hand
-- asymptotics of a real exponential power series at x = 1 is c = -1/2.
-- This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2024B6 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

oneN : Nat
oneN =
  suc zero

twoN : Nat
twoN =
  suc oneN

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse absoluteValue : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    absolute-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (absoluteValue x)
    absolute-of-nonnegative :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      absoluteValue x == x
    absolute-of-nonpositive :
      (x : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x zeroR ->
      absoluteValue x == negate x

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n ->
          lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals x y =
  multiply reals x (inverse reals y)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

InHalfOpenUnitInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
InHalfOpenUnitInterval reals x =
  lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x
  and
  StrictLess reals x (oneR reals)

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (absoluteValue reals (subtract reals x center))
    radius

naturalPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
naturalPower reals x zero =
  oneR reals
naturalPower reals x (suc n) =
  multiply reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    x

factorial : Nat -> Nat
factorial zero =
  oneN
factorial (suc n) =
  suc n * factorial n

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : _) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

SeriesHasSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
SeriesHasSum reals terms value =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n -> sumFirst reals n terms)
    value

exponentialTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
exponentialTerm reals x n =
  divide reals
    (naturalPower reals x n)
    (fromNat reals (factorial n))

record StandardExponential
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) :
  Set1 where

  field
    exponential logarithm : R -> R

    exponential-is-power-series :
      (x : R) ->
      SeriesHasSum reals
        (exponentialTerm reals x)
        (exponential x)
    exponential-positive :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) (exponential x)
    logarithm-of-exponential :
      (x : R) ->
      logarithm (exponential x) == x
    exponential-of-logarithm :
      (x : R) ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) x ->
      exponential (logarithm x) == x

open StandardExponential

positiveRealPower :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardExponential reals ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
positiveRealPower reals analysis base exponent =
  exponential analysis
    (multiply reals exponent (logarithm analysis base))

putnamTerm :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardExponential reals ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Nat ->
  R
putnamTerm reals analysis a x n =
  multiply reals
    (multiply reals
      (positiveRealPower reals analysis
        (fromNat reals (suc n))
        a)
      (exponential analysis
        (multiply reals
          (fromNat reals twoN)
          (fromNat reals (suc n)))))
    (naturalPower reals x ((suc n) * (suc n)))

SeriesDefinition :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardExponential reals ->
  (R -> R -> R) ->
  Set
SeriesDefinition {R} reals analysis F =
  (a x : R) ->
  InHalfOpenUnitInterval reals x ->
  SeriesHasSum reals
    (putnamTerm reals analysis a x)
    (F a x)

ApproachesOneFromLeft :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
ApproachesOneFromLeft reals delta x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals (oneR reals) delta)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals x (oneR reals)

LeftLimitZero :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
LeftLimitZero {R} reals function =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        ApproachesOneFromLeft reals delta x ->
        StrictLess reals
          (absoluteValue reals (function x))
          epsilon))

LeftLimitAtTop :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
LeftLimitAtTop {R} reals function =
  (bound : R) ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((x : R) ->
        ApproachesOneFromLeft reals delta x ->
        lessOrEqual reals bound (function x)))

normalizedValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardExponential reals ->
  (R -> R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
normalizedValue reals analysis F a x =
  multiply reals
    (F a x)
    (exponential analysis
      (negate reals
        (divide reals
          (oneR reals)
          (subtract reals (oneR reals) x))))

ThresholdProperty :
  {R : Set} ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  StandardExponential reals ->
  (R -> R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ThresholdProperty {R} reals analysis F c =
  ((a : R) ->
    StrictLess reals a c ->
    LeftLimitZero reals
      (normalizedValue reals analysis F a))
  and
  ((a : R) ->
    StrictLess reals c a ->
    LeftLimitAtTop reals
      (normalizedValue reals analysis F a))

negativeHalf :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
negativeHalf reals =
  divide reals
    (negate reals (oneR reals))
    (fromNat reals twoN)

putnam-2024-b6 : Set1
putnam-2024-b6 =
  (R : Set) ->

  (analysis : StandardExponential reals) ->
  (F : R -> R -> R) ->

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b6:
  the threshold real exponent governing whether the exponentially normalized
  power series tends to zero or positive infinity as x approaches 1 from the
  left is -1/2. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory realTheory seqTheory transcTheory;

val putnam_2024_b6 =
  ``let left_tends_to =
      \f : real -> real.
      \l : real.
        !epsilon : real.
          0 < epsilon
          ==>
          ?delta : real.
            0 < delta /\
            !x : real.
              0 < 1 - x /\ 1 - x < delta
              ==>
              abs (f x - l) < epsilon
    in
    let left_tends_to_posinfinity =
      \f : real -> real.
        !M : real.
          ?delta : real.
            0 < delta /\
            !x : real.
              0 < 1 - x /\ 1 - x < delta
              ==>
              M < f x
    in
      !F : real -> real -> real. !c : real.
        (!a x : real.
           0 <= x /\ x < 1
           ==>
           (\n : num.
              (&(n + 1) : real) powr a *
              exp (2 * (&(n + 1) : real)) *
              x pow ((n + 1) EXP 2))
             sums F a x)
        ==>
        (((!a : real.
             a < c
             ==>
             left_tends_to
               (\x : real.
                  F a x * exp (-(1 / (1 - x))))
               0) /\
          (!a : real.
             c < a
             ==>
             left_tends_to_posinfinity
               (\x : real.
                  F a x * exp (-(1 / (1 - x))))))
         <=>
         c = -(1 / 2))``;

title: putnam_2024_b6

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2024_b6:
% the threshold c = -1/2 separates zero and positive-infinity left limits at
% one for a scaled real power-exponential series. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2024_b6: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_family: TYPE = [real -> real_function]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  nat_factorial(index: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF index = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      index * nat_factorial(index - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE index

  converges_to(sequence: real_sequence, value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
        FORALL (index: nat):
          cutoff <= index IMPLIES
            abs(sequence(index) - value) < epsilon_value

  exponential_partial(x: real, count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      LET index: nat = count - 1 IN
        exponential_partial(x, count - 1)
          + safe_div(
              x ^ index,
              nat_factorial(index) :: real)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  real_exponential(x: real): real =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (value: real):
        converges_to(
          LAMBDA (count: nat):
            exponential_partial(x, count),
          value))

  natural_log(x: real): real =
    IF x > 0 THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (value: real):
          real_exponential(value) = x)
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  real_power(base, exponent: real): real =
    IF base > 0 THEN
      real_exponential(exponent * natural_log(base))
    ELSIF base = 0 AND exponent = 0 THEN
      1
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  series_term(a, x: real, index: nat): real =
    LET n: nat = index + 1 IN
      real_power(n :: real, a)
        * real_exponential(2 * (n :: real))
        * x ^ (n ^ 2)

  series_partial_sum(
      a, x: real,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      series_partial_sum(a, x, count - 1)
        + series_term(a, x, count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  represents_series(F: real_family): bool =
    FORALL (a, x: real):
      (0 <= x AND x < 1)
        IMPLIES
          converges_to(
            LAMBDA (count: nat):
              series_partial_sum(a, x, count),
            F(a)(x))

  scaled_value(F: real_family, a, x: real): real =
    F(a)(x)
      * real_exponential(-safe_div(1, 1 - x))

  tends_to_zero_from_left(
      F: real_family,
      a: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (x: real):
          (x < 1 AND 1 - x < delta)
            IMPLIES
              abs(scaled_value(F, a, x)) < epsilon_value

  tends_to_positive_infinity_from_left(
      F: real_family,
      a: real): bool =
    FORALL (bound: real):
      EXISTS (delta: posreal):
        FORALL (x: real):
          (x < 1 AND 1 - x < delta)
            IMPLIES
              bound <= scaled_value(F, a, x)

  putnam_2024_b6_solution: real = -1 / 2

  putnam_2024_b6: bool =
    FORALL (F: real_family), (c: real):
      represents_series(F)
        IMPLIES
          (((FORALL (a: real):
                a < c IMPLIES
                  tends_to_zero_from_left(F, a))
            AND
              (FORALL (a: real):
                a > c IMPLIES
                  tends_to_positive_infinity_from_left(F, a)))
            IFF c = putnam_2024_b6_solution)
END putnam_2024_b6

import Mathlib

/--
Let $m_0$ and $n_0$ be distinct positive integers. For every positive integer $k$,
define $m_k$ and $n_k$ to be the relatively prime positive integers such that
$$\frac{m_k}{n_k} = \frac{2m_{k-1} + 1}{2n_{k-1} + 1}.$$
Prove that $2m_k + 1$ and $2n_k + 1$ are relatively prime for all but finitely many
positive integers $k$.
-/
theorem putnam_2025_a1
  (m n : ℕ → ℕ)
  (hm : ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < m k)
  (hn : ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < n k)
  (h_distinct : m 0 ≠ n 0)
  (h_coprime : ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → Nat.Coprime (m k) (n k))
  (h_recurrence : ∀ k : ℕ,
    (m (k + 1) : ℚ) / (n (k + 1) : ℚ) = (2 * (m k : ℚ) + 1) / (2 * (n k : ℚ) + 1)) :
  {k : ℕ | ¬Nat.Coprime (2 * m k + 1) (2 * n k + 1)}.Finite :=
sorry

          ((2 * putnam_2025_a1_nat_to_Q (m k) + 1) /

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a1:
;; positive coprime numerator-denominator sequences satisfying the stated
;; rational recurrence have only finitely many indices where their odd
;; transforms are not coprime. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; These conservative interfaces represent the two arbitrary sequences from
;; the source theorem. Their natural-valuedness, positivity, recurrence, and
;; coprimality assumptions are all explicit in the statement predicate.

(defstub putnam-2025-a1-m (k) t)
(defstub putnam-2025-a1-n (k) t)

;; On positive integers, checking every possible common divisor from the
;; smaller input down to 2 is equivalent to Nat.Coprime in the Lean source.

(defun putnam-2025-a1-coprime-through-p (a b divisor)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix divisor)))
  (if (and (natp divisor) (< 1 divisor))
      (and
       (not
        (and
         (equal (mod a divisor) 0)
         (equal (mod b divisor) 0)))
       (putnam-2025-a1-coprime-through-p
        a b (- divisor 1)))
    t))

(defun putnam-2025-a1-coprime-p (a b)
  (and
   (posp a)
   (posp b)
   (putnam-2025-a1-coprime-through-p
    a b (if (< a b) a b))))

(defun-sk putnam-2025-a1-positive-sequences-p ()
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (natp k)
     (and
      (posp (putnam-2025-a1-m k))
      (posp (putnam-2025-a1-n k))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2025-a1-reduced-positive-tail-p ()
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and (natp k) (< 0 k))
     (putnam-2025-a1-coprime-p
      (putnam-2025-a1-m k)
      (putnam-2025-a1-n k)))))

;; Under positivity, this cross-multiplied equality is equivalent to
;;
;;   m_(k+1) / n_(k+1) = (2*m_k+1) / (2*n_k+1).

(defun-sk putnam-2025-a1-recurrence-p ()
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (natp k)
     (equal
      (*
       (putnam-2025-a1-m (+ k 1))
       (+ (* 2 (putnam-2025-a1-n k)) 1))
      (*
       (putnam-2025-a1-n (+ k 1))
       (+ (* 2 (putnam-2025-a1-m k)) 1))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2025-a1-eventual-coprime-tail-p (cutoff)
  (forall (k)
    (implies
     (and
      (natp k)
      (< cutoff k))
     (putnam-2025-a1-coprime-p
      (+ (* 2 (putnam-2025-a1-m k)) 1)
      (+ (* 2 (putnam-2025-a1-n k)) 1)))))

;; A subset of the natural numbers is finite exactly when it is bounded.
;; Therefore this existential cutoff is equivalent to finiteness of the
;; exceptional set in the Lean conclusion.

(defun-sk putnam-2025-a1-finite-exceptional-set-p ()
  (exists (cutoff)
    (and
     (natp cutoff)
     (putnam-2025-a1-eventual-coprime-tail-p cutoff))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2025-a1-statement ()
  (implies

    (putnam-2025-a1-positive-sequences-p)
    (not

    (putnam-2025-a1-reduced-positive-tail-p)

title: putnam_2025_a1

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a1:
-- two positive coprime natural-number sequences related by a rational
-- recurrence have only finitely many indices where the transformed terms are
-- not coprime. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2025A1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _∣_ _~Q_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

record _∣_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    equation : divisor * quotient == dividend

record IsGCD (a b g : Nat) : Set where
  field
    gcd-divides-left : g ∣ a
    gcd-divides-right : g ∣ b
    greatest-common-divisor :
      (d : Nat) ->
      d ∣ a ->
      d ∣ b ->
      d ∣ g

Coprime : Nat -> Nat -> Set
Coprime a b =
  IsGCD a b one

record NonnegativeFraction : Set where
  constructor fraction
  field
    numerator   : Nat
    denominator : Nat

open NonnegativeFraction

_~Q_ : NonnegativeFraction -> NonnegativeFraction -> Set
x ~Q y =
  numerator x * denominator y ==
  numerator y * denominator x

data Member {A : Set} (x : A) : List A -> Set where
  at-head :
    {xs : List A} ->
    Member x (x ∷ xs)
  in-tail :
    {y : A} ->
    {xs : List A} ->
    Member x xs ->
    Member x (y ∷ xs)

record FiniteSubset (P : Nat -> Set) : Set where
  field
    elements : List Nat
    complete :
      (k : Nat) ->
      P k ->
      Member k elements

sequenceRatio :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Nat ->
  NonnegativeFraction
sequenceRatio m n k =
  fraction (m k) (n k)

transformedRatio :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Nat ->
  NonnegativeFraction
transformedRatio m n k =
  fraction
    (two * m k + one)
    (two * n k + one)

ExceptionalIndex :
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  (Nat -> Nat) ->
  Nat ->
  Set
ExceptionalIndex m n k =
  Not
    (Coprime
      (two * m k + one)
      (two * n k + one))

putnam-2025-a1 : Set
putnam-2025-a1 =
  (m n : Nat -> Nat) ->
  ((k : Nat) -> Positive (m k)) ->
  ((k : Nat) -> Positive (n k)) ->
  m zero != n zero ->
  ((k : Nat) ->
    Positive k ->
    Coprime (m k) (n k)) ->
  ((k : Nat) ->
    sequenceRatio m n (suc k) ~Q
    transformedRatio m n k) ->
  FiniteSubset (ExceptionalIndex m n)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a1:
  positive integer sequences satisfying the given rational recurrence have
  only finitely many indices at which their doubled-plus-one terms are not
  relatively prime. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory gcdTheory pred_setTheory ratTheory;

val putnam_2025_a1 =
  ``!m n : num -> num.
      (!k : num. 0 < m k) /\
      (!k : num. 0 < n k) /\
      m 0 <> n 0 /\
      (!k : num. 0 < k ==> coprime (m k) (n k)) /\
      (!k : num.
         rat_of_num (m (k + 1)) / rat_of_num (n (k + 1)) =
           (2 * rat_of_num (m k) + 1) /
           (2 * rat_of_num (n k) + 1))
      ==>
      FINITE
        {k : num |
           ~coprime (2 * m k + 1) (2 * n k + 1)}``;

title: putnam_2025_a1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2025_a1: positive integer sequences, coprime at every positive
  index and related by the stated rational recurrence, have only finitely
  many indices at which the shifted terms fail to be coprime. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  NN0 ^m NN0 is SetMM's class of all natural-valued sequences indexed by
  the nonnegative integers, and NN is the class of positive integers. Thus
  the first two universal conditions preserve positivity at every index and
  coprimality at every positive index. Complex division restricted to
  natural inputs is exact rational division, so the displayed recurrence is
  the source equality in QQ.

  For natural numbers, relative primality is equivalent to integer gcd equal
  to one. The restricted class in the conclusion is therefore exactly the
  source exceptional set, and membership in Fin states its finiteness. The
  declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; there is no $p
  proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d k m n $.

  putnambench-putnam-2025-a1 $a |-
    A. m e. ( NN0 ^m NN0 )
      A. n e. ( NN0 ^m NN0 )
        (
          (
            (
              A. k e. NN0
                (
                  0 < ( m ` k )
                  /\
                  0 < ( n ` k )
                )
              /\
              ( m ` 0 ) =/= ( n ` 0 )
            )
            /\
            (
              A. k e. NN
                ( ( m ` k ) gcd ( n ` k ) ) = 1
              /\
              A. k e. NN0
                (
                  ( ( m ` ( k + 1 ) ) / ( n ` ( k + 1 ) ) )
                  =
                  (
                    ( ( 2 x. ( m ` k ) ) + 1 )
                    /
                    ( ( 2 x. ( n ` k ) ) + 1 )
                  )
                )
            )
          )
          ->
          {
            k e. NN0
            |
            (
              (
                ( ( 2 x. ( m ` k ) ) + 1 )
                gcd
                ( ( 2 x. ( n ` k ) ) + 1 )
              )
              =/=
              1
            )
          }
          e.
          Fin
        )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2025_a1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a1:
% distinct positive integer sequences, coprime at every positive index and
% satisfying the stated rational recurrence, have 2m_k + 1 and 2n_k + 1
% coprime for all but finitely many indices. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2025_a1: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> nat]

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  coprime_nat(left, right: nat): bool =
    FORALL (divisor: nat):
      nat_divides(divisor, left) AND nat_divides(divisor, right)
        IMPLIES divisor = 1

  ratio_recurrence(m, n: natural_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (k: nat):
      m(k + 1) * (2 * n(k) + 1)
        = (2 * m(k) + 1) * n(k + 1)

  putnam_2025_a1: bool =
    FORALL (m, n: natural_sequence):
      ((FORALL (k: nat): 0 < m(k))
        AND (FORALL (k: nat): 0 < n(k))
        AND m(0) /= n(0)
        AND (FORALL (k: nat):
          0 < k IMPLIES coprime_nat(m(k), n(k)))
        AND ratio_recurrence(m, n))
      IMPLIES
        EXISTS (cutoff: nat):
          FORALL (k: nat):
            cutoff <= k IMPLIES
              coprime_nat(2 * m(k) + 1, 2 * n(k) + 1)
END putnam_2025_a1

title: putnam_2025_a2
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench putnam_2025_a2: the sharp
   real constants bounding sine by x(PI-x) on [0, PI]; this file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2025_a2_solution : (R * R)%type :=
  (1 / PI, 4 / PI ^ 2).

Definition putnam_2025_a2_lower_bound (a : R) : Prop :=
  forall x : R,
    0 <= x /\ x <= PI ->
    a * x * (PI - x) <= sin x.

Definition putnam_2025_a2_upper_bound (b : R) : Prop :=
  forall x : R,
    0 <= x /\ x <= PI ->
    sin x <= b * x * (PI - x).

Definition putnam_2025_a2_is_greatest
    (property : R -> Prop) (greatest : R) : Prop :=
  property greatest /\
  forall candidate : R, property candidate -> candidate <= greatest.

Definition putnam_2025_a2_is_least
    (property : R -> Prop) (least : R) : Prop :=
  property least /\
  forall candidate : R, property candidate -> least <= candidate.

Theorem putnam_2025_a2 (a b : R) :
  (a, b) = putnam_2025_a2_solution <->
  putnam_2025_a2_is_greatest putnam_2025_a2_lower_bound a /\
  putnam_2025_a2_is_least putnam_2025_a2_upper_bound b.
Admitted.

definition putnam_2025_a2_solution :: "real \<times> real" where
