(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a5
   (putnambench__rocq__putnam_2025_a5): the sign sequences maximizing the
   number of permutations with prescribed adjacent rises and falls are exactly
   the two alternating sign patterns. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Lists.List Arith.PeanoNat ZArith.

Import ListNotations.

Fixpoint putnam_2025_a5_insert_everywhere
    (x : nat) (values : list nat) : list (list nat) :=
  match values with
  | [] => [[x]]
  | y :: ys =>
      (x :: y :: ys) ::
      map (cons y) (putnam_2025_a5_insert_everywhere x ys)
  end.

Fixpoint putnam_2025_a5_permutations
    (values : list nat) : list (list nat) :=
  match values with
  | [] => [[]]
  | x :: xs =>
      flat_map (putnam_2025_a5_insert_everywhere x)
        (putnam_2025_a5_permutations xs)
  end.

Definition putnam_2025_a5_satisfies
    (n : nat) (s : nat -> Z) (permutation : list nat) : bool :=
  forallb
    (fun i : nat =>
      Z.ltb 0
        (s i *
         (Z.of_nat (nth (S i) permutation 0) -
          Z.of_nat (nth i permutation 0))))
    (seq 0 n).

Definition putnam_2025_a5_f
    (n : nat) (s : nat -> Z) : nat :=
  length
    (filter
      (putnam_2025_a5_satisfies n s)
      (putnam_2025_a5_permutations (seq 0 (S n)))).

Definition putnam_2025_a5_sign_sequence
    (n : nat) (s : nat -> Z) : Prop :=
  forall i : nat,
    (i < n)%nat ->
    s i = 1%Z \/ s i = (-1)%Z.

Definition putnam_2025_a5_solution
    (n : nat) (s : nat -> Z) : Prop :=
  (forall i : nat,
      (i < n)%nat ->
      s i = Z.pow (-1) (Z.of_nat (S i))) \/
  (forall i : nat,
      (i < n)%nat ->
      s i = Z.pow (-1) (Z.of_nat i)).

Theorem putnam_2025_a5 :
  forall (n : nat) (s : nat -> Z),
    (1 <= n)%nat ->
    putnam_2025_a5_sign_sequence n s ->
    ((forall t : nat -> Z,
        putnam_2025_a5_sign_sequence n t ->
        (putnam_2025_a5_f n t <= putnam_2025_a5_f n s)%nat) <->
     putnam_2025_a5_solution n s).
Admitted.

title: putnam_2025_a5
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a5
  (putnambench__isabelle__putnam_2025_a5): the sign sequences maximizing the
  number of permutations satisfying prescribed adjacent ascent or descent
  inequalities are exactly the two alternating sign sequences. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

theory putnam_2025_a5
  imports Main
begin

definition putnam_2025_a5_sign_sequence ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> int) \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "putnam_2025_a5_sign_sequence n s \<longleftrightarrow>
    (\<forall>i<n. s i = -1 \<or> s i = 1)"

definition putnam_2025_a5_permutation :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat list \<Rightarrow> bool" where
  "putnam_2025_a5_permutation n p \<longleftrightarrow>
    length p = Suc n \<and>
    distinct p \<and>
    set p = {0..n}"

definition putnam_2025_a5_f ::
    "nat \<Rightarrow> (nat \<Rightarrow> int) \<Rightarrow> nat" where
  "putnam_2025_a5_f n s =
    card {p :: nat list.
      putnam_2025_a5_permutation n p \<and>
      (\<forall>i<n.
        0 < s i * (int (p ! Suc i) - int (p ! i)))}"

theorem putnam_2025_a5:
  fixes n :: nat
    and s :: "nat \<Rightarrow> int"
  assumes "1 \<le> n"
    and "putnam_2025_a5_sign_sequence n s"
  shows
    "(\<forall>t :: nat \<Rightarrow> int.
        putnam_2025_a5_sign_sequence n t \<longrightarrow>
          putnam_2025_a5_f n t \<le> putnam_2025_a5_f n s)
      \<longleftrightarrow>
      ((\<forall>i<n. s i = (-1 :: int) ^ (i + 1)) \<or>
       (\<forall>i<n. s i = (-1 :: int) ^ i))"
  sorry

end

  sequences that maximize the number of permutations with prescribed adjacent

title: putnam_2025_a5

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a5:
;; the sign sequences maximizing the number of compatible permutations are
;; exactly the two alternating sign sequences. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; A function Fin n -> Z-units is exactly a length-n list with every entry
;; equal to 1 or -1. Likewise, a permutation of Fin (n+1) is represented by
;; its value list on the increasing domain 0,...,n. The generators below
;; enumerate both finite function spaces completely, so the internal
;; maximality check preserves the source's universal quantifier over t.

(defun putnam-2025-a5-range-from (start count)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      nil
    (cons start
          (putnam-2025-a5-range-from
           (+ start 1) (- count 1)))))

(defun putnam-2025-a5-prefix-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (cons (cons item (car lists))
          (putnam-2025-a5-prefix-each
           item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-2025-a5-insert-everywhere (item list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list (list item))
    (cons
     (cons item list)
     (putnam-2025-a5-prefix-each
      (car list)
      (putnam-2025-a5-insert-everywhere
       item (cdr list))))))

(defun putnam-2025-a5-insert-into-each (item lists)
  (if (endp lists)
      nil
    (append
     (putnam-2025-a5-insert-everywhere
      item (car lists))
     (putnam-2025-a5-insert-into-each
      item (cdr lists)))))

(defun putnam-2025-a5-permutations (list)
  (if (endp list)
      (list nil)
    (putnam-2025-a5-insert-into-each
     (car list)
     (putnam-2025-a5-permutations (cdr list)))))

(defun putnam-2025-a5-sign-sequence-p (signs n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (equal signs nil)
    (and
     (consp signs)
     (or (equal (car signs) 1)
         (equal (car signs) -1))
     (putnam-2025-a5-sign-sequence-p
      (cdr signs) (- n 1)))))

(defun putnam-2025-a5-prefix-sign (sign sequences)
  (if (endp sequences)
      nil
    (cons
     (cons sign (car sequences))
     (putnam-2025-a5-prefix-sign
      sign (cdr sequences)))))

(defun putnam-2025-a5-all-sign-sequences (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      (list nil)
    (let ((tails
           (putnam-2025-a5-all-sign-sequences
            (- n 1))))
      (append
       (putnam-2025-a5-prefix-sign 1 tails)
       (putnam-2025-a5-prefix-sign -1 tails)))))

;; Reading a permutation list from left to right, this is exactly
;; s_i * (a_(i+1) - a_i) > 0 at every index.

(defun putnam-2025-a5-compatible-p (signs permutation)
  (if (endp signs)
      t
    (and
     (consp permutation)
     (consp (cdr permutation))
     (< 0
        (* (car signs)
           (- (car (cdr permutation))
              (car permutation))))
     (putnam-2025-a5-compatible-p
      (cdr signs) (cdr permutation)))))

(defun putnam-2025-a5-count-compatible
    (signs permutations)
  (if (endp permutations)
      0
    (+ (if (putnam-2025-a5-compatible-p
            signs (car permutations))
           1
         0)
       (putnam-2025-a5-count-compatible
        signs (cdr permutations)))))

(defun putnam-2025-a5-all-counts-at-most-p
    (sequences bound permutations)
  (if (endp sequences)
      t
    (and
     (<=
      (putnam-2025-a5-count-compatible
       (car sequences) permutations)
      bound)
     (putnam-2025-a5-all-counts-at-most-p
      (cdr sequences) bound permutations))))

(defun putnam-2025-a5-alternating-from-p
    (signs expected)
  (if (endp signs)
      (equal signs nil)
    (and
     (equal (car signs) expected)
     (putnam-2025-a5-alternating-from-p
      (cdr signs) (- expected)))))

(defun putnam-2025-a5-solution-p (signs)
  (or
   (putnam-2025-a5-alternating-from-p signs 1)
   (putnam-2025-a5-alternating-from-p signs -1)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2025-a5-statement (n signs)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp n)
    (<= 1 n)
    (putnam-2025-a5-sign-sequence-p signs n))
   (let* ((permutations
           (putnam-2025-a5-permutations
            (putnam-2025-a5-range-from 0 (+ n 1))))
          (sign-sequences
           (putnam-2025-a5-all-sign-sequences n))
          (selected-count
           (putnam-2025-a5-count-compatible
            signs permutations)))
     (iff
      (putnam-2025-a5-all-counts-at-most-p
       sign-sequences selected-count permutations)
      (putnam-2025-a5-solution-p signs)))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2025_a5
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2025_a5): the sign sequences maximizing the
-- number of permutations with prescribed adjacent ascent and descent signs
-- are exactly the two alternating sequences. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2025A5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; true; false)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 5 _::_
infixr 3 _andB_
infixr 2 _or_

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left-injection  : A -> A or B
  right-injection : B -> A or B

record Iff (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor equivalence
  field
    forward  : A -> B
    backward : B -> A

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

toNat : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
toNat fzero =
  zero
toNat (fsuc index) =
  suc (toNat index)

data Vec (A : Set) : Nat -> Set where
  []   : Vec A zero
  _::_ : {n : Nat} -> A -> Vec A n -> Vec A (suc n)

data List (A : Set) : Set where
  []L   : List A
  _::L_ : A -> List A -> List A

mapList :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  List A ->
  List B
mapList function []L =
  []L
mapList function (x ::L xs) =
  function x ::L mapList function xs

appendList :
  {A : Set} ->
  List A ->
  List A ->
  List A
appendList []L ys =
  ys
appendList (x ::L xs) ys =
  x ::L appendList xs ys

concatMap :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> List B) ->
  List A ->
  List B
concatMap function []L =
  []L
concatMap function (x ::L xs) =
  appendList (function x) (concatMap function xs)

allFin : (n : Nat) -> List (Fin n)
allFin zero =
  []L
allFin (suc n) =
  fzero ::L mapList fsuc (allFin n)

allVectors :
  {A : Set} ->
  (length : Nat) ->
  List A ->
  List (Vec A length)
allVectors zero alphabet =
  [] ::L []L
allVectors (suc length) alphabet =
  concatMap
    (\ x ->
      mapList
        (\ tail -> x :: tail)
        (allVectors length alphabet))
    alphabet

notB : Bool -> Bool
notB true =
  false
notB false =
  true

_andB_ : Bool -> Bool -> Bool
true andB right =
  right
false andB right =
  false

finEqual : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin n -> Bool
finEqual fzero fzero =
  true
finEqual fzero (fsuc right) =
  false
finEqual (fsuc left) fzero =
  false
finEqual (fsuc left) (fsuc right) =
  finEqual left right

memberFin :
  {bound length : Nat} ->
  Fin bound ->
  Vec (Fin bound) length ->
  Bool
memberFin value [] =
  false
memberFin value (x :: xs) with finEqual value x
... | true =
  true
... | false =
  memberFin value xs

allDistinct :
  {bound length : Nat} ->
  Vec (Fin bound) length ->
  Bool
allDistinct [] =
  true
allDistinct (x :: xs) =
  notB (memberFin x xs) andB allDistinct xs

lessNat : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
lessNat zero zero =
  false
lessNat zero (suc right) =
  true
lessNat (suc left) zero =
  false
lessNat (suc left) (suc right) =
  lessNat left right

data Sign : Set where
  plus  : Sign
  minus : Sign

signedIncrease :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Sign ->
  Fin n ->
  Fin n ->
  Bool
signedIncrease plus left-value right-value =
  lessNat (toNat left-value) (toNat right-value)
signedIncrease minus left-value right-value =
  lessNat (toNat right-value) (toNat left-value)

hasRequiredSigns :
  {n bound : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Sign) ->
  Vec (Fin bound) (suc n) ->
  Bool
hasRequiredSigns {zero} signs (x :: []) =
  true
hasRequiredSigns {suc n} signs (x :: y :: rest) =
  signedIncrease (signs fzero) x y
  andB
  hasRequiredSigns
    (\ index -> signs (fsuc index))
    (y :: rest)

isQualifyingPermutation :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Sign) ->
  Vec (Fin (suc n)) (suc n) ->
  Bool
isQualifyingPermutation signs values =
  allDistinct values andB hasRequiredSigns signs values

countSatisfying :
  {A : Set} ->
  (A -> Bool) ->
  List A ->
  Nat
countSatisfying predicate []L =
  zero
countSatisfying predicate (x ::L xs) with predicate x
... | true =
  suc (countSatisfying predicate xs)
... | false =
  countSatisfying predicate xs

f : (n : Nat) -> (Fin n -> Sign) -> Nat
f n signs =
  countSatisfying
    (isQualifyingPermutation signs)
    (allVectors (suc n) (allFin (suc n)))

flipSign : Sign -> Sign
flipSign plus =
  minus
flipSign minus =
  plus

alternatingFrom :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Sign ->
  Fin n ->
  Sign
alternatingFrom start fzero =
  start
alternatingFrom start (fsuc index) =
  alternatingFrom (flipSign start) index

PointwiseEqual :
  {A B : Set} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set
PointwiseEqual {A} left-function right-function =
  (x : A) ->
  left-function x == right-function x

AlternatingSolution :
  {n : Nat} ->
  (Fin n -> Sign) ->
  Set
AlternatingSolution signs =
  PointwiseEqual signs (alternatingFrom minus)
  or
  PointwiseEqual signs (alternatingFrom plus)

putnam-2025-a5 : Set
putnam-2025-a5 =
  (n : Nat) ->
  Positive n ->
  (signs : Fin n -> Sign) ->
  Iff
    ((other-signs : Fin n -> Sign) ->
      f n other-signs <=N f n signs)
    (AlternatingSolution signs)

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a5
  (putnambench__hol4__putnam_2025_a5): the sign sequences maximizing the
  number of permutations with prescribed consecutive ascent and descent
  directions are exactly the two alternating sequences. This file contains
  no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory integerTheory listTheory pred_setTheory;

val putnam_2025_a5 =
  ``let valid_signs =
      \n : num.
      \s : int list.
        LENGTH s = n /\
        EVERY (\x : int. x = 1 \/ x = ~1) s
    in
    let f =
      \n : num.
      \s : int list.
        CARD
          {p : num list |
             PERM p (GENLIST I (n + 1)) /\
             !i : num.
               i < n
               ==>
               0 <
                 EL i s *
                   (int_of_num (EL (SUC i) p) -
                    int_of_num (EL i p))}
    in
    let alternating =
      \n : num.
      \s : int list.
        (!i : num.
           i < n
           ==>
           EL i s = (~1 : int) ** (i + 1)) \/
        (!i : num.
           i < n
           ==>
           EL i s = (~1 : int) ** i)
    in
      !n : num. !s : int list.
        1 <= n /\ valid_signs n s
        ==>
        ((!t : int list.
            valid_signs n t
            ==>
            f n t <= f n s)
         <=>
         alternating n s)``;

$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2025_a5 (putnambench__metamath__putnam_2025_a5): the sign
  sequences maximizing the number of permutations with prescribed adjacent
  ascent and descent directions are exactly the two alternating sequences.
  This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  For positive n, 0 ..^ n is the canonical n-element carrier corresponding
  to Fin n, and { -u 1 , 1 } ^m ( 0 ..^ n ) is the full space of sign
  functions, exactly representing the integer units in the Lean source.
  A bijection p of 0 ..^ ( n + 1 ) represents a permutation of Fin (n+1).

  For each sign function, the restricted class counted by # contains exactly
  those permutations for which every signed adjacent difference is positive.
  The universal comparison with every sign function therefore states that s
  maximizes this count. The biconditional identifies the maximizers as the
  two alternating sign functions, with the two possible initial signs.

  The source parameter n counts signs rather than permutation entries, so
  n e. NN is equivalent to its hypothesis 1 <= n and to the informal
  requirement that the permutation have at least two entries. The declaration
  below is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database contains no
  $p proof declaration.
$)

${
  $d i n p s t $.

  putnambench-putnam-2025-a5 $a |-
    A. n e. NN
      A. s e. ( { -u 1 , 1 } ^m ( 0 ..^ n ) )
        (
          A. t e. ( { -u 1 , 1 } ^m ( 0 ..^ n ) )
            (
              #
              `
              {
                p |
                (
                  p
                  :
                  ( 0 ..^ ( n + 1 ) )
                  -1-1-onto->
                  ( 0 ..^ ( n + 1 ) )
                  /\
                  A. i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                    0
                    <
                    (
                      ( t ` i )
                      x.
                      (
                        ( p ` ( i + 1 ) )
                        -
                        ( p ` i )
                      )
                    )
                )
              }
            )
            <_
            (
              #
              `
              {
                p |
                (
                  p
                  :
                  ( 0 ..^ ( n + 1 ) )
                  -1-1-onto->
                  ( 0 ..^ ( n + 1 ) )
                  /\
                  A. i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
                    0
                    <
                    (
                      ( s ` i )
                      x.
                      (
                        ( p ` ( i + 1 ) )
                        -
                        ( p ` i )
                      )
                    )
                )
              }
            )
          <->
          (
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
              ( s ` i ) = ( ( -u 1 ) ^ ( i + 1 ) )
            \/
            A. i e. ( 0 ..^ n )
              ( s ` i ) = ( ( -u 1 ) ^ i )
          )
        )
  $.
$}

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a5
% (putnambench__pvs__putnam_2025_a5): the sign sequences maximizing the
% number of permutations with prescribed adjacent ascent and descent signs
% are exactly the two alternating sign sequences. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2025_a5: THEORY
BEGIN
  sign_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> int]

  admissible_sign_sequence(n: nat, s: sign_sequence): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < n IMPLIES (s(index) = 1 OR s(index) = -1)

  permutation_code_count(n: nat): nat =
    (n + 1) ^ (n + 1)

  permutation_entry(code, index, n: nat): nat =
    mod(ndiv(code, (n + 1) ^ index), n + 1)

  permutation_code(code, n: nat): bool =
    code < permutation_code_count(n)
      AND
        (FORALL (left, right: nat):
          (left < n + 1
            AND right < n + 1
            AND permutation_entry(code, left, n)
              = permutation_entry(code, right, n))
          IMPLIES left = right)

  satisfies_signs(
      code, n: nat,
      s: sign_sequence): bool =
    permutation_code(code, n)
      AND
        (FORALL (index: nat):
          index < n IMPLIES
            0
              < s(index)
                  * ((permutation_entry(code, index + 1, n) :: int)
                      - (permutation_entry(code, index, n) :: int)))

  qualifying_permutation_count(
      n: nat,
      s: sign_sequence,
      limit: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF limit = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      qualifying_permutation_count(n, s, limit - 1)
        + IF satisfies_signs(limit - 1, n, s) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE limit

  f(n: nat, s: sign_sequence): nat =
    qualifying_permutation_count(
      n, s, permutation_code_count(n))

  alternating_sign(index: nat): int =
    IF mod(index, 2) = 0 THEN 1 ELSE -1 ENDIF

  alternating_solution(n: nat, s: sign_sequence): bool =
    (FORALL (index: nat):
      index < n IMPLIES
        s(index) = alternating_sign(index + 1))
      OR
        (FORALL (index: nat):
          index < n IMPLIES
            s(index) = alternating_sign(index))

  putnam_2025_a5: bool =
    FORALL (n: nat), (s: sign_sequence):
      (1 <= n AND admissible_sign_sequence(n, s))
        IMPLIES
          ((FORALL (t: sign_sequence):
              admissible_sign_sequence(n, t)
                IMPLIES f(n, t) <= f(n, s))
            IFF alternating_solution(n, s))
END putnam_2025_a5

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a6:
;; exact 2-adic divisibility of differences formed from a recursively defined
;; integer sequence. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; On natural inputs this is exactly b_0 = 0 and
;; b_(n+1) = 2*b_n^2 + b_n + 1 from the source.
(defun putnam-2025-a6-b (n)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      0
    (let ((previous
           (putnam-2025-a6-b (- n 1))))
      (+ (* 2 previous previous)
         previous
         1))))

;; Both moduli are positive powers of 2, so remainder zero is equivalent to
;; integer divisibility. The second conjunct states exact nondivisibility by
;; the next power.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2025-a6-statement (k)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp k)
    (<= 1 k))
   (let* ((b-at-power
           (putnam-2025-a6-b (expt 2 k)))
          (b-at-next-power
           (putnam-2025-a6-b (expt 2 (+ k 1))))
          (difference
           (- b-at-next-power (* 2 b-at-power)))
          (lower-modulus
           (expt 2 (+ (* 2 k) 2)))
          (upper-modulus
           (expt 2 (+ (* 2 k) 3))))
     (and
      (equal (mod difference lower-modulus) 0)
      (not
       (equal (mod difference upper-modulus) 0))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_a6
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2025_a6): exact powers of two dividing a
-- difference formed from a recursively defined integer sequence. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Main where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Int using (Int; pos; negsuc)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_ _divides_
infixr 3 _and_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

negative : Nat -> Int
negative zero =
  pos zero
negative (suc n) =
  negsuc n

negateInt : Int -> Int
negateInt (pos n) =
  negative n
negateInt (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc n)

differenceNat : Nat -> Nat -> Int
differenceNat zero zero =
  pos zero
differenceNat (suc m) zero =
  pos (suc m)
differenceNat zero (suc n) =
  negsuc n
differenceNat (suc m) (suc n) =
  differenceNat m n

addInt : Int -> Int -> Int
addInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m + n)
addInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  differenceNat m (suc n)
addInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  differenceNat n (suc m)
addInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  negsuc (suc (m + n))

subtractInt : Int -> Int -> Int
subtractInt x y =
  addInt x (negateInt y)

multiplyInt : Int -> Int -> Int
multiplyInt (pos m) (pos n) =
  pos (m * n)
multiplyInt (pos m) (negsuc n) =
  negative (m * suc n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (pos n) =
  negative (suc m * n)
multiplyInt (negsuc m) (negsuc n) =
  pos (suc m * suc n)

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

three : Nat
three =
  suc two

naturalPower : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalPower base zero =
  one
naturalPower base (suc exponent) =
  base * naturalPower base exponent

integerPower : Int -> Nat -> Int
integerPower base zero =
  pos one
integerPower base (suc exponent) =
  multiplyInt base (integerPower base exponent)

b : Nat -> Int
b zero =
  pos zero
b (suc n) =
  addInt
    (addInt
      (multiplyInt
        (pos two)
        (integerPower (b n) two))
      (b n))
    (pos one)

_divides_ : Int -> Int -> Set
divisor divides dividend =
  Exists Int
    (\ quotient ->
      dividend == multiplyInt divisor quotient)

sequenceDifference : Nat -> Int
sequenceDifference k =
  subtractInt
    (b (naturalPower two (k + one)))
    (multiplyInt
      (pos two)
      (b (naturalPower two k)))

putnam-2025-a6 : Set
putnam-2025-a6 =
  (k : Nat) ->
  one <=N k ->
  (pos (naturalPower two (two * k + two))
    divides sequenceDifference k)
  and
  Not
    (pos (naturalPower two (two * k + three))
      divides sequenceDifference k)

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b1:
   a two-coloring of the real plane closed under circumcenters of monochromatic
   noncollinear triples is constant. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals Bool.Bool.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2025_b1_point : Type := (R * R)%type.

Definition putnam_2025_b1_noncollinear
    (A B C : putnam_2025_b1_point) : Prop :=
  (fst B - fst A) * (snd C - snd A) -
  (snd B - snd A) * (fst C - fst A) <> 0.

Definition putnam_2025_b1_squared_distance
    (P Q : putnam_2025_b1_point) : R :=
  (fst P - fst Q) ^ 2 + (snd P - snd Q) ^ 2.

Definition putnam_2025_b1_is_circumcenter
    (A B C O : putnam_2025_b1_point) : Prop :=
  putnam_2025_b1_squared_distance O A =
    putnam_2025_b1_squared_distance O B /\
  putnam_2025_b1_squared_distance O A =
    putnam_2025_b1_squared_distance O C.

Theorem putnam_2025_b1
    (color : putnam_2025_b1_point -> bool)
    (h :
      forall A B C : putnam_2025_b1_point,
        putnam_2025_b1_noncollinear A B C ->
        color A = color B ->
        color A = color C ->
        forall O : putnam_2025_b1_point,
          putnam_2025_b1_is_circumcenter A B C O ->
          color O = color A) :
  exists c : bool,
    forall P : putnam_2025_b1_point, color P = c.

  (putnambench__hol-light__putnam_2025_b1): every two-coloring of the real
  plane that preserves the color of monochromatic noncollinear triples at
  their circumcenters is constant. This file contains no proof.
*)

let statement =
  `let squared_distance =
     \(P:real#real) (Q:real#real).
       (FST P - FST Q) pow 2 + (SND P - SND Q) pow 2 in
   let noncollinear =
     \(A:real#real) (B:real#real) (C:real#real).
       ~((FST B - FST A) * (SND C - SND A) =
         (SND B - SND A) * (FST C - FST A)) in
   !color:(real#real)->bool.
     (!A B C O:real#real.
        noncollinear A B C /\
        color A = color B /\
        color A = color C /\
        squared_distance O A = squared_distance O B /\
        squared_distance O A = squared_distance O C
        ==> color O = color A)
     ==> ?c:bool. !P:real#real. color P = c`;;

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench artifact putnam_2025_b1:
;; a two-coloring of the plane that assigns every noncollinear monochromatic
;; triangle's circumcenter the same color is constant. This file contains no
;; proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Circumcenters are rational expressions in the six point coordinates.
;; Conservative generic symbols therefore give ACL2 the exact first-order
;; theorem schema over the real field, without restricting the coloring to an
;; APPLY$ function object or introducing any axiom event.
(defstub p2025b1-scalar-p (x) t)
(defstub p2025b1-add-op (x y) t)
(defstub p2025b1-multiply-op (x y) t)
(defstub p2025b1-negate-op (x) t)
(defstub p2025b1-inverse-op (x) t)
(defstub p2025b1-color (x y) t)

(defun p2025b1-add (x y)
  (p2025b1-add-op x y))

(defun p2025b1-mul (x y)
  (p2025b1-multiply-op x y))

(defun p2025b1-neg (x)
  (p2025b1-negate-op x))

(defun p2025b1-inv (x)
  (p2025b1-inverse-op x))

(defun p2025b1-sub (x y)
  (p2025b1-add x (p2025b1-neg y)))

(defun p2025b1-square (x)
  (p2025b1-mul x x))

(defun p2025b1-two (one)
  (p2025b1-add one one))

(defun p2025b1-nat-value (n zero one)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix n)))
  (if (zp n)
      zero
    (p2025b1-add
     (p2025b1-nat-value (1- n) zero one)
     one)))

(defun-sk p2025b1-field-laws-p (zero one)
  (forall (x y z)
    (implies
     (and
      (p2025b1-scalar-p x)
      (p2025b1-scalar-p y)
      (p2025b1-scalar-p z))
     (and
      (p2025b1-scalar-p (p2025b1-add x y))
      (p2025b1-scalar-p (p2025b1-mul x y))
      (p2025b1-scalar-p (p2025b1-neg x))
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (p2025b1-scalar-p (p2025b1-inv x)))
      (equal (p2025b1-add (p2025b1-add x y) z)
             (p2025b1-add x (p2025b1-add y z)))
      (equal (p2025b1-add x y)
             (p2025b1-add y x))
      (equal (p2025b1-add x zero) x)
      (equal (p2025b1-add x (p2025b1-neg x)) zero)
      (equal (p2025b1-mul (p2025b1-mul x y) z)
             (p2025b1-mul x (p2025b1-mul y z)))
      (equal (p2025b1-mul x y)
             (p2025b1-mul y x))
      (equal (p2025b1-mul x one) x)
      (implies
       (not (equal x zero))
       (equal (p2025b1-mul x (p2025b1-inv x)) one))
      (equal
       (p2025b1-mul x (p2025b1-add y z))
       (p2025b1-add (p2025b1-mul x y)
                    (p2025b1-mul x z)))))))

(defun-sk p2025b1-characteristic-zero-p (zero one)
  (forall (n)
    (implies
     (and (natp n) (< 0 n))
     (not
      (equal
       (p2025b1-nat-value n zero one)
       zero)))))

(defun p2025b1-field-p (zero one)
  (and
   (p2025b1-scalar-p zero)
   (p2025b1-scalar-p one)
   (not (equal zero one))
   (p2025b1-field-laws-p zero one)
   (p2025b1-characteristic-zero-p zero one)))

(defun p2025b1-boolean-p (value)
  (or (equal value nil)
      (equal value t)))

(defun-sk p2025b1-coloring-p ()
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (p2025b1-scalar-p x)
      (p2025b1-scalar-p y))
     (p2025b1-boolean-p
      (p2025b1-color x y)))))

(defun p2025b1-determinant
    (ax ay bx by cx cy one)
  (p2025b1-mul
   (p2025b1-two one)
   (p2025b1-add
    (p2025b1-mul ax (p2025b1-sub by cy))
    (p2025b1-add
     (p2025b1-mul bx (p2025b1-sub cy ay))
     (p2025b1-mul cx (p2025b1-sub ay by))))))

(defun p2025b1-radius-square-term (x y)
  (p2025b1-add
   (p2025b1-square x)
   (p2025b1-square y)))

(defun p2025b1-center-x-numerator
    (ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (p2025b1-add
   (p2025b1-mul
    (p2025b1-radius-square-term ax ay)
    (p2025b1-sub by cy))
   (p2025b1-add
    (p2025b1-mul
     (p2025b1-radius-square-term bx by)
     (p2025b1-sub cy ay))
    (p2025b1-mul
     (p2025b1-radius-square-term cx cy)
     (p2025b1-sub ay by)))))

(defun p2025b1-center-y-numerator
    (ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (p2025b1-add
   (p2025b1-mul
    (p2025b1-radius-square-term ax ay)
    (p2025b1-sub cx bx))
   (p2025b1-add
    (p2025b1-mul
     (p2025b1-radius-square-term bx by)
     (p2025b1-sub ax cx))
    (p2025b1-mul
     (p2025b1-radius-square-term cx cy)
     (p2025b1-sub bx ax)))))

(defun p2025b1-center-x
    (ax ay bx by cx cy one)
  (p2025b1-mul
   (p2025b1-center-x-numerator ax ay bx by cx cy)
   (p2025b1-inv
    (p2025b1-determinant ax ay bx by cx cy one))))

(defun p2025b1-center-y
    (ax ay bx by cx cy one)
  (p2025b1-mul
   (p2025b1-center-y-numerator ax ay bx by cx cy)
   (p2025b1-inv
    (p2025b1-determinant ax ay bx by cx cy one))))

(defun p2025b1-same-color-p
    (ax ay bx by cx cy)
  (and
   (equal (p2025b1-color ax ay)
          (p2025b1-color bx by))
   (equal (p2025b1-color ax ay)
          (p2025b1-color cx cy))))

(defun-sk p2025b1-circumcenter-closure-p (zero one)
  (forall (ax ay bx by cx cy)
    (implies
     (and
      (p2025b1-scalar-p ax)
      (p2025b1-scalar-p ay)
      (p2025b1-scalar-p bx)
      (p2025b1-scalar-p by)
      (p2025b1-scalar-p cx)
      (p2025b1-scalar-p cy)
      (not
       (equal
        (p2025b1-determinant ax ay bx by cx cy one)
        zero))
      (p2025b1-same-color-p ax ay bx by cx cy))
     (equal
      (p2025b1-color
       (p2025b1-center-x ax ay bx by cx cy one)
       (p2025b1-center-y ax ay bx by cx cy one))
      (p2025b1-color ax ay)))))

(defun-sk p2025b1-all-color-p (color-value)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (p2025b1-scalar-p x)
      (p2025b1-scalar-p y))
     (equal
      (p2025b1-color x y)
      color-value))))

(defun p2025b1-monochromatic-p ()
  (or
   (p2025b1-all-color-p nil)
   (p2025b1-all-color-p t)))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2025-b1-statement
    (zero one)
  (implies
   (and
    (p2025b1-field-p zero one)
    (p2025b1-coloring-p)
    (p2025b1-circumcenter-closure-p zero one))
   (p2025b1-monochromatic-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2025_b1
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b1
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2025_b1): a two-coloring of the real plane that
-- preserves the color of every monochromatic noncollinear triangle at its
-- circumcenter is constant. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2025B1 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc)

infix 4 _!=_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) -> add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z == multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) -> fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) -> P x -> lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R
square reals x =
  multiply reals x x

two :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R
two reals =
  add reals (oneR reals) (oneR reals)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals numerator denominator =
  multiply reals numerator (inverse reals denominator)

record Point (R : Set) : Set where
  constructor point
  field
    x-coordinate : R
    y-coordinate : R

open Point

point-square :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  R
point-square reals p =
  add reals
    (square reals (x-coordinate p))
    (square reals (y-coordinate p))

signed-area :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
signed-area reals a b c =
  add reals
    (multiply reals
      (x-coordinate a)
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate b) (y-coordinate c)))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals
        (x-coordinate b)
        (subtract reals (y-coordinate c) (y-coordinate a)))
      (multiply reals
        (x-coordinate c)
        (subtract reals (y-coordinate a) (y-coordinate b))))

Noncollinear :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
Noncollinear reals a b c =
  signed-area reals a b c != zeroR reals

circumcenter-denominator :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
circumcenter-denominator reals a b c =
  multiply reals (two reals) (signed-area reals a b c)

circumcenter-x-numerator :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
circumcenter-x-numerator reals a b c =
  add reals
    (multiply reals
      (point-square reals a)
      (subtract reals (y-coordinate b) (y-coordinate c)))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals
        (point-square reals b)
        (subtract reals (y-coordinate c) (y-coordinate a)))
      (multiply reals
        (point-square reals c)
        (subtract reals (y-coordinate a) (y-coordinate b))))

circumcenter-y-numerator :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  R
circumcenter-y-numerator reals a b c =
  add reals
    (multiply reals
      (point-square reals a)
      (subtract reals (x-coordinate c) (x-coordinate b)))
    (add reals
      (multiply reals
        (point-square reals b)
        (subtract reals (x-coordinate a) (x-coordinate c)))
      (multiply reals
        (point-square reals c)
        (subtract reals (x-coordinate b) (x-coordinate a))))

circumcenter :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R
circumcenter reals a b c =
  point
    (divide reals
      (circumcenter-x-numerator reals a b c)
      (circumcenter-denominator reals a b c))
    (divide reals
      (circumcenter-y-numerator reals a b c)
      (circumcenter-denominator reals a b c))

Monochromatic :
  {R : Set} ->
  (Point R -> Bool) ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Point R ->
  Set
Monochromatic color a b c =
  color a == color b and color a == color c

module Putnam2025B1Statement
  {R : Set}
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) where

  Plane : Set
  Plane =
    Point R

  proposition : Set
  proposition =
    (color : Plane -> Bool) ->
    ((a b c : Plane) ->
      Noncollinear reals a b c ->
      Monochromatic color a b c ->
      color (circumcenter reals a b c) == color a) ->
    Exists Bool
      (\ constant-color ->
        (p : Plane) ->
        color p == constant-color)

putnam-2025-b1 : Set1
putnam-2025-b1 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  Putnam2025B1Statement.proposition reals

title: putnam_2025_b1
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b1:
  a Boolean coloring of the real Euclidean plane that preserves the color of
  every noncollinear triangle at its circumcenter is constant. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pairTheory realTheory;

val putnam_2025_b1 =
  ``let cross =
      \A B C : real # real.
        (FST B - FST A) * (SND C - SND A) -
        (SND B - SND A) * (FST C - FST A)
    in
    let noncollinear =
      \A B C : real # real. cross A B C <> 0
    in
    let squared_distance =
      \P Q : real # real.
        (FST P - FST Q) pow 2 + (SND P - SND Q) pow 2
    in
    let circumcenter =
      \A B C : real # real.
        @center : real # real.
          squared_distance center A = squared_distance center B /\
          squared_distance center B = squared_distance center C
    in
      !color : (real # real) -> bool.
        (!A B C : real # real.
           noncollinear A B C /\
           color A = color B /\
           color A = color C
           ==>
           color (circumcenter A B C) = color A)
        ==>
        ?c : bool.
          !P : real # real. color P = c``;

title: putnam_2025_b1
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact
  putnam_2025_b1 (putnambench__metamath__putnam_2025_b1): every red-green
  coloring of the real Euclidean plane that preserves color at the
  circumcenter of each monochromatic noncollinear triple is constant. This
  file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  P25B1R2 is the full real coordinate plane. P25B1DistSq is squared
  Euclidean distance, P25B1Noncol is determinant noncollinearity, and
  P25B1Circumcenter O A B C says that O is equidistant from A, B, and C.
  Under P25B1Noncol A B C, that equidistant point exists uniquely and is
  exactly the circumcenter of the corresponding ordered 2-simplex.

  Relabeling the two coordinates from Fin 2 to 1 ... 2 is an isometry, and
  the two-element ordinal 2o = {0,1} is a definitional encoding of Bool.
  The condition that all three vertex colors agree is written using two
  equalities. Thus the final declaration retains the arbitrary coloring,
  every noncollinear triple, its circumcenter, and the internally
  existential constant color. It is a single unproved $a corpus statement;
  this database contains no $p proof declaration.
$)

$c P25B1I P25B1R2 P25B1DistSq P25B1Noncol P25B1Circumcenter $.

p25b1-index-syntax $a class P25B1I $.
p25b1-plane-syntax $a class P25B1R2 $.
p25b1-distance-square-syntax $a class ( P25B1DistSq A B ) $.
p25b1-noncollinear-syntax $a wff ( P25B1Noncol A B C ) $.
p25b1-circumcenter-syntax $a wff ( P25B1Circumcenter O A B C ) $.

p25b1-index-definition $a |- P25B1I = ( 1 ... 2 ) $.

p25b1-plane-definition $a |- P25B1R2 = ( RR ^m P25B1I ) $.

${
  $d A B k $.

  p25b1-distance-square-definition $a |- (
    P25B1DistSq A B
  ) = (
    sum_ k e. P25B1I
      ( ( ( A ` k ) - ( B ` k ) ) ^ 2 )
  ) $.
$}

p25b1-noncollinear-definition $a |- (
  ( P25B1Noncol A B C )
  <->
  (
    (
      ( ( B ` 1 ) - ( A ` 1 ) )
      x.
      ( ( C ` 2 ) - ( A ` 2 ) )
    )
    =/=
    (
      ( ( B ` 2 ) - ( A ` 2 ) )
      x.
      ( ( C ` 1 ) - ( A ` 1 ) )
    )
  )
) $.

p25b1-circumcenter-definition $a |- (
  ( P25B1Circumcenter O A B C )
  <->
  (
    ( P25B1DistSq O A ) = ( P25B1DistSq O B )
    /\
    ( P25B1DistSq O A ) = ( P25B1DistSq O C )
  )
) $.

${
  $d A B C O P c f $.

  putnambench-putnam-2025-b1 $a |-
    A. f e. ( 2o ^m P25B1R2 )
      (
        (
          A. A e. P25B1R2
          A. B e. P25B1R2
          A. C e. P25B1R2
          A. O e. P25B1R2
            (
              (
                ( P25B1Noncol A B C )
                /\
                ( P25B1Circumcenter O A B C )
              )
              ->
              (
                (
                  ( f ` A ) = ( f ` B )
                  /\
                  ( f ` A ) = ( f ` C )
                )
                ->
                ( f ` O ) = ( f ` A )
              )
            )
        )
        ->
        E. c e. 2o
          A. P e. P25B1R2
            ( f ` P ) = c
      )
  $.
$}

title: putnam_2025_b1
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b1:
% every two-coloring of the real plane that preserves the color of each
% monochromatic noncollinear triple at its circumcenter is constant.
% This file contains no proof.

putnam_2025_b1: THEORY
BEGIN
  point: TYPE = [# x_coord: real, y_coord: real #]
  coloring: TYPE = [point -> bool]

  cross_from(A, B, C: point): real =
    (x_coord(B) - x_coord(A)) * (y_coord(C) - y_coord(A))
      - (y_coord(B) - y_coord(A)) * (x_coord(C) - x_coord(A))

  noncollinear(A, B, C: point): bool =
    cross_from(A, B, C) /= 0

  squared_distance(P, Q: point): real =
    (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q)) * (x_coord(P) - x_coord(Q))
      + (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q)) * (y_coord(P) - y_coord(Q))

  circumcenter(A, B, C: point): point =
    epsilon(
      LAMBDA (O: point):
        squared_distance(O, A) = squared_distance(O, B)
          AND squared_distance(O, A) = squared_distance(O, C))

  same_color(color: coloring, A, B, C: point): bool =
    color(A) = color(B) AND color(A) = color(C)

  circumcenter_closed(color: coloring): bool =
    FORALL (A, B, C: point):
      (noncollinear(A, B, C)
        AND same_color(color, A, B, C))
      IMPLIES color(circumcenter(A, B, C)) = color(A)

  putnam_2025_b1: bool =
    FORALL (color: coloring):
      circumcenter_closed(color)
        IMPLIES
          EXISTS (constant_color: bool):
            FORALL (P: point):
              color(P) = constant_color
END putnam_2025_b1

title: putnam_2025_b2
content:
import Mathlib

open Set Real MeasureTheory Interval

/--
Let $f: [0,1] \to [0, \infty)$ be strictly increasing and continuous.
Let $R$ be the region bounded by $x = 0$, $x = 1$, $y = 0$, and $y = f(x)$.
Let $x_1$ be the $x$-coordinate of the centroid of $R$.
Let $x_2$ be the $x$-coordinate of the centroid of the solid generated by rotating $R$ about the $x$-axis.
Prove that $x_1 < x_2$.
-/
theorem putnam_2025_b2
    (f : ℝ → ℝ)
    (hf_cont : ContinuousOn f (Icc 0 1))
    (hf_mono : StrictMonoOn f (Icc 0 1))
    (hf_nonneg : ∀ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, 0 ≤ f x) :
    (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, x * f x) / (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, f x) <
    (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, x * (f x) ^ 2) / (∫ x in (0:ℝ)..1, (f x) ^ 2) := by
  sorry

title: putnam_2025_b2
content:
(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b2
   (putnambench__rocq__putnam_2025_b2): comparison of the normalized first
   moments determining the centroid abscissas of a planar region and its
   solid of revolution; this file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Reals ClassicalEpsilon RiemannInt.

Open Scope R_scope.

Definition putnam_2025_b2_unit_interval (x : R) : Prop :=
  0 <= x <= 1.

Definition putnam_2025_b2_continuous_on_unit
    (f : R -> R) : Prop :=
  forall x : R,
    putnam_2025_b2_unit_interval x ->
    forall epsilon : R,
      epsilon > 0 ->
      exists delta : R,
        delta > 0 /\
        forall y : R,
          putnam_2025_b2_unit_interval y ->
          Rabs (y - x) < delta ->
          Rabs (f y - f x) < epsilon.

Definition putnam_2025_b2_strictly_increasing_on_unit
    (f : R -> R) : Prop :=
  forall x y : R,
    putnam_2025_b2_unit_interval x ->
    putnam_2025_b2_unit_interval y ->
    x < y ->
    f x < f y.

Definition putnam_2025_b2_unit_integral
    (g : R -> R) : R :=
  epsilon (inhabits (0 : R))
    (fun value : R =>
      exists integrable : Riemann_integrable g 0 1,
        value = RiemannInt integrable).

Theorem putnam_2025_b2
    (f : R -> R)
    (hf_cont : putnam_2025_b2_continuous_on_unit f)
    (hf_mono : putnam_2025_b2_strictly_increasing_on_unit f)
    (hf_nonneg :
      forall x : R,
        putnam_2025_b2_unit_interval x ->
        0 <= f x) :
  putnam_2025_b2_unit_integral (fun x : R => x * f x) /
    putnam_2025_b2_unit_integral f <
  putnam_2025_b2_unit_integral (fun x : R => x * (f x) ^ 2) /
    putnam_2025_b2_unit_integral (fun x : R => (f x) ^ 2).
Admitted.

(*
  Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b2
  (putnambench__isabelle__putnam_2025_b2): for a continuous, strictly
  increasing, nonnegative real function on [0,1], the x-coordinate of the
  centroid weighted by the square of the function exceeds the one weighted
  by the function. This file contains no proof.
*)

theory putnam_2025_b2
  imports Complex_Main
begin

definition putnam_2025_b2_integral :: "(real \<Rightarrow> real) \<Rightarrow> real" where
  "putnam_2025_b2_integral g =
    Lim sequentially
      (\<lambda>n :: nat.
        if n = 0 then 0
        else (\<Sum>k<n. g (real k / real n)) / real n)"

theorem putnam_2025_b2:
  fixes f :: "real \<Rightarrow> real"
  assumes hf_cont: "continuous_on {0..1} f"
    and hf_mono: "strict_mono_on {0..1} f"
    and hf_nonneg: "\<forall>x \<in> {0..1}. 0 \<le> f x"
  shows
    "putnam_2025_b2_integral (\<lambda>x. x * f x) /
        putnam_2025_b2_integral f
      <
      putnam_2025_b2_integral (\<lambda>x. x * (f x) ^ 2) /
        putnam_2025_b2_integral (\<lambda>x. (f x) ^ 2)"
  sorry

end

let statement =

     \(f:real->real).
       !x:real.
         &0 <= x /\ x <= &1
         ==> !e:real.
               &0 < e
               ==> ?d:real.
                     &0 < d /\
                     !y:real.
                       &0 <= y /\ y <= &1 /\ abs (y - x) < d
                       ==> abs (f y - f x) < e in
   !f:real->real.
     continuous_on_unit_interval f /\

     ==>

title: putnam_2025_b2
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b2:
;; a continuous, strictly increasing, nonnegative real function on [0,1] has
;; smaller planar-region centroid abscissa than its solid-of-revolution
;; centroid abscissa. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; F-APPROX is a generic rational approximation oracle on the rational points
;; of [0,1]. The predicates below make each precision-indexed value a regular
;; Cauchy name and impose uniform continuity. Thus the oracle presents an
;; arbitrary continuous real-valued function on [0,1], rather than restricting
;; the source function or its values to rationals.

(defstub putnam-2025-b2-f-approx (x precision) t)

(defun putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p (value)
  (and
   (rationalp value)
   (< 0 value)))

(defun putnam-2025-b2-unit-rational-p (value)
  (and
   (rationalp value)
   (<= 0 value)
   (<= value 1)))

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-regular-value-p (x)
  (forall (epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p eta))
     (let ((left
            (putnam-2025-b2-f-approx x epsilon))
           (right
            (putnam-2025-b2-f-approx x eta)))
       (and
        (rationalp left)
        (rationalp right)
        (<= (abs (- left right))
            (+ epsilon eta)))))))

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-regular-function-p ()
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (putnam-2025-b2-unit-rational-p x)
     (putnam-2025-b2-regular-value-p x))))

;; For regular names, this is exactly |f(x)-f(y)| <= BOUND.

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-value-distance-at-most-p
    (x y bound)
  (forall (epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p eta))
     (<=
      (abs
       (-
        (putnam-2025-b2-f-approx x epsilon)
        (putnam-2025-b2-f-approx y eta)))
      (+ bound epsilon eta)))))

;; A rational upper bound strictly below RADIUS makes this exactly the strict
;; inequality |f(x)-f(y)| < RADIUS.

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-value-distance-below-p
    (x y radius)
  (exists (bound)
    (and
     (rationalp bound)
     (<= 0 bound)
     (< bound radius)
     (putnam-2025-b2-value-distance-at-most-p
      x y bound))))

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-continuity-delta-p
    (epsilon delta)
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2025-b2-unit-rational-p x)
      (putnam-2025-b2-unit-rational-p y)
      (< (abs (- x y)) delta))
     (putnam-2025-b2-value-distance-below-p
      x y epsilon))))

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-continuity-delta-exists-p
    (epsilon)
  (exists (delta)
    (and
     (putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p delta)
     (putnam-2025-b2-continuity-delta-p
      epsilon delta))))

;; Continuity on the compact interval is equivalent to this uniform
;; continuity condition on its dense rational subset.

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-continuous-on-unit-p ()
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (putnam-2025-b2-continuity-delta-exists-p
      epsilon))))

;; For regular names, VALUE-GAP-AT-LEAST-P states
;; f(x) + GAP <= f(y). Existence of a positive rational gap is therefore
;; exactly f(x) < f(y).

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-value-gap-at-least-p
    (x y gap)
  (forall (epsilon eta)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
      (putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p eta))
     (<=
      (+ (putnam-2025-b2-f-approx x epsilon)
         gap)
      (+ (putnam-2025-b2-f-approx y eta)
         epsilon
         eta)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-value-strictly-below-p
    (x y)
  (exists (gap)
    (and
     (putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p gap)
     (putnam-2025-b2-value-gap-at-least-p
      x y gap))))

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-strictly-increasing-p ()
  (forall (x y)
    (implies
     (and
      (putnam-2025-b2-unit-rational-p x)
      (putnam-2025-b2-unit-rational-p y)
      (< x y))
     (putnam-2025-b2-value-strictly-below-p
      x y))))

;; A regular Cauchy name has nonnegative limit exactly when every
;; precision-EPSILON approximation is at least -EPSILON.

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-value-nonnegative-p (x)
  (forall (epsilon)
    (implies
     (putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p epsilon)
     (<= (- epsilon)
         (putnam-2025-b2-f-approx x epsilon)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-nonnegative-on-unit-p ()
  (forall (x)
    (implies
     (putnam-2025-b2-unit-rational-p x)
     (putnam-2025-b2-value-nonnegative-p x))))

;; Uniform midpoint Riemann sums converge to the interval integrals of f,
;; x*f, f^2, and x*f^2. The approximation precision is the reciprocal of the
;; grid size, so both sampling and value errors tend to zero without bounding
;; the grid or the represented real values.

(defun putnam-2025-b2-integrand-approx
    (mode x precision)
  (let ((value
         (putnam-2025-b2-f-approx x precision)))
    (cond
     ((equal mode 'f)
      value)
     ((equal mode 'x-times-f)
      (* x value))
     ((equal mode 'f-squared)
      (* value value))
     ((equal mode 'x-times-f-squared)
      (* x value value))
     (t 0))))

(defun putnam-2025-b2-riemann-sum
    (mode count grid-size precision)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix count)))
  (if (zp count)
      0
    (let ((midpoint
           (/ (- (* 2 count) 1)
              (* 2 grid-size))))
      (+
       (putnam-2025-b2-integrand-approx
        mode midpoint precision)
       (putnam-2025-b2-riemann-sum
        mode (- count 1) grid-size precision)))))

(defun putnam-2025-b2-integral-prefix
    (mode grid-size)
  (if (posp grid-size)
      (let ((precision (/ 1 grid-size)))
        (/
         (putnam-2025-b2-riemann-sum
          mode grid-size grid-size precision)
         grid-size))
    0))

(defun putnam-2025-b2-left-product-prefix
    (grid-size)
  (*
   (putnam-2025-b2-integral-prefix
    'x-times-f grid-size)
   (putnam-2025-b2-integral-prefix
    'f-squared grid-size)))

(defun putnam-2025-b2-right-product-prefix
    (grid-size)
  (*
   (putnam-2025-b2-integral-prefix
    'x-times-f-squared grid-size)
   (putnam-2025-b2-integral-prefix
    'f grid-size)))

;; Strict inequality of the two real product limits is equivalent to the
;; existence of an eventual positive rational gap between their prefixes.

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-product-gap-eventually-p
    (gap cutoff)
  (forall (grid-size)
    (implies
     (and
      (posp grid-size)
      (natp cutoff)
      (<= cutoff grid-size))
     (<=
      (+
       (putnam-2025-b2-left-product-prefix
        grid-size)
       gap)
      (putnam-2025-b2-right-product-prefix
       grid-size)))))

(defun-sk putnam-2025-b2-centroid-inequality-p ()
  (exists (gap cutoff)
    (and
     (putnam-2025-b2-positive-rational-p gap)
     (natp cutoff)
     (putnam-2025-b2-product-gap-eventually-p
      gap cutoff))))

;; Strict increase and nonnegativity make both centroid denominators positive.
;; Cross multiplication therefore turns the source quotient inequality into
;; exactly the product-limit inequality above.

(defun putnambench-putnam-2025-b2-statement ()
  (implies
   (and
    (putnam-2025-b2-regular-function-p)
    (putnam-2025-b2-continuous-on-unit-p)
    (putnam-2025-b2-strictly-increasing-p)
    (putnam-2025-b2-nonnegative-on-unit-p))
   (putnam-2025-b2-centroid-inequality-p)))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

title: putnam_2025_b2
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b2
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2025_b2): comparison of the centroid abscissas
-- for the region under a nonnegative continuous strictly increasing graph and
-- the solid formed by rotating that region about the x-axis. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2025B2 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _!=_ _<=N_
infixr 3 _and_
infixr 2 _or_

data Bottom : Set where

Not : Set -> Set
Not A =
  A -> Bottom

_!=_ : {A : Set} -> A -> A -> Set
x != y =
  Not (x == y)

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

record CompleteOrderedRealField (R : Set) : Set1 where
  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    add multiply : R -> R -> R
    negate inverse : R -> R
    lessOrEqual : R -> R -> Set
    fromNat : Nat -> R

    one-not-zero :
      oneR != zeroR

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> add x y == add y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      add (add x y) z == add x (add y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) -> add x zeroR == x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) -> add x (negate x) == zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) -> multiply x y == multiply y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply (multiply x y) z ==
      multiply x (multiply y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) -> multiply x oneR == x
    multiply-zero :
      (x : R) -> multiply x zeroR == zeroR
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) ->
      multiply x (add y z) ==
      add (multiply x y) (multiply x z)
    inverse-zero :
      inverse zeroR == zeroR
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : R) ->
      x != zeroR ->
      multiply x (inverse x) == oneR

    order-reflexive :
      (x : R) -> lessOrEqual x x
    order-transitive :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y z ->
      lessOrEqual x z
    order-antisymmetric :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual y x ->
      x == y
    order-total :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y or lessOrEqual y x
    add-order :
      (x y z : R) ->
      lessOrEqual x y ->
      lessOrEqual (add z x) (add z y)
    multiply-nonnegative :
      (x y : R) ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR x ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR y ->
      lessOrEqual zeroR (multiply x y)
    zero-less-than-one :
      lessOrEqual zeroR oneR and zeroR != oneR

    fromNat-zero :
      fromNat zero == zeroR
    fromNat-successor :
      (n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (suc n) == add (fromNat n) oneR
    fromNat-addition :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m + n) == add (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-multiplication :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat (m * n) == multiply (fromNat m) (fromNat n)
    fromNat-injective :
      (m n : Nat) ->
      fromNat m == fromNat n ->
      m == n

    archimedean :
      (x : R) ->
      Exists Nat
        (\ n -> lessOrEqual x (fromNat n))
    least-upper-bound :
      (P : R -> Set) ->
      Exists R P ->
      Exists R
        (\ upper ->
          (x : R) ->
          P x ->
          lessOrEqual x upper) ->
      Exists R
        (\ supremum ->
          ((x : R) ->
            P x ->
            lessOrEqual x supremum)
          and
          ((upper : R) ->
            ((x : R) ->
              P x ->
              lessOrEqual x upper) ->
            lessOrEqual supremum upper))

open CompleteOrderedRealField

subtract :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
subtract reals x y =
  add reals x (negate reals y)

divide :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R
divide reals numerator denominator =
  multiply reals numerator (inverse reals denominator)

StrictLess :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
StrictLess reals x y =
  lessOrEqual reals x y and x != y

CloseTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  Set
CloseTo reals center radius x =
  StrictLess reals
    (subtract reals center radius)
    x
  and
  StrictLess reals
    x
    (add reals center radius)

ConvergesTo :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
ConvergesTo {R} reals sequence limit =
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists Nat
    (\ cutoff ->
      (n : Nat) ->
      cutoff <=N n ->
      CloseTo reals limit epsilon (sequence n))

sumFirst :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  Nat ->
  (Nat -> R) ->
  R
sumFirst reals zero terms =
  zeroR reals
sumFirst reals (suc n) terms =
  add reals
    (sumFirst reals n terms)
    (terms n)

rightRiemannSum :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Nat ->
  R
rightRiemannSum reals lower upper function pieces =
  let
    step =
      divide reals
        (subtract reals upper lower)
        (fromNat reals pieces)
  in
  sumFirst reals pieces
    (\ i ->
      multiply reals
        (function
          (add reals lower
            (multiply reals
              (fromNat reals (suc i))
              step)))
        step)

IntervalIntegralValue :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  Set
IntervalIntegralValue reals lower upper function value =
  ConvergesTo reals
    (\ n ->
      rightRiemannSum reals
        lower
        upper
        function
        (suc n))
    value

InClosedUnitInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  R ->
  Set
InClosedUnitInterval reals x =
  lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) x
  and
  lessOrEqual reals x (oneR reals)

ContinuousOnUnitInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
ContinuousOnUnitInterval {R} reals function =
  (x : R) ->
  InClosedUnitInterval reals x ->
  (epsilon : R) ->
  StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) epsilon ->
  Exists R
    (\ delta ->
      StrictLess reals (zeroR reals) delta
      and
      ((y : R) ->
        InClosedUnitInterval reals y ->
        CloseTo reals x delta y ->
        CloseTo reals
          (function x)
          epsilon
          (function y)))

StrictlyIncreasingOnUnitInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
StrictlyIncreasingOnUnitInterval {R} reals function =
  (x y : R) ->
  InClosedUnitInterval reals x ->
  InClosedUnitInterval reals y ->
  StrictLess reals x y ->
  StrictLess reals (function x) (function y)

NonnegativeOnUnitInterval :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  Set
NonnegativeOnUnitInterval {R} reals function =
  (x : R) ->
  InClosedUnitInterval reals x ->
  lessOrEqual reals (zeroR reals) (function x)

linearMomentIntegrand :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
linearMomentIntegrand reals function x =
  multiply reals x (function x)

squaredIntegrand :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
squaredIntegrand reals function x =
  multiply reals (function x) (function x)

squaredMomentIntegrand :
  {R : Set} ->
  CompleteOrderedRealField R ->
  (R -> R) ->
  R ->
  R
squaredMomentIntegrand reals function x =
  multiply reals x (squaredIntegrand reals function x)

putnam-2025-b2 : Set1
putnam-2025-b2 =
  (R : Set) ->
  (reals : CompleteOrderedRealField R) ->
  (function : R -> R) ->
  ContinuousOnUnitInterval reals function ->
  StrictlyIncreasingOnUnitInterval reals function ->
  NonnegativeOnUnitInterval reals function ->
  Exists R
    (\ linearMoment ->
      IntervalIntegralValue reals
        (zeroR reals)
        (oneR reals)
        (linearMomentIntegrand reals function)
        linearMoment
      and
      Exists R
        (\ linearMass ->
          IntervalIntegralValue reals
            (zeroR reals)
            (oneR reals)
            function
            linearMass
          and
          Exists R
            (\ squaredMoment ->
              IntervalIntegralValue reals
                (zeroR reals)
                (oneR reals)
                (squaredMomentIntegrand reals function)
                squaredMoment
              and
              Exists R
                (\ squaredMass ->
                  IntervalIntegralValue reals
                    (zeroR reals)
                    (oneR reals)
                    (squaredIntegrand reals function)
                    squaredMass
                  and
                  StrictLess reals
                    (divide reals linearMoment linearMass)
                    (divide reals squaredMoment squaredMass)))))

title: putnam_2025_b2
content:
% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b2:
% for a continuous, strictly increasing, nonnegative real function on the unit
% interval, the x-coordinate of the centroid increases when the region under
% its graph is rotated about the x-axis. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2025_b2: THEORY
BEGIN
  real_function: TYPE = [real -> real]
  real_sequence: TYPE = [nat -> real]

  in_closed_unit_interval(x: real): bool =
    0 <= x AND x <= 1

  continuous_on_closed_unit_interval(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      in_closed_unit_interval(x) IMPLIES
        FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
          EXISTS (delta: posreal):
            FORALL (y: real):
              (in_closed_unit_interval(y)
                AND abs(y - x) < delta)
              IMPLIES
                abs(f(y) - f(x)) < epsilon_value

  strictly_increasing_on_closed_unit_interval(
      f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: real):
      (in_closed_unit_interval(x)
        AND in_closed_unit_interval(y)
        AND x < y)
      IMPLIES f(x) < f(y)

  nonnegative_on_closed_unit_interval(f: real_function): bool =
    FORALL (x: real):
      in_closed_unit_interval(x) IMPLIES 0 <= f(x)

  valid_partition(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    count > 0
      AND points(0) = 0
      AND points(count) = 1
      AND FORALL (index: nat):
        index < count IMPLIES
          points(index) < points(index + 1)

  valid_tags(
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index) <= tags(index)
          AND tags(index) <= points(index + 1)

  mesh_less_than(
      points: real_sequence,
      count: nat,
      bound: real): bool =
    FORALL (index: nat):
      index < count IMPLIES
        points(index + 1) - points(index) < bound

  riemann_sum(
      f: real_function,
      points, tags: real_sequence,
      count: nat): RECURSIVE real =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count - 1)
        + f(tags(count - 1))
            * (points(count) - points(count - 1))
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  has_unit_interval_integral(
      f: real_function,
      integral_value: real): bool =
    FORALL (epsilon_value: posreal):
      EXISTS (mesh_bound: posreal):
        FORALL
            (points, tags: real_sequence),
            (count: nat):
          (valid_partition(points, count)
            AND valid_tags(points, tags, count)
            AND mesh_less_than(points, count, mesh_bound))
          IMPLIES
            abs(
              riemann_sum(f, points, tags, count)
                - integral_value)
              < epsilon_value

  unit_interval_integral(f: real_function): real =
    IF EXISTS (integral_value: real):
        has_unit_interval_integral(f, integral_value)
    THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (integral_value: real):
          has_unit_interval_integral(f, integral_value))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  safe_div(numerator, denominator: real): real =
    IF denominator = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      numerator / denominator
    ENDIF

  first_moment(f: real_function): real =
    unit_interval_integral(
      LAMBDA (x: real): x * f(x))

  squared_first_moment(f: real_function): real =
    unit_interval_integral(
      LAMBDA (x: real): x * f(x) ^ 2)

  putnam_2025_b2: bool =
    FORALL (f: real_function):
      (continuous_on_closed_unit_interval(f)
        AND strictly_increasing_on_closed_unit_interval(f)
        AND nonnegative_on_closed_unit_interval(f))
      IMPLIES
        safe_div(
          first_moment(f),
          unit_interval_integral(f))
        <
          safe_div(
            squared_first_moment(f),
            unit_interval_integral(
              LAMBDA (x: real): f(x) ^ 2))
END putnam_2025_b2

import Mathlib

open Finset

abbrev putnam_2025_b3_solution : Prop := sorry
-- True

/--
Suppose $S$ is a nonempty set of positive integers with the property that if $n$ is in $S$,
then every positive divisor of $2025^n - 15^n$ is in $S$. Must $S$ contain all positive integers?
-/
theorem putnam_2025_b3 :
    putnam_2025_b3_solution ↔
    ∀ S : Set ℕ,
      S.Nonempty →
      (∀ n ∈ S, 0 < n) →
      (∀ n ∈ S, ∀ d : ℕ, 0 < d → d ∣ (2025 ^ n - 15 ^ n) → d ∈ S) →
      S = {n : ℕ | 0 < n} := by
  sorry

;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b3:
;; every positive integer is reachable from every other by repeatedly taking
;; positive divisors of 2025^n - 15^n. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun putnam-2025-b3-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun putnam-2025-b3-list-term (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'cons
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2025-b3-list-term (cdr terms)))
    (putnam-2025-b3-quoted nil)))

(defun putnam-2025-b3-and-terms (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'if
       (car terms)
       (putnam-2025-b3-and-terms (cdr terms))
       (putnam-2025-b3-quoted nil))
    (putnam-2025-b3-quoted t)))

(defun putnam-2025-b3-add-term (left right)
  (list 'binary-+ left right))

(defun putnam-2025-b3-subtract-term (left right)
  (putnam-2025-b3-add-term
   left
   (list 'unary-- right)))

(defun putnam-2025-b3-expt-term (base exponent)
  (list 'expt base exponent))

(defun putnam-2025-b3-nth-term (index sequence)
  (list 'nth index sequence))

(defun putnam-2025-b3-singleton-function ()
  '(lambda (index)
     (cons index 'nil)))

(defun putnam-2025-b3-wrapped-range-term (lower upper)
  (list
   'collect$
   (putnam-2025-b3-quoted
    (putnam-2025-b3-singleton-function))
   (list
    'from-to-by
    lower
    upper
    (putnam-2025-b3-quoted 1))))

;; A path step from n to d requires positive integers n and d and the exact
;; source divisibility condition d | (2025^n - 15^n).
(defun putnam-2025-b3-path-step-function ()
  (let* ((path (list 'car 'loop$-gvars))
         (index (list 'car 'loop$-ivars))
         (next-index
          (putnam-2025-b3-add-term
           index
           (putnam-2025-b3-quoted 1)))
         (current
          (putnam-2025-b3-nth-term index path))
         (next
          (putnam-2025-b3-nth-term next-index path))
         (difference
          (putnam-2025-b3-subtract-term
           (putnam-2025-b3-expt-term
            (putnam-2025-b3-quoted 2025)
            current)
           (putnam-2025-b3-expt-term
            (putnam-2025-b3-quoted 15)
            current)))
         (body
          (putnam-2025-b3-and-terms
           (list
            (list 'integerp current)
            (list '< (putnam-2025-b3-quoted 0) current)
            (list 'integerp next)
            (list '< (putnam-2025-b3-quoted 0) next)
            (list
             'equal
             (list 'mod difference next)
             (putnam-2025-b3-quoted 0))))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(loop$-gvars loop$-ivars)
     body)))

(defun putnam-2025-b3-path-valid-term (path)
  (let ((short-path
         (list
          '<
          (list 'len path)
          (putnam-2025-b3-quoted 2))))
    (list
     'if
     short-path
     (putnam-2025-b3-quoted t)
     (list
      'always$+
      (putnam-2025-b3-quoted
       (putnam-2025-b3-path-step-function))
      (putnam-2025-b3-list-term (list path))
      (putnam-2025-b3-wrapped-range-term
       (putnam-2025-b3-quoted 0)
       (putnam-2025-b3-add-term
        (list 'len path)
        (putnam-2025-b3-quoted -2)))))))

;; For a directed graph, every nonempty forward-closed subset is the whole
;; vertex set iff every target is reachable from every start by a finite path.
;; Thus this finite-path formulation is bidirectionally equivalent to the
;; source's quantification over arbitrary sets of positive integers.
(defun putnam-2025-b3-witness-failure-function (start target)
  (let* ((path 'path)
         (last-index
          (putnam-2025-b3-add-term
           (list 'len path)
           (putnam-2025-b3-quoted -1)))
         (qualification
          (putnam-2025-b3-and-terms
           (list
            (list 'true-listp path)
            (list 'consp path)
            (list
             'equal
             (list 'car path)
             (putnam-2025-b3-quoted start))
            (list
             'equal
             (putnam-2025-b3-nth-term last-index path)
             (putnam-2025-b3-quoted target))
            (putnam-2025-b3-path-valid-term path)))))
    (list
     'lambda
     '(path)
     (list
      'if
      qualification
      (putnam-2025-b3-quoted nil)
      (putnam-2025-b3-quoted t)))))

(defun putnam-2025-b3-true-function ()
  (list
   'lambda
   '(path)
   (putnam-2025-b3-quoted t)))

;; Inequality with the constant-true predicate expresses the internal
;; existential quantifier over arbitrary finite paths.
(defun putnambench-putnam-2025-b3-statement (start target)
  (implies
   (and
    (integerp start)
    (< 0 start)
    (integerp target)
    (< 0 target))
   (let ((failure
          (putnam-2025-b3-witness-failure-function
           start target))
         (always-true
          (putnam-2025-b3-true-function)))
     (and
      (tamep-functionp failure)
      (tamep-functionp always-true)
      (not (fn-equal failure always-true))))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b3
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2025_b3): every nonempty set of positive
-- integers closed under positive divisors of 2025^n - 15^n contains exactly
-- all positive integers. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2025B3 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _-_; _*_)

infix 4 _divides_
infixr 3 _and_

record _and_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

record Exists (A : Set) (P : A -> Set) : Set where
  constructor witness
  field
    value    : A
    property : P value

data Positive : Nat -> Set where
  positive : {n : Nat} -> Positive (suc n)

record _divides_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  constructor quotient-witness

% contains no proof.

putnam_2025_b3: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_set: TYPE = [nat -> bool]

  nat_subtract(minuend, subtrahend: nat): nat =
    IF subtrahend <= minuend THEN minuend - subtrahend ELSE 0 ENDIF

  nat_divides(divisor, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  power_difference(n: nat): nat =
    nat_subtract(2025 ^ n, 15 ^ n)

  positive_naturals: natural_set =
    LAMBDA (n: nat):
      0 < n

  putnam_2025_b3_solution: bool = TRUE

  putnam_2025_b3: bool =
    putnam_2025_b3_solution
      IFF
        FORALL (S: natural_set):
          ((EXISTS (n: nat): S(n))
            AND (FORALL (n: nat):
              S(n) IMPLIES 0 < n)
            AND (FORALL (n: nat):
              S(n) IMPLIES
                (FORALL (d: nat):
                  0 < d
                    AND nat_divides(d, power_difference(n))
                  IMPLIES S(d))))
          IMPLIES S = positive_naturals

import Mathlib

open BigOperators Finset Matrix

/--
For $n \geq 2$, let $A = [a_{i,j}]_{i,j=1}^n$ be an $n$-by-$n$ matrix of nonnegative integers such that:
(a) $a_{i,j} = 0$ when $i + j \leq n$;
(b) $a_{i+1,j} \in \{a_{i,j}, a_{i,j} + 1\}$ when $1 \leq i \leq n-1$ and $1 \leq j \leq n$; and
(c) $a_{i,j+1} \in \{a_{i,j}, a_{i,j} + 1\}$ when $1 \leq i \leq n$ and $1 \leq j \leq n-1$.

Let $S$ be the sum of the entries of $A$, and let $N$ be the number of nonzero entries of $A$.
Prove that $S \leq \frac{(n+2)N}{3}$.
-/
theorem putnam_2025_b4
    (m : ℕ)
    (A : Matrix (Fin (m + 2)) (Fin (m + 2)) ℕ)
    (ha : ∀ (i j : Fin (m + 2)), (i : ℕ) + (j : ℕ) ≤ m → A i j = 0)
    (hb : ∀ (i : Fin (m + 1)) (j : Fin (m + 2)),
      A (Fin.succ i) j = A (Fin.castSucc i) j ∨
      A (Fin.succ i) j = A (Fin.castSucc i) j + 1)
    (hc : ∀ (i : Fin (m + 2)) (j : Fin (m + 1)),
      A i (Fin.succ j) = A i (Fin.castSucc j) ∨
      A i (Fin.succ j) = A i (Fin.castSucc j) + 1)
    (S : ℕ)
    (hS : S = ∑ i : Fin (m + 2), ∑ j : Fin (m + 2), A i j)
    (N : ℕ)
    (hN : N = #{p : Fin (m + 2) × Fin (m + 2) | A p.1 p.2 ≠ 0}) :
    3 * S ≤ (m + 4) * N := by
  sorry

  | S height' =>

    (m : nat)
    (A : nat -> nat -> nat)
    (ha :

        (j < m + 2)%nat ->

    (total : nat)
    (h_total :
      total = putnam_2025_b4_matrix_sum (m + 2) (m + 2) A)
    (nonzero : nat)
    (h_nonzero :
      nonzero = putnam_2025_b4_nonzero_count (m + 2) (m + 2) A) :
  (3 * total <= (m + 4) * nonzero)%nat.

;; below range over every valid row and column index in canonical order.

(defun putnam-2025-b4-natural-row-p (row columns)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix columns)))
  (if (zp columns)
      (equal row nil)
    (and
     (consp row)
     (natp (car row))
     (putnam-2025-b4-natural-row-p
      (cdr row) (- columns 1)))))

(defun putnam-2025-b4-natural-matrix-p
    (matrix rows columns)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix rows)))
  (if (zp rows)
      (equal matrix nil)
    (and
     (consp matrix)
     (putnam-2025-b4-natural-row-p
      (car matrix) columns)
     (putnam-2025-b4-natural-matrix-p
      (cdr matrix) (- rows 1) columns))))

(defun putnam-2025-b4-zero-region-row-p
    (row row-index column-index m)
  (if (endp row)
      t
    (and
     (implies
      (<= (+ row-index column-index) m)
      (equal (car row) 0))
     (putnam-2025-b4-zero-region-row-p
      (cdr row) row-index (+ column-index 1) m))))

    (matrix row-index m)

    (and
     (putnam-2025-b4-zero-region-row-p
      (car matrix) row-index 0 m)
     (putnam-2025-b4-zero-region-p
      (cdr matrix) (+ row-index 1) m))))

  (if (endp upper)
      (endp lower)
    (and
     (consp lower)
     (or
      (equal (car lower) (car upper))
      (equal (car lower) (+ (car upper) 1)))
     (putnam-2025-b4-adjacent-rows-p
      (cdr upper) (cdr lower)))))

      t
    (and

      (car matrix) (cadr matrix))

      (cdr matrix)))))
