-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b4
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2025_b4): a finite matrix of natural numbers
-- satisfying the stated zero region and unit-step conditions obeys the given
-- bound relating its entry sum and number of nonzero entries. This file
-- contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Putnam2025B4 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _*_)

infix 4 _<=N_
infixr 2 _or_

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

data Fin : Nat -> Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} -> Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)

finValue : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Nat
finValue fzero =
  zero
finValue (fsuc index) =
  suc (finValue index)

castSucc : {n : Nat} -> Fin n -> Fin (suc n)
castSucc fzero =
  fzero
castSucc (fsuc index) =
  fsuc (castSucc index)

one : Nat
one =
  suc zero

two : Nat
two =
  suc one

three : Nat
three =
  suc two

four : Nat
four =
  suc three

Matrix : Nat -> Set
Matrix n =
  Fin n -> Fin n -> Nat

sumFin :
  (n : Nat) ->
  (Fin n -> Nat) ->
  Nat
sumFin zero term =
  zero
sumFin (suc n) term =
  term fzero +
  sumFin n (\ index -> term (fsuc index))

matrixSum :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix n ->
  Nat
matrixSum {n} A =
  sumFin n
    (\ i ->
      sumFin n
        (\ j -> A i j))

nonzeroIndicator : Nat -> Nat
nonzeroIndicator zero =
  zero
nonzeroIndicator (suc value) =
  one

nonzeroCount :
  {n : Nat} ->
  Matrix n ->
  Nat
nonzeroCount {n} A =
  sumFin n
    (\ i ->
      sumFin n
        (\ j -> nonzeroIndicator (A i j)))

putnam-2025-b4 : Set
putnam-2025-b4 =
  (m : Nat) ->
  (A : Matrix (suc (suc m))) ->
  ((i j : Fin (suc (suc m))) ->
    finValue i + finValue j <=N m ->
    A i j == zero) ->
  ((i : Fin (suc m)) (j : Fin (suc (suc m))) ->
    A (fsuc i) j == A (castSucc i) j
    or
    A (fsuc i) j == A (castSucc i) j + one) ->
  ((i : Fin (suc (suc m))) (j : Fin (suc m)) ->
    A i (fsuc j) == A i (castSucc j)
    or
    A i (fsuc j) == A i (castSucc j) + one) ->
  (S : Nat) ->
  S == matrixSum A ->
  (N : Nat) ->
  N == nonzeroCount A ->
  three * S <=N (m + four) * N

title: putnam_2025_b4

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b4:
% a nonnegative integer matrix with a triangular zero region and unit-step
% horizontal and vertical growth satisfies the stated sum-versus-support
% bound. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2025_b4: THEORY
BEGIN
  natural_matrix: TYPE = [nat, nat -> nat]

  row_sum(
      A: natural_matrix,
      row, column_count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF column_count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      row_sum(A, row, column_count - 1)
        + A(row, column_count - 1)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE column_count

  matrix_sum(
      A: natural_matrix,
      row_count, column_count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF row_count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      matrix_sum(A, row_count - 1, column_count)
        + row_sum(A, row_count - 1, column_count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE row_count

  row_nonzero_count(
      A: natural_matrix,
      row, column_count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF column_count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      row_nonzero_count(A, row, column_count - 1)
        + (IF A(row, column_count - 1) /= 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE column_count

  matrix_nonzero_count(
      A: natural_matrix,
      row_count, column_count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF row_count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      matrix_nonzero_count(A, row_count - 1, column_count)
        + row_nonzero_count(A, row_count - 1, column_count)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE row_count

  has_triangular_zero_region(m: nat, A: natural_matrix): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      (i < m + 2 AND j < m + 2 AND i + j <= m)
        IMPLIES A(i, j) = 0

  has_vertical_unit_steps(m: nat, A: natural_matrix): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      (i < m + 1 AND j < m + 2)
        IMPLIES
          (A(i + 1, j) = A(i, j)
            OR A(i + 1, j) = A(i, j) + 1)

  has_horizontal_unit_steps(m: nat, A: natural_matrix): bool =
    FORALL (i, j: nat):
      (i < m + 2 AND j < m + 1)
        IMPLIES
          (A(i, j + 1) = A(i, j)
            OR A(i, j + 1) = A(i, j) + 1)

  putnam_2025_b4: bool =
    FORALL (m: nat), (A: natural_matrix), (S, N: nat):
      (has_triangular_zero_region(m, A)
        AND has_vertical_unit_steps(m, A)
        AND has_horizontal_unit_steps(m, A)
        AND S = matrix_sum(A, m + 2, m + 2)
        AND N = matrix_nonzero_count(A, m + 2, m + 2))
      IMPLIES
        3 * S <= (m + 4) * N
END putnam_2025_b4

import Mathlib

open Finset BigOperators

def modInv (p : ℕ) (k : ℕ) : ℕ := ZMod.val ((k : ZMod p)⁻¹)

def descentCount (p : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  #{k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (p - 2) | modInv p (k + 1) < modInv p k}

/--
Let $p$ be a prime number greater than 3. For each $k \in \{1, \ldots, p-1\}$,
let $I(k) \in \{1, 2, \ldots, p-1\}$ be such that $k \cdot I(k) \equiv 1 \pmod{p}$.
Prove that the number of integers $k \in \{1, \ldots, p-2\}$ such that
$I(k+1) < I(k)$ is greater than $p/4 - 1$.
-/
theorem putnam_2025_b5
    (p : ℕ)
    (hp_prime : p.Prime)
    (hp_gt : 3 < p) :
    (p : ℚ) / 4 - 1 < descentCount p := by
  sorry

(* Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b5
   (putnambench__rocq__putnam_2025_b5): a lower bound for the number of
   descents among consecutive nonzero modular inverses modulo a prime greater
   than 3. This file contains no proof. *)

From Stdlib Require Import Arith.PeanoNat QArith ZArith ZArith.Zcong.

Open Scope Q_scope.

Definition putnam_2025_b5_prime (p : nat) : Prop :=
  (2 <= p)%nat /\
  forall d : nat,
    Nat.divide d p ->
    d = 1%nat \/ d = p.

Definition putnam_2025_b5_mod_inv (p k : nat) : nat :=
  Z.to_nat (Z.invmod (Z.of_nat k) (Z.of_nat p)).

Fixpoint putnam_2025_b5_descent_count_from
    (p k remaining : nat) : nat :=
  match remaining with
  | O => O
  | S rest =>
      ((if Nat.ltb
          (putnam_2025_b5_mod_inv p (S k))
          (putnam_2025_b5_mod_inv p k)
        then 1
        else 0) +
       putnam_2025_b5_descent_count_from p (S k) rest)%nat
  end.

Definition putnam_2025_b5_descent_count (p : nat) : nat :=
  putnam_2025_b5_descent_count_from p 1%nat (p - 2)%nat.

Theorem putnam_2025_b5
    (p : nat)
    (hp_prime : putnam_2025_b5_prime p)
    (hp_gt : (3 < p)%nat) :
  (inject_Z (Z.of_nat p) / 4 - 1 <
   inject_Z (Z.of_nat (putnam_2025_b5_descent_count p)))%Q.
Admitted.

theory putnam_2025_b5

definition putnam_2025_b5_mod_inv :: "nat \<Rightarrow> nat \<Rightarrow> nat" where

  "putnam_2025_b5_descent_count p =

  fixes p :: nat
  assumes hp_prime: "prime p"
    and hp_gt: "3 < p"
  shows
    "rat_of_nat p / 4 - 1 <
      rat_of_nat (putnam_2025_b5_descent_count p)"
  sorry

end

     prime p /\ 3 < p
     ==>
     let modular_inverse =
       \k:num.
         @i:num. i < p /\ (k * i) MOD p = 1 in

title: putnam_2025_b5
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b5:
;; for every prime p greater than 3, the number of descents between consecutive
;; nonzero modular inverses modulo p is greater than p/4 - 1. This file contains
;; no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

;; For a natural p, this checks every possible proper divisor from candidate
;; down through 2.
(defun putnam-2025-b5-no-divisor-through-p (p candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (or (not (natp candidate))
          (<= candidate 1))
      t
    (and
     (not (equal (mod p candidate) 0))
     (putnam-2025-b5-no-divisor-through-p
      p (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-2025-b5-primep (p)
  (and
   (natp p)
   (< 1 p)
   (putnam-2025-b5-no-divisor-through-p
    p (- p 1))))

;; Under the statement hypotheses, each k in 1,...,p-1 has exactly one
;; candidate in 1,...,p-1 whose product with k is 1 modulo p. The descending
;; search therefore returns the canonical residue represented by ZMod.val.
(defun putnam-2025-b5-mod-inverse-through (p k candidate)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix candidate)))
  (if (or (not (posp p))
          (not (natp candidate))
          (zp candidate))
      0
    (if (equal (mod (* k candidate) p) 1)
        candidate
      (putnam-2025-b5-mod-inverse-through
       p k (- candidate 1)))))

(defun putnam-2025-b5-mod-inverse (p k)
  (putnam-2025-b5-mod-inverse-through
   p k (nfix (- p 1))))

;; Descending recursion over k counts exactly the source interval
;; Finset.Icc 1 (p-2).
(defun putnam-2025-b5-descent-count-through (p k)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix k)))
  (if (or (not (natp k))
          (zp k))
      0
    (+
     (if (< (putnam-2025-b5-mod-inverse p (+ k 1))
            (putnam-2025-b5-mod-inverse p k))
         1
       0)
     (putnam-2025-b5-descent-count-through
      p (- k 1)))))

(defun putnam-2025-b5-descent-count (p)
  (putnam-2025-b5-descent-count-through
   p (nfix (- p 2))))

(defun putnambench-putnam-2025-b5-statement (p)
  (implies
   (and
    (natp p)
    (putnam-2025-b5-primep p)
    (< 3 p))
   (< (- (/ p 4) 1)
      (putnam-2025-b5-descent-count p))))

(value-triple :itpeval-statement-checked)
:q

-- Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b5
-- (putnambench__agda__putnam_2025_b5): for every prime p greater than 3,
-- the number of descents among the canonical nonzero modular inverses modulo p
-- is greater than p/4 - 1. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module putnam-2025-b5 where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality renaming (_≡_ to _==_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using
  (Nat; zero; suc; _+_; _-_; _*_; mod-helper)

infix 4 _<=N_ _<N_ _divides_
infixr 2 _or_

data _<=N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set where
  zero<=N   : {n : Nat} -> zero <=N n
  suc<=sucN : {m n : Nat} -> m <=N n -> suc m <=N suc n

_<N_ : Nat -> Nat -> Set
m <N n =
  suc m <=N n

record _divides_ (divisor dividend : Nat) : Set where
  field
    quotient : Nat
    division-equation : dividend == divisor * quotient

data _or_ (A B : Set) : Set where
  left  : A -> A or B
  right : B -> A or B

record Prime (p : Nat) : Set where
  field
    at-least-two : 2 <=N p
    only-trivial-divisors :
      (d : Nat) ->
      d divides p ->
      (d == 1) or (d == p)

naturalMod : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
naturalMod numerator zero =
  numerator
naturalMod numerator (suc denominator) =
  mod-helper zero denominator numerator denominator

natEqual : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
natEqual zero zero =
  true
natEqual zero (suc n) =
  false
natEqual (suc m) zero =
  false
natEqual (suc m) (suc n) =
  natEqual m n

natLess : Nat -> Nat -> Bool
natLess zero zero =
  false
natLess zero (suc n) =
  true
natLess (suc m) zero =
  false
natLess (suc m) (suc n) =
  natLess m n

searchInverse : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat
searchInverse modulus value zero candidate =
  zero
searchInverse modulus value (suc fuel) candidate
  with natEqual (naturalMod (value * candidate) modulus) 1
... | true =
  candidate
... | false =
  searchInverse modulus value fuel (suc candidate)

modInv : Nat -> Nat -> Nat
modInv modulus value =
  searchInverse modulus value modulus zero

countDescents : Nat -> Nat -> Nat -> Nat
countDescents modulus index zero =
  zero
countDescents modulus index (suc remaining)
  with natLess
    (modInv modulus (suc index))
    (modInv modulus index)
... | true =
  suc (countDescents modulus (suc index) remaining)
... | false =
  countDescents modulus (suc index) remaining

descentCount : Nat -> Nat
descentCount p =
  countDescents p 1 (p - 2)

putnam-2025-b5 : Set
putnam-2025-b5 =
  (p : Nat) ->
  Prime p ->
  3 <N p ->
  p <N (4 * suc (descentCount p))

  least positive modular inverses modulo p have more than p/4 - 1 descents on

$(

  declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement; this database
  contains no $p proof declaration.

% Statement-only formalization of PutnamBench corpus artifact putnam_2025_b5
% (putnambench__pvs__putnam_2025_b5): a lower bound for the number of descents
% among consecutive canonical multiplicative inverses modulo a prime greater
% than 3. This file contains no proof.

putnam_2025_b5: THEORY
BEGIN
  nat_divides(divisor: posnat, value: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (quotient: nat):
      value = divisor * quotient

  prime_nat(value: nat): bool =
    value >= 2
      AND FORALL (divisor: posnat):
        nat_divides(divisor, value)
          IMPLIES divisor = 1 OR divisor = value

  nat_subtract(minuend, subtrahend: nat): nat =
    IF subtrahend <= minuend THEN minuend - subtrahend ELSE 0 ENDIF

  nat_congruent(left, right, modulus: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (offset: int):
      (left :: int) - (right :: int) = (modulus :: int) * offset

  has_modular_inverse(p, k: nat): bool =
    EXISTS (value: nat):
      value < p
        AND nat_congruent(k * value, 1, p)

  modular_inverse(p, k: nat): nat =
    IF has_modular_inverse(p, k) THEN
      epsilon(
        LAMBDA (value: nat):
          value < p
            AND nat_congruent(k * value, 1, p))
    ELSE
      0
    ENDIF

  count_true(
      property: [nat -> bool],
      count: nat): RECURSIVE nat =
    IF count = 0 THEN
      0
    ELSE
      count_true(property, count - 1)
        + IF property(count - 1) THEN 1 ELSE 0 ENDIF
    ENDIF
  MEASURE count

  descent_count(p: nat): nat =
    count_true(
      LAMBDA (offset: nat):
        modular_inverse(p, offset + 2)
          < modular_inverse(p, offset + 1),
      nat_subtract(p, 2))

  putnam_2025_b5: bool =
    FORALL (p: nat):
      (prime_nat(p) AND p > 3)
        IMPLIES
          (p :: rat) / 4 - 1 < (descent_count(p) :: rat)
END putnam_2025_b5
